questions.question_text: In major-culture mounds:

options.A: Many important archaeological cultures are found successively.
options.B: Several archaeological cultures are represented but only one culture is dominant among them.
options.C: Only one important culture is found.
options.D: Presence of one major religious monument is mandatory.

questions.explanation: Remains of old settlements and cultures are found under mounds. These cultures can be of several types—single-culture, main-culture, and multi-cultural. In single-culture mounds, only one culture is seen throughout. Some mounds represent only the Painted Grey Ware (P.G.W.) culture. Some are of Satavahana culture and some are of Kushana culture. In main (dominant) culture mounds, one culture remains dominant and other cultures, which may be of earlier periods or later periods, are not of special importance. In multi-cultural mounds, many cultures are found successively, which sometimes run alongside each other. Mounds excavated like those of Ramayana and Mahabharata can be used in the study of material aspects of culture. Excavation of mounds can be done in two ways—vertical and horizontal

questions.question_text: Where have tools made of bones been found in the following Neolithic sites?
questions.explanation: The division of history has been made into three parts: Prehistoric, Proto-historic, and Historic periods. Neolithic civilizations fall within the ambit of the Prehistoric period. Tools made of bones are found at the following Neolithic sites, among which Gufkral and Chirand are prominent Gufkral – This site is located in the Kashmir province. Its excavation was conducted by A.K. Sharma in 1981 AD. Bones of animals like sheep-goats etc., and tools made from them, have been obtained from here, such as—needles made of bone. The tools here include axes, adzes, scrapers, chisels, hoes etc. made on trap stone. Chirand – The important Neolithic site Chirand is located in the Saran district of Bihar in the Middle Ganga Valley. Among the tools here, polished stone axes, querns, hammers, chisels, borers, arrows, hoes, needles, bangles etc. made of bone and horn are found. Sarutaru – It is located 25 km south-east of Guwahati. During its excavation, material like axes was found. Pottery found from here is brown and grey in color with rope marks. This is a recent Neolithic site. Daojali Hading – It is located in Assam. Remains of axes made of Neolithic wood from 45 cm thick deposits, and stone axes, chisels, querns, mortars, pestles, and red-colored stamps on hand-made pottery can be seen here.

questions.question_text: Below are two statements: Statement (I): Iron tools of hoes and sickles, small weapons and horses have been found from Megalithic sites. Statement (II): Maski and Nagarjunakonda are sites of the Megalithic period. In the light of the above statements, select the correct answer from the options given below:

options.A: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true
options.B: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are false
options.C: Statement (I) is true, but Statement (II) is false
options.D: Statement (I) is false, but Statement (II) is true

questions.explanation: The culture that arose in the South after the end of the Neolithic period is called the Great Stone or Megalithic culture. People of this culture used large stones to preserve the remains of their dead. Large stones are called Megaliths. They were well-acquainted with agriculture. The main grains produced by them were rice, barley, gram, ragi etc. Cows, oxen, sheep, goats, horses etc. were their domestic animals. They used iron tools. Various types of iron tools such as swords, daggers, tridents, flat axes, hoes, chisels, sickles, knives, spears etc. were found in the excavation of graves. Along with this, iron tools of small weapons and horses were also found. Many Megalithic sites related to the Megalithic period have been found, among which Maski, Brahmagiri, Hallur from Karnataka and Nagarjunakonda, Kadamberpur from Andhra Pradesh are important. Both given statements I and II are correct

questions.question_text: Which of these Chalcolithic sites is located in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The period in which weapons of copper and stone are used together is called the 'Chalcolithic period'. This period extends to the pre-Harappan, Harappan, and post-Harappan periods. Gordon Childe has explained the importance of copper in his book 'WHAT HAPPENED IN HISTORY'. In North India, the Chalcolithic culture came into practice after the Stone Age cultures, whereas in South India, the Iron Age started directly after the Stone Age culture Ganeshwar Civilization - This is located at the source of the Kantli river in the Sikar district of Rajasthan. This civilization developed in 2800 BC. It is the oldest among the Chalcolithic cultures, hence it is called the Mother of Chalcolithic cultures. Its main sites are Ahar, Gilund, Marmi, and Balathal. Its excavation was done by R.C. Agrawal and Vijay Kumar in 1977. Songaon - This Chalcolithic site falls under the 'Jorwe culture'. Songaon, Inamgaon, and Chandoli in Pune are important Jorwe culture sites. Eran - This Chalcolithic site falls under the 'Malwa/Kayatha' culture. Its areas include Nagda, Navadatoli, Eran, and Gungeria. Its study was conducted by V.S. Wakankar.

questions.question_text: The stone tools of the Middle Palaeolithic period were made of:
questions.explanation: In the Middle Palaeolithic period, stones of jasper, chert, flint etc. began to be used instead of quartzite stones. The industry at this time was mainly of objects made from flakes. Due to the abundance of flakes, this period was termed as Flake Culture. A flake was a type of tool made by breaking a stone

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites belongs to the Neolithic period?
questions.explanation: The sites of the Neolithic period are as follows * In North-West India – (Baluchistan) – Mehrgarh, Kili Gul Mohammad, Rana Ghundai, Jalilpur, Sarai Khola. * In Kashmir – (Jhelum Valley) – Burzahom, Gufkral. * North India – Koldihwa (U.P.), Mahagara (U.P.), Chirand (Bihar), Senwar (Bihar). * East India – Pandu Rajar Dhibi in West Bengal, Sarutaru (Assam), Markdola (Assam). * Peninsular India – Brahmagiri, Hallur, Kodekal, Kupgal, Maski, Sanganakallu, Nagarjunakonda, Piklihal and Utnur, Paiyampalli (Tamil Nadu).

questions.question_text: From which period did stone paintings start in Bhimbetka?
questions.explanation: The Mesolithic period started around 9000 BC. Information about the Mesolithic period in India was first obtained in 1867 AD when C.L. Carlyle discovered microliths from the Vindhyan region. Its sites have been obtained from Rajasthan, Gujarat, U.P., West Bengal, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh. Two rock shelters of the Mesolithic period have been found near Pachmarhi in Madhya Pradesh, named Jambu Dwip and Dorothy Deep. The stone paintings and rock paintings obtained from Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh are indicative of the Mesolithic period

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites is not located in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Maheshwar is an ancient city and a famous tourist destination located in the Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh. It is situated on the banks of the Narmada river. Maheshwar is also known by the name 'Mahishmati'. In ancient times, this city was the capital of the Holkar state. Mention of Maheshwar is also found in Hindu religious texts 'Ramayana' and 'Mahabharata'

questions.question_text: Who obtained the first Neolithic tool in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The word Neolithic was first used by John Lubbock in 1865 in the book 'Prehistoric Times'. In the context of the world, the Neolithic period starts from 9 thousand BC, but in India it started in 7 thousand BC. First of all, in 1860 AD, 'Le Mesurier' obtained the first stone tool of this period from the Tons river valley of Uttar Pradesh

questions.question_text: On May 30, 1863, from which Palaeolithic tradition did Robert Bruce Foote find tools at Pallavaram near Madras?
questions.explanation: On May 30, 1863, Robert Bruce Foote discovered Palaeolithic tools of the handaxe-cleaver tradition from Pallavaram near Madras. Again in January 1864, many tools were obtained from Pallavaram. The handaxe culture is also called Madras culture or Madras industry

questions.question_text: Robert Bruce Foote found the first Early Palaeolithic tool in India in:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation─See the explanation of the above question.

questions.question_text: Robert Bruce Foote found a handaxe in 1863 at:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) PGT History, 2013 Explanation– See the explanation of the above question.

questions.question_text: Who studied the animal bones at the Mesolithic site 'Damdama'?
questions.explanation: The Mesolithic site Damdama is located in the Pratapgarh district of Uttar Pradesh in the Middle Ganga Valley region. Excavation of Damdama was carried out between 1982 and 1987 under the leadership of Prof. G.R. Sharma. Stone tools and animal bones and horns have been obtained from here. The animal bones here were studied by P.K. Thomas and P.P. Joglekar

questions.question_text: The early agricultural site located on the banks of a lake is—
questions.explanation: The oldest evidence of agriculture in the Indian subcontinent has been found from Lahuradewa, located on the banks of a lake in the Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. The oldest evidence of rice production has been found from here. It is important to note that the evidence of agriculture obtained from Mehrgarh is from 7000 BC, while the evidence of agriculture from Lahuradewa is available from 9000-7000 BC

questions.question_text: Which of the following are two excavated Acheulean sites? (1) Chirki-Nevasa (2) Chirand (3) Baghor (4) Hunsgi
questions.explanation: Chirki-Nevasa and Hunsgi are excavated Acheulean sites. Acheulean tools include handaxe, cleaver, scraper etc. which were mostly found in South India and Deccan. The oldest date of the Lower Palaeolithic period has been known from the site named Chirki-Nevasa located in Maharashtra. Remains of a tool manufacturing center have been found from the banks of Hunsgi located in Karnataka

questions.question_text: Arrange the cultural sequence of the following sites according to chronological order— (I) Ahar (II) Birbhanpur (III) Shravasti (IV) Gufkral Code :
questions.explanation: The cultural sequence of the sites given according to the question is Birbhanpur, Gufkral, Ahar and Shravasti. Birbhanpur is a Mesolithic site located in West Bengal, which was excavated by B.B. Lal in 1954 AD. Gufkral is a Neolithic site located in Kashmir, which was excavated by A.K. Sharma in 1981 AD. Ahar is a Chalcolithic site located in the Banas river valley in Rajasthan, which was first excavated by A.K. Vyas in 1953 AD. Shravasti was an important city of the Mahajanapada period and Buddha's time, which was the capital of the Kosala Mahajanapada

questions.question_text: In which of the following cultures was the lower part of the feet of the deceased cut before burial?
questions.explanation: In the Jorwe Chalcolithic culture, the lower part of the feet of the deceased was cut before burial. The expansion of Jorwe culture was in Western Maharashtra. Daimabad, Jorwe, Nevasa, Inamgaon, Chandoli, Bahal, Prakash etc. are the main sites of Jorwe culture. Although the Jorwe culture was rural, many of its settlements like Daimabad and Inamgaon had reached the urban stage. Evidence of circular huts has been found from Inamgaon

questions.question_text: Which of the following human groups is considered the most intelligent type?
questions.explanation: Homo neanderthalensis is generally considered the human of the Middle Palaeolithic period, who is the most intelligent type of human among the given options. Homo-neanderthalensis was the first human to use fire extensively and was the first human to perform funeral rites for the deceased. Homo neanderthalensis started using clothes made of leather to cover the body. Homo erectus is considered the human of the Lower Palaeolithic period

questions.question_text: Muchchatla Chintamanu Gavi, an archaeological cave site, is associated with:
questions.explanation: Muchchatla Chintamanu Gavi archaeological cave site is an Upper Palaeolithic site located in Andhra Pradesh from where tools made of bone and horn have been found in maximum numbers. Other Upper Palaeolithic sites in Andhra Pradesh are Renigunta, Betamcherla, Vemula, Kurnool etc. The remains of the oldest hearth in India have been obtained from the Bilasurgam cave of Kurnool. Signs of human existence and fire have been found from the Kurnool caves

questions.question_text: (I) Jwalapuram-9 (II) Attirampakkam (III) Isampur (IV) Jalalpur and Dina Select the correct answer from the code given below: Arrange the following Palaeolithic sites in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The sequence of Palaeolithic sites given as per the question is Attirampakkam, Isampur, Jalalpur and Dina, and Jwalapuram-9. Attirampakkam is the richest Palaeolithic site in Tamil Nadu. Excavation was first carried out here by King in 1863 AD. Similarly, Isampur located in Karnataka was an extremely important center for making Palaeolithic tools. Jwalapuram-9 is an important Palaeolithic site located in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh. Similarly, Jalalpur and Dina are Palaeolithic sites located in the Riwat Valley of Pakistan

questions.question_text: Which of the following Neolithic sites are dated to the sixth millennium BC? (I) Koldihwa (II) Mahagara (III) Tokwa (IV) Panchoh
questions.explanation: The date of Neolithic sites Koldihwa and Tokwa located in the Belan Valley is 6000 BC. Evidence of paddy cultivation and burnt ears of paddy have been obtained from the Neolithic site of Koldihwa. The people here were familiar with both wild and cultivated species of rice, which is evidence from 6000 BC. Evidence of agriculture from 6000 BC has also come to light from the Tokwa site located at the confluence of the Belan and Adwa rivers in Mirzapur

questions.question_text: Which of the following human types is associated with Lower Palaeolithic culture?
questions.explanation: &b) : Homo erectus and Homo habilis humans are associated with the Lower Palaeolithic period. Similarly, Homo neanderthal human is associated with the Middle Palaeolithic period while Homo sapiens human is considered to be associated with the Upper Palaeolithic period. Homo erectus is the oldest bipedal human and was the first straight-walking ape-man. The credit for the invention of fire is given only to Homo erectus. The first human to perform funeral rites for the dead was Homo neanderthal, while Homo sapiens is considered the first modern and wise human. The commission has accepted both options a and b as correct in its revised answer key

questions.question_text: Which of the following methods was not used in the manufacture of Mesolithic tools?
questions.explanation: Fluting technique, impact-counter impact technique and pressure technique were used in the manufacture of Mesolithic tools. Grinding technique was not used in tool manufacturing in this period. Mesolithic tools were called microliths because of their small size compared to Palaeolithic tools. These tools were generally made on small flakes with parallel edges from silica stones like quartzite, chert, chalcedony, jasper, agate

questions.question_text: In which year did the Archaeological Survey of India become a permanent department?
questions.explanation: The Archaeological Survey of India was established in 1861 AD during the period of Viceroy Lord Canning. The Archaeological Survey of India was made permanent in 1906 AD. In 1871 AD, General Cunningham was appointed as the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India. Cunningham was essentially a numismatist. He is also called the father of Indian Archaeology. Dayaram Sahni was the first Indian who was appointed as the Director General of the Archaeological Department in 1931 AD

questions.question_text: Who was made the Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India after John Marshall?
questions.explanation: After John Marshall, H. Hargreaves was made the Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India. The Archaeological Survey of India was established in 1861 AD, which was made permanent in 1906 AD. Cunningham was made the first Director General of the Archaeological Department in 1871 AD. John Marshall remained the Director General of the Archaeological Department from 1902-1928, after which H. Hargreaves remained its Director General from 1928-1931. Dayaram Sahni became its Director General in 1931 AD, who was the first Indian

questions.question_text: Which of the following is suitable for Potassium-Argon dating?
questions.explanation: Basalt is suitable for Potassium-Argon dating. The Potassium-Argon method is a method for determining the date of extremely old objects. In this method, the amount of radioactive potassium (K40) available in objects and the argon (Ar40) formed from its decay is used as a measuring scale. This method was developed by W. Gentner around 1950 AD. Through this method, the date of objects from 30 thousand years old up to 30 crore years old can be determined

questions.question_text: Mortimer Wheeler compared which excavation method to a railway timetable of a train whose whereabouts are unknown?
questions.explanation: Mortimer Wheeler compared the vertical or longitudinal excavation method to a railway timetable of a train whose whereabouts are unknown. Generally, there are two methods of excavation: vertical and horizontal. Vertical excavation means digging straight down vertically so that the chronological sequence of various cultures can be revealed. It is generally limited to only some parts of the site. Horizontal excavation means digging the whole mound or a large part of it. Through this type of digging, a complete impression of the culture of a specific period of that site can be obtained

questions.question_text: Which of the following civilizations was initially known as the Black and Red Ware culture?
questions.explanation: Stone-age humans initially resided in the area of the Ahar civilization. In ancient inscriptions, the old name of Ahar is recorded as 'Tambavati' (Copper city). These people used red, brown, and black clay vessels which were fired using the inverted firing style. Houses were made of baked bricks. Animal husbandry was the main basis of their economy. In other words, this civilization is known as the Black and Red Ware culture

questions.question_text: Which Stone Age is called a 'revolution' in human life?
questions.explanation: The Neolithic revolution was the first revolution of world humanity. In the Neolithic age, humans learned to practice agriculture and learned animal husbandry and pastoralism to assist in agricultural work. He made sharper tools from stone. Humans began to farm systematically through irrigation systems by building dams on rivers and began to make tools by melting copper and bronze. When he built cities as centers of trade, he entered the state of civilization. If the characteristics of these three revolutions and the societies formed due to them are considered, it is found that simple society came into existence due to the Neolithic agricultural revolution

questions.question_text: Which hominid species developed the stone tool technique "Acheulean"?
questions.explanation: Along with diversity, a lot of refinement is seen in the tools of Homo erectus. They can be called the pioneers of the culture of double-edged hand-axes and sharp cutting tools. Compared to the crude tools made by the Oldowan technique, the tools of Homo erectus were quite refined. This human is called the human of the Acheulean technique

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river is the famous Mesolithic site Bagor located?
questions.explanation: The most famous site in Rajasthan is the Bagor site of Bhilwara district, from where remains of ancient animal husbandry have been obtained in addition to Mesolithic sites. This site is situated on the bank of the Kothari river, a tributary of the Banas river. The excavation work was done in 1968-70 by Dr. Virendra Nath Misra, Dr. L.S. Leshnik, and Deccan College Poona with the cooperation of the Rajasthan Archaeology Department. This site is considered a Stone Age civilization; remains of fourteen types of agriculture have been found from the Bagor civilization

questions.question_text: The first evidence of metal in the Indian subcontinent was at -------.
questions.explanation: In the Indian subcontinent, a system like ancient agriculture and animal husbandry has been found in Mehrgarh, which is located in Baluchistan. Mehrgarh is an area dating to 7000 BC from where tools and vessels have also been found. A drill made of copper has been obtained here. Evidence of making sharp metal weapons and tools has been found. This proves that the use of metal must have started first from here

questions.question_text: On which river is the Kayatha site situated?
questions.explanation: Kayatha culture is a Chalcolithic site situated on the bank of the Chhoti Kali Sindh river in Ujjain (M.P.). It is considered junior to and contemporary with Harappa. 29 bangles and two axes were found in a house here; this is also called Malwa culture. High-quality black-and-red pottery has been found from Malwa. Navdatoli is a site of Malwa which was discovered by Sankalia. This is the largest rural settlement among all Chalcolithic sites. Kayatha culture is located in western Madhya Pradesh. Meanwhile, the Banas (Ahar) culture developed in south-eastern Rajasthan and the Jorwe culture in western Maharashtra

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the Chalcolithic cultures of India?

options.A: Chalcolithic cultures were primarily rural cultures.
options.B: People of Chalcolithic cultures mostly lived near rivers and hills.
options.C: Black and red colored pottery were widely used in these cultures.
options.D: Jorwe is a Chalcolithic site which is related to the Malwa culture.

questions.explanation: Jorwe culture is a Chalcolithic culture discovered by M.N. Deshpande. Jorwe culture is situated on the bank of the 'Pravara' river, a tributary of the Godavari river in the Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra state, which is an archaeological site. The main sites of Jorwe culture are Chandoli, Songaon, Inamgaon, Jorwe, Nasik, and Daimabad. This culture is not related to the Malwa culture because Malwa is a Chalcolithic culture of Madhya Pradesh. The Commission has deleted this question in the final answer key

questions.question_text: In India, Sohan culture is related to which era?
questions.explanation: In India, the emergence of Sohan culture is considered to be from the Sohan river, a small tributary of the Indus river. This river valley has been considered of special importance for prehistoric study. In 1928 AD, D.N. Wadia obtained tools of the Early Stone Age from this area. This team surveyed a vast area from the Kashmir Valley to the Salt Range

questions.question_text: The feature which is not a characteristic of the Neolithic period:

options.C: Remarkable progress in pottery making art compared to previous ages.

questions.explanation: The Neolithic age was a period of development in human technology which is considered to have started from 9000 BC. In this period, human life began to move towards a civilized society. Through settled life, animal husbandry, and tools with grinding and polishing, progress was made in the agricultural field, which led to an increase in productivity and dependence on grain. The main tools of the Neolithic age include the central tool axe (central tool, meaning- main/central/special), adze, scraper, chisel, hoe, etc. Option (c) is wrong because compared to previous ages, there was an increase in the quantity of pottery making rather than remarkable progress in the art itself

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the Paleolithic age in India?

options.A: Paleolithic sites have been found from all over India.
options.B: Paleolithic sites have been found in the maximum number in the alluvial plains of Ganga and Indus.
options.C: Paleolithic sites have been obtained from Marwar and Mewar.
options.D: Layers of material from Early Paleolithic to Upper Paleolithic have been found from Sanghi Talab in Didwana.

questions.explanation: Paleolithic sites have been obtained from almost all parts of the Indian subcontinent, but their number is almost negligible in the alluvial plains of the Ganga and Indus rivers. Paleolithic sites have been found in abundance in the Rajasthan region, where remains of Lower, Middle, and Upper or Late Paleolithic stratigraphy are found from Marwar, Mewar, Chittor, Amarpura, Singi Talab, and Didwana

questions.question_text: Under whose leadership was excavation first started in India by the ASI?
questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham first started excavation in India through the A.S.I. The Archaeological Survey of India is an organization for archaeological research and conservation of cultural heritage; its main task is the maintenance of ancient monuments and archaeological sites and remains of national importance. It was established in 1861 AD, and its headquarters is located in New Delhi. Marshall conducted the first excavation of the Indus civilization. The Rajasthan Commission has considered option (a) as the answer to this question

questions.question_text: Who provided information about the discovery of tools and their implementation in the Neolithic age?
questions.explanation: The practice of polishing stones starts from the Neolithic age itself. Neolithic tools were first obtained from Lingsugur in Mysore, Karnataka in 1842, but information about the discovery of tools and the Neolithic age on a wide scale was provided by Le Mesurier. In 1860, he obtained polished celts of the Neolithic age from the Tons river valley in the Allahabad district of Uttar Pradesh. Major Neolithic tools include polished axes, adzes, chisels, picks, and pointed tools, etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Mesolithic age is wrong?

options.A: This was a transition period between the Mesolithic and Neolithic ages.
options.B: They started domesticating animals like cows, dogs, bulls, and goats.
options.C: The qualitative characteristic of Mesolithic tools was that they were microlithic.
options.D: In the year 1867, Carlyle first discovered microliths from the rock shelters of the Vindhyas.

questions.explanation: The Mesolithic age is considered the transition period between the Upper Paleolithic age and the Neolithic age. The Mesolithic age is placed around 9000 BC. This period is seen as the timeframe after the end of the Ice Age around 10,000 BC and the beginning of climate change. The beginning of animal husbandry is considered the main feature of this era, evidence of which has been obtained from Adamgarh and Bagor

questions.question_text: The date of Neolithic stabilization in India is approximately:
questions.explanation: While the Neolithic age is considered to start from 9000 BC in the global context, the chronology of the Neolithic settlement obtained from Mehrgarh in the Indian subcontinent has been placed at 7000 BC. On this basis, the date of Neolithic stabilization in India is considered to be 7000 BC

questions.question_text: The information about making collections found in the salt-lake of the Sambhar region suitable for agriculture is of approximately this period:
questions.explanation: From the study of the deposits of the old salt-lake Sambhar in Rajasthan, it appears that plants were grown around 7000-6000 BC and agricultural work had already begun

questions.question_text: In which of these Neolithic regions did tools and equipment made from bones start appearing without hindrance? (1) Burzahom (2) Chirand (3) Allahabad (4) Mehrgarh Choose the correct group:
questions.explanation: There are many characteristics of the Neolithic culture of Kashmir, such as pit-dwellings, diversity of pottery, and various types of tools made of bone along with stones. Similarly, Chirand near Patna is also a place in the Ganga valley from where bone tools have been obtained. In this way, bone tools have been obtained from Chirand along with places like Burzahom and Gufkral in Kashmir

questions.question_text: The Chalcolithic economy was:
questions.explanation: In the cultures of the Chalcolithic period, humans used tools made of stone and copper together. The economic base of the people of the Chalcolithic culture was based on a rural economy, which was spread over vast areas of the country in hilly and riverine regions

questions.question_text: What is meant by the word 'Dolmens'?

options.A: Making tools using bone and wood
options.B: Clay vessels made on a wheel

questions.explanation: The word 'Dolmens' refers to tombs built over buried dead. This is a word of the Celtic language which literally means stone table. Its shape used to be like a rectangular table. Generally, they were constructed above the ground surface. To make a box-shaped grave for burying the dead, such structures were constructed by standing four or more stone slabs on all sides

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): Neolithic people had established their habitats away from hilly regions. Reason (R): Neolithic people were completely dependent on stone-made tools and weapons.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: In the Neolithic period, humans had become associated with food production and agriculture. Therefore, by this period, humans had started making residences away from hilly regions. Due to the development of agricultural work and the production process, there was some decrease in the dependence on stone tools, although stone was still being used in this period

questions.question_text: The first subject learned by primitive man was:
questions.explanation: The beginning of animal husbandry is considered to be from the Mesolithic age itself. Whereas the remaining other subjects are related to the Neolithic age

questions.question_text: Hominids that are racially different from Homo sapiens are generally called:
questions.explanation: Human-like creatures, i.e., early creatures from which humans evolved, are called hominids

questions.question_text: Which of the following Neolithic sites is known for ash mounds?
questions.explanation: One of the main features of South Indian Neolithic settlements is ash mounds. Ash mounds have been obtained from sites like Pallavoy (Andhra Pradesh), Utnur (Andhra Pradesh), Piklihal, Brahmagiri, Maski (all in Karnataka), etc

questions.question_text: Identify the Neolithic sites where evidence of rice cultivation has been found: (1) Koldihwa (2) Utnur (3) Mahagara (4) Mehrgarh Choose the correct code:
questions.explanation: Evidence of rice cultivation has been found from the Neolithic sites of Koldihwa and Mahagara located in the Belan Valley region

questions.question_text: Ancient evidence of _______ has been found from Adamgarh in Madhya Pradesh and Bagor in Rajasthan:
questions.explanation: The Mesolithic age is considered the transition period between the Upper Paleolithic age and the Neolithic age. The Mesolithic age is placed around 9000 BC. This period is seen as the timeframe after the end of the Ice Age around 10,000 BC and the beginning of climate change. The beginning of animal husbandry is considered the main feature of this era, evidence of which has been obtained from Adamgarh and Bagor

questions.question_text: Which statement regarding Alexander Cunningham is not correct?

options.A: He was the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India department.
options.B: He is called the father of Indian Archaeology.
options.C: He carried forward Lord Curzon's work of preserving ancient Indian heritage.
options.D: Harappa was excavated during his tenure.

questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham was the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India. He is called the father of Indian archaeology. Harappa was excavated during his tenure. The statement that he carried forward Lord Curzon's work of preserving ancient Indian heritage is not correct

questions.question_text: "Archaeological material is the best touchstone of history." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: 'Archaeological material is the best touchstone of history'; this is the statement of Rahul Sankrityayan. Rahul Sankrityayan, who is given the title of Mahapandit, was a major literary figure of Hindi and was a renowned polyglot

questions.question_text: Microliths are mainly related to:
questions.explanation: Microliths are mainly related to the Mesolithic age. Information about the Mesolithic age in India was first obtained in 1867 AD when C.L. Carlyle discovered microlithic tools from the Vindhya region. The tools of this period were blades, burins, scrapers, and borers

questions.question_text: At which of the following places have remains of modern humans 80,000 to 100,000 years old from the present time been found?
questions.explanation: Remains of modern humans 80,000 to 100,000 years old from the present time were obtained from the Niah Cave of Borneo

questions.question_text: Which of the following was probably the first metal used in India?
questions.explanation: The first metal used for tools was 'copper'. It is believed that the first use of copper was around 5000 BC. Copper was obtained from Khetri in Rajasthan. Before the use of copper, stone tools were used. Due to the discovery of copper, this period was called the Chalcolithic age

questions.question_text: Evidence of digging pits on an Indian site has been found from which of the following ancient sites?
questions.explanation: The first Neolithic extension tools were obtained by Le Mesurier in 1860 AD in the Tons river valley of U.P. Many pit-dwellings (pit houses), pottery, and several bone tools have been obtained from Neolithic sites Burzahom and Gufkral (located in the Kashmir province). In the graves found from Burzahom, pet dogs were buried along with their masters

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not associated with a tool tradition of ancient India?
questions.explanation: Groessian is not associated with a tool tradition of ancient India. Mousterian has been placed under a tool category. Acheulean and Oldowan have also been displayed as tool types. All these tools have been placed in the category of the oldest tools

questions.question_text: Which region is called the textbook of Indian prehistory?
questions.explanation: The Belan river valley (a tributary of the Tons river) originates from the Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh and meets the Tons river in Allahabad district after passing through Mirzapur district. This valley region is famous for archaeological discoveries; this valley region is also called the textbook of Indian prehistory

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a type of hand-axe tool?
questions.explanation: Flake technique, Chopper-Chopping technique, and Borer technique were used in the manufacture of hand-axe (kuthar) type stone tools, whereas hand-axe tools were first obtained from Madras and Attirampakkam. These also include tools like cleavers, scrapers, etc. Pebble tools are not of this category. The Commission had removed this question in its revised answer key Ans: (*) The manufacturing of various (crude) types of stone tools involved the flake method, chopper-chopping method, and borer method, while handaxe tools were first obtained from Madras and Attirampakkam. These included tools like cleavers and scrapers. Pebble tools do not belong to this category. The Commission had removed this question from its revised answer key.

questions.question_text: Basuli (adze), chisel, and perforated round stones belong to which culture?
questions.explanation: In Neolithic sites like Burzahom and Gufkral (Kashmir region), many types of pottery and tools made of stone and bone have been found. The main tools here were adzes, chisels, etc., which were used to perform agricultural activities

questions.question_text: Burzahom is the center of which prehistoric culture?
questions.explanation: Burzahom (Jammu-Kashmir) is considered a major center of the Neolithic Age. Evidence of agriculture, animal husbandry, and pit dwellings has been found here

questions.question_text: In which metal was tin first mixed?
questions.explanation: Copper holds a prominent place in the history of human civilization because, in ancient times, the names of copper and bronze (copper + tin) appear among the first metals and alloys used by humans

questions.question_text: Which metal was called the 'democratic metal' by V. Gordon Childe?
questions.explanation: V. Gordon Childe was an Australian archaeologist. He called iron the democratic metal. He was famous for emphasizing the role of revolutionary technological and economic development in human society. His views related to the Neolithic Revolution and Urban Revolution reflect the influence of Marxist thoughts related to social development. Childe used technological criteria to subdivide the Stone Age into Palaeolithic and Neolithic. He was the first to define the 'Neolithic-Chalcolithic Age' as a self-reliant food economy

questions.question_text: The main characteristics of the Neolithic Age are/is:
questions.explanation: The main characteristics of the Neolithic Age include two elements - animal husbandry and agriculture. Early evidence of animal husbandry begins to be found in the final phase of the Mesolithic period, in which Adamgarh (Hoshangabad, M.P.) and Bagor (Bhilwara, Rajasthan) are the prominent sites. In the Neolithic Age, agriculture and animal husbandry traditionally began; the manufacture of polished stone tools is main in this period. The production of food grains first occurred in the Neolithic Age; in this period, wild varieties of barley and wheat were made suitable for cultivation, which led to the emergence of cultivated wheat. In recent discoveries, the oldest evidence of rice production was found in Lahuradewa (Sant Kabir Nagar, (U.P.)) between 9000 BC and 8000 BC

questions.question_text: Which of these ages is called the transition period?
questions.explanation: The Mesolithic Age is considered a transition period. By this age, the Ice Age had completely ended and the climate had become warm and humid. The most important achievement of the Mesolithic Age was making humans animal herders. Along with this, sharp and refined tools began to be used in this period. The oldest evidence of human skeletal remains and plantation is found in the Mesolithic Age itself

questions.question_text: Match the authors in List-I with their published books in List-II. List-I List-II A. D.D. Kosambi 1. Indian Feudalism B. R.S. Sharma 2. Myth and Reality C. G.C. Pande 3. Somanatha: The Many Voices of History D. Romila Thapar 4. Foundations of Indian Culture Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is D.D. Kosambi - Myth and Reality R.S. Sharma - Indian Feudalism G.C. Pande - Foundations of Indian Culture Romila Thapar - Somanatha: The Many Voices of History

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following Chalcolithic cultures in India? 1. Kayatha 2. Ahar 3. Malwa 4. Jorwe
questions.explanation: Indian Chalcolithic cultures are rural cultures. Based on the remains available from the excavation of Chalcolithic sites, the chronological order of the major Chalcolithic cultures of India is - Kayatha, Ahar, Malwa, Jorwe. Information is obtained from sites like Kayatha (Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh), Ahar (Udaipur, Rajasthan), Malwa (Madhya Pradesh), and Jorwe (Ahmednagar in Maharashtra)

questions.question_text: Which of the following prehistoric sites in Rajasthan belongs to the Chalcolithic period?
questions.explanation: Ahar, Gilund, Marmi, and Balathal are the major Chalcolithic sites located in Rajasthan. Since these sites are in the Banas river region, the Chalcolithic culture here is also called the Banas culture. Balathal was discovered by V.N. Misra. Red-slipped pottery, berries, and evidence of U-shaped hearths are found at Balathal

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct regarding the Bagor site?

options.B: We have carbon dates for the period 5365-3775 BC regarding its pure Mesolithic pre-pottery phase.
options.C: Agricultural signs have been found from its beginning.
options.D: Zebu, cattle, sheep, goats, and pigs were domesticated as pets from around 5000 BC.

questions.explanation: Bagor is located in the Bhilwara district of Rajasthan. V.N. Misra conducted excavation work here from 1968 to 1970. Bagor is the largest Mesolithic site in India. Evidence of the Mesolithic, Chalcolithic, and Iron Age is found here. Adamgarh in Madhya Pradesh and Bagor are two Mesolithic sites that present the oldest evidence of animal husbandry. Chalcedony tools have been found in large quantities from Bagor. Zebu, cattle, sheep, goats, and pigs were domesticated as pets at Bagor from around 5000 BC. Regarding its pure Mesolithic pre-pottery phase, we have carbon dates for the period 5365-3775 BC. Agricultural signs are not found here from the beginning

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the Bharatpur archaeological site?

options.A: It is located in West Bengal.
options.B: It is located in Rajasthan from where remains of migratory birds' bones were found.
options.C: Evidence of fishing, hunting, and agriculture was found in Period I.
options.D: Evidence of the use of iron and Northern Black Polished Ware was found in Period II.

questions.explanation: The Bharatpur archaeological site is located in West Bengal. Copper objects have been obtained from Period-I here, which are associated with the Black and Red Ware culture. Along with these, microliths, Neolithic axes, and baked clay beads have also been found. Burnt remains of rice were found in a pit here. In Chalcolithic Period-II, some quantity of copper objects has been found. From this same period, iron spearheads and iron slag have also been found. Many other types of pottery have also been found here, including black pottery coated with a slurry of fine clay and a grey/buff-slipped pottery. Remains of bones of animals like domestic cattle, buffalo, goat, and deer along with sambar, fish, turtle, and birds have been found

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the largest known Mesolithic settlement area in India?
questions.explanation: The tools of the Mesolithic period were extremely small, so they were called 'Microliths'. It appears as a transitional phase between the Palaeolithic Age and the Neolithic Age. Mesolithic centers are found in large numbers in Rajasthan, southern Uttar Pradesh, central and eastern India, and south of the Krishna River. Evidence obtained from Adamgarh in Madhya Pradesh and Bagor in Rajasthan indicates animal husbandry. Five human skeletons were found from Bagor from the Mesolithic Age, which were buried in an organized manner. The maximum amount of Stone Age material has been obtained from this site. Among these, scrapers, points, borers, scrapers, etc., are prominent. Very small objects were manufactured in the industry here, and they were very advanced from a geometric point of view. This area was considered the largest site of the Mesolithic settlement area

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites were human fossils found in situ with Palaeolithic tools?
questions.explanation: Among the fossils in the Narmada Valley of India, remains of a human skull were discovered at Hathnora in Sehore on December 5, 1982, along with fossils of elephants, horses, hippopotamuses, and wild buffaloes. Human fossils here were found along with tools. Fossils of both teeth and the upper jaw of the oldest extinct elephant (Stegodon) were also found on the northern bank of the Narmada at Surajkund

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites was a fossilized human infant skull found in 2001?
questions.explanation: In the year 2001, P. Rajendran of Kerala University found a complete infant skull at Odai in Villupuram district. Its date was determined to be 166,000 years, which belongs to the Middle to Upper Pleistocene period

questions.question_text: At which of the following Neolithic sites of the Indian subcontinent has the oldest evidence of crop production been found?
questions.explanation: Mehrgarh, located between the border regions of modern Pakistan and Iran, is considered a major site from the pre-pottery Neolithic period to the Harappan period. Evidence of cultivation of three varieties of wheat and two varieties of barley has been found here. It is called the "Bread Basket of Balochistan". Therefore, it is known as the major area for crop production at a Neolithic site

questions.question_text: At which of the following Palaeolithic sites has evidence of a set of animal footprints been found along with Acheulean tools?
questions.explanation: Remains of Palaeolithic culture have been found from the Soan River Valley, Belan River Valley, and Narmada River Valley, and from the painted rock shelters named 'Bhimbetka' near Bhopal. Tools related to the Palaeolithic Age have been divided into two parts - Chopper-Chopping Pebble culture, Handaxe culture. Tools of the Handaxe culture were first obtained from Vadamadurai and Attirampakkam near Madras. These were manufactured by the core and flake system from ordinary stones. The tools of this culture are cleavers and scrapers. Evidence of a set of animal footprints along with Acheulean tools has been found at Attirampakkam

questions.question_text: Evidence of a slaughterhouse area has been obtained from-
questions.explanation: Mahadaha (Patti, Pratapgarh) is a Mesolithic site; evidence of an animal killing site (slaughterhouse) has been found here

questions.question_text: Who among these is credited with starting the study of the prehistory of India?
questions.explanation: Robert Bruce Foote was a British geologist and archaeologist. Associated with the Geological Survey, Bruce Foote first started the exploration of Stone Age settlements in India in 1863 AD

questions.question_text: Where has the bone figurine of Mother Goddess been obtained?

options.A: From the Lower Palaeolithic of the Vindhyan Valley
options.B: From the Middle Palaeolithic of the Son Valley
options.D: From the Upper Palaeolithic of the Vindhyan Valley

questions.explanation: In addition to Upper Palaeolithic tools, a bone-made figurine of Mother Goddess was found in the Lohanda Nala area of the Belan Valley located in the Vindhyan Valley, which is currently preserved in the Kaushambi Museum. The time of the Upper Palaeolithic culture of the Belan Valley has been determined between 30 thousand and 10 thousand BC

questions.question_text: From which of the following Mesolithic sites have burials containing skeletons of considerable length emerged? (i) Adamgarh (ii) Bhimbetka (iii) Mahadaha (iv) Sarai Nahar Rai Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
questions.explanation: Burials containing skeletons have been found at Mesolithic sites, among which Mahadaha and Sarai Nahar Rai, located 15 km away from the Pratapgarh district headquarters, are important places. In addition to pair burials, 15 human skeletons and 08 pit hearths have been obtained from here. The graves (cemeteries) here were located inside the settlement area

questions.question_text: Bagor Phase I belongs to which of the following cultures?
questions.explanation: The oldest evidence of animal husbandry has been found from the Mesolithic sites named Adamgarh in M.P. and Bagor in Rajasthan. Their time could be approximately 5000 BC. The tools used in the Mesolithic Age were very small. Therefore, they were called Microlithic. The first remains of the human skeleton in this period were obtained from the sites named Sarai Nahar Rai and Mahadaha in Pratapgarh (U.P.)

questions.question_text: From which of the following sites in the Indian subcontinent was the first hominid fossil discovered?
questions.explanation: A human skull has been obtained from Hathnora (M.P.) in the Narmada Valley. It is considered the first human remain obtained in India. The credit for its discovery goes to Dr. Arun Sonakia. Hathnora is a site of the Lower Palaeolithic Age. Other Lower Palaeolithic sites are as follows - Pallavaram, Attirampakkam, etc

questions.question_text: From which of the following sites have circular pit dwellings been found in the Chalcolithic period?
questions.explanation: Inamgaon is a Chalcolithic site located on the bank of the Ghod River, a tributary of the Bhima River, in the Pune district of Maharashtra. Large-scale excavation of Inamgaon was conducted under the leadership of H.D. Sankalia, M.K. Dhavalikar, and Z.D. Ansari (1968-1983). Evidence of rectangular and circular pit dwellings has been obtained from here, which were constructed under a definite plan. Residential evidence of potters, blacksmiths, bead makers, lime makers, ivory craftsmen, etc., has been found here

questions.question_text: Which Neolithic site in India was first reported?
questions.explanation: The credit for first revealing Indian prehistory goes to Dr. Primrose, who obtained prehistoric tools in 1842 AD from a Neolithic site named Lingsugur in the Raichur district of Karnataka

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a famous prehistoric site for rock paintings?
questions.explanation: The prehistoric site Bhimbetka is located near Bhopal. Many painted caves, rock shelters (shelters made of rocks), and many prehistoric artworks have been obtained from this Palaeolithic site. Bhimbetka is located in the Narmada River Valley. The oldest evidence of painting has been obtained from Bhimbetka itself. It is related to the Palaeolithic Age

questions.question_text: Which of the following prehistoric sites is known for the production of microlithic tools in large quantities?
questions.explanation: Both Bagor and Adamgarh are related to the Mesolithic Age. The Mesolithic Age was associated with the tools of the Microlithic Age; ancient evidence of animal husbandry is also found at both places. The caves of Adamgarh, which are in Madhya Pradesh, yield about 2500 small microlithic tools. Adamgarh is located near the Narmada River, 2 km from Hoshangabad city in Madhya Pradesh state. Remains of Microlithic Age civilization can be easily seen in the paintings done in the caves of Adamgarh

questions.question_text: Which of the following objects are known from copper hoard sites?
questions.explanation: All these four objects are known from copper hoard sites– (a) Anthropomorphic figures (b) Antennae swords (c) Harpoons (d) Flat celts

questions.question_text: From which prehistoric site has evidence of India's oldest huts been found?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Evidence of the oldest huts has been found from Paisra (Bihar). Paisra is a site of the Stone Age. It was discovered by Vidula Jayaswal in 1947. Evidence of huts and floors made by stone paving has also been found from the Mesolithic site Bagor (Rajasthan). Many small furnaces, one large community furnace, a hut floor, and many graves have been found from Sarai Nahar in U.P. Evidence of post-holes has also been found from here.

questions.question_text: What is correct about the Mesolithic Age? Select the correct answer from the codes given below: (i) Generally, microlithic tools have been found. (ii) Bagor, Langhnaj, and Bhimbetka are some important sites. (iii) Bones of wild and domestic animals have been found. (iv) Rock paintings of this period are available. Codes:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Information regarding the Mesolithic Age in India was first obtained in 1867 AD when C.L. Carlyle discovered microliths from the Vindhyan region. After this, such microliths were discovered from different parts of the country. The most prominent site of Rajasthan is Bagor, located in Bhilwara district. V.N. Misra conducted excavation work here from 1968 to 1970. In addition to tools from the Mesolithic Age, tools from the Iron Age also came to light here. Langhnaj, located in Gujarat province, is the most important site where extensive excavation was conducted by archaeologists like H.D. Sankalia, B. Subbarao, A.R. Kennedy, etc. Similarly, tools of the Mesolithic Age are obtained from the rock shelters and caves of Bhimbetka. Evidence of human burial is also found here. This cave was discovered by V.S. Wakankar in 1958 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.A: Lower Palaeolithic Age : Hunting, food gathering
options.B: Upper Palaeolithic Age : Hunting, food gathering

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June 2012) Explanation– In the Mesolithic Age, along with hunting and food gathering by humans, animal husbandry had also started, whereas food production began in the Neolithic Age. Along with this, permanent human life started.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Neolithic site located in the Vindhyan region?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation– The Neolithic site Mahagara is located in the Vindhyan region, which is situated on the bank of the Yamuna River, about 70 km south of Allahabad city. It is known that it was discovered by Prof. G.R. Sharma of Allahabad University in 1949 and 1951-56.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below: List-I
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation – The correct match is as follows: List-I List-II Palaeolithic – Chipped stone tools Mesolithic – Microlithic stone tools Neolithic – Ground stone tools Upper Palaeolithic – Rock painting

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities is not related to the Megalithic culture?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation – The culture that emerged in the South after the end of the Neolithic age was called the Large Stone or Megalithic culture. Its various sites are Brahmagiri, Maski, Adichanallur, Hallur etc. An ash mound has been found at Utnoor. This site is related to the Neolithic period.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following archaeologists in their chronological order and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below: (i) James Fergusson (ii) James Prinsep (iii) Alexander Cunningham (iv) Edward Thomas Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – Alexander Cunningham is considered the founder of the Archaeological Survey of India. First of all, in 1837 AD, James Prinsep succeeded in reading the Delhi-Topra inscription of Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Flake tools made by the Levallois technique are a characteristic of which geological era?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – The Levallois technique is a characteristic of the Middle Palaeolithic period. During this time, instead of quartzite stones, stones like jasper, chert, flint etc. were used. Due to the predominance of flakes, this period is given the name of flake culture. A flake was a type of tool that was made by breaking a stone.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the following codes: List-I
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – A. Sohagi Ghat – I. A. C. L. Carlleyle B. Balathal – II. Ahar culture site C. Bhimbetka – III. V. S. Wakankar D. Burzahom – IV. Kashmir Neolithic Burzahom is a Neolithic period site in the Jammu-Kashmir state of India. Evidence of pit-dwellings is found here. Evidence of burial of a dog along with a human is found here.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given codes. List-I
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation – The correctly matched answer is as follows– List-I List-II (a) Son culture/Sohan culture – (i) Lower Palaeolithic culture (b) Nevasa culture – (ii) Middle Palaeolithic culture (c) Bagor culture – (iii) Upper Palaeolithic culture (d) Koldihwa culture – (iv) Neolithic culture

questions.question_text: At which of the following Chalcolithic sites has evidence of the use of copper been found, but stone tools have not been found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation – The ancient name of Ahar is Tambavati, meaning the place of copper. Because here, mostly copper tools have been found instead of stone. Black and red pottery have also been found from here, which are decorated with white linear designs.

questions.question_text: From the excavation of which region is it known that the Neolithic human there lived by digging pits in the ground?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) RPSC 2018 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – From the excavation of the Kashmir region, it is known that the Neolithic human there lived by digging pits in the ground. Evidence of this is obtained from Burzahom. It is known that the first Neolithic site was discovered in Kashmir. The basic element of the Neolithic economy is knowledge of food production and domestication of animals.

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites was an ivory pendant found in a Microlithic context?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – From Damdama, a Mesolithic site located in the Pratapgarh district of U.P., an ivory pendant and many types of tools made from bones have been found. Besides this, 41 human burials and pit-hearths have come to light from here.

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites was the Jhukar culture found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation – The city of Chanhudaro, located south of Mohenjodaro, was first discovered in 1934 by N. Gopal Majumdar and excavation was conducted here by Mackay in 1835 AD. In Chanhudaro, besides the Indus culture, remains of Pre-Indus culture, Jhukar culture and Jhangar culture have also been found.

questions.question_text: The human fossil of Hathnora is:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper June, 2015) Explanation – A team led by scientist Arun Sonakia of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) discovered the fossil of Homo erectus on December 5, 1982, on the banks of the Narmada River at Hathnora (Madhya Pradesh). The research team claimed that it is a fossil of a female. It is believed that Homo erectus are the ancestors of modern humans Homo sapiens and existed about two lakh years ago.

questions.question_text: Practice of burial was started by?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper June, 2015) Explanation – Homo neanderthalensis represented the Middle Palaeolithic period. Neanderthal human respected the dead and buried the bodies in graves along with worship materials. In this way, he had some kind of belief in religion and rebirth. After Neanderthals, modern Homo sapiens emerged about forty thousand years ago today. It had many subspecies such as – Cro-Magnon, Grimaldi and Chancelade etc.

questions.question_text: Where has the largest number of copper hoards been found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper June, 2015) Explanation – The largest number of copper hoards has been obtained from Gungeria in Madhya Pradesh. These include 424 copper tools and 102 thin silver plates. But almost half of these copper hoards are concentrated in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab. These copper hoards are sometimes also associated with Ochre Coloured Pottery (O.C.P.).

questions.question_text: The archaeological remains of the oldest hearth in India were found from:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – The archaeological evidence of the oldest hearth in India has been obtained from Billasurgam located in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question_text: Where in South Asia has evidence of the oldest wheat-barley cultivation been found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – In South Asia, three cultural phases – Neolithic, Pre-Harappan and Harappan levels – are found from the excavation of a place named Mehrgarh (Pakistan) in Baluchistan. This was the oldest agrarian settlement of the Indian subcontinent and here evidence of cultivation of wheat, barley and lentils was found around 7000 B.C.

questions.question_text: Where has the largest semi-circular place of worship in the Indian subcontinent been discovered?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – The largest semi-circular place of worship in the Indian subcontinent has been obtained from Sirkap. This site is located in Taxila (modern Pakistan). Sun temple, semi-circular temple, stupa etc. have been obtained from here. Sirkap was built in the second century B.C. by the Indo-Greek ruler Demetrius, which was renovated by Menander I. Sirkap was first excavated by John Marshall and subsequently by Mortimer Wheeler.

questions.question_text: Where did humans live in the prehistoric age?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation – The period in which humans did not cite any written records of events is called the Prehistoric period. Humans of this period lived on platforms (machans), in caves and in huts.

questions.question_text: Which was the place in the Neolithic period from where a large number of tools and weapons made of bone were obtained?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Neolithic remains were obtained after the excavation of the rural site named Chirand in Bihar in 1962-63 AD under the leadership of Prof. V. K. Sinha. During the excavation, weapons and tools made from deer antlers were obtained in large quantities.

questions.question_text: Residents of the Ancient Stone Age had knowledge of which of the following subjects?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Remains of weapons of the Ancient Stone Age have been obtained from the Belan Valley of Mirzapur (U.P.), the Sohan River Valley of Punjab, and the caves of Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh. Humans of this period were unaware of fire. Humans lived a completely hunter-gatherer life and lived in groups in caverns and caves.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Neolithic archaeological sites is not known for ash mounds?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – The site named Burzahom was discovered in 1935 AD by De Terra and Paterson. Remains of houses with pits were found from the excavation of Burzahom. The examples of burial found there show that the practice of burying the pet dog along with the human was prevalent. Therefore, Burzahom is not known for ash mounds.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below: List-I (Mesolithic site) A. Birbhanpur B. Loteshwar C. Paisra D. Sarai Nahar Rai List-II (Location) (i) Bihar (ii) Gujarat (iii) Uttar Pradesh (iv) West Bengal Code: A (B) (C) (D)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – List-I (Mesolithic site) List-II (Location) A. Birbhanpur – West Bengal B. Loteshwar – Gujarat C. Paisra – Bihar D. Sarai Nahar Rai – Uttar Pradesh

questions.question_text: The oldest evidence of transition from the stage of hunting and food-gathering to the stage of animal husbandry and agriculture in the Indian subcontinent has been obtained from:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – The oldest evidence of transition from the stage of hunting and food-gathering to the stage of animal husbandry and agriculture in the Indian subcontinent has been obtained from Mehrgarh. The first clear evidence has been obtained from Mehrgarh on the banks of the Bolan River in the Kacchi plain on the border of Sindh and Baluchistan. Various varieties of agricultural wheat and barley have been obtained from here. Its certified date is the seventh millennium Before Christ (7000 B.C.). The date of Kili Gul Mohammad is 3500 B.C.

questions.question_text: The discovery of metal was a revolutionary event in human history. In which part of India were the mines providing the most copper located? (i) Bihar (ii) Gujarat (iii) Rajasthan (iv) Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – The discovery of metal was a revolutionary event in human history. The mines providing the most copper in India were located in Bihar, Gujarat and Rajasthan. Copper was obtained from the mines of Khetri in Rajasthan. In addition, copper was also obtained from Bihar and Gujarat. Singhbhum district of Bihar and Kutch region of Gujarat were famous for this.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a Neolithic site?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July, 2017 Explanation – Arikamedu, located in the Union Territory of Puducherry, India, is a site from the first century AD, which was excavated by Mortimer Wheeler in 1945. Evidence of Indo-Roman trade relations has been found here. Brahmagiri, Sanganakallu and Piklihal are Neolithic sites of South India.

questions.question_text: The cultural sequence of the excavated site Hastinapur from bottom to top is as follows: (i) Kushan period (ii) N.B.P. pottery period (iii) O.C.P. period (iv) P.G.W. period Code:
questions.explanation: Cultural sequence of Hastinapur (after excavation) O.C.P. period – Chalcolithic period P.G.W. period – Iron Age N.B.P. pottery period – Sixth century B.C. Kushan period – First century Excavation of this site, located in Meerut district of U.P., was conducted by B.B. Lal in 1950-52.

questions.question_text: In which of the following sites have proofs of animal husbandry been found in the Mesolithic period? (i) Adamgarh (ii) Bagor (iii) Loteshwar (iv) Ratanpur Code:
questions.explanation: Adamgarh in Madhya Pradesh, Bagor in Rajasthan and Loteshwar located in Patan district of Gujarat are such Mesolithic sites where evidence of animal husbandry has been found

questions.question_text: Match the subject of List-I with List-II: List-I (Remains) A. Ash mound B. Ayagapatta C. Eleven-headed Bodhisattva D. Stone reliquaries List-II (Finding place) (i) Kanheri (ii) Mathura (iii) Sanchi (iv) Utnoor Code: A (B) (C) (D)
questions.explanation: The correct match is as follows Ash mound - Utnoor Ayagapatta - Mathura Eleven-headed Bodhisattva - Kanheri Stone reliquaries - Sanchi

questions.question_text: Where has the oldest evidence of domestic buffalo been obtained in the Indian subcontinent?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation - The oldest evidence of domestic buffalo in the Indian subcontinent has been obtained from Mehrgarh, which describes buffaloes with their heads down and bellowing, in a fighting posture. The domestic animals of the Indus residents included bulls, cows, buffaloes, dogs, pigs, sheep-goats, deer, rabbits etc. They were acquainted with elephants because ivory was used in making artistic objects. Among birds, roosters, ducks, parrots, swans etc. were reared. Some animals had religious significance. Some were reared for meat. It is not certain whether they were acquainted with the horse or not. S.R. Rao is of the opinion that clay statues of horses have been found from Lothal and Rangpur. Similarly, bones of a domestic horse have been found from the Surkotada site located in Kutch.

questions.question_text: What was the main occupation of the people of the Early Stone Age?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – The main occupation of the Early Stone Age people was hunting. It should be noted that the people of this period did not have knowledge regarding agriculture. Therefore, their life was dependent on wild animals and fish obtained from rivers, lakes and other wild fruits.

questions.question_text: What was the main characteristic of the people of the Mesolithic period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The main characteristic of the people of the Mesolithic period was – use of microlithic tools. The tools of this period were made of small stones. There were also some tools whose shape was geometric.

questions.question_text: Is making clay pottery related to the Neolithic period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation– Pottery is first visible in the Neolithic period. From this it is clear that making clay pottery is related to the Neolithic period, it is true.

questions.question_text: The oldest mention of rice is related to which place?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 PGT History, 2005 Explanation – The oldest mention of rice has been obtained from the excavation of the major Neolithic site Koldihwa of the Vindhyan region. The oldest evidence of paddy cultivation (7000-6000 B.C.) occurs at this site.

questions.question_text: Where are the oldest records of agriculture in ancient India found?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The oldest records of agriculture in ancient India have been obtained from Mehrgarh. It is located in the Balochistan province of present-day Pakistan. Evidence of the oldest Neolithic settlement and mud houses, along with three varieties of wheat and two varieties of barley, has been obtained here.

questions.question_text: Stone Age man had knowledge of fire in—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Stone Age man first gained knowledge of fire in the Neolithic period when he learned to ignite fire by striking stones, which brought a revolutionary change in his life. With the use of fire, he began to get roasted meat and cooked food for eating. Fire was also used for light.

questions.question_text: Hand-axe, Cleaver etc. tools are indicative of which Stone Age tradition?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Tools like the axe or hand-axe, cleaver, and chopper (Khandak) etc. are indicative of the Lower Palaeolithic tradition. A large number of sites of the Lower Palaeolithic age have been found in the 'Sohan River Valley', a tributary of the Indus River.

questions.question_text: Blade-burin type tools are indicative characteristics of which of the following traditions?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – The Upper Palaeolithic period came after the Middle Palaeolithic period. Its primary stone tool is the blade. A blade is a stone flake of thin and narrow shape whose both edges are parallel. Its length is twice its width.

questions.question_text: Mesolithic human burials equipped with ornaments have been obtained from—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Necklaces of deer antlers and bone ornaments were first found at the site named Mahadaha, located in the Patti tehsil of Pratapgarh district. This site was discovered by G.R. Sharma.

questions.question_text: Food production-based economy is related to—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Neolithic culture was more developed compared to its preceding cultures. Man of this period became a food producer; he knew agriculture and also domesticated animals. In this period, man was not a nomad. He established permanent settlements.

questions.question_text: From which site have the oldest evidences of rice production in the Ganga Valley been obtained?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The oldest evidence of rice production in the Ganga Valley has been obtained from a site named Lahuradewa. It is located in the Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Here, evidence of rice husks was found in excavations dating to 9000-8000 BC.

questions.question_text: The subject of study of prehistory is—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Prehistory refers to that period when humans had not developed the art of script or writing. All Stone Age civilizations fall within the limits of this prehistoric period. Later, evidence of cuneiform script was found from the Harappan civilization. In fact, it has remained unreadable. Subsequently, in the Vedic period, the education system was oral. Both these periods are kept under Proto-history. That period whose history is known on the basis of written facts is called the Historical period.

questions.question_text: The discovery of fossils of early Palaeolithic humans in Hathnora was made by—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – The discovery of fossils of early Palaeolithic humans in Hathnora was made by A.K. Sonakia (Arun Kumar Sonakia). This site is located in the Hoshangabad district in the Middle Narmada Valley on the northern bank of the Narmada River. Following excavations on December 5, 1982, a fossil of a human skull was found. It was placed under the Homo erectus category. This obtained fossil is the oldest specimen of human remains.

questions.question_text: From which Neolithic culture has the rectangular stone tool for harvesting crops (harvester) been obtained?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – The rectangular stone tool for harvesting crops (harvester) is obtained from the Kashmiri Neolithic culture. Among the stone tools obtained from here, sickles or choppers with two holes, spindles, sling stones, and stone engravers or scrapers are particularly noteworthy. Evidence of ornamentation by engraving has been found on the two-holed sickles.

questions.question_text: Evidence of burying domestic animals like dogs and goats along with human remains in burials has been found in—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – Evidence of burying domestic animals like dogs and goats along with human remains has been found in Burzahom burials. Burzahom burials were mainly located within the residential area; the burial pits were oval and the edges of the pits were plastered with lime. Along with human burials, some animal burials have also been found, in which burials of dogs, wolves, and ibex (sakin) have mainly been found. In some burials, dogs were buried with their masters. Pit-dwellings (houses in pits) have also been a feature of Burzahom. This site was discovered by De Terra and Paterson in 1935 AD.

questions.question_text: Through vertical archaeological excavation, special knowledge of which of the following aspects of a culture is obtained?

options.A: The area of expansion of the culture
options.D: The chronological measurement of the culture

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Through vertical archaeological excavation, the entire culture cannot be visualized, but rather knowledge of the chronology of various cultures is obtained. In this type of excavation, long and deep digging is done at a place.

questions.question_text: What was the main tool of the Palaeolithic Age?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The main tools of the Palaeolithic Age were hand-axes, cleavers, and scrapers etc. The main tool of this culture, the hand-axe, was first obtained by Robert Bruce Foote in 1863 AD from Pallavaram near Madras. Subsequently, Palaeolithic tools were also discovered from Attirampakkam. Collectively, the tools of these regions are associated with the 'Madrasian Culture'.

questions.question_text: The age of refined tools is considered to be—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The Upper Palaeolithic period is considered the age of refined tools. In this age, the use of blade-dominated tools by Homo sapiens humans began.

questions.question_text: The yield of grain first started in—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The production of grain first occurred in the Neolithic period. This is the time when man became acquainted with agriculture and animal husbandry. In the Indian subcontinent, Koldihwa and Mehrgarh were two such Neolithic settlements from where clear evidence of rice and wheat has been obtained.

questions.question_text: 1. Palaeolithic Age 2. Copper Age 3. Mesolithic Age 4. Neolithic Age Options: Arrange the following chronologically—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The naming of the Indian Stone Age culture chronologically is— (a) Palaeolithic Age (b) Mesolithic Age (c) Neolithic Age After the end of the Stone Age, the age of the use of metals began. The use of stone and copper together is seen; this was called the Chalcolithic period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites is famous for prehistoric rock paintings?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation – The prehistoric site named Bhimbetka is famous for rock paintings. This Palaeolithic site is located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cultures is not a Stone Age culture?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Sohan culture, Madrasian culture, and Vindhyan culture are related to the Stone Age culture. Sothi culture is not related to the Stone Age culture.

questions.question_text: The hand-axe tool was a tool of which of the following methods?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Traditionally, the Indian Early Stone Age is divided into two tool traditions—the Son or Sohan culture and the Acheulian or Madrasian culture. In the Son or Sohan culture, pebble or core tools and chopper traditions were present, whereas in the Acheulian or Madras culture, hand-axes and cleavers were prominent. In 1863, the first hand-axe tool was discovered in Madras, which was a bifacial stone craft tool.

questions.question_text: Microlithic tools are the primary industry of which of the following cultures?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Microlithic tools are the primary industry of the Mesolithic culture. In this period, stone tools are generally found in small sizes. Due to this smallness in size, archaeologists call them Microlithic tools or Microliths.

questions.question_text: Evidence of cattle pens has been found from the following Neolithic site:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – Mahadaha, Koldihwa, and Panchoh are Neolithic archaeological sites located in the Belan River region in the Prayagraj district, in the Vindhya region. Evidence of cattle pens has been found from Mahadaha.

questions.question_text: Inamgaon is a primary site of
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – The period in which humans used stone and copper tools together is called the Chalcolithic period. Sites of Jorwe culture have been obtained from excavations in Maharashtra, which include Inamgaon, Songaon, Nevasa, and Daimabad.

questions.question_text: Megalithic culture is associated with
