questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – The Megalithic culture is related to iron. The discovery of iron occurred around 1000 BC in Atranjikhera. Harappans did not have knowledge about iron, whereas Aryans were acquainted with it.

questions.question_text: The famous Bhimbetka caves are located in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – Bhimbetka is located in Raisen. About 500 caves are located here, in which a unique world of rock paintings exists. The discovery of Bhimbetka was made by Mr. V.S. Wakankar. Its time period is from about 8000 BC to 1500 BC.

questions.question_text: The oldest evidence of rice has been found in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – The first stone tools of the Neolithic Age were first obtained by Le Mesurier in 1860 in the Tons River Valley of U.P. In the Neolithic period, the oldest evidence of paddy (rice) was obtained from Koldihwa located in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question_text: From which Neolithic site has the oldest evidence of rice cultivation been found?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – The invention of agriculture in India occurred in the Neolithic period. The prehistoric grain-producing site Mehrgarh is situated in western Balochistan. The oldest crops adopted for agriculture were wheat and barley. The oldest evidence of rice cultivation has been found from the Neolithic site named Lahuradewa.

questions.question_text: The Mesolithic site Chopani Mando is located in

options.B: Koraon tehsil of Allahabad on the banks of Old Belan

questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – The Mesolithic site Chopani Mando is located in the Koraon tehsil of Allahabad on the banks of the Old Belan. During this period, people lived their lives by hunting, catching fish, and collecting food items. During the Mesolithic period, small tools of stone were made. The first microlithic tools in India were discovered in 1867 by C.L. Carlyle.

questions.question_text: Arrange in chronological order:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation – In the chronological order, the Palaeolithic Age comes first. After this, sequentially, are the Neolithic Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age.

questions.question_text: (1) Navdatoli (2) Ropar (3) Nal (4) Kayatha Which of these are Chalcolithic cultures of Central India? A list of some archaeological sites is given below:
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation – Near Ujjain, on the banks of the Chhoti Kali-Sindh, the excavation of Kayatha has been done twice, and three stages of Chalcolithic settlement are found there. The initial period of the settlement was determined between 2400 BC and 2120 BC. Four stages of Chalcolithic settlements have been obtained in Navdatoli, located on the southern bank of the Narmada, whose period falls between 2020 BC and 1660 BC. The main feature here is black and red painted pottery.

questions.question_text: From which of the following Mesolithic sites has evidence of necklaces of deer antler rings been found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation – Evidence of necklaces of deer antler rings has been found from the Mahadaha site of the Mesolithic period. In the second sub-period of the site named Mahadaha, a single male skeleton was wearing a necklace of five rings made of deer antlers around the neck. The male in a joint burial was wearing a necklace of twelve rings made of antlers around the neck and was wearing a circular earring made of antler in the left ear. Tools and ornaments made of horn and antler have been found in greater numbers at Mahadaha compared to Sarai Nahar Rai. Tools made of horn and antler include arrowheads, borers, scrapers, saws, chisels, knives, etc. Earring and rings are noteworthy among the ornaments of antler. Broken grindstones and mullers made on sandstone, sling-stones, and hammers, etc., have also been found from Mahadaha. The discovery of grindstones and mullers indicates that perhaps the seeds of wild grass were ground and used as food material. The analysis of ancient pollen provides an indication of lush green grasslands.

questions.question_text: From which of the following Neolithic sites is evidence of pit-dwellings found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – There has been a prosperous Neolithic culture in Kashmir since the third century BC, where the most important site discovered is Burzahom. It is located near the modern Srinagar province. The first period of this site is Neolithic. In the first phase, there are handmade potteries with mat impressions on the base. Various kinds of bone tools, including hooks, saws, needles, and spearheads, are included here, and many oval or circular pit-houses with stairs for descending and niches in the walls were built. There are hearths near the entrance, and there are post-holes around the boundary, indicating thatched roofs. The bone and stone tool industry continued in the next phase, but now houses of mud and sun-dried bricks, knife-made pottery, and limited use of copper are seen there.

questions.question_text: From where was the statue of the Mother Goddess made of bone of the Upper Palaeolithic period obtained?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The bone-made statue of Mother Goddess was obtained from Lohanda Nala located in the Belan Valley of Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh), which belongs to the Upper Palaeolithic period.

questions.question_text: By what name was the early complete man known?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – About 3.5 crore to 2 crore years ago, a group of apes 3 to 4 feet tall emerged from the dense forests of the tropics where they used to live on trees. About two crore years ago, this ancestral group became a branch of division, it is called 'Ramapithecus'. The branch that remained in the forests but was more suitable for living on the ground developed as the Great Ape category, and the one that started looking for open grasslands is called 'Australopithecus'. 'Australopithecus' became the early ancestor of man and appeared in the early Pleistocene period. In the early Middle-Pleistocene period, a more developed human species appeared in many parts of the world; we call them 'Pithecanthropus' or 'Erectus'. Neanderthal man appeared at the end of the Middle-Pleistocene and at the beginning of the Upper-Pleistocene. About 30,000 years ago, 'modern man' developed. We call him 'Homo sapiens' or 'Wise Man' or by specific research names such as 'Cro-Magnon', 'Chancelade Grimaldi', etc.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below— List-I List-II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation – The matched list of sites with cultures is as follows: Sarai Nahar Rai – Mesolithic period, Patne – Upper Palaeolithic, Saipai – Ochre Coloured Pottery tradition, Mahurjhari – Megalithic burial.

questions.question_text: Where did the Amri culture develop?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation – The Amri culture developed from the Sindh province of Pakistan. Besides this, sites like Mohenjo-daro, Chanhudaro, Juderidaro, Kot Diji, Alimurad, etc., were also in the Sindh province.

questions.question_text: From where was the oldest evidence of animal husbandry obtained?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Two Mesolithic sites are located in Madhya Pradesh near Hoshangabad at Adamgarh and the other in the Bhilwara district of Rajasthan at Bagor. The date for both has been fixed around 5000 BC. Evidence of domestication of cattle and sheep-goats is found at both these sites. It is possible that evidence of agriculture may also be obtained from both these sites in different areas, but no such definite discovery has been made so far. Sarai Nahar Rai is an important site in Pratapgarh district (within 50 km from Allahabad). The radiocarbon date of Sarai Nahar Rai has been found to be 8395 BC. This is the first site where evidence of post-holes (stambha garta) has been found. Huts must have been built for residence. Extremely important evidence of human aggression or war has also been obtained from Sarai Nahar Rai. In one burial, a microlith was found embedded in the skull of a skeleton. Among the microliths obtained, very few geometric forms were found, and from a typological-technical point of view, they appear to be much older than the superior forms found in Bagor.

questions.question_text: Which site of the prehistoric period is famous by the name 'Tambavati'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The ancient name of Ahar is Tambavati. This place is surrounded by the Aravalli mountain ranges and is situated on the banks of the Ahar river to the east of Udaipur. In inscriptions, it has been called Aghatpur. A large furnace and copper items were found here during excavation, which indicates that copper smelting and vessel making work used to take place here. This place was settled eight times; each time people settled in a different place. Copper items were found only in the fourth settlement layer. Copper tools have been found in the debris of the walls. Houses were made of sun-dried unbaked bricks and stones. The houses were quite large. Several hearths (chulhas) were found in a line at a single place during excavation. It seems they belonged to a single family. Stones for grinding spices of various shapes have been found. Coins and seals of the second period have also been found here, with Brahmi script written on them. Beads of clay and stone have been found, on which paintings have been made.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Human fossils have not been obtained from the Stone Age in India.
options.B: Human activities have not been found on Paleolithic tools.
options.C: Human society was not formed in the Neolithic period.
options.D: Human activities are not depicted in prehistoric rock shelters.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Human activities are depicted in the caves of Bhimbetka, a Lower Paleolithic site located in the Narmada Valley (Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh). Bhimbetka indicates the habitation of people who were extremely skilled and experienced in the manufacture of cleavers. Their flake tools are numerous and of various types, and they closely resemble the Western European Middle Paleolithic period. Hand-axes are very well made, which are small and flat. Therefore, there is no doubt that at these levels, a group of late Acheulean people was settled, but there... ...not a single chopper or Abbevillian hand-axe has been found there. This should provide sufficient indication that the Narmada deposits may represent diverse cultures from olden times, along with which new groups were also found. The developed nature of Acheulean tools matches well with the late chronological position of this culture, and here it can be compared with Western Europe.

questions.question_text: From which of the following Mesolithic sites have ornaments made of bone been obtained?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation– The first remains of a human skeleton from the Mesolithic period have been obtained from a place named Mahadaha (Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh). Tools and ornaments made of horn and antler have been found in greater numbers at Mahadaha compared to Sarai Nahar Rai. Among the tools of horn and antler are arrowheads, piercers, scrapers, saws, chisels, knives, etc. Among the ornaments of antler, earrings and rings are noteworthy. Broken slabs and mullers made of sandstone, sling-stones, and hammers, etc., have also been found at Mahadaha. The discovery of slabs and mullers indicates that perhaps the grains of wild grass began to be used as food material after grinding. Analysis of paleo-pollen gives indications regarding lush green grasslands.

questions.question_text: The megalithic burials of South India are related to:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : After the Stone Age in South India, the Megalithic culture emerged in the Deccan plateau and the far peninsula. This culture is also found to some extent in the eastern central and north-western regions of India. However, it has special importance in the context of South India. The Megalithic culture has two characteristics of historical importance—(a) its continuous link with the Iron Age and (b) being associated with the appearance of Black and Red Ware.

questions.question_text: 'Sihawal' is a site of:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : More than 30 sites related to the Lower Paleolithic period have come to light so far. Lower Paleolithic tools have been obtained from the Sihawal deposit of the Middle Son Valley. The lowest and oldest deposit of the Son River is called the Sihawal deposit because it has its best deposit near the site named Sihawal, where it has been studied.

questions.question_text: Ash mounds are related to the Neolithic culture of which region?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: The baseline of rural life located in South India is obtained from the Neolithic culture. Among the agricultural crops, millet and gram have been found. Extensive remains of cattle, sheep-goats, and bones of other animals have been found, which indicate the importance of domestic animals in the economy. The people of this culture probably tied their cattle outside their houses during a certain period of every year. In the area where cattle were kept, a fence of wooden sticks was put up. The dung that collected inside the fence was burnt every year along with the wooden sticks. This burning work was probably done around the Pongal ceremony, which falls on Makar Sankranti. The result of the continuous repetition of this process every year was that at the place where that bonfire was burnt, a mound of ash was formed. In South Indian archaeology, these mounds are called Ash mounds.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following sites has the oldest fossil of prehistoric man in India been found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation: A fossil of a human skull has been found from Hathnora located in Hoshangabad district of Madhya Pradesh; some scholars have placed it under Homo erectus and some under the evolved Homo sapiens category. Bhimbetka—Located in Raisen (M.P.). The area of this site is famous for caves and rock shelters, whose number here is about 500. The credit for discovering the caves of Bhimbetka goes to V.S. Wakankar. Evidence of Mesolithic culture remains and contemporary paintings are found in most of the rock shelters here. Sarai Nahar Rai and Damdama are Mesolithic sites located in Pratapgarh district.

questions.question_text: The main occupation of the Paleolithic man was:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: The life of Paleolithic man was completely natural. They primarily depended on hunting (Akhet). Their food used to be meat or tubers. Due to being unacquainted with the use of fire, they ate meat raw. They did not have any fixed place of residence and their life was nomadic or migratory. In this primitive age of civilization, man was not acquainted with agriculture or animal husbandry, nor did he know how to manufacture vessels. The man of this period was only a consumer of food items. He had not yet become a producer. There was no difference between the living conditions of humans and wild animals.

questions.question_text: Sarai Nahar Rai and Mahadaha are related to -

options.A: Neolithic culture of the Vindhyan region
options.B: Mesolithic culture of the Vindhyan region
options.C: Mesolithic culture of the Ganga Valley
options.D: Neolithic culture of the Ganga Valley

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation– Sarai Nahar Rai and Mahadaha are related to the Mesolithic culture of the Ganga Valley. Out of these, Sarai Nahar Rai is located in Pratapgarh district, which was discovered by K.C. Ojha. 11 human burials and 8 pit-hearths have been found here. There is one burial here in which four humans were laid together. The Mesolithic site named 'Mahadaha' is also located in Pratapgarh district, which was discovered through the department of archaeology of Allahabad University and the courtesy of the then Pargana Officer of Patti Tehsil, Lal Bihari Pandey. Human burials have also been obtained from here. Apart from human burials, half-burnt bones of animals, horns, etc., have also been obtained from here, due to which it has been called a slaughter-site (Vadh-sthal).

questions.question_text: The evidence of the oldest artifacts is related to–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The relation of the oldest artifacts has been established with the Upper Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods because the subject matter of the paintings of this category matches a lot with the economic activities, social and cultural customs of the humans of the Upper Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods. Among the major artifacts, animals have been shown running, jumping, grazing, standing or being pursued by hunters or being hunted by laying an ambush.

questions.question_text: Which of the following facts is correct about the man of the Lower Paleolithic period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- The development of Stone Age civilization took place in the Ice Age or Pleistocene period. The main industries of Stone Age man in India were limited to microlithic tools, flake tools, and hand-axes. Quartzite or crystal was mainly used in making tools. These stone tools were first found in the Sohan Valley. Therefore, they are also called 'Sohan Culture'. In this period, man used core-tools. He neither used any metal nor was he an animal herder, but rather depended on hunting for livelihood.

questions.question_text: A skull of 'Homo erectus' was obtained from which of the following sites?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Arun Sonakia of the Geological Survey of India found a fossil of a human skull from a site named Hathnora located in Hoshangabad district in the Middle Narmada Valley. Some scholars have placed it under the 'Homo erectus' category and others describe it as 'evolved Homo sapiens'.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Birbhanpur 1. Banas culture B. Ujjain 2. Copper hoard C. Kayatha 3. Ochre Coloured Pottery tradition D. Ahar 4. Microlithic tools Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The Mesolithic site named Birbhanpur is located on the left bank of the Damodar river near Durgapur in Burdwan district of West Bengal, which was discovered by B.B. Lal in 1954 AD. Microlithic tools have been obtained from excavation here. Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) is a major site related to the Malwa culture. During excavation here, many types of vessel traditions have come to light, among which basins, shallow plates, lotas, pots, etc., are prominent. These mainly represent the 'Ochre Coloured Pottery tradition'. The site named Kayatha is located in Ujjain district. This site is probably known in Indian literature as 'Kapitthaka', the birthplace of Varahamihira. A 'Copper hoard' has been obtained from excavation here. Information about the Ahar culture was first obtained during the excavation of Udaipur city in Rajasthan by Ratan Chandra Agrawal in 1952-53 AD, from where many archaeological evidences of Chalcolithic culture were obtained. Since a large number of sites related to this culture are located in the valleys of the Banas and its tributaries in South-East Rajasthan, this culture is also called 'Banas Culture'. According to the above facts, the answer to this question will be (b).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The site named Kayatha is located in Ujjain district of Madhya Pradesh. In Indian literature, it has been identified as 'Kapitthaka', the birthplace of Varahamihira. 'Copper hoards' have been obtained from excavation here. 'Chirand' is a Neolithic site located in Saran district of Bihar where dwellings, clay pots, and some axes with small size and round parallels have been obtained from excavation. Among other stone tools, mention can be made of slabs-mullers, hammers, and sling-stones, etc. Another specialty here is the tools made on bone and horn. Pandu Rajar Dhibi is a major proto-historic site located in West Bengal from where some major archaeological evidence of the proto-historic period has been found. Daimabad is a major site located in Maharashtra where a rhinoceros, an elephant, a buffalo, a chariot, etc., have been obtained from its excavation.

questions.question_text: Where were the remains of Neolithic pit-dwellings found? 1. Burzahom 2. Gufkral 3. Kuchai 4. Mahadaha Select the correct answer from the codes below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Remains of the Neolithic period in Northern India have been obtained from various sites located in the Jhelum valley in Jammu-Kashmir state. Remains of pit-dwellings have been obtained from the excavation of Burzahom and Gufkral. The largest pit in Burzahom has a diameter of 2.74 meters at the mouth and 4.57 meters at the base.

questions.question_text: Where was the evidence of wild rice found in a Mesolithic context?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Evidence of wild rice in a Mesolithic context has been found from 'Chopani-Mando'. This site is situated on the left bank of the Old Belan river in Meja tehsil of Allahabad district. The credit for discovering this site goes to Shri B.D. Mishra in 1967.

questions.question_text: Who among the following has been called the 'Father of Prehistoric Archaeology' in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 PGT History, 2004 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 L.T. Grade Exam. 2018 Explanation - Famous archaeologist and geologist Robert Bruce Foote is called the Father of Prehistoric Archaeology in India, while A. Cunningham is considered the Father of Archaeology in India. Robert Bruce Foote himself had discovered the first Paleolithic tool in India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has been called 'Flake Culture'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The tools of the flake-dominant Paleolithic period found from various parts of India are placed in the middle of this period. Due to the predominance of flakes, the Middle Paleolithic period is given the designation of 'Flake Culture'. These tools were manufactured from good quality quartzite stone. Precious stones like chert, jasper, flint were used in these.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Paleolithic period (i) Kucha and Pucca houses B. Mesolithic period (ii) River bank settlement C. Neolithic period (iii) Rock shelter settlement D. Chalcolithic period (iv) Pit settlement Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - A. Paleolithic period - River bank settlement B. Mesolithic period - Rock shelter settlement C. Neolithic period - Pit settlement D. Chalcolithic period - Kucha and Pucca houses

questions.question_text: Robert Bruce Foote, who discovered the first Paleolithic tool in India, was originally a-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ Research on Stone Age civilization in India first started in 1863 AD, when Robert Bruce Foote, a scholar of the Geological Survey of India, obtained a stone tool of the Paleolithic period from a place named Pallavaram located near Madras. Robert Bruce Foote was both a geologist and an archaeologist. The answer to this question has been considered (b) by the Commission.

questions.question_text: Sanghao cave is a site of–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– Remains of deposits more than three meters thick from the Middle Paleolithic period to the Upper Paleolithic period have been obtained from the Potwar plateau area between Indus and Jhelum rivers and the Sanghao caves of the North-West Frontier Province of Pakistan. Along with stone tools, evidence of human and animal bones has also been obtained from here.

questions.question_text: From which of the following rock shelters has evidence of human burial been found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Apart from Mesolithic microlithic tools, seventeen human skeletons have been obtained from rock shelter number 1 of Lekhahia, some of which are in safe condition and most are mutilated. Based on stratification and overlap, 14 out of 17 skeletons have been divided into 8 sub-periods. Most are extended burials.

questions.question_text: The Narhan culture of the Ganga Valley is related to:
questions.explanation: The Narhan culture of the Ganga Valley was related to the Chalcolithic period. Archaeological stratigraphy from the second century BC to the seventh century BC has been obtained from Narhan. From the Narhan culture (Saryu, Ghaghara river valley), remains of Black-and-Red Ware, bone tools, beads, pottery terracotta and polished axes, post-holes and hearths along with remains of reed and mud houses have been obtained. Large-scale excavation work here was conducted under the leadership of Purushottam Singh

questions.question_text: To whom goes the credit for the discovery of the first Paleolithic tool in India, which opened the way for prehistoric studies in the country?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Robert Bruce Foote is called the father of Indian prehistoric period. In 1863, Robert Bruce Foote first discovered the first Paleolithic hand-axe from Pallavaram near Madras. As a result of which, the way for the study of the prehistoric period in India opened. Mr. Burkitt and De Terra and Paterson are also researchers of the prehistoric period, while H.D. Sankalia is an archaeologist related to the Indus civilization.

questions.question_text: In which of the following regions have remains of the Paleolithic period, Mesolithic period, and Neolithic period been found in a sequence?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– Remains of all three periods—Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic—are found in the Belan Valley, Vindhyan region, and Narmada Valley. Here, signs of human civilization from hunter-gatherer to food-producer are found, which are sequential developmental characteristics of any civilization.

questions.question_text: In which state of India is Inamgaon located?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – During 1600 BC, many human settlements came to light in Maharashtra, among which Prakash (Dhule district), Daimabad (Ahmednagar district), Inamgaon (Pune district) were the largest human settlements. Where first the Malwa culture and later the Jorwe culture developed.

questions.question_text: The Jorwe culture of ancient India has been named after a place in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Jorwe culture of ancient India is related to Maharashtra. A kind of residential hierarchy (order of high-low) is seen in the Jorwe settlements found in Maharashtra. This gives the practice of two-tier residence here. Jorwe is located in western Maharashtra

questions.question_text: At which Harappan site was a group (set) of twelve bathrooms fitted with floor drainage found?
questions.explanation: Apart from Harappa and Mohenjodaro, Lothal is also a major site of the Indus civilization. The mound of Lothal is located near the village named Saragwala in the Ahmedabad (Gujarat) district. It was discovered in 1954-1955, and excavations were carried out between 1957-1958 under the direction of S.R. Rao, where remains of a city settled in a two-mile circumference were found. The city and building plan of Lothal was well-planned and well-organized. Excellent arrangements for drains and manholes are seen. A set (group) of twelve bathrooms fitted with floor drainage has been found at this site

questions.question_text: From which one of the following Harappan sites has evidence of pit-dwellings been obtained?
questions.explanation: The Kunal site, located on the banks of the Saraswati River in the Hisar district of Haryana, was discovered by Jagatpati Joshi and R.S. Bisht in 1974 AD. Evidence of pit-dwellings has been found at Kunal among the Harappan period sites. Two silver crowns and gold ornaments have been obtained from here. Red pottery of Harappan style was first obtained from here

questions.question_text: At which one of the following sites have Late Harappan, Malwa, and Jorwe cultures been found?
questions.explanation: Daimabad is the largest site of the Jorwe Chalcolithic culture, which is spread over an area of about 20 hectares. Between 1976-79, S. A. Sali conducted the excavation of Daimabad. Pottery of several cultural levels has been found at Daimabad, which are respectively: Savalda pottery, Late Harappan pottery, Daimabad pottery, Malwa pottery, and Jorwe pottery. Daimabad is fortified with stones on all four sides

questions.question_text: Which of the following Harappan sites is not related to the Early Harappan phase?
questions.explanation: Hulas, located in the Saharanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, is a Late Harappan period site. Remains of the Early Harappan phase have not been found here. A seal containing the Indus script has come to light from here. Clear evidence of wheat cultivation has been found here. Evidence of the Early Harappan phase is obtained from Rakhigarhi, Dholavira, and Kunal

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites of the Indus Valley was discovered by Rakhal Das Banerji?
questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro was discovered by Rakhal Das Banerji in 1922 AD. He was a famous historian. He was born in Murshidabad The Harappan archaeological site was discovered by Dayaram Sahni in 1921 under the direction of Sir John Marshall. Both Harappa and Mohenjodaro sites are located in Pakistan.

questions.question_text: The materials found in the excavation of Rangpur include:

options.A: Rice husk, toys, and a huge granary
options.B: Old copper axe, beads, and earthen pots
options.D: Old copper axe, rice husk, and toys

questions.explanation: Rangpur is a city located in the Saurashtra province of Gujarat. This site is considered a site of Pre-Harappan and Late Harappan times, and tools and evidence from this period have also been obtained. This site was discovered in 1953-54 by S.R. Rao. In the excavation, materials of the Pre-Indus civilization include yellow and grey colored earthen pots, and in the materials of the Indus civilization, evidence of mud-brick forts, drains, pottery, weights, stone blades, and clay lumps, etc., old copper axe, and rice husk has been obtained

questions.question_text: Which of the following Harappan sites is located in Haryana?
questions.explanation: The Harappan civilization archaeological site Rakhigarhi is located in the Jind district of Haryana. This site was discovered by Prof. Suraj Bhan and Rafique Mughal. Remains of the Pre-Indus civilization have also been obtained from here. Rakhigarhi is one of the largest cities of the Harappan civilization in India

questions.question_text: In which of the following Harappan settlements was the first evidence of a dockyard found?
questions.explanation: Lothal is located in the Gulf of Khambhat between the Sabarmati and its tributary Bhogava river near Saragwala village in Gujarat. It was discovered in 1954-55 AD by S.R. Rao. A much-discussed port (dockyard) or godiwada has been found here, which is located on the eastern end of this site. This is the oldest known dockyard in the world. The most important achievement of Lothal is a large enclosure made of burnt bricks (214×36 m), which Mr. Rao has described as a 'ship dockyard'

questions.question_text: Archaeological findings from which of the following sites in the IVC show that dentistry was practiced by skilled standard craftsmen by 7000 BCE?
questions.explanation: In the present time, archaeologists at Mehrgarh in the Balochistan province found that the people of the Indus Valley Civilization of the Harappan period had knowledge of medicine and dentistry. Physical anthropologists, whose examination by Professor Andrea Cucina of the University of Missouri discovered it at that time when they were cleaning teeth in one of the men. Later research carried out in the same area found that the dating of the teeth was done to 7000 BCE. Technically, it has not been classified as written evidence

questions.question_text: Which of the following civilizations was not linked to the economy of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.explanation: & c) : The Indus civilization was primarily trade-oriented. In this civilization, trade was carried out at both water and land levels. It had close trade relations with Central Asia, the Persian Gulf, North-Eastern Afghanistan, Iran, Bahrain Island, Mesopotamia, Egypt, Crete, etc. The source of information regarding the long-distance trade of the Harappan civilization is the difference in the findings of items of this civilization at various places outside the subcontinent. This proves that the Harappan civilization would not have had commercial relations with South-East Asia Note - According to the DSSSB board, the correct option is (b).

questions.question_text: What was the main source of Harappan 'images and writing'?
questions.explanation: Maximum information about the Indus script and Indus religion is known only from the seals. Seals are considered the best artworks of the Harappan culture. The most frequent marking on the seals is of the Pipal tree, followed by a one-horned animal. After this, markings of elephant, tiger, barasingha (swamp deer), crocodile, buffalo, rhino, bull, etc., have been made. Marking of cow, horse, and camel has not been done on them. Seals were used in trade and commerce, on documents related to contracts, and for stamping commercial bundles

questions.question_text: Name the tributary of the Indus that dried up immediately after the Harappan civilization; its remains had been protecting it from annual floods.
questions.explanation: Based on the evidence of the Rigveda, some scholars consider the entry of the Hakra river around the Saraswati river itself, but many archaeologists have identified the Saraswati river with the Ghaggar and Hakra rivers. At the time when the spread of Aryans on the Indian land had started, this river had dried up. Rafique Mughal has studied this area where he found signs of Painted Grey Ware settlements on the 'dry bed' of the Ghaggar-Hakra. In this way, the Cholistan desert is located to the east and south of the Hakra bed. In the lower part, the Hakra joined the Indus river and fell into the Rann of Kutch

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a Harappan metallurgical technique?
questions.explanation: Hydrometallurgy involves the use of aqueous chemistry for the recovery of metals from ore concentrates and recycled or waste materials. This process is used in the extraction of less electropositive or less reactive metals. This technique is a technique of the modern century, which was not a metallurgical technique of the Harappan civilization. In this civilization, metal was used only through hammering or two-piece stone molds or shallow casting

questions.question_text: At which of these Harappan sites was sophisticated water conservation through drains, reservoirs, and water harvesting discovered?
questions.explanation: Dholavira - Located on Khadir Island between the Manhar and Mansar rivers in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat. It was discovered in 1967-68 by Dr. Jagatpati Joshi. Evidence of excellent water management 'water harvesting' has been found at Dholavira. Water was collected by building dams at the confluence of the Manhar and Mansar rivers. Rainwater was also collected. The reservoir equipped with 31-32 steps is particularly noteworthy. The oldest evidence of reservoir construction by cutting stones has been found here

questions.question_text: The 'Pashupati Seal' of the Indus Valley Civilization was discovered at which of the following sites?
questions.explanation: In the Pashupati seal of the Indus Valley Civilization, a yogi is shown in a seated posture, who is probably Shiva Pashupati. Around this yogi are four animals - rhino, buffalo, an elephant, and a tiger. Two deer are shown below the throne. Pashupati means the master of animals. It has been obtained from Mohenjodaro of the Harappan civilization. According to Sir John Marshall, the Pashupati seal is of an ancient Buddha or Jain Tirthankara

questions.question_text: To which of the following periods does the Indus Valley Civilization belong in history?
questions.explanation: Bronze Age Civilization - Until the beginning of the twentieth century, all archaeologists believed that the Vedic civilization was the oldest civilization of India. But when Harappa was excavated in 1921 under the leadership of Dayaram Sahni, the whole world came to know that not the Vedic civilization, but the Indus Valley Civilization is the oldest civilization of India The most developed civilization of the Bronze Age in India was the Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.question_text: Match the following: List-I (Excavator) List-II (Place) A. Dayaram Sahni - i. Rakhigarhi B. H. D. Sankalia - ii. Harappa C. Alexander Cunningham - iii. Nevasa D. Suraj Bhan - iv. Taxila Codes:

options.A: A - i, B -iii, C- iv, D -ii
options.B: A - ii, B -iii, C- iv, D -i
options.C: A - iv, B -ii, C- i, D -iii
options.D: A - iii, B -iv, C- ii, D –i

questions.explanation: The correct matching from List-I and List-II is List-I (Excavator) | List-II (Place) Dayaram Sahni | Harappa H.D. Sankalia | Nevasa Alexander Cunningham | Taxila Suraj Bhan | Rakhigarhi

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched? Harappan Settlement | Excavator
questions.explanation: Correct matching – Harappan Settlement | Excavator 1. Banawali – R.S. Bisht 2. Dholavira – Jagatpati Joshi 3. Mitathal – Suraj Bhan 4. Rakhigarhi – Vasant Shinde

questions.question_text: Which of the following artworks was not obtained at Mohenjodaro?

options.C: Statue of a man or priest in a seated posture

questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro is located on the right bank of the Indus River in the Larkana district of Sindh. It was discovered in 1922 by Rakhal Das Banerji. It is the largest and most prosperous city and the most important center of the Indus civilization. Remains obtained from the excavation here include cylindrical seals, stone yogi statues, and Pashupatinath i.e., Shiva marked on a seal. Among these remains, the bronze dancing girl was also obtained. In the above question, the sandstone male torso was obtained not from Mohenjodaro but from Harappa

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Indus-Saraswati civilization is not correct?

options.A: Wheat and barley were their major food grains.
options.B: Cow and bull were the major animals reared.
options.C: Their trade also took place with Mesopotamia, China, and Rome.
options.D: The manufacture of beads was a developed industry.

questions.explanation: The Indus Valley Civilization or Indus-Saraswati civilization flourished on the banks of the Indus River and most of its sites have been found in the Hakra-Ghaggar river, due to which this civilization would have been more fertile and prosperous. Wheat and barley were their major food grains in the civilization. Apart from this, there were peas, sesame, mustard, bajra, and jowar. Among their animals, there were buffalo, bull, donkey, cow, goat, elephant, and dog. Making beads was a developed industry here. In this question, the trade of the Indus civilization used to take place with Mesopotamia. No description is found regarding the existence of trade with China and Rome

questions.question_text: The governance system of the Indus Valley was
questions.explanation: The governance system of the Indus Valley Civilization was 'Oligarchy'. Oligarchy means wealthy, aristocratic class, or mercantile class. According to Dr. R. S. Sharma, the people of the Indus civilization paid the most attention to commerce and trade. Therefore, the governance of the Harappan or Indus civilization was in the hands of the mercantile class (Oligarchy)

questions.question_text: How many granaries are there in Harappa?
questions.explanation: From Harappa, remains of a granary with a total of 12 chambers built in two rows of 6-6 compartments have been obtained, the total area of which was more than 2,745 square meters

questions.question_text: The pre-Harappan stage of Kalibangan in Rajasthan and Banawali in Haryana is clearly
questions.explanation: The pre-Harappan stages of Kalibangan in Rajasthan and Banawali in Haryana are mainly Chalcolithic

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): The Himalayan mountain is the reason for the Indus-Ganga plains being full of irrigated gardens and excessive population. Reason (R): It has been the correct reason for Asian nomadism.

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is correct but R is wrong.
options.D: A is correct but R is correct.

questions.explanation: The Himalayas are the major reason for the Indus-Ganga valley being full of irrigated gardens and excessive population, because the Himalayas not only protect from icy polar winds but the Indus-Ganga rivers originating from it promoted the development of agriculture. Agriculture and excessive production contributed to state formation and the development of civilization-culture. Asian nomadism is not related to the Indian region but to the dry region of Central Asia

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): Man had achieved technical sophistication in the Bronze Age. Reason (R): This remained the reason for being prosperous in all areas.

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is correct but R is wrong.
options.D: A is correct but R is correct.

questions.explanation: In the Bronze Age, human technology had developed considerably and the outline of a permanent life had developed. The Harappan civilization was a Bronze Age culture which is direct proof of this, but it cannot be considered the sole reason for the prosperity of every area because the clear development of literature and script had not yet been possible

questions.question_text: Match the correct pairs: A. Harappa - 1. Burial R. 37 B. Lothal - 2. Dockyard C. Kalibangan - 3. Statue of a dancing girl D. Mohenjodaro - 4. Ploughed field Codes- A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched pairs are as follows Harappa - Burial R. 37 Lothal - Dockyard Kalibangan - Ploughed field Mohenjodaro - Statue of a dancing girl

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a Harappan site?
questions.explanation: Atranjikhera is not a Harappan site; this site is a protohistoric site located on the banks of the Kali River, a tributary of the Ganga, in the Etah district of Uttar Pradesh. It was discovered by Alexander Cunningham

questions.question_text: With whom did the Harappans have contact via sea route?
questions.explanation: The sea trade of the Harappans was mainly with Mesopotamia. Lothal city, located on the coast of the Arabian Sea, was a major port for trade with West Asia. There is also documentary evidence of trade between Mesopotamia and the Indus civilization. 'Etched' beads from Harappa and a piece of greenish chlorite stone from Mohenjodaro have been found in Mesopotamia

questions.question_text: In which of the following states have Harappan remains not been obtained?
questions.explanation: Harappan civilization is an important civilization of India which originated in the northwestern part of India. No site of the Harappan civilization is found in South India. Therefore, Harappan remains have not been obtained in Tamil Nadu

questions.question_text: Harappan culture site Dholavira is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Dholavira, located in Gujarat, is probably the largest city of the Harappan civilization located in India. Unlike other cities, it is divided into 3 parts - Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town. R. S. Bisht carried out its excavation work in 1990-91 Ans. (d) : Dholavira, located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, was probably the largest Harappan city located in India. Unlike other cities, it is divided into 3 parts - Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town. R.S. Bisht conducted the excavation work here in 1990-91.

questions.question_text: The area included in Mesopotamia is known today by what name?

options.B: Eastern Syria, South-Eastern Turkey, and most of Iraq

questions.explanation: The areas included in Mesopotamia currently consist of Eastern Syria, South-Eastern Turkey, and most parts of Iraq

questions.question_text: In which year was the Indus Valley Civilization discovered?
questions.explanation: The Indus Valley site of Harappa was discovered in 1921 by Dayaram Sahni, from where statues of the human body made of sandstone, granaries, and evidence of bullock carts have been found

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of the word 'Mesopotamia'?

options.B: A Greek word meaning 'land between two rivers'
options.C: A Greek word related to mountains

questions.explanation: Mesopotamia is a Greek word - which means 'land between two rivers'

questions.question_text: Writing in ancient Mesopotamia started

options.A: When the society needed to keep records of transactions.
options.B: When suitable material for writing was found.
options.C: When rulers felt the need to make a code of laws.
options.D: When cities emerged from early human settlements.

questions.explanation: Writing in ancient Mesopotamia started when cities emerged from early human settlements. Cuneiform script or wedge-shaped script is one of the oldest methods of writing in the world. This script first emerged in the Sumerian civilization in the 30th century BCE

questions.question_text: The 'Near East' in the Roman perspective refers to

options.A: The region located east of the Tigris River
options.B: The region located east of the Indus River
options.C: The region located east of the Mediterranean Sea
options.D: The region located east of the Caspian Sea

questions.explanation: The 'Near East' in the Roman perspective refers to the region located east of the Mediterranean Sea

questions.question_text: The Indus Valley Civilization has not yet been deciphered. Consider the following reasons: 1. No information is available about their language. 2. Short length of inscriptions. 3. Absence of bilingual records. Which of the above is/are the correct reason(s)?
questions.explanation: All the above statements related to the decipherment of the Indus Valley Civilization are true, i.e., there is no information about the language of the Indus Valley Civilization, the length of its inscriptions is short, and bilingual records are absent in it

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites in Uttar Pradesh is not a center of the Indus Civilization?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh has a special contribution among the major sites of the Indus Civilization. The main sites here are Alamgirpur, Sothi, and Hulas (Saharanpur), while Koldihwa (Allahabad) is considered a Neolithic site

questions.question_text: Which of the following languages replaced the Sumerian language in Mesopotamia?
questions.explanation: The oldest language of Mesopotamia, Sumerian, was gradually replaced by the Akkadian language after 2400 BCE. The practice of cuneiform writing in this language continued until the first century CE

questions.question_text: Identify the region from the following where archaeological sites of the Indus Civilization have not been found:

options.B: Hilly region of the North-Western Frontier Province

questions.explanation: Archaeological sites of the Indus Civilization have not yet been found in the Lower Himalayan region. Remains have been obtained from Mehrgarh and Sutkagen Dor in Baluchistan, Kalibangan in the hilly region of the North-Western Frontier Province, and Daimabad and Inamgaon in Northern Maharashtra

questions.question_text: Remains of a massive fortification wall with dressed stone cladding and stone pillars have been found from the citadel area of which of the following sites?
questions.explanation: Remains of a massive fortification wall with dressed stone cladding and stone pillars have been obtained from the Dholavira site located in the Kutch district of Gujarat. Dholavira was divided into three main parts, two of which were fully protected by rectangular fortifications or walls. Such town planning is not seen in other Harappan cities

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not known during the Harappan civilization period?
questions.explanation: Scientifically constructed arches have not been found from the Harappan civilization period. However, burnt bricks from Chanhudaro and the English bond system of walls from Kalibangan have been found

questions.question_text: Which one of the following animals was present in the Harappan civilization?
questions.explanation: An idol of a three-faced deity (Pashupati Nath) has been found on a seal from Mohenjo-daro of the Harappan civilization, in which an elephant, rhinoceros, tiger, and buffalo are seated around him

questions.question_text: Burial 'H' is related to:

options.C: Fully developed and Late Harappan culture

questions.explanation: The cemetery found in Harappa, named Burial H, belongs to the post-Harappan period (Late Harappan culture). Meanwhile, a cemetery from the civilization period has been found in Harappa, located in the southern area, which has been named Cemetery R-37

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites is known as the oldest agricultural settlement in India?
questions.explanation: Mehrgarh is located near the Bolan Pass in the Baluchistan province of Pakistan. Evidence of the oldest agricultural settlement in India has been obtained from here. This place was used as a temporary human habitation. Daimabad (Maharashtra), Hulas (Uttar Pradesh), Kalibangan (Rajasthan), and Alamgirpur (Meerut, Uttar Pradesh) were also major Harappan sites

questions.question_text: What is the correct geographical sequence of the following Harappan cities from North to South? 1. Harappa 2. Mohenjo-daro 3. Kalibangan 4. Lothal
questions.explanation: The correct geographical sequence of Harappan cities from North to South is - Harappa (Montgomery in Punjab), Kalibangan (Rajasthan), Mohenjo-daro (Larkana district of Sindh), and Lothal (Gujarat). This order is based on geographical structure

questions.question_text: The platforms found at Kalibangan are made of:-
questions.explanation: The platforms found at Kalibangan are made of raw mud bricks. Kalibangan is located on the banks of the ancient Saraswati River in the Ganganagar district of Rajasthan (present-day Hanumangarh district). It was discovered by Amlananda Ghosh, and the excavation was done by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar. Evidence of a bangle manufacturing center, wooden drainage, bifurcation of the fort, paved roads, ploughed fields, etc., has been found from here

questions.question_text: Who among the following excavated Balathal?
questions.explanation: Balathal (Rajasthan) was excavated by V.N. Misra in 1993. It is the latest known site. Pottery similar to the Harappan culture has been found here. Tools of the late Harappan era made of iron and iron-smelting furnaces have been obtained from here

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Harappan Burial System) with List-II (Site): List-I List-II
questions.explanation: Harappan Burial System List-I List-II Coffin Burial Harappa Extended Burial Sanauli Joint Burial Lothal Pot Burial Mohenjo-daro

questions.question_text: Which of the following tributaries of the famous Indus River were located in Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: Flowing through Pakistan, the Indus River is one of the longest rivers in Asia; it flows through Pakistan, India (Jammu and Kashmir), and China (Western Tibet). It is the longest river and the national river of Pakistan. There are five sub-rivers of the Indus which are divided between Pakistan and India: Vitasta (Jhelum), Askini (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), Vipasha (Beas), and Shatudri (Sutlej). The tributaries of the Indus flowing in Afghanistan are Kubha, Krumu, and Hari-rud
examinations: UGC/NTA Dec 2019 IInd Paper (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014)

questions.question_text: A bead-making workshop has been found at which of the following Harappan sites?
questions.explanation: ,c) : Bead-making workshops have been obtained from major Harappan sites like Lothal, Banawali, and Chanhudaro. Meanwhile, Amri is considered the first site where pre-Harappan remains were found. Rice husk was primarily obtained from Rangpur

questions.question_text: Based on available evidence, the two permanent gifts provided to mankind by the Harappan civilization were—

options.B: Knowledge of mathematics and decimal system
options.D: Making soak pits and clay pipes

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation—Barley, wheat, rice, cotton, mustard, rapeseed, sesame, peas, and millet were the major agricultural products of the Harappan civilization that continued into later cultures. There were two species of wheat, Triticum and Compactum. In this context, the description of cotton is particularly interesting; the Harappan civilization was the first user of cotton thread and its various products, and from here its use spread to neighboring and later cultures.

questions.question_text: In which part of the Indian subcontinent did the Harappan culture arise?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation—The Harappa or Indus culture arose in the North-Western part of the Indian subcontinent on a Chalcolithic background. The Indus or Harappan civilization was an urban civilization. Major sites with a mature phase obtained from the Harappan civilization are designated as major cities. These are—Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Banawali, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, and Chanhudaro.

questions.question_text: The residents of the Indus Valley did not have knowledge of which metal?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 PGT History, 2011 Explanation—Through modern analysis methods like Radio Carbon C-14, the generally accepted date of the Indus civilization is considered to be 2350 BCE to 1750 BCE. This civilization was discovered by Rai Bahadur Dayaram Sahni. This civilization can be placed in the Proto-historic or Bronze Age. The people of this civilization did not have knowledge of iron.

questions.question_text: For the people of the Indus civilization, the humped bull was a—
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation—For the religious knowledge of the Harappan people, one has to depend mainly on evidence from seals, small idols, and stone statues, etc. Animal worship was prevalent in the Indus civilization. In this, the rhinoceros, bull, tiger, buffalo, and humped bull are prominent. Among these, the humped bull was worshipped as a sacred animal.

questions.question_text: People of the Indus civilization period built houses with—
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation—The Harappan civilization was an urban and Bronze Age civilization. Houses, drains, and bathrooms here were built with the help of well-burnt bricks. Bricks were rectangular. Three types of buildings are found - residential houses, large buildings, and public baths.

questions.question_text: In which site of Harappan culture has a joint burial been found?
questions.explanation: &b) Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Both options (a) and (b) are correct. Three double burials have been obtained from Lothal and two double burials have been obtained from Kalibangan. A dockyard, Persian seal, small clay model of a horse, etc., have been obtained from Lothal. Meanwhile, fire altars or fire pits, decorated bricks, plow marks (evidence of a ploughed field), etc., are obtained from Kalibangan.

questions.question_text: Who among the following first expressed the view that Aryans entered India from the North-West and destroyed the Harappan culture?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- According to Wheeler, the Harappan civilization existed until the middle of the second millennium BCE, although in its late period, it was moving toward gradual decline. The sudden and accidental end of this civilization around 1500 BCE was the result of some external invasion. In the second millennium BCE, there was large-scale migration of various races in Western Asia. Based on human skeletons found in a scattered manner on the upper surface of Mohenjo-daro, it was concluded that an external invasion occurred in the final phase of the Harappan civilization. Most of the skeletons were found lying in houses and on public roads in a scattered state without formal last rites. A. Town Planning- Harappa and Mohenjo-daro

questions.question_text: "We know nothing about prehistoric Egypt, Mesopotamia or Western Asia that can be compared with the well-built baths and large residences of the citizens of Mohenjo-daro." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: John Marshall stated that the baths and residential houses of citizens in Egypt and Mesopotamia were not in as advanced a state as those found in Mohenjo-daro. John Marshall wrote about the Harappan civilization in his book 'Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization' (1931). He believes that Mohenjo-daro was destroyed 7 times due to floods, which is indicated by the 7 levels found during excavation. Mohenjo-daro means 'Mound of the Dead'. It was first discovered in 1922 by Rakhal Das Banerji. From 1922 to 1930, excavation work was carried out here under the direction of John Marshall, Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India. A Great Bath, assembly hall, priest's residence, and granary, etc., were found here. John Marshall called the Great Bath the 'greatest wonder of the world' at that time. Examples of water-proofing along with engineering efficiency are found here. Large houses were the size of palaces, and two rooms were found in small houses. A house with 27 rooms and a courtyard was found at one place. According to Mortimer Wheeler, "The largest building in Mohenjo-daro is the granary." H.D. Sankalia says that the square or rectangular platforms obtained from Baluchistan are similar to the Ziggurats of Mesopotamia. A.N. Ghosh discovered Kalibangan (Rajasthan) in 1951

questions.question_text: Arrange the following archaeological cultures of India according to their chronology –
questions.explanation: The archaeological cultures of India are arranged chronologically as follows – Kot Diji - It was a center of the ancient Harappan civilization located at a place named 'Khairpur' in the Sindh province of Pakistan. It was discovered by G.S. Ghurye in 1935 and excavated by Fazal Ahmed Khan in 1953. Kayatha Culture - This is a Paleolithic/Chalcolithic site in the Ujjain district of Madhya Pradesh. Its period is 2300-2000 BCE; its subordinate areas are Nagda, Navadatoli, Eran, and Gungeria. The study of this culture was done by V.S. Wakankar. Malwa Culture - This Chalcolithic site exists in the Malwa region of Central India and some parts of the Deccan peninsula of Maharashtra. The pottery obtained in this culture was the best among all Chalcolithic cultures. Jorwe Culture - This is a Chalcolithic culture. It developed in 2 districts of Maharashtra - Ahmednagar and Pune; estimatedly its period was 1500-900 BCE. There were three important sites in Ahmednagar - Jorwe, Nevasa, and Daimabad.

questions.question_text: Who provided the first modern account of the ruins of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.explanation: Charles Masson 1826 - He was a soldier of the British East India Company, an independent explorer, and a pioneer archaeologist and numismatist. He was the first European to discover the ruins of Harappa near Sahiwal in Punjab, which is now in Pakistan

questions.question_text: The city of which of the following Indus sites was divided into three parts (Citadel, Middle and Lower city)?
questions.explanation: Dholavira is located in the Bhachau taluka of the Kutch district of present-day Gujarat. It was excavated in 1990-1991 by R.S. Bisht and is considered the largest site of the Harappan civilization. The city of the Dholavira site was divided into three parts: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town

questions.question_text: Consider the following: Which of the following statements are true in the context of Indus cities? 1. The plan of the Indus city is not based on grid-layout. 2. The grid-layout is not visible in the plan of the cities of Harappa, Banawali, and Chanhudaro. 3. Evidence of burnt bricks has not been found from many sites. 4. Ample use of burnt bricks is seen in Harappa, but probably it was not primarily used here.
questions.explanation: True statements regarding Indus cities (1) Evidence of burnt bricks has not been found from many sites. (2) Ample use of burnt bricks is seen in Harappa, but probably it does not appear as a primary feature from here. * The town planning of the Indus civilization was based on a grid-layout. Roads intersected each other at right angles. * A grid-layout is seen in the town planning of Harappa, Banawali, and Chanhudaro, where there were upper (Citadel) and lower towns surrounded by protective walls. (a) 1 and 2 (b) 3 and 4 (c) 1, 2 and 3 (d) 1, 2, 3 and 4 RPSC College Lecturer -2016 Ans. (b) : True statements about Saindhav cities- (1) Evidence of burnt bricks has not been found from many sites. (2) Extensive use of burnt bricks is seen in Harappa, but perhaps this is not seen as a prominent feature from here. * The city planning of the Saindhav civilization was based on the grid pattern. Roads cut each other at right angles. * The grid pattern is visible in the city planning of Harappa, Banawali and Chanhudaro, in which there were upper (citadel) and lower cities which were surrounded by defensive walls.

questions.question_text: Who was the first to discover a large number of Saindhav sites on the dry bed of the Saraswati river in the Cholistan desert of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Cholistan desert is situated in the southern part of the Punjab province of present-day Pakistan, which is a part of the Thar desert. Rafique Mughal discovered a large number of Saindhav sites here

questions.question_text: The civilization after the Harappan civilization is________
questions.explanation: After the Harappan civilization comes the Chalcolithic age (Copper-Stone age), followed by the Vedic age, then the rise of the Magadha empire, and thereafter the Maurya dynasty

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Saindhav sites from South to North according to their geographical location:
questions.explanation: The correct arrangement of the given options from South to North is as follows 1- Bhagatrav- This Saindhav site is located in the present state of Gujarat. Excavation was carried out by the Archaeological Survey of India under the leadership of Dr. S.R. Rao. 2- Megham- This Saindhav site is also located in the present state of Gujarat. It was located on a traderoute of the Saindhav period. 3- Rakhigarhi- This site is located on the banks of the Ghaggar river in the Hisar district of present-day Haryana. Its excavation was carried out by Amarendra Nath. It is considered the second largest site of the Saindhav civilization. 4- Alamgirpur- This is considered the easternmost site of the Saindhav civilization, which is situated on the banks of the Hindon river in the Meerut district of present-day Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a very important enterprise of the Harappans located in Lothal and Chanhudaro?
questions.explanation: Bead manufacturing was a major enterprise of the Harappans in Lothal and Chanhudaro

questions.question_text: Which was the most prominent item imported by the Harappans?
questions.explanation: The people of Harappa imported copper from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan and imported tin from Afghanistan because the quantity of tin was low in the Indian subcontinent. People were proficient in making food items, textiles, and pottery

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river was the excavation of Mohenjodaro completed?
questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro is located on the right bank of the Indus river in the 'Larkana' district of Sindh. It was first discovered by 'Rakhal Das Banerji' in 1922 AD. Important evidence obtained from Mohenjodaro includes- Great Bath, Great Granary, College building, bronze statue of a dancing girl, statue of a priest (Yogi), statue of Pashupatinath (Shiva) inscribed on a seal, six kilns of potters, cotton cloth, elephant skull fragment, heaps of melted copper, a scale made of shell, and evidence of cloth on wet clay

questions.question_text: The ratio of the measurement of Harappan bricks is
questions.explanation: The great center of Proto-historic culture, Harappa, was discovered by Rai Bahadur Daya Ram Sahni in the year 1921 AD. In this civilization, the measurement of the size of bricks was in a certain ratio. The burnt bricks of the Harappan civilization and their fixed ratio were 4:2:1 or 1:2:4, which distinguishes it from the various shapes and sizes of bricks of the Sumerian civilization

questions.question_text: ________ proved that there was a common burial practice among the people of Harappa.

options.A: The heads of the dead buried in the ground were always towards the North direction
options.B: Items were commonly used while burying the dead
options.D: The dead were buried only in a sitting posture

questions.explanation: The head of the dead buried in the ground was always towards the North direction and personal items were usually buried with them at the time of burial. This proved that there was a common burial practice among the people of Harappa

questions.question_text: Which of the following animals is not engraved on the Pashupati seal obtained from Mohenjodaro?
questions.explanation: Rhinoceros and buffalo were found on the left side and elephant, tiger and deer on the right side of the Pashupati seal obtained from Mohenjodaro. There is no depiction of a bull on this seal. Marshall has described it as Proto-Shiva

questions.question_text: At which of the following places were the remains of the Great Bath obtained?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath is the most notable monument of Mohenjodaro, which measures 54.86 meters from North to South and 33 meters from East to West. It is 11.89 meters long, 7.01 meters wide and 2.44 meters deep. Stairs are built on the North and South sides to descend into it. Marshall described it as 'a wonderful construction of the world at that time'

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The most important achievement of Surkotada, located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, is the discovery of some bones of a horse. This city was divided into 2 fortified parts, the Citadel and the Residential area. Evidence of buildings with stone masonry has been found here. We also get an example of pot burial from here

questions.question_text: Mohenjodaro is located in the district of
questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro is located on the right bank of the Indus river in the Larkana district of Sindh province of Pakistan, which was discovered by Rakhal Das Banerji in 1922 AD. It is the most famous site of the Harappan civilization. This city was situated on a platform of raw bricks. The main evidence found here includes the oldest evidence of textile manufacture, a tower, evidence of Sumerian boats on seals, oldest evidence of silver, a granary of 50×27 meters, the heaviest weight of the Saindhav civilization (10.9 grams), silver jars along with silver seals, and Shilajit are prominent

questions.question_text: Which site of Harappa shows the early evidence of an earthquake?
questions.explanation: The oldest evidence of an earthquake is found from the Harappan site Kalibangan. Prominent evidence from Dholavira includes a bathhouse and evidence of stone in construction, etc., and from Mohenjodaro, a statue of a three-faced deity (Pashupatinath) has been found on a seal, with elephant, rhinoceros, tiger, and buffalo seated around him

questions.question_text: What was the nature of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.explanation: The Indus civilization was of urban nature. Evidence such as drains outside the houses, granaries and baths inside the houses, etc., is found here, from which it is known that they all lived in a well-organized manner

questions.question_text: The first astronomical observatory of the Harappan civilization has been found at which of the following ancient Indian sites?
questions.explanation: The first astronomical observatory of the Harappan civilization has been found from the ancient site named Dholavira. Dholavira is located in the Kutch district of Gujarat. Its discovery (1990) was made by R.S. Bisht. Dholavira is one of the largest Harappan sites discovered to date. It was divided into three main parts

questions.question_text: The widest roads in the citadel and city in Mohenjodaro were respectively:
questions.explanation: The main feature of Mohenjodaro was its road construction art. Generally, roads cut each other at right angles. The main road has been called 'First Road' or 'Rajpath'. The roads of the citadel and city were respectively 7 to 11 meters wide. The intersection where the auxiliary roads of Mohenjodaro met the main road has been called 'Oxford Circus' by archaeologists

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not known in the Harappan civilization?
questions.explanation: Evidence of a canal was not obtained in the Harappan civilization. Evidence of construction of a dam on the Indus River is found, and evidence of wells in houses is also obtained

questions.question_text: At which Harappan site is there a shipyard (dockyard)?
questions.explanation: Being located on the sea coast, Lothal was a major port for trade from Western Asia. Prominent evidence such as cylindrical seals, plough marks, fire altars, platforms made of bricks, etc., have been obtained from Kalibangan

questions.question_text: At which place in Harappan cities was a field ploughed with a plough found?
questions.explanation: Kalibangan is located in the Ganganagar district of present-day Rajasthan, which was discovered by A. Ghosh in 1952. The most important achievement of the Pre-Saindhav culture here is the evidence of a ploughed field

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements about Harappan cities: (1) All cities were located on the banks of the Indus river. (2) There was a port in Lothal city. Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Not all cities in the Harappan period were located on the banks of the Indus river itself. Major ports developed on the coast of the Arabian Sea were Sutkagen-dor, Balakot, Allahdino, and Lothal, etc. Evidence of a port is found from Lothal

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A) : Now there is very little doubt in this regard that some aspects of the Indus Valley Civilization are found in the cultures of the second and first millennium. Reason (R) : The existence of a continuous civilization between the Indus Valley Civilization and the Vedic culture is no longer accepted. What is correct among the following in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Where this first saga of humanity was born, that area remained the fertile land of civilizations. The oldest Aryan civilizations - Egyptian, Sumerian, Assyrian, Hebrew, Hittite, and Greek civilizations were all around the Mediterranean Sea, which maintained their coordination. The influence of the Indus Valley Civilization is visible on the Hittite civilization. In the beginning, there were remains and interaction of the culture, language, etc., of these civilizations, but the existence of the Hittite civilization was not found between the Indus Valley Civilization and the Vedic culture later

questions.question_text: Identify the site where there is no evidence of a horse?
questions.explanation: The literal meaning of Burzahom is 'Place of Birch' (Bhuri tree). This site of Birch trees was discovered by De Terra and Peterson in 1935. Evidence of pit-dwellings and burying dogs with the owner is found from here. Evidence of a harvester is found from Burzahom. A picture of a horned deity has been found on a pot obtained from here, which was popular in the Pre-Harappan stage of Kot Diji. No evidence of a horse is obtained from here

questions.question_text: Kalibangan, where many sites of Pre-Harappan culture have been found, was located in which of the following areas?
questions.explanation: Kalibangan is an important site of the Saindhav civilization located on the left bank of the Ghaggar river in the Ganganagar district of Rajasthan. B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar got the excavation done here in 1961 AD. Possibly this was the third capital of the Saindhav civilization. Evidence of a ploughed field is found here. The oldest evidence of an earthquake is found here, as a result of which the Pre-Harappan civilization here came to an end (around 2700-2600 BC)

questions.question_text: Which of the following Harappan cities was destroyed due to recurrent floods?
questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro in Sindhi language means "Mound of the Dead". It is located on the bank of the Indus River in the Larkana district of Sindh (Pakistan). It is a city of the Indus Valley civilization which is covered by massive mounds. It was first discovered by Rakhal Das Banerji in 1922 AD. The Great Bath is the most important public place of Mohenjodaro. A water tank or reservoir is built in the middle of its central open courtyard. A massive bronze statue of a dancing girl has been found from here which is made by the lost wax process. This city was destroyed due to recurrent floods

questions.question_text: With which culture is the lowest first phase deposit of Dholavira associated?
questions.explanation: Dholavira is located in Bhachau taluka of Kutch district of Gujarat. It was first discovered by J.P. Joshi in 1967-68 AD and R.S. Bisht carried out extensive excavation work here in 1990-91 AD. The time period of the lowest first phase of Dholavira is considered to be 2650 to 2500 BC. In this phase, evidence of Pre-Harappan culture is obtained from here

questions.question_text: In the citadel of which archaeological site were 'seven fire altars' obtained?
questions.explanation: Evidence of seven fire altars has been obtained from Kalibangan. Kalibangan is currently in Hanumangarh (Rajasthan)

questions.question_text: From which of the following Harappan sites were camel bones found?
questions.explanation: Kalibangan is located in the Ganganagar district of Rajasthan. This site was discovered by Amlanand Ghosh in 1953 AD and the excavation was done by B.B. Lal and Thapar. Mainly ploughed field, couple burial, camel bones, fire altars, and all three methods of funerary rites- complete inhumation, partial inhumation, and cremation have been found from here. The houses here are made of raw bricks. Evidence of the use of decorated bricks has been found from the city mounds. The oldest evidence of an earthquake has been obtained here

questions.question_text: In which of the following cities of the Harappan civilization was dressed stone used in masonry work along with raw bricks?
questions.explanation: Dholavira, located in Bhachau taluka of Kutch district of Gujarat, is a simple village today. Its excavation was done by R.S. Bisht in (1990-91) AD. In this city, dressed stone was used in masonry work along with raw bricks. Dholavira was the second largest city discovered in India. The first largest city was Rakhigarhi which was located in Haryana

questions.question_text: From which of the following archaeological sites is the evidence of awareness and technical skill for the water resource management of the people of Harappan culture found?
questions.explanation: Evidence of awareness and technical skill for the water resource management of the people of Harappan culture is found from Dholavira and Mohenjodaro. Dholavira is situated between the Bhajar and Manhar rivers of Bhachau taluka of Kutch district of Gujarat. It was discovered by Jagatpati Joshi in 1967-68 but its detailed excavation was done by Ravindra Singh Bisht in 1990-91. 16 reservoirs of different shapes and sizes have been found here, which is evidence of a unique water collection system. In Mohenjodaro, apart from a Great Bath, there were about 700 wells. Seeing the unmatched drainage, wells, tanks, etc., here, it can be said that the Saindhav residents were very aware in terms of water resource management

questions.question_text: Which of the following Harappan civilization sites are located in Balochistan? (i) Dabarkot (ii) Sotkakoh (iii) Sutkagen-dor (iv) Shortugai Select the correct answer from the given code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–The first civilization of India is called the Indus Civilization or Harappan Civilization. So far, remains of the Indus civilization have been found in Northern Afghanistan, Balochistan, North-West Frontier Province, West and East Punjab, Kashmir, Sindh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat, and Maharashtra. Some remains of the Indus civilization have also been found in Balochistan, which include Dabarkot, Sotkakoh, and Sutkagen-dor. Dabarkot is located in southern Balochistan. This site was discovered by Aurel Stein in 1928 AD. Sotkakoh is located on the banks of the Shadi Kaur river in southern Balochistan. This site was discovered by George Dales in 1962 AD. Sutkagen-dor is located on the banks of the Dashk river in southern Balochistan. This city was discovered by Aurel Stein.

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Harappan site) with List-II (Archaeological remains) and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II
