questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July, 2017 Explanation–The matching of List-I (Harappan site) with List-II (Archaeological remains) is as follows– Mohenjodaro - Great Granary Lothal - Dockyard made of bricks Kalibangan - City citadel and lower town Sutkagen-dor - City citadel and fortified lower town

questions.question_text: At which of the following archaeological sites was evidence of water storage found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2011) Explanation– Evidence of water storage has been obtained from Lothal. Lothal was a major site of the Harappan civilization, from where specimens of a dockyard have been obtained. It is known that Lothal is situated near the Gulf of Khambhat close to the Bhogava river. The evidence of the dockyard obtained from Lothal informs about it being a previously developed port.

questions.question_text: Which game were the people of the Indus Valley aware of?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2011) Explanation– The people of the Indus Valley were aware of the game of dice. For entertainment, the people of the Indus civilization mainly used the game of dice, dance, hunting, and animal fights. Religious festivals and ceremonies were also celebrated with pomp and show from time to time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites is not associated with a mature Harappan site?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation– Sarai Khola is a pre-Harappan site. It is located in modern Taxila (Punjab province, Pakistan). Amri, Nal, Kulli, Mehrgarh, Kot Diji, Kili Ghul Mohammad etc., are pre-Indus sites. Dholavira, Lakhmirwala, and Surkotada are Harappan period sites. Dholavira is the largest site discovered in India of the Indus civilization. Evidence of horses and evidence of lipstick are found from Surkotada. It is located in the state of Gujarat.

questions.question_text: Which feature of the Harappan civilization was not known in other contemporary civilizations?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2013) Explanation– The most prominent feature of the Harappan civilization was the production of cotton cloth, because the Harappans were the first to produce cotton. This was not known in other contemporary civilizations. Later, people of other civilizations became aware of cotton. It is noteworthy that an impression of cotton cloth has been found on a piece of clay pottery from Kalibangan.

questions.question_text: Who first propounded the theory of the Aryan invasion of India?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2013) GIC Lecturer Exam-2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– The theory of the Aryan invasion of India was first propounded by R.P. Chanda. This view of Chanda was later supported by Mortimer Wheeler. The Aryan invasion is also considered one of the causes for the decline of the Indus civilization.

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Place name) with List-II (Geographical location) and select the correct answer using the codes given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2013) Explanation– The correct match is as follows: List-I – List-II Meluhha – Indus region Dilmun – Bahrain Makan/Makan – Makran coast Kurgon – Central Asia

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2014) Explanation– Scholar R.E.M. Wheeler had suggested the adoption of the grid-type excavation method for the discovery of the Harappan civilization. While the principle of stratigraphy was suggested by Thomas Jefferson, the radiocarbon dating method was suggested by F.W. Libby. Pitt Rivers attempted to measure Harappan evidence through the three-dimensional measurement method.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below: List-I (Theory of the destruction of Harappan civilization) List-II (Supporter)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-III Paper June, 2015) Explanation– List-I (Theory of the development of Harappan civilization) List-II (Supporter) A. Aryan Invasion – I. R.P. Chanda and Mortimer Wheeler B. Change in the course of the Indus river – II. H.T. Lambrick C. Gradual Desiccation – III. M.R. Mughal D. Constant Floods – IV. Robert L. Raikes, George F. Dales

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.D: Kalibangan – Joint burial of male and female

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation— The archaeological site named Harappa is located in the Montgomery district of the current Punjab province of Pakistan. In 1921, Dayaram Sahni surveyed it and regular excavation started from 1923. In 1926, Madho Swarup Vats and in 1946, Mortimer Wheeler conducted excavations on a large scale. To the south of the general residential area of Harappa, there is a cemetery which has been named Cemetery R-37.

questions.question_text: For approximately how many centuries did the fully developed Harappan civilization survive?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- On the basis of the radiocarbon dates obtained from Mohenjodaro, Kot Diji, Kalibangan, Lothal, Rojdi, and Surkotada, the date of the Indus civilization is determined from 2400-1700 BC. From about 2250 BC to 1750 BC, this civilization was at the peak of its development. The fully developed Harappan civilization survived for about five centuries.

questions.question_text: Who ruled the Harappan-era cities?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- We do not know anything about the governance system of the Indus cities. In this regard, we can only make guesses. It seems that the governance of Mohenjodaro and Harappa was carried out through strong forts. Central officials resided in these forts. Possibly they also had a king who was a priest and ruled as a representative of the deity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the most prominent feature of the Indus Valley civilization?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—In 1921-22, the excavation of Harappa and Mohenjodaro took place under the leadership of Rakhaldas Banerji and Dayaram Sahni. Remnants of cities in a developed state were obtained from the excavation. In the history of India, the rise of the first cities is found only in the Indus civilization, which is the most prominent feature of the Indus Valley.

questions.question_text: Which of the following facts given regarding the decline of the Indus Valley civilization is/are correctly matched? (k) Garden – Foreign invasion (Kh) Aurel Stein – Climatic change (g) Dales – Geographical sequence of events (Gh) V. N. Mishra – Tectonic change Codes:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Scholars have expressed different views regarding the decline of the Indus Valley. Gordon Childe and Mortimer Wheeler considered external invasion; Aurel Stein and A. N. Ghosh considered climatic change; Dales considered geographical sequence of events and V. N. Mishra considered tectonic change, while K. U. R. Kennedy considered diseases like malaria and epidemics for the decline of the Indus.

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river is the site 'Rangpur', associated with Harappan culture, located?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – The site Rangpur associated with Harappan culture is located on the bank of the Bhadar river, which is in the Ahmedabad district of Gujarat province. It was discovered by Madho Swarup Vats in 1931 and by S. R. Rao in 1953. The later phase of the Indus culture is visible from this site.

questions.question_text: Which was the largest building of the Indus Valley civilization?

options.A: The Great Water Tank of Mohenjodaro

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The largest building of the Indus Valley civilization is the Granary, which is not in the specified options. Therefore, its answer will be (d). The granary here is 45.71 meters long and 15.33 meters wide.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Who discovered the "Great Bath of Mohenjodaro"?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The Great Bath of Mohenjodaro was discovered by R. D. Banerji. It is 11.88 m long, 7.01 m wide and 2.43 m deep. Sir John Marshall has described it as an 'extraordinary construction' of the contemporary world.

questions.question_text: The famous city of the Indus Valley civilization, Harappa, was located—

options.A: On the bank of the Indus river
options.B: On the bank of the Ravi river
options.C: On the bank of the Ganga river
options.D: On the bank of the Saraswati river

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation- The famous city of the Indus Valley civilization, Harappa, is located on the left bank of the Ravi river in the Montgomery district of the Punjab province of Pakistan. This site was discovered in 1921 AD by Rai Bahadur Dayaram Sahni. To the south of the general residential area here, a cemetery has been found which has been named Cemetery R-37.

questions.question_text: The Indus site where the Jhukar-Jhangar culture developed was—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Jhukar-Jhangar culture developed at the Indus site Chanhudaro (located about 130 km south of Mohenjodaro, this site was discovered in 1931 AD by N. G. Majumdar and excavation was carried out here by Mackay in 1935). The development of Jhukar-Jhangar culture took place after the Indus culture. Chanhudaro is the only site from where curved bricks have been found and baked clay pipe-like drains have been used.

questions.question_text: From which province of India have the most Indus archaeological sites been discovered after independence?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– After independence, the maximum number of Indus archaeological sites have been discovered in the state of Gujarat in India. In Gujarat, there are 18 sites of the mature Harappan phase and 120 sites have been identified from the late Harappan period. Rangpur, Rojdi, Babarkot, and Padri are late Harappan period sites.

questions.question_text: What was the main food item of the Indus residents?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– Agriculture was the main occupation of the Indus people. The main reason for its fertility was the annual flood in the Indus river. Their agricultural implements were made of stone and bronze metal. The main food crop (food item) of the Indus residents was 'wheat and barley'. Other crops included cotton, peas, sesame, and millet. 6 varieties of millet have come to light from Rojdi. The Indus residents were unaware of sugarcane. The Indus residents had knowledge of a total of 9 crops.

questions.question_text: Match the sites mentioned in List-I with the facts mentioned in List-II and select the correct option from the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Harappa (i) Cemetery B. Lothal (ii) Dockyard C. Kalibangan (iii) Figure of a dancing girl D. Mohenjodaro (iv) Ploughed field
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—Signs of a cemetery have been found from Harappa. While a dockyard has been obtained from Lothal. Signs of a ploughed field have been found from Kalibangan and a figure of a dancing girl was obtained from Mohenjodaro.

questions.question_text: The excavation of the easternmost site of the Indus civilization (Alamgirpur) was done by—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—The excavation of the easternmost site of the Indus civilization (Alamgirpur) was done in the year 1958 AD by Y. D. Sharma. This site is located on the bank of the Hindon river in the Meerut district (Uttar Pradesh). Evidence of cotton cloth (cotton) is also found here.

questions.question_text: Which site of the Indus civilization was considered the main center of sea trade?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Lothal, situated on the bank of the Bhogava river, was an important site of the Indus civilization which is located in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. A dockyard with an enclosure of 214 × 36 meters was found here, which is an indicator of the maritime trade of the Indus civilization. Lothal was also called mini-Harappa or mini-Mohenjodaro. It was discovered in 1954 AD by S. R. Rao. Three coupled burials, remnants of a fire altar, a bead-making factory, and a dyeing vat were found from Lothal.

questions.question_text: To which period of human history does the Indus civilization belong?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – History has been divided into three parts by historians - 1. Pre-historic, 2. Proto-historic, 3. Historic period. Pre-history refers to that period when man had not developed the art of script or writing. Proto-history includes those civilizations in which written material is found but cannot be read. The period whose history is known through written evidence is called the historic period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Harappan archaeological sites is located to the north of the Hindu Kush mountain range?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—The development of the Harappan civilization occurred up to Afghanistan in the northwest. Two Harappan archaeological sites named Shortugai and Mundigak are located in Afghanistan across the Hindu Kush. Important evidence obtained from the excavation of the Sotugai (Shortugai) site: * Remnants of canals originating from the Kokcha river. * Dry farming and an Indus trading settlement. * Drills for perforating beads. * Seals engraved with rhinos (one-horned rhinoceros). * The 'trading settlement' of Sotugai (Shortugai) was the primary center for obtaining lapis lazuli beads.

questions.question_text: Of which culture are the Malwa cultures (1700–1200 B.C.) of Navdatoli, Eran, and Nagda a proof?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation- Many cultures came to light after Harappa in the Malwa region situated on the banks of the Narmada river, among which Navdatoli, Eran, and Nagda are major Chalcolithic cultures. Because of their extension in the Malwa region, they are called Malwa culture.

questions.question_text: The Indus Valley civilization was not contemporary with which of the following civilizations?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– From the chronological point of view, the Indus Valley civilization was contemporary with the civilizations of Egypt and Mesopotamia.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which Indus archaeological site is considered a metropolis?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– The discovery of the Indus civilization was made by Rai Bahadur Dayaram Sahni. The Indus civilization was an urban and Bronze Age civilization. Among the sites with a mature stage obtained from the Indus civilization, only 6 are given the designation of big cities: Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi, Dholavira, and Lothal. So far, about 1000 sites of this civilization have been found in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question_text: Jhukar culture is a
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- There is disagreement among scholars regarding the date of the Indus civilization, but scholars have considered it from 2500 BC to 1750 BC. At this time it was an urban civilization; after this, this civilization became rural because the cities gradually declined. The rural culture or late culture was given the name Jhukar culture.

questions.question_text: From which site of the Harappan culture has evidence of a middle town been found?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- Evidence of a middle town has been found from Kalibangan of the Harappan culture. Evidence of pre-Harappa has also been found from Kalibangan. Evidence of ploughed fields, barley, and gram and mustard has also been found from here. In addition to this, there is also a fire altar.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ascending orders is correct for the residential areas of the Indus Valley?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The work of bringing the Indus civilization to light was done by Dayaram Sahni and Rakhaldas Banerji in 1921. First, Dayaram Sahni obtained some evidence by excavating a site named Harappa in 1921, and in this same sequence, Rakhaldas Banerji had Mohenjodaro excavated in 1922, and Ravindra Nath Bisht had Dholavira excavated in 1990-91.

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river is Alamgirpur situated?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Alamgirpur is situated on the bank of the Hindon river. While determining the area of the Indus civilization, four important cities have been mentioned, which include Bhagatrav, Rehman Dheri, and Alamgirpur. The extension of the Indus civilization is found in India, Pakistan, and Afghanistan.

questions.question_text: From which of the following Harappan sites have the remains of workers' houses been obtained?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In 1921, Dayaram Sahni surveyed Harappa and its regular excavation started from 1923. From the excavation, there are some buildings outside the fort of Harappa which have been identified as residences of employees. There are also two-room barracks in Harappa which were for the laborers to live in.

questions.question_text: In which of the following Harappan sites has wood been used in the construction of a drain?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Amalananda Ghosh discovered Kalibangan in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan in 1952 AD. From the excavation here, cylindrical seals, marks of a plough, use of decorated bricks, use of raw bricks in the construction of houses, etc., are found. A good system of water drainage is not found in Kalibangan, but evidence of a wooden drain is found.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation – Ropar is a Harappan site situated on the left bank of the Sutlej river in the Punjab province of India. This was the first Harappan site to be excavated in India after independence. Its modern name is Rupnagar. It was discovered in 1950 by B.B. Lal, and Y.D. Sharma carried out its excavation during 1953-55. Six cultural phases have been found here. The first of these is of the Harappan period. A cemetery has been found here in which a pet dog was buried along with a human.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Remains of ploughed fields have been found at Kalibangan.
options.B: Remains of a fort have been obtained from Banawali.
options.C: Harappan-period coins have been obtained from Amri in Balochistan.
options.D: Amri was first discovered by J.M. Casal in 1929.

questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation – Kalibangan means 'black colored bangles' (settled in about 1100 hectares). This city, located in the Ganganagar district of Rajasthan, was discovered by Amlanand Ghosh in 1952. It was situated between the ancient Saraswati and Drishadvati rivers. Among the evidences here, the evidence of a field ploughed with a plough is most important. Its ploughing was done in a criss-cross manner, from which it is inferred that two crops were sown together. A couple burial has also been obtained from here.

questions.question_text: Which site related to the Indus civilization is located in Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – After the year 1947, work was carried out to search for ancient sites related to the Indus civilization in India and Pakistan, which yielded encouraging results. Among the important sites in India, Kalibangan located in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, Lothal and Rangpur located in Ahmedabad district of Gujarat, and Surkotada and Dholavira located in Kutch district are notable, as well as Banawali in Hissar district of Haryana, Rakhigarhi in Jind district, and Mitathal in Bhiwani district. Alamgirpur in Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh and Hulas in Saharanpur district are important sites of the Indus civilization. Ropar in Rupnagar district of Punjab is another site. In Balochistan, Pakistan, there is Suktagendor; in Sindh province, Kot Diji; in Punjab, Dera Ismail Khan, Jalilpur, Rehman Dheri, Gumla etc. Two important sites related to the Indus civilization, Mundigak and Shortugai, have been discovered in Afghanistan.

questions.question_text: From which of the following Harappan culture sites have evidences of a cemetery NOT been found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation – The ruins of the Indus civilization site Mohenjo-daro are located on the right bank of the Indus river in the Larkana district of Sindh province, Pakistan. The mounds of Mohenjo-daro are spread over an area of about five kilometers. The credit for the exploration of the mounds of Mohenjo-daro in 1922 goes to Rakhal Das Banerji. The residential houses of Mohenjo-daro were constructed of baked bricks. So far, there is no information about a cemetery area (if any existed) from Mohenjo-daro. Two types of evidence for disposal of the dead have been found inside the city of Mohenjo-daro: (a) partial burial, (b) complete inhumation (burial). Bones of birds, fish etc., charcoal and ash, clay lumps, ornaments etc. were found filled. Some scholars have considered these as examples of partial burial. Under the second category, forty-two skeletons obtained from the final phase of Mohenjo-daro can be placed, which were found lying in a scattered state in houses and on public roads inside the city area.

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river is the archaeological site Suktagendor, associated with Harappan culture, located?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation – The archaeological site Suktagendor, associated with Harappan culture, is located in the Balochistan province of Pakistan. The sites of Balochistan are generally found along trade routes. For example, it appears that there are many such sites on the Makran coast region. Two geographical factors are important here. First, many rivers in this area meet the seas. The mouths of these rivers can be considered convenient places. The settlements which today are found a few miles away from the sea were on the shore of the sea; therefore, these settlements had a double advantage, as they were located at the mouth of the river and also on the shore of the sea. From an archaeological point of view, three sites among these are important - Suktagendor (at the mouth of the Dasht river), Sotka-koh (at the mouth of the Shadi Kaur) and Balakot (at the mouth of the Windar river, east of Sonmiani Bay). The fort of this city was surrounded by a stone wall and it is known as a port of the Harappan period.

questions.question_text: On which river is the archaeological site named Manda, related to Harappan culture, located?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation – The archaeological site Manda, related to Harappan culture, is located in the Jammu-Kashmir state. It is situated on the bank of the Chenab river. Manda is considered the northernmost site of the Harappan civilization. The Indus civilization appeared in its fully developed stage around 2250 BC. Many archaeological sites of the Indus civilization were discovered in the provinces of Balochistan, Sindh and Punjab in Pakistan. In southern Balochistan, Suktagendor, Sotka-koh and Balakot are famous archaeological sites. In Sindh province, apart from Mohenjo-daro and Chanhudaro, there are sites of Kot Diji, Amri and Judeirjo-daro. Archaeologists have discovered numerous sites of this civilization in the provinces of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Jammu-Kashmir and Uttar Pradesh of the Indian subcontinent. Remains of the Indus civilization have been found in Ropar, Kotla Nihang and Sanghol in Punjab; Banawali, Rakhigarhi and Mitathal in Haryana; Kalibangan in Rajasthan; Rangpur, Lothal, Desalpur and Bhagatrav in Gujarat; and Alamgirpur (Meerut), Baragaon and Hulas (Saharanpur) etc. in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river have the maximum number of archaeological sites related to the Indus civilization been found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 (UGC Net. - III Paper June, 2013) PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The maximum number of archaeological sites related to the Indus civilization have been found on the bank of the Saraswati river, which is called Ghaggar and Hakra. By conducting extensive exploration of the valley areas of the Saraswati (present Ghaggar) and its tributary Drishadvati (present Chautang) in northern Rajasthan in 1950-53, Amlanand Ghosh achieved success in discovering about two dozen archaeological sites. Among these, Kalibangan located in Ganganagar is extremely important. At the archaeological site named Kalibangan, like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, two mounds of the citadel in the west and the city in the east are present. As a result of the excavation carried out under the direction of Braj Basi Lal and Bal Krishna Thapar, remains of Pre-Harappan and Harappan civilization were discovered.

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites of Harappan culture is there clear evidence of the lower town also being surrounded by defensive walls?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation – In Kalibangan, along with the arrival of the people of the Indus civilization, changes occurred in the housing plan. During this period, the fort was located in the western direction and the city area in the eastern direction. In Kalibangan, both the fort and the city area were surrounded by defensive walls. There were entrance gates in all four directions in the fort. In the southern part of the citadel mound of Kalibangan, five-six platforms made of mud and unbaked bricks have been found. On top of these, many 'fire altars' are made. The 'fort' was divided into two parts, North-South, by a long wall. The city area of Kalibangan was divided into several parts by four-five roads going towards North-South and East-West. Generally, there was a courtyard in the middle of each house, around which there were five-six small rooms. Unbaked bricks were used for building houses in Kalibangan. Baked bricks were used only for making drains, wells and thresholds. In one house, a circular design was made on the bricks of the floor.

questions.question_text: In the Great Bath complex pool at Mohenjo-daro, there were stairs - 1. On the Northern side 2. On the Southern side 3. On the Eastern side 4. On the Western side Select the correct answer from the following codes – Codes:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002, 2008 Explanation – In the citadel section of Mohenjo-daro of Harappan culture, many important public monuments and buildings were located. Based on speculation, functional names have been given to these, for example: Great Bath, Granary, Assembly Hall and Priest's Residence. Among the monuments obtained inside the fort, the Great Bath is the most remarkable. Its length from North to South is 55 meters and width from East to West is 33 meters. The length of the bathing tank built in its middle is 12 meters, width 7 meters and depth 2.50 meters. The floor of this bathing tank was made of baked bricks and 2.50 meters wide stairs were built on the Northern and Southern sides for descending and ascending into it. There were verandahs on three sides of the bathing tank and behind them many rooms and galleries were built. Above the Great Bath, eight small bathrooms were built in two rows, in which stairs were built for going to the upper floor. In a room located to the East of the bathing tank, a well built with a double row of bricks has been found; this was the main source of water supply for the Great Bath.

questions.question_text: From which province have evidences of rice been obtained from Harappan-level strata?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation – The main occupation of the life of Indus inhabitants was agriculture. The land of the Indus Valley was extremely fertile. The Indus and its tributaries brought fertile soil every year, in which the yield was quite good. The main food grains here were wheat and barley. Grains of wheat and barley have been found in the excavation. Probably they also cultivated paddy. Evidences of cultivation of paddy are found from Lothal (Gujarat) and paddy husk and millet from Rangpur. In Harappa, cultivation of peas and sesame used to take place. From the remains of cotton clothes, it is concluded that the inhabitants here also knew how to grow cotton. Among fruits, banana, coconut, melon, date, lemon, watermelon etc. were produced. Sufficient water was obtained from the river for irrigation. Farming was done with the help of tools made of stone and bronze. Remains of ploughs are found from the excavation of various sites, which indicates that the Indus inhabitants used ploughs for agricultural work.

questions.question_text: Where were the horse bones obtained from?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – Surkotada is located in the Kutch district of Gujarat. This site was discovered by Jagapati Joshi. Remains of horse bones have been obtained from Surkotada. A terracotta figurine of a horse has been found at Lothal and teeth of a horse have been obtained from Rana Ghundai. S.R. Rao is of the opinion that terracotta figurines of horses have been found from Lothal and Rangpur. However, it is ultimately believed that the Indus people were not familiar with the horse. Both the fort and city of Surkotada were surrounded by the same defensive wall.

questions.question_text: Who among the following considered 'Indra' responsible for the disintegration of Harappan culture?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – External invasion is considered a cause for the disintegration of the Indus civilization. Attention was first drawn to this by R.P. Chanda, followed by Gordon Childe in 1934. Mortimer Wheeler supported this. According to Wheeler, although the Indus civilization existed until the middle of the second millennium BC, yet in its later period it was progressing towards a gradual decline. Around 1500 BC, the sudden and accidental end of this civilization was the result of some external invasion. Based on human skeletons obtained in a scattered state from the upper surface of Mohenjo-daro, it was concluded that an external invasion occurred in the final phase of the Indus civilization. Most of the skeletons were found lying in houses and on public roads in a scattered state without formal last rites. On the basis of these evidences, Wheeler concluded that a sudden attack occurred on the city of Mohenjo-daro and these people could not escape. Wheeler very intelligently used the internal evidence of the Rigveda in this context. In some verses of the Rigveda, there is mention of 'Purandara' (destroyer of forts) Indra destroying the 'Ayas' (metal) built forts of the Asuras. Therefore, Wheeler held Indra responsible for this massacre.

questions.question_text: Which of the following archaeological sites is not associated with the Indus civilization?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – Burzahom is an important Neolithic site. It is located in the Kashmir province. The archaeological site named Burzahom was discovered in 1935 by De Terra and Peterson. Between 1960-64, the excavation of this place was carried out on behalf of the Archaeological Survey of India. From the excavation of Burzahom, remains of houses with pits have been found and this site is famous for its pit-dwellings. The shape of the pit-dwellings is narrow at the top and wide at the bottom. The Neolithic culture was more developed than its predecessor cultures. The human of this period was not only a consumer of food items but also became their producer. He had become completely familiar with agricultural work. Along with agricultural work, humans also started domesticating animals. His acquaintance increased with animals like cow, buffalo, ox, horse, sheep, goat etc.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the person who went to Mohenjo-daro?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – Mohenjo-daro, an important site of Harappan culture, is located in the Larkana district of Sindh province, Pakistan. First, in 1921-22, two famous archaeologists Rakhal Das Banerji and Dayaram Sahni proved that these two cities, settled at a distance of 483 km from each other, were once the two centers of the same civilization by obtaining antiquities from the ancient sites of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. Mr. Piggott has called them 'twin capitals of a vast empire'. After Sahni and Banerji, Sir John Marshall and Madho Sarup Vats obtained important materials by excavating in Mohenjo-daro and Harappa respectively for several years. In addition to this, some other scholars like Mortimer Wheeler, K.N. Dikshit, Ernest Mackay, N.G. Majumdar, Aurel Stein etc. also made important contributions in the discovery of this civilization. This entire civilization is called 'Indus Valley Civilization' or 'Harappan Civilization' after its main site Harappa.

questions.question_text: Which among the following Harappan sites was not fortified?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation – Chanhudaro is the only archaeological site from where curved bricks have been found and no existence of any fort has been found at Chanhudaro. Only a small part of this settlement has been excavated. Among the important construction work found here, there was also a bead-making factory. In Kalibangan, the fortified western mound has two separate but interconnected sections. One was probably for the residence of a specific class of the population and the other for many high platforms, on whose summits evidence of the existence of fire altars is found. In Lothal, the entire settlement was surrounded by a wall. It was a well-planned settlement; in the eastern section of Lothal, a tank-like enclosure made of baked bricks is found. In Surkotada, the repetition of the plan of the western mound of Kalibangan is seen. This site has no eastern mound. To the west of the western mound of Kalibangan is a cemetery, and to the east evidence of such a structure is found where probably ritual activities were performed. The plan of the eastern mound of Kalibangan is similar to the plan of Mohenjo-daro, but the difference between the two is that the houses of Kalibangan were made of unbaked bricks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with Pre-Harappan/Early Harappan culture?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Kalibangan is a major Pre-Harappan site located in the Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan. It was discovered by archaeologist Amlanand Ghosh. There are two mounds in Kalibangan. On the small mound with a citadel located in the western direction, remains of Pre-Indus civilization have been obtained below the remains of the Indus civilization. Ploughed fields and fire altars have been found from the excavation here. The remains of a skull of a child on which surgery was performed have been found from here. Evidence of barley cultivation has also been found from here.

questions.question_text: From which archaeological site is the oldest evidence of silk in India obtained?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The oldest evidence of silk in India has been obtained from Nevasa. Silk has been called 'Kausheya' in literature. From Nevasa itself, headless goddess idols, a factory for making stone axes, and evidence of a necklace of copper beads in the neck of a child's skeleton have been found. The archaeological site Nevasa is located on the bank of the Pravara river in the Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra. The credit for discovering this archaeological site goes to M.N. Deshpande. Bhagwanpura - is located in the Haryana state; remains of Harappan civilization have been found here. Rangpur and Ropar are located in Gujarat and Punjab provinces respectively; remains of Harappan-period culture have been found here as well.

questions.question_text: From which Harappan site has evidence of rice been obtained?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - Besides Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, 'Lothal' is also an important site of the Indus period. Lothal was located on the bank of the Bhogwa river in the Ahmedabad district of Gujarat. This site was discovered by S.R. Rao. The main feature of this site is the discovery of a large enclosure (214 x 36 meters) made of bricks, which archaeologists have defined as a dockyard which was used as a port. Evidence of 'rice' has been found from here. Other findings include couple burials and fire altars. No Mother Goddess idol has been found here.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites of Harappan culture are located in the Kutch region? 1. Desalpur 2. Dholavira 3. Lothal 4. Rojdi Select the correct answer from the codes below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation ─ Among the sites associated with Harappan culture, Desalpur, Surkotada and Dholavira are located in the Kutch region, while Rojdi, Rangpur and Lothal are located in the Khambhat region.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was NOT worshipped in Harappan culture?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation ─ The god Vishnu was not worshipped in Harappan culture. Scholars have associated the evidence of female figures depicted on terracotta figurines and seals obtained from sites related to the Harappan civilization with the worship of Mother Power (Matrishakti). According to Marshall and Mortimer Wheeler, the position of Mother Goddess was supreme in the divine family of the Indus civilization. On the basis of evidence obtained from the sites of the Indus civilization, it is proved that the inhabitants here used to worship Shiva, Pipal, Naga etc.

questions.question_text: The excavation of Chanhudaro was directed by -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation ─ Under the joint auspices of the 'American School of Indian and Iranian Studies' and the 'Boston Museum of Fine Arts', E.J.H. Mackay conducted the excavation of Chanhudaro in 1935-36. The discovery of Chanhudaro was made in 1931 by N.G. Majumdar. This archaeological site is located 80 miles away from Mohenjo-daro on the left bank of the Indus. This is the only site from where curved bricks have been found. Evidence of Jhukar and Jhangar culture has been found from here.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sites of Harappan culture are located in Haryana? 1. Banawali 2. Kalibangan 3. Rakhigarhi 4. Ropar Indicate your answer from the following codes -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Many sites of Harappan culture are located in Haryana. A site of the early Harappan period is - Rakhigarhi, while sites of the later period are - Banawali, Mitathal, Daulatpur, Siswal etc. Whereas Kalibangan is a Pre-Harappan archaeological site located in Rajasthan. Ropar is located on the bank of the Sutlej river in Punjab, whose excavation was carried out by Yagya Dutt Sharma in 1953-55.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the largest Harappan site found in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Among the given options, the largest Harappan site found in India is Rakhigarhi. Dholavira is one of the two largest Harappan-period cities discovered in present-day India. The second largest city in this category is Banawali, which is located in Haryana. Its excavator is R.S. Bisht. In addition to this, Kalibangan is located in Rajasthan and Lothal in Gujarat.

questions.question_text: Which of the following archaeological sites related to the Indus civilization is located in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The archaeological site related to the Indus civilization which was located in Uttar Pradesh is Alamgirpur. Alamgirpur is located in the Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh; this was the easternmost boundary of the Indus civilization. Alamgirpur is located on the bank of the Hindon river

questions.question_text: In which of the following Harappan sites have evidences of rice cultivation been found? Select the correct answer using the codes given below: I. Kalibangan II. Lothal III. Mohenjo-daro IV. Surkotada Codes –
questions.explanation: Evidences of rice cultivation have been found from Kalibangan and Lothal. In addition to these, evidence of a ploughed field has been found from Kalibangan. A dockyard has been found from Lothal. Evidence of fire altars has been found from both these sites

questions.question_text: The eastern boundary of the Harappan culture was–
questions.explanation: The area of the entire Saindhava (Indus) civilization was 1,215,000 square kilometers. Its extension was from Manda, Kashmir in the North to Daimabad, Maharashtra in the South and from Sutkagen-dor in the West to Alamgirpur (U.P.) in the East B. Stone Statues, Terracotta Figurines, and Seals

questions.question_text: From which place was a fragment of pottery containing an engraving of a dancer obtained?
questions.explanation: Bhirrana is a site of the mature Harappan culture located in Haryana. An engraving of a woman has been found on red pottery here, which has been compared with the bronze dancer obtained from Mohenjo-daro. Three buildings with many rooms have been found here. One building with 4 rooms is located exactly in the center of the mound. One building also had a veranda and a courtyard in addition to 10 rooms

questions.question_text: In which state is the Harappan site Daimabad located?
questions.explanation: Daimabad is an archaeological site located in the Godavari valley of Maharashtra. Evidence of Late Harappan and Chalcolithic life has been obtained from this site. Between 1976-79 AD, a team from the Archaeological Survey of India conducted excavation work under the direction of S.A. Sali. Daimabad is the largest site of the Jorwe culture; here, two button-shaped seal-seals engraved in Harappan script have been found

questions.question_text: In the Indus civilization, information about which metal is found?
questions.explanation: The Indus Valley Civilization is called the Bronze Age civilization because bronze (a mixture of copper and tin) was used for the first time during this period

questions.question_text: Match the following lists: Pottery Type Period associated with A. Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) 1. Early Vedic Period B. Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) 2. Second Urban Revolution C. Black-and-Red Ware 3. Not associated with a specific period D. Painted Grey Ware (PGW) 4. Later Vedic Period Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: (A) Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) - (3) Chalcolithic Period (B) Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) - (2) Second Urban Revolution (C) Black-and-Red Ware - (1) Early Vedic Period (D) Painted Grey Ware (PGW) - (4) Later Vedic Period

questions.question_text: From which Saindhava site was a clay model of a plow found?
questions.explanation: A clay model of a plow has been found from Banawali. Banawali is an archaeological site located in the Hisar district of Haryana which is related to the Indus Valley Civilization. It was located on the banks of the ancient Saraswati River. Its excavation was conducted by R.S. Bisht in 1973. There was a lack of a drainage system in Banawali

questions.question_text: In which type of society was the concept of Mother Goddess primarily prevalent?
questions.explanation: The concept of Mother Goddess was essentially prevalent in agricultural societies. Examples of this are found in the Harappan culture. The Mother Goddess was considered the goddess of fertility. In Harappa, a statue shows a plant emerging from a woman's womb, which is considered to be the image of the Earth Goddess. She was worshipped as the goddess of the earth's fertility

questions.question_text: By what name did the residents of Mesopotamia know the Indus region?
questions.explanation: India's Indus civilization was one of the early periods of ancient Egypt and the ancient civilization of Mesopotamia. It is also known as the 'Harappa or Indus-Saraswati civilization'. It is known from Sumerian records that the traders of those cities used to exchange goods with the traders of 'Meluhha'. Meluhha is identified with the Sindh region

questions.question_text: Which of the following scripts was used in the Harappan civilization?
questions.explanation: Pictographic script has been used in the Harappan civilization. There are about 64 basic symbols and 250 to 400 letters in the Indus script, which are found on rectangular steatite seals, copper tablets, etc. The Saindhava script is indigenous in origin and has no connection with the scripts of West Asia. The Harappan script is ideographic/pictographic

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not correct?

options.A: Trade was a major part of the Harappan economy.
options.B: Harappan people conducted both inland and maritime trade.
options.C: Harappans had close commercial relations with the Nile Valley civilization.
options.D: Models of bronze and terracotta bullock carts and seals depicting boats have been obtained from excavations.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – The Saindhava residents were also interested in trade, and both their internal and external trade were prosperous. Trade was a major part of the Harappan economy. The traders here conducted both inland and maritime trade. In addition to Indian regions, the Saindhava residents had trade and cultural relations with many other countries of the world. Models of bronze and terracotta bullock carts and seals depicting boats have been obtained from Saindhava excavations.

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites was a short inscription found written in very large letters in the Harappan script?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – A short inscription written in very large letters in the Harappan script was obtained from Dholavira. First of all, in 1967-68, Dholavira was discovered by J.P. Joshi of the Archaeological Survey of India, and during 1990-91, large-scale excavation work was started by R.S. Bisht which continued for many years. While other cities of the Harappan civilization were divided into only two parts—the Citadel and the Lower Town—Dholavira was divided into three parts: the Citadel, the Middle Town, and the Lower Town.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The Harappan civilization had deep trade relations with Southern Turkmenistan. Reason (R): Harappan material or material produced under Harappan influence has been obtained from Kish, Ur, Nippur, etc. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – The Harappan civilization had deep trade relations with Southern Turkmenistan. Harappan material or material produced under Harappan influence was obtained from Kish, Ur, Nippur, etc. In addition to this, various materials were also imported from Southern Turkmenistan. Pottery, seals, terracotta bulls, beads, male figurines, toy carts, copper plates, etc., of the Harappan civilization type have been found from excavations at various places. Therefore, the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.question_text: Most of the seals of the Harappan civilization are made of the following:
questions.explanation: – Harappan Seals: About 2000 seals have been obtained from Saindhava sites so far, which are mostly made of steatite. These are generally 2.8 × 2.8 cm in size, on which various symbols, figures, and scripts are engraved

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities located in North-East Afghanistan was a Harappan trading port?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation—Shortugai, located in North-East Afghanistan, was a Harappan trading port. This site was discovered in 1962 AD.

questions.question_text: What is the ratio of Harappan weights?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation – The ratio of Harappan weights was 1 : 2 : 4 : 8. Measurement was done based on this. The Harappan people also had knowledge of the foot. A shell instrument was used for surveying, which has been found at both Lothal and Mohenjo-daro.

questions.question_text: Which of the following weapons of war is unavailable in the remains of Harappan culture? (i) Bow and arrow (ii) Sword (iii) Shield (iv) Helmet Select the correct answer with the help of the code given below –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation – Bows and arrows have been obtained from the remains of war weapons of the Harappan culture. Whereas swords, shields, and helmets have not been obtained from the Harappan culture. It is noteworthy that Harappan tools and weapons were of simple types because the people of the Harappan civilization were less war-loving and more peace-loving.

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Material obtained from Harappan site) with List-II (Probable source) and select the correct answer from the code given below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation – The probable sources of material obtained from Harappan archaeological sites are as follows – Copper (Rajasthan), Shell (Kutch), Lapis Lazuli (Afghanistan), and Gold (Deccan). It is noteworthy that Harappan people traded with local and external regions. Cylindrical seals of Mesopotamia have been obtained from Lothal. Whereas in local trade, trade of stone, metal, bone, etc., used to take place.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): The people of Harappan culture had knowledge of plow-based agriculture. Reason (R): A terracotta model of a plow was obtained from the Mature Harappan level at Banawali. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – The main basis of the economic life of the Saindhava civilization people was agriculture, animal husbandry, craft, and trade. Evidence of furrows (plow lines) has been found in the Pre-Harappan stage of Kalibangan. The Harappan people perhaps used wooden plows and stone sickles were used for harvesting crops. A terracotta toy model of a plow is found from Banawali.

questions.question_text: As revealed by the obtained evidence (for example, metal tools for cutting seals), which one of the following sites was a major center for the manufacture of Harappan seals?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Excavation of Chanhudaro, located in the Sindh province of Pakistan, was conducted by E.J.H. Mackay in 1935 AD. Among the remains here, factories for bead manufacturing and seal manufacturing are prominent.

questions.question_text: Who among the following first propounded that Harappan culture developed spontaneously in the Indus region and there was no Western influence in it?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper June, 2015) Explanation – According to Madho Sarup Vats, who held the indigenous view, the origin of the Indus civilization took place from Iranian, Baloch, and Indus cultures and the local cultures of India. There was no Western influence in it.

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Harappan site) with List-II (Archaeological remains) and select the correct answer using the code given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation—The correct matching will be as follows— List-I List-II (a) Mohenjo-daro (i) Engraved bronze axe (b) Harappa (ii) Bronze chariot (c) Lothal (iii) Ivory scale (d) Banawali (iv) Terracotta plow

questions.question_text: Which of the following groups of animals is depicted on the Pashupati seal of Mohenjo-daro?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation—An image of a yogi sitting in a Padmasana posture has been found on a seal obtained from Mohenjo-daro. To the right of the person, a tiger and an elephant, and to the left, a buffalo and a rhinoceros are found. There is a trident-like ornament on the head; it has three faces. Marshall has related this deity to 'Rudra-Shiva', who has been called Trimukha (three-faced), Pashupati (lord of animals), Yogeshwar, or Mahayogi.

questions.question_text: What were the common household vessels of the Harappan people made of?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- For making vessels, Indus clay was used in which lime or mica was mixed. Harappan vessels were heavy and functional. The vessels were of various types—plain, glazed, or painted. Most of the vessels were plain and made of red clay (actually, they turned red due to being fired in the open), on which red or brown bands were often made.

questions.question_text: Remains of the Painted Grey Ware tradition along with the archaeological materials of the Late Harappan period have been found at—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—Remains of the Painted Grey Ware tradition along with archaeological remains of the Late Harappan period have been found from an archaeological site named Bhagwanpura located on the southern bank of the Saraswati River in the Kurukshetra district of Haryana. Its excavation was conducted by J.P. Joshi.

questions.question_text: Information about the script of the Indus Valley is obtained from-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Information about the script of the Indus Valley is obtained from seals. From excavations in more than a hundred sites in the Indus Valley, two thousand seals have been obtained, on which human, fish, animal, and plant figures are engraved along with script symbols. It is noteworthy that there are 64 basic symbols in the Indus script. 25 symbols of the script of the Northern Harappan period are also included in these 64 symbols; in the Late Harappan script, the practice of putting alternating lines was stopped.

questions.question_text: The weights of the Saindhava civilization were multiples of which number—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—The weights of the Saindhava civilization were multiples of 16. The ratio of the weight of the weights was 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 160, 208, 320, etc.

questions.question_text: The Greeks learned about cotton from Indians. They called it:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Cotton was cultivated in the Indus River basin, evidence of which is found from the cotton wrapped around a seal found in Harappa. Because it was produced in Sindh, the Greeks called it Sindon.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.B: Coastal city of Harappan civilization : Lothal
options.D: Meaning of Kalibangan : Black clay vessels

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Kalibangan means bangles made of black-colored clay. This site is located on the bank of the Ghaggar River in the Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan.

questions.question_text: From which Harappan site was a goat's skeleton obtained near a human skeleton?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Evidence of a goat's skeleton along with a human skeleton has been obtained from the Saindhava site named Lothal. Three joint burials have also been obtained from Lothal. Lothal is a Harappan site located in the Gulf of Khambhat on the banks of the Bhogava River in present-day Ahmedabad (Gujarat). Its discovery was made by S.R. Rao in 1954-55 AD. The much-discussed discovery of Lothal is the port (Dockyard) or Godiwada.

questions.question_text: 274 ancient clay seals were obtained from the excavation of which archaeological site?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- 274 ancient clay seals have been obtained from the excavation at Basarh. Mohenjo-daro is located on the bank of the Indus River in Pakistan; this site is located in the Larkana district of Sindh province, Pakistan. The granary obtained from Mohenjo-daro is probably the largest building of the Saindhava civilization. Kayatha is a Chalcolithic site from where evidence of the Chalcolithic period has been obtained.

questions.question_text: Which of the following metals is not discovered at Lothal?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Lothal is located on the bank of the Bhogava River; its excavation was done by Dr. S.R. Rao in 1957. Persian seals, joint burials, terracotta figurines of horses, etc., have been obtained in the excavation here. Note- The commission's answer is (a), but evidence of gold, bronze, and copper is obtained from Lothal.

questions.question_text: Below is a list of some gods and goddesses: (1) Pashupati (2) Indra (3) Mother Goddess (4) Prajapati Among these, whose evidence do we not find in the remains of Harappan culture?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation – Indra was the most important and glorious deity of the Rigvedic Aryans. He has been called Purandara, meaning the destroyer of forts. He is also depicted as a war leader. There are 250 hymns on Indra. Indra is known by names like Vritrasura Hanta, Purabhid, Somapa, Shatakratu, Madhavan, etc. In the Later Vedic era, there was also a significant increase in the powers of the Sabha and Samiti. In the Atharvaveda, the Sabha and Samiti have been called the two daughters of Prajapati.

questions.question_text: While matching List-I and List-II, choose the correct answer from the code table given below the lists: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation– The correct matching is as follows– Sacrificial Altar – Kalibangan Port – Lothal Dancing Girl Statue – Mohenjodaro Silver Crown – Kunal

questions.question_text: A seal depicting a man fighting a tiger is found from which Harappan site?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Within Harappan art, seals hold a special place where relief sculpture can be seen. In a seal found at Mohenjodaro and Lothal, a man is shown fighting two tigers. A seal of Pashupati Shiva has been found at Mohenjodaro.

questions.question_text: From which of the following countries did the people of Harappa culture obtain Lapis Lazuli?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Trade and commerce held an extremely important place in the economic structure of the Indus Civilization. Relatively more evidence is available regarding the external trade of the Indus Civilization. The cities of the Indus Civilization had close trade relations with countries of Central and West Asia. Evidence of trade contacts of Indus cities has been found with Afghanistan, Soviet Russia, Southern Turkmenistan, and countries located in the Persian Gulf like Iran and Iraq. Lapis lazuli and silver were imported from Afghanistan. The Badakhshan region of Afghanistan is very famous for Lapis lazuli. Archaeological remains of the Indus Civilization have been found from the excavation of a site named Shortugai in Afghanistan. No other expansion of the Indus Civilization is found in this region of Afghanistan. Therefore, Shortugai can be considered an intermediary trade settlement.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below– List-I (Cause of the decline of Indus Civilization) A. Indus river floods B. External invasion C. Climate change List-II (Scholar's opinion) 1. Aurel Stein 2. Gordon Childe and Mortimer Wheeler 3. Raikes and Dales 4. Marshall and Mackay 5. Stuart Piggott Codes: A B C D D. Geological change
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Correct matching– (a) Indus river floods - Marshall and Mackay, S.R. Rao (b) External invasion - Gordon Childe and Mortimer Wheeler (c) Climate change - Aurel Stein (d) Geological change - Raikes and Dales

questions.question_text: Archaeological evidence revealed that the Indus Valley Civilization had relations with the following ancient civilization -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation– Besides Indian regions, the Indus residents also had trade and cultural relations with many other countries of the world. The Indus residents had close trade contacts with Central Asia, North-Eastern Afghanistan, Iran, Bahrain Island, Mesopotamia (Iraq), Egypt, etc.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below: Assertion (A): As a feature of Harappan religion, the worship of Mother Goddess was prevalent in all major cities of Harappa culture. Reason (R): Terracotta female figurines have been found in large numbers from Harappa and Mohenjodaro. Codes:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Female terracotta figurines have been found from many archaeological sites located in the Sindh and Punjab regions of the Indus Civilization. Scholars have associated these terracotta figurines with the worship of Mother Goddess. Female terracotta figurines have not been found in major cities like Kalibangan and Lothal.

questions.question_text: A Harappan-era copper chariot was found at:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: A Harappan-era copper chariot has been found at Daimabad. This archaeological site is located in the Ahmednagar district on the banks of the Pravara River, a tributary of the Godavari, in the Maharashtra province. A dog is shown with the driver on the chariot found here. Three bronze statues of a rhinoceros, an elephant, and a buffalo have been found. A terracotta scale and 28 houses of the Malwa culture have been found. Three types of cemeteries have been found at Daimabad - pit burials, urn burials, and symbolic burials. An example of infantile scurvy disease is found from here.

questions.question_text: Which type of seals were most popular in the Harappa culture?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ In the field of established art of the Harappan civilization, seals hold an important place. Developed sculpture is seen on the seals. The shape of the seals is mainly square or rectangular. Square seals were the most popular. Figures of bulls, elephants, rhinoceroses, and tigers, as well as leaves, branches, etc., have been made with extreme precision using very sharp and fine tools on the seals. The seals are mostly made of steatite. Copper seals have been found at Lothal and Desalpur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common motif on Indus seals?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ The most common motif on Indus seals is the Unicorn (Eka-shringi). Indus seals are usually square or rectangular and are made of ivory, faience, and steatite. In addition to the depiction of the Unicorn, figures of chimeras (Ihramriga), trees, and women-men have also been found on Indus seals.

questions.question_text: Evidence of fortification is found at which of the following early Harappan sites?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– Kot Diji is a distinct Harappan archaeological site located in the Sindh province of Pakistan. Where evidence of fortification with defensive walls of the pre-Harappa civilization is found. This is more standardized and systematic than pre-Indus civilization Kalibangan. The construction of the defensive fort at Kot Diji had already taken place in the first phase of the Indus Civilization. Therefore, based on the fortification system, Kot Diji is considered a fortified settlement earlier than Kalibangan.

questions.question_text: An ivory scale for linear measurement has been found at
questions.explanation: An ivory scale for linear measurement has been found at Lothal. The Harappan city of Lothal is located on the banks of the Bhogwa River in the Ahmedabad district of Gujarat. Excavation was carried out here in 1957-58 AD under the leadership of archaeologist Rangnath Rao. The main feature here was the port. It was discovered by S.R. Rao in 1954

questions.question_text: A terracotta scale is reported from the Harappan level at
questions.explanation: Terracotta scales have been found at Kalibangan from the Harappan level. The plan of the eastern mound of Kalibangan resembles the plan of Mohenjodaro. Remains of pre-Harappan cultures have been found at Kalibangan. Ploughed fields have been found at Kalibangan, which provide evidence of two crops being sown together C. Religion and Economy

questions.question_text: Wheeler said after seeing the skeletons in ______ that a military attack or a mass destructive incident must have happened to the people of Harappa.
questions.explanation: After seeing the skeletons in Mohenjodaro, Wheeler said that a military attack or a mass destructive incident must have happened to the people of Harappa

questions.question_text: What was the unit of measurement of length called in ancient India?
questions.explanation: In ancient India, the units for measuring length or distance were called Yava, Angula, Vitasti, Hasta, Dhanu, and Krosa. Raktika and Karsha were the weights of goldsmiths, and Nimisha used to be a measure of time

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was an important port on the Gujarat coast?
questions.explanation: In the Indus era society, the major ports located on the coast of Gujarat were Lothal and Mundra

questions.question_text: The Harappan people had knowledge of which of the following fruits?
questions.explanation: The Harappan people had knowledge of fruits like watermelon, dates, lemon, and pomegranate

questions.question_text: In which period is the earliest reference to the Swastika symbol found?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The earliest reference to the Swastika symbol is found from the Harappan civilization. The Swastika was a symbol of sun worship. The basis of the religious outlook of the Harappan civilization was more worldly and practical.

questions.question_text: Which animal was associated with the symbol of power in the Indus Valley society?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation- The animal associated with the symbol of power in Indus society was the bull. The image of this animal is found on many Indus-era sites and recovered seals, sealings, copper plates, etc.

questions.question_text: From which place has the famous priest figure been found?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Among the remains found at Mohenjodaro are the priest figure statue, Great College, the statue of a bronze dancing woman, the statue of Pashupati Nath (Shiva) depicted on a seal, six kilns of potters, cotton cloth, a fragment of an elephant's skull, heaps of melted copper, a scale made of shell, skeletons scattered at the final level and found in a well, and evidence of cloth on wet clay.

options.A: A charioteer standing on a chariot drawn by a dog and two bulls
options.B: Bull, elephant, rhinoceros and a chariot drawn by two horses
options.C: Horse, elephant and a charioteer standing on a chariot drawn by two bulls

questions.question_text: From Harappan sites, Citadel, Middle Town, and Outer Town have been found under city planning– (i) Kunal (ii) Lothal (iii) Rangpur (iv) Dholavira Select your correct answer based on the following codes: Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– Citadel, Middle Town, and Outer Town have been found under city planning from the Harappan site (Dholavira). Dholavira is located in the Kutch district of Gujarat state.

questions.question_text: In which of the following Harappan cities were square or circular fire altars found inside houses? 1. Harappa 2. Mohenjodaro 3. Lothal 4. Kalibangan Select the correct answer from the following- Codes :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 KVS TGT 2018 GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation- In the Harappa culture, evidence of square or circular fire altars has been found inside houses at Lothal, located in Gujarat, and Kalibangan, located in Ganganagar, Rajasthan. With the entry of the Indus civilization people in Kalibangan, significant changes occurred in the housing planning. During this period, the fort was located in the west and the "city area" in the east. At Kalibangan, both the fort and the city area were surrounded by defensive walls. There were entrance gates in all four directions in the fort. In the southern part of the fort mound at Kalibangan, five or six platforms made of mud and unbaked bricks have been found, on top of which several fire altars or vedikas are built. The fort was divided into two parts, North-South, by a long wall. The archaeological site named Lothal associated with the Indus civilization is located 2 km north of Saragwala village on the banks of the Bhogwa River in the Ahmedabad district of Gujarat. It was discovered by S.R. Rao.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not of the Harappan era?
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014 Explanation– Except for Jakhera, Padri, Bhirrana, and Kuntasi etc. are Harappan-era archaeological sites. It is known that the Harappan civilization was a Bronze Age civilization, which is known by names like Harappan civilization and Indus Valley civilization. Its date has been determined as 2300-1750 BC. Jakhera, located in the Etah district, is an Iron Age archaeological site in North India. Other Iron Age sites in North India include Ahichchhatra (Bareilly), Atranjikhera (Etah), Hastinapur (Meerut), and Kaushambi.

questions.question_text: Which deity did the people of the Indus civilization worship?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The people of the Indus civilization worshipped Pashupati. Although we have found many statues of Mother Goddess as a result of excavations at Indus sites, this makes it clear that the worship of Mother Goddess was also prevalent in that period. It is clear that a picture of a yogi seated in Padmasana is found on a seal obtained from Mohenjodaro. There is a trident-like ornament on the head and it has three faces. Marshall has addressed this deity by the name of Rudra Shiva, who is also addressed by names like Trimukha, Maheshwar, and Pashupati, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a pre-Harappan culture?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation- The Kulli culture located in South Balochistan (Pakistan) comes under the pre-Harappan culture. The pottery of this culture is of buff pink color and paintings have been done on them with red and black colors.

questions.question_text: What were Anuloma and Pratiloma in ancient India?
questions.explanation: In ancient India, Anuloma and Pratiloma were two systems of marriage. In Anuloma marriage, a man of a higher Varna married a girl of the Varna immediately below his. Such marriages often occurred in Vedic society. The sons born from this were granted fewer rights. Under Pratiloma marriage, a girl of a higher Varna married a man of a lower Varna. This type of marriage was considered reprehensible and its prevalence in society was very low. The offspring born of Pratiloma marriage were described as degraded and untouchable. Therefore, the origin of the Varnasankara (inter-mixture of castes) system in society was considered to be from such marriages. Untouchables were called 'Antyaja'. Salvation (Moksha) has been accepted as the ultimate goal of life in Indian religion. As an integral part of the Indian way of life, the Keshakartana (Keshantha) ceremony also comes among the 16 Sanskaras. In the Keshakartana ceremony, the student's beard and mustache were shaved for the first time. In the end, he observed a vow of silence and lived a life of strict discipline for one year

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II List-I
questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows List-I (A) Brahma-Yajna - (B) Bhuta-Yajna - (C) Deva-Yajna - (D) Manushya-Yajna - List-II Reading and teaching the Vedas Offering to all living beings Offering to Agni (Fire) Honoring guests

questions.question_text: Astronomy in ancient India-
questions.explanation: Since ancient times in India, astronomy has been a part of Vedanga. Vedangas were composed to understand the Vedas correctly. The total number of Vedangas is 6, which include Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda, and Jyotish. Predictions regarding the universe and constellations are the subject of Jyotish. The first text based on astronomy is 'Vedanga Jyotish' composed by Lagadha Muni, whose subject matter is based on astrological knowledge. Other texts of Jyotish are Garga Samhita, Brihat Samhita. The Maitrayani Upanishad describes seven planets including the Sun and the Moon. In the field of ancient Indian astronomy, there were astronomers like Aryabhatta, Bhaskaracharya, Brahmagupta, Varahamihira, etc. In ancient Indian astronomy, Varuna (Neptune) was not included in the list of planets. Currently, the total number of planets is 8, which includes Varuna. The Moon is a satellite of the Earth that orbits the Earth

questions.question_text: According to historians, the word 'Grama' in the Vedic period could have one or more of these meanings:
questions.explanation: Evidence of the use of the word 'Grama' in the Vedic period is found in broad terms. The basic unit of labor division in political organization was the 'Kula' or family. Several Kulas joined together to form a Grama; the head of the Grama was the Gramani. He performed both military and civil duties. A larger unit than the Grama was the 'Vish', whose master was called Vishpati. Grama or group also functioned as a small military unit by tribes. At the same time, the structure made of chariots used by pastoralists was also called Grama because it was also used as a military system

questions.question_text: The Sunahshepa legend, in which a father is described selling his son, is found in:
questions.explanation: Aitareya Brahmana – Its compiler was Mahidasa. Mahidasa was called 'Aitareya' due to being the son of a Shudra woman 'Itara'. The points described in the Aitareya Brahmana are—It gives the rules for the coronation of the king and the theory of the origin of the state and the king. In it, the subcontinent is divided into 5 geographical divisions—Udichyadik, Dakshinadik, Prachyakdik, Pratichyadik, and Pratishthadik, and it mentions 10 types of governance systems. This system belongs to Vairajya, Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, etc. It contains legends associated with 'Bharata', the son of Dushyanta. In it, the king is called 'Vishmattā' (consumer of the Vaishya) and 'Dharmasyagopta' (protector of religion). In the Aitareya Brahmana, the Vaishya is called 'Adya', the Shudra is called 'Yathakamavadhya', and the girl is called 'Kripana' (one who causes grief). It contains the story of Sunahshepa, in which a father is described selling his son. It contains a beautiful explanation of the four ages (Kaliyuga, Dvapara, Treta, and Satyayuga). In the Aitareya Brahmana, 'Hospitality to guests is the greatest sacrifice.' It also mentions the ocean

questions.question_text: In which of these texts are the Sabha and Samiti mentioned as two daughters of a Vedic deity?
questions.explanation: In the Atharvaveda, the Sabha and Samiti are called the two daughters of Prajapati. A prayer for harmony between these two is made in it. The Sabha and Samiti do not allow the king to become autocratic. The Sabha was an institution of the noble class; it also performed some judicial functions, whereas the Samiti was an institution of the common people. In the Rigveda, the Sabha is mentioned 8 times and the Samiti 9 times. The Sabha is also mentioned in the Yajurveda, where the entry of youth is discussed. The Sabha and Samiti are mentioned in the Chhandogya Upanishad, while they are not mentioned in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad

questions.question_text: Ishvarakrishna was

options.A: A Vaishnava Acharya of early medieval Odisha
options.B: A king of Assam in the eighth century
options.C: A philosopher of one of the Shad-Darshanas
options.D: A lawgiver of the medieval period

questions.explanation: Among Vedic philosophies, the Shaddarshana (six philosophies) are most famous and ancient. The Shaddarshana are as follows—Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta. Their founders were respectively Kapila, Patanjali, Gautama, Kanada, Jaimini, and Badarayana. The oldest and most authentic text of Samkhya philosophy is 'Samkhyakarika', which was composed by Ishvarakrishna. Ishvarakrishna was an important philosopher of Samkhya philosophy

questions.question_text: Was there a different penal code according to Varna for theft? Who among the following was given the maximum punishment?
questions.explanation: Manusmriti is the oldest Smriti text. According to Manu, the rod of punishment (Danda) itself is the king, and Danda is of 4 types - 1. Dhig-danda 2. Vag-danda 3. Dhana-danda 4. Vadha-danda. There are 12 chapters in Manusmriti. The eighth chapter describes the investigation of litigation, rules for giving punishment, all types of crimes, and punishments. The basis of the ancient Indian justice and punishment system is Manu's justice system— Ashtapadyam tu shudrasya steye bhavati kilbisham | Shodashamstu vaishyasya dvatrimshatkshatriyasya cha || (Manu., 8-236) Meaning - If a Shudra, Vaishya, or Kshatriya commits theft, they have to become partakers of the sin respectively eight, sixteen, and thirty-two times. Brahmansya chatuhshashtipurnam vapi shatam bhavet | Dvigurana cha chatuhshashtistaddoshaguna viddhi sa: || (Manu. 8-237) Meaning - Similarly, since a Brahmin has the most knowledge of the merits and demerits of theft, therefore if he commits theft, he has to become a partaker of the sin sixty-four or even a hundred times. For this reason, the Shudra received the least and the Brahmin received the most punishment.

questions.question_text: Lajahoma was a part of -
questions.explanation: After the Panigrahana (taking the hand), the bride and groom stand facing east, then the bride takes parched grains (fried rice) from her brother and, while offering them into the fire altar, prays to the deities to unite herself with her husband's family.
