At this time, she also desires from the deities that her husband be long-lived and that their mutual affection increases. This ritual performed during the marriage ceremony is called the 'Lajahoma Sanskara'

questions.question_text: In the Rigveda, for what has the word 'Tasar' been used?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, mentions of artisans like carpenters, chariot-makers, weavers, leather-workers, potters, etc., are found. The word 'Ayas' is used in the sense of copper or bronze, which shows that the Aryans had knowledge of metallurgy. In the Rigveda, the word 'Takshan' is found for the carpenter and 'Karmara' for the metallurgist. The word 'Hiranya' has been used for gold. A class named 'Vasavaya' did the work of weaving clothes. The weaving of clothes was done with looms. The shuttle was called 'Tasar', the warp was called 'Otu', and the woof was called 'Tantu'

questions.question_text: What was 'Gavishti'?
questions.explanation: The early life of the Rigvedic Aryans was unsettled. Therefore, animal husbandry was more important than agriculture in their lives. Among the animals, the cow had the highest importance. The cow was counted as property. In the Rigveda, the cow is mentioned 176 times. Most of the battles of the Aryans were over cows. In the Rigveda, the synonym for war is "Gavishti" (search for cows); similarly, words like Gaveshana, Goshu, Gatyu, Gabyu, etc., are used for war

questions.question_text: The word 'Hiranyastupa' was first mentioned in–
questions.explanation: The first mention of the Stupa is found in the Rigveda, where it is called 'Hiranyastupa'. The literal meaning of Stupa is 'heap' or 'mound'. Since it is built at the site of the funeral pyre, one of its names is also 'Chaitya'. There are 4 types of Stupas: Paribhogika, Sharirika, Uddeshika, and Sankalpita. Paribhogika is based on objects used by the Buddha; Sharirika is based on the remains of the Buddha and his prominent disciples; Uddeshika is based on events of the Buddha's life; and Sankalpita Stupas are built by devotees out of faith

questions.question_text: In the Rigveda, the strip of land between two cultivable lands was called –
questions.explanation: The culture of the Aryans was essentially rural, so the basic foundations of their economic life were agriculture and animal husbandry. Cultivable land was called 'Urvara' or 'Kshetra'. In the Rigveda, the strip of land between two cultivable lands was called Khilya. In the Rigveda, mentions of Langala and Sira (for the plow), Phala, Sita (the furrow made by the plowshare), etc., are found. The Aryans were familiar with activities like sowing, reaping, threshing, etc. The field was plowed with the help of a plow and oxen and seeds were sown in it

questions.question_text: Among the following deities, which one deity was not offered sacrifices like the others?
questions.explanation: The early life of the Rigvedic Aryans was tribal, so their deities were also symbols of natural forces. Yaska, in his text Nirukta, has formed a group of Rigvedic deities whose number is 33. These have been divided into deities of the Sky, Atmosphere, and Earth. Rudra holds a prominent place among the deities of the atmosphere. Rudra was not offered sacrifices like the other deities. He is described in 3 hymns of the Rigveda. His nature is wrathful, and he is considered the early form of Shiva

questions.question_text: Shrimad Bhagavad Gita is a part of which Parva of the Mahabharata?
questions.explanation: The Mahabharata was compiled by Maharishi Vedavyasa, but it was completed in its final form around 400 AD. Initially, it had only 8800 verses, then it was called Jayasamhita. Eventually, it came to have one lakh verses and accordingly, it came to be known as Shatasahasri Samhita or Mahabharata. It is the largest epic in the world. There are a total of 18 Parvas in the Mahabharata. Shrimad Bhagavad Gita is a part of the Bhishma Parva (6th Parva)

questions.question_text: In the Rigveda, the word 'Dhanyakrit' has been used for–
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, the word 'Dhanyakrit' has been used for the winnower. In the Rigveda, agriculture held a secondary position compared to pastoralism. Among the total 10,462 verses of the Rigveda, agriculture is mentioned in only 24. Three words of importance in agriculture are found in the core part of the Samhita – Urdar, Dhanya, and Vapanti The word 'Charshani' was used for agriculture or cultivation. The plowed field was called "Kshetra" and the "fertile" land was called "Urvara". The land was divided into fields between which were strips of land called "Khilya". The word "Khilya" was also used for fallow or barren lands, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following words was used for a wealthy person in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, the word 'Gomat' was used for a wealthy person. In the Rigveda, animal husbandry was more important than agriculture. Among the animals, the cow had the highest importance. The cow was counted as property. Most of the battles of the Aryans were over cows. In the Rigveda, the synonym for war is Gavishti (search for cows). Similarly, words like Gaveshana, Goshu, Gatyu, Gabyu, etc., were used for war. Rigvedic society was based on a tribal system. The Rigvedic people were divided into Janas and tribes. The tribe had a king who was called 'Gopa'

questions.question_text: Whose son is the Sun deity considered to be in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: The Sun is one of the mythological deities. He is considered the form of the supreme Lord Adi-shakti. He is called the son of Goddess Aditi and Dyaus. Usha is considered the goddess of dawn. The Vedas have considered her as the incarnation of the light and attraction of sunrise. Usha was the morning goddess of the Aryans. The period before sunrise was called Usha. When the sun begins to shine, it is called Savita. The famous Gayatri Mantra of the Rigveda is dedicated to Savita. Rudra's nature is wrathful; he is considered the early form of Shiva. Urvashi was the most famous Vedic Apsara

questions.question_text: In the Rigveda, Nishkagreeva is a type of–
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, Nishkagreeva is a type of ornament. Before the regular circulation of coins, since the Vedic period, 'Nishka' was a gold ornament worn around the neck. In later times, it began to be used in commercial transactions. By the Maurya era, regular coins had come into circulation in trade and business; the coins were made of gold, silver, and copper. These coins were called 'Nishka' and 'Suvarna'. It is noteworthy that before the post-Mauryan period, 'Punch-marked' coins were in circulation

questions.question_text: In the Vedic period, who was considered the mediator deity between other deities and humans?
questions.explanation: The most important and glorious deity of the Rigvedic Aryans was Indra. Agni's place is after Indra. There are 200 hymns for him. The deity Agni performed the work of a mediator between deities and humans. The first mantra of the Rigveda starts with the praise of Agni. It is understood that the offerings put into the fire (Agni) become smoke and go to the sky and finally reach the deities. Agni was the only deity who could be included in all three: Sky, Atmosphere, and Earth

questions.question_text: Shaunaka and Pippalada are branches of which Veda?
questions.explanation: The Vedas have many branches. The Shakala branch is the only living branch associated with the Rigveda. The Yajurveda is divided into the branches of Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. Kauthuma, Ranayaniya, and Jaiminiya are the three branches of the Samaveda. The branches of the Atharvaveda are Shaunaka and Pippalada

questions.question_text: During the Rajasuya sacrifice, the Rigvedic king used to visit the houses of about a dozen Ratnins. How many of those Ratnins were women?
questions.explanation: By the time of the Post-Vedic period, significant changes are visible in the religious life of the Aryans. Large sacrifices were started in this period. Among these sacrifices, Rajasuya, Ashvamedha, and Vajapeya sacrifices were prominent. The Ratnins had an important role in the Rajasuya sacrifice. The 12 Ratnins were mentioned for the first time in the Shatapatha Brahmana. Among these 12 Ratnins, 4 were women

questions.question_text: In the Dharmashastras, what term (word) is used for women whose husbands are living abroad?
questions.explanation: In the Dharmashastras, the word Proshitabhartrika or Proshitapatika has been used for women whose husbands are living abroad. For those women whose husband is about to return from abroad, the word 'Agamatapatika' has been used in the Dharmashastras. Later, various Smriti-writers advocated for many rights for women, including Stridhana. Yajnavalkya has given the most liberal interpretation regarding the rights of women

questions.question_text: The Janaka-Yajnavalkya narrative is found in:
questions.explanation: The primary spokesperson of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad is Yajnavalkya. It contains the description of Yajnavalkya establishing Brahma-vidya by defeating Brahma-vadi scholars in a philosophical debate in the royal court of King Janaka of Videha. In the history of human thought, for the first time in this Upanishad, the Brahma or the Absolute Element was grasped and its true expression was made. The description of the importance of self-knowledge given to Maitreyi by Yajnavalkya, the famous 'Yajnavalkya-Gargi' dialogue, etc., are found in this

questions.question_text: In the Vedic period, who was considered the deity who safely brings home strayed cows?
questions.explanation: In the Rigvedic period, Pushan was an important deity. Pushan's main function is as a protector of paths. He also shows the way to strayed animals. In the Rigvedic period, he was the deity of animals and in the Post-Vedic period, he became the deity of the Shudras. Pushan's chariot is pulled by goats. Pushan is also the prominent deity of marriage. The marriage hymn of the Rigveda is dedicated to Pushan itself

questions.question_text: Match the following and select the correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: Veda - Priest Rigveda – Hotri Yajurveda – Adhvaryu Samaveda – Udgatri Atharvaveda – Brahma

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedic deities are mentioned in the Boghazkoi inscription?
questions.explanation: Boghazkoi was the capital of the ancient Mitanni kingdom. This inscription describes a treaty between the Hittite king and the Mitanni king, and for this purpose, deities named Indra, Varuna, Nasatya, and Mitra were considered witnesses. This inscription dates back to 1400 BCE and was discovered in 1906 by Hugo Winckler in Turkey in the form of inscriptions on clay tablets. In this inscription, the word 'Avartana' is also used in the sense of the rotation of the wheels of the chariot

questions.question_text: Which tributaries of the Saraswati river are mentioned in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: The tributaries of the Saraswati river, Drishadvati and Apaya, are mentioned in the Rigveda. In the Nadi Sukta of the Rigveda, 19 rivers are mentioned, while in the entire Rigveda 25 and in the entire Vedic Samhita 31 rivers are mentioned. It is noteworthy that the Vyas river is not mentioned in the Nadi Sukta of the Rigveda. It has been called the Pariganita river. In the Rigveda, the Parushni (Ravi) river is also called the Iravati river. The region between the Saraswati and Drishadvati rivers was called Brahmavarta

questions.question_text: Of what was the Rigvedic Parjanya the deity?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, Parjanya was the deity of the clouds. He was primarily worshiped for rain, water, rivers, etc. Indra is also partially considered the deity of storm, thunderbolt, and rain. Varuna is also considered the deity of rivers and the ocean. Mitra and Varuna were deities who lived in a palace of a thousand pillars. Rudra was the deity who caused fear, while Ashvins were considered the deities of medicine in the Rigvedic period

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a living branch of the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: There are many branches of the Vedas which were given the designation of 'Charana'. The Shakala branch is the only living branch associated with the Rigveda. Yajurveda is divided into two branches, Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. Kauthuma, Ranayaniya, and Jaiminiya are the three branches of Samaveda. The branches of Atharvaveda are Shaunaka and Pippalada. Although five branches of Rigveda—Shakala, Bashkala, Ashvalayana, Shankhayana, and Mandukayana—are mentioned, at present the Shakala branch is the most authentic and living branch

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched among the sacrifices and their organizers:
questions.explanation: The Later Vedic period is the age of expansive regional kings. In this period, the power of kings increased and new theories of kingship were established in which kings were described as being endowed with divine power. In these new theories, the creation of vast states was stated as the duty of the kings. Various titles of kings were mentioned; these titles were Adhiraja, Rajadhiraja, Ekarat, and Samrat, which the kings used to assume. Various types of sacrifices were performed for the establishment of vast empires. It is stated in the Gopatha Brahmana that a Raja should perform the Rajasuya sacrifice, a Samrat the Vajapeya sacrifice, an Ekarat the Ashvamedha sacrifice, a Virat the Purushamedha sacrifice, and a Sarvarat should perform the Sarvamedha sacrifice

questions.question_text: Choose the false statement among the following:

options.A: Aitareya Brahmana is related to the Rigveda.
options.B: Kaushitaki Brahmana is related to the Rigveda.
options.C: Both Aitareya and Kaushitaki Brahmanas are related to the Rigveda.

questions.explanation: In the following questions, all statements are correct 1. Aitareya Brahmana is a text related to the Rigveda; it has 40 chapters. Each chapter is divided into 8 groups. Its main subject is Somayaga. Additionally, it also contains descriptions of Agnihotra and Rajasuya sacrifices. 2. Kaushitaki Brahmana is also related to the Rigveda. It is also known as the Shankhayana text. It has 30 chapters. In its first six chapters, sacred sacrifices like Agnyadhana, Agnihotra, Darshapurnamasa sacrifice, and Ritu sacrifice are described. 3. Both Aitareya and Kaushitaki Brahmana texts are related to the Rigveda.

questions.question_text: The story of Nachiketa is in:
questions.explanation: The main basis of Indian philosophy and the final category of Vedic literature are the Upanishads. They are also called Vedanta. Upanishad means - sitting near the Guru for the purpose of attaining knowledge by the disciple. In these very Upanishads, in the Kathopanishad, which is an Upanishad of the Katha branch of the Krishna Yajurveda, the elements related to life and death are discussed through the Yama-Nachiketa dialogue in the Nachiketopakhyana

questions.question_text: In 600-321 BCE, the development of cities took place near those places where certain types of crafts were prevalent in those villages and they were also commercial centers. Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: The period of the sixth century BCE is known as the phase of second urbanization in the Indian subcontinent. After the decline of the urban centers of the Harappan period, after a gap of a thousand years, cities developed again. But this time the development of cities took place in the region of the middle Ganga valley and not in the plains of the Indus river. It is said that between 600 and 300 BCE, sixty cities like Pataliputra, Shravasti, Varanasi, Vaishali, Champa, Kaushambi, and Ujjayini developed, which became centers of craftsmanship, products, and trade, and where potters, carpenters, and textile weavers and traders began to reside

questions.question_text: Detailed information about rituals (Karmakandas) is obtained from-
questions.explanation: In the Kalpa Sutras, there are six Vedangas: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda, and Jyotish. In this, the Kalpa Sutra has three parts (1) Shrauta Sutra (2) Grihya Sutra (3) Dharma Sutra. Some scholars consider Shulba Sutra as the fourth part of the Kalpa Vedanga. But it should be considered under the "Shrauta Sutra" itself. Detailed information about religious rituals is found in these. This Sutra includes the explanation of sacrificial rules and sacraments (Samskaras). These texts were composed by different sages for each branch of the Vedas. The credit for compiling these is given to the sage Lomaharsha

questions.question_text: Choose the false statement among the following:

options.A: According to the Dharmasutras, the king was not the maker of laws.
options.B: According to the Dharmasutras, the king was the protector of laws.
options.C: The Dharmasutras were admirers of rural life.
options.D: The Dharmasutras were in favor of urbanization.

questions.explanation: The rules of social life are expounded in detail in the Dharmasutras (1) Discussing Varnasrama Dharma, the duty of the Brahmachari (2) Rules and duties of householders (Grihasthas) (3) Mention of the duties of the king (4) Mention of the types of marriage and its variations (5) Prohibited food (6) Types of purification and village life (7) Atonement (Prayashchitta) A detailed description of all these activities is found. From these very Dharma-sutras, Smritis originated later, whose arrangements are considered valid in Hindu society even today.

questions.question_text: In which time period do we see significant benefit for women in education, marriage, art, and even in war?
questions.explanation: In the Rigvedic period, women enjoyed many types of rights equal to men. There was an excellent arrangement for education for women and they were married only upon becoming adults. Women of this period were also proficient in arts and also participated in wars

questions.question_text: What is the language of the Vedas?
questions.explanation: The Vedas are those texts of Indian culture, in which there is a storehouse of knowledge related to almost all subjects like astrology, music, mathematics, science, religion, medicine, nature, astronomy, etc. The Vedas are considered the backbone of our Indian culture and are the word of God, in which the Sanskrit language has been used, which has been called the divine language or the language of the gods

questions.question_text: According to Varna-samskara (mixture of Varnas), how many castes are there?
questions.explanation: Due to Varna Shankara, i.e., the mixture of Varnas, anarchy in the social system has been mentioned. There was a rapid increase in the number of castes during the Gupta and post-Gupta periods. 61 castes were mentioned in the Manusmriti and 100 castes were mentioned in the Brahmavaivarta Purana Note - The DSSSB board has considered the answer option (d).

questions.question_text: Antyaja is formed of which caste?
questions.explanation: Antyaja means those born at the end; those living outside civilized colonies were called forest and mountain regions and those settling there were called Antyaja. Among these Antyaja, neighboring foreigners, Mlechchhas, Chandala, Paukasa, Vidalkar, Charmakar, etc., are counted. In today's context, the word Antyaja has become inherent in Dalit, as washermen (Dhobi), shoemakers (Charmakar), Nats, Varudas, Kaivartas, Medas, and Bhils—these seven have been considered Antyaja

questions.question_text: Which of the following ancient Janapadas of Rajasthan is mentioned in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: The Matsya region was surrounded by the Chambal and Saraswati rivers. Its mention is first found in the Rigveda. This Janapada falls in the modern Alwar, Jaipur, and Bharatpur area. In the Manu Samhita, along with Matsya, Kurukshetra, Panchala, and Shurasena are mentioned as the sacred residence of Brahmana sages. This region was included in the Chedi kingdom, which Ashoka later merged into Magadha

questions.question_text: 'Vajasaneyi' is related to which of the following Vedas?
questions.explanation: The Vajasaneyi Samhita is related to the Shukla Yajurveda of the Yajurveda. Upon worshipping the Sun by Yajnavalkya, Lord Sun gave him the knowledge of the Veda in the form of Speech. Therefore, the Samhita spoken by him was called the Vajasaneyi Samhita

questions.question_text: In which text were the four Ashramas first mentioned?
questions.explanation: The mention of the four Ashramas is found in the Jabala Upanishad. Whereas, three Ashramas are discussed in the Chandogya Upanishad. The Ashrama system is as follows 1. Brahmacharya Ashrama 2. Grihastha Ashrama 3. Vanaprastha Ashrama 4. Sannyasa Ashrama.

questions.question_text: Which of the following composers of the Rigveda is an example of social mobility?
questions.explanation: In the Vedic period, there is a wonderful name, Kavasha Ailusha, who was a Shudra according to the caste system, but he was a great Rishi who wrote Vedic Richas (verses). He connected the Vedic hymns associated with the gods to the ground. He wrote an important Sukta 'Aksha Sukta'. Aksha means the dice used for gambling. In this, the painful feelings of a gambler have been expressed

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II– List-I List-II A. Mudga i. Sugarcane B. Vrihi ii. Moong C. Ikshu iii. Rice D. Yava iv. Barley Using the codes given below, select the correct answer– A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct matching– List-1 List-2 1. Mudga – Moong 2. Vrihi – Rice 3. Ikshu – Sugarcane 4. Yava – Barley

questions.question_text: In which Upanishad is the dialogue related to the soul between Uddalaka Aruni (father) and Shvetaketu (son)?
questions.explanation: The dialogue related to the soul between Uddalaka Aruni and Shvetaketu is found in the Chandogya Upanishad. In this Upanishad, it is said that the soul is located in the depths. The cause of death and rebirth is Avidya (ignorance). Liberation or Moksha from this is possible only through knowledge (Jnana). In this very Upanishad, information about the three worlds—Mrityuloka, Pitriloka, and Svargaloka—is obtained

questions.question_text: Match the following– Upanishad Famous Quote A. Chandogya i. Tat Tvam Asi B. Brihadaranyaka ii. Aham Brahmasmi C. Mandukya iii. Ayam Atma Brahma D. Mundakopanishad iv. Satyameva Jayate Code– A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct matching– Upanishad Famous Quote 1. Chandogya – Tat Tvam Asi 2. Brihadaranyaka – Aham Brahmasmi 3. Mandukya – Ayam Atma Brahma 4. Mundakopanishad – Satyameva Jayate

questions.question_text: Which of the following facts about Vedic literature are true? A. Hiranyagarbha Sukta is an example of monotheism. B. Pippalada Samhita is a branch or version of the Atharvaveda. C. Aitareya Brahmana tells us about the systems of governance prevalent in the Later Vedic period. D. Satapatha Brahmana tells us about the eastward expansion of the Aryans. Mark the correct answer–
questions.explanation: The Hiranyagarbha or primordial egg burst from extreme heat. Aitareya Upanishad is a part of the Aitareya Aranyaka of the Rigveda. The Upanishad contains the description of the bursting of this egg which is said to be a part of one Brahman. The Pippalada Samhita is a branch or version of the Atharvaveda. Hiranyagarbha Sukta: Hiranyagarbhah samavartatagre bhutasya jatah patireka asit. Sadasadhara prithivim dhyamutemam kasmai devaya havisha

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true in the context of Later Vedic religious trends?

options.B: Indra lost his supremacy in the Vedic group of gods.
options.C: The concept of the Trinity (Trimurti) began to take shape.

questions.explanation: In the Later Vedic period, religious rituals related to sacrifices and Karmakandas increased and the need for more priests in sacrifice-dependent religious activities began to be felt. In the Later Vedic period, the supremacy of Indra disappeared and Prajapati was given the position of the supreme deity, because he was the presiding deity of sacrificial rituals, and gradually Prajapati, Rudra, and Vishnu became established as the concept of the Trinity (Trideva). Whereas the concept of belief in Avataravada did not start in the Later Vedic period

questions.question_text: The origin of the sixteen Samskaras can be searched in
questions.explanation: There is no mention of Samskaras in the Rigveda, but in some Suktas of this text, descriptions of some religious acts related to marriage, conception (Garbhadhana), and funeral rites (Antyesti) are found. In the Atharvaveda, a more detailed description of marriage, funeral, and conception Samskaras is found. In the Gopatha and Satapatha Brahmanas, mention of religious acts of Upanayana and Godana Samskaras is found. In the Taittiriya Upanishad, the description of the convocation education of the Acharya upon the completion of education is found Note – The detailed source of the origin of the sixteen Samskaras is found in the Grihyasutras.

questions.question_text: Brahmana texts shed extensive light on Vedic rituals and ceremonies. Which of the following Brahmana text and Vedic Samhita pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Vedic Samhita – Brahmana Rigveda Samhita – Aitareya and Kaushitaki Brahmana Samaveda Samhita – Tandya Samhita (Panchavimsha Brahmana) Yajurveda Samhita – Satapatha and Taittiriya Brahmana Atharvaveda Samhita – Gopatha Brahmana

questions.question_text: To which clan (family) does the seventh mandala of the Rigveda belong?
questions.explanation: Rigveda is a Samhita in which there are 10 mandalas. In this, mandalas from two to seven are considered the oldest. The first, eighth, ninth, and tenth mandalas belong to a later period. The tenth mandala, which also contains the Purusha Sukta, is the latest. Among these, the seventh mandala is related to the Rishi Vashistha. In the seventh mandala of the Rigveda, there is a description of the Dasharajna war (Battle of Ten Kings) which was fought on the bank of the Ravi (Parushni) river. This war was fought between King Sudas of the Bharata clan (Tritsu dynasty) and the kings of ten other tribes. The reason for this war was the removal of his priest Vishvamitra by King Sudas and appointing Vashistha in his place. In this, Sudas was victorious. In the fifth mandala is Atri, in the sixth mandala is Bharadwaj, and the third mandala is related to Vishvamitra

questions.question_text: What was the original name of the Jhelum river?
questions.explanation: The ancient name of the Jhelum river was Vitasta. This river is located at the foot of the Pir Panjal range in Kashmir. Verinag Spring is the source of this river; it is located at an altitude of about 4900 meters. The tributaries of this river are Nallah Liddar, Nallah Sindh, Nallah Vishav, Ram Biyara, Kishanganga, etc. It is also called a mythological river which was mentioned in the Mahabharata and the name Vitasta is mentioned in the Rigveda

questions.question_text: Shutudri is the ancient name of which river?
questions.explanation: The Shutudri river is known by the name of Sutlej river in modern times. It is known by the name of Vedic or Rigvedic river. The Sutlej river was known by the name of Shutudri in ancient times. This river originates from Rakshastal lake in Tibet and enters India through the Shipki La pass. This river has been described as the main tributary of the Indus river in the south. The tributaries of the Sutlej river are Beas, Spiti, and Parechu

questions.question_text: Which of the following texts confirms the divine theory of the origin of the Varna system?
questions.explanation: Information about the divine theory of the origin of the Varna system is found in the Purusha Sukta of the tenth mandala of the Rigveda. It is described in it that the Brahmana originated from the mouth of the Primordial Being (Adi Purusha), the Kshatriya from the arms, the Vaishya from the thighs, and the Shudra Varna from the feet

questions.question_text: According to ancient Indian writings, the land between which of the following two rivers is called 'Brahmavarta'?
questions.explanation: In Manusmriti, the area between Drishadvati and Saraswati has been called 'Brahmavarta'. Drishadvati is identified with the Hakra river of Rajasthan. Drishadvati is considered a tributary of the Saraswati river which used to flow in Rajasthan. The Saraswati river is the most sacred river of the Rigveda. It was called the best among rivers, i.e., 'Naditama'. The area of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers has been called 'Brahmarshi Desha'

questions.question_text: The Battle of Ten Kings was fought on the bank of the _____________ river.
questions.explanation: The Battle of Ten Kings was fought on the bank of the Parushni river. Its mention is found in the 7th mandala of the Rigveda. On one side was the advisor Vishvamitra and on the other side was Rishi Vashistha. In this war, King Sudas of the Bharata clan was victorious

questions.question_text: 'Asikni' is the ancient name of which river?
questions.explanation: Asikni is the ancient name of the Chenab river. The old name of Vyas is Vipasha, Ghaggar is Drishadvati, and Saraswati's ancient name is Chaitang

questions.question_text: Match the list of rivers in List-I with their Vedic names given in List-II. List-I List-II A. Jhelum 1. Vipasha B. Sutlej 2. Vitasta C. Kabul 3. Shutudri D. Vyas 4. Kubha A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct match is Jhelum - Vitasta Sutlej - Shutudri Kabul - Kumbha/Kubha Vyas - Vipasha

questions.question_text: For which Vedic text is the word 'Vedanta' used?
questions.explanation: For Vedic texts, the word Vedanta was used for Upanishad

questions.question_text: In many sections of the Rigveda, the word 'Aghanya' (should not be killed) is used for ________.
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, the word Aghanya was used for cows, which means they should not be killed. Priests were given superiority in the Varna system

questions.question_text: These policies related to human Grihastha Dharma from the conceptual stage are given in detail in ________.
questions.explanation: These policies related to human Grihastha Dharma from the conceptual stage are given in detail in the Grihya Sutra

questions.question_text: In the Vedic period, the word ________ was used for ploughed land.
questions.explanation: In the Later Vedic period, the word Urvara or Kshetra was used for 'ploughed' land. In the Rigveda text, the word 'Sita' has been used for ploughed land

questions.question_text: Match: Word - Meaning A. Uttariya - I. Class of ascetics B. Adhivasa - II. Barber or Napit C. Ajin - III. Upper garment D. Vapta - IV. Overall dress A B C D
questions.explanation: Word - Meaning A. Uttariya - Upper garment B. Adhivasa - Overall dress C. Ajin - Class of ascetics D. Vapta - Barber or Napit

questions.question_text: Who was the propounder of the theory that the birth of the Rigveda did not occur in North-West India but in Iran?
questions.explanation: Max Müller believed that the birth of the Rigveda did not occur in North-West India but in Iran (Central Asia)

questions.question_text: Which of these goddesses is not mentioned in the Rigveda? 1. Sita 2. Taravati 3. Usha 4. Aditi
questions.explanation: Mention of Sita and Taravati is not found in the Rigveda. Taravati belonged to the Vajrayana branch of Buddhism. Description of Usha and Aditi is found in the Rigveda

questions.question_text: What was the core subject matter of Sushruta Samhita actually related to?
questions.explanation: Sushruta Samhita is an ancient Sanskrit text on Ayurveda and Surgery. It mentions 1120 diseases, 700 medicinal plants, 64 procedures based on mineral sources, 57 procedures based on animal sources, and 8 types of surgical procedures in 186 chapters

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding Stridhan: (1) It meant 'woman's property' (2) It was not transferred from mother to daughter Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Stridhan is a word associated with Hindu tradition. The character of property that is a woman's property depends on the source from which it was obtained. A woman has full rights over Stridhan and she can claim it even after separating from her husband

questions.question_text: Identify the false statement regarding Vedic religion:

options.A: Vedic hymns sing praises of various gods and also collectively as Vishvedevas.
options.B: The presence of Vishwakarma and Prajapati in the Vedic divine family is proof of monotheism.
options.C: Truth is one and sages call it by various names.
options.D: Vedic sages seem to humanize natural forces.

questions.explanation: The false statement regarding Vedic religion is ♦ In the Later Vedic period, the deities Prajapati, Vishnu, and Shiva become prominent in place of the Vedic period deities Indra and Agni. This does not mean that it is proof of monotheism. In the Vedic period, two main deities 'Rudra' (god of animals) and Vishnu (protector of people) were considered. ♦ Yet, Vedic people, despite being polytheistic, believed in monotheism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Puranas have been called ancient history by their creators?
questions.explanation: Matsya and Vayu Puranas have been called the most ancient Puranas by their creators Vishnu Purana - Vishnu is depicted as the supreme deity. Its orator is Parashara Rishi. Vayu Purana - Specially contains descriptions of Shiva.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true?

options.A: Thirty-three gods are mentioned in the Rigveda.
options.B: The first mention of the four Ashramas is found in the Jabalopanishad.
options.C: In the Rigveda period, Kuru was one of the tribes fighting against the Bharata tribe.
options.D: The four Varnas are mentioned in the 10th Mandala of the Rigveda.

questions.explanation: 33 gods are mentioned in the Rigveda, while the first mention of all four Ashramas is found in the Jabalopanishad. In the Rigvedic period, the Dashrajan war took place in which on one side were the Bharata people and on the other side was a confederacy of 10 kings (Anu, Druhyu, Yadu, Turvasha, Puru etc.)

questions.question_text: Ranayaniya Samhita is associated with-
questions.explanation: Samaveda has 3 branches – Kauthuma Samhita (related to Gujarat), Ranayaniya Samhita (related to Maharashtra) and Jaiminiya Samhita (related to Karnataka). The Kauthuma Samhita of Samaveda is the most prevalent

questions.question_text: The aphorism ‘Ekamevadvitiyam Brahma’ is mentioned in–
questions.explanation: Chandogya Upanishad is considered the oldest Upanishad. In this, Advaitavada was established by saying Sarvam Khalvidam Brahma (Ekamevadvitiyam Brahma), meaning Brahman is everything. The first mention of Devaki-putra Krishna is found in the Chandogya Upanishad

questions.question_text: What status was given to the offspring born from a ‘Pratiloma’ marriage?

options.C: Status higher than that of mother-father
options.D: Status lower than that of mother-father

questions.explanation: Pratiloma marriage was a marriage between a high-caste woman and a low-caste man, while Anuloma marriage was a marriage between a high-caste man and a low-caste woman

questions.question_text: The idea of the fourfold classification of society is not obtained from
questions.explanation: The idea of the four-varna system of society is first found in the Purusha Sukta of the 10th Mandala of the Rigveda, in which the origin of Brahmanas from the mouth, Kshatriyas from the arms, Vaishyas from the thighs and Shudras from the feet is mentioned

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is false for Rigvedic women?

options.A: Girls had full freedom to choose their husbands.
options.B: Child marriage was not prevalent in the Rigvedic age.
options.C: The Purdah system was in existence in the Rigvedic age.
options.D: Women used to participate in sacrifices and meetings of the Sabha-Samiti.

questions.explanation: The Rigvedic period was an important period from the perspective of the status of women. In this period, girls had the freedom to choose their husbands, women could participate in Sabha-Samiti, child marriage was not prevalent and the Purdah system was also not in existence

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not true for ‘Yajna’?

options.A: Yajna was an important part of Vedic religion.
options.B: Through Yajna, Vedic Aryans worshipped Surya, Prithvi, Vayu, Agni, Indra etc.
options.D: The practice of Yajna ended in the Later Vedic period.

questions.explanation: Yajna was performed even in the Rigvedic period to please the gods, but in the Later Vedic period, Yajna took an institutional base. In the Later Vedic period, large-scale Yajnas began to be performed and animal sacrifice started to be performed in large numbers in these Yajnas

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not true regarding ‘Purushartha’?

options.A: Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha are the four Purusharthas.
options.B: Their concept was made for a balance between Pravritti (enjoyment) and Nivritti (renunciation).
options.C: Purushartha shows the coordination between materialism and spirituality.
options.D: The first mention of Purusharthas is found in Kautilya's 'Arthashastra'.

questions.explanation: The first mention of Purushartha appeared in Later Vedic texts. Four Purusharthas were told - Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha. Among these Purusharthas, Moksha was given the first place. Therefore, the first mention of Purushartha is found in Later Vedic texts and not in Arthashastra

questions.question_text: In which of the following marriages was the bride married to the priest?
questions.explanation: Giving one's daughter in charity as the base of religious rituals is called Daiva marriage. Kanyadan performed to the Ritvij sitting at the altar of marriage is Daiva marriage. In this, after the consent of the groom's side, the girl is bid farewell by performing sacraments etc. according to Vedic tradition

questions.question_text: Which was the first sacrament among the ancient Indian sixteen sacraments?
questions.explanation: Garbhadhana was the first sacrament among the ancient Indian 16 sacraments. After this, respectively, Pumsavana, Simantonnayana, Jatakarma, Namakarana, Nishkramana etc. were the major sacraments

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The correct match is Rigveda - Ayurveda Samaveda - Gandharvaveda Atharvaveda - Shilpaveda Yajurveda - Dhanurveda

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not included in the principle of ‘Three Debts’?
questions.explanation: In the Later Vedic period, the system of Tri-Rina was established in which it was considered necessary for a man to be free from 3 debts. These are Rishi Rina, meaning study of Vedic texts, Pitri Rina, meaning procreation of a son, and Deva Rina, meaning performing sacrifices etc

questions.question_text: Which Vedic deity's name is not found in the Boghazkoi inscription?
questions.explanation: The Boghazkoi inscription was obtained from a place named Boghazkoi in Central Asia, dating to around 1400 BC. In this inscription, there is mention of a treaty between kings, in which kings considered Vedic era deities as witnesses. In this, the names of four deities are Indra, Mitra, Varuna, and Nasatya

questions.question_text: Which is the oldest text of Vedic literature?
questions.explanation: The oldest text of Vedic literature is the Rigveda. Its oldest manuscript was found in Sharada script. The recitation of the hymns of the Rigveda was done by 'Hotri', therefore it is also called Hotriveda. The Rigveda has wonderful similarities with the Iranian text Zend Avesta. Avesta and Rigveda are two oldest texts of the Indo-European language. The Rigveda begins with the worship of Agni. The time of the Rigvedic period is (1500 BC - 1000 BC). In the Upanishads, there was a strong reaction against sacrificial rituals and the dominance of Brahmanas; this reaction occurred especially in the Panchala and Videha kingdoms where the Upanishads were compiled around 600 BC

questions.question_text: The most powerful deity of the Rigvedic period was
questions.explanation: The main deity of the Rigvedic period was Indra, who is mentioned 250 times in the Rigveda. After him are Agni (200 times), Soma deity (144 times) and Varuna deity (30 times). From the Rigveda, priests used to invoke gods through Vedic mantras by offering to Agni in the sacrificial pit

questions.question_text: The theory of the divine origin of kingship is found for the first time in
questions.explanation: The first mention of the theory of the divine origin of kingship was made in 'Aitareya Brahmana'. 'Aitareya Brahmana' was a composition of the Later Vedic period. Instead of general titles, the king had started adopting titles like Rajadhiraja, Samrat, Ekarat

questions.question_text: What was the main food of the Vedic Aryans?

options.D: Barley, milk, dairy products, vegetables and fruits

questions.explanation: The main food of the Vedic Aryans was barley, milk, dairy products, vegetables and fruits. The cow and horse were their favorite animals

questions.question_text: 'Satyameva Jayate' inscribed in the Indian national emblem is taken from here -
questions.explanation: 'Satyameva Jayate' inscribed in the Indian national emblem is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad, which means truth alone triumphs

questions.question_text: 'Tamaso ma jyotirgamaya' or 'Lead us from darkness to light' appears in which of the following Upanishads?
questions.explanation: In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, 'Tamaso ma jyotirgamaya', meaning 'Lead us from darkness to light', is mentioned. In this same Upanishad, the Yajnavalkya and Gargi dialogue is mentioned. This is the largest Upanishad

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a ritualistic Veda?
questions.explanation: Yajurveda is a ritualistic Veda. In this, various rituals and methods related to Yajnas are mentioned. This Veda is composed in both 'prose' and 'verse'. The priest who performed the rituals of Yajurveda was called 'Adhvaryu'. There are two branches of Yajurveda - Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. Shukla Yajurveda is also called 'Vajasaneyi Samhita'. The Brahmana text of Shukla Yajurveda is 'Satapatha' and the Brahmana text of Krishna Yajurveda is 'Taittiriya'

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedic writings for the first time gives an authentic explanation of the "theory of rebirth"?
questions.explanation: The authentic explanation of the "theory of rebirth" is obtained in the Satapatha Brahmana. Satapatha Brahmana is the Brahmana text of Shukla Yajurveda (Yajurveda). It is the oldest and largest Brahmana text, divided into 100 chapters and 14 Kandas. In this, descriptions of the Yajnavalkya-Maitreyi dialogue, story of Videha Madhava, Purushamedha Yajna, Upanayana sacrament, story of the flood, agricultural process, theory of rebirth, Pururava-Urvashi legend etc. are found. The authentic explanation of the theory of rebirth for the first time is described in detail in the Chandogya Upanishad

questions.question_text: 1/4 of the hymns of the Rigveda Samhita refer to .................
questions.explanation: Indra is mentioned 250 times in the Rigveda. That is, Indra alone is mentioned in about one-fourth of the Samhita. Indra is the most prominent deity of the Rigvedic Aryans; he is depicted as Purandara i.e., the breaker of forts and leader of war, and naturally, he is considered the god of rain

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedic deities is not mentioned in the Boghazkoi inscription?
questions.explanation: The Boghazkoi inscription obtained from Asia Minor (about 1400 BC) is a major source for knowing Vedic history. In this inscription, mention of four major Vedic deities, Indra, Mitra, Varuna and Nasatya, is found. This inscription is also important epigraphic evidence for determining the chronology of Vedic history

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a branch of Samaveda?
questions.explanation: Kauthuma, Ranayaniya and Jaiminiya, Chandogya are branches of Samaveda, while Aitareya and Kaushitaki are branches of Rigveda

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: List-I List-II (a) Sangrahitri – Treasurer (b) Bhagadugha – Officer collecting royal tax (c) Palagala – Messenger (d) Vavata – A word from the Sanskrit dictionary

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak wrote the book named 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas' (Original country of the Aryans). In this, he expressed the view that the original home of the Aryans was the North Pole (Arctic) region

questions.question_text: What is the subject matter of the Upanishads?
questions.explanation: Upanishads are compositions of the Later Vedic period. Soul, God, Salvation, Search for truth, Rebirth etc. have been their subject matter. Therefore, they have also been called Paravidya or Adhyatma Vidya. The number of authentic Upanishads is considered to be 10

questions.question_text: Ancient Indian marriage in which the bride's father had a condition of giving a pair of cattle was called:
questions.explanation: Smritis, Dharmashastras, and Kautilya in Arthashastra have mentioned eight types of marriages. In exchange for giving the daughter to the groom, the daughter's father used to receive a pair of cow and bull. This is described in the Arsha marriage Daiva marriage - The daughter was married to the priest who performed the yajna ritual methodically. Prajapatya marriage - When the groom and bride married while behaving according to Dharma. Brahma marriage - This marriage was considered the best. In this, the girl's father looks for a groom who is knowledgeable in the Vedas and virtuous.

questions.question_text: Match the Samhitas of List-I with the Brahmanas of List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I	List-II A. Rigveda	1. Taittiriya Brahmana B. Yajurveda	2. Kaushitaki Brahmana C. Samaveda	3. Gopatha Brahmana D. Atharvaveda	4. Panchavimsha Brahmana Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: List-I	List-II Rigveda	Kaushitaki Brahmana Yajurveda	Taittiriya Brahmana Samaveda	Panchavimsha Brahmana Atharvaveda	Gopatha Brahmana

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to the Vedas: (1) Among them, the most ancient is the Rigveda (2) Samaveda is in Pali Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: In Indian culture, the Vedas are the root and most ancient texts of Sanatana Varnashrama Dharma. Rigveda is the most ancient Veda and all Vedas are written in the Sanskrit language

questions.question_text: Who is known by the name ‘Purandara’ in Vedic literature?
questions.explanation: In Vedic literature, ‘Indra’ has been called Purandara (conqueror of forts). Indra was the deity of bravery, power, clouds, and lightning. He was also called Vajrabahu. The word Indra is mentioned 250 times in the Rigveda. This indicates that Indra was an important deity of the Vedic period

questions.question_text: Which of the following institutions was responsible for the distribution of resources in society during the early Vedic period?
questions.explanation: Vidatha was the most ancient institution in the early Vedic period. There is a mention of the distribution of resources of society in this institution. It was also called a public assembly. A group of several villages was called Vish. Sabha was considered an institution of elderly (noble) and elite (distinguished) people, while Samiti was the central political institution (representative assembly of common people)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Vedas is not true?

options.A: Rigveda is a collection of 1028 hymns. These hymns are mostly prayers used in yajnas.
options.B: Yajurveda contains sacrificial formulas in the form of prose and mantras.
options.C: These mantras were recited by the priest. This priest performed the Agnihotra of the yajna.
options.D: In Samaveda, there are mantras taken from Yajurveda for religious rituals.
options.E: Atharvaveda mainly contains magical spells and tantra.

questions.explanation: There are a total of 10 Mandalas, 1028 Suktas, and 10,580 Rikas in the Rigveda. These Rikas are mostly prayers used in yajnas. Yajurveda is in both prose and verse; the priest who recites its mantras is called ‘Adhvaryu’. Samaveda is mainly a collection of mantras to be sung on the occasion of yajnas; it is called the father of Indian music. The one who sings its mantras is called ‘Udgatr’

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): Aryans had developed a good political and administrative structure even in the early Vedic period. Reason (R): Aryans had long and extensive experience of organized political administration. Select the correct statement from the following in context of the above two statements?

options.D: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.E: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The civilization that emerged in India after the Indus civilization is known by the name of Vedic civilization or Aryan civilization. Knowledge of Aryan civilization comes from the Vedas. The expansion of Aryans was up to Afghanistan, Punjab, and western Uttar Pradesh, but they could not develop a good political and administrative structure. The main reason for this was their lack of long and extensive experience of organized, political administration

questions.question_text: Which ancient Indian civilization is identified by the Painted Grey Ware culture?
questions.explanation: The main center of the Later Vedic period civilization was ‘Madhya Desha’, whose spread was from Saraswati to the Ganga Doab. Painted Grey Ware was the characteristic feature of this period because the inhabitants here used painted and grey-colored bowls and plates of clay. These sites were identified by the name Painted Grey Ware (P.G.W.). The civilization here is identified by the Grey Ware culture

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Dharmashastra works?

options.A: They contain references to four varnas and norms of social life
options.B: They do not contain references to various castes
options.C: They contain references to Desha-dharma and Kula-dharma
options.D: They emphasize that every person should follow the dharma of his own varna

questions.explanation: Dharmasutras, Smritis, and commentaries are kept under Dharmashastra. Gautama Dharmasutra is the most ancient. A clear description of the Varna system is found in the Sutras. Information about the concept of Varna-samkara (mixed varna) and the origin of caste or mixed caste is found for the first time in Sutra literature. Later, these concepts are seen expanding in the Smritis. For the first time in Gautama Dharmasutra, Varta was told as the varna-dharma of the Shudra

questions.question_text: In which Mandala of the Rigveda is the ‘Gayatri Mantra’ written?
questions.explanation: Mention of the Gayatri Mantra is found in the Third Mandala of the Rigveda. Its creator is Vishvamitra. This mantra is dedicated to Savitr (Sun deity)

questions.question_text: The earliest mention of the identification of Vishnu with Narayana is found in?
questions.explanation: The mention of the identification of Vishnu with Narayana is first found in the Shantiparva of the Mahabharata where he is said to be omnipresent and the creator of all. Although the first mention of ‘Narayana’ is found in the Brahmana texts. Upon the establishment of the identification of Vishnu with Narayana, the Pancharatra religion (Bhagavata religion) came into existence. Worshippers of Narayana were called Pancharatras

questions.question_text: Who among the following is the most ancient commentator on the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: An analytical analysis of the Rigveda, the most ancient and reliable text of Indian literature, has been presented by many great literati. Prominent scholar Skandasvamin was the first commentator on the Rigveda

questions.question_text: From the Nadi Stuti Sukta of the Rigveda, the location of the Vedic river Saraswati is understood to be between which two rivers?
questions.explanation: In the Nadi Stuti Sukta of the Rigveda, the location of the Vedic river Saraswati is between the Yamuna and Shutudri (Sutlej) rivers; its modern name was Ghaggar, which was counted among the prominent rivers of that time

questions.question_text: The story of the great flood, in which there is a description of Manu being protected by a divine fish, is available in which text?
questions.explanation: Yajurveda is a ritualistic Veda; it contains mentions of the ritual methods related to various yajnas. This Veda is composed in both prose and verse. There are two branches of Yajurveda - Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. Shatapatha Brahmana is the only Brahmana text of Shukla Yajurveda. It is considered the most ancient and the largest Brahmana. Shatapatha Brahmana describes the story of the flood, the principle of rebirth, the Pururava-Urvashi narrative, the Rama story, and the gift of youth to Chyavana Rishi by Ashvin Kumars. The author of Shatapatha Brahmana is Maharishi Yajnavalkya

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts is Itihasa-Purana called the Fifth Veda?
questions.explanation: In Itihasa-Purana, besides Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda, Chandogya Upanishad has been considered the fifth Veda. This is an Upanishad of the Samaveda. Chandogya Upanishad is considered the most ancient Upanishad. The first mention of Devaki's son Krishna is in this. It describes the first three ashramas and the famous dialogue between Uddalaka Aruni and his son Shvetaketu regarding the identity of Brahman and Atman

questions.question_text: In which Upanishad is the philosophical dialogue between Yajnavalkya and Maitreyi described?
questions.explanation: The main Upanishads of Yajurveda are Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, Kathopanishad, Ishopanishad, and Shvetashvatara Upanishad. The philosophical dialogue of Yajnavalkya-Gargi/Maitreyi is described in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. Whereas Kaushitaki is an Upanishad of the Rigveda and Chandogya Upanishad is the main Upanishad of the Samaveda. Chandogya Upanishad is considered the most ancient Upanishad. The first mention of Devaki's son Krishna is in this

questions.question_text: In which text is ‘Avataravada’ discussed?
questions.explanation: The mention of the discussion of ‘Avataravada’ is first found in the ‘Bhagavad Gita’. Narayana, Narasimha, and Vamana are considered divine incarnations and the remaining seven are considered human incarnations. Worshipping four Vrishni heroes including Vasudeva Krishna was conceived as Chaturvyuha. The first use of Chaturvyuha worship is found in the Vishnu Samhita

questions.question_text: Which one of the following texts mentions the list of Ratnins (court officials) of the Vedic period?
questions.explanation: Some high officials of the state are mentioned in the Samhitas and Brahmana texts of the Yajurveda, who were called ‘Ratnin’. Mention of 12 types of Ratnins is made in the Shatapatha Brahmana

questions.question_text: In which of the following Vedas are the formulas related to oblation (sacrifice) contained?
questions.explanation: According to the Yajurveda, the Adhvaryu performed the methods of sacrificial rituals in a proper manner. In the Yajurveda, oblation (sacrifice) was given while performing sacrificial rituals. In the Rigveda, deities were invoked by Vedic mantras. In the Samaveda, priests of the Udgatr class sang the Saman. Atharvaveda supervised the entire sacrificial process. Secondary Education Service Selection Board has considered its answer (a) Rigveda

questions.question_text: What was ‘Nishka’ in the Vedic period?
questions.explanation: In the Vedic period, the words Hiranya and Suvarna were used for gold. Nishka was an ornament of gold. In the Rigveda, Sharda, Vrata, and Gana were military units. Pathikrit was used for the deity Agni. Child marriage did not take place in the Rigveda

questions.question_text: In which of the following Upanishads was one of the kings of the Kaikeya Janapada a philosopher?
questions.explanation: The king who ruled over a tribe in the Rigvedic period now began to rule over that territory. In the Upanishad period, there were many such kings who were associated with Brahma-jnana and spiritual contemplation. Among them, the prominent ones were Ashvapati of Kaikeya, Janaka of Videha, Ajatashatru of Kashi, and Pravahana Jaivali of Panchala. In the later Vedic period, Panchala was the most developed state. In Shatapatha Brahmana, they have been called the best representatives of Vedic civilization

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedas is partly written in prose?
questions.explanation: Yajurveda is written partly in prose and partly in verse. There are two parts of Yajurveda – Krishna Yajurveda and Shukla Yajurveda. The Brahmana of Shukla Yajurveda is ‘Shatapatha Brahmana’. Krishna Yajurveda is written in prose

questions.question_text: In which text does the word ‘Punarbhu’, used for a remarried woman, first appear?
questions.explanation: Rigvedic society was a male-dominated society. Still, the condition of women in society was fine. It is mentioned in the Rigveda that if the husband died suddenly, the wife could remarry. This woman was called Punarbhu. No evidence of the Sati practice is found in the Rigveda. The Niyoga practice was used on a large scale in the Rigveda. Niyoga children were those born from another man. The commission has considered its answer (b) Atharvaveda. Whereas the mention of Punarbhu (remarried woman) is found in the Rigveda

questions.question_text: Which of the following Janas are mentioned in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: Puru, Yadu, Chedi, Matsya. The word Yaduvamsha or Yaduvamshi Kshatriya is used for that community of India who used to call themselves descendants of the ancient king Yadu. This is one of the five Indian Aryan tribes (Panchajana, Panchakshatriya, or Panchamanusha) described in the Rigveda. While the Puru lineage was also seen and read in the ancient Rigveda itself. King Yayati had two sons Yadu and Turvasha from Devayani, and three sons Druhyu, Anu, and Puru from Sharmishtha. The names of five Janas found in the Rigveda are Anu, Druhyu, Yadu, Puru, and Turvasha

questions.question_text: In the Vedic age, the important official after the king was:
questions.explanation: The Vedic period is a time period of ancient Indian culture, during that period the Vedas were composed. After the decline of the Harappan culture, a new civilization emerged in India. Based on the sources of information of this civilization, it was given the name Vedic civilization. Among the state officials, the Purohita and Senani were prominent. The Purohita and Senani, along with 12 Ratnins, provided administrative support to the king. The Purohita was the chief advisor to the king

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (King of the Upanishad period) - (State)
questions.explanation: In the Later Vedic period, a royal family named Brahmadatta took control over Kashi. In that family, there were great learned rulers. In their family was King Ajatashatru, who was incomparable in the knowledge of Atman and Paramatman. In the Kaikeya royal family in Punjab was King Ashvapati; the Panchala ruler located in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab was King Pravahana Jaivali, and the ruler of the Videhas in Janakpur Mithila was Janaka, in whose court learned sages like Yajnavalkya and learned women like Gargi used to debate on the scriptures

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code provided: List-I (Vedic Rivers)	List-II (Modern Names)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The correct match is as follows– Kubha – Kabul Parushni – Ravi Sadaneera – Gandak Shutudri – Sutlej

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements– Assertion (A) : The territory lying between the Indus and the Hindukush can be called a part of India from a cultural point of view in almost the entire Hindu period. Reason (R) : From the mention of Kubha, Krumu, and Gomati rivers in the Rigveda, there remains no doubt that the Indo-Aryans had a deep connection with Afghanistan.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– It is estimated that the expansion of the Aryans was from Afghanistan to the Ganga Valley. In the Rigveda, names of many rivers and mountains are found here and there. A peak of the Himalayas has been called ‘Mujavant’ which was famous for Soma. From the mention of Kubha (Kabul), Krumu (Kurram), Gomati, and Suvastu rivers in the west, it is known that Afghanistan was also a part of India at that time.

questions.question_text: Who has been invoked the most number of times as the most useful and also the most fearsome deity of the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Indra has been invoked the most number of times as the most useful and also the most fearsome deity of the Rigveda. Indra has been called the lord of the universe. He is primarily the deity of war. The Aryans believed that it was he who gave them victory over the Asuras. The main epithet of Indra was Purandara. He used to cause rain by blocking the clouds. He is mentioned in 250 Suktas of the Rigveda. Compared to any other deity, the description of Indra's physical characteristics was done in the greatest detail.

questions.question_text: Match the subjects of List-I with List-II: List-I (King)	List-II (State)
questions.explanation: – The correct matching is as follows List-I (King)	List-II (State) Ashvapati – Kaikeya Parikshit – Kuru Nicakshu – Vatsabhumi Pradyota Mahasena – Avanti

questions.question_text: At which of the following sites was the evidence of Painted Grey Ware (PGW) first found?
questions.explanation: The discovery of Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture was first made at Ahichchhatra (Bareilly), but its importance increased significantly after its discovery at Hastinapur by B.B. Lal. Painted Grey Ware (PGW) has been found at various sites in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Kashmir.

questions.question_text: What does 'Panchajan' denote in Rigveda?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2011) Explanation–In Rigveda, 'Panchajan' is indicative of the five tribes of Aryans. According to the Vedic text, there were five clans or 'Janas' of the Aryans. These five clans were Anu, Druhyu, Puru, Turvasa, and Yadu. The chief of these clans was called Janapati or Raja.

questions.question_text: How many factors for promoting agriculture are mentioned in Rigveda?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2011) Explanation–Mainly 05 factors for promoting agriculture are mentioned in Rigveda. It is noteworthy that agriculture is mentioned in a total of 24 verses of the Rigveda. The mention of irrigation is found in the later verses.

questions.question_text: King Sudas, regarding whom it is described in the Rigveda that he defeated ten kings, belonged to which 'Jana'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2012) Explanation–King Sudas was associated with the Tritsu tribe of the Bharata dynasty. Later, a war took place between King Sudas and 10 other kings, in which the chiefs of 5 Aryan and 5 non-Aryan tribes were included. King Sudas was victorious in this war. Among the defeated tribes, the most prominent were the Purus.

questions.question_text: In which of the following is the narrative of Videha Madhava traveling towards the east with his priest Gautama Rahugana mentioned?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The narrative of Videha Madhava traveling towards the east with his priest Gautama Rahugana is mentioned in the Shatapatha Brahmana. It is noteworthy that Shatapatha Brahmana, an important part of Vedic literature, is written in prose.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The correct match is – List-I List-II (a) Rigveda (I) Shakala (b) Yajurveda (II) Kanva (c) Samaveda (III) Ranayaniya (d) Atharvaveda (IV) Pippalada, Shaunaka

questions.question_text: The famous philosopher king of the Panchala kingdom during the later Vedic period was:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation–In the later Vedic Panchala kingdom, there were many philosophers like Pravahana Jaibali and Aruni etc. Among these, Pravahana Jaibali was a famous philosopher king. It is noteworthy that the period of the later Vedic age was 1000-600 BC. In the later Vedic period, there were many kings like Janaka of Videha, Ashvapati of Kaikeya, and Ajatashatru of Kashi who were associated with divine knowledge and spiritual contemplation.

questions.question_text: Under whose leadership was the war of ten kings, mentioned in the Rigveda, fought against Sudas?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation–Vishvamitra was a ruler of ancient India who was also known by the name 'Kaushika'. He was the great-grandson of a great king Kusha. According to the Rigveda, the war of ten kings against Sudas was fought under the leadership of Vishvamitra only.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct in the context of the Rigvedic Sabha and Samiti?

options.A: Sabha represented the common class while Samiti represented the elite class.
options.B: Sabha represented the elite class, while Samiti represented the common class.
options.C: The number of members in Sabha and Samiti was in equal proportion.
options.D: The number of members in Samiti was more than the number of members in Sabha.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation–The Rigvedic Samiti was mainly an institution related to political functions. It represented the common people. The chairman of the Samiti was called Ishan. The Sabha was an institution of wealthy or superior people (elite people). In the Atharvaveda, Sabha and Samiti have been called the 'two daughters of Prajapati'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following priests supervised the performance of the Yajna?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation- In the Vedic age, the worship of deities was done through Yajnas. The responsibility of completing these Yajnas was of the Brahmin priests. These Brahmin priests were of four types- (1) Hota or Hotri – He was the knower of the Rigveda. He used to establish the fire in the Yajna altar and invoke the deities through mantras. (2) Udgata – He was the knower of the Samaveda. He used to sing the Sama (hymns) during the Yajna. (3) Adhvaryu or Yajnika – He was the knower of the Yajurveda who used to perform the procedures of the sacrificial rituals. (4) Brahma – His role during the Yajna was that of a supervisor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rivers mentioned in the Rigveda indicates the relationship of the Aryans with Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-III Paper June, 2015) Explanation–In the Rigveda, four rivers of Afghanistan – Kubha (Kabul), Krumu, Gomal, and Suvastu are mentioned. Thus, the mention of the Sapta-Sindhava region is found in the Rigveda. It is clear from this that the Aryans first settled in the Punjab and Afghanistan regions.

questions.question_text: Who was the learned woman during the time of the Upanishads who could debate on higher knowledge in the assembly of philosophers?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-III Paper June, 2015) Explanation–The Yajnavalkya-Gargi dialogue mentioned in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, while on one hand shows that some women in society could receive the highest education, it also gives indications that perhaps there were limits to it. Once during a debate, Yajnavalkya told Gargi not to argue too much, otherwise her head would be broken.

questions.question_text: The oldest epigraphic evidence of Indo-European language is found from:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2015) Explanation–The oldest specimen of Indo-European language is found in an inscription from around 2200 BC found in Iraq. The mention of Aryan names is found in the Kassite inscriptions from around 1600 BC found in Iraq and the Mittani inscriptions in Syria, which informs about the presence of Aryan language speakers in Western Asia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following priests compiled the Gayatri Mantra?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2015) Explanation– The mention of the Gayatri Mantra is found in the third Mandala of the Rigveda. The priest Vishvamitra compiled the Gayatri Mantra. When the sun starts shining, it is called Savitr. The famous Gayatri Mantra of the Rigveda is dedicated to Savitr only.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedangas is associated with poetic composition?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2015) Explanation–Vedangas were composed to understand the Vedas correctly. Their total number is six: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda, and Jyotisha. Chhanda is in verse. It is also called 'Chatuspadi Vritta'. The book 'Chhandashastra' composed by Pingala is its oldest text.

questions.question_text: Where in India has the oldest evidence of Bhojpatra (a widely used writing material of India) been found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation─A place named Singraur, located 22 miles northwest of Allahabad, was known as Shringverpur in ancient times. The oldest evidence of India's widely used writing material, Bhojpatra, is found from here.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the Samhita of Shukla Yajurveda?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation─Yajurveda is a prose text. In this, emphasis has been laid on the methods of Yajna. It has two parts─Krishna Yajurveda and Shukla Yajurveda. Kathaka Samhita (Katha Samhita), Maitrayani Samhita, and Taittiriya Samhita belong to Krishna Yajurveda, while Vajasaneyi Samhita is related to Shukla Yajurveda.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedic Yajnas had a direct relationship with kingship?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Yajnas named Rajasuya, Ashvamedha, and Vajapeya had a direct relationship with kingship. Vajapeya is a type of Shrauta Yajna. According to the Shatapatha Brahmana, this Yajna is performed only by Brahmins or Kshatriyas. Chariot racing is an essential part of this Yajna. Ashvamedha was mainly a political Yajna and could only be performed by that emperor whose suzerainty was accepted by all other rulers, while in the Rajasuya Yajna, a certain part of the earth was conquered and taxes were collected from the kings there to perform the Yajna.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not included in 'Prasthanatrayi' –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Bhagavata is not mentioned under Prasthanatrayi, rather Bhagavad Gita, Upanishad, and Brahmasutra are mentioned.

questions.question_text: Which part of Indian geography were the Aryans not aware of in the later Vedic period?

options.B: Various mountain peaks of the Himalayas
options.C: South India up to the Krishna River Valley

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- In the later Vedic period, the Aryans were not aware of South India up to the Krishna River Valley. The expansion of Aryan civilization had not yet been able to reach south of the Vindhya Mountains. We do not find the mention of southern kingdoms in any Vedic text.

questions.question_text: Which of the following texts were not parts of the Vedas or Shrutis?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Puranic texts were not parts of the Vedas or Shrutis. Vedic literature is divided into four parts for convenience - (1) Samhitas of the Vedas (2) Brahmana texts (3) Aranyaka texts (4) Upanishads. In addition to these, the best chronological description of Indian historical stories is found in the Puranas. The composers of the Puranas are considered to be Lomaharsha or his son Ugrashrava. Their number is 18.

questions.question_text: "War begins in the minds of men", in which text is it mentioned?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- "War begins in the minds of men" is written in the Atharvaveda. Descriptions of subjects like tantra-mantra, magic, curses, and subjugation etc., are found in the Atharvaveda.

questions.question_text: At what order is the Upanayana ceremony in the sixteen Sanskaras?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─ Under the Hindu concept, 16 Sanskaras were prescribed. These Sanskaras are as follows─ (i) Garbhadhana (ii) Pumsavana (iii) Simantonnayana (iv) Jatakarma (v) Namakarana (vi) Nishkramana (vii) Annaprashana (viii) Chudakarana (ix) Karnavedha (x) Vidyarambha (xi) Upanayana (xii) Vedarambha (xiii) Keshanta (xiv) Samavartana (xv) Vivaha and (xvi) Antyeshti.

questions.question_text: Boghazkoy inscription has been found in:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Among the archaeological sources in India, the most important source is inscriptions. Inscriptions of ancient India are obtained from stone rocks. The most ancient inscriptions have been found from a place named Boghazkoy in Central Asia (Turkey) in 1400 BC. In this inscription, names of Vedic deities like Indra, Mitra, Varuna, and Nasatya etc., are found.

questions.question_text: The poetic part of the Vedas is called –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – The poetic part of the Vedas is known by the name Samhita. A vast storehouse of knowledge regarding Indian culture is contained in the Vedas. Their number is four which are respectively Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda. In Samaveda, sung verses (hymns) are included; these were sung for the invocation of deities at the time of Yajnas. Atharvaveda is related to magic-spells, tantra-mantra. Rigveda is related to the praise of deities. Yajurveda is related to Yajna.

questions.question_text: What was the most ancient institution of the Vedic age?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – The power of the king was limited by the opinions of the people. Various institutions used to act as checks on his administration, the assembly of the people – which was called the Janasabha in which the proceedings of the 'Jana' took place. The institution of the Vedic Aryans in very ancient times is known to us by the name 'Vidatha', it has been called a popular assembly.

questions.question_text: What is the foundation stone of Indian culture?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Rigveda is called the foundation stone of Indian culture because a detailed description of the ancient social, economic, religious, and political condition of India is found in it, while Ganga has been considered a holy river.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a Vedic deity?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – In the specified options, option (b) Krishna is not mentioned in the Vedic texts. The discussion of Krishna first appeared in the Chandogya Upanishad. Vishnu, Indra, and Brahma etc. are Vedic deities. In this, Krishna has been described as a disciple of Ghora Angirasa.

questions.question_text: The subject matter of the Upanishads is –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 PGT History, 2003 Explanation – The subject matter of the Upanishads is philosophy. That is, to satisfy the curiosity for the philosophy of knowledge by sitting near the Guru. They were composed in the later Vedic period. Their theme is related to Brahma-vidya (divine knowledge) and Atma-vidya (self-knowledge).

questions.question_text: In which Mandala of the Rigveda is the word 'Shudra' mentioned?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The first mention of the Varna system is found in the Purusha Sukta of the tenth Mandala of the Rigveda. According to which the origin of Brahmin from the mouth, Rajanya from the arms, Vaishya from the thighs, and Shudra from the feet of the cosmic being (Virat Purusha) has been clarified. The mention of the word Shudra in the question first occurred in the Purusha Sukta itself.

questions.question_text: In which text is the first mention of the origin of the king found?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The first mention regarding the origin of the king is found in the Aitareya Brahmana. In which it is stated that now the king used to assume titles like Rajadhiraja, Samrat, Ekarat instead of general titles.

questions.question_text: What was the main crop of the later Vedic period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The main crops of the later Vedic period were wheat and rice. The people of the Rigvedic period produced barley (Yava). Rice was called Brihi, barley as Yava, and wheat as Godhuma. The mention of activities related to agriculture is found in the Shatapatha Brahmana.

questions.question_text: In which region was the Rigveda Samhita composed-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation–The Rigveda Samhita was composed in the Sapta-Sindhava region. It is noteworthy that the entire region where the Aryan people first settled in India was known by the name 'Sapta-Sindhu'. The mention of the following seven rivers of the Sapta-Sindhava region is found in the Rigveda - Sindhu, Saraswati, Shatudri or Sutlej, Vipasa or Beas, Parushni or Ravi, Vitasta or Jhelum, and Asikni (Chenab). In addition to these, some other rivers are also mentioned.

questions.question_text: Which Veda Samhita is the Chandogya Upanishad associated with-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation–Chandogya Upanishad and Kenopanishad are associated with the Samaveda Samhita. Prashnopanishad, Mundakopanishad, Mandukyopanishad are associated with the Atharvaveda Samhita, and Aitareyopanishad is associated with the Rigveda Samhita.

questions.question_text: What was the language of the Rigvedic Aryans?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The language of the Rigvedic Aryans was Sanskrit.

questions.question_text: The Vedic word 'Rita' means –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In the Rigveda, the word 'Dharma' has been used in the sense of 'Laws'. It is not related to morality. Apart from Dharma, another word 'Rita' is found. All deities are considered to be related to 'Rita' (the moral and physical order of the universe). 'Rita' means – truth and an imperishable existence.

questions.question_text: The literal meaning of the word 'Arya' is –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Arya is a word of the Sanskrit language. The literal meaning of the word Arya is noble, superior, aristocratic, high-born. The mention of the word Arya is found in the mantras of the Rigveda.
