questions.question_text: In which Mandala of the Rigveda is the concept of Chaturvarnya (four-fold varna system) found?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – The first mention of the Chaturvarnya system is found in the Purusha Sukta of the tenth Mandala of the Rigveda. In which the origin of Brahmin from the mouth, Rajanya from the arms, Vaishya from the thighs, and Shudra from the feet of the cosmic being (Virat Purusha) has been described. The mention of the deity 'Soma' is in the 'Ninth Mandala'. The mention of the popular Gayatri Mantra (Savitri) is also in the third Mandala of the Rigveda. It is noteworthy that the second to seventh Mandalas of the Rigveda are ancient and the rest are considered interpolated, i.e., fake (added later).

questions.question_text: The number of deities during the Vedic period was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – 33 categories (Kotis) of Rigvedic deities have been described in Yaska's Nirukta-Shastra. Their division was done in the form of deities of the atmosphere, celestial (sky), and earth.

questions.question_text: 'The ruler of the earth up to the ocean is called Ekarat' –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─ In the later Vedic period, the king assumed titles like Rajadhiraja, Samrat, Ekarat, etc. It is said in the Aitareya Brahmana that "the ruler of the earth up to the ocean is Ekarat." In the Atharvaveda, Ekarat was the title given to the supreme ruler. The theory of the origin of the king is first found in the Aitareya Brahmana.

questions.question_text: To which deity is the ninth mandala of the Rigveda dedicated?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—The ninth mandala of the Rigveda is dedicated to the deity Soma. In addition to this, there are supreme hymns in other mandalas as well whose deity is Soma. Soma was a plant whose juice was considered by the Vedic Aryans to provide strength and agility.

questions.question_text: The 'Third Mandala' of the Rigveda was composed by:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation—The Rigveda is the oldest among the Vedas. It contains 1028 hymns which are divided into 10 mandalas. Its third mandala was composed by Vishvamitra. Vishvamitra is considered the first religious guru. The mention of the Gayatri Mantra is found in this very mandala, which is addressed to 'Savitar Deva'. This is a form of the Sun and the morning goddess.

questions.question_text: Where is the first mention of Ayodhya found?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation—In Rigvedic period literature, three cities are mainly mentioned, in which the description of Ayodhya has appeared in the Atharvaveda. In this same text, a person named Takshaka is mentioned as a resident of Vaishali and Bimbisara is mentioned as the king of Kashi.

questions.question_text: A detailed description is given in the 'Satapatha Brahmana' of:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—Satapatha Brahmana is a Brahmana of the Shukla Yajurveda branch of the Yajurveda, in which a detailed description of religious rituals is given. This is a Brahmana text. In this, the structure of creation and the dissolution (Pralaya) are described.

questions.question_text: What was the Ashvattha tree called in the Rigvedic period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—In the Rigvedic period, the Ashvattha tree was the name given to the Pipal tree. It was a sacred tree. In the later period, in a verse of the Gita, Lord Krishna, while preaching to Arjuna, said, "O Arjuna! Among trees, I am the sacred Ashvattha (Pipal)," which is proof of its sanctity during the Vedic period.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statement (A) and reason (R) and select the correct answer from the code given below: Statement (A): There was a rural civilization in the Rigveda. Reason (R): Agriculture and animal husbandry were primarily practiced in the Rigveda. Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—The Rigvedic culture was a culture based on a rural economy and the basic foundation of their life was agriculture and animal husbandry. Cultivable land was called Urvara or Kshetra. A plough in the form of Sira or Langala was used for tilling the land. The ploughshare was called Sita and mention of tilled land is found.

questions.question_text: In which of the following institutions is the participation of women mentioned?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—Women held an important position in the Rigvedic period. For the administration of governance, mentions of Sabha, Samiti, and Vidatha are found. Vidatha was the most important assembly of the Rigvedic period. It is mentioned 122 times in the Rigveda. There is a mention of women participating along with men in the Vidatha. In the Satapatha Brahmana, woman has been called 'Ardhangini'. In the later Vedic period, women were stopped from participating in the Sabha and Vidatha.

questions.question_text: Which thinker of the later Vedic period rejected the glory of the Vedas?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—According to Hindu beliefs and the mythological epic Mahabharata, 'Kautsa' was a noted sage of ancient times who was the husband of Bhagiratha's daughter Kalama. Kautsa had rejected the glory of the Vedas.

questions.question_text: Which Vedic deities are described in the Rigveda as residing in a building with a thousand pillars?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—In the Rigveda, the deities Mitra and Varuna are described as residing in a building with a thousand pillars. Varuna is called 'Ritasya Gopa' (protector of the cosmic order) and was considered the coordinator of natural events.

questions.question_text: Where did the Aryans first make their residence after arriving in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—After arriving in India, the Aryans first made their residence in the Sapta-Sindhu region.

questions.question_text: What was the person who invoked the deities with the mantras of the Yajurveda called?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—Yajurveda - The 'Adhvaryu' (Yajnika) used to perform the rituals of the sacrificial ceremonies in a proper manner. The priest of the Rigveda was the Hota, the priest of the Samaveda was the Udgata, and the priest of the Atharvaveda was the Brahma.

questions.question_text: In which Veda is the description of medicines found?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—Atharvaveda contains descriptions of mantras related to disease prevention medicines, tantra-mantra, magic-spells, curses, subjugation (Vashikaran), blessings, royal duties, and the glory of the motherland.

questions.question_text: Which of the following practices was not prevalent in the Rigvedic period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation—The practice of child marriage was not prevalent in the Rigvedic period. Inter-caste marriages also used to take place.

questions.question_text: Which of the following texts is the oldest evidence of Indian mathematics?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—The text named Sulvasutra is the oldest evidence of Indian mathematics. The meaning of this word is the measuring cord with which the sacrificial altars are measured and their location is selected.

questions.question_text: Satapatha Brahmana is related to which Veda?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—Satapatha Brahmana is related to the Yajurveda. In the text named Satapatha Brahmana, mentions of kings like Gandhara, Koshala, Panchala, Videha, Kuru, Kekaya, Shalya, etc., are found.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Rigveda 1. Hota B. Yajurveda 2. Adhvaryu C. Samaveda 3. Udgata D. Atharvaveda 4. Brahma Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—The correctly matched sequence is as follows: (a) Rigveda — 1. Hota (b) Yajurveda — 2. Adhvaryu (c) Samaveda — 3. Udgata (d) Atharvaveda — 4. Brahma

questions.question_text: Koushitaki Brahmana is the Brahmana text of which of the following Samhitas?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation—All Vedas have different Brahmana texts, such as Aitareya and Koushitaki for Rigveda, Taittiriya and Satapatha Brahmana for Yajurveda, Panchavimsha and Tandya Brahmana for Samaveda, and Gopatha Brahmana for Atharvaveda.

questions.question_text: Meru cosmology is associated with:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—Meru cosmology is related to the Mahayana branch of Buddhism. In this, an attempt has been made to bind the entire world into one thread by considering the principles of Buddha and Bodhisattva as the central point. Traditionally, one who is inspired by great compassion, generated by Bodhicitta, and attains Buddhahood through spontaneous desire for the benefit of all sensitive beings is considered a Bodhisattva.

questions.question_text: How many times is the horse mentioned in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—In the early life of the Rigvedic Aryans, animal husbandry was of more importance than agriculture. Among animals, the cow had the highest importance. In the Rigveda, the terms 'Go' (cow) and 'Vrishabha' (bull) are used 176 and 170 times respectively. The horse (Ashva) was the second important animal domesticated by the early Aryans. The horse is praised in two detailed hymns of the Rigveda. It seems that in the Rigvedic pastoral society, the dominance of the tribal chiefs was maintained on horseback. In the Rigveda, the horse and its synonyms have been used 215 times.

questions.question_text: The Vedas are called
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—The Vedas are called sound pronunciation. In the Indian tradition, the Vedas are said to be 'Apaurusheya' (not created by man). They are also called 'Shruti'.

questions.question_text: In which text is the word 'Hiranyakara' first found?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—The Yajurveda has two parts: Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. Shukla Yajurveda is known by the name Vajasaneyi Samhita, and the word 'Hiranyakara' (goldsmith) is found in it.

questions.question_text: What was the number of Ratnins in the later Vedic period?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—Mention of Ratnins is found in the later Vedic period; in the Samhitas of the Yajurveda and the Brahmana texts, some high officials of the state are mentioned who were called 'Ratnin'. These were members of the state council; their number was 11 to 12 and they were assistants to the state.

questions.question_text: With which grain were the Rigvedic Aryans familiar?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—Aryans ate both vegetarian and non-vegetarian food. In food, they ate milk, curd, kheer, and cheese. Besides this, they made a food item called 'Karambha' by mixing barley flour in curd.

questions.question_text: Who was the priest of the Bharatas in the Battle of Ten Kings?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—In the tenth mandala of the Rigveda, the Battle of Ten Kings is described, which was led by Vishvamitra, while the king of the Bharatas was Sudas, whose priest was Vashistha. This war took place over the position of the priest; there were Aryans and non-Aryans on both sides.

questions.question_text: In which mandala of the Rigveda is the Shudra mentioned?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—There are a total of 10 mandalas in the Rigveda, each mandala composed by different sages. The tenth and the first mandala were composed last; the fourth varna, i.e., Shudra, is mentioned in the tenth mandala itself.

questions.question_text: Who was considered the water-deity in the Vedic period?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—In the Vedic period, deities were worshiped for material happiness. Indra was worshiped first, and among the important deities, Indra was considered the god of rain, while Varuna was considered the god of the water-mass. He was called 'Ritasya Gopa'.

questions.question_text: In ancient India, a widow who remarried was called:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—In ancient India, a widow who remarried was called Punarbhu.

questions.question_text: The Vedas are called:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—In the Rigvedic period, the Rigveda was composed by the Aryans, and in the later Vedic period, the Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda were composed. These Vedas were also called Shruti.

questions.question_text: With which Veda is 'Valakhilya' associated?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—Rigveda is the oldest Veda; it has ten mandalas and 1028 hymns. 'Valakhilya' is associated with the Rigveda. The Rigveda was composed by the Aryans in the Vedic period (1500 BC to 1000 BC). At this time, the medium of education was oral. The Vedas were memorized. There are 11 hymns in it. It is mentioned in the 8th mandala of the Rigveda.

questions.question_text: There was no regular land tax in the Rigvedic period, because:

options.A: People were not settled permanently in one place
options.B: The government was unaware in this regard
options.C: The king was not considered the owner of the land
options.D: People were not accustomed to paying land tax

questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—In the Rigvedic period, there was no regular land tax because people were not settled permanently in one place. Thus, the early life of the Rigvedic Aryans was unstable, and animal husbandry was of more importance in their life than agriculture. In the Rigvedic period, land was not private property; rather, there was collective right over it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a part of Vedanga?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—The total number of Vedangas is 6: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda, Jyotisha. Agama is not a part of Vedanga. These Vedangas have been compared in various ways. 'Varttika' was composed by Katyayana; it is a book of grammar.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not included in Vedic literature?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation—Vedic literature includes the four Vedas, which are called Samhitas, as well as the Brahmana texts, Aranyakas, and Upanishads. After this, the Smritis were composed; Manusmriti is considered the oldest and most authentic. Other Smritis include Yajnavalkya, Narada, Katyayana, Devala, etc.

questions.question_text: 'Purusha Sukta' is a part of—
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation—Mention of Purusha Sukta is found in the tenth mandala of the Rigveda. The word 'Shudra' is first mentioned in the Purusha Sukta itself. In this, the origin of the four varnas is described as being from different parts of a 'Virata Purusha' (Universal Man).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: According to David Frawley, the Rigveda was composed in 1200 BC.
options.B: The Dasharajna war took place on the banks of the Saraswati river.
options.C: The Ashvamedha Yajna is described in the Satapatha Brahmana.
options.D: The Rathakara was considered low despite being from the Brahmana varna.

questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation—There is only one Brahmana text of the Shukla Yajurveda, the Satapatha Brahmana. It is considered the oldest and largest Brahmana. Its author is Maharishi Yajnavalkya. The Satapatha Brahmana contains the story of the flood (Jala Plavana), the theory of rebirth, the Pururava-Urvashi narrative, and the description of the Ashvamedha Yajna.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched regarding the original home of the Aryans?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation—Based on certain archaeological and linguistic materials, Meyer, Peake, and Gordon Childe have accepted Southern Russia as the original residence of the Aryans. Remains of a culture similar to that which existed during the time of the Aryans have been found from excavations in Southern Russia. Remains of the horse, which was the favorite animal of the Aryans, have also been found from excavations here.

questions.question_text: In which mandala of the Rigveda is the Purusha Sukta given?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation—The Purusha Sukta is in the tenth mandala of the Rigveda. In this, the mention of Shudra along with Brahmana, Kshatriya, and Vaishya is found for the first time. It is considered the oldest mention of the Chaturvarna system. According to this, Brahmanas originated from the mouth, Kshatriyas from the arms, Vaishyas from the thighs, and Shudras from the feet of the Adi Purusha.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a Soma Yajna?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation—The Agnishtoma Yajna is considered a Soma Yajna. In this sacrifice, offerings were made to Agni, and Soma was drunk in the afternoon and evening. Soma and Sura were the main drinks of the Aryans. Soma was famous for its intoxicating quality, which was obtained from the Munjavant mountain. There was a practice of obtaining Soma juice on the occasion of sacrifices and offering it to the deities to drink. Drinking it filled the body with enthusiasm and a charming intoxication spread in the mind. Many hymns are found in praise of Soma in the ninth mandala of the Rigveda. At one place, Kanva Rishi claims that after drinking Soma juice, they have attained immortality and have known the gods. Mentions of the ill effects of Sura have occurred in the Rigveda and it is said that people become arrogant after drinking it and start fighting in the Sabha and Samitis.

questions.question_text: In which Yajna was there a provision for the use of 25 Yupas (sacrificial posts)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation—There was a provision for the use of 25 Yupas in Purushamedha, while there was a provision for 21 in Vajapeya and 16 Yupas in Ashvamedha Yajna. From a detailed study of the important sacrifices of this era like Ashvamedha, Vajapeya, Rajasuya, etc., it is known that basically their objective was to increase agricultural production. Vajapeya was indeed related to food and drink, as were Ashvamedha and Rajasuya, which are considered indicators of so-called political power. There were many such rituals and symbols. There are important mentions in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad and Vajasaneyi Samhita regarding such actions in the Vajapeya Yajna.

questions.question_text: For which of the following deities in the Rigveda is it described that goats pulled his chariot?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation—Just as the social and economic life of the Rigvedic Aryans was simple, the religious life was equally complex. Here we find the vision of 'polytheism' in the beginning. The chief deities of the Aryans are representatives of natural forces who have been personified. The Rigvedic deities are classified into three parts—(a) Deities of the Earth—Earth, Agni, Soma, Brihaspati, and deities of rivers, etc. (b) Deities of the Atmosphere—Indra, Rudra, Vayu, Vata, Parjanya, Apah, Matarishvan, Aditi, etc. (c) Deities of the Sky—Dyaus, Varuna, Mitra, Surya, Savitar, Pushan, Vishnu, Aditya, Usha, Ashvin, etc. Rigvedic deities are predominantly male deities. Sometimes the visualization of deities is also found in animal form. For example—Indra or Dyaus is visualized as a bull and Surya as a horse, but to understand from this that the Rigvedic Aryans also worshiped animals would not be correct. The belief of considering an animal as an ancestor and regarding it as sacred and a deity is also not found in the Rigveda, but in the Rigveda, hymns are said for the deity named Pushan. Pushan was the deity of paths, shepherds, and animals, and goats pulled his chariot.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct regarding Rigvedic women?

options.A: They participated in the proceedings of the assembly (Sabha)
options.C: They took an active part in wars
options.D: They were married before reaching puberty

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation—The condition of women in society was good. Child marriages did not take place. Polygamy and widow marriage were prevalent. 10 wives of Manu have been mentioned in the Maitrayani Samhita. Sufficient education was given to women. They could participate in festivals and religious ceremonies. The Aitareya Brahmana generally describes a daughter as a cause of anxiety. The Atharvaveda also condemns the birth of daughters. In the Maitrayani Samhita, a woman is placed in the category of dice and wine. The rest of the life of society—such as food, entertainment, clothing-ornaments, etc.—was similar to the Rigvedic period.

questions.question_text: According to the Aitareya Brahmana, rulers of which region assumed the title of 'Samrat'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - Prachya is in the East. According to the Aitareya Brahmana, the kings of the Eastern direction (Magadha, Kalinga, and Bengal, etc.) are consecrated for an empire and are called 'Samrat'. In the Southern direction, the state of the Satvatas (Yadavas) is 'Bhojya' and their rulers are called 'Bhoja'. In the Western direction (Saurashtra, Kutch, Sauvira, etc.), the government is 'Svarajya' and their rulers are called 'Svarastra'. In the Northern direction in the Himalayan region (Uttarkuru, Uttarmadra, etc.), there is a 'Vairajya' system and the rulers there are called 'Virat'. Rulers of states in the Middle Country (Madhya Desha), Kuru, Panchala, Koshala, etc., are called 'Raja'. Thus, in the Aitareya Brahmana, there is mention of five types of systems: Rajya, Bhojya, Svarajya, Vairajya, and Rajya. Samrats were those rulers who, being hereditary, were eager to eradicate other states for the expansion of their power. Magadha Samrats like Jarasandha, etc., were of this type.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List-I (Ancient names of rivers) List-II (Modern names) B. Parushni - 2. Beas C. Shatudri - 3. Sutlej D. Vipasha - 4. Jhelum 5. Ghaggar-Hakra Code: A B C D A. Saraswati - 1. Ravi
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - In the Rigveda, the word 'Sapta Saindhava' (Land of Seven Rivers) has been used everywhere for the Aryan habitat. Although there is considerable disagreement among scholars regarding the identification of these seven famous rivers, it is certain that the land which we today call Punjab (portions of India and Pakistan in the current geographical position) and some land extended beyond it was called 'Sapta Saindhava' in the Rigveda. The Rigveda mentions Ganga, Yamuna, Sindhu, Saraswati, Parushni, Shatudri, Vipasha, Asikni (Chenab), and Vitasta (Jhelum). Saraswati was known by the name Ghaggar-Hakra in Rajasthan. Saraswati has great importance in the Rigveda. It was also a highly praised river of the Aryan habitat.

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts is the description of the construction of sacrificial altars primarily found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Kalpasutras are primarily of four types - Shrautasutra, Grihyasutra, Dharmasutra, and Shulvasutra. Their description is as follows. Shrautasutra refers to the sacrificial portion related to Shruti or the Vedas; we find a systematic description of the sacrificial portions described in the Vedas in the Shrautasutras. From their study, we can gain knowledge of the religious rituals and traditions of that period. The Grihyasutras contain descriptions of religious rituals and duties related to the household stage (Grihastha ashrama). Detailed descriptions of the sacraments and sacrifices, etc., of the household stage are found in it. In the Dharmasutras, social rules and codes of conduct have been described in detail. In the Shulvasutras, the word 'Shulva' means a measuring cord. It contains descriptions of measuring sacrificial altars, selecting their location, and their construction, etc. These are indicative of the geometric knowledge of the Aryans. Generally, the period of the Sutras is considered to be from 600 BC to 300 BC.

questions.question_text: Many Vedic sacrifices are performed in 'Darsha'. What day does this refer to?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - Most sacrifices in the Vedic period were performed on special occasions and festivals. The Darsha sacrifice was performed on the day of Amavasya (New Moon), while the Paurnamasa sacrifice was performed on the day of Purnima (Full Moon). We first obtain definite knowledge about the religion of ancient Indians from Vedic literature, which includes the Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and Upanishads. The oldest text of this literature is the Rigveda, in which we first see polytheism. The Aryans believed in the existence of various gods. Most of their gods are symbols of various forces of nature which have been personified, and it is believed that the activities of the world are conducted only by the grace of the gods. Each god is shown as the creator and controller of the world. Mention of hymns spoken to various gods is found in the Rigveda. In the sacrifices, offerings of fire, ghee, grain, meat, etc., were given, and the gods themselves were believed to be present to accept the offerings. The presiding deities of the Darsha sacrifice were 'Agni and Indra', and the presiding deities of the Paurnamasa were 'Agni and Soma'.

questions.question_text: The Vedic mountain Mujavant was considered the habitat of-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - Soma and Sura were the main drinks of the Aryans. Soma was famous for its intoxicating quality, which was obtained from the Mujavant mountain. There was a practice of drinking Soma juice on the occasion of sacrifices and offering it to the gods to drink. Many hymns are found in praise of Soma in the ninth mandala of the Rigveda. At one place, Sage Kanva claims that after drinking the Soma juice, they have attained immortality and have known the gods. The ill effects of Sura are mentioned in the Rigveda, and it is stated that people became arrogant after drinking it and started fighting in the assemblies (Sabha-Samiti). Sura has been counted along with harmful things like anger, gambling, and ignorance. It has been described as condemnable and to be renounced. Macdonell is of the opinion that 'Soma' was actually the drink of the Indus inhabitants, and the Aryans adopted it from them.

questions.question_text: Who is famous as the author of 'Vedanga-Jyotisha'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Lagadha Muni is famous as the author of 'Vedanga-Jyotisha'. He composed Arch-Jyotisha related to the Rigveda and Yajush-Jyotisha related to the Yajurveda. The word 'Yajush' means 'sacrifice'. Therefore, the Yajurveda Samhita is a collection of hymns useful for conducting sacrifices, which were chanted by the Adhvaryu priest on the occasion of the sacrifice. The Yajurveda is primarily ritualistic. It contains descriptions of the methods of performing sacrifices. The Yajurveda has two parts - Krishna Yajurveda and Shukla Yajurveda. In the Krishna Yajurveda, there is a mix of metrical hymns and prose sentences, while in the Shukla Yajurveda, there are only hymns. Both of these have many branches. The main branches of the Krishna Yajurveda are Taittiriya, Kathaka, Maitrayani, and Kapishthala. The main branches of the Shukla Yajurveda are Madhyandina and Kanva. The Samhitas of the Shukla Yajurveda are also called 'Vajasaneyi' because Yajnavalkya, the son of Vajasanein, was their seer. It has a total of forty chapters.

questions.question_text: The habitat of the Rigvedic Bharatas was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - In one place in the Rigveda, there is a mention of a war of ten kings (Dasharajna), which took place against Sudas, the king of the Bharatas. Vasishtha was the priest of Sudas. Against them was a confederacy of ten kings, which included five minor tribes—Anu, Paktha, Bhalanas, Shiva, and Vishanin—in addition to the five main clans (Panchajana). Sage Vishvamitra was the priest of this confederacy. This war was fought on the question of succession between the former inhabitants settled in the North-West region and the later Aryans of Brahmavarta. In this, Sudas, the lord of the Bharata clan, defeated this confederacy of ten kings in a fierce battle on the banks of the Ravi River and thus he became the supreme Samrat of Rigvedic India. Our country was named Bharat after the name of the Bharata clan. This was the most important clan of the Rigvedic period, which lived in the region between the Saraswati and Yamuna rivers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following supported the sacrificial Vedic tradition and opposed the principle of Sanyasa?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - Kumarila, a follower of the Mimamsa philosophy, supported the Vedic sacrifice. In the Mimamsa philosophy (whose followers are Prabhakara and Kumarila), while giving great emphasis to Vedic rituals, it has been described as mandatory for every person to perform them. Mimamsakas teach the correct performance of sacrifices prescribed by the Vedas and their rituals. Religion has a very high importance in Mimamsa philosophy. According to Jaimini (the founder of Mimamsa philosophy), Dharma is that command which inspires man to action. Knowledge of Dharma is obtained only from the apaurusheya Vedas. What the Vedas prescribe is Dharma, and what they forbid is Adharma. We can attain Dharma only by behaving according to the rules described in the Vedas. Mimamsa philosophy gives importance only to Karma (action), which is capable of providing fruits through its power (Apurva). For this, they do not consider the existence of God necessary. The thoughts of Mimamsakas regarding God are not clear. The main goal of this philosophy is to establish the importance of Karma.

questions.question_text: With whom is the Yadu clan mostly paired in the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - The Yadu clan mentioned in the Rigveda was mostly paired with the Turvasa clan. Both Yadu and Turvasa were prominent clans of the Rigvedic period. The Bharata clan was an older clan than these. For example, the Yadu and Turvasa tribes were undoubtedly counted among the Aryan Panchajanas. However, at one place, they too have been called Dasa. The sounds of the names of two important heroes of the Rigveda, Divodasa and Sudas, are also not less important. From a linguistic point of view, names of Dasas like Sambara, Shushna, Tugru, Vetasu, Chumuri, and Arbuda do not seem non-Aryan. Regarding the Dasa people, it has been said that they neither offered oblations in the fire nor were they partisans of Indra-Varuna. Dasyus are described as Adevayu (those who do not have faith in gods), Abrahman (those who do not believe in the Vedas), and Ayajvan (those who do not perform sacrifices). Overall, in the Rigveda, the Dasyus have been described as greater enemies of the Aryans as compared to the Dasas.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements about the Vedic god Indra and choose your answer from the code given below the statements- Statements: 1. Was the god of storms 2. Was the guardian of the moral order 3. Was the god of rain 4. Punished the sinners Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation - The Vedic god Indra was the god of rain and storms, while the god of the moral order (Ritasya Gopa) was Varuna, who punished the sinners. And in the Vedic period, Varuna was called Samrat.

questions.question_text: Who held the ownership of land in the Early Vedic period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation - In the Early Vedic period, people lived in groups, meaning a group took the form of a clan; the land on which they resided belonged to the whole clan. The king was not the owner of the land but rather the lord of war.

questions.question_text: Which of the following did not compose Vedic hymns (Richas)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation - In the Rigveda, names of women like Ghosha, Lopamudra, Vishvavara, etc., appear, who were sufficiently educated and had also composed some hymns. The social and religious rights of women were just like those of men, but in two respects, Rigvedic society considered them ineligible - (a) They did not have the right to participate in politics. (b) They did not have rights related to property. In other respects, they were equal to men. Marriage was considered a sacred bond in Rigvedic society. In the Shatapatha Brahmana, the wife is called the 'Ardhangini' (half-body) of the husband. She could participate in sacrificial activities along with her husband; a person without a wife was not eligible for sacrifice. In the Rigveda, by saying 'Jayedastam', meaning the wife herself is the home, her importance has been clearly accepted. The practice of monogamy was generally prevalent in the family, although some people of the noble class kept many wives. Child marriage and widow marriage did not occur. The main purpose of marriage was to obtain a son. Prayers were constantly made for the abundance of sons.

questions.question_text: Establish the identity of the rivers given in List-I with their Vedic names in List-II and choose the correct answer from the code given below the lists- List I List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation - It is estimated that the expansion of the Aryans was from Afghanistan to the Ganges Valley. Names of many rivers and mountains are found here and there in the Rigveda. The Himalayan mountain is clearly mentioned. One peak of the Himalayas was called Mujavant, which was famous for Soma. From the mention of the rivers Kubha (Kabul), Krumu (Kurram), Gomati, and Suvastu in the West, it is known that Afghanistan was also a part of India at that time. After this, there is mention of the five rivers of Punjab - Sindhu, Vitasta (Jhelum), Asikni (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), and Vipasha (Beas). Along with these, names of Shatudri (Sutlej), Saraswati, Yamuna, and Ganga are also found.

questions.question_text: Who was the first agricultural scientist described in the Atharvaveda?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation - The first agricultural scientist described in the Atharvaveda was Prithu Vainya (the god of agriculture), who first gave birth to the plow and agriculture. The Atharvaveda Samhita gives worldly fruits; it contains mention of the rituals performed to make human life happy and free from sorrow. A sage named Atharva is its first seer. Therefore, it has been named Atharvaveda after him. Its second seer is Sage Angiras. For this reason, this Veda is also called the Atharvangiras Veda. Hymns related to various subjects like disease prevention, tantra-mantra, magic-spells, curses, subjugation, blessings, praise for long life, beauty, rain, atonement, marriage, love, royal duties, and the glory of the motherland are also found in the Atharvaveda. Many things about the principles and practices of Ayurveda are also filled in it. Thus, this text is an encyclopedia of worldly conduct and behavior. From the point of view of Kalpa also, it is a high-quality compilation in which very beautiful and heart-touching lyrics and poems have been included.

questions.question_text: Who among the following believed that the original habitat of the Aryans was the Arctic region?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - The first scholar to consider the original home of the Aryans in the North Pole is Pt. Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He has described this in his book 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'. Tilak ji is of the opinion that the Aryans composed the Rigveda in the Sapta Saindhava region. In this, under one hymn, there is praise for the long-duration Dawn (Usha). Long-duration Dawns are visible only at the North Pole. Mention of Mount Sumeru is found in the Mahabharata, where there is a day of six months and a night of six months. This also points towards the North Pole. Therefore, we can say that the Aryans were residents of the North Pole and for this reason, the memory of their original land remained in their minds. However, the above opinion of Tilak is not acceptable because it is based on pure literature. The Aryans themselves called the Sapta Saindhava region 'created by the gods' (Devakrita Yoni). If the North Pole (Arctic region) were their original country, they would have mentioned it clearly somewhere.

questions.question_text: The Reva (Narmada) river is mentioned in-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation - Mention of the Later Vedic period rivers Reva and Sadanira is found in the Shatapatha Brahmana. In the Shatapatha Brahmana, it is said that 'Videgha Mathava carried the Agni Vaishvanara in his mouth. As soon as the name of Ghee (clarified butter) was taken, that fire came out of Mathava's mouth and reached the earth. At that time, Videgha Mathava lived on the banks of the Saraswati. That fire proceeded towards the East burning everything, and Videgha Mathava and his priest Gautama Rahugana followed it. It went on burning the rivers; suddenly it could not burn the Sadanira river, which flows from the North Giri Himalayas. Because of not being burnt by fire, Brahmin people did not cross it in olden times. Videgha Mathava asked the fire where he should reside now; the fire replied to the East of this river. It is because of the Sadanira that the dignity of the Koshala and Videha countries is maintained even today.'

questions.question_text: In which Upanishad is sacrifice compared to a broken boat?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation - The 'Mundaka Upanishad' was composed for the shaven-headed, i.e., the sanyasis. This Upanishad is influenced by the Shramana tradition and follows the renunciation of action (Karma Sanyasa). In this, two types of knowledge, Para and Apara, and phrases like 'Satyameva Jayate' and 'Sacrifice is a broken boat' are mentioned. The subjects of Apara Vidya are ritualistic, while Para Vidya relates to the eternal Brahman. The 'Mandukya Upanishad' explains the 'Four-fold Soul' (in which the four syllables of OM are described as the four feet or legs of the soul) and the 'poignant explanation of Omkara'. On this very Upanishad, Gaudapada wrote the Karikas (Mandukya-Karika). In the 'Brihadaranyaka Upanishad', the 'Yajnavalkya-Vachaknavi Gargi dialogue' and the 'Yajnavalkya-Maitreyi dialogue' are found in the court of King Janaka of Videha. The 'Chandogya Upanishad' is considered the oldest Upanishad. There is the first mention of Devakiputra Krishna, and Krishna is described as the disciple of 'Ghora Angirasa'.

questions.question_text: The Family Mandalas (Vamsha Mandalas) of the Rigveda usually start with a hymn to whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The mandalas from the second to the seventh of the Rigveda are known by the name Gotra or Vamsha Mandala (Family Mandalas) because each of these mandalas is associated with a single lineage of sages. The first hymn of each of these mandalas is regularly addressed to Agni. Thereafter come the hymns of Indra and then the hymns of other gods. The sages of the Family Mandalas are collectively called 'Pragatha'.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs of Vedic kings and states is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – During the Upanishad period, there were many kings who were dedicated to the knowledge of Brahman and spiritual contemplation. Janaka of Videha, Ashvapati of Kaikeya, Ajatashatru of Kashi, and Pravahana Jaivali of Panchala country, etc., are famous, whereas according to the Shatapatha Brahmana, Janamejaya was a king of the Kuru clan whose capital was named Asandivat. The lord of many horses, this king performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice under the priesthood of Sage Shaunaka.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vedic gods has a resemblance to the Avestan god Ahura Mazda?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – The Vedic period god 'Varuna' has a resemblance to the Avestan god 'Ahura Mazda'.

questions.question_text: The ceremonies related to 'Rajasuya' are described in –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – The Yajurveda is a compilation of Yajus. The literal meaning of 'Yajush' is sacrifice, worship, shraddha, respect, etc. The hymns of this Veda are recited by the class of priests called Adhvaryu in the sacrifice. There are 40 chapters in its Vajasaneyi Samhita. The first 25 chapters are very important from the point of view of content. The hymns for the 'Darsha' and 'Paurnamasa' sacrifices are compiled in the first and second chapters. In the third chapter, there is a collection of hymns for the daily 'Agnihotra' and 'Chaturmasya' sacrifices. From the fourth to the eighth chapter, hymns related to 'Agnishtoma etc.' Soma sacrifices and animal sacrifice are obtained. Some sacrifices that are completed in one day are also found in the tradition of Soma sacrifices. Among these, the Vajapeya sacrifice is foremost. Also in the tradition of Soma sacrifices is the Rajasuya sacrifice to be performed by kings. Prayers for the Vajapeya and Rajasuya sacrifices have been made in the ninth and tenth chapters of the Vajasaneyi Samhita. It is noteworthy that in Rigvedic religion, sacrifices were performed to gain the grace of gods or boons from them and to worship the gods. The offerings given in the sacrifices were of milk, grain, ghee, meat, and Soma. In the Rigveda, there is an extensive mention of only the Soma sacrifice.

questions.question_text: Which is the most popular meter of the Rigveda?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – The most popular meter in the Rigveda is Trishtubh (4253 times). After this, the Gayatri meter (2467 times) and the Jagati meter (1358 times) have been used. The Gayatri meter has the fewest words (24), and the Jagati meter has the most (48).

questions.question_text: In the Later Vedic period, rulers of the Prachya (Eastern) country were called –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – In the Later Vedic period, the words Samrat, Svarat, Virat, Bhoja, and Rajan have been used for the rulers of the East, West, North, South, and Middle Country respectively in the Aitareya Brahmana, and the words Ekarat and Sarvabhauma are reserved for those who conquered all four directions.

questions.question_text: Included under 'Vedatrayi' are -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - In 'Vedatrayi', mainly three Vedas - Rigveda, Yajurveda, and Samaveda - are counted. Among these, the Rigveda is a compilation of hymns that were sung on the occasion of sacrifices. The 'Yajurveda' is a compilation of hymns useful for conducting sacrifices, which were chanted by the 'Adhvaryu' priest on the occasion of the sacrifice. The Yajurveda is primarily ritualistic, containing descriptions of the methods of performing sacrifices. The 'Samaveda' is a collection of hymns to be sung on the occasion of sacrifices. The person who sang these hymns was called 'Udgata'. These three Vedas together are called 'Vedatrayi'.

questions.question_text: Who was the head of the village in the Rigvedic period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - In the Rigveda, mention is found of these three officers: Purohita, Senani, and Gramani. Among these, the Purohita accompanied the king to the battlefield and prayed for the king's victory there. He was, in a way, the king's teacher, guide, and friend. The Senani was the chief official of the army and performed tasks in war according to the king's orders. In peacetime, the Senani probably had to perform civil functions as well. 'Gramani' was the head of the village and the leader of the village for administrative and military tasks. He represented the interests of the rural populace.

questions.question_text: In which text are the mantras of Apala Atreyi collected?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The status of women in the Rigvedic period was better compared to the Later Vedic period. They had the right to participate in religious activities. The practice of child marriage did not exist, and women were married only after becoming adults. This had a positive impact on women, and they received sufficient opportunities for education. Literary evidence informs us that during this period, there were several learned women (Vidushi) who composed Vedic hymns (richas). These richas are collected in the Rigveda. Among these women, Lopamudra, Ghosha, Apala, and Vishwavara were prominent.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following texts is there primarily a description of the construction of sacrificial altars?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - The Sulvasutra contains descriptions of geometry related to the construction of sacrificial altars (Yagya Vedis). The Shrautasutras provide detailed discussions of sacrificial procedures. The Grihyasutras contain descriptions of household rituals and sacrifices (which were necessary for a householder to perform). The Dharmasutras deal with subjects related to politics, law, and conduct. Among the major sutra-writers, the names of Gautama, Baudhayana, Apastamba, and Vashistha are particularly noteworthy.

questions.question_text: Where is the earliest mention of Krishna, the son of Devaki, found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation - The propagator of the Bhagavata religion was Krishna of the Vrishni clan, who is called Vasudeva because he was the son of Vasudeva. He was originally a resident of Mathura. In the Chandogya Upanishad, he is called the son of Devaki and the disciple of Ghora Angirasa. Followers of Krishna called him Bhagavata (the Adorable One). During the Mahabharata period, Krishna was identified with Vishnu. Vaishnavism flourished most during the Gupta period. The Guptas made it their state religion.

questions.question_text: By what term was the son of an unmarried girl known?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - A 'Kanina son' was born through physical contact between a girl living in her father's house and a secret man. Later, the man who married the girl was considered his father. Gudhaja son - These were sons whose father's identity was not known. Parashava son - A son born from the union of a Brahmin man and a Shudra woman was considered a Parashava son.

questions.question_text: The description of Aindra Mahabhisheka is given in:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation – The description of Aindra Mahabhisheka is found in the Rigveda. The Rigveda is the oldest Veda. It contains 1017 suktas and 10 mandalas. The first and tenth mandalas are the newest. Mandalas 2 to 7 are ancient.

questions.question_text: For whom was the 'Shulagava' sacrifice performed?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The 'Shulagava sacrifice' was performed for Rudra. In the Rigveda, Shiva is called Rudra. When angry, he destroyed human and animal life or spread epidemics. In Rudra, both destructive and auspicious powers were inherent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following incarnations are described as 'forms' of Prajapati in ancient literature? (i) Matsya (ii) Varaha (iii) Vamana Select the correct answer from the following codes: (iv) Narasimha
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation – The Varaha and Matsya incarnations are described as forms of Prajapati in ancient Indian literature.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Upanishads is written in prose?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation – The main foundation of Indian philosophy and the final category of Vedic literature are the Upanishads; they are also called Vedanta. The total number of Upanishads is 108, which is mentioned in the 'Muktikopanishad'. Among them, 13 are important Upanishads. Of these, two—Aitareya and Kaushitaki—are related to the Rigveda; two—Chandogya and Kena—are related to the Samaveda; four—Taittiriya, Katha, Shvetashvatara, and Maitrayani—are related to the Krishna Yajurveda; two—Brihadaranyaka and Isha—are related to the Shukla Yajurveda; and three—Mundaka, Prashna, and Mandukya—are related to the Atharvaveda. The Katha, Shvetashvatara, Isha, and Mundaka Upanishads are in verse (metrical), while parts of Kena and Prashna Upanishads are in verse and parts are in prose. The remaining seven Upanishads are in prose. Therefore, the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad is in prose.

questions.question_text: Which of the following animals are mentioned in the Rigveda? 1. Cow 2. Horse 3. Goat 4. Buffalo Indicate your answer from the following codes:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Animal husbandry was a major occupation of the Rigvedic Aryans. Prayers were made to the gods for the increase of animal wealth. The cow had the highest importance. It was counted in economic terms. Goods were purchased through the exchange of cows. The buffalo was also a domestic animal for milk, meat, and hide. In the Rigveda, the buffalo is called 'Gawala'. The Aryans were also familiar with sheep and goats. The horse was a highly useful animal for the Aryans, which was used in their wars. Horses were also given in charity/donation and occasionally their meat was also eaten. Aryans also used elephants in battle. Along with horses and camels, oxen were also used to pull carts and chariots. Among domestic animals, dogs, pigs, donkeys, and deer were also prominent.

questions.question_text: In which Upanishad is Ajatashatru called the King of Kashi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, Ajatashatru is called the King of Kashi. Many Brahmins also used to come to the Kshatriya ruler Ajatashatru of Kashi for spiritual knowledge. Balaki Gargya obtained philosophical knowledge from him.

questions.question_text: 'The Rigvedic Aryans and the people of Harappan culture were the same.' Who is the proponent of this theory?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation - B.B. Lal is the proponent of the theory that the Rigvedic Aryans and the people of Harappan culture were the same. B.B. Lal is a renowned archaeologist of India. He has explored and excavated many archaeological sites in different regions of India. In the year 2000, the Government of India honored him with the Padma Bhushan.

questions.question_text: 'Dyuta Krida' (Gambling game) was a part of which ritual?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Shrauta sacrifices are divided into two categories – Haviryagya and Somayagya. In the first category are Agnihotra, Darshapurnamasa, Chaturmasya, Agrayana, Pashubandha, Sautramani, and Pindapitri-yagya. Among Somayagyas, the most important are Ashvamedha and Rajasuya. Among these, the Ashvamedha sacrifice was for the prosperity or fulfillment of the ambitions of the Kshatriya class, i.e., kings, and some were for the increase of the brilliance, splendor, and intellectual power of the Brahmin class. In the Vajapeya sacrifice, a chariot race was organized. Meanwhile, in the Rajasuya sacrifice, a gambling game (Dyuta Krida) was organized.

questions.question_text: In which of the following Samhitas of the Yajurveda are there only hymns and no prose?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Yajurveda is mainly divided into two parts - Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. The Shukla Yajurveda is also called the Madhyandina and Vajasaneyi Yajurveda. The purpose of calling the Shukla Yajurveda 'Shukla' (white/pure) is that it contains pure mantra portions. It does not have explanatory, descriptive, or applicative portions. These mantras were recited in various sacrifices. Because of its purity and refinement, it is called Shukla (clean, unmixed) Yajurveda. In the Krishna Yajurveda, there is an application of metrical mantras and prose sentences, whereas the Shukla Yajurveda contains only mantras. The main branches of the Krishna Yajurveda are – Taittiriya, Kathaka, Maitrayani, and Kapisthala.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was a philosophical king of the Kekaya Janapada mentioned in the Upanishads?
questions.explanation: The names of several kings are mentioned in the Upanishads, such as Ashvapati of Kekaya. In this, Ashvapati, the king of Kekaya Janapada, was a philosopher. It is mentioned in the Chandogya Upanishad that Uddalaka, Aruni, Panchagni, and Vaishvanara went to King Ashvapati of Kekaya to obtain education

questions.question_text: Who among the following is called the author of 'Nirukta'?
questions.explanation: Yaska composed the Nirukta. It was composed in the 5th century BC. Rules and laws related to education were given in it. The derivation of Vedic words is discussed in this book itself. Vedic subjects are described in it

questions.question_text: In which Mandala is the Nadi Sukta of the Rigveda found?
questions.explanation: The description of the Nadi Sukta in the Rigveda is given in the tenth Mandala. The first and tenth mandalas of the Rigveda are considered the newest mandalas. The Indus river (Sindhu) is mentioned most frequently in the Rigveda. The most sacred river of the Rigveda is the Saraswati river; it is called Naditama and Ambitama

questions.question_text: What was the ancient name of the Sutlej river?
questions.explanation: The 'Sapta-Saindhava' rivers are mentioned in the Rigveda. Sapta-Saindhava refers to the Indus (Sindhu) and its tributaries: Sutlej (Shatudri), Beas (Vipasha), Ravi (Parushni), Chenab (Asikni), Jhelum (Vitasta), and the Saraswati river

questions.question_text: In the Later Vedic period, 'Palagala' referred to:
questions.explanation: In the Later Vedic period, the person who gave messages to the king was called Palagala. Through this messenger, the king used to get all information about his kingdom on time. Palagala were ready to give messages of various types of events to the king

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: All four Vedas had different Brahmanas. The Brahmanas of the Rigveda were Aitareya and Kaushitaki. The Brahmanas of the Samaveda were Panchavimsha and Shadvimsha. The Brahmanas of the Yajurveda were Shatapatha and Taittiriya. The Brahmana of the Atharvaveda was the Gopatha Brahmana. Among these, the first three Vedas are called Vedatrayi

questions.question_text: Which river in the Rigveda is called 'Ambitame, Naditame, and Devitame'?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda, the Saraswati river is called Ambitame, Naditame, and Devitame. The Saraswati river has been declared the most sacred river in the Rigveda. The Saraswati river is mentioned in the 10th Mandala of the Rigveda. The Indus (Sindhu) river is mentioned the maximum number of times in the Rigveda

questions.question_text: In which of the following Puranas was Buddha given a place instead of Krishna in the list of Vishnu's incarnations?
questions.explanation: Among the total 18 Puranas, the Vayu Purana is given special importance. Due to more discussion on Shiva worship in this Purana, it is considered the second part of the Shiva Purana. Yet, a detailed presentation on the Vaishnava sect is found in it. In this Purana, along with astronomy, geography, sage lineages, musicology, etc., Krishna was given a place instead of Buddha. The Commission, in its revised answer key, has considered the answer to this question to be option (a)

questions.question_text: Who among these was not a Vedic Sun deity?
questions.explanation: Vishnu Urukrama is a name of Vishnu and not of the Sun. In the Shatapatha Brahmana, Vishnu is called the 'proponent of sacrifice'. In the Aitareya Brahmana, Vishnu is called the 'supreme deity' and Devnaam Dvapara. All other options are related to the Sun

questions.question_text: "Copper hoards are the creation of Aryans." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The items that the Aryans used first are worshipped in Indian Hindu religion today, such as barley, rice, mango leaves, and copper vessels, etc. Keeping this importance in mind, H. Geldern said that "Copper hoards are the duty (creation) of the Aryans."

questions.question_text: Where was the Upanishadic Ashvapati the king?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Ashvapati of the Upanishadic period was the king of Kekaya. The word Upanishad is derived from the Upanishad root, which means sitting near someone. It is known that the governance system in the Upanishad period was monarchical. In some places, there was also a republican system of government. Kuru and Panchala were the best states in the Upanishad period. Their capitals were Asandivat and Kampilya.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? Vedas - Their Brahmanas
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Among the four Vedas – Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda, the Rigveda is the oldest religious book in the world. The Brahmana texts associated with them are as follows: Rigveda - Aitareya and Kaushitaki Brahmana; Samaveda - Panchavimsha and Jaiminiya Brahmana; Yajurveda - Shatapatha and Taittiriya Brahmana; and Atharvaveda - Gopatha Brahmana.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is considered as the Future Buddha in the Buddhist tradition?
questions.explanation: Bodhisattvas are those who are capable of attaining Nirvana but do not accept it until they guide other individuals towards the attainment of Nirvana. They can be in the form of humans or animals. Among all Bodhisattvas, Maitreya is the Future Bodhisattva in the Buddhist tradition. He is the Kalashadhari (pot-bearing) Bodhisattva. His symbol is the Nagakesar flower. Additionally, Avalokiteshvara is also called Padmapani. His symbol is the lotus. He is the principal Bodhisattva. The Bodhisattva Manjusri holds a sword in one hand and a book in the other. He is also called Kumarabhuta (one who remains forever young). The symbol of Bodhisattva Vajrapani is the Vajra (thunderbolt). He is the enemy of sin and untruth, the protector of snakes, and the protector of life and death

questions.question_text: The idols of which of the following deities are made holding a plow?
questions.explanation: The founder of Bhagavatism was Vasudeva (Krishna). In Bhagavatism or Pancharatra religion, three other deities were also worshipped besides Krishna, who are Balarama (Samkarshana), Pradyumna, and Aniruddha. These four deities together are given the designation of 'Chaturvyuha'. A Kushan-era statue of Krishna and Balarama has been found from a place called Silas in Kashmir. In Silas, a statue of Krishna holding a wheel (Chakra) and a statue of Balarama in a 'plow-holding posture' have been found on the rocks. In Vaishnavism, Shri Krishna is said to be the son of Vasudeva, whereas by Patanjali and in the Vishnu Purana, the identity of Vasudeva is stated to be another form of Vishnu. Pradyumna was the son born to Krishna from Rukmini, and Aniruddha was the son of Pradyumna

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below: Statement (I): According to Samkhya philosophy, there are twenty-five fundamental elements, among which the first is Prakriti and the second is Purusha. Statement (II): Badarayana's Brahmasutra is the fundamental text of the Vedanta philosophy tradition. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.C: Statement (I) is true, but Statement (II) is false
options.D: Statement (I) is false, but Statement (II) is true

questions.explanation: Maharishi Kapila is considered the proponent of Samkhya philosophy. Since it contains a description of 25 fundamental elements, it can be called the philosophy of numbers. Samkhya philosophy is dualistic. In this, the existence of two independent powers named Prakriti and Purusha has been accepted, by whose combination the creation originates. Prakriti is the primary cause of creation, which is designated as 'Pradhana' and 'Avyakta', not the first element (in the sense of a numerical sequence where Purusha is second). Whereas the second main element of Samkhya philosophy is Purusha. Its nature is eternal, omnipresent, and pure consciousness. Consciousness is the very nature of the Soul (Atma). For this reason, statement (I) is false While Badarayana's Brahmasutra is the basic text of the Vedanta philosophy tradition. Because in this philosophy, an attempt is made to prove the authenticity of the Vedas through various types of logic. Upanishads and Vedanta are called Uttara Mimamsa because in these, knowledge is discussed instead of rituals, as we find that Badarayana's Brahmasutra and the Gita develop the philosophy of the Upanishads itself. In this way, statement (II) is true.

questions.question_text: Who among these were well-known Shaivites of early India?
questions.explanation: Many literatures were composed by Vaishnava and Shaiva devotees between the sixth and ninth centuries. Due to this, this period came to be called the 'Diamond Age' of the Alwar and Nayanar Bhakti movements. In early India, the Tamil Shaiva saints were called 'Nayanars'. Their total number is stated to be 63. Among them, Tirumular was a mystic saint. He is also considered a spiritual reformer and pioneer. Similarly, 'Aiyadigal Kadavarkon' was a Nayanar saint of Tamil Nadu In South India, the saints associated with Vaishnava Bhakti were called 'Alwars'. Their number was 12. Among them, Tirumangai belonged to the Chola military officer and robber class. Tirumangai, who was immersed (absorbed) in Vaishnava devotion, played an important role in the construction of the Srirangam temple. 'Periya Tirumoli' is his famous composition. The Alwar saint Tirumalisai was born in the Pallava region. He was a contemporary of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman.

questions.question_text: Pratimoksha refers to-

options.B: A materialistic principle of the Charvakas
options.C: Rules of the Order (Sangha) of the Buddhist tradition
options.D: A religious official of the Jains

questions.explanation: Pratimoksha or Patimokkha: This is a set of prescriptions and prohibitions. In this, rules of the order have been kept for 227 Buddhist monks and 311 Buddhist nuns. It contains a compilation of the penances to be performed upon the violation of disciplinary prescriptions and prohibitions. It was recited twice a month. The reading of Patimokkha on special days is 'Uposatha'. 'Uposatha' is called 'Roy' in Sri Lanka. A meeting of Pratimoksha could not be held if there were fewer than four monks. Actually, there are only 227 in the Pali Pratimoksha. The number in the Pratimoksha of the Mahasanghikas is 218, which is the lowest. The number in the Pratimoksha of the Sarvastivadins is the highest at 263. Pratimoksha begins with the Nidana, in which the monks gathered for Uposatha were informed that any monk who had committed a fault should reveal it. In the Parajika section of Pratimoksha, 4 sins associated with Pratimoksha, 13 offenses associated with the Sangha in the Sanghavasesa section, and 16 rules regarding robes (Chivara) are mentioned. The total number of offenses in the Parajika section is 8

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II List-I (Dhyani Buddha) | List-II (Their Bodhisattvas)
questions.explanation: The correct matching is List-I (Dhyani Buddha) - List-II (Their Bodhisattvas) 1. Amitabha - Padmapani 2. Akshobhya - Vajrapani 3. Vairocana - Samantabhadra 4. Amoghasiddhi - Vishvapani

questions.question_text: Who presided over the Jain assembly held in Vallabhi?
questions.explanation: The first Tirthankara of Jainism was Rishabhanatha or Adinatha, who is also mentioned in the Rigveda. The word Jain is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jina', which means 'Victor (one who has conquered the senses)'. There were a total of 24 Tirthankaras in Jainism; the 24th Tirthankara was Mahavira Swami. Parshvanatha prescribed four vows - non-violence, truth, non-stealing, non-possession, but Mahavira Swami added the fifth vow - 'Celibacy' (Brahmacharya). Jain assemblies were organized to compile the teachings of Jainism into literature. Mainly two Jain assemblies were organized. First Jain Assembly - 4th century B.C., in Pataliputra, which was presided over by Sthulabhadra Second Jain Assembly - 513 or 526 A.D., in Vallabhi, presided over by Devardhigani or Kshamashramana. In addition to this, in the 4th-5th centuries, Jain assemblies were called in Mathura and Vallabhi, in which the president of the Mathura council was Khandila (Skandila), while the Vallabhi assembly was presided over by 'Nagarjuna'. Bahubali - Was the son of the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha. He meditated in the Kayotsarga posture and attained Kevalya. The statue of Gommateshwara Bahubali is in Shravanabelagola (Karnataka). Kundakunda - He was a famous Acharya of the Digambara Jain sect. According to inscription number 40 of Shravanabelagola, his name at the time of initiation was 'Padmanandi'. The mention of Mangala Kundakundacharya in the 'Mangalacharana' after Mahavira Swami and Gautama Ganadhara shows his fame in the Shramana tradition.

questions.question_text: Who played a key role in the distribution of Gautama Buddha's bodily remains (relics) after his Mahaparinirvana?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gautama Buddha, the exponent of Buddhism, was born in 563 B.C. at a place named Lumbini near Kapilavastu. His father Shuddhodana was the chief of the Shakya clan of Kapilavastu and mother Mayadevi was a princess of the Koliya republic. He attained knowledge under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya (Bihar). He died in 483 B.C. in Kushinara at the age of 80. After his death, a dispute arose regarding his bone relics, for which there were 8 claimants. Therefore, a scholar named Drona distributed his remains. Ajatashatru was the ruler of the Magadha Empire who assumed the title of Kunika. Mahakashyapa was the president of the First Buddhist Council (483 B.C.), while a scholar named Upali compiled the text named Vinaya Pitaka

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Yakshini or Guardian Deity) | List-II (Association with Tirthankaras)
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is as follows List-I (Yakshini or Guardian Deity) - List-II (Association with Tirthankaras) (A) Siddhayika - Mahavira (B) Chakreshvari - Adinatha (C) Ambika - Neminatha (D) Padmavati - Parshvanatha

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the Jain text Kuvalayamala?
questions.explanation: The author of the Jain text Kuvalayamala is Udyotana Suri. This text was composed by Udyotana Suri while staying in Jalore around 778 A.D. It is essentially a Prakrit text. In this text, 18 local languages have been mentioned. Among these 18 languages, Maru Bhasha of western Rajasthan is also mentioned

questions.question_text: Which language did Mahavira Jain use for the propagation of his teachings?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami's childhood name was Vardhamana. At the age of 30, he left home to perform penance. After 12 years of severe penance, on the 10th day of the month of Vaishakha, near the village of Jrimbhikagrama on the banks of the Rijupalika River under a Sal tree, he attained Kevalya (knowledge). After attaining knowledge, he was called 'Kevalin', 'Jina (Victor)', Arhat (Worthy), and 'Nigrantha' (Free from bonds). Mahavira Swami used Prakrit or Ardhamagadhi languages for the propagation of his teachings

questions.question_text: The text 'Nettipakarana' is related to whose teachings?
questions.explanation: The text Nettipakarana is related to the teachings of Gautama Buddha. Nettipakarana, which is also called Nettippakarana or Netti. It is a Buddhist religious text which is sometimes included in the Khuddaka Nikaya of Theravada Buddhism. The main subject of this religious text is the systematization of Buddha's teachings and instructions. The Sri Lankan scholar Dhammapala wrote a commentary on this text in the fifth century. In 1962, Bhikkhu Nanamoli presented its English translation under the name 'The Guide'

questions.question_text: In which of the following literatures is it mentioned that 'Parshvanatha' was a Kshatriya?
questions.explanation: The Kalpa Sutra contains a depiction of the birth of Mahavira. The life stories of the Tirthankaras (Parshvanatha, Mahavira Swami, etc.) are described in the Jain text named Kalpa Sutra. It is mentioned in the Kalpa Sutra that 'Parshvanatha' was a Kshatriya. Bhadrabahu is considered its author. Traditionally it is believed that this text was composed 150 years after the Nirvana of Mahavira Swami. During the eight-day Paryushana festival, Jain monks and nuns recite the Kalpa Sutra

questions.question_text: Dharmachakra Pravartana is related to which religion?
questions.explanation: The birth of Gautama Buddha is believed to have taken place in 563 B.C. in the Amra-kunja near Lumbini village close to Kapilavastu. At the age of 29, he left home. This event was called Mahabhinishkramana. Buddha attained knowledge under the Bodhi tree on the banks of the Niranjana River in Bodh Gaya. After attaining knowledge, Buddha gave his first sermon to five Brahmins in Rishipattana or Mrigadava (Sarnath). This event was called Dharmachakra Pravartana. Buddha died at the age of 80 in Kushinagar, which was called Mahaparinirvana in Buddhist texts

questions.question_text: Who was called the chief 'Nigrantha' of a sect?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami's name was Vardhamana. At the age of 30, he left home and went to perform penance. After 12 years of severe penance, on the 10th day of the month of Vaishakha, near Jrimbhikagrama on the banks of the Rijupalika River under a Sal tree, he attained Kevalya (knowledge). After attaining knowledge, he was called 'Kevalin', 'Jina' (Victor), Arhat (Worthy), and 'Nigrantha' (Free from bonds). Mahavira Swami used Prakrit and Ardhamagadhi languages for the propagation of his teachings

questions.question_text: The 'Digambara' sect of Jainism was related to –
questions.explanation: After the death of Mahavira Swami, Sudharman became the first president of the Jain Sangha; after Sudharman, Jambu, Sambhutivijaya, and Bhadrabahu became the presidents of the Sangha. After the death of Sambhutivijaya, Sthulabhadra became the president of the Sangha. At this time, a severe famine of 12 years occurred in Magadha. At this time, Bhadrabahu, who was the contemporary president, went to South India with his followers. Sthulabhadra stayed in Magadha itself and started wearing white clothes, therefore they were called Shvetambara, and the followers of Bhadrabahu who had gone to South India were called Digambara

questions.question_text: 'Jaggayyapeta' sculpture is related to –
questions.explanation: The Jaggayyapeta sculpture is related to Buddhism. The Jaggayyapeta stupa is one of the oldest stupas in the Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh) region, dating back to the second century B.C. Known as Velagiri during the Satavahana period, the Jaggayyapeta stupa was an important Buddhist establishment for monks. Over time, through the donations of various rulers and merchants, it became very grand and decorated

questions.question_text: Who was the architect of the ancient city "Rajgriha"?
questions.explanation: The architect of the ancient city, 'Rajgriha', was Mahagovinda. Bimbisara, the founder of the Haryanka dynasty, had this city established under the supervision of Mahagovinda Jivaka was the royal physician of Bimbisara, who was the son of Shalavati, the courtesan of Rajgriha. Udayin established a city named Pataliputra (Kusumapura) at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers in the fourth year of his reign and made Pataliputra the capital of Magadha instead of Rajgriha.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Jainism prohibited both war and agriculture. Reason (R) : In both, violence to living beings occurs. Choose the correct answer from the code given below- Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: In Jainism, extreme emphasis is placed on non-violence. Among the five great vows (Panchamahavratas) propounded by Lord Mahavira, non-violence is the first. For this reason, both war and agriculture were prohibited in Jainism, because it was believed in Jainism that along with war, killing of living beings also occurs in agriculture

questions.question_text: On what basis has the date of Buddha's Parinirvana been fixed at 483 B.C.?
questions.explanation: On the basis of the Canton record of China, scholars fix the date of Gautama Buddha's Parinirvana around 483 B.C. On this basis, the date of birth of Gautama Buddha is fixed at 567-566 B.C

questions.question_text: The southernmost Mahajanapada of the 6th century B.C. was-
questions.explanation: The southernmost Mahajanapada of the 6th century B.C. was the 'Ashmaka' Mahajanapada. The Ashmaka Mahajanapada was located on the banks of the Godavari River (Andhra Pradesh). Its capital was Potana or Potali. It is noteworthy that the Public Service Commission has accepted the answer 'd', which is not true. The Chedi Mahajanapada was located in the Bundelkhand region, whose capital was 'Sotthivati', which is identified with Shuktimati of the Mahabharata

questions.question_text: According to Mahabodhivamsa, who among the following was not a son of Kalasoka?
questions.explanation: According to Mahabodhivamsa, Kalasoka had 10 sons who were as follows: Bhadrasena, Koranda Varna, Mangura, Sarvajna, Jalika, Ubhaka, Sanjaya, Koravya, Nandivardhana and Panchamaka. They ruled collectively for 22 years. Nandivardhana/Mahanandin was the last ruler of the Shishunaga dynasty. Later, the Nanda dynasty was established in the Magadha region, whose founder was Mahapadma Nanda; he was also called Ugrasena in the Mahabodhivamsa

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a minister of the Kosala king Prasenajit?
questions.explanation: 16 Mahajanapadas emerged in the 6th century B.C. Among these 16 Mahajanapadas, 4 Mahajanapadas - Magadha, Avanti, Kosala, and Vatsa - were the most important. The Kosala Mahajanapada extended from the foothills of Nepal to the modern Awadh region. The capital of this Mahajanapada was Shravasti. At the time of Buddha, Prasenajit was the king here. Dirghacharayana, Shri Vriddha, Mrigadhara, etc., were ministers of Prasenajit. Bandhula was not a minister of Prasenajit

questions.question_text: With reference to some important characteristics of the position of women in early Buddhism, which of the following statements is/are correct? (1) Attainment of Nirvana was possible for women as well. (2) Construction of separate monasteries for nuns. Choose the correct answer through the code given below- Code :
questions.explanation: Among the religions that arose in the 6th century B.C., Buddhism was the most important. This religion played a significant role in improving the condition of Shudras and women. By 600 B.C., while most rights were snatched from women in Brahmanical religion, Buddhism made provisions for Nirvana for women as well. Women could also join the Sangha. They were given all those rights which were available to Buddhist male monks. Separate monasteries were also established for nuns

questions.question_text: Who among the following did not translate Buddhist texts after Kumarajiva in China?
questions.explanation: Shantarakshita did not translate Buddhist texts in China after Kumarajiva. Among the Indians who went to China, Kumarajiva was the most important person. Kumarajiva wrote the life story of Ashvaghosha in the Chinese language in China. He died in 413 A.D. in Hangane, where his funeral was performed according to Indian customs. Kumarajiva was later declared the Rajguru (Royal Preceptor) of China. Among the scholars who went to China after Kumarajiva, Dharmayashas, Buddhayashas, Punyatrata, Paramartha, Bodhiruchi, etc., were prominent

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correct?
questions.explanation: The correct matching is– Region - Republic Alakappa - Buli Kapilavastu - Shakya Pipphalivana - Moriya (Maurya) Pava - Malla Sumsumara - Bhagga

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts is it mentioned that Chetaka formed an alliance with the kings of Kashi and Kosala against Ajatashatru?
questions.explanation: According to the Jain text Niryavalika Sutta, Chetaka, the head of the Vajji confederacy, had formed an alliance with the kings of Kashi and Kosala against Ajatashatru. This alliance included 18 states of Kashi and Kosala and 18 other states, totaling 36 states. The mention of Ajatashatru's vow for the complete destruction of the Vajji confederacy is found in the Mahavagga. The conflict between Magadha and Vaishali (Vajji) lasted for 16 years, and finally, the Magadha ruler Ajatashatru emerged victorious

questions.question_text: According to the Shvetambaras, who was the female Tirthankara?
questions.explanation: According to the Shvetambara tradition, the 19th Tirthankara of Jainism, Mallinatha, whose symbol was the Kalasha (pot), was a female Tirthankara, whereas the Digambara tradition considers Mallinatha to be a male Tirthankara. The first Tirthankara of Jainism was Rishabhanatha, whose symbol was the Bull. The first historical Tirthankara of Jainism whose authenticity has been proven is the 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanatha, whose symbol is the Serpent. The last and most famous Tirthankara of Jainism was Mahavira, whose symbol is the Lion

questions.question_text: Which group of monks held hostile feelings towards the Buddha?
