questions.explanation: Seeing the growing popularity of the Buddha in contemporary society and the attraction of the general public towards his religion, some people became jealous of the Buddha. Such people were both inside the Buddhist Sangha and outside it. The Buddha's first strong opponent was Devadatta. In addition to him, opposition was also carried out by the Shadvargiya monks. These monks never followed the rules of the Sangha. They were insolent and undisciplined

questions.question_text: Vaipulya Sutra is related to:
questions.explanation: Vaipulya Sutra is a text written in the Sanskrit language regarding Buddhist beliefs. It consists of nine texts in which the rules of Buddhism are described. It is a historical text of Sri Lanka. This book is related to the Mahayana sect

questions.question_text: Stupas where the physical/bodily remains of Buddha or his main disciples were kept were known as;
questions.explanation: At the time of Buddha's attainment of Nirvana, there was great ambiguity in his sect regarding his body. Stupas are among the best monuments of the post-Mauryan period. Based on the structure of the stupas and their purposes, they are divided into the following four parts– Stupa - Nature 1. Sharirika - Remains of the body of Buddha or monks. 2. Paribhojika - Objects used by Buddha or monks. 3. Uddeshika - For the fulfillment of a purpose. 4. Pujarthaka/Samkalpita - Small stupas made for worship.

questions.question_text: 'Girivraja' was at one time the capital of which Mahajanapada?
questions.explanation: The ancient capital of the Magadha dynasty was Girivraja. This capital was identified by different names from the time of Jarasandha of the Mahabharata era until the Maurya dynasty. The city of Girivraja was established by Vasuraja on the banks of the Ganges. Jarasandha, the son of Brihadratha, established the terror of Magadha over all states with his immense power and gave his state the form of a vast empire

questions.question_text: Which of the following places is not related to Gautama Buddha?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha was born in 563 BCE in Lumbini. He was a prince of the Shakya clan. He renounced his home at the age of 29, which was called Mahabhinishkramana. Gautama Buddha was endowed with 32 great-man qualities from birth. Gautama Buddha's life spanned 80 years, during which he established places for his teachings, penance, and residence in many locations, including Sarnath, Kushinagar, Bodh Gaya, Shravasti, etc Sarnath - First sermon, Bodh Gaya - Attainment of knowledge, Kushinagar - Death. Note - Pawapuri is related to the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, Mahavira Swami.

questions.question_text: Who among the following destroyed the Licchavi Republic?
questions.explanation: Ajatashatru was known by the name Kunika; he carried forward his father's imperialist policy. He defeated Kosala and married Prasenajit's daughter Vajira. It is believed that he broke the power of the confederacy of the Licchavi republic. With the help of his ministers Sunidha and Vassakara, he succeeded in creating a rift in this confederacy and then destroyed it. According to the Bhagavati Sutra, Ajatashatru defeated the confederacy of 9 Licchavis, 9 Mallas, and 18 republics of Kashi-Kosala. According to the Puranas, his closest successor was Darshaka. However, Jain and Buddhist writers consider Udayin as his successor. Udayin is credited with laying the foundation of Kusumapura or Pataliputra

questions.question_text: The study of God and religious subjects is called ______________.
questions.explanation: Maharishi Jaimini, in the twelve chapters of Dharmamimamsa, analyzed the rituals prescribed by the Vedas. Maharishi Kashyap, in the four chapters of Daivata Mimamsa, sequentially analyzed the nature of deities, their types, their worship, and the fruits of their worship. Karma is the means (sadhya) and Brahman is the proven (siddha) Dharma. Daivata Mimamsa is the link connecting the means-Dharma with the proven-Dharma. By contemplating the means-Karma as ritual and the proven-Karma as Dharma in every field of life, a practitioner is able to fully develop his essential knowledge and experience his inherent eternal Dharma

questions.question_text: Which of the following dynasties did not contribute to the rise of the Magadha Empire?
questions.explanation: There is a difference of opinion between the Puranas and Buddhist texts regarding the first dynasty to rule over the Magadha state. According to the Mahabharata and Puranas, the primary dynasty of Magadha was the Brihadratha dynasty, and later the Haryanka dynasty, Shishunaga dynasty, Nanda dynasty, and Maurya dynasty were leaders in its contribution. The extent of the Magadha state was in the south of present-day Bihar. To its north was the Ganges, to the west the Son, to the east the Champa river, and to the south were the ranges of the Vindhya mountains. Magadha remained a leader in the supremacy of imperialism

questions.question_text: To which dynasty did Bimbisara belong?
questions.explanation: Bimbisara was initially the commander of the Licchavis. In the Suttanipata, Vaishali, the city of the Licchavis, is called Magadhapurama. People of the Haryanka clan were a sub-branch of a branch of the Nagavansha, whose founder was Bimbisara. He was called the real founder of the Magadha empire. According to Jain literature, Bimbisara's name is found as 'Shrenika'

questions.question_text: According to the Puranas, Jain, and Buddhist texts, to which Varna do they relate Mahapadma Nanda?
questions.explanation: According to the Mahabodhivamsa, the ten sons of Kalashoka of the Shishunaga dynasty ruled collectively for 22 years. Probably Mahapadma Nanda was their protector. Mahapadma Nanda was the founder of the Nanda dynasty. In the Puranas, he is said to be Shudragarbhodbhava, meaning born from the womb of a Shudra mother. The Avashyaka Sutra of Jain sources calls him Napita-dasa (slave of a barber) and the Parishishtaparvan declares him the son of a barber father and a courtesan mother

questions.question_text: What is Mahapadma Nanda not described as in the Puranas?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Nanda dynasty, Mahapadma Nanda, was a Shudra ruler. He had assumed the titles of Ekarat and Ekachhatra. In the Puranas, Nanda is called Sarvakshatrantaka, the destroyer of Kshatriyas, and the incarnation of Parashurama. Among his titles, Amitraghata is not one; that was the name of Bindusara, who was a ruler of the Maurya dynasty

questions.question_text: During the reign of which king did 36 republics, including Vajji and Malla, form a confederacy and start a war with Magadha?
questions.explanation: According to Jain texts, Ajatashatru broke the group of eastern countries which included Kashi, Kosala, and the neighboring republics there, as well as nine Mallas and nine Licchavis. Conquering the Licchavis was not an easy task. They were the leaders of a vast confederacy of 36 states and relied on their combined strength. It is said that to attack them, Ajatashatru used heavy weapons named Mahashilakantaka and Rathamusala. He fought continuously for 16 years to conquer the Vaishali grand-confederacy

questions.question_text: Under the reign of which king was Anga annexed to Magadha?
questions.explanation: Bimbisara conquered the state of Anga and merged it into the Magadha empire and appointed his son Ajatashatru as the ruler there. The capital of the Magadha state was initially Girivraja (Rajgriha). Special Fact– According to Dr. Raychaudhuri, "With Bimbisara's conquest of Anga, that policy of conquest and expansion of Magadha began which ended with Ashoka's conquest of Kalinga."

questions.question_text: The First Buddhist Council (483 BCE) was organized under the patronage of which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Ajatashatru– Ajatashatru was a king of the Haryanka dynasty who became emperor after killing his father. He is also known by the names Kunika and Ashoka Chanda. In the same year after the Parinirvana of Mahatma Buddha, 483 BCE, Ajatashatru organized the First Buddhist Council in the Saptaparni Cave of Rajgriha. It was presided over by Mahakassapa. In this council, the Sutta Pitaka was compiled by Ananda and the Vinaya Pitaka by Upali

questions.question_text: Which of these dynasties was the first non-Kshatriya dynasty to come to power in Magadha?
questions.explanation: The Nanda dynasty (344 BCE - 322 BCE) was established by Mahapadma Nanda. According to the Puranas, he was a Shudra ruler. He was the most powerful ruler of the Nanda dynasty. In the Mahabodhivamsa, the name of Mahapadma Nanda is found as Ugrasena. In the Vishnu Purana, Mahapadma Nanda is called Sarvakshatrantaka (destroyer of all Kshatriyas) and Bhargava (incarnation of the second Parashurama). He had assumed the titles of Ekarat, Ekachhatra, and 'Kali ka Ansha' (part of Kali)

questions.question_text: Which of the following metals was responsible for the second urbanization in India?
questions.explanation: The second urbanization in India is considered to be from the 6th century BCE. At this time, with the proper use of iron, deep ploughing of fields began, which increased agricultural production and led to the emergence of the second urbanization. The Harappan period is considered the first urbanization. Ram Sharan Sharma has called the "sixth century BCE an urban revolution."

questions.question_text: 'Bhagavati Sutra' is related to which of the following religions?
questions.explanation: The Bhagavati Sutra describes the life characters of Jain Tirthankaras, mainly Mahavira Swami, and their relations with other contemporaries (such as Makkhali Gosala). Through dialogue with his favorite disciple Indrabhuti, it contains the exposition of Jain principles, heaven-hell, 16 Mahajanapadas, etc

questions.question_text: Identify the correct option of those six elements from which, according to Jain philosophy, the creation was formed:

options.A: Jiva, Pudgala, Dharma, Kala, Vayu, and Agni
options.B: Jiva, Pudgala, Kala, Akasha, Dharma, and Adharma
options.C: Jiva, Pudgala, Vayu, Bhumi, Akasha, and Agni
options.D: Jiva, Pudgala, Vayu, Dharma, Prithvi, and Agni

questions.explanation: According to Jainism, this world is made up of six elements. These six elements are– Jiva, Pudgala, Dharma, Adharma, Akasha, Kala. They believe that this world has always existed and will always exist in the future

questions.question_text: Who among the following thinkers of the Buddha's time is considered a complete materialist?
questions.explanation: Other religious movements before the birth of Buddha Sr.No. - Sect - Founder (1) Nityavadi - Pakudha Kacchayana (2) Ghora Akriyavadi - Purana Kassapa (3) Uchchedavadi (Materialist) - Ajita Kesakambali (4) Sandehavadi (Agnostic, Skeptic) - Sanjaya Belatthiputta (5) Ajivika Sect (Fatalist) - Makkhali Gosala

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mahajanapada and their capital pairs are not matched?
questions.explanation: The 'Jana' in the Rigvedic period took the form of 'Janapada' in the later Vedic period and 'Mahajanapada' in the 6th century. At that time there were 16 Mahajanapadas which are mentioned in the Buddhist religious text Anguttara Nikaya and the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra. On the other hand, there is mention of 22 Mahajanapadas in Panini's Ashtadhyayi Mahajanapada - Capital Kashi - Varanasi Kosala - Shravasti/Kushavati Anga - Champa Magadha - Girivraja (Rajgriha) Vajji - Videha/Mithila Malla - Pava and Kushinara Chedi - Shuktimati Vatsa - Kaushambi Kuru - Indraprastha Panchala - Kampilya & Ahichhatra Matsya - Virat Nagar Shurasena - Mathura Asmaka (Ashmaka) - Paithan Avanti - Mahishmati & Ujjayini Gandhara - Taxila Kamboja - Hataka/Rajpur

questions.question_text: Which one is not correct regarding the transformations that took place in North India in the 6th century BCE?
questions.explanation: While R.S. Sharma called the 6th century BCE the period of urban revolution, on the other hand, G.C. Pande called it the Age of Awakening. In fact, this century was a century of intellectual turmoil. In this century, many sects came into existence in India, among which only Buddhism and Jainism became more famous

questions.question_text: Where did Mahatma Buddha first grant permission for women to enter the Buddhist Sangha?
questions.explanation: Initially, Buddha was against the entry of women into the religion. Finally, in the 5th year of religious preaching and the establishment of the Bhikkhu Sangha, the question of women's entry into the Sangha first arose in Kapilavastu due to the plea of Gautami Prajapati. On the plea of Gautami and mainly on the insistence of Ananda, Buddha granted permission for women to enter the Sangha in Vaishali and established the Bhikkhuni Sangha. The first woman to enter the Sangha was Prajapati Gautami, followed by Yashodhara, Nanda, and Amrapali

questions.question_text: Kangyur and Tengyur are–

options.D: Collection of oral history of ancient China

questions.explanation: Kangyur and Tengyur are a translated collection of the discourses given by Buddha, which is a major text of Buddhist literature. It is a religious text of Tibet. It was composed by Taranatha. In this text, the teachings and instructions of Buddha are described systematically

questions.question_text: Which statement is false about Banaras (Varanasi), which is one of the ancient cities of India?

options.A: The first mention of Varanasi occurred in the Atharvaveda as the capital of the Kashi state.
options.B: Kashi was a Janapada in the Mahajanapada period.
options.D: Bimbisara obtained Kashi by fighting a war with the Kosala ruler Prasenajit.

questions.explanation: The history of the antiquity of Kashi is obtained from Vedic literature. The description of Kashi is found in all three levels of Vedic literature: Samhita, Brahmana, and Upanishad. The first mention of Kashi occurred in the Pippalada branch of the Atharvaveda. In ancient times, Kashi was famous as a Janapada and Varanasi was its capital. Mention of Kashi is also found in the accounts of Chinese travelers, Buddhist literature, Jain literature, Mahabharata, Ramayana, Rigveda, Puranas, and Jataka stories. Bimbisara obtained the Kashi Janapada not by fighting a war with the Kashi ruler Prasenajit, but as a gift (dowry)

questions.question_text: Which one is not correctly matched? Events of Buddha's life - Symbol
questions.explanation: The symbol of Gautama Buddha's renunciation of home or Mahabhinishkramana is the Horse (Ashva). It is described in the Buddhist text Lalitavistara that Gautama Buddha, leaving his wife Yashodhara and son Rahula sleeping, left the city of Kapilavastu at midnight riding a horse named Kanthaka. After this, Gautama had ordered his servant Chandaka or Channa to take the horse back. That is why the event of Buddha's Mahabhinishkramana (the great renunciation) is expressed by the Horse. In the above question, footprints are known for Nirvana and the Stupa for Mahaparinirvana

questions.question_text: Which one is correctly matched? Modern site - Mahajanapada period city
questions.explanation: Charsadda– This district is located in modern Pakistan. Pushkalavati, the capital of Taxila, was also located in this district Sahet-Mahet– The remains of ancient Shravasti have been found at modern places named 'Sahet-Mahet'. Here, Sahet is identified with Jetavana and Mahet with the ancient city of Shravasti. Kampil– Kampilya or Kampil is related to the Mahajanapada era. It used to be the capital of the Panchala Janapada, which is located in the area of the Ganges river between Badaun and Farrukhabad in modern Uttar Pradesh. Rajghat– The confirmation of the discovery of modern Varanasi is considered to be from Rajghat, which is one of its ancient sites.

questions.question_text: Considering the following statements in the context of Jainism, select the false one:

options.A: The Shvetambara tradition accepts that a woman can attain salvation (moksha) in her lifetime.
options.B: A Jain nun was obliged to give formal respect to any Jain monk, no matter how junior he was.
options.C: Whether the 19th Tirthankara Mallinatha was male or female is a dispute.
options.D: According to the Kalpasutra, at the time Mahavira attained Nirvana, the number of Jain nuns was much less than the Jain monks.

questions.explanation: As for the question of Jain nuns in Jainism, if we follow the traditional Jain accounts, then the dominance of women is seen. According to the Kalpasutra, at the time Mahavira died, there were 14,000 monks, 36,000 Jain nuns, 159,000 Jain male lay-worshippers, and 318,000 Jain female lay-worshippers. During his lifetime, while 1400 women attained Nirvana, only 700 men did. Jain nuns played an important role in attracting the general class of women towards Jainism

questions.question_text: Read the following statements about the economic life of the Mahajanapada period– (i) In Pali texts, the term Gahapati has been used for that wealthy person who was engaged in craft and manufacturing activities. (ii) In Pali texts, the term Setthi has been used for a high-level businessman who was associated with commerce and money-lending. Select the correct code:
questions.explanation: During the Mahajanapada period, the literal meaning of Gahapati was the head of the household, but in Pali texts, a Gahapati was not merely the master of the house but a wealthy person as a unit of production who was engaged in agriculture as well as crafts and manufacturing. In the same sequence, traders located in rural areas and sometimes in cities were also called Sethi or Gahapati-Sethi. This class belonged to a high professional class who also performed the work of commerce and money-lending

questions.question_text: Read the following statements about the republics of the Mahajanapada period- (i) In all republics, power was in the hands of the aristocrats. (ii) Most of the republics were located in the foothills of the Himalayas. Select the correct code:
questions.explanation: During the Mahajanapada period, the entire power in the republics was in the hands of the tribal aristocratic system, which had become hereditary. In the Shakya and Lichchhavi republics, the ruling class belonged to a single family and a single class, whereas in monarchies, people of many varnas were included in the ruling class. During the Mahajanapada period, most of the janapadas were located in the foothills of the Himalayas, such as Panchala, Asmaka, Kosala, Vajji, Malla etc

questions.question_text: Which metal was used in the Purana or Dharana type of currency?
questions.explanation: Purana or Dharana were pre-Mauryan and Mauryan punch-marked coins which were made of silver. The words Purana and Dharana have been used in Manusmriti for punch-marked coins. Kautilya used the word 'Pana' and Katyayana used the word 'Prati' for punch-marked coins. Pana, Karshapana, Rupyaroopa, Dharana etc. were silver punch-marked coins. Suvarna and Nishka were gold punch-marked coins, while Mashaka and Kakini were copper punch-marked coins

questions.question_text: 'Pushkalavati' was the capital of which state?
questions.explanation: Gandhara was located in the areas of modern Peshawar and Rawalpindi. Its capital Taxila was a famous center of education and trade in ancient times. It is known from the Ramayana that this city was established by Bharata's son Taksha. The second major city of this Janapada was Pushkalavati. In the 6th century BC, 'Pushkarasarin' used to rule in Gandhara. He had defeated Chandrapradyota, the ruler of Avanti

questions.question_text: Reliable information about the Andhra and Shishunaga dynasties is found in
questions.explanation: We get knowledge about many dynasties, names of kings and their ruling periods from Vishnu Purana, Matsya Purana, Vayu Purana and Bhagavata Purana. Matsya Purana is considered the most ancient and old Purana, in which very important knowledge regarding the Andhra dynasty and Shishunaga dynasty is obtained. Puranas are considered the religious pillars of Indian culture

questions.question_text: Considering the following statements in the context of the Hakamani (Achaemenid) dynasty, select the correct answer from the given codes:
questions.explanation: The last Persian (Iranian) emperor was Darius III. The war took place between Alexander and Darius III in 331 BC at Arbela (Gaugamela). In this war, Alexander severely defeated Darius III and ended Persian power from India. Arbela (Gaugamela) was located in the modern Iraq-Kurdistan region. Behistun, Persepolis, Naksh-e-Rustum and Hamadan inscriptions belong to the reign of Darius I

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians was contemporary to Alexander?
questions.explanation: The contemporary historians of Alexander were Nearchus, Aristobulus and Onesicritus. Ctesias, Herodotus, Scylax etc. were historians before Alexander, while Megasthenes, Deimachus, Justin, Pliny, Plutarch etc. are historians after Alexander. Among these historians, Megasthenes has an important place, based on whose book 'Indica', later historians Strabo, Pliny, Justin etc. composed their books

questions.question_text: Ashva[ghosha] was in the court of ________.
questions.explanation: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kundalvan (Kashmir) during the reign of the Kushan ruler Kanishka. According to historian Taranath, it was held in Jalandhar (Punjab). This council was presided over by Vasumitra, while the responsibility of Vice President was performed by Ashvaghosha (Ashva). In this council, Buddhism was divided into two sects named Hinayana and Mahayana

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was not an ancient Indian Mahajanapada?
questions.explanation: Suvarnagiri was not among the 16 ancient Indian Mahajanapadas. Suvarnagiri (Mountain of Gold) is a historical site located in the Koppal district of the state of Karnataka, India. It is also called Kanakagiri

questions.question_text: In the 6th century BC, which of these 4 towns ultimately remained? 1. Anga 2. Avanti 3. Vatsa 4. Kosala 5. Kashi 6. Magadha 7. Kuru 8. Gandhara Select the correct answer group:
questions.explanation: Evidence of Kosala, Avanti, Vatsa and Magadha is found in the 6th century BC; therefore, evidence of only these 4 towns ultimately remaining is found. Its correct sequence is- 2, 3, 4, 6 Note- The DSSSB board has accepted option (d) as the answer.

questions.question_text: Join the given philosophies with their creators: Philosophy / Founder A. Nyaya Philosophy / 1. Kapila B. Samkhya Philosophy / 2. Patanjali C. Vaisheshika Philosophy / 3. Badarayana D. Yoga Philosophy / 4. Jaimini E. Purva Mimamsa / 5. Gautama F. Uttara Mimamsa / 6. Kanada Rishi A B C D E F
questions.explanation: Philosophy / Founder A. Nyaya Philosophy / i. Gautama B. Samkhya Philosophy / ii. Kapila C. Vaisheshika Philosophy / iii. Kanada Rishi D. Yoga Philosophy / iv. Patanjali E. Purva Mimamsa / v. Jaimini F. Uttara Mimamsa / vi. Badarayana

questions.question_text: Very ancient coins did not exist before ________.
questions.explanation: Very ancient coins in India are considered to be from the 5th to 6th century BC, which are called punch-marked coins. Actually, punch-marked coins are first found in the same period as Mahatma Buddha, which was the period of second urbanization in the Ganga Valley

questions.question_text: Match the following- List I / List II A. Vedanta Sutra / 1. Jaimini B. Vaisheshika Sutra / 2. Patanjali C. Yoga Sutra / 3. Badarayana D. Purva Mimamsa / 4. Kanada A B C D
questions.explanation: A. Vedanta Sutra / 3. Badarayana B. Vaisheshika Sutra / 4. Kanada C. Yoga Sutra / 2. Patanjali D. Purva Mimamsa / 1. Jaimini

questions.question_text: With which of the following can Basarh be identified?
questions.explanation: Basarh is identified with ancient Vaishali. Vaishali is a city in the Ganga Valley. It is located in the state of Bihar. Another name for this city was also Vishala. It is believed that it was established by a king named 'Nabhanedishta' of the Ikshvaku dynasty. It is included among the main tourist destinations of Bihar. Lord Mahavira was born in the Jhatrika clan of Kundagrama near Vaishali

questions.question_text: By what name is the oldest coin found in the Indian subcontinent known?
questions.explanation: The oldest coins found in the Indian subcontinent are called punch-marked (panch-marka) coins. Many types of symbols are engraved on these coins and there is no writing of any kind. The exact meaning of these symbols has not been understood. Besides kings, these coins were probably also issued by traders, merchant guilds, and city corporations

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of the last four Tirthankaras and their symbols is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Mahavira - Lion Arishtanemi - Conch Nemi - Blue Lotus Parshvanath was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism; his symbol was the "Serpent hood". * Mention of the first Tirthankara of Jainism, Rishabhanath/Adinath, and Arishtanemi (22nd) is found in the Rigveda.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Tripitakas are the oldest texts of Buddhism.
options.B: In Abhidhamma Pitaka, essentially the same topics are discussed as are found in Sutta Pitaka.
options.C: Vinaya Pitaka contains a collection of philosophical concepts inherent in Buddha's teachings.

questions.explanation: Tripitaka - It is the ancient text of Buddhism. It contains a collection of Buddha's teachings and sermons, divided into three parts (Pitakas) (1) Vinaya Pitaka - This is part of the Tripitaka. It is mainly based on monks and nuns. It has detailed descriptions of rules and discipline. (2) Sutta Pitaka - Its meaning is religious discourse. It is a collection of Buddha's religious thoughts and sermons. Its number is 5. (a) Digha Nikaya (b) Majjhima Nikaya (c) Samyutta Nikaya (d) Anguttara Nikaya (e) Khuddaka Nikaya (Anguttara) Nikaya (mention of 16 Mahajanapadas of ancient India) - in this, Buddha has given sermons to the monks. (3) Abhidhamma Pitaka - It contains a collection of philosophical principles.

questions.question_text: Consider the following: Included under the texts named Dharmashastra are: 2. Smritis 3. Commentaries on Smritis 4. Nibandha texts 1. Dharmasutras
questions.explanation: Dharmasutras, Smritis, Bhashya, Nibandha and commentaries on Smritis are collectively called Dharmashastra. The period of Dharmasutras is generally determined to be around 500 - 200 BC. The first description of the Varna system is found in the Dharmasutras. The Dharmasutras of Apastamba, Baudhayana and Gautama are considered the most ancient

questions.question_text: In which Jain text is the mention of sixteen Mahajanapadas found?
questions.explanation: The mention of sixteen Mahajanapadas is found in the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra. Apart from this, the mention of 16 Mahajanapadas is also found in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya. Among these 16 Mahajanapadas, 14 were monarchies and 2 were republics (Vajji and Malla)

questions.question_text: Match the following republics/kingdoms and their capitals: List-I / List-II A. Gandhara / 1. Mathura B. Anga / 2. Taxila D. Kosala / 4. Champa A B C D C. Shurasena / 3. Shravasti
questions.explanation: The matched pairs are as follows Gandhara - Taxila (currently some areas of Afghanistan and Pakistan) Anga - Champa (currently in Bihar) Shurasena - Mathura (U.P.) Kosala - Shravasti (U.P.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true?

options.A: Sthaviravada is a sect of Jains.
options.B: Nikaya texts are associated with Buddhism.
options.C: Early Buddhist texts were written in the Pali language.
options.D: Mahavira gave his sermons in Ardhamagadhi.

questions.explanation: The ruler of Magadha, Kalashoka, organized the Second Buddhist Council in Vaishali during his reign. In this, a split occurred in the Buddhist Sangha and it was divided into two sects (1) Sthaviravada (2) Mahasanghika That is, Sthaviravada is related to Buddhism and not to Jainism.

questions.question_text: The Vajji Mahajanapada was a union of how many clans?
questions.explanation: The 16 Mahajanapadas mentioned in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya and Jain text Bhagavati Sutra had two types of states (1) Monarchy (2) Republic In this, 14 were under monarchy and 2 were under republic; the republics were Vajji and Malla. Vajji was a union of eight clans. It was a powerful union during the time of Buddha. Ajatashatru, with the help of Buddha, defeated the Vajji union and merged it into the Magadha Empire.

questions.question_text: Ancient statues of Gautama Buddha were often made in ________ in one period.
questions.explanation: Ancient statues of Gautama Buddha were made in Mathura and Gandhara at the same time. The maximum number of Buddha statues was created under the Gandhara style

questions.question_text: Which scholar is considered the Luther of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Nagarjuna is called the Luther of Buddhism. He went to China in the first century AD and translated Buddhist works into the Chinese language

questions.question_text: Where did Mahavira attain the highest spiritual knowledge (Kevalya)?
questions.explanation: After rigorous penance, during the fourth quarter of the tenth day of the bright half of the month of Vaishakha, in Jrimbhika village of Magadha, on the banks of the Rijupalika river, in a cow-milking posture (Goduh Aasana), Mahavira remained in a meditative state for twelve years, 5 months and 15 days, then he attained spiritual knowledge (Kevalya)

questions.question_text: By which great Acharya was Jainism brought to South India?
questions.explanation: Bhadrabahu brought Jainism to South India. Bhadrabahu and his followers were called Digambara; they were called Southern Jains

questions.question_text: Where did Mahavira attain Nirvana?
questions.explanation: Lord Mahavira attained Nirvana (salvation) on Kartika Krishna Amavasya in 527 BC at the age of 72 in Pawapuri (Rajgriha), Bihar. A Water Temple (Jal Mandir) is located in Pawapuri, about which it is said that this is the place where Mahavira Swami attained salvation

questions.question_text: Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon in ________.
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon to five Brahmins (Kaundinya, Assaji, Vappa, Anja, Bhaddiya) in Mrigadava (Sarnath) of Rishipattanam. This religious discourse is known as Dharma Chakra Pravartana. This is represented by a wheel with a deer in Buddhist art

questions.question_text: The first king who was a follower of Buddhism is
questions.explanation: The first ruling follower of Buddhism was King Bimbisara, the founder of the Haryanka dynasty. He was a patron and friend of Buddha. His wife Khema was also a follower of Buddha. The First Buddhist Council was held in the Saptaparni cave (Rajgriha) under the patronage of the Haryanka dynasty ruler Ajatashatru, which was presided over by Mahakashyapa

questions.question_text: By which council was the Abhidhamma Pitaka organized?
questions.explanation: After the death of Gautama Buddha, 4 Buddhist councils were organized respectively. The Third Buddhist Council was held in Pataliputra under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka, presided over by 'Moggaliputta Tissa'. In this same council, the 'Abhidhamma Pitaka' was composed by Moggaliputta Tissa

questions.question_text: Match the events given below: Council / Place A. I Buddhist Council / 1. Vaishali B. II Buddhist Council / 2. Rajgriha C. III Buddhist Council / 3. Pataliputra D. IV Buddhist Council / 4. Kashmir A B C D
questions.explanation: Council / Place First Buddhist Council - Rajgriha Second Buddhist Council - Vaishali Third Buddhist Council - Pataliputra Fourth Buddhist Council - Kashmir

questions.question_text: The follower of Gautama Buddha, who was present in Kushinagar in the context of his demise, is
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha's disciple Ananda was with him in Kushinagar at the time of his demise

questions.question_text: Where did Mahavira Swami establish the four-fold Sangha?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami established the four-fold Sangha in Pawa (Bihar). Mahavira Swami established the four Tirthas- Shravaka, Shravika, Sadhu, Sadhvi after attaining 'Kevalya' at the age of 42 years

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers were patrons of Jainism? (1) Shishunaga (2) Kharavela (3) Chandragupta Maurya
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya dynasty, and Kharavela, the ruler of Kalinga, provided patronage to Jainism

questions.question_text: Where did Gautama Buddha attain Mahaparinirvana?
questions.explanation: Buddha's Mahaparinirvana took place in the Malla republic of Kushinagar (Kushinara) at the age of 80 years in 483 BC

questions.question_text: The most important philosophical text of the Mahayana sect is:
questions.explanation: The most important philosophical text of the Mahayana sect is Prajnaparamita. Mahayana was a supporter of the concept of Trikaya (Dharmakaya, Nirmanakaya, Sambhogakaya) and Sukhavati (Heaven). There was special development of the principles of Paramitas and Bhumis in Mahayana

questions.question_text: For what is Nagarjunakonda, located in Andhra Pradesh, famous?
questions.explanation: Nagarjunakonda, located in Andhra Pradesh, is named after the famous Acharya Nagarjuna of the Mahayana branch of Buddhism. In the first century, there was the kingdom of Satavahana kings here. A Satavahana king named Hala had built a Vihara on the Shri Parvata peak for Acharya Nagarjuna; information about this is obtained from the inscriptions found there. It is a famous Buddhist monastery

questions.question_text: Where are the famous Ajanta caves?
questions.explanation: The Ajanta caves are Buddhist monument caves made by cutting about 30 rocks located in the Western Ghats region, which date back to the second century BC. Excellent examples of painting and craftsmanship related to Buddhism are found here. These caves are located near a village named Ajanta, which is in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a part of the Triratna (Three Jewels) of Jainism?
questions.explanation: The Triratna of Jainism are Samyak Drishti (Right Vision/Faith), Samyak Gyana (Right Knowledge) and Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct). In this, unmarried life is not included as a part of the Triratna

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: Bhikshu - One who lives on the alms of the king
options.C: Grihastha - Performer of religious rituals in temples

questions.explanation: Parivrajakas were seekers of truth who did not stay permanently at one place; they left their homes and kept wandering from village to village and from village to the forest. There they were called Parivrajaka (traveler) or Bhikshu. Among these Parivrajakas, Vardhamana Mahavira, Gautama Buddha, and Makkhali Gosala became very famous

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to Buddhism: 1. According to it, Varna was a man-made system. 2. For persons wishing to enter the Sangha, Varna and caste were irrelevant. Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. During the time of Buddha, the caste system was firmly established in India. Buddha condemned it and considered it an injustice. To join the Buddhist Sangha, any monk had to take Sanyasa (renunciation), for which he had to renounce his worldly identity and become a monk, which also involved renouncing caste. Entry into the Sangha was open to people of all castes and Varnas

questions.question_text: To which of the following universities is the credit for the propagation of Buddhism in Tibet given?
questions.explanation: The spread of Buddhism in Tibet took place between 1 BC - 1 AD. Along with Buddhist scholars, Buddhist educational institutions also contributed to the spread of Buddhism in Tibet, among which Nalanda and Vikramshila located in Bihar and Jagaddala educational institution located in Bengal (now Bangladesh) have been prominent

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Yogachara (Vijnanavada) sect in the third century AD?
questions.explanation: Yogachara (Vijnanavada) is a branch of Mahayana Buddhism whose founder was Maitreya (Maitreyanatha). Yogachara explains how our mind constructs our experiences. According to it, there is no source of sensation outside the mind

questions.question_text: Vaibhashika and Sautrantika are major sects of:
questions.explanation: There are two sects of Hinayana Buddhism - Vaibhashika and Sautrantika. The Vaibhashika doctrine originated in Kashmir, and the main basis of the Sautrantika doctrine is the Sutta Pitaka. Sautrantika believes in the existence of both the mind (internal) and the external world

questions.question_text: Who among the following does not represent Bengal Vaishnavism?

options.C: Jayadeva, the author of Gita Govinda

questions.explanation: Aurobindo Ghosh was a yogi and philosopher. In his youth, he participated in the freedom struggle as a revolutionary, but later he became a yogi and established an ashram in Pondicherry

questions.question_text: Which of the following states was not included in the 16 Mahajanapadas?
questions.explanation: Description of 16 Mahajanapadas of ancient India is obtained from the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya. Among these Mahajanapadas, Anga, Magadha, Kashi, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti, Ashmaka, Surasena, etc., were prominent. Kalinga was not included in the 16 Mahajanapadas. Later, all Mahajanapadas were unified under the leadership of Magadha

questions.question_text: Which of the following philosophies has similarity with Jain philosophy?
questions.explanation: Samkhya philosophy has similarity with Jainism. Both Jainism and Samkhya philosophy are among the oldest philosophies in the world. Samkhya philosophy believes that the origin of the world is not from God but from the union of Purusha and Prakriti. This is called Satkaryavada. They have given the theory of Triguna - Satguna, Rajguna, and Tamguna

questions.question_text: Who was the President of the fourth Buddhist Council?
questions.explanation: 585 years after the death of Buddha, in 102 AD, during the reign of Kanishka, the fourth Buddhist Council was organized in Kundalvana, Kashmir, which was presided over by Vasumitra, while Ashvaghosha was the Vice-President. In this council, a book named Vibhashashastra was composed; at this time, Buddhists adopted the Sanskrit language

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Ajivika sect?
questions.explanation: Makkhali Putta Gosala was the proponent of the Ajivika sect. He was first a disciple of Mahavira, but due to differences, he left Mahavira and established the Ajivika sect. According to him, every thing in the world is pre-determined and controlled by destiny. Man's actions have no effect on his life

questions.question_text: What was called 'Upasampada' in the Buddhist period?
questions.explanation: In the Buddhist Sangha, Upasampada was called entering the Sangha. After giving his first sermon in Sarnath, Buddha established the Sangha with 5 Brahmin disciples. The organization of the Buddhist Sangha was based on a republican system. Renunciation of household life was called Pravrajya in the Buddhist Sangha

questions.question_text: Vasumitra and Nagarjuna were associated with the court of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Vasumitra and Nagarjuna were related to the court of Kanishka I. Nagarjuna propounded the Madhyamika Shunyavada of Buddhism, while Vasumitra presided over the fourth Buddhist Council organized in Kundalvana, Kashmir, during the time of Kanishka

questions.question_text: The beginning of the 'Kollam Era' is considered from the time of which philosopher's reforms?
questions.explanation: In 820 AD, news of Adi Shankaracharya's bodily disappearance reached Kerala a short time later. In 825 AD, the Kollam Era was started in South India (Kerala) in his memory. The beginning of the Kollam Era occurs as a reform movement

questions.question_text: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
questions.explanation: Rishabhanatha was the first Tirthankara of Jainism; there were a total of 24 Tirthankaras. Rishabhanatha was also called Adideva or Kesariyavanath. His symbol was Vrisha (Bull) Arishtanemi was the 22nd Tirthankara; he was born in Gujarat and performed penance on Girnar Mountain. His symbol was the Conch. Considering non-violence as the root of the religious view and giving it a theoretical form is his contribution. Parshvanatha was the 23rd Tirthankara; his symbol was the Serpent. His first followers were his mother (Vama) and wife Prabhavati. Mahavira Swami was the 24th and last Tirthankara.

questions.question_text: Under whose presidency was the third Buddhist Council held?
questions.explanation: There is a total of 4 mentions of Buddhist Councils, in which the first Buddhist Council was held in Rajgriha during the reign of Ajatashatru, which was presided over by Mahakassapa The second Buddhist Council was held in Vaishali under the presidency of Sabbakami (Sabakmir) during the reign of Kalashoka; the third Buddhist Council was organized in Pataliputra under the presidency of Moggaliputta Tissa during the reign of Ashoka; and the fourth Buddhist Council was completed in Kundalvana, Kashmir, under the presidency of Vasumitra during the reign of Kanishka.

questions.question_text: From which of the following places was the 23rd Jain Tirthankara associated?
questions.explanation: The 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism, Parshvanatha, was associated with Varanasi. He was born here. Mahavira Swami was born in Vaishali

questions.question_text: Which Janapada was a republican state in the 6th century BC?
questions.explanation: In the 6th century BC, Vajji was an independent republic. In the Buddhist period, it was a part of the Mahajanapadas. It was a confederacy of Licchavi republics and Vaishali was its capital. It was established by Nabhanedishtha

questions.question_text: In which of the following is the list of 16 Mahajanapadas available?
questions.explanation: The mention of 16 Mahajanapadas is found in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya. The oldest reference to Vasudeva Krishna is found in the Chandogya Upanishad

questions.question_text: How many Mahajanapadas were located in the Ganga valley?
questions.explanation: There were 10 Mahajanapadas located in the Ganga valley - Magadha, Vajji, Anga, Kashi, Vatsa, Kosala, Malla, Chedi, Panchala and Kuru, etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mahajanapadas was located on the banks of the Godavari river?
questions.explanation: Ashmaka Mahajanapada was located on the banks of the Godavari river. Its capital was Potali or Potana. It was the only Mahajanapada located in South India. This system of state was established by the rulers of the Ikshvaku dynasty

questions.question_text: In which Mahajanapada was the city of Mahishmati located?
questions.explanation: The capital of Avanti Janapada was Mahishmati, which was located on the banks of the Vetravati river. During the time of Mahabharata, the king here was Nila, whom Sahadeva defeated in battle

questions.question_text: During whose reign was the second Buddhist council held?
questions.explanation: The second Buddhist council was held in 383 BC during the reign of Kalashoka in Vaishali, which was presided over by Sabbakami (Sabakmir). The first Buddhist council was organized during the time of Ajatashatru, the third during the time of Ashoka, and the fourth Buddhist council was organized during the time of Kanishka

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of Buddha?
questions.explanation: The literal meaning of the word Buddha is 'Enlightened'. A Buddha is one who has attained Bodhi, and Bodhi means knowledge, an ideal state of intellectual and moral perfection which can be attained by man purely through human efforts. After six years of tireless hard work and severe penance, at the age of 35, on a night of Vaishakha Purnima, Siddhartha attained knowledge under a Peepal tree on the banks of the Niranjana (Punpun) river. From this day he became Tathagata. After attaining knowledge, Gautama became famous by the name 'Buddha'

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct? I. History of the Harshavardhana period is known from the description of Xuanzang (Hieun Tsang). II. Xuanzang studied in Nalanda Buddhist Vihara. III. Faxian visited India during the period of Harshavardhana. Code:
questions.explanation: At the time of Faxian's visit, it was the reign of Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' of the Gupta dynasty of India, not Harshavardhana

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Adi Shankaracharya is not correct?

options.A: The philosophy of Adi Shankaracharya is called Advaitavada.
options.B: Adi Shankaracharya considered the Vedas as the original source of real knowledge.
options.C: Adi Shankaracharya linked Bhakti with the Vedanta tradition.
options.D: Adi Shankaracharya was born in Tamil Nadu.

questions.explanation: Adi Shankaracharya was born in Kaladi (Kerala). He was a follower of the path of knowledge; his philosophy is known by the name Advaitavada. He considered the Vedas as the root source of knowledge and established the supremacy of Vedanta philosophy by defeating Kumarila Bhatta, Mandana Mishra and his wife Bharati in philosophical debate

questions.question_text: According to the Sutta Pitaka:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Both the statement and the reason are true, but the reason does not explain the statement

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct in the context of Buddhism and Jainism?

options.A: Both have the same perspective regarding the caste system.
options.B: Both advocated a simple and puritanical life.
options.C: Both Gautama Buddha and Mahavira were Kshatriyas by birth.

questions.explanation: Buddhists followed the Middle Path while Jains were puritanical. Therefore, Jainism advocates a simple and puritanical life but Buddhists follow the Middle Path

questions.question_text: Two lists are given below. List-I mentions those important events that are linked with the life of Buddha and List-II mentions the symbols linked with these events. Choose the correct option by matching both these lists among the given options: List-I
questions.explanation: Event - Symbol/Icon Birth - Lotus and Bull First Sermon - Dharma Chakra Great Renunciation - Horse Nirvana - Bodhi Tree

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered the first concrete evidence of the expansion of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: The inscriptions of Ashoka are considered the first concrete evidence of the expansion of Buddhism. In the minor rock edict of Maski related to the coronation, Ashoka has called himself 'Buddha Shakya'

questions.question_text: Consider the following: 1. Both Nalanda University and Vikramshila University developed during the Pala dynasty. 2. Both Nalanda University and Vikramshila University were destroyed by the Khalji dynasty. Which of the above statements is true?
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was established during the reign of ruler Kumaragupta of the Gupta dynasty. This university is called the 'Oxford of Mahayana Buddhism'. The Pala dynasty ruler Dharmapala established Vikramshila University in Bihar, and both universities were protected and developed during the reign of the Pala dynasty. Nalanda University and Vikramshila University were not destroyed by the Khalji dynasty (1290-1320 AD), rather they were destroyed by Qutubuddin Aibak's general Ikhtiyaruddin Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji around 1202 AD. Therefore, only statement (1) is true

questions.question_text: The establishment of Shvetambara as a separate sect in Jainism resulted in ...........
questions.explanation: In the 4th century BC, the first Jain council was held in Pataliputra, the capital of Magadha, under the presidency of Sthulabhadra. In this very council, Jainism was divided into two sects named Shvetambara and Digambara. The followers of Sthulabhadra were called Shvetambara while the followers of Bhadrabahu were called Digambara. Therefore, its correct answer will be Pataliputra. However, the Board has considered option (b) i.e., Vallabhi as correct in the answer key

questions.question_text: Which city was not known from Pali literature in the 6th century BC among the following?
questions.explanation: The cities that existed in the 6th century BC include Champa (Anga state), Rajgriha (Magadha), Shravasti/Ayodhya (Kosala), etc., while there is no mention of Bhita. Other prominent cities of the Buddhist era are Kashi (Varanasi), Kaushambi (Vatsa Janapada), Indraprastha (Kuru), Mathura (Surasena), etc

questions.question_text: From which place has the seal inscribed 'Kapilavastu Mahavihare' been obtained?
questions.explanation: Piprahwa is identified as Kapilavastu, which is related to the life of Lord Buddha. This site is located in the Terai region near the Indo-Nepal border in the Naugarh tehsil of Siddharthnagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Among the archaeological remains obtained from this site are copper bowls, plates, weights for measurement made of stone, beads of clay and stone, and a seal inscribed with 'Kapilavastu Mahavihare' has also been obtained

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I
questions.explanation: List-I List-II (a) Moriya – Pipphalivana (b) Bulli – Alakappa (c) Kalama – Kesaputta (d) Bhagga – Sumsumaragiri

questions.question_text: Jain scriptures are called:
questions.explanation: Jain literature is called Agama or Siddhanta (Jainagama). The most important among the Jain Agamas are the 12 Angas. The Acharangasutra mentions the conduct/rules for Jain monks, while the Bhagavatisutra throws some light on the life of Mahavira. Each of the 12 Angas has Upangas, and many commentaries have been written on them

questions.question_text: Who was the President of the Second Buddhist Council?
questions.explanation: Buddhist Council President Reign (a) First (Rajgriha) – Mahakassapa Ajatashatru (b) Second (Vaishali) – Sabakami Kalashoka (c) Third (Pataliputra)– Moggaliputta Tissa Ashoka (d) Fourth (Kashmir) – Vasumitra Kanishka

questions.question_text: Shishunaga was originally related to:
questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Haryanka dynasty, 'Nagadashaka', was killed by his minister Shishunaga. Shishunaga was originally a resident of Magadha. He established the Shishunaga dynasty (412-344 BC). He included Avanti and Vatsa into the Magadha Empire. He made Vaishali his capital in addition to Pataliputra. The Commission removed this question in the revised answer key

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I
questions.explanation: List-I List-II (a) Digha Nikaya – Mahaparinibbana Sutta (b) Khuddaka Nikaya – Dhammapada (c) Vinaya Pitaka – Khandhaka (d) Abhidhamma Pitaka – Kathavatthu

questions.question_text: Which of the following reasons was not responsible for the rise of cities in the sixth century BC?
questions.explanation: Reasons responsible for the rise of cities in the sixth century BC were the use of iron in eastern Uttar Pradesh and western Bihar, economic changes due to agricultural surplus, increase in commercial activities, etc. Whereas floods in the Saindhava river were responsible for the decline of the Indus civilization, not for the rise of urban civilization

questions.question_text: Which Buddhist literature provides a list of ancient scripts of India?
questions.explanation: Ancient scripts of India are described in the Buddhist literature Lalitavistara. This is a text of the Mahayana Buddhist sect; it also describes the divine plays (leelas) of Lord Buddha

questions.question_text: With which of the following is the terminology 'Dharmachakra' associated?
questions.explanation: The terminology 'Dharmachakra' is associated with Sarnath Buddhist Vihara

questions.question_text: Where among the following did the Mahasamghika sect of Buddhism originate?
questions.explanation: The Second Buddhist Council was held in Vaishali under the presidency of Sabakami (Sarvakamin) under the patronage of the Shishunaga dynasty ruler Kalashoka. The Mahasamghika sect originated in this very council. This was a group of reformist monks led by Mahakassapa, whose main center was Magadha

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): Buddhist philosophy was for 'the welfare of many and the happiness of many'. Reason (R): Buddha wanted to rid the majority of people of their troubles. Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is the wrong explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Buddhist philosophy was the promoter of 'welfare of many and happiness of many', which wanted to rid the majority of people of their troubles

questions.question_text: The 'Second Urbanization' in India is generally associated with which pottery tradition?
questions.explanation: The Second Urbanization in India connects the pottery tradition to the Northern Black Polished Ware

questions.question_text: At which place did Buddha attain Nirvana (attainment of knowledge)?
questions.explanation: In Buddhism, Nirvana means attainment of knowledge, while Mahaparinirvana means death. Buddha attained Nirvana in Bodh Gaya, while Buddha's Mahaparinirvana occurred in Kushinagar. The Commission has given the answer to this question as (c)

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a Janapada republic?
questions.explanation: The Licchavi Mahajanapada was a republic. The ruler here was Chetaka. Mahavira's mother was Chetaka's sister. Licchavi were the leaders of a large confederation of 36 states

questions.question_text: Who were the proponents of the materialist philosophy of Ucchedavada (Annihilationism) in the 6th century BC?
questions.explanation: Ajita Kesakambali was a philosopher of the Buddhist era. He gave the principle of Ucchedavada (Annihilationism). This was, in a way, complete nihilism. He called heaven and hell imaginary. The belief of this principle was that Homa, Yajna, charity, and penance are all useless. He is also considered the "proponent of the materialist philosophy" of Ucchedavada

questions.question_text: Which of the following materialist philosophical sects of ancient India laid the foundation of physics in India?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Vaisheshika philosophy was Rishi Kanada. Among the materialist philosophical sects, the foundation of physics was laid in India through this philosophy. According to this philosophy, the physical world is composed of five great elements (earth, water, fire, air, and ether). The principle of the five basic elements is based on the sensation of our five sense organs

questions.question_text: Which of the following was added by Mahavira to the already existing basic tenets of Jainism?

options.B: Achaurya (Not taking any property of others)
options.C: Aparigraha (Keeping no property of one's own)

questions.explanation: There were a total of 24 Tirthankaras in Jainism; among them, the first was Rishabhanatha and the 24th Tirthankara was Mahavira Swami. Mahavira Swami is considered the actual founder of Jainism. The Tirthankaras before him believed in four great vows—Truth, Non-violence, Non-possession, and Non-stealing (Achaurya). Mahavira added the fifth great vow, Brahmacharya (vow of celibacy), to these

questions.question_text: From which of the following Mahajanapadas was the Persian army fighting against the Greeks supplied with men and material?
questions.explanation: Before the Greeks, the Gandhara Janapada was a part of the Hakamani (Achaemenid) or Persian Empire. The Persian army fighting in the war against the Greeks was supplied with men and material from this very Mahajanapada

questions.question_text: In which of the following Puranas has Buddha been included in the list of incarnations of Vishnu?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha is considered an incarnation of Lord Vishnu in the Vaishnava sect of Hindus. Among the ten incarnations described in religion, Buddha is currently considered the ninth incarnation. In the future, the final incarnation will be Kalki. Buddha has been mentioned in all major Puranas and all important Hindu texts. In his Puranas, Buddha is considered an incarnation of Vishnu, such as—Agni Purana, Bhagavata, Matsya, Garuda Purana, Vishnu, Naradiya Purana

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Tirthankara) with List-II (Special Cognizance (Emblem)): List-I
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Adinatha - Bull (Vrishabha) Mallinatha - Water-pot (Kalasha) Mahavira - Lion (Simha) Parshvanatha - Serpent There were a total of 24 Tirthankaras in Jainism. All Tirthankaras are identified by their different symbols. The symbols of other Tirthankaras are as follows- Ajitanatha - Elephant Arishtanemi - Conch Neminatha - Blue Lotus

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Stupa is correct?
questions.explanation: The development of the stupa probably occurred from such earthen mounds which were constructed over the pyre of the deceased or to keep the collected bones of the deceased. The practice of constructing stupas is considered to be from the pre-Buddhist period. Stupas were also constructed at places associated with major events of Gautama Buddha's life, birth, enlightenment (Sambodhi), turning the wheel of law (Dharmachakra Pravartana), and Nirvana. Later, Jains also had such stupas constructed as monuments in the early period

questions.question_text: According to the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra, how many republics of Kashi and Kosala were part of the powerful confederation of Eastern India that opposed King Ajatashatru of Magadha?
questions.explanation: Bhagavati Sutra is the most important text of Jainism. In addition to the principles of Jainism, it contains a detailed description of heaven and hell. In Bhagavati Sutra, 15 Karmabhumis are mentioned, including five Bharata, five Airavata, and five Mahavideha. Along with birth in the Karmabhumi, the Kulakara system began, which taught the basic rules of discipline of society. According to the Bhagavati Sutra, 18 republics of Kashi and Kosala, which were part of the powerful confederation of Eastern India, had opposed King Ajatashatru of Magadha

questions.question_text: With which religion is the 'Shri Sampradaya' associated?
questions.explanation: Vaishnava saint Ramanujacharya emphasized the worship of Lakshmi and Vishnu in his devotion. It is believed that his sect was based on the teachings given by Lakshmi, therefore this sect is also called 'Shri Sampradaya'. Ramanujacharya is considered an incarnation of Sheshanaga

questions.question_text: Kanishka was a follower of which sect of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Kanishka was a famous Kushan dynasty ruler. He provided royal patronage to the Mahayana branch of Buddhism and propagated it in Central Asia and China. During his reign, the Fourth Buddhist Council was organized in Kundalvana of Kashmir. It was presided over by Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha was its Vice-President

questions.question_text: Who convened the First Jain Council?
questions.explanation: The First Jain Council was organized in 300 BC. This council took place during the time of Chandragupta Maurya. This council was organized in Pataliputra under the presidency of Sthulabhadra. In this, 12 Angas of Jainism were compiled. Jainism was divided into two parts, Digambara and Shvetambara

questions.question_text: Where did Lord Buddha give his first sermon?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha gave his first sermon in Rishipattana (Sarnath) where five Brahmins became his first disciples. The maximum propagation of Buddhism occurred in the Kosala kingdom. Here Buddha had performed the maximum 21 rainy season retreats (varshavasas)

questions.question_text: Paramartha stayed in China for more than 20 years and there he translated 70 Buddhist texts into the Chinese language. Where was he from?
questions.explanation: The propagation of Buddhism has been from India to the Far East. Many scholars from India went to many regions for this purpose; Paramartha, staying in China for many years, remained engaged in this work and for this he translated 70 Buddhist texts into the Chinese language. He was a resident of Ujjain

questions.question_text: Where are the oldest Ajanta paintings available?
questions.explanation: Ajanta caves, located in Maharashtra, India, are Buddhist monument caves made by cutting 29 caves, which are of the 2nd century BC. Excellent examples of paintings and sculpture related to Buddhism are found here but now paintings of only 7 caves (1, 2, 9, 10, 16, 17 and 19) remain. Among these 16, 17 and 19 are from the Gupta period. Cave numbers 9 and 10 of Ajanta are the oldest (from the Vakataka period) while cave numbers 1 and 2 are from the time of Pulakeshin II. Among the paintings of the 16th cave, the painting of the dying princess is very beautiful. The paintings of the 17th cave have been called the picture gallery (Chitrashala)

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R). Read the statements and choose the correct answer using the codes given below. Assertion (A): Gautama Buddha believed in reincarnation. Reason (R): He did not accept the existence of an eternal soul. Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: In the second half of the sixth century BC, many religious sects emerged in the middle Ganges plain. Their number is stated as 62 in the Buddhist text Brahmajala Sutta and 368 in the Jain text Sutrakritanga. The prominent figure of Buddhism was Gautama Buddha. Gautama Buddha did believe in reincarnation but he never accepted the existence of an eternal soul. Buddhism is mainly atheistic. Buddha emphasized human dignity instead of God

questions.question_text: In Shravasti, Makkhali Gosala mostly stayed in the workshop of Halahala. To which community did that woman belong?
questions.explanation: Makkhali Gosala was a prominent Ajivika philosopher of the 6th century. He is considered the most popular of the atheist traditions, the founder of the Ajivika sect, and the philosopher who promoted fatalism (Niyati-vada). He was a contemporary of Mahavira and Buddha. Gosala used to propagate his sect in Shravasti and other places, and for residence in Shravasti he stayed in the workshop of a woman named Halahala, who was a potter woman. Makkhali Gosala had six main disciples who propagated and spread his views

questions.question_text: On the banks of which of the following rivers did Mahavira Swami attain Kaivalya?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was the 24th Tirthankara of the Jains and the actual founder of Jainism. Mahavira renounced his home at the age of 30. After 12 years of rigorous penance, at the age of 42, Mahavira attained Kaivalya (supreme knowledge) under a Sal tree on the banks of the Rijupalika river near Jrimbhikagrama

questions.question_text: With which religion is 'Syadvada' associated?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was the 24th Tirthankara of the Jains and the actual founder of Jainism. Syadvada was associated with Jainism. Syadvada (Anekantavada) or Saptabhanginaya is called the theory of relativity of knowledge. Mahavira himself established a Sangha during his lifetime in which he included 11 main disciples. These were called Ganadharas

questions.question_text: Which of the following were associated as a disciple of Mahavira Jain?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was the 24th Tirthankara of the Jains and the actual founder of Jainism. Mahavira himself established a Sangha during his lifetime in which there were 11 Ganadharas. These were given the designation of main disciples. Among them, the prominent one was Makkhali Putta Gosala. 10 Ganadharas died during the time of Mahavira himself. Only Sudharmana was alive after Mahavira

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first nun?
questions.explanation: The promoter of Buddhism was Gautama Buddha. Buddha first gave his sermon in Sarnath to five pundits. The first woman to be initiated into Buddhism was Mahaprajapati Gautami. After his mother's death on the seventh day of Buddha's birth, he was brought up by Mahaprajapati Gautami

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the last person to be initiated into his religion by Gautama Buddha?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha, the promoter of Buddhism, was born in 563 BC in the Shakya Kshatriya clan in Lumbini village of Kapilavastu located in the Terai of Nepal. After renouncing his home at the age of 29, he attained knowledge after 6 years of rigorous penance. Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon to five Brahmin ascetics and his last sermon to a monk named Subhadda

questions.question_text: In which text is it mentioned that when a person enters the Sangha, he becomes casteless?
questions.explanation: When a person enters the Sangha, he becomes casteless (Vevanniyanti). This statement/quote is related to the Anguttara Nikaya. The 16 Mahajanapadas are mentioned in the Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra

questions.question_text: With what is the Vira-Nirvana era related?
questions.explanation: The Vira-Nirvana Samvat (era) is a calendar era. It commemorates the Nirvana of Lord Mahavira Swami, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. It is one of the ancient systems of chronological calculation

questions.question_text: According to Buddhist belief, which of the following gods requested Buddha three times to come forward and spread the light of his knowledge in all four directions?
questions.explanation: Brahma requested Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, to bring forward the light of his knowledge and spread it in all four directions in the world. According to Buddhism, the ultimate goal of human life is to achieve Nirvana. Nirvana means the extinguishing of the lamp. That is, getting freedom from the cycle of birth and death. This Nirvana can be achieved in this life itself

questions.question_text: The main dispute between the Digambara and Shvetambara sects was due to the emphasis on:
questions.explanation: There are two main branches of Jainism, Digambara and Shvetambara. In the Digambara Sangha, monks remained naked and in the Shvetambara Sangha, monks wore white clothes. These two groups were formed due to this main difference. After Lord Mahavira, it is known from the tradition of Jain Sthaviras that until the time of Acharya Bhadrabahu, there was no special difference between the Digambara and Shvetambara traditions, but later the differences grew. The main reason for this was the orthodox views of the Digambaras, where the Shvetambaras were not ready to accept their discipline and austere life. The main reasons for the differences are as follows (1) Digambara denies female liberation; in the Shvetambara tradition, the 19th Tirthankara Mallinatha was accepted as Mallikumari. (2) In the Digambara sect, the omniscient Lord did not take morsels of food (Kavalara) upon becoming all-knowing. (3) According to the Shvetambara view, white clothes are not an obstacle in the attainment of salvation and they did not believe in harsh penance. (4) According to the Digambara view, the renunciation of clothes and harsh penance are necessary for the attainment of salvation.

questions.question_text: At which of the following places did the Shakyas build a stupa over the physical remains of Gautama Buddha, which is supported by archaeological evidence?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Piprahwa is an ancient Buddhist site located near the Nepal border, 13 miles north of Naugarh in the Basti district of U.P. An ancient Buddhist stupa and a casket containing Buddha's relics were found here. From an inscription engraved in Brahmi script, it is known that it was built by the Shakyas. The diameter of the stupa was 119 feet and its height was 21 feet. The Piprahwa Buddhist stupa is one of the eight original stupas built after the Parinirvana of Buddha. The Shakyas built it by obtaining a portion of his body-relics.

questions.question_text: Which is the most extensive and developed Chaitya-griha of the Hinayana chronology among the following monuments?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Karle is located in the Pune (Poona) district of Maharashtra. Here, a Chaitya has been built by cutting the mountain, which is the largest and most beautiful among all the excavated Chaitya-grihas in India. It is 124 feet 3 inches long, 45 feet 5 inches wide, and 46 feet high. A huge pillar is built at the entrance of the cave, on top of which four lions are seated. There are three entrances to go inside the mandapa. Karle is the most extensive and developed Chaitya-griha of the Hinayana period. It was built during the Satavahana era (around the first century BC). An inscription is carved here, according to which a merchant (Shresthi) named Bhutapala of Vaijayanti had it built.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? List-I (Mahajanapada) List-II (Capital)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The ancient Panchala Mahajanapada was formed by combining the districts of Bareilly, Badaun, and Farrukhabad of modern Rohilkhand. Initially, it had two parts– (1) Northern Panchala, whose capital was Ahichhatra (present Ramanagar located in Bareilly) (2) Southern Panchala, whose capital was Kampilya (Kampilya located in Farrukhabad). The famous city of Kanyakubja was located in this state. Therefore, the correct matching is as follows– Panchala – Ahichhatra/Kampilya Matsya – Bairat Kosala – Shravasti Magadha – Girivraja Surasena – Mathura

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below: List-I (Philosophy) List-II (Proponent) A. Yoga i. Kapila B. Mimamsa ii. Patanjali C. Samkhya iii. Kumarila D. Vaisheshika iv. Kanada Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The correct matching is as follows– Yoga – Patanjali Mimamsa – Kumarila Samkhya – Kapila Vaisheshika – Kanada

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a part of Buddhist architectural art?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Anda, Medhi, and Chhatra are parts of Buddhist architectural art while Antarala is not a part of Buddhist architectural art.

questions.question_text: By what other names were the followers of the Ajivika sect also known? (i) Hatthapalekkhana (ii) Ekadandika (iii) Magandika (iv) Tedandika Codes:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The followers of the Ajivika sect were also known by other names such as Hatthapalekkhana and Ekadandika. The founder of the 'Ajivika sect', Makkhali Gosala, was initially a disciple of Mahavira. But later, due to differences, he left Mahavira and established an independent sect named "Ajivika". The "Ajivika" sect continued until about 1002 AD. Their view is called Niyativada (Fatalism), according to which everything in the world is pre-determined and controlled by destiny. Man's actions have no effect on his life.

questions.question_text: From which tribe were the real founders of Jainism?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-II Paper Dec. 2011) Explanation– The real founders of Jainism were from the Jnatrika tribe. Mahavira Swami was born in 540 BC in Kundagrama (Vaishali). It is known that his mother Trishala (Videhadatta) was the sister of Licchavi King Chetaka. Mahavira Swami was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): The very existence of Kautilya during the time of Chandragupta Maurya is considered doubtful. Reason (R): Patanjali does not mention Kautilya although he mentions Chandragupta's assembly and the Mauryas. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Kautilya was the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya. Kautilya made Chandragupta Maurya the king after destroying the Nanda dynasty. During the time of Chandragupta Maurya, Kautilya's existence is not considered doubtful. Therefore, Assertion (A) is incorrect. Patanjali does not mention Kautilya, although he mentions Megasthenes, the ambassador of Seleucus, in Chandragupta's royal assembly. Therefore, Reason (R) is correct

questions.question_text: Who gave the following statement– ‘Bhagavapi Khattiyo ahampi Khattiyo’ (Lord (Buddha) was a Kshatriya and I am also a Kshatriya)?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Ajatashatru (Haryanka dynasty) gave the statement ‘Bhagavapi Khattiyo ahampi Khattiyo’, meaning Lord Buddha was also a Kshatriya and I am also a Kshatriya. It is noteworthy that Ajatashatru became the ruler of Magadha after killing his father Bimbisara. He had built a stupa over the remains of Buddha in Rajgriha.

questions.question_text: The mention of religious sects contemporary to Buddha is found in which Buddhist literature?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation– In the Brahmajala Sutta, the mention of 62 philosophical views or religious sects contemporary to Mahatma Buddha is found.

questions.question_text: Below are two statements. The first statement is called Assertion (A) and the second is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): The commercial economy began to flourish during the time of Buddha. Reason (R): Jains abandoned agriculture in large numbers and adopted trade. Read the above statements and select the correct answer from the provided codes. Codes:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The commercial economy became very developed during the time of Buddha because Buddha gave much encouragement to traders. Like the Buddhists, the Jains also gave encouragement to trade. But their inclination towards agriculture remained less.

questions.question_text: The depiction of a deity on the reverse corresponding to the king's name given on the obverse was a special feature of coins from where?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Panchala was one of the 16 Mahajanapadas of ancient India. Later it was divided into two parts. The capital of Northern Panchala was Ahichhatra and the capital of Southern Panchala was Kampilya. The depiction of a deity on the reverse corresponding to the king's name given on the obverse was a special feature of Panchala coins.

questions.question_text: Maharaja Ramagupta got the idols of which of the following Tirthankaras made? 1. Mahavira 2. Parshvanatha 3. Chandraprabha 4. Pushpadanta Select the correct answer from the codes below:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Gupta ruler Ramagupta got the idols of Tirthankaras Chandraprabha and Pushpadatta made.

questions.question_text: Kayavarohan, which is considered the residence of Lakulisha, the founder of the Lakulisha-Pashupata sect, was located in which of the following?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation– Kayavarohan, which is considered the birthplace of Lakulisha, the founder of the Pashupata sect, was in the state of Gujarat. This sect is considered the most ancient sect of Shaivism. It is noteworthy that the Pashupata sect originated in the second century BC. People of this sect are called Pancharthikas.

questions.question_text: The role of which contemporary sect is mentioned in the destruction of the Nanda dynasty?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The role of the contemporary Jain sect is mentioned in the destruction of the Nanda dynasty because in 324 BC, Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of his guru Chanakya, killed Dhanananda and established the Maurya dynasty. Chandragupta Maurya was a follower of Jainism. In his last days, Chandragupta went to Shravanabelagola with his Jain guru Bhadrabahu, where he gave up his body through fasting.

questions.question_text: Various caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri hills in Odisha prove that:

options.A: Jainism existed for a long time in Odisha.
options.C: Both Buddhism and Jainism existed in Odisha.
options.D: Ashoka had a special contribution to the ancient art of Odisha.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation- Udayagiri and Khandagiri inscriptions are located in Odisha. A Jain inscription of Gupta Samvat 106 = 425 AD has been found here. In this, the installation of an idol of Parshvanatha by a person named Shankar is recorded.

questions.question_text: Who issued the order that whoever does not welcome Buddha would have to pay a fine of 500 Karshapanas?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation- Buddha had a special attachment to Kushinagar. Even in previous births, this city had been his playground. According to one account, he had ruled in Kushinagar as a Chakravartin emperor seven times. When Buddha came here for the last time, the Mallas welcomed him warmly. On this occasion, the Mallas announced that persons not participating in the welcome of Buddha would have to pay a fine of 500 Karshapanas.

questions.question_text: Where did Buddha give his maximum number of sermons?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation- The maximum number of Buddha's disciples were in the Kosala kingdom and he gave the maximum number of sermons in its capital Shravasti.

questions.question_text: Who was the head of Swami Mahavira's nunnery (Bhikkhuni Sangha)?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation- On the request of the people, the nunnery (Bhikkhuni Sangha) was established by Mahavira Swami. At the time of the primary Sangha, there were 1,59,000 Shravakas (monks) and 3,18,000 Shravikas (nuns) of Mahavira. It was the largest religious organization in the world at that time. The monk Sangha was led by Indrabhuti and the head of the nunnery was Princess Chandanabala (Chandana).

questions.question_text: Who claimed a share in the relics of Buddha on the basis of being a Kshatriya descendant?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation- The ruler of Magadha, Ajatashatru (422-460 BC), claimed a share in the relics of Buddha on the basis of being a Kshatriya descendant. The eight stupas built on the relics of Buddha are as follows–(1) Magadha (Ajatashatru) (2) Vaishali (Licchavis) (3) Kapilavastu (Shakyas) (4) Allakappa (Buliyas) (5) Ramagrama (Koliyas) (6) A Brahmin of Vethadwipa (7) Mallas of Pava and (8) Mallas of Kushinara.
