questions.question_text: Two statements are given below. One is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): The Virashaiva sect became a revolutionary movement against the caste system and the Brahminical ancient path. Reason (R): Its founder Basava himself belonged to the non-Brahmin class. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation (c) The Virashaiva sect or Lingayat sect was founded by Basava in South India. The Virashaiva sect became a revolutionary movement against the caste system and the Brahminical ancient path. This statement is correct, but as far as the question of reason is concerned - its founder Basava himself belonged to the Brahmin Varna. Therefore, the reason is incorrect.

questions.question_text: Which is the text in which Buddha's final journey to Kushinagar is described?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ Mahatma Buddha was born in 563 BC in the Lumbini forest near Kapilavastu. He attained enlightenment at the age of 35. He gave his first sermon in Sarnath, after which he continuously made people aware of his thoughts. Buddha spent the rainy season retreat in Shravasti the most, 21 times. At the age of 80, he gave up his body in Kushinagar. This is called 'Mahaparinirvana' in Buddhist texts. The description of Buddha's final journey to Kushinagar is found in the 'Mahaparinirvana Sutra'.

questions.question_text: Inscriptions in Shankha script have been obtained from the stupa remains of which of the following sites-
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ Bharhut (near Satna district) is an important stupa built during the Shunga period. Apart from this, stupas were also built in Sanchi, Besnagar and Bodhgaya. The Bharhut stupa was discovered by Mr. Cunningham in 1873 AD. Inscriptions in Shankha script were obtained from the stupa remains from Bharhut itself. Sculptures and paintings engraved on railings, pillars and torana panels have been found. The Bharhut stupa was made of bricks.

questions.question_text: In which sculptural art did scenes from the Ramayana first appear?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ There is a temple of Parvati at a place called Nachna-Kuthara near Ajaigarh in the Panna district of Madhya Pradesh. Scenes from the Ramayana are first found in the sculptural art here.

questions.question_text: In which of the following caves of Ajanta is the scene of the 'Dying Princess' depicted?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ The Ajanta caves are located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra. The paintings in caves 9-10 are the oldest. Initially, there were paintings in 29 caves in Ajanta, but now only paintings of six caves (1-2, 9-10 and 16-17) remain. Among the paintings in Cave 16 of Ajanta, the painting named 'Dying Princess' is the most beautiful and attractive. This is a painting of a princess dying in separation from her husband. Family members are standing around her in a grief-stricken state. Scholars have identified her with Sundari, the wife of Buddha's half-brother Nanda.

questions.question_text: In which of the following stupa remains located in South India is the sculptural depiction of Dasaratha Jataka found –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ Nagarjunakonda is an ancient place located 100 miles southeast of Hyderabad. It was a beautiful city during the time of Acharya Nagarjuna, the famous teacher of Mahayana Buddhism. Located on the banks of the Krishna River, this city was both naturally beautiful and secured like an invincible fort. The remains of nine Buddhist stupas have been found here. The sculptural depiction of Dasaratha Jataka has been found in these stupas. This stupa was built by the rulers of the Ikshvaku dynasty.

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the first Buddhist Council?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The first Buddhist Council took place in the Saptaparni cave in Rajgriha immediately after the death of Buddha. At this time, the ruler of Magadha was Ajatashatru. This council was presided over by Mahakassapa and Buddha's prominent disciples Ananda and Upali were also present. In this, the teachings of Buddha were compiled and divided into two Pitakas named Sutta and Vinaya.

questions.question_text: The compilation of Buddha's discourses, the famous Dhammapada, is a part of which of the following texts–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The compilation of Buddha's discourses, the famous 'Dhammapada', is a part of the Sutta Pitaka text. The Sutta Pitaka is divided into five Nikayas which are as follows- 1. Digha Nikaya 2. Majjhima Nikaya 3. Samyutta Nikaya 4. Anguttara Nikaya 5. Khuddaka Nikaya. The Khuddaka Nikaya is independent and complete in itself. Some of its other texts are as follows- Khuddakapatha, Dhammapada, Udana, Sutta Nipata, Vimanavatthu, Petavatthu, Theragatha, Therigatha and Jataka.

questions.question_text: The famous Buddhist scholar Ashvaghosha was a contemporary of—
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation— The famous Buddhist scholar Ashvaghosha was a contemporary of Kanishka. He was the court poet of Kanishka. He has three major compositions— (1) Buddhacharita (2) Saundarananda (3) Sariputra-Prakarana. Among these, the first two are epic poems and the last is a dramatic text.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does Buddhism advocate?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation— Gautama Buddha was the founder of Buddhism. He is called the Light of Asia. We get detailed knowledge about Buddhism from the Pali Tripitakas. This religion was basically atheistic; there is no concept of a soul in it. It is based on the concept of the Middle Path. They believe in Karma and Reincarnation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following places is not related to Buddhism?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation— Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, attained enlightenment at the age of 35 on the night of Vaishakha Purnima under a Peepal tree on the banks of the Niranjana river in Bodh Gaya. Nalanda was a center of Buddhist education. Buddha gave his first sermon in Sarnath (Rishipattana), which is called Dharmachakrapravartana in Buddhist texts, whereas Somnath is related to a Shiva temple.

questions.question_text: Where was Gautama Buddha born?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation— Gautama Buddha was born in approximately 563 BC in the Lumbini forest (modern-day Rummindei forest) near Kapilvastu. His father Shuddhodana was the head of the Shakya clan of Kapilvastu. His mother's name was Mahamaya. Gautama's childhood name was Siddhartha. At the age of 29, he renounced household life.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Buddhacharita'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 PGT History, 2004 PGT History, 2011 PGT History, 2013 Explanation— Ashvaghosha was the court poet of Kanishka, who composed Buddhacharita, Saundarananda, and Sutralankara. Buddhacharita is called the Ramayana of the Buddhists. Ashvaghosha, Vasumitra, Parshva, Charaka, Nagarjuna, Mahachet, and Sangharaksha graced the court of Kanishka.

questions.question_text: At which place is the oldest Lingodbhava statue of Shiva found?
questions.explanation: The first mention of Linga worship is in the Matsya Purana. Linga worship is mentioned in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata. The oldest statue of Shiva in the form of a Linga was found in the famous Gudimallam in Renigunta near Madras in the first century AD

questions.question_text: Ramayana was written by—
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 TGT History, 2005, 2009 Explanation— The author of the Ramayana was Valmiki. It is a great epic of the Hindu religion. It is divided into seven sections (Kandas), which are: (i) Balakanda (ii) Ayodhyakanda (iii) Aranyakanda (iv) Kishkindhakanda (v) Sundarakanda (vi) Lankakanda (vii) Uttarakanda.

questions.question_text: In which Buddhist council did the Hinayana and Mahayana branches of Buddhism emerge?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation— The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalvana in Kashmir during the reign of the Kushan ruler Kanishka. It was presided over by Vasumitra, and Ashvaghosha became its vice-president. At this time, Buddhism was divided into two distinct and independent sects named Hinayana and Mahayana. The text named 'Vibhashashastra' was composed at this time. It was composed by Vasumitra.

questions.question_text: In which text is the philosophical discussion of Buddhist philosophy found?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation— After the death of Mahatma Buddha, his teachings were compiled and divided into three Pitakas: (1) Vinaya Pitaka (2) Sutta Pitaka (3) Abhidhamma Pitaka. The Vinaya Pitaka contains rules related to the Sangha and a collection of conduct, thoughts, and regulations related to life. The Sutta Pitaka contains a collection of the principles and teachings of Buddhism. The Abhidhamma Pitaka contains a collection of philosophical principles. The compilation of the Abhidhamma Pitaka took place during the time of Ashoka in the Third Buddhist Council.

questions.question_text: Former Jain religious teachers, by boycotting the Sanskrit language, made which language the medium for the spread of their religious teachings?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation— The teachings and instructions of Mahavira were compiled by his Ganadharas by composing 12 Angas and 14 Purvas under the twelfth Anga Drishtivada. These texts are written in Ardhamagadhi or Prakrit language.

questions.question_text: Where did Buddha attain enlightenment?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Buddha attained enlightenment at a place called Bodh Gaya. The common people of that time were troubled by the ritualistic system of the Brahmins; as a reaction to this, Gautama Buddha established the religion of the Middle Path, which was accessible to all. Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a Banyan tree on the full moon of the month of Vaishakha in Bodh Gaya. From then on, he became known as 'Tathagata'.

questions.question_text: The religious text of the Buddhists, in which the stories of the previous births of Gautama Buddha are compiled, is called—
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation— Jataka stories contain a compilation of the stories of the previous births of Lord Buddha. The total number of Jataka stories is 547 or 549. In the Vinaya Pitaka, the conduct, thoughts, and rules for Buddhist monks and nuns are discussed.

questions.question_text: In which period did the Kharosthi script originate?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – The Kharosthi script originated from the Iranian script during the Buddha period. The time period of the Iranian rulers is the 5th century BC. Therefore, the Iranian rulers were contemporaries of Buddha. The first use of this script in India is seen in the inscriptions of Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the philosophical sect of the Bhagavata religion?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation— The philosophical sect of the Bhagavata religion was Vishishtadvaitavad. The Bhagavata religion is also called the Vaishnava religion. Ramanuja was the acharya of the Vaishnava sect, whose philosophy was Vishishtadvaita. Shankaracharya's Advaitavad was influenced by the Shunyavad of the Mahayana branch of Buddhism.

questions.question_text: In which period was the realization of the non-dual period (Advaitakal) experienced?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – In the Later Vedic period, apart from the last three Vedas, Brahmin texts and Upanishads, etc., were composed. The ultimate culmination of Vedic thought is found in the Upanishads. Its main subject was self-knowledge (Atmajnana) and divine knowledge (Brahmajnana). Idealistic Advaitavad was the main principle of the Upanishads. The Upanishads are also called Vedanta.

questions.question_text: What was the view of Jainism towards God?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation— Followers of Jainism do not believe in the concept of God. Among the Buddhist and Jain acharyas who emerged in the 6th century BC, the name of Mahavira Swami is established as an atheist thinker. He was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. Mahavira's concept was deeply rooted in the doctrines of Karma and Reincarnation, but he had no belief in the existence of God. According to Mahavira, the ultimate goal of life is the attainment of Kevalya.

questions.question_text: The founder of the Bhagavata religion was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Initial information about the Bhagavata religion is found in the Upanishads. The propounder of this religion was Krishna, who belonged to the Vrishni clan and whose place of residence was Mathura. Krishna was first mentioned in the Chhandogya Upanishad as the son of Devaki and a disciple of Ghora Angirasa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is also known by the name 'Shakyamuni'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation— Gautama Buddha is also known by the name Shakyamuni because of his birth in the Shakya clan. He was born in 563 BC in Lumbini near Kapilvastu. His father Shuddhodana was the head of the Shakya clan of Kapilvastu.

questions.question_text: The cave that represents all three religions—Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist—is –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation— The cave representing all three religions—Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist—is the 'Ellora Cave', which is located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra. Here, many caves have been created by cutting the mountains, which are associated with the Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu religions.

questions.question_text: Under Buddhism, the propounder of 'Madhyamika philosophy' was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation— The propounder of Madhyamika philosophy was Nagarjuna. His famous work is 'Madhyamikakarika'. It is also known as the Theory of Relativity. Its basic principle is that every object has arisen from some cause or other. Nagarjuna called Pratityasamutpada itself 'Shunyata' (emptiness).

questions.question_text: Choose the true statement from the following –

options.A: Both Buddha and Mahavira believed in the existence of the Supreme Soul
options.B: Both Buddha and Mahavira believed in the existence of the Soul
options.C: Both Buddha and Mahavira were in favor of worship and rituals
options.D: Both Buddha and Mahavira were supporters of the doctrine of Karma

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Gautama Buddha was the founder of Buddhism. He is called the Light of Asia. He was born in 563 BC at a place named Lumbini in Kapilvastu. Mahavira Swami was the 24th and final Tirthankara of Jainism. He was born in 540 BC in Kundagrama (Vaishali). Both religions believe in the doctrine of Karma.

questions.question_text: What is the special name for Mahavira's teaching?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The special name for Mahavira's teaching is Pancha Mahavrata. Mahavira Swami, the real founder of Jainism, added a fifth Mahavrata named Brahmacharya to the four Mahavratas propounded by his predecessor Tirthankara Parshvanatha, which became known as the Pancha Mahavratas.

questions.question_text: Who was the first schismatic of the Jain Sangha during Mahavira's lifetime?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation— The first schismatic of the Jain Sangha during Mahavira's lifetime was Jamali. Mahavira gave his first sermon in Rajgir on the Vipulachala hill (Vipulanagiri).

questions.question_text: Who was the main deity of the Pashupata sect?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation— The Pashupata sect is the oldest sect of Shaivism. Its founder was Lakulisha. He is considered one of the 18 incarnations of Shiva.

questions.question_text: The birthplace of Gautama Buddha, Lumbini, is located in—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation— Gautama Buddha's birthplace is in Lumbini, which is located in a village named Rummindei within the borders of Nepal. The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka visited the village of Lumbini in the 20th year of his coronation. Due to the sanctity of this place, he reduced the land revenue here to 1/8 part.

questions.question_text: The name of Mahavira's mother was—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation— The name of Mahavira's mother was Trishala. She was the sister of Chetaka, the chief of the Lichchhavi clan. Mahavira Swami was born in 540 BC in Kundagrama near Vaishali.

questions.question_text: Among the religious movements that emerged in the 6th century BC, which of the following acharyas was a radical materialist?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation— Ajita Kesakambali was a Nihilist (Uchchhedavadi). His view was that everything is destroyed after death. Therefore, he taught to live a happy life by making the present life the goal. Purana Kassapa was an Amoralist (Akriyavadi) or a preacher of non-action; according to him, there are no fruits for good or bad deeds. Pakudha Kaccayana was an Eternalist (Nityavadi); he stated seven elements to be eternal—earth, water, fire, air, pleasure-pain, and soul. Makkhali Gosala established an independent sect named Ajivika. His view is called Fatalism (Niyativad).

questions.question_text: The 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism is considered to be—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 DSSSB PGT 2016 Explanation— According to Jain belief, there were 23 other teachers before Vardhamana Mahavira, the founder and great teacher of Jainism, who are called 'Tirthankaras', among whom the first was Rishabhadeva or Adinatha and the 23rd was Parshvanatha.

questions.question_text: Where was Shuddhodana, the father of Gautama Buddha, a king?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation— Shuddhodana, the father of Gautama Buddha, was a Kshatriya clan king of the Shakya lineage of Kapilvastu. It is noteworthy that Gautama Buddha was born at King Shuddhodana's place (in 563 BC). Due to the death of his mother Mahamaya (of the Kosala dynasty) in Gautama Buddha's childhood, his maternal aunt Prajapati Gautami brought him up.

questions.question_text: The concept of 'Navadha Bhakti' is an important ritual of which religion?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation— The concept of 'Navadha Bhakti' is an important ritual of Vaishnavism in which the worship of God is done through nine types of devotion. The main devotions are—Shravana (listening), Kirtana (chanting), Smarana (remembering), Padasevana (serving the feet), Sakhya Bhava (friendship), and Atmanivedana (self-surrender). It is noteworthy that Bhagavata religion itself is known in the form of Vaishnavism. The propounder of this religion was Krishna, the leader of the Vrishni tribe, who was the king of Mathura.

questions.question_text: The original name of the Mahabharata was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In the 'Mahabharata' epic composed by Maharishi Ved Vyasa, there were initially only 8800 verses and its name was 'Jaya Samhita' (a text related to victory). Later, when the number of verses increased to 24,000, it became famous by the name 'Bharata'. Subsequently, there were 100,000 verses in it and it came to be called 'Shatasahasri Samhita' or 'Mahabharata'.

questions.question_text: With which religion are 'Pancha Mahavrata' and 'Triratna' associated?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In Jainism, liberation from the bonds of worldly desires is called Nirvana. Only by getting liberation from the fruits of action can a person move towards Nirvana. For liberation from the fruits of action, the practice of 'Triratna' (Three Jewels) is necessary. The Triratna are—Right Perception (Samyak Darshan), Right Knowledge (Samyak Jnana), and Right Conduct (Samyak Charitra). In the practice of Triratna, special emphasis has been laid on conduct. For this, there is a provision for following the following five Mahavratas—Non-violence (Ahinsa), Truthfulness (Satya Vachan), Non-stealing (Asteya), Non-attachment (Aparigraha), and Celibacy (Brahmacharya).

questions.question_text: The compilation of the rules of conduct for Buddhist Sanghas is found in which of the following texts?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The principles of Buddhism are compiled in the 'Tripitaka', which has three parts— (a) Sutta Pitaka - a collection of Buddha's religious teachings, (b) Vinaya Pitaka - a description of the rules of conduct for Buddhist Sanghas. (c) Abhidhamma Pitaka - The Abhidhamma Pitaka was codified in the Third Buddhist Council held in Pataliputra during the time of Ashoka. It contains philosophical explanations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers had the figure of Shakyamuni Buddha inscribed on his coins?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation— Kanishka was a follower of Buddhism. On some of his coins, there is an image of Buddha in a standing posture with a halo, and below it 'Boddo' (Buddha) is engraved in Greek script. Figures of Hindu gods and goddesses are also found on some gold and copper coins of Kanishka.

questions.question_text: In 'Syadvada', the possibilities are—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation— Syadvada is also known by the name 'Saptabhanginaya'. It is the belief of Jains that all our judgments regarding worldly objects are relative and limited. We can neither fully accept nor fully reject anything. It has seven types— 1. Syad asti (perhaps it is), 2. Syad nasti (perhaps it is not), 3. Syad asti cha nasti (perhaps it is and is not), 4. Syad avyaktavyam (perhaps it is indescribable), 5. Syad asti cha avyaktavyam (perhaps it is and is indescribable), 6. Syad nasti cha avyaktavyam cha (perhaps it is not and is indescribable), 7. Syad asti cha nasti cha avyaktavyam cha (perhaps it is, is not, and is indescribable).

questions.question_text: Which religion believes in 'Triratna'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation— In Jainism, three means have been stated for attaining salvation, which are known as 'Triratna'. These Triratna are— 1. Samyak Darshan (Right Perception)— Firm belief in the Jain Tirthankaras and their teachings is Right Perception or faith. 2. Samyak Jnana (Right Knowledge)— Knowledge of Jainism and its principles is Right Knowledge. 3. Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct)— Putting into practice whatever has been known and accepted as right is Right Conduct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following inscriptions is important for the history of the Bhagavata religion?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation— The Besnagar Pillar Inscription is a very important inscription from the perspective of knowledge of the history of the Bhagavata religion. It makes it clear that the Greek ambassador Heliodorus of Taxila accepted the Bhagavata religion and had this pillar installed. A special account of the popularity of the Bhagavata religion is obtained from archaeological evidence.

questions.question_text: The first Jain religious council was held?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation – The first Jain religious council was held in Pataliputra in the 4th century BC under the chairmanship of Sthulabhadra, in which the Jain principles were compiled, which later became the basic principles of the Shvetambara sect.

questions.question_text: What were the Tripitakas?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – After the Mahaparinirvana of Mahatma Buddha, his teachings were compiled and divided into three Pitakas— 1. Vinaya Pitaka, 2. Sutta Pitaka, 3. Abhidhamma Pitaka. These are given the designation of Tripitaka. Their compilation was done through various Buddhist councils.

questions.question_text: Which is not in accordance with the principles of Jainism –

options.B: Ending the body through physical penance
options.C: Propagation in the language of the people

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation— The principles regarding non-violence in Jainism are extremely strict. Inappropriate behavior towards anyone through mind, speech, or action is violence. In Jainism, excessive emphasis has also been laid on physical penance. Under this, there is also a provision for suicide through fasting. This method is called Sallekhana or Nishidhi.

questions.question_text: By whom was the Vinaya Pitaka compiled?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation— Due to increasing anarchy in Buddhism, after the death of Mahatma Buddha, the First Buddhist Council was organized in the Saptaparni cave in Rajgir during the reign of Ajatashatru. In this first Buddhist council, Upali composed the Vinaya Pitaka and Ananda composed the Sutta Pitaka. This Buddhist council was presided over by Mahakassapa.

questions.question_text: Which Jain Tirthankara gave the order to completely renounce clothes?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—After leaving home at the age of 30, following 12 years of severe penance and wandering, Mahavira's body became free of clothes. After achieving Kaivalya, he came to be known as 'Jina' and 'Nigrantha'. Being thus free from bonds, Mahavira did not wear clothes for the rest of his life and remained nude.

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler who destroyed the Bodhi tree?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—According to Xuanzang, the original tree under which Mahatma Buddha attained enlightenment was destroyed by Emperor Shashanka in the 7th century. The current tree is of the fourth generation, which was planted by Alexander Cunningham. The Mahabodhi temple has been built here.

questions.question_text: Followers of which Shaiva sect considered Bhairava as their personal deity?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation—Kapalika was also a branch of the Shaiva sect in which Bhairava, the fearsome form of Shiva, was worshipped. Meat and liquor were consumed in abundance in this sect. Its description is also found in Bhavabhuti's play titled Malatimadhava, in which a place called Shrishail is described as the primary center of the Kapalikas.

questions.question_text: What is meant by the 'Middle Path' taught by Lord Buddha?

options.A: The path between sorrow and happiness
options.B: The path between the soul and the supreme soul
options.D: Neither too much sensual indulgence nor too much self-mortification

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—There are eight limbs of the Noble Eightfold Path that remove sorrow and destroy craving. These are also called the 'Majjhima Patipada', meaning the Middle Path. This signifies neither too much sensual indulgence nor too much self-mortification.

questions.question_text: Where was the capital of Vatsa Janapada?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—Kaushambi was the capital of the Vatsa Mahajanapada, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of the 6th century BC. In ancient times, the areas of the three districts of present-day Allahabad, Kaushambi, and Banda were part of the Vatsa Mahajanapada.

questions.question_text: Where did the first compilation of Jain religious texts take place?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—The first compilation of Jain religious texts took place in Pataliputra during the First Jain Council. This council was held under the supervision of Sthavir Sthulabhadra and Sambhutivijaya. In this, 12 Angas of Jainism were compiled. However, the second Jain council was held in Vallabhi, Gujarat, under the leadership of Devardhigani Kshamashramana, in which the religious texts were finally compiled and put into writing.

questions.question_text: Who built the Dilwara temples at Mount Abu?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—The Solanki rulers built the Dilwara temple along with other temples constructed on Mount Abu (Rajasthan). Dilwara is a group of two temples made of marble.

questions.question_text: Who was the proponent of Samkhya philosophy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation—Kapila Muni was the proponent of Samkhya philosophy. The most ancient and authentic text of this philosophy is 'Samkhyakarika' written by Ishvarakrishna.

questions.question_text: The literature of the Mahayana branch was written in—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation—Buddhism was divided into two sects, Hinayana and Mahayana, during the Fourth Buddhist Council held in Kundalvan, Kashmir, in approximately the first century AD during the reign of Kanishka. This council was presided over by Vasumitra, with Ashvaghosa as the vice-president. Those who introduced changes to the strict and traditional rules of Buddhism were called Mahayanists. Mahayana means - the Great or Superior Path. In this, special emphasis was placed on service to others and altruism. The texts of this sect were written in the Sanskrit language.

questions.question_text: The division into Mahayana and Hinayana branches in Buddhism occurred—

options.A: During the First Buddhist Council in Rajgir
options.B: During the Second Buddhist Council in Vallabhi
options.C: During the Third Buddhist Council in Pataliputra
options.D: During the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation—See the explanation of the above question.

questions.question_text: During whose reign did Jainism divide into "Shvetambara" and "Digambara" sects?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation—During the reign of Chandragupta Maurya, Jainism was divided into Shvetambara and Digambara sects. Bhadrabahu and his followers were called Digambaras. They were known as Southern Jains. Sthulabhadra and his followers were called Shvetambaras.

questions.question_text: Which of the following theories did Shankaracharya give?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation—Dvaita Vedanta, Dvaitadvaita, Vishishtadvaita, and Advaita Vedanta were established by Acharya Madhva, Acharya Nimbarka, Acharya Ramanuja, and Adi Shankaracharya, respectively.

questions.question_text: Who is considered the proponent of 'Lokayata philosophy'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation—Charvaka is considered the proponent of Lokayata philosophy or Materialist philosophy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation— Mahajanapada — Capital Kosala — Shravasti Anga — Champa Chedi — Shuktimati or Sotthivati Matsya — Viratnagar Southern Panchala — Kampilya

questions.question_text: According to Jain tradition, Bahubali is the son of which Tirthankara?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—According to Jain tradition, Bahubali was the son of Rishabhanatha, the first Tirthankara of Jainism.

questions.question_text: How is Devananda famous in Jainism?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—Devananda has gained fame in Jainism as the mother of Mahavira Swami, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. According to the description in the Kalpasutra, Mahavira first entered the womb of Devananda, the wife of a Brahmin named Rishabhadatta, but later he was transferred by Indra to the womb of the Kshatriyani Trishala because Jain Tirthankaras could not be born in any varna other than Kshatriya.

questions.question_text: Where was the oldest Vishnu idol obtained from?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—Malhar, located in the Bilaspur district of Chhattisgarh, is a village of archaeological importance, from where the country's oldest four-armed Vishnu idol was obtained. Other temples discovered during excavation here include Deuri Temple, Pataleshwari Temple, and Dindeshwari Temple.

questions.question_text: What is the name for the combined form of Vishnu and Shiva?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—The combined form of Vishnu and Shiva is named Harihara. The combined idol of Shiva and Vishnu in the form of Harihara was first created during the Gupta period.

questions.question_text: Lakulisha was the main deity of which religion?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—Lakulisha was the main deity of the Pashupata sect; followers of this sect considered him an incarnation of Shiva. He established the Pashupata sect, which is the oldest sect of Shaivism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings is known as 'Kunika' in Jain tradition?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation—Ajatashatru, the ruler of the Magadha Empire, is known by the name 'Kunika' in Jain tradition. Mahatma Buddha attained Nirvana in the eighth year of Ajatashatru's reign.

questions.question_text: Who was the first known Greek follower of the Bhagavata religion?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—Preliminary information about Vaishnavism is found in the Upanishads. It developed from the Bhagavata religion. Worshippers of Narayana were originally called Pancharatrikas. The first mention of Krishna is found in the Chandogya Upanishad. Krishna was the proponent of Vaishnavism. Heliodorus was the first known Greek follower of the Bhagavata religion. He was the ambassador of the Greek ruler of Taxila, 'Antialcidas', who established a Garuda Pillar in Vidisha in honor of Vasudeva.

questions.question_text: 'Anekantavada' is a special feature of—
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation—The founder and first Tirthankara of Jainism was Rishabhadeve; Mahavira Swami was the 24th Tirthankara. Syadvada (Anekantavada) is included in the philosophical aspects of Jainism. Jainism believes in the soul but does not recognize God. Mahavira Swami added the fifth great vow, Brahmacharya, to Jainism. Jainism has adopted its spiritual ideas from Samkhya philosophy.

questions.question_text: Where is Ghoshitarama located?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—Ghoshitarama is located in Kaushambi. It was built by the famous merchant Ghoshitarama for the residence of Mahatma Buddha. Near the Ghoshitarama garden, Emperor Ashoka had built a stupa.

questions.question_text: Syadvada is associated with
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—According to Jain tradition, there were a total of 24 Tirthankaras in this religion. Among these, the first was Rishabhadeve. The 23rd was Parshvanatha and the last was Mahavira Swami. Jainism expresses philosophical thoughts in which Syadvada (Anekantavada) or Sapta-bhangi-naya is called the theory of relativity of knowledge. According to Jainism, three sources of knowledge are described, which include perception, inference, and the words of the Tirthankaras.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is the author of Yoga Sutra?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—There is mention of 6 main philosophies in India, among which Patanjali is considered the main proponent of Yoga philosophy. He composed the Yoga Sutra. The Yoga Sutra shows how a person can achieve a healthy life.

questions.question_text: Kapilavastu has been identified with
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation—Mahatma Buddha, the proponent of Buddhism, was born in 563 BC in the Shakya Kshatriya clan in Lumbini village of Kapilavastu, located in the Terai of Nepal. Kapilavastu is identified with modern Piprahwa. Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and death occurred on the full moon day.

questions.question_text: Haimavata sect was a branch of
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation—After the Mahaparinirvana of Mahatma Buddha, the monk devotees of the Buddhist Sangha were divided into two classes: Mahasamghikas and Sthaviravadis. Mahasamghikas were divided into 9 groups; similarly, divisions also occurred in Sthavir. Haimavata is related to these divisions.

questions.question_text: Piprahwa, which is being identified with Kapilavastu, is located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—Piprahwa, which is being identified with Kapilavastu, is located in the Siddharth Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Lord Buddha was born in Lumbini village of this Kapilavastu. Later, when Ashoka became the ruler of the Maurya dynasty, he visited Lumbini village a few years after his coronation and declared all of Lumbini tax-free.

questions.question_text: With which sect is the 'Samaraichcha Kaha' associated?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—'Samaraichcha Kaha' is associated with the Jain sect. The founder and first Tirthankara of Jainism was Rishabhadeve, the twenty-third Tirthankara was Parshvanatha, and the last was Mahavira Swami. The philosophical expression of Jainism is found in 'Samaraichcha Kaha'.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of Triratna in Buddhism?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—In Buddhism, the meaning of Triratna is Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha. The most ancient Buddhist texts are called Tripitaka. Under the Tripitaka in Buddhism come the Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka, and Vinaya Pitaka. In the Vinaya Pitaka, there is mention of rules related to the discipline of Buddhist monks.

questions.question_text: Sir Edwin Arnold's book 'The Light of Asia' is based on:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—Sir Edwin Arnold's book 'The Light of Asia' is based on Lalitavistara. Lord Buddha is called 'The Light of Asia'. Lord Buddha's name for peace itself is the mass of light.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not included in the Triratna of Jainism?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation—It is also necessary for every seeker to be free from the fruits of the karma of their previous births because if one is not free from this, one will remain trapped in the cycle of birth and death and will not be able to attain Moksha, i.e., Nirvana. For this, i.e., for freedom from the fruits of karma, Triratnas are mentioned in Jainism—Right Vision or Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct or Character.

questions.question_text: 'Tripitaka' is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation—The basic literature of Buddhism is "Tripitaka". These contain the teachings and sermons of Lord Gautama Buddha and a description of the conduct, thoughts, and philosophical principles of Buddhism. It is in three parts, which were originally written in the "Pali" language.

questions.question_text: The famous Jain teacher Sthulabhadra was born in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation—The famous Jain teacher Sthulabhadra was born in Pataliputra. In 317 BC, when a famine occurred in the Magadha kingdom, Bhadrabahu went to South India with his disciples, but many monks remained in Magadha, North India, under the leadership of Sthulabhadra. The followers of Sthulabhadra were called 'Shvetambara'.

questions.question_text: With what is the text named Vajrachhedika associated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The Vajrachhedika text, composed by Asanga, is related to the Mahayana sect of Buddhism. The reformist sect of Buddhism was called 'Mahayana'. Mahayana means - the Superior Path. In this, special emphasis was placed on service to others and altruism. Worship of Buddha in the form of an idol began. This path was easy for the common people. Looking at its comprehensiveness and generosity, its name Mahayana seems completely appropriate. Through this, more people could attain salvation. The goal of Mahayana is the welfare of the entire human race. It believes in faith and rebirth. There is also provision for idol worship in it. And Buddha's grace was considered necessary for salvation. The ideal of Mahayana is the 'Bodhisattva'. Bodhisattvas continue to strive for the liberation of other beings even after attaining salvation. 'The secret of the greatness of Mahayana is its selfless service and tolerance.

questions.question_text: Which place represents the Jetavana Vihara?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Anathapindika bought the garden from Prince Jeta and gave it for the residence of Buddha. This garden is in Saheth (Shravasti). Shravasti was the capital of the Kosala kingdom. During Prasenajit's time, the kingdom of Kosala was at its peak; besides Kashi, it also had authority over the republics of the Shakyas of Kapilavastu, the Kalamas of Kesaputta, the Mallas of Pava and Kushinara, the Koliyas of Ramagrama, the Moriyas of Pipphalivana, etc. According to the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya, he led a group of five kings. Prasenajit was devoted to Mahatma Buddha and his doctrine. Buddha often visited and rested in his capital.

questions.question_text: According to Jain tradition, the 22nd Tirthankara Neminatha was related to—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 PGT 2016 Explanation- Among the non-conformist sects that emerged during the time of Gautama Buddha, the name of Mahavira of Jainism is most famous. He was not the founder of Jainism, but we can call him the proponent of the Jain movement of the sixth century BC. He is the most important among the Indian atheist teachers after Buddha. Tradition calls him the twenty-fourth Tirthankara. Twenty Tirthankaras have preceded him. Among these, the historicity of the twenty-third Tirthankara Parshvanatha has been proven. Other Tirthankaras are as follows- "(1) Rishabha or Adinatha, (2) Ajitanatha, (3) Sambhava, (4) Abhinandana, (5) Sumati, (6) Padmaprabhu, (7) Suparshva, (8) Chandraprabha, (9) Pushpadanta, (10) Shitala, (11) Shreyamsa, (12) Vasupujya, (13) Vimala, (14) Ananta, (15) Dharma, (16) Shanti, (17) Kunthu, (18) Ara, (19) Malli, (20) Munisuvrata, (21) Neminatha, (22) Arishtanemi, (23) Parshvanatha, (24) Mahavira. The 22nd Tirthankara of Jainism, Neminatha, was related to Krishna. He is described as a contemporary of Krishna.

questions.question_text: Who among the following contemporary kings was of the same age as Gautama Buddha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The ruler of the same age as Gautama Buddha was Prasenajit. Prasenajit was the great ruler of the Kosala kingdom. The Kosala kingdom extended from Nepal in the north to the Sai river in the south and from Panchala in the west to the Gandak river in the east. The Sarayu river divides this Janapada into two parts. The capital of North Kosala was Saket and the capital of South Kosala was Shravasti. The Magadha ruler Bimbisara was also a contemporary of Prasenajit, to whom Prasenajit's sister Mahakosala was married and Prasenajit had given the Kashi province in dowry. But a war broke out between Prasenajit and Ajatashatru, and finally a compromise was reached between the two, and Prasenajit married his daughter Vajira to Ajatashatru.

questions.question_text: Keeping whose wish in mind did Buddha allow women to enter the Sangha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- To preach Buddhism, when Gautama Buddha walked from Rajgir and reached Vaishali, the capital of the Lichchhavis. Here he spent the fifth rainy season. The Lichchhavis had the famous Kutagashala built in Mahavana for his residence. Amrapali, the famous courtesan of Vaishali, became his disciple and she gave her mango grove (Amravatika) for the residence of the Bhikshu-Sangha. At this same place, Buddha for the first time granted permission for women to enter his Sangha and established a Sangha of nuns. The first woman to gain entry into the Sangha was Buddha's stepmother Prajapati Gautami, who had reached there from Kapilavastu after the death of King Suddhodana. It is said that Buddha was initially against taking women into the Sangha, but on the entreaty of Gautami and the insistence of his favorite disciple Ananda, he granted permission for it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Indian dynasties did not provide royal patronage to Jainism?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The Satavahanas did not provide royal patronage to Jainism. Satavahana rulers were followers of the Vedic religion and patrons of Brahmanism. During the reign of Rashtrakuta kings (9th century), Jainism spread significantly in South India. Jainism was more popular in Gujarat and Rajasthan during the 11th and 12th centuries. The Magadha ruler Ajatashatru and his successor Udayin contributed to its propagation. Jainism also flourished during the time of the Nanda dynasty because they were not against Jainism. It is known from the Hathigumpha inscription that a Nanda king had taken away the statue of the first 'Jina' from Kalinga. This religion also spread during the time of Chandragupta Maurya because, according to Jain tradition, he had accepted the discipleship of Jain Acharya Bhadrabahu. Along with him, in the later part of his life, he renounced his kingdom and went to the South to perform penance.

questions.question_text: Select the correct chronological order of the Buddhist councils held at the following four places from the code given below- 1. Vaishali 2. Rajgriha 3. Kundalvan 4. Pataliputra Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- After the Mahaparinirvana of Mahatma Buddha, the first Buddhist council was organized in 483 BC in Rajgriha under the patronage of Ajatashatru. This council was presided over by Mahakassapa and Buddha's prominent disciples Ananda and Upali were also present. In this, the teachings of Buddha were compiled and they were divided into two Pitakas named 'Sutta and Vinaya'. The second Buddhist council was organized in 383 BC in Vaishali during the reign of Kalashoka. In this council, Buddhist monks were divided into two sects. The third Buddhist council was called in Pataliputra during the time of Mauryan ruler Ashoka. It was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa; the Sthavira sect predominated in it. In this council, the teachings of Buddha were divided into three parts: 'Sutta Pitaka', 'Vinaya Pitaka' and 'Abhidhamma Pitaka'. The fourth and final council of Buddhism took place in Kundalvan, Kashmir, during the reign of Kushan ruler Kanishka, which was presided over by Vasumitra, and Ashvaghosha became its Vice-President. At this time, Buddhism was divided into two sects, Hinayana and Mahayana.

questions.question_text: Where did Buddha spend the maximum number of rainy retreats (Varshavas)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Buddha gave his first sermon in Sarnath where five Brahmins became his disciples. After this, he started the propagation of the religion. During the rainy season, he would rest in various cities and during the remaining seasons, he would travel from one place to another to propagate his views. He spent the second, third, and fourth rainy seasons in Rajgriha. Moving from Rajgriha, Buddha reached Vaishali, the capital of the Licchavis. There he spent his fifth rainy season. The maximum propagation of Buddhism took place in Shravasti, the capital of the Kosala kingdom. There, Buddha spent twenty-one rainy retreats. The Kosala ruler Prasenajit also accepted the discipleship of Buddha along with his family and built a monastery named 'Pubbarama' for the Sangha. While living in Shravasti, Buddha succeeded in initiating the notorious dacoit named Angulimala, who used to cut off people's fingers and wear them as a garland, into his sect. In this way, Buddha gained more followers in the Kosala kingdom.

questions.question_text: Which of the following dedicated caves for Jains?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Kalinga ruler Kharavela was a great protector of Jainism. He provided protection to Jain monks, gave unprecedented donations for their maintenance, and built comfortable residences for them to live. The purpose of the Hathigumpha inscription was to preserve the details of such monk residences built on Udayagiri hill. However, despite being a Jain himself, he was tolerant towards other religions. In the thirteenth year of his coronation, Kharavela had cave-monasteries built for the residence of Jain monks by cutting the hills of Udayagiri and Khandagiri near Bhubaneswar. 19 cave monasteries were constructed in Udayagiri and 16 in Khandagiri. The images carved in the caves of Ranigumpha in Udayagiri and Anantagumpha in Khandagiri are of high quality from the perspective of art.

questions.question_text: Under which council were the Jain religious texts, the Angas, first compiled?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Due to internal differences in Jainism, the Jain sect was divided into two parts, 'Shvetambara' and 'Digambara', in 300 BC. The people who lived in Magadha were called Shvetambaras. They wore white clothes. Bhadrabahu and his supporters, who believed in remaining naked, were called Digambaras. According to them, only Bhadrabahu had complete knowledge of the ancient Jain scriptures. Since the ancient Jain scriptures were lost, a first grand assembly of Jainism was organized in Pataliputra in the 4th century BC to recollect them and determine their form, but the followers of Bhadrabahu did not participate in it. This conference was presided over by Sthulabhadra. In this conference, the principles of the Jains were compiled into 12 Angas. The grand assembly of Vallabhi has had a special contribution in determining the form of Jainism. This was completed in the sixth century.

questions.question_text: By what name is the wife of Bodhisattva known in Vajrayana Buddhism?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, (Spl.) 2004 Explanation- In Vajrayana Buddhism, the wife of Bodhisattva was known by the name Tara. From the fifth or sixth century AD, the influence of tantra-mantras began to increase on Buddhism, resulting in the birth of a new sect named Vajrayana. In these, a provision for attaining salvation through mantras and tantric rituals was presented. Vajrayanists consider 'Vajra' as a supernatural element. Its identity has been established with Dharma. To attain this, instead of education and penance, emphasis was laid on the consumption of sexual intercourse, meat, etc. The rituals of Vajrayanists are similar to the followers of the Shakta sect. In this, importance has been given to goddesses like Tara etc. It has been propounded that Buddha should be worshipped with enjoyments like form, sound, touch, etc. The practice of passion (Raga-charya) has been described as supreme. The maximum development of Vajrayana took place in the eighth century. Vajrayana paved the way for the decline of Buddhism (in India).

questions.question_text: In which text is the history of early Jainism found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The history of early Jainism is found in the Kalpa Sutra. It is known from the Jain Kalpa Sutra composed by Bhadrabahu that Sudharman died twenty years after Mahavira and after him, Jambu remained the head of the Sangha for 44 years. From the time of the last Nanda king, Sambhutivijaya and Bhadrabahu were the heads of the Sangha. These two were the last persons to know about the 14 Purvas (ancientmost Jain texts) given by Mahavira. Sambhutivijaya died at the time of Chandragupta Maurya's accession; his disciple was Sthulabhadra. At this time, a famine of 12 years occurred in Magadha, as a result of which Bhadrabahu went to Karnataka along with his disciples. They were called Southern Jains (Digambaras) and those who lived under the leadership of Sthulabhadra in Magadha were called Shvetambaras. In the first part of Kalpa Sutra, there is a mention of the 23 Tirthankaras before Mahavira. In the second part, there are rules and principles of Jainism. In the third part, there is a description of Jain stories.

questions.question_text: Who was the teacher of Krishna, the founder of Bhagavatism?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, (Spl.) 2004 Explanation- Vaishnavism developed from Bhagavatism. According to tradition, its founders were Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan, who is called Vasudeva Krishna because he was the son of Vasudeva. He was originally a resident of Mathura. In the Chandogya Upanishad, he is described as the son of Devaki and the disciple of Ghora Angirasa. The followers of Krishna call him 'Bhagavat' (Worshipful). For this reason, the religion initiated by him was designated as Bhagavat. During the Mahabharata period, 'Vasudeva Krishna' was identified with Vishnu. The Vishnu of Bhagavatism is a Rigvedic deity and like other deities, he is a deity of nature. He represents the active form of the Sun. Vishnu's greatest importance is because he measured the entire Earth in three steps. He has been described as Urugaya (of great stride) and 'Urukrama' (of wide-extending foot-throws).

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the founder of the Pashupata sect?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation- The Pashupata sect is the oldest sect of the Shaivas, which originated in the second century BC. According to the Puranas, it was founded by a celibate named Lakulisha or Lakuli. The followers of this sect consider Lakulisha as an incarnation of Shiva. The people of this sect used to carry a staff (lakuta) or danda in their hands, which was considered a symbol of Shiva. Its earliest depiction is found on a coin of the Kushan ruler Huvishka. There were followers of this sect in the Gupta period as well. In the Mathura inscription of the time of Chandragupta II, there is mention of a Pashupata follower named Uditacharya who had two lingas installed. Banabhatta has mentioned this sect in 'Kadambari' and written that its followers smeared ash on their foreheads and wore rudraksha beads in their hands.

questions.question_text: Who were the Nayanars?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, (Spl.) 2004 Explanation- Shiva worship was widely propagated in South India. During the Pallava period, Shaivism was propagated by the Nayanars. The number of Nayanar saints is stated to be 63, among whom the names of Appar, Tirujnana Sambandar, Sundaramurti, Manikkayavachakar, etc., are noteworthy. Their devotional songs were compiled together in the Devalaya. Among these, Appar, whose other name is also found as Tirunavukkarasu, was a contemporary of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I. He was born in the Vellala family of Tiruvamur. It is said that at first, he lived a monk's life in a Jain monastery. Later, by the grace of Shiva, he was cured of an incurable disease, as a result of which he renounced the Jain faith and became a devout Shaivite. Appar performed devotion to Shiva with the attitude of a servant (dasa bhava) and propagated it among the common people.

questions.question_text: Arrange the names of the following historical personalities chronologically and choose your answer from the code given below- (1) Parshvanatha (2) Mahavira (3) Buddha (4) Bhadrabahu Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The chronology of the religious figures is as follows- Parshvanatha 9th century BC, Mahavira 599-527 BC, Buddha 563-483 BC, Bhadrabahu 4th century BC.

questions.question_text: By what name is 'Vardhamana' mentioned in early Buddhist literature?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- In early Buddhist literature, the name of Vardhamana, the real founder of Jainism, who is known as Swami Mahavira, is found as 'Nigantha Nataputta'. In the Jain text Acharanga Sutra, Mahavira's parents are called worshippers of Parshvanatha and followers of Shramanas. In the Rigveda, there is mention of two Tirthankaras of Jainism, Rishabhadeva and Arishtanemi.

questions.question_text: With which of the following was Vardhamana Mahavira related?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Mahavira's mother Trishala was the sister of Chetaka of Vaishali. Bimbisara married Chellana, the daughter of Chetaka. Thus Mahavira was related to Bimbisara.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a contemporary of Buddha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- At the time of Mahatma Buddha (563 BC - 483 BC), the ruler of Magadha was Bimbisara (544 BC - 492 BC). Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty was the founder of the Magadhan Empire. During the time of Buddha himself, Ajatashatru defeated the Kosala ruler Prasenajit. Udayabhadra was not a contemporary ruler of Gautama Buddha.

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts are the names of the sixteen Mahajanapadas mentioned? 1. Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra 2. Bhagavati Sutra and Bhagavata Purana 3. Indriya Jataka and Anguttara Nikaya 4. Lalitavistara and Indriya Jataka Choose your correct answer from the code given below- Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- In the Anguttara Nikaya, a part of the Sutta Pitaka among the Buddhist Tripitakas, and the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra, there is mention of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. In Anguttara Nikaya, there is a mention of Angulimala, and in Bhagavati Sutra, there is a mention of the lives of Jain Tirthankaras.

questions.question_text: Where was Jetavana monastery located?
questions.explanation: Jetavana monastery is located in Shravasti. Shravasti is currently located in Uttar Pradesh. Gautama Buddha gave the maximum number of sermons in Shravasti itself. Gautama Buddha spent the maximum number of rainy retreats in Shravasti itself

questions.question_text: The concept of Bhakti (devotion) was expressed for the first time in-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The mention of 'Bhakti' is found in the Shvetashvatara Upanishad. Vaishnavism, in the form of the Bhagavata sect, initiated the Bhakti movement. In the Aitareya Brahmana, the duties of the four Varnas are described. The Brahmins have been called givers of alms (men), Somapayi (drinkers of Soma), active and wandering at will (Yatha Pramale). The Shatapatha Brahmana gives a place to the Shudra in the Somayajna. In the Brihadaranyaka and Chandogya Upanishads, it is said that everyone is equal in Brahmaloka; therefore, even a Chandala is entitled to receive the remnants of the sacrifice. In the Shatapatha Brahmana, there is a discussion about the spread of Vedic sacrificial rituals towards North-East India. From the Upanishads, we also learn that King Janaka performed large Vedic sacrifices.

questions.question_text: In which of the following religious books are the words 'Bali' and 'Bhaga' used for land tax?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- In the religious books of Buddhist literature, the words 'Bali' and 'Bhaga' are used for land tax. The Brahmin law-makers of this period condemned the practice of lending and interest, as mentioned in the Apastamba and Baudhayana Dharmasutras. However, the practice of taking loans was extremely necessary for trade. In Buddhist texts, there is a discussion of the practice of taking loans for trade, but it has not been condemned. Many instructions have been given to traders regarding the price of goods and efficiency in buying and selling, which prove helpful in their prosperity. In Brahmanism, the conduct related to food and the attitude towards courtesans were not favorable to the activities of civic life, but the beliefs of Buddhism were helpful in the process of urbanization.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct?

options.A: Jainism did not exist before Mahavira
options.B: Mahavira was the founder of Jainism
options.C: Mahavira added one more dimension to the four dimensions of Parshvanatha
options.D: Rather than a founder of a new sect, Mahavira was more of a reformer

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Swami Mahavira was not the founder of Jainism, but he was the last and most famous Tirthankara of this religion. He made necessary reforms in this religion and propagated it on a large scale. According to Jain tradition, there have been 24 Tirthankaras in this religion. Among these, the first is Rishabhadeva and the twenty-third Tirthankara was Parshvanatha. Parshvanatha had established the four-fold (Chaturyama) religion of non-violence (ahimsa), truth (satya), non-stealing (asteya), and non-possession (aparigraha). Mahavira added the fifth vow of celibacy (brahmacharya) to it. Also, Parshvanatha was not against wearing clothes, but Swami Mahavira considered nudity necessary for complete detachment from worldliness. Nudity promotes physical penance and non-possession. Also, a monk becomes free from the illusion of many worldly beliefs like shame etc. Later, based on wearing clothes and remaining naked, Jainism was divided into two sects, Shvetambara and Digambara.

questions.question_text: The book Suvarnaprabhasa Sutra is related to-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Among the Mahayana Sutras, some religious texts famous as Vaipulya Sutras are very important. Some of the important texts among these are- Saddharma-Pundarika, Suvarnaprabhasa, Lalitavistara, Samadhiraja, Madhyamaka Shastra, Vigraha Vyavartani, Shunyata-saptati, Ratnavali, Upaya-Kaushalya, Prajnaparamita Shastra, Ashtasahasrika, Prajnaparamita, Lankavatara Sutra, Samadhiraja Sutra, Karandavyuha Sutra, Dashabhumika Sutra, Suvarnaprabhasa Sutra and Gataguhyaka Sutra, etc.

questions.question_text: Who propagated Buddhism in Avanti?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- During his journey of religious propagation, Gautama Buddha went to Sumsumagiri, the capital of the Bhaggas, and spent the eighth rainy retreat there. Here, Bodhi Kumar became his disciple. From here, he went to Kaushambi, the capital of Vatsaraja Udayana, and took the ninth rest there. From here, Buddha went to Veranja near Mathura where he made the twelfth stay. King Pradyota of Avanti also invited him, but expressing his inability to go there due to his old age, he asked his disciple Mahakachchayana to preach to him. Some followers of Buddha also emerged in Avanti. Buddha also visited Champa and Kajangala and by staying at those places for some time, initiated many people into his faith. The maximum propagation of Buddhism took place in the Kosala kingdom. Here, Buddha made twenty-one stays. A very wealthy merchant named Anathapindika accepted his discipleship.

questions.question_text: Buddha's famous disciple Ananda was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The Shakya republic gave birth to Buddha's famous disciple Ananda. Ashvaghosha is a contemporary writer of Kanishka, whose one verse-bound poem is Saundarananda, which is based on the context of Buddha's step-brother Ananda being initiated into Buddhism. Since Buddha was the son of King Shuddhodana and King Shuddhodana was the king of the Shakya republic in North-East Bihar. Kanishka spread his kingdom from Magadha to West Asia, but his fame is much more due to his being a patron of Buddhism. His personal religion was Buddhism; he did many things for its propagation and organization. At the behest of Parshva, he organized the fourth grand assembly (Mahasabha) of Buddhists in Kashmir Kundalvan, in which many scholars participated. The head of this assembly was Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha was the Vice-President.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a Buddhist work?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation- Baveru Jataka, Dasharatha Jataka and Shibi Jataka are Buddhist works, while Yavana Jataka is an astrological text.

questions.question_text: Who among the following lived longer than the others?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation- Devadatta was the son of Gautama Buddha's maternal uncle who was also a disciple of Buddha. His life ended during the time of Buddha himself. Therefore, in the question, Ajatashatru is the only option who lived longer than the others.

questions.question_text: In Jainism, 'Sallekhana' refers to-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation- In Jainism, 'Sallekhana' refers to giving up life through fasting. Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta Maurya became a Jain in the last days of his life. At the end of his reign, a famine of 12 years occurred in Magadha. Failing to deal with the famine situation, Chandragupta Maurya renounced the throne in favor of his son and went to perform penance in Shravanabelagola (Mysore) with Bhadrabahu. At this very place, he gave up his life through the Sallekhana method.

questions.question_text: The teachings of Parshvanatha are collectively known as:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation- Parshvanatha was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism. He had prescribed only 4 vows for monks - non-violence (ahimsa), truth (satya), non-stealing (asteya) and non-possession (aparigraha). Later, the 24th Tirthankara Swami Mahavira added a fifth vow, celibacy (brahmacharya), to this and made it mandatory to follow it. Under 'Triratna' in Jainism, (a) Right perception (samyak darshana), (b) Right knowledge (samyak jnana), (c) Right conduct (samyak charitra) have been kept and these have been stated as three necessary means for salvation. In Pancha Mahavrata, there are - non-violence, truth, non-stealing, non-possession, and celibacy.

questions.question_text: According to Mahavamsa, who went to the Himalayan region after the third Buddhist council?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation- According to the Ceylonese traditions Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa, the third council of Buddhism took place in Pataliputra during the reign of Ashoka. It was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa. After this council, monks were sent to different countries for the propagation of Buddhism, whose names are obtained in Mahavamsa as follows- Religious Preacher - Country 1. Majjhantika - 1. Kashmir and Gandhara 2. Maharakkhita - 2. Yavana Country 3. Majjhima - 3. Himalayan Country 4. Dharmarakkhita - 4. Aparantaka 5. Mahadharmarakkhita - 5. Maharashtra 6. Mahadeva - 6. Mahishamandala (Mysore or Mandhata) 7. Rakkhita - 7. Banavasi (North Kanara) 8. Sona and Uttara - 8. Suvarnabhumi 9. Mahendra and Sanghamitra - 9. Lanka

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists: List-I (Tirthankara) List-II (Birthplace) A. Rishabhanatha 1. Kashi B. Sambhavanatha 2. Kaushambi C. Padmanatha 3. Shravasti D. Parshvanatha 4. Ayodhya Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Rishabhanatha—He was the first Tirthankara of Jainism. He was the first Chakravartin emperor of Jambudvipa and in his old age, he gave the kingdom to his son Bharata and became a Tirthankara himself. His birthplace was Ayodhya. Sambhavanatha—He was the third Tirthankara of Jainism. He was born in Shravasti. The 8th Tirthankara Chandraprabhu was also born here. Makkhali Gosala, the main preacher of the Ajivika sect, was also born in Shravasti. Padmanatha—He was a Tirthankara of Jainism. He was born in Kaushambi. In medieval Jain texts, Kaushambi is referred to as Vividha Tirtha Kalpa. This place is also considered a pilgrimage site for Buddhism. Parshvanatha—He was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism. He was the son of King Ashvasena of Varanasi. His marriage took place with Princess Prabhavati of the Kushasthala country.

questions.question_text: Who among the following scholars established the Vajrayana sect of Buddhism in Tibet?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: The entry of Buddhism into Tibet occurred in the 4th century. In the 8th century, the King of Tibet invited the Indian Acharya named Shantarakshita to come to Tibet. With the help of Acharya Padmasambhava, Shantarakshita preached Buddhism in Tibet. Shantarakshita was an Acharya of the Sarvastivada sect. He called 12 other scholars from India for his assistance, and through their efforts, Tibetan people began to become Buddhist monks. Padmasambhava believed in Tantric rituals; through his efforts, Vajrayana entered Tibet.

questions.question_text: Which of the following places did Buddha not visit?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Mahatma Buddha did not visit Ujjayini; instead, he sent one of his disciples named Mahakatyayana there to preach the religion. He visited other places such as Vaishali, Kapilavastu, and Kaushambi. In Vaishali, he spent several rainy seasons. Here, the Licchavis built the famous Kutagarasala for Buddha in the Mahavana. In Vaishali itself, the city-courtesan Amrapali became a disciple of Buddha. It was here that Buddha first gave permission for women to enter his Sangha. Similarly, during his stay in Rajgriha, Buddha visited his home city Kapilavastu several times and initiated all the members of his family into his faith. In the course of his religious propagation, Buddha also visited Kaushambi, the capital of Vatsaraja Udayana.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Shaiva sect? 1. Pashupata 2. Jangama 3. Satvata 4. Kapalika Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Along with the development of Shaivism, various groups who worshipped Shiva in different ways also developed, who worshipped Shiva according to their own thoughts, beliefs, and principles. Gradually, separate groups of such worshippers were formed which became established as independent Shaiva sects. In Shaivagama, the number of such Shaiva sects is stated to be four - (1) Shaiva, (2) Pashupata, (3) Kapalika, (4) Kalamukha. In this, the founder of the Pashupata sect was a brahmachari named Lakulisha, who is considered an incarnation of Shiva. The mention of Kapalikas is found in the play named 'Malatimadhava'. The followers of the Vira Shaiva sect were called Lingayats or 'Jangama'. Kalamukha was also a major Shaiva sect which was called 'Mahavratadhara'. Vasudeva is called Satvatarsama or Satvata.

questions.question_text: Where was the earliest epigraphic evidence mentioning the birthplace of Shakyamuni Buddha found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation- Mauryan Emperor Ashoka's Rummindei pillar inscription is the earliest epigraphic evidence mentioning the birthplace of Shakyamuni Buddha. In the 20th year of his coronation, Ashoka went to Lumbini village. He built a strong stone wall there and erected a stone pillar. Since Lord Buddha was born there, the village of Lumbini was declared tax-free and the announcement was made to take only 1/8th part of the produce. This information is obtained from the Rummindei minor pillar inscription.

questions.question_text: Kurchaka was a sect of—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation—Digambara and Shvetambara were the two main sects of Jainism. Besides these, the Yapaniya sect was established by a Shvetambara monk Shri Kalasha in 148 AD. In the inscriptions of Kadamba rulers, along with Shvetambara, Digambara, and Yapaniya sects, the mention of Kurchaka and Shvetapata Jain sects is also found.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I (Jain Tirthankara) List-II (Identification) A. Shantinatha 1. Deer B. Mallinatha 2. Lion C. Parshvanatha 3. Serpent D. Mahavira 4. Water-jar (Kalasha) Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—There were a total of 24 Tirthankaras in Jainism—(1) Rishabha or Adinatha, (2) Ajitanatha, (3) Sambhava, (4) Abhinandana, (5) Sumati, (6) Padmaprabha, (7) Suparshva, (8) Chandraprabhu, (9) Pushpadanta, (10) Shitala, (11) Shreyansa, (12) Vasupujya, (13) Vimala, (14) Ananta, (15) Dharma, (16) Shanti, (17) Kunthu, (18) Ara, (19) Malli, (20) Munisuvrata, (21) Naminatha, (22) Arishtanemi, (23) Parshvanatha, (24) Mahavira. The symbol of Shantinatha was the deer, Mallinatha's was the water-jar, Parshvanatha's was the serpent, and Mahavira's was the lion.

questions.question_text: In search of knowledge before attaining Bodhi, to which teachers did Siddhartha Gautama go? 1. Alara Kalama 2. Udraka Ramaputra 3. Makkhali Gosala 4. Nigantha Nataputta Indicate your answer from the following code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—After renouncing home, Buddha wandered from one place to another in search of knowledge and first went to the ashram of an ascetic named Alara Kalama near Vaishali. He performed penance there but did not find peace. From here, he reached another teacher named Udraka Ramaputra, who lived in an ashram near Rajgriha. Even here, his restless mind could not find peace. Being distressed, he left him as well and decided to perform penance alone at a place named Uruvela (Bodh Gaya). It was here that he attained knowledge.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code below: Assertion (A): Gautama Buddha lived in Shravasti during the maximum number of rainy seasons. Code: Reason (R): King Prasenajit of Shravasti was of the same age as Gautama Buddha.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—Buddhism propagated the most in the Kosala kingdom. Buddha stayed there for 21 rainy seasons. An extremely wealthy merchant named Anathapindaka became his disciple and purchased the Jetavana Vihara from Prince Jeta for 18 crore gold coins and provided it to the Sangha. King Prasenajit of Kosala and King Pradyota of Avanti were contemporaries of Gautama Buddha. Prasenajit along with his family became a disciple of Buddha and built a Vihara named 'Pubbarama' for the Sangha. The maximum number of followers of Buddha were in the Kosala kingdom. Therefore, both statements are correct, but Assertion A is not correctly explained by Reason R.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—Evidence of the existence of several republics in the Ganges valley during the Buddha period is found— (1) Shakyas of Kapilavastu, (2) Bhaggas of Sumsumagiri Hill, (3) Bullis of Allakappa, (4) Kalamas of Kesaputta, (5) Koliyas of Ramagrama, (6) Mallas of Kushinara, (7) Mallas of Pava, (8) Moriyas of Pipphalivana, (9) Licchavis of Vaishali, (10) Videhas of Mithila.

questions.question_text: With which of the following sects is the 'Santhara' practice associated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation— The Santhara practice is related to the Jain sect. This is also called the Sallekhana practice, in which life is sacrificed through fasting.

questions.question_text: What is 'Kalyana Mitra' in Buddhist philosophy?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– Regarding the Eightfold Path, Mahatma Buddha says to Ananda, "O Ananda, at this time I have also established this Kalyanavartya i.e., Kalyana-mitra which is for complete detachment, for dispassion, for cessation, for tranquility, for direct knowledge, for enlightenment, and for Nirvana—this is the Noble Eightfold Path. In fact, following the Eightfold Path was considered necessary for every spiritual practice because the attainment of the state of Nirvana was possible through this only.

questions.question_text: Which one of the four Noble Truths in Buddhism explains the principle of 'Pratityasamutpada'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – All twelve forms of Pratityasamutpada are derived from the four Noble Truths themselves. Some of these are causes of the past and are in the form of effects in the present, and some are causes in the present and are for effects to occur in the future. In this way, the second 'Noble Truth' (Dukkha Samudaya) is related to it, and the causes of the present birth that relate to previous births are in the form of 'Dukkha Samudaya'. Therefore, Pratityasamutpada states the cause-effect relationship which matches the second principle of the four Noble Truths in which it is said that "Suffering has a cause."

questions.question_text: The earliest Jain bronze idols have been found from—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–The earliest Jain bronze idols have been found from Chausa. In addition to this, a huge stone statue of Gommateshwara has been found from Shravanabelagola. The world-famous Nalanda University was located in Nalanda, and twenty caves were carved out of Udayagiri to create idols related to Hindu and Jain sects.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I (Acharya) List-II (Religion) A. Haribhadra 1. Buddhism B. Lakulisha 2. Jainism C. Nathamuni 3. Shaivism D. Vasubandhu 4. Vaishnavism Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–Haribhadra was a scholar of Jainism. According to the Puranas, the Pashupata sect was established by a brahmachari named Lakulisha or Lakuli. Nathamuni is a scholar of Vaishnavism, while the Buddhist sect named Vijnanavada (Yogachara) was established by Maitreyanatha in the third century AD. Asanga and Vasubandhu developed it.

questions.question_text: Gosala first met Mahavira Swami at:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– Gosala first met Mahavira Swami in Nalanda. Mahavira Swami was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism. Gosala first met Mahavira Swami in Nalanda. Gosala initially became a disciple of Mahavira Swami, but later due to differences of opinion, he left Mahavira and established an independent sect named 'Ajivika'.

questions.question_text: The principle of 'Pratityasamutpada' is related to–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The principle of 'Pratityasamutpada' is related to Buddhism. Just as birth is the cause of the accumulation of suffering, similarly birth is also a cycle of ignorance that produces the fruit of action, which in technical terminology is called Pratityasamutpada (or Paticcasamuppada in the Pali language), meaning 'Pratitya' (on this being) 'Samutpada' (this arises). There are 12 links in this cycle, which are the causes of producing one another, these are – (1) Avidya (Ignorance), (2) Samskara (Mental formations), (3) Vijnana (Consciousness), (4) Namarupa (Name and form), (5) Sadayatana (Six sense bases), (6) Sparsha (Contact), (7) Vedana (Feeling), (8) Trishna (Thirst/Craving), (9) Upadana (Clinging), (10) Bhava (Becoming), (11) Jati (Birth), (12) Jara-marana (Old age and death).

questions.question_text: Where did the Mahasanghika school originate?
