questions.explanation: The Mahasanghika school was related to Buddhism which was located in Vaishali. Its president was Sabakami. To resolve differences regarding discipline, Buddhism was divided into two parts: Sthavira and Mahasanghika

questions.question_text: ‘Mahaparinibbana of Buddha’ was an event during the reign of which ruler of Magadha?
questions.explanation: The Mahaparinibbana of Buddha is related to the reign of the Magadha ruler Ajatashatru. Digha Nikaya (in Sanskrit language) is related to the Sutta Pitaka. Mahaparinibbana Sutta is a part of Digha Nikaya. It is related to the death of Mahatma Buddha and his Parinirvana. It is the longest sutra of the Tripitaka

questions.question_text: The Fourth Buddhist Council was organized:
questions.explanation: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in the first century AD at Kundalavana in Kashmir. At that time, it was the reign of Kanishka of the Kushana dynasty. The council was presided over by Vasumitra and the vice-president was Ashvagosha. In this council, Buddhism was divided into two sects: Hinayana and Mahayana

questions.question_text: _______ During the period of, the Haryanka dynasty reached its peak.
questions.explanation: Haryanka dynasty (544 BC - 412 BC). Bimbisara was the founder of this dynasty. His son Ajatashatru obtained power by killing his father. He was the most glorious king of this dynasty. He annexed Kashi and Vajji to the Magadha empire after a long struggle. During his tenure, the first Buddhist council was organized in Rajgriha

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is wrong?
questions.explanation: Ajatashatru was the king of Magadha. During his time, the first Buddhist council was organized in Rajgriha. His son Udayin killed him and became the king of Magadha, who founded the city of Pataliputra (Kusumapura)

questions.question_text: Jivaka was the royal physician of which king?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The great Ayurveda practitioner Jivaka was born from the womb of the courtesan Salavati of Rajgriha. He was brought up under the protection of Prince Abhaya, the son of the Haryanka dynasty ruler Bimbisara. After being brought up, he was sent to Taxila for studies where he studied Ayurveda extensively. After returning from there, Bimbisara appointed him as his royal physician. He was sent to serve Buddha for the diagnosis of some incurable disease. After that, he became a follower of Buddhism.

questions.question_text: Kalashoka was related to –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Kalashoka (Kakavarna) was related to the Shishunaga dynasty. According to Sinhalese epics, about a hundred years after the Mahaparinirvana of Gautama Buddha, in the tenth year of Kalashoka's reign, the second Buddhist council (383 BC) was organized in Vaishali.

questions.question_text: Who was the last emperor of the Nanda dynasty?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 DSSSB PGT 10/07/2021 Explanation–According to the Puranas, the founder of the Nanda dynasty was Mahapadmananda and the last emperor was Dhanananda. In 322 BC, Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of his guru Chanakya, killed Dhanananda and laid the foundation of the rule of the Mauryan dynasty.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Udayin or Udayabhadra founded the city named Pataliputra. Udayin established Pataliputra city right at the confluence of Ganga and Son and moved his capital there from Rajgriha. It was surrounded by a perimeter. Gates were built for entry into it and archer soldiers were stationed for the security of the city.

questions.question_text: As mentioned by Gautama and Baudhayana, the annual interest rate in the post-Vedic period was:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Mention is found in the post-Vedic period details related to land revenue by Gautama and Baudhayana that annual interest was collected at the rate of 15 percent.

questions.question_text: Which was the capital of the Vajji confederacy during the sixteen Mahajanapada period?
questions.explanation: The Vajji confederacy was one of the 16 Mahajanapadas of ancient India. This Mahajanapada was located to the north of Magadha. It originated from the combination of several small states. This confederacy was formed by the union of 8 clans. In which 4 (Videha, Jnatrika, Vajji, Licchavi) clans were more important. Its capital was Vaishali

questions.question_text: According to the Baudhayana Sutra, the king protected his subjects, in return for which he received from the subjects
questions.explanation: According to the Baudhayana Sutra, since the Vedic period, the king has been the protector, nourisher, and supporter of the subjects. The subjects follow him. The classical theory of taxation has also been presented in the epics and Smritis. Following Kautilya, Gautama, Baudhayana, and Narada have also discussed the theory of taxation. According to them, the king is the owner of the entire land and he can receive 1/6th part from the subjects. However, different opinions are found regarding the ownership period of the land

questions.question_text: Arrange the following inscriptions in chronological order:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The systematic chronology of the inscriptions is as follows. * Boghazkoi inscription – 1400 B.C. from Asia Minor. * Three inscriptions of the reign of Darius * Behistun – 520-518 B.C. * Persepolis – 518-515 B.C. * Naqsh-e-Rustam – 515 B.C. Mention of 'Hindu' occurred as a province of his empire in these writings.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Dharma-sutrakaras considers the practice of Niyoga as improper?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– To keep Vedic literature intact, Sutra literature was composed. Such sutras in which mention of religious, social, and political duties is found are called Dharmasutras. In the Apastamba Dharmasutra, the practice of Niyoga is stated as improper.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—To keep the Vedic literature intact and to condense it, Sutra literature was composed between the 6th century BC and the 3rd century BC. Their total number is 6 – Education (Shiksha), Rituals (Kalpa), Grammar (Vyakarana), Etymology (Nirukta), Meters (Chhanda), and Astronomy (Jyotisha). Education (Shiksha) was composed for the correct pronunciation of Vedic vowels. Kalpa means rituals or prescribed rules. It has three parts – Shrauta Sutra (provisions regarding sacrifice and rituals), one part of which is the Sulba Sutra where the measurement of sacrificial altars etc. is mentioned. Geometry is considered to have started from this. Grihya Sutras contain details of domestic rituals and sacrifices, while Dharma Sutras mention political, social, and religious duties. The function of Grammar is to provide a scientific style to the language. Nirukta means etymology. Chhanda (Meters) was composed to bind verses into feet, while Jyotisha (Astronomy) is the subject of prediction regarding the universe and stars.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): Gautam Buddha spent a large number of rainy seasons (Varshavas) in Shravasti, which was a major city of Kosala. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct? Reason (R): Gautam Buddha and King Prasenajit of Kosala were of the same age.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation—Mahatma Buddha reached Shravasti in the 20th year of attaining enlightenment and there he made a dacoit named Angulimala his disciple. The maximum number of Buddha's disciples were in the Kosala state and here he propagated his religion the most. King Prasenajit of Kosala was also a disciple of Buddha and described himself as being the same age as Mahatma Buddha. Buddha spent the maximum of 21 rainy seasons (Varshavas) in the Jetavana Vihara of Shravasti. He had made a rule of 4 months of rainy season residence and 8 months of propagation in a year.

questions.question_text: In the course of Ajatashatru's war against Chetaka, the ruler of Vaishali, where did Ajatashatru's minister Vassakara meet Buddha?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2015) Explanation—In the course of Ajatashatru's war against Chetaka, the ruler of Vaishali, Ajatashatru's minister Vassakara met Buddha in Rajgriha. This is mentioned in the Buddhist text 'Mahaparinibbana Sutta'. In this regard, it is known that Ajatashatru consulted Mahatma Buddha and he told him that the destruction of the Vajji confederacy is possible only through creating a rift (dissension). Subsequently, he sent his minister Vassakara to create a rift in the Vajji confederacy.

questions.question_text: Where was Prasenajit the king of?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation—Mention of 16 Mahajanapadas is found in the Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra. In the 6th century BC, there were various kings of these Janapadas. Among them, the capital of Kosala was Shravasti; the king here, Prasenajit, was a contemporary of Buddha. The Kosala Mahajanapada was formed by combining modern Faizabad and some nearby districts.

questions.question_text: 'Bhagavapi Kosalako Ahamapi Kosalako' (The Lord is a Kosalan, I too am a Kosalan) is a quote from which Buddhist text?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation- 'Bhagavapi Kosalako Ahamapi Kosalako' is a quote from the Majjhima Nikaya Buddhist text. Kosala was established by combining modern Faizabad, Basti, Shravasti etc. At the time of Buddha, the king here was Prasenajit and he was also a friend and patron of Lord Buddha. Buddha spent twenty-one rainy seasons of his life in Shravasti itself. Shravasti was the capital of Kosala at that time.

questions.question_text: In which text is the earliest pre-Mauryan mention of Anga found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- There is mention of Anga country in Pali literature. Its capital was Champa. The modern area of Bhagalpur and Munger was included in the ancient Anga country. At the time of Gautam Buddha, a state of constant war existed between the Anga and Magadha Janapadas. For some time, Magadha became a part of the Anga country, but soon Anga declined and Bimbisara brought not only Magadha but also Anga under his control. Mention of the Anga country is found in the Atharvaveda where it is called a distant region.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order:
questions.explanation: Persepolis was a magnificent city and capital of the Achaemenid Empire of Iran. It was a great city during the time of Darius I (522-486 BC). Alexander started his conquest campaign in the eastern direction along with burning this city. Finally, in 327 BC, Alexander established dominance over Eastern Iran across the Hindu Kush. Due to his generals and adverse circumstances, Alexander planned to return from India in 326 BC. After Alexander's death, an agreement for the division of his empire took place at Triparadisus in Babylonia in 323 BC, which was completed in several stages later

questions.question_text: Which of the following Greek accounts predates Alexander?
questions.explanation: After the Iranian invasion, India had to face the Greek invasion, i.e., the invasion of the Macedonian ruler Alexander. Greek writers prior to Alexander were Herodotus and Ctesias

questions.question_text: Who among the following were Shaiva Acharyas in the South?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation—Worshippers of Shiva were called Shaivas and the religion related to them was called Shaivism. This is an ancient religion of India. Its antiquity goes back to proto-history (Indus civilization), as Marshall proved the image inscribed on a seal obtained from Mohenjo-daro to be the early form of Shiva. The name Rudra for Shiva is found in the Rigveda. There he was the god of the atmosphere. Rudra is described in three hymns of the Rigveda. The saints who propagated Shaivism in South India were called Nayanars. Their total number was 63. In the South, the Shaiva Acharya Sundaramurti was given the title of Tambiran-tolan (Friend of God).

questions.question_text: Who among the following came to India with Alexander during his Indian military campaigns?
questions.explanation: Nearchus (Admiral) and Onesicritus and Aristobulus also came with Alexander during his Indian military campaigns

questions.question_text: Which of the following metals was responsible for the second urbanization in India?
questions.explanation: The period of second urbanization is considered to be 600-321 BC. It is called second urbanization because for the first time after the fall of Harappa, details of cities are found in the literature of the 6th century BC. Iron played the most important role in the second urbanization

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (State)
questions.explanation: List-I (State) (A) Avanti - (i) Malwa region of Western Central India (B) Gandhara - (ii) Modern Peshawar and Rawalpindi districts and Kashmir Valley (C) Chedi - (iii) Eastern part of Bundelkhand in Central India (D) Vajji - (iv) Northern part of Ganga up to the hills of Nepal

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the founder of Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: The third ruler of the Haryanka dynasty and son of Ajatashatru (ruled from 461 BC to 445 BC). According to Puranas and Jain texts, he established a city named Pataliputra (Kusumapura) at the confluence of Ganga and Son rivers and made it his capital. Udayin was a follower of Jainism. Udayin had obtained power by killing his father Ajatashatru

questions.question_text: At the time of Alexander's invasion of India, in which of the following regions did two kings rule along with a council of elders?
questions.explanation: Alexander was the son of Philip II, the Satrap of Macedon. At the time of his invasion of India, there were a total of 28 independent powers present in the regions of Punjab and Sindh. Chief among them were - (I) Saubhuti (Sophytes) state - A monarchy on the banks of Jhelum. (II) Kshudraka - A republic situated on the banks of the Beas River. (III) Patala (Patale) - This monarchy was situated in the delta of the Indus River; Patala was its capital. Similar to Sparta, there was a "Diarchy system" where two kings ruled along with a council. (IV) Puru - Situated between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers

questions.question_text: In which of the following Dharma Sutras is sea voyage called a degrading act (Pataniya Karma)?
questions.explanation: In Baudhayana Dharma Sutra, sea voyage has been called a degrading act. Baudhayana was an ancient Indian mathematician and the author of Sulba Sutras and Shrauta Sutras. At that time, geometry in India was called Shulba Shastra

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below: List-I (Mahajanapada) A. Asmaka B. Avanti C. Chedi D. Kamboja List-II (Capital) (i) Hataka (ii) Mahishmati (iii) Potali (iv) Shuktimati Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation— List I (Mahajanapada): List-II (Capital) Asmaka – Potali/Potana Avanti – Mahishmati Chedi – Shuktimati Kamboja – Hataka

questions.question_text: Which was the main city of the Asmaka Mahajanapada?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- At the beginning of the 6th century BC, there was a complete lack of sovereign power in North India. The entire region was divided into many independent states. No ruler of this period was capable of organizing under the bond of political unity. An authentic description of the political situation of this period is not available from any literary evidence; however, it is known from the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya that before the rise of Mahatma Gautam Buddha, the whole of North India was divided into 16 large states. These were called 16 Mahajanapadas. Among these Mahajanapadas, Asmaka (Asmaka or Ashvaka) was situated on the banks of the Godavari River (Andhra Pradesh). Its capital was Potana or Potila. Among the Mahajanapadas, only Asmaka was situated in South India. It is known from the Puranas that the monarchy of Asmaka was established by the Ikshvaku dynasty rulers. Before Mahatma Buddha, there was a continuous conflict between Asmaka and Avanti and during the Buddha period, Avanti conquered it and integrated it within its borders.

questions.question_text: The mention of five heroes of the Vrishni clan occurs in which of the following inscriptions?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The concept of Vrishni heroes dates before the second century BC. Its oldest mention is found in the Brahma Sutras. From an inscription of the 1st century obtained from Mora near Mathura, it is known that a woman named Tosha had established the idols of the said four persons (Sankarshana, Pradyumna, Samba, Aniruddha) along with Vasudeva, and Vasudeva in a temple. All use only Bhagavata analysis. Mention of worshippers of Sankarshana is also found in the Arthashastra; it seems that like Krishna, the other four also propounded new theories and became established as religious teachers (Dharmacharyas), later divinity was attributed to them. Considering Vasudeva Krishna as the ultimate reality, the other four were accepted as his parts. Sankarshana, Aniruddha, and Pradyumna were considered symbols of Life (Jiva), Ego (Ahankara), and Mind/Intelligence (Buddhi) respectively.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was related to Vishishtadvaita?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Among Indian philosophers, after Shankara, the name of Ramanuja is very important, who was the propounder of Vishishtadvaita Vedanta. He attempted to establish a coordination of Advaitism with personal devotionalism through his thoughts. He was born in 1017 in the Kerala province of the South and lived for 120 years. He was a disciple of Yamunacharya. Ramanuja explains the philosophical ideas inherent in the Upanishads in his own way and states that although God is the only transcendental reality, He is qualified (Vishishta) or combined with unconscious nature and conscious soul. For this reason, his view is called Vishishtadvaita. Ramanuja was a worshipper of Saguna Ishvara and a famous Vaishnava Acharya. Through his thoughts, he provided a philosophical basis by taking forward the tradition of ancient Bhagavata (Vaishnava) religion. He also wrote a commentary on the Gita and his thoughts are found in Shri Bhashya and Vedartha Sangraha.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and choose the correct answer using the code given below the lists- List I (Janapada) A. Asmaka B. Mulaka C. Kalinga D. Avanti List II (Capitals) 1. Potana 2. Pratishthana 3. Tosali 4. Ujjayini Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Asmaka (Ashvaka) Mahajanapada was situated on the banks of the Godavari River (Andhra); its capital was Potana or Potila. Among the Mahajanapadas, only Asmaka was situated in South India. It is known from the Puranas that the monarchy of Asmaka was established by the Ikshvaku dynasty rulers. The capital of Mulaka was Pratishthana and the capital of Kalinga was Tosali. The Avanti Mahajanapada was settled in the region of Western and Central Malwa. It had two parts - Northern Avanti whose capital was Ujjayini and Southern Avanti whose capital was Mahishmati. The Vetravati River flowed between the two. It is known from Pali religious texts that during the Buddha period, the capital of Avanti was Ujjayini itself where Pradyota was the king. Ujjayini is identified with the modern Ujjain city of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question_text: The Mora inscription near Mathura is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The Mora inscription located near Mathura is related to Vaishnavism. This 1st-century inscription belongs to a woman named Tosha. This inscription mentions the establishment of idols of the five Vrishni heroes related to Vaishnavism. Vaishnavism evolved from Bhagavata religion. According to tradition, its propounder was Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan who is called Vasudeva Krishna due to being the son of Vasudeva. He was originally a resident of Mathura. In the Chandogya Upanishad, he is called Devakiputra and described as a disciple of Ghora Angirasa. From Mathura, Bhagavata religion gradually started spreading to other parts of India. After the Mauryan period, this religion became extremely popular in Central India. This religion developed during the time of the Shungas and foreigners also started adopting it. Information about the popularity of this religion is also obtained from archaeological evidence. The first stone monument related to Bhagavata religion is the Garuda Pillar of Besnagar, Vidisha.

questions.question_text: The capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada was situated in:
questions.explanation: Among the 16 Mahajanapadas, the name of Vatsa was counted among the powerful Janapadas. The capital of Vatsa was Kaushambi. The four powerful monarchies during the Buddha period were Kosala, Magadha, Vatsa, and Avanti. In ancient times, ancient sages considered monarchy as the most prevalent and excellent system of governance

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors was not responsible for the rise of cities in the 6th century BC?
questions.explanation: For the rise of cities in the 6th century BC, the use of iron in eastern Uttar Pradesh and western Bihar, economic change due to agricultural surplus, increase in trade activities etc. were responsible factors. Whereas floods in the Indus river were responsible for the fall of the Indus civilization, not for the rise of urban civilization

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mahajanapadas did not have a monarchical rule in the 6th century BC?
questions.explanation: Evidence of 16 Mahajanapadas is found in the 6th century BC, which is mentioned in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya and the Jain text 'Bhagavati Sutra'. Among these 16 Mahajanapadas, there were 10 republics. Among them, 8 were under the Vajji confederacy and 2 under the Mallas

questions.question_text: Whose Guru was Govinda?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Shankaracharya was born in 788 AD in Kaladi village of Kerala. His father's name was Shivaguru and his Guru's name was Govinda Yogi. Shankaracharya presented the view of Advaitism.

questions.question_text: Where did Shankaracharya meet Kumarila?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The famous 8th-century Hindu thinker Shankaracharya, who established Sanatana Dharma by strongly opposing Buddhism. Shankaracharya met the Mimamsa scholar Kumarila Bhatta in Prayag. Born in Kaladi, Kerala, Shankaracharya established four monasteries in India—Badrinath, Kedarnath, Rameshwaram, and Jagannath Puri—and propagated Vedic philosophy.

questions.question_text: Besarh can be identified with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Besarh is identified with ancient Vaishali. Vaishali is a city in the Ganga Valley. It is situated in the state of Bihar. The other name of this city was also Vishala. It is believed that it was established by a king named 'Nabhanedishta' of the Ikshvaku dynasty. It is included in the main tourist spots of Bihar. Mahavira Swami was born in the Jnatrika clan of Kundagram near Vaishali

questions.question_text: Who among the following is not an Alwar saint?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- In the Tamil region, Vaishnavism was propagated by Alwar saints. The word 'Alwar' means 'wise person'. The number of Alwar saints is said to be twelve, among whom names like Tirumangai, Periyalwar, Andal, Nammalwar etc. are especially noteworthy. Their emergence took place between the 7th and 9th centuries. Among the early Alwar saints, the names of Poygai, Pudam, and Pey are found, who were residents of Kanchi, Mallai, and Bhayalappuram respectively. They preached devotion in a direct and simple manner. Their ideas were free from narrowness or sectarian tension. After them, the name of Tirumangai is found, who possibly lived during the time of Pallava King Mahendravarman I. Tirumangai was an extremely famous Alwar saint. By attacking Jainism and Buddhism through his devotional songs, he strongly propagated Vaishnavism. Tirujnana was a Nayanar (Shaiva) saint. " } ```

questions.question_text: In which of these is the mention of remissions from royal demands and claims found?
questions.explanation: From the Nasik inscription of Gautamiputra Satakarni, it is known that two different guilds of weavers were given a permanent deposit (Akshayanivi) of 2000 Karshapanas at a monthly interest rate of one percent. Similarly, another fund of 1000 Karshapanas was deposited, on which 3/4 percent monthly interest was given. The guilds could also give donations in their own name. Thus, it is clear that the Nasik inscription of Gautamiputra Satakarni mentions remissions from royal demands and claims In the Sarnath minor pillar inscription, Ashoka gives orders to his 'Mahamatras' to prevent schism in the Sangha. The primary source for the history of Samudragupta is his inscription known as the 'Allahabad Pillar Inscription' or 'Prayag Prashasti'. It was composed by his 'Sandhivigrahika' (Minister of War and Peace) Secretary, Harishena. The Junagarh inscription of the Shaka Mahakshatrapa Rudradaman dates to Shaka Samvat 72 (78+72 = 150 AD). It is one of the oldest inscriptions written in pure Sanskrit. It is the first inscription written in the Champu style (mixture of prose and poetry).

questions.question_text: The authors of Vasavadatta and Ravanavadha are—
questions.explanation: Vasavadatta is a Sanskrit play. Its author is Subandhu. Subandhu is said to have lived in the sixth century AD. Scholars are of the opinion that descriptive portions are more prominent in his poetry. Subandhu has said nothing about himself except 'Sujanekabandhu' (a friend to good people). Regarding his personal life and personality, just like his time and place, it can only be said on the basis of inference that he was a follower of the Vedic religion. Bhattikavya is an epic poem composed by the great poet Bhatti. Its real name is 'Ravanavadha'. It describes the story of Lord Rama from his birth to the destruction of Ravana, the lord of Lanka. This epic is a mixture of art and science due to being a blend of the two great traditions of Sanskrit literature: the Ramayana and Panini's grammar Bhavabhuti was an ancient scholar whose three plays are very famous. They are as follows: (1) Malatimadhava (2) Uttararamacharita (3) Mahaviracharita. Magha was the author of the oldest epic of Marwar, 'Shishupala Vadha'. He is one of the trinity of the greatest Sanskrit epic poets. After Kalidasa and Ashvaghosha, the third noteworthy epic poet is Bharavi. However, his poetry is also called the 'Vichitra Marga' (strange path). His work is Kiratarjuniyam. Bhartruhari is famous as a moralist (Nitikar) who was a great poet of Sanskrit. The didactic stories of his 'Shatakatraya' (three centuries of verses) particularly influence the Indian public consciousness.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following according to their chronological order.
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order is (B) Menander – Greek ruler (A) Gondophares – Indo-Parthian/Pahlava dynasty (D) Chastana – Kardamaka dynasty (C) Rudradaman – Shaka dynasty

questions.question_text: The first epigraphic reference to Bharad-varsha (Bharatvarsha) is obtained from:
questions.explanation: The 'Hathigumpha Inscription' of Kharavela, written in the Prakrit language in the latter half of the 1st century BC, was found at Udayagiri hill near Bhubaneswar in Odisha. In this inscription, the first mention of Bharad-varsha (Bharatvarsha) is found. Kharavela was the powerful ruler of the Chedi dynasty (Mahameghavahana dynasty). He was a follower of Jainism The Besnagar inscription of Heliodorus was found in Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh. It reveals that the Greek ambassador Heliodorus, being influenced by Vedic religion, adopted the Bhagavata religion. The oldest eulogy (Prashasti) written in Sanskrit is Rudradaman's Junagarh inscription. It is written in the Champu style (mixture of prose and poetry). The first epigraphic evidence providing information about the Ashvamedha sacrifice is Dhanadeva's Ayodhya inscription.

questions.question_text: According to the inscription of Nasik Cave number 10, the interest rate on Akshayanivi (permanent endowment) in the Shaka-Satavahana period was:
questions.explanation: The Nasik Cave number 10 inscription of Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta), the son-in-law of the Shaka (Kshaharata) ruler Nahapana, is the only inscription where the clear determination of the interest rate obtained from capital investment is described. In this inscription, it is clearly stated that the principal should never be touched, and only the interest should be used. It mentions that the monthly interest is 100 Karshapanas. The purpose of giving the donation was to provide clothing and drinks for Buddhist monks. Ushavadatta deposited Akshayanivi with two guilds of weavers (2000 Karshapanas with one and 1000 with the other) He took interest at different rates from these two (at the rate of 1 percent per month from one and 3/4 percent from the other). Based on this, the annual interest rate on Akshayanivi in the Shaka-Satavahana period was 9 to 12 percent, which is much lower than the ideal interest rate of 1 1/4 percent per month (15% annual) determined by the Arthashastra and Smritis.

questions.question_text: Which of these texts permit divorce? (A) Narada Smriti (B) Manu Dharmashastra (C) Arthashastra (D) Yajnavalkya Smriti Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Kautilya permitted the dissolution of marriage (divorce) for women in his book Arthashastra. Kautilya used the word 'Moksha' for divorce. A wife could abandon her husband if he resided abroad for a long time or if there was a defect in his body. Similarly, a husband had the right to abandon his wife if she was unfaithful or barren. In addition to this, Smriti literature developed later from Dharmasutra literature. The creation of Smritis indicates the peak development of Hinduism. Smritis were given the designation of 'Dharmashastra'. Among the Smritis, Manusmriti is the oldest and most authentic. Yajnavalkya Smriti and Narada Smriti are compositions of the Gupta period (5th century). These Smritis are written in verses, and their language is classical Sanskrit

questions.question_text: For whom was the term 'Vivitadhyaksha' used in the Arthashastra?
questions.explanation: Various superintendents (Adhyakshas) are mentioned in the second chapter, 'Adhyaksha-Prachara', of the Arthashastra. These were heads of various departments and worked under the supervision of ministers. Probably, Megasthenes called these superintendents 'Magistrates'. Some main superintendents are as follows – Panyadhyaksha – Superintendent of the Commerce department – Suradhyaksha – Superintendent of the Excise department – Sunadhyaksha – Superintendent of the Slaughterhouse – Ganikadhyaksha – Superintendent of Courtesans – Hastyadhyaksha – Officer in charge of the care of elephants – Vivitadhyaksha – Superintendent of Pastures. His other tasks included the construction of wells, construction of reservoirs, and the protection of people passing through forests, etc.

questions.question_text: How many superintendents (Adhyakshas) appointed by the state are mentioned in Kautilya's Arthashastra?
questions.explanation: Superintendents are mentioned in the second book (Adhikarana) of the Arthashastra, titled 'Adhyaksha-Prachara'. These were the heads of various departments and worked under the supervision of ministers. Probably, Megasthenes called these superintendents 'Magistrates'. Their names are as follows: Panyadhyaksha, Suradhyaksha, Sunadhyaksha, Ganikadhyaksha, Sitadhyaksha, Akaradhyaksha, Koshthagaradhyaksha, Kupyadhyaksha, Ayudhagaradhyaksha, Shulkadhyaksha, Sutradhyaksha, Lohadhyaksha, Lakshanadhyaksha, Dyutadhyaksha, Vivitadhyaksha, Mudradhyaksha, Navadhyaksha, Pattanadhyaksha, Sansthadhyaksha, Devatadhyaksha, Pautavadhyaksha, Manadhyaksha, Ashvadhyaksha, Hastyadhyaksha, Suvarnadhyaksha, Akshapataladhyaksha. In this same work of Kautilya (the second book Adhyaksha-Prachara of Arthashastra), references to other superintendents are also found. Therefore, due to the number of superintendents not being fixed, the Commission has deleted this question

questions.question_text: In which period was the Great Stupa of Amaravati originally established?
questions.explanation: The literal meaning of Stupa is 'heap' or 'mound'. Stupa is derived from the Sanskrit root 'Stup', which means 'to collect or to pile up'. The Prakrit word for this is 'Thupa'. The actual work of constructing Stupas began during the time of Ashoka, and Stupas were expanded throughout the country. In Buddhist tradition, Ashoka is credited with the construction of 84,000 Stupas. The Great Stupa of Amaravati, known as Mahachaitya, is a Stupa from the Satavahana period

questions.question_text: To whose court was Deimachus (an ambassador) sent from Syria?
questions.explanation: The Greeks called Bindusara 'Amitrochates' or 'Amitraghata', which means the destroyer of enemies. Another of his names is Simhasena. During Bindusara's time, the ruler of Syria, Antiochus I, sent an ambassador named "Deimachus". The ruler of Egypt, Ptolemy II Philadelphus, sent an ambassador named "Dionysius" to Bindusara's court. During Bindusara's time, a revolt occurred in Taxila against the ministers there, to suppress which Ashoka, the governor of Malwa or Ujjain, was sent

questions.question_text: From which of the following places has a 'Fire Temple' been obtained?
questions.explanation: Surkh Kotal, also called Chashma-i-Shir or Sar-i-Chashma, is an ancient archaeological site located in the southern part of the Bactria region. It is the site of monumental constructions made during the reign of the Kushans. The Rabatak inscription, which provides significant evidence on the genealogy of the Kushan dynasty, was found here. The most famous artifacts of this site are the Surkh Kotal inscription, the statue of King Kanishka, and the 'Fire Temple'

questions.question_text: In the Mauryan period, 'Sannidhata' meant—

options.A: Chief custodian of the treasury and storehouse
options.D: Chief officer of assessment and collection

questions.explanation: In the Mauryan period, 'Sannidhata' means the chief custodian of the treasury and storehouse. Generally, he can be called the treasurer and the chief manager of the royal palace. His main task was to maintain the accounts of the state income earned in the form of cash and gifts. There were many sub-departments under the Sannidhata such as—Treasury (Koshagriha), Trading-house (Panyagriha), Granary (Kosthagara), Forest-produce-house (Kupyagriha), Armory (Ayudhagara), and Jail (Bandhanagara); these were sub-departments over which the Sannidhata had control

questions.question_text: On which of the following ruler's coins is the name 'Roma' written and the figure of this goddess in Roman attire is depicted?
questions.explanation: Huvishka introduced many gold and copper coins. Some silver coins of Huvishka have also been found. The figure of the king in Iranian attire is made on them. Figures of various types of deities are on Huvishka's coins. Along with inscriptions in Greek and Roman scripts, the figure of a goddess in Roman attire is also depicted, on which the name 'Roma' is written. Figures of Greek goddesses and gods, Persian gods, and Indian gods are also found on his coins

questions.question_text: The 'Ahuramazda' deity depicted on Huvishka's coins was related to—
questions.explanation: Huvishka introduced many gold and copper coins. Some silver coins of Huvishka have also been found. The figure of the king in Iranian attire is made on them. Figures of various types of deities are on Huvishka's coins, and along with Greek and Roman scripts, the figure of a goddess in Roman attire is also depicted, on which the name 'Roma' is written. Figures of Greek deities, Persian deities, and Indian deities are also found on his coins. The 'Ahuramazda' deity depicted on his coins is related to a Persian deity. Ahuramazda is the supreme deity of the Persians

questions.question_text: An account of the early life of Chandragupta Maurya has been presented in—
questions.explanation: An introduction to the early life of Chandragupta Maurya is obtained from the Buddhist text Mahavamsa Tika. From this text, it is known that Chandragupta was born in the Kshatriya clan named 'Moriya'. It is noteworthy that Jain and Buddhist religious texts clearly accept Chandragupta Maurya as belonging to the Kshatriya Varna

questions.question_text: Consider the following rulers of the Kanva dynasty and arrange them chronologically— (I) Vasudeva (II) Narayana (III) Bhumimitra (IV) Susarman Select the correct answer using the code given below— Code:
questions.explanation: After killing Devabhuti, the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty, Vasudeva established the Kanva dynasty in the Magadha region. According to the Puranas, a total of 4 rulers of the Kanva dynasty ruled for 45 years. The order of the 4 rulers of this dynasty is Vasudeva (ruled for 9 years), Bhumimitra (14 years), Narayana (12 years), and Susarman (10 years). After killing Susarman, the last ruler of the Kanva dynasty, Simuka established the Satavahana dynasty

questions.question_text: Who issued the 'Oesho' type of currency?
questions.explanation: Kanishka primarily issued gold and copper currencies. He adopted the Greek script and Greek language on his currencies. Figures of Iranian, Greek, and Indian deities are inscribed on Kanishka's coins. Prominent among these are Miiro and Mao (Persian Sun and Moon), Helios and Selene (Greek Sun and Moon), Athsho (Persian Fire God), Oesho (Indian God Shiva), and Boddo (Buddha). The depiction of 'Shakyamuni Buddha' is found on Kanishka's coins

questions.question_text: According to the Rabatak inscription, Kanishka ordered one of his officers to build a temple where the images of Goddess 'Nana' and other deities were to be installed. Who was that officer?
questions.explanation: According to the Rabatak inscription, Kanishka ordered one of his officers, Shafar, to build a temple where the images of Goddess 'Nana' and other deities were to be installed. The Rabatak inscription was discovered in 1993 from a hill named 'Kafir's Castle' in Afghanistan. The first editing and translation of this inscription, written in the Bactrian language and Greek script, was done by Nicholas Sims-Williams and Joe Cribb

questions.question_text: On which inscription of Ashoka is the text 'Gajatame' inscribed along with the engraving of an elephant figure at the top?
questions.explanation: On the top of Ashoka's Kalsi inscription, the text 'Gajatame' is inscribed along with the engraving of an elephant figure. Ashoka's Kalsi inscription is located in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, which was discovered in 1860 by Mr. Forrest. A total of 14 major rock edicts of Ashoka have been obtained from 10 sites. The Sannati rock edict is the most recently discovered inscription of Ashoka, which was found in 1989 in Gulbarga, Karnataka

questions.question_text: Which of the following inscriptions is written in the 'Boustrophedon' (Balivarda) style?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's Erragudi inscription is written in the 'Boustrophedon' style. The Erragudi inscription is in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh, which was discovered by Anu Ghosh in 1929. Besides major rock edicts, minor rock edicts have also been found at Erragudi. The script of the Erragudi text is found from right to left. This script is exactly in the same way an ox plows a field from right to left. That is why this text is called a text in the 'Boustrophedon' (Balivarda) style

questions.question_text: Which Greek ruler got the inscription 'Kavisive Nagar Devata' engraved on his coins?
questions.explanation: Eucratides was an important ruler of the Greeks (Yavanas). In one of his important coins obtained from Kapisa, he is called the city deity of Kapisa (Kavisive Nagar Devata). The Sirkap area in Taxila was first brought into use during the time of this ruler. His coins in Greek and Kharosthi scripts have been found in the northwestern province of India. According to Strabo, he made himself the ruler of 1000 cities from Bactria. He made Taxila his capital

questions.question_text: Which inscription gives a notable indication of the genealogy of the Kushan dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Rabatak inscription was discovered in 1993 from a hill called Kafir's Castle near a place called Rabatak, located in the Baghlan province of Afghanistan. The first editing and translation of this text in the Bactrian language and Greek script was done by Nicholas Sims-Williams and Joe Cribb. The Rabatak inscription is the first inscription in which the genealogy of the Kushan rulers is given. In this inscription, an officer named 'Shafar' from the time of Kanishka is also described

questions.question_text: The introduction of coins featuring inscriptions and portraits in India was done by:
questions.explanation: The introduction of coins featuring inscriptions and portraits in India was first done by the Indo-Greek rulers. The first Indo-Greek ruler to introduce square-shaped currency in the Indian territory was Antiochus I. Pantaleon and Agathocles were the first Indo-Greek rulers who used the Indian Brahmi script along with Kharosthi on their coins and issued the first nickel coins in the world. Agathocles was the first Indo-Greek ruler on whose coins the figures of Vasudeva and Balarama (Sankarshana) are found. The engraving of a conical stupa is also found on his coins

questions.question_text: Which of the following are included in the seven limbs of the ancient Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra composed by Kautilya is the first book of India in which the state has been defined. In this book, he discusses the 'Saptanga Theory' (seven essential limbs of the state). In the later period, the description of the 'Saptanga Theory' is also found in the Manusmriti and the Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata, and it was compared with various parts of the body— (1) Swami (King) - Head part (2) Amatya (Members of the Council of Ministers) - Eyes (3) Janapada (People, resources, capital) - Thighs/Legs (4) Durga (Fortified capital) - Arms (5) Kosha (Treasury) - Mouth (6) Danda/Bala (Justice system and army) - Brain (7) Mitra (Power having friendship with the state) - Ears A total of 18 Tirthas (chief officials) are mentioned in the Arthashastra, in which 'Yuvaraja' was considered the successor to the king.

questions.question_text: Where is the seventh pillar edict of Emperor Ashoka found?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's Delhi-Topra Pillar Edict: It is the most famous pillar edict, which is called Firoz Shah's Lat, Bhimsen's Lat, and Delhi-Shivalik Lat. Firoz Tughlaq called this pillar Minar-i-Zarin (Golden Pillar). The Delhi-Topra inscription was read by James Prinsep. It is significant that all seven edicts of Ashoka are engraved only on this. Three inscriptions of Vigraharaja IV (12th century) are engraved on the rock inscription. Shams-i-Siraj Afif has stated in his book Tarikh-i-Firozshahi that in 1356 AD, Firoz Tughlaq brought two pillars from Topra and Meerut. He installed the pillar from Topra in the 'Firozabad' palace in Delhi

questions.question_text: Under the control of which of the following officers were two departments, currency and accounts?
questions.explanation: Various Adhyakshas (superintendents) are mentioned in the Adhyaksha-Prachara chapter of the Arthashastra. Among these was the Akshapataladhyaksha, under whose control were two departments—Currency and Accounts. The Akshapataladhyaksha was primarily the Accountant General.

questions.question_text: What is the nature of the evidence linking Bhadrabahu with Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: In the final stage of his life, Chandragupta Maurya abdicated the throne in favor of his son (Bindusara), took initiation into Jainism from the Jain monk 'Bhadrabahu', and went to Shravanabelagola (Mysore) where he gave up his body through fasting (Sallekhana) in 298 BC. Bhadrabahu and his followers were called Digambaras. They were known as Southern Jains. Mention of Chandragupta and Bhadrabahu is found in numerous inscriptions from the 5th to 15th centuries obtained from Shravanabelagola (mainly the inscription of 1129 AD). The 'Bhadrabahu Cave' and 'Chandragiri Hill' are located here, where Chandragupta and Bhadrabahu practiced penance. A temple named Chandrabasti is located in Shravanabelagola; it was likely constructed by Chandragupta. 90 scenes related to the lives of Bhadrabahu and Chandragupta are inscribed on stone in this temple. Therefore, this epigraphic evidence is the proof linking Bhadrabahu with Chandragupta Maurya

questions.question_text: With which department was the officer Astynomoi, mentioned by Megasthenes, associated?
questions.explanation: Astynomoi was a prominent officer of the Mauryan period. Megasthenes described an officer named Astynomoi. He was a city officer. The Nagarika was the chief officer of the city. Megasthenes has mentioned this. Some prominent Mauryan officers are as follows • Agronomoi - Chief officer of the district and road construction. • Rupadarshaka - Chief officer for inspecting coins. • Sauvarnika - Chief officer of the mint. • Pradeshta - He was the chief officer of the criminal court. • Vyavaharika - He was the chief judge of the civil court.

questions.question_text: In the Mauryan period, Samaharta meant –
questions.explanation: Mauryan administration holds an important place in Indian administrative history. This is the mention of India's first centralized administration system. The king was the center point of the administration. He was the head of the executive, legislature, and judiciary. 18 Tirthas (departments/officials) are mentioned in the Arthashastra. The main Tirthas are as follows Prime Minister and Purohita - The Purohita were the chief religious officials. During the time of Chandragupta Maurya, both these departments were under Kautilya. Samaharta - He was the chief officer of the revenue department. Sannidhata - He was the royal treasurer. Pradeshta - Judge of the criminal court (Commissioner). Vyavaharika - Judge of the civil court.

questions.question_text: Which of the following officers controlled the collection of districts in his province?
questions.explanation: Mauryan administration holds an important place in Indian administrative history. Here, India's first centralized administration system is mentioned. The king was the center point of the administration. He was the head of the executive, legislature, and judiciary. 18 Tirthas are mentioned in the Arthashastra. Some important Tirthas are as follows – Samaharta – He was the chief officer of the revenue department. – Sannidhata – He was the royal treasurer. – Senapati – He was the minister of the war department. – Yuvraja – He was the successor to the king. – Pradeshta – He was the judge of the criminal court. – Vyavaharika – He was the chief judge of the civil court. Note that the Samaharta controlled the revenue collection of the districts of his province.

questions.question_text: Based on the writing, which one of the following pillars of Ashoka was the oldest?
questions.explanation: The excellent display of Mauryan art is seen in Ashoka's pillars. These pillars were made of red sandstone brought from the hills of Mathura and Chunar. The Rummindei pillar is the oldest among Ashoka's pillars based on the writing. The inscription engraved on this pillar is in Brahmi script and is read from left to right. It is from this inscription that it is known that Emperor Ashoka came to Lumbini twenty years after his coronation and he worshipped here and exempted the village from religious taxes

questions.question_text: Ashoka's inscriptions show that royal edicts were followed throughout the entire kingdom except for one part:
questions.explanation: The history of Ashoka is known to us mainly from his inscriptions. So far, more than 40 inscriptions have been found, scattered from one corner of the country to the other. These inscriptions help us in determining his imperial boundaries and on the other hand, they provide information about many important matters related to his religion and administration. Ashoka's inscriptions show that his royal edicts were followed throughout the entire kingdom except for the eastern part. Note that Ashoka's inscriptions have not been found in the eastern part of India 32. Under the control of which of the following officers were the two departments - Currency (Chala Mudra) and Accounts? (a) Samaharta (b) Sannidhata (c) Akshapataladhyaksha (d) Samsthadhyaksha UP PGT 2021 Ans. (c) : Various Adhyakshas (superintendents) are mentioned in the Adhyaksha-Prachara chapter of the Arthashastra. These were the heads of various departments and worked under the supervision of the ministers. Megasthenes likely called these Adhyakshas 'Magistrates'. Among these Adhyakshas was the Akshapataladhyaksha, under whose control were two departments - Currency and Accounts. The Akshapataladhyaksha was primarily the Accountant General.

questions.question_text: In which inscription does Ashoka call himself 'Piyadasi Laja Magadhe' (Piyadasi, King of Magadha)?
questions.explanation: The Bhabru inscription is located near Jaipur in Rajasthan. An inscription related to Ashoka was found here on a rock. In this, Ashoka's name is found as 'Piyadasi Laja Magadhe'. In this same inscription, mention of the Triratna of Buddhism - Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha - is found. Some examples of Buddhist texts are also given in the Bhabru inscription

questions.question_text: Which missionary did Emperor Ashoka send to Maharashtra for the propagation of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Ashoka sent religious missionaries to many countries for the propagation of Dhamma, which are mentioned in the Buddhist text Mahavamsa Religious Missionary - Country Mahendra and Sanghamitra - Sri Lanka (Tamraparni) Majjhantika - Kashmir and Gandhara Maharakshita - Greek country (Yavana) Mahadharmarakshita - Maharashtra Mahadeva - Mahishamandala (Mysore) Rakshita - Vanavasi (Karnataka) Dharmarakshita - Aparantaka Majjhima - Himalayan country Sona and Uttara - Suvarnabhumi

questions.question_text: From which of the following places was the four-lion capital obtained?
questions.explanation: Sanchi is located in the Raisen district of the state of Madhya Pradesh, India. The city of Sanchi is famous for Buddhist stupas. (Stupa - a semi-circular structure, which is related to the life of Buddha or his followers). Emperor Ashoka built the stupas of Sanchi. Note that the four-lion capital was obtained from Sanchi. These four lions are sitting back to back. Below these lions, swans are shown pecking at grain

questions.question_text: The nature of the centralized state of the Mauryas became paternal during Ashoka's time. In which of his inscriptions is this clearly mentioned?
questions.explanation: In the First Separate Kalinga Rock Edict, instructions are given by Ashoka to the Mahamatras of Kalinga and the city's judicial officers, and Ashoka says that all men are like my children; just as I want my children to attain happiness in both this world and the next, in the same way, I wish for all men

questions.question_text: In Mauryan administration, 'Kupyadhyaksha' was the officer-in-charge of:
questions.explanation: In Kautilya's Arthashastra, mention of 26/27 types of Adhyakshas is found, who were the masters of various departments and worked under the ministers. Among these, Panyadhyaksha (Superintendent of Commerce), Kupyadhyaksha (Superintendent of Forest Resources), Pautavadhyaksha (Superintendent of Weights and Measures), Sitadhyaksha (Superintendent of Crown Lands), Vivitadhyaksha (Superintendent of Pastures), Mudradhyaksha (Passport Officer), etc., were prominent

questions.question_text: In which inscription of Ashoka is there a mention of Kaurwaki and son Tivara?
questions.explanation: The Kaushambi or Prayagraj Minor Pillar Edict is called the Queen's Edict or the Empress's Edict. It was discovered in 1834 AD by Captain Burt. This inscription also mentions the charity of Ashoka's queen Kaurwaki. Along with this, mention of Ashoka and his son Tivara is found in it. This is the only wife and son mentioned in Ashoka's inscriptions. It is also called a donative inscription. In this Minor Pillar Edict, it is written that the devotees should come on every Uposatha day and follow this rule

questions.question_text: 'Charaka' was a contemporary of which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Charaka was the son of Vishuddha and a disciple of Sage Vaishampayana. He was a prominent Ayurvedacharya; he is counted among the original founders of Indian medicinal science. His education took place in Taxila. He composed the Charaka Samhita, which is even today a unique text of Ayurveda. He was the royal physician of Kanishka, the ruler of the Kushan dynasty

questions.question_text: Which inscription of Rudradaman proves the merger of Saurashtra in Western India by Chandragupta?
questions.explanation: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman (150 AD) proves the merger of Saurashtra in Western India by Chandragupta Maurya. The governor appointed by Chandragupta Maurya in Saurashtra was Pushyagupta, who had constructed the Sudarshana Lake in Saurashtra. Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription was the first inscription written in Sanskrit

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a distinct region of the Mauryan Empire?

options.A: Core region in the Ganges Valley

questions.explanation: Socio-economic, political, and cultural inequalities and imbalances are also kept in mind in the extensive regions of the Mauryan Empire. On the image of the Mauryan Empire as a welfare-oriented ancient state, the question now arises that despite the long rule of the Mauryas in the Deccan, only nominal changes are seen in physical conditions. In fact, the priority of the Mauryan rulers was to make the mineral regions of the Deccan prosperous

questions.question_text: The last great Mauryan ruler, Samprati, was a patron of which of these religions?
questions.explanation: Samprati has been called a patron and follower of Jainism, who built thousands of Jain Tirthankara temples. Jain Acharya Suhastin initiated Samprati into Jainism. Samprati's rule was in Ujjain. Samprati's title was Trikhandadhipati

questions.question_text: "Arunad Yavanah Saketam! Arunad Yavano Madhyamikam!!" In which book is this mention of the Yavana invasion during the Shunga period found?
questions.explanation: "Arunad Yavanah Saketam! Arunad Yavano Madhyamikam!!" This statement about the Yavana invasion during the Shunga period is found in the book named Mahabhashya authored by Patanjali. According to this, the Yavanas attacked the Saketa (Ayodhya) region of Faizabad, Uttar Pradesh, and the city near 'Madhyamika' (Chittor)

questions.question_text: Which inscription informs that the daughter of Shaka Kshatrapa Rudradaman was married to the Satavahana king Vashishtiputra Pulumayi?
questions.explanation: It is clear from the inscription obtained from Kanheri that the queen of the Satavahana ruler Vashishtiputra Pulumayi was the daughter of the Mahakshatrapa Shaka Kshatrapa Rudradaman. Therefore, Pulumayi was the son-in-law of Rudradaman. By this time, the Shakas had again seized the regions of Kukura, Surashtra, Maru, Shvabhra, Avanti, and Akara from the Satavahanas. During this crisis period, Pulumayi began to expand his kingdom towards the eastern Deccan region

questions.question_text: Arrange the Satavahana rulers given below in the correct chronological order: a. Vashishtiputra Shri Pulumayi b. Gautamiputra Satakarni c. Satakarni I d. Simuka Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The Vayu Purana states that Simuka, of the Andhra race, will kill Susharman, the last ruler of the Kanva dynasty, and rule the earth. Therefore, it is certain that Simuka was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty. Mention of Raja Simuka Satavahana is found in the Nanaghat inscription. Chronological mention of Satavahana rulers - Simuka, Kanha or Krishna, Satakarni I, Hala, Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vashishtiputra Pulumayi, Yagnashri Satakarni

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true?

options.A: During the time of Kanishka, the Kushan Empire extended from the Ganges River valley in the east to Malwa in the south.
options.B: The Rabatak inscription related to Kanishka has been obtained from the North-Western Province.
options.C: Buddhist scholars like Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha enjoyed the patronage of Kanishka.
options.D: Kanishka's coins include symbols of Indian, Greek, and West Asian religious traditions.

questions.explanation: Rabatak Inscription - The Rabatak inscription is located in the Baghlan province of Afghanistan. This is the first inscription to provide information about the genealogy of the Kushans. This inscription was discovered in 1993. This Kushan record of 23 lines in Bactrian language and Greek script was first edited and translated by Nicholas Sims-Williams and Joe Cribb. All other options given in the question above are correct regarding Kanishka

questions.question_text: In the Mauryan administration, 'Sannidhata' was the head of which of the following departments?
questions.explanation: Sannidhata - During the Mauryan period, he was an officer of the royal treasury whose job was to maintain the accounts of royal income and expenditure and determine its policy. There are many sub-departments under the Sannidhata, and he is made the treasurer, who also does the work of looking after the king's treasury and depositing the income received from the state

questions.question_text: Which of the following inscriptions mention measures to deal with famine? 1. Shahbazgarhi inscription 2. Maski inscription 3. Sohgaura copper plate 4. Mahasthan inscription Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: It is clear from Ashoka's inscriptions and Buddhist literature that the empire was divided into many provinces. A copper plate from Sohgaura in Uttar Pradesh and an inscription from Mahasthan in Bengal have been found in fragmented condition. These inscriptions provide information about grain storehouses for facing famines

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler of Egypt, a contemporary of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: Emperor Ashoka was a great ruler of the Mauryan dynasty and was the son of Bindusara. He was a follower of Buddhism and he propagated the religion and sent his missionaries to far-off countries. Ptolemy Philadelphus II was the emperor of Egypt, who was a contemporary king of Ashoka; he sent his ambassador Dionysius to Ashoka's royal court

questions.question_text: In the Mauryan period, which type of land was the main source of state income?
questions.explanation: Sita land was state-owned land in the Mauryan period; this has been mentioned by Kautilya in the Arthashastra. This land was important for the state's income. This land was given to people ranging from the general public to slaves. In this, 1/6th part or even more of the agricultural income was taken. The state imposed tax on this only after classifying the lands. Work on this land was done by slaves, laborers, Shudras or tribes, and prisoners. It was overseen by a 'Sitadhyaksha' officer

questions.question_text: To whom was the route connecting Pataliputra with Taxila credited?
questions.explanation: Among the trade routes in the Mauryan Empire, the most prominent route was called Uttarapatha. It connected Pataliputra with Taxila, the capital of the Gandhara nation. The work of special security and repair of these roads was done by Ashoka. This same Uttarapatha route was known by the name of Sher Shah Suri Road in the medieval period and is known as G.T. Road in the modern period

questions.question_text: Who said, 'Indians neither do evil to anyone nor do they tolerate evil from anyone'?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes came to India during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya; he was the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator who described his visit to India in a special way. He has given a detailed description of the political, social, economic, and geographical conditions of India. He wrote about Indians that Indians neither did evil to anyone nor did they tolerate evil. Historians have expressed conflicting views about the reliability of Megasthenes' account of India. It is said that his account cannot be relied upon much because he was not a knower of any language of India, he was familiar only with Pataliputra and Punjab, he stayed in India for a short time, and being a foreigner, he could not properly understand the institutions and practices of India

questions.question_text: According to Megasthenes, which of these rulers first attempted to establish a navy?
questions.explanation: Mauryan ruler Chandragupta Maurya had formed a navy. According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the army was divided into four boards. The first board of which operated the navy. He was known as Navadhyaksha. Their job was to discharge various responsibilities related to sea ships. Such as arranging boats for passengers, collecting toll from traders, arresting suspicious persons, protecting trade from sea pirates. Megasthenes has described this army in his Indica, which has been credited with establishing the first navy in India

questions.question_text: With which daughter of Seleucus did Chandragupta marry?
questions.explanation: Seleucus Nicator was the chief general of Alexander, who fought a war with Chandragupta Maurya and made a treaty. Under this treaty, he settled this war by giving some part of his kingdom and marrying his daughter Helena to Chandragupta Maurya. In this treaty, Chandragupta Maurya had to be given the states of Kabul, Kandahar, Herat, and Gedrosia. In exchange, Chandragupta Maurya gave 500 elephants as a gift to Seleucus

questions.question_text: In which script are most of the inscriptions engraved on Ashokan pillars written?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's inscriptions are found written in Kharosthi, Aramaic, Greek, and Brahmi scripts. Most of his inscriptions are found written in the popular Brahmi script, which is written from left to right. This same Brahmi script is the mother script of most scripts of India and many scripts of Southeast Asia like Burmese, Tibetan, Sinhalese, etc. Two rock edicts of Ashoka, located at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, are written in Kharosthi. Two inscriptions obtained from Taxila and Kandahar are written in Greek and Aramaic scripts

questions.question_text: Chandragupta Maurya became a disciple of which of these Jain monks?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya - According to Parishishtaparvan, in the last years of his life, Chandragupta Maurya had accepted Jainism and was initiated into Jainism by Bhadrabahu. At the time of a famine in Magadha, Chandragupta Maurya came to Shravanabelagola (Mysore) with his guru Bhadrabahu and gave up his life through the method of Sallekhana (the ritual of giving up life by renouncing food and water)

questions.question_text: Which of the following scripts was uniformly adopted throughout the Maurya Empire during Ashoka's reign?
questions.explanation: Brahmi script - It is one of the oldest scripts of India. Ancient examples of its use are available in the form of Ashoka's inscriptions. It is written from left to right Kharosthi script - Excluding the pictographic script of the Indus Valley, Kharosthi script is one of the two oldest scripts of India. It was written from right to left. Ashoka got the Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra inscriptions written in Kharosthi only. Aramaic script - This is a fragmentary inscription written in Aramaic script from Taxila, and an inscription of Ashoka has been found from a place named Sher-e-Kuna. Devanagari script - This script is an Indian script in which many Indian languages and several foreign languages are written. It is written from left to right. It is identified by a horizontal line called the Shirorekha.

questions.question_text: During which ruler's reign did the Mauryas defeat Seleucus Nicator?
questions.explanation: Alexander's general Seleucus Nicator was the ruler of Syria. He was the son of Antiochus. He crossed the Indus river in 305 BC. He was defeated in a war with Chandragupta and a treaty was made in 303 BC. This is the first international treaty in the history of India. The Hindu Kush mountain was accepted as the boundary of both empires. Strabo has mentioned the treaty

questions.question_text: Under which of these inscriptions did Ashoka declare himself an 'Upasaka'?
questions.explanation: Rupnath version (Minor Rock Edict - 1) - "It has been two and a half years since I became a 'Shakya' (an ordinary follower of Buddha) in a determined manner. In the beginning, I was not dedicated; but in the past one year, I have come quite close to the Sangha." In this same record, Ashoka says that he has proven the Bhu-devos (Brahmins) to be false Special Facts- (1) Minor Rock Edict - 3 / Bhabru Minor Rock Edict (Bairat) Jaipur - In 1837, Captain Burt discovered two stone records of Ashoka from 'Bijak ki Pahari'. Cunningham got them placed in the Calcutta Museum. (2) Major Rock Edict - 8 / Eighth Rock Edict - In the tenth year of his coronation, Emperor Ashoka started 'Dhamma Yatra' instead of 'Bihar Yatra' (hunting of animals like deer for entertainment, drinking). (3) Lumbini/Rummindei Minor Pillar Edict - The mention of the Dhamma Yatra to Lumbini by Ashoka 20 years after his coronation is found in this. Information about the Maurya period tax system is found in this inscription of Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Read the following statements related to Indian epigraphy– (i) Kharosthi script, which was written from right to left, was mainly used in the Gandhara region of ancient India. (ii) Gupta Brahmi developed into a script named Siddhamatrika. (iii) James Prinsep identified Maurya ruler Ashoka as the ruler of the inscriptions issued in the name of Piyadassi. Which of the above statement(s) is/are false?
questions.explanation: Consideration of statements related to Indian epigraphy– 1. Kharosthi script which was written from right to left, was mainly prevalent in practice in the Gandhara Mahajanapada region of ancient India. 2. Brahmi script, having developed in the Gupta period, came to be known as the script of Siddhamatrika. 3. James Prinsep had identified King Tissa of Sri Lanka as the ruler of the inscriptions issued in the name of Piyadassi. Later, Mr. Turnour first identified Piyadassi with Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Traders used to move in 'groups' while taking goods from one place to another, this was called:
questions.explanation: In the Maurya period, the head of trading caravans was known by the name Sarthavaha, whose mention is in Kautilya's Arthashastra describing foreign Sarthavahas (head of trading caravans). A prosperous description of internal trade of the Maurya period is found in the Arthashastra

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not sent by Ashoka Maurya for the propagation of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: After the organization of the Third Buddhist Council, Buddhist monks were sent to different regions of India and other countries for the propagation of Buddhism, which has been mentioned in Mahavamsa. Among the options given in the above question, Rakshita was sent to Vanavasi (North Kanara), Dharmarakshita to Aparantaka, Western India and Mahadeva was sent to Mahishamandala (Mandhata - the southern region of Narmada or Mysore)

questions.question_text: Read the following statements- Assertion (A): The Maurya state was an extremely centralized state. Explanation (E): The vast Maurya empire was divided into provinces, which were generally ruled by princes. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (E) are correct and (E) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (E) are correct, but (E) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: An extremely detailed description of Maurya period central administration is obtained in the Arthashastra. The Maurya state was essentially a monarchy in the center of which was a powerful Emperor, which was divided into many departments. These departments were called Tirtha. The vast Maurya empire was divided into provinces. Rashtriya Governors or Kumar or Aryaputra used to rule in these provinces. The provincial governor is usually a person related to the royal family. But sometimes governors were also appointed on the basis of merit. The word Kumar is indicative of a general prince. Therefore, both the Assertion and Explanation are correct and (E) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.question_text: Match the following: Yavana Ruler Region
questions.explanation: In Major Rock Edict number 13, the names of 5 Yavana kings are found where Ashoka had sent religious missionaries - among these, the ruler of Syria located on the north-western border was Antiochus II. The ruler of Egypt, Ptolemy II Philadelphus, had established a huge library in Alexandria which was famous for the translation of Indian texts. Magas was the ruler of Cyrene and Antigonus II was the ruler of Macedonia

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a land-related tax in the Maurya period?
questions.explanation: In the Maurya period, the basic foundation of the economy was agriculture, for the development of which good efforts were made and for its development and progress, various types of taxes were arranged Bhaga - This tax was taken from private land. Bali - Tax taken in the form of religious offering. Udaka - Water tax taken from farmers for the management of artificial irrigation by the state. Shulka - This tax was taken in the form of customs duty.

questions.question_text: Read the following statements about Ashoka's pillars- A. Major pillar edicts of Ashoka are found in North India. B. There are six pillar edicts which are found on seven pillars. C. The shaft and capital of the pillars are made of two different stones. D. All the figures on the capital are of animals. Which of the above statements are true? Select the correct code:
questions.explanation: The works done during the Ashokan period are mentioned in the pillars of Ashoka. These pillar inscriptions hold a prominent place in the world for their fame. Ashoka started a new style in the history of architecture. Major pillar edicts of Ashoka were obtained from North India in which there are 7 pillar edicts found at 6 different places. The construction of pillars has been done in two parts under an upright shape and their figures have also been displayed in different images

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: The correct match is as follows List-I List-II (A) Mullai - Pastoral region (B) Palai - Dry land (C) Kurinji - Hilly region (D) Marudam - Riverine land

questions.question_text: On the coins of which rulers is the title 'Dharmika' (Religious) inscribed?
questions.explanation: The title 'Dharmika' (Religious) is inscribed on the coins of Pahlava rulers. Pahlava rulers came to India from Iran in the second century BC. The founder of this dynasty was Mithridates I (171-130 BC). The greatest ruler of this dynasty was Gondophernes. The Kushans had started the system of dual rule and joint rule in India and had first produced pure gold coins in India. Satavahanas had produced coins made of lead

questions.question_text: Who was given the alias Kumar and Aryaputra?
questions.explanation: In the Maurya dynasty, the management of provincial administration was carried out from the royal or princely families. During the Maurya period, the state was divided into five parts. Its unit was in the form of a province, whose administrators were appointed from the royal family, who were called Kumar or Aryaputra

questions.question_text: What is the probable date of the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea?
questions.explanation: The probable date of the composition of the book 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea', written by an unknown author in the Greco-Roman language, is the 1st-2nd century AD. This text sheds light on the trade and commerce occurring through sea routes and maritime transport in ancient times, in which the Red Sea (Erythraean Sea) and Persian Gulf, Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal are mentioned in brief. This also sheds light on the study of trade-commerce and sea routes with the ancient Roman Empire and the Indian subcontinent

questions.question_text: Which metal was in excess in the manufacture of 'Rupyaruupa' type coins?
questions.explanation: Silver was in excess in the manufacture of Rupyaruupa type coins. In the Maurya period, Rupyaruupa, Karshapana, Pana, Dharana etc. were punch-marked coins of silver. In the Maurya period, Suvarna and Nishka were gold punch-marked coins while Mashaka and Kakani were copper punch-marked coins

questions.question_text: Which South Indian dynasty did Megasthenes mention in his book 'Indika'?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes has mentioned the Pandya dynasty of South India in his book 'Indika'. According to Megasthenes, the ruler of the Pandya state was a woman named Pandya. According to Megasthenes, the Pandya kingdom was famous for pearls. Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus to the royal court of Chandragupta Maurya who probably remained in the court of Chandragupta Maurya from 304-299 BC. Megasthenes has given a detailed description of the city administration of Pataliputra and the military administration of Chandragupta Maurya

questions.question_text: To which discipline is the Sangam literature text 'Tolkappiyam' related?
questions.explanation: Tolkappiyam is the only available oldest Sangam literature of the Second Sangam. Its author Tolkappiyar was one of the 12 disciples of Sage Agastya. It is a Tamil grammar book written in the Sutra style. 3 important epic texts of the Sangam period are available which are Silappadikaram (Author - Ilango Adigal), Manimekalai (Author - Sattanar) and Jivaka Chintamani (Author - Tirutakkatevar)

questions.question_text: From which of the following excavated sites were evidence of trade relations between South India and the Roman world found?
questions.explanation: Arikamedu was an important center of Indian maritime trade. Mortimer Wheeler first excavated it in 1945 AD. Evidence of developed trade relations between South India and the Roman world has been found from Arikamedu. Roman coins, Roman settlement, Roman amphorae and Roman Arretine pottery, and gems inscribed with the figure of Augustus have been obtained from here. Arikamedu has been addressed by the name 'Poduke' in the Periplus

questions.question_text: 'Dharana' and 'Purana' are identified as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Dharana and Purana were punch-marked coins of ancient times. The mention of Purana and Dharana as punch-marked coins has occurred in Manusmriti. In Pali literature, punch-marked coins have been called Kahapana and in Sanskrit Karshapana. Kautilya has called punch-marked coins Pana and Katyayana has called them by the name Prati. The oldest hoards of punch-marked coins have been found from eastern Uttar Pradesh and Magadha of North India

questions.question_text: How many Adhikaranas and Shlokas are there in Kautilya's Arthashastra?
questions.explanation: The language of Arthashastra is Sanskrit. It is a mixture of prose and verse and is written in Sutra style or Granth style. It contains 6000 Shlokas, 15 Adhikaranas and 180 Prakaranas. Kautilya composed the oldest book on Hindu governance, the Arthashastra. The first manuscript of the Arthashastra was discovered by Pt. Shamasastry in 1905 AD. The first English translation of the Arthashastra became available in 1915 AD

questions.question_text: Which of the following matches of the sub-divisions of administration described in the Arthashastra is not correct?
questions.explanation: & d) : The correct matching is Unit Gram (Village) Sthanika - Group of 800 villages Dronamukha - Group of 400 villages Kharvatika - Group of 200 villages Sangrahana - Group of 10 villages Note - The Higher Education Service Commission has accepted (a) as its answer.

questions.question_text: Kanishka was a follower of which branch of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Kanishka was a ruler of the Kushan dynasty. Just like Chandragupta, Kanishka expanded the empire, and like Ashoka, he also spread Buddhism by providing patronage to it. During his time, the Fourth Buddhist Council was organized. This council was presided over and vice-presided over by Vasumitra and Ashvaghosa respectively, who were courtiers of Kanishka. During this time, Buddhism was divided into two sects, Hinayana and Mahayana. Kanishka was a supporter of the Mahayana sect

questions.question_text: In which inscription is the performance of two Ashvamedha Yagyas by Pushyamitra mentioned?

options.C: Nasik inscription of Gautami Putra Satakarni

questions.explanation: On the basis of the evidence of the Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva, it is said that Pushyamitra Shunga performed two Ashvamedha Yagyas. The Ashvamedha Yagya was performed under the presence of Pushyamitra's royal priest Patanjali. Pushyamitra's empire expansion was from Punjab to Bengal and up to its sea coast, and in the south-east up to Narmada and modern Bundelkhand

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the epic 'Silappadikaram'?
questions.explanation: Three major epics were composed in the third Sangam literature of South India, in which the most famous text is considered to be Silappadikaram. It was composed by Ilango Adigal. This epic is not only heart-touching from the viewpoint of the plot but is also full of poetry, music, dramatic elements and beautiful descriptions

questions.question_text: Read the following statements about Sangam literature– i. Ettutokai is one of the oldest collections of the Sangam literature tradition. ii. Purananuru is a part of Ettutokai, in which poems of bravery are compiled. iii. The Agam category of Sangam poems is related to the praise of rulers. iv. Tirukkural is a later work, which is primarily a work related to love and morality. Which of the above statements are true?
questions.explanation: There are eight anthologies in Ettutokai. Purananuru is a part of Ettutokai, in which poems of bravery are compiled. It contains 400 poems in praise of kings.
