In Sangam poems, Agam poetry is mainly a compilation of poems of Shringar Rasa (love). Tirukkural is a later work in which light has been shed on issues like ethics, royal duty, citizenship, love, the art of living etc. It was composed by Thiruvalluvar and it is considered a sacred and high religious text like the Vedas in the Tamil land

questions.question_text: "As much land as an elephant can lie on, the same amount of land can feed seven men." To which region of ancient India is this statement related?
questions.explanation: In ancient India, this statement was prevalent about the Kaveri Delta that "As much land as an elephant can lie on, the same amount of land can feed seven men." During the Satavahana period and the Sangam age, the part of the Kaveri Delta was quite famous for its agricultural production. During this period, the production of rice and turmeric was highest in this region

questions.question_text: In which book was Chandragupta Maurya called "Lord of the whole Jambudvipa"?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya has been called the lord of the whole Jambudvipa in the Mahavamsa text of the Buddhist source, the Ceylonese tradition

questions.question_text: In whose kingdom were the caves of Nasik and Karle located?
questions.explanation: The Nasik and Karle caves are related to the Satavahana kingdom. Nasik and Karle were famous Buddhist sites during the Satavahana period. Karle Chaitya is one of the most beautiful and grand monuments of ancient India. This Chaitya is the largest and is in a well-preserved condition

questions.question_text: Ashtangahridayam of Vagbhata is a book related to which subject?
questions.explanation: The Ashtangahridayam of Vagbhata contains a description of all eight branches of Ayurveda, including Kaya, Shalya, Shalakya, etc. It provides a detailed description of daily routine, night routine, seasonal routine, properties of substances, and science

questions.question_text: Of which metal was the Bhattiprolu inscription made?
questions.explanation: Among the prominent inscriptions of the Satavahana period, information about Stupas, Chaityas, and Viharas is obtained from places like Amaravati, Bhattiprolu, and Nagarjunakonda. Bhattiprolu is also known for its Buddhist stupa; it is a small village in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh. The Bhattiprolu inscription is made of silver

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an event of ancient Indian history in the B.C. era?
questions.explanation: Kanishka's reign is considered to be around 78 AD; he was the greatest ruler of the Kushan dynasty. During his reign, the Fourth Buddhist Council was organized in the first century AD. The Indo-Greek empire was established around 183 BC. Demetrius is credited with being the first to enter the Indian border. Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription belongs to the first century BC. The Vikram Samvat started in 57 BC

questions.question_text: The original work of Megasthenes is lost and we get information about his accounts through citations given by some later Greek writers, such as: 1. Arrian 2. Diodorus 3. Justin 4. Plutarch 5. Strabo Select the correct answer from the code below:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation—Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus who stayed in the court of Chandragupta Maurya between 304 BC and 299 BC. Reliable information about the administration of Chandragupta Maurya is obtained from his work 'Indica'. Although this work is not available in its original form, its examples are obtained from citations by many Greek writers such as Arrian, Justin, etc.

questions.question_text: During the reign of Chandragupta Maurya, the administration of Pataliputra was managed by a committee, the number of whose members was—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006, 2008 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation—In the Mauryan era, the administration of major cities was run by municipalities. There was an assembly for city administration whose head was called 'Nagaraka' or 'Purmukhya'. Megasthenes mentioned 6 committees of the city council of Pataliputra, each having five members. The first committee inspected various types of industrial arts. The second committee arranged for the food, residence, and medical care, etc., of foreign travelers. The third committee kept records of census. The fourth committee looked after the trade and commerce of the city. The fifth was the industrial committee, which prevented adulteration in goods sold in markets and got traders punished for the crime of adulteration. The sixth committee was the tax committee, which collected tax on items of purchase and sale.

questions.question_text: To which period does the Dhauli elephant sculpture near Bhubaneswar in Odisha belong?
questions.explanation: The Dhauli rock sculpture of the elephant near Bhubaneswar in Odisha was built by Ashoka during the Mauryan period in the third century BC

questions.question_text: Which dynasty ruled Magadha after the Nanda dynasty?
questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Nanda dynasty was Dhanananda, who was killed by Chandragupta Maurya with the help of Chanakya in 322 BC to establish the Mauryan dynasty

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not included in the concept of Saptanga mentioned in 'Arthashastra'?
questions.explanation: Preksha is not included in the Saptanga concept in 'Arthashastra'. The description of Svamin, Amatya, Rashtra, Durga, Bala, Kosha, and Mitra is found in the Saptanga

questions.question_text: Which of the following is in the correct chronological order?
questions.explanation: Haryanka Dynasty (544 BC - 412 BC) - Mauryan Dynasty (323 BC - 184 BC) - Kushan Dynasty - Gupta Dynasty (319 AD - 550 AD)

questions.question_text: Which of the following sculptures does not belong to the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: The reference to the Standing Buddha in Mathura is found from the post-Mauryan period, which was patronized by the Kushan rulers

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of 'Prashasti'?

options.C: It was a royal charter on a metal plate

questions.explanation: Prashasti means to praise the king. Prashastis mentioned the great deeds performed by the king

questions.question_text: There is only one inscription in which Ashoka has talked about taxation. Which of these is that inscription?
questions.explanation: Ashoka mentioned taxation in the Rummindei Pillar inscription. This inscription is located in the Terai of Nepal. It is known from this inscription that Ashoka came here in the 20th year of his coronation, he exempted the religious tax 'Bali' here and reduced the land tax to 1/8 part. This is also called an economic inscription

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an archaeological reference of the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW), ring wells, burnt bricks, inscriptions of Ashoka, accounts of Greek travelers, etc., are archaeological and literary sources of the Mauryan period, whereas Painted Grey Ware (PGW) is related to Vedic period history

questions.question_text: Which of the following evidence is not evidence for the knowledge of Mauryan period history?
questions.explanation: Knowledge of Mauryan period history is obtained from Ashoka's inscriptions, accounts of Greek writers, Kautilya's Arthashastra, etc. Whereas Painted Grey Ware is related to Vedic civilization. Therefore, it cannot be used as a source for knowledge of Mauryan history

questions.question_text: In which of the following years did James Prinsep read Brahmi?
questions.explanation: James Prinsep first successfully deciphered (read) the Brahmi script engraved on Ashoka's 'Delhi-Topra Pillar Inscription' in 1837 AD, but he identified 'Devanampiya' and 'Piyadassi' in the inscriptions with the Sri Lankan ruler 'Tissa' Special Fact - The first discovery of Ashoka's inscriptions was made by T. Tieffenthaler in 1750 AD, which was named 'Delhi Meerut Pillar Inscription'.

questions.question_text: Identify the date of the conflict between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus Nicator:
questions.explanation: In 305 BC, Chandragupta defeated the then Greek ruler Seleucus on the banks of the Indus River. In this, Seleucus was defeated, and by marrying his daughter to Chandragupta, matrimonial relations were established between the two states

questions.question_text: In which ancient Indian dynasty were Shudras provided help by the state for the first time to settle as farmers on land owned by the state?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of his teacher Chanakya, defeated the last ruler of the Magadha Empire, Dhanananda, and established the Mauryan Empire. Brahmanical literature describes Chandragupta Maurya as Shudra, while Mudrarakshasa by Vishakhadatta calls him Vrishala (of low lineage). Kautilya considered the Varnashrama system as the basis of social organization and prescribed occupations for all four Varnas. In this dynasty, for the first time, Shudras were provided assistance by the state to settle as farmers on state-owned land. In addition to crafts and service professions, Shudras were permitted to earn a livelihood through agriculture, animal husbandry, and commerce

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Indica'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 PGT History, 2003 PGT History, 2004 Explanation—Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. He was present in the court of Pataliputra sometime between 304 BC and 299 BC. Whatever he saw and heard while staying in India, he recorded in his book named 'Indica'. In this same book, he described the city administration.

questions.question_text: Three ambassadors were sent to Pataliputra by Greek kings. Their names were Megasthenes, Deimachus and—
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation—Megasthenes, the ambassador of the Greek ruler Seleucus, stayed in the court of Chandragupta Maurya for 14 years and composed 'Indica' from his studies. Deimachus, who was the ambassador of the Syrian King Antiochus, came to the court of Bindusara. Dionysius, who was the ambassador of the Egyptian King Ptolemy II Philadelphus, came to the court of the Mauryan Emperor Bindusara. Megasthenes has described the city administration of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.question_text: Who founded Srinagar in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Mauryan ruler Emperor Ashoka established the cities named Srinagar in Kashmir and Lalit Patan in Nepal. Chandragupta I is considered the founder of the Gupta dynasty. Bindusara was the father of Emperor Ashoka. Harsha, the ruler of the Lohara dynasty, is called the Nero of Kashmir.

questions.question_text: During the reign of Bindusara, the region whose administration was entrusted to Ashoka was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation—According to Divyavadana, during the reign of Bindusara, Ashoka was sent to suppress the rebellion in Taxila. Ashoka had already been the provincial governor of Taxila and Avanti during his father's reign. During Ashoka's reign also, a rebellion occurred in Taxila, and he sent his son there.

questions.question_text: What is the subject matter of the book 'Arthashastra'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 PGT History, 2005 Himachal PGT 2020 Explanation – State and governance policy is the subject of Arthashastra composed by Kautilya. Kautilya is also known by other names like Chanakya and Vishnugupta. Chanakya was the Prime Minister and Chief Priest of Chandragupta Maurya. This book has fifteen chapters (Adhikaranas) and one hundred and eighty sections (Prakaranas). The credit for bringing it to light goes to a scholar named R. Shamasastry.

questions.question_text: Which dynasty ruled immediately after the Mauryan dynasty?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – After the Mauryan dynasty, the Shunga dynasty ruled. After killing the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha in 185-184 BC, his commander Pushyamitra Shunga established the Shunga dynasty. He performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices in his lifetime. Buddhist literature describes Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists because of his destruction of Viharas.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mauryan rulers was a supporter of the Ajivika sect?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation—The Mauryan ruler Dasharatha was a worshipper of the Ajivika sect (Dasharatha was the son of Kunala). Dasharatha built three caves for the Ajivika sect in the Nagarjuni hills. The last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty was Brihadratha.

questions.question_text: The first emperor of the Mauryan dynasty was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The first emperor of the Mauryan dynasty was Chandragupta Maurya (322 BC - 298 BC). Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of his teacher Chanakya, defeated the last Nanda ruler Dhanananda and ascended the throne of Magadha at the age of 25. Brahmanical literature (Puranas etc.) describe Chandragupta Maurya as born of 'Shudra' lineage, while Buddhist and Jain literature describe him as born of 'Kshatriya' lineage. In the play Mudrarakshasa, the epithet 'Vrishala' (low lineage) is used for him.

questions.question_text: Into how many Adhikaranas is the Arthashastra divided?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 MP Asst. Prof. 2017 Explanation – Arthashastra was composed by Chanakya. He is also known by the names Kautilya and Vishnugupta. There are 15 Adhikaranas and 180 Prakaranas in Arthashastra.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sources is related to Mauryan period history?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – All three sources given in the question options provide knowledge of the past regarding Mauryan period history.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sources considers Chandragupta Maurya as a Kshatriya?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation - Buddhist texts Divyavadana, Mahaparinibbana Sutta, Digha Nikaya, Mahavamsa consider Chandragupta Maurya as a Kshatriya. Whereas Mudrarakshasa by Vishakhadatta describes them as being of Vrishala lineage. Chandragupta Maurya was a powerful ruler; he took the help of Chanakya to build the empire. Chanakya later became the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was sent by Ptolemy Philadelphus of Egypt to India as an ambassador during the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 TGT History, 2011 PGT History, 2010 Explanation - It is known from Pliny's account that the Egyptian King Ptolemy Philadelphus sent an ambassador named Dionysius to the court of Bindusara, but by the time Dionysius arrived, Ashoka had become the Emperor and Bindusara had died.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first empire extending from sea to sea - from the Bay of Bengal to the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The borders of India expanded during the reign of the Mauryas. During Ashoka's time, the Mauryan Empire extended from Afghanistan to Mysore and from the Bay of Bengal in the east to Aparantaka, i.e., the Arabian Sea in the west. This region was called "Jambudvipa", which is used in the first Minor Rock Inscription. Ashoka's utterance regarding his empire is as follows – Mahalabohivijite mahante hi vijaye savhaputhiviyam (All earth).

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Western writers, whose works are important sources for ancient Indian cultural history, in their correct chronological order: 1. Nearchus 2. Pliny 3. Strabo 4. Ptolemy Select the correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Among the writers who came with Alexander, the accounts of Nearchus, Onesicritus, and Aristobulus are relatively more authentic and reliable. Some parts of Megasthenes' book named 'Indica' are found in the works of writers like Arrian, Strabo, Justin, etc., as citations. This work of Pliny belongs to the first century AD. In the second century, Ptolemy wrote the Geography of India.

questions.question_text: Which Jain literature does not provide information about the Mauryan era?
questions.explanation: Jain texts Kalpasutra of Bhadrabahu and Parishishtaparvan of Hemachandra provide some preliminary information regarding Chandragupta Maurya. Therefore: Kalpasutra gives information about Mauryan history. However, its answer was given as (d) Kalpasutra by the Commission

questions.question_text: The major eastern coastal port during the period of the Mauryas was
questions.explanation: In the Mauryan period, trade took place through both water and land routes. At this time, India's external trade was with Rome, Syria, Persia, Egypt, and other western countries. This trade was carried out through the ports of Bhrigukachchha in western India and Tamralipti in eastern India

questions.question_text: Whose Prime Minister was Kautilya?
questions.explanation: Kautilya was the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya. Kautilya was a teacher at Taxila University and a nation builder along with being a skilled strategist; in his work Arthashastra, he describes the main components of a welfare state

questions.question_text: Which of these literary works describes in detail that the Nandas were driven out by Chandragupta Maurya and Kautilya together?
questions.explanation: A detailed description of how Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya brought about the downfall of the Nanda dynasty and established their state is found in Mudrarakshasa by Vishakhadatta. It mentions Chandragupta's accession, the active opposition of Rakshasa, Chanakya's political alertness, and finally the acceptance of Chandragupta's supremacy by Rakshasa Vishakhadatta's Devichandraguptam contains the story between the Gupta King Ramagupta's wife Dhruvaswamini and his younger brother Chandragupta Vikramaditya.

questions.question_text: Who was that Mauryan king who, after renouncing his royal crown, accepted Jainism?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, in his final phase, after renouncing the throne in favor of his son, took initiation into Jainism from the Jain monk Bhadrabahu and went to Shravanabelagola (Mysore), where he gave up his body by fasting in 298 BC

questions.question_text: Which foreign traveler entered the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes came during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya as the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator. In his book Indica, he described the Mauryan dynasty and the political system of India

questions.question_text: What was the rate of land tax in the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: The rate of land tax in the Mauryan period was between 1/4 and 1/6. Such government land on which cultivation was not done by the Sitadhyaksha (Superintendent of Agriculture), or if someone made uncultivated land fit for cultivation, then such land was given to the farmers for cultivation, and the farmers used to give 1/4 part to the state as land tax. Apart from this, for cultivating on the private land of householders and other farmers, they had to give 1/6 part to the state, although this could also be 1/4. It is clear from all sources that the entire land of the state belonged to the king

questions.question_text: Who among the following foreign travelers came to India first?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes (Chandragupta Maurya), Fa-Hien (Chandragupta II), Hiuen Tsang (Harshavardhana), Al-Biruni (Mahmud Ghazni) came during these respective times. Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya as an ambassador of Seleucus Nicator. The Chinese traveler Fa-Hien traveled to India during the reign of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)

questions.question_text: Which of the following departments was related to Kantakashodhana?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The Judiciary department was related to Kantakashodhana. In the Mauryan period, there were mainly two types of courts– (a) Dharmasthiya (b) Kantakashodhana. The difference between these courts is not very clear. Still, we can generally call them civil and criminal courts. In both these, three judges sat together to perform the work of justice. Special types of courts were organized to hear cases of foreigners.

questions.question_text: (i) Arrian (ii) Pliny (iii) Ptolemy (iv) Strabo Code: Arrange the following classical authors in chronological order:
questions.explanation: Arrian - 36 BC - 16 BC Strabo - 63 BC - 19 AD Pliny - 23 AD - 79 AD Ptolemy - 90 - 116 AD

questions.question_text: According to the Arthashastra, the ratio of the maximum and minimum salary of government employees was:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the highest annual salary of government employees was 48,000 Pana and the lowest officers/employees received a minimum salary of 60 Pana. The salary of the members of the Council of Ministers kept changing from time to time.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below: List-I (Officer)
questions.explanation: (Officer) (Department) A. Kupyadhyaksha - III. Head of Forest Wealth B. Sannidhata - IV. Head of the Treasury C. Panyadhyaksha - II. Head of the Department of Trade and Commerce D. Pautavadhyaksha - I. Head of the Department of Weights and Measures

questions.question_text: The capital of Chandragupta Maurya was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─ The founder of the Maurya dynasty was Chandragupta Maurya. Its capital was Pataliputra (present-day Patna). The confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers is in this city. The capital of the Haryanka dynasty ruler Udayin was also Pataliputra.

questions.question_text: Which of the following regions was not included in the empire of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– It is proven by the inscriptions of the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka. There were 5 provinces under his rule – Dakshinapatha – Suvarnagiri Uttarapatha – Taxila Kalinga – Tosali Prachi (Eastern) – Pataliputra Avanti Rashtra – Ujjain

questions.question_text: A probable cause of the decline of the Mauryan Empire was–

options.A: Decline of military power due to the adoption of non-violence by Ashoka
options.B: The Buddhist merchant community became so powerful that it dwarfed the royal power before it.
options.C: The economy of the Maurya Empire faltered due to the expenditure incurred in maintaining a huge army, the salary received by the officers, and the financial expenditure incurred in land settlements.

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– There were many reasons for the decline of the Mauryan Empire, which included incompetent and weak successors, lack of national consciousness, atrocities of provincial rulers, economic and cultural inequalities, excess of taxes, excessive centralization of administration, etc.

questions.question_text: Who was Megasthenes?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 PGT History, 2005 Explanation- Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus 'Nicator' to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. He was present in the court at Pataliputra at some time between 304 and 299 BC. Megasthenes authored the book named 'Indica'.

questions.question_text: What is Chandragupta Maurya called in Greek texts?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Chandragupta Maurya is called Sandrocottus in Greek texts. Among Greek writers, Strabo, Plutarch, and Justin, etc., have addressed the Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta Maurya by the said name. British historian Sir William Jones was the first to identify this name with Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.question_text: Chandragupta Maurya had gone to South India with a Jain monk in the last years of his life. The name of that monk (Jain sage) was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Chandragupta Maurya had gone to South India with a Jain monk named Bhadrabahu at the end of his life. At a place named Shravanabelagola, around 298 BC, he (Chandragupta Maurya) gave up his life through the Jain method of Sallekhana, i.e., fasting.

questions.question_text: What is the state currency in the Mauryan period called?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– The state currency of the Mauryan period was the Pana. This was a silver coin equal to 3/4 Tola. This currency was used for state work and the salaries of officers, etc. It is noteworthy that Kautilya has mainly mentioned two coins - Pana and Mashaka. Pana was of silver and Mashaka was of copper.

questions.question_text: In which text is the word 'Vrushala' used for Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– In the play Mudrarakshasa, the epithet 'Vrushala' (of low origin) is used for Chandragupta Maurya. The author of this book is Vishakhadatta.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the provincial governor of Saurashtra during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Chandragupta Maurya appointed Pushyagupta Vaishya as the governor of Kathiawar. According to the Arthashastra, a governor received an annual salary of 12,000 Pana. They managed the administration of the provinces with the help of many ministers and heads of departments.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Ashoka gave up war after the Kalinga war.
options.D: Brihadratha was the last Mauryan Emperor.

questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014 Explanation– Eight years after his coronation, Devanampriya Priyadarsi conquered Kalinga. There, one and a half lakh people were captured and exiled, one lakh were wounded, and many times more than that died. After that, Devanampriya felt great enthusiasm for the protection of Dharma, longing for Dharma, and instruction in Dharma. This is the repentance of the beloved of the gods over the victory of Kalinga. It seems that Ashoka's weak successors could not maintain their authority over Kalinga, and after his death, the kingdom of Kalinga became independent again. In the first century BC, Kalinga became a very powerful kingdom in India. Chandragupta Maurya did not defeat Kharavela because there is a great difference between their dates.

questions.question_text: Who was not included in the seven classes of Mauryan society described by Megasthenes?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Megasthenes, in his work Indica, divided Indian society into seven classes- (1) Philosopher (2) Farmer (3) Warrior (4) Herdsman (5) Artisan or Craftsman (6) Overseer (7) Minister. Special Fact - Kautilya defined the state in his book 'Arthashastra', in which he presented the political-administrative nature of the state in the form of the Saptanga theory, which are as follows- (1) Swami (2) Amatya (3) Janapada (4) Durga (5) Kosha (6) Danda (7) Mitra.

questions.question_text: From where was the Greek ruler, whom Chandragupta Maurya defeated, ruling?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - After the death of Alexander, Seleucus was the successor of his eastern territories. Seleucus had acquired sufficient power by conquering Babylon and Bactria. On the other side, Chandragupta Maurya was busy in building his empire. Around 305 BC, Seleucus, who was ruling from Syria at this time, crossed the Indus River in the course of his eastern campaign and clashed with Chandragupta. Although no account of a war between the two is found from any source, there is mention of the establishment of a treaty and matrimonial relations between the two. From this account, it is clear that Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus.

questions.question_text: Who among the following prescribed punishment for a person who became a monk without making proper arrangements for his dependent wife and children?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation- In Kautilya's Arthashastra, very little respect is shown towards Buddhists. Kautilya clearly prevented people from taking Sannyasa without making arrangements for the maintenance of their family.

questions.question_text: Rulers of which of the following dynasties maintained diplomatic relations with distant countries in the West like Syria?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ Rulers of the Maurya dynasty maintained diplomatic relations with distant countries in the West like Syria. During the time of Chandragupta Maurya, Seleucus, the ruler of Syria, sent his ambassador Megasthenes to the Mauryan court. According to Strabo, the Syrian King Antiochus sent an ambassador named Deimachus to the court of Bindusara. He came in place of Megasthenes. Another Greek writer named Athenaeus has given an account of a friendly correspondence between Bindusara and King Antiochus I of Syria. In Ashoka's inscriptions also, there is a mention of a Syrian King named Antiochus.

questions.question_text: Who among the following said that Chandragupta Maurya attacked and occupied the whole of India with the help of six lakh soldiers?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The credit for the elimination of the Nanda dynasty and the end of foreign rule in Punjab and Sindh does not belong solely to the Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta, but he established his dominance over most parts of India. Plutarch has written that Chandragupta Maurya, taking an army of 6 lakhs, established his dominance over the whole of India. According to Justin, the whole of India was in his possession. In the Mahavamsa, it is said that Kautilya made Chandragupta the emperor of Jambudvipa. Pliny, whose account is based on Megasthenes' Indica, has written that - the boundary of Magadha is the Indus River. In the west, Saurashtra was under the authority of Chandragupta. This is confirmed by the Junagadh inscription of the Shaka Kshatrapa Rudradaman.

questions.question_text: Shravanabelagola is located in:
questions.explanation: Shravanabelagola is located in Karnataka. In the last stage of his life, Chandragupta Maurya left the throne for Bindusara, took initiation into Jainism from the Jain monk Bhadrabahu, and went to Shravanabelagola, where he gave up his body in 298 BC through fasting (Sallekhana method)

questions.question_text: Megasthenes came to the court of the Mauryas as ________.
questions.explanation: Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya as the ambassador of Seleucus

questions.question_text: Which of the following sequences is correct in the administrative structure of the ascending order?
questions.explanation: The hierarchical division of Mauryan administration was as follows – (1) Empire, (2) Province, (3) Ahara or Vishaya, (4) Sthaniva (group of 800 villages) (5) Dronamukha (group of 400 villages) (6) Kharvatika / Karvatika (group of 200 villages) (7) Sangrahana (group of 100 villages). Option (c) is correct in descending order, not ascending order.

questions.question_text: The terminology 'Rupadarsaka' is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: In Kautilya's Arthashastra, the officer who examined coins in the Mauryan period was called Rupadarsaka. By the Mauryan period, the circulation of regular coins had begun in trade and business. Coins were made of gold, silver, and copper

questions.question_text: Match the officials of List-I with the departments of List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II A. Akradhyaksha 1. Head of Commerce Department B. Kupyadhyaksha 2. Head of Forest Resources C. Panyadhyaksha 3. Head of Mining Department D. Pautavadhyaksha 4. Head of Weights and Measures Department Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: The nature of the administration of the Mauryan Empire was centralized. Kautilya has discussed 18 departments and their heads in the Arthashastra. In which the head of the mining department was called Akradhyaksha, the head of forest resources was called Kupyadhyaksha, the head of the commerce department was called Panyadhyaksha, and the head of the weights and measures department was called Pautavadhyaksha

questions.question_text: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, 'Sthaniva' was an administrative unit:
questions.explanation: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, administrations are divided into eight parts. 1. Empire, 2. Province, Ahara or Vishaya, Sthaniva - a group of 800 villages in this, Dronamukha - a group of 400 villages, Kharvatika - a group of 200 villages, Sangrahana - a group of 100 villages, and Village, which was the smallest unit of administration

questions.question_text: In Mauryan administration, reporters were called:
questions.explanation: For running the Mauryan administration in a strong way, officers were appointed for different departments. Major Mauryan period officers- 1. Nagaraka- Chief officer of the city 2. Yukta- Revenue officer under the Rajjuka 3. Rajjuka- Chief officer of the district, he also had revenue authority 4. Prativedaka- The officer who conveyed the public's words to the king, i.e., reporter 5. Pradeshta- Chief judge of the criminal court 6. Rupadarsaka- Chief officer who checked coins 7. Sthanika- The work of collecting land revenue from villages

questions.question_text: Who were the 'Agronomoi' mentioned in Megasthenes' writings?
questions.explanation: The head of the district was Aharapati (Vishayapati) whom Megasthenes called Agronomoi. He was also the chief officer of road construction

questions.question_text: The word Shreshthin has been used for

options.A: One who invests capital in trade

questions.explanation: The head of the organization of guilds was called Shreshthin (Seth/Sethi), Jyeshthaka, or Pramukha. These organizations lived in the Mauryan Empire. The head of the guild of traders was called Sarthavaha. Megasthenes has mentioned the caste system in the form of seven classes. Among these castes, the number of farmers was the highest

questions.question_text: Who has referred to counterfeiters in his text?
questions.explanation: For the first time in the Mauryan period, the outline of the revenue system was prepared, mention of which is also found in Kautilya's Arthashastra. Kautilya has described counterfeiters in his book Arthashastra. Kautilya was the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya. Counterfeiters meant issuing fake currency and putting it into circulation, which spread disorder in the market

questions.question_text: By what name was the judge of the Kantakashodhana court known during the time of the Mauryas?
questions.explanation: The court that decided disputes between the state and citizens is called the Kantakashodhana court. These were criminal courts. Pradeshta was called the judge of the criminal court. Cases of assault, murder, theft, etc., were settled in the criminal court

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? Tax-collecting term - Meaning
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– In ancient times, land tax was called 'Bhaga'. The remaining pairs are correctly matched– Vishti – Forced labor Bhaga – Land tax Kara – Tribute/Customs Pranaya – Emergency tax

questions.question_text: The 'Indica' written by Megasthenes has been lost, but in which Greek and Roman (Greco-Roman) writers' works do its fragments remain? (i) Ctesias (ii) Pliny the Elder (iii) Diodorus Siculus (iv) Strabo Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The 'Indica' written by Megasthenes has been lost, but its fragments remain in the works of Greek and Roman (Greco-Roman) writers. These writers are Pliny the Elder, Diodorus Siculus, and Strabo. Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya as the ambassador of Seleucus 'Nicator'. He wrote about Mauryan society and culture in a book named 'Indica'. 'Indica' is basically the most precious gem in the knowledge obtained by the Greeks regarding India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the first book that suggests giving cash as salary to officers?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– Arthashastra, written by Kautilya, is an important book for the study of the Mauryan period governance system. In this, the suggestion of giving cash salary to officers was first given. According to this book, high-level officers received 48,000 Pana and the lowest-level employees received 60 Pana salary.

questions.question_text: From which of the following inscriptions of Ashoka is it indicated that he did not abolish the death penalty?
questions.explanation: Ashoka has said in his Fourth Pillar Edict that today it is my order that those people who have been sentenced to death, they should be given a respite of three more days. In this same inscription, Ashoka says that my Rajjukas are appointed over lakhs of people

questions.question_text: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, who among the following was responsible for the circulation of coins?
questions.explanation: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, in Mauryan administration, the Lakshanadhyaksha was the head of currency and the mint, and the Panyadhyaksha was the head of trade and commerce. Meanwhile, Sauvarnikas were the primary jewel merchants of the state, and the Akshapataladhyaksha was the superintendent of the land revenue records department

questions.question_text: Which of the following present-day provinces of India was/were NOT a part of the Mauryan Empire?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The present-day provinces of India, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, were not part of the Mauryan Empire. In the Second Rock Edict, Ashoka mentions the Chola, Pandya, Satiyaputra, Keralaputra, and Tamraparni located on his southern border. All these were Tamil states and were outside his empire. The Chola kingdom included the Tiruchirappalli and Tanjore regions of Tamil Nadu, and the Pandya kingdom included the districts of Madurai, Ramnad, and Tirunelveli. The Keralaputra kingdom included the South Malabar region. The identification of Satiyaputra remains uncertain.

questions.question_text: What was the correct descending order of Mauryan officials at the district (Janapada) level?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The correct descending order of Mauryan officials at the district level was: Pradeshika, Rajuka, Yukta. The Pradeshika was senior to the other two officials. The Pradeshika and Rajuka received assistance in their work from subordinate officials called Yuktas. The Pradeshika was the head of the division (Mandala). Rajukas were like modern settlement officers. Yuktas collected revenue and maintained its accounts.

questions.question_text: The 'Sitadhyaksha' mentioned in the Arthashastra was the head of which department?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Kautilya's Arthashastra mentions various types of lands. The income derived from state-owned land was called 'Sita', while the chief officer managing state-owned land was called 'Sitadhyaksha', and agriculture on such lands was carried out by slaves, prisoners, and laborers.

questions.question_text: Under the Mauryan administrative management, the name of the officer overseeing the revenue system was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 PGT 2016 Explanation – The main officials for the management of Mauryan administration were as follows: Purohita – Head of the Department of Religion and Charity Dauvarika – Royal gatekeeper Antarveshika – Head of the harem (Antahpura) Samaharta – Collector of income Sannidhata – Head of the royal treasury Prashasta – One who recorded royal documents and royal orders Nagaraka/Paura – City Police Chief (Kotwal) Antapala – Guardian of border forts

questions.question_text: According to Kautilya, 'Kantakashodhana' were –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The Kantakashodhana described in Kautilya's Arthashastra functioned like modern-day criminal courts. According to the Arthashastra, the courts that decided disputes between the state and citizens were called Kantakashodhana.

questions.question_text: Which official did Emperor Ashoka appoint to administer justice?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 TGT - 2016 Explanation – According to Ashoka's inscriptions, Rajukas were appointed for the oversight of rural areas. They possessed judicial powers along with tax collection powers. There is mention of them ruling over hundreds of thousands of people (panas).

questions.question_text: The Pautavadhyaksha was the head of which department in the Mauryan era?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation — In the Mauryan Empire, the Pautavadhyaksha was the head of the weights and measures department. The head of the currency and mint who issued coins was called Lakshanadhyaksha.

questions.question_text: In which of the following is the division of Mauryan society into seven classes mentioned?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Megasthenes, the ambassador of the Greek ruler Seleucus, came to the court of the Mauryan ruler Chandragupta Maurya. Megasthenes described the contemporary Indian society in his work 'Indica'. From Megasthenes' account, it is known that peace and prosperity prevailed during the Mauryan era. The people were fully self-reliant, and the land was very fertile. People were excellent from a moral point of view and lived a life of simplicity. Indians were courageous, brave, and truthful. Their attire was simple. Wheat and barley were the main food grains. According to Megasthenes, there were seven classes in society: Philosophers, Farmers, Hunters, Herdsmen, Traders/Artisans, Warriors, Inspectors, and Ministers. Megasthenes praised the Brahmin ascetics. According to him, Indians worshipped the Greek gods Dionysus and Herakles. In reality, this refers to the worship of Shiva and Krishna.

questions.question_text: The term 'Samstha' mentioned in Kautilya's Arthashastra is related to—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – Kautilya's Arthashastra provides a detailed description of Mauryan administration. In the Arthashastra, 'Samstha' refers to spies. The intelligence department was placed under a separate Amatya known as 'Mahamatyapasarpa'. Spies were called 'Gudha Purusha' in the Arthashastra. Men whose purity of character and loyalty had been tested in all ways were appointed to this department. A network of spies was spread throughout society. They traveled in various disguises and provided information on daily activities to the emperor. Two types of spies are mentioned in the Arthashastra – 'Samstha', meaning those staying in one place, and 'Sanchara', meaning those who moved from place to place. In addition to men, clever women also worked as spies. The Arthashastra reveals that courtesans were also appointed to the posts of spies.

questions.question_text: Who were the 'Astynomoi' mentioned in Megasthenes' work?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UGC/NTA Dec 2019 IInd Paper Explanation – Megasthenes calls city officers 'Astynomoi'. An officer named 'Agronomoi' also looked after the work of road and building construction in the city.

questions.question_text: Which Greek writer mentioned 'Kalyan' (Kalliena) as a commercial center?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation – The Greek writer Cosmas mentioned the commercial center named Kalyan (Kalliena). Megasthenes was the ambassador sent by Seleucus to the court of Chandragupta Maurya, who wrote the book named 'Indica' and mentioned only seven castes in Mauryan society.

questions.question_text: Who among the following wrote that Indians had no knowledge of the art of writing?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation – Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya, who recorded his account in a book named 'Indica', which is not available in its original form today. Excerpts from Megasthenes' Indica are found as citations in other works, which seem partially erroneous. For example, Megasthenes described seven basic castes instead of four in India and described Indians as being unfamiliar with the art of writing and written law.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings spent significant money on water resource management in the Saurashtra region? 1. Chandragupta Maurya 2. Ashoka 3. Rudradaman 4. Skandagupta Indicate the correct answer using the codes below –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – The Sudarshana Lake was constructed by Pushyagupta Vaishya, the governor of the Saurashtra province under the first Mauryan emperor Chandragupta, for irrigation facilities in Western India. Tushaspa, of the Yavana race, under Ashoka, had a dam constructed on that lake. This dam broke for the first time during the era of the Shaka Mahakshatrapa Rudradaman (130-150 AD). He had it reconstructed by spending immense wealth under the direction of his governor Suvishakha. It is known from the Junagadh inscription that during the reign of Skandagupta, the dam of the historic Sudarshana Lake broke due to heavy rains. For a moment, that beautiful lake took on a terrible appearance (Sudarshana became Durdarshana) for the whole world. This caused great suffering to the people. To alleviate this suffering, Chakrapalita, the son of Parnadatta, the governor of the Saurashtra province, who was the city chief of Girnar, reconstructed the dam of that lake within two months by spending immense wealth and using stone masonry. According to the text, this dam was one hundred hands long and sixty-eight hands wide. With this, the people breathed a sigh of relief, and the Sudarshana Lake became stable eternally.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the inscriptions of Ashoka is false?

options.A: Most of Ashoka's inscriptions are engraved in the Brahmi script.
options.B: Some of Ashoka's inscriptions are engraved in the Kharosthi script.
options.C: Some of his inscriptions are engraved in Greek and Aramaic scripts.
options.D: Three of his pillar edicts were found by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq found two pillars of Ashoka – First: Delhi-Meerut – This was originally in Meerut and was later brought to Delhi by Firoz Shah. Second: Delhi-Topra – This was located at a place named Topra in the Saharanpur (Khizrabad) district of U.P. and was later brought to Delhi by Firoz Shah.

questions.question_text: Which of the following inscriptions was not issued by Ashoka?
questions.explanation: The Junagadh inscription was got engraved by Rudradaman I. Records of Ashoka and Skandagupta are also carved on this. James Prinsep first discovered this record in 1832 AD. There are a total of 20 lines in this record. It is in pure Sanskrit language and Brahmi script

questions.question_text: Match the provinces of List-I with the capitals of List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II A. Uttarapatha 1. Pataliputra B. Dakshinapatha 2. Toshali C. Madhyadesha 3. Suvarnagiri D. Kalinga 4. Taxila Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: List-I List-II Uttarapatha Taxila Dakshinapatha Suvarnagiri Madhyadesha (Prachya/Prasee) Pataliputra Kalinga Tosali Avanti Rashtra Ujjain (Mahishmati)

questions.question_text: At which place was the inscription identifying Ashoka as Devanampiya Piyadassi found?
questions.explanation: The name of Ashoka was first read in the Maski record. 'Devanampiya Asokasa' is engraved in the Maski record. Maski is located in the Raichur district of Karnataka. The mention of Emperor Ashoka's personal name is found in the records of Maski, Gujarra, Nittur, and Udegolam

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to the inscriptions of Ashoka: (1) They are engraved on copper plates (2) They provide information about Ashoka's genealogy Choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Ashoka's inscriptions are found on pillars, rocks, and cave walls; his genealogy is not described in these inscriptions

questions.question_text: The practice of public display of edicts engraved on rocks and free-standing pillars by Indian rulers was an imitation of the associated practice adopted by whom among the following?
questions.explanation: The best specimens of the Mauryan period are the monolithic pillars of Ashoka. These pillars are made of Chunar sandstone. There are two main parts of these pillars – (1) Shaft or monolithic column, and the capital. Due to the shiny polish, bell-shaped base, and animal figures on the capital of the pillars, Western scholars believe that the inspiration for this art came from the Achaemenids (Iran)

questions.question_text: On which inscription of Ashoka was a peacock engraved?
questions.explanation: Ashoka had got two types of pillar edicts engraved. One, Major Pillar Edicts, and the second, Minor Pillar Edicts. The number of Major Pillar Edicts was seven. These were engraved at six places. Among these, Ashoka had got a peacock engraved on the Lauriya-Nandangarh pillar edict

questions.question_text: On which cave of the Barabar group is Ashoka's inscription not engraved?
questions.explanation: Mauryan Emperor Ashoka was a follower of Buddhism. He did much work for the development of Buddhism. He got three caves constructed on the Barabar hills for the residence of Ajivikas, whose names were – Karna-Chaupar cave, Sudama cave, and Vishva Zhopri cave. The Lomas Rishi cave was not constructed by Ashoka but by Dasharatha

questions.question_text: Which of the following successors of Ashoka used the title Devanampiya?
questions.explanation: After Ashoka, the weak rule of his successors continued for the next 50 years. Among the successors of Ashoka, Dasharatha also ruled, whose title was Devanampiya. He was the only ruler after Ashoka to adopt this popular title. The ruler who ruled after Ashoka was Kunala. Dasharatha was a follower of Buddhism. Besides this, he also respected other religions

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not correctly matched? (Ashoka's Pillars) (Animal on Capital)
questions.explanation: A statue of a lion is made on the capital of the Ashoka pillar at Lauriya Nandangarh, not a bull. The pillar at Lauriya Nandangarh is more secure and intact compared to other pillars. Lauriya Nandangarh is associated with Lord Buddha

questions.question_text: Which of the following inscriptions provides information about Ashoka's 'Dharmavijaya'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Ashoka's Thirteenth Rock Edict provides information about Ashoka's Dharmavijaya. In his Thirteenth Rock Edict, he claims 'Dharmavijaya' in foreign lands over Greek rulers and in the southern neighboring states outside the empire within the country. According to the said inscriptions, in all these countries, people listen to the Dhamma instructions (religious teachings) and conduct themselves according to the Dhamma.

questions.question_text: In the versions obtained elsewhere of the series of fourteen rock edicts of Ashoka, which edicts have been replaced by the separate Kalinga edicts obtained from Dhauli and Jaugada?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka are a group of 14 different inscriptions obtained from 8 different places. Due to the mention of 14 inscriptions, these are also called the Fourteen Rock Edicts. On the inscriptions of Dhauli and Jaugada, the 11th, 12th, and 13th Rock Edicts have not been engraved. In their place, two other inscriptions are carved which have been called 'Separate Kalinga Edicts'. Many matters related to administration and Dhamma are mentioned in these inscriptions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct regarding the Rummindei pillar edict of Ashoka?

options.A: It is located in Lumbini, which Ashoka himself visited.
options.B: The memory of the journey to offer floral tributes to Buddha Konakamana by Ashoka is combined in this.
options.C: Ashoka freed the village of Lumbini from the burden of the Bali tax.
options.D: He reduced the land revenue there to 1/8 of the produce.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Ashoka went to places sanctified by the footprints of Mahatma Buddha and worshipped them. It is known from the Minor Pillar Edict of Rummindei that he went to the village of Lumbini in the twentieth year of his coronation. He got a strong stone wall built there and a stone pillar erected. Since Lord Buddha was born there, the village of Lumbini was declared tax-free. And an announcement was made to take only 1/8 part as tax. The Rummindei pillar edict is located in Lumbini. Therefore, option (b) is not correct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Rummindei pillar inscription of Ashoka?

options.C: Regarding the reduction in taxes obtained from the village
options.D: Regarding the prohibition of animal slaughter in the royal kitchen

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– According to the Rummindei inscription located in Lumbini, because it was the birthplace of Buddha, Ashoka visited here in the 20th year of his coronation and reduced the land revenue from 1/6 to 1/8.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below. One is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): Kharosthi inscriptions have been found in Bengal. Reason (R): Kharosthi was very popular in Bengal. Read the above statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, and Aramaic scripts have been used in Ashoka's inscriptions. Greek and Aramaic script inscriptions are from Afghanistan, while Kharosthi script inscriptions have been obtained from N.W. Pakistan and Bengal.

questions.question_text: 'Dharmaraja' was also a title of?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Emperor Ashoka (273-236 BC) was a prominent ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. He created a vast empire, which extended all over India. Ashoka was honored with the title of 'Dharmaraja'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following officials was not in the administration of the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Except for the official named Nayaka, Pradeshika, Rajuka, and Yukta, etc. are among the main officials of the Mauryan administration. The work of the Pradeshika was to inspect the entire administration within his jurisdiction. Meanwhile, the work of the Rajuka was associated with land survey and revenue assessment. The work of the Nayaka was to be the commander of the army or the protector of the city. This was associated with the administration of Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: In which of his inscriptions has Ashoka mentioned the Kalinga War?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The mention of the Kalinga War is in the Shahbazgarhi rock edict (13th Rock Edict) of Ashoka. After the Kalinga victory, Ashoka adopted Dhammaghosha instead of Vijayaghosha. The conquered Kalinga state became a part of the Magadha Empire and its capital became 'Tosali'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was an administrative center of the southern part of Ashoka's empire?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The capital of the Mauryan Empire was Pataliputra (modern Patna). For administrative convenience, the empire was divided into four provinces, the details of which are as follows – Province - Capital Eastern Part - Tosali (Dhauli) Western Part - Ujjayini Southern Part - Suvarnagiri Northern Part - Taxila

questions.question_text: In which inscription of Ashoka is there a mention of his paternal thoughts regarding the duty of a king?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation- The mention of Ashoka's paternal thoughts regarding the duty of a king is found in his first separate Kalinga inscription. In this, Ashoka clearly says "All men are my children."

questions.question_text: From which of the following sites has a stone-engraved image of Ashoka with his name been found from stupa remains?
questions.explanation: (TGT History, 2013) Explanation – A stone-engraved image of Ashoka along with his name has been found from the stupa remains at Kanaganahalli. This site is located in Chittapur taluka of Gulbarga district in Karnataka.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rock edicts of Ashoka speaks about religious harmony?
questions.explanation: (TGT History, 2013) (UP TGT 2021) (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009) (UPPSC (Pre) Indian History 2004) Explanation– In the twelfth rock edict, Ashoka, while making his view towards various religions more natural and clear, says 'Man should respect his own religion and should not criticize other religions without reason. One should respect other religions for one reason or another. By doing so, a man increases his own sect and does a favor to the other's sect.'

questions.question_text: What is the script of Ashoka's rock edicts?
questions.explanation: (TGT History, 2011) Explanation- All inscriptions of Ashoka are written in the Prakrit language and Brahmi script. Only two inscriptions - Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra have the Kharosthi script instead of Brahmi. This script was written from right to left. Ashoka's inscriptions can be divided into three classes- (1) Rock Edicts, (2) Pillar Edicts, (3) Cave Inscriptions.

questions.question_text: Which rock edict of Ashoka reveals his inner agony caused by war and violence?
questions.explanation: (TGT History, 2011) Explanation- In the 13th rock edict of Ashoka, the terrible consequences of the Kalinga war are mentioned as follows- 'In this, one lakh fifty thousand people were taken prisoner and deported, one lakh people were killed and many times more than this died. The heart-wrenching violence and massacre events of the Kalinga war touched Ashoka's heart. Rock edicts 11th, 12th, 13th were not engraved on the Dhauli and Jaugada rock edicts. Dhauli and Jaugada are also famous as separate proclamations or rock edicts.'

questions.question_text: Which animal is not engraved on the Ashokan pillar obtained from Sarnath?
questions.explanation: (TGT History, 2011) Explanation- The deer is not engraved on the Ashokan pillar obtained from Sarnath. The lion capital of the Sarnath pillar is the best. On its abacus, four lifelike lions are sitting firmly back-to-back and facing all four directions. A Mahadharmachakra was established on the heads of the lions, which originally had 32 spokes. Below the lions, four wheels are made which are symbols of the turning of the wheel of law (Dharmachakrapravartana). On this, figures of four animals—elephant, horse, bull and lion—are engraved.

questions.question_text: Ashoka's fourteen rock edicts were found at –
questions.explanation: (TGT History, 2001) Explanation– Ashoka's fourteen rock edicts were found in the Girnar hill near Junagadh in the Kathiawar region of Gujarat. In 1822, Colonel Todd discovered these inscriptions, which are divided into two parts with a line drawn from top to bottom between them. The first five inscriptions are engraved on the left and seven inscriptions on the right. The third inscription is at the bottom, to the right of which is the fourteenth inscription.

questions.question_text: The inscription of which place of Ashoka is called the Queen's Edict?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2000) Explanation– In the Kaushambi or Prayagraj inscription of the Mauryan ruler Ashoka, there is a mention of a donation given by Queen Kaurvaki. This itself is called the Queen's Edict.

questions.question_text: What is the language of Ashoka's inscriptions?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2000, 2009, 2010) Explanation- The language of Ashoka's inscriptions is Prakrit. The scripts of these inscriptions are also different. Only two inscriptions, Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, are in the Kharosthi script. This script was written from right to left. Taxila and Laghman are in Aramaic script, Shar-e-Kuna is in Aramaic and Greek, and others are in Brahmi script.

questions.question_text: In which rock edict of Ashoka is his Kalinga victory mentioned?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2003) (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015) Explanation–Mention of his Kalinga victory is found in the 13th rock edict of Ashoka. Ashoka had attacked Kalinga in 261 BC, in which one lakh people were killed and about 1 lakh 50 thousand people were taken prisoner. Consequently, Emperor Ashoka announced the renunciation of weapons (according to the 13th rock edict).

questions.question_text: Which of the following scripts have been used in Ashoka's inscriptions?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2004) Explanation – The knowledge of Ashoka's history is mainly based on epigraphic evidence. More than 40 of his inscriptions have been found so far. The original language of Ashoka's inscriptions is Prakrit, while these are written in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Aramaic and Greek scripts. First of all, a scholar named James Prinsep succeeded in reading these inscriptions in 1837 AD.

questions.question_text: The Rummindei pillar belongs to whose time?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2005) Explanation─The Rummindei pillar inscription located in the Terai of Nepal is related to the reign of Ashoka. This inscription provides proof of Buddha's birthplace. According to this inscription, Priyadarsi Ashoka came here and he worshipped Shakyamuni Buddha. And he reduced the land tax of Lumbini village to 1/8.

questions.question_text: Which ruler built the Dhamekh Stupa of Sarnath?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2009, 2010) Explanation– The Dhamekh Stupa in Sarnath was built by Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in 249 BC, but its actual expansion took place in the Gupta period. Among the Buddhist stupas of the Gupta period, the Dhamekh Stupa of Sarnath is famous; it is made of bricks. It was built on a level ground without any platform. Its base is not square like other stupas but circular.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best example of Mauryan art?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2010) Explanation – Ashoka had erected pillars made of a single piece of stone 30 to 50 feet long at various and important places throughout his empire, on top of which there are excellent animal capitals. These stone-built pillars are the best examples of Mauryan period art.

questions.question_text: Who first discovered the Ashokan pillar in 1750 AD?
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2010) Explanation – T. Tieffenthaler first discovered Ashoka's inscriptions in 1750 AD. James Prinsep first succeeded in reading these inscriptions in 1837 AD. Sir William Jones established the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784.

questions.question_text: The Thirteenth Rock Edict is related to –
questions.explanation: (PGT History, 2011) Explanation–Detailed information about the Kalinga war and its consequences is obtained from the 13th rock edict of Ashoka. According to this rock edict, Ashoka attacked Kalinga in 261 BC in the 8th year of his coronation. In this war, one lakh people were killed and fifty thousand people were taken prisoner.

questions.question_text: In which inscription of Ashoka is there a mention of five states of South India?
questions.explanation: (Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009) (PGT 2016) Explanation- Ashoka's second rock edict mentions five states of South India, including Chera (Keralaputra), Chola, Pandya, Satiyaputra, and Tamraparni (Sri Lanka). Additionally, the thirteenth rock edict mentions some foreign states where Ashoka had sent his envoys.

questions.question_text: Which of the following foreign kings was not a contemporary of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: (Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012) (DSSSB PGT 2019) Explanation– Ashoka was the most powerful ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. In his 13th rock edict, he mentions 5 Yavana kings who were his contemporaries and where Dhamma preachers had gone. These kings were– 1. Antiochus Theos 2. Ptolemy Philadelphus II 3. Antigonus Gonatas 4. Magas 5. Alexander. Darius II was not a contemporary of Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Ashoka's Shar-e-Kuna inscription is located in
questions.explanation: (Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012) Explanation– Ashoka's Shar-e-Kuna inscription is located in Kandahar. It is written in Aramaic and Greek (bilingual script) scripts.

questions.question_text: The earliest inscription in which the name of Ashoka is mentioned
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009) Explanation- Ashoka was the most powerful and great ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. His earliest name is found in the inscriptions of Maski, Netur, Udegolam, and Gujarra, in which he is called Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Which region of South India was not a part of Ashoka's empire?
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009) Explanation- Ashoka's empire was quite extensive, yet he did not have control over some parts of present-day India. He did not have control over some kingdoms of the South, which include the areas of Chola, Chera, Pandya, which in modern times are roughly the areas of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question_text: In which year of his reign did Ashoka visit Lumbini, the birthplace of Buddha?
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012) (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004) Explanation- In the 20th year of his reign, Ashoka visited Lumbini, the birthplace of Buddha. Ashoka exempted Lumbini from religious tax and reduced the revenue tax from 1/6 to 1/8 part. Ashoka was the most powerful ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. During his time, the Kalinga war took place. In this war, Ashoka was victorious and more than one lakh people were killed. After this, Ashoka adopted Buddhism and used his rule for the propagation of Buddhism.

questions.question_text: In which of his rock edicts did Ashoka mention the 'Atavi tribes'?
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012) Explanation- Ashoka mentioned the 'Atavi tribes' in his 13th rock edict. Ashoka's 13th inscription is the most extensive; in this, in addition to the Kalinga war, five foreign states, five border states, and many forest tribes have been mentioned, in which Ashoka speaks about a peace-loving life with them.

questions.question_text: At which of the following places was the Ashokan pillar with the bull capital located?
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015) Explanation- The number of Ashoka's pillars is not certain; Faxian has mentioned 6 and Xuanzang has mentioned 15 pillars, but the actual number was more than this. 15 of these are safe. These are of two types: (a) pillars on which Dhamma scripts are engraved, (b) pillars which are completely plain. In the first type are Delhi-Meerut, Allahabad, Lauriya Nandangarh, lion capital obtained from Rampurva, etc. In the second type is the pillar with the bull capital obtained from Rampurva. From the above description, it is known that two pillar inscriptions have been found from Rampurva.

questions.question_text: Ashoka maintained friendly relations with his contemporary rulers. This is mentioned in his:
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015) Explanation- Ashoka had maintained friendly relations with his contemporary rulers. This is mentioned in his 13th inscription. In his 13th rock edict, names of five Yavana kings are found, including Antiochus (Syrian King), Turamaya (Egyptian King), Antigonus (Macedonian King), Magas (Epirus) and Alexander (Cyrene), etc.

questions.question_text: The builders of the Sanchi Stupa were
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015) Explanation- Near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh (Raisen district), the famous stupa at Sanchi was built by Ashoka. During the Shunga period, the size of the stupa built by Ashoka was almost doubled. This stupa is built on a high hill. There is a beautiful circumambulation path all around it. Buddha has been depicted in symbolic forms in Sanchi.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions is Ashoka's deep faith in Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha mentioned?
questions.explanation: (G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015) Explanation- The mention of Ashoka's deep faith in Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha is obtained from the Bhabru Minor Rock Edict. The second and third inscriptions of Ashoka show his deep faith in Buddhism and the twelfth rock edict mentions religious tolerance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Ashoka used Kharosthi script in South Indian inscriptions.
options.B: Ashoka has defined 'Dhamma' in the Second Rock Edict.
options.C: Ashoka has defined his 'Dhamma' in the Second Pillar Edict.
options.D: Ashoka used Kharosthi script in the rock edicts of Odisha.

questions.explanation: (Higher Edu. Exam. (Anc. History) 2014) Explanation– In the second pillar edict, Ashoka raised a question: 'Kiyam Chu Dhamma' (What is Dhamma?). In this, he explained that – less sin, excessive welfare, compassion-donation, truthfulness, purity, gentleness and goodness itself is Dhamma.

questions.question_text: Which rock edict of Ashoka describes the sending of missionaries to five Yavana states?
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000) Explanation– It is known from Ashoka's 13th rock edict that he had sent missionaries for the propagation of Buddhism in five Yavana states. These states are as follows- (1) Antiochus (Syrian king) (2) Turamaya (Egyptian king) (3) Antigonus (Macedonian king) (4) Magas (Epirus) (5) Alexander (Cyrene)

questions.question_text: The names of the three officers we find in Ashoka's third rock edict are-
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000) Explanation– The names of some important officers of his administration are found in Ashoka's inscriptions. The names of three officers—Yukta, Rajuka, and Pradeshika—are found in Ashoka's third rock edict. Yuktas were the officers of the district. They also had the right to spend money in that work by which revenue could be increased. The Rajuka officer is related to the "Rajjugahaka" (rope-holder) of the Jataka texts. Such officers kept a rope with them to measure land. They were like the "Settlement Officers" of today. Pradeshika was the head officer of the division. His work was like the 'Divisional Commissioner' of today. He also had to perform judicial work. In his third rock edict, Ashoka says that he has ordered the Yukta, Rajuka and Pradeshika to go on a five-year tour. This type of tour was called 'Anusandhana'.

questions.question_text: What is the correct sequence of animals displayed on the abacus of Ashoka's Sarnath Lion Capital pillar?
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003) Explanation- Mauryan Emperor Ashoka got the capital of Sarnath pillar built. On its abacus, four lifelike lions are sitting firmly back-to-back and facing all four directions. The Mahadharmachakra was established on the heads of the lions, which originally had 32 spokes. Figures of Horse, Lion, Elephant, Bull are engraved on this, which have been shown in a moving state. Among these, the Elephant is considered a symbol of the dream and thought of Buddha being in the womb, the Bull of his birth, the Horse of leaving home (Renunciation) and the Lion of sovereign power. Even in Hindu and Jain traditions, these four animals have been given a place in auspicious objects. In Buddhist tradition, these four animals, symbols of Brahman, are called the guardians of the four gates of Anavatapta Lake in which Buddha had bathed, from where four great rivers emerge. Each animal is associated with one wheel. The wheel is the man in the form of life. In this way, each pair is a symbol of 'Man-Animal'. The first is a symbol of divine power and the second is a symbol of physical element.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions is the name of both Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka mentioned?
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004) (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004) Explanation- The Junagadh inscription was got engraved by Mahakshatrapa Rudradaman in 72 Shaka Samvat (150 AD). This inscription is inscribed on the rock fragment of Ashoka's major rock edict. In this, the individual names of Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka are found.

questions.question_text: In which rock edict of Ashoka are the Cholas, Pandyas, Keralaputras and Satiyaputras mentioned as neighboring powers?
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003) Explanation- Ashoka's Second Rock Edict describes the neighboring powers on the borders of the country like Chola, Pandya, Keralaputra and Satiyaputra. All these were Tamil states and were outside his empire. Mr. Bhandarkar is of the view that the mention of Chola and Pandya is in the plural and the mention of Satiyaputra and Keralaputra is in the singular. Thus, the first two represent tribes and the last two represent rulers. The Chola kingdom included the area of Trichinopoly and Tanjore in Tamil Nadu and the Pandya kingdom included the districts of Madurai, Ramnad and Tirunelveli. The Keralaputra kingdom included the South Malabar region. The identification of Satiyaputra is doubtful. Tamraparni refers to Lanka. Ashoka had friendly relations with all these. From this, it is clear that except for the far southern part which was under the control of Chola, Pandya, Satiyaputra and Keralaputra, the whole of India was under Ashoka's control.

questions.question_text: From which source/sources is it known that Ashoka fought a fierce war in Kalinga? 1. Ashoka's separate Kalinga rock edict 2. Ashoka's thirteenth rock edict 3. Dipavamsa 4. Divyavadana Select the correct answer from the code below -
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005) Explanation – Detailed information about the Kalinga war and its results is obtained from the 13th rock edict of Ashoka. After the victory, two subordinate administrative centers were established in Kalinga. The ancient kingdom of Kalinga was located in present-day southern Odisha. From this, it becomes clear that this war was very terrible in which incidents of massive bloodshed and massacre took place. Finally, Ashoka succeeded in winning this kingdom and merging it into his empire. Unfortunately, we do not know the name of the ruler of Kalinga from any evidence. The terrible consequences of this war are mentioned in the 13th rock edict as follows – in this, one lakh 50 thousand people were taken prisoner and deported, one lakh people were killed and many times more than this died. The Brahmins, Shramanas and householders who did not take part in the war suffered great pain due to the death of their relatives. The emperor had seen this massive massacre with his own eyes.

questions.question_text: The title 'Devanampiya' was adopted by: 1. Ashoka 2. Dasharatha 3. Samprati 4. Brihadratha Select the correct answer from the code below:
questions.explanation: (UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006) Explanation – Maurya Emperor Ashoka sat on the throne of Magadha around 273 BC. In his inscriptions, he is everywhere addressed by titles like 'Devanampiya', 'Piyadassi', and 'Raja' (King) etc. Among Ashoka's successors, Dasharatha also held the title of 'Devanampiya' like Ashoka.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sources provides authentic information about the inclusion of Gujarat in the empire of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Information is obtained from the Girnar inscription (150 AD) or Junagadh inscription of Saka Mahakshtrapa Rudradaman that Chandragupta Maurya had conquered the region up to Saurashtra in Western India and brought it under his direct rule. From this inscription, it is known that Pushyagupta Vaishya was the governor of Chandragupta Maurya in this region and he had constructed a lake named Sudarshana there.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions did Ashoka make his famous declaration, 'All men are my children'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—In his first Separate Kalinga Edict, Ashoka declared that, 'All men are my children. Just as I desire that my children should attain happiness and welfare in this world and the next, I desire the same for all people.' Information regarding Ashoka's foreign policy, policy towards the tribes settled in the border areas, and his policy towards neighboring countries is found in the second Separate Kalinga Edict. It is noteworthy that the two inscriptions engraved at Jaugada and Dhauli are termed as Separate Major Rock Edicts.

questions.question_text: Who identified 'Sandrocottus' of Greco-Roman literature with Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation—Greek writers have used the names Sandrocottus and Androcottus for Chandragupta Maurya. Sir William Jones first identified these names with Chandragupta Maurya. This helped in reaching the important conclusion that Chandragupta Maurya was a contemporary of Alexander.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions did Ashoka announce some tax concessions?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– In the tenth year of his reign, Ashoka first visited Bodh Gaya. After this, in the twentieth year of his coronation, Ashoka visited the village of Lumbini. Because the village of Lumbini was the birthplace of Buddha, it was declared free of religious tax (bali) and the announcement of reducing the land revenue tax from 1/6 to 1/8 part was made in the Lumbini Pillar Edict.

questions.question_text: On which Maurya pillar/pillars is there a lion-capital? 1. Sarnath Pillar 2. Sanchi Pillar 3. Kolhua Pillar 4. Lauriya Nandangarh Pillar Give your correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – A lion is atop the pillar at Basarh (Kolhua), an elephant atop Sankissa, a bull and a lion at Rampurva, a lion at Lauriya Nandangarh, and the figures of four lions together are carved atop the pillars at Sanchi and Sarnath. The Ashoka pillars are unique from both the perspective of architecture and sculpture.

questions.question_text: For whom did Ashoka have caves dug in the Barabar hills in Gaya district?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation – Ashoka started a new style in the history of architecture, that is, creating caves by cutting rocks. In the 12th year of his coronation, Ashoka donated the Sudama cave in the Barabar hills near Gaya to Ajivika monks.

questions.question_text: The Buddhist council organized by Ashoka was presided over by _____.
questions.explanation: During the reign of Emperor Ashoka Maurya (251 BC), the third Buddhist council was organized in Pataliputra. It was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa

questions.question_text: Which state did not exist in the south during the reign of Ashoka?
