questions.explanation: The Pallava state did not exist in the south during the reign of Ashoka. The Pallava dynasty established its kingdom in Kanchipuram in the 6th century, which was founded by Simhavishnu. Pandya was the southernmost state

questions.question_text: In which inscription has Ashoka explained the meaning of ‘Dhamma’?
questions.explanation: The number of Ashoka's pillar edicts is 7, which have been obtained from 6 places. Ashoka explains the meaning of Dhamma in his Second Pillar Edict—Dhamma is goodness, performing many good deeds, mercy, charity etc. In this same pillar edict, serving parents and respecting teachers has also been described as Dhamma

questions.question_text: Who was the officer of Dhamma and morality during the reign of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: In the thirteenth year of his coronation, Ashoka appointed a special officer ‘Dhamma-Mahamatra’ for the propagation of Buddhism, whose task was to end the sense of hatred between various religious sects and emphasize the unity of Dhamma. His primary duty was to protect Dhamma and to increase Dhamma

questions.question_text: What is the name of that king of Sri Lanka who was contemporary to Ashoka?
questions.explanation: King Devanampiya Tissa of Sri Lanka was a contemporary of Ashoka. Ashoka's son Mahendra initiated Tissa, the ruler of Tamraparni (Sri Lanka), into Buddhism

questions.question_text: Which of the following foreign rulers was not contemporary to Ashoka?
questions.explanation: The major foreign rulers contemporary to Emperor Ashoka were - (1) Antiochus (King of Syria) Antiochus II Theos, (2) Turamaya, the ruler of Egypt Ptolemy II Philadelphus, (3) Antikini, Antigonus Gonatas of Macedonia, (4) Maka, King Magas of Cyrene, (5) Alikasundara (Ruler of Epirus). Ashoka had sent Dhamma missionaries to their kingdoms. Seleucus Nicator was a contemporary of Chandragupta Maurya

questions.question_text: Arrange the Greek rulers in the order in which they are mentioned on Ashoka's stone pillars.
questions.explanation: For the propagation of Buddhism, Emperor Ashoka sent envoys to all the people of India and to the Greek kings as far as the Mediterranean Sea. The names of many contemporary Greek rulers from Greece to North Africa are found on his pillars, who are respectively: Greek King Antiyoka (Antiochus), Turamaya (Ptolemy), Antikini (Antigonus), Maka (Magas), Alikasundara (Alexander). Similarly, he had also sent his son and daughter (respectively Mahendra and Sanghamitra) to Chola, Pandya, and Tamraparni (Sri Lanka) in the south for the propagation of Buddhism

questions.question_text: Which of the following queens of Emperor Ashoka is mentioned in his inscriptions?
questions.explanation: In the inscriptions engraved by Ashoka, one of his queens, Karuvaki, is mentioned. In the Kausambi Prayag Pillar Edict, there is a description of donations given by Ashoka's queen Karuvaki. This is also called the Queen's Edict

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below: List-I (Dhamma missionaries appointed in the third Buddhist Council) List-II (Their regions) A. Majjhantika - (i) Kashmir and Gandhara B. Maharaksita - (iv) Yona D. Sona and Uttara - (iii) Suvarnabhumi Code: A B C D C. Mahadharmaraksita - (ii) Maharashtra
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– List-I List-II Majjhantika – Kashmir and Gandhara Maharaksita – Yavana country Mahadharmaraksita – Maharashtra Sona and Uttara – Suvarnabhumi

questions.question_text: Which of the following aspects is not a theoretical aspect of Ashoka's Dhamma?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Ashoka enumerates those qualities in the second and seventh pillar edicts which constitute Dhamma. We can list them in this way—'Aphasinave bahukayane daya dane sache sochae madave sadhave cha.' That is, Dhamma is little sin (aphasinave), much goodness (bahukayane). It is mercy, charity, truthfulness. It is purity (sochae), gentleness (madave), and saintliness (sadhave). Ashoka preaches non-violence to the people. He also preaches proper behavior with everyone and restraint.

questions.question_text: With what main objective did Ashoka propagate 'Dhamma' among his subjects?

options.D: For the moral and spiritual development of his subjects

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation—Ashoka propagated 'Dhamma' for the moral and spiritual development of his subjects. Dhamma is just the Prakrit transformation of the Sanskrit word Dharma. Dhamma and its propagation is the primary reason for Ashoka becoming famous in world history. The mention of things related to Dhamma is found in the second and seventh pillar edicts.

questions.question_text: The transformation of the word Dharma into 'Dhamma' is related to–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation–The code of conduct presented by Maurya Emperor Ashoka is called 'Dhamma' in his inscriptions. The definition of Dhamma given by Ashoka has been taken from the Buddhist text Rahulovada Sutta. Dhamma is the transformation of the word Dharma from Sanskrit into Prakrit language. The message of Dhamma is described in his second and seventh pillar edicts. In his second edict, Ashoka himself asks the question - 'Kiyam chu dhamme' (What is Dhamma?). He gives its answer also in the second and seventh pillar edicts.

questions.question_text: Which ruler called himself 'Beloved of the Gods'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 PGT History, 2005 Explanation– In Ashoka's inscriptions, many of his titles are mentioned. These include 'Devanampiya', 'Piyadassi' etc. The use of the title 'Devanampiya' is also found by Ashoka's successor ruler Dasharatha. The title of Chandragupta Vikramaditya was 'Shri Vikrama'. Kanishka's title was 'Maharaja Rajadhiraja Devaputra'.

questions.question_text: Which ruler organized the third Buddhist council in Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Maurya Emperor Ashoka organized the third Buddhist council in Pataliputra in 251 BC during his reign. This council was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa. He compiled the text named 'Kathavatthu', which comes under the Abhidhamma Pitaka.

questions.question_text: When did Emperor Ashoka conquer Kalinga?

options.A: Fourth year after obtaining the kingdom
options.B: Eighth year after obtaining the kingdom

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation– In 261 BC, that is, in the eighth year of his coronation, Ashoka attacked the Kalinga state which was the southern part of the present-day Odisha state. This war was so horrific that one lakh people were killed and one and a half lakh people were injured. Seeing the horror of this war, Ashoka turned towards Buddhism; since then, he left Rann-ghosha (the sound of war) and became a follower of Bherighosha (the sound of Dhamma).

questions.question_text: Where was Kakanadabota Mahavihara located?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – The famous stupa of Sanchi, which was built during Ashoka's time, includes the Kakanadabota Vihara, in which the relics of Buddha's body were kept; other parts of which were also expanded during the Shunga period. Its ruins are still located today at a place named Sanchi in Raisen district, 35 km away from Bhopal. The remains of Buddhist period art can be seen here.

questions.question_text: The function of the Prativedaka was:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Prativedakas used to perform the task of exchange of information. Their mention is found in Ashoka's inscriptions. The army was led by the Senapati. The task of collecting revenue was done by the Samaharta, and the administration of provinces was conducted through a Kumara or provincial governor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following initiated Ashoka into Buddhism?
questions.explanation: & c) PGT History, 2011 Explanation–According to the Ceylonese traditions Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa, a monk named Nigrodha initiated Ashoka into Buddhism in the fourth year of his reign. According to Divyavadana, a Buddhist monk named Upagupta initiated Ashoka into Buddhism.

questions.question_text: In which regnal year did Ashoka visit Lumbini?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – It is clear from the Rummindei inscription that Ashoka himself came to Lumbini 20 years after his coronation and removed the 'economic tax' from here. According to Divyavadana, Ashoka had undertaken Dhamma pilgrimages with his guru Upagupta. Vincent Smith has fixed the order of Ashoka's travels in this way – Lumbini, Kapilavastu, Sarnath, Sravasti, Bodh Gaya and Kushinagar. In Divyavadana, this event is in the chronological order of life events.

questions.question_text: Which of these major rock edicts of Ashoka provides the description and summary of ‘Dhamma’?
questions.explanation: The description of the characteristics of Dhamma conquest is found in Ashoka's eleventh inscription. The appointment and work instructions of Dhamma Mahapatras and the mention of Mauryan society and varna system are found in the fifth inscription. The mention of the policy of religious tolerance is found in the twelfth inscription. The description of the Kalinga war and the names of 5 border Greek kings where he had sent Dhamma missionaries are described in the thirteenth inscription

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a provincial capital during the reign of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: The Maurya empire was divided into 5 provinces Province – Capital Uttarapatha – Taxila Kalinga – Tosali Dakshinapatha – Suvarnagiri Avanti – Ujjayini Madhyadesha (Prachya) – Pataliputra

questions.question_text: Which of the following is Ashoka's bilingual inscription?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's Shar-i-Kuna inscription located in Kandahar is a bilingual inscription. In this, Greek and Aramaic scripts have been used together

questions.question_text: In whose reign did the Maurya empire spread in the Karnataka region?
questions.explanation: The Maurya empire spread in the Karnataka region of South India during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya. Mention is found in an inscription obtained from 14th-century Mysore that the protection of the taluka of Shikarpur (North Mysore) was the responsibility of the Mauryas. The Commission has considered the answer to this question as option (c) Ashoka

questions.question_text: In which of the following places in South India have Ashoka's inscriptions with 14 declarations been found?
questions.explanation: Ashoka was the son of the Mauryan ruler Bindusara. The history of Ashoka is known mainly from his inscriptions only. First of all, in 1837 AD, James Prinsep achieved success in reading Ashoka's Delhi-Topra inscription. The division of Ashoka's inscriptions has been done respectively in the form of Rock Edicts, Cave Inscriptions and Pillar Edicts. The language of all these inscriptions is Prakrit, while they are written in Brahmi, Kharoshthi, Aramaic and Greek scripts. Information about Ashoka's personal life is obtained from the Minor Rock Edicts; prominent among these are - Erragudi (Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh), Sannati (Gulbarga, Karnataka), Gujarra (Madhya Pradesh), Rajula Mandagiri, Maski, Netur, Udegolam (Bellary, Karnataka). Among these, Ashokan inscriptions with fourteen declarations have been found from Erragudi and Sannati

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): In the 5th century, Faxian, in the course of his journey to India, gave the description that no noble person in the country used to eat meat. Reason (R): Ashoka, who himself strictly followed the principle of non-violence towards living beings, had imposed a ban on animal sacrifice and had regulated the killing of animals for food. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: In the 5th century, Faxian, in the course of his journey to India, gave this description that no noble person in this country used to eat meat, this statement is absolutely correct; and Ashoka, who himself strictly followed the principle of non-violence towards living beings, had imposed a ban on animal sacrifice and had regulated the killing of animals for food. Both these assertion and reason are correct but the reason does not correctly explain the assertion

questions.question_text: The inner brick-built part of the largest stupa at Sanchi, which is called Stupa No. 1 or Mahastupa, was made during whose time?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Sanchi is famous all over the world due to its unparalleled Buddhist monuments and archaeological material. General Taylor drew the attention of the public towards the monuments of Sanchi. Sanchi is also one of the 84,000 stupas of Ashoka, in which Stupa 1, 2, 3 have been found in a preserved state. It was made of bricks, around which was a wooden fence. Subsequently, many stupas, viharas and temples were built here. The inner brick-built part of the Mahastupa was made during Ashoka's time.

questions.question_text: The most famous center of education in the Mauryan period was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Taxila was a famous center of education in the Mauryan period. Kautilya was the chief teacher of the educational center of Taxila. He was very conservative and short-tempered by nature. In the Puranas, he has been called Dvijarshabha (best among Brahmins). Chandragupta Maurya had received education while staying with the teacher Chanakya of Taxila. Among the educational centers of ancient India, Nalanda University is the most notable. It was founded by Kumaragupta I (415-455 AD). Vallabhi University was founded by the Maitraka dynasty ruler Bhattarka. This was the capital of the Maitraka dynasty.

questions.question_text: In the Mauryan period, buildings were also made of wood. Archaeological evidence of this has been found from─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─ In the Mauryan period, buildings were also made of wood, archaeological evidence of this has been obtained from Bulandi Bagh and Kumhrar near Patna. Its discoverer was Mr. Spooner. Remains of the city wall have been obtained from Bulandi Bagh and remains of the royal palace have been found from Kumhrar.

questions.question_text: In Mauryan administration, 'Lakshanadhyaksha' was─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─ In the Mauryan period, the superintendent of the mint was called Lakshanadhyaksha. 'Rupadarshaka' was the inspector of coins. 'Akaradhyaksha' was the superintendent of the mine department and 'Vivitadhyaksha' was the superintendent of pastures.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions of Ashoka is the city named 'Isila' mentioned─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─ The name 'Ashoka' is found in the Maski, Netur, Gujarra, and Udegolam inscriptions. The city named 'Isila' is mentioned in the Siddhapura inscription.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings prescribed harsh punishment for Buddhist monks and nuns who caused division in the Sangha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – In the minor pillar edicts of Sanchi and Sarnath, Ashoka warns the monks and nuns who create a rift in the Buddhist Sangha – "Whosoever, monk or nun, shall break up the Sangha, shall be made to wear white robes and reside in an unsuitable place. Thus this order should be made known in the Sangha of monks and in the Sangha of nuns, for my desire is that the Sangha may be united and endure for a long time."

questions.question_text: Where were the Kumars appointed during the reign of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- For the convenience of administration, the vast empire of Ashoka was divided into many provinces. The names of five provinces are found in his inscriptions. (a) Uttarapatha (Capital Taxila), (b) Avantirattha (Ujjaini), (c) Kalinga (Tosali), (d) Dakshinapatha (Suvarnagiri), (5) Prachya or Eastern Province (Pataliputra). In provinces of political importance, only persons related to the royal family were appointed as governors. They were called 'Kumar' and 'Arya Putra'. Kumars were appointed in this way in Taxila, Suvarnagiri, Tosali, and Ujjaini. It is known from Divyavadana that Ashoka's son Kunala was the governor of Taxila. It is known from Mahavamsa that he appointed his younger brother Tishya as 'Upraja' (Vice-king). Upon him becoming a monk, Ashoka's son Mahendra was appointed to this post. Probably the post of Upraja was like the Prime Minister. In other provinces, other high officials were appointed as governors. Appointments to these posts were made without any discrimination of caste or religion.

questions.question_text: Who founded the city named Srinagar in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─ According to Kalhana's Rajatarangini, Ashoka had established the city named 'Srinagar' in Kashmir and the city named Devpattana (Devpatan) in Nepal. He had the temple of Ashokeshwar established in Kashmir according to religious rites. Kalhana mentions Ashoka as the first Mauryan ruler of Kashmir.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the governor of Surashtra during the reign of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– A special description of the non-Kumar ruled regions is not found, but it is known from the Junagadh inscription that the burden of regional administration in Saurashtra was in the hands of a Yavana named Tushaspa. The other three people were governors of the Saurashtra province of the kings mentioned below. Governor of Saurashtra | Ruler Pushyagupta | Chandragupta Maurya Suvishakha | Rudradaman Chakrapalita | Skandagupta After Chanakya, Khallataka and Radhagupta became Prime Ministers. Therefore, Radhagupta was the Prime Minister and not a governor.

questions.question_text: Where was Turamaya, a contemporary foreign king of Ashoka, the ruler?
questions.explanation: Ashoka sent people to all parts of India and Greek kings up to the Mediterranean for the propagation of Buddhism. On his pillars, names of many contemporary Greek rulers from Greece to North Africa are written, which include Antiyoka (Antiochus II Theos of Syria), Turamaya (Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt), Antikini (Antigonus II of Macedonia), Alikasundara (Alexander II of Epirus) as the main envoys during their reigns

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A) : The Maurya dynasty of India was closely related to the region of present-day Nepal. Reason (R) : A daughter of Ashoka the Great had married a person of the noble class there. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Ashoka had conquered the Nepal region when he was still a prince, and also one of his daughters had married a person named Devapala, a noble Kshatriya of Nepal. Charumati's Mauryan dynasty was closely related to Nepal

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order and choose the appropriate option using the codes -
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation— Chanakya was the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya (320 BC), the founder of the Mauryan Empire. In 261 BC, the Kalinga war took place, at that time Emperor Ashoka was the ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. Kanishka's coronation took place in 78 AD. Chandragupta Vikramaditya ruled India from 375 AD to 415 AD.

questions.question_text: Ashoka attacked Kalinga–

options.A: In the 8th year of his reign
options.B: In the 10th year of his reign
options.C: In the 13th year of his reign
options.D: In the 15th year of his reign

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Mauryan Emperor Ashoka attacked Kalinga in the 8th year of his coronation (261 BC). Information about this war is also found from the 13th Rock Edict of Ashoka. One lakh people were killed in this war and one lakh fifty thousand people were taken prisoner.

questions.question_text: When did Ashoka attack the Kalinga state?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation- Ashoka attacked Kalinga in the 8th year of his coronation (261 BC), in which about 1 lakh people were killed and about one lakh fifty thousand people were taken prisoner. On the basis of the Hathigumpha inscription, it is estimated that probably at that time some king named Nandraja ruled over Kalinga.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the codes below – Statement (A): Scenes from the life of Buddha are depicted in Sanchi art. Reason (R): Sanchi had a close connection with the life of Buddha. Codes :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The stupa of Sanchi near Bhopal was built by Emperor Ashoka. Its expansion took place in the Shunga period. Scenes from the life of Buddha are indeed depicted in the stupa art of Sanchi. However, Sanchi did not have a close connection with the life of Buddha. Therefore, the statement is true but the reason is false.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not among the causes for the decline of the Mauryan Empire?

options.C: They centralized the nature of Mauryan administration.
options.D: The policy of conquest adopted by the later Mauryan rulers.

questions.explanation: Among the causes for the decline of the Mauryan Empire, the policy of conquest adopted by the later Mauryan rulers was not one

questions.question_text: Included in the Mauryan army were: (i) Infantry (ii) Cavalry (iii) Chariots (iv) Elephants Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants were included in the Mauryan army. Chandragupta Maurya had a very large army. It had 6 lakh infantry, 30 thousand cavalry, 9 thousand elephants, and probably 800 chariots. The number of soldiers in society was the highest after the farmers. The soldiers received cash salaries and special attention was given to their discipline and training.

questions.question_text: Who presented evidence of the iron technology developed in India in ancient times by referring to white iron?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Greek historian Curtius, referring to white iron, said that the iron industry was in a very developed state in the Mauryan period. Spooner's view is that a miraculous polish has been applied to the metal relic casket of the Piprahwa Buddhist stupa, the Yaksha statues of Patna, the torsos of Jain Tirthankaras obtained from Lohanipur, etc. A notable fact in this regard is that shiny black pottery has been found from various sites of North India of the pre-Mauryan era. Whose time is fixed between 600-200 BC. They are called N.B.P.W. It takes the antiquity of polishing utensils to the sixth century BC. Therefore, the Mauryan pillars and their polish are completely Indian. There is mention of such evidences in Buddhist literature and Mahabharata which are installed in religious and public places.

questions.question_text: The meaning of 'Pranaya Kar' described in Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' was–

options.B: Tax levied on inter-caste love relationships
options.C: Tax levied on widow love relationships

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– In the Mauryan period, the main source of state income was land tax. This was theoretically 1/6th of the produce, but in practice, it was increased slightly according to the economic situation. As is known from Arthashastra and Greek evidence, in Mauryan rule, people had to pay up to 25% tax on agricultural income. Farmers also had to pay irrigation tax. Water and building taxes were levied in cities. Other main sources of royal income were income from the king's personal land, customs duty, toll, sales tax, taxes levied on trade routes, roads and houses, license fees, and fines received in the form of economic punishment, etc. An official named Samaharta was responsible for collecting taxes and keeping the account of income and expenditure. Pranaya kar was an emergency tax.

questions.question_text: In the Mauryan administrative system, the officer named Rupadarshaka was-

options.A: Examiner of silver and other metals

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the officer who inspected coins in the Mauryan administration was called Rupadarshaka. In the Mauryan era, coins were made of gold, silver, and copper. These coins were called Nishka and Suvarna. Silver coins were called 'Karshapana' or 'Dharana'. Copper coins were called Mashaka. Very small coins were called 'Kakini'. These coins were circulated by rulers, merchants, and guilds, and ownership symbols were placed on them. It is notable that most of the punch-marked silver coins found in large numbers from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar belong to the Mauryan period. There is also mention of the royal mint in Arthashastra. Whose superintendent was 'Lakshanadhyaksha'.

questions.question_text: In Mauryan administration, what was meant by 'Sita'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Chandragupta's well-organized administrative system was based on a strong financial foundation, there was strict government control over all economic activities of the empire. Special attention was given to the progress of agriculture and more and more land was made suitable for cultivation. Both the state and the farmer had rights over the land. The chief officer managing the state land was 'Sitadhyaksha', who got the farming done with the help of slaves, laborers, and prisoners. Some state land was given to farmers for cultivation. The main source of state income was land tax, which was theoretically 1/6th of the produce. The income obtained from state land has been called 'Sita'. Such people gave a 'Bhaga' (portion) of their produce to the king in the form of tax. Land tax was called Bhaga.

questions.question_text: The Superintendent of Commerce in the Mauryan period was called-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– We find descriptions of many officials in Kautilya's Arthashastra. A long list of departmental heads and their works is found in Arthashastra. Probably these heads themselves have been called magistrates by Greek writers. The names of some of them are as follows- Panyadhyaksha (Superintendent of Commerce - Panyadhyaksha along with fixing the price of goods also ensured their supply in the market), Suradhyaksha, Sunadhyaksha (Superintendent of the slaughterhouse), Ganikadhyaksha (Inspector of prostitutes), Sitadhyaksha (Superintendent of the state agricultural department), Akaradhyaksha (Superintendent of mines), Shulkadhyaksha, Sutradhyaksha (Superintendent of the spinning and weaving department), Kosthagaradhyaksha, Kupyadhyaksha (Superintendent of forest and its wealth), Pattanadhyaksha (Superintendent of ports), Sansthadhyaksha (Superintendent of trade routes), Devatadhyaksha (Superintendent of religious institutions).

questions.question_text: Who is in third place in the seven-fold classification of Indian society by Megasthenes?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Megasthenes was a Greek envoy sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by Seleucus 'Nicator'. Before this, he had been the envoy of Seleucus in the court of the Satrap of Arachosia. Probably he appeared in the court of Pataliputra between 304 BC and 299 BC. Megasthenes lived in the Mauryan court for a long time. Whatever he heard or saw while staying in India, he recorded in his book named 'Indica'. According to Megasthenes, there were seven classes in society. Philosophers, farmers, hunters and shepherds, traders and artisans, warriors, inspectors, and ministers. Megasthenes says that peace and prosperity prevailed in the Mauryan era, the people were completely self-reliant and the land was very fertile. People were excellent from a moral point of view and led a simple life. Indians were courageous, brave, and truthful.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a contemporary of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Ashoka enumerates the names of those countries in his second and thirteenth rock edicts where he had sent his envoys. Among these, the states situated on the southern border are mentioned as Chola, Pandya, Satiyaputra, Keralaputra, and Tamraparni (Lanka). In the thirteenth rock edict, names of five Yavana kings are found in whose kingdoms his religious preachers had gone- (1) Antiyoka (Syrian King), (2) Turamaya (Egyptian King) (3) Antikine (Macedonian King), (4) Magas (Cyrene), and (5) Alikasundara (Epirus). Also, Pliny tells us that King Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt had sent an envoy named Dionysius to the Mauryan court. Therefore, Diodotus is not a contemporary of Ashoka. Antiyoka is the Syrian king Antiochus II Theos and Turamaya is the Egyptian ruler Ptolemy II Philadelphus. Antikine is considered to be Antigonus Gonatas of Macedonia. Magas refers to the Cyrenian king Magas. The identification of Alikasundara is not certain, some scholars consider him to be Alexander of Epirus and some consider him to be Alexander of Corinth.

questions.question_text: Who among the following identified 'Sandrocottus' of Greek writers with Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Knowledge of Mauryan history and culture is obtained from the descriptions of classical (Greek-Roman) writers. Greek writers have used the name Sandrocottus for Chandragupta Maurya. First of all, Sir William Jones established the identification of these names with Chandragupta. This helped in drawing the important conclusion that Chandragupta Maurya was a contemporary of Alexander. Among the Buddhist texts, Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa Tika, Mahabodhivamsa, Divyavadana, etc., are prominent. From these, information about Chandragupta Maurya, Bindusara, Ashoka, and later Mauryan rulers is obtained. Bhadrabahu's Kalpasutra and Hemachandra's Parishishtaparvan are Jain texts. From these, some incidents of Chandragupta Maurya's life are known. In Brahmin literature, Puranas, Kautilya's Arthashastra, Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa play, etc., are prominent. From which all necessary information regarding the personality and work of the Mauryan emperor is obtained.

questions.question_text: 'Adevamatrika' land was the land–

options.A: For whose irrigation there was sufficient rain
options.B: Whose irrigation was done by artificial means
options.C: Whose irrigation was not done by any means

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Describing the Mauryan economy, Kautilya said that the characteristic of a good district is that its land should be suitable for agriculture. It should be 'Adevamatrika', that is, it should be such land that good farming could be done in it even without rain. Plowing and sowing were done on the state land by slaves, laborers, and prisoners. Food etc. was given to the slave laborers and cash monthly salary was also given during work, but there was also such state land on which farming was not done by the Sitadhyaksha. Such land was farmed by farmers. Megasthenes has written that the land is suitable for the subsistence of animals, and provides other food items. Since it rains twice a year, therefore crops are harvested twice in India. In almost all the plains of the country, there is such moisture which keeps the land uniformly fertile.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (a) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): The decline of the Mauryan Empire started after Ashoka. Reason (R): Ashoka followed the policy of Dhamma-vijaya and disbanded his army. In the context of the above statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.A: (A) and (R) are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The decline of the Mauryan Empire started after the death of Ashoka. The main reasons for this were the lack of capable successors, excessive centralization of administration, economic and cultural inequality, atrocities on the public by officials, etc. Ashoka followed Dhamma-vijaya and put all his energy into its propagation. But this fact is not correct that after adopting Buddhism he disbanded his entire army. Because information is found in the inscriptions that his military power existed as before. Therefore, the statement of the question is true, but the reason is false.

questions.question_text: Megasthenes divided the Indian society into seven classes in which the second class was:
questions.explanation: Megasthenes had divided the Indian society into seven classes in which the first class was philosophers, the second class was farmers. After this sequentially were Ahir (Shepherds), Artisans, Sculptors (Artisans/Craftsmen), Soldiers, Inspectors, and Councilors. Among these castes, the number of farmers was the highest

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers in ancient India accepted Jainism and took sanyas (renunciation)?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 TGT History, 2009 Explanation─ Chandragupta Maurya accepted Jainism and took sanyas. Chandragupta Maurya was a great conqueror, empire builder, and a skilled administrator. Despite being born in an ordinary family, he reached the position of a universal emperor on the strength of his ability. According to Jain tradition, in the last time of his life, he became a Jain and accepted the discipleship of the Jain saint Bhadrabahu. Chandragupta Maurya gave up his life through the Sallekhana method.

questions.question_text: Who became the ruler of the Kushan dynasty immediately after the death of Kanishka I?
questions.explanation: After the death of Kanishka (101 AD), his eldest son Vashishka (from 102 AD to 106 AD) became the ruler of the Kushan dynasty. There is no evidence of coins issued by him, but two inscriptions have been found according to the Kanishka era: (1) Mathura (24 Kanishka Era) (2) Sanchi (28 Kanishka Era). Possibly in the 'Rajatarangini', Vashishka is mentioned as 'Jushka'

questions.question_text: Identify the dynasty from the following which first issued land grants:
questions.explanation: The first mention of a land grant is found in the Nasik cave inscription of the Satavahana dynasty ruler Gautamiputra Satakarni, which mentions the donation of two villages to an Agrahari

questions.question_text: Which dynasty's rulers first introduced bilingual and bi-script coins in India?
questions.explanation: Bilingual and bi-script coins were first introduced in India by the Indo-Greek rulers. From the point of view of coins, the post-Mauryan period is unprecedented, in which Indo-Greek rulers were the first to issue coins with legends and gold coins. Prior to this, images of deities were inscribed on coins and no name or date was engraved. With the start of the rule of the Greek kings of Bactria in the northwestern part of India, the name and date of the king began to be inscribed on the coins

questions.question_text: Who is credited as the author of 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—The author of 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' was an unknown Greek sailor. He composed this book based on his personal travels. Detailed information about the Indian maritime coasts is obtained from this book. This book is written in the Greek language.

questions.question_text: What is the difference in years between the start of the Shaka and Vikrama eras?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation—Vikrama Samvat is the name of a time calculation system in the Hindu calendar. This era starts in 57 BC. Its initiator is considered to be King Dharmapal Bhutivarma Vikramaditya of the Lichchhavi dynasty of Nepal. This fact has also been validated by the explorer from Gujarat, Pt. Bhagwan Lal Indraji. Shaka Samvat is an ancient era of India which starts from 78 AD. Shaka Samvat is the national calendar of India. Regarding the Shaka Samvat, it is the opinion of Buhler that the Kshatrapa Chashtana of Ujjayini started it.

questions.question_text: Who among the following rulers was the last ruler of the Satavahana dynasty?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—According to the Puranas, after Yajnashri, rulers like Vijayashri, Chandragupta Shri Pulumavi IV (the last ruler of the Satavahana dynasty) were weak and incompetent. As a result, the Satavahana kingdom began to disintegrate and was divided into 5 small states. It is noteworthy that the founder of the Andhra Satavahana dynasty was Simuka.

questions.question_text: Whose foreign account provides information about the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Megasthenes has described the Mauryan city administration in his book 'Indika'. According to him, six committees consisting of five members each were formed. There were a total of 30 members; the responsibility of city administration was upon them. The city officials were called Astynomoi.

questions.question_text: In Manusmriti, by what name is the area between the Sarasvati and Drishadvati rivers designated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation - In Manusmriti, the area between the Sarasvati and Drishadvati rivers is described as the divine-created country 'Brahmavarta'; the Ganga-Yamuna Doab region is Brahmarshidesha, the area between the Himalayas and Narmada is Aryavarta, and the area between the seven rivers is Sapta-Sindhava.

questions.question_text: Which Jain literature does not provide information about the Mauryan era?
questions.explanation: Some preliminary information regarding Chandragupta Maurya is obtained from Jain texts like Bhadrabahu's Kalpasutra and Hemchandra's Parishishtaparvan, Harishena's Brihatkathakosh, Kshemendra's Brihatkathamanjari, and Somadeva's Kathasaritsagara. In addition, information about the Mauryan period is also obtained from Jain literature Bhadrabahucharitra and Bhagavati Sutra. However, the answer given by the Commission was Kalpasutra

questions.question_text: Who is the author of Mahabhashya?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation — Patanjali was the priest of Pushyamitra Shunga. The Yavana invasion is discussed in the book 'Mahabhashya' composed by him, in which it is mentioned that the Yavanas had trampled over Saketa and Madhyamika.

questions.question_text: For the propagation of Buddhism, Ashoka appointed officials who were called –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation - For the propagation of Buddhism, Ashoka appointed officials who were called Dhamma Mahamatras. Other officials appointed during his time were such as - Rajjuka, who was the head of the revenue and judicial system; Yukta, who searched for stolen property; and Amatya, who used to be the Prime Minister. The names of three officials are found in the third inscription of Ashoka: Yukta, Rajjuka, and Pradeshika. The mention of Dhamma Mahamatras is found in the 12th inscription.

questions.question_text: Who among the following built the Garuda pillar at Besnagar?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – It is known from the Garuda pillar of Besnagar that the Greek king Antialcidas sent a person named Heliodorus, a resident of Taxila, as his ambassador to the court of King Bhagabhadra of Vidisha. After arriving there, he became a Bhagavata (Vaishnava) and called himself a Bhagavata. He dedicated a Garuda pillar to his revered deity Vasudeva in front of the Vishnu temple, on which three immortal sentences like self-restraint, sacrifice, and alertness were engraved.

questions.question_text: From which inscription of Ashoka is information about the rules of Buddhism obtained?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The strongest evidence of Ashoka's Dhamma and his viewpoint of being a follower of Buddhism is his minor rock inscription obtained from Bhabru (Bairat-Rajasthan), in which Ashoka mentions the rules of Buddhism and salutes the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha.

questions.question_text: In the Indo-Chinese context, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: The most famous Indo-Greek ruler was Menander (Milinda).
options.C: Indo-Greek rulers were the first rulers to start gold coins on a large scale.
options.D: Menander got a long inscription written in pure Sanskrit for the first time.

questions.explanation: & d) : The credit for having a long inscription written in pure Sanskrit for the first time in India goes to the Shaka ruler Rudradaman, whose Junagadh inscription it is. Indo-Greek rulers were indeed the first to issue gold coins in India, but their number was very small

questions.question_text: Which two Indian deities described by Megasthenes, Dionysus and Herakles, are generally identified with?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation - Megasthenes has described in 'Indika' that the people of India worshipped the Greek deities Dionysus (Shiva) and Herakles (Krishna).

questions.question_text: What was the head of mines called in Mauryan administration?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In Mauryan administration, the head of mines (Superintendent of Mines) was called Akara-adhyaksha; Lakshana-adhyaksha was the head of the mint, Sita-adhyaksha was the head of agriculture, Pautava-adhyaksha was the head of weights and measures, and Panya-adhyaksha was the head of trade. Loha-adhyaksha was the head of iron mines, while Suna-adhyaksha was the superintendent of the slaughterhouse.

questions.question_text: In Sangam literature, with whom is 'Kaveripattinam' associated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation - In Sangam literature, Kaveripattinam was associated with the Cholas. The capital of the Chola dynasty was first Uraiyur, later it was shifted to Puhar, which came to be known as Kaveripattinam. Kaveripattinam was a prosperous port of this period, from where large ships used to come and go to foreign countries loaded with goods. The poet of Pattinappalai has presented a very detailed and vivid description of the progress of industry and trade in the regions of Kaveripattinam. Encouragement was given to convert forests into agricultural land and the number of ponds for irrigation was increased. Prosperity in Karikala's kingdom was natural due to these efforts. For this reason, he ruled happily for a long time.

questions.question_text: On the banks of which river was the ancient port Puhar situated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Puhar port is located at the mouth of the Kaveri. Initially, the Chola ruler Karikala secured the port of Puhar by building a fort on the banks of the Kaveri. He had employed war prisoners of Sinhala (Lanka) in this work. In the Tamil literature of the first century AD, Puhar is described as a busy port. A very lively description of Puhar is found in the Tamil text Pattinappalai.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are given in 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'? Select the correct answer from the code given below: (i) Colchi, Camara, and Poduca were South Indian ports. (ii) Ivory was produced in Dosarene. (iii) Large ships named Kolandia used to sail towards the Ganges and Chryse. (iv) Masalia was to the south of Muziris. Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation—Adequate information about Sangam period trade is obtained from the book named 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'. According to this book, Naura, Tondis, Muziris, and Nelcynda were the major ports of the western coast, while Colchi, Camara, and Poduca were South Indian ports. Information is also obtained from this that large ships named Kolandia used to sail towards the Ganges and Chryse. In addition to spices, ivory, pearls, muslin, and silk clothes were exported to western countries. Ivory was produced in Dosarene.

questions.question_text: Match the Sangam authors in List-I with their works in List-II. List-I	List-II A. Tolkappiyar	1. Manimekalai B. Tiruttakkatevar	2. Tolkappiyam C. Ilango Adigal	3. Silappadikaram D. Sattanar	4. Jivaka Chintamani A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Tolkappiyar — Tolkappiyam Tiruttakkatevar — Jivaka Chintamani Ilango Adigal — Silappadikaram Sattanar/Seethalai Sattanar — Manimekalai

questions.question_text: The famous king of the Sangam period, Karikala, belonged to which of these dynasties?
questions.explanation: Karikala was the most important ruler among the early Chola kings; his tenure is considered to be 140-190 AD. He established the coastal capital of the Cholas, Puhar (modern Kaveripattinam), and built a 160 km long dam along the Kaveri river

questions.question_text: Which of these is considered the 'Bible of Tamil Nadu'?
questions.explanation: Pathinenkilkanakku is a code-based book with 18 minor poems, it is related to the Third Sangam literature. Among these 18 poems, the important poem is Tirukkural written by the great Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar; it is also called the Bible of Tamil literature or the Fifth Veda

questions.question_text: The actual name of the post of ministers during the Sangam age was:
questions.explanation: In the Sangam age, the power of the king was controlled by councils of 5 people, who were known as the five great assemblies (Pancha Mahasabha)– Minister — Amaichchar Priest — Purohitar Army Chief — Senapathiyar Envoy/Ambassador — Thuthar Spy — Orar

questions.question_text: In which of the following rulers' court did Heliodorus, the ambassador of the Greek ruler Antialcidas of Taxila, come?
questions.explanation: Heliodorus was the ambassador of the Yavana ruler Antialcidas of Taxila, who came to the court of Shunga ruler Bhagabhadra. He adopted the Bhagavata religion and established the 'Garuda Pillar' in Vidisha (Besnagar) and worshipped Lord Vishnu

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not a correct statement regarding the Shakas?

options.A: The Shakas attacked Bactria due to the increasing pressure of the Yuezhi tribe.
options.B: Moving forward from Bactria, they attacked the Parthians of Iran and subsequently the Greeks in India.
options.C: By the middle of the first century BC, the Shakas had reached as far as Mathura.
options.D: In India, they stopped selecting Greek and Prakrit inscriptions on coins.

questions.explanation: The Shakas first used the Greek script on the obverse and the Kharosthi script on the reverse of the coins they issued in India. Later, rulers used the Brahmi script and the Kharosthi script on their coins

questions.question_text: Identify the false statement:

options.A: Indo-Greek rulers issued coins with legends in bilingual and bi-script.
options.B: Joint coins issued by some Indo-Greek rulers are indicators of their joint rule.
options.C: Coins were issued only by rulers; other establishments or agencies, such as city administrations, guilds, etc., did not issue their own coins.
options.D: Coins with the names of cities, such as Ujjaini, Madhyamika, etc., have also been found.

questions.explanation: On the Indian coins circulated by Indo-Greek rulers, the figure of the king was on one side and the figure of some deity or their symbol was on the other side. Indo-Greeks first started writing inscriptions on coins. Menander was the powerful and justice-loving ruler of this dynasty, who ruled an extensive empire stretching from Mathura to the Jhelum river

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Sangam literature is false?

options.A: The composition of Sangam literature was completed in about three to four centuries.
options.B: Sangam literature is mainly divided into two main categories - Patthinenkilkanakku (eighteen didactic texts) and Pattupattu (ten idylls).
options.D: Sangam poems are songs of praise dedicated to various heroes and heroines.

questions.explanation: Sangam literature is not religious literature; the chronological history of South India at the beginning of the historical era is known from the literature called Sangam literature. Apart from Sangam literature, no other historical text is obtained from South India. Thus, the main source of the early history of South India is Sangam literature Three Sangams- (i) First - Madurai (Capital of Pandya kings) Chairman - Sage Agastya (ii) Second - Kavantapuram or Kapatapuram Chairman - Sage Agastya and Tolkappiyar (Composition- Tolkappiyam) (iii) Third - Madurai - Chairman - Nakkirar Their division was into Agam (related to love) and Puram (related to praise of kings).

questions.question_text: By what name was the merchant class known in Sangam literature?
questions.explanation: In Sangam literature, the merchant class was called Vanigar, but their social status was not good. They were kept in the category of Shudras. Vellalar was the farmer class and Pulaiyan was the artisan class

questions.question_text: Which of the following centers was not a center of Shunga art?
questions.explanation: The centers of Shunga art were Bodh Gaya, Sanchi, and Bharhut. In Shunga period art, the depiction of animals was less in royal form like the Mauryan period and more from the social importance and religious point of view. In this period, the sculptor's imagination is also seen through the statues

questions.question_text: In which Purana is the longest list of Andhra Satavahana rulers?
questions.explanation: Matsya Purana is especially useful for knowing Satavahana history. The longest list of Satavahana rulers is given in it. In this, the Satavahanas are called 'Andhrabhritya' and 'Andhrajatiya'

questions.question_text: With whom is the Hathigumpha inscription related?
questions.explanation: The Kalinga king Kharavela got the Hathigumpha inscription engraved; this inscription is in the Prakrit language. Kharavela was a follower of Jainism

questions.question_text: Which of the following is related to Sudarshana Lake?
questions.explanation: Sudarshana Lake is located on the Suvarnarekha (river) in Girnar of Saurashtra province. This lake was constructed by Pushyagupta Vaishya, the provincial governor of Chandragupta Maurya. Later, in the time of Ashoka, Tushaspa got it repaired. During the time of Rudradaman, the dam of this lake broke, which Rudradaman got repaired free of cost

questions.question_text: Kharavela was a ruler of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Kharavela was the most powerful king of the Chedi dynasty of Kalinga. An undated inscription has been obtained from the Hathigumpha of Udayagiri hill, in which a chronological description of the events of Kharavela's life and the 13 years of his reign after accession to the throne is given

questions.question_text: Who was the great scholar during Kanishka's time?
questions.explanation: & d) : Kanishka's reign is known for the progress of art and literature. He was a generous patron of knowledge. High-quality scholars and philosophers resided in his court, which included Ashvaghosa, Nagarjuna, Vasumitra, Charaka, etc. Among them, Ashvaghosa was the foremost and a great scholar. He was Kanishka's court poet; he composed two epics, Buddhacharita and Saundarananda, and a play, Shariputra-prakarana. Along with being a poet and playwright, he was also a musician, storyteller, politician, and philosopher. In addition to them, Acharya Nagarjuna (the proponent of Shunyavada), Vasumitra (the president of the fourth Buddhist council), and leading scholars of Ayurveda like Charaka, along with Matricheta, Sangharaksha, etc., resided in Kanishka's court Ans. (b & d) : Kanishka's reign is known for the progress of art and literature. He was a generous patron of learning. High-level scholars and philosophers resided in his court, including Ashvaghosa, Nagarjuna, Vasumitra, Charaka, etc. Among them, Ashvaghosa was the foremost and a great scholar. He was the court poet of Kanishka; he composed two epics, 'Buddhacharita' and 'Saundarananda', and a play, 'Sariputraprakarana'. Besides being a poet and playwright, he was also a musician, storyteller, politician, and philosopher. Additionally, Acharya Nagarjuna, the proponent of Shunyavada (the doctrine of voidness), Vasumitra, the president of the Fourth Buddhist Council, and Charaka, a leading scholar of Ayurveda, and scholars like Matrcheta, Sangharaksha, etc., resided in Kanishka's court.

questions.question_text: Under whom were the provincial Kshatrapas?
questions.explanation: The states established by the Shakas in India had a Kshatrap-based administrative system. In the joint ruling system of the Shakas in India, the senior ruler was called 'Mahakshatrapa' and the other junior rulers were called 'Kshatrapa'. The use of the word 'Kshatrapa' started in Iran

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is wrong?

options.B: Sangam literature poems were compiled in groups of hundreds of Puranas (Purananuru).
options.C: Religion is not included in Sangam literature.
options.D: There is glorification of deities like Shiva, Kartikeya, and Ganesha in Sangam literature.

questions.explanation: Religion is not included in Sangam literature. From this literature, a chronological history of South India is obtained. In the 'Ettuthokai' of Sangam literature, there is a mention of a collection of eight poems. The description of Shiva, Kartikeya, and Ganesha is also found in Sangam literature

questions.question_text: Who became the ruler after Pushyamitra Shunga?
questions.explanation: The Shunga dynasty was established in 185 BC by the Maurya commander Pushyamitra Shunga after killing the last Maurya ruler Brihadratha. Pushyamitra Shunga was a staunch Brahminist. After his death, his son Agnimitra became the ruler

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: List-I | List-II (a) Arasar – Ruling class and Warrior class (b) Mullavar – Dacoits (Plunderers) (c) Eniyar – Hunters (d) Venejar – Merchant class Note – All these come under the classes of Sangam period society. Besides these, there were also Vellalar (farmer class) and Suddugum (Brahmin and intellectual class).

questions.question_text: In Sangam literature, which popular Chola ruler's name do we find?
questions.explanation: Karikala was the most important ruler among the early Chola kings. He founded the coastal capital of the Cholas, Puhar (Kaveripattinam). He moved his capital from Uraiyur to Kaveripattinam. Karikala was a knower of the seven notes and a follower of the Vedic religion

questions.question_text: Which city of South India does the Periplus state to be the center of the cotton textile trade?
questions.explanation: Detailed information about trade and commerce of the post-Maurya period is obtained from the book titled 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'. It has mentioned Uraiyur as a major center for cotton textiles. According to it, Korkai (famous for the pearl industry) and Bharuch (for the slave trade) are mentioned

questions.question_text: Which foreign author has given accounts of the Shunga dynasty?
questions.explanation: List-I (Traveler) | List-II (Description) (a) Faxian – Gupta period (b) Xuanzang – Vardhana period (Pushyabhuti period) (c) Yijing – Early Medieval period (d) Taranatha – Shunga period

questions.question_text: Of which place was Patanjali a resident?
questions.explanation: Maharishi Patanjali was the priest of the Shunga king Pushyamitra Shunga. He wrote a commentary named 'Mahabhashya' on Panini's Ashtadhyayi. He was originally a resident of Gonarda (Gonda district)

questions.question_text: From which place were the Yakshi idols of the Shunga era obtained?
questions.explanation: The Bharhut stupa was discovered by Mr. Cunningham in 1873. Its railing and Gateway belong to the Shunga period. A Yakshi idol of the Shunga era is depicted on this stupa; additionally, a Yaksha-Yakshini idol and a scene of a woman embracing a tree are also prominent depictions

questions.question_text: Which of the following Indo-Greek rulers issued coins with the figures of Krishna and Balarama?
questions.explanation: Figures of Krishna and Balarama are found on the coins of the Greek-Yavana ruler Agathocles. The most famous ruler among the Indo-Greek rulers was Menander, whose bronze coins feature the symbol of the Dharma Chakra. Greek Yavana rulers were the first to issue coins with inscriptions (in India)

questions.question_text: From which site were the remains of a Roman merchant settlement in India obtained?
questions.explanation: Arikamedu is a major site located in South India. Sir Mortimer Wheeler conducted archaeological excavations here in 1945. It had close trade relations with China, Malaya, and Rome. Remains of a Roman merchant settlement have also been obtained from here. Located on the Coromandel coast, it was a major trade center in the first century. Arikamedu has been addressed by the name 'Poduke' in the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'

questions.question_text: Among the following scripts, which script is NOT found on the coins of Rajuvula?
questions.explanation: Brahmi, Greek, and Kharosthi scripts are inscribed on the coins of Rajuvula, whereas Aramaic script is not found

questions.question_text: During the reign of which Kushana ruler did Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna go to China to propagate Buddhism?
questions.explanation: During the time of the Kushana ruler Vima Kadphises, Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna went to China to propagate Buddhism. The Kushana ruler Vima Kadphises first issued gold coins in large quantities. He was also a follower of Shaivism and had adopted the title of 'Maheshwara'. Kanishka was a follower of the Mahayana branch of Buddhism

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.A: Date of Kanishka 58 BC : Fleet and J. Kennedy
options.B: Date of Kanishka 78 AD : Rapson and Oldenberg
options.C: Date of Kanishka 90 AD to 138 AD : Konow and Poussin
options.D: Date of Kanishka 144 AD : Smith and A. K. Narain

questions.explanation: List-I (Date of Kanishka's Coronation) | List-II (Scholar) (a) 58 BC – Fleet and Kennedy (b) 78 AD – Ferguson, Rapson, and Oldenberg, Thomas (c) 90 AD – 138 AD – Konow and Poussin (d) 144 AD – Ghirshman Shriharsha was the court poet of the Gahadavala king Jayachandra, and Vakpati was the court poet of the Kannauj king Yashovarman.

questions.question_text: In which Tamil work is the virtue of the devoted wife (Pattini-worship) glorified?
questions.explanation: Silappadikaram is known as the first epic of Tamil literature. Its literal meaning is 'The Tale of the Anklet'. It was composed by Ilango Adigal. The mention of wife-worship is found in this book. From here, a signal of the society changing from a matriarchal system to a patriarchal system is obtained

questions.question_text: Which is the oldest available text of ancient Tamil grammar among the following?
questions.explanation: Tolkappiyam is an important work of Sangam era literature, in which the first evidence of ancient Tamil grammar is found. It was composed by Tolkappiyar. He was one of the 12 competent disciples of Sage Agastya. Mention of eight types of marriages is found in this book. In this book, love marriage is called 'Panthinai', one-sided love is called 'Kaikkilai', and improper love is called 'Peruntinai'

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following foreign invasions after the Maurya period in India? 1. Indo-Parthian 2. Indo-Greek 3. Indo-Scythian 4. Kushana
questions.explanation: The first foreigners to invade India after the Maurya period were the Greeks of Bactria, i.e., Indo-Greeks. They have been called Yavanas in ancient Indian literature. Thereafter, Shakas (Indo-Scythians) and Pahlavas (Indo-Parthians) came. The Kushanas came last, whose major ruler was Kanishka

questions.question_text: Ancient site from where coins of Menander were obtained?
questions.explanation: Coins of the Greek ruler Menander have been obtained from places like Bajaur, Swat Valley, Bairat (Viratnagar), etc. On the coins of Menander, depictions of the king's head, camel, and wheel, and inscriptions like 'Dhammika', 'Soter', and 'Dikaios' are found

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Tamil grammar work?
questions.explanation: Tolkappiyam is a work of Tamil grammar. It was composed by Tolkappiyar. A description of 8 types of marriages is also found in this book

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the capital of the Pandya kingdom?
questions.explanation: The Pandya kingdom was located in the far south and southeastern part of the peninsula. Madurai was its capital. Their symbol was a fish. Megasthenes made the first mention of the Pandyas

questions.question_text: Where is the inscription of Rudradaman located?
questions.explanation: Evidence of Rudradaman's inscription has been found from Girnar (Junagadh)

questions.question_text: From which place was the famous headless statue of Kanishka obtained?
questions.explanation: The famous headless statue of Kanishka was obtained from Mathura. The last Buddhist council was organized in Kashmir during the time of Kanishka himself

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a port located on the west coast of India?
questions.explanation: Muziris was a major port located on the west coast of India, which is mentioned in Tamil poems and classical sources. Muziris was a major point between South India and Persia, Middle East, North Africa, and the Mediterranean region

questions.question_text: Where is the Nanaghat inscription located?
questions.explanation: Nanaghat inscription is a historical site located in Pune (Maharashtra). These inscriptions belong to the 2nd century BC or 1st century BC when the Satavahana dynasty ruled. These inscriptions establish a link between Vedic and Vaishnava deities

questions.question_text: In which inscription is the description related to Gautamiputra Satakarni available?
questions.explanation: The description related to Gautamiputra Satakarni is found in the Nasik inscription. Satakarni defeated the Shaka ruler Nahapana; this is confirmed by the silver coins obtained from Jogalthambi near Nasik

questions.question_text: The most famous ruler among the Shaka Kardamaka rulers was
questions.explanation: In Indian sources, the Shakas have been given the name Scythians. The Shaka rulers in India called themselves Kshatrapas. They had two main branches—Northern Kshatrapas (Taxila and Mathura) and Western Kshatrapas (Nasik and Ujjain). Among these, Rudradaman (130-150 AD) was the most famous Shaka ruler of the Kardamaka dynasty (Ujjain) of the Western Kshatrapas

questions.question_text: The invasion of Yavanas on Saketa and Madhyamika is described in
questions.explanation: The invasion of foreigners from the north-western route was the most important political event of the post-Maurya period. The first of these invaders were the Greeks of Bactria, who have been addressed by the name Yavana in earlier Indian literature. It is mentioned in Patanjali's Mahabhashya that the Greeks besieged Saketa in Avadh and Madhyamika near Chittor in Rajasthan. It is known from the Yugapurana chapter of the Garga Samhita that the wicked, brave Yavanas, after conquering Saketa, Panchala (Ganga-Yamuna Doab), and Mathura, made a dash to Pataliputra, but returned due to internal wars

questions.question_text: The Satavahanas have also been addressed as Andhra-Bhrityas in
questions.explanation: The rulers who are mentioned as Satavahanas in the inscriptions are also addressed as Andhra-Bhrityas in the Puranas. Scholars interpret this as 'servants of the Andhras', meaning the Satavahana rulers were initially servants of the Andhra dynasty kings. According to the Puranas, the date of the rise of the Andhras can be said to be around 30 BC. The first Satavahana ruler was Simuka. The central point of the Satavahana kingdom was a place named Pratishthana in Maharashtra

questions.question_text: Which of the following ambassadors adopted the title 'Bhagavata'?
questions.explanation: In the 14th year of the reign of Bhagabhadra (Bhagavata), the ninth ruler of the Shunga dynasty, Heliodorus, the ambassador of the Yavana ruler Antialcidas of Taxila, erected a Garuda pillar in Vidisha in honor of Vasudeva. In the Shunga period, there was a revival of the Sanskrit language. Maharishi Patanjali had a special contribution to its rise

questions.question_text: Which of the following does the early Tamil literature present as evidence?

options.B: A complex political and economic system

questions.explanation: Tamil literature is related to literary writings recorded in the Tamil language. The Tamil language is a language of the Dravidian family. Indian Tamil writers and Sri Lankan Tamil writers have contributed to the Tamil language. The historical development of Tamil literature follows the history of Tamil Nadu, which is considered favorable to the social and political trends of different periods. The revival of Tamil literature began from the latter half of the 19th century, when religious and philosophical leanings were presented in such a style that it became easy for the general public to be delighted along with the absence of the caste system

questions.question_text: Where was a Kushana 'Devakula', where statues of royal family members were kept, found?
questions.explanation: The Kushanas were of the Yuezhi tribe of Western China in Central Asia. Among the Kushana rulers, Kujula Kadphises, Vima Kadphises, and Kanishka were prominent. Statues of royal family members were kept in the Mat region of this period. The Kushanas promoted a mixed culture, which can be understood through the various deities—Greek-Roman, Iranian, and Indian—depicted on their coins

questions.question_text: Which of the following are the representatives of the inland markets of Dakshinapatha mentioned in the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'?
questions.explanation: Both internal and external trade were at a peak during the Satavahana period. Information about commercial progress is obtained from the Periplus, Ptolemy's Geography, and Satavahana inscriptions and coins. Full protection was provided to trade and commerce by the rulers. There were many commercial cities within the country such as Paithan (Pratishthana), Tagar, Junnar, Nasik, Vaijayanti, Dhanyakataka, etc. The route from Golconda (Hyderabad), Tagar, and Paithan went to Bharuch. Bharuch was the main market of western India. Famous cities like Pratishthana, Tagar, Mathura, and Ujjayini also represented the inland markets of Dakshinapatha

questions.question_text: By which of the following was Buddha symbolized in Shunga art?
questions.explanation: In Shunga art, Buddha has been symbolized by the Umbrella, Footprints, Dharma Chakra, and Bodhi Tree. During the reign of the Shungas, many works were done for the decoration of Buddhist stupas. For example, those parts in the stupas of Bharhut and Sanchi, such as the railing etc., which were made of wood (were replaced or improved)

questions.question_text: In the exemptions (pariharas) received by the recipients of land grants in Satavahana inscriptions, which of the following is not mentioned?

options.A: Restriction on the entry of the army
options.B: Restriction on the administrative control of the king
options.C: Restriction on the mining of salt by royal employees

questions.explanation: During the Satavahana period, the exchange of land was done between Brahmins and Buddhists. Among the exemptions (pariharas) received by the recipients of Satavahana inscriptions, there is a mention of a restriction on the entry of the army, a restriction on the administrative control of the king, and a restriction on the mining of salt by royal employees, whereas there is no mention of a restriction on Vishti (forced labor)

questions.question_text: What was the exchange rate between Suvarna and Karshapana during the time of Nahapana in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Nahapana was the most famous ruler of the Kshaharata dynasty. His coins have been found from the region ranging from Ajmer to Nasik. These are of silver or copper. The coins are of a fixed standard. During his time, the exchange rate of gold and silver coins (Karshapana) was 1:35. In an inscription from Nasik, the value of 70,000 Karshapanas is given as 2000 Suvarna coins. On the coins, he holds the title of 'Rajan'. An inscription of Nahapana's minister Ayamas is found from Junnar (Pune).

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings claimed to end the practice of Varna-sankara (mixing of castes)?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Satavahana-era society was based on Varnasrama Dharma. Among the traditional four Varnas (Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra), the position of Brahmins was supreme. The Satavahana kings were Brahmins themselves. In the Nasik Prashasti, Gautamiputra is called a 'Unique Brahmin' (Aditiya Brahmana) who attempted to establish Varnasrama Dharma in society and stop Varna-sankara. At this time, many new castes were beginning to be organized on the basis of occupations.

questions.question_text: For which Kushana king has 'Maharajasya Rajatirajasya Devaputrasya Kaisarasya' been used in which of the following inscriptions?

options.A: Ara Stone Inscription of Kanishka II, year 41
options.B: Mathura Image Pedestal Inscription of Kanishka I, year 11
options.C: Mathura Image Pedestal Inscription of Kanishka I, year 23
options.D: Mathura Image Pedestal Inscription of Vasudeva, year 80

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–After Huvishka, Kanishka II (Kanishka Samvat 62 to 67) became the king. He is mentioned in the Ara Stone Inscription year 41. He was the son of Vashishka. It seems that he had ruled for some time along with Huvishka. In the Ara Stone Inscription year 41, the titles 'Maharaja', 'Rajadhiraja', 'Devaputra', and 'Kaisar' (Caesar) were adopted in imitation of the contemporary Roman kings. This is mentioned in the Ara Stone Inscription. "} Explanation– After Huvishka, Kanishka II (Kanishka-Era 62 to 67) became king. He is mentioned in the Ara Stone Inscription 41. He was the son of Vashishka. It seems that he had ruled together with Huvishka for some time. In the Ara Stone Inscription 41, he assumed titles like Maharaja, 'Rajadhiraja', 'Devaputra' and, following the contemporary Roman kings, 'Kaisar' (Caesar) etc., which is mentioned in the Ara Stone Inscription.

questions.question_text: On whose coins is the name of Goddess Uma inscribed among the following?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Although the practice of gold coins in North-West India was started by the Greek kings, the credit for making them regular and completely prevalent can be given to the Kushan kings. On the reverse side of the coins of Kushan ruler Huvishka, figures of various gods and goddesses and their names in the Greek language are engraved. Among Indian deities, besides Buddha and Shiva, depictions of Vishnu, Mahasena, Kumar, Vishakha, Uma, etc., are also found. Uma is shown with a lotus or cornucopia in her hand.

questions.question_text: Given below are two statements, one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): In the early centuries of the Christian era, India had maritime trade with the Roman Empire. Reason (R): Large numbers of Roman coins have been found from the excavations at Arikamedu. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following answers is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– Based on the Roman coins and other archaeological evidence found from Arikamedu, it is clear that Indo-Roman maritime trade was in its advanced state in the first centuries of the Christian era.

questions.question_text: Which of the following were the major ports of the Pandyas? Select the correct answer from the code given below: (i) Korkai (ii) Madurai (iii) Musiri (iv) Puhar Code:
questions.explanation: Among the kingdoms of South India, the Pandya kingdom was important from a commercial point of view. There were important commercial relations with surrounding kingdoms. Among the major ports here, Korkai and Madurai were ports of the Sangam-era Pandya kingdom. Musiri was a port of the Cheras, while Puhar was a port and maritime capital of the Cholas

questions.question_text: According to epigraphic statements, which of the following rulers respected all sects? (i) Ashoka (ii) Kanishka (iii) Kharavela (iv) Pushyamitra Shunga Code:
questions.explanation: According to his seventh pillar edict and 12th rock edict of Ashoka, and according to the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela, both these rulers respected all sects

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): Immediately after his accession, Maharaja Kharavela set out on a campaign of global conquest (Digvijaya). Reason (R): Upon knowing about Kharavela's achievements, the Indo-Greek ruler Demetrius of Eastern Punjab retreated to Mathura, from where he planned to challenge Kharavela. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: According to the Hathigumpha inscription: Kharavela attacked Gorathagiri in the eighth year of his coronation. Due to his terror, the Yavana king Demetrius fled to Mathura, but there is no mention that he had any plan to attack Kharavela

questions.question_text: The 'Kannagi' described in Sangam literature is—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– 'Kannagi' was the heroine of the Sangam literature Silappadikaram. Silappadikaram (The Story of the Anklet) was composed by Ilango Adigal. Ilango Adigal was the younger brother of the Chera ruler Senguttuvan. The plot is based on a popular story. "Kovalan, the son of a famous wealthy merchant of Puhar (Kaveripattinam), marries Kannagi, the daughter of another merchant. For some days, the married life of both passes happily. One day, in a royal palace ceremony, Kovalan meets a dancer named Madhavi. The dancer attracts Kovalan with her beauty and gestures, and he, getting caught in the bond of her love, not only forgets his beloved Kannagi and her sweet love, but also sacrifices his entire property for Madhavi's deceptive love. When Kovalan has nothing left, he realizes his mistake and returns to his beloved Kannagi again."

questions.question_text: Where was the third Tamil Sangam held?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Mention of three Sangams is found in Sangam literature, which were organized under the patronage of the Pandya kings. The third Sangam was established in Northern Madurai. There were 49 members in it, and 49 Pandya rulers provided patronage to it. It is said that 449 poets had presented their works before it for approval, and all had received administrative permission. Nakkeerar's name is mentioned as its chairman. Among the outstanding works related to the third Sangam, Nedunalvadai, Kuruntokai, Natrinai, Ainkurunuru, Padhirrupattu, Kalithogai, Paripadal, Vari, Perisai, and Sitrisai are noteworthy. Although most of the texts of the third Sangam are also lost, all the remaining ones are related to Tamil literature.

questions.question_text: Which dynasty issued the maximum number of copper coins?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The Kushan dynasty issued the maximum number of copper coins. This shows that the monetary economy had entered the rural areas as well. Only copper coins are found of Emperor Kujula Kadphises, the founder of the Kushan dynasty. Marshall found many of his coins from the excavation of Taxila; these are of two types. On the first type of coins, there is a mention of both the Greek king of Kabul, Hermaeus, and Kujula. The weight of the copper coins of Kujula Kadphises is about 30 grains. The coins of Vima Kadphises that are found weigh 270 grains. A standing figure of the king is made on these copper coins. He is offering an oblation at the altar. On his left side, a trident and Vima Kadphises are inscribed.

questions.question_text: Who had the image of Shakyamuni Buddha inscribed on his coins?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Numerous gold and copper coins of the Kushan ruler Kanishka have been obtained from various places in the North-West province, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Bengal, and Odisha. The gold coins are equal to Roman coins in weight (about 124 grains). On the reverse side of some coins of Kanishka, there is a figure of four-armed Shiva and 'Oesho' (Shiva) inscribed in the Greek language. There is a trident, drum, and goad in hand. On some coins, there is a Buddha statue in a standing posture with an aureole, and below it 'Boddo' (Buddha) is engraved in the Greek script, and some copper ones have been found on which the figure of the king is made in a sitting posture. Among these, four coins weigh 68 grains. Gardner has mentioned some bronze coins of Kanishka. On their obverse, there is a standing figure of the king and a Greek title inscribed. On the reverse, there are figures of Greek gods and goddesses.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List I A. Tirukkural B. Silappadikaram C. Manimekalai D. Tolkappiyam List II 1. Ilango Adigal 2. Sathanar 3. Tolkappiyar 4. Tiruvalluvar Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The Sangam text Tirukkural was composed by Tiruvalluvar. The Sangam era epic Silappadikaram was composed by Ilango Adigal. Ilango Adigal was the younger brother of the Chera ruler Senguttuvan and tradition has it that he had left home and became an ascetic out of fear of him. Manimekalai was composed by a grain merchant of Madurai, Sathanar (or Kulavanigan Sathanar). He was a Buddhist. Tolkappiyam was composed by Tolkappiyar. It was the oldest text of ancient Tamil literature. It was composed in sutra style. Along with grammar, it is also a high-quality text of poetics. This treatise is divided into three sections.

questions.question_text: What was the exchange rate between gold and Karshapana during the time of Nahapana?
