questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Nahapana was a ruler of the Kshaharata dynasty. His coins have been found from the area of Ajmer to Nasik. They are of silver and copper and the exchange rate between gold and Karshapana was 1:35. On the coins, he bears the title 'Rajan'. An inscription of Nahapana's minister Ayamon is found from Junnar (Pune). Cave inscriptions of his son-in-law Rishabhadatta (Ushavadata) have been found from Nasik and Karle (Pune). Rishabhadatta was the viceroy of Nahapana's southern province-Govardhana (Nasik) and Mamala (Pune). It is known from a cave inscription in Nasik that when people of the Uttamabhadra tribe of Rajasthan were surrounded by the Malavas, Rishabhadatta went there for their protection. He badly defeated the Malavas and after this gave donations at Pushkar Tirtha. From this, it seems that he gave donations at Pushkar Tirtha in Rajputana. From this, it seems that Nahapana also had influence over the Pushkar Tirtha (Ajmer) area of Rajputana.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ports were situated on the east coast of South India? 1. Kaveripattinam 2. Korkai 3. Musiri 4. Tondi Indicate the correct answer from the code below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- According to the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea', twenty-four ports from the mouth of the Indus to the mouth of Kanyakumari have been mentioned. The Chola era port Kaveripattinam (Puhar) and the capital of the Pandyas, Korkai, were ports situated on the eastern coast of South India. Naura (Cannanore), Tondi (Ponnani), Muziris (Musiri or Cranganore) and Nelcynda were famous ports of the western coast. It is said that in Muziris, "Roman and Arab ships used to bring Roman goods to exchange for Indian goods. Pliny writes that "the merchants who first came here traded with the Cheras without any conversation." A temple was also built for Augustus in Muziris. There was also a Yavana colony in Kaveripattinam. Greek merchants used to buy pearls obtained from the Gulf of Mannar and pearls obtained from the Palk Strait along with ordinary pearls from Tamralipti, Nelcynda and Muziris. The women of Rome had a great need for these pearls.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of the word 'Rudradamaka' found in the inscriptions of Western India?

options.A: A coin issued by a Shaka king

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The meaning of the word 'Rudradamaka' found in the inscriptions of Western India is a coin issued by a Shaka king. Information about their relations with the Shakas is obtained from the inscriptions of the Satavahana kings. In addition to the inscriptions, numerous coins of the Shaka kings have been obtained from a large part of Western and Northern India. From Kanishka's inscriptions, it is known that some Shaka-Kshatrapas and Mahakshatrapas ruled in some parts of the country under his subordination. Mention of the Shakas is found here and there in Indian literature as well. In the Ramayana and Mahabharata, the Shakas are mentioned along with foreign tribes like Yavanas, Pahlavas, etc. Katyayana and Patanjali were also familiar with the Shakas. In Manusmriti, we find mention of it along with Parada, Dravida, Pahlava, etc. The Shakas, Murundas, Yavanas, etc., tribes have also been mentioned in the Puranas.

questions.question_text: Where was the Kanishka Vihara, which Xuanzang had seen, located?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Kanishka's fame in Indian history is not because of his conquests but because of providing patronage to the religion of Shakya Muni. The story of Kanishka's initiation into Buddhism in North Buddhist traditions is similar to that of Ashoka. We get to know that he was extremely cruel and oppressive, who later became liberal and virtuous under the influence of Buddhism. But such descriptions of Buddhist writers are mostly imaginary. Based on Kanishka's coins and the Peshawar inscription, it seems that he had become a Buddhist in the early years of his reign. By building a famous Chaitya in Purushapura (Peshawar), he expressed his devotion to this religion. Xuanzang had visited the Kanishka Vihara located in Peshawar. Kanishka provided royal patronage to the Mahayana branch of Buddhism and had it propagated in Central Asia and China.

questions.question_text: Where are the Greco-Roman traders mentioned as Yavanas?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Greco-Roman traders are mentioned as Yavanas in Sangam literature. In Sangam literature, there is a description of Yavanas bringing gold in ships to India and taking away black pepper from here. In exchange, the Romans had established their commercial centers in South India. There is not much information related to the early history and culture of these kingdoms. But from around the first century AD, a lot of light starts to be shed on their history and culture through Tamil literature. The oldest literature of the Tamil language is known as Sangam literature. Sangam means a union or council. Sangam was a council of Tamil poets, scholars, teachers and astrologers and other intellectuals, which we can consider as a modern academy or council.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was not a Sangam era port?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Tagara was not a Sangam-era port while Arikamedu, Uraiyur and Korkai were Sangam-era ports. From the excavation of Arikamedu (Pondicherry), pieces of Roman island, glass bowls, gems, beads and vessels have been obtained. The picture of Roman Emperor Augustus is made on one bead. From this, it is known that in the first two centuries of the Christian era, there was a deep commercial relationship between India and Rome. Arikamedu was a famous commercial center where commercial goods from different parts of the country were collected and then sent to Rome from here. India also benefited from the commercial relations with Rome. As long as the commercial relationship with Rome continued, the Tamil kingdoms of the South remained prosperous. But when trade declined, the decline of these kingdoms also began. The anonymous author of 'Periplus' (1st century AD) provides a description of the close commercial relations between India and Rome. He mentions prosperous ports of the western coast like Naura, Musiri, Tondi, and Nelcynda.

questions.question_text: To which subject is the Sangam literature named 'Tolkappiyam' related?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Tolkappiyar, the chairman of the second Sangam which was held in Kapatapuram (Alaiwai), composed the literature named 'Tolkappiyam', whose subject was grammar. It was the oldest text of the Tamil language.

questions.question_text: Who established the first Tamil Sangam?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The first Sangam was organized in Madurai, the capital of the Pandyas, which was established by Rishi Agastya. Rishi Agastya is credited with the spread of Aryan culture in South India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following were epics in early Tamil literature?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The epics of early Tamil literature were Silappadikaram, Manimekalai, Jivaka Chintamani, Valayapathi and Kundalakesi.

questions.question_text: In the early period of Indian history, Tondi was a prosperous seaport of which of the following?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Tondi (modern Ponnani) was an important port for establishing commercial relations between India and the Roman Empire. Important information about this was given by the author of the Periplus (75 AD). Since only the Cheras ruled in the west of South India among the options of the above question, therefore its answer will be Chera.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code below - Assertion (A) : Arikamedu was a center of Indo-Roman trade. Reason (R) : Roman coins have been found in large numbers from the excavation of Arikamedu. Code :

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Arikamedu is situated about three kilometers south of Pondicherry. This city was an important center of trade and commerce with the western world and a center of Indo-Roman maritime trade in the early centuries of the Christian era. After the second century AD, it did not remain an active commercial center. From here, many Italian and Greek pottery remains and Roman coins have been found.

questions.question_text: The rulers of which of the following dynasties issued lead coins?
questions.explanation: Satavahana rulers were the first to issue lead coins for currency. Satavahana rulers used gold as a precious metal because they did not issue gold coins like the Kushans. Other coins of the Satavahanas were of potin, copper, and bronze

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers was influenced by the Buddhist monk Nagasena?
questions.explanation: Menander is famous in Buddhist literature by the name of Milinda. Nagasena had initiated Menander into Buddhism. Therefore, Menander was greatly influenced by Nagasena. The detailed dialogue between Buddhist monk Nagasena and Menander is compiled in the famous Buddhist text Milindapanho. Menander asks questions which Nagasena answers with great ease. Influenced by this, Menander adopted Buddhism

questions.question_text: The life-size standing statue obtained from Mathura is related to:
questions.explanation: The life-size standing statue obtained from Mathura is related to the Kushan period. In the Kushan period, two styles developed in the field of art: first, the Mathura art style; second, the Gandhara art style. The Mathura art style is the oldest style. The Gandhara art style developed the most in the Kushan period

questions.question_text: The depiction of Shiva in physical form along with his vehicle bull (Vrishabha) first appears on coins of:
questions.explanation: Huvishka was a ruler of the Kushan dynasty. On the coins of Huvishka, figures of deities like Shiva, Skanda, and Kumara etc., are found engraved. Among the Kushan rulers, Vima was a Shaiva, Kanishka and Huvishka were Buddhists and Vasudeva was a Shaiva follower

questions.question_text: In which of the following languages is Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription engraved?
questions.explanation: Kharavela was the ruler of Kalinga. Kharavela had the Hathigumpha inscription written in Kalinga, whose language was Prakrit. This inscription is inscribed on the Udayagiri hill in which the date is not mentioned. According to the inscription, Kharavela was from the Mahameghavahana dynasty

questions.question_text: From which place were bird figurines of the Shunga era obtained?
questions.explanation: The Bharhut stupa was discovered in 1873 by Mr. Cunningham. Its railing and torana (gateway) are of the Shunga period. Bird figurines of the Shunga era are depicted on this stupa; in addition, statues of Yaksha-Yakshini and the scene of a woman embracing a tree are also prominent images

questions.question_text: The ancient trade route 'Dakshinapatha' extended -
questions.explanation: The Dakshinapatha trade route was one of the 2 great highways that connected different parts of the sub-continent after the Iron Age. The ancient trade route Dakshinapatha used to go from Pataliputra to Pratishthana

questions.question_text: Which of the following Gupta rulers issued archer type coins?
questions.explanation: The credit for formally introducing currency in the Gupta period is given to Samudragupta by historians. Samudragupta introduced 6 types of gold coins, among which the archer type was prominent. On these coins, the inscription of his titles 'Apratiratha' and 'Samudra' is found. Chandragupta II Vikramaditya introduced 5 types of gold coins, in which the archer type was the most numerous. On his coins, the inscriptions 'Shri Vikram', Garuda standard, and 'Devashri Maharajadhiraja' are found. In the coins of Kumaragupta, types such as archer, Ashvamedha, Kartikeya, etc., are found. On his coins, the figure of a peacock is found instead of Garuda. Skandagupta introduced 4 types of gold coins, in which the archer and King-Lakshmi types are prominent

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II List-I (I) Rashtrakuta
questions.explanation: The correct match is List-I (Ruler) 1. Mahendrapala - Gurjara-Pratihara 2. Nanuka - Chandela 3. Vakpatiraja - Paramara 4. Govinda - Rashtrakuta

questions.question_text: Which of the following dynasties link their origin to the demon Naraka?
questions.explanation: The Varman dynasty of Assam links its origin to the demon Naraka. In the Mahabharata, there is a description of the ruler Narakasura being killed by Shri Krishna. Kalidasa, in the Raghuvamsha, mentions Raghu's victory over the ruler of Pragjyotishpur (Kamrupa). After the Guptas, the Varman dynasty ruled here, whose famous ruler Bhaskaravarman was a friend and ally of Harsha The Bhanja rulers of Odisha state their origin from a peahen's egg and call themselves 'Andajavansha Prabhava' (born from an egg). The founder of the Pala dynasty of Bengal was a person named Gopala. Major rulers of the Pala dynasty included Dharmapala, Devapala, and Vigrahapala. In the latter half of the sixth century, the Shailodbhava dynasty originated in the Kongoda region of Odisha (modern Puri and Ganjam districts). Most of the rulers of this dynasty are referred to as 'Parama-Maheshvara' in their inscriptions.

questions.question_text: In whose inscriptions is the mention of two posts, Sachiva and Mantri, for state officials found?
questions.explanation: The mention of two posts, Sachiva and Mantri, for state officials is found in the inscriptions of the rulers of the Gupta period. The king was the central point of the Gupta administration. Gupta rulers adopted titles like Maharajadhiraja and Paramabhattaraka. There was a council of ministers (Mantriparishad) to assist the king, most of whose members belonged to the high class. These were called Amatyas. The post of ministers was mostly hereditary. A single minister held many departments. For example - Harishena held three posts: Sandhivigrahika, Kumaramatya, and Mahadandanayaka

questions.question_text: What was the purpose of Xuanzang's visit to India?

options.A: To know the geography of India
options.B: To visit places related to Buddha
options.C: To know the culture of India

questions.explanation: The most prominent event of Harsha's time is the arrival of the Chinese traveler Xuanzang (Yuan Chwang) to India. Xuanzang was born around 600 AD in a place called Chen-Liu in the Henan province of China. Religious books were very dear to him. His great desire was to see the places sanctified by the footprints of Lord Buddha and to study the holy Buddhist texts in their original language, which were easily available in India in those days. To fulfill this objective, he departed from Chang'an, the capital of the Tang rulers, for India in 629 AD TGT PGT History Planner | 183 | YCT

questions.question_text: In which chapter of 'Harshacharita' is the description of various religious sects living in the forests of Vindhya found?
questions.explanation: The author of Harshacharita is Banabhatta, who was the court poet of Harsha. This was the first successful attempt at writing prose poetry on historical subjects. It contains eight Uchchhvasas (chapters). In the first three, Bana has written his autobiography and in the remaining five, he has written the biography of Harshavardhana. A description of various religious sects living in the forests of Vindhya is found in the eighth chapter of 'Harshacharita'

questions.question_text: From which region did the Guptas obtain iron ore?
questions.explanation: The Guptas are considered feudatories of the Kushans. It is believed that they were originally Vaishyas. They (Guptas) ruled over the fertile parts of the Madhyadesha such as – the middle Ganga basin, Saket (modern Ayodhya) and Magadha. Gupta rulers easily exploited the iron ore reserves of Central India and South Bihar

questions.question_text: After escaping from imprisonment, in which area did Harshavardhana's sister Rajyashri enter?
questions.explanation: Harshavardhana became the ruler of Thanesar in 606 AD. After ascending the throne, his first task was to take revenge on his brother's killer Shashanka and to free his sister Rajyashri from his imprisonment. Meanwhile, Harsha's cousin Bhandi informed him that Rajyashri had escaped from prison and fled into the forests and mountains of Vindhya. With the help of a Buddhist monk Divakaramitra, Harsha found Rajyashri in the forests of Vindhya just as she was going to commit Sati

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings died on the battlefield?
questions.explanation: The ruler of Kannauj, Yashovarman, died on the battlefield. Actually, the history of Kannauj for about 50 years after the death of Harshavardhana is in darkness. After this, Yashovarman's war for the throne of Kannauj took place with Lalitaditya Muktapida of Kashmir, in which he probably died. The great Sanskrit dramatist Bhavabhuti lived in Yashovarman's court. Yashovarman's court poet Vakpati described his victories in the poem 'Gaudavaho' written in the Prakrit language

questions.question_text: Paramartha was a Buddhist scholar of which period?
questions.explanation: Paramartha was a resident of Ujjain. In 546 AD, during the time of a Gupta dynasty emperor, he was part of the Indian diplomatic mission sent in exchange for the embassy sent by the Emperor of China to India. The works written by Paramartha and translated into the Chinese language also include the Tripitaka

questions.question_text: The Gupta period 'Bower' manuscript is related to-
questions.explanation: The Bower manuscript is an important discovery related to the oldest medical knowledge of the 4th and 5th centuries AD, Ayurveda, reading of omens, and prophecy. It was discovered by Hamilton Bower in 1890 from the Gobi Desert. It is essentially a collection of 7 treatises by a Buddhist monk named Yashomitra. These Buddhist monks resided in the Kamatura Buddhist Vihara

questions.question_text: In which inscription is 'Harichandra', the first man of the Gurjara Pratihara dynasty, mentioned?
questions.explanation: The first man of the Gurjara Pratihara dynasty, Harichandra, is mentioned in the Jodhpur inscription of Bauka. Although the genealogy of the Pratiharas is also found in the Gwalior Prashasti of Mihir Bhoja, the Gwalior Prashasti starts with Nagabhata I. Harichandra is not mentioned in this inscription. In the Gwalior inscription, the Pratihara dynasty is called the descendant of Lakshmana, the brother of Rama, and pure Kshatriyas

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Ramacharita', the historical biography of Pala ruler Ramapala?
questions.explanation: Sandhyakar Nandi composed the historical biography 'Ramacharita' of the Pala ruler Ramapala. In this text, Sandhyakar Nandi has called himself the Valmiki of Kali Yuga (Kalikal Valmiki) and Ramapala as Rama. This text is an example of a text written in a double-meaning (Shlesha) style. In Ramacharita, there is a mention of defeating Bhima, the leader of the Kaivartas. It is noteworthy here that Sandhyakar Nandi's father Prajapati Nandi had been the Sandhivigrahika of Ramapala

questions.question_text: Vikramshila Mahavihara in Eastern India was the main center for which Buddhist sect?
questions.explanation: The Vikramshila Mahavihara was established by the Pala ruler Dharmapala and it developed during the time of Devapala. There were 6 colleges here and 108 teachers were appointed in each college. The central hall of the college was called Vijnana Bhavan. This university was basically specially prestigious for education in the Vajrayana sect of Buddhism. The most famous Vice-Chancellor here was Dipankara Srijnana Atisha

questions.question_text: On which Gupta ruler's coin is 'Chamaradharini' depicted?
questions.explanation: The depiction of 'Chamaradharini' (fly-whisk bearer) is found on the coins of Gupta rulers. Among the Gupta rulers, the depiction of 'Chamaradharini' is found on the coins of both Samudragupta and Kumaragupta I. Samudragupta issued a total of 6 types of gold coins, among which the Garuda standard coin was the most popular. Similarly, Kumaragupta issued a maximum of 14 types of gold coins, among which Apratigha and Mayur-Kartikeya types were his new coins

questions.question_text: Harshacharita is divided into chapters which are called-
questions.explanation: There are a total of 8 chapters in Harshacharita which are called 'Uchchhvasa'. The autobiography of Bana is written in the first 3 Uchchhvasas. In the fourth Uchchhvasa, Harsha's childhood and Rajyashri's marriage are described, and in the fifth, the death of Prabhakarvardhana is described. In the sixth Uchchhvasa, the death of Rajyavardhana and Harsha's vow are described, in the 7th, Harsha's conquest journey is described, and in the 8th Uchchhvasa, the account of the search for Rajyashri is given

questions.question_text: Who was the Vice-Chancellor (Kulapati) of Nalanda Mahavihara in ancient times?
questions.explanation: As a center of education, the Nalanda Buddhist Vihara was established by Kumaragupta in 450 AD. Xuanzang himself stayed in Nalanda for 18 months and studied Yogasastra. The most famous Vice-Chancellor of Nalanda University was Shilabhadra, who was the Vice-Chancellor of that university during the time of Xuanzang. Shilabhadra was the only Acharya who was a knower of all collections. Study of medical science was mandatory in Nalanda University

questions.question_text: The author of the book 'Svapnavasavadattam' was:
questions.explanation: The most discussed play of the renowned Sanskrit dramatist Mahakavi Bhasa is Svapnavasavadattam, in which the story of an inseparable love is described. Mahakavi Kalidasa has mentioned his name in his works. This proves that Mahakavi Bhasa is considered to be a poet before Kalidasa or before the Gupta period. His following works include Pratima Nataka, Pancharatra, Karnabhara, Urubhanga, Avimaraka, etc

questions.question_text: During the reign of which Pratihara ruler was the famous text "Kuvalayamala" composed?
questions.explanation: After the death of Nagabhata I, his son Vatsaraja became the next ruler. He defeated the Bhandi dynasty and also defeated the Pala ruler Dharmapala of Bengal. Nagabhata II was born to Vatsaraja's queen Sundari Devi, who is called Nagavaloka. During his time, Udyotana Suri composed Kuvalayamala and the Jain Acharya Jinasena composed Harivansha Purana

questions.question_text: Under which of these medieval states were provinces divided into 'Bhukti, Pradesh, and Bhoga'?
questions.explanation: During the Gupta administration, the provincial administration was divided into Bhuktis and each Bhukti had many Vishayas. We can call Bhukti similar to a modern-day commissionary. Bhoga- In the Mauryan period, the Bhoga tax was called the toll tax which later came to be called Bhoga tax in the Gupta empire. Provinces were called Bhukti, Desha or Avani. The ruler of a Bhukti was called Uparika, who was appointed by the emperor

questions.question_text: Given below are two statements. One is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Pulakeshin-II defeated Harshavardhana. Reason (R): He wanted to expand his kingdom in Northern India. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Harsha attacked Vallabhi (Saurashtra) for the expansion of his empire in the South, which became the cause of the war between Harsha and Pulakeshin II. Harsha's empire extended up to the banks of the Narmada in the South. Pulakeshin II of the Vatapi Chalukyas defeated Harshavardhana in a battle on the banks of the Narmada river. This fact was described by Ravikirti in the Aihole inscription in 634 AD

questions.question_text: Match the following: Gupta Period Administrative Responsibility Officer A. Dandapashika (i) Commander-in-chief B. Mahapratihara (ii) Royal Palace Security C. Mahakshapatalika (iii) Land Revenue Officer D. Mahabaladhikrita (iv) Police Code:
questions.explanation: Details of Gupta period administrative officers – Dandapashika – Chief officer of the police department. Mahapratihara – Was the chief of the royal palace guards. Mahakshapatalika – Officer who maintained the records of income and expenditure. Mahabaladhikrita – Supreme officer of the army or Commander-in-chief. TGT PGT History Planner | 185 | YCT

questions.question_text: In Harsha's administration, there was an officer named 'Sthapita'.

options.A: A spy who roams at night
options.B: Inspector of the employees of the harem (Ranivas)
options.C: Inspector who brought visitors to the king's assembly

questions.explanation: In Harsha's administration, the officer named Sthapita inspected the employees appointed in the harem. The officer named Dibira was a scribe of the Amatya class

questions.question_text: In which inscription does the name of the Gupta dynasty ruler Ramagupta appear?

options.C: Sanjan Copper Plate Inscription of Amoghavarsha

questions.explanation: After the death of Govinda III, his son Amoghavarsha I ascended the Rashtrakuta throne. At that time, his age was 7 years. He was a generous patron of knowledge and art. He himself was a scholar and also a patron of scholars. In the Sanjan Copper Plate, he was described as even greater than the Gupta ruler 'Sahasanka' (Chandragupta II) as a patron of knowledge and literature. There is also a mention of the Gupta dynasty ruler Ramagupta in the Sanjan Copper Plate inscription. Amoghavarsha wrote a book named Kavirajamarga in Kannada which is one of the early works of Kannada literature and composed Prashnottara Ratnamalika (an ethical text written in Sanskrit)

questions.question_text: From whom among the following did the Guptas learn to wear trousers?
questions.explanation: After the fall of the Kushans, the Gupta dynasty emerged in Magadha. The Guptas were probably feudatories of the Kushans. Kushan remains have been found after Gupta remains at many places in present-day Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. It is possible that the Guptas learned the use of the saddle, bridle, buttoned coats, trousers, and shoes from the Kushans

questions.question_text: After Prabhakarvardhana's death, on the banks of which river did his wife commit self-immolation?
questions.explanation: A systematic and detailed history of the Vardhanas of Thanesar is found from the time of Prabhakarvardhana. In fact, he was the founder of the independence of this dynasty. Prabhakarvardhana was a powerful king. To indicate his independent status, he adopted honorable titles like 'Paramabhattaraka' and 'Maharajadhiraja'. Prabhakarvardhana had many queens. Among them, Yashomati was his chief queen (Agra-mahishi). After fighting the Hunas, Prabhakarvardhana became seriously ill and died, and Queen Yashomati committed self-immolation by jumping into a pyre on the banks of the Saraswati river

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the play 'Devi Chandraguptam'?
questions.explanation: Devi Chandraguptam is a Sanskrit play composed by Vishakhadatta. The plot of this play is related to the reign of Ramagupta, the elder brother of Chandragupta II. In this play, there is a description of the killing of the Shaka king and Ramagupta by Chandragupta II and his marriage with Dhruvadevi

questions.question_text: When Xuanzang was returning to his country, who was given the task of being his route-protector to the border?
questions.explanation: Xuanzang was a Chinese traveler who came to India in the seventh century AD to collect Buddhist texts and stayed in this country for about 15 years. He compiled his travel memoirs in the form of a book named 'Si-Yu-Ki'. According to Watters, he was the "Yin-tu" of India, "Shakyamuni", and the "Prince of Pilgrims". When Xuanzang was returning to his country, Udhita was entrusted with the responsibility of being his route-protector to the border

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched? (Inscription) (Related)

options.C: Udayagiri Cave Inscription - Minister Virasena Shaaba

questions.explanation: Bilsad is located in Etah district of Uttar Pradesh. An inscription of Gupta ruler Kumaragupta has been obtained from here. In this inscription, there is a description of the construction of a temple of Lord Kartikeya by a Brahmin named Dhruvasarma. The remaining options are true and these inscriptions were written during the time of Chandragupta II. 'Amrakardava' was the chief commander of Chandragupta II, while Minister Virasena Shaaba and Feudatory Sanakanika were respectively the Chief Secretary and the Governor of Eastern Malwa

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the text named "Namalinganushasana"?
questions.explanation: The text Amarakosha composed by Amarasimha is called the 'Encyclopedia of Sanskrit'. Another name for this text is 'Linganu-shasana'. Because it is divided into three sections (Kandas), it is also called 'Trikanda'. The most famous commentator of Amarakosha is Kshirasvamibhatta. Among ancient Indian texts, the maximum number of commentaries (50) has been written on this text

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists: List-I (Ruler)
questions.explanation: The correct matching of List-I and List-II is as follows– List-I List-II (A) Chandragupta I 1. Kumaradevi (B) Samudragupta 2. Datta Devi (C) Chandragupta II 3. Kuberanaga (D) Kumaragupta 4. Ananta Devi Chandragupta–I

questions.question_text: Which Gupta emperor has been described as 'Maharajadhiraja'?
questions.explanation: The first king of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta I, who made his state fully independent and adopted the title of 'Maharajadhiraja'. He is considered the real founder of the Gupta dynasty. Chandragupta I is also credited in history for the introduction of a new era which in later writings was called the Gupta Era (Samvat), and according to Fleet's calculation, this era was started in 319-20 AD

questions.question_text: Who is the oldest historical astronomer in India?
questions.explanation: Aryabhatta was the oldest historical astronomer in India. In the 5th century, he was the first to state that the Earth is round and rotates on its axis

questions.question_text: During the reign of the Guptas, which of the following officers kept land-related documents safely?
questions.explanation: In the revenue system of the Gupta period, the Dhruvadhikarana was responsible for land tax collection, and officials named Mahakshapatalika and Karanika were responsible for keeping land records safely

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not result in any way on foreign trade after the Gupta age?

options.B: Lack of coins for common use
options.C: Stagnation in the movement of artisans and traders from one corner of the country to another
options.D: Many crafts had been completely destroyed

questions.explanation: After the Gupta period, crafts were not completely destroyed. During this period, the textile industry was in an excellent state, which is described by Xuanzang, who mentions various types of silk and cotton garments

questions.question_text: In the Gupta period, the largest center of maritime trade from Eastern India was–
questions.explanation: During the Gupta period, the largest center of maritime trade from Eastern India was the port of Tamralipti located in Bengal. From here, trade was conducted with countries like China, Lanka, Java, Sumatra (South East Asia), etc

questions.question_text: In the Gupta period, the word 'Vishti' was used for
questions.explanation: In the Gupta period, 'Vishti' was used for forced labor. In this period, the highest officers were Kumaramatyas

questions.question_text: Hiranya tax was
questions.explanation: 'Hiranya tax' was a tax of the Gupta period. This tax was the amount received in the form of cash taken by the king in exchange for agricultural products

questions.question_text: Which Gupta king was also known as Devagupta?
questions.explanation: The Gupta ruler Chandragupta II was known by names like Devagupta, Devaraja, and Devasri. Samudragupta was a poet, musician, and patron of learning. That is why he was called Kaviraja. During the reign of Kumaragupta, Nalanda University was established and evidence of Ashvamedha Yajna is found on his coins

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the largest hoard of Gupta period coins?
questions.explanation: The largest hoard of Gupta period coins has been found from Bayana (Rajasthan). A large pile of gold coins was obtained from Bayana in 1821 AD

questions.question_text: The name of the Gupta gold coin 'Dinar' is taken from which language?
questions.explanation: The name of the Gupta gold coin 'Dinar' is taken from the Latin language

questions.question_text: Which of the following temples is not in Khajuraho?
questions.explanation: The Dashavatara Temple is located in Deogarh, Uttar Pradesh, and is a temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu. It was built during the Gupta period. This temple belongs to the Panchayatana category of the Nagara style. The first mention of a shikhara (spire) is found in this very temple

questions.question_text: Who was the administrator of 'Bhukti' in the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: In the Gupta period, from the perspective of administrative convenience, the state was divided into various provinces. These provinces were called 'Bhukti'. They were also called Pradesh or Bhoga. The administrator of the 'Bhukti' was mainly called Uparika, whose appointment was made by the emperor. This administrator was also called Gopta, Bhogapati, and Sthaniya. Their chief advisor was the Kumaramatya

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to Gupta period coins: (1) They are made of gold and silver (2) The dates of the rulers are available in numerals on them Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Coins of the Gupta period rulers are found in three metals: gold, silver, and copper. Numerical dates are found on silver coins. Since the word 'un' (they/them) in the option refers to gold and silver, therefore, option (a) will be correct

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Ruler) with List-II (Inscription) and give the correct answer from the codes provided – List-I (Ruler) List-II (Inscription)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – The correct match is – List-I (Ruler) List-II (Inscription) (a) Kumaragupta-I (I) Bilsad Inscription (b) Kumaragupta-II (II) Sarnath Inscription (c) Budhagupta (III) Eran Inscription (d) Parantaka-II (IV) Uttiramerur Inscription

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Mudrarakshasa'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation—Unprecedented progress took place in the fields of literature and science during the Gupta era. Vishakhadatta was a very famous playwright of this period who composed plays named Mudrarakshasa and Devi Chandraguptam in the Sanskrit language. Both these books are full of political events.

questions.question_text: "The Moon revolves around the Earth and the Earth revolves around the Sun." Which scholar proved this–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation–Varahamihira was a famous astronomer and his famous book is Brihat Samhita. The above description is in that book, whereas Aryabhatta discovered that the Earth is round and revolves around the Sun and there is gravity in the Earth. Brahmagupta was also a famous astronomer.

questions.question_text: Why is the Gupta period called the 'Classic Age'?

options.A: Due to progress in commerce and trade
options.B: Due to progress in art and literature

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The Gupta period is called the 'Classical Age' due to the progress of literature, science, and art. Sanskrit was installed as the state language and unprecedented development of Sanskrit literature took place. Proper development of various aspects of art—architecture, sculpture, painting, etc.—occurred. It was in the Gupta period that world-famous mathematicians and astronomers like Aryabhatta and Varahamihira lived.

questions.question_text: Which caves of Ajanta were built in the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation—Caves 16, 17, and 19 of Ajanta belong to the Gupta period. The construction of these caves was done from the 2nd century BC to the 7th century AD.

questions.question_text: Coins of Gupta rulers included in the Bayana hoard:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation- Bayana is located in Bharatpur district of Rajasthan. Gupta coins have been found here in abundance. Among the coins found from the time of Gupta ruler Chandragupta-I to the time of Skandagupta, the maximum number of coins belong to the time of Chandragupta-II, while only one coin from the time of Skandagupta has been obtained from here.

questions.question_text: On which of the following regions did Chandragupta-I not rule?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Chandragupta-I was the third and the first great ruler of the Gupta dynasty, who ruled over states like Prayag, Saket, and Magadha, leaving out Vaishali. It is known that Chandragupta I adopted the title of Maharajadhiraja and Chandragupta is considered the founder of the Gupta Era (319 AD).

questions.question_text: In the temple architecture of which period do the figures of Ganga and Yamuna first appear?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – The complete development of temples in India is found from the Gupta period. Many temples were built at this time, among which the temples of Sanchi, Eran, Tigawa, etc. are famous. Figures of Makarvahini Ganga and Kurmavahini Yamuna are found carved on the doorframes at the entrance of the sanctum sanctorum, which is a specialty of the Gupta period.

questions.question_text: Who was not a Gupta ruler?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation—The rise of the Gupta dynasty took place in Kaushambi near Prayag at the end of the third century. The founder of the Gupta dynasty, Srigupta, ruled from (240-280 AD). Other rulers of this dynasty in order are—Ghatotkacha (280-319 AD), Chandragupta I (319-350 AD), Samudragupta (350-375 AD), Chandragupta II (375-415 AD), Kumaragupta I or Govindagupta (415-455 AD), Skandagupta (455-467 AD), and the last Gupta ruler was Bhanugupta.

questions.question_text: Where is the Gupta period Dashavatara Temple established?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– The Gupta period Dashavatara temple is at a place named Deogarh in Lalitpur district (ancient Jhansi) of U.P. This temple is considered an excellent example of Gupta period architecture. Deogarh is situated on the banks of the Betwa river. The time of this temple is considered to be the 4th-5th century AD.

questions.question_text: Which era is called the 'Classical Age'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2010 Explanation—The reign of the Gupta kings represents the most glorious era of ancient Indian history. In fact, at this time, unprecedented progress took place in every field of civilization and culture. Seeing the all-round progress of the Gupta era, scholars designated the Gupta period as the 'Golden Age' or 'Classical Age' of Hindu culture. The Gupta kings ruled from 275 AD to 550 AD. This era is also called the Periclean Age of India.

questions.question_text: What was Bhukti in the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation– For administrative convenience, the Gupta Empire was divided in the form of Bhukti, which was similar to modern-day provinces. The division of Bhukti was into many districts which were called Vishaya. The division of Vishayas was into tehsils which were called Vithi. The smallest unit was Gram (village), whose administration was run by the Gram Sabha or Gramika.

questions.question_text: Who is considered the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – We have many inscriptions to introduce the Gupta genealogy, among which the most prominent are Samudragupta's Prayag Prashasti inscription, Kumaragupta's Bilsad inscription, and Skandagupta's Bhitari pillar inscription. Based on these inscriptional evidences, it appears that the founder and first ruler of the Gupta dynasty was Srigupta.

questions.question_text: The first inscription mentioning the practice of Sati was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The first inscriptional evidence of the practice of Sati is found in the Eran inscription, which mentions the Sati of the wife of a general named Gopraja. This inscription is from 510 AD.

questions.question_text: By what name were the provincial governors known in the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- In the Gupta period, for administrative convenience, the empire was divided into many provinces. A province was called Desha, Avani, or Bhukti. The major provinces of the Gupta administration were Saurashtra, Western Malwa (Avanti), Eastern Malwa (Eran), Tirabhukti, Pundravardhana, Magadha, etc. The ruler of a Bhukti was called Uparika, whose appointment was made by the emperor, and he was responsible only to the emperor. The rulers of the border regions were called Gopta, whose appointment the emperor made after considerable thought. The post of Uparika was often given to princes or persons related to the royal family. Chandragupta II's younger son Govindagupta was the governor of Tirabhukti (modern Darbhanga) and Kumaragupta I's son Ghatotkacha Gupta was the governor of Eastern Malwa. The Vishayapati has also been called 'Kumaramatya'.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists- List I List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 PGT History, 2005 Explanation- The most important event of the reign of Chandragupta I was the establishment of matrimonial relations between the Guptas and the Lichchhavis. Chandragupta I was a far-sighted emperor; he obtained the cooperation and support of the Lichchhavis and married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi. Chandragupta I was the first in the Gupta dynasty to introduce silver coins. On the obverse of the said coins, figures of Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi are inscribed along with their names. To gain the support of the Nagavanshi rulers, Chandragupta II married the Naga princess Kuberanaga. Kumaragupta I had established matrimonial relations with Mahadevi Anantadevi. The people of the Kadamba dynasty ruled in Kuntala (Karnataka). It is known from the Talagunda inscription that Kakusthavarman, a ruler of this dynasty, married one of his daughters to a Gupta prince. It is estimated that the son of Chandragupta, Kumaragupta I, was married into the Kadamba dynasty. Samudragupta

questions.question_text: Who first got metrical legends inscribed on his coins?
questions.explanation: Gupta rulers first started getting metrical legends inscribed on their coins. Among the Gupta rulers, Samudragupta was the first ruler whose coins are found with metrical legends inscribed. In ancient Indian history, the Gupta rulers issued the maximum number of gold coins. It is noteworthy here that Gupta gold coins were heavier in weight and standard than Kushan gold coins, but the amount of gold in Gupta gold coins was less compared to the Kushans

questions.question_text: Who introduced copper currency in the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: Samudragupta introduced copper currency in the Gupta period. Gupta rulers issued gold, silver, and copper coins. The gold coins of the Guptas were called Dinars. Among the Gupta rulers, Chandragupta II was the first to issue silver coins to commemorate his victory over the Shakas, which were approximately 26.3 grains to 32 grains in accordance with the Shaka standard. Samudragupta first (in the Gupta period) introduced copper currency

questions.question_text: Who among the following was a poet and musician who felt pleasure in the pseudonym 'Kaviraja' or 'King of Poets'?
questions.explanation: The successor of Chandragupta I was his son Samudragupta. In Indian history, Samudragupta is counted as a great conqueror and a talented emperor. A new awakening of Indian civilization and culture took place. He is placed in the category of a poet and musician, which is why he is also known by the pseudonym Kaviraja or King of Poets of the Gupta period

questions.question_text: According to numismatic knowledge about the Gupta period, which of the following rulers has been shown playing the Veena on some gold coins?
questions.explanation: Samudragupta introduced 6 types of gold coins 1- Standard-bearer or Staff-bearer or Garuda type coins 2- Archer type coins 3- Battle-axe type coins 4- Ashvamedha type coins 5- Tiger-slayer type coins 6- Lyrist (Veena playing) type coins

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not mentioned in the Prayag-Prashasti?

options.A: Chandragupta I had not nominated Samudragupta as his successor.
options.B: The goal of the world conquest (Digvijaya) was 'Dharani-bandha' (binding the earth).
options.C: It contains a mention of the victories of Aryavarta.
options.D: Devarashtra is mentioned in the Dakshinapatha victories of Samudragupta.

questions.explanation: The composer of Prayag Prashasti is Harishena. It describes the prowess of Samudragupta. In this, the victory of Aryavarta, the southern victory, the victory of border states, etc., of Samudragupta are mentioned

questions.question_text: The contemporary king of Sri Lanka of Samudragupta was:
questions.explanation: The contemporary king of Lanka of Samudragupta was Meghavarna. It is known from Chinese sources that he sent an embassy with gifts to Samudragupta. With the permission of Samudragupta, he built a magnificent vihara for the Buddhist monks of Lanka to the north of the Bodhi tree

questions.question_text: According to 'Prayag Prashasti', what kind of relations did the Gupta ruler Samudragupta have with the border kings?
questions.explanation: Details of Samudragupta's strategic victories are found in Harishena's panegyric poem (Prayag Prashasti). It also contains the account of Chandragupta I choosing him as his successor. Samudragupta defeated nine rulers of Aryavarta (India). Republican states tried to satisfy his fierce rule through payment of all taxes, obeying orders, and attendance

questions.question_text: The Prayag Prashasti in the Allahabad Pillar inscription is a panegyric for Samudragupta, whose composer was his court poet—
questions.explanation: DSSSB PGT 10/07/2021 TGT History, 2004 PGT History, 2005, 2009 Explanation–Harishena, the minister and court poet of Samudragupta, wrote an inscription in praise of Samudragupta on the Ashoka pillar located in Allahabad. It is written in Brahmi script and Sanskrit language. It is a beautiful example of the Sanskrit Champu style. This inscription mentions Samudragupta's victories.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Prayag Inscription 1. Kumaragupta B. Bilsad 2. Chandragupta II C. Bhitari 3. Samudragupta D. Mehrauli 4. Skandagupta A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct match is Prayag Inscription — Samudragupta Bilsad — Kumaragupta I Bhitari — Skandagupta Mehrauli — Chandragupta II

questions.question_text: Which of the following temples is known as a representative example of Gupta temple architecture?
questions.explanation: The Gupta period is called the Golden Age of ancient India because of its temple architecture and sculpture. The major temples here are the Krishna temple of Bhitargaon, the Laxman temple of Sirpur, and the Dashavatara temple of Deogarh. The Dashavatara temple is located in Lalitpur, Uttar Pradesh. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. The Gajendramoksha, Nara-Narayana penance, and Anantashayi Vishnu panels made along with the walls of this temple show scenes from Vishnu Purana. It is also considered a representative example of architecture

questions.question_text: Write the states of Dakshinapatha conquered by Samudragupta mentioned in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription in order:
questions.explanation: Samudragupta was the successor of Chandragupta I. He defeated 12-12 rulers of Aryavarta and Dakshinavarta respectively. Because of these victories, historian Vincent Smith called him the "Napoleon of India." Samudragupta defeated three major powers of North India (Achyuta, Nagasena, and Kotakulaja rulers). The total 12 conquered states in Dakshinapatha were: Kaurala, Mahakantara, Kosala, Pishtapura, Kottura, Erandapalla, Kanchi, Avamukta, Vengi, Palakka, Devarashtra, Kusthalapura

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler of Kanchi during the reign of Samudragupta?
questions.explanation: After Chandragupta I, his son Samudragupta became the ruler; during his time, the Gupta Empire expanded the most. He defeated a group of twelve states of Dakshinapatha, whose main leader was Vishnugopa, who was the king of Kanchi. Raychaudhuri designated Samudragupta's Dakshinapatha victory as 'Dharmavijaya'. Harishena was the court poet of Samudragupta

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Samudragupta? Use the code: (i) He was a conqueror, a poet, and a musician. (ii) He was called Lichchhavi-dauhitra. (iii) He copied the coins of the Western Kshatrapas. (iv) There is no mention of his Ashvamedha in the Allahabad pillar inscription. Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation–According to the coins and inscriptions of Samudragupta, he was a poet and musician as well as a warrior. He is shown playing the Veena on coins. In inscriptions, he has also been called 'Lichchhavi dauhitra' because of being born to the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi. Along with this, there is no mention of the organization of any Ashvamedha in the Prayag Prashasti. Chandragupta II copied the silver coins of the Western Kshatrapas.

questions.question_text: Who was the imperial ruler of the mid-4th century AD?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation–In the middle of the 4th century AD, between 350-375 AD, the Gupta ruler Samudragupta was ruling. Samudragupta is called the Napoleon of India. He had defeated the states of Aryavarta and the South. Mention of this is found in Harishena's Prayag Pillar Inscription.

questions.question_text: In which of the following Gupta inscriptions is Chandragupta II described as 'Rajadhirajarsi'?

options.A: Udayagiri cave inscription of Chandragupta II
options.B: Mathura stone inscription of Chandragupta II
options.D: Bilsad stone inscription of Kumaragupta I

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) KVS TGT 2018 Explanation– Chandragupta II has been described as 'Rajadhirajarsi' in the Udayagiri cave inscription of Chandragupta II. It is known that another name of Chandragupta was Devaraja or Devagupta. He had assumed titles like Vikramanka, Vikramaditya, Paramabhagavata, Deva Shri, etc. During his period, the Gupta state reached the pinnacle of progress. The Chinese traveler Faxian came to India during his period.

questions.question_text: The 6th-century astronomer Varahamihira belonged to which part of the country?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation–The 6th-century astronomer Varahamihira belonged to the Western Malwa of the country. The renowned astrologer Varahamihira was one of the greatest personalities of the Gupta era. He contemplated the positions of various planets and constellations. He was the first to tell that the Moon revolves around the Earth. He was included among the nine gems of Chandragupta II. His major works are—Brihat Jataka, Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita, Laghu Jataka, etc.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following facts about Samudragupta is not confirmed by his Allahabad Pillar Inscription?

options.A: His father nominated him for kingship.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation–The main source for knowing the history of Samudragupta is the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Eulogy) composed by Harishena. Mention of Ashvamedha sacrifice is not found in this. Mention of this is found on the coins of Samudragupta.

questions.question_text: Whose title is 'Napoleon of India'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 PGT History, 2009 PGT History, 2011 Explanation—Samudragupta is called 'Napoleon of India'. The account of Samudragupta's achievements that we get from the Prayag Prashasti, in which the extermination of the kings of Aryavarta and the conquest of the states of the far south, are indicators of his excellent military talent. Historian Smith, being impressed by the bravery of Samudragupta, called him the 'Napoleon of India'. One of his titles is also found as 'Apratirathah'.

questions.question_text: Who called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation – Chandragupta I appointed Samudragupta (350-375 AD) as his successor. Seeing the victories of Samudragupta, Dr. V. A. Smith called him the 'Napoleon of India'. According to the Prayag Prashasti, Samudragupta never lost in war. He has also been called 'Kaviraja' (King of Poets).

questions.question_text: Who was the Gopta of Saurashtra during the time of Skandagupta?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – It is known from the Junagarh inscription that Skandagupta had appointed Parnadatta as the Gopta (Military Governor) of the Saurashtra region, whereas in 456 AD, Parnadatta's son Chakrapalita was appointed as the city chief here, who got the dam of Sudarshana Lake, built by Rudradaman, repaired again.

questions.question_text: Which religion developed the most in the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation— The rise of the Gupta Empire took place in Kaushambi near Prayag at the end of the third century. The Pauranic religion developed the most in this dynasty. The composition of the Puranas in their current form took place in the Gupta period. Historical traditions have been mentioned in it.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal ruler's inscription is engraved on the Prayag Prashasti of Samudragupta?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The primary source of Samudragupta's history is his own inscription which is called 'Allahabad Pillar Inscription' or Prayag Prashasti. It was composed by his Sandhivigrahika (Minister of Peace and War) Secretary Harishena. According to Cunningham, this inscription was originally engraved in Kaushambi. In the upper part of the inscription, there is an inscription of the Mauryan ruler Ashoka who had it engraved in Kaushambi. In the medieval period, Mughal ruler Akbar brought it from Kaushambi and got it secured in the Allahabad fort. An inscription of Akbar's courtier Birbal is also found in it. Later, Jahangir also got his inscription written. In the beginning of the Prayag Prashasti, Ashoka's inscription is found. It contains an order given to the Mahamatras of Kaushambi to prevent the division of the Buddhist Sangha; after that, Samudragupta's inscription is engraved. It is written in Brahmi script and in pure Sanskrit language.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the lists. List-I (King) List-II (Title) A. Mahapadma Nanda 1. Sarvarajochchhetta B. Bindusara 2. Amitraghata C. Satakarni 3. Sarvakshatrantaka D. Samudragupta 4. Dakshinapathapati Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Mahapadma Nanda was the founder of the Nanda dynasty. He was the most powerful among all the rulers who sat on the throne of Magadha so far. He was honored with titles like 'Kaliyug ka Ansh' (Part of Kaliyuga), the destroyer of all Kshatriyas ('Sarvakshatrantaka'), and the incarnation of the second Parashurama, etc. 'Bindusara' has been called 'Amitraghata' (Destroyer of enemies). Satavahana ruler Satakarni had assumed titles like 'Dakshinapathapati' and 'Apratihatachakra'. Samudragupta was called 'Sarvarajochchhetta' because of defeating all kings. Mahapadma Nanda - Sarvakshatrantaka Bindusara - Amitraghata Satakarni - Dakshinapathapati Samudragupta - Sarvarajochchhetta

questions.question_text: Which one of the following titles is not related to Samudragupta?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - After Chandragupta I, his son Samudragupta sat on the throne, about whom detailed information is obtained from the Prayag Prashasti. Samudragupta's reign in the Gupta Empire is full of various types of achievements. He was born to Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi, due to which he was called 'Lichchhavi-dauhitra'. Because of exterminating all the kings, he was given the title of 'Sarvarajochchhetta'. Another of his titles was 'Ashvamedha Parakramah', which is confirmed by his Ashvamedha type coins. The title of 'Vikramaditya' was assumed by Chandragupta II after the victory over Shakas.

questions.question_text: Who among the Gupta rulers was called 'Lichchhavi-dauhitra'?
questions.explanation: Among the Gupta rulers, Samudragupta is called Lichchhavi-dauhitra. Samudragupta's mother Kumaradevi was a Lichchhavi princess. Samudragupta is called the Napoleon of India. Samudragupta was skilled in playing the Veena. Prayag Prashasti and Eran inscription are for the study of Samudragupta Chandragupta-II

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vakataka rulers married Chandragupta II's daughter Prabhavatigupta?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II is called Vikramanka or Vikramaditya. His mother's name was Dattadevi. His period is considered the Golden Age of the Gupta period. To get the support of the Vakatakas, Chandragupta married his daughter Prabhavatigupta to the Vakataka ruler Rudrasena II. The combined power of the Vakatakas and Guptas exterminated the Shakas. It is noteworthy that the Vakataka people used to rule in the modern Maharashtra province

questions.question_text: From which Gupta ruler were the most coins obtained from the Bayana hoard?
questions.explanation: Most coins of the Gupta dynasty ruler Chandragupta II were obtained from the Bayana coin hoard. Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' (375-76 to 415 AD) had assumed the titles of Paramabhagavata, Sahasanka, and Shakari. He had issued gold, silver, and copper coins. Chandragupta II had circulated 8 types of gold coins, among which the most prominent was the Archer type coin which has been obtained in the maximum number from Bayana. Chandragupta I had issued Kumaradevi type gold coins; besides this, he issued Lichchhavi type, King-Queen type, etc. Samudragupta had issued 6 types of gold coins, including Garuda type, Archer type, Ashvamedha type, etc. Kumaragupta had issued a maximum of 14 types of gold coins, which included Apratigha type, Peacock-Kartikeya type, etc

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): Faxian came to India during the time of Chandragupta II. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct? Code: Reason (R): He described Chandragupta II ruling from his capital Pataliputra.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Faxian came to India during the reign of Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II. He has not mentioned the names of his contemporary rulers, but he praises their rule. According to him, the ruler was a follower of Brahminical faith and the citizens of the state were kind and tolerant, the king's rule was well-organized, and the people were happy

questions.question_text: Who got the Udayagiri inscription engraved?
questions.explanation: 20 caves were built at Udayagiri near Vidisha during the period of Chandragupta II. The cave built by Chandragupta II's foreign minister Virasena is called 'Tawa' 'cave'. Only one cave here is related to Jainism. Sanakanika Maharaja, a feudatory of Chandragupta II, built the Varaha cave which is the most famous cave here, in which a giant statue of Vishnu's Varaha incarnation is engraved. Ganga-Yamuna holding pots are engraved at the entrance of the Varaha cave. Udayagiri caves have also been called 'Mithya caves'. Cave number 9, which Cunningham called the Amrita cave, is the largest cave here. Vishnu along with two wives and a twelve-armed goddess are depicted in the Udayagiri cave

questions.question_text: Who among the following assumed the titles of Devaraja, Devagupta, and Devashri?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II became the ruler in 375 AD. He was the successor of Samudragupta who assumed the title of Vikramaditya. He was the greatest and most powerful emperor of India. His era is designated as the Golden Age. Nine gems also used to reside in his court. He had assumed many titles along with Vikramaditya, which are as follows— 'Devaraja, Deva Shri, and Devagupta'. The Chinese traveler Faxian came to India during his time and he has written a detailed account about the people of India

questions.question_text: With which of the following dynasties did the Gupta rulers establish matrimonial alliances with the aim of increasing their status and prestige? 1. Lichchhavi 2. Vakataka 3. Naga 4. Kadamba
questions.explanation: A. Lichchhavi - Chandragupta I B. Vakataka - Chandragupta II married his daughter C. Naga dynasty - Chandragupta II (with princess Kuberanaga) D. Kadamba dynasty - Chandragupta II got Kumaragupta married.

questions.question_text: Which statement is false regarding the currencies of the Gupta period?

options.A: Gold coins were called Dinar in Gupta inscriptions.
options.B: After the Gujarat victory, Gupta rulers issued a large number of copper coins for local exchange.
options.C: Gupta coins depict the love of Gupta rulers for war and arts.
options.D: Gold in Gupta coins is less pure compared to the gold of Kushana coins.

questions.explanation: 1. Gupta rulers issued the most gold coins, which were called Dinar in Gupta inscriptions Untrue 2- After the Gujarat victory, Gupta rulers issued silver coins (not copper) for local exchange. (According to Faxian, common people used cowries for buying and selling). 3. The love of Gupta rulers for war and arts is depicted on Gupta coins. 4. Gold in Gupta coins is less pure compared to the gold of Kushana coins. * Archer type, Garuda type, Ashvamedha type, Parashu type - Samudragupta coins. - King-Queen type - Chandragupta I - Chhatradhari type - Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) * Gupta ruler Chandragupta II first issued silver coins after the victory over Shakas. These were used in local transactions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Faxian, Xuanzang, and Yijing?

options.A: All three wrote their memoirs which were translated into English.
options.B: All three spent many years in India and learned the languages here.
options.C: All three traveled the whole country.
options.D: Faxian and Yijing did not mention the rulers of the states they visited, but Xuanzang described his patron Harsha sufficiently.

questions.explanation: Faxian and Yijing did not mention the rulers of the states they visited, whereas Xuanzang described his patron Harsha sufficiently - During Faxian's travel, it was the period of Chandragupta Vikramaditya of the Gupta dynasty in India. All three were Chinese travelers; the main objective of their lives was to see the places associated with Buddhism in India, not to travel the whole country.

questions.question_text: Identify the literary sources that mention the story of Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi: (1) Devi Chandraguptam (2) Kavyamimansa (3) Harshacharita (4) Malatimadhava Choose the correct code:
questions.explanation: The mention of the Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi story is found in Devi Chandraguptam by Vishakhadatta, Harshacharita by Banabhatta, Kavyamimansa by Rajasekhara, Shringara Prakasha by Bhoja, and Mujmal-ut-Tawarikh by Abul Hasan Ali Ans. (b) : The story of Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi is mentioned in Vishakhadatta's Devi-Chandraguptam, Banabhatta's Harshacharita, Rajashekhara's Kavyamimansa, Bhoja's Shringaraprakasha and Abul Hasan Ali's Mujmal-ut-Tawarikh.

questions.question_text: The Gupta period Buddha statue with a shaven head was found in:
questions.explanation: The only such statue of Buddha made in Mathura style, which dates back to the time of Kumaragupta, is found from Mankuwar (Allahabad). It is seated on a throne in Abhaya Mudra. Its head is shaven and the upper part is naked and muscular

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Among ancient Indian coins, the maximum number belong to the Kushana period.
options.B: In the oldest coins found in India, only a few symbols are found.
options.C: Silver coins were issued in large numbers during the Gupta rule.
options.D: Post-Mauryan coins are made of lead (graphite), potin, copper, bronze, silver and gold.

questions.explanation: Chandragupta II had issued silver coins as a symbol of victory after defeating the Shaka rulers and bringing the state of Gujarat under his control, but these currencies were not for the daily use of the common man; silver coins were not issued in large quantities during the Gupta period

questions.question_text: In which language do women and Shudra characters speak in Sanskrit plays of Kalidasa?
questions.explanation: In the Sanskrit plays of Kalidasa, women and men (common characters) conversed in Prakrit language

questions.question_text: Prabhavatigupta was the ruler of:
questions.explanation: To bring the Vakataka dynasty under influence, Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavatigupta to the Vakataka king Rudrasen II. Shortly after the marriage, after the death of Rudrasen, Prabhavatigupta started ruling as the regent of the Vakataka state

questions.question_text: Ashvamedha type gold coins were introduced by the following:
questions.explanation: Samudragupta and Kumaragupta I introduced Ashvamedha type gold coins, evidence of which is obtained from the Mandsaur inscription of Kumaragupta I

questions.question_text: The Bagh caves near Gwalior represent the painting of which of the following eras?
questions.explanation: The Bagh caves near Gwalior represent the painting of the Gupta period. From the point of view of the development of art and literature, the Gupta period has been called the 'Classical Age' or 'Golden Age' of Indian history. Painting developed during the Gupta period. Remnants of paintings of this period can be seen in the Bagh caves, Ajanta caves and Badami caves

questions.question_text: Which text was composed by Kalidasa?
questions.explanation: Abhigyan Shakuntalam was composed by Kalidasa; it contains the story of the love, marriage, separation and reunion of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala. Saundarananda was composed by Ashvaghosa and Pattuppattu is a collection of ten songs

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'Prakritaprakasha'?
questions.explanation: The author of 'Prakritaprakasha' was Vararuchi. Vararuchi was one of the nine gems (Navaratnas) of Vikramaditya. Katyayana, who wrote Vartika on Panini's grammar, and the author of the Prakrit grammar named Prakritaprakasha, are also known by the name Vararuchi. In the history of Sanskrit literature, the name Vararuchi is found as the author of several texts and is also cited as the author of verses in some collections of sayings like 'Subhashitavali', 'Sharngadharapaddhati' and 'Saduktikarnamrita'. Taranatha in his 'History of Buddhism in India' has cited 'Brahmana Vararuchi' or 'Acharya Vararuchi'

questions.question_text: Who among the following Gupta rulers first issued silver coins?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II got silver coins engraved following the imitation of Shaka coins. As a result of the Western Shaka victory, he got 'Vyaghra' (tiger) coins engraved and had assumed the title of 'Vikramaditya'. The record of the conquests of Chandragupta II is found in his Udayagiri inscription

questions.question_text: With whom was the Navaratnas (nine gems) of the court associated?
questions.explanation: The greatest ruler of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II. There were nine gems (Navaratnas) who graced the court of Chandragupta II. Among these, the name of Kalidasa is most famous. Kalidasa was a poet and playwright. Other scholars included in the Navaratnas are as follows— Dhanvantari, Kshapanaka, Amarasimha, Shanku, Vetalabhatta, Ghatakarpara, Varahamihira and Vararuchi

questions.question_text: Harishena, the author of Prayag Prashasti, held which of the following positions? (i) Khadyatapakika (ii) Kumaramatya (iii) Mahadandanayaka (iv) Sandhivigrahika Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation–Harishena, the author of Prayag Prashasti, held the positions of 'Kumaramatya', 'Mahadandanayaka' and 'Sandhivigrahika'. In Gupta records, Vishayapati, Governor, Commander, Minister, etc., were all called 'Kumaramatya'. Harishena was the Commander-in-Chief and Foreign Secretary. Sandhivigrahika was the minister of peace and war. The foreign department was under him. Mahadandanayaka was the chief officer of the police department and the judge of criminal cases.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): The victory over the Shaka-Kshatrapa dynasty of Gujarat was the greatest success of the Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II. Reason (R): This must have given the Guptas access to Indian trade in the Mediterranean Sea. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: With the elimination of the Shaka Kshatrapas of Gujarat by the Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II, Gujarat came under the Gupta Empire, as a result of which the Guptas reached the Arabian Sea. Certainly, this gave the Guptas access to Indian trade in the Mediterranean Sea

questions.question_text: Bhinmal is known as the birthplace of which astronomer?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Brahmagupta was born in Bhinmal near Ujjain in 598 AD. Aryabhatta was born in Pataliputra, Bihar in 476 AD. Bhaskaracharya was born in Bijapur, Karnataka in 1114 AD, and Varahamihira was born in 505 AD in Kapitthaka or Kayatha in Ujjain.

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts is the story of Ramagupta not mentioned?
questions.explanation: The description of the historicity of Ramagupta is found in Natyadarpana composed by Gunachandra. The story of Ramagupta is also found in Banabhatta's Harshacharita. The story of Ramagupta is also described in Mujmal-ut-Tawarikh composed by Abul Hasan Ali. The account of Ramagupta is not found in Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa.

questions.question_text: Mention the name of the Gupta-Vakataka queen who gave land as a grant –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavatigupta to the Vakataka ruler Rudrasen II. Rudrasen II had two sons. After the death of Rudrasen, Prabhavati Gupta became the regent after placing her son Divakarasen on the throne. Mention of her giving land grants is found in the Poona copper plate of Prabhavati.

questions.question_text: Which of the Gupta rulers assumed the title of 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation–Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II (375-415 AD) was the greatest ruler of the Gupta dynasty who assumed the title of 'Vikramaditya' after defeating the Shakas. Chandragupta II was a staunch devotee of Vishnu. His most popular title was 'Paramabhagavata'. There is mention of nine gems in his reign.

questions.question_text: During whose reign did Faxian visit India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The Chinese traveler Faxian came to India during the reign of the Gupta dynasty emperor Chandragupta II. His time was 399 to 414 AD. He has given a proper portrayal of the then prevailing conditions in his travelogue.

questions.question_text: Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' did not establish matrimonial relations with which one dynasty?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation–Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' had established matrimonial relations with three dynasties- (i) Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) married the Naga dynasty princess Kuberanaga. (ii) Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavatigupta to the Vakataka king Rudrasen II. (iii) Matrimonial relations were established with the Kadamba dynasty (probably for his son Kumaragupta I).

questions.question_text: Who is credited with starting the Gupta Era (319-20)?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Chandragupta I (319-350 AD) started an era, which is famous by the name of Gupta Era (319-320 AD). It is noteworthy that the founder of the Gupta dynasty was Srigupta.

questions.question_text: When did Chandragupta-II assume the title of 'Vikramaditya'?

options.A: After the elimination of the Shakas

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Chandragupta II was the son of Samudragupta. By gaining victory over the Shakas, he assumed the title of 'Vikramaditya'. He was also called 'Shakari'. He had assumed titles like Deva, Devagupta, Devaraja, Devashri, Shrivikrama, Vikramaditya, Paramabhagavata, Narendrachandra, Simhavikrama, Ajitavikrama etc.

questions.question_text: Mehrauli pillar inscription is related to which ruler?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation–The victory glory of a king named Chandra is inscribed on the iron pillar of Mehrauli in South Delhi. This king named Chandra is considered to be Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) himself. Some other inscriptions of his time are as follows – Mathura pillar inscription, Udayagiri cave inscription, Garhwa stone inscription (in which Chandragupta is called Paramabhagavata), Sanchi inscription, Udayagiri cave inscription, Mathura stone inscription etc.

questions.question_text: Who was not included among the nine gems of Chandragupta Vikramaditya:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation– Nagarjuna was a famous chemist. He was not included in the nine gems of Vikramaditya. The names that appear in the context of the enumeration of the nine gems of Vikramaditya are described as follows - Kalidasa, Dhanvantari, Kshapanaka, Amarasimha, Shanku, Vetalabhatta, Ghatakarpara, Varahamihira, Vararuchi etc.

questions.question_text: Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavatigupta with the king of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation─ Gupta Emperor Chandragupta Vikramaditya married his daughter Prabhavatigupta to the Vakataka ruler Rudrasen II. Who, coming under his influence, had adopted Vaishnavism.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Gupta rulers was the first to assume the title 'Paramabhagavata'?
questions.explanation: PGT 2016 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 PGT History, 2011 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- After Samudragupta, his son Chandragupta II, born from his queen Dattadevi, became the most important and powerful ruler of the Gupta dynasty. In Gupta dynasty writings, he has been called 'Tatparigrihita', meaning chosen by him (Samudragupta). Some scholars propound on this basis that Samudragupta himself had nominated Chandragupta as his successor. This view completely negates the historicity of Ramagupta. Chandragupta II has another name 'Deva' and he has been called Devagupta, Devaraja, Devashri etc. Vikramanka, Vikramaditya, Paramabhagavata etc. were his famous titles. While on one hand this indicates his matchless prowess, on the other hand it also proves him being a religious Vaishnava.

questions.question_text: The weight standard of coins issued by Gupta rulers after the conquest of the Kshatrapa state was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Three inscriptions of Chandragupta II are found in Eastern Malwa, from which information about the Shaka victory is obtained indirectly. From the combined evidence of these three inscriptions (Bhilsa, Udayagiri, Sanchi), it appears that Chandragupta had gone on an expedition in Eastern Malwa with his feudatories and high military officers. The objective of this expedition was certainly to conquer the Shaka state located just west of Eastern Malwa. Chandragupta's Shaka rival was Rudrasimha III. He was killed and his state of Gujarat and Kathiawar was merged into the empire. Chandragupta II got silver coins engraved following the imitation of Shaka coins, which he had circulated in the Shaka state. From here some silver coins of Rudrasimha III are found which were restruck by Chandragupta. The Vyaghra (tiger) style coins of Chandragupta are also proof of the victory of Gujarat and Kathiawar. The silver coins of the Gupta rulers were called 'Rupaka'. The weight standard of these coins was 32 to 36 grains.

questions.question_text: At the time of Chandragupta II, a strong center of Pashupatas was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - People of the Pashupata sect hold a laguda (staff) in hand which is a symbol of Shiva in a way. A similar picture is inscribed on the coin of the Kushana ruler 'Huvishka', which is the oldest evidence providing knowledge about the Pashupata sect. It is known from the Mathura-pillar inscription of Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' that a Pashupata follower named Uditacharya had established two lingas named Upamiteshvara and Kapileshvara in Mathura. Therefore, it is clear that in the time of Chandragupta II, Mathura was a major center of the Pashupata sect.

questions.question_text: The name of Faxian's travelogue is:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Faxian was a resident of a place named 'Wu-yang' in Changan, the capital of Shanxi province of China. He traveled to India with the aim of studying Buddhist scriptures and visiting Buddhist pilgrimage sites. He came to India during the reign of Chandragupta II. The name of Faxian's travel account is 'Fo-Kwo-Ki'. 'Si-Yu-Ki' is the travel account of Xuanzang. A colleague of Xuanzang, Hwui-Li, composed a book named 'Life of Xuanzang'. Upon the entry of Buddhism into China in the first century AD, the Chinese used the word 'Tien-Chu' or 'Chu-Andu' for India. But after Xuanzang, the word 'Yen-Tu' became prevalent there.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the mother of Prabhavati Gupta?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The Naga people during the Gupta rule were one of the major dynasties of ancient India.
