Mention of many Naga dynasties is found in the Prayag Prashasti of Samudragupta who ruled in Mathura, Ahichhatra, Padmavati etc. Although Samudragupta had conquered many Naga kings, yet their power was still quite strong. To get the cooperation of the Nagas, Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' married the Naga princess Kuberanaga. As a result of this matrimonial relation, a daughter was born whose name was Prabhavati Gupta. In the Poona copper plate, Prabhavati Gupta has also called her mother 'Nagakulasambhuta' (born in the Naga clan).

questions.question_text: Which of the following Gupta kings ascended the throne in the year 56 of the Gupta Era?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation–Gupta ruler Chandragupta I had also started an era in 319-20 AD which is famous as the Gupta Era. The same era was used by his descendants. Therefore, according to the question, adding 319+56 comes to 375 AD, which is considered the reign of Chandragupta II, which lasted until 415 AD.

questions.question_text: The Mathura pillar inscription of Gupta Era 61 is related to?
questions.explanation: The Mathura pillar inscription of Gupta Era 61 is related to the Gupta dynasty emperor Chandragupta 'Vikramaditya'/Chandragupta II. This was found from a garden near Rangeshwar Mahadev in Mathura. In this stone inscription, there is a description of the installation of Shiva idols named Upamiteshvara and Kapileshvara by Uditacharya. This inscription confirms the existence of Shaivism in then Mathura Kumaragupta-I

questions.question_text: Which king of the Gupta dynasty is considered the founder of Nalanda University?
questions.explanation: The Gupta Emperor Kumaragupta I (415-455 AD) established Nalanda University. Students from Korea, Mongolia, Bukhara, China, Japan and Tibet used to come to receive education in this university along with Indian students

questions.question_text: Mandsaur Prashasti is related to which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: A famous inscription of the reign of Gupta Emperor Kumaragupta has been obtained from Mandsaur, in which there is a description of silk merchants of Lata Desha coming and settling in Dashapura. They had built a Sun temple in Dashapura

questions.question_text: In an inscription of the time of Kumaragupta, there is mention of year 493 of the Malava Era. Which is its equivalent year in the following?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of Gupta period inscriptions have been found during the time of Kumaragupta, the number of which is about 18. During his time, the largest cache of Gupta period coins was found from Bayana hoard (in Bharatpur district of Rajasthan). In an inscription of the time of Kumaragupta, there is mention of year 493 of Malava Era, which is considered equivalent to 436 AD. Major inscriptions of the time of Kumaragupta are considered to be Bilsad, Karamadanda, Mankuwar and two inscriptions of Garhwa

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions is the 'Pattavaya Shreni' mentioned?

options.B: Indore copper plate inscription of Skandagupta

questions.explanation: Trade, which was also done with foreign countries during the Gupta period, declined. We get proof of this from the Mandsaur inscription of the time of Kumaragupta I, which reveals that the Pattavaya Shreni (guild of silk weavers) left its work from the Lata Vishaya (district) and settled in Western Malwa and started doing other work

After the death of Kumaragupta I, Skandagupta became the ruler. The Huna invasion began as soon as he took the reins of the government. The Huna invasion has been a specific reason for the decline of the Guptas. The mention of the Huna invasion is in the Bhitari inscription. The first Huna invasion occurred during the time of Skandagupta, and its leader was Khushnevaz. During the time of Narasimhagupta 'Baladitya', the Huna leader was Mihirakula. Dhanyavishnu, the younger brother of Budhagupta's feudatory Matrivishnu, used to rule under the subjection of the Huna king Toramana
examinations: The Huna invasion is described in

questions.question_text: Which of the following Gupta rulers performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice?
questions.explanation: After Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I became the ruler, but before Kumaragupta, the name of another ruler appears, who was Govindagupta, the son of Queen Dhruva Devi (wife of Ramagupta). It is known from the coins of Kumaragupta that he had performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice. The maximum number of inscriptions among the Gupta rulers are found of Kumaragupta. Kumaragupta adopted titles like Mahendraditya, Shri Mahendra, etc

questions.question_text: Which new types of gold coins were introduced by Kumaragupta I? (i) Apratigha type (ii) Gajarudha type (iii) Khadga-nihanta type (iv) Khadga type Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation–Kumaragupta I 'Mahendraditya' (approx. 415-455 AD) introduced new types of coins—Apratigha type, Gajarudha type, Khadga-nihanta type, and Khadga type. Gold, silver, and copper coins of Kumaragupta are obtained from a vast land area of Western India. The circulation of silver coins in Central India happened during his period.

questions.question_text: The name of the guild organization described in the Mandsaur inscription of Kumaragupta was
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation—The Mandsaur inscription of Kumaragupta was composed by Vatsabhatti. Mandsaur is situated on the banks of the Shivna river in Western Malwa. Today, this place is also called Dasore. Its ancient name was Dashpur. This place formerly fell under the Scindia princely state. In the first three verses of this panegyric, the Sun is praised, and thereafter it begins with a charming description of central Gujarat (Lata Vishaya). In this, there is a detailed mention of the Tantuvaya (weaver) guild. These people were proficient in various arts in addition to their ancestral profession. These artisans, from the wealth accumulated through their craft, got a distinctively grand Sun temple constructed.

questions.question_text: The commodity traded by the guild coming from Lata to Dashpur during the period of Kumaragupta was—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Evidence from the Mandsaur inscription of the Kumaragupta period shows that the Patwaya guild (silk thread making committee) left the Lata region and settled in Dashpur. This guild used to trade in silk cloth.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an illustration of 'Anuloma' type of marriage?

options.A: Marriage of a Brahmin boy with a Kshatriya girl
options.B: Marriage of a Kshatriya girl with a Kshatriya boy
options.C: Marriage of a Brahmin boy with a Brahmin girl
options.D: Marriage of a Vaishya girl with a Kshatriya boy

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In ancient Hindu society, Anuloma and Pratiloma types of marriages were prevalent. In Anuloma, a person of a higher Varna married a girl of the Varna immediately below his. Such marriages often occurred in Vedic society because the bonds of the Varna system were not rigid. Many Brahmin sages married Kshatriya girls. Chyavana married Sukanya, Shyavasya married Rathavithi, Agastya married Lopamudra, etc. Under Pratiloma marriage, a girl of a higher Varna married a man of a lower Varna. This type of marriage was considered reprehensible.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is famous for his commentary written on 'Manu-smriti'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–The prominent commentators of Manusmriti are Bharuchi, Medhatithi, Govindaraja, and Kulluka Bhatta. Vishvarupa, Vijnanesvara, and Apararka are the prominent commentators of Yajnavalkya Smriti.

questions.question_text: Who stopped the military expansion of Harsha in the Deccan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–Pulakeshin II stopped the military expansion of Harsha in the Deccan. Pulakeshin II was a powerful king of the Chalukya dynasty. Xuanzang praises his power and influence. As a result of Harsha's victories, the western boundary of his kingdom reached the Narmada river. On the other hand, Pulakeshin also wanted to expand his kingdom towards the north. In such a situation, war between the two became inevitable. Consequently, a battle took place between Harsha and Pulakeshin II on the banks of the Narmada river, in which Harsha was defeated.

questions.question_text: The smallest unit of village administration mentioned in the Kahaum inscription of Skandagupta was—
questions.explanation: In the Kahaum inscription of Skandagupta, 'Kakubha' has been stated as the smallest unit of village administration. This inscription was obtained from a place named Kahaum. From this inscription, it is known that a person named Bhadra got the statues of five Jain Tirthankaras constructed

questions.question_text: Which of the following tribes is Skandagupta credited with defeating?
questions.explanation: Skandagupta—The Junagadh inscription is the most important and first inscription of Skandagupta (Gupta Era 136 or 455 AD). It is mentioned in this that Skandagupta had defeated the Hunas (Mlecchas) Bhitari Pillar Inscription—In this, the description of Skandagupta's war with Pushyamitras and Hunas is preserved.

questions.question_text: From which source is the mention of Skandagupta's Huna victory not obtained?
questions.explanation: The mention of Skandagupta's Huna victory is obtained from the Bhitari Pillar Inscription found in Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh, in which the clear description of Skandagupta's war with the Pushyamitras and Hunas is found only in this record. Along with this, the description of the mothers of Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, and Kumaragupta I and their title 'Mahadevi' is also found in it Note–The mention of Skandagupta's Huna victory is not found in Aryamanjushrimulakalpa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers restored the Somnath temple of Gujarat after it was destroyed by Mahmud Ghaznavi?
questions.explanation: Among the Chalukya dynasty rulers of Gujarat (Anhilwad), Kumarapala was an ambitious ruler. At the beginning of his reign itself, he proved his ability by failing the attacks of Arnoraja Chauhan, Vikramsimha Paramara, and Ballala, the ruler of Malwa. Jain Acharya Hemachandra had initiated him into Jainism, after which he assumed the title of Parama Arhata and implemented the principles of non-violence in the entire empire. Kumarapala was a Jain, but he got the Somnath temple reconstructed in its final form and worshipped Shiva in the Somnath temple along with Jain Acharya Hemachandra. A poet named Jayasimha Suri has sung the praises of his reign in a poem named Kumarapalacharita

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the provincial governor of Surashtra during the reign of Skandagupta?
questions.explanation: Skandagupta was not only a capable commander but also a skilled administrator. He had entrusted Chakrapalita, the son of Parnadatta, the governor of Surashtra, for the restoration of Sudarshana Lake situated on Girnar mountain. He also got a Vishnu temple constructed on the bank of the lake

questions.question_text: Which of the following temples is constructed from bricks?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation–Lakshmana Temple of Sirpur: Sirpur is an archaeological site situated on the banks of the Mahanadi in Chhattisgarh. There is an ancient Lakshmana temple built of bricks here, constructed by the Gupta dynasty kings.

questions.question_text: The date in the inscription of Kumaragupta obtained from Sarnath is year 154. Which of the following is its equivalent year?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation–The date in the inscription of Kumaragupta-II obtained from Sarnath is year 154. Its equivalent year will be 154 + 319 = 473 AD.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions is the mention of evidence of a Sun temple?
questions.explanation: It is known from the Mandsaur inscription of Kumaragupta-I that due to the decline of the silk industry, a guild of weavers migrated from Lata (Southern Gujarat) and settled in Dashpur (Mandsaur). The mention of getting a Sun temple constructed in Mandsaur by this guild is obtained.

questions.question_text: Where was the poet Bana a resident of?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – The great poet Banabhatta was a resident of Shahabad. We get this information from the book Harshacharita composed by him, which is divided into a total of eight Ucchvasas (chapters). In the first three Ucchvasas, Banabhatta has recorded his autobiography. In the second Ucchvasa, he has described himself as a resident of a village named Pritikuta in Shahabad.

questions.question_text: Who was the mother of Emperor Kumaragupta I?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation— The name of the mother of Emperor Kumaragupta I was Dhruva Devi. After Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I ascended the throne. Under his robust administrative system, Kumaragupta I remained on the throne of the Gupta dynasty for 40 years. Kumaragupta I established Nalanda University, and this university is called the Oxford of Mahayana Buddhism.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first Gupta ruler who issued gold coins?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Chandragupta I was considered a powerful ruler of the Gupta dynasty. He assumed the title of 'Maharajadhiraja'. He had issued gold coins. It is known from these very coins that Chandragupta I had established matrimonial relations with the Licchavi people.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct?

options.A: The Gupta Empire came to an end with the death of Skandagupta.
options.B: After the death of Skandagupta, the empire continued, but central control became weak.
options.C: After the death of Skandagupta, local rulers became independent.
options.D: After the death of Skandagupta, only nominal control of the Gupta emperors remained to the west of Kashi.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation–Skandagupta ruled until 455-467 AD. He was the last great ruler of the Gupta dynasty. After his death, the central control of the Gupta dynasty became weak and local rulers started becoming independent.

questions.question_text: To which university did Harsha provide special protection?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation—During Harsha's time, Nalanda was the center of education for the Mahayana sect. Nalanda was situated near a village named Baragaon in the Rajgir district of Patna, Bihar. This Vihara was established by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta. During Harsha's time, Nalanda University was at the height of its progress. Harsha provided the income of one hundred villages to cover its expenses and got a 100-feet high brass Vihara built here. Xuanzang had studied at Nalanda University.

questions.question_text: Among the following, whose gold coins were the heaviest in weight?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation–The weight of the gold coin became maximum during the reign of the Gupta ruler Skandagupta because we start finding adulteration in the gold coins of the Guptas from the middle of the fifth century.

questions.question_text: What was the annual rate of normal interest in the post-Gupta period?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- The annual rate of normal interest in the post-Gupta period was 24%. If seen, the interest rate that existed after Harsha, the interest rate of 24% was low because the interest rate in the Rajput period was very high. [Heading] Huna Invasion and its Effect

questions.question_text: For what purpose was 'Hun' a unit?
questions.explanation: 'Hun' was a unit of currency that remained prevalent in the Kashmir region by the Huna rulers. It is known from the Sanjeli copper plate and the inscriptions of Eran and Gwalior that around 510 AD, the Huna state had been established in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. The panegyrics and coins of the Huna rulers reveal the gradual expansion of Huna power. This coin was of gold, which continued to be used by later rulers as well

questions.question_text: Which was the main port of Eastern India in the post-Harsha period?
questions.explanation: Tamralipti was the prominent port of the eastern coast in the post-Gupta period

questions.question_text: Who among the following explained for the first time that sunrise and sunset occur every day due to the rotation of the Earth on its axis?
questions.explanation: Aryabhatta was a great scientist of the Gupta period; he was the one who told that the Earth rotates on its axis and sunrise and sunset occur every day due to the rotation of the Earth on its axis

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A) : Both Samudragupta and Kumaragupta issued Ashvamedha type coins. Reason (R) : Both had not mentioned the performance of Ashvamedha sacrifice in their inscriptions. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation—The reign of the Gupta dynasty is called the Golden Age of Indian history. The Gupta dynasty began in 275 AD with the first ruler Sri Gupta. The gold coins of the Gupta period were called Dinars. The maximum number of gold coins were made during the Gupta period. Samudragupta and Kumaragupta have not mentioned the performance of Ashvamedha sacrifice in their inscriptions; rather, the mention of Ashvamedha sacrifice is found on the coins of both. On the obverse of these coins, figures of horses tied to the sacrificial post (Yupa) are inscribed.

questions.question_text: Among the following Khajuraho temples, which temples are of Sandhara style? (i) Chitragupta Temple (ii) Lakshmana Temple (iii) Parshvanatha Temple (iv) Vamana Temple Select the correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Among the Khajuraho temples, the Lakshmana temple and the Parshvanatha temple are built in the Panchayatana style (Sandhara style). The Lakshmana temple was built around 930 AD. This temple of Lord Vishnu was built by a king named Yashovarman. His other name was also Lakshmana Varman, therefore it is also called by the name Lakshmana temple. The Parshvanatha temple is a Sandhara temple built in the 10th century, contemporary to the Vishvanatha temple. Originally built for Adinatha, this temple contains the statue of Parshvanatha.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (Composition) – (Subject)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Lilavati is an ancient treatise on Mathematics and Astronomy composed in Sanskrit by the Indian mathematician Bhaskara II in 1150 AD; it is also a part of Siddhanta Shiromani. Algebra has been discussed in Lilavati. Lilavati was the name of Bhaskaracharya's daughter. This book contains questions and their answers on Arithmetic (Ankaganita), Algebra, and Geometry.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the lists– List-I (Administrator)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The matched list is as follows– (A) Bhandagaradhikrita - (iv) Treasury (B) Dashaparadhika - (ii) Justice (C) Mahakshapatalika - (i) Archives (D) Shaulkikaka - (iii) Revenue

questions.question_text: (i) Aryabhatta (ii) Brahmagupta (iii) Lagadha (iv) Varahamihira Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code: Place the following astronomers in the correct chronological order:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation–Among the given astronomers, Lagadha's chronology comes first. After this, the name of Aryabhatta comes. He gave his views in the book named 'Aryabhatiyam'. He believed that the Earth is round and rotates on its axis. Brahmagupta (598 AD) composed the Brahmasiddhanta. Varahamihira composed 'Pancha-siddhantika'. Thus their order is as follows– Lagadha, Aryabhatta, Varahamihira, Brahmagupta.

questions.question_text: Which of the following words is related to currency?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation–Dramma was an ancient silver coin of the value of 16 Panas. Its use was specific before the invasion of the Muslims. This very coin has been used in solving problems, etc., in the book Lilavati.

questions.question_text: (i) Harishena (ii) Ravikirti (iii) Vatsabhatti Code: Arrange the following writers of inscriptions in chronological order: (iv) Virasena
questions.explanation: – Harishena - Prayag Prashasti (Samudragupta) Virasena - Udayagiri Cave Inscription (Foreign Secretary of Chandragupta II) Vatsabhatti - Mandsaur Prashasti (Kumaragupta) Ravikirti - Aihole Inscription (Pulakeshin-II)

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings performed the Vajapeya sacrifice? (ii) Pushyamitra Shunga (iii) Shantimula I (iv) Gautamiputra Satakarni Code: (i) Pravarasena I
questions.explanation: Vakataka king Pravarasena I (275 - 335 AD) and Ikshvaku king Shri Shantimula I performed the Vajapeya sacrifice; Shri Shantimula I was the founder of the Ikshvaku dynasty "}

questions.question_text: The Hunas circulated only the following coins: (i) Gold (ii) Silver (iii) Copper (iv) Potin Codes:
questions.explanation: Huna coins - Hunas circulated silver and copper coins in their conquered provinces. In Indian tradition, these are called 'Gadhaiya' or 'Gadhiya'

questions.question_text: (i) Aryabhata II (ii) Bhaskaracharya (iii) Bhattotpala (iv) Brahmagupta Codes: Arrange the following astronomers in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The chronological arrangement is as follows (i) Brahmagupta - (598-670 AD) (7th century) (ii) Aryabhata - (920-1000 AD) (10th century) (iii) Bhattotpala - (10th century) (iv) Bhaskaracharya - (1114-1185 AD) (12th century) Note: The Commission has accepted option (d) as the answer to this question.

questions.question_text: Which other Central Asian tribe came to India along with the Hunas?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation – The other Caucasian Central Asian tribe that came to India with the Hunas were the Gurjaras. According to historians, Gurjaras were Aryan warriors who came from the Caucasus region of Central Asia (present-day Armenia and Georgia). According to Gurjara inscriptions, they were Suryavanshi (Solar dynasty) or Raghuvanshi. Ancient great poet Rajasekhara has called Gurjaras 'Raghukula-tilaka' and 'Raghugramini'.

questions.question_text: Select the incorrect statement from the following:

options.A: Huna invasion occurred during the time of Kumaragupta.
options.B: The first Huna ruler Toramana was successful in winning Central India around Western India and Eran.
options.D: Mihirakula was successful in winning Sri Lanka.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation - Hunas were residents of Central Asia. The first Huna invasion was carried out by Khushnavaz during the time of the Gupta ruler Skandagupta. From Skandagupta's Bhitari and Junagarh inscriptions, it is known that he was defeated by Skandagupta. The second Huna invasion took place under the leadership of Toramana, who was the first Huna invader to establish his kingdom in India. Toramana was a follower of Jainism. Mihirakula was the son of Toramana. The Chinese traveler Song-Yun visited India during his time in 520 AD. Yashodharman, who was the ruler of Malwa, defeated Mihirakula. Mihirakula was a follower of Shaivism and was a staunch enemy of Buddhists.

questions.question_text: Who uprooted the Huna power from Malwa?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation – According to the Mandsaur inscription, around 532 AD, the Malwa ruler Yashodharman defeated Mihirakula and built a victory pillar in commemoration of establishing his dominance in North India.

questions.question_text: Who deposed Mihirakula from the Ganges Valley?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 Explanation – Mihirakula attacked the later Gupta ruler Narasimhagupta 'Baladitya' but was defeated and taken prisoner. Later, Narasimhagupta released him at the behest of his mother. After this, Mihirakula fled to Kashmir and killed the ruler there and destroyed 600 stupas and sangharamas.

questions.question_text: During whose time did the Hunas invade India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Hunas were a nomadic barbaric tribe living in Central Asia. The first Huna invasion took place during the time of Skandagupta. According to U.N. Roy, its first leader was Khushnavaz, who attacked India after suppressing the Sassanian rulers of Iran.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers is credited with having Mihirakula pay obeisance at his feet?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation - Mihirakula (518-530 AD) was a famous Huna ruler after Toramana. In the 6th century AD (around 530 AD), the valiant ruler of Malwa, Yashodharman, badly defeated Mihirakula. In his inscription found at Mandsaur, the description of this defeat is found in a very poetic manner: "He who had not bowed his head before anyone except Lord Shiva, and whose arms embraced the Himalayas, making them feel vainly inaccessible, Yashodharman, by his own strength, forced that Mihirakula's head to bow down and made him worship his two feet with the flowers stuck in his locks of hair." In the Mandsaur inscription, the credit for being the first to defeat Mihirakula is given to Yashodharman, which seems to be a complete exaggeration. Baladitya had defeated him before this. This fact is confirmed by the internal evidence of the Mandsaur inscription itself. G. Decline of the Gupta Empire, Society and Culture

questions.question_text: Who among these were sharp critics of the Sati practice?
questions.explanation: In ancient India, an evil practice was prevalent where, after the death of the husband, the wife was forcibly or by her will made to sit alive in the cremation along with the husband's body. This tradition is known as Sati practice. In the 510 AD Eran stone inscription, it is mentioned that when Bhanugupta's friend Goparaja was killed in the war against the Hunas, his wife burned in the fire and became Sati. This is the first written evidence of Sati practice Banabhatta was a Sanskrit prose writer of the seventh century and the court poet of King Harshavardhana (606-647 AD). His two main works are Harshacharita and Kadambari. In the field of prose composition, he holds the same place as 'Kalidasa' in the field of Sanskrit poetry. He strongly criticized the Sati practice. He strongly opposed the decision of Harshavardhana's mother 'Yashomati' to become Sati. Banabhatta criticized it by calling it "the practice of fools".

questions.question_text: Arrange the following poets, who are known as writers of inscriptions, in chronological order.
questions.explanation: The correct order of the following poets is Poet / Ruler / Inscription 1- Harishena / Samudragupta / Prayag Prashasti (Sanskrit language, Champu style, Brahmi script), total 33 lines. 2- Vatsabhatti (Suryabhakta) / Kumaragupta / Mandsaur Inscription (This is the only inscription in which the date of the Gupta Era is given in Vikram Samvat, it has a total of 44 verses). 3- Ravishanti / - 4- Ravikirti (Jain writer) / Pulakeshin II / Aihole Inscription (This inscription describes the war between Harsha and Pulakeshin II).

questions.question_text: Where is the depiction of the performance of sacrifice by King Bali known from in Gupta period sculpture?
questions.explanation: The depiction of the performance of sacrifice by King Bali in Gupta period sculpture is known from the sculpture art of Pawaya. Mithuna (amorous couple) figures are carved on the walls of the Parvati temple of Nachna-Kuthara from the Gupta period. In this temple, Shiva-Parvati are carved with musical instruments. The Nachna-Kuthara temple has features of Buddhist Chaitya halls. In the Gupta period, the main centers of sculpture were Mathura, Sarnath, and Pataliputra

questions.question_text: Arrange the following coins chronologically and select the correct answer from the given codes: (i) Apratigha type coins (ii) Archer type coins (iii) Couch (Simhasana) type coins (iv) Standard (Dhvajadhari) type coins
questions.explanation: According to the question, the correct sequence of the given coins is: Standard (Dhvajadhari) type coins, Archer (Dhanurdhari) type coins, Couch (Simhasana) type coins, and Apratigha type coins. It is noteworthy here that the same type of coins was issued by many rulers such as Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, etc., issued Archer type coins. Apratigha type coins were issued by Kumaragupta I, while Apratighata type coins were issued by Samudragupta

questions.question_text: From which metal were the earliest punch-marked coins in India made?
questions.explanation: Literature on ancient Indian punch-marked coins is very minimal and gives scattered information. Similarly, excavation also sheds very little light on this. But the most coins found are made of silver, which are from the 3rd-4th century BC found from the excavation of the Bhir mound in Taxila. These were called Shatamana, which are found made in the context of 100 Ratti. These have been called punch-marked (Aahat) coins

questions.question_text: The rock temples of Mahabalipuram belong to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Mahabalipuram temples were built by the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I. This temple is a Hindu temple located in Tamil Nadu. Mahabalipuram was a port during the famous Pallava period. This temple, built in Dravidian architecture, is full of Lord Vishnu, Shore Temple, Pancha Ratha Temple, Descent of the Ganges monument, Tiger Cave, Krishna's Leela, etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following periods is known as the Golden Age of Indian currency?
questions.explanation: The Gupta period is considered the Golden Age of ancient India. Its main feature is that cultural and political achievements made the period attractive; the depiction of color, joy, celebration, and gatherings that occurred. The commercial development during this period and the developed organizational activities of symbolic craftsmen in the Mandsaur inscription, the creation of new agricultural areas, the abundance of gold coins, etc., have been considered by some scholars as indicative of the advanced economic condition of the Gupta period

questions.question_text: From which place punch-marked coins have not been obtained?
questions.explanation: The ancientmost coins of India are known by the names punch-marked or Aahat coins, which are actually pieces of metal of different shapes, sizes, and weights and on which one or more symbolic signs are printed. In archaeological literature, the words 'Purana' or 'Dharana' give information about these coins. These coins have been obtained from almost most places in India, among which Noha, Raid, and Sambhar, etc., of Rajasthan are major sites. Tilwara is located in Jabalpur of Madhya Pradesh. Gandhi ji's ashes were immersed at Tilwara Ghat

questions.question_text: Match the following and choose the correct group: List-I (Gupta Period Temples) / List-II (Place)

options.E: Parvati Temple / v. Deogarh Choose the correct answer using the codes given below:

questions.explanation: Dashavatara Temple - Ancient name Keshavpur, which is a significant example of Vaishnavism from the Gupta period at a place named Deogarh in Jhansi. Shiva Temple - Bhumara (Satna, Madhya Pradesh). Laxman Temple – Sirpur, built of bricks (Raipur, Chhattisgarh). Parvati Temple – Nachna-Kuthara, Madhya Pradesh. The subject matter of Gupta period temples is taken from Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas

questions.question_text: Who among the following has termed the Gupta era as the Golden Age?
questions.explanation: K.M. Munshi termed the Gupta era as the Golden Age

questions.question_text: Land grant by the state was a common thing in the early medieval period of Indian history. Which of the following statements does not correctly express the effect of land grants?

options.A: Agriculture expanded as a result of land grants.
options.B: The influence of a class of Brahmins in rural areas increased significantly.
options.C: Castes also expanded due to land grants. Tribes living on the fringes of land grant areas were included in agricultural work in these areas and given a place as untouchable castes in society.
options.D: The Brahmadeya and Agrahara areas of Tamil Nadu were parts of Ur and Sabha villages.

questions.explanation: Although the practice of land grant/donating land started with the Satavahana dynasty, its extensive use further increased in the Gupta period and post-Gupta period (early medieval period) False - The influence of a class of Brahmins in rural areas increased significantly. Although the position of Brahmins has always been good because the practice of donating villages to Brahmins and monks was started first. Effects - Feudalism; emergence of a new caste Kayastha; Shudras and Vaishyas as farmers; decline in trade (cause of the rise of feudal system).

questions.question_text: The Chinese traveler 'Song Yun' traveled to Gandhara around the middle of:
questions.explanation: Chinese traveler Song Yun came on a journey to Gandhara around 520 AD. In his account, he has written the name of the country of Kabul as 'Kiphin', which is a transformation of Kubha. In 'Kubha', Suvastu meets from the north and 'Krumu' and Gomatī meet from the south. The city of Kabul is situated on the banks of 'Kubha'

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one called Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R). Assertion (A): The period of the oldest paintings of Ajanta is considered to be the second and first century BC. Reason (R): Chronologically, the paintings of caves no. 1 and 2 are the latest and belong to the post-Gupta period. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The period of excavation of the thirty caves obtained from Ajanta was considered to be between the second century BC and the seventh century. Among these, Chaitya (temple) and Vihara (monastery) are prominent. The main attraction of the caves of Ajanta is considered to be the mural painting. The caves here are inspired by Buddhism and are permeated with sculpture and painting full of their compassionate feelings. Of the total 29 caves built in Ajanta, currently only cave numbers 1, 2, 9, 10, 16, 17 remain. In these 6 caves, cave numbers 16 and 17 are from the Gupta period, cave numbers 9 and 10 are the oldest (pre-Gupta period) and cave numbers 1, 2 are from the post-Gupta period. Ajanta was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1983

questions.question_text: The Vallabhi era is identified with –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – According to Al-Beruni, a king named Vallabha started the Vallabhi era 241 years after the Shaka era. The Shaka era is considered to have started in 78 AD. Therefore, the date of the Vallabhi era comes to 241 + 78 = 319 AD, which is the date of the Gupta era. Therefore, the Vallabhi era is identified with the Gupta era. Chandragupta I is also credited in history with starting a new era, which was called "Gupta Era" (Gupta Prakala) in later inscriptions. According to Fleet's calculation, this era was introduced in 319-20 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the Dharmashastra writers rejected 'Sati-practice' by calling it an act of suicide?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – An important evidence of the Sati practice is the Eran inscription of 510 AD, which describes the becoming of Sati by the wife of a general named Goparaja. This inscription was established in the form of a monument. In some military castes of North India, there was praise for widows dying by burning on a large scale. When military husbands were killed while fighting, women used to become Sati to protect their honor. Later, this practice reached the upper classes of Central India, Eastern India, and India and Nepal. Harshavardhana's mother Yashomati had become Sati in 604 AD on the mere possibility of her husband's death. He had saved Harsha's widowed sister Rajyashri from becoming Sati. Contrary to this, there is no evidence of any Gupta queen becoming Sati. Dharmashastrakara Medhatithi called the Sati practice a hateful act and a social evil. Opposing the Sati practice, he called it suicide.

questions.question_text: Which of the following plays was written by Shudraka?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - Shudraka was born in the Gupta period. His famous play is 'Mrichchhakatikam', which holds a prominent place among social plays. In its ten acts, the story of the ideal love between the Brahmin Charudatta, who is poor due to the cycle of time, and the famous courtesan of Ujjayini, Vasantasena, is described. Shudraka has achieved special success in the characterization of the characters. Shudraka has depicted the ideal citizen of India through Charudatta. In Vasantasena, we see the inclusion of many noble female qualities. Even after being a prostitute, she constantly tries to become the virtuous wife of Charudatta. The prosperity of that time is indicated by the play. It is also known that Brahmins had also started doing trade and commerce work. Charudatta's family was engaged in this profession for many generations. The style of Mrichchhakatikam is simple and the description is detailed. The use of all natural languages is found in it together. For the first time, in Sanskrit, Shudraka has made people of the middle class of society his characters, leaving aside the royal family.

questions.question_text: Who among the following has given a liberal interpretation of the property rights of widows?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - The beliefs expressed in the Yajnavalkya Smriti regarding the property rights of women are important. He has stated the wife also as the owner of the husband's property. In the absence of a son, the wife will have the first right on the man's property and after her, his daughters. This opinion is completely contrary to the laws of Manu, Apastamba, etc. Brihaspati and Narada have also said that a daughter is also an offspring like a son. Therefore, in the absence of a son, she should have a right to the property. Katyayana has stated the wife as the receiver of wealth (Dhanahari) and in her absence, the daughter. However, this subject was controversial. There were also such lawmakers who did not consider the widow to be the owner of the property. According to Narada, the property of a childless person should go to the state. Although it is the duty of the king to maintain the widow. Narada has called this Sanatana Dharma.

questions.question_text: What is meant by 'Dhruvadhi-karanika'?

options.A: A religious ritual in Hindu marriage
options.B: The official who collected the king's share of grain
options.D: Navigator who knows direction from stars

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- In the Gupta period, there were officials named 'Dhruvadhi-karana' for collecting land revenue and 'Mahakshapatalika' and 'Karanika' for keeping land records safe. Merchants named Nyayadhikarana used to settle land-related disputes. There was an excellent irrigation system. Gupta rulers had constructed wells, ponds, canals, etc. The son of Parnadatta, the governor of Junagarh, Chakrapalita, got the dam of Sudarshana Lake in Girnar reconstructed during the time of the Emperor. Those who practiced agriculture on royal land had to give a part of their yield to the king as tax, which was usually one-sixth. In Gupta inscriptions, the land tax is called Udranga and Bhagakara. In Smriti texts, it is called the king's Bali (Vritti). According to Narada, in exchange for protecting the subjects, the king is entitled to receive one-sixth of the harvest as revenue.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of the word 'Nala' mentioned in Gupta and post-Gupta inscriptions?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation— In the Gupta period, different revenues were collected from land. Nala, Kulyavapa, Dronavapa, and Pataka were units of land measurement in the Gupta and post-Gupta periods. Nala referred to a metal rod or a rope of the same length used for measuring land. The length of the Nala varied according to local traditions. In Gupta inscriptions, land tax was called 'Udranga' and 'Bhagakara'. In Smriti texts, it was called the king's 'Vritti' (livelihood). According to Narada, the king is entitled to one-sixth of the produce as revenue in exchange for protecting the subjects. In the Gupta period, only one-sixth part was taken as revenue. Land tax could be paid in both cash or grain. A major source of revenue was the toll (chungi) which was levied on goods coming into the city.

questions.question_text: In which Gupta period inscription is the detail regarding the sale of land given?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation— During the time of Kumaragupta I, three copper plates were obtained from Damodarpur (Dinajpur, Bangladesh). The third copper plate of Damodarpur provides details regarding the sale of land. The Damodarpur copper plate also contains details of many officials of the Kumaragupta era.

questions.question_text: Which of the following authors first described 'Varta' as the general occupation of the Shudra varna?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation— Among the Sutras, the Gautama Dharmasutra is considered the oldest. Gautama has determined the duties of all varnas. Gautama stated the social prestige of Brahmins to be supreme. The main duty of the King (Kshatriya) was to fight wars and rule. The Vaishyas maintained themselves through agriculture, cattle rearing, and commerce. The condition of Shudras was miserable. The social status of Vaishyas was gradually coming closer to Shudras. Gautama was the first to call 'Varta' (i.e., agriculture, cattle rearing, commerce) the general occupation of the Shudra varna. Varnas became rigid and turned into castes, the basis of which was considered birth rather than action. Inter-varna marriage and dining were clearly restricted. Shudras were considered the most degraded and rightless class of society. Along with the varna system, the Ashrama system was established with the objective of regulating a person's life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following authors first used the word 'Samanta' in the sense of a subordinate ruler?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation— Many socio-economic historians in the modern age have expressed their views on the origin and development of feudalism. However, the mention of the word 'Samanta' in Kautilya's Arthashastra was made in the sense of an "independent neighbor". Ashvaghosha (1st century) first used this word for a landlord (Jagirdar) in Buddhacharita. From the Gupta period, the word Samanta generally began to be used in this sense. The seeds of feudalism were sown in the Shaka-Kushana period and by the Rajput period, it became fully prevalent in society. It is known from the narrative of the Jain text 'Kalakacharya' that Shaka emperors were called 'Shahanushahi' and there were many Samantas (Shahi) under their subordination. The title 'Rajadhiraja' of Kushana emperors is also an indicator of the feudal system. Among the Shaka rulers of western India, the titles 'Mahakshatrapa' and 'Kshatrapa' were prevalent. Later, following them, the Gupta emperors adopted the title 'Maharajadhiraja'. In this way, feudalism became fully established in the political field during and after the Gupta period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following used to pay the Udranga tax?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation—In Gupta inscriptions, apart from 'Bhaga' and 'Bhoga', there is mention of taxes named 'Udranga' and 'Uparikara'. According to historians, Udranga was the land tax paid to the state. Farmers could pay land tax in both Hiranya (i.e., cash) or Meya (i.e., by weight of grain).

questions.question_text: Who had declared the 'Theory of Gravity' long before 'Newton's theory'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation—Long before Newton, the famous mathematician Brahmagupta discovered the theory of gravity. Aryabhatta discovered that the earth is round and revolves around the sun, and the earth has gravity. He also calculated the positions of the constellations. He understood the causes of lunar and solar eclipses. The name of his famous work is 'Aryabhatiyam'. Varahamihira was also a famous astrologer and his famous book is 'Brihat Samhita'. According to him, the moon revolves around the earth and the earth revolves around the sun. He acknowledged the debt to foreign Yavanas (Greeks) and Romans in the field of astrology.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is famous as the founder of the Veerashaiva sect?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation—The Veerashaiva or Lingayat sect was founded by Allama Prabhu and his disciple Basava. They acted contrary to the varna system and wore a silver Shivalinga around their necks. There are 5 great men (Mahapurushas) considered in this sect—Renukacharya, Darukacharya, Ekoramacharya, Panditradhya, and Shivaradhya. In this philosophy, selfless action (nishkama karma) is given prominence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following authors considered the Narmada river as the line dividing Aryavarta and Dakshinapatha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation—Under Dakshinapatha, the entire region from the Narmada river in the north to the Tungabhadra river in the south was included. In ancient literature, the boundary of Dakshinapatha was stated to be up to Mahishamandala in the south. In a broader sense, this word was used for the vast land area located between the Vindhya mountains and the southern sea. In Natyashastra, the boundary of Dakshinapatha was expressed by saying 'Dakshinasya samudrasya vindhyasya chantare'. In Matsya Purana, its northern boundary was stated to be Karusha (the area around the Kaimur hills of the eastern Vindhyas). In Kavyamimansa by Rajasekhara, Dakshinapatha is considered beyond Mahishmati and Narmada.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are famous for their criticism of the Sati system? 1. Kalidasa 2. Bana 3. Medhatithi 4. Madhava Select the correct answer from the code below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation—Around the fourth century AD, the Sati system began to gain popularity. Authors like Vatsyayana, Bhasa, Kalidasa, and Shudraka have mentioned it. The first epigraphic evidence of the prevalence of the Sati system is from the Gupta period. From the Eran inscription of 510 AD, it is known that Goparaja, a friend of the Gupta king Bhanugupta, was killed while fighting the Hunas, then his wife burnt herself to death in fire. But the great poet Banabhatta, while opposing it, called it a great foolish act which has no result. This is suicide, by following which a woman goes to hell. Medhatithi, considering it suicide, states it to be prohibited for women. Devabhatta's view is that becoming Sati is more heinous than a widow living as a Brahmachari.

questions.question_text: From which of the following did the word 'Dinar', used for gold coins in Gupta inscriptions, originate?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation—The word Dinar is derived from the word 'Denarius', which is a Latin word. The circulation of Dinar coins was based on Roman coins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following temples was built of bricks?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Among the Gupta period temples, the temple of Bhitargaon located in the Kanpur district of Uttar Pradesh is built of bricks. Also, another temple built of bricks has been obtained from a place named Sirpur in the Raipur district of Madhya Pradesh, of which only the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha) remains. It is called the 'Lakshmana Temple'. Its architecture is similar to the Bhitargaon temple.

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions is the word 'Mahasamanta' first mentioned?

options.C: Damodarpur Copper Plate Inscription of Kumaragupta

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The word 'Mahasamanta' is first mentioned in the Gunaighar Inscription of the Gupta ruler Vainyagupta. In the 16th line of this inscription, there is a mention of his Mahasamanta Upairika Maharaja Vijayasena and Rudradatta - (Upairika Maharaja - Shri Mahasamanta - Vijayasena). In this inscription, Vainyagupta is called 'Bhagavan Mahadevpadanudhyata'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation— 'Ratnavali' is a play by Harsha. It is noteworthy that the Vardhana dynasty emperor Harshavardhana is considered the author of three Sanskrit plays—Priyadarshika, Ratnavali, and Nagananda. Ratnavali is a play in 4 acts, in which a very interesting description of the love story of Vatsaraja Udayana and his queen Vasavadatta's attendant 'Ratnavali' (Sagarika) is given. Nagananda is a work influenced by Buddhism, it has five acts. This play describes the story of the self-sacrifice of a Vidyadhara prince named Jimutavahana. Priyadarshika describes the love story of Vatsaraja Udayana's inner quarters (antahpura).

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements— Assertion (A): According to Mitakshara, a father could divide his property among his sons during his lifetime. Reason (R): Mitakshara did not recognize the son's right by birth in ancestral property. Select the correct answer from the code given below:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– Vijnaneshwara, the commentator on Yajnavalkya Smriti, propounded the principle in his book Mitakshara that sons have the right to get the division of property from their father. Vijnaneshwara recognized the son's right in the property as soon as he is born.

questions.question_text: The Poona copper plate inscription is related to:
questions.explanation: The Poona copper plate inscription is related to Prabhavati Gupta. Prabhavati Gupta was the daughter of Chandragupta II, who was married into the Vakataka dynasty. Prabhavati Gupta held an important position in the governing power. Influenced by this, she got the Poona copper plate inscribed

questions.question_text: Rupaka coins were in circulation:

options.A: During the reign of the Mauryas
options.B: During the reign of the Kushanas
options.C: During the reign of the Shungas
options.D: During the reign of the Guptas

questions.explanation: The silver coin was called the Rupaka coin. These coins were issued by the Gupta rulers. Chandragupta II was the first to issue silver coins

questions.question_text: Ajanta caves are located in:
questions.explanation: Ajanta caves are located in Maharashtra. Their number is 29, some of which are about 100 feet deep and are carved in the shape of a horse-shoe. Ajanta caves number 16, 17, and 19 are of the Gupta period

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a feudatory (Samanta) of the Gupta kings?
questions.explanation: Sendraka was not a feudatory of the Gupta kings. While Parivrajaka, Varmana, Uchchhakalpa, etc., were feudatories of the Guptas

questions.question_text: Which Smritikar mentioned giving a woman her inheritance?
questions.explanation: Gautama was the first to mention giving a woman her inheritance (share in ancestral property) in his book Gautama Smriti. This is the oldest Smriti/Dharma Sutra. In this, the king is stated to be the ruler of all other classes. A long list of taxes is found in this same book

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correct?
questions.explanation: List-I List-II Champa – Annam Sumatra – Srivijaya Siam – Thailand Cambodia – Yashodharpur

questions.question_text: Which ruler made a significant contribution to the development of Vikramshila University?
questions.explanation: Vikramshila University was founded by the Pala ruler Dharmapala; he is called 'Paramsaugata' in his inscriptions. Like Dharmapala, Devapala was also a follower of Buddhism. After the death of Dharmapala, Devapala also contributed to the development of Vikramshila University. Vikramshila is located in the present Bhagalpur district of Bihar. In this university, education in grammar, logic, Mimansa, Tantra, jurisprudence, etc., was given

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the author of Dayabhaga?
questions.explanation: Dayabhaga is an ancient Hindu religious text written by Jimutavahana, whose philosophy is prevalent in Bengal. The literal meaning of Dayabhaga is - division of ancestral wealth, i.e., the system of dividing the property of a father, grandfather, or relative among sons or relatives

questions.question_text: Arrange the following chronologically and choose the correct option from the given alternatives:
questions.explanation: Manusmriti was composed in 220 BC, Ramayana in 31 BC, Charaka Samhita in 78 AD during the time of Kanishka, and Kumarasambhava is a work of the Gupta period

questions.question_text: According to Mitakshara, a son has a right to ancestral property:

options.A: As soon as he is born
options.D: After the death of both his mother and father

questions.explanation: In the Rigvedic period, the father had a monopoly over the family's property. Yajnavalkya propounded the principle of property rights in Mitakshara that the son has a right to his property during the father's lifetime itself

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct regarding the different statuses given to mixed castes in Manusmriti?

options.A: Children born from a wife of one varna lower in the varna system were accepted as a part of the Dvijas.
options.B: Children born from a woman two or three degrees lower according to varna status formed a new group among Shudras.
options.C: If the woman's status was higher than the man's status, the offspring of such marriages were placed below the parents' statuses.
options.D: Anuloma marriage was considered much more of a violation of the sacred law than Pratiloma marriage.

questions.explanation: Manusmriti is an ancient Dharmashastra of Hinduism. It is also known by names like Manava Dharmashastra, Manu Samhita, etc. A detailed description of the varna system is found in Manusmriti. According to it, children born from a wife of one varna lower in the varna system were accepted as part of the Dvijas. Children born from a woman two or three degrees lower according to varna status formed a new group among Shudras. If the woman's status was higher than the man's status, then the offspring of such marriages were placed below the parents' statuses. Pratiloma marriage was considered much more of a violation of the sacred law than Anuloma marriage

questions.question_text: Who was the first famous knower of astrology in ancient India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation—Aryabhatta was the first knower of astrology in ancient India. Astrology and astronomy developed during the Gupta period. The famous astrologers of the Gupta period are Aryabhatta I and Varahamihira. Aryabhatta was a great mathematician as well as a famous astronomer. Aryabhatta was born in Pataliputra around 476 AD. At the age of 23 (499 AD), he composed his book 'Aryabhatiyam'. Aryabhatta discovered that the earth is round and revolves around the sun and that the earth has gravity.

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Panchatantra'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation— Vishnu Sharma composed 'Panchatantra'. This is a famous collection of stories in which many stories of ancient times have been compiled. Vishnu Sharma was a luminary of the Gupta period. It is said that it was composed with the objective of making the foolish sons of a king named Amarkirti scholars by educating them. Panchatantra has been translated into many languages.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Indian mathematicians discovered the decimal place value?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The use of the zero digit and decimal is a unique contribution of India to mathematics. Indians were the first to use the decimal; the famous mathematician Aryabhatta had knowledge of this, he discovered the decimal place value while calculating the value of pi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ancient Smritikars has placed widows after sons in relation to inheritance?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The ancient Smritikar Yajnavalkya has described women's inheritance. He has clarified the woman's right to property and has placed the widow after the son in inheritance.

questions.question_text: Who was the Chancellor of Nalanda University during Harsha's reign?
questions.explanation: Shilabhadra * The first Chancellor was Nagarjuna, who was famous for chemistry.

questions.question_text: Which state located in the southern part of Central Asia was a major center of Indian civilization in the 4th century AD?
questions.explanation: Khotan, located in the southern part of Central Asia, was a major center of Indian culture in the 4th century AD. According to Buddhist tradition, Ashoka's son Kunala had established a Hindu kingdom. Khotan was a major center of the Mahayana branch of Buddhism

questions.question_text: Which was the first Hindu kingdom in Southeast Asia?
questions.explanation: Srivijaya was the first Hindu kingdom in Southeast Asia. According to the Chinese traveler I-tsing, Srivijaya was a major center of Buddhism. The architecture of Southeast Asia includes the Borobudur Stupa of Java, the Angkor Wat temple of Kamboja (Cambodia), the Ananda Temple of Burma, etc

questions.question_text: Who was Bhaskaracharya's daughter, who is known in India for her book on mathematics?
questions.explanation: Lilavati was Bhaskaracharya's daughter who is known for her book on mathematics. Bhaskaracharya was a famous mathematician and astrologer of ancient India. His main work is 'Siddhanta Shiromani', which has 4 parts named Lilavati, Bijaganita, Grahaganita, and Goladhyaya

questions.question_text: In which of the following places is it considered that Harsha held two great religious assemblies?
questions.explanation: Emperor Harshavardhana organized two great religious assemblies in Prayag and Kannauj

questions.question_text: In which period did the concept of Ardhanarishvara, the combined form of Shiva and Shakti in Shaivism, arise?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation—The concept of Ardhanarishvara, the combined form of Shiva and Shakti in Shaivism, arose in the Gupta period. It was during the Gupta period itself that the worship of the Trimurti began, under which Brahma (the creator), Vishnu (the preserver), and Mahesh or Shiva (the destroyer) were worshipped. The concept of Ardhanarishvara, the combined form of Shiva and Shakti, is imagined in Kalidasa's epic 'Kumarasambhava'.

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Mudrarakshasa'?
questions.explanation: Mudrarakshasa is a historical Sanskrit play composed by Vishakhadatta. In this, an analysis of the political successes of Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya is found. The plot of Mudrarakshasa is famous; in it, Rakshasa becomes stunned/helpless upon seeing his own seal (mudra) being used against himself. In this, the story of Chanakya's foiling of Rakshasa's political claims after Chandragupta's accession is expressed in 7 acts

questions.question_text: Where is Harsha called 'Sakala-uttarapatha-nath' (Lord of all North India)?
questions.explanation: Harsha is called 'Sakala-uttarapatha-nath' in the Chalukya inscription (Aihole inscription). Harsha (606-647 AD) was an important ruler of North India who achieved significant accomplishments in the cultural field (religion, literature, etc.) along with politics

questions.question_text: The scholar who was not in the court of Harshavardhana—
questions.explanation: Harsha was not only a scholar and lover of learning himself but was also a generous patron of scholars. Many poets and writers resided in Harsha's court. Among these, the names of Banabhatta, Mayurbhatta, and Matanga Divakara are particularly noteworthy

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vakataka rulers performed 'four Ashvamedha sacrifices' and assumed the title of Emperor?
questions.explanation: The Vakataka dynasty ruler Pravarasena I assumed the title of 'Emperor' and performed 4 Ashvamedha sacrifices and one Vajapeya sacrifice

questions.question_text: Which deity has been mentioned as Lokarka during the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: Sun worship was prevalent during the Gupta period. In Kalidasa's Raghuvamsa, seven green horses of the Sun are mentioned, and during the reign of Kumaragupta, a guild of silk weavers built a Sun temple in Dashapura near Mandsaur. In many inscriptions, names like Lokarka, Bhaskara, Aditya, Martanda, Varunasvami, etc., are found for the Sun

questions.question_text: What was the first example of advertising in ancient India?
questions.explanation: The description of the achievements of the reign of the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I is found in the Mandsaur Inscription. The first example of advertising in ancient India was also found in this inscription

questions.question_text: Where is the Varaha avatar statue of Vishnu from the Gupta period located?
questions.explanation: The Gupta emperors were worshippers of Vaishnavism. The statue of the Varaha avatar of Lord Vishnu is found in the Udayagiri caves. These caves were built by Chandragupta Vikramaditya

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): The Gupta period is often called the Classical Age in the field of cultural development. Reason (R): While praising the artistic ideals of the Gupta period, the argument is given that this is an age in which an amazing development of artistic activities was seen. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The reign of the Gupta emperors represents that age of ancient Indian history in which unprecedented progress occurred in every field of civilization and culture, and Hindu culture reached the pinnacle of its excellence. Taking into account the all-round progress of the Gupta period, historians have designated this period as the 'Golden Age'. This period has also been known by names like the cultural 'Classical Age' or the 'Periclean Age' of India. The following features made the Gupta period the Golden Age of Indian history— 1 - Age of political unity 2 - Age of great emperors 3 - Age of excellent administration system 4 - Age of economic prosperity 5 - Age of religious tolerance 6 - Age of the pinnacle of literature, science, and art 7 - Age of propagation of Indian culture, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (Rulers of Dakshinapatha of the pre-Gupta/early Gupta period)—(Their Kingdoms)
questions.explanation: Samudragupta was a powerful ruler of the Gupta dynasty. He defeated nine rulers of North India (Aryavarta). Among the defeated kings, Achyuta, Nagasena, and Ganapatinaga were prominent. He had also defeated twelve rulers of Dakshinapatha, who are as follows—Koshala, Mahakantara, Kaurala, Pishtapura, Erandapalla, Kanchi, Avamukta, Vengi, Palakka, Devarashtra, and Kusthalapura. His southern expedition reached as far as Kanchi. The names and regions are mentioned in the Prayag Prashasti. In the question, Mantaraja is not matched. Mantaraja was the ruler of Koshala

questions.question_text: In the Gupta period, Sarthavaha was the name given to:
questions.explanation: In the Gupta period, commercial bodies were divided based on their actual work or nature. There was a committee of traders which was called Nigama. The head of the Nigama was called Shreshthi. The group of traders was called Sartha and their leaders were called Sarthavaha. Nagara Shreshthins worked as bankers and moneylenders

questions.question_text: From where have the Jain statues containing Gupta period Brahmi inscriptions been obtained?
questions.explanation: From the perspective of development of art and literature, the Gupta period was called the 'Classical Age' or Golden Age of Indian history. Jain statues containing Gupta period Brahmi inscriptions have been obtained from Durjanpur near Vidisha. Although the Gupta rulers were followers of Vaishnavism, they also recognized other religions. Among the Buddhist cave temples of their reign, the Ajanta and Bagh caves are important

questions.question_text: During the Gupta period, the 'Minister of War and Peace' was known as:
questions.explanation: The central administration of the Gupta Empire was divided into several departments. For example—Sandhivigrahika was related to matters of war and peace (War Minister). The commander-in-chief was called Mahabaladhikrita. Mahadandanayaka was called a Judge. The highest official of the Gupta Empire was called Kumaramatya

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists— List-I (Contemporary kings of Samudragupta in South India) List-II (Their Kingdoms)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation—The correct match is as follows— Dhananjaya – Kusthalapura Nilaraja – Avamukta Ugrasena – Palakka Vishnugopa – Kanchi

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions of Samudragupta is he called 'Parama-Bhagavata'? (i) Gaya copper-plate (ii) Nalanda copper-plate (iii) Eran pillar inscription (iv) Allahabad pillar inscription Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation—In the 'Gaya copper-plate' and 'Nalanda copper-plate' inscriptions, Samudragupta is called 'Parama Bhagavata'. Detailed light is shed on Samudragupta's coronation, conquests, and personality in the Allahabad pillar inscription. In the Eran pillar inscription, Samudragupta is considered more charitable than kings like Prithu and Raghav.

questions.question_text: Which Chola ruler adopted the titles 'Maduraikonda' and 'Madurantaka'?
questions.explanation: Parantaka I (907-955 AD) was the son of Aditya I and became king after his death. He was the real founder of the Chola dynasty and the first sovereign or all-powerful ruler of his dynasty. He attacked the Pandyan ruler Rajasimha II of Madurai and defeated him in the battle of Vellore. On the occasion of the victory over Madurai, he adopted the title 'Maduraikonda'. His other titles were—Madurantaka, Virachola, and Sangramaghava

questions.question_text: In which inscription is the conquest of Tanjore by the Chola ruler Vijayalaya mentioned?
questions.explanation: Inscriptions are the most authentic sources of Chola history, which have been found in large numbers. In these, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada languages have been used. Chola history after Vijayalaya (850-871 AD) is mainly known through inscriptions. The mention of the victory of Tanjore by Chola ruler Vijayalaya is found in the Tiruvedungalam inscription. The main inscriptions of the time of Rajendra I are Tiruvalangadu and Karandai grant plates, which give a description of his achievements. From a historical perspective, the most important inscription is the Tiruvendipuram inscription of the time of Rajaraja III

questions.question_text: According to Chinese sources, which of the following Chola rulers sent an embassy to China to promote trade?
questions.explanation: Kulottunga I was a valiant king and a great administrator of the Chola dynasty. Kulottunga made many reforms in the internal administration of the Chola Empire, of which the most important reform was that he conducted land surveys twice (1086 AD and 1110 AD) and fixed taxes based on the yield of different areas. He removed many painful taxes. He established diplomatic and political relations with foreign states. In 1077 AD, he sent an embassy of 72 merchants to the court of the Chinese ruler

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chola rulers persecuted Ramanuja and expelled him from his kingdom?
questions.explanation: Kulottunga II was the successor ruler of Vikramachola. He was religiously intolerant. He had the idol of Govindaraj, installed in the courtyard of the Nataraja temple, removed and thrown into the sea, and Ramanuja recovered this idol and installed it in Tirupati. For this reason, he had Ramanuja exiled from his kingdom Note- The Commission has considered Kulottunga I (option a) for this question, but Ancient History of India by Dr. Vimal Chandra Pandey and D.P. Mahajan considers it to be Kulottunga II.

questions.question_text: Which of these dynasties was actively involved in countering maritime piracy in the Strait of Malacca in Southeast Asia?
questions.explanation: A characteristic of the Chola army was that they had a naval fleet organization. It was because of this powerful naval fleet that the Chola kings conquered the sea or many islands. In this context, the Cholas provided security from pirates to the maritime trade passing through the Strait of Malacca in Southeast Asia and also established a place for a standing army in the seas. They even created a 'Chola Lake' in the Bay of Bengal. The operation of this navy was carried out by the Cholas according to rank

questions.question_text: During the reign of which of these dynasties was the 'Kaikkolar' community of weavers and merchants given more participation in temple administration and land ownership rights?
questions.explanation: In the Chola dynasty, the Kaikkolar or Kaikkolar community was a class of weavers and merchants, but they also maintained armies. They had major commercial and military roles during the Chola period. During the reign of the Imperial Chola rulers from the 10th to 13th centuries, they had a large participation in temple administration and land ownership; the credit for this is given to the change in wealth and power. The class of weavers and merchants was made skilled and prosperous. Land ownership was no longer the exclusive privilege of Brahmins and Vellalar landowners. This system continued until the Vijayanagara Empire A. Achievements of Rajaraja I

questions.question_text: Arumolivarman was the name of which Chola emperor?
questions.explanation: The initial name of Rajaraja I was Arumolivarman, who sat on the throne in 985 AD in the name of Rajaraja I. The history of the extensive victory and prosperity of the Cholas starts from the reign of Rajaraja I. His wars are described in the Tanjore inscription engraved in the nineteenth year of his reign. The greatest achievement of Rajaraja I and an example of naval prowess was the conquest of 1200 islands of the Lakshadweep and Maldives groups. Rajaraja I conquered the entire Dravida region, Karnataka, Andhra, Kalinga, and Lanka (Northern Lanka)

questions.question_text: Which Chola ruler introduced his gold and copper coins in Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The initial name of Rajaraja I was Arumolivarman, who sat on the throne in 985 AD. Information is obtained from an inscription of Rajaraja I that he defeated the kings of Kollam, Kollamdesh, and Kodungallur and made the ruler of the sea serve him. After conquering the Kerala and Pandya kingdoms, Rajaraja destroyed Anuradhapura and he issued gold, silver, and copper coins. The description of his military campaigns is obtained from the Tanjore inscription

questions.question_text: Who was the first ruler to conquer the Maldives among the following Chola rulers?
questions.explanation: The revival of the Cholas took place in the 9th century under the leadership of Vijayalaya. The Chola dynasty was founded by Vijayalaya. Later, the most important ruler of this dynasty was Rajaraja I (985-1014 AD). He conquered Pandya, Kerala, and Simhala. He conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka and took control over it. An important victory of Rajaraja was that of the Maldives. The conquest of the Maldives was the final victory of Rajaraja I. He adopted major titles like Nityavinoda, Shivapadasekhara, Cholamartanda, etc

questions.question_text: Who was the Srivijaya ruler who completed the construction work of the Buddhist Vihara started by his father in Nagapattinam during the time of Rajaraja I?
questions.explanation: During the time of Chola ruler Rajaraja I, the Chudamani Vihara started in Nagapattinam by the Shailendra dynasty ruler of Srivijaya was completed by Vijay's son Maravijayottungavarman, for the maintenance of which Rajaraja had given villages in donation

questions.question_text: During the reign of which Chola king did dependent officials take the place of hereditary landholders in many places?
questions.explanation: Before the reign of Rajaraja-I, a large part of the Chola region was ruled by hereditary kings and local princes, who were in a loose alliance with the Chola rulers. After this, until the reign of Vikram Chola in 1133 AD, when Chola power was at its peak, these hereditary lords and local princes disappeared from Chola inscriptions, either they were replaced or changed into dependent officials. Through these dependent officials, administration improved and the Chola kings became capable of controlling different parts of the empire. The expansion of the administrative structure first started after the reign of Rajaraja I, in which the government had a large land revenue department which was divided at many levels. Its large-scale maintenance and assessment and collection of revenue were done by corporate bodies like Ur, Nadu, Sabha, Nagaram, and sometimes by local chiefs who gave revenue to the center. During the reign of Rajaraja I, a massive project of land survey and assessment was started and the empire was reorganized into units named Valanadu

questions.question_text: Which Chola ruler performed sacrifices named Hemagarbha and Tulabhara?
questions.explanation: The first sovereign Chola ruler was Parantaka I and he performed sacrifices named Hemagarbha and Tulabhara. In the battle of Vellore, he defeated the combined army of the Pandya and Simhala kings and took control over Madurai

questions.question_text: What was the name of Rajaraja I's mother?
questions.explanation: Rajaraja I (985 – 1015 AD) is considered the first powerful ruler of the Chola Empire. His father's name was Sundara Chola and his mother's name was Vanavan Mahadevi. He had built the famous Rajarajeshwara Temple, Brihadisvara Temple, of Tanjore

questions.question_text: For the determination of land revenue, which of the following Chola rulers started the land survey in his kingdom?
questions.explanation: With the accession of Rajaraja I in 985 AD, the era of greatness in Chola history began. Rajaraja I conducted a land survey in 1000 AD for the determination of land revenue and encouraged local self-government in his entire kingdom and conducted audits of village assemblies and self-governed corporations to prevent the misuse of public funds. It is known from contemporary inscriptions that the measure of the foot of Rajaraja I and Kulottunga was the measurement for land surveying

questions.question_text: The greatness of the rulers of the Chola dynasty was based on which work?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation– An excellent governance system was the greatest achievement of the rulers of the Chola dynasty. In addition to excellent central administration, the Cholas created local autonomous rural institutions endowed with extraordinary power and capability. In the records of Parantaka I, descriptions of institutions named Ur, Sabha or Mahasabha, and Nagaram are found.

questions.question_text: Give the chronological order of the following and select the correct answer from the given codes: (i) Rajaraja Chola I (ii) Aditya Chola (iii) Rajendra Chola (iv) Parantaka Chola I Codes:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation–The correct order of the given codes is as follows – (a) Aditya Chola (871-907 AD) (b) Parantaka Chola I (907-955 AD) (c) Rajaraja Chola I (985-1014 AD) (d) Rajendra Chola (1015-1044 AD).

questions.question_text: Rajarajeshwar temple is dedicated to:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation–Rajarajeshwar or Brihadisvara Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It was built by Chola ruler Rajaraja I in Tanjore. It is the largest among the temples of India and is a symbol of the peak of Dravidian architecture.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chola rulers started the practice of giving a 'historical introduction' at the beginning of royal inscriptions?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation–Rajaraja Chola started the practice of giving a 'historical introduction' at the beginning of royal inscriptions. His original name was Arumolivarman. In an inscription found in Karnataka, he has been called 'Chola Narayana'.

questions.question_text: Which Chola ruler allowed the Shailendra ruler of Srivijaya, Shrimar Vijayottungavarman, to build a Buddhist monastery in Negapatam?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation–Chola ruler Rajaraja I (985-1015 AD) allowed the Shailendra ruler of Srivijaya, Shrimar Vijayottungavarman, to build a Buddhist monastery in Negapatam.

questions.question_text: The Cholas established their empire by ending the rule of whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- After the reign of Karikala, the political power of the Cholas declined and until the middle of the 9th century AD, their history became full of darkness. Chola power was revived in the middle of the 9th century (around 850 AD). At that time, we find a powerful Chola king named Vijayalaya ruling in the area near Uraiyur (Tiruchirappalli) as a feudatory of the Pallavas. Uraiyur was the ancient residence of the Cholas. At this time, there were constant conflicts between the Pallavas and the Pandyas. Taking advantage of the weak position of the Pandyas, Vijayalaya took control over Tanjore and re-established the Chola state. There he built a temple for the goddess Durga. Vijayalaya ruled until about 871 AD.
