questions.question_text: Who was that Chola king during whose reign the Brihadisvara Temple of Tanjore was built?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - A fine example of Chola architecture is the Brihadisvara Temple, the credit for whose construction goes to Rajaraja I. This temple was built around 1000 AD. It is a massive temple which is 82 feet long and its pyramid-shaped shikhara is 190 feet high. The four parts of this temple are connected to each other on the same axis. These parts are - Nandi Mandapa, Ardhamandapa, Mandapa, and Garbhagriha. The whole temple is built within a boundary wall. The most important parts of the temple are the Garbhagriha and the Shikhara. In the words of Percy Brown, the Brihadisvara Temple of Tanjore is the best work of Dravidian craftsmanship and the touchstone of Indian architecture. B. Achievements of Rajendra Chola I

questions.question_text: Which one of the following Chola rulers conquered the entire Ceylon (Simhala)?
questions.explanation: After Rajaraja I, his son Rajendra I sat on the throne and he proved to be a great conqueror like his father. After hoisting his victory flag in the Indian subcontinent, Rajendra I carried out a military campaign in Southeast Asia. Like his father, Rajendra I also attacked Lanka (Simhala) in 1017 AD. The king of Lanka, Mahinda V, was defeated and was sent to the Chola kingdom as a prisoner, where he died in prison after 12 years. Control was established over the entire Simhala

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chola rulers had conquered Sumatra and Malaya?
questions.explanation: After Rajaraja I, his son Rajendra I sat on the throne and he proved to be a great conqueror like his father. After hoisting his victory flag in the Indian subcontinent, Rajendra I carried out a military campaign in Southeast Asia. According to the Tiruvalangadu copper-plate inscription, Rajendra I's naval fleet crossed the sea and conquered Kataha or Kedaram (Sumatra), the capital of the Srivijaya empire, and took the ruler there, Sangrama Vijayottungavarman, as a prisoner. Rajendra I adopted the title of 'Kadaramkonda' on the occasion of the victory over Kedaram. In the course of victory over the Srivijaya empire, apart from Kedaram, he took control over cities like Pannai, Malaiyur, Mappappalam, Ilangasoka, etc. All these places were located in the Malay Peninsula

questions.question_text: Who built the Brihadisvara Temple in Gangaikondacholapuram?
questions.explanation: A very notable military campaign during the reign of Rajendra I was the attack on Bengal via Kalinga. This attack was led by Vikram Chola. In 1022-23 AD, the Chola general attacked the Pala ruler Mahipala and defeated him. The purpose of this campaign was to bring the holy water of the Ganges River. In memory of this victory, Rajendra I adopted the title of 'Gangaikondachola'. He settled a new capital at the mouth of the Kaveri and named it Gangaikondacholapuram and here he built the Brihadisvara Temple

questions.question_text: Which of these Chola rulers had the title 'Gangaikonda'?
questions.explanation: Rajendra I was the greatest ruler of the Chola dynasty. Through his great victories, he expanded the Chola Empire and made it the most powerful empire in South India. He adopted the title of 'Gangaikonda' and established a new capital named Gangaikondacholapuram. It was here that he also built a huge reservoir named Chola Gangam

questions.question_text: The Chola Gangam pond was built by
questions.explanation: Rajendra I, included among the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty, ruled from 1015-1044 AD. Rajendra I defeated the Pala ruler Mahipala of Bengal in the North. On the success of this campaign in the Ganges Valley, Rajendra adopted the title of 'Gangaikonda' and on its occasion, he established a new capital named Gangaikondacholapuram. He built a huge pond named Chola Gangam for irrigation near the new capital

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chola rulers was declared king on the battlefield?
questions.explanation: Rajendra II was the younger brother of Rajadhiraja and despite the murder of Rajadhiraja in the battlefield of Koppam, he defeated the Chalukyas of Kalyani in this very field and had his coronation done in the battlefield itself. In 1062 AD, the Chalukyas (Somesvara I) were defeated by the Chola armies in the battle of Kudal-sangamam

questions.question_text: From whose time did Gangaikondacholapuram become the capital of the Chola Empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 TGT History, 2004 PGT - 2016 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation─ Rajendra I had collected jars filled with Ganges water from the defeated kings of Bengal with great respect in the newly built lake named 'Cholagangam'. On this occasion, he adopted the title of 'Gangaikonda'. He also had a victory pillar consecrated with Ganges water built. Around the said lake filled with Ganges water, he laid out his new capital 'Gangaikondacholapuram' which is located in the present Tiruchirappalli district of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question_text: Which Pala king did Rajendra Chola defeat?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Rajendra Chola had defeated the Pala king Mahipala I. Rajendra Chola sent the army under the leadership of his son Vikram Chola. After conquering Govindachandra, he attacked the Pala ruler Mahipala of Bengal and defeated him too. The defeated Pala king fled from the battlefield. The purpose of this campaign was to bring the holy water of the Ganges.

questions.question_text: Who was the real founder of the Cholas in South India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011"} Explanation - Parantaka I is considered the real founder of the Cholas in South India. He defeated the Pandyan ruler Rajasimha II of Madurai and assumed the title 'Maduraikondan'.

questions.question_text: The emblem of the Chola rulers was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation- The emblem of the Chola rulers was the 'Tiger'. It was located between the Pennar and Vellaru rivers in Tamil Nadu. The earliest mention of the Chola dynasty was made by Katyayana. The greatest ruler of this dynasty was Karikala. He established the coastal capital named Kaveripattinam.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chola rulers attacked Srivijaya?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Among the Chola rulers, Rajendra I was such a ruler who attacked Srivijaya. The Chola naval fleet crossed the Bay of Bengal, defeated the Srivijaya King Sangrama Vijayottungavarman, and captured his 12 islands.

questions.question_text: Who among the following rulers of the Chola dynasty first launched a naval expedition against South-East Asia?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – Rajendra Chola I, after unfurling his victory banner in the Indian subcontinent, conducted a military campaign in South-East Asia. He sent a powerful army to conquer the Srivijaya (Shailendra) kingdom. This kingdom included the Malay Peninsula, Java, Sumatra, and other islands. This campaign of his was completely successful. The Shailendra ruler Sangrama Vijayottungavarman was defeated and taken prisoner. The account of this military campaign is found in the Tiruvalangadu copper plate. This victory is also discussed in the Karandai copper plates engraved in the 8th year of Rajendra's reign.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chola rulers had the title 'Pandit Chola'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Rajendra I was the son of the Chola ruler Rajaraja I. He ruled from 1015 to 1044 AD. His titles were - Gangaikonda, Vira Rajendra, Kadaramgonda, Mudigondachola, Panditchola, Parakesarivarman, Nigrilichola. V.A. Smith has also called him the 'Napoleon of the South'. The title 'Panditchola' of Chola ruler Rajendra I confirms his love for learning. C. Autonomous Local Government System

questions.question_text: What was 'Ur'?
questions.explanation: The greatest feature of Chola administration was its autonomous institutions. These institutions existed before the Cholas, but Rajendra Chola organized them systematically Ur - The village assembly was called Udhar or Ur or Sabha. Kottam or village were of two types: general villages in which members of all castes lived were called Ur. The assembly of such villages was called Ur or Urar. Villages of the second category were those given in donation to scholars.

questions.question_text: Under Chola village administration, 'Erivariyam' was
questions.explanation: During the Chola period, under village administration, Erivariyam was also known by the name of tank committee, whose work was to take care of and repair the tank, for which a regular tax named Eriyayam was collected. Its number of members was 6

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the revenue officer of the Chola dynasty?
questions.explanation: The rise of the Chola Empire took place in the 9th century. This empire was established by Vijayalaya. Among the main rulers of this period, Rajaraja I and Rajendra I hold important places. In this period, the revenue officer's work was looked after by Varitpottagakka. The Mahasabha had ownership over public land. Members of the Sabha were called Perumakkal

questions.question_text: During the time of Cholas, the executive of the Ur was called
questions.explanation: 'Ur' was a general type of village assembly (of common people) in which both village Pur or Nagaram were included. The literal meaning of Ur is Pur. Its executive committee was called Alunganam

questions.question_text: The medium of tax collection in Chola rule was:
questions.explanation: Chola administration is famous in the history of ancient India and in self-governance, the village assemblies that existed were given significant powers. The authority to collect taxes was given to the village assemblies in Chola rule

questions.question_text: In the context of the election of the Uttaramerur assembly of the Chola period, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: The village was divided into 30 sub-divisions (wards).
options.B: Two representatives were elected from each sub-division.
options.C: The age of the candidates used to be between 35 and 70 years.
options.D: It was mandatory for them to have some educational qualification and immovable property.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation – Uttaramerur Sabha - In the 9th regnal year of Chola Emperor Parantaka I, the Uttaramerur assembly passed a resolution and fixed the rules for the executive committee- - Each village was divided into 30 sub-divisions. - One representative was elected from each sub-division. - Candidates were between 35-70 years of age. - It was mandatory for them to have some educational qualification and immovable property. - Election was based on the lottery system.

questions.question_text: To which department was 'Udasin Variyam' related in Chola administration?
questions.explanation: Regarding Udasin Variyam, some scholars believe that it was an institution of ascetics, but its work was to look after foreigners. An executive committee used to work in Chola village administration. The Sabha worked mainly through its committees. These have been called 'Variyam'. These committees looked after the work of different departments. Like- 'Tottavariyam-Garden-committee', 'Nyayattar Variyam- Justice committee'

questions.question_text: Arrange the following chronologically and select the correct answer from the code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The chronological arrangement of the given code is as follows – Virarajendra-I (1064 AD to 1070 AD), Vikrama Chola (1120 AD to 1133 AD), Rajaraja-II (1150 AD to 1173 AD), Kulottunga-III (1179 AD to 1218 AD).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct about the village community?

options.A: Buchanan's survey of South India became the basis of theories related to the 'Indian village community'.
options.B: B.H. Baden-Powell saw the 'village community' as an expression of the management of their property by the successors of an original owner.
options.C: W.H. Wiser was of the opinion that village servants and artisans were connected to the villages.
options.D: Hiroshi Fukazawa found that rural and servant individuals were bound to the whole village rather than individuals.

questions.explanation: The statements given in the above options regarding the village community are correct – (i) Buchanan's survey of South India became the basis of theories related to the 'Indian village community'. (ii) B.H. Baden-Powell saw the 'village community' as an expression of the management of their property by the successors of an original owner. (iii) Hiroshi Fukazawa found that rural and servant individuals were bound to the whole village rather than individuals. W.H. Wiser was an American anthropologist. He has described through his research the social, economic, and religious life of rural farmers in his book 'The Hindu Jajmani System'

questions.question_text: From which of the following is the correct descending order of the administrative divisions of the Chola Empire known:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- For the convenience of administration, the vast Chola Empire was divided into six provinces. The province was called 'Mandalam'. The division of Mandalam was into 'Kottam' or 'Valanadu' which were equivalent to today's commissionerates. In each Kottam, there were many districts; the name for a district was 'Nadu'. Therefore, the correct descending order of the administrative divisions of the Chola Empire is- Mandalam, Kottam, Nadu.

questions.question_text: Information about the local autonomous village administration of the Cholas is obtained from the Uttaramerur inscription. With which Chola ruler is this inscription related-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation–Parantaka I (907-955 AD) got the land surveyed. He performed many sacrifices and built temples. Information about the local government of the Cholas is found from his Uttaramerur inscription.

questions.question_text: Under whom was the assembly of common people in Chola period local administration?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In Chola period governance, mainly two types of institutions were functional in the villages – 'Ur' and 'Sabha or Mahasabha', Ur was the institution of the common people.

questions.question_text: In Chola administration, 'Padi Kaval' implies─

options.D: Tax given for the maintenance of tanks

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation─In Chola administration, 'Padi Kaval' is considered as a fee for village watchkeeping. In this period, a special type of security tax was provided separately to the local feudatory or powerful officer. In return for which, he took the responsibility of the security of a special area upon himself.

questions.question_text: What was Nadu?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Local self-government was fully developed in Chola period administration, in which Nadu was an administrative unit and Nadu was similar to a district. The assembly of the Nadu was called 'Nattar'.

questions.question_text: The details of the formation of 'Sabha' in the Uttaramerur inscription are related to whose reign?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Two inscriptions of the Chola ruler Parantaka I of 919 AD and 929 AD have been found in Uttaramerur. Description of the Chola autonomous government system is found from the Uttaramerur inscription. From this, the details of the formation of the Sabha are obtained. Sabha or Mahasabha existed in villages; such villages were also called Brahmadeya or Mangalam. Mainly learned Brahmins resided in Agrahara villages. Information regarding Agrahara is obtained from the records of Tondaimandalam and Cholamandalam. It is clear from this that there were many such Sabhas in Kanchi and Madras regions. The Sabha worked mainly through its committees. These were called 'Variyam'. The meaning of this word is not clear. In Tamil its meaning is 'income' and in Kannada it is 'stern demand'. Shastri considers it the Tamil form of Sanskrit 'Varya' which means chosen. In one record, the executive committee of the Sabha is called 'Varanam'. Individuals appointed by the Sabha for any special work were called 'Variyar'.

questions.question_text: Under the Cholas, 'Tattoli' tax was paid by-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Under the Cholas, "Tattoli" tax was paid by goldsmiths. Goldsmiths were engaged in gold work. They used to make various types of jewelry and conical bangles with the help of gold, corals, gems, etc. Jewelry was in great demand among women of high families. High-born women, wearing these, used to enjoy the festivals happening on the streets by standing at the windows of their houses. The basis of the Silappadikaram story is Kannagi's jewelry (anklet). The trend of gem-studded jewelry was in both women and men. Women used to wear a cap-like ornament studded with pearls named Yamme with great fondness.

questions.question_text: What was the meaning of the word 'Nattu Viniyogam' in the Chola state?

options.C: A tax for the expense of the Nadu

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- In the Chola state, Nattu Viniyogam was a tax for the expense of the Nadu. The lands donated to temples in the Chola state were tax-free. The collection of special fees from the ryots on this land was called Nattu Viniyogam. There were many districts in each Kottam. The name of the district was 'Nadu'. The assembly of the Nadu was called 'Nattar' in which there were representatives of all villages and towns. Its main function was to manage the land revenue. It also had the authority to grant exemption in any land revenue. Nadus gave donations in their own name and received permanent endowments. Nattar was also entrusted with the work of classifying the land and accordingly determining the revenue. It also had the authority to grant exemption in any land revenue. Sometimes it also managed the temple.

questions.question_text: During the time of Chola rulers, which of the following Variyam looked after the work of garden administration?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- During the Chola period, an executive committee looked after the business of the villages which was called Variyam. Samvatsara Variyam was called the annual committee. Erivariyam was called the tank committee and the garden committee was called Tottavariyam. Under each Sabha or Mahasabha, there were many committees which were called Variyam. These committees looked after the work of different departments.

questions.question_text: While selecting officers in Chola administration, which of the following processes were used? 1. Eligibility of all landowners 2. Change of post 3. Selection by lottery 4. Nomination of candidates Select the correct answer from the following code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Information about the selection of officers is obtained from the Uttaramerur record of Chola ruler Parantaka I. According to this, only those persons were eligible for membership who - (a) were in the 35 to 70 age group, (b) who have 1/4 Veli land, (c) who is a knower of at least one Veda and its commentary and who has his own residence. In addition to this, the election was done by the lottery system and there was also a provision for change of post because if a person has already been a member of a committee, then after three years he could be re-elected as a member of some other committee. But no information is found about the nomination of candidates. Therefore, code 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.question_text: What was 'Kurram' under Chola emperors?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – For administrative convenience, the Chola Empire was divided into six provinces or Mandalams. The Mandalam was divided into Kottam (Valanadu) which were equivalent to today's commissionerates. Kottam was divided into Nadu (district). Under the Nadu, there were many village unions which were called 'Kurram'. The smallest unit of administration was the Gram Sabha. In this way, Chola Empire - respectively (in descending order) State - Mandalam - Kottam (Valanadu) – Nadu – Kurram – Gram. D. Art and Culture of the Chola Period

questions.question_text: What were 'Eriveerapattinams' in South India?
questions.explanation: In South India during the Chola period, Eriveerapattinams refers to protected commercial towns. These were settlements of merchants where merchants used to exercise special privileges in trade matters with the approval of local government and central government. In Chola administration, trade was mainly controlled by guilds, among which Manigramam, Nanadesi, Valanjiyar were prominent. Among these, Nanadesi was the most powerful

questions.question_text: In the context of agricultural production in South India, what do Kudaihappan Kar and Sambae Peshanam indicate?

options.A: Two main seasons for rice cultivation whose name is kept on the basis of rice varieties grown in summer and winter seasons

questions.explanation: Along with diverse climatic zones in India, there is a very large land area for various crops. In South India, there were two main seasons for rice cultivation - Kudaihappan Kar and Sambae Peshanam. They are named after the variety of rice grown in summer and winter seasons. A portion of the best land was allocated for the summer crop, whose productivity was higher. Winter crops were grown in more widely sown areas, although productivity was less than half or one-third and total productivity was very much abundant. Rice crop is a crop of tropical-humid climate. For which average temperature should be 21°C to 42°C (degree Celsius). Soil should be clayey, deep loamy, alluvial. Main area of production - Eastern India (Bihar, Bengal, Odisha), along with some parts of eastern UP, southern coast of Gujarat and South India were main parts for rice cultivation. In the 16th century, Barbosa has mentioned the use of a type of seed drill in the coastal area for sowing rice

questions.question_text: What among these was Veeravalanjiyar?

options.B: Merchant guild spread on a large scale in early medieval South India

questions.explanation: Veeravalanjiyar – was a merchant guild spread on a large scale in early medieval South India. This itself is also called Valanjiyam or Valanjiyar. In records, apart from Veeravalanjiyar, information regarding merchant guilds like Manigramam, Nanadesiam, Valangai, Idangai, Telin, etc., is obtained. The local organization of merchants was called Nagaram. These organizations existed mainly in Kanchi and Mamallapuram. In the Hirahadagalli record, 500 masters of Ayyavolepur have been called "Five hundred Veeravalanjiyar". Their charters were called '500 Veerashasana' and their place of residence was called 'Veerapattana' or 'Veerapattanam'

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below: Statement (I): Brihadisvara Temple of Tanjore is built of granite stone. Statement (II): Granite rocks are available in nearby areas. In the light of the above statement, select the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.C: Statement (I) is correct, but Statement (II) is incorrect
options.D: Statement (I) is incorrect, but Statement (II) is correct

questions.explanation: The grand Shiva temple of Tanjore which is called Rajarajeshwara temple or Brihadisvara temple, is the largest and highest among all Indian temples. Granite stones have been used in its construction work, which were brought from far-off regions. The construction work of this temple took place between 1003 AD and 1010 AD during the reign of Chola ruler Rajaraja I. The multi-storeyed Vimana of this temple stands to a sky-kissing height of 70 meters, on the top of which is a monolithic Shikhar which is a stupi in the shape of an octagonal dome; this is the highest Vimana of Dravida style. In this temple, various forms of Shiva – Nataraja, Harihara, Bhikshatana, Vishnuanugraha, Virabhadra, Chandrashekhar, Dakshinamurti, Ardhanarishwara, Bhairava and Tripurantaka, etc., statues have been engraved

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The terms Left-hand and Right-hand were first used during the French Revolution. In India, both the Right-hand and Left-hand groups included non-peasant castes. Both groups kept untouchables, mainly the Paraiyars, out of their groups In the Tamil region of India, the Right-hand was called Valangai and the Left-hand was called Idangai. Therefore, option (a) is incorrect. In the question, Right-hand was written as Idangai and Left-hand as Valangai.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of Kalingattuparani?
questions.explanation: The reign of Chola kings is famous for the development of Tamil language and literature. Among Tamil writers, Jayamgondar was the most famous. He was the court poet of the Chola ruler Kulottunga I and he composed the work named 'Kalingattuparani'. It describes the events of Kulottunga's Kalinga war. During the reign of Kulottunga III, the famous poet Kamban lived, who composed 'Tamil Ramayana' or 'Ramavataram'

questions.question_text: Match the following rulers with their dynasties: Ruler Dynasty A. Vijayalaya 1. Chalukya B. Pulakesin I 2. Pallava C. Simhavarman 3. Chalukya D. Vijayaditya 4. Chola Code - A B C D
questions.explanation: Ruler Dynasty A. Vijayalaya 4. Chola B. Pulakesin I 1. Chalukya (Badami) C. Simhavarman 2. Pallava D. Vijayaditya 3. Chalukya (Vengi)

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to Chola administration: (1) They had a massive land revenue department. (2) The assessment and collection of revenue was done by corporate bodies. Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: During the Chola period, the Land Revenue Department was the main source of their income. Tax was collected either by royal servants or by the village officials of the village

questions.question_text: The smallest unit of Chola administration was:
questions.explanation: In ancient India, the Chola Empire of South India was famous for its administration in addition to its glorious emperors. In administration, local or village administration was most remarkable where autonomy was recognized. The smallest unit of Chola administration was called Kurram. In a Kurram, towns were also included in addition to village groups. A Kurram formed in large towns was called Taniyur/Tan-kurram. Each Kurram generally had 50 villages. Therefore, the Chola Empire in ascending order is as follows Kurram - Nadu - Kottram (Valanadu) - Mandalam.

questions.question_text: Under the Chola period local self-government and village system, where did the institution named 'Sabha' function?

options.C: In villages given as gifts to Brahmins

questions.explanation: Local self-government and village system were the most noteworthy systems of Chola rule. In Chola inscriptions, three types of local institutions - Ur, Sabha, and Nagaram - are mentioned Sabha or Mahasabha - existed in Agrahara (land granted to Brahmins) villages. Such villages were also called 'Brahmadeya or Mangalam'. Ur - This was the institution of the common people. Alunganam was the executive committee of Ur. Nagaram - This was limited only to the commercial towns.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a Chola period temple?
questions.explanation: The Brihadisvara temple of Tanjavur was built by Chola king Rajaraja I in 1010 AD. This temple is made entirely of granite. The Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi was built by the Pallava ruler 'Narasimhavarman II' (Rajasimha) in the 'Rajasimha style'. The Muktesvara temple of Bhubaneswar (during the Somavamsi period) is dedicated to Lord Shiva in the Nagara style. The Dashavatara temple of Deogarh is a Gupta period temple related to Lord Vishnu. It is located at a place named Deogarh in Lalitpur (ancient Jhansi) district of Uttar Pradesh

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an ancient Shiva temple?
questions.explanation: Brihadisvara temple is the most ancient Shiva temple whose construction was carried out by the Tamil king Rajaraja I in 1010 AD. Built in Dravidian architecture, this temple is located in Tanjore

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct in the context of Cholas?

options.A: The Chola Empire, which took a large part of the peninsula under its control, rose in the ninth century.
options.B: The Chola Empire was founded by Vijayalaya.
options.C: Vijayalaya was a feudatory of the Pallavas in his early life.
options.D: The Pallavas of Kanchi were later defeated by the Cholas.
options.E: Rashtrakuta Emperor Krishna III was also defeated by the Cholas.

questions.explanation: The Chola Empire rose in the ninth century. This empire was founded by Vijayalaya (850-871 AD). Vijayalaya was a feudatory of the Pallavas. In 949 AD, Rashtrakuta King Krishna III, with the help of the Western Gangas, attacked the Cholas and in the 'Battle of Takkolam', the Cholas were badly defeated and the northern part of the empire was merged into the Rashtrakuta Empire

questions.question_text: The Chola rulers were strong followers of:
questions.explanation: Although the political rise of the Cholas began in the mid-tenth century, its early history started from the Sangam age (third century). Chola rulers were strong supporters of Shaivism. Rajaraja I built the Brihadisvara or Rajarajesvara temple in Tanjore, which was dedicated to Shiva. Rajaraja I assumed the title of Shivapadashekhara

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Srivijaya kingdom are correct? Select the correct answer from the codes given below: (i) Devapala of the Pala dynasty gave villages in donation for the maintenance of the Buddhist monastery built by Balaputradeva. (ii) Rajaraja I of the Chola dynasty had cordial relations with the Srivijaya kingdom. (iii) The relations of Rajendra I with Srivijaya were friendly in the beginning, but later enmity developed between them. (iv) Mara Vijayottunggavarman had built a Buddhist monastery in Nagapattinam. Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – At the request of the Shailendra dynasty ruler Balaputradeva of Java (Srivijaya Kingdom), Devapala (810-850 AD) gave five villages in donation for the construction of a Buddhist Vihara in Nalanda. Rajaraja I (985-1015 AD) of the Chola dynasty had cordial relations with the Srivijaya kingdom. He encouraged the Shailendra ruler of Srivijaya, Shri Mara Vijayottunggavarman, to build a Buddhist Vihara in Nagapattinam and himself also built a Vishnu temple there. The relations of Rajendra I with Srivijaya were friendly in the beginning, but later enmity developed between them. He sent a powerful navy to conquer the Srivijaya (Shailendra) kingdom. The Shailendra ruler Sangrama Vijayottunggavarman was defeated and taken prisoner.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): The Nanadesi community, which was a large merchant guild, claimed to travel to different countries. Reason (R): It is known from an inscription found in Pagan that the Nanadesi community had established a Vishnu temple in that remote city of Upper Burma. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Merchants of the Nanadesi community were involved in trade with other countries besides India. They traded in countries like Southeast Asia and also propagated their religion. This was a large community. The Vaishnava temple located in Pagan, Burma, was built by the Nanadesis themselves.

questions.question_text: Which of the following places in the Chola country was famous for cotton cloth?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Uraiyur, located on the banks of the Kaveri River in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, was the capital of the Sangam period Cholas and ancient Pandyas. In the Sangam age, Uraiyur was a very large center for cotton clothes. Kalidasa has described it in his work Raghuvamsha Mahakavya. Uraiyur is also known by the names Kari and Varanasi.

questions.question_text: Which Chola ruler had issued the first gold coin?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Uttama Chola (973-985 AD) was the first among Chola rulers to issue gold coins. By the time of Uttama Chola's reign, the Cholas had regained the territory of Tondaimandalam from the Rashtrakutas. Later, Rajaraja I issued gold coins in significant quantities.

questions.question_text: Which Chola ruler received the title of 'Sungadtavirtta Chola' (the one who removes taxes)?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Chola ruler Kulottunga I (1070-1120 AD) abolished customs duties and transit duties which were obstacles in the progress of trade, due to which he received the title 'Sungadtavirtta Chola' (the one who removes taxes).

questions.question_text: In the Chola period 'Vetti' referred to─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─In the Chola period, 'Vetti' was forced labor for public work.

questions.question_text: The Battle of Takkolam took place between─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─The Battle of Takkolam took place between the Cholas and the Rashtrakutas. This battle took place in 949 AD between the Chola ruler Parantaka I and the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III. In this battle, Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III defeated the Chola ruler Parantaka I and took possession of Tondaimandalam.

questions.question_text: Who assumed the title of 'Maduraikonda'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The establishment of Chola supremacy in the Dravidian country actually took place during the time of Parantaka I (907-955 AD). He assumed the title 'Maduraikonda' after defeating the Pandya king of Madurai.

questions.question_text: What was the function of the official named 'Udaikottam' in Chola administration?

options.B: Organizing meetings of the Gram Sabha

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – In Chola administration, the official named 'Udaikottam', according to Mr. Neelakanta Sastri, were assistants to the King who worked as public relations officers for the King.

questions.question_text: What was the main source of income for Chola rulers?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The main source of revenue or income for the Chola rulers was land tax. The Gram-Sabhas used to collect land tax and deposit it in the government treasury. For this, Chola rulers got all the land measured and determined the tax on the basis of its productivity. It used to be between one-half and one-fourth part.

questions.question_text: Which Southern kingdom was responsible for the decline of the Chola state? (1) Hoysala (2) Pandya (3) Kakatiya Options:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – During the reign of the last Chola ruler Rajendra III, independent Pandya, Hoysala, and Kakatiya kingdoms were established on the ruins of the Chola Empire.

questions.question_text: Which of the Chola rulers sent their trade missions to China?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – During the time of Chola rulers Rajaraja, Rajendra, and Kulottunga, trade missions were sent to China; Kulottunga had even sent a Chola mission of 72 merchants to China in 1077 AD.

questions.question_text: The Chola administrative unit that looked after the welfare of traders was:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009, Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation - The Chola administrative unit Nagaram looked after the welfare of traders. In Chola inscriptions, Nagaram is often mentioned for the management work of commercial centers. Traders were mainly included in the administrative system of Nagaram.

questions.question_text: Evidence of Chola period painting is found from the following site:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Evidence of Chola period painting is found from the site of Tanjore. According to the historian Goetz, in South India, the Chola period can be termed as the Golden Age in some areas. There were many important cities during the time of the Cholas. Chola rulers were famous for their village administration; the statue of Nataraja is also found from their time.

questions.question_text: Which Chalukya prince of Vengi sat on the Chola throne?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Kulottunga I was the son of Chalukya King Rajaraja. His mother was the daughter of Rajendra Chola. He had a mixture of Chola blood. After the murder of Chola ruler Adhirajendra, Chalukya prince Kulottunga I sat on the throne of the Chola Empire. Kulottunga I was a great ruler of the Chola dynasty. His long reign has been a period of prosperity and success overall. He placed public interest above personal interests and for this, he made many reforms. In Chola writings and traditions, he is called "Sungadtavirtta" (remover of taxes), which indicates his popularity. At the end of his reign, he ruled peacefully. He got the temple of Chidambaram and the Samadhi of Srirangam expanded. He died around 1120 AD.

questions.question_text: Who said that 'Chola artists conceived like giants and finished like jewelers'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- According to art critic Fergusson, "Chola artists conceived like giants and finished like jewelers." Chola dynasty rulers were enthusiastic builders and significant progress took place in the field of art and architecture during their time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not engraved on the coins of the Cholas?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The rulers of the Chola dynasty issued silver and gold coins. Signs of fish, bow, and tiger are marked on the coins issued by them. These three signs appear to be the royal symbols of the Chola, Pandya, and Kerala (Chera) states respectively. After gaining control over all these states, the Chola rulers issued coins with the said symbols. It is clear from the above facts that the symbol of an elephant was not marked on the coins of the Cholas.

questions.question_text: 1. Brihadisvara Temple, Tanjore 2. Draupadi Ratha, Mamallapuram 3. Kailasa Temple, Ellora 4. Meenakshi Temple, Madurai Select the correct answer from the code below: Arrange the following monuments in chronological order:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─The Pallava style developed during the time of Pallava King Narasimhavarman. He had also assumed the title of 'Mamalla'. The Rathas of the Mamalla style are famous by the name 'Sapta Pagoda'. Their number is eight such as─Draupadi Ratha, Arjuna Ratha, Bhima Ratha, Dharmaraja Ratha, Sahadeva Ratha, etc. Among these, Draupadi Ratha is of a different style. From the shape of its roof, it is known that it is an imitation of a portable deity chariot (Devratha). The Kailasa temple of Ellora was built by Rashtrakuta King Krishna I. He had a lot of wealth obtained from many victories, along with a strong religious feeling. The construction of the temple was possible by the combination of these. Altekar is of the opinion that the Kailasa temple was built by artists called from the Pallava capital Kanchi. The specialty of the Kailasa temple is that to build it, the mountain was not only dug downwards, but the craftsmen started carving the rock from the top part. In this way, by carving from top to bottom, all parts of the temple were made. Brihadisvara Temple was built by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I (985-1015 AD) in the Dravidian style; it is a Shaiva temple. Meenakshi temple is located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. It is related to Lord Shiva and Parvati. It is also known by the names Meenakshi Sundaresvara Temple and Meenakshi Amman Temple.

questions.question_text: Which of the following temples is not related to the Cholas?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ Brihadisvara Temple or Rajarajesvara Temple: Chola ruler Rajaraja I Koranganatha Temple: Chola ruler Parantaka I Kailasanatha Temple: Pallava King Rajasimha Airavatesvara Temple: Rajaraja II Chola In this, all temples were built by Chola rulers, only the Kailasanatha temple was built by the Pallava King Rajasimha, which was the title of Narasimhavarman II. Another name for the Kailasanatha temple located in Kanchipuram is also Rajarajesvara Temple.

questions.question_text: What was the specialty of Chola administration?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The main specialty of Chola administration was autonomous village administration. Mention of three types of village assemblies is found in their inscriptions – Ur, Sabha, and Nagaram. Ur was the assembly of common people, while Sabha was the institution of Agrahara Brahmins and Nagaram was the institution of traders.

questions.question_text: An inscription of 1121 AD mentions a medical institution, where Charaka-Samhita and Vagbhata's Ashtanga-Hridaya were taught, it was located in–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– In the medical institution located in Tiruvaduturai, Charaka Samhita and Vagbhata's Ashtanga-Hridaya were taught. In addition to this, education of Nyaya and Vaisheshika, etc., was also given here. This is a famous medical institution of the eleventh century.

questions.question_text: The famous Tamil writer Kamban was in whose royal court?
questions.explanation: Kamban was the author of the famous Tamil work Kambaramayanam; he was born in the Chola kingdom of Tamil Nadu. Kamban was a Vaishnava saint. He was in the court of Kulottunga III

questions.question_text: Who established the Chola dynasty as an independent power?
questions.explanation: The Chola Empire rose in the 9th century. This empire was founded by Vijayalaya (850-871 AD). Vijayalaya assumed the title of Parakesari after occupying Tanjore or Tanjavur. Vijayalaya initially worked as a feudatory of the Pallavas

questions.question_text: What is the other name of 'Fatehnama'?
questions.explanation: The other name for Fatehnama is Chachnama. This book is related to the history of Sindh; it contains the history of the Chach dynasty and a description of the conquest of Sindh by the Arabs. The author of this text, originally written in the Arabic language, is unknown; later, Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi translated it into the Persian language during the time of Nasiruddin Qubacha. In this text, a description is found of Muhammad bin Qasim's Sindh campaign, his administrative arrangements, and the death penalty given to Muhammad bin Qasim by Caliph Walid after the conquest of Sindh

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler there at the time of the early Arab invasion of Sindh?
questions.explanation: At the time of the early Arab invasion of Sindh, the ruler of Sindh was Dahir and Alor was his capital. The first successful invasion of the Arabs on Sindh took place in 712 AD under the leadership of Muhammad bin Qasim. Information about the Arab invasion of Sindh is found in a text named Chachnama written in Arabic. The Persian translation of this text was done by Abu Bakr Kufi

questions.question_text: To which tribe of the Arabs did Prophet Muhammad belong?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad belonged to the Quraish (Hashemite) tribe. He was born in Mecca, which is in Saudi Arabia. Mecca is to the west of India, therefore Indian Muslims face west while praying

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Prophet Muhammad?

options.A: Prophet Muhammad preached the prayer to only one God.
options.B: Prophet Muhammad preached the membership of only one community of believers.
options.C: Prophet Muhammad was from Arabia by language and culture.
options.D: The followers of Prophet Muhammad had declared him the messenger of God.

questions.explanation: Not the followers of Prophet Muhammad, but Muhammad Saheb himself had declared himself the messenger of God

questions.question_text: In which text is the conquest of Sindh by the Arabs mentioned?
questions.explanation: The book 'Chachnama' written in 1216, which was written in the Persian language, is essentially a Persian translation of an Arabic original. Mention of the Sindh conquest is found in it

questions.question_text: Arrange the following rulers in chronological order and select the correct answer using the codes given below- 1. Muhammad bin Qasim 2. Mahmud Ghaznavi 3. Timur 4. Genghis Khan Codes:
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of the reigns of the rulers will be as follows– 1. Muhammad bin Qasim (711-12 AD) 2. Mahmud Ghaznavi (997-1030 AD) 3. Genghis Khan (1162 – 1227 AD) 4. Timur (1370 – 1405 AD)

questions.question_text: Which of the following states was first attacked by Muhammad Ghori?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation—Muhammad Ghori first attacked Multan in 1175 AD. The ruler here was a 'Shia'. Therefore, he considered it his religious duty to conquer his state.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Muslim conquerors appointed Hindus in his multi-ethnic army?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Arab invader Muhammad bin Qasim attacked Sindh in 712 AD. Mahmud Ghaznavi appointed Hindus in his multi-ethnic army. A soldier named Tilak was his prominent commander.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and choose your correct answer from the codes given below the lists- List I (Dynasty) List II (Capital) A. Gujarat - (b) Anhilwad B. Kalachuri of Chedi - (a) Tripuri C. Paramara of Malwa - (d) Dhara D. Chauhan of Shakambhari - (c) Ajmer Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Chalukyas of Gujarat-Anhilwad, Kalachuri of Chedi-Tripuri, Paramara of Malwa-Dhara, Chauhan of Shakambhari-Ajmer.

questions.question_text: Where was the capital of the Hindu Shahi state at the time of Mahmud Ghaznavi's invasion?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 MP Asst. Prof. 2017 Haryana PGT 2020 PGT History, 2005 Explanation- The Hindu Shahi dynasty ruled over the Kabul Valley and the North-Western frontier regions. The capital of this Hindu Shahi state located in the North-Western frontier region was 'Udbhandapur' (Waihind). The Hindu Shahi state was the first victim of the Muslim invasion.

questions.question_text: The last ruler of the Ghazni dynasty in Lahore was—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The last ruler of the Ghazni dynasty in Lahore was Khusrau Malik. In 1186 AD, Muhammad Ghori captured Khusrau Malik through deceit, which resulted in Ghori's control over the entire Punjab and the end of the Ghazni dynasty.

questions.question_text: According to Al-Beruni, who were the successors of the Kushans who ruled North India in the tenth-eleventh century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 PGT History, 2000 Explanation- According to Al-Beruni, the rulers of the Hindu Shahi dynasty were descendants of the Kushan King Kanishka. The capital of the Hindu Shahi state was Udbhandapur (Waihind). The Hindu Shahi dynasty was a victim of Muslim invasion.

questions.question_text: What is not correct about the Arab traveler Istakhri?

options.A: He was a resident of Karkh in Khorasan.
options.C: He wrote Kitab al-Aqalīm and Masālik wal-Mamālik.
options.D: It is said that he made a map of the world.

questions.explanation: Arab traveler Istakhri visited India in 951. He wrote Kitab al-Aqalīm and Masālik wal-Mamālik. It is said about him that he made a map of the world. He was a resident of the city of Istakhr in Iran

questions.question_text: In which of the following places/regions were Naphtha and Mangonels first used in India?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation—Naphtha and Mangonels were first used in India in the Sindh region in 712. These were very dangerous weapons. Among these, the Mangonel was used like modern missiles.

questions.question_text: In which languages were Chachnama and Baburnama respectively written:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July 2017 Explanation—Chachnama was composed in the Arabic language by some unknown author, in which the Arab invasion of Sindh is mentioned. Baburnama is the autobiography of the Mughal ruler Babur composed in the Turkish language.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: – Correct matches are– Shihabuddin Suhrawardi - Awarif-ul-Maarif Al-Hujwiri - Kashf-ul-Mahjub Ibn Arabi - Fusus-al-Hikam Sir Syed Ahmed Khan - Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq Al-Ghazali - Tahafut al-Falasifa

questions.question_text: Chachnama is the history of Sindh and was originally written in which language?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2011) Explanation—Chachnama is originally in the Arabic language. It is mainly related to the history of Sindh, which is an account of the Arab conquest of Sindh. It was composed by 'Ali Ahmed'. It is noteworthy that the book Tahqiq-i-Hind (Discovery of India) by the Arabic writer Al-Beruni is still an important source for historians today.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) – Assertion (A): With the establishment of the Turkic empire in India, the art of historiography was firmly established. Reason (R): The paper industry developed in India during the Sultanate period. Read the above statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below – Codes:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June 2014) Explanation—The art of historiography was firmly established in India with the establishment of the Turkic empire. Information about the history of this time is found from the works of Al-Beruni (Tahqiq-i-Hind), Minhaj-us-Siraj (Tabaqat-i-Nasiri), and Amir Khusrau. It is known that the paper industry developed during the Sultanate period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct?

options.A: Damaras were the factor of most trouble in the political life of Kashmir.
options.B: Al-Beruni says that only Shudras could not study the Vedas.
options.C: According to Ibn-ul-Athir, Muslims had been living in Benares since the time of Mahmud bin Sabuktigin.
options.D: Ata Malik Juwayni is an important source for information about the objectives of Mu'izzuddin's Indian invasions.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2015) Explanation—According to Al-Beruni, only Brahmins could study the Vedas. It was forbidden for others. Apart from Shudras, other Antyaja castes and Vaishyas also did not have the right to study the Vedas. In this way, statement (b) is false. The remaining statements are true.

questions.question_text: Medieval Indian history written in the Persian language is known as Persian historiography. Its focal point is:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2015) Explanation—The development of Persian literature in India began with the arrival of Muslim conquerors. Here it was given a new form. Initially, it was the language of the ruling class and the noble class, and it also received their patronage. First, Lahore remained the center of development of Persian literature in India.

questions.question_text: Regarding which Arab traveler is it said that he came to India during the reign of Pratihara King Mihir Bhoja?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2015) Explanation – Mihir Bhoja I (836–885 AD) was the most important ruler of the Pratihara dynasty. We also get information about the events of his time from the accounts of Kalhana and the Arab traveler Suleiman.

questions.question_text: Who compiled Na't-i-Muhammadi, the biography of Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2015) Explanation— Ziauddin Barani compiled Na't-i-Muhammadi, the biography of Prophet Muhammad.

questions.question_text: The land tax levied by Muhammad bin Qasim after the Arab occupation of Sindh was called –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – The Arabs achieved the conquest of Sindh in 712 AD under the leadership of Muhammad bin Qasim and levied two new taxes, one of which was Jizya, which was a religious tax, and the second was 'Kharaj', which was a land tax. This used to be from 2/5 to 1/4 of the produce.

questions.question_text: Which of the following historical works highlights the beginning of Muslim rule in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Sufficient information regarding the Arab invasion of India is found in the 9th-century work 'Kitab Futuh al-Buldan' by Al-Biladuri. Another book written in 1216 AD is 'Chachnama' which is written in the Persian language (a Persian translation of Arabic), which also provides sufficient information regarding the Arab invasion of India.

questions.question_text: Chachnama is a famous source of information for the history of where?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Information about the conquest of Sindh by the Arabs is found from the Persian text 'Chachnama'.

questions.question_text: The first Muslim invader of India was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The first Muslim invasion of India was carried out in 712 AD by the Arab invader Muhammad bin Qasim. After a heavy struggle, the Arabs conquered Sindh in 712 AD, but it did not have any permanent result.

questions.question_text: The text 'Fatehnama' is related to
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - 'Fathnama' book contains a description of the conquest of Sindh by the Arabs. The Arabs made many attempts to conquer India and could only win a small part.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the book 'Tarikh-i-Subuktigin'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The court poet of Ghazni ruler Subuktigin, Baihaqi, composed ''Tarikh-i-Subuktigin''. Historian Lane-Poole gave the title of 'Pepys of the East' to historian Baihaqi. It contains a description of the bravery and administration of Subuktigin and his son Mahmud.

questions.question_text: In 731 AD, the Arabs established a city on the banks of the Indus river, which was named—
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- In 731 AD, the Arabs established the first city Mahpuja on the banks of the Indus river and after that, the second city was established in Mansura. Muhammad bin Qasim attacked Sindh in 712 AD. After reaching Makran, he obtained help from the local king and won over the Jats and Meds who were dissatisfied with Dahir's rule. The rebellious Buddhists also helped him. First of all, Muhammad bin Qasim attacked Debal, brought it under his control, and had all males over 17 years of age killed. Dahir himself was panicked by his attack and did not send any army to confront him in Debal. In this way, without any resistance, Muhammad got the southern part of Sindh. After this, while conquering Nerun, Sehwan, and Sisam, he crossed the Indus river.

questions.question_text: From which book does one get a direct account of Muhammad Ghori's conquest of India and the history of the newly established Turkic Sultanate?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Minhaj-us-Siraj's book 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' gives a direct account of Muhammad Ghori's conquest of India and the history of the newly established Turkic Sultanate. This book is dedicated to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud. Minhaj was the first historian who only stated that Qutb-ud-din Aibak circulated coins in his name and had the Khutba read. Minhaj wrote the account of the reign from Sultan Iltutmish to his patron Sultan Nasiruddin based on self-witnessed events.

questions.question_text: Which of the following places was called 'Svarnagriha' (Golden House/City) by the Arab travelers?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation - In 713 AD, Muhammad bin Qasim achieved victory over Multan; this was the last victory of the Arabs. So much gold was found from Multan that it was named 'City of Gold' (Svarnagriha) by the Arab travelers.

questions.question_text: Which region did the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty control at the time of the Turkic invasion of North India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– At the time of the Turkic invasion of North India, the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty held dominance over the Kannauj region. By the middle of the tenth century, the Pratihara empire had completely disintegrated. Now it remained confined only around Kannauj. Rajyapala, who was the son of Vijayapala, ruled over Kannauj until 1018 AD. He surrendered before Mahmud Ghaznavi and the Muslims gained control over Kannauj. Rajyapala fled with his body (fled) and Mahmud looted Kannauj thoroughly. Angered by this cowardice of Rajyapala, the Chandela ruler Vidyadhar killed him.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of Muruj-ul-Zahab?
questions.explanation: The author of 'Muruj-ul-Zahab' was Al-Masudi, whereas the book composed by Al-Biladhuri is 'Kitab-Futuh-ul-Buldan'. The book written by Al-Biruni is Kitab-ul-Hind. In all these works, an account of Arab invasions on pre-medieval India and Sindh is found. Arab traveler Sulaiman called the Pala ruler Devapala the most powerful among the Pratihara and Rashtrakuta rulers B. Ghaznavid Invasion and its Impact

questions.question_text: In which language was 'Kitab-ul-Hind' written?
questions.explanation: Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) is a book written by Al-Biruni in the Arabic language. Sachau translated it into the English language for the first time. Its translation into the Hindi language has been done by Rajnikant Sharma. It has 80 chapters. This book contains a detailed account of the political, economic, social, and religious conditions of India at the time of Mahmud Ghaznavi. Al-Biruni was born in 973 AD in Khwarizm (Central Asia). He came to India with Mahmud Ghaznavi. He studied Hindu religion, philosophy, and language-literature. He was the first Muslim to study the Puranas. He has mentioned 8 types of Antyajas (low caste/outcastes) in India

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers formed a confederacy of Indian kings against Mahmud Ghaznavi?
questions.explanation: &d) : First of all, in 1009 AD, against Mahmud Ghaznavi, the Hindu Shahi ruler Anandapala formed a confederacy of Indian kings and confronted Ghaznavi near Waihind, but was defeated. After this, his successor Trilochanapala also confronted Mahmud Ghaznavi with the help of the rulers of Kashmir and Bundelkhand, but he too was defeated. The Public Service Commission, Uttar Pradesh has considered the answer to this question to be 'b'

questions.question_text: Which scholar of the Islamic Golden Age is often called the founder of the ideology, father of comparative religion, and the first anthropologist in India?
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni was born in Khwarizm located in Uzbekistan, which is known by the name of Khiva in modern times. Al-Biruni was a great mathematician, philosopher, astrologer, and scholar of Sanskrit. Impressed by his ability and scholarship, Mahmud Ghaznavi provided him with an honored place in the royal court. During Mahmud's invasion, he came to India many times and did in-depth study on social, political, literary, geographical, philosophy, and Sanskrit here. He was a knower of many languages, hence it was easy for him to translate into any language. He also translated Arabic, Persian, and Patanjali's grammar. He is considered the founder of the ideology, father of comparative religion, and the first anthropologist in India in Indian history

questions.question_text: 'Tahqiq-i-Hind' is a famous literary work composed by whom?
questions.explanation: The author of the book named 'Tahqiq-i-Hind' or Kitab-ul-Hind was Al-Biruni (973-1048 AD), who was a Persian scholar, writer, scientist, theologian, and thinker. Impressed by his scholarship, Mahmud Ghaznavi appointed him as the state astrologer. Al-Biruni was a prominent knower of Arabic, Persian, Turkic, Sanskrit, Mathematics, Astronomy, Science, etc. During Sultan Mahmud Ghaznavi's invasion of India, Al-Biruni also came to India and lived in Punjab for several years. Whatever he saw and studied while living in India, he described it with a scientific perspective in his book 'Tahqiq-i-Hind' or Kitab-ul-Hind

questions.question_text: The invasions of Mahmud Ghaznavi and Muhammad Ghori resulted in—

options.D: Exposed the military weakness of Indian rulers

questions.explanation: After the Ghaznavid invasions, the Indian kings should have paid attention to their military strength but this did not happen. After some time, this weakness was highlighted by Muhammad Ghori's invasion. The India conquest campaign of Ghori and Ghaznavi mainly depended on his very superior military organization, war strategy, and military maneuvers. The feudal form of the army ended and the exclusive right to participate in wars did not remain the right of any one particular caste. The Turkic army was fast and followed professional strategy, which also had an impact on the Rajput army in the long run

questions.question_text: Which of the following was given the responsibility by Mahmud Ghaznavi to write about the Indian subcontinent?
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni was the court writer of Mahmud Ghaznavi, whom he gave the responsibility of writing about his rule and victories

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler of Mathura at the time of Mahmud Ghaznavi's invasion?
questions.explanation: Mahmud Ghaznavi made his 13th invasion on Mathura, where the ruler was Kulchand. Mathura is called a city of strong and beautiful temples in every way. Utbi has praised Mathura a lot. Mahmud devastated Mathura city and did severe looting

questions.question_text: Shahnama's author Firdausi was the court poet of whose court among the following?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation Shahnama's author Firdausi was the court poet of Mahmud Ghaznavi. The book named 'Shahnama' contains a description of the rulers of Iran. Babur brought the Shahnama book with him to India.

questions.question_text: How many times did Sultan Mahmud Ghaznavi invade India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Due to the disorganized circumstances of India, Mahmud Ghaznavi invaded India many times at the beginning of the 11th century. Sir Henry Elliot has stated that Mahmud invaded India 17 times.

questions.question_text: Who led the confederacy of Rajput rulers to defeat Mahmud Ghaznavi?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – First of all, in 1009 AD against Mahmud Ghaznavi, the Hindu Shahi ruler Anandapala formed a confederacy of Indian kings but was defeated. After this, his successor Trilochanapala also confronted Mahmud Ghaznavi with the help of the rulers of Kashmir and Bundelkhand, but he too was defeated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Hindu Shahi rulers committed self-immolation by jumping into a pyre lit by himself—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─In the invasion near Peshawar in 1001 AD by Mahmud Ghaznavi, he captured Jaipal, the ruler of the Hindu Shahi dynasty. Jaipal and his relatives were released after taking 25 elephants and 250,000 dinars. Distressed by this defeat, Jaipal committed self-immolation.

questions.question_text: Who was the Indian king defeated by Mahmud Ghaznavi on the banks of the Indus river?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – In 1009 AD, Mahmud Ghaznavi defeated the Gurjara Pratihara ruler Anandapala in a decisive battle on the banks of the Indus river and destroyed his new capital Nandana or Nandanpur located in the Salt Range. He also destroyed the fort of Anandapala named Nagarkot. Anandapala was allowed to rule from Lahore for some time as a subordinate king.

questions.question_text: What was the name of that scholar who came to India with Mahmud Ghaznavi?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 DSSSB PGT 2019 Explanation- Al-Biruni was born in 973 AD in Khiva. In 1017, Mahmud Ghaznavi obtained Al-Biruni as a prisoner of war during the conquest of Khiva. Al-Biruni was a scholar, therefore he came to India during the invasions of Mahmud Ghaznavi. Al-Biruni was the first Muslim who studied the Puranas.

questions.question_text: Who among the following rulers gave a Sanskrit translation of the Kalima on the reverse of his coins— Avyaktamekam Muhammad Avtarah?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- After the death of his father Sabuktigin, Mahmud took control over Ghazni. With Sultan Mahmud, a new chapter began in the history of Islam. He is considered the first Sultan of Ajam. According to Tarikh-i-Guzida, only after defeating King Khalak-bin-Ahmed of Sistan did Mahmud assume the title of 'Sultan'. Historians believe that Mahmud was the first ruler to receive the title of 'Sultan'. Mahmud Ghazni had the Sanskrit translation of the Kalima inscribed on one side of his coins as: Avyaktamekam Muhammad Avtarah.

questions.question_text: Al-Biruni has described which of the following religious practices as prevalent? 1. Daily Yajnas 2. Fasts 3. Charity 4. Pilgrimage Select the correct answer from the code given below— Code
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Al-Biruni, before the Indian conquest of Mahmud Ghaznavi, was in the service of the last ruler of the country of Khiva as a scholar and diplomat. Later, Al-Biruni became associated with the court of Mahmud, and when Mahmud attacked India, he came to India with him. His most important and remarkable creation is the survey of Indian life conducted by him. His work is based on the study and observation of Indian life between 1017 and 1030 AD. At the time of Mahmud Ghaznavi's Indian campaign, he came to India along with him. Kitab-ul-Hind is a unique work composed by him. In this book, he has described Indian traditions, customs, festivals, celebrations, and religious rituals such as daily Yajnas, worship, pilgrimage, fasts, etc.

questions.question_text: What was the main objective of Sultan Mahmud's Indian conquest?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Sultan Mahmud Ghaznavi was the son of Sabuktigin. In 997 AD, after the death of Sabuktigin, he became the ruler of Ghazni. On the occasion of his coronation, he had taken a pledge that he would invade India every year. In addition to this, he needed wealth for the expansion of his empire in Central Asia. He could easily obtain wealth in India. Therefore, only for the collection of wealth, Mahmud carried out several invasions one after another on India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following foreign invaders had looted the Somnath temple?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- The Ghaznavid dynasty was a branch of the rulers of Iran. Alptigin established this dynasty as the ruler of an independent state. Sabuktigin was a prominent ruler of this dynasty and the son-in-law of Alptigin. In 997 AD, Sabuktigin died. After his death, his eldest son Mahmud assumed power. On the occasion of his coronation, he pledged to invade India every year. In addition to this, he also needed wealth for his empire expansion in Central Asia. To fulfill these objectives, Mahmud invaded India about 17 times. Since at that time the temples of India were the main sources of obtaining wealth, therefore Mahmud attacked the temple of Somnath (Kathiawar) in 1025 AD and carried away immense wealth from there to Ghazni. At the time of the attack on Somnath in 1025 AD, the Solanki ruler Bhima I was ruling Gujarat, who fled at the time of the attack. C. Invasion of Muhammad Ghori and its Impact

questions.question_text: Which Rajput ruler is known by the name 'Rai Pithora'?
questions.explanation: At the time of Muhammad Ghori's invasion, Delhi and Ajmer were ruled by the Chauhan dynasty ruler Prithviraj III, who is also known by the name 'Rai Pithora'. He was the most powerful among all contemporary Indian rulers. Due to being highly ambitious, he conflicted with neighboring kings and earned enmity with everyone. In 1191 AD, in the First Battle of Tarain, Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori, but in 1192 AD, in the Second Battle of Tarain, he was defeated by Muhammad Ghori

questions.question_text: Shahabuddin Muhammad Ghori defeated which Indian monarch and took control over Banaras?
questions.explanation: Shahabuddin Muhammad Ghori defeated the Indian monarch Jaichand and took control over Banaras. After defeating the Chauhan dynasty ruler Prithviraj III in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 AD, Ghori defeated King Jaichand, who was the important and final ruler of the Gahadavala dynasty, in the Battle of Chandawar in 1194 AD. The Gahadavala dynasty ruled over the region from Kannauj to Banaras. Therefore, Ghori gained control over these areas

questions.question_text: According to Merutunga's Prabandha Chintamani, who among the following defeated Muhammad Ghori?
questions.explanation: In 1178 AD, Muhammad Ghori attacked Gujarat. Here the ruler Mularaja or Bhima II, under the leadership of his widowed mother Nayaki Devi, defeated Muhammad Ghori in the field of Kayadara near Mount Abu. This was Muhammad Ghori's first defeat in India

questions.question_text: After the conquest of Mahoba, whom did Prithviraj Chauhan appoint as the official there?
questions.explanation: Prithviraj III was a great conqueror and a valiant military leader. He defeated the Chandela king named Paramardi Deva and in 1182 AD, he captured his capital Mahoba. After this, he made Panju or Panjan Rai the administrator of Mahoba. Epigraphic evidence of Prithviraj Chauhan's victory over the Chandela monarch is also found. From this inscription, it is known that he could not keep control over Mahoba for a long time

questions.question_text: Who among the following Indian monarchs first defeated Muhammad Ghori?
questions.explanation: After Mularaja II, Bhima II became the ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Gujarat. In 1178 AD, under the leadership of Muhammad Ghori, the Turks attacked his state, but in the field of Kayadara, Bhima II defeated them badly

questions.question_text: At which place did the coronation of the famous Chauhan dynasty ruler Prithviraj III take place?
questions.explanation: The Chauhan dynasty king Prithviraj Chauhan had his coronation performed at Rai Pithora, Delhi. After defeating Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 and granting him a pardon, subsequently, in 1192, Muhammad Ghori defeated him in the Second Battle of Tarain and took him prisoner

questions.question_text: The minister who advised Prithviraj III against providing help to the Chalukyas at the time of Ghori's invasion was:
questions.explanation: The minister who advised Prithviraj III against helping the Chalukyas at the time of Ghori's invasion was Kadambavasa. At the time of Prithviraj III, the Chalukya (Solanki) ruler was Bhima II. Many wars took place between Prithviraj III and the Chalukyas due to mutual animosity, but neither of the two could achieve a decisive victory over the other. Therefore, when Ghori attacked the Chalukyas, Prithviraj III got this golden opportunity to weaken the Chalukyas. That is why he did not provide any help to the Chalukyas

questions.question_text: Who was the first Indian ruler defeated by Muhammad Ghori?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The first Indian ruler defeated by Muhammad Ghori was Prithviraj Chauhan. After being defeated in the First Battle of Tarain (1191 AD), he defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 and established Turkish rule in India.

questions.question_text: Which Indian ruler did Muhammad Ghori defeat in the Battle of Chandawar in 1194 AD—
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation–In the Battle of Chandawar in 1194 AD, Muhammad Ghori had defeated Jaichand. It is noteworthy that in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan III.

questions.question_text: Prithviraj Chauhan lost to which Turkish invader in the Second Battle of Tarain?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan III in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192. In the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, Prithviraj Chauhan III had defeated Muhammad Ghori.

questions.question_text: The capital of Prithviraj Chauhan was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The ruler of Ajmer, Prithviraj III (1177-1192 AD) itself is famous by the name 'Prithviraj Chauhan', who defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 AD. However, in 1192 AD, in the Second Battle of Tarain, he was defeated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Chandela rulers forced Mahmud Ghaznavi into a treaty?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The first invasion of Mahmud Ghaznavi on the Chandelas took place in 1019-20 AD. At that time, the ruler of the Chandela dynasty was Vidyadhara, who was the most powerful ruler of his dynasty. No result came out of this war. Consequently, Mahmud Ghaznavi was forced to make a treaty with Vidyadhara.

questions.question_text: By whom was Muhammad Ghori killed while going to Ghazni?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Muhammad Ghori was killed by the Khokhars while going to Ghazni.

questions.question_text: On which Muslim ruler's coins was Lakshmi inscribed?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation ─ It should be noted that Muhammad Ghori had minted coins with the figure of Lakshmi type. The figure of Lakshmi is also found on Kalachuri and Chandela coins.

questions.question_text: Who among the following first started the Iqtadari system in India?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- 'Iqta' is a word from the Arabic language. Initially, under this system, the right to the revenue of specific land fragments was given to soldiers in exchange for their salary. The Iqtadari system first started in India during the time of Muizuddin Muhammad Ghori, but Ghori never lived and ruled in India, rather he ruled through his generals. Therefore, Iltutmish alone is considered the initiator of the Iqtadari system.

questions.question_text: "The Turkish victory over North India was an important aspect of the urban revolution." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation - At the beginning of the 13th century, with the invasions and conquests of Ghori, a new ruling class in the form of Turks arrived. The result of these Turkish conquests was not merely a change of state power, but rather, from the clash and conflict of two developed social systems, comprehensive changes also occurred in the new social and economic fields. 'Muhammad Habib' has termed these changes an 'Urban Revolution'. According to him, the Turks uprooted the caste and theoretical bonds that had been going on for years on technology and social forces. In this way, Habib considers the Turkish victory over North India to be the revolution of the urban artisans of India.

questions.question_text: The great poet Firdausi graced whose court?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – The poet Firdausi, known as the Homer of the East, graced the court of Sultan Mahmud Ghaznavi. His important work is 'Shahnama'. It is said that for writing the Shahnama, the Sultan had pledged to give him sixty thousand gold coins. Finally, going back on his word, he gave sixty thousand silver miskals in its place. Consequently, Firdausi became enraged and left Ghazni forever.

questions.question_text: Who among the following gave orders to issue such coins on which the figure of a Hindu goddess was inscribed?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Muhammad Ghori had coins issued with the figure of a Hindu goddess inscribed. Like the Chauhan coins, he had currency prepared in the Indian style in Delhi. questions.question_text: In Java island of Southeast Asia:
questions.explanation: Java island of Southeast Asia (mentioned as 'Yavadvipa' in Ramayana), where there were gold mines. According to tradition - an Indian named 'Ajika' started the 'Java Samvat' in 78 AD. The first Indian settlements were established in Java island in the first century AD. "Fa-Hien (a Buddhist traveler) traveling here tells that only Brahmanical religion was prevalent here until the fifth century. The names of the rulers here ended in 'Varman'. From the fifth century, Buddhism was propagated in Java under the leadership of Gunavarman. This religion was propagated in Java and surrounding islands. The credit for taking this religion to an advanced stage in Java and nearby islands goes to 'Gunavarman'. There is a mention of a ruler named Purnavarman in four Sanskrit inscriptions found from western Java in the sixth century AD. 'Taruma' was their capital. His ancestor 'Rajadhiraja' got the Chandrabhaga canal and Purnavarman himself got the Gomati canal constructed

questions.explanation: The chronology of the history of art in ancient India is as follows Sequence Number | Chronology | Features --- | --- | --- 1. | Nagarjuni (232 BC) (Gaya, Bihar) | ♦ It is the residence of monks of the Ajivika sect. ♦ Mauryan ruler Dasharatha got the Gopi cave constructed on the Nagarjuni hill. ♦ Shining Mauryan polish has been found on the inner walls of this cave. 2. | Bhaja (First century) (Lonavala, Maharashtra) | ♦ This is a small group of Buddhist caves built by the Hinayana sect. ♦ It is known as the old Buddhist rock-cut monasteries in the Deccan. 3. | Kanheri (100 AD) (Lonavala, Maharashtra) | ♦ Its ancient name was Valuraka. ♦ It presents an excellent example of Satavahana architecture. 4. | Elephanta (Approx. 600 to 900 AD) (Mumbai) | ♦ Cave made by cutting mountains in the Vakataka period. ♦ Its real name was Dharapuri and the Portuguese named it Elephanta. ♦ Here, Trimurti, mutilated sculpture of Shiva Tandava (Nataraja) and other sculptures have been found.
