questions.explanation: Pallava dynasty played an important role in the history of South India. Information about the achievements of the heroes in the Pallava empire is obtained from Veerakal inscriptions (memorials of heroes). The script of these inscriptions is Vatteluttu or Vatteluttu. In this, information mainly related to livestock and information about the protection of the empire from dangerous animals like tigers and lions is obtained. Evidence of memorials being built on the death of pet dogs that protected from robbers by the heroes is also obtained. No mention is found in these inscriptions about protection from elephants

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are true?
questions.explanation: A stirrup is a frame or finger-shaped iron structure, on which the rider keeps his foot to provide stability, which helps the rider in balancing his body while fighting or riding a horse at high speed. It is attached to the saddle by a belt. Starting from China, the stirrup gradually became visible throughout Europe and the entire Asia. By the end of the sixth century or the beginning of the seventh century, the use of stirrups had started in Arab armies. This same stirrup gradually turned into the form of an iron stirrup in Persian from the Arabic word Paintings of stirrups are not found in the paintings of horsemen in the Ajanta wall paintings.

questions.question_text: Write the following composers in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of the following composers is (Composer) | (Composition) 1- Yaska | Nirukta 2- Patanjali | Mahabhashya 3- Sitalaisattanar (Sattanar) | Manimekalai 4- Sandhyakar Nandi | Ramacharita Instructions (9-13): Read the following passage and answer the questions given below it: Ancient India has provided us with a huge treasure of texts, which represent intellectual and literary activities for more than two thousand years and whose scope is very wide. The oldest literature Rigveda Samhita is at least three thousand years old or it could be even older than that. The stream of literature shedding light on ancient Indian civilization remained flowing for centuries with continuity, which included all fields of human activity besides political history. Such a situation is not seen in other cultures of the world. In this huge treasure of literature, along with religion and philosophy, jurisprudence, rituals and religious ceremonies, cosmology, cosmogony, geography, astronomy and associated sciences, political and economic theories and practices, i.e., in short, all areas of worldly life are included. Apart from detailed religious texts, pure literary tradition texts like epic, lyric poetry, poetry, drama, prose, biography texts and folk tales are included in it. This literature is as rich in terms of its subject matter as it is heavy in terms of its form. Although they are not very helpful in the reconstruction of India's political history, they are extremely useful for the study of the development of various phases of Indian civilization and culture. Such resources are not available for the study of the civilizations of ancient Egypt, Western Asia, China and even Greece and Rome.

questions.question_text: The popular subject matter of ancient Indian dramas is mainly based on Ramayana, Mahabharata, courtly-love and folk tales. In which of the following plays believed to be written by Bhasa, the plot is taken from the Ramayana?
questions.explanation: Ancient India has provided us with a huge treasure of texts, which represent intellectual and literary activities for more than two thousand years and whose scope is very wide. The popular subject matter of ancient Indian dramas is mainly based on Ramayana, Mahabharata, courtly-love and folk tales. The plot of the play 'Abhisheka' written by playwright Bhasa is taken from the Ramayana. Abhisheka is a six-act play. In this, the story from the Kishkindha Kanda of the Ramayana to the end of the Yuddha Kanda is described, i.e., the story from the killing of Vali to the coronation of Rama. Avimaraka, Balacharita and Pancharatra are also important plays of Bhasa. In which, Avimaraka describes the love and marriage of Prince Avimaraka (hero), son of King Kuntibhoja, with Kurangi, daughter of King Kuntibhoja. Balacharita play is based on the childhood pastimes of Lord Shri Krishna. Pancharatra play is based on the Virata Parva of the Mahabharata

questions.question_text: India's great philosopher Vedanta Deshika wrote a messenger poem (a type of lyric poetry), which is named:
questions.explanation: Vedanta Deshika is known as an important Acharya in the Shri Vaishnava tradition of South India, who propagated the philosophical doctrine of Vishishtadvaita. Vedanta-Deshika wrote a messenger poem (a type of lyric poetry) 'Hamsa-Sandesha'. This is a Sanskrit love poem written in the 13th century. In this, the hero of the Ramayana epic, Rama, sends a message to his wife Sita through a swan, whom Ravana has abducted. Meghaduta, Pavanaduta, and Shiladuta are all messenger poems, which were written by Kalidasa, Dhoyi, and Charitra Sundar respectively

questions.question_text: Which of the following historical texts are written by Bilhana?
questions.explanation: Bilhana was originally a resident of Kashmir. He first stayed for some years in the court of Kalachuri ruler Lakshmi-Karna. Eventually, he went to Kalyani. Bilhana was the court poet of Vikramaditya VI (1076-1126). Vikramaditya VI gave him the title of 'Vidyapati'. Among his (Bilhana's) important texts are Vikramankadeva-Charita, Karnasundari, Shanti-shataka, Chaurapanchashika etc. Among these, Vikramankadeva-Charita was written in Sanskrit in the 11th century. In this book, Bilhana has described the biography of Kalyani's Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya VI. Bhuvana-bhyudaya was written by Shankhu, one of the nine gems (Navratna) of Gupta-period Chandragupta II Vikramaditya

questions.question_text: Which of the following cave temples of Ellora are related to the Brahmanical religion?
questions.explanation: Ellora was built by the rulers of the Rashtrakuta dynasty. It is located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra. Eighteen Brahmanical temples and four Jain cave temples were built on the Ellora hill. Among the temples of Ellora, the 'Kailasa Temple' is world-famous for its amazing style. Its construction was done by Krishna I. In Ellora, 'Ravan ki Khai' and 'Dhumara Lena' cave temples are related to the Brahmanical religion. In the 'Ravan ki Khai' cave temple, the scenes of Shiva dancing and Ravana lifting the Kailasa mountain are beautiful. Some caves of Ellora are also related to the Jain religion, in which Indra Sabha and Jagannatha cave are notable

questions.question_text: Which is the king described in Rajatarangini who himself went to the house of a cobbler and asked for the land of his hut to build a temple of Tribhuvanasvami?
questions.explanation: In the seventh century, a person named Durlabhavardhana established the Karkota dynasty in Kashmir. Durlabhavardhana's son and successor was Durlabhaka, who assumed the title of Pratapaditya. Pratapaditya had three sons - Chandrapida, Tarapida, and Muktapida, who are also called Vajraditya, Udayaditya, and Lalitaditya respectively. Durlabhaka ruled for 50 years. After him, Chandrapida became the ruler, who was a pious and noble ruler. It is described in Rajatarangini that Chandrapida himself went to a cobbler's house and asked for the land of his hut to build a temple of Tribhuvanasvami. Thereafter Tarapida became king, whom Kalhana describes as a cruel and merciless king. Lalitaditya Muktapida proved to be the most powerful ruler of the rulers of Kashmir. He was an imperialist ruler

questions.explanation: From the 8th century to the 12th century, the Chandela dynasty ruled over Bundelkhand and the south-western part of Uttar Pradesh. Which was a famous Rajput dynasty of India. Chandelas were originally jagirdars of Gurjara-Pratiharas. The founder of this dynasty was a person named Nannuk. The Chandela dynasty is famous for its architectural art, prominent examples of which are Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, Chausath Yogini Temple, Lakshmana Temple, etc. It is known from Trailokyavarman's (1203-1247 AD) 'Ajaygarh inscription' that dependents of warriors who attained martyrdom showing excellent bravery on the battlefield were given land for livelihood, which was called 'Mrityuka-Vritti'

questions.question_text: What were the orders issued by the Rashtrakuta kings and recorded by their secretaries called?
questions.explanation: The orders issued by the Rashtrakuta kings and recorded by their secretaries were called 'Rajashavitedam'. Those who listened to the oral orders given by the king and later wrote them on paper in a proper manner and sent them to the concerned officer for proper action were called 'Rahasyadhikrita' or Vayul-Katpar. Apart from village courts and tribal and vocational panchayats for the settlement of disputes, there was an arrangement of courts on behalf of the central government for providing justice, which was called Adhikaran or Dharmasana. Written orders issued by the king to run the governance of his state properly were called Rajpatra

questions.question_text: Arrange the following parts of the temples of Odisha in chronological order from bottom to top:
questions.explanation: Temples of Odisha represent pure Nagara style. These temples were built between the 7th and 13th centuries. The work of temple construction took place in the city of Bhubaneswar. In which prominent temples- Lingaraj temple, Jagannath temple of Puri, Sun temple of Konark (13th century) - The construction of this vimana of Arka (Sun) is the result of the combined talent of architecture experts and sculptor-craftsmen. Lingaraj temple - is the best example of fully developed Nagara style, its main parts are - Garbhagriha, which is called 'Deul' and the second part attached to it is called 'Jagamohana' The order of parts of Odisha temples from bottom to top is → Pabhaga → Band → Beki → Khapuri.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following queens who played an important role in the administration and culture of Kashmir according to Kalhana, in chronological order –
questions.explanation: Sugandha - Gopal Varman of Utpala dynasty became ruler in 902 AD. His mother - 'Sugandha' became his guardian, after the murder of Gopal Varman, Sugandha ruled as an independent ruler until 914 AD Didda - The marriage of Kshemagupta (950-58), son of Yashaskara of Kashmir, took place with 'Didda' of Lohara dynasty. Queen Didda ruled from 958 AD to 972 AD as the guardian of her minor son-'Abhimanyu'. Suryamati - was the wife of 'Ananta', ruler of Lohara dynasty. Under the influence of his wife Suryamati, he got many temples built and did charity work. Radda - The famous ruler of Karkota dynasty was Lalitaditya Muktapida (724-60). Kalhana gives him the credit for victory over the Arabs and he had defeated the queen 'Radda/Radda' of Karnata country.

questions.question_text: The famous commentator of Yajnavalkya Smriti, Apararka, was a king of:
questions.explanation: Smritis are given the status of Dharma Shastra. In Indian history, various Smriti texts were composed from the second century BC to the medieval period. Yajnavalkya Smriti (fifth century) are works up to the Gupta period. It is written in verses and its language is 'classical Sanskrit'. The commentators of Yajnavalkya Smriti are Vishwarupa, Vijnaneshwara, Apararka etc. Apararka was a king of the Shilahara (Konkan) dynasty Sena dynasty - This was a Hindu dynasty in Bengal in the 11th-12th century, its founder was Samanta Sena. Its prominent rulers were Ballal Sena, Lakshmana Sena. Kakatiya dynasty - This was a South Indian dynasty, which ruled in the 12th-14th century. Their capital was Warangal. Kakatiya people consider themselves descendants of Chola Karikala. The powerful king of this dynasty was Ganapati, later his daughter- Rudramba also became the ruler of the state. In 1323 AD, Muhammad Tughlaq merged it into his state. Shailodbhava dynasty - This dynasty ruled over some parts of Eastern India during the 6th-8th century, its core area is known as Kangoda Mandala. It includes some parts of present-day Odisha's Ganjam, Khordha and Puri districts. Their capital was Kangoda. Which is identified by the modern name Banpur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following texts are written by the Kashmiri poet Kshemendra?
questions.explanation: Kalavilasa, Samayamatrika (Autobiography of a prostitute), Ramayana Manjari, Bharat Manjari, Brihatkathamanjari, Dashavatar Charita, Avadana Kalpalata etc. works are written by Kashmiri poet Kshemendra. Kshemendra (990 - 1070 AD) was a contemporary of King Ananta and King Kalasha. No one except Vedavyasa has written as much literature in Sanskrit as Kshemendra has written Kutanimata/Kutanimat (book on Kamashastra) this work was written by Damodaragupta in the 7th century AD. 'Prabodhachandrodaya' this work is written by poet Krishna Mishra.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Gurjara-Pratihara kings in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The chronology of Gurjara-Pratihara kings is as follows Vatsaraja (775 - 800 AD) Nagabhata II (800 - 833 AD) Ramabhadra (833 - 836 AD) Mihira Bhoja I (836 - 885 AD) Mahendrapala I (885 - 910 AD) Mahipala (912 - 944 AD) Mahendrapala II (945 - 948 AD) Devapala (948 - 949 AD)

questions.question_text: According to ancient grammarians, which of the following pairs indicates female teachers?
questions.explanation: According to ancient grammarians, Acharya and Upadhyaya indicate female teachers. In ancient times, in the Gurukul education system, along with Acharya and Upadhyaya, female Acharya and Upadhyaya were also selected to provide education in the Gurukul by sages and Mahaupadhyayas. They were not only expert in Shastra Vidya but also expert in all other known sciences along with Shastra Vidya. Keeping 32 subjects and 64 arts in the center, they provided knowledge of major subjects like Vedas, Philosophy, Upanishads, Grammar, Mathematics, Medicine, Music, Art, Nyaya, and War-Science

questions.question_text: In which of the following inscriptions is the mention of the time calculation of the Bharata-war found?

options.A: In the Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II
options.C: In Prabhavati Gupta's Poona copper plate

questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II was a powerful ruler of the Chalukya dynasty. Detailed information about the Chalukya dynasty is found in the Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II. The author of this inscription is 'Ravi Kirti'. In this inscription, the mention of time calculation from the event of the Bharata-war (Mahabharata war) (3102 BC) has been made. Madhuban copper plate (631 AD) has been obtained from Ghosi tehsil of Mau district of Uttar Pradesh. In this, there is mention of Agrahara (land grant) given by Harsha to Bhatta Vatsaswami of Savarni gotra and Bhatta Shivadevaswami of Vishnukriti gotra of Somkunda village of Shravasti Bhukti. Prabhavati Gupta was the daughter of Gupta emperor Chandragupta II. Her marriage took place with Vakataka ruler Rudrasena II. An important inscription of Prabhavati Gupta is the Poona copper plate inscription. Haraha inscription was obtained from Barabanki district of Uttar Pradesh. This inscription was got inscribed by Suryavarma, son of Maukhari ruler Ishanavarman. By studying this, we get knowledge of the events of the reign of the first four kings of this dynasty

questions.question_text: Who carried out the excavation of the Buddhist site Nalanda University?
questions.explanation: Information about Nalanda was first given by Hamilton in 1812 AD. The exploration work of Nalanda Mahavihara was first started by General Cunningham in 1862 AD and in 1870 AD Broadley excavated Chaitya No. 12 there and published an inscription. In 1915 AD, the Archaeological Survey of India took the excavation work in its hands for the renovation of Nalanda. This work started under the guidance of the then Director of the Archaeological Department Sir John Marshall and Spooner (Dr. Spooner)

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the Sanskrit poem, 'Setubandha' book?
questions.explanation: The author of the Sanskrit poem, 'Setubandha' book was Pravarasena II. This book contains a description of Rama's Lanka victory. Pravarasena II was a ruler of the Vakataka dynasty. The establishment of this dynasty was done around 255 AD by Vindhyashakti of Vishnuvriddhi gotra. His ancestors were local rulers of Berar under the Satavahanas. After the Satavahanas, Vindhyashakti declared his independence

questions.question_text: In which cave is the Kailasa temple located?
questions.explanation: Rashtrakuta rulers were great patrons of art. No notable archaeological remains of Rashtrakuta art have been found from their capital Manyakheta yet. But important monuments of Rashtrakuta art are located in Ellora, Elephanta, Jogeshwari, and Mandleshwar. Among these, Ellora and Elephanta are famous for their cave architecture, sculpture or stone sculpture, and painting. Under royal patronage, cave temples related to Shaiva religion were built in Ellora, the number of which is 17 (seventeen). Among the major cave temples or mandapas here, Ravan ki Khai, Dashavatara temple, Kailasa temple, Sita ki Nahani or Ghumarlele, Devavada, Lambeshwar, Rameshwar, Nilakantha etc., are especially notable. The Kailasa temple was built by Krishna I

questions.question_text: Who was the Chancellor (Kulapati) at the Nalanda University when Xuanzang studied there?
questions.explanation: Xuanzang (629-645 AD) was a Chinese traveler who came to India in the seventh century AD to collect Buddhist texts and stayed here for about 15 years. He has compiled his travel memoir in the form of a book named 'Si-Yu-Ki'. Other names of Xuanzang are 'Yuan Chwang' or 'Shuanchang', 'Shakyamuni' and Prince of Travelers. Xuanzang stayed at Nalanda University for one and a half years and studied. During his time, the principal (Acharya) here was Shilabhadra

questions.question_text: Where are the Chaitya caves of Bhoja and Kanheri located?
questions.explanation: The Chaitya caves of Bhoja and Kanheri are located in Lonavala, Maharashtra. Lonavala is a hill station and municipal council located in Pune district of the Indian state of Maharashtra. Kanheri caves in Lonavala are very ancient and historical caves. Its construction is considered to be 160 years before Christ. Kanheri cave includes the largest Chaitya cave of India

questions.question_text: By what other name is 'Kutila' script also known?
questions.explanation: 'Kutila script' is also known as 'Siddhamatrika script'. This script was prevalent in Northern India in the early medieval period. This script is a developed form of Brahmi script

questions.question_text: In the ancient Indian administrative system, the post named "Kanchuki" was used for-

options.B: For In-charge of the inner chamber (Antahpura)

questions.explanation: In the ancient Indian administrative system, 'Kanchuki' was the in-charge of the ruler's inner chamber (Antahpura). This official managed the ruler's family life

questions.question_text: Which of the following Rashtrakuta rulers gave liberal patronage to the Digambara sect of Jain religion?
questions.explanation: Rashtrakuta ruler Amoghavarsha (814-878 AD) gave liberal patronage to the Digambara sect of Jain religion. Famous Jain scholar 'Jinasena' lived in his royal court, who wrote 'Adi Purana'. Amoghavarsha was of a religious nature and a liberal patron of learning and art. He wrote a poetic text in Kannada language named 'Kavirajamarga'. Even after becoming a follower of Jain religion, Amoghavarsha used to respect Hindu gods and goddesses. He was a staunch devotee of Mahalakshmi

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is/are correct regarding the Tripartite struggle? (1) Mihira Bhoja - Dhruva - Dharmapala (2) Nagabhata-II - Govinda-III - Vigrahapala (3) Ramachandra - Amoghavarsha-I - Vigrahapala Use the code given below to select the correct answer- Code-

The commission has given the answer to this question as option (b).

questions.question_text: In which dynasty's inscriptions was the word 'Hindustan' first mentioned?
questions.explanation: The word 'Hindustan' was first mentioned in the inscriptions of the Sassanid dynasty of Iran. The Sassanid dynasty was established in Iran in the third century

questions.question_text: The famous 'Vaidya Vagbhata' was the composition of-
questions.explanation: The famous works of 6th-century great Ayurveda Acharya Vagbhata are 'Ashtanga Sangraha' and 'Ashtanga Hridaya'. Ancient sources and Chinese travelers' accounts show that Vagbhata was born in Sindh and he was a follower of Buddhism Important text- 'Naishadha Charita' was written by 12th-century great philosopher and Shringara-rasa poet Shri Harsha. They lived in the court of Gahadvala rulers of Kannauj, Vijaya Chandra and Jaya Chandra. 'Naishadha Charita' is a Shringara-dominant poetic text based on the love story of Nala-Damayanti. Kashikavritti is a Sanskrit grammar text, which is a commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi, whose authors are Jayaditya and Vamana.

questions.question_text: Who identified the five distinct chronological and cultural phases of the epic 'Ramayana'?
questions.explanation: In the year 1984 AD, J.L. Brockington identified five phases of development and culture of Ramayana after careful study of language, style, and subject matter. Similarly, James L. Fitz-Gerald has presented this argument regarding Mahabharata. The Brahmanical system saw the increasing popularity of Buddhist and Jain religions as a challenge and presented its response in the form of Mahabharata against this system

questions.question_text: Early medieval text written in Slesh (double meaning) is-
questions.explanation: An important early medieval text written in Slesh (double meaning) is Ramacharita written by Sandhyakar Nandi. In this text, Sandhyakar Nandi calls himself 'Valmiki of Kaliyuga' (Kalikalyug Valmiki) and Rama Pala as 'Rama'. Ramacharita mentions the defeat of Bhima, the leader of Kaivartas. This text is an important source for the study of the history of the Pala dynasty, especially the later rulers

questions.question_text: During which period was Kalhana's Rajatarangini written?
questions.explanation: Rajatarangini is an important text written by Kalhana in Mahabharata style between 1148-1150 AD, in which there is a description of the history of Hindu dynasties of Kashmir. Rajatarangini has a total of 8 chapters (Tarang) and 8000 verses. Kalhana started Rajatarangini during the time of King Harsha and this text ended in the time of King Jayasimha

questions.question_text: Which Smritikars (law-givers) gave legal recognition to widow remarriage?
questions.explanation: Narada and Parashara have given permission for remarriage to the wife in 5 special circumstances. In the case of husband's death, husband not being found, husband becoming an ascetic, husband being impotent, and husband becoming fallen, Narada and Parashara have given permission for remarriage to the wife. Vishnu, Yajnavalkya and Brihaspati consider widows as the full owners of the property. While Manu, Narada and Katyayana were against this

questions.question_text: Arrange the following parts of Khajuraho temple architecture in descending order and select the correct answer from the codes given below: (i) Jagati (ii) Amalaka (iii) Kalash (iv) Adhisthana Code:
questions.explanation: The descending order of the various parts of Khajuraho temple architecture is Kalash, Amalaka, Adhisthana, and Jagati. Kalash used to be the topmost part of the temple where Kalash-like structure was established. Below the Kalash used to be the Amalaka which was spherical. Jagati used to be a type of temple base and the part above the Jagati was called Adhisthana. Higher Education Selection Commission has given (b) as the answer to this question

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Kuttanimata'?
questions.explanation: The author of Kuttanimata was Damodaragupta. Damodaragupta lived in the court of Vinayaditya Jayapinda, the last powerful ruler of the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir. This book was written to teach Kamashastra to prostitutes. questions.question_text: Whose temple's spire (shikhara) among the following temples of Odisha is of Dravidian style?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation - Temples of Dravidian style used to be of a completely different kind from North Indian temples. Some North Indian temples show Southern influence. Such as - the famous Vaital Deul temple (1000 AD) located in Bhubaneswar (Odisha) has a spire of Gopuram style (Dravidian style). Among Odisha's temples, the Lingaraja temple (1000 AD) located in Bhubaneswar is considered the most excellent example of Hindu temple architecture. Lingaraja temple, Jagannath temple, and Rajarani temple are examples of Nagara style. The spire (ganda) of Vaital Deul temple rises upwards just like other temples of Odisha for some distance. After that, it takes the form of a wagon-back in two storeys. There is some internal incision between the two storeys. There is a trident-equipped triple amalaka on top of the upper storey. It does not have a chariot-like shape on the front in its bar. Its walls are also unique in their own way. In the bar, there are carved protruding strips on every wall on all four sides, in which there is a depiction of figures. This arrangement is a feature of South Indian temples.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation - The author of Katha Manjari (Brihatkatha Manjari) is Kshemendra. With the intention of making this book elegant, the poet has included some other stories in the original story. The main purpose of this composition is to familiarize students of Sanskrit with the story-line of Brihatkatha. There are various features in Kshemendra's story system. Kshemendra got skill in describing female beauty and the heroism of princesses. There are a total of 7500 verses in it which are divided into 16 chapters (sargas). Sometimes the language has become complicated and sometimes easy to understand. The description of seasons and natural scenes is also spectacular. Kshemendra has included the humor element in the story very beautifully. Through this, he made fun of the hypocrites of his era. Kshemendra's purpose for the composition was not just to present an interesting and humorous plot, but through them, to make ordinary public life elevated from a moral point of view.

questions.explanation: The first mention of Linga worship is in the Matsya Purana. Linga worship is mentioned in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata. Shiva's oldest sculpture in the form of a Linga was obtained in the famous Gudimallam near Madras in the first century AD

questions.question_text: Identify the dynasty of Queen Rudramadevi:
questions.explanation: Rudradeva Maharaja (Rudramadevi) ruled in the Kakatiya dynasty of Warangal, who was essentially a woman. Her original name was Rudramadevi. She was one of the female rulers in the history of India. Queen Rudradevi kept the flag of the Kakatiya dynasty flying in the Deccan plateau from 1263 until her death

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a problem of the objectivity of history?
questions.explanation: Bias in writing, personal belief towards a particular belief or idea, ignoring the demand of time, the personal side (subjectivity) of any historian is that which influences history writing, and also influences its objectivity

questions.question_text: 'Time and space are the eyes of history' who said this?
questions.explanation: Along with other aspects in history writing, the geographical environment of that area or reign also has special importance because in the imagination used to connect the facts, the time period and geographical perspective play an important role in their determination. Keeping this fact in mind, Janssen has given the definition of 'time and space being the eyes of history'

questions.question_text: Ajanta caves are situated in:
questions.explanation: Ajanta caves are situated in Maharashtra. Their number is 29, which are up to 100 feet deep and are dug in the shape of a horseshoe. Ajanta cave numbers 16, 17, 19 are Gupta period

questions.question_text: Historical research is composed of:
questions.explanation: Collecting new data and interpreting data in a new way are both involved in the creation of historical research. Other steps of research are – (1) Determination of research problem, (2) Survey of research literature, (3) Formation of research hypothesis, (4) Analysis of data, etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following chronological order is correct?

options.A: Vindhyashakti I, Pravarasena I, Rudrasena I, Prithvisena I
options.B: Pravarasena I, Rudrasena I, Vindhyashakti I, Prithvisena I
options.C: Vindhyashakti I, Rudrasena I, Pravarasena I, Prithvisena I
options.D: Vindhyashakti I, Prithvisena I, Rudrasena I, Pravarasena I

questions.explanation: All rulers are related to the Vakataka dynasty. Vindhyashakti founded this dynasty, then Pravarasena I became the ruler. He was the only ruler who assumed the title of 'Samrat'. After him, Rudrasena I became the ruler. In the Vakataka inscriptions, he has been described as a devotee of 'Mahabhairava'. After him, Prithvisena I became the ruler

questions.question_text: The author of Aihole inscription was:
questions.explanation: The author of the Aihole inscription was Ravikirti. The Aihole inscription was related to Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II. In this inscription, there is a description of the war between Harsha and Pulakeshin-II. The Aihole inscription calculates time from the Mahabharata war. Ravikirti was a follower of Jain religion

questions.question_text: Pallavamalla title was of:
questions.explanation: Nandivarman II was a follower of Vaishnavism. He encouraged art and literature and got the Mukteshvara temple and Vaikuntha Perumal temple of Kanchi built. His title was 'Pallavamalla'

questions.question_text: Who was the first Iranian invader of India?
questions.explanation: The first Iranian invader of India was Cyrus. Cyrus is also called Cyrus II. Darius or Darius I was also an Iranian who invaded India. Alexander was a Greek ruler who came up to the Beas river while conquering some parts of western India

questions.question_text: King Amoghavarsha is related to:
questions.explanation: After Govinda III, the minor successor Amoghavarsha (814-880 AD) became the ruler. He was a Rashtrakuta ruler. Amoghavarsha was a liberal patron of learning and art. He composed 'Kavirajamarga', the first poetic work in the Kannada language. In his court lived the author of 'Adi-Purana', Jinasena, and the author of 'Ganitasara Sangraha', Mahaviracharya

questions.question_text: Who was the first Greek writer to mention India?
questions.explanation: The first Greek writer to mention India was Scylax. Whereas Megasthenes was a Mauryan period writer who composed Indika, through which information about Mauryan society and culture is obtained

questions.question_text: Which of the following Greek accounts pre-dates Alexander?
questions.explanation: Ctesias was a famous Iranian royal physician. He obtained all information about India from Iranian officials. Strabo, Pliny, Ptolemy, Arrian were writers after Alexander's time. Onesicritus, Nearchus, Aristobulus were Greek writers contemporary to Alexander

questions.question_text: In which source has Mihirakula been identified as an 'avatar of a demon'?
questions.explanation: Rajatarangini by Kalhana, which is the most detailed book written on Kashmir. In that same book, there is a description of Mihirakula as an 'avatar of a demon'

questions.question_text: Who among the following called Brahmins and Shramanas as eternal enemies like snake and mongoose?
questions.explanation: Born in 1575 AD, Lama Taranatha in his book 'History of Buddhism in India' in 1608 AD called Brahmins and Shramanas eternal enemies like snake and mongoose. He was a Tibetan historian

questions.question_text: Match the sculptures of List-I with the places of List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I | List-II A. Buddha sculpture of Pital khora | 1. Bhojpur B. Buddha sculpture of bronze | 2. Kangra C. Sitting Buddha sculpture | 3. Mankunwar D. Parshvanatha sculpture | 4. Sultanganj Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: List-I | List-II Buddha sculpture of Pital khora | Kangra Buddha sculpture of bronze | Sultanganj Sitting Buddha sculpture | Mankunwar Parshvanatha sculpture | Bhojpur

questions.question_text: Identify the rivers from which Alexander was forced to return:
questions.explanation: In 305 BC, Chandragupta defeated Alexander on the banks of the Beas river and forced him to return

questions.question_text: Match the authors of List-I with the patrons of List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I | List-II A. Bilhana | 1. Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya B. Padmagupta | 2. Gahadvala ruler Jayachandra C. Sri Harsha | 3. Kannauj ruler Yashovarman D. Vakpati | 4. Paramara ruler Sindhuraja Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Bilhana was the royal poet of Chalukya dynasty's greatest ruler Vikramaditya VI. Padmagupta was the royal poet of Paramara ruler Sindhuraja

questions.question_text: Match the temples of List-I with the places given in List-II~ List-I | List-II A. Brihadisvara | 1. Thiruvananthapuram B. Meenakshi Amman | 2. Tirupati C. Sri Venkateswara Swamy | 3. Madurai D. Padmanabhaswamy temple | 4. Thanjavur A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is Brihadisvara | Thanjavur Meenakshi Amman | Madurai Sri Venkateswara Swamy temple | Tirupati Padmanabhaswamy temple | Thiruvananthapuram

questions.question_text: Match the areas of List-I with the Rajput dynasty of List-II~ List-I | List-II A. Malwa | 1. Chauhan B. Kannauj | 2. Gahadvala C. Ajmer | 3. Paramara D. Jabalpur | 4. Kalachuri A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is Malwa | Paramara dynasty Kannauj | Gahadvala dynasty Ajmer | Chauhan dynasty Jabalpur | Kalachuri dynasty

questions.question_text: Match the list of authors (List-I) with the list of books written by them (List-II)~ List-I | List-II A. Banabhatta | 1. Vikramorvashiyam B. Varahamihira | 2. Mrichchhakatikam C. Kalidasa | 3. Brihatsamhita D. Shudraka | 4. Harshacharita A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is Banabhatta | Harshacharita Varahamihira | Brihatsamhita, Panchasiddhantika Kalidasa | Vikramorvashiyam, Kumarasambhavam, Malavikagnimitram, Abhijñanasakuntalam, Ritusamhara Shudraka | Mrichchhakatikam

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Mathura sculpture style is not correct?

options.A: The school of sculpture preserved in Mathura by followers of Jain religion is called Mathura school.
options.B: White marble sandstone was used in the sculptures of Mathura school.
options.C: The beginning of this school is considered to be the end of the second century BC.
options.D: Later, the Kushanas gave patronage to this school. Some of their portrait sculptures have been found near Mathura.
options.E: It is believed that the first image of Buddha was created by Mathura school.

questions.explanation: Mathura art style was prevalent during the Kushan era similar to Gandhara style. Mathura was a huge center of this art. This art style started at the end of the first century BC. During the Mathura period, Buddha's Dharmachakra-pravartana mudra, Abhaya-mudra, Dhyana-mudra, Bhumi-sparsha mudra, etc. sculptures were created. White spotted red sandstone was used in their sculptures

questions.question_text: The court poet of Pratihara ruler Mahendrapala I and Mahipala was:
questions.explanation: Rajasekhara was the royal Guru of Pratihara ruler Mahendrapala I of Kannauj. He also lived in the court of his son Mahipala. Later, he left Kannauj and went to the Kalachuri ruler Yuvaraja of Tripuri. Rajasekhara composed many books in which Bhuvanakosha, Harivilasa, Balaramayana, Kavyamimamsa, Viddhashalabhanjika, Karpuramanjari are major

questions.question_text: Which inscription tells us that Vigraharaja IV made Delhi his subordinate?
questions.explanation: Bijolia inscription tells us that Vigraharaja IV made Delhi his subordinate. Bijolia inscription is a Sanskrit language inscription carved on a rock near the Parshvanatha temple in Bijolia village in Udaipur district. It mentions the achievements of the rulers of the Chauhan dynasty of Amber and Shakambhari (Sambhar). According to it, a person named Vasudeva laid the foundation of the Chauhan kingdom of Shakambhari and had the Sambhar lake built

questions.question_text: Patrons of Mahameru temple construction architecture style were:
questions.explanation: Pratihara were the patrons of the Mahameru temple construction architecture style. The Dadhichimata, Goth-Manglod, Bateshwar Mahadeva temple, etc., were built in Mahameru style. In the Pratihara-era sculpture of Rajasthan, the oldest depiction of the Ramayana scene is found in the Dadhichimata temple

questions.question_text: Which of the following literary sources of Rajasthan history is composed in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: Prithviraja Vijaya is a Sanskrit epic. It was composed by Kashmiri Jayanka between 1191-93 AD. This work describes Prithviraja III and the First Battle of Tarain (1191 AD). It does not contain a description of the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD). Samarayicchakaha was composed by Haribhadra Suri in Prakrit prose. Kuvalayamala was composed by Udyotana Suri in Prakrit language. Rajarupaka was composed by Virabhan

questions.question_text: Match the books of List-I with the authors of List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I | List-II A. Panchasiddhantika | 1. Varahamihira B. Kavyamimamsa | 2. Rajasekhara C. Visuddhimagga | 3. Buddhaghosa D. Kadambari | 4. Banabhatta Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Panchasiddhantika is a book by Varahamihira, which happened during the time of Maharaja Vikramaditya, it contains a description of astronomy. The Kavyamimamsa composed by Sanskrit poet Rajasekhara is a massive book written on rhetoric, which originally had 18 sections Visuddhimagga is a Pali book composed by Buddhaghosa, it is considered the most important Theravada book after the Tripitaka. Kadambari is a great novel of Sanskrit composed by Banabhatta, it is considered the first novel of the world.

questions.question_text: To whom were the Alvars of South India devotees?
questions.explanation: Alvars used to be devotees of Vishnu, their number was 12. Andal was the only female saint among Alvars. Periyalvar emphasized sense control and self-discipline

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was not a season of the ancient Indian year?
questions.explanation: In ancient times, 6 seasons were believed which are Vasant, Greeshma, Varsha, Sharad, Hemant and Shishir. According to the Hindi almanac, Ashadha is the fourth month of the year starting from Chaitra

questions.question_text: In which range are the Nashik caves carved?
questions.explanation: Nashik caves are situated in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri) range

questions.question_text: Which color is least used in Ajanta paintings?
questions.explanation: The description of the use of green color in Ajanta paintings is found to be less, evidence of the use of all other colors is found in the cave

questions.question_text: Which one of the following books is composed by Bhasa?
questions.explanation: Svapnavasavadatta is a famous Sanskrit play by the great poet Bhasa. It has 6 acts. The other three works - Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam are by Kalidasa, and Devichandraguptam is by Vishakhadatta

questions.question_text: Which one of the following food items was not available in ancient India?
questions.explanation: Date was not used in ancient India. After the Arab invasion in 712 AD, the use of this fruit started in India from the Arabs

questions.question_text: Which one of the following substances was used in making blue color in ancient India?
questions.explanation: Lapis lazuli was used in making blue color in ancient India. Evidence of red, blue, and other colors is found in the paintings of Ajanta caves. Lapis lazuli, mined in Afghanistan, was used for jewelry and ornaments and later crushed to make a blue colored powder which reached other countries from here

questions.question_text: Match List A with List B and choose the correct answer using the code given below: List A (Poet) | List B (Work) A. Tulsidas | (i) Uddhav Shatak B. Jagannathdas Ratnakar | (ii) Usne Kaha Tha C. Premchand | (iii) Vinaya Patrika D. Chandradhar Sharma 'Guleri' | (iv) Godan Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Vinaya Patrika is Tulsidas's, Godan is Munshi Premchand's, Usne Kaha Tha is Chandradhar Sharma 'Guleri's' and Uddhav Shatak is Jagannathdas Ratnakar's work

questions.question_text: Where was the capital of Nanda rulers?
questions.explanation: The capital of Nanda rulers was Pataliputra. Dhanananda was the last ruler of this dynasty who was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya and laid the foundation of the Mauryan dynasty

questions.question_text: Which book's main subject is the story of Krishna Vasudeva?
questions.explanation: The main subject of the Shiva Purana is Shiva Purana - Description of the various forms of Shiva. Agni Purana - It contains a description of the Trinity (Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh). It is also called the 'Encyclopedia of Indian Culture'. Brahma Purana - It contains the description of the incarnation theory through the story of Rama and Krishna.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following places was related to Harsh?
questions.explanation: Thanesar was the capital of the Pre-Vardhana dynasty of Harsh, but Harsh made Kannauj his capital. Daimabad is related to the Copper Age, where evidence of copper objects is found in large quantities

questions.question_text: Which one of the following books is in the Telugu language?
questions.explanation: Sumatishatakam is a collection of verses (niti-grantha) written in the Telugu language. According to some scholars, its author was Baddena Bhupala. Among the other options, Silappadikaram and Thirukkural are Sangam-era Tamil works, while Mṛcchakatikam is a Sanskrit work written by Shudraka

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to ancient Indian sites: (1) Lomas Rishi cave is in Bihar (2) Bagh cave is in Madhya Pradesh Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Lomas Rishi cave is located near the Nagarjuni hills in Jehanabad, Bihar. Bagh caves are located on the banks of the Baghini river in Madhya Pradesh. Therefore, both statements are correct

questions.question_text: In ancient history, which city is called the first wall-enclosed city?
questions.explanation: Jericho is considered the oldest city in the world, where humans started living about 11 thousand years ago. It is situated on the banks of the Jordan River. It is believed that Jericho is the first city that was surrounded by a wall. In 1967, Israel captured it from Jordan. It has been under Palestine since 1994. It is mentioned in the Hebrew Bible as the 'Jericho City of Palm Trees'. The Old Testament of the Bible was written here

questions.question_text: How many dynasties of Rajputs are mentioned in Rajatarangini and Kumarapala Charita?
questions.explanation: In post-medieval literature, the word Rajput was used for the Kshatriya caste. Kalhana's Rajatarangini and Kumarapala Charita mention 36 clans of Rajputs, in which they are given the designation of Rajput (Rajputra)

questions.question_text: Which Gurjara-Pratihara king has been described as the 'destroyer of Mlechchhas' in the Gwalior Prashasti?
questions.explanation: Nagabhata I (730-756 AD) was the real ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty. Nagabhata established a powerful kingdom in western India by fighting against the Arabs. He has been called the 'destroyer of Mlechchhas' in the Gwalior Prashasti. This dynasty was the most famous Pratihara dynasty among the Agnikula Rajputs

questions.question_text: Which king got the Kailasa temple of Ellora built?
questions.explanation: Krishna I became the ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty in 756 AD. Krishna I was a conqueror as well as a builder. He got the famous Kailasa temple (cave temple) of Ellora built. This temple has been made by cutting a single rock. This temple is located in Ellora cave number 16. A replica of Mount Kailash has been built in this temple

questions.question_text: Which Vakataka ruler assumed the title of 'Maharaja'?
questions.explanation: The Vakataka dynasty was founded around 255 AD by Vindhyashakti, who is called the 'Vakataka Dynasty Ketu' in inscriptions. Vindhyashakti's son Haritiputra Pravarasena was the only Vakataka king to assume the title of Samrat (Maharaja). During his reign, the Vakataka kingdom extended from Bundelkhand to Hyderabad. According to the Puranas, he performed four Ashvamedha sacrifices, one Vajapeya sacrifice, and other Vedic sacrifices

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not relevant for the rise of regional organizations during the period between 600 and 1200 AD? (i) Development of Sanskrit texts (ii) Development of regional languages (iii) Refinement of architecture and art (iv) Rise of distinct regional styles of art and architecture (Rise of styles) Select the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: During the period between 600 AD and 1200 AD (Early Medieval period), the relevant points for the rise of regional organizations were - development of regional languages, and the rise of distinct regional styles of art and architecture. Whereas the development of Sanskrit texts and the refinement of architecture and art are not relevant

questions.question_text: ‘‘It was probably the cultural innovation adopted by the Sakas for their political dominance that a new era was named after them.’’ According to Sheldon Pollock, what was this ‘cultural innovation’?

options.C: Use of wine, meat and stitched clothes
options.D: Use of Sanskrit for political purposes

questions.explanation: The Scythians were called Sakas in India. Chinese writers called them Sai or Sai-Wang. After the Greeks, the Sakas attacked India. The most famous and powerful Saka ruler was Rudradaman. His Girnar or Junagadh inscription is the first inscription written in Champu style and pure prose Sanskrit language. According to Sheldon Pollock, the use of Sanskrit for political purposes was probably the cultural innovation adopted by the Sakas for their political dominance, that a new era was named after them

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): It is believed that Ajatashatru killed his father in 493 BC. He annexed Kosala into his kingdom although the ruler there was his maternal uncle. Reason (R): Bimbisara's son Ajatashatru of Magadha was eager to become the ruler of Magadha and he annexed other regions into his kingdom. What is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Ajatashatru became the ruler of Magadha after killing his father Bimbisara. Ajatashatru was eager to become the ruler of Magadha and he annexed other regions into his kingdom. It is believed that Ajatashatru also annexed the Kosala Janapada into his kingdom, although the ruler there was his maternal uncle

questions.question_text: Identify the temple from the group of temples located near Mahakuteshwara near Badami, of which a part of the sanctum sanctorum has some significance.
questions.explanation: The Mahakuteshwara temple group located between Badami and Pattadakal are temples of the Trilokya type endowed with Nagara style shikharas. Among the temples of this group, the Sangameshwara temple is the oldest, which was built around 725 AD during the reign of Vijayaditya (697-733 AD). The construction of the Vimana (sanctum sanctorum) of this temple is of the trilokya type, which has a simple base with double walls. The pillar-supported outer enclosure forms the Ardh-mandapa located in front of the Vimana

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?

options.A: R.S. Sharma : Urban Decay in India
options.B: John Williams : The Art of Gupta India: Empire and Province
options.C: A.L. Basham : The Wonder That Was India
options.D: Romila Thapar : Myths and Realities: Studies in the Formation of Indian Culture

questions.explanation: The author of the book 'Myths and Realities: Studies in the Formation of Indian Culture' is D.D. Kosambi

questions.question_text: Which of the statements regarding Agraharas are correct?
questions.explanation: In the Gupta period, the land given in charity to temples and the Brahmana class was called 'Agrahara'. Such land was free from all taxes and the holders had full ownership over them. The purpose of such land grants was purely educational and religious

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): It is argued that the praise sung by poets in early historical South India was not the basis of political power. Reason (R): Poets of that period depended on kings for their material prosperity. What is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: In early historical South India, poets wrote many poems in praise of kings. In return for this, they received good rewards from the state. According to tradition, besides wealth, they were also rewarded with land, horses, chariots, elephants, etc

questions.question_text: In which of the following is the radiocarbon dating technique applied?
questions.explanation: The dating method by Carbon-14 is called the radiocarbon dating technique. It is used in archeo-biology to determine the life period and time cycle based on the remains of animals and plants

questions.question_text: ‘‘If we leave aside the iron found in Ahar, then all the Carbon-14 (14C) dates for the early iron level in India come from about 1000 BC or a little earlier.’’ Whose opinion is this?
questions.explanation: Irfan Habib's statement is that 'if we leave aside the iron found in Ahar, then all the Carbon-14 (14C) dates for the early iron level in India come from about 1000 BC or a little earlier.'

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Rajasekhara?

options.A: He was the most powerful ruler of the Chola dynasty (985-1014 AD).
options.B: He was the court poet (c. 9th-10th century AD) of the Pratihara rulers Mahendrapala and Mahipala.
options.C: He was the first known ruler of the Satavahanas (c. 230 BC) mentioned in the Puranas.
options.D: He composed one of the ten consolation poems of the Sangam collection, Siripanduru-Pattala.

questions.explanation: Rajasekhara used to live in the royal court of the Pratihara king Mahendrapala and his son Mahipala (9th-10th century AD) of Kannauj. He was a famous Sanskrit poet and playwright. Rajasekhara was more of a poet than a playwright. There is more poeticism in his works. He is a word-poet. He used idioms and proverbs openly. His plays are not suitable for the stage, but rather they are quite interesting to read His main works are - (1) Bala Ramayana (2) Bala Bharata (3) Viddhashalabhanjika (4) Karpuramanjari (5) Kavyamimansa

questions.question_text: Which of the following is called the first available Indian work with a well-organized description of instruments?
questions.explanation: Brahmagupta was a famous mathematician of the Gupta period. He composed two important works - Brahmasphuta Siddhanta and Khandakhadyaka or Khandakhadyaka Paddhati. Chapters 19 to 24 of Brahmasphuta Siddhanta are dedicated to astronomical instruments and observations

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.A: Nagara Style: The base of Nagara temples is square, the middle of each side has many projections that provide a cross-shape.
options.B: Dravidian Style: The most important feature of this style is their pyramidal shikharas.
options.C: Kashmiri Style: This is a pure local style free from any kind of influence from the outside world.
options.D: Besara Style: This is a mixture of Northern and Southern styles.

questions.explanation: The best example of the Kashmiri style is the Martand Sun temple. This temple was built by the Karkota dynasty king Lalitaditya Muktapida. The feature of the architecture of this temple is its arches. The architectural style of the pillars and doorways of the temple resembles the Gothic style of Rome in some parts. Greek structure has been used in its pillars. A glimpse of Chinese, Roman, Greek, and Indian styles is seen in this temple

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect?

options.A: Long after the daily work of writing was known, the fascination for oral tradition remained.
options.B: Bhartrihari declared that 'knowledge remains in the form of words... revealed consciousness is the foundation of all types of knowledge.'
options.C: Thus, Indians gave priority to 'Ganathasth' (memorized) over 'Kanthasth' (learning by heart).
options.D: The idea of the Latin grammarians of the ninth century was completely different from ideal Indian ideas. Therefore, in Europe, an educated person was one who was 'literatus' i.e., learned (lettered man).

questions.explanation: Shruti is the supreme and paramount religious text of Hindu religion. The literal meaning of Shruti is heard, i.e., the voice of God which was heard by the sages in ancient times and spread in the world. They are called Vedas. Besides these, other texts are considered Smriti. That is, texts made by the memory and intellect of humans, which are considered human descriptions and interpretations of Shruti in reality. In case of any dispute between Shruti and Smriti, Shruti gets recognition

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Book) | List-II (Author)
questions.explanation: List-I (Book) | List-II (Author) (A) Kavyadarsha | (iv) Dandin (B) Ashtadhyayi | (iii) Panini (C) Mahabhashya | (ii) Patanjali (D) Tantraloka | (i) Abhinavagupta

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.explanation: The purpose of historiography is not just to present a description of past events, but to analyze the gradual development of those ideologies which have arisen and developed in different periods of history. In this context, it is a complex process which includes searching for main sources of information, their evaluation, synthesis and presentation. German scholar Leopold von Ranke published his influential work on history in 1924. Ranke criticized traditional methods and made it clear that history can be studied scientifically, free from subjective bias. He emphasized that historical research will be based on primary sources, for this he accessed the Royal Archives of the Berlin University to build access to archives, especially government archives. Therefore, the credit for the development of government archives can be given to Ranke. Spengler's philosophy of history attacks the European periodization of history into Ancient, Medieval and Modern. According to him, war and the construction of cities are indicators of the decline of civilization. Although his theory cannot be considered scientific. His pessimism is revealed by his theory

questions.question_text: Which philosopher of history said, ‘‘All history is contemporary history’’?
questions.explanation: Benedetto Croce was a famous idealist philosopher of Italy who wrote on many subjects, among which philosophy, history, and aesthetics were prominent. He was a liberal thinker but opposed free trade. He is considered the pioneer of Expressionism. His opinion about history was that ‘‘All history is contemporary history’’. Spengler emphasized the need for synthesis and purpose in history and proposed a new theory ‘‘Every human civilization has a limited life-span’’

questions.question_text: Which deity has held the supreme place in Java?
questions.explanation: In ancient times, Java Island was called 'Yava Dwipa'. Many temples of Hindu and Buddhist communities and their remains have been found here. Near Magelang, the 'Borobudur' temple is the world's largest Buddhist temple. Along with Buddhist religion, evidence of Lord Shiva's temple has also been found here, which are considered symbols of the faith of the Hindus. On 27 December 1949, the Republic of Indonesia was established, of which Java is the main island. The Prambanan temple of Lord Shiva located in Java is considered a unique and ancient temple of the 10th century

questions.question_text: According to epigraphic evidence, which of the following rulers were skilled musicians?

questions.explanation: Oppression of human by human on a large scale has occurred under slavery. Slavery is called the culmination of institutional exploitation. Under slavery, usually, debt-ridden or people captured in wars were made slaves. In India, this practice was abolished in 1843 by Lord Ellenborough

questions.question_text: Abhinavagupta was a famous Acharya of which of the following sects?
questions.explanation: Abhinavagupta (975-1025) was a philosopher, mystic, and Acharya of literary theory. He was also a musicologist, poet, playwright, theologian, and logician. He established literary theory at a high level of philosophy by providing a psychological interpretation of this theory (Abhivyaktivada) and provided a mature commentary on 'Pratyabhijna' and 'Trika philosophies', establishing them on the test of logic. His initial works include the composition of 'Kramastotra' in 66 Laukika Samvat (991 AD) and 'Bhairavastotra' in 68 Samvat (933)

questions.explanation: The merchant class had to pass through many states and forests to trade. Therefore, they usually traveled together in caravans and formed trade unions (guilds) to protect their interests. In South India, in the eighth century and later periods, there were many such unions, among them the most famous were 'Manigramam' and 'Nanadesi'. These trade unions used to trade far and wide, both within the peninsula and with South-East Asia and China. They are mentioned in a fragmented Tamil inscription of the eleventh century found at Lobu Tua in Sumatra

questions.question_text: Which of the following temples of Odisha is Pancharatha?
questions.explanation: Odisha temples represent the pure Nagara style. These were built between the 7th and 13th centuries. The work of temple construction was done in Bhubaneswar city. Among these, Lingaraj, Mukteshwar, Rajarani are the best examples of fully developed Arya Nagara style. Their main part, i.e., the sanctum sanctorum, is called Deul. The other part connected to it is Jagamohan, which is a type of mandap. The vertical strips of the temple's main shikhara make it more influential than its skyscraper shikharas. All these temples have been given the form of a chariot and their base is a huge platform. The height of the Deul including the shikhara is 225 feet. Due to their abundant decoration and excellent sculptural technique, this can be considered the most excellent sample of temple construction

questions.question_text: Who was the Chola king who established peace with Vijayabahu of Sri Lanka to end bitterness and married his daughter to a Sinhalese prince?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – Kulottunga I (1070-1120 AD) was the son of Eastern Chalukya ruler Rajaraja but there was a mixture of Chola blood in him. His mother was the daughter of Rajendra Chola. His own marriage took place with the daughter of Rajendra II, the victor of the Koppam war. Kulottunga strengthened his position by suppressing his rebels. He proved to be a powerful ruler of his time. Meanwhile, King Vijayabahu of Ceylon declared his independence against Kulottunga. Rana Kumbha (1433-1468) was a great ruler of Mewar. His real name was Kumbhakarna. Kumbha composed a commentary named Rasikapriya on Gita Govinda and the final part of a book named Ekalinga Mahatmya. After Kumbha came Uda (1468-73 AD) and then Raimal (1473-1508 AD) became ruler. Rana Sanga (1509-28 AD) was the son of Raimal. On March 17, 1527 AD, Rana Sanga had to face defeat by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – Tamil poets named Appar and Sundaramurti were related to Kanchi. Appar's other name is also found as 'Tirunavukkarasu', he was a contemporary of Pallava ruler Mahendravarman. Appar worshipped Shiva with the slave-attitude and spread it among the common people. Sundaramurti was born in a poor Brahmana family. His upbringing was done by the army chief Narasinga Munaiyaraiyar. Although his life was only eighteen years long, yet he became a unique Shaiva devotee of his time. He wrote about a thousand devotional songs. Sundaramurti was addressed by the title 'God-Friend'.

Xuanzang called the Valabhi ruler Dhruvasena the brother-in-law of Harsha. In 637 AD, Xuanzang went to Nalanda University. Here the chancellor Acharya Shilabhadra was there. After living in Nalanda for about one and a half years, he went to Bengal, Odisha, Dhanyakataka (on the banks of Krishna river) and reached Kanchi, the capital of the Pallavas.

Reason (R): At one time he was a follower of Jain religion, but leaving it he went into Shaiva religion. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I (600-630 AD), who was also called 'Vichitrachitta', was among the greatest rulers of the Pallava dynasty. He assumed titles like Mattavilasa, Vichitrachitra, Gunabhara etc. He was a great builder, poet, and musician. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false. Mahendravarman adopted Shaiva faith after abandoning Jainism under the influence of Shaiva saint Appar. He got many cave temples built and composed 'Mattavilasa Prahasana'.

questions.question_text: Which dynasty of South India claimed that their ancestors had ruled over Ayodhya?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – The Kalyani Chalukya dynasty claimed that their ancestors had ruled over Ayodhya. In the 'Kethesceram' inscription of Vikramaditya VI of this dynasty, it is said that 59 Chalukya kings ruled in Ayodhya, then they went to the South. Apart from this, the Kannada language inscriptions of the kings of this dynasty and their feudatories throw light on contemporary history. In these evidences, they have been told to be the descendants of the Chalukyas of Vatapi and the original inhabitants of Ayodhya.
