questions.question_text: Karkav was the ancient name of:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – The ancient name of Sanchi was Karkav. According to an inscription in Sanchi, Chandragupta Vikramaditya appointed a Buddhist named Amrakardava to a high post. He gave twenty-five dinars in charity to the Mahavihara of Karkav named Karkav-dwar. Through this, lamps were lit, and five monks were fed. Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh is famous for Buddhist stupas. Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan dynasty got a huge stupa built on the hill here. Three stupas are found here. In the great stupa, the relics of Buddha, in the second, those of Ashoka-era Buddhist missionaries, and the third is built on the relics of Buddha's favorite disciples Sariputra and Maudgalyayana.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a Shaiva Acharya?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – There was widespread promotion and expansion of Shiva worship in South India. During the time of the Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Pallava, Chola dynasties ruling in the South, Shaiva religion advanced, and many Shiva temples and idols were built. During the Pallava period, the promotion of Shaiva religion was done by the Nayanars. The number of Nayanar saints is said to be 63, among whom the names of Appar, Tirujnana, Sambandar, Sundaramurti, Manikkavasagar, etc., are noteworthy. Their devotional songs have been collected together in 'Tevaram', among them Appar, whose other name is also Tirunavukkarasu, was a contemporary of Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I. He was born in the Vellalar family of Tirumundur.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not correct regarding the social and cultural conditions of the post-Gupta period?

options.A: There was an increase in the number of land grants.
options.B: There was an increase in the number of castes.
options.C: There was an increase in central control.
options.D: There was an increase in Tantric activities.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– In the early medieval society, a specific class arose which is called 'feudal'. This is called the most powerful class of society. The weakness of central power prepared such a class of influential people in society upon whom the responsibility of local security fell. The land and village grants given by the contemporary rulers also had a major contribution in the development of feudalism. R.S. Sharma's view is that the rise of feudalism in India happened due to the giving of land and villages in charity by kings to Brahmins and administrative and military officers. Due to the excess of land grants, the uneven distribution of land and power led to the rise of new classes in society. For whom the compilers of early medieval times made efforts to find a place in the traditional Varna system. To maintain purity in society, the rules of marriage, food and drink, and untouchability were made very strict.

questions.question_text: Narada has given permission to a woman to obtain a second husband if her first husband- 1. Is impotent 2. Has become fallen from caste 3. Is dead 4. Has become an ascetic Select the correct answer from the code given below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Narada has given permission to a woman to obtain a second husband on the following grounds- such a woman, whose husband is impotent or has been living in a foreign country for more than seven years or is dead and has become fallen from caste, in such a situation the woman was given permission for a second marriage.

questions.question_text: Who performed the Vajapeya Yajna?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Pravarasena I (275-335 AD) was the only ruler of the Vakataka dynasty who adopted the title of Samrat. This indicates his power and prestige. He was a conquering ruler who expanded his kingdom in all directions. Pravarasena I was a religion-devout Brahmin, who, apart from four Ashwamedha and one Vajapeya Yajna, also performed many other Vedic Yajnas. Altekar estimates that he must have performed each Yajna at the end of each military campaign. In the first campaign, he won the eastern and north-eastern parts of the Central Province. The second military campaign took place in the south. In that, he won southern Berar and northern Andhra Pradesh. In his remaining campaigns, Pravarasena must have attained victory over the Shakas of Gujarat and Kathiawar. Thus, as a result of his victories, Pravarasena built a vast empire for himself.

questions.question_text: Who has advocated for the shaving (tonsure) of widows?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Among the texts given in the options, shaving of widows has not been advocated in any of them. Smriti literature developed in later times from Dharma Sutra literature. The creation of Smritis indicates the ultimate development of Hindu religion. These shed special light on ancient Indian civilization. Smritis are termed as 'Dharma Shastra'. In Indian history, various texts were composed from the second century BC to the medieval period. Their number is found differently in various texts. In Matsya Purana, their number is given as 36, in Buddha Gautama 56, and in Vosh Mitra-uday 57. Manusmriti is the most ancient and authentic. Its composition took place approximately during the Shunga period (second century BC). Most Smritis have been written dedicating to this only. In Yajnavalkya Smriti, reference to Manusmriti has been given. In both these Smritis, the shaving of widows has not been advocated.

questions.question_text: Who founded Dhara Nagari?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Bhoja founded Dhara Nagari. In Indian history, Bhoja is more famous as a generous patron of his scholarship and knowledge and art. In the Udaypur inscription, it is said that he accomplished everything, fulfilled, gave, and knew, which was not possible by anyone else. What more praise can there be for Kaviraj Bhoja? He established his capital Dhara Nagari. And got it decorated in various ways. It became a well-known center of knowledge and art. Many palaces and temples were built here, among which Saraswati temple was the most prominent. He himself was a scholar. And his title was that of Kaviraj. He composed important texts on subjects like astrology, poetry theory, architecture, etc., and established a famous Sanskrit school in the Saraswati temple of Dhara. His royal court was a major center for pandits and scholars.

questions.question_text: The author of 'Navasahasankacharita' was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The name of the author of 'Navasahasankacharita', considered the first epic of Sanskrit literature, Padmagupta 'Parimala', is most notable, who lived in the royal court of Paramara dynasty ruler Munja (973-995 AD) of Dhara. He has presented the description of the events of the life of Munja and his brother Sindhuraja in this epic. Following Kalidasa, the composition of this text has also been done in Vaidarbhi style. The language is decorated and heart-touching. Whereas Somadeva had composed Kathasaritsagara. Somadeva had composed this book for the entertainment of Queen Suryavati, the queen of Kashmir ruler Ananta.

questions.question_text: The famous commentator Apararka of 'Yajnavalkya Smriti' was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Among the Smritis, Manusmriti is the most ancient and authentic. Its composition took place approximately during the Shunga period (second century BC). Most Smritis have been written by modifying this only. In the Smritis of Yajnavalkya, Vishnu, Narada, Brihaspati, etc., references to Manusmriti have been given. All these are compositions of the Gupta period (fifth century AD). In later times, important commentaries were written on the Smritis of Manu, Yajnavalkya, etc. The famous commentators of Manusmriti are Medhatithi, Govind Raja, and Kulluka Bhatta, and the commentators of Yajnavalkya Smriti are Vishwarupa, Vijnaneshwara, and Apararka, etc. Apararka was the famous Shilahara dynasty ruler of Konkan. From the point of view of studying Indian history, the usefulness of Smritis is important. They provide comprehensive discussion of the state administration, religion, social, economic, traditions, customs, etc., of their time.

questions.question_text: Below are given pairs of Dharma Shastra authors and their patrons. Identify the wrong pair-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Ballalasena and Dharmapala were both rulers. Ballalasena became the ruler of the Sena dynasty of Bengal around 1159 AD. After ending the remaining power of the Pala dynasty of Bengal, he adopted the title of Gaudeshwar. His other titles were – Paramabhattaraka, Maharajadhiraja, Parameshwar, Paramamaheshwar, Nisshanka Shankara, etc. Ballalasena himself was a scholar and patron of scholars, he had composed a text named Danasagara and had started the composition of a text 'Adbhut Sagara' but could not complete it. After Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty, his son Dharmapala became the ruler. Dharmapala was an enthusiastic Buddhist. In his inscriptions, he has been called 'Paramasaugata'. He established famous monasteries in Vikramshila and Somapuri (Paharpur). In his royal court, the famous Buddhist author Haribhadra lived. According to Ramcharit, he had established 50 religious schools. But as a king, he did not have religious intolerance and fanaticism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities issued coins in their own name? 1. Rajagriha 2. Shravasti 3. Kaushambi 4. Varanasi Select the correct answer from the code below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Shravasti was the capital of Kosala kingdom, this was a major kingdom of north-east India. Before Mahatma Buddha, King Kansa had won the Kashi kingdom. In Jataka texts, Kansa has been called 'Baranasi-gaho', i.e., the one who conquered Banaras. Kansa's successor was Mahakosala. During his time, Kosala had complete control over Kashi. Evidence of coins issued by Shravasti has been found. Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada. In ancient times, the districts of modern Allahabad and Banda constituted the Vatsa Mahajanapada. After Hastinapur was washed away in the Ganga flow, King Nichakshu of Hastinapur made Kaushambi his capital. In the Buddha period, the Paurava dynasty ruled here, whose ruler was Udayana. The present Varanasi and its surrounding region was the Kashi Mahajanapada in ancient times. Surrounded by Varuna river in the north and Assi river in the south, Varanasi city was the capital of Kashi Mahajanapada. Evidence of coins issued by all these great cities has been found.

questions.question_text: Drona was a measurement of-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Drona was a unit for measuring grain. Besides this, the units for measuring grain were Bat, Prastha, Adhaka, and Khari. Both the state and the farmer had rights over the land. The main officer managing royal land was 'Sitadhyaksha' who used to get farming done with the help of slaves, laborers, and prisoners. Some royal land was given to farmers for farming. The main source of state income was land tax. This principle used to be 1/6th of the produce, but in practice, it was increased somewhat according to economic condition. Arthashastra and some Greek evidences show that in the Mauryan period, people had to pay tax up to 25% on agricultural income. Such land meant royal land.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below– List-I (Dynasty) List-II (Power-center) A. Chalukya 1. Suvarnagiri B. Paramara 2. Dhara C. Chalukya 3. Anhilwada D. Pratihara 4. Kanyakubja 5. Kalyani Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– (A) Chalukya - Kalyani (B) Paramara - Dhara (C) Chalukya - Anhilwada, (D) Pratihara - Kanyakubja Tailapa II laid the foundation of the Chalukya dynasty of Kalyani. Famous King Bhoja of the Paramara dynasty shifted the capital from Ujjain to Dhara. The capital of the Chalukyas of Gujarat was Anhilwada, the Pratihara ruler made Kanyakubja (Kannauj) his capital.

questions.question_text: Famous for criticizing Buddhist religion and supporting Vedic tradition?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Saint Kumarila Bhatta of South India established the Purva Mimamsa philosophy. He worked for the revival of Hindu religion and heavily criticized Buddhism. Mimamsa, which is called Purva Mimamsa, aims to give decisions regarding Vedic rituals and to establish their philosophical importance. This doctrine considers Vedas as self-existent and eternal and tries to prove the authenticity of the Vedas through various types of logic. Upanishads and Vedanta are called Uttara Mimamsa because in these, instead of rituals, a discussion of knowledge is found. The propounder of Purva Mimamsa is Jaimini. Whose text 'Mimamsa Sutra' is the sutra of this philosophy. Kumarila Bhatta and Prabhakara are other philosophers of this whose names have led to the prevalence of two independent sects of Mimamsa. The main subject of Mimamsa has been told as Dharma, according to which Vedas alone are the root of Dharma.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings got Munjasagar lake dug?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Vakpati II (973-995) was a Paramara ruler. He was also called Munja. He had built Munjasagar lake in his capital Dhara. The first independent and powerful king of the Paramara dynasty was Siyaka or Harsha. He had a conflict with the Rashtrakutas and by defeating Khottiga, Siyaka looted immense wealth. Vakpati Munja's time began. He defeated kings of Tripuri, Lata (Gujarat), Karnataka, Chola, and Kerala in war. His most famous victory was over Chalukya king Tailapa II of Kalyani. But later in another skirmish, Tailapa was also victorious. Bhoja was the most popular king of this dynasty. According to Udaypur Prashasti, he fought wars against many Indian kings, especially the Indraratha of Chedi, First Jogal and Bhima of Gujarat, kings of Lata and Karnata, Gurjaras, and Turks. To avenge the death of his uncle (Vakpati Munja), he defeated Chalukya king Vikramaditya IV of Kalyani.

questions.question_text: Who was the Acharya of the Sanaka sect of Vaishnava religion?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Nimbarka, by refuting the Advaita philosophy, established the 'Dvaitadvaita' philosophy doctrine and also established the Sanaka sect. He was a follower of Vaishnava religion. The development of Vaishnava religion happened from Bhagavata religion. According to tradition, its propounder (Vrishni) was Krishna of the Satvata dynasty, who being the son of Vasudeva is called Vasudeva Krishna. They were originally residents of Mathura. In Chhandogya Upanishad, he has been called the son of Devaki and the disciple of Ghora Angirasa. Krishna's followers called him 'Bhagavat' (worshippable). For this reason, the religion propagated by him was named Bhagavata. In the Mahabharata period, Vasudeva Krishna was equated with Vishnu and Bhagavata religion became Vaishnava religion.

questions.question_text: Who established the huge statue of Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Chamundaraya, the minister of Ganga king Rajamalla IV, got the huge statue of Gommateshwara, the son of the first Tirthankara, established at Shravanabelagola located in Mysore. This statue is 17 meters high. Chamundaraya had the statue of Gommateshwara established at midnight on Chaitra Shukla Panchami 13 March, 981 AD, in the glorious year of the sixth century. This statue is standing in Kayotsarga posture, carved from all sides from head to thighs. This statue has been raised by cutting the rock from knees to feet. The remaining rock has been given the form of an anthill, in which snakes are emerging. Creepers of Madhavi have been made on the arms. Daily worship is done only of the feet. Mastakabhisheka (head anointing) happens after a fixed period. This happens after ten to fifteen years in a fixed planetary combination. Many monks, priests, pilgrims participate in this. A huge fair of planets also happens here. This is the world's largest statue built on Vindhyagiri mountain by cutting the rock.

questions.question_text: In Charana literature, the origin of which of the following dynasties is said to be from the sacrificial pit (yajna-kunda) of Vashistha on Mount Abu? 1. Chauhan 2. Chalukya 3. Paramara 4. Pratihara Select the correct answer from the code given below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Mention of the 'Agni Kunda theory' of the origin of Rajputs is found in 'Prithviraj Raso' composed by Chand Bardai. Vashistha Muni performed a yajna on Mount Abu from which four warriors were born, and which later led to the establishment of Chauhan, Chalukya, Paramara, and Pratihara dynasties. It seems that the origin of Rajputs through Agni Kunda is told in 'Prithviraj Raso' only with the purpose of including these foreign tribes into Indian society through purification. According to this story, 'when Parashurama destroyed the Kshatriyas, there was a shortage of rulers. The atrocities of Mlechchhas and demons increased. The earth became distressed. Therefore, to take away the distress of the earth, Vashistha performed yajnas on Mount Abu.' From this story, a clear reference is found that Indian Varna system compilers had provided a place within the Indian Varna system to foreign tribes through purification.

questions.question_text: From whom did the Chauhans snatch Delhi (Dhillika)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Among the Chauhan dynasty kings, Vigraharaja IV (1153-1162) was the most powerful ruler. He defeated the Tomara kings and captured Delhi. Information about this victory is received from the Bijolia inscription. The conflict of Chauhan rulers against the Tomara rulers of Delhi had been going on for a long time, but they had not yet achieved success. Ending the independence of the Tomara dynasty and making it his feudatory was Vigraharaja's greatest success. According to Dasharatha Sharma, the defeated Tomara king was Tanwar. Vigraharaja also achieved success against his contemporary Chalukya and Paramara kings. His father Ajayaraja had to face defeat at the hands of Chalukya ruler Kumarapala. Therefore, with the aim of washing this stain, Vigraharaja started a conflict against the Chalukyas. He defeated Kumarapala and captured Mewar and Marwar.

questions.question_text: Who among the following first propounded the atomic theory in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- First of all Kanada (Vaisheshika philosophy) propounded the atomic theory in India. Kanada told that the creation of all material substances of the world is done by four types of atoms- earth, water, fire, and air. The creation of things happens due to the combination of atoms and their destruction happens due to their separation. But the combination and separation of atoms do not happen automatically. According to Vaisheshika doctrine, atoms are inactive, the power that provides them motion is of God. God, in turn, facilitates the activities of atoms to make the living beings experience the fruits of their deeds. Due to accepting the existence of God, Vaisheshika atomism is spiritual. Its provision has been made only to explain the perishable substances of the world. Eternal substances like ether, direction, time, mind, soul are free from creation and destruction.

questions.question_text: What did Chinese travellers call India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Chinese travellers called India 'Yin-tu' or 'Tien-chu'. Influenced by the simplicity and practicality of Buddhism, many Chinese travellers visited India to take copies of Buddhist texts and to visit holy Buddhist places. Among these, the names of Fa-Hien, Xuanzang, and I-tsing are most famous. Fa-Hien came here in the fourth century and visited various places. At this time, it was the rule of Chandragupta II. In his travel account, he has painted a beautiful picture of Gupta-era society and culture. Xuanzang came to India during the reign of Harshavardhana and he has described the political and cultural condition of Harsha-era India. I-tsing came to India in the seventh century (671 AD). In his travel account, he has described Nalanda University.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a text of Vastu Shastra?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Bhatta Bhuvanadeva composed 'Aparajita Prichchha', a text of Vastu Shastra. It was composed in the 12th century. In this text, there is a mention of different shapes and types of houses for classes of feudatories including Mahamandaleshwar, Mandalika, Mahasamanta, and small samanta. Contemporary texts give clear indications that this type of various ranks were not limited only to Kshatriyas. Due to land grants and division, a new educated class (Kayastha) arose. The transformation of Shudras into farmers and the fall of Vaishyas to the level of Shudras also caused specific changes in the Varna system, to the extent that in the new Brahmanical system established in Bengal and South India, provision was mainly made only for Brahmins and Shudras. The most astonishing change of this era was the proliferation of castes which affected all Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras.

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts, the description of the construction of various types of boats is found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The description of the construction of boats is found in Yuktikalpataru. Ballalasena became the ruler of the Sena dynasty around 1159 AD. He himself was a scholar and a patron of scholars. He composed the Danasagara text and started the composition of another text 'Adbhut Sagara', but could not complete it. His teacher Aniruddha was a great scholar of his era. Ballalasena's son and successor Lakshmanasena became the king of the Sena dynasty after his father. His reign remained famous from the point of view of cultural achievements. He himself has been a scholar and patron of scholars. He completed the composition of the text named 'Adbhut Sagara' started by his father. Some poems composed by him are received in Saduktikarnamrita, which was composed by his court poet Shridhardasa.

questions.question_text: 'Tujmat-i-Bahari' is the Persian translation of an Indian text related to which subject?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- 'Tujmat-i-Bahari' is the Persian translation of an Indian text related to the subject of astrology. From the descriptions of Xuanzang and Al-Biruni, it is known that there was a lot of prevalence of teaching of grammar and astrology in India. Scholars related to these subjects had great respect in society. Many astrologers lived in the royal court. Along with religious subjects in educational centers, secular subjects were also taught properly. To obtain desired results from Yajnas, it was necessary that they be performed at auspicious times and moments. This time was known by studying the positions of planets and constellations. This study gave birth to the Vedanga named Astrology. The oldest composition of astrology is 'Vedanga Jyotisha' composed by Lagadha Muni, it has a total of 44 verses. In these, it is said that he who knows astrology is the only one who knows the true nature of Yajnas.

questions.question_text: Who among the following are Ashwamedha performers? 1. Samudragupta 3. Pulakeshin I 4. Harsha Select the correct answer from the code below- Code: 2. Pravarasena I
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- 'Ashwamedha Parakramah' is engraved on Samudragupta's coin. On its obverse side is the picture of a horse tied to the Yajna post and the coin legend is "Rajadhiraja conquering the earth and performing Ashwamedha Yajna wins the heaven" (Rajadhiraja prithvim vijitya divam jayatya hritvajmedha) is engraved. On the reverse side, along with the figure of the Queen (Dattadevi), Ashwamedha Parakramah is inscribed. Puranas reveal that Pravarasena I performed four Ashwamedha Yajnas. Altekar says that Pravarasena must have performed each Yajna at the end of each military campaign. Pravarasena I was a religion-devout Brahmin who performed many other Vedic Yajnas besides four Ashwamedha and one Vajapeya Yajna. The founder of the Chalukya dynasty of Badami was a person named Pulakeshin I. He adopted titles like Satyashraya and Ranavikrama and he performed Vedic Yajnas like Ashwamedha, Vajapeya, etc., and he was a knower of Manusmriti, History, Purana, Ramayana, Mahabharata, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following texts has a reference to the Indo-Greek (Yavana) invasion on Saket and Madhyamika?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Patanjali was the priest of Pushyamitra Shunga. His Mahabhashya mentions the Yavana invasion. In which it is said that the Yavanas had trampled Saket and Madhyamika. Malavikagnimitram is a drama text of the great poet Kalidasa. Knowledge of Shunga-era political activities is obtained from this. It is known that Pushyamitra's son Agnimitra was the governor of Vidisha and he had won Vidarbha and merged it into his kingdom. Kalidasa also mentions the Yavana invasion. According to which Agnimitra's son Vasumitra had defeated the Yavanas on the right bank of the Indus river. In Puranas, Matsya, Vayu, and Brahmanda are especially notable. Puranas reveal that Pushyamitra was the founder of the Shunga dynasty. Pargiter considers the account of Matsya Purana to be authentic. According to this, Pushyamitra ruled for 36 years.

questions.question_text: In Jain tradition, which of the following kings is mentioned as a persecutor of Jains?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- We mainly know the history of the Chalukya dynasty of Gujarat from the texts of Jain authors. These authors lived in the royal court of Chalukya rulers. In these books, Dwayashraya Kavya, Merutunga-composed Prabandha Chintamani, Someshvara-composed Kirtikaumudi, Jayasimha Suri-composed Kumarapala Charita, etc., can be mentioned. Studying which, we get a description of the political and cultural achievements of the rulers of this dynasty. Besides Indian literature, from the accounts of Muslim authors, Al-Idrisi, Ibn-ul-Athir, Hasan Nizami, etc., we get an introduction to the conflict between Turks and Chalukyas. After the reign of Chalukya or Solanki ruler Kumarapala, Ajayapala became the ruler, who ruled until 1172-76 AD. During his time, there was a Shaivite reaction. According to Jain texts, he got Jain saints killed and had Jain temples demolished. One of his servants stabbed him to death.

questions.question_text: Which of the following dynasties claimed that their ancestors ruled in Ayodhya?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The rise of the Chalukya dynasty of Kalyani happened after the fall of the Rashtrakutas. There is no information about the origin of this dynasty from its inscriptions. Later authors establish its relation with the Chalukya dynasty of Badami, calling it a descendant of the younger brother of Vikramaditya II, whose name is unknown but whose title was 'Bhima Parakrama'. The rulers of the Later Chalukya dynasty of Kalyani claimed that their ancestors ruled in Ayodhya. The Kauthum inscription of Vikramaditya VI mentions that 59 Chalukya kings ruled in Ayodhya. In the absence of any clear evidence, we can accept this as a possible hypothesis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings prohibited the production and sale of liquor in his kingdom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Kumarapala was the Chalukya dynasty ruler of Gujarat. He became king after Jayasimha. Jain texts tell us that Kumarapala attacked Malwa ruler Ballala and killed him, and defeated the Shilahara dynasty ruler of Konkan in war. By suppressing the rebellions of Paramaras of Mount Abu and Virodha, he kept them under his control. In this way, Kumarapala proved to be a great powerful king of his era. He was a follower of Jainism. He propagated non-violence in his kingdom and imposed a ban on sacrificial violence. While following Jain religion, Kumarapala prohibited animal slaughter, gambling, and the production and sale of liquor in the kingdom. But despite being a Jain, he went to the Somnath temple and worshipped Lord Shiva and he also got some Shaivite temples built.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the help of the code given below- List I List II A. Bhattarak 1. Coin B. Kollam 2. Era C. Gadyanaka 3. Script D. Velsugtu 4. Title Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- (a) Bhattarak - Title (This is a royal title of the Gupta period) (b) Kollam - Era (Kollam was a prevalent era in Kerala in ancient times) (c) Gadyanaka - Coin (Gadyanaka was a type of coin) (d) Velsugtu - Script (Velsugtu was a specific script of South India)

questions.question_text: 1. Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur 2. Draupadi Rath, Mahabalipuram 3. Kailasa Temple, Ellora 4. Meenakshi Temple, Madurai Select the correct answer from the code below- Code: A B C D Arrange the following monuments in chronological order-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Pallava style developed during the time of Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman. He also adopted the title of 'Mamalla'. The rathas of Mamalla style are famous by the name of Seven Pagodas. Their number is eight, such as- Draupadi Rath, Arjuna Rath, Bhima Rath, Dharmaraja Rath, Nakula Rath, etc. Among these, Draupadi Rath is of a different style. From the shape of its roof, it is known that it is a replica of a wooden chariot portable from one place to another. The Kailasa temple of Ellora was built by Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I. He had immense wealth obtained from many victories, along with that he had strong religious sentiments. Due to the combination of these, the construction of the temple was possible. Altekar's opinion is that the construction of the Kailasa temple was done by artisans called from the Pallava capital Kanchi. The specialty of the Kailasa temple is that the mountain was not dug downwards to build it, rather the artisans started carving the rock from the top part. In this way, all parts of the temple were made by carving from top to bottom.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is famous for his criticism regarding the Sati system? 1. Kalidasa 2. Bana 3. Medhatithi 4. Madhava Select the correct answer from the code below- Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Sati system started gaining popularity around the fourth century AD. Authors like Vatsyayana, Bhasa, Kalidasa, and Shudraka have mentioned this. The first epigraphic evidence of the prevalence of the Sati system is of the Gupta period. From the 510 AD Eran inscription, it is known that when Goparaja, the friend of Gupta ruler Bhanugupta, was killed while fighting against the Huns, his wife burnt herself in fire. But great poet Banabhatta, while opposing this, called it a greatly foolish act which has no result. This is suicide; a woman who follows this is a hell-goer. Medhatithi, considering this as suicide, calls it prohibited for women. Devabhatta's view is that becoming Sati is more heinous than a widow remaining celibate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Paramara rulers adopted the title of 'Nirvana-Narayana'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- We obtain the history of the Paramara dynasty on the basis of inscriptions, literature, and foreign accounts. Among the inscriptions of this dynasty, the first is the Harsola inscription (948 AD) of Siyaka II. From which the initial history of the Paramara dynasty is known. In other inscriptions, there is the Ujjain inscription of Vakpati Munja (980 AD), Banswara and Betma inscriptions of Bhoja, Udaypur Prashasti of Udayaditya's time, and Lakshmanadeva's Nagapur Prashasti, which is engraved on a stone slab of the Nilakantheshvara temple in a place named Udaypur near Bhilsa. This is a major means of knowing the names and achievements of the rulers of the Paramara dynasty. Such a description is not found anywhere else. This description reveals that Paramara dynasty ruler Naravarman had adopted the title of 'Nirvana-Narayana'.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below- List-I List-II A. Bilhana 1. Anantadeva of Kashmir B. Jayadeva 2. Govinda Chandra of Kannauj C. Kshemendra 3. Lakshmanasena of Bengal D. Sriharsha 4. Vikramaditya VI of Kalyani Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- (a) Bilhana - Vikramaditya VI of Kalyani (b) Jayadeva - Lakshmanasena of Bengal (c) Kshemendra - Anantadeva of Kashmir (d) Sriharsha - Govinda Chandra of Kannauj Bilhana was a court poet of Kalyani Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya VI and he had composed the famous 'Vikramankadevacharita'. Jayadeva was the court poet of Bengal ruler Lakshmanasena and 'Geet-Govinda' is his famous composition. Kshemendra, the author of 'Brihatkathamanjari', was in the court of Kashmir ruler Anantadeva, and Sriharsha was a courtier of Gahadvala ruler Govinda Chandra of Kannauj.

questions.question_text: In which Sanskrit text is the history of the Palas described?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- 'Ramacharita' is a famous text composed by Sandhyakar Nandi. It describes the history of Pala ruler Ramapala and later Pala rulers. After Shashanka, contemporary of Harsha, the power of Bengal was organized under the leadership of the Pala dynasty, and gradually it started being counted among the major powers of North India. The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala, a follower of Buddhism. The feudatories of Bengal, to end the political quarrel and upheaval of Bengal, impressed by Gopala's ability, had elected him as their ruler. These feudatories sacrificed their individual self-interest for the benefit of the state. According to Tibetan historian Taranatha, Gopala was born in a Kshatriya family of Pundravardhana (Bogra district). He expanded the kingdom through war and also provided a strong organization to the state.

questions.question_text: Who among the following never took Sanyasa?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Followers of Vaishnava sect- Ramanujacharya, Vallabhacharya, and Nimbarkacharya opposed the Advaita philosophy and knowledge-path of Shankaracharya. Despite having some differences, the inclination of all these kept moving towards Saguna Bhakti. All these rejected the complete unity of Brahman and Jeeva and propagated the idea that after worldly birth, the merging of Jeeva with Brahman ends. Due to the efforts of Vaishnavas, Bhagavad Gita got importance-prestige, along with the establishment of Incarnation theory, worship of incarnations, and the superiority of Brahmins, etc., got a place. Vallabhacharya especially emphasized the idol worship of God. Vallabhacharya was the main saint of the Krishna Bhakti branch. He established the 'Pushti Marg' and developed Shuddhadvaita. Vallabhacharya never took Sanyasa and lived in household life and gave the message of salvation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following considered their origin from Vishnu?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Tondaiman considered their origin from Vishnu. The Chera kingdom was spread in western Tamilakam, i.e., in the region of modern Northern Travancore, Cochin, and Southern Malabar. The capital of the Cheras was Vanji. The Chola kingdom is located on the Coromandel coast in South India, its capital was Thanjavur. The Pandya kingdom is situated in the extreme south, its capital was Madurai, where three Sangams were organized.

questions.question_text: In which of the following texts, evidence of polyandry is found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Polyandry is a form of such a union in which a woman chooses more than one husband at one time. The five Pandavas were husbands of Draupadi, but Draupadi's father declared this to be against Dharma, Veda, and tradition.

questions.question_text: According to ancient Indian texts, a gold coin weighed-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - In ancient India, a gold coin weighed 80 Ratti. In ancient India, the ratio of silver and gold coins was fixed at 10 : 1. In the Nashik cave inscription, 70 thousand Karshapana (silver) has been called equal to the value of two thousand gold coins. That is, 35 Karshapana = 1 gold coin. Respectively, their weight was equal to 32 (35 × 32) and 80 Ratti (80 × 1), that is, 35 × 32 : 80 : 1 = 14 : 1. Therefore, the weight of silver and gold coins in ancient India was 32 and 80 Ratti, respectively.

questions.question_text: 'Karpuramanjari' author Rajshekhar was whose guru?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – 'Karpuramanjari' author Rajshekhar was the guru of Pratihara ruler Mahendrapala I. Rajshekhar has called Mahendrapala I 'Nirbhaya Raja' and 'Nirbhaya Narend'. Living under the patronage of Mahendrapala I, Rajshekhar composed the drama 'Karpuramanjari' (Prakrit language) and in Sanskrit, dramas 'Viddhashalabhanjika', 'Bala Ramayana', 'Bala Bharata' (Prachanda Pandava) and composed poetic texts named 'Kavya Mimamsa', 'Bhuvanakosha', and 'Harivilasa'. Rajshekhar also lived during the time of Mahendrapala I's successor Mahipala I and provided the attribute of 'Raghukulamuktamani' and 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta' to Mahipala I.

questions.question_text: Dhruva Dharavarsha was a ruler:
questions.explanation: Dhruva Dharavarsha, the first ruler of South India to participate in the Tripartite struggle, was related to the Rashtrakuta dynasty. Dhruva Dharavarsha defeated Pratihara ruler Vatsaraja and Pala ruler Dharmapala. Dhruva defeated Pallava ruler Dantivarman and Vengi ruler Vishnuvardhana IV

questions.question_text: 'Prabodhachandrodaya' was composed:

options.A: During the reign of Chandela rulers
options.B: During the reign of Pratihara rulers
options.C: During the reign of Gupta rulers
options.D: During the reign of Satavahana rulers

questions.explanation: Prabodhachandrodaya was composed during the reign of Chandela rulers. Its author was Krishnamishra. The reign of Chandela rulers is called the era of temple construction

questions.question_text: Pallava chariot temples are located in:
questions.explanation: Pallava chariot temples were built in Mahabalipuram. Its construction was done under Mamalla style by Narasimha Varman I. These are monolithic. Their number is eight. Dharmaraja Rath (Yudhishthira) is the largest. Draupadi Rath is the smallest. For the first time, a pyramid-shaped Shikhar was built on Dharmaraja Rath

questions.question_text: Who was the king of Vallabhi during Harsha's reign?
questions.explanation: During the time of Harsha's reign, the king of Vallabhi was Dhruvasena II. Bhaskaravarman and Harsha had together defeated Shashanka. Pulakeshin II had defeated Harsha

questions.question_text: Vakpati Munja and Sindhuraja's court poet Padmagupta was the author of:
questions.explanation: Padmagupta, who was the court poet of both Vakpati Munja and Sindhuraja. He had composed Navasahasanka Charita. Vakpati Munja defeated the Huns and Chalukyas. Vakpati Munja's title was Amoghavarsha. Both Vakpati Munja and Sindhuraja were lovers of literature

questions.question_text: Who was the author of Vikramankadevacharita?
questions.explanation: The author of Vikramankadevacharita was Bilhana. This book contains a description of the character of the Kalyani Chalukya dynasty ruler Vikramaditya VI. Bilhana lived in the court of Vikramaditya VI. From here he started writing about him. Vikramaditya VI was a great ruler of the Chalukya dynasty

questions.question_text: Which of the following Pallava rulers built the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi?
questions.explanation: The development of independent temples of Rajasimha style took place during the reign of Pallava ruler Rajasimha (Narasimha Varman II). Narasimha Varman II only got the Kailasa temple of Kanchi built. All the specialties of architecture are visible in this temple

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers had the title 'Vichitrachitta'?
questions.explanation: Mahendra Varman was a Pallava ruler. Mahendra Varman I had adopted the title of Vichitrachitta and Mattavilasa. Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II had defeated Mahendra Varman. The center of Pallava political power was Kanchi. The most influential ruler of the Pallavas was Narasimha Varman I

questions.question_text: Who was the creator of Natya Shastra?
questions.explanation: Bharata is considered the creator of Natya Shastra. Bharata Muni first mentioned Rasa in his famous text Natya Shastra. He has told nine types of 'Rasa'. Acharya Abhinavagupta and Mammaṭa have also told nine types of 'Rasa'

questions.question_text: King Amoghavarsha is related to:
questions.explanation: The underage successor of Govinda III, Amoghavarsha (814-76 AD), became the ruler. He was a Rashtrakuta dynasty ruler. Amoghavarsha was a generous patron of knowledge and art. He composed the Kannada language poetry text 'Kavirajamarga'. In his court lived 'Adi-Purana' author Jinasena and 'Ganitasarasangraha' author Mahaviracharya

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and give the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II Temple style Name of the temple
questions.explanation: List-I List-II Nagara – Nilakantheshwar Mahadeva temple of Shaunaka Dravida – Kailasanatha temple of Ellora Chalukya – Lakukuli Jain temple Foreign – Paharpur temple

questions.question_text: Which author has given information about the relations between Pulakeshin II and Khusrau II?
questions.explanation: Tabari (Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Jarir at-Tabari 839–923 AD) was a great Arab historian and Islamic theologian. His major composition is Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, a history of the world which is written on 30 thousand sheets of paper. This very author gave information about the relations between Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II and Khusrau II

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below under the lists─ List-I List-II A. Mahabhashya 1. Kalidasa C. Ashtadhyayi 3. Chanakya D. Arthashastra 4. Patanjali Code: A B C D B. Kumarasambhava 2. Panini
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─The correct match is as follows─ List-I List-II A. Mahabhashya 4. Patanjali B. Kumarasambhava 1. Kalidasa C. Ashtadhyayi 2. Panini D. Arthashastra 3. Chanakya

questions.question_text: In Yajnavalkya's method, who has the first place in the succession order of a sonless deceased?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In Yajnavalkya's method, the wife has the first place in the succession order of a sonless deceased. Vijnaneshwara made its scope very extensive and also included within this the property obtained through succession, purchase, partition, finding, and acceptance. (Rikta-kraya-samvibhaga-parigraha-adhigama-prathamesh-etat-stri-dhanam). In this way, almost every type of property under the woman was included within Stri-dhana.

questions.question_text: In which of the following royal families, men usually followed the Brahmin religion and women were Buddhist?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – People of the Ikshvaku dynasty ruled in the Krishna-Guntur region. In Puranas, they have been called "Shriparvatiya" (ruler of Shri Parvat) and 'Andhrabhritya' (servant of Andhras). Earlier they were feudatories of Satavahanas but after their fall, they declared their independence. The founder of this dynasty was Shri Shantamula. On the occasion of establishing his independent power, he performed 'Ashwamedha Yajna'. In this royal family, men usually followed the Brahmin religion and women were Buddhists.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'Abhijnanashakuntalam'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─Kalidasa is the best poet and playwright of Sanskrit. 'Abhijnanashakuntalam' is composed by Kalidasa. Abhijnanashakuntalam is his best creation. Abhijnanashakuntalam has a total of seven acts in which the story of the meeting, separation, and reunion of King Dushyanta of Hastinapur and Kanva Rishi's foster daughter Shakuntala has been portrayed with great liveliness and expressiveness. Apart from this, Kalidasa has also composed Meghaduta, Kumarasambhava, etc.

questions.question_text: Who composed 'Brihatsamhita'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation– Varahamihira was a famous astrologer and his famous book is Brihatsamhita. According to Varahamihira, the moon moves around the earth and the earth moves around the sun. He accepted the debt of foreigners, Yavana, and Roman in the field of astrology. Aryabhata composed 'Aryabhatiya'.

questions.question_text: Who got the famous Jain temples of Dilwara built?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The famous Jain temple of Dilwara was built by Chalukya ruler Bhimadeva's feudatory Vimal Shah on Mount Abu through Vastupala and Tejapala. The idol of Rishabhadeva (Adinatha) is in the sanctum of this marble-built temple.

questions.question_text: Which Chinese traveller came for India travel despite not receiving the Emperor's permission and whose secret exit from the country was not only forgiven on returning to China, but he was welcomed with respect?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Xuanzang was born around 600 AD at a place named Chin-liu in the Honan province of China. In 629 AD, he started for India from Chang'an, the capital of Tang rulers. In 637 AD, Xuanzang went to Nalanda University. The head of this place was Acharya Shilabhadra. Living in Nalanda for about one and a half years, he studied Yoga Shastra. On returning to China, not only was the matter of his secret exit from the country forgiven, but he was welcomed with respect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: In the court of Shunga-era ruler Pushyamitra Shunga, a scholar named Patanjali lived who described his reign in his book "Mahabhashya"

questions.question_text: Match List-I (Text) with List-II (Subject-matter): List-I List-II
questions.explanation: The correct match is List-I List-II Bhuvanakosha – Geography Brihatjataka – Astrology Dasharupaka – Drama art Manasara – Architecture Detailed material of ancient Indian geography is found in Bhuvanakosha. In Puranas, geography has been called Bhuvanakosha. The description of Bhuvanakosha has also occurred in Matsya, Vayu, Brahmanda, Vamana, and Markandeya Puranas. Five chapters (38, 43, 45, 47, 48) related to the subject of geography are found in Kurma Purana.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is not correctly matched? (Ancient city) (Location)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The correct match of the question is– Pushkalavati – Charsadda Shakala – Sialkot Tamralipti – Tamluk Vijayapuri is not related to Dharanikota.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Buddhist stupas in chronological order and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.-III Paper June, 2015) Explanation– In Buddhist texts, it is mentioned that Ashoka had built 84 thousand stupas. Ashoka built the Great Stupa of Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh. The Amaravati stupa was built by Ikshvaku dynasty rulers, in the Gupta period, the Dhamekh stupa of Sarnath was built. It is made of bricks. Gupta ruler Kumaragupta had built Nalanda University.

questions.question_text: Mahendravarman's composed 'Mattavilasa Prahasana' mentions:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Mahendravarman's composed 'Mattavilasa Prahasana' mentions Buddhists and Kapalikas. This is the oldest farce of Sanskrit. It describes the mental state of a Kapalika drunk in temple intoxication.

questions.question_text: Meaning of 'Siddhamatrika' is-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Apart from Dravidian scripts, all other scripts have originated from Brahmi script. In the Mauryan era, this script became fully developed. Later, in the Gupta period, it was called 'Gupta Brahmi' and it spread to South-East Asia and Central Asia. From this Gupta Brahmi's western branch's eastern sub-branch, a specific script Siddhamatrika or Nyunakshar script developed. The time of its development is considered to be about the sixth century. Later, Gupta Brahmi developed into three main (a) Sharada, (b) Kutila, (c) Nagari scripts. These three scripts only are the mothers of modern North Indian scripts.

questions.question_text: Match List A with List B and select the correct answer using the code given below: List A List B (King) (Temple) A. Chola (i) Brihadisvara B. Pandya (ii) Mahabalipuram C. Gupta (iii) Hampi D. Vijayanagara (iv) Bhitargaon Code: A B C D

questions.question_text: The Vimal temple of Dilwara is dedicated to one of the following:
questions.explanation: Solanki ruler Bhimadeva I's minister Vimal Shah built the Vimalvasahi temple in the 11th century, which is dedicated to Adinatha

questions.question_text: Which of the following books was not written by Ziauddin Barani?
questions.explanation: Fatawa-i-Firozshahi is the autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, the writing of which was done by Firoz Shah Tughlaq himself, whose objective was to prove himself an ideal Muslim ruler. It contains detailed descriptions of the works and policies done for the spread of Islam. All other works were written by Ziauddin Barani

questions.question_text: In whose reign was "Kaka Pheru" the chief expert of the mint?
questions.explanation: Kaka Pheru was an Indian mathematician. Alauddin Khalji appointed him as an expert in coins, metals, and gems during his reign. He composed many books based on mathematics, currency, and gems. His main book is `Ganit Sar Kaumudi`

options.B: Chaudhary - Chief officer of the Pargana

questions.explanation: (Administration Word) (Description) 1. Kharitadar - Officer who sends firmans 2. Chaudhary - Chief officer of the Pargana 3. Paik - Foot soldier 4. Diwan-i-Kohi - Muhammad bin Tughlaq C. Diwan-i-Arz - Ghiyasuddin Balban D. Sarai Adl - Alauddin Khalji

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct about Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra?
questions.explanation: The mosque named Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra was built in Ajmer by Qutbuddin Aibak. This mosque was built on the site of a Sanskrit school. This mosque has 7 arches and 70 pillars. The inscription written on the dome of this mosque mentions the name of Abu Bakr bin Ahmed Khalut Al-Harawi as the supervisor, and the inscription on the arch mentions the name of Ahmed bin Muhammad Al-Arid as the inspector. The inscription on the central arch of the jaali in Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra mosque gives the credit for its construction to Iltutmish Whereas, the first mosque built by Turks in India is Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, which is situated in Delhi. Its construction was ordered by Qutbuddin Aibak.

questions.question_text: In which of the following Persian works is the earliest reference to the magnetic compass found?
questions.explanation: The earliest reference to the magnetic compass (magnetic qutubnuma) is found in the book 'Jawami-ul-Hikayat' written in Persian by 'Sadiduddin Muhammad Awfi'. Muhammad Awfi lived during the reign of the Turk Sultan Iltutmish (1210-1236). This book contains descriptions of tools and instruments as well as exploratory information. This book is dedicated to his minister Nizam-ul-Mulk. 'Adab-ul-Harb Wa Shuja'at' was composed by Fakhr-e-Mudabbir. The book named 'Futuh-us-Salatin' was authored by Malik Isami. Miftah-ul-Fuzala is a manuscript related to a collection of rare words and paintings obtained from Mandu (Malwa Sultanate)

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I List-II Mongol Invasion Related Delhi Sultan's Reign
questions.explanation: The correct match is as follows List-I List-II (A) Tayir Bahadur - Muizzuddin Bahram Shah (B) Tarmashirin - Muhammad Tughlaq (C) Sher Mughal - Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (D) Qutlugh Khwaja - Alauddin Khalji

questions.question_text: Arrange the following experiments/projects of Muhammad bin Tughlaq chronologically:
questions.explanation: The chronological order of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's experiments-projects is as follows Capital Transfer - (1326 - 27 AD) Token Currency - (1329 - 30 AD) Khurasan Expedition - (1332 - 34 AD) Karachil Expedition - (1337 - 38 AD)

questions.question_text: What were the following features of Razia's accession to the throne of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Razia Sultan (1236 - 1240) was the first time the people of Delhi took a decision on the issue of succession on their own. On the issue of succession, Iltutmish said that 'my sons are engrossed in pleasure and none is worthy of ruling.' Razia abandoned the veil and started appearing before the people wearing a coat (qaba) and cap (kulah) like men. Minhaj says "she ruled for 3 years, 6 months, 6 days. Sultan Razia was a great ruler. She was wise, just, generous, a well-wisher of her subjects, a brave ruler, and the leader of her armies. All royal qualities were present in her—except for womanhood, for this reason, in the eyes of men, all qualities were useless." The army, people, and officers of Delhi supported Razia's accession. She asked for support from the people in the Friday prayer by wearing 'red clothes' (symbol of seeking justice), and she said that "if I do not fulfill their (people's) expectations, then without hesitation remove me from the throne of Delhi." In this way, she gave the coronation the form of a (temporary) contract.

questions.question_text: Who was the officer 'Barid-i-Mumalik' in the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: In the Delhi Sultanate, Diwan-i-Barid was the Intelligence Department. Its head was called Barid-i-Mumalik. He was also the chief news writer of the state. Under him were spies, messengers, and post stations. Under him, many barids were appointed in cities, markets, and all populated places. They used to send secret information to Barid-i-Mumalik, which he used to send to the Sultan's service

questions.question_text: Which one of the following Sultans stopped recognizing the authority of the Caliph?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah Khalji sat on the throne in April 1316 AD. He was the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who declared himself Caliph and refused to accept the authority of the Caliph. He adopted the title of "Al-Imam-ul-Imam wa Khilafat-ul-Lah". He was an unworthy son of his worthy father. He liked the company of naked men and women

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi'?
questions.explanation: The author of 'Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi' is Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi. The composition of Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was done by Yahya bin Ahmad under the patronage of the Sayyid dynasty ruler Mubarak Shah. This book is the only contemporary source of the Sayyid dynasty. Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi was a contemporary of Mubarak Shah. He dedicated this book to Mubarak Shah

questions.question_text: Which of the following mosques was the first Turkish mosque in India?
questions.explanation: Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, situated in Delhi, is the first building built in Hindu-Muslim style. Its construction was ordered by Qutbuddin Aibak in memory of his victory over Prithviraj Chauhan. Regarding this mosque, it is said that it was built on the ruins of a Jain temple. Earlier there was a Vaishnava temple here. Breaking this Vishnu temple, Aibak built the first mosque of Delhi and India

questions.question_text: In the Delhi Sultanate, members of the Chahalgani were related to–
questions.explanation: After the expansion of the empire, Iltutmish tried to organize it. He formed a group of forty slave officers, i.e., Turkan-i-Chahalgani. Iltutmish formed a new ruling class to get freedom from the dominance of Muizzi and Qutbi Amirs and to carry out administrative work smoothly, which consisted of two major groups- (i) Turkish slaves (ii) Tajiks. The number of Turks was highest in Chahalgani

questions.question_text: In the Delhi Sultanate, 'Mushrif-i-Mumalik' was known as –

options.B: Head of the royal information agency

questions.explanation: Under the Wazir, there were many employees among whom Nayab Wazir, Mushrif-i-Mumalik, and Mustaufi-i-Mumalik were given special importance. Below the rank of Nayab Wazir, there was Mushrif-i-Mumalik (Accountant General). In the Diwan-i-Wizarat department, the audit department was managed by officials named Mushrif-i-Mumalik and Mustaufi-i-Mumalik

questions.question_text: Which is an early example of a mosque in India on which the influence of Muslim ideas is predominant?
questions.explanation: Jamait Khana or Jamait Khana Mosque is an early example of a mosque in India on which the influence of Muslim ideas is predominant. This mosque was built by the Delhi Sultan Alauddin Khalji near the shrine of Nizamuddin Auliya. Red stone has been used in this mosque, which is built entirely in Islamic style

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi suppressed the 'Thugs'?
questions.explanation: Jalaluddin Khalji was a generous, gentle, and kind person. He hated bloodshed. Jalaluddin was the first ruler who tried to satisfy his opponents. Jalaluddin showed his generous policy regarding thieves and thugs as well. About a thousand thugs who used to steal, loot, rob, and kill were caught in Delhi. The Sultan did not punish them but sat them on a boat and sent them towards Bengal

questions.question_text: Which ruler of the Khalji dynasty made 'Kilokheri' his capital?
questions.explanation: The Khalji dynasty was founded by Jalaluddin Firoz Shah Khalji. There were a total of four rulers in this dynasty who ruled for 30 years. Jalaluddin was a Turk of the 'Khalji' tribe whose coronation took place on 13 June 1290 AD in the incomplete Kilokheri (Kailugarhi) palace built by Kaiqubad. He made Kilokheri his capital and decided to stay there for a year because the people of Delhi were accustomed to the rule of the Ilbari Turks for eighty years, so they were not ready to accept Jalaluddin's rule suddenly

questions.question_text: From which region did Ibn Battuta come to India?
questions.explanation: The original name of Ibn Battuta was Sheikh Fath Abu Abdullah, who was a native of Morocco (North Africa). He came to India in 1333 AD during the tenure of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and stayed in India for 14 years. Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed him as the Qazi of Delhi and he remained on this post for ten years. In due course, some allegations of corruption and dishonesty were leveled against him, due to which the Sultan was unhappy with him and put him in prison, but later released him. In 1342 AD, Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent him to China as his ambassador. However, due to the ship getting damaged on the way, he returned halfway

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, what was the meaning of 'Fawazil'?

options.A: Extra payment given to the nobility
options.B: Fixed land revenue in lieu of salary
options.C: Extra amount deposited by Iqtadars in the government treasury
options.D: Illegal forced collection made from farmers

questions.explanation: In the Sultanate period, Fawazil meant the extra amount deposited by Iqtadars in the government treasury. In the Sultanate period, every Iqtedar was allocated some land. This was called Iqta. From the income generated from this land, the Iqtedar used to pay for his salary and expenses on the army. The amount left after these expenses was called Fawazil, which had to be deposited in the government treasury

questions.question_text: Who was the first Sultan to impose irrigation tax?
questions.explanation: Haq-i-Sharb/Habs-i-Sharb (Irrigation Tax), Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to impose this tax. The rate of this tax was kept at 10 percent of the total produce. Firoz Shah Tughlaq used to get an annual income of 2 lakh tankas from this tax. He used to distribute it as charity among religious people and scholars Special Fact According to Ferishta – Where there were no canals, Firoz built dams and constructed 30 huge reservoirs. According to Afif – The Sultan constructed 7 dams in Delhi and its neighboring areas.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi imposed grazing tax?
questions.explanation: Delhi's Sultan Alauddin Khalji was the first to impose a 'Grazing' tax in addition to land revenue. 'Grazing tax/Chari tax' was a tax on all milking animals (cows, goats, buffaloes, sheep, etc.) Special Fact According to Ferishta, the following number of cattle was fixed for ordinary farmers (Balahar) and Muqaddams - two pairs of oxen, two cows, one pair of buffaloes, and ten goats for farming, i.e., these were free from tax.

questions.question_text: Under the revenue system, who took concrete steps in the direction of introducing the practice of sharing produce instead of the measurement system in Khalisa areas?
questions.explanation: Barani gives an account in this regard that Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq abandoned Alauddin's measurement system (under which the farmer had to give the state's share according to the area under cultivation) and restarted the Nasq or Hukm-i-Hasil (estimating the produce of the land roughly) and the sharing system (Batai). He took concrete steps in the direction of introducing the practice of sharing the produce instead of the measurement system in the Khalisa areas, which was considered an initiative to give relief to the farmers

questions.question_text: Which Sultan started the tradition of writing the name of the mint on coins in India?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish was the first Sultan who started the tradition of engraving the name of the mint (the city in which they were cast) on the coins (first on silver tanka in 1219 AD). On one of his coins, the name of the mint 'Bilaul Hind' is found Special Fact 1. Balban opened new mint houses in Alwar, Sultanpur, and Fatehabad. 2. The weight of Alauddin's gold coins is 167-170 grains, these were issued from Delhi and Devagiri. The legend engraved on these coins is also different from the previous coins and they contain on one side Al-Sultan Al-Azam, Alauddin Wal Din Abu Al-Muzaffar Muhammad Shah Al-Sultan Khilafath Nasir Amir Momineen and on the other side Sikandar Sani Yamin Al (Second Alexander) along with the name of the mint and date. In this way, he also removed the Caliph's name from his coins. 3. During the time of Muhammad Tughlaq, coins were issued from maximum mint houses like - Delhi, Dhar, Ranthambore, Lakhnauti, Satgaon, Sultanpur, Mulk-i-Tilang, Tughlaqpur (Tirhut), and Daulatabad, etc.

questions.question_text: Sultan Garhi tomb was -
questions.explanation: Sultan Garhi tomb – This is the tomb of Iltutmish's son Nasiruddin Mahmud (built in 1231 AD), which is in Malikapur at a distance of three miles from Qutub Minar. Iltutmish was the founder of tomb architecture in India

questions.question_text: I. Ruknuddin Firoz II. Bahram Shah III. Masud Shah IV. Nasiruddin Mahmud Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Code: Consider the reign of the following rulers and arrange them chronologically:
questions.explanation: The chronological order is as follows– I. Ruknuddin Firoz - April/May 1236 - November 1236 AD II. Bahram Shah - 1240 AD-1242 AD III. Masud Shah - 1242 AD-1246 AD IV. Nasiruddin Mahmud - 1246 AD to 1265 AD

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi collected many books on Astronomy and Mathematics in his royal library (Kitab Khana-i-Khas), and wanted everyone who was interested to be able to use them?
questions.explanation: Tughlaq dynasty ruler Firoz Shah Tughlaq collected books related to subjects like Astronomy, Philosophy, Mathematics, etc., in his royal library (Kitab Khana-i-Khas), which were accessible to all, anyone who wanted could use them. The most important book translated from Sanskrit to Persian during his time was 'Dalail-i-Firozshahi'. A scholar named Ajuddin Kirmani translated it into Persian. Firoz Shah Tughlaq himself composed his autobiography Futuhat-i-Firozshahi

questions.question_text: In Iltutmish's nobility, people of which category were the Tajiks?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish established two new ruling classes to get freedom from the influence of Amirs and to get help in his administrative work - (1) Tajiks (2) Turkish slaves. Among these, Tajiks were high-born non-Turkish foreigners. These people came to India in search of security and livelihood. Iltutmish's Prime Minister Nizamulmulk Junaidi and Isami's ancestors were included in the Tajik class. Until Iltutmish's time, the Turkish slaves (Shamsi slaves) were loyal to the master. After his death, the Turkish slaves (Turkish slave officers) started calling themselves slaves of the Sultan. From this class of Turkish slaves, Iltutmish had formed a group of forty. The appointment of Turkish slaves was on important administrative and military posts. They were Iltutmish's main advisors

questions.question_text: Immediately after his accession, which of the following Sultans assured his subjects with this decision that he would follow in his father's footsteps and declared that 'every elderly person present within the borders of my kingdom is like my father and every young person will be entitled to the same love and affection as my brother'?
questions.explanation: In 1325 AD, Muhammad Tughlaq (Ulugh Khan) sat on the throne after the death of his father Ghiyasuddin. After the coronation, he stayed in Tughlaqabad for 40 days, after which he entered Delhi. He distributed gold and silver coins to his subjects (Riyaya) and appointed Amirs to high posts. According to Isami, after attaining power, he declared that "in my affectionate view, every old man of my empire is like my father and every young man (har naujawan) is my brother like Bahram Khan." In the Rajamundry inscription, he has been called the Khan of the world. Muhammad Tughlaq distributed posts without any discrimination based on merit. He was the first Sultan to participate in Holi. Ibn Battuta and Barani have described his policies in their works. Balban was the first Sultan to adopt the policy of blood and iron. Alauddin Khalji gave priority to the separation of religion and politics, strengthening the principle of autocracy, imperialism, and state interest. Sikandar Lodi was influenced by Turkish kingship instead of Afghan brotherhood. He says "if I seat one of my slaves in a palanquin, then at my order, the nobles will lift him on their shoulders and take him."

questions.question_text: Tell the name of the Sultan who is also known by the name Lakh Baksh for his generosity:
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210) was the founder of the Turkish empire in India. He was a slave, whom Muhammad Ghori had bought. Through his merit, skill, leadership, after the second battle of Tarain in 1192 AD, he was appointed the ruler of the Indian empire by Muhammad Ghori. Scholars like Hasan Nizami and Fakhr-e-Mudabbir used to get shelter in his court. He built mosques named 'Quwwat-ul-Islam' in Delhi and 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' in Ajmer. Muslim writers called him 'Lakh Baksh' due to his generosity. And due to reading the Quran in a melodious voice, he was called 'Quran Khan'. The author of Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Minhaj-us-Siraj, called Aibak 'Second Hatim'. In Delhi, he started the construction of Qutub Minar, but Iltutmish completed it

questions.question_text: A commemorative coin was issued in memory of the 1232 Gwalior campaign. Apart from Iltutmish, whose name was engraved on it?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish (1210-1236 AD) was a Turk of the Ilbari tribe. He was Aibak's slave. Turkish Amirs and military officers made him sit on the Delhi Sultanate. In 1229, he received 'Khilat' legal recognition and a certificate from the Caliph of Baghdad 'Al-Mustansir Billah'. In 1231 AD, Gwalior was besieged and after a difficult struggle of one year, it was conquered, and in memory of the victory of this campaign, a coin was issued in which Iltutmish and his capable daughter 'Razia' Sultan's name was engraved. Which was engraved on the coins by the name of 'Ummatul Niswan'. Iltutmish was the first ruler who issued pure Arabic coins; the silver Tanka was of 175 grains, and Arabic text was engraved on it. A.B. Tripathi considers Iltutmish the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct in the context of Balban's theory of kingship?
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Balban (1265 - 1287 AD) was the ruler of the Slave dynasty (Mamluk dynasty) in the Delhi Sultanate. His theory of kingship was based on power, prestige, and justice, which laid the foundation of autocratic kingship. To bring high prestige to kingship, he considered the King as the representative of God on earth 'Niyabat-i-Khudai', and in terms of decorum, he is only after the Prophet. The King is 'Zille-Allah' i.e., God's shadow; his heart is a treasure of divine inspiration and grace. God inspires and directs him for the fulfillment of royal duties. Balban himself told that he is a descendant of the Turkish mythological hero Afrasiyab described in Firdausi's Shahnameh. He neither kept personal contact with low-born people nor gave them any post, he said "When I see a person of a low family, the veins of my body get agitated with anger." He introduced Sijda and Paibos, which were Persian traditions

questions.question_text: Ibn Battuta mentions that the Sultan fixed Wednesday for freeing male slaves, Friday for freeing female slaves, and Saturday for the marriage of male slaves with female slaves. Identify the Sultan:
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta was a native of Morocco (Africa). His famous work/travelogue is 'Kitab-ul-Rehla', which is written in Arabic. He started the journey in 1325 AD and after traveling through other countries, reached Sindh via the land route on 12 September 1333. Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325 - 1351 AD) appointed him the Qazi of Delhi who remained on the post for 8 years. In 1342 AD, Muhammad bin Tughlaq also ordered him to be sent to China as an ambassador to the Mongol ruler. Ibn Battuta has written in his book that - "Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq fixed Wednesday for freeing male slaves, Friday for freeing female slaves, and Saturday for the marriage of male slaves with female slaves."

questions.question_text: In whose reign did debased currency (billan currency) almost completely replace silver coins?
questions.explanation: Tughlaq dynasty ruler Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351 – 1388 AD) was the son of Ghiyasuddin's younger brother Rajab, who was born from his Hindu wife Bibi Zaila. His original name was Kamaluddin Firoz. He introduced silver coins named Shashgani (6 jitals) and introduced mixed coins of silver and copper named Adha (1/2) and Bikh (1/4), which gradually completely replaced silver coins. Alauddin Khalji had issued copper and silver coins on which the ruler's name, the name of the mint, and the impression of the Kalima are found. Token currency (copper or jital) was introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. The impression of the Caliphs' names is found on Balban's coins

questions.question_text: 'The Sultan ordered the Maliks, Amirs, court officials, and people with status not to visit each other and not to have common parties in banquet halls, there was no permission for inter-marriage between them without informing the Sultan and without his permission.' Identify the Sultan:
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316 AD) was the greatest ruler of the Khalji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. His original name was Ali Gurshasp. He adopted titles like Second Alexander "Sikandar-i-Sani", Sultan of the rulers of the earth, shepherd of the people, world conqueror, and keeping religion separate from politics, he also adopted the title of "Yamin-ul-Khilafate" (Deputy of the Caliph). He issued 4 ordinances to suppress rebellions – (1) Confiscating the property of wealthy people (2) Formation of an intelligence department (3) Implementation of prohibition of liquor (4) Order for Amirs, Maliks, court officials, and people with status not to visit each other and not to host common banquet halls. During Alauddin Khalji's time, the maximum number of 6 Mongol invasions occurred.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan among the following addressed the Amirs as Masnad-i-Ali in his firmans?
questions.explanation: Bahlul Lodi was the founder of the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, the Lodi dynasty. He addressed his Amirs (nobles) as 'Masnad-i-Ali'. His theory of kingship was based on equality. He considered the Afghan nobles his equals. Bahlul Lodi also used to stand when his nobles stood. Qutbuddin Aibak, Balban, and Firoz Tughlaq were important rulers of the Slave dynasty and Tughlaq dynasty, respectively

questions.question_text: Alai Darwaza, built by Alauddin Khalji, was an entrance gate to which place?
questions.explanation: Alai Darwaza built by Alauddin Khalji is an entrance gate to Quwwat-ul-Islam. Alai Darwaza was constructed by Alauddin Khalji in Delhi in 1311 near Qutub Minar. This mosque situated in Delhi, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, is the first building built in Hindu-Muslim style. Alai Darwaza provides access to Quwwat-ul-Islam

questions.question_text: By which Sultan was poetry written in Persian under the pseudonym 'Gulrukhi'?
questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi was an educated and learned ruler. He was a scholar of the Persian language and wrote poetry in Persian under the pseudonym "Gulrukhi". He respected scholars and gave them patronage. Every night, 70 scholars used to sit near his bed and discuss various types of things. During his time, many Sanskrit books were translated into Persian. Under the patronage of Sikandar Lodi, his wazir Miyan Bhua translated a book on Sanskrit medical science into the Persian language under the name Tibb-i-Sikandari or Farhang-i-Sikandari

questions.question_text: Whose original name was Juna Khan?
questions.explanation: After the death of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, his son Juna Khan (Juna Khan) sat on the throne in 1325 AD, adopting the title of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Ghiyasuddin had five sons among whom Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the eldest. His original name was Malik Fakhruddin. He was known by the name Juna Khan. In 1320 AD, when Sultan Ghiyasuddin became ruler, he gave Juna Khan the title of Ulugh Khan and declared him his crown prince and successor

questions.question_text: Who established Amir-i-Sada, which was an administrative organization and whose members were revenue collectors and military officers?
questions.explanation: The lower-ranking Mongol officers were called Sada. Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq gave them patronage. Sada or hundred, was called the officer leading a hundred soldiers in the Mongol army. But in India, its use started for a unit of 100 villages. In Sada Amir, apart from Mongols, Turks, Afghans, Rajputs, and Indian Muslims were also included. Their function was to maintain law and order along with tax collection in their administrative area

questions.question_text: Which Delhi Sultan is called the 'Aristotle' of his age due to his scholarship?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the most educated ruler among the medieval rulers. He had good knowledge of Arabic, Persian, Mathematics, Astronomy, Physics, Logic, and Medicine. He was a good poet and calligrapher. He had good knowledge of Persian poetry. Due to his scholarship, he is called the 'Aristotle' of his age. In the words of S.R. Sharma – "Apart from being proficient in the military victories of his age, he was a sharp student of Persian art, a master of writing style, a sharp exponent of the age of eloquence, a philosopher, logician, and adept in Greek learning and spiritual science."

questions.question_text: Which ruler introduced the silver Tanka and copper Jital coins?
questions.explanation: The meaning of Iltutmish is "master of the empire". He was a Turk of the Ilbari tribe and was the first Sultan of Delhi. Iltutmish was the first Sultan to make Delhi the capital. Aibak's capital was Lahore. Iltutmish was the first Turkish ruler to introduce pure Arabic coins. He was a great coin expert. He has the credit of introducing the tradition of writing the mint's name on coins prevalent in foreign countries in India. Iltutmish introduced the silver Tanka and copper Jital and got the Caliph's name engraved on the coins

questions.question_text: Rajwah and Ulughkhani were -

options.A: Names of gardens planted by Firoz Tughlaq
options.B: Names of cities founded by Firoz Tughlaq
options.C: Names of canals built by Firoz Tughlaq

questions.explanation: For the development of agriculture, the rulers of the Delhi Sultanate paid special attention to artificial means of irrigation. The most development of irrigation system took place in the Tughlaq period. The first ruler to build canals for irrigation was Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq. Firoz Tughlaq was the first ruler to implement a scheme to collect rainwater by building a dam. There are five main canals built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq – 1. Ulughkhani canal. 2. Rajwah canal. 3. Canal from Sirmur hills to Hansi. 4. Canal from Ghaggar to Firozabad. 5. Canal from Yamuna to Firozabad.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi was first honored by the Caliph with the title of 'Nasir-Amir-ul-Muminin'?
questions.explanation: The meaning of Iltutmish is "master of the empire". He was a Turk of the Ilbari tribe. After Aibak's death, Aram Shah sat on the throne. Defeating Aram Shah in the "Battle of Jud", Iltutmish became the ruler in 1210 AD. Iltutmish was a slave and became the first Sultan of Delhi. He received recognition for the post of Sultan in 1229 AD from the Caliph of Baghdad Al-Mustansir Billah. The Caliph gave him special authority letter and honorary dress (Khilat) and the title of 'Nasir-Amir-ul-Muminin'

questions.question_text: The independent Yadava kingdom of Devagiri was established by:
questions.explanation: Yadavas, during the rise of Rashtrakutas and Chalukyas, held the position of subordinate feudatory kings, but when the power of Chalukyas weakened, they became independent and made Devagiri (Daulatabad), the present Hyderabad region, their center. In 1187 AD, Yadava king Bhillama defeated the last Chalukya king Someshvara IV and occupied Kalyani as well

questions.question_text: Who was the first legal Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – In 1229 AD, Iltutmish received the authority letter of recognition from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad, through which his independent position as Sultan and formal recognition of the Delhi Sultanate was obtained.
