questions.question_text: Knowledge of the main events of Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq is in the book 'Rehla', in which language was it written?
questions.explanation: Information about the main events of Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq is obtained from the book named 'Rehla'. The writing of Rehla was done in the Arabic language by the African traveler Ibn Battuta, which is his travelogue. Detailed descriptions of the political, social, economic, and cultural situation of India have been given in this book. It contains a description of Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's intelligence system, post system, and the circumstances of his death

questions.question_text: The Sultan who believed in sovereignty, not in divine power, was
questions.explanation: Alauddin was the Sultan who believed in sovereignty, not in divine power. Alauddin was also a person who believed in the theory of kingship like Balban. Alauddin also believed in the divine rights of the king. In the words of Alauddin himself, "I do not know what is appropriate and what is inappropriate in the eyes of the law. I order to do whatever I consider appropriate for the benefit of the state or for a particular occasion, what my fate will be on the day of final judgment, I do not know."

questions.question_text: During the Delhi Sultanate period, in whose reign was the word 'Masahat' used for land measurement?
questions.explanation: During Alauddin's time, the rate of land revenue was the highest. Through an ordinance, he fixed 50 percent land tax (Kharaj) on produce. Alauddin was the first Muslim ruler who fixed revenue on the actual income of the land. For this, he considered Biswa as the unit. In the Sultanate period, the credit for reviving the 'Masahat' (land measurement) system goes to Alauddin Khalji. He liked to take the tax in the form of grain

questions.question_text: Before his death, whom did Balban nominate as his successor?
questions.explanation: Before his death, Balban appointed his grandson Kai-Khusrau (son of Muhammad) as his successor, but after Balban's death, Delhi's Kotwal Fakhruddin Muhammad hatched a conspiracy and gave Kai-Khusrau the governorship of Multan and sent him there, and made Bughra Khan's son Kaiqubad the Sultan. On the occasion of coronation, Kaiqubad's age was only 17 or 18 years The Secondary Education Service Selection Board has deleted this question in its revised answer key.

questions.question_text: Nizamuddin Junaidi was the Wazir of-
questions.explanation: Wazir Nizamuddin Junaidi was the famous Wazir of Iltutmish. During Iltutmish's time, when the Ulema offered the condition of death or Islam before the Hindus, then Wazir Junaidi said that "Recently victory has been achieved in India, Muslims are like a drop in the ocean, and it is possible that on implementing this order, Hindus might unite and widespread disorder might arise."

questions.question_text: Among Alauddin Khalji's famous generals, who died while fighting against the Mongols?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji's famous general Zafar Khan died fighting bravely against the Mongol invasion that took place under the leadership of Qutlugh Khwaja in 1299 AD. This invasion of Mongols was the most dangerous invasion of Alauddin Khalji's period. The maximum number of Mongol invasions occurred during Alauddin Khalji's time

questions.question_text: During the reign of which Sultan did the rebellion of Akat Khan take place?
questions.explanation: During the reign of Sultan Alauddin Khalji of the Khalji dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate, the rebellion of Akat Khan took place. Apart from this rebellion, during Alauddin's time, 3 other people rebelled. To stop these rebellions, Alauddin banned marriage among Amirs and started depositing more and more of their wealth in the government treasury

questions.question_text: When Sikandar Lodi invaded and could not win the fort, who was the Tomar ruler of Gwalior at that time?
questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi was certainly successful in winning the Rajput states but could not completely bring the Tomar ruler of Gwalior, Man Singh, under his control

questions.question_text: 'Tughlaqabad' city was built by–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq established 'Tughlaqabad' on the hills located in Delhi. He built a fort in this city which is known as 'Chhappankot'. Inside this fort, on the northern part, the pentagonal tomb of Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq is situated inside an artificial lake. Red stones and marble have been used in its construction. He built the Nahar-i-Bahisht inside the Delhi fort, which was also called the Heaven Canal and the reconstruction of the Rajwah canal built by Delhi Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq was done by the name of Nahar-i-Sah.

questions.question_text: Who was defeated in the battle of Raichur?
questions.explanation: In 1520 AD, Sultan Ismail Adil Khan of Bijapur, by forming an alliance with the Gajapatis of Odisha, occupied the 'Raichur Doab'. Nuniz has described Krishnadevaraya's campaign to regain this. He marched with 10 lakh soldiers and besieged the Raichur Doab. On 19 May 1520 AD, a decisive battle took place between both sides. Initially, the Muslim army suffered heavy losses to the dense Hindu military ranks due to the use of cannons, but eventually, Krishnadevaraya's military skill scattered the Muslim leaders. Ismail Adil Khan himself saved his life by escaping the battlefield while riding an elephant

questions.question_text: Who had to pay Jizya tax?
questions.explanation: Jizya was a non-religious tax imposed on non-Muslims, in return for which their life and property were protected and they were exempted from military service. Women, children, beggars, priests, ascetics, etc., were exempt from this tax. Firoz Tughlaq imposed Jizya on Brahmins who were previously exempt from this tax

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements about Ziauddin Barani 1. He was born in Golconda. 2. He was a contemporary of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. 3. He was the author of Tarikh-i-Firozshahi. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Ziauddin Barani was born in 1285 AD in an educated family. His father was a high official during the reign of Sultan Balban and Barani also proved to be a scholar. Sultan Ghiyasuddin gave him a respected place in the court and he also remained in close contact with Muhammad Tughlaq. But Sultan Firoz Tughlaq became unhappy with him, due to which Barani's last life was spent in financial crisis Note - Ziauddin Barani was born in a Sayyid family in 'Baran', which is known as modern 'Bulandshahr'.

questions.question_text: Name the book written by Fakhr-e-Mudabbir~
questions.explanation: Fakhr-e-Mudabbir was the court historian of Qutbuddin Aibak, the Sultan of the Slave dynasty in the Sultanate period. In his book Adab-ul-Harb Wa Shuja'at, he has given a very detailed description of war by the king and his bravery. These were Persian writers who were active in the Delhi Sultanate. It is believed that he also worked as a Wazir of Qutbuddin Aibak. His full name was Fakhr-ud-din Muhammad bin Mansur Mubarak Shah Al-Qureshi. He has been known by the pseudonym Fakhr-e-Mudabbir

questions.question_text: Who was the author of "Gora Badal Padmini Chaupai"?
questions.explanation: Jain monk Hemratan Suri ji created 'Gora Badal Chaupai', after listening to this literary work, the public of every village used to get inspired by heroism and get ready to serve the motherland. Suri ji was considered his guru by Maharana Pratap. Queen Padmini, Veer Gora, and Badal's character was considered a national character, and this character also created a sharp national feeling among every person of Mewar, which feeling became an unshakable part of the Maharana's struggle at every step

questions.question_text: Who headed Diwan-i-Insha?
questions.explanation: During the time of the Sultanate period, for the work of correspondence, the Sultans established a department called Diwan-i-Insha, which was managed through Dabir-i-Mumalik or Dabir-i-Khas. All these royal records prepared the drafts of the Sultan's declarations and letters. Dabirs and writers were his assistants. The work of this department was extremely confidential. Firmans of the Sultan were issued from Diwan-i-Insha only

questions.question_text: Which of the following does the word 'Jizya' or 'Kharaj-o-Jizya' refer to?

options.A: Financial levy imposed by Islamic law on non-Muslim subjects.
options.B: General consensus among Muslim jurists on a particular legal issue.
options.C: A non-binding law passed by the Islamic authority.
options.D: The process, path, or road taken by Prophet Muhammad.

questions.explanation: Jizya or Kharaj-o-Jizya is taken as a financial charge on the permanent non-Muslim subjects of the state ruled by Islamic law. This is a per capita annual tax and is implemented in Islamic states. In the Quran, Jizya has been mentioned without any rate or amount. During Islamic history, Jizya was used in different forms. Along with Kharaj, a word is sometimes used with Jizya and sometimes with another. The rate of Jizya depends on the annual income of the payer, how much amount is payable. Different classes received exemptions from Jizya. In which, disabled, women, children, elderly, insane, beggars, jurists, slaves, etc., were exempted from this.

questions.question_text: In the reign of which dynasty were private markets replaced by state-run markets, with strict regulation of the prices of all goods?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji implemented the market system after the Chittor victory in 1303 AD. A detailed description of this is found in Barani's Tarikh-i-Firozshahi. Under strict rules, he fixed the prices of all goods and put a stop on hoarding. He registered all markets so that no person/farmer/trader could hoard any item. The state built its own warehouses and implemented a Public Distribution System (Rationing System). Alauddin Khalji became the first Sultan of the Sultanate period to do so

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first dynasty of the Sultanate period?
questions.explanation: There is a difference of opinion among historians regarding the naming of the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, who address it by different names - Slave Dynasty, Mamluk Dynasty, Ilbari Dynasty, and Early Turk, etc. Initially, it was named Slave Dynasty or Slave Dynasty because its founder was Muhammad Ghori's slave. Among the 11 rulers of this dynasty, only three rulers Aibak, Iltutmish, and Balban were slaves and before accepting power, they were freed from slavery. From which it is proved that the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was the Slave Dynasty or Mamluk Dynasty

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs related to Mughal administration is false?
questions.explanation: Mughal administrative system was a highly centralized bureaucratic system. It had a mixture of Indian and foreign (Persian and Arabic) elements. Its main officers are as follows Mir Atish - Head of Artillery Mir Bar - Forest Superintendent Mushrif - Revenue Secretary Nazir-i-Buyutat - Superintendent of Royal Workshops Mustaufi - Chief Auditor

questions.question_text: Who was the author of ‘Futuh-us-Salatin’?
questions.explanation: ‘Futuh-us-Salatin’ is a book written by Khwaja Abdullah Malik Isami (Isami). This book contains the poetic history from the time of the Ghaznavid dynasty up to the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. This book is dedicated to the first ruler of the Bahmani dynasty, Alauddin Bahman Shah I. It was written in Persian

questions.question_text: In which epic is the story of Sohrab Rustam described?
questions.explanation: The story of Sohrab Rustam is described in ‘Shahnameh’. Rustam was a brave warrior of Persia (Iran). The Shahnameh epic was written by the Persian poet Firdausi

questions.question_text: Which of the following is mismatched–
questions.explanation: Book – Author 1. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi – Ziauddin Barani 2. Tabaqat-i-Akbari – This work was composed by Nizamuddin Ahmad. 3. Muntakhab-ul-Lubab – Khafi Khan 4. Iqbalnama – Mutamad Khan

questions.question_text: According to Barani, what is the descending order of the military cavalry organization? i. Sarkhail ii. Sipahsalar iii. Amir iv. Malik
questions.explanation: According to Barani, the military cavalry organization is mentioned in ‘Fatawa-i-Jahandari’. The army was organized based on the decimal system of the Mongols. In this order– 10 Malik = 1 Khan 10 Amir = 1 Malik 10 Sipahsalar = 1 Amir 10 Sarkhail = 1 Sipahsalar

questions.question_text: ‘‘After this incident, a strong storm came, there was heavy rain and a famine occurred.’’ This statement of Barani points towards which incident?
questions.explanation: This writing of Barani is a description of the terrible calamity that occurred after the murder of Sidi Maula when he was trampled to death by an elephant, Barani wrote in his grief-stricken words– ‘‘After the incident of his death, a strong storm came, there was heavy rain and a famine occurred.’’ The famous historian Isami confirmed this writing

questions.question_text: What was the Sultanate era ‘Itlaq’?

options.A: Order letter for tax collection from Khalisa land
options.B: Payment order letter to royal cavalry
options.C: Permission letter for cavalry to keep extra horses
options.D: Correspondence between Sultan and provincial rulers

questions.explanation: The practice of ‘Itlaq’ was started by Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Itlaq-nama was a type of hundi with the help of which soldiers used to receive salaries from revenue officials. When a soldier went to the officials collecting tax with this letter, he used to get only 50% of the tax, the remaining 50% was left for government expenses

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans abolished the ‘Chahalgani’ (Group of Forty)?
questions.explanation: Balban destroyed the Chahalgani group created by Iltutmish to establish the prestige of the Sultan's position and absolute power. This group claimed monopoly on high positions and wanted to keep control over the Sultan. Their arrogance, selfish attitude, mutual jealousy and conflict were harmful to the security of the Sultanate. Therefore, Balban decided to destroy this group First- He appointed low-caste Turks to high positions and made them equal to the Amirs of this group. Second- He gave severe punishments to the Amirs of this group on the pretext of minor offenses. He had Badaun's Subedar Malik Baqbaq beaten so much that he died. He had the Governor of Awadh, Haibat Khan, lashed. He had another Amir hanged at the city gate. Third- He had his cousin Sher Khan killed by poison.

questions.question_text: In which original language was ‘Chachnama’ written?
questions.explanation: We get information about the history of Sindh from the book named ‘Chachnama’. It has been written by some unknown author. It is an authentic source regarding the attack of Muhammad bin Qasim and his rule, etc. All the facts and descriptions written in it cannot be accepted; nevertheless, due to it being a local history of Sindh, sufficient information is obtained from it regarding the Arab invasion. It describes the history of the Chach dynasty and the conquest of Sindh by the Arabs. The Persian translation of ‘Chachnama’ was done by Abu Bakr Kufi during the time of Nasiruddin Qabacha.

questions.question_text: The work ‘Futuh-us-Salatin’ is related to the history of whom?
questions.explanation: The book named ‘Futuh-us-Salatin’ was written by Khwaja Abdullah Malik Isami. This book gives important details about Muhammad Tughlaq and the establishment of the Bahmani state, etc. In this book, history from 999 AD to 1350 AD is obtained. During Muhammad Tughlaq's transfer of capital from Delhi to Daulatabad, his 90-year-old grandfather had died. Therefore, he has criticized Muhammad Tughlaq in this book. In this, he has given a detailed description of the court of the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate, Alauddin Bahman Shah, and the religious, social, and political situation of his kingdom, which is entirely dedicated to his kingdom

questions.question_text: Who among the following translated ‘Kokashastra’ into Persian?
questions.explanation: Zia Nakhshabi was the first person who translated a series of Sanskrit stories into Persian, under which a "parrot" tells a story to a "separated" heroine, whose husband had gone on a journey. This book "Tutinama", which was composed during the time of Muhammad Tughlaq, became very popular and was also translated from Persian into Turkish and many European languages. Zia Nakhshabi translated the book ‘Kokashastra’, written on Indian sexology, into Persian

questions.question_text: Alauddin Khilji became the Sultan of Delhi in 1296 AD after killing his uncle and protector. Who among the following was his protector?
questions.explanation: All Khilji sardars were aware of Alauddin's ambition. Alauddin Khilji was the son of Jalaluddin Firoz Khilji's brother Shihabuddin. His real name was Ali Gurshasp. When the Sultan was in Gwalior, Ahmad Chap advised him to stop Alauddin, who was coming with huge wealth from Devagiri, but the Sultan did not accept his advice and returned to Delhi. The Sultan went to Kara via the river route. He went to meet Alauddin unarmed and without bodyguards on the advice of Ulugh Khan. On the shore, Alauddin's army was standing in a war-ready position. When Jalaluddin hugged Alauddin, at that very moment, on Alauddin's signal, a soldier attacked the Sultan with a sword, cut off his head, and killed him

questions.question_text: In whose court was Ziauddin Barani an advisor?
questions.explanation: Ziauddin Barani was born in 1285 AD into an educated family. His father was a high official during the reign of Sultan Balban and he became the Naib of Prince Arkali Khan during the time of Sultan Jalaluddin Khilji. Barani was a scholar whom Sultan Ghiyasuddin gave an honorable position in the court. And he remained close to him during the time of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, but Firoz Tughlaq became displeased, due to which Barani's life in the final moments was spent in financial crisis. Barani received patronage for 17 years during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. For fear of Firoz Tughlaq, he dedicated his book Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi to Firoz Tughlaq

questions.question_text: Where was Ulugh Khan the Subedar at the time of Alauddin Khilji's Jalore invasion?
questions.explanation: At the time of Alauddin Khilji's Jalore invasion, Ulugh Khan was the Subedar of Bayana and he was his most trusted, capable, loyal Subedar, who was made the Subedar of Bayana to attack the South and to manage the army. But Khilji was very worried due to his death in the middle. Later, this responsibility was handed over to his special, Hazar Dinari, who trampled the entire South

questions.question_text: The famous poet Amir Khusrau, known by the title ‘Tota-i-Hind’, was NOT a contemporary of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The famous poet Amir Khusrau, known by the name Tota-i-Hind, was born on 1253 AD in Patiali district Kasganj, Uttar Pradesh. His real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin. Khusrau was also adept in diplomatic conduct suitable for social life. Khusrau spent his entire life under royal patronage. He saw the rise and fall of 8 Sultans of the Slave dynasty, Khilji, and Tughlaq dynasty with his own eyes. He was a contemporary of Balban, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, and Alauddin Khilji. Iltutmish had no relation with him

questions.question_text: Who was the Chauhan ruler of Jalore at the time of Iltutmish's invasion of Jalore?
questions.explanation: In 1228-29 AD, Delhi Sultan Iltutmish attacked Jalore fort. Jalore's Chauhan ruler Uday Singh, along with the Vaghela ruler of Gujarat, formed a joint front but Iltutmish forced Uday Singh to accept his suzerainty and pay annual tax. Uday Singh, the successor of Samar Singh, also got many constructions done in the fort in the thirteenth century.

questions.question_text: In which of the following battles did the ruler of Mewar, Jaitra Singh, defeat Iltutmish's army?
questions.explanation: After Bappa Rawal, until the early 13th century, restlessness and chaos prevailed in Mewar, which ended during the reign of Jaitra Singh. Jaitra Singh defeated the Paramaras and captured Chittor. Jaitra Singh defeated the Paramaras of Malwa and forced Iltutmish's army to return in the ‘Battle of Bhutala’. The drama ‘Hammir Mada-Mardana’ written by Jai Singh contains the description of Iltutmish's attack. Jaitra Singh's successors are Tej Singh, Samar Singh, and Ratan Singh

questions.question_text: Under which ruler did the Delhi Sultanate reach its peak in terms of geographical expansion?
questions.explanation: At the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's accession to the throne, the Delhi Sultanate was divided into a total of 23 provinces. Among which the main ones were Delhi, Devagiri, Lahore, Multan, Jajnagar (Odisha), Dwarasamudra, etc. Kashmir and Baluchistan were not included in Delhi. At that time, under the state were the Doab in the north, the plains of Punjab, Lahore and from Sindh to the sea coast of Gujarat, the entire province of Bengal in the east, the states of Malwa, Mahoba, Ujjain, and Dhar in the central part, and they were situated in the south. This proves that the Delhi Sultanate had reached its peak in terms of its geographical expansion

questions.question_text: Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khilji was responsible for destroying which of the following places?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khilji- Ikhtiyaruddin Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khilji was the military Sipahsalar of Qutbuddin Aibak. He led the Muslim conquest in the eastern Indian regions of Bengal and Bihar and established himself as their ruler. Between 1197-1206 AD in the Indian subcontinent, he massacred Buddhist monks and, considering Bihar's Nalanda University a military cantonment, destroyed it and set the library part of it on fire

questions.question_text: Which Sultan got ‘Sikandar Sani’ (Second Alexander) inscribed on his coins?
questions.explanation: After overcoming his initial difficulties, Alauddin Khilji made ambitious plans for state expansion and administration. His victory and success encouraged him so much that he accepted the title of ‘‘Sikandar-i-Sani’’ (Second Alexander) and got it inscribed on his coins

questions.question_text: Match the following– Alauddin Khilji's General Title A. Alaul Mulk i. Zafar Khan B. Malik Hisamuddin ii. Ulugh Khan C. Malik Sanjar iii. Nusrat Khan D. Malik Jalesari iv. Alp Khan A B C D
questions.explanation: The chronological detail of Alauddin Khilji's generals' titles is as follows– 1. Alaul Mulk – Ulugh Khan 2. Malik Hisamuddin – Zafar Khan 3. Malik Sanjar – Alp Khan 4. Malik Jalesari – Nusrat Khan

questions.question_text: Which Sultan's patronage did the Persian scholar Sheikh Jamaluddin, who is called the second Khusrau of the Delhi court and who wrote ‘Siyar-ul-Arifin’, receive?
questions.explanation: During the Sultanate period, under the patronage of the Lodi dynasty, the Persian scholar Sheikh Jamaluddin, who is called the second Khusrau of the Delhi court, wrote ‘Siyar-ul-Arifin’. He received the patronage of Sikandar Lodi, who himself was known as a Persian poet. Sikandar Lodi used to write poetry under the pen name Gulrukhi

questions.question_text: To which ruler did Fakhr-i-Mudabbir dedicate his work ‘Adab-ul-Harb wash-Shujaat’?
questions.explanation: Fakhr-i-Mudabbir wrote his work ‘‘Adab-ul-Harb wash-Shujaat’’ in honor of Iltutmish. This book sheds special light on the importance of governance and military organization of the Sultanate period

questions.question_text: Name the Sultan who removed ‘Zakat’ from grain?
questions.explanation: Lodi dynasty ruler Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517 AD) removed the tax named Zakat from grain. He strengthened the economic policies during his reign in which he fixed the rate of revenue collection according to produce, used Gaj-i-Sikandari (39 inches) for land measurement. He founded the city named Agra. He was a good scholar of Persian language, used to work on writing poetry under the pseudonym 'Gulrukhi' in the Persian language

questions.question_text: At the time of his coronation, whom did Firoz Tughlaq give the title of 'Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul' and make his Wazir?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq, after taking over the Delhi Sultanate, gave generous religious grants to the mosques, shrines, and khanqahs on the way from Sindh to Delhi and made Malik Maqbul his Wazir by giving him the title of Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul. Both tried to end the difficulties created by Muhammad Tughlaq

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first medieval ruler who adopted the title of 'Zille-i-Ilahi'?
questions.explanation: Balban was the first ruler who adopted the title of 'Zille-i-Ilahi'. Zille-i-Ilahi means shadow of God. Balban's theory of kingship was based on the 'blood and iron policy', prestige, power, and justice. According to the Niyabat-i-Khudai theory, the Sultan is the representative of God (Nayab-i-Khudai) in the world. After the Prophet, the place is of the Sultan. Balban told his son Bughra Khan that there is a part of divinity in the King. No human can resemble him

questions.question_text: Below List-I and List-II are given. After matching these two correctly, select the correct option from the given alternatives : List-I List-II
questions.explanation: List-I List-II (a) Diwan-i-Risalat - 1. Religious affairs department and Justice department (b) Diwan-i-Kohi - 2. Agriculture department (c) Diwan-i-Insha - 3. Correspondence Department (d) Diwan-i-Arz - 4. Military affairs department

questions.question_text: According to P.N. Chopra, the nature of the Delhi Sultanate was:
questions.explanation: According to P.N. Chopra, the nature of the Delhi Sultanate was theocratic (religion-centered)

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Jamaluddin Hansvi was a disciple of Baba Farid. Baba Farid was related to the Chishti sect. His real name was Sheikh Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar His birth happened in Multan and death in Punjab, Baba Farid's (1175 AD to 1265 AD) shrine is in Ajodhan, Punjab.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultan married his daughter to Sufi saint Baba Farid?
questions.explanation: Sultan Balban married his daughter Huzra to the Chishti sect saint Baba Farid, Balban respected Baba Farid very much. His real name was Sheikh Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar

questions.question_text: Match the following: First List Second List (Minister) A. Diwan-i-Wizarat 1. Religious matters B. Diwan-i-Risalat 2. Finance C. Diwan-i-Arz 3. Military recruitment and organization D. Diwan-i-Insha 4. Royal correspondence A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct order is– Diwan-i-Wizarat – Finance department and chief supervisor Diwan-i-Risalat – Foreign department / Religious matters Diwan-i-Arz – Military department Diwan-i-Insha – Royal correspondence

questions.question_text: The inspiration behind building .............. was Khwaja Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki.
questions.explanation: The foundation of Qutub Minar situated in Delhi was laid by Qutbuddin Aibak and it was completed by Iltutmish. Aibak laid its foundation in the name of the famous Sufi saint 'Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki'

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi established Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi to improve the condition of agriculture?
questions.explanation: Delhi's Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq established a department related to agriculture 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' for the expansion and improvement of agriculture. Its head was called Amir-i-Kohi. Provided Taccavi loans to farmers, this has also been called Son-dhar. He prepared a famine code to provide relief to farmers from famine during his reign

questions.question_text: Match the following: First List Second List A. Yahya-bin-Ahmed 1. Tarikh-i-Salatin-i-Afghana B. Abdullah 2. Futuh-us-Salatin C. Isami 3. Tarikh-i-Daudi D. Ahmed Yadgar 4. Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct order is– (1) Yahya-bin-Ahmed Sirhindi – Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi (2) Abdullah – Tarikh-i-Daudi (3) Isami – Futuh-us-Salatin (4) Ahmed Yadgar – Tarikh-i-Salatin-i-Afghana

questions.question_text: Which historian among the following propounded the theory of Urban Revolution in India in the 13th and 14th century?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Habib has called the 13th and 14th century an Urban Revolution in India. He has given the status of urban revolution on the basis of the following facts – New use of wheel or spinning wheel, which led to expansion in means of irrigation. – During this time, the custom of rearing silkworms and planting pens was also started. – New crafts were also started by the Turks, which included paper production. – Improvement in the production of clothes due to the use of spinning wheels. Apart from this, new conquerors brought new culture and technology with them. Hence, along with the change in the nature of power, on the basis of changes in the socio-economic, cultural, and technical fields, Muhammad Habib called it an urban revolution.

questions.question_text: In whose court of Delhi Sultan did Genghis Khan send his ambassador?
questions.explanation: Mongol ruler Genghis Khan sent his ambassador to the court of Delhi Sultan Iltutmish, because he wanted Iltutmish not to help the ruler of Persia (Iran), Jalaluddin Mangabarni. He had come to India fleeing from Persia

questions.question_text: Which Sultan adopted the title of Caliph?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah Khalji (1316 AD - 1320 AD) was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who declared himself Caliph and refused to accept the Caliph's authority. This was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who included the southern state Devagiri in his empire. He destroyed the market system established by Alauddin Khalji. He lived a life full of debauchery, liked the company of naked men and women, used to come to the court wearing women's clothes himself

questions.question_text: Who built 'Hazar Situn' palace?
questions.explanation: 'Hazar Situn' (palace with thousand pillars) palace was built by Alauddin Khalji in Delhi (Siri) in 1303 AD. Alauddin adopted the title of Alexander Second (Sani). He built Alai Darwaza in Delhi, was the first Sultan of Delhi to attack South India

questions.question_text: What was the original name of Amir Khusrau?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusro's real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusro. He was born in 1253 AD in Patiali village of Etah district of Uttar Pradesh. He died in 1325 AD in Delhi. Amir Khusro was a disciple of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya of the Chishti order. He witnessed the reign of 8 Sultans of Delhi. The Indianization of Persian poetry was done first by Khusro. The new poetic style expounded by him in Persian is called 'Sabk-i-Hindi'

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of Diwan-i-Riyasat:
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji established the department named 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' to implement the market control system. The superintendent of the market was called 'Shahna-i-Mandi'

questions.question_text: Identify the false statement regarding Tabaqat-i-Nasiri:

options.A: It contains an account of the Mongol invasion of India.
options.C: In this, often the same event is repeated many times.
options.D: It has been completed in 1260 AD.

questions.explanation: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri- is authored by 'Minhaj-us-Siraj', it contains information about Muhammad Ghori's conquest of India and the early history of the Turkish Sultanate up to approximately 1260 AD - This work is dedicated to the Slave dynasty ruler Nasiruddin Mahmud. - It has 26 Tabaqats (chapters).

questions.question_text: What was 'Ushr':

options.D: 1/5th part of war booty was the state's share

questions.explanation: Ushr was the land tax taken from Muslims. On land where irrigation was done through natural resources, the state collected 1/10th of the produce, and on irrigation through artificial means, it collected 1/5th of the produce as tax Zakat - Religious tax levied on the income of Muslims Khums - Tax levied on wealth looted in war Jizya - Tax levied on non-Muslims

questions.question_text: 'Lakh Baksh' was the title for________.
questions.explanation: Lakh Baksh was the title of Qutbuddin Aibak, he is known by this title for giving lakhs in charity. Apart from this, he also received titles like Quran Khan, Peel Baksh, Hatim the Second, etc

questions.question_text: Who started the Iqta system during the Sultanate period?
questions.explanation: Administratively, the Iqta was established by Iltutmish. This is an Arabic word, which means - land. The administration of Iqta was under the 'Muqti'

questions.question_text: Which state of South India did not accept Alauddin's hegemony________.
questions.explanation: Pandya rulers never accepted Alauddin's hegemony and neither paid any tax. Although, from the point of view of wealth, the Madurai campaign was the most successful Under the leadership of Malik Kafur, Devagiri, Hoysala, and Telangana were conquered and brought under the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question_text: Match the following: A. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq 1. Determination of land tax based on accurate measurement B. Firoz Tughlaq 2. Revival of the prestige of the royal crown C. Balban 3. Establishment of various agriculture departments D. Alauddin Khalji
questions.explanation: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq — Establishment of various agriculture departments; Firoz Tughlaq — Establishment of industrial workshop; Balban — Revival of the prestige of the royal crown; Alauddin Khalji — Determination of land tax based on accurate measurement.

questions.question_text: Establishment of industrial workshop A B C D
questions.explanation: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq - Establishment of various agriculture departments Firoz Tughlaq - Establishment of industrial workshop Balban - Revival of the prestige of the royal crown Alauddin Khalji - Determination of land tax based on accurate measurement

questions.question_text: ............... Sultan refused to accept the authority of the Khalifa.
questions.explanation: Among the medieval rulers, Alauddin Khalji was the first ruler who never tried to get recognition for the post of Sultan from the Khalifa, although for the sake of nominal tradition, he accepted the title 'Yamin-ul-Khilafat' (Naib of the Khalifa). In this way, Alauddin Khalji never accepted the authority of the Khalifa

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the Sultans of Delhi? 1. Razia 2. Nasiruddin Mahmud 3. Balban 4. Kaiqubad 5. Qutbuddin Aibak 6. Iltutmish Choose the correct answer group:
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210 AD) Iltutmish (1210-1236 AD) Razia Sultan (1236-1240 AD) Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-1265 AD) Balban (1265-1287 AD) Kaiqubad (1287-90 AD)

questions.question_text: Where was Amir Khusro born?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusro was born in 1253 in Patiali village of Kasganj district of Uttar Pradesh. Khusro is called Tota-e-Hind (Parrot of India)

questions.question_text: Finally, the Pandya Empire merged into________.
questions.explanation: In 1377 AD, the Vijayanagara ruler Bukka I conquered Madurai, the capital of the Pandyas, and merged it into the Vijayanagara Empire. Alauddin did invade the Pandya state and conquered it but did not merge it into the Delhi Sultanate. The Pandyas never accepted Alauddin's subordination

questions.question_text: Which ruler brought the Seven Pillar edicts to Delhi?
questions.explanation: Two pillars of Ashoka were brought to Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq from Topra (Haryana) and Meerut (U.P.) respectively. He called the Topra pillar inscription the Golden Pillar and got it installed in Firozabad (Delhi)

questions.question_text: Who founded the city of Jaunpur?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded the city of Jaunpur in 1359 AD in memory of his cousin Juna Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq). Jaunpur was the capital of the eastern province of the Delhi Sultanate

questions.question_text: When did Muhammad Tughlaq change his capital from Delhi to Devagiri?
questions.explanation: In 1326-27, Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Devagiri (Daulatabad). Its name was kept Qutub-ul-Islam

questions.question_text: Who started the practice of branding horses in India?
questions.explanation: The practice of branding horses in India was started by Alauddin Khalji. He was a capable general and ruler. To ensure that horses and persons could not be changed at the time of war, the tradition of branding (Dagh) and Huliya (description roll) respectively was started

questions.question_text: Whom did Iltutmish nominate as his successor for the throne of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish nominated his daughter Razia as his successor to the throne of Delhi, but after the death of Iltutmish, the Turkish nobles seated his son Rukn-ud-din on the throne, but Razia soon gained power with the help of other nobles

questions.question_text: Who built Sultan Ghari in Delhi?
questions.explanation: The tomb of Sultan Ghari is located in Delhi, which was built by Sultan Iltutmish in 1231 AD in memory of his son Nasiruddin Mahmud. This is considered the first Islamic tomb. Iltutmish is considered the father of tomb architecture

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a Sultan of the Slave dynasty?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah was a ruler of the Khalji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate who ruled Delhi from 1316-1320 AD. Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah declared himself Khalifa. His Wazir Khusro Khan killed him in 1320

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities was not founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was a ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate who ruled from 1351-1388 AD. His era is known for many creative works such as canal construction, founding of cities, garden construction, etc. Firoz Shah founded Jaunpur, Hisar, Firozabad in cities. Firoz Shah Tughlaq did not establish Fatehgarh. In 1478 AD, Bahlul Lodi named Fatehgarh after his son

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler who gave a gold coin to a soldier for giving a bribe to the inspecting clerk:
questions.explanation: Among the Sultans of the Delhi Sultanate, Firoz Shah Tughlaq promoted bribery when he gave money to one of his soldiers to get a horse passed. Firoz Tughlaq established the slave department and built many important canals and cities

questions.question_text: The Sultan, who founded the city of Agra, was
questions.explanation: In 1501 AD, Sikandar Lodi laid the foundation of the city of Agra with the objective of securing his authority over the rulers of Rajasthan and establishing control over trade routes. Here he also built the Badalgarh fort and made Agra his capital in 1504

questions.question_text: After capturing Chittor, Alauddin Khalji named it
questions.explanation: After achieving victory over Chittor in 1303, Alauddin Khalji named Chittor 'Khizrabad' after his son Khizr Khan

questions.question_text: Which Sultan assumed the title of 'Sikandar Sani'?
questions.explanation: Sikandar-i-Sani was the title of Alauddin Khalji, which meant Second Alexander

questions.question_text: Who destroyed Nalanda University in 1202?
questions.explanation: In 1202, Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed Nalanda University. Its establishment was done by Gupta era ruler Kumaragupta I. It was the most important center of higher education in India. In this education center of Mahayana Buddhism, along with Hinayana Buddhism, students from other religions and many countries studied. It was the main center of education for religion, politics, education, history, astrology, science, etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following ended the Iqta system?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji ended the Iqta system. This system was started by Iltutmish. Under this, land was given to soldiers/state officials in lieu of salary

questions.question_text: Where was the 'Horse-shoe arch' presented for the first time?

options.B: In the tomb of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq

questions.explanation: Alai Darwaza was the southern gateway of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, which was built by Alauddin Khalji. In this, the dome was built for the first time using a scientific method based on triangular stone slabs. For the first time, an arch shaped like a horseshoe was made here. It has been heavily decorated with Quranic verses

questions.question_text: By whom was the silver Tanka of Delhi Sultanate first issued?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish first introduced the silver Tanka and copper Jital in the Sultanate period. He is also considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate

questions.question_text: In which of the following have the dynasties of Delhi Sultanate been arranged chronologically?
questions.explanation: Slave Dynasty (1206-1290), Khalji Dynasty (1290-1320), Tughlaq Dynasty (1320-1412), Sayyid Dynasty (1414-51) and Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526)

questions.question_text: Which of the following foreign travelers lived in the court of Muhammad Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta came to India from Morocco in 1333 AD during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. In 1292, the Italian traveler Marco Polo came to South India, and the Italian resident Niccolo Conti also came to Vijayanagara in 1420-21. Al-Biruni (998 AD) was the court poet/writer of Mahmud Ghaznavi

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not matched?

options.D: Sunni - Modern practices of the Prophet

questions.explanation: Sunni is not the modern practice of the Prophet but a branch of the Muslim religion

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below: List-I | List-II
questions.explanation: – The correct matching of List-I with List-II is as follows– Kavya - Army Hashm - Cavalry soldier Fawazil - Revenue received in excess of fixed revenue Tawfir - Increase in the estimated income of Iqta

questions.question_text: Who mentioned 'Turkan-e-Chahalgani' first?
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- III Paper June 2012 TGT History 2013 Explanation– The mention of Turkan-e-Chahalgani was first made by Isami in his work Futuh-us-Salatin. Isami was the historian of the time of Bahman Shah. It is noteworthy that Iltutmish had formed a group of 40 slave nobles which was called Turkan-e-Chahalgani.

questions.question_text: "During his approximately 40 years of Khan-ship and Sultanate, he never talked to the people of the market, people of low class, musicians and buffoons." Ziauddin Barani said this statement in the context of which of the following Sultans?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Ziauddin Barani had said about Ghiyas-ud-din Balban (1265-1287 AD), "During his approximately 40 years of Khan-ship and Sultanate, he never talked to the people of the market, people of low class, musicians and buffoons." Balban became Sultan through his own merits. He was harsh and cruel but perhaps, in the circumstances of that time, his being like this was necessary.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs is incorrect?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Diwan-e-Bandagan was the slave department. It was established by Firoz Tughlaq. Speculation and black marketing were completely ended. To look after these works, Alauddin Khalji appointed big officers named Diwan-e-Riyasat and 'Shahna-e-Mandi', and for justice, 'Sarai-e-Adl'. Diwan-e-Siyasat department was opened by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Firoz Shah Tughlaq gave financial aid to a department 'Diwan-e-Khairat' and used to arrange for the marriage of poor Muslim girls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Munhiyan was related to the spy system. Mushrif was the accountant, whereas the head of the royal workshop was Mutasarrif. Barid was also a spy, whereas Shahna was called the superintendent of the market.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was given the title of 'Hazar Dinari'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Malik Kafur was a capable commander of Alauddin Khalji. He was a eunuch slave. He was purchased for one thousand dinars during Alauddin's Gujarat invasion. He is also called 'Hazar Dinari'. After coming in contact with Alauddin, Malik Kafur, who was a Hindu initially, accepted the Muslim religion. The Sultan gave him a high post in the army and he soon became the commander-in-chief. The credit for Alauddin Khalji's South India victory goes to Malik Kafur only.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans implemented a vocational curriculum in education?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005, 2003 Explanation – In 1351 AD, Firoz Tughlaq, the cousin of Muhammad Tughlaq, sat on the throne. Firoz was the first Sultan who gave preference to the physical development of his subjects over conquests and wars, and expanded the duties of the ruler. He made the Islamic religion the basis of state governance. Helping the unemployed, establishment of Diwan-e-Khairat and charitable (Dar-ul-Shafa) hospitals were his humanitarian works. Firoz implemented a vocational curriculum in education.

questions.question_text: Who among the following has given a detailed account of the postal system in the Sultanate period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Ibn Battuta came during the time of Muhammad Tughlaq. He has given a detailed description of the postal system of the Sultanate period. Daroga-i-Dakchowki was the chief officer of the postal department and the spy department. He used to collect information about events happening in different parts of the empire with the help of his subordinate employees and send that information to the service of the Emperor. This officer also used to arrange for the carrying of post in different parts of the empire. For the help of the Daroga in this work, there were Waqia-navis, Sawaneh-nigar, Khufiya-navis and Harkaras.

questions.question_text: What word was used for land measurement in the Sultanate period?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– In the Sultanate period, the word 'Masahat' was used for land measurement. Based on Masahat (land survey), the produce was determined.

questions.question_text: Which was the most influential class of the Sultanate period?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– The Sultanate era Muslim state was theoretically a religion-dominated state. The Khalifa was the head of the Muslim world. Most of the Sultans of the Delhi Sultanate called themselves the Naib of the Khalifa, but Qutbuddin Mubarak Khalji declared himself the Khalifa. In the Sultanate period, the Ulema class had a considerable influence on the administration. This class had influence over religion as well as the policies of the administration.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– In the administration of the Delhi Sultanate, Hajib were officers under Barbak. They used to stand amidst the courtiers in the royal court and without their permission, no one could reach the Sultan. Their leader was called Amir Hajib. All applications could reach the Sultan only through Amir Hajib. Vakil-i-Dar - The biggest officer who managed the royal palace and special employees of the Sultan. The Prime Minister was called Wazir. The administration of the state and the finance department were under him. His assistants were called Naib-i-Wazir. The chief officer of the spy department was Barid-i-Mumalik. Under this, there were Barids (messengers or Harkaras) who were appointed in cities. They used to give information about every event happening in the state to the Sultan.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities was given the name 'Qutb-ul-Islam'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Devagiri was given the name Qutb-ul-Islam. Muhammad bin-Tughlaq made Devagiri his capital. In the Delhi Sultanate, the Slave dynasty ruler Qutbuddin Aibak was a king with a large heart filled with noble sentiments. He was very charitable. Due to his generosity, he used to give so much charity that he was called 'Lakh Baksh' (giver of lakhs). Ferishta has written that if people praised someone's generosity, they used to call him the Aibak of his age. He built mosques named Quwwat-ul-Islam in Delhi and 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' in Ajmer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans visited the shrine of Sayyid Salar Masud Ghazi in Bahraich?
questions.explanation: & c) UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Both Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq visited the shrine of Sayyid Salar Masud Ghazi. Firoz Shah Tughlaq wrote in his autobiography 'Futuhat-i-Firozshahi' that he considered himself the sole ruler of the Muslims and called Hindus 'Zimmis'. He has written that ''I forced my infidel subjects to accept the religion of the Prophet and announced that whoever leaves their religion and becomes a Muslim will be exempted from Jizya.'' R.C. Majumdar has written that Firoz was the greatest religious bigot (Sultan) of this age and in this field, he was the precursor of Sikandar Lodi and Aurangzeb. Firoz took recognition for his post of Sultan from the Khalifa twice. He called himself the 'Naib' of the Khalifa and got the Khalifa's name engraved on his coins. In all this, his objective was to gain the sympathy of the कट्टर (hardline) Muslims and the Ulema class, with whose support he became Sultan.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I | List-II A. Taj-ul-Ma'asir | 1. Ziauddin Barani B. Fatawa-i-Jahandari | 2. Amir Khusro C. Tughlaqnama | 3. Isami D. Futuh-us-Salatin | 4. Hasan Nizami Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Taj-ul-Ma'asir is the work of Hasan Nizami, Fatawa-i-Jahandari is by Ziauddin Barani, Tughlaqnama is by Amir Khusro and Futuh-us-Salatin is the work of Khwaja Abdullah Isami.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not included in the main departments of Iltutmish's army?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Artillery was not included in the main departments of Iltutmish's army. Infantry, Cavalry and Archery were the main departments of his army.

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, 'Sar-jandar' was
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Sar-jandar used to be the Chief Bodyguard in the Sultanate period.

questions.question_text: What was meant by 'Munhiyan' of the Sultanate period
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- In the Sultanate period, the spy was called 'Munhiyan'. He could enter houses and also stop minor crimes. Whereas Barid-i-Mumalik was the chief of the spies.

questions.question_text: The language patronized by the Delhi Sultanate was
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Persian language was patronized by the Delhi Sultanate. Early Sultans of Delhi gave state patronage to the Persian language instead of Arabic because later Muslim invaders used this language.

questions.question_text: In whose reign was Madrasa-i-Nasiri built?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Madrasa-i-Nasiri was built during the reign of Iltutmish. Iltutmish sat on the throne of Delhi in 1210 AD, he was a capable ruler. Along with victory, he tried for the elevation of culture. He built Madrasas for the development of education and also circulated coins in Arabic and Persian.

questions.question_text: In the Delhi Sultanate period, Kharaj was

options.B: Land tax collected from Muslim farmers
options.D: Land tax collected from Hindu landlords

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– In the Delhi Sultanate period, land tax on non-Muslims (Kharaj) was taken from 1/3 to 1/2. It was land tax collected from Hindu landlords (Zamindars).

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, Amir-i-Hajib was an officer of which of the following?

options.B: To look after the royal family
options.C: To implement the court etiquette and maintain its splendor
options.D: To look after the justice department and religious affairs

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– In the Sultanate period, the work of Amir-i-Hajib was to implement court etiquette and maintain its splendor.

questions.question_text: Alai Darwaza is located at which of the following places?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Alai Darwaza is located in Delhi. It was built by Alauddin Khalji. Marshall has said about Alai Darwaza that ''Alai Darwaza is a beautiful jewel of the treasure of Islamic architecture.''

questions.question_text: Who composed the royal proclamation making Razia the successor for Iltutmish?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– After coming from the Gwalior campaign (1232 AD), Iltutmish ordered his Mushrif-e-Mamalik (Mushrif-al-Mumalik) Taj-ul-Mulk Muhammad Dabir to prepare a nomination letter to make Razia the successor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers was of the Mamluk dynasty?
questions.explanation: Sultan Balban of the Sultanate period was related to the 'Mamluk' dynasty. Sultans ruling Delhi from 1206 to 1290 AD were related to three different dynasties. Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Qutbi, Iltutmish founded the Shamsi, and Balban founded the Balbani dynasty. In the beginning, it was named Slave Dynasty, because the first ruler of this dynasty, Qutbuddin Aibak, was a slave. Later, historian Habibullah called them 'Mamluk' rulers

questions.question_text: The 'octagonal' shape of tombs was a feature of which of the following dynasties of medieval India?
questions.explanation: The octagonal shape of tombs was a feature of the Lodi dynasty of medieval India. The Lodi dynasty is also called the 'era of tombs'. The tombs of the Lodi era can be divided into two parts 'Octagonal' and 'Quadrilateral' tombs. The first octagonal tomb in Delhi is the tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani. During the time of Sikandar Lodi, a new style started, in which instead of one dome, two domes were built. It is noteworthy that the tomb of Sikandar Lodi was the first building constructed in India, in which the double dome technique was used in which instead of one dome, two domes were built. It is noteworthy that the tomb of Sikandar Lodi was the first building constructed in India, in which the double dome technique was used.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences is false?

options.B: Harihara-I founded the Vijayanagara dynasty of the South
options.C: Balban completed the construction of Qutub Minar

questions.explanation: The construction of Qutub Minar happened in Delhi. Aibak started its construction. His plan was to build a 225 feet high 4-storey building, but only one storey could be built during Aibak's time. The construction of three storeys was completed during Iltutmish's time. During Firoz Tughlaq's time, its fourth storey was damaged. He got two more storeys built in its place. In this way, this building became five-storeyed now. Balban has no contribution to the construction of Qutub Minar. Hence, statement (c) is false

questions.question_text: During the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, which of the following taxes was 1/5th of the booty received during war?
questions.explanation: Firoz Tughlaq took 1/5th part of Khums (loot during war) as tax. Firoz Tughlaq abolished 24 prevalent taxes and imposed only four taxes permitted by Islamic Shariat law - Kharaj, Zakat, Jizya, Khums. Firoz Tughlaq was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who imposed Jizya tax on Brahmins also. Firoz Tughlaq was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to take irrigation tax (Haq-e-Sharb). Irrigation tax was 10 percent of the agricultural produce

questions.question_text: 'Fatawa-i-Alamgiri', which describes Islamic laws in complete form, was codified under whose order of which ruler of medieval India?
questions.explanation: 'Fatawa-i-Alamgiri' was prepared by a team of jurists during the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. This work is considered a very authentic and detailed collection of the essence of Muslim laws. Aurangzeb had it composed with the help of many texts

questions.question_text: Ibn Battuta, the famous Muslim explorer who came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, was from which country?
questions.explanation: In 1333 AD, during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, African traveler Ibn Battuta came to India. Ibn Battuta was originally a resident of the African country Morocco. The Sultan appointed him the Qazi of Delhi. In 1342 AD, Ibn Battuta went to the court of the Chinese ruler Toghon Temür as the Sultan's ambassador. This traveler described the events of the time of Muhammad Tughlaq in his book 'Rehla'

questions.question_text: The Sharqi kingdom in Jaunpur was established by~
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq laid the foundation of Jaunpur city on the banks of the Gomti river in memory of his cousin Juna Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq). In 1394 AD, Nasiruddin Mahmud sent one of his slaves Malik Sarwar Khwaja Jahan to Jaunpur to administer with the title of 'Malik-us-Sharq' (Lord of the East). Taking advantage of the instability caused by Timur's invasion of Delhi, he laid the foundation of the 'Sharqi Dynasty' in Jaunpur. The area of this Sultanate was from Aligarh in Uttar Pradesh to Darbhanga in North Bihar and in the south to Bundelkhand from the border of non-North Nepal. Finally, the Lodi dynasty, the Sultans of Delhi, won Jaunpur and merged the Sharqi Sultanate into the Delhi Sultanate. The Jaunpur state is also called 'Shiraz of the East'

questions.question_text: In medieval India, for the first time, non-Muslims got entry into government jobs.

options.A: In the reign of Alauddin Khalji
options.B: In the reign of Jalal-ud-din Khalji
options.C: In the reign of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq
options.D: In the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq

questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sat on the throne of Delhi Sultanate in 1325 AD. He was the owner of an attractive yet controversial personality. He was proficient in subjects like logic, philosophy, astronomy, mathematics, etc., at the same time he was also religiously tolerant. Ibn Battuta, who came from Morocco, has described him in detail in 'Rehla'. According to him, the King used to work in the administration with high and impartial thinking. Therefore, to operate the administration in a better way, he gave space to capable Hindus and non-Muslims in government jobs. With this policy, he dealt a blow to the feeling of ethnic superiority of the Turks

questions.question_text: Which of the following Delhi Sultans started 'symbolic currency'?
questions.explanation: After the death of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq, Ulugh Khan (Juna Khan) ruled by the name of Muhammad Tughlaq. Two important sources of his reign are Tarikh-i-Firozshahi (Barani), Rehla (Ibn Battuta). He issued a copper coin instead of a silver coin and got it circulated as 'token currency' like a silver coin. This symbolic currency was circulated with the objective of maintaining a very large army because the Sultan had a plan to conquer other kingdoms continuously. At that time, due to the scarcity of gold and silver coins, such a coin was issued as 'token currency'. The circulation of this symbolic currency was done with the objective of maintaining a very large army because the Sultan had plans to conquer other kingdoms continuously. At that time, due to the scarcity of gold and silver coins, this type of coin was issued.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi made a failed attempt to implement prohibition?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji was the main ruler of the Khalji dynasty. With the accession of Alauddin, the 'imperialist era of the Sultanate' started. Alauddin made many reforms to provide strength to the maintenance and administration of his vast empire. He imposed a ban on the sale of liquor in his empire. He got his officials to announce prohibition among the public. The Sultan himself also stopped drinking liquor. However, the prohibition law implemented by him remained completely unsuccessful

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi faced the most Mongol invasions?
questions.explanation: In the Sultanate period, the most Mongol invasions (total 6) happened during the time of Alauddin Khalji. The first Mongol invasion of his time happened under the leadership of Qadir Khan (1296 AD)

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is matched?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta wrote Kitab-ul-Rehla which is matched. Minhaj wrote Tabaqat-e-Nasiri, Badauni wrote Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh and Inayat Khan wrote Shahjahan-nama

questions.question_text: Which ruler started the practice of giving loans (Sondhar) from the government treasury to farmers for the revival of agriculture?
questions.explanation: The practice of giving loans to farmers from the government treasury for the revival of agriculture was started by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Which was called Takkavi. For this, he established a new department Diwan-i-Amirkohi, prepared a famine relief code, and got hundreds of wells dug. Alauddin Khalji had done the work of market control system and Firoz Shah Tughlaq had done the work of construction of ponds and canals

questions.question_text: Which Sultan imposed a ban on drinking liquor, gambling, and eating bhang?
questions.explanation: After knowing the causes responsible for rebellions, Alauddin Khalji imposed a ban on the following things Confiscating the property of rich people, formation of a spy department, ban on social gatherings and matrimonial relations of nobles, and implementation of prohibition under which the use of substances like liquor and bhang and gambling were stopped. He was the first Sultan of Delhi to do this. Iltutmish had formed a group of 40 slave nobles i.e. Turkan-e-Chahalgani.

questions.question_text: Which of the following officers did Alauddin Khalji appoint to oversee price control measures? 1. Shahna-i-Mandi 2. Barid and Munhiyan 3. Sarai-i-Adl Select the correct answer from the following codes:
questions.explanation: Alauddin was the first Sultan of Delhi who implemented rationing and market control rules. In Shahna-i-Mandi, all farmers had to buy grain only from registered traders. The Shahna-i-Mandi had a list of prices of goods. Sarai-i-Adl was the second market established by him (built near Badaun Gate), which received government aid. Barid and Munhiyan were spy officers established during Alauddin's time

questions.question_text: Which new crop did the Sultanate period start bringing into use?
questions.explanation: Indigo is a crop started in the Sultanate period, the origin of betel is Malaya island. In the Vedas, there is a mention of the sanctity of the consumption of betel

questions.question_text: In 1221, Jalal-ud-din Mangabarni arrived on the north-western border of India and reached the Indus. Who was he?

options.A: Son of the Shah of Khwarizm

questions.explanation: Mongol leader Genghis Khan completely destroyed the entire empire of Persia (Iran) ruler Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Khwarizm Shah in 1221. Khwarizm Shah himself fled towards the Caspian Sea coast and his eldest son Jalal-ud-din Mangabarni fled towards the Indus. At that time, the Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate in India was Iltutmish

questions.question_text: Which Suhrawardi saint poet had the recommendation of Sikandar Lodi, who wrote a panegyric in praise of Babur and who was with Humayun during the Gujarat campaign?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Fazlullah Jamali or Jalal Khan belonged to the Suhrawardi order. Jamali was a friend of Sikandar Lodi. Babur respected Sheikh Jamali very much. He was with him in Humayun's Gujarat campaign, therefore his death also occurred in Gujarat Sheikh Gadai was his son whom Akbar appointed to the post of Sadr-us-Sudur during the Bairam Khan regency period.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Statement (A) : Turkan-e-Chahalgani was a group of 40 Turkish slave officers established by Iltutmish. Reason (R) : There was only one master of Shamsi slaves and one group. Each declared that 'I am and there is none other than me' and addressed one another that 'what are you that I am not and what are you doing that I am not doing'. Regarding the above, which of the following is correct? Code:

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) explains (A) correctly.
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The given statement and reason both are correct and the explanation is also. Iltutmish formed an organization of 40 slave nobles, which was called Turkan-e-Chahalgani, who were appointed to important posts in his state

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the reorganization of his army by Balban? 1. Balban increased the number of soldiers and their salaries and perks. 2. To keep his army alert, he emphasized the drill and practice of the army. 3. Balban kept his military campaigns secret and informed his Maliks about his military campaigns only one night before marching. Select the correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: The autocratic monarchy, the foundation of which was laid by Balban, for that he reorganized the army, along with an increase in the number of soldiers, he also increased the salaries. He first established the Ariz-i-Mumalik or Diwan-i-Arz department. The credit for the good organization of his army goes to Imad-ul-Mulk

questions.question_text: Into which class/classes did Firoz Shah Tughlaq divide his workshops? 1. Ratibi and non-Ratibi 2. Detraj and Kumas 3. Yawmiya-wa-Salana Select the correct answer from the following code:
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq divided his workshops into Ratibi and non-Ratibi classes. Under Ratibi, it received state patronage, and under non-Ratibi, it was based on private ownership. During the reign of Firoz, there were a total of 36 royal workshops

questions.question_text: Which Sultan weakened the power of the Muqtis in some areas by separating revenue collection and military tasks?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji weakened the power of the Muqtis in some areas by separating revenue collection and military tasks

questions.question_text: Who is considered the greatest among slave kings?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Qutbuddin Aibak established the Slave dynasty in India and the history of Muslim sovereignty in India starts from Iltutmish. V.A. Smith has written that ''Iltutmish was the greatest among the slave rulers.''

questions.question_text: Which history writer said that by giving loans to nobles in lieu of their Iqtas, traders and Sahus (moneylenders) became very rich?
questions.explanation: Shams Siraj Afif mentions in his book Tarikh-i-Firozshahi that traders and Sahus became rich by giving loans to nobles in lieu of their Iqtas

questions.question_text: Amir Khusro is generally given credit for which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusro discovered important instruments in the field of music, in which Sitar, Tabla, and Sangit are prominent

questions.question_text: Who were the Lodi Sultans of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Lodis were the first Afghans who ruled the Delhi Sultanate. They ended the power of the Turks and laid the foundation of Afghan rule. The second Afghan empire was established by Sher Shah Suri in 1540

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs is matched?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta wrote Kitab-ul-Rehla which is matched. Minhaj wrote Tabaqat-e-Nasiri, Badauni wrote Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh and Inayat Khan wrote Shahjahan-nama

questions.question_text: What were the tracts of land under royal control called in medieval times?
questions.explanation: Tracts of land under royal control in medieval times were called Khalisa. Zabti was a method of revenue collection. Madad-i-Maash was government grant, whereas Ijara system was contract system

questions.question_text: Where did Alauddin Khalji kill his uncle Jalal-ud-din Khalji?
questions.explanation: In 1296, Alauddin killed his uncle Jalal-ud-din in Kara Manikpur and became the Sultan of Delhi

questions.question_text: Where did Muhammad Tughlaq shift his capital?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Devagiri in 1327 which he named Daulatabad

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to Delhi Sultan Iltutmish: (1) He built Hauz-i-Khas (2) He built his capital in Siri Use the code given below to choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Hauz-i-Khas and the capital Siri were built by Alauddin Khalji. Iltutmish had shifted his capital from Lahore to Delhi

questions.question_text: Who was Muqaddam in Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: In the Delhi Sultanate, the 'village headman' was called Muqaddam. Small landowners were called Khut

questions.question_text: Who translated Patanjali's Yoga Sutra into Arabic language?
questions.explanation: In the 11th century, Al-Biruni translated Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra into Arabic language

questions.question_text: Who was the Sultan of Delhi at the time of Timur's invasion?
questions.explanation: During the reign of Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq (1394-1412), the Mongol commander Timur invaded India in 1398 AD. This invasion proved to be extremely lethal for both India and the Sultanate

questions.question_text: Assertion (a) : The most controversial decision taken by Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the so-called transfer of capital from Delhi to Devagiri. Reason (R) : This step was taken by the Sultan to punish the people of Delhi, as they had become his opponents. Regarding the two statements above, which of the following is correct?

options.D: (A) and (R) both are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.E: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq chose Devagiri, about 700 miles away from Delhi, with the objective of making it the capital. The main reason for this was Devagiri's location in the center of the empire. He renamed Devagiri to Daulatabad. He ordered the residents of Delhi to leave Delhi and go to Devagiri with the intention of punishing them (although this is not a universally accepted opinion). His shifting of the capital from Delhi, circulation of symbolic currency, and military campaign of Karachil are counted among the reasons for failure

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not of the Slave dynasty?
questions.explanation: In the Delhi Sultanate, the first rule was of the Slave dynasty. The founder of this dynasty is considered Qutbuddin Aibak. They made their capital in Lahore. After them, successively Iltutmish, Razia, and Balban ruled. Iltutmish is considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate. Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khalji ended the Slave dynasty and laid the foundation of the Khalji dynasty

questions.question_text: After conquering Jalore, Alauddin named Jalore:
questions.explanation: Delhi Sultan Alauddin Khalji's commander Kamal-ud-din Gurg captured Jalore in 1311 AD and changed the name of Jalore to Jalalabad. The last Chauhan dynasty ruler of Jalore Kanhaddev and his son Viramdev were killed

questions.question_text: Mongol Khan Tarmashirin invaded India during the reign of which of the following Tughlaq rulers?
questions.explanation: Tarmashirin invaded India in 1327-28 AD during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Muhammad Tughlaq sent him back by giving assistance of 5000 dinars. This was the only Mongol invasion during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Takkavi loans is not correct? (i) These were given to farmers for agricultural purposes. (ii) These were given to traders for commercial purposes. (iii) These were given through Chaudharis and Muqaddams, who distributed them to different farmers. (iv) Chaudhari and Muqaddam did not give guarantees for their repayment. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq established a new department Diwan-i-Amirkohi related to agriculture. Which provided Takkavi loans on behalf of the state. These were given for agricultural purposes which were distributed to farmers through Chaudharis and Muqaddams

questions.question_text: After the death of Alauddin Khalji, his price control system fell apart and during the reign of Qutbuddin Mubarak Khalji, prices increased rapidly. Which of the following historians/travelers mentions the increasing prices during the reign of Mubarak Khalji?
questions.explanation: After the death of Alauddin Khalji, his price control system fell apart and during the reign of Qutbuddin Mubarak Khalji, prices increased rapidly, which is mentioned by Sheikh Mubarak

questions.question_text: Many changes were made by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq in the agricultural system of Alauddin. In this context, which of the following is not correct?

options.A: He replaced Hukm-e-Masahat (measurement) with Hukm-e-Hasil (crop sharing) to reduce the burden of farmers.
options.B: Ghiyas-ud-din did not believe in Alauddin's theory of bringing village heads to the level of common farmers and restored their perks.
options.C: He provided exemption from tax assessment to farming and pasture.
options.D: He also continued the land revenue system and promoted it.

questions.explanation: Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq ruled Delhi as Sultan from 1320-1325 AD. The basis of his economic policies was Rasam-i-Miana i.e. balancing between restraint, harshness, and softness. He made many changes in Alauddin Khalji's agricultural system, namely (1) To reduce the burden of farmers, he replaced Hukm-e-Masahat (measurement) with Hukm-e-Hasil (crop sharing). (2) He did not believe in Alauddin's theory of bringing village heads to the level of common farmers and restored their perks. (3) He provided exemption from tax assessment to farming and pasture. Read the following paragraph and give answers to the given questions. Barani was a different type of historian, whose work written in 1357 about the history of Delhi Sultanate starts from that point where Minhaj-us-Siraj ended his account. Barani is different from his contemporaries, especially because he raises aspects of life like economic, social, intellectual and religious instead of genealogical and political. He is also unique in that he himself presents a distinct historical theory regarding events. This theory is based on the triangular relationship between autocratic monarchy, established aristocratic class, and the new class among the non-elite class.

questions.question_text: What are the elements of the triangular relationship described by Barani?

options.A: Autocratic monarchy, established aristocratic class, new class of non-elite classes.
options.B: Autocratic monarchy, new aristocratic class, aristocratic class moving ahead of non-elite classes.
options.C: Autocratic monarchy, established aristocratic class, individuals of elite classes.
options.D: Autocratic monarchy, new aristocratic class, groups of non-elite classes

questions.explanation: Ziauddin Barani was a historian and political thinker who lived in India during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Barani's famous work is Tarikh-i-Firozshahi. Barani raised aspects of life like economic, social, intellectual and religious instead of genealogical and political. The theory presented by him is considered based on the triangular relationship between autocratic monarchy, established aristocratic class and non-elite class, new class

questions.question_text: Tell the name of the book that starts about the history of Delhi Sultanate from the point where Minhaj-us-Siraj ended his book.
questions.explanation: Regarding Barani's famous work Tarikh-i-Firozshahi, it is said that this book starts about the history of Delhi Sultanate from the point where Minhaj-us-Siraj ended his book 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri'. Barani had presented his own distinct historical theory regarding the events of that time

questions.question_text: What is correct about Barani's writing style?

options.B: Barani is accurate in providing dates of political events.
options.C: Barani's description ends at the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
options.D: Barani believed in important analysis of socio-economic and intellectual history.

questions.explanation: Barani wanted to guide his contemporary upper class through his history and wanted to present an ideal before his contemporary rulers. He raised aspects of life like economic, social, intellectual and religious instead of genealogical and political. He described the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq

questions.question_text: The purpose of Barani writing Tarikh-i-Firozshahi was-

options.D: To shed light on the events of Iltutmish-Sikandar Lodi era

questions.explanation: Barani, while shedding light on the features of history through his book Tarikh-i-Firozshahi, also mentioned the duties of a historian. In this history, he wrote the history from the reign of Sultan Balban to the first six years of the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Through this only, by guiding the contemporary upper class through history, he wanted to keep an ideal before his contemporary Sultan Firoz Shah

questions.question_text: What is the title of Minhaj-us-Siraj's book?
questions.explanation: Minhaj-us-Siraj was the prominent historian of the Mamluk Sultanate of Delhi. He wrote the book named Tabaqat-i-Nasiri for the Sultan of Delhi, Nasiruddin Mahmud. In this book, Siraj told about his religious views, Islam and his historical perspective for Muslim rulers

questions.question_text: Which statements about Sultan Alauddin Khalji are correct?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji, the second ruler of the Khalji dynasty. His real name was Ali Gurshasp/Juna Khan Khalji. He was an imperialist ruler who expanded his empire aggressively up to Madurai in South India, he was the first Sultan of Delhi who, ignoring the Ulema class, established control of the state over religion. He banned intoxicating substances. He made arrangements for a permanent army to maintain his dominance. Soldiers were recruited on the basis of merit, not on the basis of lineage or caste. He was not in agreement with Ulema for running his state. To establish law and order in the empire, the Sultan paid special attention to the judicial system

questions.question_text: Which of the following features of the Gulbarga Jama Masjid are correct?
questions.explanation: During the time of Bahmani ruler Sultan Firoz Shah, the Jama Masjid of Gulbarga was built in the 14th century AD. Main features of this mosque 1. Indian and Iranian styles are integrated in such a way that they cannot be separated. 2. It is a rare example of an Indian mosque without a courtyard because the entire structure is covered by a roof. 3. The entire roof is covered with small domes arranged in seven rows. 4.
