There is very little decoration in this building but it is an example of intellectual greatness and originality

questions.question_text: In the classical Sanskrit language situated in Delhi, the long Palam inscription, naturally, it is claimed that due to the 'good governance' of the king, Lord Vishnu is 'leaving all worries and is resting peacefully in the Ocean of Milk (Ksheersagar).' This claim has been made about which king?
questions.explanation: Ghiyas-ud-din Balban was Iltutmish-Turk. Balban rose due to his merit and foresight and founded a new dynasty 'Balbani Dynasty'. Due to his merit, during the time of Razia Sultan, he was "Amir-i-Shikar", during the time of Alauddin Masud, 'Amir-i-Hajib', during the time of Muizuddin Bahram Shah, 'Amir-i-Akhur' and became the center of the entire state power. He crushed the "Forty group" created by Iltutmish and to establish Iranian ideals, started practices like "Sijda" and "Paibos" and started celebrating the Iranian festival "Nauroz". Seeing the firmness of his reign, Lord Vishnu left all worries and was resting peacefully in the Ocean of Milk (Ksheersagar), it was claimed so

questions.question_text: In the early 13th century, who among the following founded an autonomous state by combining Bihar and Bengal?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ghori's commander Bakhtiyar Khalji (Ghazi Ikhtiyar) took his campaign to Eastern India, Bengal-Bihar. At that time, the ruler of Sena dynasty of Bengal-Bihar region opposed him. Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bihar in 1202 AD, destroyed the Nalanda University established there, and after defeating Lakshman Sen, conquered the Bengal and Bihar regions and organized them as a province

questions.question_text: Identify the Sultan who refused to implement Shariat on the advice of the Qazi.
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji was the first Sultan of Delhi who, ignoring the Ulema class, established control of the state over religion and assumed the title of 'Yamin-ul-Khilafat, Nasir-Amir-ul-Muminin' (Naib of the Khalifa). His most important characteristic was that he never let politics be affected by religion

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans was known as Ali Gurshasp earlier?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji, the nephew and son-in-law of Jalal-ud-din Khalji, the founder of the Khalji dynasty. His childhood name was Ali Gurshasp. With his accession, the imperialist era of the Sultanate started. He assumed the title of "Sikandar-i-Sani" or "Sikandar Second Sani". He got this mentioned on his coins

questions.question_text: Who could issue a Farman?
questions.explanation: Farman was issued by kings ruling from ancient times to the public, soldiers, and other countries' kings. Everyone was bound to accept this Farman. Whoever refused to accept this Farman was made to suffer punishment by the King. This tradition was seen more in Delhi Sultanate and Mughal dynasty rulers

questions.question_text: Who built 'Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque'?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak, the first ruler of the Slave dynasty, built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque near Qutub Minar in Delhi in 1192 AD. Iltutmish added some more parts to it in 1230 AD and Firoz Shah Tughlaq also added some parts to its courtyard in 1351 AD

questions.question_text: Regarding Iltutmish, which of the following statement/statements is/are correct? I. Iltutmish obtained recognition of his authority by the Khalifa. II. Iltutmish defeated the Sultan of Bengal Ghiyas-ud-din and captured Lakhnauti. Select the correct answer with the help of the code given below~
questions.explanation: Iltutmish is considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate. He obtained recognition of the Sultan post not from any ruler of Ghor but from the Khalifa. In February 1229 AD, the representative of the Khalifa of Baghdad, Al-Mustansir, reached Delhi carrying the recognition letter In 1211 AD, Husamuddin Iwaz Khalji sat on the throne of Bengal assuming the title of Sultan Ghiyas-ud-din. In 1226 AD, Iltutmish's son Nasiruddin Mahmud defeated Ghiyas-ud-din in battle and captured his capital Lakhnauti. Thus both statement 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.question_text: Who was the Yadava ruler of Devagiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji's invasion?
questions.explanation: In 1296 AD, Alauddin invaded Devagiri, where the ruler Ramchandradeva was forced to promise to send the income of Ellichpur every year. In 1307 AD, Malik Kafur again invaded Devagiri. On Ramchandradeva's surrender, he was sent to Delhi where Alauddin gave him the title of 'Ray-i-Rayan' and after six months, gave him one lakh gold Tankas and the district of Navsari and sent him back to his state

questions.question_text: Which of the following monuments is the last example of the use of 'sloping wall' technique of Tughlaq-era?
questions.explanation: In Tughlaq's architecture, glimpses of contemporary political instability and economic problems are seen. Prominent tombs of Tughlaq era are the tomb of Ghiyas-ud-din (Tughlaqabad), Madrasas near Hauz Khas in buildings built by Firoz Shah, and the city and fort of Firoz Shah Kotla are famous. The important feature of Tughlaq-era architectural style is the sloping wall (Salam-i-method), of which the last example is the tomb of Isa Khan. Whereas Tughlaq-era 'Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani tomb' is the first octagonal tomb built in Delhi

questions.question_text: "Bread is available for one paisa (dangi), but who has the paisa?" In the above statement, Ziauddin Barani is referring to the state of whose reign?
questions.explanation: Ziauddin Barani mentioned Alauddin's market control system in 'Tarikh-e-Firozshahi'. Alauddin had made this system to keep a large army so that if the price remained low, a large army could be kept in the capital, at the same time he also controlled people's income to resolve the problem of rebellion, i.e., in market control prices were reduced but control over income affected people's purchasing power. In this context, Barani had said the above statement

questions.question_text: "In those days, entertainment was a common thing. On the days of pilgrimages or the last Wednesday of the month of travel, it was difficult to find a place (to sit) near the galleries, public gardens, or ponds. There was an atmosphere of music and dance all around. One Tanka or more was spent on these feasts." Sheikh Nasiruddin Chiragh was talking about the reign of whom?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Nasiruddin Chiragh had said the above sentence in the context of the early years of Alauddin's reign, through which the luxurious life of that time can be portrayed. Strict measures were taken by Alauddin to end this

questions.question_text: When this Sultan changed his clothes and bedding, they were sold and the money obtained from it was given to orphan girls as dowry. Identify this Lodi Sultan~
questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi was the best ruler of the Lodi dynasty. He started the auditing system of the state's accounts during his reign. He laid the foundation of Agra city. He abolished food grain taxes and removed restrictions on trade, which gave a boost to people's economic prosperity. He introduced an authentic measurement "Gaj-i-Sikandari" for land which was 30 inches. He provided dowry from the money obtained by selling his clothes for poor and orphan girls and also made arrangements for free food for the poor

questions.question_text: For whom has the epithet 'Tuti-e-Hind' been used?
questions.explanation: Famous poet Amir Khusro whose epithet was Tuti-e-Hind (Parrot of India). Amir Hasan and Amir Khusro had started their literary life during the time of Prince Muhammad. Amir Khusro was the first poet of India who used Khari Boli in his poetry. His famous works were - Khazain-ul-Futuh Ashiqa, Nuh Sipihr and Tughlaqnama etc

questions.question_text: Who appointed Ibn Battuta as the Qazi of Delhi and ambassador to China?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta was an African traveler who came to India in 1333 AD during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed him the Qazi of Delhi. In 1342 AD, Ibn Battuta went to the court of Chinese ruler Toghon Temur as the Sultan's ambassador. He wrote his travelogue by the name of 'Rehla'

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, 'Diwan-i-Waqf' department was related to
questions.explanation: The founder of the Khalji dynasty was Jalal-ud-din Khalji. He created an expenditure department which was called Diwan-i-Waqf. Whose work was to look after expenditure papers and keep those papers safe, which were related to land

questions.question_text: According to Ibn Battuta, who got gold coins named Dinar circulated?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta came to India from North Africa (Morocco) in 1333 AD, at that time it was the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in India. According to Ibn Battuta, the circulation of gold coins named Dinar was done by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Ibn Battuta's book's name is Rehla. Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta the Qazi of Delhi. In gold coins, he increased the quantity of gold from 175 grains to 200 grains

questions.question_text: Who got the fortified city Tughlaqabad built?
questions.explanation: The foundation of the Tughlaq dynasty was laid by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq (Ghazi Malik) in 1320 AD. Tughlaqabad, which was a fortified city, was built by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq

questions.question_text: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi to introduce non-Islamic practices in the court?
questions.explanation: The ruler of the Slave dynasty to rule on Iranian traditions was Balban. Balban introduced non-Islamic practices in his empire. He implemented Sijda and Paibos which was kissing the feet of the king in court and adopted the policy of blood and iron

questions.question_text: Which of the following taxes was levied by the Sultans of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Five types of taxes were taken in the Sultanate period (1) Ushr- Land tax taken from Muslims 5% to 10% (2) Kharaj- Land tax on non-Muslims 1/3 to 1/2 (3) Khums- Wealth received from looted treasures or buried treasures on which the state had the right to 1/5th part. The remaining 4/5th was distributed among the soldiers. (4) Jizya tax- Religious tax taken from non-Muslims (5) Zakat - Religious tax levied on Muslims

questions.question_text: Which metal was used in his symbolic currency by Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: While experimenting with symbolic currency, Muhammad bin Tughlaq circulated copper coins of less weight, which could not become popular. This coin was also called Adli. His silver coin of less weight was called Kani. There are different opinions of scholars on copper coins 1- Barani called it copper. 2- Ferishta called it brass/bronze. The commission removed this question from the question paper.

questions.question_text: 'Market Control' is related to which Delhi Sultan?
questions.explanation: The most powerful ruler of the Khalji dynasty was Alauddin Khalji. He did many works for the welfare of his subjects in which market control was in the first place. Market control meant that the price of goods should always remain fixed at a certain price. Probably, this market control policy was effective only in the areas around Delhi. Which was in the interest of keeping a large army

questions.question_text: In which year did Timur invade India?
questions.explanation: During the reign of Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq, a great Mongol commander Timur of Central Asia invaded India in 1398 AD. Timur's invasion proved to be a fatal blow for both the Tughlaq dynasty and Delhi. After some time of Timur's invasion, the Tughlaq dynasty ended. On the death of Nasiruddin Mahmud, people used to say sarcastically that ''The empire of the Emperor of the world extended from Delhi to Palam.''

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not connected to Turkan-e-Chahalgani?
questions.explanation: Baharuddin Tughril, Qutlugh Khan, and Balban were members of Turkan-e-Chahalgani, whereas Imad-ud-din Raihan became 'Naib' of Nasiruddin Mahmud for one year in 1253 AD, later he was removed and Balban was given the post of Naib again and finally Balban captured the Delhi Sultanate with his diplomacy

questions.question_text: Which Mongol commander defeated Alauddin Khalji?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2012) TGT History, 2013 Explanation– Targhi (Mongol commander) defeated Alauddin Khalji. Later, Alauddin Khalji defeated the Mongols and expanded his empire over almost the entire India. It is known that the credit for Alauddin Khalji's victory of South India goes to Malik Kafur. PGT 2016

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): Balban's theory of kingship was based on the policy of 'Blood and Iron'. Reason (R): The prestige of the crown had declined under Iltutmish's successors. Answer the following question from the codes given below:

options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.C: (A) is correct, but (R) is incorrect, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options.D: (A) is correct and (R) is incorrect, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Balban's theory of kingship was based on the policy of 'Blood and Iron'. It is known that the prestige of the crown had declined under Iltutmish and his successors, which Balban took to the peak. Balban had made strict provisions for punishment during his reign.

questions.question_text: Who separated the posts of Wali and Amir?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) TGT History, 2013 Explanation – To make the Amirs and officers loyal and to improve administration, Muhammad bin Tughlaq dismissed those old officers and employees who were suspected of spreading disturbances or participating directly or indirectly in any rebellion. Ending the distinction of race and class, Muhammad bin Tughlaq adopted the policy of appointing officers on the basis of merit.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II (Rulers of Delhi Sultanate) (Work or Event)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2013) Explanation – Jalaluddin Khalji - Murder of Sidi Maula Alauddin Khalji - Conquest of Malwa and Gujarat Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq - Bengal conquest Firoz Shah Tughlaq - Establishment of Public Works Department

questions.question_text: The names of the three successors of Khizr Khan, the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty, are as follows: (i) Mubarak Shah (ii) Alauddin Alam Shah (iii) Muhammad Shah Which of the following sequences is in the correct chronological order?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2013) Explanation – The founder of the Sayyid Dynasty was Khizr Khan. - Khizr Khan – 1414-21 AD. - Mubarak Shah - 1421-34 AD. - Muhammad Shah - 1434-43 AD. - Alauddin Alam Shah – 1443–51 AD.

questions.question_text: How many Sultans ruled from 1236 to 1296?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2013) Explanation – During the Sultanate period, 10 Sultans ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1296. It is noteworthy that after the death of Iltutmish in 1236 AD, Rukn-ud-din Firoz, Shah Turkan are not counted in the category of rulers; Razia, Bahram Shah, Alauddin Masud Shah, Nasir-ud-din Mahmud, Balban, Kaiqubad, Jalaluddin, and Alauddin (1296) were the rulers. Note – Rukn-ud-din Firoz had handed over the administrative work to Shah Turkan.

questions.question_text: In which book is a detailed account of Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canal project found?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) (GIC Lec. Exam 2018) Explanation – Detailed information about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canal project is found in Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi. Firoz Shah had laid a network of canals. Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi has mentioned five canals of the Firoz era. Yamuna to Hisar (Ulughkhani canal), Satluj to Ghaggar, Sirmur to Hansi, Ghaggar to Firozabad, Yamuna to Firozabad. Apart from this, Afif has mentioned two canals built by Firoz Shah in Tarikh-i-Firozshahi.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the reforms of Alauddin Khalji: (i) Confiscating all revenue-free land given in jagirs. (ii) Implementing 'Dagh' (branding) and 'Chehra' (descriptive roll) in his army. (iii) Abolishing the 'Iqta' of big Amirs and commanders. (iv) Banning the public sale of liquor. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – Alauddin first took back all land grants which were given by the state in the form of gifts, grants or rewards to the Amir class, government employees, scholars and theologians. Alauddin issued orders related to village headmen, zamindars, and common farmers, taking away the special rights of Khut-Muqaddam. He implemented 'Dagh' (branding) and 'Chehra' (descriptive roll) in his army. He put a ban on the public sale of liquor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements related to the founding of the Tughlaq Dynasty by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq is not correct?

options.A: At the time of accession, the authority of Ghiyas-ud-din was accepted by consensus.
options.B: Ghiyas-ud-din had a large number of loyal soldiers who supported him.
options.C: For the stability of the Sultanate, the people of Delhi gave huge contributions.
options.D: The treasury of the Sultanate that he received as inheritance was very strong.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq laid the foundation of the Tughlaq Dynasty in 1320 AD. Ghiyas-ud-din had a large number of loyal soldiers who fully supported him, and he also received considerable encouragement from the people of Delhi. At this time, Alauddin Khalji's revenue system had collapsed, due to which even the collection of tax had become difficult. Therefore, the treasury Ghiyas-ud-din received in inheritance was actually empty.

questions.question_text: There are two statements below, the first is called Assertion (A) and the second is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): During the Sultanate period of Delhi, the behavior of government officials was guided by Sharia. Reason (R): The state's goal was not to convert the entire country from Dar-ul-Harb to Dar-ul-Islam. Select the correct answer from the given code: Code:

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct, and (A) is the correct explanation of (R).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (A) is not the correct explanation of (R).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – In the Delhi Sultanate, the behavior of government officials is based on Islamic law, Quran, Sharia, and Hadith. The king's goal was not to convert Dar-ul-Harb to Dar-ul-Islam.

questions.question_text: Shiqqdar was –

options.B: Military officer at the Pargana level

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – During the Sultanate period, Shiqqdar was the chief officer of the Pargana. His main task was to establish peace and order in the Pargana and to help the Amin in collecting revenue.

questions.question_text: The Ilbari ruler who started Sijda, Paibos, and Nauroz in the Delhi Sultanate was –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation – In the Delhi Sultanate, Balban made rules for the court and implemented them strictly. He introduced the traditions of Sijda (prostrating on the ground to greet) and Paibos (kissing the Sultan's feet by coming near the throne). Apart from this, the Iranian festival 'Nauroz' began to be celebrated with great pomp in his court. Foreigners were stunned to see the grandeur of his court.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Bahlul Lodi is not correct?

options.A: He completely destroyed the power of the Sharqi Sultans of Jaunpur.
options.B: During his long reign of thirty-eight years, he made many experiments in the field of civil administration.
options.C: He maintained the administrative institutions of the Delhi Sultanate received as inheritance from the Sayyid Sultans.
options.D: The circulation of Bahluli coins is considered an important innovation in the monetary history of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Bahlul Lodi was related to the important branch of Afghans, Shahkhel. He established the first Afghan empire in 1451 AD. Bahlul Lodi achieved major success in 1484 AD by conquering the Jaunpur state into the Delhi Sultanate. He started Bahluli coins, which remained the main medium of exchange in Northern India before and after Akbar.

questions.question_text: There are two statements given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R): Assertion (A): Under the successors of Alauddin Khalji, the policy of expansion and centralization continued. Reason (R): Bengal was re-conquered in 1324 and direct control was achieved up to almost the southernmost point of the Indian peninsula during the time of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq and Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the above two statements? Code:

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – The policy of expansion by Alauddin Khalji was continued by his successors like Ghiyas-ud-din, Muhammad bin Tughlaq, etc., and Ghiyas-ud-din also attacked Bengal and brought it under his rule. And Muhammad Tughlaq, after winning the southern states, made Deogiri his capital in 1327 AD.

questions.question_text: Mark the following correct chronological order of the Sayyid Sultans on the throne of Delhi:

options.A: Khizr Khan – Muhammad Shah – Mubarak Shah – Alauddin Shah
options.B: Khizr Khan – Mubarak Shah – Muhammad Shah – Alauddin Shah
options.C: Mubarak Shah – Khizr Khan – Alauddin Shah – Muhammad Shah
options.D: Alauddin Shah – Muhammad Shah – Khizr Khan – Mubarak Shah

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Khizr Khan established the Sayyid Dynasty in 1414 AD. He assumed the title of Rayat-i-Ala. Mubarak Shah ruled from 1421-1434 AD. After Mubarak Shah, his adopted son Muhammad Shah (1434-1443 AD) sat on the throne. Alauddin Alam Shah ruled from 1443 AD to 1451 AD. This was the last ruler of the Sayyid Dynasty.

questions.question_text: Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq probably had 1,80,000 slaves; how many of them worked as artisans?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – A total of 1,80,000 slaves were collected during the time of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Some of them were trained for religious studies, while 12,000 were trained as artisans or craftsmen and sent to various Parganas. According to Afif, Diwan-i-Bandagan was established to look after them.

questions.question_text: "People were happy and satisfied during his reign, so young and old, slave and free, all wore black clothes and mourned his death." Ferishta writes this in his Tarikh-i-Ferishta regarding which Sayyid Sultan?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – After Tamerlane returned, his representative Khizr Khan established the Sayyid Dynasty in 1414 AD. He was a generous ruler. Ferishta has written in his book Tarikh-i-Ferishta regarding Khizr Khan: "People were happy and satisfied during his reign. So young and old, slave and free, all wore black clothes and mourned his death."

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following Slave Sultans of Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – Alauddin Masud Shah – Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – Nasir-ud-din Mahmud
options.B: Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – Nasir-ud-din Mahmud – Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – Alauddin Masud Shah
options.C: Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – Alauddin Masud Shah – Nasir-ud-din Mahmud
options.D: Alauddin Masud Shah – Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – Nasir-ud-din Mahmud

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) (c) Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – Alauddin Masud Shah – Nasir-ud-din Mahmud (d) Alauddin Masud Shah – Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – Nasir-ud-din Mahmud Answer – (c) (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – The correct chronological order of the Slave Sultans of Delhi Sultanate is as follows– Rukn-ud-din Firoz Shah – 1236–1236 Razia Sultan – 1236–1240 Muiz-ud-din Bahram Shah – 1240–1242 Alauddin Masud Shah – 1242–1246 Nasir-ud-din Mahmud – 1246-1265

questions.question_text: What was the head of the intelligence department called in the administration of Alauddin Khalji?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Alauddin Khalji was the most capable Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate and ruled over the largest land area. He made many reforms in his administration, in which Barid-Mumalik was also a major reform. The main task of Barid-i-Mumalik was to lead the intelligence department and convey information to the ruler.

questions.question_text: In an inscription of the Sun temple built in Gaya during the Sultanate period, the name of a Sultan has appeared twice. Who was this Sultan?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2015) Explanation – The name of Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq appears twice in an inscription of the Sun temple built in Gaya (Bihar). He had destroyed this Hindu temple. Apart from this, there is a description of Firoz destroying many Hindu temples, breaking Hindu fairs, converting Hindus to Muslims or killing them.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct?

options.A: Fakhr-i Mudabbir dedicated his book on warfare to Iltutmish.
options.B: Isami does not agree with Minhaj-us-Siraj's statement that people from different parts of the world lined up towards the newly established city of Delhi.
options.C: Minhaj says that "Razia had all the commendable qualities and necessary abilities to become a ruler."
options.D: The appointment of non-Turks to important posts by Razia annoyed the Turkish Amirs, due to which they planned to depose Razia.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2015) Explanation – According to Minhaj-us-Siraj, Razia had all those administrative qualities that a Sultan should have. Appointing foreign and Turkish Muslims to various government posts was Razia's plan, through which she wanted to break the power of the Turkish slave chiefs. This the Turkish slave chiefs could not tolerate. Fakhr-i Mudabbir was in the reign of Iltutmish.

questions.question_text: What is Madan-i-Shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi related to?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2015) Explanation – During the time of Lodi ruler Sikandar Lodi, the book Madan-i-Shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi related to Ayurveda was composed. Apart from this, by the order of Sikandar Lodi, an Ayurvedic book was translated into Persian, which was named Farhang-i-Sikandari.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Alauddin Khalji?

options.A: He was associated with almost every incident happening in public markets and the houses of Amirs.
options.B: According to Barani, the Sultan issued an order that people would not go to each other's houses, and inter-marriages would not take place between them until formal permission was obtained from the Sultan for this.
options.D: The account of Padmini has been mentioned in all contemporary sources.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2015) Explanation – Understanding the causes of rebellions, Alauddin Khalji issued four ordinances. Through the second ordinance, a good intelligence department was formed. Barid (intelligence officer) and Munhi (spy) who were appointed to the houses of Amirs, offices, provincial capitals, and markets used to give information about every important incident to the Sultan. Alauddin stopped the use of intoxicating substances like alcohol and bhang; the Sultan himself had stopped drinking alcohol. The main reason for Alauddin's market system was not to reduce the salary of soldiers but to stop the rise in the prices of goods. The mention of Queen Padmini, the main basis of Malik Muhammad Jayasi's story, is the poetic work Padmavat written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi in 1540 AD. Padmini was the very beautiful wife of Rana Ratan Singh.

questions.question_text: Barani has described about a Sultan of Delhi that when he sat on the throne, "Hindus and Muslims felt relief," and he also wrote that by the year 1357, Khuts and Muqaddams became Amirs and they had countless horses and cattle. Who was that Sultan?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2015) Explanation – Barani has described in Tarikh-i-Firozshahi that when Sultan Firoz Shah sat on the throne, Hindus and Muslims felt relief and he wrote that by the year 1357, Khuts and Muqaddams became Amirs and they had countless horses and cattle.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Tamerlane's invasion is not correct?

options.A: Tamerlane's skilled craftsmen built a bridge of boats on the Indus river, which was crossed on September 21, 1398.
options.B: Talmi city, which was at a distance of thirty koss from Multan, where both Hindus and Muslims opposed Tamerlane.
options.C: The Muqaddams and Rais of the Salt Range (Koh-i-Judi) helped Tamerlane cross his area and obtained his favor.
options.D: Sharaf-ud-din Ali Yazdi has argued to justify Tamerlane's invasion of India that although the central power of Delhi was in the hands of Muslims, it was weak.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Talmi city, which was situated at a distance of thirty koss from Multan. There, both Hindus and Muslims opposed Tamerlane, only this statement in the above options is incorrect. While other options are correct.

questions.question_text: There are two statements below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) – Assertion (A): By building forts and punishing the tribes, Tamerlane wanted to ensure that his movement from the Afghan borders to Kabul remained safe. Reason (R): The destruction and massacre of two Afghan tribes named Purniyan or Khalatiyan by Tamerlane's cruel and aggressive methods had created an atmosphere of fear and terror for the security of those routes. Which of the following is correct regarding these two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) explains (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) does not explain (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – By building forts and punishing the tribes, Tamerlane wanted to ensure that his movement from the Afghan borders to Kabul remained safe because the destruction and massacre of two Afghan tribes named Purniyan and Khalatiyan by Tamerlane's cruel and aggressive methods had created an atmosphere of fear and terror for the security of those routes. Therefore, it is clear that the reason confirms the statement.

questions.question_text: 'Khizr Khan and Malika-i-Jahan remained busy throwing feasts and celebrating, and were not paying any attention to the Sultan's treatment and nursing. The Sultan felt that the reason for his illness was the neglect done by them and his heart broke. He separated himself from them completely.' Regarding which Sultan is this statement and what is its source? Source Name of Sultan
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – "Khizr Khan and Malika-i-Jahan remained busy throwing feasts and celebrating, and were not paying any attention to the Sultan's treatment and nursing. The Sultan felt that the reason for his illness was the neglect done by them and his heart broke. He separated himself from them completely." This statement is about Alauddin Khalji. Its source is Tarikh-i-Ferishta.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – The correct matched order of the code is: Manager – Bar-bak Chief In-charge of the Royal Palace – Wakil-i-Dar Chief of Bodyguards – Sar-i-Jandar Porter/Carrier – Kewani

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: With the establishment of the Sultanate, the old system or systems did not end immediately, but they remained, although the dominance of a new ruling class was established over them.
options.C: Alauddin's system of determination and collection of land revenue was quite similar to the system which was later called Kankut.
options.D: Two historians, Barani and Yahiya, give information about various methods of measuring increase in agricultural tax of Muhammad Tughlaq. Yahiya says that a new additional tax (Abwab) was imposed on farmers and Barani says that three big taxes were determined with more seriousness and were collected strictly.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – In the given options, options (a), (b) and (c) are correct, while option (d), that "two historians, Barani and Yahiya, give information about various methods of measuring increase in agricultural tax of Muhammad Tughlaq. Yahiya says that a new additional tax (Abwab) was imposed on farmers and according to Barani, three big taxes were determined with more seriousness and were collected strictly," this statement is not correct.

questions.question_text: Read the following excerpt: "I made an in-depth inspection of the buildings of Man Singh and Vikramjit, they are wonderful, made by carving heavy asymmetrical blocks of stones completely. Among the buildings of all kings, Man Singh's building is the most lofty and excellent." After seeing the royal palace of Gwalior, who expressed these thoughts?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – "I made an in-depth inspection of the buildings of Man Singh and Vikramjit, they are wonderful, made by carving heavy asymmetrical blocks of stones completely. Among the buildings of all kings, Man Singh's building is the most lofty and excellent." After seeing the royal palace of Gwalior, these thoughts were expressed by Babur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July, 2018 Explanation : Sultan Iltutmish used to express deep respect for Sufi saints like- Sheikh Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki, Qazi Hamid-ud-din Nagauri, Sheikh Baha-ud-din Zakariya, etc. While nominating his daughter Razia as his successor, Iltutmish did not care to know the opinion of the Ulemas. Razia became the first female ruler. Due to leading a holy private life, Iltutmish had acquired the friendship of Sufis, which he took full advantage of.

questions.question_text: 'The Sultan internalized the Persian royal tradition and molded them according to the Indian environment. Books like Adab-us-Salatin and Ma'asir-us-Salatin, which he had ordered from Baghdad for the education of his sons, were related to the theories of Iranian kingship, which he was longing to emulate completely in Delhi.' Identify the Sultan.
questions.explanation: The Sultan internalized the Persian royal tradition and molded them according to the Indian environment. Books like Adab-us-Salatin and Ma'asir-us-Salatin, which he had ordered from Baghdad for the education of his sons, were related to the theories of Iranian kingship, which he was longing to emulate completely in Delhi." This statement is about Iltutmish

questions.question_text: 'In fact, he made Delhi not only the political and administrative center of the Turkish empire in India, but also made it the center of his cultural activities. It is noteworthy that Delhi was never referred to by its name in the literature of the Sultanate period. It was called 'Hazrat-i-Delhi' (Majestic Delhi) or 'Shahr' (The City).' Who is this Sultan?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – The real Sultan of Delhi Sultanate was Iltutmish, who did not receive the acceptance of the post of Sultan from any ruler of Ghur but from the Caliph. Iltutmish was an Ilbari tribal Turk. He made Delhi the capital instead of Lahore. In contemporary literature, it was called Hazrat-i-Delhi (Majestic Delhi) or Shahr (The City). On February 12, 1229, envoys of the Abbasid Caliph Al-Mustansir Billah came from Baghdad to provide the power of Islamic emperor to Iltutmish and gave the Sultan the investiture letter.

questions.question_text: On the issue of successful maintenance of spies, which Sultan advised his son: 'The reporters and spies should not be allowed to loiter around the court, their closeness to the ruler creates fear among the obedient and trusted friends and destroys their trust in the king—which is the basis of good governance—'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – 'The reporters and spies should not be allowed to loiter around the court, their closeness to the ruler creates fear among the obedient and trusted friends and destroys their trust in the king—which is the basis of good governance—', Balban had advised his son on the issue of successful maintenance of spies.

questions.question_text: When Kamal Mahiyar, who accepted Islam, was chosen for the post of Mustashrif of Amroha and when he was presented before the Sultan, the Sultan's reaction was: 'When I see a person born in a low class, every artery and vein in my body starts tensing with anger.' Identify the Sultan:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – When Kamal Mahiyar, who accepted Islam, was chosen for the post of Mustashrif of Amroha and when he was presented before the Sultan, the Sultan's reaction was: 'When I see a person born in a low class, every artery and vein in my body starts tensing with anger.' The above statement is related to Balban.

questions.question_text: Regarding the relations of Ulugh Khan (Balban) with the Afghans, consider the following statements: (i) Ulugh Khan had recruited about 3000 Afghans in his army. (ii) When Ulugh Khan became Sultan, he built his new military outposts near Delhi in Patiali, Kampil and Bhojpur and kept them under the control of Afghans. (iii) Sultan Balban appointed the Afghan Amir Ikhtiyar-ud-din as his Vazir. (iv) Sultan Balban appointed many Afghans as his governors. Select the correct answer with the help of the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – Ghiyas-ud-din Balban (1265-1287 AD) had recruited Afghans into his army. He recruited about 3000 Afghans into his army. When he became Sultan by the name of 'Ulugh Khan', he built his new military outposts near Delhi in Patiali, Kampil, and Bhojpur and kept them under the control of Afghans. Therefore, statement (i) and (ii) are correct. Balban was the first Sultan of Delhi who expressed his views regarding the post, authority and kingship of the Sultan. Balban appointed Khwaja Hasan Basri as Vazir. He did not appoint Afghans as his governors. Therefore, (iii) and (iv) are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a regulation (Zawabit) of Alauddin Khalji's grain price control policy?

options.A: Fixing the prices of grain by the Sultan.
options.B: Storing revenue grain in many warehouses.
options.C: Not to sell grain without the prior permission of the Shahna.
options.D: In times of drought, in order to maintain the cheap price of grain, no person should be allowed to buy even the minimum grain without proving necessity.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – Information about Alauddin's market control is found in Khazain-ul-Futuh (Amir Khusrau), Futuh-us-Salatin (Isami) along with Tarikh-i-Firozshahi (Barani) and Rihla (Ibn Battuta) – The following rules were made by Alauddin for price control of grain: – Grain prices were fixed by the government. – A market inspector (Shahna) was appointed. – Collecting grain in government warehouses. – Traders transporting grain were under the authority of Shahna. – Strict punishment for profiteering.

questions.question_text: The Sultan ordered, "Whatever they produce... its measurement should be done according to the yield produced per biswa, and everyone should be made to deposit half of it without any discrimination." In the above statement, which Sultan made the measurement of land the basis of estimation of crop?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – Sultan Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316 AD) ordered, "Whatever they produce... its measurement should be done according to the yield produced per biswa, and everyone should be made to deposit half of it without any discrimination." Thus, Alauddin was the first ruler who started collecting revenue after measuring the land. For this, 'Biswa' was considered a unit. Under this scientific method of measurement, revenue was collected at a uniform rate of 50% on all land.

questions.question_text: Identify the place among the following where Sultan Alauddin Khalji declared himself Sultan or seated himself on the throne:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – In 1296 AD, Alauddin (1296-1316 AD) attacked Deogiri and brought the enormous wealth looted from there. He called Jalaluddin to Manikpur and killed him treacherously. In this task, he received a lot of help from his brother Almas Beg because he had a major role in betraying the Sultan. Alauddin declared himself Sultan at Kara-Manikpur and gave prestigious posts to his supporters.

questions.question_text: There are two statements given below, one is called Assertion and the other is called Reason: Assertion (A): Barani writes, "Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq used to say that I hate people born of low origin more than idols, yet I have seen (Barani) him giving such promotion to Najiba, the son of a musician born of low origin, that he reached higher positions than many maliks. Gujarat, Multan, and Badaun were given under his control.........it is surprising how he gave administration of high posts, vast land areas and big provinces to a person born of low origin." Reason (R): The Sultan believed that appointments to posts should be on the basis of merit. He ended whatever views were prevalent regarding birth in administration and appointed people born of low origin to high posts in the administration. Regarding the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC NET-II Paper July, 2018) (b) (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (c) (A) is correct, but (R) is incorrect. (d) (A) is incorrect, but (R) is correct. Answer – (a) UGC NET-II Paper July, 2018 Explanation : Barani writes, "Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq used to say that I hate people born of low origin more than idols, yet I have seen (Barani) him giving such promotion to Najiba, the son of a musician born of low origin, that he reached higher positions than many maliks. Gujarat, Multan, and Badaun were given under his control- it is surprising how he gave administration of high posts, vast land areas and big provinces to a person born of low origin." Therefore, Assertion and Reason both statements are correct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans ordered that Muslim women would not go out of their homes or visit tombs outside the city of Delhi? Select the correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was a king of the Tughlaq Dynasty who imposed restrictions on Muslim women going out of their homes and Muslim women were not free to visit tombs outside the city of Delhi. Whereas Sikandar Lodi, the second ruler of the Lodi Dynasty, had also kept similar conditions in front of Muslim women

questions.question_text: 'It is their custom that whoever is given this ('paan' platter), he takes the platter in his hand and keeps it on his shoulder and after that, he greets (Kornish) by touching the ground with his other hand.' While mentioning the feasts for his Amirs and foreign guests by Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq, who among the following wrote the above description?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation – Ibn Battuta wrote the above description while mentioning the feasts for his Amirs and foreign guests by Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq (1325-1351 AD). Ibn Battuta was a resident of Africa and came to India in 1333 AD as a traveler. Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq appointed him to the post of Qazi of Delhi in 1334 AD. Muhammad Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta his ambassador and sent him to China in 1342, on which post he worked for ten years. Ibn Battuta wrote a detailed account of the conditions of Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq's reign in his book 'Rihla'.

questions.question_text: "I am nothing else." "What are you that I am not, and what were you not that I was not?" The above statement was expressed by which group/Sultan?
questions.explanation: Turkan-i-Chahalgani - Iltutmish formed a group of his slave chiefs. In later times, this group worked to enthrone/dethrone the successors of Iltutmish at their own will. Balban suppressed this group during his reign. It is noteworthy that Balban himself was a member of that group

questions.question_text: Zill-i-Illahi, which is a concept related to royal authority, is related to –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Qutb-ud-din Aibak is considered the first ruler of the Sultanate in India, but Balban was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who expressed his views regarding the post, authority, and kingship of the Sultan. The most prominent feature of Balban's theory of kingship is that he considers the Sultan as the representative of God on earth 'Niyabat-i-Khudai' and from the point of view of prestige, he accepts him after the Prophet. He considers the Sultan as the reflection of God (Zill-i-Illahi) and his heart as a repository of divine inspiration and grace.

questions.question_text: Which was the first state against which Alauddin Khalji started the attack?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – In 1292 AD, Alauddin Khalji looted Bhilsa by the order of Sultan Jalaluddin Khalji of Delhi, as a result of which Alauddin Khalji was given the governorship of Awadh. In 1296, Alauddin Khalji looted Deogiri and killed his uncle Jalaluddin Khalji and became the Sultan of Delhi. Alauddin's first military campaign was against the ruler of Gujarat, Baghela Rajput Raykaran-II in 1298. According to the question, its answer will be Ranthambore, which Alauddin annexed to the Delhi Sultanate in 1301 AD.

questions.question_text: Who used the term 'Hind and Sindh' for the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 TGT History, 2013 Explanation – The real name of Ibn Battuta was Muhammad bin Abdullah Ibn Battuta. He was a resident of Africa. Traveling through various cities of Western Asia, he entered Sindh in 1333 AD and lived in India for about 14 years. Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed him the Qazi of Delhi. After returning to his country Morocco, Ibn Battuta wrote his travelogue named 'Rihla' and he referred to Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign territory as 'Hind' and 'Sindh'. Explanation – Ibn Battuta's real name was Muhammad bin Abdullah Ibn Battuta. He was a resident of Africa. Traveling through various cities of Western Asia, he entered Sindh in 1333 AD and lived in India for about 14 years. Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed him the Qazi of Delhi. After returning to his country Morocco, Ibn Battuta wrote his travelogue named 'Rihla' and he referred to Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign territory as 'Hind' and 'Sindh'.

questions.question_text: Whose tomb was Sultan-Ghari?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – During the Delhi Sultanate era, architecture developed mainly among various fine arts. The beginning of Qutub Minar happened during the time of Qutb-ud-din Aibak and its full construction happened during the time of Iltutmish. Iltutmish built the tomb of his eldest son Nasir-ud-din Muhammad, 'Sultan-Ghari', in Malikpur village, 30 miles away from Qutub Minar. Its construction was done in 1231-32 AD. This was the first tomb built by Turk Sultans in India. The literal meaning of 'Sultan-Ghari' is 'Sultan of the cave'. It is India's first Islamic tomb.

questions.question_text: On whom was the 'Sharb' tax imposed?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Firoz Tughlaq issued immediate orders to maintain stability and order as soon as he sat on the throne. He tried to win the trust of people of all communities. Firoz tried to increase his income through 'Haq-i-Sharb' or irrigation tax and income from orchards on land irrigated through canals (irrigation tax rate was 1/10th of the produce) with the help of agriculture and promotion of high-quality crops. Firoz built 5 big canals.

questions.question_text: Which Delhi Sultan talked to Hindu Yogis and Muslim Fakirs?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Among the Sultans of Delhi Sultanate, Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the person with the most unique personality. Muhammad Tughlaq was not orthodox religiously. He used to participate in both Holi and Muharram. He welcomed Jain scholars Jinaprabha Suri and Rajshekhar in his court and appointed the famous Sufi Sheikh Shihab-ud-din of Delhi in his court.

questions.question_text: Which ruler gave the thought that the state cannot actually be an Islamic state?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Jalaluddin Khalji was the first Turk Sultan of Delhi who kept the ideal of liberal autocracy before him. He tried to satisfy his opponents. Although he was a capable commander. He adopted the policy of generosity and kindness instead of fear and terror and emphasized on the change of heart of his enemies. He believed that the state cannot actually be an Islamic state.

questions.question_text: The first sovereign or independent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - The first sovereign or independent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was Iltutmish. He obtained the authority letter of recognition not from any ruler of Ghur but from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad in 1229 AD. After this, he assumed the title of Nasir-Amir-ul-Mominin.

questions.question_text: Firoz Tughlaq collected only those taxes which had the recognition of Islamic religion. Which one of the following was an additional tax which Firoz imposed?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Firoz Tughlaq was a Sultan who followed Islam. He imposed only four taxes recognized by Islamic laws - Jizya, Zakat, Khums, and Kharaj. Kharaj was a land tax, Khums was 1/5th part of the wealth looted in war which went to the Sultan and 4/5th part was distributed among the soldiers. Jizya was a religious tax on Hindus. Zakat was a religious tax taken from Muslims and spent for their benefit which was 2.5% of the total income. In addition to this, he also imposed Irrigation Tax or Haq-i-Sharb after the approval of the Ulema class which was imposed on the public after the approval of the Ulema class. Firoz Tughlaq was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to impose irrigation tax.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate declared that a king has no kinsmen?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Inspired by the theory of Turk kingship, Ibrahim Lodi declared that a king has no kinsmen. Kingship resides only in the Sultan. Therefore, he should take decisions being unbiased.

questions.question_text: A vivid description of the attack on the fort of Chittor by Alauddin Khalji is found in –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – The vivid picture of the fort of Chittor conquered by Alauddin is in the famous Awadhi poetic work Padmavat written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi in 1540 AD. In its story, Alauddin attacked Chittor to obtain the extremely beautiful queen Padmini of Rana Ratan Singh, in which after the defeat of the Rajputs, Padmini also performed the Jauhar Vrat. Alauddin got only the fort, Padmini could not be found. Famous Rajput historian Colonel Tod has also supported this story.

questions.question_text: Lodi dynasty rulers were originally related to which tribe or region?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - The rulers of the Lodi dynasty were related to an important branch of Afghans 'Shahkhel'. All the previous Sultans of Delhi were Turks, but the Lodis were pure Afghans. The Lodi dynasty ruled from 1451 to 1526 AD. Finally, in the first battle of Panipat, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi and established the Mughal dynasty in 1526 AD.

questions.question_text: What was the objective behind the market control system or economic regulations of Alauddin Khalji?

options.B: Keeping his soldiers satisfied with limited salary
options.C: Keeping control over Hindu merchants and traders

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - Alauddin's objective in market control and fixing the prices of goods was political. To keep a large army, to provide his soldiers a fixed and cash salary and to provide them with the facilities of life, and for the fulfillment of this objective, to stop the prices of goods from rising was his main objective and market control was a means for the fulfillment of this objective.

questions.question_text: Due to what reason did the experiment regarding the circulation of token currency by Muhammad bin Tughlaq prove to be a failure?

options.A: Not accepting token currency by foreign traders
options.B: Minting of fake coins on a large scale
options.D: Using token currency as metal after melting it

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced copper coins instead of silver coins as token currency. There were inscriptions in both Arabic and Persian languages on the token currency. Later on, silver went out of circulation and land revenue started being paid in fake token currency. Due to which his token currency circulation failed.

questions.question_text: Firoz Shah Tughlaq established the city of Jaunpur in memory of whom?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - Firoz Tughlaq built 300 new cities. Among the cities established by him, Fatehabad, Hisar, Firozepur, Jaunpur, and Firozabad were prominent. He established the city of Jaunpur in memory of his brother Jauna Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq).

questions.question_text: Who was the Sultan who called himself Naib-i-Khudai or representative of God?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 PGT History, 2013 Explanation - Balban calls himself Naib-i-Khudai or representative of God. In this way, the form and essence of Balban's theory of kingship was inspired by the kingship of Persia. According to him, the king is 'Zill-i-Illahi' i.e. a reflection of God. Balban believed that the heart of the Sultan is a special treasure of divine grace, for this reason, its existence is unique.

questions.question_text: Why is the dynasty established by the Sayyid dynasty representative Khizr Khan called Tamerlane's representative?

options.A: He and his successors ruled under the name of Tamerlane.
options.B: Khizr Khan was a descendant of the Prophet.
options.C: Khizr Khan was of the Sayyid tribe of Eastern Turkistan.
options.D: He was a famous scholar of Islamic theology.

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - The dynasty established by Sayyid dynasty representative Khizr Khan is called the dynasty established by the representative of Tamerlane because Khizr Khan was a descendant of the Prophet. Great military commander of Central Asia, Tamerlane, attacked India in 1398 AD during the reign of Sultan Nasir-ud-din Mahmud Tughlaq and had entrusted the governorship of Lahore, Multan, and Dipalpur to Khizr Khan.

questions.question_text: What was the common rule of succession in the Sultanate period?

options.A: Based on the seniority of birth
options.B: According to the rule of primogeniture
options.D: Personal strength or ability of the claimant for the throne as well as the opinion of Amirs

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation - There was no fixed rule of succession in the Sultanate period. There was recognition of the right to be nominated by the paternal Sultan. In the event of an incompetent successor, the nobles used the inspiration of choosing a Sultan. Apart from this, the power of the sword also ensured the right to the throne. Alauddin Khalji, Khizr Khan, and Bahlul Lodi were such rulers.

questions.question_text: Who were Barids?

options.C: Responsible officers keeping accounts of royal income and expenditure

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 PGT History, 2000 Explanation - During the Sultanate period, Barids were spies and information collectors. The chief officer of the intelligence department was Barid-i-Mumalik. Diwan-i-Barid comes under the Diwan-i-Risalat department.

questions.question_text: "I do not know what is legal or illegal, I make laws according to the need of the state." Who said this?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation – 'I do not know what is legal or illegal, I make laws according to the need of the state.' This statement was said by Alauddin Khalji himself. Alauddin Khalji was an autocratic ruler. He believed in complete autocracy. Alauddin Khalji succeeded in keeping politics free from the influence of religion. He said to Qazi Mughis regarding Sharia, "Maulana, Mughis, I do not have knowledge and I have not read any book. Still, I am born a Muslim and my ancestors have been Muslims for generations. I give orders to my subjects which I consider beneficial for the state and suitable for the situation, I do not know if Sharia provides permission for them or not."

questions.question_text: In whose reign did Ibn Battuta come to India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 TGT History, 2010 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Ibn Battuta came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351 AD). Ibn Battuta was a resident of Morocco (North Africa) and came to India as a traveler. He entered India in 1333 AD. He lived in India for 14 years. Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed him to the post of Qazi in Delhi, which post he held for ten years. Ibn Battuta wrote the account of his foreign travel in a book named 'Rihla'. Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent him to China by making him an ambassador.

questions.question_text: Who were 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani'?

options.B: A group of forty Turk Amirs

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Important works done by Iltutmish are as follows– (i) Completed the construction of Qutub Minar. (ii) Issued the first pure Arabic coins (silver Tanka and copper Jital) (iii) Started Iqta system. (iv) Formed an organization of forty slave chiefs which became known as Turkan-i-Chahalgani.

questions.question_text: Which Delhi Sultan started the practice of branding horses?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation – Alauddin Khalji started the practice of branding horses. Alauddin Khalji made many changes in the military system. In times of war, soldiers should not send any other person in their place. To prevent this, he started the practice of writing the descriptive roll (Huliya) of soldiers. Similarly, to prevent soldiers from changing good horses, he also laid the foundation of the practice of branding horses. The conquest of South India was done by Alauddin during the Sultanate period.

questions.question_text: When did the first battle of Tarain happen?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation – The first battle of Tarain happened in 1191 AD between Prithviraj Chauhan III and Shahab-ud-din Muhammad Ghori near Bhatinda. In this battle, Muhammad Ghori was defeated. According to 'Hammir-Mahakavya', Prithviraj imprisoned Muhammad Ghori but generously released him.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order and use the code given to select the appropriate option-
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation – Qutb-ud-din Aibak established the Slave Dynasty, which lasted from 1206 to 1290. Jalaluddin Khalji established the Khalji Dynasty, which lasted from 1290 to 1320. Tughlaq Dynasty remained from 1320 to 1412 and the Sayyid Dynasty was started by Khizr Khan in 1414, which lasted till 1451. Lodi Dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1451 to 1526 AD.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the answer on the basis of the code given below:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation – The first battle of Tarain took place in 1191 between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan. The capital was shifted from Delhi to Deogiri by Muhammad Tughlaq in 1327. Tamerlane invaded India in 1398, whereas the construction of Qutub Minar happened during Aibak's time (1206 AD - 1210 AD).

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II correctly and use the code given below the lists to choose the correct answer - List-I List-II A. First battle of Panipat (i) 1527 B. Second battle of Panipat (ii) 1529 C. Battle of Ghaghra (iii) 1526 D. Battle of Khanwa (iv) 1556 Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation – In 1526 AD, the first battle of Panipat took place between Ibrahim Lodi and Babur, and the second battle of Panipat took place in 1556 AD between Akbar and Hemu's army, and the battle of Ghaghra took place between Babur and Afghan army in 1529 AD. The battle of Khanwa took place in 1527 AD between Babur and Rana Sanga.

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler who ended the Sayyid Dynasty?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – After the death of Muhammad Shah, his son sat on the throne by the name of 'Alauddin Alam Shah'. He went to Badaun after having a dispute with his Vazir Hamid Khan. Later on, Bahlul Lodi ended the Sayyid Dynasty by occupying Delhi and established the Lodi Dynasty in 1451.

questions.question_text: The reason for the shifting of his new capital to Daulatabad by Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq was–

options.A: This city was in the center of the empire
options.C: It was a city full of wealth and luxury
options.D: He wanted to keep a second capital here to control the southern provinces more easily

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Qutb-ud-din Mubarak Khalji had named Deogiri as Qutubabad and Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq named it Daulatabad. The main reason for making Deogiri (Daulatabad) the capital instead of Delhi, according to Barani, is that it was in the center of the empire. Governing from Deogiri was easy in both northern and southern directions. According to Prof. Habibullah, "He wanted to make Deogiri the capital for the development of Muslim culture in South India and for the facility of southern prosperity and administration." This is considered the most valid view.

questions.question_text: According to Ziauddin Barani, the main objective of Alauddin Khalji's market control system was–

options.A: Maintenance of a huge standing army
options.B: Prosperity and welfare of common people

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Regarding Alauddin's market system, Barani said, if such a large army were given normal salary, the state treasury would be finished in five or six years. Alauddin reduced the soldiers' salaries to reduce military expenditure. But for the soldiers to live comfortably, he fixed the prices of goods and reduced their rates.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the answer on the basis of the code given below: (ka) Reform in market prices (kha) Defeat of Prithviraj Chauhan (ga) Capital transfer (gha) Construction of Qutub Minar Code:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – The description of the main events of the Sultanate era is as follows – Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated in the war with Muhammad Ghori in 1192 AD, the construction work of Qutub Minar was completed during the time of Iltutmish, Alauddin Khalji reformed market prices to maintain a huge military system, and in 1327 Muhammad Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (old name Deogiri).

questions.question_text: In which war did the Turk ruler Shahab-ud-din Ghori defeat Prithviraj Chauhan?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Muhammad Ghori's first attack took place in 1175 AD on Multan. In 1191, Ghori was defeated in the first battle of Tarain, but in the second battle of Tarain in 1192, Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan III. The defeat of Chauhan almost confirmed the establishment of Turk power in Northern India.

questions.question_text: Who established the slave (Slave) dynasty in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Sultans of Delhi Sultanate from 1206 to 1290 AD became famous by the name of Slave dynasty Sultans, although they were neither of one dynasty nor was anyone among them a slave at the time of becoming Sultan. The first Muslim ruler of Delhi was Qutb-ud-din Aibak and he is also considered the founder of Turk state in India.

questions.question_text: Where did Muhammad bin-Tughlaq shift his capital from Delhi?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Deogiri in 1327 AD. The purpose of this capital change was done keeping in mind the safety from Mongol invasions. But after the failure of this plan, he again shifted his capital to Delhi in 1335 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first Muslim ruler of Delhi who penetrated the Deccan?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – Alauddin Khalji was the first Muslim ruler of Delhi who tried to win South India for the first time. Political and economic reasons were important for this military campaign of Alauddin. In his southern campaign, Malik Kafur got a lot of success in his army.

questions.question_text: After the death of Muhammad Ghori, Qutb-ud-din Aibak ruled Indian provinces and established a dynasty, which was named–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – After the death of Muhammad Ghori in 1206 AD, Qutb-ud-din Aibak established the Slave Dynasty. The rule of Turk rulers in India from 1206 AD to 1290 AD has been divided into Muizzi, Qutbi, Shamsi, and Balbani classes. Qutb-ud-din received the title of 'Lakh Baksh', Lahore remained his capital during his time.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Mongols gather on the banks of the Indus river under the leadership of their famous leader Genghis Khan –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Mongols gathered on the banks of the Indus river in 1221 AD under the leadership of Genghis Khan. Genghis Khan reached Lahore after winning the Indus while chasing the last Shah of Khwarizm, Jalaluddin Mangabarni. Understanding the reality of the situation, Sultan Iltutmish did not give shelter to Mangabarni in Delhi. In 1224 AD, Jalaluddin Mangabarni went to Persia.

questions.question_text: The first battle of Panipat broke the backbone of the Lodi dynasty and as a result, a very large land area came under Babur's control. That land area extended to–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – In 1526 AD, in the first battle of Panipat, Babur's army defeated Ibrahim Lodi and established the Mughal dynasty in India. Delhi and Agra were also included under Mughal power. In the battle of Panipat, Babur used the war policy of Uzbeks 'Tulugma war method' and 'Osmani method' (Rumi method) to arrange cannons.

questions.question_text: After the second battle of Tarain, the area that was transferred under Turk rule was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – In 1191 AD, Muhammad Ghori was defeated in the first battle of Tarain, but in 1192 AD, Prithviraj Chauhan III was defeated in the second battle of Tarain. Muhammad Ghori captured Delhi and Ajmer. Here he appointed his subordinate ruler. This area falls in Eastern Rajasthan. The Chauhans ruled these areas.

questions.question_text: Alauddin Khalji gave which Hindu ruler the title of 'Rayarayan'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Alauddin Khalji gave the title of Rayarayan to the ruler of Deogiri, Ramchandra Dev, and also honored him by giving a canopy. Along with one lakh gold tankas, he also gave him the jagir of Navsari.

questions.question_text: Sultan Qutb-ud-din Aibak's capital was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Due to the death of Muhammad Ghori in 1206 AD, Qutb-ud-din Aibak assumed power in Lahore at the request of local citizens. Due to the danger from Yildiz, he always lived in Lahore, which became his capital. Although Qutb-ud-din Aibak is considered the founder of Turk state in India. Iltutmish brought the capital from Lahore to Delhi after the death of Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans collected 'Jizya' tax from Brahmins for the first time?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Firoz Shah was the Sultan who collected Jizya tax from Brahmins for the first time. To demonstrate religious zeal and to satisfy the Ulemas, he imposed this tax on Brahmins.

questions.question_text: Tamerlane invaded India –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Tamerlane invaded India in 1398 AD. At that time, Sultan Nasir-ud-din Mahmud was ruling (1394-1412).

questions.question_text: What is not true about Alauddin Khalji?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – During Alauddin's time, there was an increase in land revenue and he formed an intelligence system. Apart from this, he also prohibited liquor. As far as the matter of providing jagirs to military officers is concerned, this did not happen during Alauddin Khalji's time.

questions.question_text: Who was leading the opposition Amir group of Razia?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The opposition Amir group of Razia was led by Nizam-ul-Mulk-Junaidi. Razia Sultan was the first female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. She had defeated all opposition Amir groups.

questions.question_text: What was the basis of assuming power by Iltutmish?

options.C: Delhi's Turk Amirs and military officers chose him
options.D: He was chosen by Amirs based in Lahore

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The main basis for assuming power by Iltutmish was his selection by Delhi's Turk Amirs and military officers. Iltutmish sat on the Delhi throne without any resistance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following says that the history of Muslim sovereignty in India actually begins from Iltutmish's reign?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – This is the statement of Ram Prasad Tripathi that the history of Muslim sovereignty in India actually begins from Iltutmish's reign. Iltutmish was the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate. He was a capable commander and brave warrior.

questions.question_text: Diwan-i-Mustakhraj department was established –

options.B: To crush the powers of jagirdars.

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – The objective of establishing Diwan-i-Mustakhraj department was – to collect arrears of revenue. This department was established by Alauddin Khalji. The three main tasks of this department were – (i) Names of revenue-collecting officers, (ii) To check arrears amount and (iii) To collect revenue.

questions.question_text: "Hanuz Dilli Dur Ast" is a statement related to which Sultan?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 PGT History, 2000 Explanation – 'Hanuz Dilli Dur Ast' this statement is related to Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq. This statement was said by Sufi saint Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya for him.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was both the military and administrative officer of the province?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Bakshi was both the military and administrative officer of the province. His main task was to look after the army of the province. Sometimes he was also made the Waqia-i-Navis of the province.

questions.question_text: The first Turk invader to attack India was-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – The first Turk invader to attack India was Subuktigin. In 986-87 AD, he attacked the then ruler of Sindh, Jaipal, and forced him to sign a treaty. By the time of Subuktigin's death (997 AD), his kingdom included the entire Afghanistan, Khorasan, Balkh, and the border regions of North-West India. Mahmud Ghaznavi was Subuktigin's son and after his father's death in 997 AD, he sat on the throne. Mahmud Ghaznavi attacked India 17 times between 999 AD and 1027 AD. Muhammad bin Qasim was the first Arab Muslim ruler to attack India who won Sindh and Multan (712 AD).

questions.question_text: Qutb-ud-din Aibak conducted the administration from which place-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Qutb-ud-din Aibak's official coronation took place on 25 June, 1206 AD. He received the recognition and appointment letter for power three years later. His capital was Lahore (meaning he conducted the administration from Lahore). He was also called 'Lakhbaksh' (giver of millions).

questions.question_text: During whose reign did the first Mongol invasion occur-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – The first Mongol invasion occurred during the time of Sultan Iltutmish in 1221 AD. When Temujin i.e. Genghis Khan reached the Indus while chasing the last Shah of Khwarizm, Jalaluddin Mangabarni. Jalaluddin Mangabarni asked for shelter from Iltutmish which Iltutmish refused. In this way, Iltutmish saved the newly formed Turk empire from Mongol destruction.

questions.question_text: The first Muslim female ruler to sit on the throne of Delhi Sultanate was-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – The first Muslim female ruler to sit on the Delhi Sultanate throne was Razia Sultan (1236-40 AD). Razia Sultan was the daughter of Iltutmish. It is noteworthy that after the death of Iltutmish, Razia captured power with the help of the public after seeing the situation of disorder.

questions.question_text: What is the main source of detailed information about Alauddin Khalji's market control policy-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Historian Barani has given a detailed description of Alauddin Khalji's market control system in his book 'Tarikh-i-Firozshahi'. He has written that the Sultan has made some rules to ensure proper arrangement of food and drink in the capital.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of the Sultanate used the title 'Commander of the Prophet'-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Khusrau Shah became a Muslim Sultan after converting from Hindu religion. Showing himself as a devoted Muslim, he assumed the title of "Commander of the Prophet". His enemies raised slogans against him that he was an enemy of Islam and Islam is in danger.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers restored the old rights of Khuts and Muqaddams-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq 1320-25, the founder of Tughlaq dynasty, abandoned the harsh revenue system (which was implemented during Alauddin Khalji's time). The Amirs whom Alauddin had deprived of land were returned the land. The old rights of Khuts and Muqaddams were restored.

questions.question_text: Which foreign traveler who came to India during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign was-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Morocco (African) traveler Ibn Battuta came to India in 1333 AD during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign (1325-1351 AD). The Sultan appointed him to the post of Qazi of Delhi. In 1342, he was sent to China by the Sultan as his ambassador. His autobiography is named "Rihla".

questions.question_text: The department 'Diwan-i-Amir Kohi', which was related to agriculture, was established–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – The task of Diwan-i-Amir Kohi department was to make the land where farming was not taking place, cultivable, meaning it was related to the agriculture department. This department was established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: In which year did Muhammad Tughlaq shift his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – After the death of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq, his son 'Juna Khan' sat on the Delhi throne in 1325 AD by the name of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. His original name was 'Ulugh Khan'. He has been called 'eccentric', 'mad' and 'bloodthirsty'. Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Deogiri in 1326-27 AD. Deogiri was also called 'Qutbatul Islam'. Qutb-ud-din Mubarak Khalji had named Deogiri 'Qutubabad' and Muhammad bin Tughlaq changed its name to 'Daulatabad'. In 1335 AD, he gave permission to return to Delhi again.

questions.question_text: After death, Qutb-ud-din Aibak was buried –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1206-1210) died due to falling from a horse while playing (Chaugan) polo. After death, he was buried in Lahore. It is noteworthy that Qutb-ud-din Aibak's capital was also Lahore. Aibak is a Turk word meaning - 'god of the moon'. Aibak has also been called 'Quran Khan'.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of Tughlaq Dynasty in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Tughlaq Dynasty was a dynasty of the Sultanate that ruled the Delhi power from 1320 to 1412 AD. The Tughlaq Dynasty was founded by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq. Ghazi Malik or Tughlaq Ghazi, sat on the Delhi throne on 8 September, 1320, by the name of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq (1320-1325 AD). He made 29 Mongol invasions failed. He was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who added the word 'Ghazi' (killer of infidels) to his name.

questions.question_text: Malik Kafur, a capable commander, was working under which ruler?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In 1297 AD, Alauddin Khalji sent an army to conquer the Hindu state of Gujarat. At that time, the king there was Rai Karan Dev II. Alauddin's army defeated king Karan Dev II and returned with a lot of wealth and a slave Malik Kafur from there. Alauddin was impressed by Malik Kafur's capability. He gave him the title of Malik Naib.

questions.question_text: Who built 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Qutb-ud-din Aibak built the "Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra" in Ajmer which is a mosque. This building was actually a Sanskrit school which was built by Chauhan emperor Vigraharaja IV. Its upper parts were broken and domes and arches were built.

questions.question_text: Under whose control was the management of the market control system introduced by Alauddin Khalji?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Diwan-i-Riyasat was the market control system introduced by Alauddin Khalji. He got sales done on the basis of a list of goods sold in the market. If any kind of mistake was found by the trader class, they were punished.

questions.question_text: Who started the 'Dagh-o-Chehra' (branding of horses and descriptive roll of soldiers) practice?
