questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Alauddin Khalji started the practice of checking the descriptive roll of soldiers to ensure that soldiers should not send any other person in their place at the time of war. Similarly, he also laid the foundation of the practice of branding horses to ensure soldiers do not change good horses.

questions.question_text: Whose statement is this that Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq wanted to make Deogiri his capital because "it was situated in the center of the empire"?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – There are many reasons for making Deogiri the capital instead of Delhi. Barani says that Deogiri was important because it was situated in the center of the empire. Whereas Ibn Battuta says that the Sultan received disrespectful letters from the citizens of Delhi. Therefore, he decided to make Deogiri the capital to punish them. Isami says he wanted to take them to South India to break the power of the citizens of Delhi. Dr. Nizami says that Muhammad Tughlaq's goal was to make two capitals Delhi and Daulatabad.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the head of the military department under Delhi-Sultans?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – The head of the military department under Delhi Sultans was 'Ariz-i-Mumalik'. His department was 'Diwan-i-Arz'. His task was recruitment of soldiers, keeping their records, and arranging for weapons.

questions.question_text: The department named 'Diwan-i-Amir Kohi', which was related to agriculture, was established–
questions.explanation: GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 PGT History, 2005 Diwan-i-Kohi, a department related to agriculture, was established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. He opened this department for the progress of agriculture and appointed a new minister post called 'Amir-i-Kohi'. According to Moreland, "For the first time in Indian history, it appeared that the government was responsible for improving cultivation, methods of farming, and agricultural resources."

questions.question_text: Name the Sultan who persecuted the Amir-i-Sada?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation - Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq persecuted the Amir-i-Sada. He ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1325 to 1351.

questions.question_text: Whose reign is described in Ibn Battuta’s ‘Rehla’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation - Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta came to India in 1333 AD, whom Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed as the Chief Qazi of Delhi and later sent him to China as his diplomatic envoy. Ibn Battuta wrote about his life in the book titled ‘Rehla’.

questions.question_text: What was ‘Iqta’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 PGT History, 2010 Explanation - Iqta was land that was given to military commanders for the purpose of maintaining an army, so that from its income, the commander could manage his army. In this way, Iqta land was a piece of official land whose owner was called Mukti.

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, what was ‘Majlis-i-Khalwat’?

options.A: An advisory body of the Sultan
options.C: A committee of the revenue department

questions.explanation: Explanation - Majlis-i-Khalwat was a council of ministers to advise the Sultan. In the Slave period, the number of ministers in this council was four, who were considered the four pillars of the state. Later, its number increased to 6, which are as follows - 1. Wazir, 2. Ariz-i-Mumalik, 3. Diwan-i-Risalat, 4. Diwan-i-Insha, 5. Sadr-us-Sudur, 6. Diwan-i-Qaza. Instead of calling everyone, the Sultan used to call only a few people of his choice to the Majlis-i-Khalwat.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers was known as ‘Lakh-Baksh’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Qutb-ud-din Aibak was a generous ruler among the rulers of the Slave dynasty. His title was 'Lakh-Baksh'. He was given this title because of his generosity in donating lakhs. His other title was 'Quran Khan' because he had the entire Quran memorized orally.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Muslim writer to use Hindi words and Indian poetic concepts and subjects in his works?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation - Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau, who is often known as Amir Khusrau, was born in 1253 AD at a place called Patiali in Kasganj district of Uttar Pradesh. Amir Khusrau used Hindi words and Indian poetic concepts and subjects in his works.

questions.question_text: Who got the city of Delhi built?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation - From a historical point of view, Anangpal Tomar got the city of Delhi built, which is mentioned in Prithviraj Raso.

questions.question_text: During whose reign was the Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta appointed as the Chief Qazi of Delhi?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation - Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta came to the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in India in 1333 AD. Tughlaq appointed him as the Qazi of Delhi. Ibn Battuta wrote a book about the events of the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, titled Rehla.

questions.question_text: Which Delhi Sultan's court had two Jain scholars named Jinaprabha Suri and Rajshekhar?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation - We find proof of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's liberal views in some Jain traditions, according to which he honored Jain scholars Jinaprabha Suri and Rajshekhar in his court.

questions.question_text: (1) Ranthambore (2) Gujarat (3) Chittor (4) Telangana Options: Arrange the conquests of Alauddin Khalji in chronological order.
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– The systematic chronological description of Alauddin Khalji's conquests is as follows- Gujarat Conquest – in 1297 AD Ranthambore Conquest – in 1301 AD Chittor Conquest – in 1303 AD Telangana Conquest – in 1309 or 1310 AD

questions.question_text: The Mamluk Sultan who was a proponent of the divine theory of kingship –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Balban was a proponent of the divine theory of kingship. According to him, 'The Sultan is the representative of God on earth and his position is second only to the Prophet.'

questions.question_text: The main reason for Alauddin Khalji's economic reforms was–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– The main reason for Alauddin Khalji's economic reforms was that he wanted to maintain a powerful army, and Ziauddin Barani has mentioned this in his book Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

questions.question_text: The only Indian Muslim to sit on the Delhi throne during the Sultanate period was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– The only Indian Muslim to sit on the Delhi throne during the Sultanate period was Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah, who was a convert from the Hindu religion. He had assumed the title of Commander of the Prophet's Army.

questions.question_text: Which tax was not imposed by Alauddin Khalji?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Alauddin Khalji did not impose the tax named Kismat-i-Khoti. Ghari was a housing tax. Charai tax – was levied on milch cattle. Zakat – was a religious tax taken only from Muslims. Kismat-i-Khoti and Haqq-i-Khoti were taxes taken from farmers by the traditional landlord class.

questions.question_text: Which dynasty ruled for the longest period in the history of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– The Sultans of the Slave Dynasty ruled from 1206 to 1290 AD, Khalji Dynasty from 1290 to 1320 AD, Lodi Dynasty from 1451 to 1526 AD, and Tughlaq Dynasty from 1320 AD to 1412 AD in Delhi. Thus, the Tughlaq dynasty ruled for the longest period in the history of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question_text: Bahlul Lodi was the governor of which province?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – In 1451 AD, when Alauddin Alam Shah of the Sayyid dynasty left the throne of Delhi, at that time Bahlul Lodi was the Subedar (governor) of Lahore and Sirhind. With the help of his Wazir Hamid Khan, he captured Delhi and laid the foundation of the Lodi Dynasty.

questions.question_text: Dar-ul-Harb was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Dar-ul-Harb was a Hindu kingdom territory. Ending this area was the main objective of Muslim rulers. It also included converting the people of this area to Islam and making everyone accept Islam.

questions.question_text: Which woman did not remain a ruler in the medieval period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Of the 14 children born to Shah Jahan's wife Mumtaz Mahal, only 4 sons and 3 daughters survived. Their names were – Jahanara (born 1614 AD), Dara Shikoh (1615 AD), Roshan Ara (born 1617 AD), Aurangzeb (born 1618 AD), Murad Baksh (born 1629 AD) and Gauhar Ara (born 1631 AD). In the given options, besides Roshan Ara, Razia Sultan, Rudrama Devi, and Tarabai had handled the reins of administration in their time.

questions.question_text: Which of the rulers of the Sultanate period started ‘Diwan-i-Khairat’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Firoz Tughlaq was such a Sultan among the rulers of the Sultanate period who established a department named Diwan-i-Khairat. Through this, he provided financial assistance to Muslim orphan women and widows and arranged for the marriage of poor Muslim girls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans is known for the work done for the welfare of slaves?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Firoz Shah Tughlaq was such a ruler who is known for the work done for the welfare of slaves. He established a department named ‘Diwan-i-Bandagan’ for slaves.

questions.question_text: Balban was born in which tribe of Turks?
questions.explanation: Asharam Padhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - According to Dr. P.S.I. Srivastava, "Balban, like Iltutmish, was an Ilbari Turk." Balban was the Sultan of Delhi from 1265 to 1287 AD. He was the last powerful ruler of the Slave Dynasty. After the death of Nasiruddin, he became the Sultan of Delhi in 1265 and adopted the policy of 'Iron and Blood'. Firdausi has described Balban as a descendant of Afrasiyab in his Shahnameh.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan crushed the Turkan-i-Chahalgani?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– The Sultan of Delhi, Iltutmish, established a group of forty amirs, this was called Turkan-i-Chahalgani (a group of commanders). Balban crushed the Turkan-i-Chahalgani. He adopted the 'policy of blood and iron' to establish the prestige of the Sultan.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of the Slave Dynasty introduced pure Arabic coins?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Iltutmish was an Ilbari Turk of Turkestan, he was Aibak's slave. Iltutmish shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi. Iltutmish issued pure Arabic coins which include the silver Tanka and copper Jital.

questions.question_text: In which year was Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji coronated?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– The founder of the Khalji Dynasty was Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji. His coronation took place on 13 June 1290 AD in Kilokhri. Jalaluddin was the first Sultan of Delhi who maintained the ideals of liberal autocracy. He made Kilokhri his capital.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was called ‘Hazar Merdi’?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - In 1236 AD, Razia Sultan became the ruler in the Sultanate period, which some commanders opposed. Among them were the Iqtedars of Badaun, Multan, Hansi, and Lahore. Razia created a rift among the opponents and brought some to her side. In this, Kabir Ayaz Khan of Multan was the Iqtedar who was called ‘Hazar Merdi’.

questions.question_text: Which of the following used to spend most of his time at night in prayer and contemplation?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - In 1211, Iltutmish became the Sultan of Delhi. He had received the recognition of the Sultan's post from the Caliph. Iltutmish was an Ilbari Turk. He was an excellent ruler; he used to spend most of his time at night in prayer and contemplation.

questions.question_text: Who assumed the title of ‘Rayyat-i-Ala’?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Khizr Khan was the founder of the Sayyid dynasty. He had claimed himself to be a descendant of Prophet Muhammad. In 1414, he snatched Delhi from Daulat Khan Lodi and became the first Sayyid Sultan, but Khizr Khan did not accept the title of Sultan, but took the title of ‘Rayyat-i-Ala’.

questions.question_text: Who called Ashoka’s stone pillars ‘Golden Pillars’?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - After Muhammad Tughlaq, Firoz Shah Tughlaq became the Sultan of Delhi. He got two pillars of Ashoka, Topra and Meerut, brought to Delhi and installed them. He named these pillars ‘Golden Pillars’.

questions.question_text: On whose order did Amir Khusrau write his work ‘Ashiqa’?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010, 2001 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Amir Khusrau wrote Ashiqa on the order of Khizr Khan. Its composition in poetry describes the love between Deval Devi, the daughter of Raja Karan of Gujarat, and Khizr Khan, the son of Alauddin Khalji. It also contains a description of Khizr Khan's moral downfall.

questions.question_text: Who gave up his claim to the throne in exchange for one elephant and the governorship of Nagaur?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Alauddin Masud was the Sultan of Delhi from 1242 to 1246 AD and Nasiruddin Mahmud ruled Delhi from 1246 to 1265 AD, and under an agreement with Kishlu Khan, he gave up his claim to the throne in exchange for one elephant and the governorship of Nagaur.

questions.question_text: Balban was famous for his
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Balban (1265-87 AD) was Iltutmish's slave. His name was Bahauddin. Balban adopted a policy of ‘iron and blood’ against his opponents. During his time, famous Persian poets Amir Khusrau and Amir Hasan lived. The rebellion of Tughril in Bengal also happened during his time.

questions.question_text: The camp named ‘Swarg-Dwari’ was related to which Sultan?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq had set up a camp named Swarg Dwari (in Delhi) to save from famine and epidemic in the Doab region. Among all the medieval Sultans, Muhammad Tughlaq was the most educated, scholarly, and capable person. Due to his eccentric plans, cruel deeds, and indifference towards the joys and sorrows of others, he was called a dreamer, crazy, and bloodthirsty.

questions.question_text: The Tughlaq Empire was divided into
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - The Tughlaq Empire was divided into 23 Muktis (provinces). On 5 September 1320 AD, defeating Khusrau Khan, Ghazi Malik sat on the throne of Delhi in the name of Tughlaq Ghazi Ghiyath-ud-din Tughlaq. After this, Muhammad bin Tughlaq became the ruler. Their empire was divided into 23 parts.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan implemented the ‘principle of heredity’ in the army?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Firoz Tughlaq implemented the ‘principle of heredity’ in the army. Firoz Shah Tughlaq's coronation took place in 1351 AD. He showed leniency in the army, the result of which was that people used to get others' horses paraded in place of their own. Therefore, corruption increased. Finally, Firoz Shah Tughlaq made the post of soldiers hereditary. Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the first Sultan who imposed Jizya tax on Brahmins.

questions.question_text: Who said, “Some Hindus know that Islam is the true religion, but they do not accept Islam”?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Barani said, “Some Hindus know that Islam is the true religion, but they do not accept Islam”. During the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Ziauddin Barani had received royal patronage. He wanted to prove himself a religious person, that is why he expressed his special inclination towards Islam.

questions.question_text: Whom did Razia appoint to the post of Amir-i-Hajib?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Razia appointed Ikhtiyaruddin Aetigin to the post of Amir-i-Hajib. Jamaluddin Yaqut was appointed Amir-i-Akhur (Head of the Stable). During Razia's reign, some provincial rulers were opposing her, to deal with which Razia had appointed some special officers.

questions.question_text: The group of Turk Amirs formed by Iltutmish was called
questions.explanation: Turkan-i-Chahalgani (group of forty Amirs) was a group of loyal slave Amirs of Iltutmish. Through this, Iltutmish tried to control administration and military. This group played its role later as well, but Balban ended this group for his absolute power

questions.question_text: A coin named Jital was made of
questions.explanation: Iltutmish was the first Turk ruler who introduced pure Arabic coins - silver Tanka and copper Jital. On these coins, Iltutmish is mentioned as the representative of the Caliph, and also, evidence of the tradition of writing the name of the mint on it is obtained

questions.question_text: A new class of officers ‘Khwaja’ was appointed by one of the following for the assessment of the income of Iqtedars:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - A new class of officers ‘Khwaja’ or Sahib-i-Diwan was appointed by Balban for the assessment of the income of Iqtedars. In the Sultanate period, there used to be a problem in collecting land revenue. To deal with this problem, the help of Khwaja or Sahib-i-Diwan was taken.

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians has given the most official account of Malik Kafur’s southern campaigns?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Amir Khusrau's works contain the most detailed account of Malik Kafur's southern campaigns. Alauddin had bought Malik Kafur for one thousand dinars. That is why Kafur is also called Hazar Dinari.

questions.question_text: Who among the following first assumed the title of Sultan?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Iltutmish was the first Sultan of Delhi; he received the recognition of the Sultan's post not from any ruler of Ghur but from the Caliph. In this way, he was the first independent Sultan of Delhi legally. He is also considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans first implemented the ‘market control’ system in the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 PGT History 2004 Explanation - Alauddin Khalji kept a large army in the center and paid them in cash. The expenditure of that army was very high, so he fixed the prices of goods so that soldiers could perform their duties on a common salary. He established a total of four markets in the market control system - Grain Mandi, Sarai-i-Adl, market for horses, slaves, and cattle, and a general market. Among these, Grain Mandi was the most successful.

questions.question_text: Which Muslim ruler in medieval India played ‘Holi’ for the first time?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - In medieval India, Muhammad bin Tughlaq participated in the festival ‘Holi’ of Hindus for the first time. He ruled from 1325 to 1351 AD. He was an intellectual and tolerant ruler. He had debated on religious principles with scholars of almost every religion. He also had close relations with Jain scholars.

questions.question_text: A list of departments is given below. Which of these were established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq? (i) Diwan-i-Khairat (ii) Diwan-i-Bandagan (iii) Dar-ul-Shafa (iv) Employment office Select the correct answer from the code below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - All the given departments were established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Through the charity house named ‘Diwan-i-Khairat’, financial assistance was given for the marriage of poor Muslim girls and to widows. ‘Dar-ul-Shafa’ was a royal hospital, in which free treatment facility was provided. ‘Diwan-i-Bandagan’ was the slave department. Firoz was very fond of slaves. He had 1 lakh 80 thousand slaves. Through the employment office, unemployed youth were given employment.

questions.question_text: Who among the following said that I do not worry about ‘Shara’?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Alauddin Khalji had obtained power by the strength of force. For this reason, he did not let religion dominate politics. He did not worry about ‘Shara’ while doing his works.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans established a separate Public Works Department?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Firoz Shah Tughlaq established a separate Public Works Department. He has described this work of his in his work named ‘Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi’. He founded Jaunpur, Firozabad, Hisar, and other cities.

questions.question_text: During the reign of Sultan Iltutmish, a person seeking justice had to wear
questions.explanation: GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018, 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- During the reign of Sultan Iltutmish, a person seeking justice had to wear red clothes. Iltutmish's daughter Razia, before becoming Sultan, on a Friday, wearing red clothes, had demanded her right from the citizens of Delhi, after which she became the Sultan of Delhi.

questions.question_text: The Sultans of Delhi appointed spies in different parts of their Sultanate. They were called:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The Sultans of Delhi appointed spies in different parts of their Sultanate. They were called Barid. Their work was to find out about conspiracies being made against the state and the Sultan and to convey that information to the Sultan.

questions.question_text: Who among the following killed Muizzuddin Ghori?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Muizzuddin Ghori attacked India in 1205. There was a battle with the Khokhars between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers. The Khokhars were defeated in this, but on 15 March 1206, the Khokhars suddenly attacked Ghori's group and killed Muizzuddin Ghori.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers had established a ‘charity kitchen’ in his capital?
questions.explanation: GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Sher Shah had established a charity kitchen in his capital. The daily expenditure of the government dining hall was 500 ashrafis. Every soldier, farmer, merchant, religious person, etc., used to get free food there.

questions.question_text: On the banks of which river was Sultan Jalaluddin Khalji killed?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- On 19 July, 1296 AD, Jalaluddin Khalji went to meet his nephew Alauddin and congratulate him (after the victory of Devagiri) at Kara Manikpur on the banks of the Ganga and right there, he was murdered by his nephew Alauddin Khalji.

questions.question_text: Who among the following used to call his nobles ‘Masnad-i-Ali’?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Bahlul Lodi sat on the throne of Delhi by the name of ‘Ghazi’ and laid the foundation of the first Afghan Empire. Bahlul Lodi belonged to the important branch of Afghans, ‘Shahu Khel’. Bahlul Lodi used to call his nobles ‘Masnad-i-Ali’/my sons.

questions.question_text: Milk, Inam and Waqf grants were abolished by
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- As soon as his power became strong on the throne, Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316 AD) crushed the nobles. The Sultan ordered that all land properties, villages, and other land which people had in the form of Milk (property), Inam, and Waqf (gift), should be taken back and converted into Khalisa land.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan established the first ‘Madrasa’?
questions.explanation: With the establishment of Muslim rule in India, Muslim education stepped on Indian soil. Muhammad Ghori first started the practice of destroying temples and building mosques and providing Muslim education. In the Sultanate period, there were three types of educational institutions – Maktab, Madrasa, and Khanqahs. Iltutmish established the Madrasa in a real sense. In memory of Muhammad Ghori, he established ‘Madrasa-i-Muizzi’ in Delhi and Badaun and ‘Madrasa-i-Nasiriya’ in Delhi. He also built a Madrasa in Uchch, which was named Madrasa-i-Firozi

questions.question_text: Who among the following declared himself the ruler of Lakhnauti with the title of ‘Sultan Mughisuddin’?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Tughril declared himself the ruler of Lakhnauti with the title of ‘Sultan Mughisuddin’. He was a Turk Amir, whom Sultan Ghiyath-ud-din Balban had appointed as the Subedar of Bengal. In 1279 AD, during Balban's time, Tughril rebelled and assumed the title of Sultan Mughisuddin and declared himself the ruler of Lakhnauti.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans advocated the theory of ‘Niyabat-i-Khudai’?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Balban (1265-1287 AD) ruled Delhi for 20 years as a Wazir and 20 years as a Sultan. He adopted the ‘policy of blood and iron’ to establish the prestige of the Sultan post. According to him, the Sultan is the representative of God on earth and his position is second only to the Prophet. Balban also advocated the theory of ‘Niyabat-i-Khudai’ (representative of God).

questions.question_text: Which of the following travelers was an African?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Ibn Battuta was an African traveler of Moroccan origin. He came to India during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-51). Muhammad bin Tughlaq had appointed him as the Qazi of Delhi. Later, in 1342 AD, he was sent to China as the Sultan's ambassador. Ibn Battuta has given an account of his journey in a book named ‘Rehla’.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was called ‘Lakhbaksh’?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak was given the title of Lakh Baksh, which means - one who gives in charity in lakhs. Aibak was a slave of Muhammad Ghori and he laid the foundation of the Slave Dynasty in 1206 AD. He is also known by the name of Quran Khan (due to knowing the Quran by heart)

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians was with Malik Kafur during his southern campaign?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Alauddin Khalji sent an army under the leadership of Malik Kafur in 1307 AD to attack Devagiri. Raja Ramchandra Deva was defeated in the war and he surrendered. Malik Kafur looted Devagiri and brought Raja Ramchandra along with his relatives to Delhi. Alauddin treated Raja Ramchandra with respect and gave him the title of ‘Raya-i-Rayan’. After six months, he was given one lakh gold tankas and the district of Navsari and sent back to his state. Amir Khusrau also went to Devagiri with Malik Kafur during this campaign.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans threatened Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya with serious consequences if he failed to express respect in person?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Mubarak Shah Khalji had threatened Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya with serious consequences if he failed to express respect in person.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans established a separate department for the care of slaves?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Firoz Shah Tughlaq was very fond of slaves. The number of his slaves probably reached up to one lakh eighty thousand. A separate department ‘Diwan-i-Bandagan’ was formed for their care. Full attention was paid to the education of those slaves. Every slave used to get a salary between 10 to 100 tankas and sometimes even jagirs were received. This hobby of Firoz eventually proved harmful to the state.

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians justifies the rebellions against Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Historian Isami justifies the rebellions against Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans issued an order that in his rule all foreigners should be addressed as ‘Aizza’?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Muhammad bin Tughlaq had issued an order that in his rule, all foreigners should be addressed as ‘Aizza’.

questions.question_text: Iltutmish was given the Iqtedari of Badaun by–
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Qutb-ud-din's son-in-law and successor Iltutmish was an Ilbari Turk. Iltutmish was the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate. At the time of Qutb-ud-din Aibak's death, he was the Subedar of Badaun.

questions.question_text: During whose reign did people not marry their daughters to revenue clerks?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- During the reign of Alauddin Khalji, people did not marry their daughters to revenue clerks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following died fighting in a war?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- On 21 April, 1526, the first battle of Panipat took place between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Ibrahim fought with courage and bravery, but due to Babur's capable leadership, superior war tactics, and artillery, Ibrahim was defeated and died on the battlefield. With the death of Ibrahim Lodi, along with the Lodi dynasty, the history of the Delhi Sultanate ended and the foundation of the Mughal dynasty was laid in India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following did not accept Alauddin Khalji’s supremacy in South India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– On the orders of Alauddin, Malik Kafur made the first attack in South India on Telangana, in which Kakatiya dynasty ruler Pratap Rudradeva II was defeated and he gave the world-famous Kohinoor diamond to Malik Kafur. In this sequence, Yadava dynasty ruler Ramchandra of Devagiri and Hoysala ruler Ballala Deva also accepted the suzerainty of Alauddin. Pandya ruler Vira Pandya did not accept the suzerainty of Alauddin.

questions.question_text: The title of Amir Khusrau’s book which gives information about the political and social life of Qutb-ud-din Mubarak Shah’s time was:
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– The title of Amir Khusrau’s book which gives information about the political and social life of Qutb-ud-din Mubarak Shah Khalji’s time is ‘Nuh-i-Sipihr’. ‘Khazain-ul-Futuh’ contains a description of Alauddin's crushing campaigns. In ‘Mifta-ul-Futuh’, information about Jalaluddin Khalji is obtained. In ‘Tughlaqnama’, information about the reign of Ghiyath-ud-din Tughlaq is obtained.

questions.question_text: Which of the following started the custom of ‘Zaminbos’ (Sijda)?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Balban (1265–1287 AD) restarted the custom of ‘Sijda (Zaminbos)’ and ‘Paibos’ in his court, which was originally a Persian custom and which was considered non-Islamic. Apart from this, he also started the custom of the Persian festival Nauroz.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan’s mother was famous for giving gifts and alms to scholars and holy men?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Ruknuddin Firoz Shah’s mother Shah Turkan was famous for giving gifts and alms to scholars and holy men. Whereas Ruknuddin was a person of luxurious temperament who remained completely incapable of managing the rule of Delhi. His mother Shah Turkan, who was a Turk slave woman, took the reins of administration in her hands. She started a reign of terror and had Iltutmish’s capable son Qutb-ud-din blinded and murdered. As a result, ‘the trust of the Maliks in the rule was lost and rebellions started in different parts of the country. Razia took advantage of the anarchy spread in the state and the rebellions happening all around the Maliks. She asked for help from the people gathered for prayer. The crowd attacked the palace and imprisoned Shah Turkan. The army and nobles joined Razia, and Ruknuddin was imprisoned and killed.

questions.question_text: The main reason for Alauddin’s order for prohibition in Delhi was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Alauddin Khalji issued several ordinances for political purposes. Through the third ordinance of these, Alauddin stopped the use of intoxicating substances like wine and bhang and gambling. Drinking wine was completely stopped in Delhi and wine vessels were thrown in front of the public. Harsh punishment was given to those who broke this law. Due to which those who drank wine could drink wine only after going 20 or 25 miles away from Delhi, but considering this task impossible, Alauddin made some changes in this rule. People were allowed to drink and make wine in their homes, but they could neither make wine in public, nor could they drink it, nor could they host wine parties. For the fulfillment of Alauddin’s goal, this was sufficient.

questions.question_text: The tradition of inscribing the name of the mint on the ‘Tanka’ was started by-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000, 2001 Explanation– Iltutmish was the first Turk ruler who introduced pure Arabic coins. His contribution to the coinage system is the greatest because he introduced two major silver coins, namely the silver Tanka and the copper Jital. Iltutmish had the name of the Caliph inscribed on the coins. At the same time, he also declared himself the 'Protector of the chief religion', ‘Nasir-Amir-ul-Muminin’. The credit for introducing the tradition of writing the name of the mint on the large silver coins on which these names were inscribed in India also goes to Iltutmish. The credit for introducing the Jital as a specific coin also goes to Iltutmish.

questions.question_text: The main objective of Alauddin Khalji’s economic orders was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Alauddin Khalji’s economic reforms were a special part of his administration. Alauddin’s continuous conquests and Mongol invasions made it imperative for him to maintain a huge army. A lot of money was spent on the state’s employees, soldiers, and civil administration. It was calculated that if the Sultan recruited soldiers in large numbers at a normal salary, the entire treasury would be empty in five years. It is difficult to say whether Alauddin made economic reforms keeping only the army in mind because the economic reform policy was kept running even after the race for conquest had almost ended. But there is no doubt that the army was an important part of his economic reforms.

questions.question_text: According to historian Minhaj, the ideal Sultan of Delhi was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– According to Minhaj, the ideal Sultan of Delhi was Nasiruddin Mahmud. Minhaj has dedicated his book “Tabaqat-i-Nasiri” to his patron Mahmud.

questions.question_text: “Balban was an excellent actor and kept his audience spellbound like modern film stars.” Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Prof. K. A. Nizami has said that Balban was an excellent actor and kept his audience spellbound like modern film stars, and his concept of sovereignty was based on power and justice. Whereas S.B.M. Habibullah has written that “Balban’s only and greatest task was to restore the Sultanate (kingship) to the highest place in the state.” Describing Balban’s weaknesses, Prof. K.A. Nizami also says that he can be credited with establishing peace and order in the state, but his failures appear in other areas. He writes that Balban’s policy of establishing the superiority of the Turks caused harm instead of benefit.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans had close relations with Jain scholars?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007, 2001 Explanation- Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the most tolerant ruler among the Sultans of Delhi. He respected the scholars of all religions. He honored Jain scholar and saint Jinaprabha Suri by calling him to his court. He came into contact with Sufis, Sheikhs, and saints of other various sects. His behavior towards his Hindu subjects was tolerant. On the occasion of the attack on Nagarkot, he did not destroy the Jwala Devi temple. He appointed Hindus to honorable posts. Probably, he was the first among the Sultans of Delhi who participated in festivals, mainly Holi, and he appointed non-Turks and Indian Muslims to official posts, due to which Barani criticized him bitterly and called such people ‘scavenger, gardener, weaver, barber, cook, etc.’.

questions.question_text: Who was the Sultan who made Delhi the capital?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the ruler of the Slave Dynasty, established the capital of the Delhi Sultanate in Lahore. His successor Iltutmish, who is called the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate, was the first to shift the capital from Lahore to Delhi. Iltutmish completed those tasks that Aibak had left incomplete. By ending Yaldoz and Qabacha, he freed the Delhi Sultanate from the claims of ownership of Ghur and Ghazni. By regaining the territories snatched by the Rajput rulers of Rajasthan and curbing the rebellion of Doab, he proved the reality of the Delhi Sultanate. By protecting the Delhi Sultanate from Mongol invasions, he saved it from a great crisis. Dr. K. M. Nizami has written- Aibak had made a rough shape of the Delhi Sultanate. Iltutmish gave it a personality, a position, an inspiring power, a direction, an administrative system, and a ruling class.

questions.question_text: Alauddin Khalji's grain market's first regulation was related to-

options.B: Fixing prices of all types of grains

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001, 2002 Explanation- The first and most difficult regulation (Zabta) of Alauddin’s grain market was related to fixing prices of all types of grain. Khusrau and Barani clearly state that no increase in the fixed prices could be made. Prices of all types of food grains, pulses, cloth, slaves, or even horses, as well as daily necessity items like vegetables, dry fruits, meat, fish, sugarcane, needle, thread, comb, etc., were also fixed. Separate markets were fixed for every item. Grain market for grain, Sarai-i-Adl for cloth, separate markets for horses, slaves, and animals, and a separate market for other items of daily use were fixed. Arrangements were made to store all necessary items in government warehouses for protection in times of difficulty and in such situations, the limit of purchasing necessary items for every person was fixed.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi to introduce non-Islamic customs in the court?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Balban introduced non-Islamic customs in his court in the Delhi Sultanate. For the court, Balban made rules befitting the court of a great Sultan and implemented them strictly. In this area, his ideals were Persian kings. He started many of their traditions in his court. He started the method of ‘Sijda’ (lying on the ground to greet) and ‘Paibos’ (coming near the Sultan's throne and kissing his feet). These customs implemented by Balban were considered non-Islamic. Drinking wine was forbidden for courtiers and they were ordered to come to the court only wearing special clothes. Every year, the Persian festival ‘Nauroz’ began to be celebrated with great pomp in his court. Foreigners were surprised to see the splendor of his court.

questions.question_text: Who said that ‘Delhi is still far away’?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006, 2007 Explanation- There was a difference of opinion between the Delhi Sultanate ruler Ghiyath-ud-din Tughlaq and Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. According to Ibn Battuta, when Sultan Ghiyath-ud-din was in Bengal, he received alarming news about Ulugh Khan’s behavior. He received information that he was increasing the number of his supporters and had become a disciple of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. The Sultan did not have good relations with that Sheikh. The Sultan threatened to punish Ulugh Khan and Nizamuddin Auliya on reaching Delhi, about which Auliya said ‘Delhi is still far away.’ The Sultan returned from Bengal in a hurry and Ulugh Khan had built a wooden palace in a village named Afghanpur, three or four miles away from the new capital Tughlaqabad, for his welcome. That palace was built by Ahmad Ayaz (whom later Ulugh Khan alias Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq made his Wazir) in such a way that by the push of elephants at a specific place, it could fall. Due to the push given during the elephant show, the Sultan died buried in it.

questions.question_text: Sultan Balban formed his court on-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Sultan Balban adopted the traditions of living of Persia to make his sovereignty influential. He acted according to the customs and rituals of Persia in his personal and public life. He also built his court on the basis of Persian tradition and implemented it with similar care for etiquette and formality. He made the splendor of the court such that it reflected the management, prosperity, and glory of his state. Even before the coronation, when Hulagu’s envoys came to India in 1259, Balban prepared a magnificent plan for their welcome, so that it would reflect the management, prosperity, and glory of his state.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Ilbari ruler?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Turk Amirs and military officers chose the most capable and brave Turk as the Sultan and Iltutmish ascended the throne without any difficulty. He was a Turk of the Ilbari tribe; his father Ilem Khan was a tribal leader. After the Gwalior conquest in 1200 AD, he was made the Amir of that city, later Qutb-ud-din gave him the ‘Iqta’ of Badaun to rule. Shamsuddin Iltutmish was an Ilbari Turk but Aibak was not an Ilbari Turk. Balban calls himself an Ilbari Turk but the court historian Minhaj, who gives arguments, does not prove this. Therefore, modern writers have addressed them by names like Pathan, Slave Dynasty, early Turk Sultans, Turk Mamluk, and Ilbari Dynasty. Therefore, calling all the rulers of these dynasties (Muizzi dynasty, Qutbi dynasty, Shamsi dynasty, Balbani dynasty) as ‘early Turk rulers’ or ‘early Turks’ is more logical.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans received the title of ‘Sayyid-ul-Salatin’ from the Caliph?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Among the Sultans of Delhi, Firoz was the first Sultan who gave primacy to the laws of Islam and Ulema in the administration of the state. Other rulers supported religion and adopted a policy of intolerance towards their majority Hindu subjects. Firoz adopted the principles of Islam as the basis of his state policy to get the support of the radical Sunni class and took advice and help from the Ulema class on every occasion. Firoz took the recognition of his Sultan post from the Caliph twice and called himself the ‘Naib’ of the Caliph and got the name of the Caliph inscribed on his coins and declared himself the representative of the Caliph. He broke many temples and took many types of taxes, including Jizya, from Hindus. The Caliph of Egypt granted him the title of “Sayyid-ul-Salatin”. Firoz Tughlaq's main objective was to get the sympathy of radical Muslims and the Ulema class, with whose support he became the Sultan.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Sultan to understand the economic potential of the Doab?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- In the Delhi Sultanate period, Iltutmish first understood the economic importance of Doab. He appointed two thousand Turk soldiers for economic and administrative control over the economically prosperous Doab region. During Iltutmish's reign, Hindu rulers were rebelling against the Turks in Doab. Badaun, Kannauj, Banaras, and Katehar had become free from Turk supremacy and at places like Farrukhabad and Bareilly, Hindus had built their safe forts. To weaken the power of Hindu rulers and to bring the main part of his state, Doab, under his control was necessary for Iltutmish. He adopted a firm and aggressive policy towards Hindu Rajas. Mainly, he attempted to reconquer the places snatched from the Turk state and consolidate his power in the territories under his control and achieved success in reconquering Badaun, Banaras, Kannauj, Katehar, and Bahraich and also established Turk power in Awadh.

questions.question_text: Which of the following four Khans were Alauddin Khalji’s most reliable?

options.A: Ulugh Khan, Zafar Khan, Nusrat Khan, Alp Khan
options.B: Alp Khan, Arkali Khan, Zafar Khan, Akat Khan
options.C: Arkali Khan, Zafar Khan, Akat Khan, Mangti Khan
options.D: Akat Khan, Arkali Khan, Mangti Khan, Zafar Khan

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- For an ambitious ruler like Alauddin, a large and powerful army was necessary, to suppress internal rebellions, to fulfill the desire of India conquest, to base his rule on absolute power, and for protection against Mongol invasions, Alauddin paid full attention to military management. Apart from this, Alauddin was also successful in obtaining the services of some capable commanders of his time. Nusrat Khan, Alp Khan, Ulugh Khan, Zafar Khan, and Malik Kafur not only protected the state from Mongol invasions but also expanded the state. In later times, Ghazi Tughlaq Malik also showed excellent capability in protecting the north-western border. Undoubtedly, Alauddin also had a hand in making these commanders excellent. Because capability can flourish only under the patronage of a capable person.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List I - List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- A. Futuh-us-Salatin - Isami B. Futuhat-i-Firozshahi - Firoz Shah Tughlaq C. Tarikh-i-Firozshahi - Barani D. Khazain-ul-Futuh - Amir Khusrau In Futuh-us-Salatin, Isami criticized Muhammad Tughlaq. Its composition was done in the court of Bahman Shah. ‘Futuhat-i-Firozshahi’ written by Firoz Shah Tughlaq is his own autobiography. Amir Khusrau composed Khazain-ul-Futuh. Which is also known by the name of Tarikh-i-Alai. It has a sycophantic account of fifteen years of the reign of Alauddin Khalji. Barani wrote works with the titles Tarikh-i-Firozshahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari.

questions.question_text: “India is not Arabia, it is not practically possible to convert it into Dar-ul-Islam.” This statement is connected to whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Iltutmish ruled as a Sultan. Personally, he was a true Turk; he considered Turk officers equal to himself and acting as a ruler in front of them was difficult for him. The ‘Iqtas’ played a major role in the administration established by Iltutmish. Among the Sultans of the Delhi Sultanate, especially Iltutmish, started this system for the destruction of Indian feudalism, which was also helpful in connecting the empire with far-flung areas. Iltutmish granted Iqtas to the Turks in large numbers. Iltutmish had said that “India is not Arabia. It is not possible to convert it into Dar-ul-Islam.” This statement was made by Iltutmish to a select committee of Mullahs. Iltutmish established the legal recognition of his Indian territories by obtaining a patent from the Caliph of Baghdad.

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, the post of ‘Rawat-i-Arz’ was given to-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Sultan of Delhi Sultanate, Iltutmish, gave the title of ‘Rawat-i-Arz’ to Imad-ul-Mulk. Imad-ul-Mulk was a slave and on the strength of his capability and talent, he reached the post of ‘Ariz-i-Mumalik’, which Balban also kept intact later. The ministry of Ariz-i-Mumalik was called Diwan-i-Ariz. Ariz-i-Mumalik was the head of the army. His main duties were recruiting soldiers, keeping service records related to soldiers and horses, arranging equipment for the army, planning military campaigns, and inspecting the army.

questions.question_text: Firoz Shah Tughlaq collected 1/10 of the produce as land revenue from-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Usher land (Ushr) was land tax taken from Muslims and irrigation was done on this land by natural resources, due to which 1/10th part of the produce was taken as land tax. Firoz Shah Tughlaq imposed only four taxes accepted by Islamic laws: Kharaj (revenue), Khums (1/5th part of wealth looted in war), Jizya (religious tax on Hindus), and Zakat (2 1/2 percent of income) which was taken from Muslims and spent for their benefit. Firoz Tughlaq, after approval from the Ulema class, also imposed an irrigation tax. Those farmers who used the water of royal canals for irrigation. They had to give 1/10th part of their produce to the government. Apart from these taxes, all other taxes were removed. Government employees were ordered not to demand more than the fair tax. Probably, during his time, the revenue was 1/5th to 1/3rd of the produce. His main task was to fix the revenue of the entire nation based on estimation, due to which the income of the state became fixed.

questions.question_text: Consider the four plans of Muhammad bin Tughlaq- 1. Capital transfer 2. Revenue increase in Doab 4. Token currency Code: 3. Khurasan campaign Find the correct chronological order of the plans from the code given below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Muhammad Tughlaq was an ambitious Sultan who performed new experiments. Under his foreign policy, he had a longing to conquer the whole of India. His four famous plans are as follows- First plan, tax increase in Doab (1325-27 AD). According to Barani, it was increased 10 or 20 times. At the time when tax-increase was done in Doab, there was drought and famine there, therefore farmers left farming and adopted the profession of theft and dacoity and rebelled against the revenue, due to which this plan failed. The second plan was capital transfer (1326-27 AD). Muhammad Tughlaq kept the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad. Due to the greed and possibility of the prosperity of South India and the desire to establish Muslim culture there, this transfer was done. Muhammad Tughlaq introduced token currency (1329-30 AD). According to Barani, due to the shortage of wealth in the treasury and the reason for converting the state expansion policy into action, Muhammad Tughlaq had to introduce token currency. The plan for the Khurasan military campaign was made by M. Tughlaq in 1336-37 AD.

questions.question_text: Whose work was not composed by Amir Khusrau?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, Spl. 2004 During the reign of Alauddin Khalji, there were constant Mongol invasions on the North-West frontier of India. The objective of their invasions was either the conquest of India or a sentiment of resistance. The Mongol invasion of Targhi alerted Alauddin. He strengthened the fort of Siri and had the Delhi fort repaired. The city of Siri was established near Delhi in 1303 AD. Barani called this the 'New City'. He had the old forts of the northern frontier repaired, built some new forts, kept a permanent army in those forts, appointed a separate army and a Subedar (frontier guard) for the protection of the border region, and increased the number and combat efficiency of his army.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is marked as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R)- Assertion (A): Alauddin got the Siri fort built. Reason (R): He wanted to keep Delhi protected from the Mongols. With reference to the above two statements, which one of the following is correct? Code:

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct but (A) is not the correct explanation of (R)
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct and (A) is the correct explanation of (R)

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a eunuch?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Malik Sarvar was a slave of Sultan Muhammad, son of Sardar Firoz Tughlaq, who became Wazir in 1389 AD due to his merit. Sultan Mahmud gave him the title of 'Malik-us-Sharq'. In 1394 AD, he was sent to suppress the rebellion in the Doab. He did not suppress that rebellion, but instead took control of the entire region from Aligarh to Tirhut in Bihar. He behaved like an independent ruler. Although he never assumed the title of Sultan. He did not send any help to the Delhi Sultan at the time of Timur's invasion. He died in 1399 AD. Due to his position, his dynasty was called the Sharqi dynasty. Malik Sarvar was a eunuch who founded the independent Jaunpur kingdom. The city of Jaunpur was settled by Firoz Tughlaq, 34 miles north-west of Varanasi.

questions.question_text: According to Amir Khusrau, the game of chess was invented in-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Amir Khusrau was born in 1253 AD. He came from a family that had maintained close ties with the royal court for many generations. He himself got the opportunity to serve during the reigns of six Sultans. Amir Khusrau's works shed considerable light on social conditions, and this is an area to which other historians of that time did not pay much attention. They left behind information of various kinds related to battles, military campaigns, cities, professions, players, and descriptions of music and dance in their works. Amir Khusrau considers the game of chess to be India's gift. He has described chess in his work 'Khaza'in-ul-Futuh'.

questions.question_text: Who was the first poet to Indianize Persian poetry?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Amir Khusrau was the first poet to Indianize Persian poetry. He was called 'Tuti-e-Hind' (Parrot of India). Writing history was not Amir Khusrau's primary concern. He often took historical subjects in his poems. All such works were composed between 1289-1325. Some of these were written specifically at the request of his patrons, while others were written to please his royal protectors. They were not impartial historians. Even the subjects they used for their Masnavis were not chosen by them. They were told which topic to write about. Even then, as a poet, they could mention such subjects and descriptions about which regular historians had written nothing. The insights they give about the cultural and social life of their time are extremely rare.

questions.question_text: What was the subject of Tibb-e-Sikandari, compiled from Sanskrit sources?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The book 'Tibb-e-Sikandari' or 'Yad-Nussha-Fiya-e-Sikandari', translated from Sanskrit into Persian by Mian Bhua, the Wazir of Sikandar Lodi, is related to medical science.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? Select your correct answer from the code given below- 1. Kili - Alauddin Khalji 2. Siri - Alauddin Khalji 3. Jahanpanah - Muhammad Tughlaq 4. Hazar Sutun - Firoz Tughlaq Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Alauddin founded a city in a village named Siri. Barani called this 'Nau village' or 'New City'. In this city, tanks named 'Hauz-e-Khas' or 'Hauz-e-Rani' were also constructed. The city of Jahanpanah was founded by Muhammad Tughlaq between Rai Pithora and Siri. In this way, 2 and 3 are matched. Alauddin built the Hazar Sutun palace in Siri.

questions.question_text: In which of the following works have the qualities of an ideal Muslim ruler been mentioned?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Ziauddin Barani's work Fatawa-i-Jahandari presents a true picture of the political ideology of the Sultanate period. It mentions the qualities of an ideal Muslim ruler. They suggest that it is necessary for the Badshah to protect Islam, implement Sharia (religious law), and punish non-Muslims. It is the responsibility of the state to prohibit all kinds of immorality. The administrative work should be handed over to pious and religious persons. Philosophers and intellectuals should not get any place in the administration. According to Barani, kingship as an institution can be maintained through fear. Barani feels that a state cannot be run on the basis of Sharia (religious laws). He admits that secular laws (Zawabit) are very necessary.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultanate rulers himself encouraged bribery in administration?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Based on the available facts, it seems that there was widespread corruption during the reign of Firoz Shah. According to Afif, the Sultan's Wazir, Khan-i-Jahan Maqbool, was himself famous for his honesty, but even such a Wazir was unable to stop the corruption. Almost all officials were bribe-takers. Imad-ul-Mulk Bashir Multani had amassed immense wealth through corrupt means. That same wealth became the cause of fights and conspiracies among his slaves after the death of Firoz Shah. The misuse of government positions increased so much that those taxes which had been abolished by calling them un-Islamic, the Amirs would impose those same taxes again. Afif mentions one such horseman to whom the Sultan gave a Tanka from his treasury so that he could bribe to get his horse passed in the review (Arz).

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of various departments created by various Sultans is incorrect?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The establishment of Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was done by Alauddin Khalji under the Finance Department. Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi was established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq under the Agriculture Department. Diwan-i-Khairat was established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq to provide financial assistance to Muslim orphans and widows, and the department named Diwan-i-Riyasat was established by Alauddin Khalji for the implementation of the market control system.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Sultan to appoint 'Amir-i-Sadah'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004, 2007 Explanation- Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the first Sultan of Delhi who created the post of Amir-i-Sadah. An official named Amir-i-Sadah used to look after the administration of a city or a hundred villages. Apart from Mongols, Turks, Afghans, Rajputs, and Indian Muslims were also included among the Sadah Amirs. They rebelled between 1236-45 AD.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements- 1. Delhi Sultans introduced copper coins named Jital. 2. Vijayanagara rulers introduced copper coins named Jital. Which of the following is true regarding the above? Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Among the Delhi Sultans, Iltutmish introduced the silver Tanka and copper coins named Jital. Muhammad Tughlaq introduced beautiful coins of various types in his time and fixed the appropriate value for all of them, but the introduction of token currency (copper or brass coins) remained his specialty. Along with this, the rulers of Vijayanagara had introduced copper coins named Kakini. The most famous coin of Vijayanagara was the gold Varaha (52 grains).

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not established by Firoz Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Alauddin created a department named 'Diwan-i-Mustakhraj' for the purpose of removing the shortcomings inherent in revenue collection and to reform the revenue system. The Mustakhraj was entrusted with the work of checking and recovering the outstanding amounts from the officials collecting revenue.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and choose the correct answer from the codes given below- List I | List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by Minhaj Siraj. This book contains the only account of the early conquest of India by the Turks, which is dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud. Futuh-us-Salatin is the work of Isami. In this book, he had bitterly criticized Muhammad Tughlaq. Tarikh-i-Firozshahi was written by Shams-i-Siraj Afif - in this book, he has written about Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq and Muhammad Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi made a rule that land revenue would not be increased by more than 1/10 or 1/11 in a year?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- According to Barani, the Sultan (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) ordered that the Diwani officials should fix 1/10 or 1/11 part of the produce for the levy. The traditional rate of 1/5 was going on, which became 1/2 in Alauddin's time and which Mubarak Shah had reduced and perhaps made 1/5 again. It is difficult to believe how Ghiyasuddin could solve the economic distress at the 1/10 or 1/11 rate.

questions.question_text: Under the Delhi Sultanate, which of the following coins was not in circulation?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : During the Delhi Sultanate, coins like 'Dehliwal', 'Tanka', Jital, Shashgani, 'Dogani', 'Adli', 'Khaifali', 'Bahluli' etc., were in circulation. 'Dam' was not in circulation during the Sultanate period. The introduction of 'Dam' was done by Sher Shah Suri. The following changes were made in the monetary policy during the time of Sher Shah: (a) A pure silver coin, introduced by the name of 'Rupee'. (b) Pure copper coins were called 'Dam'. (c) The weight of silver rupees was equal to 180 grains, in which there was 173 grains of pure silver. (d) The weight of Dam was fixed at 380 grains. (e) The coin named Dogani was introduced by Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians was taken prisoner by the Mongols?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The name of Amir Khusrau is noteworthy among the scholars of the Sultanate period. He was born in 1253 AD. He came from a family that had maintained close ties with the royal court for many generations. He got the opportunity to serve under 6 Sultans. In the beginning, he remained in the service of Balban's eldest son, Muhammad. In a confrontation with the Mongols, Muhammad was killed and the Mongols also took Amir Khusrau prisoner, but he escaped from jail and became associated with Balban's royal court.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi first imposed a ban on Muslim women visiting shrines located outside Delhi?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq imposed restrictions on Muslim women going out of their homes, including restrictions on visiting tombs outside the city of Delhi. The source also notes that Sikandar Lodi later kept similar conditions for Muslim women.

questions.question_text: What was the name of that Jain saint with whom Muhammad bin Tughlaq held discussions?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq was a supporter of a liberal perspective contrary to the Ulema and contrary to the Sufis, he believed in living an active life rather than being detached from the world. Although he had full faith in Islam, he also wanted to gain knowledge regarding other religions. Proofs of his debates with Jain Acharyas Rajshekhar and Jinaprabha Suri and gifting them money, etc., are found.

questions.question_text: According to historian Ziauddin Barani, the ideal Sultan of Delhi was -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : According to historian Ziauddin Barani, the ideal Sultan of Delhi was Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Both Barani and Afif consider Firoz Shah Tughlaq an ideal and best Sultan. In Tarikh-i-Firozshahi, Barani has written 'After Sultan Muizzuddin bin Sam, no other ruler, noble, kind, merciful, recognizer of others' rights, duty-bound, and believer in the rules of Islam, sat on the throne of Delhi like Sultan Firoz Shah of that time and age.' In the same book, Barani has declared Firoz Shah an ideal Sultan.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an octagonal tomb?
questions.explanation: Along with square tombs of Delhi Sultans, a large number of octagonal tombs were built. Their beginning started in 1368–69 AD with the tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani in Nizamuddin, Delhi. This design was later adopted with changes in later tombs, including Sikandar Lodi's tomb.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of the Sultanate period started irrigation tax?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- After the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Firoz Tughlaq ascended the throne in 1351 AD. He removed 24 taxes which caused a lot of trouble to the state's public. ‘Ghari’ and ‘Charai’ taxes were also included in these taxes. He also reduced the rate of land revenue. He collected only four taxes according to Sharia: Jizya, Zakat, Khums, and Kharaj. Firoz also imposed ‘Jizya’ tax on Brahmins, who were free from this tax till now. Firoz, after consulting the Ulema, also imposed a new tax called irrigation tax (Haqq-i-Shar). This tax was taken only from those who used water from government canals for irrigation.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Balban minted coins in memory of the late Caliph. Reason (R): The end of the Baghdad Caliphate was the greatest loss to Muslim power. Which of the following is correct regarding the above statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are true, but (A) is not the correct explanation of (R) no.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- Balban used to discuss taking the Caliph's permission to use political power. He knew about the fall of Baghdad and the end of the Caliph, yet he emphasized the recognition of political power of the Caliph, who was the leader of the political community of all Muslims. The name of the late Caliph was inscribed on his coins and it was read in the 'Khutba' of mosques. In 1258 AD, Hulagu Khan ended the Baghdad Caliphate. Although it had no political impact, it was a loss for Muslim power.

questions.question_text: Muhammad Tughlaq created a new department named 'Diwan-i-Kohi', its main task was
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- Muhammad bin Tughlaq was a ruler with forward-thinking who, for the development of the Sultanate era, not only conducted many new experiments but also made radical reforms in the prevailing systems. One of these reforms was the establishment of Diwan-i-Kohi. The main objective behind the establishment of this institution was to develop and expand cultivable land with the help of the state. In this way, the main objective of establishing 'Diwan-i-Kohi' was to make barren and desolate land cultivable. The chief officer of this department was Amir-i-Kohi. Apart from this, Muhammad bin Tughlaq also made loans (Sondhar) available at very low interest for the help of farmers.

questions.question_text: Sultan Firoz Tughlaq's 'Khutba' included the names of all preceding Sultans. Which of the following names was the only exception?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Firoz Tughlaq was a ruler full of religious fanaticism and made Islam the basis of his rule. He was the first Sultanate era ruler who expressed reverence towards the Caliph of Egypt and called himself his representative. During his reign, he received special letters of authority and robes of honor from the Caliph of Egypt twice. Apart from this, he got his name inscribed on his coins along with the name of the Caliph. In his Khutba, he included the names of all the preceding rulers except Qutbuddin Aibak. letter and robes of honor of the ruler. Apart from this, he got his own name inscribed on his coins along with the name of the Caliph. In his Khutba, he included the names of all the preceding rulers except Qutbuddin Aibak.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not related to Sikandar Lodi?

options.A: Land measurement for land revenue determination
options.C: Abolition of tax on food grains
options.D: Following Bahlul Lodi's theory of kingship

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - After the death of Bahlul Lodi, his third son 'Nizam Khan' ascended the throne of the Lodi dynasty by the name of Sikandar Lodi. He was the son of a Hindu woman, for this reason, some court nobles opposed his accession to the throne. But ignoring these oppositions, he sat on the throne of Delhi in 1489 AD. He did many important works during his reign, in which he developed a new standard 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' for land revenue determination. Since he was an educated person, he had an interest in literary compositions. For this purpose, he established a translation department. On his own order, he got a book of Ayurveda translated under the name 'Tibb-e-Sikandari'. He abolished the tax levied on food grains. But overturning his father's theory of kingship, he adopted Turkish and Hindu principles instead of Afghan ideals.

questions.question_text: Among the following Sultans, who conversed with Jinaprabha Suri until midnight?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation- Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the most tolerant ruler among the Sultans of Delhi. He respected the scholars of all religions. He called the Jain scholar and saint Jinaprabha Suri to the court and honored him. He had come in contact with Sufis, Sheikhs, and saints of various other sects. His behavior towards his Hindu subjects was full of tolerance. On the occasion of the invasion of Nagarkot, he did not destroy the temple of Jwala Devi. He had appointed Hindus to respected positions. He was probably the first Sultan of Delhi who participated in festivals, mainly Holi, and he had also appointed non-Turks and Indian Muslims to government positions, for which Barani criticized him bitterly and called such persons 'scavengers, gardeners, weavers, barbers, cooks, etc.'

questions.question_text: In whose time was the term 'Sondhar' used as a loan given to farmers?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation- Muhammad bin Tughlaq provided agricultural loans named 'Sondhar' to farmers for their development. This loan was made available to farmers from the state at a very low interest. When Firoz Shah Tughlaq became the ruler, he waived the loan named Sondhar.

questions.question_text: Among the Delhi Sultans, which Sultan adopted the political traditions of Iran and synchronized them with the Indian environment?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation–The element of tradition in the kingship of early Turkish rulers came from Persia. They adopted Persian kingship traditions and ideas. Both Iltutmish and Balban connected their lineage with the mythological Afrasiyab mentioned in Firdausi's Shahnameh. Even while choosing Raziya as his successor, Iltutmish took inspiration from the Iranian tradition where examples of daughters ascending the throne after their father are found.

questions.question_text: Among the following Delhi Sultans, whose mother was a Hindu? Select the correct answer based on the code given below: (i) Nasiruddin Khusrau (ii) Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (iii) Firoz Tughlaq (iv) Sikandar Lodi Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation–Nasiruddin Khusrau - He was an Indian Muslim. Initially, he was a Gujarati Hindu of a low caste called Barwari or Gadariya; later, he accepted the religion of Islam. He remained the Sultan of Delhi from 15 April to 5 September 1320. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq - He was born in a low family. His father was a Turkish slave of Balban and his mother was a Jat woman from Punjab. He ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320-1325 AD. Firoz Tughlaq - Firoz was born in 1309. He was the son of Rajab, the younger brother of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq. His mother was the daughter of Raja Mal, a Bhatti Rajput King situated in Abohar in the Hisar district of modern eastern Punjab. His reign was from 1351 to 1388 AD. Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517 AD) - He was the son of a goldsmith mother.

questions.question_text: Which dynasty was ruling Warangal at the time of Allauddin's invasion?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation–The failure of the 1303 AD Telangana invasion was hurting Allauddin's heart, and he was worried about washing away that stigma as soon as possible. In 1309 AD, he sent Malik Kafur to complete this task. The capital of the Kakatiya kingdom, Warangal, was surrounded by strong walls. A sudden attack was made. Kafur surrounded Warangal and caused heavy damage to the inner defense army. Therefore, the Raja surrendered. He gifted 300 elephants, 7000 horses, and a huge amount of cash and gems to the invader as compensation for war damages and promised to pay an annual tribute.

questions.question_text: The Vijayanagara Empire was established during whose reign?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation–In 1335 AD, when Jalaluddin, the governor of Madurai, declared himself independent, the flames of rebellion against Tughlaq rule flared up in the entire South. Muhammad Tughlaq sent Harihar and Bukka to the South as Tughlaq commanders, and they suppressed the rebellion of Kapili. Both Harihar and Bukka came under the influence of a saint named Vidyaranya and they established the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 AD. Both were sons of Sangama and they named their dynasty 'Sangama Dynasty' after their father's name. They received a lot of inspiration from Madhava Vidyaranya and his brother, the famous Vedic scholar Sayana.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which was NOT a reason for Balban to adopt the policy of consolidation instead of conquest?

options.C: The desire of Indian rulers to uproot Turkish rule

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation–Balban made good arrangements for the protection of the Turkish Sultanate and gave it new life; this was his greatest work. He was a person with a strong will. He restored internal peace and, by making proper arrangements for the defense of the north-western borders of the Sultanate, saved it from Mongol invasions. He did not try to win the land of neighboring Hindu rulers. Because of his strong willpower and strict nature, he crushed the power of big Turkish nobles and gave Turkish rule a new form in this country. Therefore, he was not a person with a weak nature.

questions.question_text: Among the following Sultans, who was NOT a child of Iltutmish, but was the last successor of his dynasty?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation–Ruknuddin Firoz was the eldest living son of Iltutmish; his mother's name was Shah Turkan, while Raziya was the eldest daughter who ruled from 1236-1240 AD. Muizuddin Bahram Shah was the third son of Iltutmish who ruled from 1240-1242 AD after the fall of Raziya. Nasiruddin Mahmud sat on the throne on 10 June 1246 AD after the fall of Allauddin Masud Shah; he was not the child but the grandson of Iltutmish, who ruled with simplicity until 1265 AD. He was the last successor of Iltutmish's dynasty. After him, Balban sat on the throne, who had ruled until 1287 AD.

questions.question_text: Among the following sons of Allauddin, who was born to his wife Jhatyapali, who was the daughter of King Ramachandra Deva of Devagiri?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation–After Allauddin's death, Malik Kafur made Allauddin's 6-year-old minor son Shihabuddin Umar, born to Ramachandra Deva's daughter Jhatyapali, the Sultan and himself became his guardian. He got Allauddin's eldest son Khizr Khan and his younger brother Shadi Khan blinded. Allauddin's third son, Mubarak Khan, whose age was about 18 years, was taken prisoner by Kafur and he sent some of his men to extract his eyes, but Mubarak bribed those men and sent them back to kill Kafur, and they completed this task easily. Two months after this incident, he deposed his brother Shihabuddin Umar, blinded him, and took the throne himself.

questions.question_text: Who wrote Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation–Sultan Firoz Tughlaq had a special love for history. Ziauddin Barani and Shams-i-Siraj Afif wrote their books under his patronage. The Sultan himself wrote his autobiography named 'Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi'. Firoz had some Sanskrit books translated into Persian; among them, he named one 'Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi'. Due to Firoz's personal interest and state patronage, the study of religious scriptures, law, and other branches of Islamic learning received encouragement.

questions.question_text: Who has given the most reliable account of Malik Kafur's southern campaign?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The reliable account of Malik Kafur's southern victory has been given by Amir Khusrau. The details of the southern victory carried out under Allauddin's instructions are found in 'Khazain-ul-Futuh', while 'Ashiqa' describes the romantic love between Deval Devi and Khizr Khan. 'Nuh-i-Sipihr' contains a description of Indian climate and the weather here.

questions.question_text: Timur was so impressed by the architecture of Delhi that he took with him artisans, stonemasons, and skilled workers from India, so that he could get the same type of buildings made in his capital –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation–On 18 December 1398 AD, Timur took control of Delhi. The conqueror received immense wealth in loot. Every soldier became rich, and there remained no such pauper who did not have at least twenty slaves with him. Timur chose craftsmen from Delhi and sent them to Samarkand, where they built a famous Jama Masjid for him.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Among the pairs, the correctly matched one is Amir Khusrau's Tughlaqnama. Other authors and their works are as follows: Author - Works Al-Biruni - Tarikh-i-Hind Hasan Nizami - Taj-ul-Ma'asir Barani - Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi Minhaj-us-Siraj - Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
