questions.question_text: Among the following Sufis, who has called India the 'Heaven of the Earth'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation–Amir Khusrau mentions the Indian climate, animals, birds, religious beliefs, and people's language in his famous Masnavi Nuh-i-Sipihr (Nine Skies). He compares India with the gardens of heaven. He praises the fertility of Indian land, its temperate climate, and peacocks. Here and there, he rates India superior to other countries of the world.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi laid the foundation of the fort of Siri and built it?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–In 1303 AD, Allauddin Khalji laid the foundation of the fort of Siri and built it. He established the city of Siri, built a palace with a thousand pillars in it, Jamaith Khana Masjid in the shrine of Nizamuddin Auliya, and built 'Alai Darwaza' near the Qutub Minar.

questions.question_text: The ruler of Bundelkhand who was defeated by Qutubuddin Aibak was–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–After dealing with Prithviraj, Paramardideva had to face the fierce attack of the Turks, which he could not survive. In 1203 AD, Qutubuddin defeated Paramardideva and captured the fort of Kalinjar. Paramardideva died in the fort of Kalinjar itself.

questions.question_text: On the orders of Sultan Balban, who among the following nobles was publicly punished with whipping?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–Malik Baqbaki, the Iqtadar (Governor) of Badaun, was whipped in front of the public on the orders of Sultan Balban because he had beaten a slave to death. Similarly, Haibat Khan, the Iqtadar of Awadh, was punished with 500 lashes for the crime of killing one of his slaves.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true regarding Muhammad bin Tughlaq?

options.B: He used to drink Ganges water.
options.D: He never went to any temple.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Muhammad bin Tughlaq had appointed Hindus to respected posts. Probably, he was the first Sultan among Delhi Sultans who participated in Hindu festivals, mainly Holi. He also appointed non-Turkish and Indian Muslims to government posts, due to which Barani criticized him harshly and called such people scavenger, gardener, weaver, barber, cook, etc. Apart from this, he also used to drink Ganges water and respected all religions. His behavior towards his Hindu subjects was also tolerant. On the occasion of the attack on Nagarkot, he did not destroy the temple of Jwaladevi.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan among the following shifted the capital of the Sultanate from Delhi to Agra?
questions.explanation: The great ruler of the Lodi dynasty, Sikandar Lodi, shifted the capital of the Sultanate from Delhi to Agra. He founded Agra in 1504 AD. Sikandar was a lover of knowledge. He used to write poetry in Persian under the pseudonym 'Gulrukhi'

questions.question_text: During which campaign did Muhammad bin Tughlaq die?
questions.explanation: During the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, the rebellion in Gujarat was easily suppressed, but Taghi ran away to Sindh. The Sultan set out towards Sindh to eliminate Taghi. On the way, the Sultan fell ill, and he died near Thatta on 20 March 1351 AD

questions.question_text: Where did Allauddin Khalji get the slave named Kafur from?
questions.explanation: Allauddin Khalji obtained a slave named Malik Kafur during the Gujarat campaign. Malik Kafur had a very large contribution to Allauddin's southern victory. In 1307 AD, Malik Kafur had defeated the ruler of Devagiri, Ramachandradeva

questions.question_text: A Lodi Sultan who used to sit on a carpet instead of sitting on the throne, he was:
questions.explanation: Bahlol Lodi was the founder of the Lodi dynasty. He sat on the royal throne in 1451 AD. According to the author of Tarikh-i-Daudi, Abdullah, he never sat on the throne and ruled by sitting on a carpet with his nobles. Bahlol Lodi introduced a coin named 'Bahloli'

questions.question_text: Who was the Sultan in Delhi at the time of Timur's invasion?
questions.explanation: The great Mongol warlord of Central Asia, Timur, invaded India in 1398 AD. At that time, Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Tughlaq dynasty was ruling. Timur's invasion proved to be a fatal blow for both the Tughlaq dynasty and Delhi. Timur looted the whole of Delhi badly

questions.question_text: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi who added the word 'Ghazi' with his name?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Tughlaq dynasty was Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, who sat on the royal throne in 1320 AD with the title Ghazi Malik. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the first in the Delhi Sultanate to have canals built for agriculture

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: The last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was the Lodi dynasty. Babur defeated the Lodi dynasty ruler Ibrahim Lodi in 1526 AD and founded the Mughal dynasty. In the Delhi Sultanate, the Slave dynasty, Khalji dynasty, Tughlaq dynasty, Sayyid dynasty, and finally the Lodi dynasty ruled. The dynasty that ruled for the most years was the Tughlaq dynasty, and the dynasty that ruled for the fewest years was the Khalji dynasty

questions.question_text: To which king did Allauddin Khalji give the jagir of Navsari and the title of Rai Rayan?
questions.explanation: Allauddin Khalji gave the jagir of Navsari and the title of Rai Rayan to Ramachandradeva of Devagiri. Allauddin gave one lakh gold tankas to Ramachandradeva. The first invasion of Muslims on South India happened during the time of Jalaluddin on the ruler of Devagiri, Ramachandra

questions.question_text: Whose statement is this that the royal jewels and musical instruments of Delhi are superior to those artisans found in the entire Muslim world?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation–Amir Khusrau has said in his book that the royal jewels and musical instruments of Delhi are superior to those artisans found in the entire Muslim world.

questions.question_text: The following quotation belongs to whom? ``We Indians are capable of speaking foreign languages but the Chinese, Mongols, Turks, and Arabs are incapable of speaking "our Hindi language"..... Indians do not go to other countries for knowledge-seeking, others have to come here.... India has given the world counting (mathematics), Panchatantra stories, and Chess........''
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation–It is Amir Khusrau's statement that "We Indians are capable of speaking foreign languages but the Chinese, Mongols, Turks, and Arabs are incapable of speaking "our language"..... Indians did not use to go to other countries for knowledge seeking. Others have to come here..... India has given the world counting, Panchatantra stories, and Chess....''

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The author of Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is Minhaj-us-Siraj. This is a book written in Persian. It contains a description of the events of Indian history during the time of the rulers of the Slave dynasty (Mamluk Sultans).

questions.question_text: During the Sultanate period, by what name was the Chief Justice known?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- During the Sultanate period, the Chief Justice was known as 'Qazi-ul-Quzat'. Often, the post of Qazi-ul-Quzat and Sadr-us-Sudur was given to the same person. Sadr-us-Sudur was the head of the religious department. His main work was to spread the laws of the Islamic religion among the public. GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018

questions.question_text: Who founded Agra?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 PGT History, 2013 Explanation – Sikandar Lodi founded the city of Agra in 1504 AD with the aim of keeping his authority secure over the rulers of Rajasthan and establishing control over trade routes. In 1506 AD, Sikandar Lodi made Agra his capital.

questions.question_text: 'Masahat' was related to the following:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation–'Masahat' was related to land. This system was introduced by Allauddin Khalji. In this, the determination of produce was done on the basis of land measurement.

questions.question_text: The word 'Milk' is a
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation–'Milk' is an Arabic word which was used for property.

questions.question_text: By what name was the first-class Mughal infantry soldier known?
questions.explanation: During the Mughal period, the number of infantry soldiers was quite high; they were called Pyade or Pihadi. According to Abul Fazl, there were nine categories of infantry soldiers in which matchlock-men, darban, khidmatia, mewra, shamshirbaz, pehalwan etc., were prominent. The first-class Mughal infantry soldier was known as Ahadi. They provided assistance in the security system of the Mughal rulers

questions.question_text: Arrange the following daughters of the Mughal royal family in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order is (C) Gulbadan Begum - 1523 (birth) (A) Jahan Ara Begum - 1614 (birth) (D) Roshan Ara Begum - 1617 (birth) (B) Zeb-un-Nissa Begum – 1638 (birth) Note: Gulbadan Begum was the daughter of Babur and sister of Humayun. Jahan Ara Begum and Roshan Ara Begum were daughters of Shah Jahan and sisters of Aurangzeb. Zeb-un-Nissa Begum was the daughter of Aurangzeb and sister of Bahadur Shah I.

questions.question_text: Babur started new military tactics in India. These included tying carts/wagons with iron chains, protecting them with trenches, and providing flanking parties (Tulugma). Where did Babur take these tactics from?
questions.explanation: Babur, the founder of the Mughal dynasty, adopted new military strategies in India, which he had learned during his conflicts with the Ottoman Empire in Central Asia and the Uzbeks. He learned the use of muskets from the Persians, cavalry from the Turks, flanking parties (Tulugma – formation system) from the Uzbeks, and formation strategy from the Mongols and Afghans. Along with this, following the Ottoman (Rumi) tactic, he made a place to keep cannons between two carts at the height of a shield. In the battles of Panipat and Khanwa, he got trenches dug in front for secondary security. By using all these novel military systems on a large scale, he paved the way for his victory

questions.question_text: In the context of the security of routes in Mughal administration, which of the following statements is/are true?
questions.explanation: Mughal administration was a centralized system based on military power, which was based on 'checks and balances'. Since the Mughal empire was completely centralized, the power of the Badshah was immense; even then, there was a council of ministers to conduct the activities of the administration. The Mughal administration was divided into five levels: central level, provincial level, Sarkar (district) administration, Pargana administration, and village level administration. The head of the provincial level administration was the Subahdar, and he used to ensure law and order in the Subah, protect and increase the interests of the public, and decide criminal cases of faujdari suppress rebellions, and ensure the security and construction of bridges, sarais, roads, etc. Regarding the security of routes in Mughal administration, what is true: ♦ The security of routes was considered a major responsibility of the administration. ♦ Caravans, sarais, Banjara tandas, which were usually armed, and boats in rivers were organized for security against robberies and looting occurring on the routes. ♦ In the Mughal Empire, the official in whose area theft or robbery occurred had to recover the goods or had to pay compensation to the victim himself. ♦ Officials adopted a policy of cruelty to fulfill this responsibility and looted suspicious villages.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following conquest campaigns of Akbar in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The order of Jalaluddin Muhammad Akbar's (1556-1605 AD) conquest campaigns Bengal - In 1574, Akbar sent a campaign against Daud in Bengal under the leadership of Munim Khan, and Akbar himself also went for the Bengal conquest. He appointed Munim Khan as the Subahdar of Bengal. In 1575, Daud Khan surrendered. Kabul - Kabul's ruler and Akbar's half-brother Mirza Muhammad Hakim attempted to get the throne of India by joining with the rebels. Akbar appointed Prince Murad against him and personally entered the fort of Kabul on 9 August 1581 AD. Mirza Hakim begged for forgiveness, and he was forgiven. After the death of Mirza Hakim in 1585 AD, Man Singh was appointed for the occupation of Kabul. Sindh - Mirza Jani Beg was the independent ruler here, Akbar appointed Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan in 1590 for the conquest of Sindh. Mirza Jani Beg accepted the suzerainty of Akbar and he was given a mansab of three thousand. Khandesh - In 1591 AD, Akbar sent Faizi as his envoy to Khandesh, and King Ali Khan of Khandesh accepted independence.

questions.question_text: In the Mughal period, among the following officials, which one is related to 'Karkhana'?
questions.explanation: Badshah Akbar appointed several Diwans to keep control over the Wazir. Among them, the first was, 'Diwan-i-Khalisa', who managed the Khalisa land of the empire. The second, 'Diwan-i-Tan', who looked after the work related to jagirs and salaries. The third, 'Diwan-i-Buyutat', who kept the account of income and expenditure of various Karkhanas. Diwan-i-Tabin kept the accounts of soldiers. The central treasury was looked after by an official named 'Mushrif-i-Khazana'.

questions.question_text: What was 'Ijara' in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, 'Ijara' was a system of revenue farming. Zulfiqar Khan was the Prime Minister of Mughal Badshah Jahandar Shah. He promoted the 'Ijara System'. Under this, the government started making this contract with 'Ijaradars' i.e., revenue contractors and middlemen, in return for collecting land revenue at a fixed rate, that they would pay a fixed amount of money to the government, in return, they were left free to collect as much revenue as they could from the farmers. This increased the exploitation of farmers. But under this system, no Ijaradar ever deposited the fixed amount in the treasury

questions.question_text: Who were 'Dakhili' in the Mughal military system?
questions.explanation: In the Mughal military system, Dakhili soldiers were supplementary soldiers, whose appointment was made by the state, although they were kept in the service of Mansabdars Ahadis were the soldiers of the Badshah; they received salary and equipment from the state. They were also bodyguards of the Badshah. Among military officials, the most prestigious rank was Khan-i-Zaman.

questions.question_text: In the context of Sher Shah Suri, which statement(s) is/are true? (1) He became the ruler of India after the Battle of Kannauj. (2) He abolished the post of Governor of Bengal and divided it into 47 Sarkars, which were directly under his control. Select the correct answer using the code given below-
questions.explanation: On 17 May 1540 AD, in the Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram, Sher Shah defeated the Mughal ruler Humayun and became the ruler of India. Sher Shah, looking at the distant geographical location of Bengal, divided it into 47 Sarkars, which were under his direct control

questions.question_text: Of how many grains was Sher Shah's silver rupee?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah's coins were mainly of two types. The silver rupee was of 178 grains and the copper dam was of 380 grains. Sher Shah increased the number of mints to 23. Among these, some of the places where they were, are Agra, Gwalior, Ujjain, Lucknow, Shergarh (Sasaram), Abot, Sakkar, Bakkar (Sindh)

questions.question_text: When did Aurangzeb impose Jizya?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb imposed Jizya tax in the 22nd year of his reign, on 12 April 1679 AD Special Facts Pilgrimage tax – 1663 AD Ban on music – 1669 AD Ban on Jharokha Darshan – 1669 AD Ban on Tuladan – 1670 AD

questions.question_text: What was the work of 'Sawanih-nigar' in Mughal administration?
questions.explanation: Sawanih-nigar – An important agency in Mughal administration to keep control over Jagirdars was 'Sawanih-nigar', who sent reports of the activities of Jagirdars and the current situation of Jagirs to the center

questions.question_text: What was meant by 'Rai' in Sher Shah's administration?
questions.explanation: In Sher Shah's administration, 'Rai' meant the demand of the state Special Facts A main feature of Zabti was measuring land and preparing a list of 'Rai' or crop rates. Cultivable land was divided into three categories: excellent, medium, and low. The standard per-bigha produce of all three categories of land was added, and by dividing by three, its average was extracted. In this way, one-third of that average was determined as the state's demand (Rai). Although the state's demand was shown in the form of grain (Dastur or Dastur-ul-Amal). In the eleventh year of his reign, Akbar introduced a uniform price list based on the rates prevalent in the royal camp. Later, it became necessary to keep local prices in mind, based on which the state's demand was made. When the Ain-i-Dahsala system was accepted, this system was abandoned.

questions.question_text: What was meant by Mahsul?
questions.explanation: Mahsul or Hasil-e-Hasil – This was the income actually received from the Jagir Special Facts 1. Khalisa Mahal – The Badshah's land. In Jahangir's time, Khalisa income decreased and remained only the twentieth part (5%) of the total income. 2. Mahal-i-Paibaqi – Reserved and unallotted land for Jagir allotment. 3. Jamadaran-e-Raiyati – Jamadaran who pay land revenue. 4. Jamadaran-e-Zortalab – Jamadaran who do not pay land revenue. The Higher Education Service Commission has considered the answer to this question as (b).

questions.question_text: Where did Murshid Quli Khan start the Zabti system?
questions.explanation: Murshid Quli Khan started the Zabti system from the Deccan Special Facts In 1652 AD, when Aurangzeb was made the Subahdar of the South for the second time, then along with him, the Persian Murshid Quli Khan was appointed as the Diwan of the South. Originally, Murshid Quli Khan was a companion of Ali Mardan Khan. Aurangzeb and Murshid jointly improved the Deccan's land revenue system. Murshid Quli Khan is called the 'Todar Mal of the South' because he implemented Todar Mal's measurement and tax determination system there.

questions.question_text: Against which Mughal commander did Rani Durgavati fight her last battle?
questions.explanation: Akbar sent Asaf Khan in 1564 AD to occupy Garh-Katanga. Near Chauragarh, Rani Durgavati faced the huge Mughal army. She fought bravely for two days. Finally, considering defeat certain, she stabbed herself with a dagger to protect her honor and committed suicide

questions.question_text: Who is famous for cutting the nose of the invading Mughal army?
questions.explanation: For cutting the nose of the invading Mughal army, Rani Karnavati of Garhwal is famous

questions.question_text: In which year of Akbar's reign were Mansabs provided?
questions.explanation: There is a reference to 'Mansab' being provided for the first time in the eleventh year of Akbar's reign. This was not a title or rank-name, rather it gave an idea of the position of any person or Amir in the Mughal administrative service order Special Facts On 14 February 1556 AD, at the age of 13 years and 4 months, Akbar's coronation took place at Kalanaur in Gurdaspur, Punjab. The coronation was done under the supervision of Bairam Khan on a brick throne. This coronation was opposed by Abul Mali.

questions.question_text: From the time of which ruler did Jharokha-Darshan stop?
questions.explanation: Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb was the son of Shah Jahan. He was born on 3 November 1618 AD in the womb of Mumtaz Mahal at Dohad (Ujjain). Aurangzeb was the only ruler of the Mughal Empire who had two coronations, the first coronation was held after the victory in the Battle of Samugarh on 31 July 1658 AD and the second and actual coronation was completed in Delhi on 15 June 1659 after his decisive victory in the battles of Khajwa and Deorai. Aurangzeb was a religion-devout Muslim. He also ended the evils prevalent in the Islamic religion, such as stopping the practice of Jharokha Darshan because he considered it against Islam

questions.question_text: Among the following, which Mughal Badshah awarded the title 'Nadir-uz-Zaman' to the Jain saint Siddha Chandra?
questions.explanation: The Mughal Badshah Jahangir awarded the title of "Nadir-uz-Zaman" to the Jain saint Siddha Chandra. Jahangir banned animal slaughter in the empire on Sundays (Akbar's birthday) and Thursdays (his own coronation day). Jahangir was also interested in the Christian religion; he had taken religious education of Christianity from the Portuguese priest 'Father Xavier'

questions.question_text: Among the following, who held the post of "Vakil-us-Saltanat" in the first four years of Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: During Akbar's reign, Bairam Khan was on the post of 'Vakil-us-Saltanat' in the first four years. From 1556 AD to 1560 AD, Bairam Khan had more influence on Akbar because he was a minor at that time. Bairam Khan was a follower of the Shia sect. He was born in Badakhshan. He used to serve as a soldier in Humayun's army. With his devotion to duty and loyalty, he soon became a confidant of Humayun. After the death of Humayun, Bairam Khan provided protection to Akbar in governance and administration and remained seated on the post of "Vakil-us-Saltanat" in the initial years

questions.question_text: When Prince Muhammad Kam Bakhsh ordered to cut his right hand, Shaikh Khan said, 'This is a base behavior, which you have received from your mother. This hand, which you have got cut without any fault, was the one that taught you archery.' Identify that mother:
questions.explanation: Prince Muhammad Kam Bakhsh was the youngest son of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, who was born from his wife Udaipuri Begum. The above statement was said by Shaikh Khan after the Prince ordered to cut his teacher's hand. Dilras Banu was the first and main wife of Emperor Aurangzeb. Whereas Nawab Bai was the intermediary wife of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Nadira Begum was a Mughal princess and the wife of Prince Dara Shikoh, the eldest son of the fifth Mughal ruler Shah Jahan

questions.question_text: There are two statements given below: one is written as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): In the time of Aurangzeb, the claim on the property of deceased Mansabdars was limited to Mutaliba. Reason (R): In 1691, Aurangzeb issued a farman to his officials that they should not confiscate the property of those Amirs whose heirs were in government service, because the heirs could be asked to pay the Mutaliba contracted by the deceased Amirs. In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
options.C: (A) is correct, but (R) is not correct
options.D: (A) is not correct, but (R) is correct

questions.explanation: Mansab is a word of Persian language, which means rank. It had two parts, Zat and Sawar. Zat was personal rank while Sawar meant the number of cavalrymen. Aurangzeb started the Mashrut in the Mansabdari system; in his time, the number of Hindu Mansabdars (33 percent) was the highest. In Aurangzeb's time, the claim on the property of deceased Mansabdars was limited to Mutaliba. In 1691 AD, a farman was issued by Aurangzeb that the property of such deceased Mansabdars should not be confiscated whose heirs are in the service of the Mughal Sultanate, because such contracted Mutaliba will be paid by the heirs of the deceased Amirs

questions.question_text: Arrange Akbar's various declarations/orders in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of Akbar's 'declarations/orders' is as follows – (1) Ban on making wives, children, and relatives of war prisoners slaves (End of slavery system) --------- (1562 AD) (2) Pilgrimage tax abolished ---------- (1563 AD) (3) Abolition of Jizya tax for the first time ----------- (1564 AD) (4) Issuing the Fathnama of Chittor --------- (1568 AD)

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II List-I (Mughal Ruler) List-II (Estimated share of Khalisa in total Jama)
questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows List-I (Mughal Ruler) List-II (Estimated share of Khalisa in total Jama) (A) Akbar - 1/4 (B) Jahangir - 1/20 (C) Shah Jahan - 1/7 (D) Aurangzeb - 1/5

questions.question_text: From where did envoys come to Aurangzeb during his reign?
questions.explanation: Between 1661-1667 AD, some foreign Muslim powers sent delegations to Aurangzeb. Among them (Sharif of Mecca, Persia, Balkh, Bukhara, Qajar, Khiva, Abyssinia, and Shah-e-Nau, Basra, Yemen and Mocha's Turkish chiefs, and Constantinople) one delegation came

questions.question_text: Buland Darwaza was built in memory of which of Akbar's conquests?
questions.explanation: Buland Darwaza is the highest entrance gate in India built in the southern gate of Jama Masjid. This 134-foot-high gate, built on a 42-foot-high plinth that is equipped with stairs, is a total of 176 feet high from the ground. Its construction was ordered by Akbar in 1573 AD in memory of his Gujarat victory. In 1601 AD, after the conquest of Asirgarh, the height of this gate was further increased. That is why it is considered a symbol of both the Gujarat victory and the Deccan victory

questions.question_text: Which one of the following Mughal rulers implemented an ordinance banning the production, sale, and public use of Bhang?
questions.explanation: Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb was the son of Shah Jahan. When Aurangzeb sat on the throne, he was surrounded by many problems. To deal with these problems, Aurangzeb first attracted his attention towards the administration and made efforts for its eradication. He ended 80 types of taxes and also banned cannabis, gambling, and prostitution. He stopped the cultivation of Bhang in the empire. For the inspection of public conduct, Aurangzeb appointed an official named Muhtasib

questions.question_text: Which one of the following rulers started the policy of 'control and balance' in the administration during the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: In the administration of the Mughal period, the policy of 'control and balance' was started by Akbar. Through Akbar's Mansabdari system, marital relations with Rajputs, etc., Akbar did all these works to make his empire strong and long-lasting. In contemporary times, Rajputs could resist Akbar firmly. That is why he established marital relations with Rajputs and made them his friends. In the administration also, Akbar made such a provision that power would not be centralized in any one official's hands. All these works come under Akbar's policy of control and balance

questions.question_text: Which English traveler received employment as a gem expert under Akbar?
questions.explanation: The travelers who came during Akbar's reign are as follows – ♦ John Newbery – This was the first Englishman who came to India in Akbar's time with a letter from the King of England. ♦ Ralph Fitch – He came to Akbar's court with a letter from Queen Elizabeth. He stayed in Agra and Fatehpur Sikri. ♦ William Leedes – He was a famous English gem expert appointed by Akbar for the verification of diamonds. ♦ John Mildenhall – He reached during Akbar's time in 1599 with the objective of trading with Indian traders.

questions.question_text: To which Sikh Guru did Akbar donate 500 bighas of land?
questions.explanation: Guru Ram Das was a contemporary of Akbar and son-in-law of Amardas. Akbar gave them 500 bighas of land. On this land, he settled a city named Amritsar. Earlier the name of this city was Ramdaspur. His followers were called Ramdasi. Ramdas made his third son Arjan the successor and made the Guru's post hereditary

questions.question_text: Where was a famous structure named Ibadat Khana built during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: Till 1575, Akbar believed in the external forms of the Sunni religion. To understand the philosophy of the Islamic religion, he accepted the discipleship of Ulema like Sheikh Abdun Nabi and Makhdum-ul-Mulk Abdullah Sultanpuri. The followers of the Shia sect, Mullah Yazdi, could also not satisfy his spiritual thirst. Therefore, in 1575 AD, Akbar built an 'Ibadat Khana' (prayer house) in Fatehpur Sikri. Religious discussions used to take place there regularly every Thursday evening

questions.question_text: Which ruler launched 'Ilahi' type coins?
questions.explanation: The credit for providing a well-organized form to the Mughal currency system goes to Akbar. In Ain-i-Akbari, Abul Fazl has described that Akbar issued 26 gold, 9 silver, and 4 types of copper coins. The gold coins issued by Akbar are as follows – Mohur (equal to nine rupees), Sansbeh (largest gold coin), Ilahi (gold coin of round shape whose value was equal to 10 rupees), Rhasa (both round and square), Atma (of 25 tolas), Binsat, Chaugul and Lal-i-Jalali

questions.question_text: Which one of the following chronicles contains history from Subuktigin to the 40th year of Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh is a book written by Abdul Qadir Badauni. Badauni was a contemporary scholar of Akbar. This book has three parts; the first part contains a description of the Delhi Sultans, Babur, and Humayun's reign. The second part mentions the reign of Akbar up to 1596 AD. The third part of Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh contains a description of Muslims and saints. Badauni, while in the service of Akbar, translated Mahabharata and Ramayana into Persian

questions.question_text: By which Mughal ruler was an official ban issued against 'Sati'?
questions.explanation: The practice of Sati had been prevalent since ancient times. This practice was especially prevalent among the Rajputs. The Delhi Sultans tried to stop it in their time. In medieval India, Muhammad Tughlaq was the first ruler who tried to stop it. During the Mughal period, Akbar also tried to stop it. Aurangzeb was the first Mughal ruler who clearly issued a farman and banned the Sati practice in his empire

questions.question_text: The book 'Fatawa-e-Alamgiri' written during Aurangzeb's time relates to–
questions.explanation: The book 'Fatawa-e-Alamgiri' written during Aurangzeb's time relates to law code. Fatawa-e-Alamgiri is a Sharia-based compilation on statecraft, general morality, military strategy, economic policy, justice, and punishment. This compilation is widely considered one of the best-organized works in the field of Islamic jurisprudence. It is a historical work, which was prepared by a team of jurists during the reign of Mughal Badshah Aurangzeb

questions.question_text: In the context of Akbar's victories, consider the following and arrange them chronologically- (I) Odisha conquest (II) Sindh conquest (III) Kandahar conquest (IV) Balochistan conquest Select the correct answer using the code given below- Code
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of Akbar's political victories is as follows (I) Sindh conquest - 1591 AD. (II) Odisha conquest - 1592 AD. (III) Balochistan conquest - 1595 AD. (IV) Kandahar conquest - 1595 AD.

questions.question_text: Who was the head of the Dutch factory located in Agra during the time of Mughal Badshah Jahangir?
questions.explanation: The head of the Dutch factory located in Agra during the time of Mughal Badshah Jahangir was Francisco Pelsaert. Pelsaert was also the head of the Dutch mint in Agra. He has described the indigo production of Bayana in great detail in his book 'Remonstrantie'

questions.question_text: Among the following, who is not a painter of Jahangir's time?
questions.explanation: Jahangir's period is called the golden age of Mughal painting. Prominent painters of Jahangir's period were Mansur, Manohar, Abul Hasan, Bishandas, Farrukh Beg, etc. Khwaja Abdus Samad was a prominent painter of Akbar's period, whom Akbar made the head of the mint Jahangir gave the title of 'Nadir-uz-Zaman' to Abul Hasan and 'Nadir-ul-Asr' to Mansur. Jahangir established a 'picture gallery' in Agra under the leadership of Herat's 'Aqa Riza'.

questions.question_text: In the war of succession, which son of Shah Jahan fought in the Battle of Bahadurpur?
questions.explanation: In the war of succession, the war between Shah Jahan's son Shah Shuja and the imperial army (led by Sulaiman Shikoh and Mirza Raja Jai Singh) took place in February 1658 at Bahadurpur, 6 miles away from Varanasi, in which Shah Shuja was defeated and returned to Bengal

questions.question_text: To which Prince did Nur Jahan marry her first daughter Ladli Begum?
questions.explanation: Nur Jahan's real name was Mehr-un-Nissa Begum. Her father's name was Mirza Ghiyas Beg who was a native of Tehran. In 1594 AD, Mehr-un-Nissa was married to Ali-Quli Beg. He was of Iranian origin. In 1607 AD, during a rebellion, Ali Quli was killed. After that, Mehr-un-Nissa and her daughter Ladli Begum were brought to the Mughal harem, after which in 1611 AD Mehr-un-Nissa was married to Jahangir, after which Jahangir gave her the title of Nur Jahan. Due to her active role in the court, to remove Khurram from her path, she married her daughter Ladli Begum to Jahangir's weak son Shahryar

questions.question_text: Who was the famous calligrapher in Akbar's court who was given the title of 'Zarin Qalam'?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperors Babur, Humayun, Akbar, and Jahangir had a special interest in painting. During Jahangir's time, painting reached its peak. Humayun brought two painters, Mir Sayyid Ali and Khwaja Abdus Samad, from Persia with him. Akbar learned painting in Kabul. Abul Fazl has told in Ain-i-Akbari that there were about 100 painters in Akbar's court. Among them, some prominent were- Abdus Samad, Sayyid Ali, Daswant, Basawan, Hariwansh, etc. Due to sweet writing, Khwaja Abdus Samad was given the title of 'Shirin Qalam' and Muhammad Hussain-Al-Katib Kashmiri was given the title of 'Zarin Qalam'

questions.question_text: What was 'Ahadi' in the Mughal military system?
questions.explanation: Ahadi soldiers were also called Badshah's soldiers because their recruitment, weapons, salary, and allowances were provided by the Badshah himself. A separate Diwan and Bakshi were appointed for the efficient operation of this work, although Ahadi soldiers were the Badshah's personal soldiers and the Badshah himself used to appoint them in the service of any Mansabdar from time to time. The number of Ahadi soldiers was not fixed. Thus, Ahadi soldiers were recruited by the Badshah. They were his loyal and capable soldiers. Special Fact Dakhili soldiers - The recruitment of Dakhili soldiers was also done by the Badshah like Ahadi soldiers but after recruiting these Dakhili soldiers, they were kept in the service of various Mansabdars.

questions.question_text: Where was Zabt not fully adopted in 1600?
questions.explanation: Zabt system meant an agreement between the farmer and the government according to which land revenue per bigha per year was fixed for three years or more. Regardless of how much produce there was in the field or not. Its rate depended on the land's fertility and its location. Zabt (Zabt) system was also called Naqdi or Zami. It was liked by the farmers. Its expansion was applicable in Bihar, Allahabad, Multan, Awadh, Agra, Malwa, Delhi, and Lahore including Ajmer. This system was not fully implemented in Gujarat

questions.question_text: What was the Mughal rank system called?
questions.explanation: Mansab means rank or grade. The start of this system was done by Akbar. The Mansabdari system was based on the decimal method. This system was adopted by Akbar from the Mongol invader Genghis Khan. There are two parts to this system. (I) Zat (II) Sawar

questions.question_text: Arrange the diplomatic missions sent by Akbar under the leadership of various Mughal officials to Maharana Pratap in chronological order and choose the correct option with the help of the code given below-
questions.explanation: Akbar sent four diplomatic missions for talks with Maharana Pratap, whose sequential description is as follows (i) Jalal Khan – 1572 AD. (ii) Man Singh – 1573 AD. (iii) Bhagwant Das – October 1573 AD. (iv) Todar Mal – December 1573 AD. • After this proposal, when Maharana Pratap was not forced to accept suzerainty, the Battle of Haldighati took place on 18 June 1576 AD, in which Maharana Pratap was defeated.

questions.question_text: Who taught Indian craftsmen the technique of making gunpowder?
questions.explanation: In Indian history, the use of gunpowder was done for the first time by the Mughals in the first battle of Panipat in 1526 AD, although the use of gunpowder had already taken place in the Vijayanagara Empire. Whatever use of gunpowder in India and knowledge to Indian craftsmen was provided in 1582 AD by Fathullah Shirazi, a Persian engineer who worked for Akbar. A beginner Matchlock-shot was developed. As earlier used in ancient Greece and China, and by the 17th century, Indians were building various types of firearms. James Riddick Partington in 'A History of Greek Fire and Gunpowder' has described Indian rockets and explosive factories

questions.question_text: What subject was 'Dastur-ul-Amal' related to in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: The declaration of Dastur-ul-Amal was made by Akbar in 1582. It was related to cash land revenue. Dastur used to change from time to time

questions.question_text: What was the work of 'Diwan-i-Buyutat' in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: During the Mughal period, the work of 'Diwan-i-Buyutat' was to take care of royal Karkhanas and to provide them funds, provide raw materials, and determine the price of goods

questions.question_text: Under Mughal rule, every detail of the administration was recorded. Among these, what was 'Siyah Hazur'?

options.B: Information about the daily routine of the court

questions.explanation: Under Mughal rule, the work of Siyah Hazur was to provide a detail of the daily routine of each day in the court

questions.question_text: What was meant by 'Suyurghal' in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: Suyurghal land was also called 'Madad-i-Maash'. This land was given as a grant to scholars and people of religious disposition. This land was tax-free. This type of land was non-productive. And this land was also called 'Milk'

questions.question_text: Most of the gardens (orchards) were planted in the Mughal period by
questions.explanation: The beginning of planting gardens in the Mughal period was started by Babur. Who worked to make nature beautiful for his rest according to India's climate. Almost all Mughal emperors paid attention to this work, but during Jahangir's reign, special attention was paid to this. Most of the gardens were planted during this ruler's time. Jahangir was a high-quality art lover, art connoisseur, nature lover, and collector of paintings. Jahangir used to get buildings constructed in places from where beautiful scenes of nature could be seen. As is proved by Shalimar Garden in Kashmir

questions.question_text: Into how many provinces was Akbar's empire divided in 1580 AD?
questions.explanation: For the operation of the empire, Akbar divided it into 12 parts/provinces in 1580 AD. In Mughal rule, the province was called Subah, these 12 Subahs were as follows- Agra, Delhi, Allahabad, Awadh, Ajmer, Ahmedabad, Bihar, Bengal, Kabul, Lahore, Multan, and Malwa. After the Deccan conquest, three Subahs of Khandesh, Berar, and Ahmednagar were established, due to which the number of Subahs in Akbar's time reached 15. In Aurangzeb's time, the number of provinces was 21. In provincial administration, the division of the Mughal empire into Subahs, and the division of Subahs into Sarkars, and the division of Sarkar into Pargana or Mahal was done

questions.question_text: Who gave the name Dandesh for Khandesh?
questions.explanation: Khandesh is located in the Tapti river valley. After the death of Firoz Tughlaq, Khandesh became separate from the Delhi Sultanate and the Subahdar here, Malik Raja Faruqi, established independent power. In 1599 AD, Akbar himself attacked the capital of Khandesh, Burhanpur, and made his beloved son Daniyal the Subahdar there. After his name, it was also named Dandesh

questions.question_text: Which ruler finally stopped the practice of 'Sijda' and 'Paibos' in the court?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan's initial education had the influence of Sufi ideology and his teachers were of liberal views. His mother was a Rajput, but he did not marry any Rajput woman. In 1636, he ended the practice of 'Sijda and Paibos', and in its place, the practice of Chahar Taslim started. The practice of Zamin Bos and putting the Emperor's picture on the turban was ended. Hijri calendar was implemented in place of Ilahi calendar. He imposed several restrictions on Hindus. They could not buy Muslim slaves, could not wear Muslim dress, could not marry Muslim women

questions.question_text: In the time of which Mughal ruler did the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur occur?
questions.explanation: Guru Tegh Bahadur was the 9th Guru of the Sikhs. Aurangzeb looked at him with suspicion. He believed that Guru Tegh Bahadur was conspiring against the Mughals and was organizing the Sikhs and teaching war and calling Aurangzeb's cruelty against religion and was spreading the Mughal Sultanate in the wrong way among people. In this perspective, Aurangzeb asked Guru Tegh Bahadur to either show some miracle or accept Islam or embrace death. Guru Tegh Bahadur refused to show a miracle and accept Islam and accepted embracing death and in this way, Aurangzeb gave Guru Tegh Bahadur the death penalty

questions.question_text: Farid was the real name of which of the following medieval rulers?
questions.explanation: Farid was the initial name of Sher Shah. His father Hasan Khan was a Jamadar of the parganas of Sahsaram, Khwaspur, and Tanda in Bihar. Hasan Khan had eight sons, among whom the eldest son Farid Khan was born in 1472 AD in Bajwara. At the age of 22, Farid, disappointed by his stepmother's ill-treatment and his father's neglect, went to Jaunpur, which was the capital of provincial administration and a famous center of education. Farid went to Agra for a test of fate. There, obtaining the protection of Daulat Khan Lodi, he requested the Sultan that he should be given the jagir of the parganas of Sahsaram and Khwaspur-Tanda

questions.question_text: Which of the following battles is not related to Babur?
questions.explanation: The existence of the Mughal empire in India came to light with the first battle of Panipat of Mughal ruler Babur. Babur, to capture his power in India, attained victory in several wars, among which some of his wars are as follows 1- First Battle of Panipat - 21 April, 1526 AD. 2- Battle of Khanwa - 16 March, 1527 AD. 3- Battle of Chanderi - 29 January, 1528 AD. 4- Battle of Ghaghra - 6 May, 1529 AD. Special Fact- The Battle of Bilgram or Kannauj was fought between Sher Shah and Humayun on 17 May 1540 AD. In this battle, Humayun was defeated, in which Sher Shah easily captured Agra and Delhi. After the Bilgram battle, Humayun went to Sindh, where he spent an exile life like a nomad for 15 years.

questions.question_text: At which place was the mortal body of Aurangzeb buried?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb, due to his narrow-mindedness, also committed atrocities on fellow Muslims. He started looking at those who followed Sufi religion with contempt and killed a Sufi saint named Sarmad. Aurangzeb died in 1707 AD. In his nearly 50 years of reign, he neither proved to be a successful ruler nor could he get a monument constructed like the Taj Mahal or Peacock Throne. The mortal body of this ruler was buried in a grave at Khuldabad in Aurangabad

questions.question_text: Whom did Shah Jahan formally appoint as his successor in September 1657 due to his illness, to avoid the war of succession?
questions.explanation: On Shah Jahan falling ill, a terrible war broke out among his sons to get the Mughal power. To stop this war, Shah Jahan, on the basis of seniority, appointed his eldest son Dara Shikoh as the successor. Dara was the Subahdar of Punjab but always stayed in Agra with his father. He was of religious-minded person and had no special interest in politics and during Shah Jahan's illness, Dara did the work of his care especially

questions.question_text: Which grandson(s) of Shah Jahan got married to the daughter/daughters of Aurangzeb?

options.A: Sipihr Shikoh - son of Dara Shikoh

questions.explanation: After Shah Jahan falling ill in September 1657 AD, the war for succession started among his sons. Aurangzeb won this conflict and after killing Dara Shikoh, his severed head was paraded in the city. After that, so that there was no possibility of rebellion by his son, Aurangzeb married his daughter Zubdat-un-Nissa to his brother Dara Shikoh's son Sipihr Shikoh on 30 January 1673 AD and after capturing the entire Mughal power, operated the state and married his fifth daughter to Murad's son Izad Bakhsh

questions.question_text: In which war was the use of cannon first done by one of the two parties?
questions.explanation: In the first battle of Panipat fought by Babur, cannons were used for the first time; this was the first war in history in which cannons were used by an army. This war was fought between Babur and the Afghan ruler Ibrahim Lodi, in which Lodi was defeated and killed. This war was fought on 21 April 1526, in which Babur used the Uzbek war tactic Tulugma and the Ottoman method of arranging cannons. His artillery was led by two capable officials named Ustad Ali and Mustafa Khan

questions.question_text: Which of the following became known as Emperor Aurangzeb upon ascending the throne?
questions.explanation: Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb was born in Dohad on 3 November 1618. He was the sixth child of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz. This Aurangzeb later sat on the throne of Delhi by the name of Alamgir I. On the account of his sharp intelligence and natural exceptional memory, his knowledge of the Quran and his study of the traditional sayings of the Prophet were complete

questions.question_text: Which were the strong opponents who paved the way for Bairam Khan's fall?

options.C: Jiji Anga and her husband Shamsuddin Atka Khan

questions.explanation: Bairam Khan's fall was a major event of Akbar's contemporary history. Bairam Khan was a very loyal and capable protector. He became a victim of the conspiracy of the people of the Mughal court. The main reasons for dissatisfaction with Bairam Khan were 1- Bairam Khan was a follower of Shia sect, while Akbar and other courtiers were Sunni. 2- Bairam Khan's decisions were autocratic and his nature was angry and jealous. 3- Along with increasing age, Akbar started taking interest in state affairs. Bairam Khan's opponents started keeping his bad qualities before Akbar. They started magnifying the mistakes of Bairam Khan's conduct. 4- Akbar's foster mother Maham Anga, her son Adham Khan, son-in-law Shamsuddin Atka, Jiji Anga, and her husband Shamsuddin were ambitious and considered Bairam Khan's increasing influence as an obstacle in their path. These people were engaged in filling Akbar's ears and increasing the distance between him and Bairam Khan.

questions.question_text: Against whom did Aurangzeb decide to organize the revenue administration in Bengal for financial funding?
questions.explanation: The base of Aurangzeb's southern policy was to end the existence of Bijapur and Golconda states and establish control over the ambitions of the Marathas. Aurangzeb decided to organize the revenue administration in Bengal for financial funding against the Marathas

questions.question_text: To maintain the principle of authority and subordination in a hierarchical pattern, which ideology did Akbar follow?
questions.explanation: Akbar followed imperial policy in establishing political unity in India. For the establishment of national unity, it was necessary to establish political unity. His Rajput policy, his policy of suppression of various rebellions, all prove this context. Akbar established administrative unity in the entire empire like the Mauryan emperors. This system was inspired by the spirit of public welfare

questions.question_text: Name the official regulation and gazetteer of Akbar's reign.
questions.explanation: Ain-i-Akbari describes the society and culture of India in detail. It contains the most detailed examination of Indian society, religious sects, and communities, knowledge, and arts after Al-Biruni. That is why it is known as the official regulation and gazetteer of Akbar's reign

questions.question_text: In which year did Aurangzeb die?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb was the sixth child of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz. He was born in Dohad on 3 November 1618 AD. Later, Aurangzeb Alamgir I sat on the Delhi throne by this name. On the account of his sharp intelligence and natural exceptional memory, he had knowledge of the Quran and had complete knowledge related to the traditional sayings of the Prophet Muhammad. Aurangzeb spent the last 25 years of his life in the suppression of Marathas in the South. He died in Ahmednagar on 4 March 1707 AD

questions.question_text: What was the original name of Bahadur Shah I?
questions.explanation: After the death of Aurangzeb, his son Muazzam became the Mughal Badshah in 1707 AD by the name of Bahadur Shah I. Khafi Khan had given him the title of 'Shah-i-Bekhabar'. Bahadur Shah I was the seventh Mughal Badshah of Delhi. He is also known by the name Alam Shah I

questions.question_text: Among the following, whom did Rai Singh defeat in the Battle of Khatoli?
questions.explanation: Rai Singh Rathore became the King of Bikaner in 1574 AD. He also served during the Mughal period. Rai Singh defeated the ruler of Gujarat, Ibrahim Hussain Mirza, in the Battle of Khatoli in 1573 AD, for which Akbar was pleased and gave him a mansab of 4000. Akbar sent Rai Singh to capture Siwana Fort. Later, Jahangir made his mansab 5000

questions.question_text: Under whose leadership did Akbar send a Mughal army to Jodhpur in 1570 AD against Chandrasen?
questions.explanation: In 1570 AD, Akbar sent an army under the leadership of Husain Quli Khan against Chandrasen. Under the leadership of Husain Quli Khan, the imperial army attacked Jodhpur and besieged Jodhpur fort. Rao Chandrasen was forced to abandon the fort and kept wandering in the forests like nomads and went to Bhadrajun. In this way, Akbar captured the Jodhpur fort

questions.question_text: Which of the following places became the main center of Chandrasen after the fall of Jodhpur?
questions.explanation: After the conflict with Akbar, Rao Chandrasen was such a ruler who never accepted the suzerainty of the Mughals. He continued the conflict by sending an army against his brother. Akbar sent an army under the leadership of Husain Quli Khan and besieged Jodhpur fort. Rao Chandrasen was forced to abandon the fort and went to Bhadrajun and after the rebellion subsided, he made Siwana his center and started his administrative work

questions.question_text: After Humayun's death, who gave guidance and advice to Akbar?
questions.explanation: Bairam Khan was Humayun's confidant. Due to this trustworthiness, Humayun had adorned Bairam Khan with titles like Protector, Khan-i-Khana, Friend, Loyalist. After Akbar became Emperor, he appointed Bairam Khan as his Wazir. Due to which he provided significant contribution in the direction of solving the initial problems of Akbar. Bairam Khan remained the protector and guide of Akbar from 1556 to 1560. Bairam Khan served with honesty and provided strength to the foundation of the poor Mughal empire

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor established agriculture, which led to a significant increase in the collective property of the empires?
questions.explanation: Akbar's land revenue-related reforms have special importance. His land-related reforms were not original because Sher Shah Suri had established them first. Sher Shah had land measurement done and fixed one-third of the produce as land revenue. When Akbar sat on the throne of Delhi, he revived the land revenue-related reforms of Sher Shah and gave them a developed form. After the Gujarat victory, Akbar himself started taking interest in land revenue; he appointed many Diwans for land system reform but later with Todar Mal's land reform system, there was significant progress. He adopted the gaz of Sikandar Lodi's time, which fixed one bigha of 3600 square gaz. During Akbar's time, it was decided to reduce Jagir land and expand Khalisa land, due to which a very large part of revenue determination was converted into Khalisa land. 182 Karoris were appointed on Khalisa land. Under each Karori, there was an area from which two lakh fifty thousand rupees were received as revenue in the form of revenue. His work was to fix the boundaries of the area, prepare accounts of resources received as land revenue, and keep an account of money received from each resource and a detail of each crop. With his help, Karkuns and Potdars were appointed. By 1580, the revenue department had enough data and information. Due to which land revenue-related reforms became strong

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor revived the pilgrimage tax?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb was a harsh ruler and a staunch traditional Sunni Muslim, due to this reason he was intolerant towards Hindus. Aurangzeb also imposed tax on Hindus for 'pilgrimage' in 1663 AD and Hindu traders were also charged tax. He imposed a ban on 'Sati practice'. In the 11th year of his reign, he imposed a ban on 'singing' in the court in 1669 AD, but no ban was imposed on playing musical instruments and Naubat. Government musicians were dismissed. In 1668 AD, he also imposed a ban on festivals and religious rituals celebrated by Hindus. In 1669 AD, Aurangzeb got Kashi's Vishwanath temple, Gujarat's Somnath temple, and Mathura's Keshavrai temples broken

questions.question_text: Under which ruler was the 'Shalimar Garden' authorized?
questions.explanation: The construction of Shalimar Garden was done by Indian empire's Emperor Jahangir in Jammu and Kashmir, India, this famous garden is an example of Mughal garden. It was built by Jahangir in Srinagar, which was dedicated to his beloved wife Nur Jahan. Especially by this name, a garden was built and developed in Lahore, Pakistan Shalimar means - Garden of love

questions.question_text: Under which ruler was 'Tutinama' illustrated?
questions.explanation: Mughal Badshah Akbar, who gave protection to ancient art and culture, had a pioneering role. A famous painting of his time is Tutinama (1560-68 AD), in which the parrot's love talk is the subject of this book. It contains 103 paintings. Around 1330 AD, the story of Tutinama was quite prevalent in Iran and the Mughal form of that is Tutinama. Its paintings are similar to those of Hamzanama. The depiction of nature and architecture (circular frame) has much similarity with Hamzanama. Here, only in the depiction of birds, there is complete liberty and they are close to the Indian tradition. Some paintings have names of artists like Basawan, Daswant, Iqbal, etc. Currently, this illustrated copy is collected in 'Cleveland Museum of Art, Cleveland' and 'Chester Beatty Library, Dublin', and some pages of it are kept in 'Lucknow Museum'

questions.question_text: Which foreign traveler/representative arriving in India during Jahangir's time and his date is not matched?
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of foreign travelers arriving in India during Jahangir's reign is as follows 1. William Hawkins - 1608-1611 2. Sir Thomas Roe - 1615-1619 3. Edward Terry - 1616-1619 4. Paul Canning - 1615-1625 Note- In the above question, among the travelers who came, Paul Canning did not come during Jahangir's reign in 1610 AD but came to India in 1615 AD.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal Prince was given the responsibility of Kandahar conquest in 1653 AD?
questions.explanation: In 1653 AD, Shah Jahan gave the responsibility of Kandahar conquest to his son Dara Shikoh but this campaign could not be successful due to which Kandahar remained out of Mughal control

questions.question_text: On the question of giving punishment to Dara Shikoh, who pleaded for his life?
questions.explanation: Bernier writes that everyone was seen weeping and lamenting over Dara Shikoh's misfortune. That same evening, Aurangzeb consulted his council of ministers for the decision of Dara's fate. Bernier's patron Danishmand Khan recommended his life-saving. But Shaista Khan, Amir Khan, Bahadur Khan, Roshan Ara demanded his death penalty for the good of religion and the state

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions was not there in the treaty (1681) made by Aurangzeb with Rana Jai Singh?

options.A: As a result of the treaty, Mandal, Pur, and Banera were handed over to the Mughals in exchange for Jizya.
options.B: The presence of Mughal government troops in Mewar was ensured.
options.C: The Rana should get back his native land.
options.D: Giving a 5000 mansab to Jai Singh was ensured.

questions.explanation: Through the mediation of Bikaner's King Shyam Singh, the treaty of Udaipur between Mewar and the Mughal empire was completed on 14 June 1681 AD. According to this treaty, to get relief from Jizya, Rana gave the parganas of Mandal, Pur, and Banera to the Mughals, although after three years these parganas went back to the Rana. Mughal troops were removed from Mewar. Jai Singh was accepted as Rana and he was honored by giving a mansab of five thousand in the imperial army and the Rana also got back his native land

questions.question_text: A. Jat rebellion under Gokula's leadership B. Martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur C. Rebellion of Prince Akbar D. Jat rebellion under Rajaram's leadership Choose the correct combination from below– Arrange the following events of Aurangzeb's period chronologically–
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of Aurangzeb's reign's events– 1. Jat rebellion under Gokula's leadership – 1669 AD. 2. Martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur – 1675 AD. 3. Rebellion of Prince Akbar – 1681 AD. 4. Jat rebellion under Rajaram's leadership – 1685 AD.

questions.question_text: A. Jahandar Shah B. Bahadur Shah-I C. Farrukhsiyar D. Muhammad Shah Rangeela Choose the correct combination from below– Arrange the following Later Mughal emperors chronologically–
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of Later Mughal emperors– 1. Bahadur Shah I – 1707-1712 AD. 2. Jahandar Shah – 1712-1713 AD. 3. Farrukhsiyar – 1713-1719 AD. 4. Muhammad Shah Rangeela – 1719-1748 AD.

questions.question_text: Which statement about Shah Jahan's Deccan policy is false?

options.A: In 1633 AD, Ahmednagar state was completely ended and merged into the Mughal empire.
options.B: In 1636, Golconda and Bijapur made a treaty with Shah Jahan and accepted suzerainty.
options.C: Shah Jahan gave the first and second Subahdari of the Deccan to Aurangzeb successively: in 1636 and 1652 AD.
options.D: The existence of Bijapur and Golconda was ended by Shah Jahan in 1656 AD.

questions.explanation: Shah Jahan's reign started the era of Mughal's Deccan policy; during Jahangir's reign, he was the Subahdar of the Deccan and had done two military campaigns in the South. He did the following work on the political and military power of Deccan states Ahmednagar, Bijapur, Golconda– 1. In 1633 AD, Fath Khan was given a pension, Khilat by Shah Jahan and Ahmednagar was ended and merged into the Mughal empire. 2. In 1636, Golconda and Bijapur made a treaty with Shah Jahan and accepted suzerainty. 3. Shah Jahan gave the first Subahdari of the Deccan to Aurangzeb in 1636 AD and the second Subahdari in 1652-53. Note– The existence of Bijapur-Golconda was not ended, rather in 1656 AD, after the death of the Sultan of Bijapur, Aurangzeb was ordered to take appropriate action to solve the state's internal deadlock.

questions.question_text: During Shah Jahan's reign, when and who expelled the Portuguese from Hugli in Bengal?
questions.explanation: In 1632 AD, a quarrel occurred between two Portuguese, in which one requested the Governor of Dhaka for help and complained against the Portuguese of Hugli. The Badshah was looking for an excuse to suppress the Portuguese. He immediately ordered Dhaka Governor Qasim Khan to attack Hugli. The army surrounded Hugli from all four sides and put thousands of Portuguese to death and after about three and a half months, the Mughals captured Hugli

questions.question_text: Regarding Babur, who laid the foundation of the Mughal empire in India, which statement is false–

options.A: Zahir-ud-Din Babur was born on 14 February 1483 in Kabul.
options.B: Babur acquired the kingdom of Farghana at the tender age of 11 years.
options.C: Babur won Samarkand three times in his lifetime and all three times it slipped from his hands.
options.D: Babur learned the use of 'Tulugma' from the Uzbeks.

questions.explanation: Zahir-ud-Din Muhammad Babur was born on 14 February 1483 AD in Farghana, not in Kabul. Babur had the blood of two brave tribes and two famous conquerors of Asia in his veins. Babur sat on the throne of Farghana on 8 June 1494 AD at the age of eleven. Babur writes in his autobiography– "I lost Farghana for Samarkand and now Samarkand has also slipped from my hands." Thus, Babur won Samarkand three times in his lifetime and all three times it slipped from his hands. Babur learned the use of "Tulugma" from the Uzbeks

questions.question_text: After 1560 AD, Akbar's first and last conquest campaigns were successively–
questions.explanation: After 1561 AD, Akbar sent his first conquest campaign under the leadership of Adham Khan to win Malwa, which defeated Baz Bahadur and brought Malwa under his control. And the last conquest was done by Akbar over Asirgarh which was done on the surrender of Miran Bahadur in January 1601

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of events of Akbar's reign? A. Mahzar's declaration (Declaration of Infallibility) B. Abolition of Jizya C. Declaration of Tauhid-i-Ilahi D. Construction of Ibadat Khana Choose the correct combination from below–
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of Akbar's reign's events– 1. Abolition of Jizya – 1564 2. Construction of Ibadat Khana – 1575 3. Mahzar's declaration (Declaration of Infallibility) – 1579 4. Tauhid-i-Ilahi's declaration – 1582

questions.question_text: Match– List-I List-II
questions.explanation: 1. Rayasin Conquest – 1543 2. Fall of Chunar – 1538 3. Battle of Chausa – 1539 4. War of Sumel – 1544

questions.question_text: The devastated city, in which piles of corpses were lying on the roads, Humayun changed its name to 'Jannatabad' and stayed there for about 8 months immersed in music and festivities, this city was–
questions.explanation: Gaur state (Bengal)'s capital Lakshmanavati or Lakhnauti is an old city situated in the Malda district of Bengal, whose name Humayun changed to Jannatabad, a devastated city in which piles of corpses were lying on the roads. According to Dr. S.L. Srivastava, "Humayun enjoyed pleasure in Bengal for eight months and kept no contact with Delhi, Agra, or Varanasi."

questions.question_text: Among the following, who was the Mughal governor of Delhi at the time of Hemu's attack?
questions.explanation: At the time of Hemu's attack, the Mughal governor was Tardi Beg. After Humayun's death, Hemu attacked with the objective of capturing Delhi, which was faced by Mughal governor Tardi Beg but Tardi Beg was defeated in the war and fled from Delhi to Punjab. Along with capturing Delhi, Hemu assumed the title of Vikramaditya. In the course of time, in the second battle of Panipat in 1556 AD, a arrow hit Hemu in his eye during the war, causing him to fall down from the elephant's howdah, which turned the victory into defeat. He was caught and brought before Akbar, where Akbar gave him the death penalty

questions.question_text: Among the following, which ruler implemented 'Rai' method to collect land revenue?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri implemented the Rai method or list of crop rates to collect land revenue. Sher Shah Suri's land revenue system was mainly Raiyatwari in which direct contact was made with the farmers. For measurement of land, he used Gaz-i-Sikandari, which was measured in Bigha. In his time, revenue could be taken in both cash or grain forms but cash was given more priority

questions.question_text: According to which historian, in 1592, there were about 120 cities and 3,200 towns in Akbar's empire?
questions.explanation: Akbar was a great ruler of the Mughal period. He was born on 15 October 1542 AD in Amarkot (Sindh) in the house of Rajput chief Rana Virsal from the womb of Hamida Banu Begum. His father's name was Humayun. The Mughal empire expanded rapidly during Akbar's time, during which urbanization and the population of cities also increased. According to Nizamuddin Ahmad, in 1592, there were about 120 cities and 3200 towns in Akbar's empire. Ain-i-Akbari reveals that the administration of the city was done by an official named Kotwal, whose work was similar to modern municipalities and police officials

questions.question_text: Among the following, who has been given the credit for establishing an improved currency system?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah made commendable reforms in the currency system. He is given the credit for establishing an improved currency system. Sher Shah issued gold coin Ashrafi, silver rupee, and copper dam coins. During Sher Shah's time, the exchange ratio between the silver rupee and copper dam was 1: 64

questions.question_text: Which ruler introduced the concept of 'Rupiya' or 'Rupayya'?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah paid special attention to the development of trade, commerce, and means of communication. For this, he introduced the circulation of Rupiya in currency circulation, in which gold, silver, and copper coins were circulated. Silver rupee which weighed 178 grains and copper dam which was of 380 grains. In Arabic script, Sher Shah got his name, title, and the name of the mint engraved. Thus, this reform of Sher Shah proved to be permanent

questions.question_text: Between which pair did the Battle of Chausa take place?
questions.explanation: Battle of Chausa - Fought between Mughal Emperor Humayun and the founder of the Suri empire, Sher Shah Suri, on 26 June 1539 AD in Chausa village located in Buxar district of modern Bihar state. In which Sher Shah Suri was victorious and Humayun was defeated. After the Chausa victory, Sher Khan assumed the title of 'Sultan-i-Adil' or 'Sher Shah'

questions.question_text: Which Mughal prince took refuge in the court of the King of Garhwal?
questions.explanation: Suleiman Shikoh, the eldest son of Dara Shikoh. He was named "Chhota Miya" by Shah Jahan. After the defeat of Dara Shikoh in the Battle of Samugarh in May 1658, Suleiman took refuge in Srinagar of Garhwal in 1659 AD. This description is given in Muntakhab-ul-Lubab. At that time, the King of Garhwal was Prithvi Shah

questions.question_text: Shah Jahan's favorite wife Mumtaz Mahal died in
questions.explanation: Mumtaz Mahal was Shah Jahan's most favorite wife, her childhood name was Arjumand Banu Begum. She was born in 1594 AD. Her father's name was Asaf Khan. In 1612 AD, she was married to Shah Jahan (Khurram). Mumtaz died in 1631 AD in Burhanpur during the 14th delivery pain. To fulfill Mumtaz's last wish, Shah Jahan got the world-famous Taj Mahal built in Agra in her memory

questions.question_text: Which woman of the Mughal royal family gave land from her jagir for the grazing of cows?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Hamida Banu Begum gave land from her jagir for the grazing of cows. Akbar was born on 15 October 1542 AD at the house of Rajput chief Raja Virsal of Amarkot from the womb of Hamida Banu Begum. Hamida Banu was a woman of very religious disposition.

questions.question_text: In the final phase of his reign, Akbar added three provinces of the Deccan to his empire. Among these, which one is not among those three?
questions.explanation: In 1591, Ali Khan of Khandesh voluntarily accepted independence. Ahmednagar fort, Berar, Daulatabad were taken in the war with Chand Bibi in 1599-1600, and Akbar could not add Bidar to his empire

questions.question_text: Which of the following foreign travelers visited India six times?
questions.explanation: French traveler Jean-Baptiste Tavernier visited India six times between 1638 and 1663. He was a jeweler by profession and came to India during the time of Mughal ruler Shah Jahan. He has described the reigns of Aurangzeb and Shah Jahan in great detail

questions.question_text: In the architectural art of tombs, the Charbagh system is found for the first time in India in whose tomb?
questions.explanation: The use of Charbagh style was done for the first time in Humayun's tomb. The construction of this tomb was done by Humayun's widow Haji Begum in Delhi in 1565 AD. Its dome is made of marble. It is considered the predecessor of Taj Mahal

questions.question_text: Regarding Mughal architecture, which statement is false?

options.A: The process of blending Hindu and Muslim styles in Mughal architecture reached its fullness.
options.B: The contribution of Babur and Humayun in the field of architecture is negligible.
options.C: The buildings built by Sher Shah are a bridge between the style developed in the time of Delhi Sultans and the later Mughal style.
options.D: Humayun's tomb is not considered the ideal of Hindu-Muslim architecture.

questions.explanation: Humayun's tomb is not considered the ideal of Hindu-Muslim architecture. This statement is false. The construction of this tomb has been done in Indo-Islamic style in Delhi. Humayun's tomb is situated in Delhi

questions.question_text: During the Mughal period, where did the production of best quality indigo take place?
questions.explanation: The regions of indigo production during the Mughal period were Bayana, (Rajasthan), Sarkhej (Gujarat), Sehwan

questions.question_text: There was a Batai system of three types during Sher Shah's time:

options.D: Khet Batai, Lank Batai, Rase Batai

questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri established the second Afghan empire in India, Sher Shah's land revenue system was mainly Raiyatwari, Sher Shah divided land into three categories based on produce– (1) Good (2) Medium (3) Bad There were three types of Batai systems prevalent during Sher Shah's time (1) Khet Batai (2) Lank Batai (3) Rase Batai Sher Shah's land revenue system later became the basis of Akbar's revenue system.

questions.question_text: 1. Battle of Dodan 2. Battle of Kannauj 3. Battle of Chausa 4. Sher Shah's Malwa conquest Choose the correct chronological order of the following events:
questions.explanation: The correct order is– (a) Battle of Dodan (Daurah) – 1532 AD. (c) Battle of Chausa – 1539 AD. (b) Battle of Kannauj – 1540 AD. (d) Sher Shah's Malwa conquest – 1542 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Sher Shah's coins is correct?

options.A: The name of the mint is not inscribed on any of his coins
options.B: The name of the emperor is not inscribed on Sher Shah's coins
options.C: Sher Shah issued gold coins of 165, 175 and 185 grains
options.D: The names of the first four Caliphs are inscribed on some of Sher Shah's coins

questions.explanation: There were 23 mints for minting coins during the time of Sher Shah Suri (1) The name of the mint was inscribed on the coins issued by him. (2) The name of Emperor Sher Shah and his title were inscribed on Sher Shah's coins in Arabic or Nagari script. (3) The gold coins issued by Sher Shah were called Ashrafi, whose value was equal to 16 silver coins. (4) On some of his currencies, in addition to the Sultan's name, the names of the first four Caliphs of Islam were also inscribed.

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler of Bijapur at the time of its annexation into the Mughal Empire?
questions.explanation: In 1686 AD, the last ruler of Bijapur, Sultan Sikandar Adil Shah, surrendered before Aurangzeb and as a result, Bijapur was merged into the Mughal Empire. Aurangzeb granted him the title of Khan

questions.question_text: Who was the proponent of the Turko-Mongol theory of Mughal kingship:
questions.explanation: The proponent of the Turko-Mongol theory of Mughal kingship was R.P. Tripathi. According to him, both the Turko and Mongol traditions together inclined the political system towards greater centralization

questions.question_text: 1. Shivaji's first encounter with the Mughals. 2. Shivaji's Karnataka campaign. 3. Night raid on Shaista Khan. 4. Killing of Afzal Khan at the hands of Shivaji. Choose the correct chronological order of the following events:
questions.explanation: The correct order is – 1– Shivaji's first encounter with the Mughals in 1657 AD. 4– Shivaji's Karnataka campaign in 1677 AD. 3– Night raid on Shaista Khan in 1663 AD. 2– Killing of Afzal Khan at the hands of Shivaji in 1659 AD.

questions.question_text: The author of "The Great Firm Theory of the Decline of the Mughal Empire" is:
questions.explanation: The author of 'The Great Firm Theory of the Decline of the Mughal Empire' is Karen Leonard, written in 1979

questions.question_text: Who started the Altamgha Jagir system:
questions.explanation: The Altamgha Jagir system was started by Jahangir in the Mughal period. This Jagir was granted to a specially favored family along with the Emperor's golden seal

questions.question_text: During whose reign was the rule of Mashrut implemented in the Mansabdari system?
questions.explanation: Mansab is a Persian word which means 'rank'. It had two parts: Zat and Sawar. Zat meant personal rank, while Sawar meant the number of cavalry. The word Mansabdar was used for an officer; this system is called the Mansabdari system. This system was started by Akbar in 1575 AD During Aurangzeb's reign, through Mashrut, a conditional or temporary appointment of a Mansabdar used to happen.

questions.question_text: In the Mughal period, which commodity constituted the largest part of exports from India?
questions.explanation: Among the items exported from India during the Mughal period, cotton cloth was in the highest quantity, which was exported to various countries, among which Sumatra, Java, Europe, Turkey, Arabia, etc., are prominent. Among the items exported from India, sugar, cloth, grain, indigo, saltpeter, cloves, camphor, saffron, sandalwood, coconut, opium, black pepper, spices, mercury, pearls, and animal skins were prominent

questions.question_text: Which ruler started the silver coin 'Rupiya'?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri started (pure silver coin which was called Rupiya which was 178 grains, copper coin was called Dam which was 380 grains). Sher Shah's currency system was extremely developed. He had introduced two new types of coins in place of the old coins. The value of the coin depended on its weight and the year it was minted

questions.question_text: During whose reign did the women artists Sahifa Banu and Nadira Banu live?
questions.explanation: Women artists Sahifa Banu and Nadira Banu were related to Jahangir's reign

questions.question_text: Under the leadership of Akbar, the battle between the Mughal army and the Afghan army took place on 5 November 1556–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– On 5 November 1556 AD, a battle took place between Akbar and the Afghan general Hemu at a place called Panipat. The Afghans were defeated. This was named the Second Battle of Panipat. At this time, the Afghan ruler was Adil Shah Sur.

questions.question_text: When did Akbar visit the tomb of Muinuddin Chishti for the first time:
questions.explanation: Akbar visited the tomb of Muinuddin Chishti for the first time in 1562 AD. Muinuddin Chishti's tomb is in Ajmer. He was born in 1143 AD in Sistan and died in 1236 AD in Ajmer. He had come to India with Muhammad Ghori in 1192 AD

questions.question_text: Babar assumed the title of Khaqan in:
questions.explanation: After the victory in the Panipat battle, Mughal ruler Babar assumed the title of Khaqan in 1526 AD. Babar was born on 14 February 1483 AD in Farghana (Uzbekistan). He died in 1530 AD in Agra. Babar wrote "Babarnama" in the Turkish language. Khaqan means "Khan of Khans"

questions.question_text: What is Gulabed?

options.B: A silver coin issued by Humayun.
options.C: The name of a Mughal mint.
options.D: The name of a painting made by Abul Hasan.

questions.explanation: Gulabed or Bandhani is a method of cloth dyeing, which is usually wavy or striped. It was made in Kashi

questions.question_text: From which of the following books do we get the information that Aurangzeb abolished various types of taxes levied on craftsmen?
questions.explanation: (1) Futuhat-i-Alamgiri was written in Persian by Ishwardas Nagar. (2) Nuskha-i-Dilkusha was written in Persian by Bhimsen. (3) Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh was written in Persian by Sujan Rai Bhandari. (4) Mirat-i-Ahmadi was written by Muhammad Ali Khan. Information is obtained from Mirat-i-Ahmadi that Aurangzeb abolished various types of taxes levied on craftsmen.

questions.question_text: During the Mughal period, shipbuilding centers were located in: 1. Bengal 2. Allahabad 3. Kashmir 4. Lahore
questions.explanation: Shipbuilding industry was not in a very developed state in the Mughal period. Akbar established a separate department for its construction so that the shipbuilding industry could be promoted Its major centers were Bengal, Allahabad, Kashmir, Lahore, and Sindh.

questions.question_text: Where did Tansen receive his music education?
questions.explanation: Tansen received his music education from Gwalior. Tansen was born in Gwalior; he was one of the Nine Gems of Akbar. He died in Agra. Akbar granted Tansen the title of 'Saraswati Kantha Bharan Vani Vilas'

questions.question_text: The influence of epics on painting and sculpture started appearing from the Gupta period. In which of the following has the depiction of Ramayana subjects not been done?

options.A: On the plinth of the Dashavatara temple of Deogarh.
options.B: In the carved sculptures on the Virupaksha temple of Pattadakal.
options.C: On the walls of the Kailasa temple of Ellora.

questions.explanation: The Persian translation of Mahabharata is known as Razmnama. During Akbar's reign, Mullah Abdul Qadir Badauni translated the Mahabharata into Persian - The context of Kailasa mountain being lifted by Ravana is on the Kailasa temple of Ellora. - The depiction of Ramayana subjects is on the carved sculptures of the Virupaksha temple. - The depiction of Ramayana subjects is on the plinth of the Dashavatara temple.

questions.question_text: Which of the Mughal emperors was very interested in painting?
