questions.explanation: Jahangir had an interest in painting. He gave more importance to painting in the Mughal period. Famous painters in his court were Farrukh Beg, Daulat, Manohar, Bishandas, Mansur, and Abul Hasan. Farrukh Beg had made a portrait of the Bijapur ruler Sultan Adil Shah

questions.question_text: In which Mughal building was the famous 'Peacock Throne' of the world kept?
questions.explanation: The Peacock Throne was established by Shahjahan in the Diwan-i-Aam of the Delhi Red Fort. This throne was known by the name 'Takht-e-Taus'. It cost 19 crore rupees; it was made of solid gold and priceless diamonds were studded in it

questions.question_text: In 1576 AD, the Mughal army fought a battle in Haldighati with ..............
questions.explanation: In 1576, the Mughal army fought a battle in Haldighati with Maharana Pratap. This battle was fought between Mughal Emperor Akbar and Rana Pratap on 18 June 1576 AD. In this battle, Maharana Pratap was defeated, but he did not accept the subordination of the Mughals. In this battle, the Mughal army was led by Raja Man Singh and Asaf Khan

questions.question_text: After conquering Gujarat from Bahadur Shah, to whom did Humayun give its authority?
questions.explanation: After the conquest of Gujarat, Humayun made Askari the in-charge of Gujarat. Gujarat was divided into 5 divisions. This arrangement was done on the basis of the administrative arrangement established by Babar in the Doab

questions.question_text: Who was the first Englishman to come to Western India?
questions.explanation: The first British person to reach Western India was Thomas Stephens, who was an English Jesuit priest and missionary, who reached Goa in October 1579 AD. William Hawkins came to Jahangir's court in 1608 AD and Sir Thomas Roe came to the Mughal court in 1615. John Mildenhall came to India in 1599 AD

questions.question_text: Which of the following musical instruments did Aurangzeb play?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb was proficient in playing the Veena, but he banned music in his kingdom. During his time, the most books on Indian classical music in Persian were written

questions.question_text: Which Jain Acharya did Akbar honor?
questions.explanation: Harivijay Suri was a Jain monk from 1526 to 1595 AD. He explained Jain philosophy to Akbar. Akbar was so impressed by him that he gave him the title of 'Jagat Guru'

questions.question_text: The tomb of which of the following persons is located outside India?
questions.explanation: After the death of Jahangir in 1627 AD, he was buried in Lahore in present-day Pakistan. Aurangzeb's tomb is in Aurangabad, and the tombs of Humayun and Jahandar Shah are located in Delhi

questions.question_text: According to Akbar's wish, who translated the Ramayana into Persian?
questions.explanation: Ramayana is a Hindu epic, which was composed by Sage Valmiki. During Akbar's time, Mullah Abdul Qadir Badauni translated it into Persian

questions.question_text: Which was the first tribe to form a marital alliance with Akbar?
questions.explanation: The first tribe to form a marital alliance with Akbar was Kachwaha. Rajput Raja Bharmal of Amer established this marital alliance by marrying his daughter Harkabai

questions.question_text: Mughal architecture is a confluence (synthesis) of which of the following styles?
questions.explanation: In Mughal architecture, a synthesis of Islamic-Persian, Turkish, and Hindu styles can be seen

questions.question_text: Which of the following gives an account of the domestic world of the Mughals?
questions.explanation: The account of the domestic world of the Mughals has been described by Gulbadan Begum in her book Humayun-nama

questions.question_text: During Akbar's reign, the land on which farming was done every year and which was never left empty. It was called
questions.explanation: During Akbar's reign, the land cultivated every year was called Polaj. In this, 2 crops were grown every year. Under the Zabti system, the most fertile land was classified under Polaj land

questions.question_text: Select the correct option from the options given below in light of the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R): Assertion (A): Mughal architecture reached its peak during the reign of Shahjahan. Reason (R): The Jama Masjid of Delhi, the Shalimar Bagh of Lahore, and the Red Fort of Delhi were built during the reign of Shahjahan.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (A) is in accordance with (R).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (A) is not in accordance with (R).

questions.explanation: Actually, from the point of view of the development of architectural art, Shahjahan's period is considered the Golden Age. This period is primarily the peak period of architectural art. He got many mosques and beautiful buildings constructed. Delhi's Jama Masjid, Delhi's Red Fort, Taj Mahal in Agra are considered Shahjahan's best architectural creations. Jahangir started the construction of Shalimar Bagh in Lahore, which was later completed by Shahjahan

questions.question_text: Select the correct option from the options given after reading the following statements:

options.A: A, B and C are correct.

questions.explanation: Akbar was very tolerant religiously. He respected all religions. For this reason, in 1575 AD, he built the Ibadat Khana (prayer house) where religious scholars of all religions exchanged their views. He slowly abandoned the orthodox thought process and opened the Ibadat Khana for all religions in 1578 AD. On 22 June 1579, he announced the Mahzar, under which restrictions were placed on the fatwas of Muslim Ulemas and he established his authority on the decisions of religious matters, due to which some Ulemas opposed it, who were thrown into the Yamuna river and killed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a great musician of Akbar's court?
questions.explanation: Tansen was the greatest musician of Akbar's court, whom Akbar obtained from Raja Ramchandra of Rewa. Akbar gave Tansen the title of 'Kantha Bharan Vani Vilas'. Akbar himself played the Naqqara (kettle drum) very well

questions.question_text: Under the Mughal land revenue system, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: One-third of the produce was considered under royal revenue during Akbar's reign.
options.B: The Sikandari gaz was considered the confirmed unit of measurement during Akbar's rule.
options.C: The Dahsala system increased the problems of the farmers tremendously.
options.D: Rope called Tanab was used for measurement.

questions.explanation: The Dahsala system was implemented by Akbar in 1580 AD on the advice of Todar Mal. For this reason, it is also called Todar Mal Bandobast. In this system, although the tax was determined on the basis of the previous 10 years of production and prevailing prices, its 1/10th part was collected every year. Which was called 'Mal-i-Harsala'. This was a type of Ryotwari system because the peasants themselves were directly responsible for paying the tax annually

questions.question_text: The Ryotwari system, which was started in some parts of British India, was one of the two main systems of collecting revenue from the peasants of agricultural land. This was originally started by ....................
questions.explanation: The Ryotwari system was originally started by Sher Shah Suri in which tax was collected by contacting the farmers directly. During the British period, this system was implemented in Madras, Bombay, Eastern Bengal, Assam, and Coorg. 51 percent of the land of British India was included under this system

questions.question_text: Babar died on 26 December 1530 AD and was buried in Agra's Aram Bagh. Later, during Sher Shah's reign, his body was taken to which of the following places and buried?
questions.explanation: On 26 December 1530 AD, Babar died in Agra and was buried in Agra in Nur-e-Afghan, whose modern name is Aram Bagh. But later, he was buried in Kabul at a place chosen by him

questions.question_text: In whose reign did Ahmad Shah Abdali first invade India?
questions.explanation: Ahmad Shah Abdali first invaded India in 1748 AD during the reign of Mughal ruler Muhammad Shah. The Third Battle of Panipat took place between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas on 14 January 1761, in which the Marathas were defeated

questions.question_text: For which of the following is Sher Shah Suri not known?

options.B: First Rupiya issued which remained in use until the 20th century
options.C: For starting the system of irrigation through canals
options.D: All were started by Sher Shah Suri

questions.explanation: Starting the system of irrigation through canals is not included in Sher Shah Suri's great works. The system of irrigation through canals was started by the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq. Sher Shah Suri was the first ruler who started the 'Rupiya' for the first time, which remained in use till almost the 20th century. The organization of the civil administration system was also done by Sher Shah Suri

questions.question_text: Who laid the foundation of Shalimar and Nishat Bagh in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Jahangir laid the foundation of the famous Shalimar and Nishat Bagh in Kashmir. Jahangir gave more patronage to painting than architecture. As a result, very few buildings were built in his time. The most notable building of Jahangir's time is 'Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula'

questions.question_text: Who among the following was appointed to the highest post in the judicial system during the reign of Mughal rulers?
questions.explanation: Qazi-ul-Quzat was appointed to the highest post in the judicial system during the reign of Mughal rulers. Muftis were appointed to assist the Chief Qazi, who interpreted the law, based on which the Chief Qazi gave the verdict

questions.question_text: Who got the Mahabharata translated into Persian and named it 'Razmnama'?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar got the Mahabharata translated into Persian and named it 'Razmnama'. The Persian translation of Mahabharata by the name of 'Razmnama' was done by Faizi, Mulla Sheri, Naqib, Sultan Haji, and Abdul Qadir Badauni. Akbar established a Translation Department under Faizi. Other major translated books during Akbar's time are as follows– translation of the astrological book Tajak by the name of 'Jayan-i-Zafar', translation of Sinhasan Battisi by the name of 'Nama-i-Khirad Afza', translation of Katha Saritsagar by the name of 'Bahr-ul-Asmar', translation of Panchatantra by the name of 'Anwar-i-Suhaili', etc

questions.question_text: The design and architecture of which building of the Mughal dynasty is associated with Ustad Isa Khan?
questions.explanation: Shahjahan's period is considered the Golden Age of Mughal architecture. The pinnacle of Shahjahan-era architecture is the tomb of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal built on the banks of the Yamuna river in Agra. Its chief architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahori, whom Shahjahan gave the title of Nadir-ul-Asar. Its chief mason or builder was Ustad Isa Khan

questions.question_text: Great Mughal Empire founder Babar linked his lineage to................

options.A: Timur from the father's lineage and Genghis Khan from the mother's lineage
options.B: Genghis Khan from the father's lineage and Timur from the mother's lineage
options.C: Chagatai Turk from father and mother's lineage
options.D: Mongol from father and mother's lineage

questions.explanation: Babar was born on 14 February 1483 AD in Farghana, a small principality of Mawar-un-Nahr (Transoxiana). Babar's father's name was Umar Sheikh Mirza, who was the owner of the Jagir of Farghana. And his mother's name was Qutlugh Nigar Khanum Begum. Babar was the 5th descendant of Timur from his father's side and the 14th descendant of Genghis Khan from his mother's side. In this way, there was a mixture of the blood of both Turks and Mongols in him

questions.question_text: Which years of the Ilahi Panchang (Era) revenue were included in the 'Dah-sala system'?
questions.explanation: Akbar made important reforms in the land revenue system. Under this, in 1580, Akbar implemented Ain-i-Dahsala (ten-year rule), this was the 24th year of Akbar's reign. Under this, production rates of grains from various regions between 1571 to 1580 AD were determined and its average was taken out. This was called 'Rai'. Based on this, not the tax but average cash rate was determined. Which was called 'Dastur'. Ilahi Panchang was started by Akbar in 1584 AD. Starting it from the first Nauroz after sitting on the throne i.e., 11 March 1556, the revenue data from the 15th to the 24th year of Akbar's reign were included in the 'Dahsala system'

questions.question_text: We get information about Aurangzeb banning music:
questions.explanation: & c) During Mughal rule, music had an important role in the cultural life of Hindus and Muslims. This journey which started from Akbar's reign continued smoothly until the Shahjahan period. Aurangzeb, giving importance to Islamic traditions, banned court singing, although it is clear from available sources that he did not ban the playing of musical instruments. He himself was a skilled Veena player. The description of the music ban by Aurangzeb is available in Manucci's 'Storia do Mogor' and Saqi Mustaid Khan's 'Maasir-i-Alamgiri'. It is important that despite the ban, the most books on Indian classical music in Persian were written during Aurangzeb's reign

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: Akbar was a major ruler of the Mughal dynasty; he did many important reform works in his reign, such as: End of Sati practice (1562), pilgrimage tax ban (1563), abolition of Jizya (1564), establishment of Ibadat-Khana (1575), announcement of Mahzar (1579), Ain-i-Dahsala (1580), etc. The Mansabdari system was also started during his time. Detailed information about the economic life of the Mughal period is obtained from Ain-i-Akbari and the memoirs of foreign writers

questions.question_text: Which of the following was responsible for the management of water transport or river movement in the Mughal provinces or Subahs?
questions.explanation: Mughal administration was a mixture of 'Indian and non-Indian (foreign) elements'. To run this administration in an organized manner, various major officers were appointed, among whom the main were– 1. Mir-i-Bahr - He was the head of the navy; his main task was to look after royal boats. 2. Waqia-Navis - He was the news writer who used to inform the center about all the news of the state. 3. Mir-i-Arz - He was in charge of applications sent to the Emperor. 4. Mushrif - He kept the accounts of the state's income and expenditure. 5. Mir Bakshi - He was the officer of the military department.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal era officer was called 'Auditor General'?
questions.explanation: To run the Delhi Sultanate's administration properly, various departments were established and their heads were appointed, such as: Ariz-i-Mumalik (Head of military department), Sadr-us-Sudur (Head of religion and charity department), Barid-i-Mumalik (Head of intelligence department), Mushrif-i-Mumalik (Accountant General), 'Mustaufi-i-Mumalik' was called the auditor (Auditor General) during the Sultanate period. In the Mughal period, this same officer was known by the name of 'Mustaufi' (Auditor)

questions.question_text: Pietra Dura or 'Pachchinkari', which is a characteristic feature of architectural art, was first used in India:
questions.explanation: Jahangir gave more patronage to painting than architecture. As a result, very few buildings were constructed in his time. The most important building of Jahangir's time is 'Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb' built in Agra This square-shaped tomb is the first such tomb made of flawless white marble in which, for the first time, 'Pietra Dura' is seen on a large scale in marble buildings. Although the use of this system (Pietra Dura) had already been done in 1600 AD in the 'Golmandal' of Udaipur (Rajasthan).

questions.question_text: Mansur, was a famous court painter, Mughal Emperor
questions.explanation: Jahangir-era major painters were Farrukh Beg, Bishandas, Ustad Mansur, Abul Hasan, Daulat and Manohar. Among whom the Emperor gave Ustad Mansur the title of Nadir-ul-Asr and Abul Hasan the title of 'Nadir-ud-Zaman'. Ustad Mansur made many paintings of rare animals, birds and unique flowers. Among his important creations - a rare Siberian crane and a unique flower of Bengal are especially notable. Abul Hasan had mastery in portrait painting. He made a painting for the front page of 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' and made a copy of the picture of Dutch saint John Paul

questions.question_text: Which emperor started the 178 grain silver coin 'Rupiya'?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah made notable improvements in the currency system. He stopped mixed metal coins and introduced pure gold, silver, and copper coins. Whose weight and size were fixed. Silver Rupiya was first issued by Sher Shah. Whose weight was 178 grains. The exchange ratio of silver and copper was 1:64

questions.question_text: Akbar had deep respect for the Chishti saints and he used to go on a pilgrimage to Sheikh Muinuddin Chishti's tomb in Ajmer every year. From which year did he stop going on foot on the annual pilgrimage to the Ajmer tomb?
questions.explanation: In 1579, Akbar started the Mahzar-nama (declaration or petition) due to which Akbar himself used to settle all disputes related to religion. In the same year, Akbar stopped the journey on foot to Muinuddin Chishti's tomb

questions.question_text: Which of the following buildings did Raja Man Singh not build?
questions.explanation: The Rohtas fort was built by Sher Shah Suri for the security of his north-western border and a powerful army was appointed under the leadership of Haibat Khan and Khawas Khan

questions.question_text: Which scholar revised the curriculum taught in Madrasas during Akbar's time?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Abu-al Faizi, elder brother of Abul Fazl and Akbar's poet laureate. In 1588, he became Akbar's special poet 'Malik-ush-Shuara'. Akbar established a translation department under Faizi, and he revised the curriculum taught in Madrasas

questions.question_text: Match the revenue-related vocabulary of List-I with the meanings of List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I | List-II A. Patta | 1. Letter of acceptance B. Qabuliyat | 2. Crop collection C. Tashkhis | 3. Land revenue demand | assessment document related to D. Tehsil | 4. Revenue estimation Code: | A | B | C | D
questions.explanation: Patta and Qabuliyat were started by Sher Shah Suri. The document in which the details of the land that the state gave to the farmer were written was called Patta, and how much tax the farmer would give for that land was called Qabuliyat. Tashkhis is related to revenue estimation and Tehsil is related to crop collection

questions.question_text: In which year did Akbar order the killing/exile of a large number of Qazis for spreading unrest and inciting rebellion?
questions.explanation: In 1579, Akbar started the Mahzar-nama (declaration or petition) in which the dispute among the religious gurus of Muslims would be resolved, in which the King's order would be supreme, about which some fundamentalist Ulemas protested, whom Akbar got killed by throwing them into the water in 1580 AD

questions.question_text: The urban population of Mughal India was approximately around 1601 AD:
questions.explanation: According to Nizamuddin Ahmad's book Tabaqat-i-Akbari, in 1593 there were 120 big cities and 3200 roughly settlements, and the total population was 1 crore, in which 15% of people lived in cities, in which 1/4 of people were associated with agriculture

questions.question_text: The king of which princely state helped Akbar in imprisoning the king of Kangra, Jai Chand?
questions.explanation: In 1556, Akbar defeated the king of Kangra, Jai Chand. The king of Nurpur helped Akbar

questions.question_text: What is the old name of Nurpur princely state?
questions.explanation: Earlier, the name of Nurpur princely state was Dhameri, later it was named Nurpur after Nurjahan

questions.question_text: Who was the first English ambassador in the Mughal royal court?
questions.explanation: The first English ambassador, Captain Hawkins, brought a letter from James I to Akbar in 1608. After this, Thomas Roe came to Jahangir's court in 1615. Given the options, Captain Hawkins is not there, hence Thomas Roe will be the correct answer

questions.question_text: Which one of the following mosques was built by Shahjahan?
questions.explanation: Shahjahan built the Jama Masjid located near the Red Fort in Delhi in 1656 AD. It has scalloped arches made of floral decoration in the Shahjahani style

questions.question_text: Which Mughal ruler shifted his capital from Agra to Delhi?
questions.explanation: In the year 1638 AD, the capital was shifted from Agra to Delhi by Mughal ruler Shahjahan

questions.question_text: On whose order was the painting of Hamzanama made?
questions.explanation: The first highly important work seen in the Mughal painting studio is Dastan-e-Amir Hamza, i.e., Hamzanama. It has about 1200 paintings. According to Badauni and Shahnawaz Khan, the work of its illustration started with Akbar's inspiration, which took 15 years. About 50 painters worked under the guidance of Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad in this, among whom Bihzad was prominent

questions.question_text: After the decline of Mughal rule, Safdarjung became the ruler of which province?
questions.explanation: After Aurangzeb's death, the decline of the Mughal Empire started. After this, independent regional powers emerged. Among which one major regional state was Awadh. Where first Saadat Khan established his power. The ruler of Awadh was called Nawab Wazir. After this, in 1739 AD, Safdarjung became the ruler of Awadh province

questions.question_text: Who was considered the head of the judiciary during Akbar's time?
questions.explanation: The head of the religious department was Sadr-us-Sudur, whose main duties were to protect Sharia and appoint Qazis and Muftis, but when he worked in the capacity of the head of the judiciary department, then he was not called Sadr-us-Sudur but Chief Qazi (Qazi-ul-Quzat)

questions.question_text: Where was Jahangir's capital?
questions.explanation: Jahangir's capital was Agra, which was first made his capital by Sultan Sikandar Lodi in 1506. In the year 1638 AD, the capital was taken from Agra to Delhi by Shahjahan

questions.question_text: Who wrote Ain-i-Akbari?
questions.explanation: Ain-i-Akbari was written in the 16th century by Abul Fazl, who was one of Akbar's nine gems. It contains descriptions about Akbar's court and administration. It is the third part of Akbarnama

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a Mughal Ameer?
questions.explanation: Yildiz was not an Ameer in the Mughal period; he was an opponent of Qutbuddin Aibak in the Delhi Sultanate and a slave of Ghori

questions.question_text: Which of the following terms signifies a Royal Order?
questions.explanation: Farman is a Persian word which means issuing an order. Other words are from the Maratha Empire. Royal orders are related to Farman. This was a royal decree issued by the Emperor

questions.question_text: Which Kumaon ruler was present in Shahjahan's court?
questions.explanation: Baz Bahadur Chand was a powerful ruler of Kumaon. At the time of the Kandahar battle, he fought for the Mughals with great bravery. Shahjahan was pleased with him and supported him in solving his state's problems, but after some time, Shahjahan attacked Baz Bahadur and forced him to accept subordination. Finally, in 1654 AD, he accepted subordination by appearing in the Mughal court

questions.question_text: "Akbar was the real founder of the Mughal Empire." Who said this?
questions.explanation: Akbar is considered the greatest ruler of the Mughal dynasty. In this context, Stanley Lane-Poole in his book called Akbar the real founder of the Mughal Empire. Apart from this, other historians also reviewed Akbar's works– According to Dr. R.P. Tripathi, he made many efforts to bring the country under one umbrella; if the southern sultanates had understood his plan and cooperated with him, then India would have been the most powerful and prosperous country of Europe and Asia, and its history would have been different. According to Vincent Smith, he was a born ruler of men and among the known rulers of history, he is the real claimant to be the best.

questions.question_text: Sher Shah was appointed 'Ataliq' in early life
questions.explanation: Sher Shah was the great-grandson of Ibrahim Sur and the son of Hasan. By his ability, Sher Shah became the confidant of his father's patron Jamal Khan. In 1528 AD, he went to South Bihar and was appointed the teacher (Ataliq) and guardian of Bihar Khan's son Jalal Khan. After the ruler's death, he was made the Naib-Subedar of South Bihar

questions.question_text: The Saiyyad brothers, whose mention is found in Mughal politics, are:
questions.explanation: In Mughal politics, Abdullah Khan and Hussain Ali Khan were famous as the Saiyyad brothers. They had a special role in the war of succession. They claimed that they were descendants of a brave person Abul Farrukh of Mesopotamia. In the war of succession, they fought on behalf of Prince Muazzam, who became the Mughal Emperor by the name of Bahadur Shah. The Saiyyad brothers had a major role in making Farrukhsiyar the Emperor

questions.question_text: After the Battle of Haldighati, under whose leadership did Akbar send military campaigns against Maharana Pratap? (1) Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana (2) Shahbaz Khan (3) Jagannath Kachwaha (4) Abdullah Khan Use the code given below to choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: After the Battle of Haldighati (June 1576 AD), between 1580-84 AD, Akbar sent several military campaigns against Maharana Pratap under the leadership of army commanders Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, Shahbaz Khan, and Jagannath Kachwaha, but they did not achieve success. Maharana Pratap won back many areas around Kumbhalgarh and Chittor and established a new capital in Chavand near present Dungarpur

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal provinces (Subahs) was Man Singh appointed as Subedar (Governor) by Akbar? (1) Kabul (2) Gujarat (3) Bihar (4) Bengal Use the code given below to choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Man Singh was given the Subedari of Kabul, Bihar, and Bengal by Akbar. Akbar made Man Singh the Subedar of Kabul against the Afghans from 1580-1587 AD. He was made the Subedar of Bihar from 1587-1594 AD, where his task was to suppress the rebellions of local Zamindars. In 1594 AD, he was handed over the Subedari of Bengal

questions.question_text: Which of the following fought on the side of Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa: (1) Mahmud Lodi, (2) Hasan Khan, (3) Maldeo, (4) Medini Rai
questions.explanation: The Battle of Khanwa (16 March 1527 AD) took place between Babar and Rana Sanga. In this battle, Rana Sanga was supported by Ibrahim Lodi's brother Mahmud Lodi, Medini Rai, Hasan Khan Mewati, and Maldeo. In this same battle, Babar gave the slogan of Jihad

questions.question_text: Two army commanders of Maldeo who fought strongly against Sher Shah in the Battle of Giri-Sumel:
questions.explanation: After Rao Ganga, Rao Maldeo (1532-62 AD) became the ruler of Marwar. Ferishta and Badauni called Maldeo the great warrior prince of India. In 1544 AD, between Ajmer and Jodhpur, at a place called Samel or Giri-Sumel, a battle took place between Maldeo and the Afghans under the leadership of Sher Shah Suri. In this battle, which lasted for about 1 month, Maldeo's two army commanders Jeta and Kumpa were killed

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the conflict between Rana Pratap and Akbar are true - 1. Akbar lured Rana Pratap's step-brother Jagmal and granted him the Jagir of Jahazpur. 2. After Man Singh left, Rana Pratap recaptured Gogunda. 3. Rana Pratap incited Narayan Das of Idar to rebel against Akbar. 4. The last unsuccessful attempt to capture Rana Pratap was launched in 1584-85, when Jagannath Kachwaha was sent with a large military unit. Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: The following statements regarding the conflict between Rana Pratap and Akbar are true 1. Akbar lured Rana Pratap's step-brother Jagmal and granted him the Jagir of Jahazpur. 2. After Man Singh left, Rana Pratap recaptured Gogunda. 3. Rana Pratap incited Narayan Das of Idar to rebel against Akbar. 4. The last unsuccessful attempt to capture Rana Pratap was launched in 1584-85, when Jagannath Kachwaha was sent with a large military unit. 5. Rana Pratap could not capture Chittor and Mandalgarh.

questions.question_text: The commander whom Shahjahan sent to suppress Aurangzeb's rebellion:
questions.explanation: Shahjahan sent Jaswant Singh to suppress Aurangzeb's rebellion. A battle took place in April 1658 AD between Aurangzeb and Murad and Jaswant Singh at a place called Dharmat, which is also known as the 'Battle of Dharmat'. Jaswant Singh lost this battle. Shahjahan granted the title of 'Maharaja' to Jaswant Singh

questions.question_text: Which of the following Ulema was a Qazi of Jaunpur, who issued a 'Fatwa' against Akbar?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Against Akbar's religious policy, Mullah Yazdi of Jaunpur issued a Fatwa in 1580 AD with the intention that now the Emperor is no longer a Muslim, therefore it is according to the rules for Muslims to rebel against him.

questions.question_text: Which ruler of Amer served three Mughal emperors?
questions.explanation: Amer ruler Mirza Raja Jai Singh served three Mughal emperors. Man Singh and Bhagwant Das or Bhagwant Das served Akbar, and Sawai Jai Singh entered Mughal service during Aurangzeb's time

questions.question_text: The feudal lords of Marwar who were kept free from service and Rekh for three generations due to being close relatives of the king, were called:
questions.explanation: The feudal lords of Marwar, who were kept free from service and Rekh for three generations due to being close relatives of the king, were called Rajvi. While distant relatives of Sardars were called by the name of Rawlot Note- (For 190- 194) Read the following paragraph and after that give answers to the questions given: Jahangir mentions a minaret, a pond, and a pavilion that used to be used as a 'hunting palace' about 29 km from Lahore. Today this place is known by the name of Sheikhupura, but in 1606 Jahangir calls it Jahangirpura and after that in 1620 he calls it Jahangirabad, the meaning of both these is 'City of Jahangir', in this Jahangirabad is more emotional. Here Jahangir's favorite deer died in 1606, it was buried in a grave. And a statue of the deer on it and an inscription written by Mulla Muhammad Hussain in Kashmir were placed. Near this memorial stone, a minaret was built in 1606 under the supervision of the area's Jagirdar Sikandar Muin Khan. According to Jahangir's orders, Sikandar Muin Khan also got a pond and a royal palace built. When the construction work was in progress, at that time Muin died, despite this, the construction work of the complex was completed properly in 1620, the construction work of the later phases was completed under the supervision of Iradat Khan. So much expenditure was incurred on its construction that the Emperor mentioned this amount in his memoirs. Jahangir considered this place a 'Royal Hunting Site', although his successors found this place insufficient and spent a lot of wealth on the reconstruction of its pavilion in 1634.

questions.question_text: In which of the following cities is the 'Hiran Minar' built during Akbar's reign located?
questions.explanation: During Akbar's reign, a wide synthesis of Hindu-Muslim styles is seen in construction works, Akbar got many forts and palaces built in Agra and Fatehpur Sikri. During his reign, Hiran Minar was built in Malwa

questions.question_text: In which of his books did Jahangir mention the minaret, pond, and pavilion twice?
questions.explanation: 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' is Mughal Emperor Jahangir's autobiography. It is written in Persian. In this book, Jahangir mentioned the minaret, pond, and pavilion twice

questions.question_text: Who among these was also called Sheikhu Baba?
questions.explanation: Jahangir was born on 31 August 1569 AD from Mughal Emperor Akbar's wife Mariam-uz-Zamani. Jahangir was born with the blessings of Sheikh Salim Chishti, so Akbar used to call him Sheikhu Baba lovingly

questions.question_text: Jahangirpura and Jahangirabad both names have the same meaning, i.e., 'City of Jahangir'. From which language has the word 'Pura' been taken?
questions.explanation: The word 'Pura' has been taken from Sanskrit language

questions.question_text: The plan of Sheikhupura minaret is similar to the Hiran Minar built during Akbar's reign. In which of the following cities is Hiran Minar located?
questions.explanation: Hiran Minar is located in Fatehpur Sikri. Akbar built it in the name of his favorite elephant, Hiran

questions.question_text: Mir Jumla attacked the Ahom state and captured the Ahom capital Garhgaon. In 1663 AD, a treaty took place between the Ahom state and him. In which year did Ahom force the Mughals to leave Kuch Hajo and accept the Manas river as the border?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb appointed Mir Jumla as the Governor of Bengal. Mir Jumla attacked the Ahom state of Assam in March 1662 and captured the Ahom capital Garhgaon. In 1663 AD, a treaty took place between the Ahom state and him. After the death of Jumla, the Ahoms in 1681 forced the Mughals to leave Kuch Hajo and accept the Manas river as the border

questions.question_text: "Sufism started becoming pantheistic when the ideas of Ibn al-Arabi (died 1240) first started influencing the Persian poetry of Jalaluddin Rumi (1207-73) and Abdur Rahman Jami (1414-92) and after that the efforts of Ashraf Jahangir Simnani (beginning of fifteenth century) inside India. At this time, the influence of the pantheism of Shankaracharya's Vedanta philosophy was constantly increasing within Brahmanical thoughts." Which of the following Mughal rulers recognized this idea first?
questions.explanation: Like Akbar, Jahangir was also always eager to meet and converse with dervishes, saints and religious thinkers of various sects, and he used to honor them with gifts and donations. Jahangir found the most peace among the followers of Vedanta. He called Vedanta the Tasawwuf philosophy. In the sequence of efforts to establish proximity with them, in the eleventh year of his reign (1616), he met the Ujjain-resident Jadrup Gosain. UGC has also given the answer (c)

questions.question_text: Who got the Sahibabad garden built in Shahjahanabad, which was used as a sarai for wealthy merchants?
questions.explanation: Jahan Ara Begum was Shahjahan's daughter. The map of Shahjahanabad was made by Jahan Ara Begum. The Sahibabad garden located in Chandni Chowk and Shahjahanabad was also built by Jahan Ara Begum. 'Sahibabad's garden' was also known as Begum ka Bagh. A sarai for wealthy merchants and travelers was also built in it

questions.question_text: "He built sarais at a distance of two kos on the highway to ensure safety on the roads and provide facilities to travelers. Here travelers could get bedding and cooked food. There was also a provision for the supply of uncooked food. He built about 1700 such sarais." Who is this ruler?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah, to make the roads safe and for the convenience of travelers, built sarais at a distance of two kos (roughly four miles) each. Separate sections were built in these sarais for Hindus and Muslims, where they could get cots, bedding, and food. Separate Brahman kitchens were kept in the sarais for Hindus, according to caste rules. For those Hindus who cooked their own food due to caste rules, there was also an arrangement for uncooked food materials

questions.question_text: Which of the following scholars prepared the draft of Mahzar in 1579 AD?
questions.explanation: In 1579 AD, Akbar issued Mahzar. The inspiration to issue Mahzar was given by Sheikh Mubarak and his son Faizi. Mahzar gave Akbar the authority that in case of disagreement among Ulemas on any subject, he can grant recognition to any one view that he considers best while keeping in mind the needs of the empire. Sheikh Mubarak had prepared the draft of the Mahzar

questions.question_text: Choose the correct statements from the following:
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar introduced various weight and value coins of gold-silver in his time and fixed their mutual ratio. Akbar established a Shahi-taksal (Royal Mint) in Delhi. Care was taken for high quality in minting coins of all three metals in his time. Gold was almost pure, there was never a decline below 96 percent in the purity of silver and the purity of copper remained. Akbar's most popular gold coin was 'Ilahi'. (1 Ilahi = 10 Rupee) while the largest gold coin was 'Shansah' which was heavier than even 100 tolas. Akbar had images of Ram-Sita engraved on some of his coins and wrote 'Ram-Siya' in Devanagari.

questions.question_text: The concept of Watan Jagir came into existence in the final years of which emperor's reign:
questions.explanation: There was a provision to give salary to Mansabdars in the form of both cash and jagir. On the death of Mansabdars, their property was confiscated in the tenure period. In this way, the position of Mansabdar was not hereditary. The jagirs of Mansabdars were transferred from one province to another. The exception to this method of giving jagir was that of Watan Jagirs. Such jagirs were granted as salary only in hereditary states, especially to Rajputs

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Mughal military campaign on Balkh and Badakhshan? (i) The declared desire of the Mughal emperors was that they should recapture their ancestral land. (ii) Shahjahan wanted to punish the ruler of Balkh and Badakhshan, Nazar Muhammad, who had eyes on Kabul. (iii) Shahjahan wanted to seat Dara Shikoh on the throne as the independent ruler of Balkh. (iv) Shahjahan wanted to give the jagir of Badakhshan to Prince Aurangzeb. Select the answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Shahjahan was concerned about the Uzbek attacks on Kabul again and again and their conspiracy with the Baluch and Afghan tribes. Their main desire was that they should recapture their ancestral land, for which they sent Murad to punish the ruler of Balkh and Badakhshan, Nazar Muhammad, and they captured it

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal emperors was influenced by Vedanta philosophy and went to meet Jadrup Gosain?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Jahangir was influenced by Vedanta philosophy. He met the Ujjain-based Vedanta scholar Jadrup Gosain many times. Later when Jadrup Gosain came to Mathura, Jahangir met him twice there too

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct answer using the code given below: 1. War of Khurram 2. Battle of Chausa 3. Battle of Dharmat 4. War of Khusrau Code
questions.explanation: Battle of Chausa - 1539 AD. Rebellion of Khusrau - 1606 AD. Rebellion of Khurram - 1623 – 26 AD. Battle of Dharmat - 1658 AD.

questions.question_text: How much percentage of the produce was taken from the farmers as land revenue during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: During Akbar's time, 1/3 part of the produce was collected as tax in the form of revenue. The tax was taken from the farmers in the form of coins and for this different prices of grains were fixed in different areas. Akbar accepted farmers as the owner of the land and the state established direct contact with the farmers

questions.question_text: "When the Charan of a princely state of Rajasthan went to the Mughal Emperor to complain about the atrocities by his own king, the Emperor, calling him a 'Mota Raja', ignored his complaint." Identify the King, his princely state, and the Mughal Emperor who called him 'Mota Raja':

options.A: Raja Uday Singh of Jodhpur and Emperor Akbar
options.B: Mirza Raja Jai Singh of Amer and Emperor Jahangir
options.C: Raja Jai Singh of Bikaner and Emperor Akbar
options.D: Rana Raj Singh of Mewar and Emperor Aurangzeb

questions.explanation: In the medieval history of India, the tradition of music that the Rajputs adopted and practiced in their court is called Charan literature. This is a regional tradition of Rajasthan which was ignored by Jodhpur king Uday Singh and restrictions were imposed on the Charans, about which a complaint was made to the Mughal Emperor Akbar. Akbar ignored his complaint and called Raja Uday Singh a 'Mota Raja' (great king)

questions.question_text: In medieval India, there used to be mutual cultural exchange among people of different sects. Mughal rulers and Ameers used to discuss with a Brahmin ascetic and proponent of Vedic thoughts, Jadrup Gosain. They were influenced by his Vedanta knowledge, which was considered similar to Sufism. Who among the following met Jadrup Gosain?

options.A: Akbar, Jahangir and Mirza Aziz Koka
options.B: Jahangir, Shahjahan and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana
options.C: Akbar, Prince Khusrau and Prince Khurram
options.D: Shahjahan, Raja Birbal and Suraj Singh Rathore

questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, in the field of folk culture and social, religious behavior, religious ideas were exchanged among Hindus-Muslims. Mughal Emperor Akbar, Jahangir, and Mirza Aziz Koka met the Ujjain-based Hindu saint proponent of Vedic thoughts 'Jadrup Gosain'. Jahangir was extremely influenced by Jadrup Gosain. He appointed a Hindu named Sri Kant as the Pesa (local tax/official) of Hindus

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Mughal rulers, who ruled after the death of Aurangzeb, in chronological order: (i) Bahadur Shah I (ii) Farrukhsiyar (iii) Rafi-ud-darajat (iv) Jahandar Shah Choose the correct answer from the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: Mughal rulers ruled after the death of Aurangzeb - Bahadur Shah I, Jahandar Shah, Farrukhsiyar, (between the murder of Farrukhsiyar and Muhammad Shah, the Saiyyad brothers made Rafi-ud-daulah, Rafi-ud-darajat the Mughal Emperor), Muhammad Shah and the last ruler Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar). Due to supporting the rebels in the 1857 rebellion, the British arrested Bahadur Shah II and exiled him to Rangoon where he died in 1862 AD

questions.question_text: Below two statements are given, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R). Read the statements and use the code given below to choose the correct answer: Assertion (A) : Manucci says, "On arriving at Surat for unloading you find abundant wealth. Because the main trade of India's Ameers was to invest their money in betting for foreign countries- France, England and even Italy." Reason (R): Although the trade by Ameers was only a part of the total trade in the country, this meant diverting a portion of resources extracted from agriculture into domestic and foreign trade. Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Venetian resident Manucci came to the Mughal court in the last days of Shahjahan's reign. His work is famous by the name 'Storia do Mogor', but it lacks reliable information. Because more reliance has been placed on rumors and hearsay. From contemporary sources, the description of trade from Surat port to the Far East is obtained

questions.question_text: Aliyar Khan was the architect of which of the following buildings?
questions.explanation: Tomb of Hasan Khan (Sher Shah's father) and Tomb of Sher Shah (Sasaram, Bihar) were built by architect Aliyar Khan. Sher Shah's tomb is a beautiful building built in the middle of a pond. The architect of Humayun's tomb was Mirak Mirza Ghiyas

questions.question_text: In Akbar's court, who among the following painters was the son of Kahar?
questions.explanation: The influence of Akbar's reign also fell on the country's art and culture. There were many Hindu courtiers, military officers, and feudal lords in Akbar's court. Akbar had 9 very competent courtiers to run his empire, whom Akbar knew as the Nine Gems. Among these, Todar Mal, Abul Fazl (historian), Tansen (singer), Birbal, Man Singh, Faizi were prominent. Daswant was a prominent painter and son of a Kahar. Paintings made by him hold an important place in Akbar-era paintings

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor celebrated Diwali in Srinagar, Kashmir?
questions.explanation: During the Mughal period, various Hindu and Muslim festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm and without any discrimination. Mughal rulers granted official recognition to many Hindu festivals- Diwali, Shivratri, Dussehra and Ram Navami. Mughal dynasty rulers used to celebrate Diwali festival with great pomp. Mughal Emperor Akbar celebrated the Diwali festival by going to Srinagar, whose description Abul Fazl has done in his famous book 'Ain-i-Akbari'

questions.question_text: Who translated the memoirs of Firdous Makani (Babar) from Turkish to Persian and presented it to Akbar and won excessive praise?
questions.explanation: Rahim's full name was Abdul Rahim (Abdur Rahim) Khan-i-Khanan. His father Bairam Khan was the guardian of Mughal Emperor Akbar. After his death, Akbar included Rahim in his Nine Gems, granted him the title of "Mirza Khan". He translated Babar's autobiography "Tuzuk-i-Babari" into Persian. He also had knowledge of Arabic, Turkish, Persian, Sanskrit and Hindi languages

questions.question_text: The conflict between Emperor Shahjahan and Guru Hargobind was on the issue of hunting, due to which one after another military conflicts took place. Which Pathan led the Sikh army?
questions.explanation: The conflict between Shahjahan and Guru Hargobind was on the issue of hunting. Due to which hostility arose between the Sikhs and the Mughals. The Sikh army was led by a Pathan named Painda Khan. Guru Hargobind planned to build a city named Sri Gobindpur on the banks of the Beas river, its construction was not in the interest of the Mughals, which was the main reason for the dispute between the Sikhs and the Mughals

questions.question_text: Who said the following sentence in the context of defining his relationship with Aziz Koka? "There is a river of milk between me and Aziz which I cannot cross."
questions.explanation: Akbar had worked under the guardianship of his Aziz since childhood. For the first three years of his birth, he remained under the guardianship of Askari. Akbar worked as the subedar of Ghazni and Lahore in his childhood. Akbar's coronation took place in 1556 AD at a place called Kalanaur in Gurdaspur district, Punjab, under the supervision of Bairam Khan. Akbar appointed Bairam Khan his Vakil (Wazir) and granted him the title of "Khan-i-Khanan". Bairam Khan had the biggest hand in strengthening Akbar's initial position, who was related to the Shia sect of Iran. After his death, Akbar ruled under the supervision of Maham Anga (foster mother). In this way, it can be said that he remained connected to his Aziz throughout his life and received service from time to time

questions.question_text: Rafiu-d-din Shirazi, who came from Iran, writes, "I was standing in a circle made of tents among the crowd (in Agra), just then a voice echoed 'May God protect the King.' I thought the king had come. I saw a twenty-year-old youth leaning towards his favorite people. I guessed that he must be the king. But people did not perform any etiquette or greetings. I was very surprised and I asked if there is no tradition of showing respect to the king. They replied that for the courtiers there are too many etiquettes, but the king himself is very informal. He does not make any distinction between companions and strangers." About which ruler has Shirazi written this?
questions.explanation: Rafiu-d-din Shirazi wrote about Akbar that "He does not make any distinction between his companions and strangers, and due to the works he did in religious, economic, and social fields, Akbar is called Akbar the Great." The main purpose of his religious policy was 'Universal Tolerance', this is also called the principle of 'Sulh-i-kul', i.e., peaceful behavior with everyone. In the context of Akbar's reign, Abul Fazl has written in 'Ain-i-Akbari' that "The Emperor is a ray that is capable of illuminating the entire universe."

questions.question_text: The concept of Watan Jagir developed at the end of Akbar's reign. Which of the following statements regarding Watan Jagir are correct? (i) This was a permanent and hereditary land grant. (ii) It can be confiscated to punish the land grant holder. (iii) A new Watan Jagir can be created to reward an Ameer. (iv) A part of the revenue of Watan Jagir can be given as a gift. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: Watan Jagir developed at the end of Akbar's reign. Main points related to Watan Jagir (1) It was a jagir given to subordinate kings in their own ruling area. (2) This was a permanent and hereditary land grant. (3) It can be confiscated to punish the land grant holder. (4) A new Watan Jagir can be created to reward an Ameer. (5) A part of the revenue of Watan Jagir can be given as a gift. (6) It was not transferable. (7) For the first time, Aurangzeb made an effort to merge 'Watan Jagir' into the empire in the context of 'Marwar'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding grants given to women are correct? (i) Abul Fazl talks about grants provided to Iranian and Turani women. (ii) Jahangir appointed a special official in charge of grants provided to women, the foster sister of his father. (iii) In Majma-ul-Shahjahani, there is a mention of two categories of Aima (land): Chak-ha-i-Mustamali (land held by women) and Muzaraat (land held by men). (iv) Regarding Madad-i-Maash, through a 1690 farman, Aurangzeb deprived his daughter of her share if she was married or had other provisions and decided that a widow could keep the grant received by her husband for her lifetime. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: Mughal-era society was divided into two classes - rich class and common people such as peasants, craftsmen and laborers. Thousands of women- concubines, mistresses and maids lived in the harem of the emperors and big chiefs of the state. Abul Fazl talks about grants provided to Iranian and Turani women and some noble women had honorable positions during the Mughal period such as- Akbar's mother 'Maham Anga' ran the petticoat government from 1560-62 and remained the all-in-all of the state. Nurjahan's mother 'Asmat Begum' discovered the method of making perfume

questions.question_text: When Shahjahan bifurcated the post of Karori/Amil (revenue collector) and Amin (tax assessor), what percentage of the Karori's remuneration was fixed?

options.A: It was reduced from 5 percent to 2.5 percent.
options.B: It was reduced from 2 percent to 1 percent.
options.C: It was reduced from 7.5 percent to 5 percent.
options.D: It was reduced from 8 percent to 5 percent.

questions.explanation: When Shahjahan bifurcated the post of Karori/Amil (revenue collector) and Amin (tax assessor), the Karori's remuneration share was reduced from 8 percent to 5 percent

questions.question_text: "This emperor gave orders not to cause harm to travelers and merchants by local and other officials and if anyone dies in a business accident and without an heir, not to grab their property. Along with this, officials were told to buy goods from merchants only at market prices."
questions.explanation: Sher Shah is known as a system reformer, not as a system founder. As an empire builder and administrator, he is considered Akbar's predecessor. Under Sher Shah's finance system, the main source of the state was the tax levied on land. Which was called 'Lagaan'. Sher Shah's land revenue system was mainly "Ryotwari"- in which direct contact was established with the farmers. This system was implemented in all parts of the state except Multan, Malwa, Rajasthan, and Western Punjab. He gave orders to his officials not to cause harm to travelers and merchants and gave orders not to grab the property of a merchant in case of an accident or death and told the officials to buy goods from merchants only at market price

questions.question_text: The word 'Mir-i-Tuzuk' was used in the royal court for
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, 'Mir-i-Tuzuk' was the Chief Secretary. His job was to fix the revenue. He was also an officer of religious ceremony. His job was to manage religious festivals, etc. The commission has removed this question in the final answer key

questions.question_text: Whose reign did the Satnami rebellion take place in?
questions.explanation: During Aurangzeb's time in 1672 AD, a battle took place between peasants and Mughals at a place called Narnaul near Mathura, which was led by a religious sect named Satnami. The Satnami rebellion started due to a fight between a Satnami and a Mughal military officer. Local Hindu Zamindars supported the Mughals in suppressing this rebellion

questions.question_text: Who built the Moti Masjid of Agra Fort?
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, Shahjahan's reign was the Golden Age from the point of view of architecture. Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, and Moti Masjid (1654) located in Agra Fort are famous buildings built of pure white marble. Aurangzeb built the Moti Masjid located in Delhi. Moti Masjid is famous for its sanctity and brightness. It is the most attractive among all buildings in Agra

questions.question_text: In the Mansabdari system, what is the meaning of 'Mansab'?
questions.explanation: In the Mansabdari system, Mansab was a post. The Mansabdari system was adopted from Central Asia. Akbar implemented the Mansabdari system in his empire. Mir Bakshi was a high-ranking Mansabdar

questions.question_text: Where did Babar die?
questions.explanation: Babar was the one who established the Mughal dynasty in India. Babar was born in Andijan of Central Asia. He attacked and defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526 AD and conquered the empire of India. After conquering and defeating four Indian rulers continuously for four years, finally, in 1530 AD, Babar died in Agra. Later he was taken to Kabul and buried

questions.question_text: Which of the Mughal emperors is called 'Kalandar' in India?
questions.explanation: Babur, who laid the foundation of the Mughal dynasty in India, was also known as 'Kalandar'. Impressed by Babur's generosity, the people gave him the title of 'Kalandar'. Babur invaded India in 1526 AD, defeated Ibrahim Lodi, and established the Mughal dynasty. Babur's reign in India was only for four years. He died in 1530 AD due to excessive consumption of alcohol

questions.question_text: In 1620 AD, under whose leadership did Jahangir send an expedition against Kangra?
questions.explanation: A remarkable success of Jahangir's reign was the capture of the fort of Kangra located in the hills of Northern Eastern Punjab in 1620 AD. Jahangir sent Raja Vikramajit for this victory expedition. During Jahangir's reign in 1622 AD, the Shah of Persia snatched Kandahar from the Mughals and established his rule over it

questions.question_text: In which language was 'Tuzk-e-Babri' written by Babur?
questions.explanation: Babur took great interest in literature. He wrote his autobiography - Tuzk-e-Babri (Baburnama) in the Turki language. Baburnama was translated into Persian three times. Baburnama contains a detailed description of the contemporary political condition of India, the contemporary living standards of Indians, crops, and flowers

questions.question_text: What was 'Zabt' in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: In the beginning, Akbar adopted the Zabt system used by Sher Shah, in which 1/3 part of the land produce was taken as tax based on the yield. Meaning, Zabt was a type of tax. Due to the Zabt system being very expensive and flawed, on the recommendation of Shihabuddin Ahmad, it was abolished in 1568 AD and replaced by the Naskh or Kankut system. The commission has considered (b) measurement of land as its answer

questions.question_text: During the reign of Sher Shah, which department head looked after the state's income and expenditure?
questions.explanation: The founder and greatest ruler of the Sur dynasty was Sher Shah Suri. The head who looked after the state's income and expenditure was called Diwan-i-Wizarat. He was the chief of revenue and economy. Looking after the state's income and expenditure and overseeing the work of other ministers was also his responsibility

questions.question_text: Under whose reign was Sheikh Abdul Haq Mohaddis Dehlvi a prominent religious scholar?
questions.explanation: After Akbar, Jahangir took over the reins of the Mughal power. Jahangir had to struggle with his son Khusrau to gain power. Jahangir was a religiously tolerant ruler. The famous religious scholar Sheikh Abdul Haq Mohaddis Dehlvi lived in his court. Jahangir's greatest quality was his love for justice, and his greatest weakness was excessive drinking

questions.question_text: Who was responsible for the conquest of Malwa during Akbar's time?
questions.explanation: In the context of empire expansion, Akbar made his first attack in 1561 AD on Malwa ruler Baz Bahadur. In this war, Akbar sent Adham Khan, Pir Muhammad, and Abdullah Khan Uzbek against Baz Bahadur. All of them were included among Akbar's great commanders. In this war, Baz Bahadur's wife, Rupmati, saved her chastity by consuming poison. The Public Service Commission has considered (b) Abdullah Khan Uzbek as its answer, whereas Akbar had sent all three - Adham Khan, Abdullah Khan Uzbek, and Pir Muhammad - for Malwa in 1561 AD. The commission has given (c) in the revised answer key, whereas according to the question, the correct answer should be (b)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Akbar's nobles is not correct?

options.A: During the early years of Akbar's reign, his nobles were mainly Turani and Khurasani nobles.
options.B: From 1561, he started the recruitment of Rajput princes who had the right to keep their ancestral lands in exchange for mansab.
options.C: Along with this, he was also discriminating against Sheikhzada (Indian Muslims) nobles.
options.D: For complete control over the nobles, he took back their jagirs and made cash payments; also, to ensure regular maintenance of the cavalry army, he strictly implemented the rules related to branding (dagh) and attendance (chehra).

questions.explanation: Since Akbar was considered a ruler of very liberal nature. He did not harbor feelings of hatred towards Hindus, which is why he also started the recruitment of Rajput princes. Among Akbar's nobles, there were mainly Turani and Khurasani nobles. To keep control over the nobles, he took their jagirs and made cash payments

questions.question_text: Who among the following kept a part of his library in the harem, where the women of the harem used to read and recite books to him before he went to sleep?
questions.explanation: Akbar was illiterate, but he was very fond of acquiring knowledge; hence, he kept a part of his library in the harem too, where the women of the harem used to read and recite books to him before he went to sleep

questions.question_text: A Mughal emperor showed conservative and religious-minded people that language is not a natural process (zaban-e-qudrat), but a worldly way of learning. To prove his argument, he kept newborn babies in an entirely secluded place, known as Gung Mahal, through a practical experiment. Who was that Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Akbar had built a dormitory for newborn babies where no one else lived, and he put those newborns in that dormitory where only a mute nurse lived. She used to raise those children, who was mute herself. After a few years, Akbar went to that palace and tried to talk to the 4-year-old children, but those children were found unable to speak, which proved Akbar's argument correct

questions.question_text: Despite being influenced by the beauty of Kashmir and its gardens, which emperor ordered in the sixth year of his reign that no emperor would visit Kashmir except for military and administrative purposes, because he believed that going to Kashmir to fulfill the hobby of recreation was not a suitable reason?
questions.explanation: When Aurangzeb visited Jammu and Kashmir, he was so influenced by the beauty there that in the sixth year of becoming emperor, he ordered that no emperor would visit Kashmir except for military and administrative purposes. Because he believed that going to Kashmir to fulfill the hobby of recreation was not a suitable reason

questions.question_text: "Among all the sovereign rulers of Timur's family, even among all the rulers of Delhi since the time of Sikandar Lodi until now, none was equal to him in resolve, self-restraint, and justice." In the above excerpt, Khafi Khan is praising the sense of justice of which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Khafi Khan has described Aurangzeb's reign in detail in his book "Muntakhab-ul-Lubab", in which Khafi Khan has also discussed Aurangzeb's resolve, self-restraint, and justice. According to him, Aurangzeb's sense of justice was superior to all other emperors

questions.question_text: Which two rulers of India and Uzbekistan agreed to conquer the routes leading to the holy regions of Mecca and Medina? Identify those rulers from the following:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–India's ruler Akbar and Uzbekistan's ruler Abdullah Khan Uzbek agreed to conquer the routes leading to the holy regions of Mecca and Medina. Among the medieval rulers of the world, Akbar is counted as a great emperor. He was not only the best among the Mughal emperors, but he also holds a leading position among the prominent and great rulers of India.

questions.question_text: "It has been ordered that the names of those living in the harem should not be mentioned publicly, but they should be referred to based on some attribute based on their birthplace, country, or city." Identify the emperor who ended the practice of making the names of the Begums public?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Mughal emperor Akbar ended the practice of making the names of the Begums public. Akbar ordered that the names of those living in the harem should not be made public, but they should be referred to based on some attribute based on their birthplace, country, or city.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal ruler observed villagers collecting date-palm liquor in the Chambal valley between Bayana and Dholpur and described the method of extracting the toddy?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Mughal ruler Babur observed villagers collecting date-palm liquor in the Chambal valley between Bayana and Dholpur and described the method of extracting the toddy.

questions.question_text: Who said: 'Whoever comes to the inn should be served food according to their rank from the government treasury and their horses should be given grain and water':
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Sher Shah also did many public welfare works. Under this, he first got roads and inns constructed. Among the roads constructed by him, four features are noteworthy. The first road went from Lahore to Sonargaon (Bengal), which was the longest road and is called 'Sadak-e-Azam'. On the banks of these roads, he planted fruit-bearing and shady trees so that travelers could rest under them and tie their horses.

questions.question_text: Name the famous astrologer of Akbar's court, who wrote an astrology-related book 'Tajaknilakanthi'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Tajak Nilakanthi is basically based on Yavan astrology, in which accurate predictions of the future are made based on Varga Kundali for the year after birth or through Prashna Kundali. In this, Acharya Nilakanth has, on one hand, given a new dimension to Vedic astrology by coordinating the Yavan method with Vedic astrology principles. On the other hand, he has also done the sacred work of the confluence of two cultures.

questions.question_text: Which ruler used to participate in the gambling session during the festival of Diwali, which continued for three nights?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The festival of Diwali is celebrated in the month of Kartik. On this occasion, houses are cleaned. On the day of Diwali, Lakshmi is worshipped. On this occasion, gambling was considered a supreme duty. People used to gamble all night long. In this gambling, most people used to lose everything they had. Mughal ruler Jahangir used to participate in the gambling session on the festival of Diwali, which continued for three nights.

questions.question_text: Shah Jahan used to reward his nobles for providing patronage to architecture. Besides the construction of a grand garden in Kashmir, which noble was promoted for his diplomatic behavior with the unruly people?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Shah Jahan used to reward his nobles for providing patronage to architecture. Besides the construction of a grand garden in Kashmir, the noble Jafar Khan was promoted for his diplomatic behavior with the unruly people.

questions.question_text: Which European traveler commented that Nur Jahan built pleasure gardens, palaces, and inns everywhere in the entire state to increase her image and prestige?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– Francisco Pelsaert (1620-27) was a Dutch merchant who came to India during the Jahangir period. He was the head of the Dutch mint in Agra. In his account, he has written about Agra city, its structure, and also about Nur Jahan.

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R): Assertion (A): Because of marriage to Nur Jahan, Jahangir became indifferent towards administration. Reason (R): During 1611-22, Nur Jahan had formed her own separate group (junta), and she had become quite powerful. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– After marriage to Jahangir in 1611 AD, Nur Jahan had formed an influential group together with her father Itimad-ud-Daulah and brother Asaf Khan and Shah Jahan Khurram, but until 1622, Jahangir himself used to take political decisions until his health deteriorated.

questions.question_text: Jizya was reimposed by Aurangzeb in 1679. What is Satish Chandra's argument regarding the reimposition of Jizya by Aurangzeb?

options.A: Jizya was imposed due to the opposition of Hindus and the greed of rulers.
options.B: Aurangzeb imposed Jizya so that non-Muslims could be forced to accept Islam.
options.C: The imposition of Jizya was an indicator of the deepening political crisis, especially due to the deteriorating situation in the Deccan.
options.D: It was a means to reduce the burden on the royal treasury.

questions.explanation: Satish Chandra has written in his book 'Medieval India' that the reimposition of Jizya by Aurangzeb in 1679 was an indicator of the deepening political crisis. At that time, the conditions in the Deccan were very bad. Therefore, the collection of Jizya had to be stopped by 1705. Later in 1712, it was finally abolished

questions.question_text: Regarding the interest of the Marathas in helping the Mughal emperor against Nadir Shah's invasion, which of the following reasons are correct? (i) The Marathas considered Nadir Shah's invasion as an invasion done by an external aggressor. (ii) If Nadir Shah had stayed in Hindustan and established a new dynasty, it would have been a heavy blow to Maratha ambitions. (iii) The Shah had asked Bajirao to reach quickly for the emperor's help, which was decided according to an agreement with Aurangzeb that whenever the empire was in trouble, the Marathas would help. (iv) Bajirao reached to help the Mughal army. Choose the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
questions.explanation: The interest of the Marathas in helping the Mughal emperor against Nadir Shah's invasion on Delhi in 1739 was because the Marathas considered Nadir Shah a foreigner. According to the Marathas, Nadir Shah could become their rival in India and could affect the ambition of empire expansion. However, they did not provide any help and Nadir Shah devastated the Delhi empire

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor was given the title of 'Mujaddid' by contemporary historians?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Mughal emperor Shah Jahan was given the title of 'Mujaddid' by contemporary historians. Whereas, on 24 February 1628, he became the ruler under the name Abul Muzaffar Shahabuddin Muhammad Sahib-e-Qiran-Sani Shah Jahan.

questions.question_text: What was the position of Mir Bakshi in the Mughal administrative system?

options.A: Chief Military Commander of the Mughal army

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Every military and non-military officer was recorded in the army list, the emperor was the chief commander. Mir Bakshi was the head of the military administration, who looked after works like recruitment in the army, salary, inspection of mansabdars' armies, etc.

questions.question_text: Who first used cannons and guns in war in India–
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Mughal-era Babur was the only emperor who first used cannons and guns in war.

questions.question_text: Which of the following North-Eastern Indian states were attacked by the Mughals? (i) Dimasa (ii) Meitei (iii) Ahom (iv) Koch Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation- Mughal ruler Aurangzeb focused his attention on the North-Eastern frontier. During the war of succession, the rulers of Koch Bihar and Assam captured the Mughal district Kamrup. In 1660 AD, Mir Jumla captured the capital of Koch Bihar. On 13 March 1662, Mir Jumla defeated the Ahom armies and captured it. As a result of this victory, sufficient wealth came into Mir Jumla's hands.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following according to the correct chronology and choose the correct answer from the code below – (i) Conquest of Odisha by Akbar (ii) Start of the Dagh system (iii) Creation of twelve subahs (iv) Start of the Dual ranks (Zat and Sawar) Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The conquest of Odisha was done by Akbar in 1592 AD through Man Singh. In 1573 AD, Akbar introduced the Dagh system. So that mansabdars could not change horses and kept horses and cavalrymen in the correct number. In 1580 AD, the entire empire was divided into 12 subahs (provinces). In 1595 AD, reforms were made in Zat and Sawar.

questions.question_text: Which of the following officers had no connection with the urban administration of the Mughal empire?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– In the Mughal era, Qazi, Mir-e-Adl, and Kotwal had a connection with urban administration. Among them, the Qazi's work was to administer justice, Mir-e-Adl's work was to look after the cavalry department for urban administration, and the Kotwal was the city chief, whereas Nazim had a connection with provincial administration, who was the governor of the province.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: (i) Shah Jahan ended the practices of Jharokha Darshan and Tula Dan. (ii) Shah Jahan refused to give land grants for the construction of a rest house for Jain monks to Shantidas, who was a prominent jeweler and banker of Ahmedabad. (iii) Shah Jahan banned matrimonial relations between Hindus and Muslims in Kashmir. (iv) Shah Jahan gave permission to religious scholars not to perform Sijdah. Which of the above statements are not correct? Select your answer from the code given below: Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– Mughal emperor Shah Jahan favored Islam in the early years of his reign. But later, due to the influence of Dara Shikoh and Jahanara, he became tolerant. He continued the practices of Jharokha Darshan, Tula Dan, and applying tilak on the foreheads of Hindu kings. Shah Jahan gave land grants to Shantidas, who was a prominent jeweler and banker of Ahmedabad, for the construction of a rest house for Jain monks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.C: Jama-e-Kamil - Revenue assessment at standard rate
options.D: Sivvan Nigah - One who sends news

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– In the Mughal army, Ahadi soldiers were the emperor's personal soldiers. Ashrafi was called a person of noble descent, whereas Jama-e-Kamil was the finance officer of the pargana who collected revenue, and the work of Sivvan Nigah was to send news.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: Second Battle of Panipat – Akbar versus Ibrahim Lodi
options.B: Battle of Haldighati – Akbar versus Rana Udai Singh
options.C: Battle of Dharmat – Aurangzeb versus Dara
options.D: Battle of Samugarh – Aurangzeb versus Shuja

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Correct matches are – (a) Second Battle of Panipat – Akbar versus Hemu (b) Battle of Haldighati – Akbar versus Maharana Pratap (c) Battle of Dharmat – Aurangzeb versus Dara (15 April, 1658) (d) Battle of Samugarh – Aurangzeb versus Dara (29 May, 1658)

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Correct matches are – List-I List-II (a) Khasa-e-Sharifa (I) Emperor's own prestige (b) Samabandi (II) Soldier appointed for special occasion (c) Talab (III) Mansabdar's salary demand (d) Zakat (IV) Toll tax

questions.question_text: There are two statements below, the first is called Assertion (A) and the second is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Every jagirdar was primarily a mansabdar, but every mansabdar was not a jagirdar. Reason (R): Some mansabdars were paid in cash, not through jagirs. Select the correct answer from the given code. Code :

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– In the Mughal era, Zamindars were those landowners who had hereditary rights to collect land revenue from some villages. A jagirdar could primarily be a mansabdar. But it is not necessary that a mansabdar be a jagirdar. Usually, mansabdars were paid in cash. Jagirdars were not paid in cash.

questions.question_text: Which statement is correct regarding Humayun?

options.A: Humayun had a deep interest in astronomy and geography.
options.B: Humayun made a heavy collection of books for the royal library.
options.C: Humayun used to carry some selected books for reading during his military campaigns.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation—Humayun was a loyal friend, an obedient son, and an affectionate brother. Ferishta writes that Humayun was peerless in astrology and mathematics. He used to compose very beautiful poetry. Humayun's library was filled with books from the country and abroad. Besides this, he used to take some books with him even during military campaigns.

questions.question_text: Din-e-Ilahi was primarily –

options.B: A mixture of Hindu religion and Islam
options.C: Repeating the principle of world equality

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation—Akbar founded 'Din-e-Ilahi' in 1582 AD, which Abul Fazl named 'Tauhid-e-Ilahi'. Under this, Akbar tried to make it acceptable to all by including the core principles of all religions. The ideals of Din-e-Ilahi were as follows—liberality and generosity, forgiving the wicked, and overlooking anger with humility, renunciation of worldly desires, longing for high deeds, etc. Din-e-Ilahi was adopted by Akbar's friend (Hindu) Birbal.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the Rathore rebellion – (i) The Rathore rebellion occurred as a result of the death of Jaswant Singh's son Prithvi Singh. (ii) Aurangzeb made Indra Singh the ruler of Marwar. (iii) The Rathore rebellion occurred as a result of Aurangzeb's plan to make Jodhpur a part of the Mughal empire. (iv) Rani Hadi was supported in the rebellion by the Rathores and the Rana of Mewar Jai Singh. Which of the above statements is correct?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation—Aurangzeb gave the throne of Marwar and ruler status of Nagaur to Indra Singh, grandson of Raja Jaswant Singh's elder brother Amar Singh, on 26 May, 1679, who expressed his gratitude by gifting 36 lakh rupees to the emperor. Similarly, when the Mughals attacked Rani Hadi, the Rathores and the Rana of Mewar Jai Singh supported her.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Aurangzeb appointed Muhtasibs in all provinces.
options.B: Aurangzeb continued the celebration of the Nowruz festival.
options.C: Most books in Persian on Indian classical music were written during Aurangzeb's reign.
options.D: Aurangzeb himself was adept at playing the Veena.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Aurangzeb's contemporary historian Khafi Khan writes in his famous book 'Muntakhab-ul-Lubab' that after ascending the throne, Aurangzeb stopped the engraving of the Kalima on coins and also stopped the celebration of the Nowruz festival. Muhtasibs were appointed for inspection for public conduct. Most books in Persian on classical music were written during Aurangzeb's reign. Aurangzeb himself was an adept scholar of the Veena.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: (i) W. C. Smith is among those historians who first talked about peasant revolts against the Mughal empire. (ii) He also argued that a middle class developed sufficiently as a result of the policy of encouraging commerce of the Mughal empire. (iii) C. A. Bayly developed the 'Great Firm' theory to explain the fall of the Mughal empire. (iv) J. F. Richards argued that a serious agricultural crisis arose as a result of peasant resistance. Which of the above statements are not correct? Select your answer from the code given below: Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2014) Explanation—On the study of the Mughal empire, (W. C. Smith) first talked about peasant revolts against the Mughal empire. He argued that a middle class developed sufficiently as a result of the policy of encouraging commerce of the Mughal empire.
