questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct? 1. Sher Shah got a new road constructed from Lahore to Multan. 2. He exiled Mirza Haidar Dughlat to Kashmir. 3. After the Marwar conquest, he attacked Gujarat. 4. He started the Dagh and Chehra practice. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Sher Shah did many public welfare works. Under this, he first constructed roads and inns. He built four roads. The first road went from Lahore to Sonargaon (Bengal), which was the longest road and was called Sadak-e-Azam. The fourth road constructed by Sher Shah went from Multan to Lahore. Sher Shah did not exile Kashmir's ruler Mirza Haidar Dughlat. Sher Shah did the Chittorgarh conquest after the Marwar conquest in 1544 AD. He kept the already prevailing Dagh and Chehra practice as it was.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements about Akbar: 1. The last part of Ain-e-Akbari contains a detailed description of India's ideologies and customs. 2. Akbar ordered Sheikh Faizi to translate the Upanishads into Persian. 3. Akbar expressed his preference in favor of a marriage for the first time in 1578 in a discussion with Sheikh Ibrahim Sirhindi. 4. Akbar issued an order in 1562-63 that women and children should not be made slaves in military campaigns against rebels and defiant villages. Which of the above statements are correct? Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Abul Fazl wrote Ain-e-Akbari under Akbar's patronage. 'Ain-e-Akbari' is divided into three parts. Its last part contains a detailed description of India's ideologies and customs. Dara Shikoh translated the Upanishads into Persian. Akbar abolished the slavery system in 1562 AD.

questions.question_text: "The reality of centralized Mughal power is one thing, whether it was good or bad is another thing." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Historian J. F. Richards has analyzed and interpreted Mughal history in the most analytical and scientific ways. He has said, "The reality of centralized Mughal power is one thing, whether it was good or bad is another thing."

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) – Assertion (A): Weak politicians and incompetent military commanders were responsible for the rapid disintegration of the Mughal empire in the first half of the eighteenth century. Reason (R): The Mughal politicians and nobles of this period were busy fulfilling their self-interests. They had no interest in the fate of the empire. In the context of the two statements above, which of the following statements is correct? Select the correct answer from the code given below – Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—The main reason for the rapid disintegration of the Mughal empire in the first half of the 18th century was incompetent rulers, not military commanders. Taking advantage of weak rulers, many independent provinces came into existence. The founding rulers of these provinces were in the Mughal military service, so calling them incompetent would not be appropriate. Whereas, due to the weak power, Mughal politicians and nobles got busy with their own self-interest fulfillment.

questions.question_text: Keep the following in correct chronology and identify which is the correct answer from the codes given in the code? (i) Battle of Khanwa (ii) Battle of Palkhed (iii) Battle of Chausa (iv) Battle of Dharmat Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Wars and their chronology are as follows– Battle of Khanwa 1527 AD. Battle of Chausa 1539 AD. Battle of Dharmat 1658 AD. Battle of Palkhed 1728 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following historical texts was not written during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Muhammad Qasim Hindu Shah or Firishta completed his work while serving the ruler of Bijapur, Adil Shah II. Historical texts like Humayun-nama (Gulbadan Begum), Tarikh Sher Shahi (Abbas Khan Sarwani), and Tabaqat-e-Akbari (Nizamuddin Ahmad) were written during Akbar's time.

questions.question_text: Which historian has written that "The relatives and acquaintances of Nur Jahan were promoted with all kinds of favors."
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Jahangir-era historian Mutamid Khan wrote in his work (Iqbalnama-e-Jahangiri) that "The relatives and acquaintances of Nur Jahan were promoted with all kinds of favors." It is known that Jahangir married Mehr-un-Nissa in 1611 AD and gave her the title of Nur Jahan.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The noble class in Mughal India was a legally recognized class like Europe.
options.B: Mughal nobles were not included in high-level administration.
options.C: The social distinction between Iranian, Turani, and Sheikhzada nobles had disappeared.
options.D: Those nobles whose ancestors had been in the Mughal ruler's service for more than one generation were called Khanazad.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation—Those nobles whose ancestors had been in the service of Mughal rulers for more than one generation. They were known as Khanazad, this statement is correct. The noble class in Mughal India was a legally recognized class like Europe. They had their own armies, and they usually lived in forts. Which were called Garhi. The size of the Garhis was considered a symbol of their prestige.

questions.question_text: Babur's grandmother, who was the wife of Yunus Khan Mughal, and who made arrangements for her grandson after his father's death and suppressed the conspirators, tell her name:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation—After the death of Babur's father, Babur's grandmother Esan Daulat Begum made a very large contribution in making Babur a disciplined, protected, and safe person. During his early struggle to capture Ferghana, she was effectively his advisor. In 1494, when Umar Sheikh Mirza II died, Babur was an insecure boy of about 11 years old. He found himself surrounded by the enemies of his own family. At that time, Esan Daulat Begum was constantly with her grandson and kept guiding Babur.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) : Assertion (A): After the death of Islam Shah, the governance system established by Sher Shah became disorganized. Reason (R): Akbar adopted the land revenue system established by Sher Shah with some modifications. In the context of the two statements above, which of the following is correct? Choose the correct answer from the codes given below~ Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation—Islam Shah was a high-class administrator and capable military commander. He made many rules related to governance. Through his death, the policies made by Sher Shah disappeared. Akbar adopted the land revenue system established by Sher Shah after some modifications.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Mughal painting is not correct?

options.A: Akbar established a large painting gallery and created a new and lively school, which illustrated the Hamzanama in the 1560s.
options.B: Throughout Akbar's reign, painters were recruited from different parts of India for the illustration of many books.
options.C: It seems that as soon as Akbar's reign began, emphasis started to be placed on realism in painting.
options.D: The characteristics of Renaissance-era painting did not affect Mughal art at all during Akbar's reign.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation—Although Akbar was not highly educated, he had a special interest in the field of art. Akbar patronized capable painters. The names of painters have been given in Ain-e-Akbari. Mir Saiyyad Ali, Khwaja Abdus Samad, Farrukh Qalam, Miskin, Daswant, Keshav, etc. Akbar first got the Dastan-e-Amir Hamza illustrated. Akbar got the Tarikh-e-Khandan-e-Timuria illustrated by Basawan.

questions.question_text: Which European wrote about the situation of education of Mughal princes and princesses during Akbar's time?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Father Anthony Monserrate was appointed by Akbar as the tutor of his son Prince Murad. In his travelogue, he has shed light on Akbar's character, personality, Mughal court, education system of princes/princesses, social-religious situation, and the lifestyle of the common people. Monserrate condemned the Sati practice and termed it heinous murder.

questions.question_text: In the context of the Watan-Jagir institution, which is not correct?

options.A: The concept of Watan-Jagir started during the reign of Sultan Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316 A.D.).
options.B: The concept of Watan-Jagir started during the last years of Akbar's reign.
options.C: The primary source of information regarding the origin and concept of Watan-Jagir is Akbar's farman for Raja Rai Singh of Bikaner.
options.D: The revenue of Watan-Jagir was part of the Watan-Jagirdar's salary.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation—During Akbar's time, 'Watan Jagir' was mainly granted to Rajputs as administrative recognition. In these jagirs, the mansabdars had administrative rights along with ownership.

questions.question_text: Who among the following collected information about disabled people and gave them maintenance allowance:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation—Sher Shah did many works for the welfare of the subjects. Besides this, he generously made arrangements for the livelihood of the blind, elderly, disabled, widows, and scholars. Contemporary historian Abbas Khan Sarwani writes that he had fixed langar (free food) for the poor, beggars, and disabled in his army. He used to give them delicious food.

questions.question_text: Which was that Mughal royal woman after whose death many Rajput nobles had their heads shaved along with Akbar?
questions.explanation: Explanation—Hamida Banu Begum, who was Akbar's mother, died in 1604 AD. On her death, many Rajput nobles along with Akbar had their heads shaved.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct choice from the code given below: List-I List-II (Traveler) (Reign)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation– List-I List-II (Traveler) (Reign) A. Ralph Fitch I. Akbar B. Bernier II. Aurangzeb C. Sidi Ali Reis III. Humayun D. Thomas Roe IV. Jahangir

questions.question_text: Which Mughal ruler mentioned that 'Salt is not available in Kashmir, hence it is brought from Hindustan'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation—Jahangir has given a description of India in his autobiography Tuzk-e-Jahangiri. He mentioned that salt is not available in Kashmir. Hence it is brought from Hindustan.

questions.question_text: Watan-Jagir is a common terminology. Whose part was its land revenue?

options.C: Part of the income of Watan Jagirdars
options.D: Part of the additional income of Watan Jagirdars

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Watan jagir was mainly granted to Rajputs. In this, usually, their own area was given to them in the form of jagir. This was a hereditary jagir.

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R): Assertion (A): In 1574 AD, Akbar allotted mansab to nobles, servants, and military officers and changed them into a single service system. This mansab indicated the rank, salary, and size of the military contingent of an officer. Reason (R): At a practical level, except for some very small or religious officers, all remaining officers of the government were mansabdars and the promotion or demotion of an officer was determined by the fact that how many mansabs under him were increased or decreased. In the context of the two statements given above, which answer is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Both the question's assertion and reason are correct. Mansab indicates an officer's rank, salary, and size of the military contingent. An officer's promotion or demotion was determined by the fact that how many mansabs were increased under him or decreased.

questions.question_text: In 1568, Akbar issued a Fathnama of Chittor. In which Persian text is the full excerpt of Fathnama given?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Full information about the Fathnama of Chittor issued by Akbar in 1568 is found in the Persian book named Munshaat-e-Namakin.

questions.question_text: "These Sharir people never spend money from their treasury..................They forcibly take money from the weak and poor peasants living under them". For his statement, who is the speaker?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – These Sharir people never spend money from their treasury, "They forcibly take money from the weak and poor peasants living under them". This statement is related to Farid alias Sher Shah.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – The correct matched sequence of the given code is – Amir-i-Hajib – Chief Manager Mir-i-Arz – Chief of army in the center Mushrif – Accountant Barid – Spy officer

questions.question_text: In the Mughal times, two methods were prevalent for giving gifts to the emperor– Peshkash and Nazar. Aurangzeb redefined this terminology. Which of the following statements is not correct in this context?

options.A: Any Peshkash given in cash should be called Nala.
options.B: Gifts given by princes should be called Niyaz.
options.C: Gifts given by nobles should be called Nisar.
options.D: Gifts given to express thanks and express respect on less important occasions should be called Nazar.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation—In the Mughal times, two methods were prevalent for giving gifts to the emperor– Peshkash and Nazar. Aurangzeb redefined this terminology in this way. In which any Peshkash given in cash should be called Nala, gifts given by princes should be called Niyaz, gifts given by nobles should be called Nisar which is true, but option (d) is false.

questions.question_text: Akbar gave the title of 'Farzand' to whom?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation—Amber (Jaipur) king Biharimal or Bharmal was a Kachwaha Rajput. Biharimal married his daughter to Mughal emperor Akbar in 1562 AD. Pleased, Akbar gave a mansab of 5000 to Biharimal in the Mughal army and also gave high mansabs to Biharimal's son Bhagwandas and Man Singh. Pleased with Man Singh's service, Akbar gave him the title of 'Farzand'.

questions.question_text: The Mughal emperor taken prisoner by Nadir Shah was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – In 1739 AD, Persian ruler Nadir Shah invaded India and took Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah prisoner. Nadir Shah entered Delhi on 20 March 1739. The Khutba in his name was read and coins were issued. Nadir Shah stayed in Delhi for two months, looted as much wealth as he could, and took it from India, and before leaving, he appointed Muhammad Shah again as the emperor of India.

questions.question_text: Who called Dara Shikoh a 'Mulhid'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Aurangzeb was a religiously firm ruler and Dara was religiously liberal. In the war of succession, Aurangzeb defeated Dara. Some people requested Aurangzeb to spare Dara's life, on which Aurangzeb called him 'Al-Mulhid' and, without forgiving him, got Dara killed in Delhi.

questions.question_text: To whom was the Mughal title of 'Mirza Raja' granted?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Jahandar Shah gave the title of 'Mirza Raja' to Amber king Jai Singh and Farrukhsiyar gave Jai Singh the title of Sawai. Jai Singh made Jaipur the new capital of his state in place of Amber on 18 November 1727.

questions.question_text: Which last Deccan state was included in the Mughal empire by Aurangzeb?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Aurangzeb conquered the Deccan states of Bijapur and Golconda. Golconda was included as the last Deccan state by Aurangzeb. Aurangzeb took Golconda ruler Abul Hasan prisoner and sent him to the fort of Daulatabad and included his state in the Mughal empire in October 1687.

questions.question_text: What was Akbar's most important achievement in the North-West frontier?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Akbar's most important achievement in the North-West frontier was the conquest of Kandahar. In 1595 AD, Kandahar was obtained by the Mughals without any war. Kandahar was in the hands of Persia but the then fort commander of there, Muzaffar Husain Mirza's relations with the Persian court had turned sour. For self-protection, he willingly handed over the fort to Mughal commander Shah Beg and himself went into the service of the Mughals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Mughal administration system is not true –

options.A: The Mughal administration system was mainly a military administration.
options.B: This was a centralized absolutism or autocracy.
options.C: The emperor had to follow Islamic traditions.
options.D: It was not necessary for the emperor to take advice from ministers.

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Undoubtedly, the basis of the origin of the Mughal administration system was military. Basically, the Mughal administration was a centralized administration, in which the emperor was the chief of the entire state and administration and the undisputed user of all powers. Besides this, it was not necessary for the emperor to take advice from ministers.

questions.question_text: Who divided the Mughal empire into provinces for the first time?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Akbar divided the Mughal empire into provinces for the first time. Akbar divided his entire empire into 12 subahs (provinces) in 1580 AD, but at the end of the reign, after the victory of Berar, Khandesh, and Ahmednagar of South India, the number of subahs increased to 15.

questions.question_text: Under the Mughal provincial administrative system of "mutual control and power balance," which officer kept control over the Subedar:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The work of the Prime Minister was given to the Diwan and in later times the Diwan became the Wazir of the state and the Prime Minister. The work of Bakshi was to look after the army. Faujdar was the chief administrator of the Sarkar (district). Waqia-e-Navis was a news writer. Hence, the Diwan kept control over the Subedar.

questions.question_text: Who was the in-charge officer of the administration of a Pargana or Mahal?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Shiqdar was the prominent officer of the Pargana. He was a military officer. His prominent responsibility was to maintain peace and order in the Pargana and provide help in collecting revenue. Akbar appointed Amil for collecting revenue of the Pargana. Bitikchi - this was a clerk who prepared land and revenue-related documents. Potdar - this was the treasurer of the Pargana.

questions.question_text: With whose reign can the origin of the Mansabdari system in India be associated?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Every military officer was given a mansab rank. The mansabdari system was the basis of the Mughal army which was based on the decimal system of the Mongols (Genghis Khan). The emperor gave them salary according to their mansab. Mansab was not a title or rank, but it indicated an officer's position. It meant rank or grade.

questions.question_text: Who successfully rebelled and took Jahangir prisoner in his military camp?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Mahabat Khan successfully rebelled and took Jahangir prisoner in his military camp. When Nur Jahan got the information that Mahabat Khan had imprisoned the emperor, she held Asaf Khan responsible for this.

questions.question_text: For the commemoration of which event did Akbar establish Fatehpur Sikri?

options.B: Birth of Salim with the blessings of Sheikh Salim Chishti
options.D: Victory of Mughals in the Battle of Haldighati

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Sheikh Salim Chishti prophesied the birth of Akbar's three sons. Immediately after this, in 1569 AD, Prince Salim was born. Two years after Salim's birth, in 1571 AD, he ordered the construction of Fatehpur Sikri. But according to other contemporary historians, Akbar got Fatehpur Sikri built with the objective of expressing respect towards Sheikh Salim Chishti. Besides this, in memory of the Gujarat victory, he got the Buland Darwaza built.

questions.question_text: Which new province was formed during the reign of Jahangir?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- During Jahangir's time, a new province named 'Odisha' was formed. In 1611 AD, Todar Mal's son Raja Kalyanchand won Khurda (Odisha) from Raja Purushottam Das. Odisha was formed by separating it from Bengal. Shah Jahan formed Kashmir and Sindh by separating them from Kabul and Multan respectively. Bijapur and Golconda were new subahs included by Aurangzeb.

questions.question_text: What were mansabdars with Zat of 500 to less than 2,500 called?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Mansabdars with Zat of 500 to less than 2500 were called Amir. Mansabdars below 500 were called 'Mansabdar' only.

questions.question_text: Who was the chief of the Mughal navy?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The chief of the Mughal navy was 'Mir-e-Bahr'. During the Gujarat conquest in 1572 AD and Bengal campaign, Akbar felt the need for a navy for the first time. As a result, Akbar established a department which was called 'Navada'. Its chief officer was 'Mir-e-Bahr'.

questions.question_text: By what name is the Chagatai Turk rule known in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– 'Chagatai Turk' rule is known as Mughal in India. The word 'Mughal' is derived from a Latin word, which means 'brave'. Babur was the founder of the Mughal dynasty in India. He was related to Chagatai Turk from his father's (Umar Sheikh Mirza) side and to the Mongol dynasty from his mother's side. But in his autobiography 'Baburnama', he emphasized considering himself from his mother's lineage, that's why the dynasty established by him was called the Mughal dynasty. After the battle of Panipat, Babur started the conquest of India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– The first Englishman to go to the Mughal court was Captain Hawkins, who went to Jahangir's court in 1608 AD as the ambassador of James I. In 1615 AD, Emperor James I sent Sir Thomas Roe as his ambassador to Mughal Emperor Jahangir's court. Manucci came to Mughal emperor Aurangzeb's court.

questions.question_text: Where is Sher Shah's tomb located?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– The founder of the Sur dynasty was the Afghan dynasty-origin Sher Shah Suri. He was born in 1472 AD at Bajwara (Hoshiarpur). His childhood name was Farid Khan. Sher Shah died in the process of winning the fort of Kalinjar. His tomb has been constructed on a high mound in the middle of a lake in Sasaram (Bihar).

questions.question_text: Hamida Banu Begum was the wife of –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– During the exile, Humayun married Hindal's spiritual guru Persian-resident Shia Mir Baba Dost alias Mir Ali Akbar Jami's daughter Hamida Banu Begum on 29 August 1541 AD. Later, great emperors like Akbar were born from Hamida.

questions.question_text: Who was the Mughal commander who conquered North-Eastern parts like Assam, Chittagong?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– Mughal commander Shaista Khan conquered North-Eastern parts like Assam, Chittagong. When Aurangzeb ascended the throne, he appointed Mir Jumla as the governor of Bengal and ordered him to attack the Assamese. In November 1661 AD, Mir Jumla won the capital of Koch Bihar, captured the eastern and central parts of Assam, defeated the king of Gargaon in 1662 AD, won his capital, and in this way established the authority of the Mughals in Assam. Mir Jumla died on 10 April 1663 AD due to illness. Being a hilly and difficult area, the Mughals always had trouble ruling there.

questions.question_text: Between whom did the Treaty of Purandar (1665) take place?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– The Treaty of Purandar took place between Shivaji and Jai Singh on 11 June 1665 AD, under which Shivaji handed over 23 of his 35 forts to the Mughals, and 12 forts remained with him as jagir. In 1666, Shivaji went to Agra to meet Aurangzeb. Due to breaking court rules, Shivaji was arrested and kept in 'Jaipur Bhavan' Agra. Deceiving the guards, Shivaji escaped from prison.

questions.question_text: Mansabdari system was started by whom?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation– Mansabdari system was started by Akbar in 1575 AD. The word 'mansab' means rank or position and mansabdar meant that officer who held a position or rank in the royal army. Mansabdari system was based on the decimal system. Akbar organized the military based on the 'mansabdari' system. In this system, the number of Sawar cannot be more than Zat.

questions.question_text: What ruined Aurangzeb in the South?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– In 1681, chasing his son Akbar II, Aurangzeb reached South India. After that, he did not get a chance to come to North India. South India proved to be Aurangzeb's graveyard. This event is called the ruin of Aurangzeb's life.

questions.question_text: For which of his works is Sher Shah Suri most famous?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– Sher Shah's childhood name was Farid. After gaining power, Sher Shah made many reforms. But his administrative reforms were important, his revenue system was new. Sher Shah was one of the great administrators of the medieval era. As an administrator, he is called the precursor of Akbar.

questions.question_text: Sir Thomas Roe was sent as an ambassador to –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – After Hawkins returned from India, the English Company sent King James I's ambassador Sir Thomas Roe to the Mughal court. When Sir Thomas Roe met Mughal emperor Jahangir for the first time in Ajmer in 1615 and stayed there from 1615 to 1619, he stayed in the Mughal court and obtained trading facilities.

questions.question_text: Those nobles whose ancestors had already been in service under the Mughal rule were called–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – 'Sheikhzada' was a term used for Indian Muslims. Whereas 'Khan-i-Khana' was a title. Akbar gave the title of 'Khan-i-Khana' to Bairam Khan's son Abdur Rahim. Mirza was a Timurid aristocratic clan surname. Hence, none of the three options is the answer to this question.

questions.question_text: Akbar's main objective in adopting the policy of conciliation with Rajputs was–

options.A: To enter into matrimonial relations with Rajput women
options.B: To merge Rajput kings into his kingdom
options.D: To make the Mughal empire powerful

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– Akbar's main objective in adopting the policy of conciliation with Rajputs was to make the Mughal empire powerful. As a result of his Rajput policy, Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563 and the Jizya tax in 1564. He established matrimonial relations with Rajputs and granted them high mansabs.

questions.question_text: Mewar state, which was challenging the Mughal empire since Babur's time, was defeated during whose time?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) TGT History, 2003 Explanation – After Maharana Pratap's death, his son ascended the throne in 1597 AD. He also refused to accept Mughal subjugation. In 1614, Jahangir ordered Shah Jahan (Khurram) to attack Mewar. Due to pressure from Shah Jahan, in 1615, Amar Singh accepted the subjugation of the Mughals.

questions.question_text: Akbar was famous for a matter, which was in very few kings and emperors of India, because –

options.C: He built excellent cities and buildings
options.D: He had forged many religions, castes, and state-loyal people into a well-organized and struggling empire.

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Akbar had forged many religions, castes, and state-loyal people into a well-organized and struggling empire. This nature was in very few kings and emperors of India. His Din-e-Ilahi religion was a burning example of this, where scholars of every religion used to gather and present the core interpretation of their religion. Akbar had all these qualities. The commission has cancelled this question.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and use the code given below to select the correct answer– List-I List-II
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – First Battle of Panipat–1526 AD. – Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi Battle of Khanwa–1527 AD. – Babur defeated Rana Sanga Battle of Chausa–1539 AD. – Sher Shah defeated Humayun Battle of Kanauj–1540 AD. – Sher Shah defeated Humayun

questions.question_text: During Sher Shah's reign, the rights and responsibilities of tenants were officially approved, and they were clearly defined. This was included in–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– During Sher Shah's time, 'pattas' were given to farmers on behalf of the government, in which it was clearly stated how much tax they have to pay this year. Farmers accepted these through the 'Kabulyat' letter.

questions.question_text: Humayun regained control over Delhi in 1555 by –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Humayun regained control over Delhi in 1555 by defeating Sikandar Shah. This battle took place on 22 June 1555 between the Mughals and the Afghans at a place named Sirhind. In this, the Afghans were badly defeated, and Humayun again got the crown of Delhi and Agra.

questions.question_text: Which Guru did Jahangir give the death penalty on the charge of helping Khusrau?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Jahangir gave the death penalty to Guru Arjan Dev on the charge of helping Khusrau. After the charge was proved against Arjan Dev, a fine of two lakh rupees was imposed on him. Due to not paying which, he was given the death penalty. Jahangir's act was not wise. After this incident, the Sikhs became strong enemies of the Mughals.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor gave the title of Rana to Jai Singh?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – The title of Rana was given to Jai Singh by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. He was a staunch imperialist ruler. In this sequence, he had a war with Mewar as well as Amber's Jai Singh, but eventually, in 1681, a treaty took place with Jai Singh. Under which he accepted Jai Singh as the Rana of Mewar.

questions.question_text: Which Jat leader established Bharatpur during Aurangzeb's time?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation– During Aurangzeb's time, Jat leader Churaman established Bharatpur in 1700 AD. He built a strong fort and challenged the power of the Mughals. However, in 1721, he was defeated by Jai Singh II. Eventually, he committed suicide. After this, his nephew Badan Singh handled the burden of the Jats.

questions.question_text: Who became the successor of Sher Shah from the following?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – After Sher Shah's death, his second son Islam Shah was appointed as his successor. He ruled from 1545 to 1553. Due to his aggressive nature towards the nobles, he behaved with cruelty, eventually, a feeling of discontent started the fall of the Sur empire.

questions.question_text: The name of the ruler who sat on the throne at the tender age of 13 was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The name of the ruler who sat on the throne at the tender age of 13 was Akbar. He was born on 15 October, 1542 AD in the palace of Rana Virsal of Amarkot from Hamida Banu's womb. After Humayun's death, Bairam Khan declared Akbar the emperor of India on 14 February 1556 by performing his coronation.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not included in Akbar's Nine Gems (Navratnas)?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Among the given options, famous musician Baiju Bawra was not among Akbar's Nine Gems. It is noteworthy that among Akbar's nine gems were Mulla Do-Piyaza, Abul Fazl, Todar Mal, Hakim Humam, Tansen, Sheikh Faizi, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana, Raja Birbal, and Man Singh.

questions.question_text: During which two Mughal rulers' middle period was Sher Shah's rule?
questions.explanation: Explanation – Sher Shah's rule (1540-45 AD) was in the middle period of Humayun and Akbar, which was immediately after Humayun's reign. Akbar's reign starts from February 1556, which is the reign after Sher Shah. Hence, Sher Shah's rule took place between Humayun and Akbar.

questions.question_text: What is the war between Babur and Rana Sanga called –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 PGT History, 2003 Explanation – On 16 March 1527 AD, the Battle of Khanwa took place between Babur and the Rajput king of Mewar, Rana Sanga. Babur was victorious in this battle. It was in this battle that Babur gave the slogan of Jihad (holy war) and took the title of 'Ghazi'.

questions.question_text: How many years did Sir Thomas Roe stay in Emperor Jahangir's court?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Sir Thomas Roe stayed in Emperor Jahangir's court for three years. Thomas Roe, the ambassador of England's King James I, was sent to the Mughal court by the East India Company. The purpose of his coming here was to obtain trading facilities. Thomas Roe stayed in Jahangir's court continuously from 1615 to 1619 and obtained trading facilities.

questions.question_text: Which historian called Akbar the 'Enemy of Islam'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Badauni called Akbar the Enemy of Islam. The reason for this is that Akbar adopted a policy of religious tolerance and Badauni always opposed his Din-e-Ilahi ideology.

questions.question_text: 1. Malwa conquest 2. Gujarat conquest 3. Battle of Haldighati 4. Kashmir conquest 5. Sindh conquest and 6. Asirgarh conquest Arrange Akbar's military campaigns in chronological order.
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The chronological order of Akbar's military campaigns is as follows – (i) Conquest of Malwa - 1561 AD. (ii) Conquest of Gujarat - 1572 AD. (iii) Battle of Haldighati - 1576 AD. (iv) Kashmir conquest - 1586 AD. (v) Sindh conquest - 1591 AD. (vi) Asirgarh conquest - 1601 AD.

questions.question_text: What was the biggest challenge before Akbar in 1580-81 AD?

options.A: Declaring Akbar's step-brother Mirza Hakim as their ruler by disgruntled nobles and officers
options.C: Rebellion of Yusufzai tribes on the North-Western frontier
options.D: Rana Pratap's escape from the Battle of Haldighati

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – In 1580-81 AD, the biggest challenge before Akbar was declaring Akbar's step-brother Mirza Hakim as their ruler by disgruntled nobles and officers.

questions.question_text: What is untrue about Sher Shah?

options.C: Construction of 'Qila-i-Kuhna' mosque in the old fort of Delhi
options.D: Construction of a fort in Sasaram (Sahsaram)

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The untrue statement about Sher Shah is that he got a fort constructed in Sasaram (Sahsaram). Sher Shah himself built his tomb in Sahsaram (Bihar). He built Qila-i-Kuhna mosque in Delhi's old fort and after getting the land measured, fixed the land revenue rate at 1/3.

questions.question_text: In which battle did Babur make the declaration of 'Jihad', abolish the tax named 'Tamga', and after winning the battle, took the title of 'Ghazi'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Babur made the declaration of Jihad in the Battle of Khanwa and abolished the tax named 'Tamga' and after winning the battle, took the title of 'Ghazi'. In the Battle of Khanwa, he defeated Rana Sanga.

questions.question_text: Who among the following foreign travelers did not come to the Mughal empire?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation – Domingo Paes came on a visit to Vijayanagar during the reign of King Krishnadeva Raya. Whereas Bernier and Tavernier came to India during the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb respectively. Sir Thomas Roe visited India during the time of Mughal emperor Jahangir.

questions.question_text: Which was not a responsible reason for the fall of the Mughal empire?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation – Reasons directly responsible for the fall of the Mughal empire were - Foreign invasions, weak successors, and peasant discontent.

questions.question_text: Brajjeet Gaur was the military commander of which Indian ruler –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Sher Shah was a religiously tolerant Muslim ruler. He appointed Hindus to various important administrative posts in his empire. His most capable military commander was Brajjeet Gaur, who was with him in many wars in which Sher Shah won.

questions.question_text: In which year did the famous Battle of Haldighati between Akbar and Rana Pratap take place –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – The famous Battle of Haldighati between Akbar and Rana Pratap took place on 18 June, 1576 AD. In this battle, the Mughal army was being led by Raja Man Singh and Asaf Khan. Rana Pratap was defeated in this battle, but the Mughals could not achieve complete success.

questions.question_text: The last victory of the life of the great Mughal emperor Akbar was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – Mughal emperor Akbar attacked Asirgarh in 1601 AD and won it. This was Akbar's last victory.

questions.question_text: In the Mughal era, who was the chief officer of the home department–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – In the Mughal era, the chief officer of the home department (Royal Home Department) was Khan-i-Saman. He looked after the royal workshops. Akbar established this post during his reign and its name was Mir-i-Saman. During Aurangzeb's reign, he came to be known as Khan-i-Saman.

questions.question_text: During whose reign did Khan-i-Jahan Lodi's rebellion take place–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – Shah Jahan's (1627-1658) coronation took place in Agra in February 1628. Many rebellions took place during Shah Jahan's reign. Among these, the first rebellion was that of Khan-i-Jahan Lodi.

questions.question_text: A mission led by Sir William Norris visited the court of which Mughal emperor to obtain trading facilities–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation – In 1698, England's King William III established the East India Company. This company sent a representative delegation led by Sir William Norris to Aurangzeb's court to obtain trading facilities, but no proper result came of it.

questions.question_text: In which of the following wars did Sher Shah Suri take part?

options.A: In the first battle of Panipat
options.B: In the second battle of Panipat
options.C: In the third battle of Panipat

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Sher Shah Suri took part in the Battle of Chanderi (1528) on behalf of Mughal emperor Babur.

questions.question_text: Nur Jahan's real name was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Nur Jahan's real name was Mehr-un-Nissa. She was the daughter of Mirza Ghiyas Beg. In May 1611, Jahangir married Mehr-un-Nissa and gave her the title of Nur Mahal. Nur Jahan was made the emperor's begum or chief queen in 1613.

questions.question_text: Where was Babur buried?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The founder of the Mughal Empire, Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur, died on December 26, 1530. Babur's dead body was first buried in Aram Bagh in Agra, by the banks of the Yamuna. But later, according to his wish, he was buried in Kabul.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal Emperor had the highest number of Rajput mansabdars?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The number of Rajput mansabdars was highest during the reign of Aurangzeb. During this time, the highest number of Marathas were also made mansabdars. Thus, the percentage of Rajputs among all mansabdars was 33%.

questions.question_text: Akbar established the 'Mansab System' in:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Akbar started his military organization through the Mansabdari system in 1575 AD. Mansab means rank or position. A mansabdar was an officer who held a position or rank in the royal army. This mansabdari system was based on the decimal system.

questions.question_text: Which kingdom in South India did Akbar first attack?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Akbar first attacked the Ahmednagar kingdom in South India. At that time, Chand Bibi was ruling there as the guardian of her nephew.

questions.question_text: Among the Mughal emperors, whose name was Zahir-ud-din Muhammad?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – After the death of his father Umar Sheikh Mirza, Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur sat on the throne at the young age of 11. Babur was the founder of Mughal power in India, who established Mughal power in India by defeating Ibrahim Lodi in 1526 AD.

questions.question_text: Which policy did Akbar NOT adopt to bring Rajputs to his side?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009

questions.question_text: What was the work of 'Mir Bakshi' under Mughal administration?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – In Mughal administration, Mir Bakshi was the head of the military department. He kept the list of mansabdars. He recommended their promotion and other matters to the Emperor. Recruitment of soldiers, salary, arrangement of their weapons, and inspection during military drills came under him. In fact, he had a separate military ministry.

questions.question_text: Niccolao Manucci, who gave an account of Aurangzeb's reign, was a resident of –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Niccolao Manucci was a resident of Venice, who was born in 1639 AD. He left his home at the age of 14 and entered the service of a foreign merchant, Descade Valesco. And while traveling with him, he reached Surat port in 1658 AD. He has given an eye-witness account of the war of succession in 'Storia do Mogor'.

questions.question_text: Which historian has called Akbar "the first conqueror of Rajput freedom"?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Historian Colonel Tod has called Akbar "the first conqueror of Rajput freedom". Colonel Tod has called the Rajput ruler Durgadas the 'Ulysses of the Rathores'. Durgadas was the hero of the thirty-year war between Marwar and the Mughals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a royal document during the reign of the Mughals?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – During the Mughal reign, Farman, Sanad, and Nishan were royal documents. Khutba was read during the Friday prayer, which also contained the name of the ruler.

questions.question_text: Which of the following military ranks was the highest paid in the Mughal military system?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – A Dahbashi soldier was, in a way, a soldier of the Badshah (Emperor). There is a mention of a Dahbashi soldier receiving a salary of 500 rupees, whereas a regular soldier received a salary of 12 to 15 rupees.

questions.question_text: 1. Battle of Khanwa 2. First Battle of Panipat 3. Battle of Ghaghra 4. Battle of Chanderi Options: Arrange the following in chronological order –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The First Battle of Panipat took place on 21 April, 1526 AD between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. The Battle of Khanwa took place on 16 March, 1527 AD between Babur and Rana Sanga. The Battle of Chanderi took place on 29 January, 1528 AD between Babur and Medini Rai. Babur defeated the joint army of Bihar and Bengal in the Battle of Ghaghra on 6 May, 1529 AD. Babur achieved victory in all the above battles.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal ruler sat on the throne twice?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Humayun was the only Mughal ruler who sat on the throne twice. First, 3 days after Babur's death, at the age of 23 on 29 December, 1530 AD, and the second time on 23 July, 1555 AD, he sat on the throne of Hindustan.

questions.question_text: 'Sadr-us-Sudur' was the minister under the Mughals for –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – During the Mughal administration, Sadr-us-Sudur was the advisor to the Emperor for religious matters. His main tasks were to arrange for charity, arrange for religious education, provide tax-free land and wazifas (stipends) to scholars, and make proper arrangements for the observance of Islamic laws. Sadr-us-Sudur was also called 'Sheikh-ul-Islam'.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was considered the chief of the Amirs in the Mughal administration?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The post of Mir Bakshi came in the Mughal era in place of the Diwan-i-Arz of the Sultanate era. He was the highest payment officer of the empire. Mir Bakshi was an important post, and during the Mughal era, the leader of the Amirs was not the Diwan but the Mir Bakshi.

questions.question_text: Muslims used to call Aurangzeb 'Zinda Pir Alamgir'. The reason for this was –

options.B: Not giving place to music in the court

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Aurangzeb was known as 'Zinda Pir' to his orthodox Sunni subjects because of his literal adherence to Islamic laws, and as 'Shahi Darvesh' because of his simple lifestyle, regular observance of fasts and prayers, and not drinking alcohol throughout his life.

questions.question_text: Who was the Safavid ruler who gave shelter to Humayun?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – The Safavid ruler who gave shelter to Humayun was Shah Tahmasp-I, who was a resident of Iran. This incident is from 1544 AD. The Shah also gave military aid to Humayun to win Kandahar.

questions.question_text: Who was the chief of the administration of a 'Pargana' during the Mughal era?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – In the Mughal era, the chief of the administration of a 'Pargana' was the Shiqdar, who was responsible for maintaining peace and good order there.

questions.question_text: To whom did Akbar grant the title of Jagatguru?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – Akbar had granted the title of Jagatguru to Harivijaya Suri. He was more influenced by Jainism compared to the Christian religion.

questions.question_text: Under the Zapti system, the most fertile land was classified in which form?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – Under the Zapti system, the most fertile land was classified as Polaj. The most important reform made by Akbar in Sher Shah's system was in the field of land classification.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal rulers first accepted Tuladan, which was a weighing ceremony of Hindus?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – The Mughal Emperor Jalaluddin Muhammad Akbar first accepted Tuladan, which was a weighing ceremony of Hindus, and he used to organize a grand ceremony on this occasion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers issued coins bearing the impression of Ram-Sita?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – The Mughal era ruler Akbar had issued coins bearing the impression of Ram-Sita. Although many types of artistic coins were issued during Akbar's time, in one silver coin, the archer Ram was depicted on one side and the figure of Sita on the other side, and 'Ramasiya' was inscribed in Devanagari script.

questions.question_text: During whose reign was the famous Peacock Throne built?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – The famous Peacock Throne was built during the reign of Shah Jahan. The best creation of this period is Takht-e-Taus (Peacock Throne). In this, there are twelve small pillars, which are adorned with figures of peacocks. It was first in the Agra Fort. From there, it was relocated to the Red Fort of Delhi. From here, the Iranian ruler Nadir Shah looted and took away this throne. It got the name Peacock Throne because two dancing peacocks were shown on its back.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal rulers remitted some taxes in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Shah Jahan was the Mughal Badshah from 1627 to 1658 AD. His time was the golden age of architecture in India. He also emphasized the development of agriculture. Due to famine, he remitted land revenue in South India and due to special circumstances, he also remitted some taxes in Kashmir.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal rulers issued a Mahzar-nama to curb the power of the Ulema?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Akbar built the Ibadat Khana in Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 for discussions on philosophical and theological subjects. He was not satisfied with the religious discussions there. Therefore, in 1579 AD, to take all religious matters into his own hands, he issued a 'Mahzar-nama' or a declaration and curbed the power of the Ulema.

questions.question_text: At which of the following places was Prince Khusrau buried?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – In 1605 AD, Jahangir became the ruler of the Mughal dynasty. The name of his first wife was Man Bai, to whom Jahangir had given the title of Shah Begum. Khusrau was the son of this very Man Bai, whose death occurred in Shah Jahan's camp in South India. On Jahangir's order, he was buried in Allahabad and named after this Khusrau, Khusrau Bagh is still situated in Allahabad today.

questions.question_text: Who gave the post of 'Vakil-e-Mutlaq' to Nizam-ul-Mulk?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Roshan Akhtar, with the help of the Sayyid brothers, sat on the Mughal throne on 28 September 1719 with the title of 'Muhammad Shah'. During his time, the end of the Sayyid brothers occurred, and Muhammad Shah gave the post of 'Vakil-e-Mutlaq' to Nizam-ul-Mulk. Ahmad Shah Abdali's invasion of India took place in 1748 AD during the time of Muhammad Shah.

questions.question_text: Which Hindu historian did Aurangzeb find to record his victories?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Aurangzeb appointed Ishwardas Nagar to record his victories. Aurangzeb had appointed Ishwardas Nagar as a civil officer in Jodhpur. Ishwardas Nagar wrote 'Futuhat-i-Alamgiri'. The history from 1657-1698 AD is obtained from Futuhat-i-Alamgiri. It describes the events of Malwa and Rajasthan.

questions.question_text: Whom did Akbar honor with the title of 'Kavi-priya'?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Akbar had granted the title of 'Kavi-priya' to Raja Birbal. Birbal was one of the nine gems of Akbar. Birbal used to write poetry under the pen name 'Brahma'. Birbal's death occurred in 1586 AD in a battle with the Yusufzais. Akbar was highly influenced by Birbal.

questions.question_text: Who has been given the credit for establishing an improved coinage system?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Sher Shah stopped the circulation of old, worn-out coins and coins issued by previous rulers. He introduced new gold, silver, and copper coins and determined their mutual ratio. His name, title, and the name of the mint were inscribed on Sher Shah's coins in Arabic or Nagari script. Sher Shah's currency system was the best, which was the basis of the current British currency system.

questions.question_text: Who was the last Mughal ruler?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – After the death of Akbar II in 1837 AD, his son Bahadur Shah II became the Mughal Badshah. After the revolt of 1857, the British removed Bahadur Shah (II) from the throne and exiled him to Rangoon, where he died a few days later. Even today, his tomb is situated in Rangoon.

questions.question_text: Who was that first Mughal ruler who made arrangements for various types of facilities during the time of famine?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – A severe famine occurred in the Deccan and Gujarat in the fourth and fifth years of the reign of Mughal ruler Shah Jahan. At that time, Shah Jahan provided various types of facilities for the welfare of the people.

questions.question_text: Who was the leader of the Gondwana campaign/Garh-Katanka victory during Akbar's time?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – The leader of the Gondwana/Garh-Katanka victory during Akbar's time was Asaf Khan. In 1564 AD, he defeated Rani Durgavati in the battle of Narhi and Chauragarh and won her capital Chauragarh (Gondwana).

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: Battle of Khanwa – Akbar and Rana Pratap
options.B: Battle of Haldighati – Sher Shah and Humayun
options.C: Battle of Dharmat – Aurangzeb and Dara
options.D: Battle of Samugarh – Aurangzeb and Shuja

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Battle of Dharmat – Aurangzeb and Dara Battle of Samugarh – Aurangzeb and Dara Battle of Haldighati – Akbar and Rana Pratap Battle of Khanwa – Babur and Rana Sanga

questions.question_text: Who among the following committed suicide by eating poison?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009, 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History 2000 Explanation – In 1605 AD, Jahangir became the Mughal Badshah. His childhood name was Salim. His first marriage took place in 1585 AD with Man Bai, the daughter of Raja Bhagwant Das of Amber (Jaipur). Khusrau was the son of this very Man Bai. There was a difference of opinion between Jahangir and his son Khusrau regarding becoming the emperor. Due to this internal conflict, Man Bai committed suicide by eating poison, whose tomb is situated in Khusrau Bagh of Allahabad. Jahangir had given the title of 'Shah Begum' to this Man Bai.

questions.question_text: Who was known as 'Daroga-i-Topkhana' in the Mughal administration?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – Mir Atish was known as 'Daroga-i-Topkhana' in the Mughal administration. He was the chief of the Royal Artillery, but this was not a ministerial post. On his recommendation, the appointment of Kotwal was made by the center in important cities. Mir Bakshi was the chief of the military department.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Dabistan-i-Mazahib', which discusses Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – The author of 'Dabistan-i-Mazahib', which discusses Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi, was Mohsin Fani. Din-i-Ilahi was established in 1582 AD. Through this, Akbar expected religious unity. For this, he also used his governance. Among the established Hindus, Birbal had accepted it.

questions.question_text: In which year of his reign did Akbar divide his empire into subahs?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – Akbar divided his empire into subahs in the 24th year of his reign. Akbar was born on 15 October, 1542 AD at Amarkot. Akbar took over the administration after the death of his father at the age of 13. Initially, Bairam Khan used to look after the work of Akbar's administration. From 1560 AD, Akbar took the administration into his own hands.

questions.question_text: At which place did Humayun fight a decisive battle against Sher Khan?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – The decisive battle against Sher Khan by Humayun was fought on 17 May, 1540 AD at Bilgram (near Kannauj). With the defeat at Kannauj, on one hand, Sher Shah's fortune shined, while on the other hand, the kingdom of the Mughals ended in a way. The root cause of the defeat of the Mughals was the mutual disagreement among his brothers.

questions.question_text: Chhatrasal's rebellion belongs to whose reign?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – Chhatrasal Bundela's rebellion belongs to the reign of Aurangzeb. Aurangzeb had his coronation done in a hurry on 31 July, 1658 AD after capturing Agra. Displeased with his religious policy, people of many communities revolted. Chhatrasal's rebellion was also the result of Aurangzeb's religious policy.

questions.question_text: 'Mahwari' salary system for Mansabdars started during whose reign?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The 'Mahwari salary system' for mansabdars started in the reign of Shah Jahan. Akbar had taken the mansabdari system from Central Asia. Under this, officials were given land in lieu of salary, which they used to deposit in the royal treasury after taking out their and the soldiers' salaries, but Shah Jahan changed this system and started giving monthly salaries.

questions.question_text: The famous historian Sujan Rai was in whose reign?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The famous historian Sujan Rai Bhandari was in the reign of Aurangzeb. His famous composition is 'Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh'. Sujan Rai Bhandari was a mansabdar during the time of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb who wrote the history of Aurangzeb's time.

questions.question_text: The Satnamis who revolted and captured Narnaul city during Aurangzeb's reign were followers of
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The Satnamis who revolted in 1672 AD and captured Narnaul city during Aurangzeb's reign were followers of Kabir. These Satnami people used to keep their heads shaved. For this reason, people also called them Mundiyas. People of some other religions were also badly affected by Aurangzeb's religious policy. Aurangzeb did not like any religion other than Islam.

questions.question_text: Between whom was the Battle of Chausa fought?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- While returning from Bengal, a battle took place between Humayun and Sher Khan on 26 June 1539 at a place called Chausa near Buxar and Humayun was badly defeated in this battle.

questions.question_text: According to which of the following historians was 'Din-i-Ilahi' a religion?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- 'Din-i-Ilahi' was established in 1582 AD during Akbar's time. Akbar wanted religious tolerance among all religions. Vincent Smith criticized Akbar for the new religion. Badauni criticized Akbar. His belief was that this is a new religion.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events of Akbar's reign in chronological order according to the code given below: 1. Abolition of pilgrim tax 2. Construction of Ibadat Khana 3. Abolition of Jizya 4. Establishment of Din-i-Ilahi Code:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Akbar made important reforms in his reign. In which abolition of pilgrim tax in 1563, abolition of Jizya tax in 1564 AD, and construction of Ibadat Khana in Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 and establishment of 'Din-i-Ilahi' in 1582 AD.

questions.question_text: Among the following women, whom did Akbar appoint as the governor of Kabul?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Akbar had appointed his cousin as the governor of Kabul. But he rebelled many times, due to which Akbar removed him and appointed his sister Bakht-un-Nissa Begum as the governor.

questions.question_text: Among the following sons of Jahangir, whom did Nur Jahan give protection in the initial days of her power?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Jahangir had four sons. Nur Jahan gave protection to Khurram (Shah Jahan) in the initial days of her power. But when she got her daughter Ladli Begum married to Shahryar Khan, she started favoring Shahryar Khan instead of Shah Jahan. Since then, differences started between Shah Jahan and Nur Jahan and Shah Jahan was forced to rebel.

questions.question_text: Akbar's son Prince Murad died of
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History 2000, 2010 Explanation- The name of Akbar's eldest son was Jahangir, after him were Murad etc. Prince Murad died due to excessive drinking. At the last time of Akbar's life, only Jahangir was left alive among his sons. For this reason, Akbar forgave many of Jahangir's actions.

questions.question_text: Which musician did Shah Jahan give the title of 'Gun Samudra'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- After Jahangir, Shah Jahan became the Mughal Emperor in 1628 AD. He was a powerful ruler. Jahangir was a lover of painting, but Shah Jahan liked architecture more and he also had an interest in music. He gave the title of 'Gun Samudra' to Lal Khan.

questions.question_text: "Humayun kept stumbling his whole life and stumbling only, he became free from this life." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- According to Stanley Lane-Poole, "Humayun kept stumbling his whole life and stumbling only, he became free from this life." Humayun's life was full of struggles; for this reason, Lane-Poole expressed such a thought about him.

questions.question_text: Among the following emperors, who issued 12 famous orders after his coronation?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation- After Akbar's death in 1605, Jahangir became the ruler of the Mughal dynasty. After obtaining the throne, he issued 12 famous orders in the state. Jahangir was famous for 'justice' during the Mughal period. He had installed the chain of justice in the Agra fort.

questions.question_text: Who are not included in the Turkic tribes?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- In the 8th century, Turkic tribes started moving from Central Asia and one after another, the Qarluk, Ghuzz, Khilji, Ivari, Khalluk etc., various Turkic tribes went on entering the Islamic regions where they established independent kingdoms. Shamsabani is not related to Turkic tribes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers divided land into three categories based on production?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Sher Shah Suri (1540-1545 AD) divided land into three categories based on production - 'Good', 'Medium', and 'Bad'. Sher Shah adopted mainly three types of systems for revenue determination - (a) Gallabakshi or Batai (b) Nashq or Muktai or Kankut (c) Naqdi or Zabti (Jami).

questions.question_text: The main reason for Babur's victory in Panipat was his
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The first battle of Panipat took place on 21 April 1526 AD between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Babur's artillery got Babur victory in this battle. Despite being more in number, Ibrahim Lodi's army was defeated and Ibrahim Lodi was killed on the battlefield. As a result, Babur got control over Delhi and Agra. On 27 April 1526 AD, Babur declared himself 'Padshah' and laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not correct in the royal order issued by Sheikh Mubarak during Akbar's time?

options.A: Ulema is the spiritual head of the state
options.D: The Emperor is the spiritual head of the state

questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- To take all religious matters into his own hands, Akbar got a 'Mahzar-nama' or a declaration issued in 1579 AD, which made him supreme in matters of religion. It had the signatures of five Ulemas or Islamic scholars. Because of this, the powers of Ulema in the state were curtailed.

questions.question_text: The foreign traveler who saw the war of succession between Dara Shikoh and Aurangzeb was:
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The foreign traveler Francois Bernier had seen the war of succession between Dara Shikoh and Aurangzeb. He was a resident of France. He was "a physician, a politician, a philosopher, and a historian. He lived in India for 12 years. In the beginning, he worked as a physician to Shah Jahan's eldest son Dara Shikoh.

questions.question_text: Which of the following emperors held the title of 'Amir-ul-Mominin'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- Among the Mughal emperors, Akbar was quite powerful; he got 'Mahzar-nama' issued to achieve religious supremacy. He also held the title of 'Amir-ul-Mominin'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following killed Abul Fazl?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000, 2006 Explanation- Abul Fazl had an important place among Akbar's nine gems. Jahangir was Akbar's son; Jahangir had this suspicion that Abul Fazl was provoking Akbar against him, that is why he got him killed by Vir Singh Deo Bundela.

questions.question_text: Which of the following considered Hindu religious texts as 'Dev Vani'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Dara Shikoh considered Hindu religious texts as 'Dev-Vani'. Among the four sons of Shah Jahan, the eldest Dara Shikoh was the most educated, a scholar, and a writer. He studied many Hindu religious texts and translated Upanishads, Yoga Vashistha, Bhagavad Gita, etc., Hindu religious texts into Persian. For his tolerance and liberality, Lane-Poole has given him the title of "Little Akbar". Not only this, Shah Jahan had also given Dara the title of "Shah Buland Iqbal".

questions.question_text: Babur had declared himself 'Ghazi'
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The battle between Rana Sanga and Babur took place on 16 March, 1527 AD at a place called Khanwa, 40 km away from Agra. After achieving victory in this battle, Babur adopted the title of 'Ghazi' (warrior and preacher of religion).

questions.question_text: In which of the following years was 'Ain-i-Dahsala' implemented?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Akbar started a new tax system named 'Ain-i-Dahsala' (Todar Mal bandobast) in the 24th year of his reign (1580) and gave a permanent form to the Mughal-era land revenue system. The actual originator of this system was Todar Mal, for this reason, it is also called 'Todar Mal bandobast'. Under this system, the average of the last ten years' production of different crops and their prevalent prices at that time was calculated, and one-third (1/3) part of that average was collected as revenue. Under this system, tax payment had to be done in cash.

questions.question_text: Which of the following emperors gave permission to the English East India Company to establish a factory in Surat?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- By a royal Farman (on behalf of Jahangir) issued on 6 February 1613 AD, the English got permission to establish a commercial house in Surat and keep an ambassador in the Mughal royal court. The East India Company's commercial house was established in Surat under Thomas Aldworth.

questions.question_text: Who, despite being Akbar's contemporary, is not mentioned in 'Ain-i-Akbari'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Tulsidas was a contemporary of Mughal Emperor Akbar. Akbar's court poet Abul Fazl did not mention Tulsidas in the third part of his work Akbarnama, 'Ain-i-Akbari'. Abul Fazl has listed the names of fifteen painters in his Ain-i-Akbari, who had risen from about a hundred painters (most of whom were Hindus) to the category of excellent artists. The names of these painters are - Daswanth, Basawan, Keshav Lal, Mukund, Miskina, Farrukh, Kalamal, Madho Jagan, Mahesh, Khemkaran, Tara, Sanwal, Haribans, and Ram. Akbar himself took deep interest in the work of his artists and used to take a ledger of their deeds every week. He used to evaluate their capability and merit and kept rewarding (or punishing) them accordingly.

questions.question_text: The practice of giving 'Jharokha Darshan' to the public was ended by-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb was a staunch Sunni Muslim. He had achieved the emperorship not only for governing well but also for the protection and expansion of Islam. Aurangzeb's main goal was to turn that (India) 'Dar-ul-Harb' (land of infidels) into 'Dar-ul-Islam' (land of Islam). His policy was one of intolerance. The main basis of his policy of religious fanaticism was his own concept of religious fanaticism. Aurangzeb stopped the engraving of Kalima on coins. He stopped the celebration of the festival of Navroz, stopped Tula Dan and Jharokha Darshan. He stopped the wearing of Tilak on the forehead of Hindu kings, which Akbar had started. He banned the production of Bhang, banned the Sati practice. Stopped the celebration of festivals like Holi, Basant, Diwali, etc.

questions.question_text: For bravery and courage, Shah Jahan had given the title of 'Bahadur'-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation– Aurangzeb, in the situation of princehood, gave proof of being a capable commander and a skilled administrator. Due to the capability he showed in the war of succession in agility, military organization, leadership, and taking advantage of opportunities, he could achieve success against his brothers. His first military campaign was against the Bundelkhand ruler Jujhar Singh, in which he achieved success, after that, Aurangzeb worked as a Subedar of the Deccan (twice), Subedar of Gujarat, Commander of the Balkh (Central Asia) and Kandahar invasion from time to time and gained experience from the perspective of military diplomacy and administration. Shah Jahan had given him the title of Bahadur for bravery and courage.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and choose your answer from the code given below: Statement (A) : Akbar established Din-i-Ilahi in 1581. Reason (R) : Akbar wanted to get the support of Rajputs in his empire. Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The source elsewhere in the same text states that Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi/Tauhid-i-Ilahi was established in 1582 AD, so Statement (A), which gives 1581, is incorrect. The source also describes Akbar's matrimonial alliances with Rajput rulers, including Amber, Bikaner and Jaisalmer, supporting the Reason (R) that he sought Rajput support. Therefore, (A) is incorrect but (R) is correct.

questions.question_text: During Shah Jahan's reign, where were secret orders issued from-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Shah Jahan used to hold private discussions with princes and prominent Amirs in Shah Burj and from here he used to give orders for highly confidential work. During Shah Jahan's time, Mughal architecture reached its excellence, Shah Jahan got Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Machhi Bhavan, Sheesh Mahal, Khas Mahal, Anguri Bagh, place of Jharokha Darshan, Shah Burj, Moti Masjid etc. built in Agra Fort. During his time, Agra's Jama Masjid, Delhi's Jama Masjid and Red Fort and the buildings built in them etc. are main. From the Shah Burj of this fort, confidential reports were issued by Shah Jahan.

questions.question_text: Among the following Mughal rulers, who first issued coins with the figure of the king?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Among the Mughal rulers, Jahangir first issued coins with the figure of the king. After becoming a ruler, Jahangir launched a gold Mohur on which the figure of Mughal Emperor Akbar was inscribed. Jahangir had inscribed his figure on his coins and on some of his coins, Nur Jahan's name was also inscribed along with him. On some of Jahangir's coins, his figure is inscribed with a cup of wine in his hand. During his time, the currency system started by Akbar continued. No change was made in the currency system during Shah Jahan's time either. The circulation of the Mughals' coins was done through state-controlled mints. These mints were in various parts of the state. According to Abul Fazl, in 1595 AD, there were four mints in the empire to mint gold coins, fourteen to mint silver coins, and forty-two to mint copper coins.

questions.question_text: Which independent state did Nizam-ul-Mulk establish?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The independent state of Hyderabad was built by Chin Qilich Khan, whom the Mughal Emperor later gave the title of 'Nizam-ul-Mulk'. On the occasion of Aurangzeb's death, Chin Qilich Khan was in Bijapur. He did not take any part in the war of succession that took place between Aurangzeb's sons for the throne. In that war, Bahadur Shah Zafar obtained the Mughal throne after finishing his opponents. He appointed Chin Qilich Khan as the Subedar of Awadh after removing him from South India. After the death of Bahadur Shah, the war again took place among the Mughal princes for the throne. On this occasion, Chin Qilich Khan gave help to Farrukhsiyar against Jahandar Shah. Farrukhsiyar succeeded in becoming the Mughal Emperor. In return for his service, Emperor Farrukhsiyar gave Chin Qilich Khan the Subedari of six subas of South India and titles of 'Khan-i-Khana' and 'Nizam-ul-Mulk Bahadur Fath-Jang'.

questions.question_text: Who has written that Babur's death was caused by poisoning?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002, 2010 Explanation- Babur's daughter Gulbadan Begum has mentioned in her famous work "Humayun-Nama" that Babur's death was caused by poisoning. Gulbadan Begum was Babur's daughter. She was born around 1523. When Babur was in control of Kabul, she had seen her father's glory. At the time of Babur's death, Begum's age was eight years. Humayun kept her with great love as she herself has written. After the defeat at Kannauj, she stayed in Kabul and was very happy on Humayun's return in 1545. She has described the fights between Humayun and Kamran in Afghanistan in a very interesting way. Humayun-Nama is divided into two parts. The first part is related to the history of Babur and the second part narrates the state of Humayun. She has not written much about Babur because due to being of young age she did not remember many things. For this, she had to take information from others. Although she has written very little about Babur, it is much more important.

questions.question_text: Who prepared the draft of the 1579 AD Mahzar?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 GIC Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The formal work of centralizing religious and worldly power into his own hands by Mughal Emperor Akbar happened through a document named Mahzar in August-September 1579. The inspiration for issuing the Mahzar was given by Sheikh Mubarak and his sons Faizi and Abul Fazl. Mahzar gave Akbar that power that in case of a difference of opinion among Ulemas on any subject, keeping the needs of the empire in mind, he can give recognition to any idea which he considers supreme. Akbar was given the right to issue any Farman for the welfare of the riaya (public) provided that there is no violation of the laws of the Quran in it. The draft of the Mahzar was prepared by Sheikh Mubarak, the father of Akbar's royal poet Faizi.

questions.question_text: In whose reign were there the highest number of Deccani Amirs in the army?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010, 2008, 2002 Explanation- During the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, there were the highest number of Deccani Amirs. During Aurangzeb's time, Deccani Amirs were appointed on a large scale, among whom Marathas were in the highest number. In the situation of princehood, Aurangzeb gave proof of being a capable commander and a skilled administrator. Due to the capability he showed in the war of succession in agility, military organization, leadership, and taking advantage of opportunities, he could achieve success against his brothers. Aurangzeb ruled for a long time, so the empire could get the benefit of his power, firmness, and capability. Aurangzeb had received a peaceful, firm, vast, and prosperous empire. He expanded it the most, but even then Aurangzeb failed. In the last days of his time, the Mughal empire had headed towards decline. Aurangzeb was a great ruler, but his failure was also unprecedented. he gave proof of being a capable commander and a skilled ruler. Aurangzeb ruled for a long time so that the empire could get the benefit of his power, firmness, and ability.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Jat leaders in chronological order according to the code given below the list- 1. Rajaram 2. Suraj Mal 3. Gokula 4. Churaman
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Troubled by the atrocities of the Mughals during Aurangzeb's reign, the local Jats of Mathura rebelled in 1669 under the leadership of Gokula. In the battle of Tilpat, the Jats were defeated, Gokula was caught. His body was cut into pieces. In 1686, the Jats rebelled under the leadership of Rajaram. Rajaram defeated many Mughal officers and dug up Akbar's grave and burnt the bones. But in 1688 AD, Rajaram was defeated in a battle and killed. After this, Rajaram's nephew Churaman continued the rebellion. This rebellion of Jats continued until the death of Aurangzeb and eventually, the Jats succeeded in establishing an independent state of Bharatpur near Mathura. In 1756 AD, Suraj Mal became the successor of the Jat state.

questions.question_text: Under whose direction was the Mahabharata translated into Persian during Akbar's reign?
