questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The political and social state which the great emperor of India Akbar had envisioned with his synthetic vision... they were fulfilled and ended in front of him. The inspiration for Akbar's 'Tauhid-i-Ilahi' was political. But its influence on social and religious fields was not less. Akbar with his keen intellect also connected himself with that great awakening whose seeds were inherent in Sufi saints, poetry, and the nirguna poetry of Kabir, Tulsidas. Not liking the fanaticism of Islam, Akbar confirmed the theory of discussion gatherings with various religions, sects, and ideas in front of the public with many efforts. Under the direction of Faizi, this great emperor had the Mahabharata translated into Persian. He got the Ramayana, Mahabharata, Yoga Vashistha, and Vedanta translated into Persian.

questions.question_text: Among Jahangir's wives, who was Rajput?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Among Jahangir's wives, Malika-i-Jahan was Rajput. Her name was Jagat Gosain. Jahangir had given Jagat Gosain the title of Malika-i-Jahan. Mughal rulers established matrimonial relations with Rajput women to create friendly relations with Rajput rulers. His love for Nur Jahan was personal and only Nur Jahan was the controller of his love and power. Similarly, Jahangir treated all his wives with respect. On the death of his wife Man Bai, he did not consume food or water for many days. His relations with women were like the contemporary rulers, rather if looked at, the feeling of love for his wives in him was much more than theirs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following emperors is called Kalandar?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Babur was the founder of the Mughal empire. In November 1525, Babur left Kabul with the objective of winning India. Babur moved towards Delhi. Ibrahim Lodi moved towards Punjab to face him; both their armies reached the battlefield of Panipat opposite each other. The battle started from the morning of 21 April 1526 and by noon it was decided. Babur won the battle; Ibrahim Lodi was killed and the Afghan army was destroyed. Babur's artillery, his battle tactics, mainly the use of Tulugma battle tactics, and the ability of his commander were the main reasons for his victory. The battle of Panipat did not decide the fate of India but it definitely decided the fate of the Lodi dynasty. After winning the battle of Panipat, Babur gave one coin each to the people of Kabul in charity. Babur is addressed by the title of 'Kalandar'.

questions.question_text: Among the following painters, who committed suicide due to mental instability?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Abul Fazl has written in Ain-i-Akbari that Akbar himself was so influenced by the work of a common painter Daswanth, who was the son of a palanquin-bearer, that he contributed to making him "the first leading artist of his time". This artist's creations are "not less in any way from the creations of Bihzad or Chinese painters. The work of this famous painter was not found anywhere else except the manuscript named Razmnama. This manuscript is now preserved in the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum, Jaipur. When Daswanth became mentally disturbed and committed suicide in the year 1584, this manuscript was being prepared. Two other creations are also considered to be composed by Daswanth- (a) Khanwade Timuriyah, (b) Tutinama.

questions.question_text: What was the name of the square silver coin prevalent during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003, 2005 Explanation- Mughal Emperor Akbar launched coins of different weights and values of gold and silver in his time and fixed their mutual ratio. Those coins were of good metal and accurate weight. Most of them were round although some square ones were also made. Apart from the emperor's name, the mint's name, and the year of issue, Quranic verses were inscribed on most of them. Akbar did not get his figure inscribed on the coins. These coins were made beautiful and tasteful. Their casting was of excellent quality. Akbar's largest gold coin was 'Shansah', which was about 101 tolas in weight, which was used in big transactions. The most widely used gold coin was called 'Ilahi', whose value was equal to ten rupees. The silver coin was called 'Rupee' whose weight was 175 grains. The square coin was called 'Jalali'. Although it did not become very popular.

questions.question_text: Among the following parts of 'Akbarnama', which is called 'Ain-i-Akbari'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- 'Akbarnama' is Abul Fazl's famous work. After seven years of hard work, Abul Fazl completed Akbarnama in 1597-98 and presented it to Akbar. It is divided into three volumes. The third volume is 'Ain-i-Akbari'. 'Ain-i-Akbari' is the soul of Akbarnama. It has five parts. The first part has 10, the second has 30, and the third has 16 'Ains', and the fourth part has a mention of India's castes, seasons, crops, and natural beauty. Light has been thrown in detail on subjects like political, literary, religious life and judicial system of Hindus. In the end, biographies of Indian saints and some foreign Sufis have been given. The fifth part has only two chapters, which contain Akbar's sayings and Abul Fazl's autobiography. Ain-i-Akbari clearly narrates Akbar's administrative system.

questions.question_text: Among the following, who was the official historian of Aurangzeb's reign?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005, 2003 Explanation- The official historian of Mughal ruler Aurangzeb was Mirza Muhammad Kazim Shirazi. He wrote the history of the first ten years of Aurangzeb, which is called 'Alamgirnama'. It contains all important events and biographies of famous people. Like other official historians, Shirazi also had access to all records, which proves its reliability. He was given a special order to investigate the things that were not mentioned in written accounts. He was also given freedom to take advice from the emperor. Shirazi has openly praised Aurangzeb and has commented on his brothers as "base", "unfortunate". Shah Jahan has also been criticized. But the Amirs have not been "troubled". Those Amirs who had opposed Aurangzeb have also been remembered by good names.

questions.question_text: Read the following events of Akbar's reign and find out the correct chronological order from the codes given below- 1. Formation of provinces 2. Branding of horses 3. Introduction of Mansabdari system 4. Abolition of Jizya Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Mughal Emperor Akbar abolished the Jizya tax in 1564 AD. Jizya was an individual tax taken from non-Muslim public living in the state. Abul Fazl says that previous rulers used to consider this tax as a means to make other religions weak and to express their hatred towards them. But Akbar did not differentiate between religions and there was no need for extra revenue for him. That is why he abolished this tax. There is a reference to giving mansab for the first time in 1593 AD of Akbar's reign. This was not a title or rank name. Rather, it indicated the position of a person or Amir in the Mughal administrative service sequence. In this way, Mansab meant rank or class and it was a difficult system. The practice of branding horses was started in 1573 AD, so that the horse could be identified. In 1580 AD, Akbar formed the provinces and divided the Mughal empire into 12 subas.

Reason (R) : The Sikh Guru had given support to the rebellious Khusrau. With reference to the above two statements, which of the following is correct? Code :

options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is correct but R is wrong
options.D: A is wrong but R is correct

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Khusrau was 17 years old. He started dreaming of becoming an emperor. He fled from Jahangir's prison on 6 April, 1606 AD. He received support from Sikh Guru Arjan Dev. Jahangir received the news of Khusrau's escape within a few hours. He sent an army to pursue the prince and himself moved towards Lahore. Khusrau confronted Jahangir in the field of Bhairowal. But he was defeated and fled. However, Khusrau was captured. In this way, Khusrau's rebellion ended in just a month. One result of Khusrau's rebellion was that the relations between the Mughals and Sikhs also became bad, because Jahangir imposed a fine of 2 lakh rupees on Sikh Guru Arjan for supporting the prince and when Guru Arjan refused to pay that fine, he was given the death penalty.

questions.question_text: Who got the madrasa named Khair-ul-Manzil built in Delhi-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003, 2005 Explanation- Akbar realized that considering Islam as the main basis of religious education to move forward is harmful for the progress of education. Akbar opened Maktabs and Madrasas at various places, gave help to Hindu schools and learning centers, and appointed liberal religious scholars. During the Mughal period, Delhi, Agra, Fatehpur Sikri, Lucknow, Ambala, Gwalior, Kashmir, Allahabad, Lahore, Jaunpur, Sialkot etc. were centers of Muslim education. With the help of Emperors, nobles, and saints, many Maktabs and Madrasas were opened. Education was given in Maktabs and Madrasas through the medium of Persian language. Maham Anga, the wet nurse of Akbar, got the madrasa named 'Khair-ul-Manzil' built in Delhi. Lucknow's Farangi Mahal Madrasa was famous for legal education, Delhi's Shah Bani Ullah's school for traditional belief education, and Sialkot's Madrasa was famous for grammar education.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer from the code given below the list- List I (Painter) List II (Painting Style)
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The foundation of Mughal painting in India was laid by Humayun. Humayun invited the famous Iranian painter Bihzad's disciple Khwaja Abdul Samad and Mir Saiyyid Ali and both Humayun and Akbar received training in painting from Khwaja Abdul Samad. In Akbar's court, Persian painters Abdul Samad, Mir Saiyyid Ali, etc. were prominent and among Hindu painters Daswanth, Basawan, Sanwaldas, Tarachand, Jagannath, Lal Mukund, Haribans etc. Jahangir gave Abul Hasan the title of 'Nadir-ul-Zaman' and Mansur (animal-bird specialist painter) the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asr'. Agha Raza, Muhammad Nadir, Muhammad Murad, Bishandas, Manohar, Madhav, Tulsidas, Govardhan, etc. were prominent painters of his court. During Shah Jahan's reign, there was a decrease in figure painting and color coordination but progress was made in sketching and making borders. Faqirullah, Mir Hashim, Anup, Chitra etc. were his court's prominent painters. Basawan is considered the most excellent painter of Akbar's time. There was European influence on his painting. Basawan's important artwork is showing Majnun wandering in a desolate area with a lean, thin horse. European influence is visible in Miskina's paintings.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Saqi Mustaid Khan's 'Maasir-i-Alamgiri' is an important source of Aurangzeb's time. It contains a description of the reign from the 11th year to the 20th year of Aurangzeb. The history of the first ten years is a summary of Kazim Shirazi's Alamgirnama. Mustaid Khan has explained the Satnami rebellion in a very interesting way. Discussion of transfers, appointments, and promotions of officers after 1680 has also been done. For this reason, Sir Jadunath Sarkar has called it the 'Gazetteer' of the Mughal state. Apart from these sources, much other material was collected during the Mughal period, which helps in writing history. To understand the administrative system of the Mughals correctly, taking the help of such written records becomes very necessary. Waqiat-i-Alamgiri of Aqil Khan, 'Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh' of Sujan Rai Bhandari, 'Muntakhab-ul-Lubab' of Khafi Khan have described Aurangzeb's reign.

questions.question_text: Who is called the originator of modern Urdu poetry?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Wali Deccani is called the originator of modern Urdu poetry. His guru was Shah Saadullah Gulshan under whose direction he gave high peaks to poetry. He composed a poem collection named 'Diwan'. He met Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah in 1779 AD and presented his poems to him. Whereas Amir Khusrau used to write poetry. Amir Khusrau got the opportunity of service under six sultans. Initially, he remained in the service of Balban's eldest son Muhammad. After this, he became associated with Balban's royal court. He remained in royal service under Kaiqubad, Jalaluddin Khalji, Alauddin Khalji, Mubarak Shah, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq. Amir Khusrau was very close to Sufis, especially Nizamuddin Auliya, and through his poetry and music, he made a great contribution to the creation of India's Sufi culture.

questions.question_text: Telling "cunning Afghan", whom did Babur warn Humayun against?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- In the first battle of Panipat in 1526 AD, after defeating Ibrahim Lodi and establishing the Mughal empire in India, Babur (1526-30 AD) warned his son Humayun against the Afghan leader Sher Khan by calling him a cunning Afghan. In fact, this assessment of Babur turned out to be completely true and Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri) defeated Humayun in the battles of Chausa (1539 AD) and Kannauj or Bilgram (1540 AD) and captured the throne of Delhi and Humayun was forced to go into exile.

questions.question_text: Among Jahangir's wives, who was not Rajput?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Jahangir's wife Mehrunissa Begum was Muslim, all others were Rajput. Mehrunissa's father Ghiyas Beg was a resident of Persia. After the death of his father Khwaja Muhammad Sharif, Mirza Ghiyas Beg, with the intention of trying his luck elsewhere other than Persia, set out for India with his two sons and daughter. On the way near Kandahar, his wife gave birth to another daughter and this daughter was Mehrunissa. Mirza Ghiyas Beg got a place in Akbar's service and he went on progressing with his ability. Jahangir had given him the title of 'Itimad-ud-Daula' in his early period. In 1594 AD, Mehrunissa's marriage was done with Ali Quli Beg. After the death of Ali Quli Beg, Mehrunissa was appointed as the attendant of Akbar's widow Salima Begum. In 1611 AD, on the festival of Navroz, Jahangir saw her and became obsessed with her. In May 1611 AD, Jahangir married her and gave her the titles of 'Nur Mahal' and 'Nur Jahan'.

The way he kept a balance among Indian and Afghan Amirs and the way he dealt with the rulers of Bihar and Bengal, it was successful. Many Afghan commanders joined him because of his diplomacy. Babur was also successful in creating division among opposing Afghans. Deniel Ross wrote "The policy with which he made Sultan Ibrahim's rebellious nobles fight among themselves was not less than Machiavelli's ability". But Babur did not make an attempt to do governance system, revenue system, tax system, and proper justice system like his time.

In fact, from the perspective of border expansion, the Mughals did not get any special success in Jahangir's time but there is no doubt that the pressure of Mughals on Deccan kingdoms increased. questions.question_text: The Amir who made important improvements in the land revenue system of the Deccan during Shah Jahan's reign is-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004, 2005 Explanation- Shah Jahan set the land revenue system and economy of the Deccan right with the help of Murshid Quli Khan Khurasani. He made land reforms on the basis of Raja Todar Mal and Malik Ambar's land revenue system. Murshid Quli Khan divided the Mughals' land into two parts for revenue system - (a) Pain Ghat - in which Khandesh and half part of Berar were included. For the administration of both parts, he appointed two Deputy-Diwans, he got the land measured, divided the land into different classes based on production, and which farmer has how much and what type of land. He found out. He appointed honest and trustworthy officers at every place. Money taken as loan in the form of Taccavi from farmers was distributed among poor farmers upon collection, so that they could buy bullocks and seeds. 1/4 part of the production was taken from farmers as revenue. Murshid Quli Khan's reforms proved beneficial.

questions.question_text: Who was the ambassador of British ruler James I in Jahangir's court?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- William Hawkins was a merchant and was an employee of the East India Company. He stayed in India from 1608 to 1611. He was a very good knower of the Persian language and he was invited to the wine parties given by Jahangir. Jahangir was very influenced by him. Hawkins gave a very reliable account of Jahangir's personality and daily routine. The emperor was fond of jewels. According to the account of which day he has to wear jewels and in what quantity - they were divided. Even his sword (blade) was made of precious pearls, rubies, diamonds, emeralds, and corals. After daily prayer (Namaz), Jahangir would come out and give Jharokha Darshan.

Abbas Khan Sherwani composed 'Tarikh-i-Sher Shahi'.

questions.question_text: Who completed the Shalimar Bagh of Lahore?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Akbar planted many gardens in Agra fort, Fatehpur Sikri, and other places like his ancestors. His best garden is in Sikandra, where his tomb is. Jahangir was the emperor of gardens. Wherever he went, he planted gardens. His most beautiful and attractive garden is Shalimar Bagh in Srinagar. Among the two other important gardens built by Jahangir, one is in the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula in Agra and the second is in Shahdara near Lahore. Shah Jahan was also a great lover of gardens. He planted the famous Shalimar Bagh near Lahore. He also decorated the Red Fort of Delhi (Shahjahanabad) in two parts. In these, Hayat Baksh Bagh was the most beautiful. Aurangzeb did not take any interest in gardens. He did not take any interest in planting new industries. Still, gardens kept being planted. During this time, a beautiful garden was planted around Lahore's Badshahi Masjid.

questions.question_text: Name the ruler who welcomed Vasco da Gama in Calicut.
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- When Vasco da Gama landed at Calicut in 1498 AD, the colony of Arab merchants living there adopted a hostile attitude towards him, but the Zamorin welcomed the Portuguese and gave them permission to take spices, black pepper, and herbs, etc. The goods brought by Vasco da Gama from Portugal sold at a cost sixty times more than the total cost of the whole expedition. In the sixteenth century, the main objective of the Portuguese was to enrich their country and their income through the use of military force. Their target was to establish control over spices sent to Europe and control other Asian trade and collect tax from it. The rulers of Portugal were determined to create a royal monopoly on eastern trade, in which no interference of competing countries of Europe and Asia, and even private Portuguese traders, should be there.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer from the code given below- List-I List-II A. Qazi-ul-Quzat 1. Revenue and Finance B. Mohtasib 2. Military Organization C. Diwan-i-Kul 3. Public Morality Inspector D. Mir Bakshi 4. Judicial Administration Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation – Qazi-ul-Quzat (Chief Justice) ─ He was the highest officer of the judicial department. He was the highest officer after the Sultan. He also used to look after the religious matters of the state. In this capacity, he was considered Sadr-us-Sudur only. Being the chief Qazi of the state, he used to hear and decide cases. There was also a provision for reconsideration on his decision. Mohtasib ─ He was the head of the public general inspection department. His work was to keep the conduct of the public high. 'Mohtasib' used to see that Muslims live according to Islamic law and religious texts and do not consume forbidden things. To keep the conduct of the public pure, Akbar had declared the sale of liquor and the residence of prostitutes forbidden in cities. Prostitutes were evicted from the city and settled in a new place and its name was kept 'Shaitanpuri'. Diwan-i-Kul– Akbar created a new post of Diwan-i-Wazarat-i-Kul in the eighth year (1565) and first appointed Muzaffar Khan Turbati to it. This was related to revenue and finance. Mir Bakshi ─ 'Mir Bakshi' was mainly the head of the military department, but calling him the chief commander would be wrong. His work was related to the salary of soldiers and military organization. He prepared the list of mansabdars, which he presented before the emperor. Recruitment of soldiers, arrangement of their weapons, and inspection of soldiers were also under his work. There were three other Bakshis for his help. Apart from this, there were Bakshis in the provinces too who worked under the control of Mir Bakshi. Mir Bakshi was also placed on the post of Wazir.

questions.question_text: Who was the greatest painter of birds in Jahangir's court?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Among the great painters of Jahangir, Ustad Mansur was a skilled painter. Mansur had attained mastery in the painting of birds. Jahangir honored him with the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asr'.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Tobacco was brought to India by the Portuguese in 1605 AD. questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – This scholar, holding the title 'Saraswati', was a favorite of Dara and Shah Jahan. He got the pilgrimage tax terminated by Shah Jahan. Pleased with this, a hundred scholars bestowed the collected praise upon him.

questions.question_text: Which terminology was used for the advance money given by traders to artisans for the desired goods?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: The terminology 'Dadni' was used for the advance money given by traders to artisans for desired goods.

questions.question_text: Kalanaur place is known as -

options.B: As the place of Akbar's coronation as emperor
options.C: As the place of Humayun's marriage ceremony

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: On 27 January 1556 AD, Humayun passed away after falling from the stairs of his library located in Sher Mandal in Delhi. Akbar received the sad news of his father's death at a place called Kalanaur, located 15 miles west of Gurdaspur in Punjab. Akbar was busy there defeating Sikandar Sur, who had taken refuge in the Mankot fort. His guardian Bairam Khan very quickly erected a brick throne and declared him Emperor on 14 February 1556 AD. Akbar was born on 15 October 1542 AD in the palace of Rana Virsal of Amarkot.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: The author of Tabaqat-i-Akbari was Nizamuddin Ahmed. His father's name was Muhammad Muqim Harwi, who was Babar's 'Diwan-i-Bayutat'. Nizamuddin accompanied Akbar on many campaigns. He worked as a Bakshi in Gujarat. He also held high offices in Malwa and Ajmer. He was also a member of the board that wrote 'Tarikh-i-Alfi'. Abul Fazl's work is 'Akbarnama', which he presented to Akbar in 1597-98 after seven years of hard work. It is divided into three volumes. The third volume is 'Ain-i-Akbari'.

questions.question_text: Which poet among the following was granted the title of 'Malik-ush-Shuara' by Akbar?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Abul Fazl has mentioned the names of fifty-nine great poets in his book in Akbar's court, among whom Sheikh Abul Faizi was the greatest poet. Akbar was familiar with Faizi's scholarship and granted him the title of 'Malik-ush-Shuara' (Poet Laureate). For many days, he wrote compositions in Faizi's name, but later he started writing compositions in Faizi's name. He attributes this change to divine inspiration in his famous composition 'Nal and Damyanti'.

questions.question_text: On which aspect of medieval Indian history have Havell, Fergusson, and Percy Brown written?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Havell, Fergusson, and Percy Brown have written on the art and architecture aspect of medieval Indian history. Books like 'Ancient and Medieval Architecture in India' and 'Indian Architecture' are by E.B. Havell. 'History of Indian and Eastern Architecture' (Vols. I & II) is a book by Fergusson.

questions.question_text: The terminology for the practice of giving contracts for land revenue collection was:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: In the Mughal period, it was difficult for small Jagirdars to collect land revenue while staying away from their Jagirs. Therefore, they started giving their Jagirs on 'Ijara' (contract for land revenue collection). Sometimes even big Jagirdars used to give their Jagirs on 'Ijara'. This practice was a curse for the farmers. Ijaradars exploited them to earn maximum profit. In the first half of the 18th century, especially after the death of Bahadur Shah, this practice became widespread on Khalisa land as well, due to which poverty increased among the farmers and the royal treasury also had to suffer consecutive losses of revenue.

questions.question_text: Jahandar Shah sat on the throne after the death of -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: After the death of Bahadur Shah I (1712), a war for succession took place between his four sons Muizzuddin Jahandar Shah, Azim-ush-Shan, Rafi-ush-Shan, and Jahan Shah, but with the help of Zulfiqar Khan, Jahandar Shah was victorious and sat on the throne. At the time of his coronation, he was 51 years old. After becoming Emperor, he appointed Zulfiqar Khan as his Prime Minister.

questions.question_text: Which of the following commodities was exported the most in Mughal-era India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Since ancient times, India has been a major center for textile production and trade. It has been a major source of income for the Indian economy. In Mughal-era India as well, cotton and silk textiles were a major commodity for export. Among the important centers of cotton textiles, Bengal, Gujarat, Varanasi, Odisha, and Malwa were prominent. Similarly, Kasimbazar, Malda, Murshidabad, Patna, Kashmir, and Varanasi were major centers of the silk industry.

questions.question_text: Who was the first historian to propose the theory of 'Jagirdar crisis' for the decline of the Mughal Empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 UP PGT 2021 Explanation: The first historian to propose the theory of 'Jagirdar crisis' for the decline of the Mughal Empire was Satish Chandra.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal emperors sent Raja Ram Mohan Roy to London as his envoy?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar II sent Raja Ram Mohan Roy to London in 1830 AD as his envoy to the court of British Emperor William IV. Akbar II's reign was from 1806 to 1837. He was the son of Shah Alam II. He was a pensioner of the British. Raja Ram Mohan Roy had also worked under the East India Company from 1803 to 1814. In England, Raja Ram Mohan Roy went to present his case before the British government regarding the insufficient amount of pension given to the Mughal Emperor. He died in England itself on 27 September 1833. It was Akbar II who granted the title of Raja to Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.question_text: Which was the court language during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - During Akbar's reign, Persian was the main language of the court. Apart from this, significant efforts were made officially for the development of the Persian language during this period. For the development of the Persian language, important educational centers were established at places like Delhi, Agra, Fatehpur Sikri, Lucknow, Gwalior, etc. Education was imparted through the medium of the Persian language in these Maktabs and Madrasas. All the books written during this period were written in the Persian language. Along with Persian, Sanskrit and Urdu languages were also developing.

questions.question_text: The name of the founder of the Portuguese Empire in a part of India was -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Among the European traders who came to India, the Portuguese were the first. When Vasco da Gama reached Calicut with four ships on 17 May 1498 AD, the ruler of Calicut, Zamorin, welcomed him. The second expedition of Portuguese traders took place in 1500 AD, when Pedro Álvares Cabral reached Calicut. Along with him was Bartholomeu Dias, the discoverer of the Cape of Good Hope. These commercial expeditions increased the Portuguese ambition. They started thinking about establishing their colony in India according to their new policy; as a result, in 1505 AD, Francisco de Almeida was appointed as the first Portuguese governor. However, the real founder of the power of the Portuguese in India was 'Alfonso de Albuquerque', who made Cochin his headquarters.

questions.question_text: The Mughal emperors had designated a separate day for providing justice. Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched in this context?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Aurangzeb used to conduct judicial work on Wednesday. Shah Jahan also used to do judicial work on Wednesday. Jahangir used to do justice on Tuesday, whereas Akbar used to do judicial work on Thursday.

questions.question_text: What was the function of the officer named 'Diwan-i-Bayutat' under Akbar's reign?

options.A: Inspection of the expenditure of royal workshops (Karkhanas)

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Under Akbar's reign, 'Diwan-i-Bayutat' was a major officer. He was an officer mainly related to the Karkhana (workshop) department. While the Mir-i-Saman was the biggest officer of the Karkhana whose main duties were taking care of the employees under him, controlling the Karkhanas of the subahs or other cities, presenting the needs of his department before the Emperor, and presenting valuable items before the Emperor, etc., the main task of 'Diwan-i-Bayutat' was to fulfill the financial responsibilities of the Karkhana department, etc. His main task was to present the papers of the income and expenditure of his department before the Emperor and to examine the expenditure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mausoleums is located in the center of a large garden and appears to be the precursor to the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Humayun's mausoleum in Delhi does not only present a beautiful example of India's building construction art, but also provides an introduction to the development of Mughal architecture. This mausoleum was built under the supervision of his favorite wife, Haji Begum. This mausoleum is a beautiful example of architecture based on the Persian style in Indian form. There was no tradition of building boundary walls on all four sides of the mausoleum before this. However, after Humayun's mausoleum, this style of mausoleum became prevalent. Apart from this, the plan to plant trees and plants outside the boundary wall also became prevalent, and arrangements for ventilators (roshandan) were made to let light inside. Due to these features, Humayun's mausoleum is considered the precursor to the Taj Mahal.

questions.question_text: Where is Babar's mausoleum located?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – Babar, the founder of the Mughal Empire, died on 26 December 1530 AD. After his death, his body was first buried in 'Aram Bagh' in Agra. But later, according to his wish, he was buried in 'Kabul' at the place chosen by himself.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not true regarding the Mughal Mansabdari system?

options.A: Each Mansabdar's introduction/verification was done through Mir Bakshi.
options.B: Mansabdars were given salary in the form of Jagirs.
options.C: Mansabdars also received conditional (mashrut) or conditional posts.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – The Mansabdari system was the foundation pillar of the Mughal administration. It was a mixed form of military, civil, and aristocratic class. Abul Fazl has mentioned 66 categories of Mansabdars. Although in practice, only 33 categories were in vogue. There were some features of this Mansabdari system. Each Mansabdar's introduction was done in the court through Mir Bakshi. There, the Mansabdar's seating place in the court was determined. Mansabdars were given their salary in the form of a Jagir. And if needed, or if a Mansabdar was appointed to such a place where more army was needed, then his post was increased for a short time, which was called 'Mashrut'. However, Mansabdars were not hereditary; rather, they could be transferred from time to time and they could also be removed from the Mansab post.

questions.question_text: Which of the following contemporary sources depicts Humayun's passion for astronomy and astrology?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Qanun-i-Humayuni is a work of Khwandamir. He started writing this book in March 1533 and completed it in May 1534. This text is a contemporary text of Humayun's time. The events Khwandamir has narrated, they were witnessed by himself. He has described in detail Humayun's expenditures, his administrative experiences, and the new rituals of the court. He has given titles like Sikandar-i-Azam, shadow of God to Humayun.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Explanation – Edward Terry came in 1616 during Jahangir's time. Peter Mundy came in 1630. Sir Thomas Roe came to India in 1615.

questions.question_text: In the Mughal land revenue administration, we find a word named 'Mahsul'. What do you understand by this?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - In Mughal land revenue administration, 'Mahsul' was used for the total revenue income of the state or province. Akbar was the founder of the Mughal land revenue system. In the beginning, he adopted Sher Shah's land revenue system. During the reign of Akbar and his successors, 4 main systems of revenue determination were prevalent - (i) Zabti or Dahsala system, (ii) Galla Bakshi or Bhaoli, (iii) Kankut, (iv) Nasaq. In this period, the crop-wise cash lists of land revenue were recorded in 'Dastur-ul-Amal'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the patron of the Kota school of painting?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – The patron of the Kota school was Ummed Singh. Unparalleled examples of Kota painting are paintings with hunting scenes which are preserved in the Kanpur Museum and the Cleveland Museum of Art in America.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?

options.A: Barbak - Record-keeper (Wrong, this should be court usher/ceremonies)

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation - Barbak - He used to look after the glory and rules of the court. Mushrif - He was the state's auditor and controlled the state's income. A Nazir used to assist him, who used to look after the account of all state income through his assistant employees. Mutasarrif - He was the officer related to the royal workshop. Actually, a 'Mutasarrif' used to be appointed for every workshop. And there used to be a chief Mutasarrif over all workshops. Barid - His main task was to inform the ruler of all kinds of information. The biggest officer of this department was called 'Barid-i-Mamalik'.

questions.question_text: In whose mausoleum among the following Mughal emperors is the middle dome absent?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Among the most important buildings built during Jahangir's time is Akbar's mausoleum built in Sikandra near Agra. Built in the middle of an extensive garden spread over an area of a mile from all sides, this 5-story mausoleum is a symbol of Akbar's vast and generous heart. There are four marble domes on the four corners of the mausoleum, but the middle dome is absent. Based on its structure, scholars have considered it a mixed form of Buddhist art. Percy Brown has considered it "the most perfect of its kind of buildings".

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor abolished old customs like 'Sijda'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - In India, the tradition of Sijda (greeting by lying on the ground) and 'Paibos' (coming close to the Sultan and kissing his feet) was started by Balban. Shah Jahan considered this un-Islamic; that is why he abolished the Sijda practice from the court forever. Sijda was originally a Persian custom; Balban's theory of kingship was based on Persian tradition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following states became an integral part of Shah Jahan's empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - During Shah Jahan's reign, Ahmadnagar became an integral part of the Mughal empire. Akbar had ended the Imad Shahi state of Berar, and Shah Jahan ended the Nizam Shahi state of Ahmadnagar and included it in the Mughal empire.

questions.question_text: Who among the following has described 'Sulah-i-kul'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Badauni has given a detailed description of Sulah-i-kul. According to Badauni, in 1582 AD, Akbar propagated 'Din-i-Ilahi' or 'Tauhid-i-Ilahi'. Its objective was to establish a national religion. Under this, Akbar gave the message of 'Sulah-i-kul' (universal friendship).

questions.question_text: One of the observatories established by Sawai Jai Singh was in -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Sawai Jai Singh was the Kachhwaha ruler of Amber and the founder of Jaipur. Sawai was his title, which was formally granted to him by Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar. In 1727 AD, he founded the city of Jaipur, which was the first city to be settled in a planned manner. He had observatories built in Jaipur, Mathura, Varanasi, Delhi, and Ujjain. He also built a fort named Jaigarh and some temples. He died in 1743 AD.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor wanted to change the format of 'Khutba', but due to the aggressive resistance of the Ulema, could not implement it?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah I ordered in 1710 AD that while reading Khutba during Friday prayers in the empire, 'Wasi' of Ali should also be added among the successors of Prophet Muhammad. But the Sunni world and Ulema opposed this order of the Emperor. Turmoil and unrest arose in various parts of the empire on the issue of this new Khutba. Under such circumstances, he withdrew the order to change the 'Khutba' and it started being read like the reign of Aurangzeb.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal emperors adopted the title of 'Alamgir II'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Upon becoming Emperor, Jahandar Shah's second son Azizuddin adopted the title of 'Alamgir II'. Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk had him seated on the throne of the Emperor in place of Ahmad Shah. His reign was from 1754 AD to 1759 AD. His whole life was spent in prison, so he had neither experience of war nor of administration. He was fond of reading history books. During his short 5-year reign, he remained a puppet in the hands of his Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - Baz Bahadur was the ruler of Malwa, from whom Akbar's general Abdullah Khan Uzbek snatched Malwa in 1562 and later Baz Bahadur was sent to Delhi after giving a Mansab of 400. Zafar Khan ruled Gujarat by assuming the title of Sultan Muzaffar Shah. He died in the year 1411. Yusuf Adil Shah was the Sultan of Bijapur who founded the Adil Shahi dynasty, which remained till 1686 AD. Whereas the founder of Ahmadnagar was Malik Ahmad, son of Nizam-ul-Mulk, who founded the Nizam Shahi dynasty. Shah Jahan merged it into the Mughal Empire in 1633 AD. Qutb Shah was the founder of the Qutb Shahi dynasty in Golconda, which was merged into the Mughal Empire by Aurangzeb in 1687 AD.

questions.question_text: Who has been called the 'Plato of Jat tribe'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - In 1756 AD, Suraj Mal became the successor of the Jat kingdom. He gave this Jat kingdom 'wisdom, sharp intellect and clear vision'. People remember him as the Plato of Jats. He died in 1763 AD and after him, the Jat kingdom declined.

questions.question_text: Who among the following accepted Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - Akbar established a new religion in 1582 AD named Tauhid-i-Ilahi, which was based on Sufi pantheistic ideology, which later became known as Din-i-Ilahi. The chief priest of this new sect was Abul Fazl. Among the Hindus, only Mahesh Das alias Birbal accepted it. Although the number of members of 'Din-i-Ilahi' reached a few thousand, most of the prestigious Hindus and special persons of the empire did not join it. Sunday was fixed for the initiation of this new religion and during this initiation, the initiated person had to say Akbar's favorite slogan 'Allahu-Akbar'.

questions.question_text: Among foreign travelers, who describes that 'Ganga water' in large copper vessels was taken for the Mughal emperors to drink?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - Edward Terry was the chaplain of Sir Thomas Roe. He stayed in India from 1616 to 1619 AD. He has written in his travelogue that even if the Padishah was anywhere, arrangements were made for Ganga water for him. Separate employees were appointed to bring water from the Ganga; Ganga water was brought in beautiful copper vessels. The inside of the copper pots was tinned, and after filling water, before giving it to the water-carriers, they were sealed well after applying a seal.

questions.question_text: Who was the member of the Ulema who issued a 'Fatwa' from Jaunpur against Akbar?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - In the year 1579, Akbar entrusted the responsibility of leading the groups of people going to Mecca for Hajj to Abun Nabi and Abdulla Sultanpuri, and at the same time also ordered that they should not return without his permission. But his exile did not stop the growing disloyalty of the Ulama. In 1580, when some nobles of Bengal and Bihar, troubled by the implementation of the Dag system, rebelled and declared Mirza Hakim as the Emperor, then the Qazi of Jaunpur, Mulla Muhammad Yazdi, issued a Fatwa that the revolt against Akbar is legal, and the Qazi of Bengal said that this revolt is a divine wrath due to depriving the Ulama of Madad-i-Maash. After suppressing the revolt, both were summoned to Agra and while crossing the Yamuna river, an order was issued to drown both and kill them. Many other Mullas were either imprisoned or they fled here and there to save themselves.

questions.question_text: Which queen of Jahangir committed suicide by taking poison?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009, 2000 Explanation - Salim or Jahangir's first marriage took place in 1585 AD with Manbai, daughter of Raja Bhagwan Das of Amber and sister of Man Singh. Khusrau was born from this wife. Salim's second marriage took place with Jagat Gosain (Jodhabai), daughter of Uday Singh (Marwar). Khurram was born from her. Salim had granted the post of 'Shah Begum' to Manbai. Manbai committed suicide in 1604 AD after going into internal depression due to her son Khusrau's unfilial behavior. This incident had such an impact on Jahangir that he did not even touch food and water for four days. There were a total of 800 women in Jahangir's harem.

questions.question_text: Roshan Akhtar was the second name of whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - After the death of Rafi-ud-Daula, the Sayyid brothers seated Roshan Akhtar on the Mughal throne by the name of 'Muhammad Shah'. This was the fourth son of Bahadur Shah I. About him, it is said that never before had a more careless emperor sat on the throne of Delhi than him. Muhammad Shah was a 17-year-old young boy, who spent most of his time in the harem inside the palace with eunuchs and women. No one had paid attention to his education because no one had even thought that he would sit on the Delhi throne. Due to his indifference towards public affairs and indulgence in wine and women, he is called Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela'.

questions.question_text: Who among the following received the title of Jagat Seth from Muhammad Shah?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Muhammad Shah gave the title of Jagat Seth to Fatehchand in 1723-24 A.D.

questions.question_text: Which year of Akbar's reign did historian Vincent A. Smith consider the 'most critical time'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - In the year 1580-81 AD, Akbar had to face the most severe difficulties of his life. He faced a very tough test. Rebellion in India, attack from Kabul, and dissatisfaction in Dera, all together tested his endurance and ability, yet Akbar fought the storm firmly and was able to overcome every difficulty. To mark this huge success, the annual court of the year 1582 was celebrated on a very large scale. All subedars received orders to attend. On this occasion, he started the festival of Nauroz, which the early Sultans of Delhi used to do following the ancient Iranian kings. Due to the severe political situation, the work of temporary stalled revenue reform was taken in hand. In 1582, Todar Mal was appointed Prime Minister.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is untrue regarding Bahadur Shah Zafar?

options.A: He was an emperor without an empire
options.B: He was a warrior without experience of war
options.C: Hasan Askari was his spiritual guide

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - After the death of Akbar II, Bahadur Shah II became Emperor. He was given permission to keep the royal title. He was an English pensioner emperor without an empire. Hasan Askari was his spiritual guru. He was fond of poetry and wrote poetry under the pen name 'Zafar'. He participated in the public revolt of 1857 AD. Upon being captured, he was exiled and imprisoned in Rangoon jail in Burma. Where he died in 1862 AD. A mausoleum has been built there in his memory. Therefore, it is untrue that he received succession in 1845 AD. His period was 1837-57 AD.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I (List-II) A. Babar 1. Jama Masjid (Sambhal) B. Humayun 2. Dinpanah C. Akbar 3. Jahangiri Mahal D. Jahangir 4. Akbar's Mausoleum Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Babar - There are two buildings left built by Babar, one is the Kabuli Bagh Mosque of Panipat and the other is the Jama Masjid of Sambhal in Rohilkhand. These two mosques were built in 1528-29 for soldiers to offer Namaz. Humayun - Humayun built a building named 'Dinpanah' in Delhi. Apart from this, he had two mosques built in Agra and Fatehabad (Hisar). Akbar - Akbar built more than 500 buildings in the Agra Fort; among them, Jahangiri Mahal and Akbari Mahal are prominent. Jahangir - Akbar's mausoleum is the most beautiful and magnificent building of Jahangir's time. It is located in a village named Sikandra which Sultan Sikandar Lodi had settled in his name. Akbar had named it 'Bahishtabad'. It is located on the road going to Delhi, five miles away from Agra.

questions.question_text: The difference between 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' and 'Gaj-i-Ilahi' was –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In the 31st year of his reign (1586-87 AD), Akbar started using 'Gaj-i-Ilahi' (41 digits or 33 1/2 inches) instead of 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' (39 digits or 32 inches) for measuring land. Before this, 'Sikandari-gaj' was used in land measurement.

questions.question_text: Which painter did Akbar appoint as the Diwan of Multan among the following?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation: Khwaja Abdus Samad was a painter of Humayun's time, whom Humayun honored with the title of 'Shirin Qalam'. It was this Khwaja Abdus Samad whom young Emperor Akbar appointed as the head of the Royal Mint and later as the Diwan of Multan. Abdus Samad was a painter of the Indo-Persian style.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not true regarding the Mughal Mansabdari system?

options.A: There were three classes of Mansabdars.
options.B: They could be granted Mashrut or conditional posts.
options.C: Suwar rank could be higher than Zat rank.
options.D: All military and civil officials were granted Mansab or post.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In Jahangir's time, amendments were made in the Suwar rank and the system of Du-Aspa, Sih-Aspa was introduced. During Akbar's time, this rule was made that a Mansabdar's Suwar rank cannot be higher than his Zat rank. Apart from this, there was also a rule that the highest post would be of 500/5000 Suwar. Compliance with this rule could only be possible in principle through the Du-Aspa, Sih-Aspa system.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the choice of Prime Minister Mir Khalifa as successor to Babar in place of Humayun?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation Mehedi Khwaja, who was Babar's brother-in-law, whom an attempt was made to seat on the Agra throne. Because Babar's Prime Minister Khalifa Nizamuddin Ali was of the opinion that the interests of the state could be protected by having a powerful person on the throne. Mehedi Khwaja was a relative of Babar. He was an experienced and capable administrator. Contrary to this, no signs of greatness were visible in Humayun, but in the final moments, Humayun got success and on 30 December 1530 AD, he sat on the throne of Agra.

questions.question_text: During his second term of Subedari of Deccan, with whose help did Aurangzeb implement Todar Mal's revenue reforms in this region?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In 1653 AD, Aurangzeb was appointed governor of the South for the second time. In the second reign, Aurangzeb implemented the same revenue system in the South which was run by Todar Mal in the North. Murshid Quli Khan helped him in this work. Advance money was given to farmers to buy tools and seeds. Capable and honest persons were appointed as administrators and consequently, there was improvement in the speed of administration.

questions.question_text: How much rank or Mansab was granted to Vir Singh Deo Bundela at the time of Jahangir's coronation?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Jahangir had Abul Fazl killed by his friend Vir Singh Deo Bundela in 1602 AD. Akbar gave him the death penalty, but he fled. When Jahangir ascended the throne, he gathered a group of his supporters. He granted a Mansab of 3000 horsemen to Abul Fazl's killer Vir Singh Bundela.

questions.question_text: Which two sons among the following were sent according to the conditions of surrender in Jahangir's court after Khurram's rebellion?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Shah Jahan revolted in 1623 instead of going to Kandahar, due to which he was completely defeated in southern Baluchpur in Delhi. He kept wandering here and there. Finally, in 1625 AD, he made peace with his father Jahangir. Shah Jahan agreed to surrender Rohtas and Asirgarh. Sent Aurangzeb and Dara as collateral to the court. With his wife Mumtaz Mahal and son Murad, Shah Jahan went to Nashik.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct definition of 'Wajesn'?

options.B: Salary given through land revenue grants

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Wajesn or Wajh was the assigned land in lieu of cash salary. The person managing this was called a 'Wajesndar' whose job was to collect revenue from that land, take his salary, and deposit the remaining amount in the royal treasury.

questions.question_text: Read the following events related to Akbar and find the correct chronological order of the events from the code given below- (1) Uzbek rebellion (2) Start of Dag (branding) system (3) Kashmir conquest Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In 1564 AD, under the leadership of Abdullah Khan Uzbek, the Uzbeks rebelled against Akbar. The start of the horse branding (Dag) system took place in 1574 AD. In 1586 AD, under the leadership of Raja Bhagwan Das, the ruler of Kashmir, Yusuf Khan, was defeated, and Kashmir was declared a part of the Kabul province and merged into the empire.

questions.question_text: The land that was kept reserved for land revenue allocation was called –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The land that was kept reserved for land revenue allocation was called Mahal-i-Paibaqi. Land kept under the direct control and management of the state was called Mahal-i-Khalisa. During the Muslim rule, the region whose revenue was given to any royal employee in lieu of his services for a fixed period as salary was called Mahal-i-Jagir.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal commanders was not sent by Shah Jahan against the Bundelas?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The first rebellion of Shah Jahan's reign was of Jujhar Singh, son of Vir Singh Deo Bundela, which lasted till 1628-29 AD. The Mughal army attacked from three sides. Abdullah Khan attacked from the east and Khan-i-Jahan from the south. The entire army was led by Mahabat Khan. Emperor Shah Jahan himself reached Gwalior in 1629 and suppressed Jujhar Singh's rebellion. In 1635-36 AD, Jujhar Singh again rebelled in Bundelkhand and without royal orders, in 1635, he attacked the Gond capital Chauragarh and killed the local Raja Prem Narayan. Shah Jahan was very angry with this incident and sent Aurangzeb to suppress his rebellion. In front of Aurangzeb's fierce attack, Jujhar Singh had to face defeat. His army was scattered. Jujhar Singh and his son Vikramjit were both killed by the Gonds, and their heads were cut off and sent to Shah Jahan in 1635 AD.

questions.question_text: Among the following people invited by Akbar to Ibadat-Khana, who was not a Jain monk?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Among the Jain monks invited by Akbar to Ibadat-Khanas, Meherji Rana was not a Jain monk; rather, he was a scholar of Parsi religion. Different religious teachers invited to the Ibadat-Khanas were – Hindu religion – Purushottam and Devi. Jain religion – Harivijaya Suri, Jina Chandra Suri, Shanti Chandra, and Vijayasena Suri, etc. Christian religion – Aquaviva and Monserrate. Parsi religion – Dastur Meherji Rana. Note:- Akbar opened the door of Ibadat Khana for followers of all religions in October 1578 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Englishmen was proficient in the Turkish language, and who received a Mansab of 400 and the title (khitab) of 'English Khan' or 'Firangi Khan'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – During Jahangir's reign, the English also tried to obtain commercial facilities from the Emperor and William Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe met the Emperor as representatives of Britain. Jahangir gave Hawkins a Mansab of 400. Apart from this, he also received the title of English Khan or Firangi Khan.

questions.question_text: Which modern historian has termed the 'Satnami rebellion' as 'Hindu reaction' in opposition to Aurangzeb's religious policies?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation Modern historian Jadunath Sarkar has termed 'Satnami rebellion' as 'Hindu reaction' in opposition to Aurangzeb's religious policies. Sir Jadunath Sarkar has also termed Aurangzeb's 'anti-Hindu religious policy' as a cause of the Mughal decline.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not correct regarding the terms of the 'Treaty of Chittor' (1615 AD)?

options.A: Jahangir was not in favor of ending the ancient Rajput dynasties.
options.B: The Rana was given back Mewar including Chittor.
options.C: The Rana would not be able to do reconstruction and fortification in Chittor.
options.D: The Rana had to be present in the Mughal court personally.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – According to the terms of the 'Treaty of Chittor', the Rana did not have to be personally present in the Mughal court. He asked for permission to send his son Karan to the court. In 1615, a treaty was reached between Mewar and the Mughals on the following terms – 1. The Rana accepted Mughal suzerainty. 2. The Rana was not asked for marital relations with the Mughal dynasty. The Rana asked for permission to send his son Karan to the court in his place, which Jahangir accepted. 3. Jahangir respectfully gave the entire land territory of Mewar and the fort of Chittor to the Raja. The only condition was that the fort of Chittor should not be fortified.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not in Jahangir's twelve edicts?

options.C: Termination of Tamgha and Mir Bahri

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation: On the occasion of his coronation, Jahangir announced his famous 12 edicts related to governance which were as follows:- (1) Removal of taxes (2) Rules related to theft and robbery on roads (3) Rules related to property of the deceased (4) Prohibition of intoxicants (5) Prohibition of occupation of houses and mutilation (6) Prohibition of slavery (7) Arrangement of hospitals and hakims (8) Prohibition of animal slaughter on fixed days (9) Respect for Sunday (10) Confirmation of Mansab and Jagir (11) Confirmation of Madad-i-Mash (Aimma land) (12) Release of prisoners.

questions.question_text: Khanzada Begum was the sister of:
questions.explanation: Khanzada Begum was Babar's sister. Babar became ruler at the age of 11. Khanzada Begum helped Babar in getting power. But Babar failed in ruling; he was defeated by his uncle. As a result, Babar attacked India. Babar's first attack on India was on the fort of Bajaur and Bhera in 1519 AD

questions.question_text: Which of the following were original books written on Akbar's order?
questions.explanation: Among the books written on Akbar's order are Tarikh-i-Alfi, Akbarnama, and Ain-i-Akbari. Among these, Ain-i-Akbari is of the most importance. This book gives the most reliable information about Akbar. Its author was Abul Fazl. Abul Fazl was one of the Navratnas of Akbar

questions.question_text: Who among the following merged the independent Golconda state into the Mughal Empire?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb won the Golconda state in 1687 AD and merged it into his kingdom. It is said that Aurangzeb opened the gates of the Golconda fort with gold keys just as Akbar opened the gates of the Asirgarh fort. The policy of the South proved fatal for Aurangzeb

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding Sher Shah Suri – 1. Sher Shah established an empire spread from Afghanistan to Odisha. 2. The use of Hindvi language in administration is an indicator of Sher Shah's practical knowledge. 3. He implemented law and order strictly. 4. Sher Shah ended the circulation of gold coins. Which of the above statements are correct? Select the correct answer from the code given below – Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June 2014) Explanation– The use of Hindvi language in administration is an indicator of Sher Shah's practical knowledge. He implemented law and order strictly. Sher Shah Suri ruled Delhi from 1540-45 AD.

questions.question_text: Emperor Akbar adopted many Indian socio-cultural customs. One of these was shaving the head after the death of any member of the Mughal royal family. Which lady's death led Akbar to shave his head and mustache in 1604 AD?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2015) Explanation– Upon the death of Akbar's mother Hamida Banu Begum, Akbar shaved his head. Akbar had adopted many Indian socio-cultural customs. Under which, he had shaved his head and mustache upon his mother's death.

questions.question_text: The Rohtasgarh fort was built:
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri had the Rohtasgarh fort built for the protection of the northwest border. With the construction of this fort, the northwest border became completely secure. Sher Shah Suri's reign was only of five years. He died in 1545 AD. Sher Shah's mausoleum is in Sasaram, Bihar

questions.question_text: Who among the following was Babar's mother?
questions.explanation: Babar, the founder of the Mughal dynasty in India, was born in Fergana in 1483 AD. His father's name was Umar Sheikh Mirza and his mother's name was Qutlugh Nigar Khanum. Babar was the fifth descendant of Timur from his father's side and the 14th descendant of Genghis from his mother's side

questions.question_text: After the death of Aurangzeb, Bengal became almost independent from the Mughal Empire under whose leadership?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ After the death of Aurangzeb, Bengal became almost independent from the Mughal Empire under the leadership of Murshid Quli Khan. In 1700 AD, Murshid Quli Khan was appointed Diwan of Bengal. Finally, in 1717 AD, he was made the Subedar (official) of Bengal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Englishmen tried to obtain a 'Firman' from Akbar to trade in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– During Akbar's reign, the Portuguese, English, and Dutch had reached India but in the 16th century, the Portuguese were dominant on the Indian coast. The English and the Dutch did not get any commercial facility in this century. The Portuguese definitely established their influence on the Indian coast near Goa, Chaul, and Bombay. They sent Christian missionaries to Akbar's court from time to time, took permission to build churches, and tried to convert Akbar to Christianity, but apart from good relations, the Portuguese could not get other benefits. However, as an envoy of Elizabeth, John Mildenhall traveled twice between 1599-1606 AD to the court of ruler Akbar and made a claim to obtain commercial concession.

questions.question_text: Which of the following authors was granted the title of 'Amir-ul-Akhbar' by Humayun?
questions.explanation: Khwandamir was granted patronage by Humayun. Khwandamir wrote Qanun-i-Humayuni. Which is also called Humayun-nama. The reign of Humayun has been described in this. Humayun granted him the title of Amir-ul-Akhbar

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct?

options.A: Akbar divided his empire into twelve provincial units. These were called Subah.
options.B: A Subah was divided into several Sarkars.
options.C: A Sarkar was divided into Parganas.
options.D: A Pargana was divided into Shiq.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– From the point of view of administration, every subah was divided into several units. These units were called Sarkar. Each Sarkar was again divided into Pargana or Mahals. These Parganas were divided into villages. These villages were the smallest unit of administration. Under Parganas, there were villages which were called Mawada or Deh. The main officer of the Pargana was the Shiqdar. Therefore, statement (d) is wrong.

questions.question_text: Where was Jahangir buried?
questions.explanation: Jahangir was Akbar's son. With the emergence of Nur Jahan in court politics, his role gradually diminished. For this reason, due to excessive consumption of alcohol etc., his health deteriorated. He died in October 1627 AD while returning from Kashmir. He was brought to Lahore where he was buried in Shahdara (Lahore), the place of his mausoleum

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the highest officer of Akbar's central administration?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- During Akbar's time, there was a council of ministers in the center. Whose head was the Vakil-i-Mutlaq (representative of the Emperor). In this, the powers of both Vakil and Diwan (Wazir) were included. That is why the Vakil was also called the 'All-powerful Wazir'. The Vakil-i-Mutlaq (Prime Minister) of the initial years of Akbar and the last of Humayun was Bairam Khan.

questions.question_text: After defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the Battle of Panipat, to which saint's shrine did Babar go to pay tribute?
questions.explanation: The First Battle of Panipat took place on 21 April 1526 AD between Babar and Ibrahim Lodi, in which Ibrahim Lodi was defeated and killed. Babar assumed the title of Padishah and laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India Babar went to the shrine of Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki to pay tribute after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the Battle of Panipat. Their shrine is in Delhi, the construction of Qutub Minar has been done in their name, they were saints of the Chishti sect.

questions.question_text: Which medieval Indian ruler started the system of "Patta" and "Qabuliyat" for the welfare of farmers?
questions.explanation: Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri) was the founder of the 'Second Afghan Dynasty' ruling Delhi. Sher Shah's administrative reforms proved to be far-reaching. Information about his administrative management is available in Abbas Khan Sarwani's book 'Tarikh-i-Sher Shahi'. Sher Shah started the system of "Patta" and "Qabuliyat" with the objective of establishing a direct relationship between the government and the farmers. Patta was given by the government to the farmers in which the details of the fixed revenue were written. The farmer used to accept these through a Qabuliyat paper

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians says that signatures were forcibly obtained from the Ulema on the Mahzar?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Historian Abdul Qadir Badauni says that signatures were forcibly obtained from the Ulema on the Mahzar. Abdul Qadir Badauni was an Indian historian and translator of Persian origin. He was active in India during the Mughal period. His father was Mulla Shah. He also studied Sufism. Akbar appointed him in his court in 1574 as an officer of the Islamic religion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following agencies kept a record of the activities of Mughal-era Jagirs and Jagirdars?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Sawanih Nigar (Sawanih Nigar) agency kept a record of the activities of Mughal-era Jagirs and Jagirdars. During the Mughal period, some important people were granted Jagir from whom it was expected that they would remain loyal to the government.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events chronologically and select the correct answer using the code given below– 1. Rebellion of Khurram 2. Battle of Chausa 3. Battle of Dharmat 4. Rebellion of Khusrau Code
questions.explanation: Battle of Chausa – 1539 AD. Rebellion of Khusrau – 1606 AD. Rebellion of Khurram – 1623–26 AD. Battle of Dharmat – 1658 AD.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor's children were born in the Khanqah of a Sufi saint instead of the royal harem?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar's children were born in the shrine of Sufi saint Salim Chishti instead of the royal harem. Actually, all of Akbar's sons had died in his youth. Sheikh Salim Chishti gave the Emperor a blessing to give three sons. When in 1569 AD, Akbar's wife, the princess of Jaipur, became pregnant, she was sent to the Sheikh's hut where on 30 August 1569 AD, she gave birth to a son whose name was kept Sultan Muhammad Salim based on the name of the Sheikh. Akbar used to call him Shekhu Baba.

questions.question_text: Which painter did Jahangir send to Iran with his envoy?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Countless painters were working under Jahangir - among them Farrukh Beg, Daulat, Manohar, Mansur, Bishandas, and Abul Hasan were prominent. Jahangir sent Bishandas to Iran with his envoy to make portraits of Shah Abbas of Persia and his family members and courtiers. When Bishandas returned from Persia, Jahangir was satisfied with his work.

questions.question_text: " 'Din-i-Ilahi' was a monument of Akbar's folly, not of wisdom." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Dr. V. A. Smith has called 'Din-i-Ilahi' a child of Akbar's imperialistic feelings or a religious cloak of his political ambitions. He says that 'Din-i-Ilahi was a product of Akbar's arrogance and dictatorial feelings. It was not a monument of his wisdom, but of his folly.'

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal emperors has been described in the Sanskrit text 'Sarvadesh Vrittant Sangrah'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: The most popular book of Akbar's reign in Sanskrit is titled 'Sarvadesh Vrittant Sangrah' by Mahesh Thakur. Perhaps there is no mention of such any military or political events in this book, which is described in contemporary Persian literature.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Abul Fazl's role in the discussions of Ibadat Khana was important.
options.B: Religious discussions in Ibadat Khana played no role in the development of Akbar's religious ideas.
options.C: In the later period, Ibadat Khana was opened for all religious leaders.
options.D: Ibadat Khana was established in 1575 AD.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation: Akbar had the Ibadat Khana built in 1575 AD. Actually, until 1575 AD, Akbar followed the external forms of the Sunni religion. At this time, he came into contact with Sheikh Mubarak and his sons - Faizi and Abul Fazl, due to which a change came in his ideas. Then he had Ibadat Khana built at Fatehpur Sikri for debate on philosophical and theological questions. In this, the Sayyids, Sheikhs, and Ulema used to have religious discussions under the chairmanship of the Emperor. In October 1578 AD, Akbar opened the door of 'Ibadat Khana' for followers of all religions. Consequently, scholars of Hindu, Jain, Christian, Parsi, etc. religions also started participating in the religious discussions of Ibadat Khana. Akbar was very impressed by this and he realized that some good elements exist in all religions. He started giving respect and honor to all religions and religious teachers. Therefore, statement (b) is wrong.

questions.question_text: Which foreigner wrote the biography of Shivaji?
questions.explanation: Cosme-da-Guarda undertook the work of writing the biography of Shivaji. He has given a detailed description in his book "Life of the Celebrated Shivaji" about Shivaji's governance, his actions towards the public, empire expansion, administrative rules, revenue management, etc

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II : List-I (Book) List-II (Author) A. Shivaji Souvenir 1. James Grant Duff B. History of the Marathas 2. G.S. Sardesai C. A Study of Muslims 3. Edward Thomas Instruction D. Chronicles of the Pathan 4. V.S. Bendrey Deccan of Delhi A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct match is as follows List-I (Book) List-II (Author) A. Shivaji Souvenir - G.S. Sardesai B. History of the Marathas - James Grant Duff C. A Study of Muslims - V.S. Bendrey Instruction D. Chronicles of the Pathan - Edward Thomas Deccan of Delhi 3. Arrange the military system of Shivaji in descending order of rank and select the correct answer from the code given below : I. Jamadar II. Havaldar III. Nayak IV. Ek Hazari Rise and fall of Marathas, Shivaji Code : (a) I, II, IV, III (b) II, I, IV, III (c) III, I, II, IV (d) III, II, I, IV UPPSC GDC 2021 Ans. (d) : In Shivaji's military system, the descending order of rank is as follows– (i) Nayak – Officer of 9 soldiers or Paiks (ii) Havaldar – Officer of 10 Nayaks/25 horsemen (iii) Jamadar – Officer of 5 Havaldars (iv) Ek Hazari – Officer of 10 Jamadars/10 Jumladars

questions.question_text: Which Muslim traveler came to the Vijayanagara court–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – In 1422 AD, Deva Raya II became the ruler of Vijayanagara. During his reign, Persian traveler Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in 1443 AD. Abdur Razzaq came to Calicut as an ambassador of Shahrukh to the King Zamorin. He described the social life and administration of Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: Who built the Hazara temple among the following?
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya built the Hazara temple. Krishnadevaraya was the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire (Tuluva Dynasty). He ascended the throne in 1509 AD, he assumed titles like Andhra Bhoja, Abhinava Bhoja, Yavanrajya Sthapanacharya, Telugu Bhoja, etc. He was a great scholar, patron of scholars, a lover of art and literature; his era is considered the classical age of Telugu literature. During his reign, eight great Telugu scholars lived in his court. He built many buildings like Hazara temple, Vitthala Swami temple, Chidambaram temple, etc. He authored 'Amuktamalyada' in Telugu language and 'Jambavati Kalyanam' in Sanskrit

questions.question_text: Abdur Razzaq, the ambassador of Persia, came to the court of which ruler of Vijayanagara?
questions.explanation: Deva Raya II was the greatest ruler of the Sangama dynasty. After ascending the throne, he kept the Quran in front of him and for the first time recruited Muslim soldiers on a large scale. During the time of Deva Raya II, Persian (Iran) ambassador Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara. Abdur Razzaq came to India as an ambassador of the ruler of Iran, Mirza Shahrukh. He gave a detailed description of Vijayanagara in his travel account

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the chief land surveyor in Shivaji's administration?
questions.explanation: In Shivaji's administration, the work of chief land surveyor was done by Annaji Datto. He was one of Shivaji's Ashtapradhans (eight ministers). Following Shivaji's instructions, he conducted a detailed land survey in 1679 AD, which resulted in the determination of a new land revenue. He ended the middlemen, and the work of revenue collection was done only by his officers. 33% of the total produce was taken as revenue, which was later increased to 40%. Revenue could be paid in both cash and kind

questions.question_text: The standard unit of Vijayanagara currency which was mentioned as 'Pagoda' in later European accounts, by what names has it been described in the inscriptions?
questions.explanation: The currency system of the Vijayanagara Empire was one of the most commendable currency systems of India. The most famous gold coin of Vijayanagara was 'Varaha', its weight was 52 grains. Which European/foreign travelers called Huna, Pardose or Pagoda. Small gold coins are called 'Pratap' and 'Phanam'. Small silver coins were called 'Tar'. On the gold 'Varaha' coins of the founder of Vijayanagara, Harihar (1336 AD), figures of Hanuman and Garuda are inscribed. On the coins of the Tuluva dynasty, figures of Garuda, Uma-Maheshwar, Venkatesha and Balakrishna are inscribed. The officer keeping the royal seal in Vijayanagara was called 'Mudra Karta'. A secretariat was established in the center and the departments of this secretariat were divided; it included officers like 'Rayasam' or Secretary, 'Karnikam' i.e., Accountant. Vijayanagara's 'Varaha' gold coin was a very respected coin, which was accepted in all major commercial cities of India and the world. There was circulation of gold, silver, copper coins in Vijayanagara

questions.question_text: He had a deep interest in debates and scholarly discussions, and when Srinatha defeated his court poet Dindima in a debate, he honored him (Srinatha) with the title of 'Kavi Sarvabhauma' and 'bathed him in gold coins'. Identify that ruler of Vijayanagara:
questions.explanation: Deva Raya II was the greatest ruler of the Sangama dynasty (Vijayanagara). He is known as Gajabetkar, Imadi Deva Raya/Praudha Deva Raya and in mythological stories he is considered an avatar of Indra. He was a patron of both learning and scholars. He himself was a scholar of Sanskrit. He authored two Sanskrit books 'Nataka Sudhanidhi' and a commentary on Badarayana's Brahmasutra. Under his patronage, thirty-four poets flourished. Among whom Dindima was his court poet. When Telugu poet Srinatha defeated Dindima in a debate, Deva Raya II honored Srinatha with the title of 'Kavi Sarvabhauma' and bathed him in gold coins. Harihar II, Mallikarjuna, and Virupaksha II were also important rulers of Vijayanagara

questions.question_text: Below two statements are given: One is written as Assertion (A) and other is its Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : Deva Raya II strengthened the military base of his empire by improving the quality of war horses and training the cavalry and archers. He established strict political control over the commercial centers of the western coast, thus linking military reforms with international trade. Reason (R) : Due to military and administrative dominance over the major ports of the Arabian Sea, Deva Raya II got a new and separate source of revenue for the state. In light of the above statements, select the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
options.C: (A) is true, but (R) is not true
options.D: (A) is not true, but (R) is true

questions.explanation: Deva Raya II was the greatest ruler of the Sangama dynasty. Who became ruler in 1422 AD.
