The public also knew him by other titles such as 'Imadi Deva Raya' or 'Praudha Deva Raya' or divine ruler, avatar of Indra, etc. Deva Raya II strengthened the military base of his empire by improving the quality of war horses and by training the cavalry and archers. He established strict political control over the commercial centers of the western coast, thus he linked military reforms with international trade. Assertion (A) is true Deva Raya II, during his reign, included most of South India including Kerala into the Vijayanagara empire and his empire extended up to the coast of Sri Lanka (Ceylon). He appointed his Lingayat follower minister Lakkana or Lakkemke as the lord of the southern ocean, due to military and administrative dominance over the major ports of the Arabian Sea, Deva Raya II got a new and separate source of revenue for the state. Reason (R) is true and is the correct explanation of the statement.

questions.question_text: In the context of the relations of Nizam-ul-Mulk with the Marathas, which of the following statements is true?
questions.explanation: In 1720 AD, Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela' appointed Chin Qilich Khan as the Subahdar of Deccan. He is also known by the name 'Nizam-ul-Mulk'. In 1724, in the battle of Shakarkhedo, with the help of the Marathas, he defeated the Mughal Subahdar of Deccan 'Mubariz Khan' and established his independent power in the Deccan. After his position became strong, Nizam-ul-Mulk again started acting against the Marathas and refused to give Chauth and Sardeshmukhi, after his successful rebellion against the Sayyids, in 1728 AD Nizam-ul-Mulk was defeated by Baji Rao in the battle of 'Palkhed', upon being defeated in the war, Nizam-ul-Mulk was forced for a treaty. On 6 March 1728, the 'Treaty of Mungi Shivgaon' took place between the two, in which Nizam accepted to give Chauth and Sardeshmukhi to the Marathas. Baji Rao and Nizam's first meeting did not happen in January 1721 but happened at the time of the Treaty of Mungi Shivgaon on 6 March 1728. The main issue of dispute between the Marathas and Nizam-ul-Mulk was not Karnataka. But rather the policy of empire expansion

questions.question_text: Which area was the subject of dispute between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Bahmani Kingdom?
questions.explanation: After the fall of Tughlaq power in the South, in the mid-14th century, the Vijayanagara and Bahmani empires both came into existence at almost the same time. Since the beginning of the establishment of both states, a long struggle continued between them. The center of the struggle of these two was the famous Raichur Doab situated between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. Therefore, this is also called the Raichur Doab problem

questions.question_text: The Vijayanagara state was established during the time of which Delhi Sultan?
questions.explanation: In the south, the establishment of Vijayanagara in 1336 AD was the result of a political and cultural movement against Tughlaq power. When Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq returned to famine-stricken North India with his army suffering from plague, it became clear that he would not be able to keep control over the far south. In 1336 AD, Harihar and his brother Bukka established a Hindu state in the south of the Krishna river, which slowly expanded in the form of the Vijayanagara state

questions.question_text: In which order was the Vijayanagara empire divided?
questions.explanation: From the point of view of administrative convenience, the Vijayanagara Empire was divided into provinces. The order of their division was as follows – State or Mandalam, Kottam or Valanadu, Nadu, Melagrama, Ur or Grama. The number of provinces kept changing continuously. Domingos Paes stated the number of provinces as 200, whereas according to H. Krishna Sastri there were 6 major provinces in the Vijayanagara empire. The number of provinces was highest during the reign of Krishnadevaraya

questions.question_text: Who were in opposition to the independent Maratha state during the time of Shivaji?
questions.explanation: Shivaji ended the Jagirdari system and converted it into the Ryotwari system and made changes in the position of hereditary revenue officials, who are known by the names Deshmukh, Deshpande, Patil and Kulkarni. During the time of Shivaji, Deshmukhs were opposing the independent Maratha state. Deshmukhs and Deshpandes were other district-level officers who acted as a control over Mamlatdar. Without their verification, no account was accepted

questions.question_text: After the coronation, Shivaji's initial campaign was against whom?
questions.explanation: Shivaji's coronation took place in Raigad in 1674 AD. To get his coronation done, Shivaji called the famous scholar of Kashi, Vishweshwar Bhatt alias Shri Ganga Bhatt. After his coronation, Shivaji's initial campaign was against the Bijapur administration (Karnataka campaign) in 1676-78 AD. Gulbarga was conquered in 1677 AD. The fort keeper here was Hussain Khan Hyderabadi. The fort of Gingee was conquered in 1678 AD. The fort keeper here was Daud Khan Habshi. The conquest of Gingee was Shivaji's last conquest

questions.question_text: Which ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire sent an ambassador to China?
questions.explanation: After Harihar, his brother Bukka First became the ruler. He was a great warrior, diplomat, and lover of learning. One great conquest of Bukka First was the Madurai conquest, due to which his empire reached Rameswaram in the deep south. Religiously, he claimed the protection of the Hindu religion and assumed the title of 'Vedamarga Pratishthapaka'. He also tried to develop the foreign policy of the state. With this objective, he sent an embassy to China. Bukka died in 1377 AD

questions.question_text: On whom did the Peshwa levy the tax named 'Patdam'?
questions.explanation: In the Maratha empire, during the time of the Peshwas, a tax named 'Patdam' was levied on widow remarriage. The major taxes collected in the Maratha empire were called Chauth and Sardeshmukhi. During this period, land revenue 2/5 part i.e. 40% was collected

questions.question_text: Italian traveler Paes says, "He is a great ruler and a very just person, but he is prone to sudden fits of anger." This statement relates to which ruler of Vijayanagara?
questions.explanation: Domingos Paes, who was a Portuguese traveler, visited Vijayanagara around 1520 AD during the reign of Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadeva Raya. He says about Krishnadeva Raya that 'He is a great ruler and a very just person but is prone to sudden fits of anger.' Paes, along with describing the prosperity of the Vijayanagara Empire, also describes in detail the social, economic and cultural events of this period

questions.question_text: Where was the Nayakara system prevalent?
questions.explanation: Nayakara system (Military Land-Holding Rights), just as the provincial system of the Delhi Sultanate rested on the 'Iqta system', in the same way, the Vijayanagara period 'Nayakara system' was a part of the provincial system. This Nayakara system is the biggest difference between the Chola period and the Vijayanagara period monarchy. The credit for strengthening and well-developing this system in the Vijayanagara empire goes to Krishnadeva Raya. Historians have different opinions regarding the nature of the Nayaka system. According to some historians, the military commanders of the Vijayanagara period were called Nayakas. According to some historians, 'Nayaka' were land-lords and military chiefs (military chiefs), to whom the king gave specific land-plots in return for salary or for the maintenance of their subordinate army, which was called Amaram or Nayakattanam

questions.question_text: Who was the in-charge of general administration as a member of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan?
questions.explanation: In Shivaji's administration, there were Ashtapradhan/eight big officers to help, who did the actual operation of the administration, whose function was merely to advise the king. These Ashtapradhan people worked as Shivaji's secretaries. Peshwa - was the Prime Minister or Chief Minister. His function was to take care of the entire state's administration period. In the absence of the king, he had to take care of his tasks. He used to put his seal below the king's on government letters and documents. Shivaji's first Peshwa was Moropant Pingle (Moropant Trimbak Pingle)

questions.question_text: Who was the finance minister of Shivaji who also guided later Maratha rulers?
questions.explanation: Shivaji's finance minister was Ramchandra Pant Bawdekar who also guided later Maratha rulers Specific Facts: Majumdar or Amatya – Was the finance minister of the state. He was the superintendent of the revenue department. Shivaji had appointed Ramchandra Neelkanth to this post.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Italian traveler 'Nicolo-di-Conti' come to Vijayanagara?
questions.explanation: Nicolo-di-Conti - He was the first Italian traveler to visit Vijayanagara who visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Deva Raya I (1420-22 AD). During this period, Venice was the center of Indian import trade in Europe. He traveled to the East with his wife. He reached Bharuch via Basra and Hormuz by sea route. From here he went to Vijayanagara. He gave a detailed account of an important source of Vijayanagara empire history, and from his account, it is known that the military power of the Vijayanagara Empire was organized and it was a powerful state. Conti has described social conditions, especially the Sati system seen with his own eyes. He has also given an account of Hindu festivals, judicial procedures, etc

questions.question_text: What part of Chauth was called Mokasa?
questions.explanation: Shivaji started the collection of 'Chauth tax' to increase his income, which was the main source of income for the Marathas. Later, Chauth tax proved helpful in his empire expansion. These taxes were collected from the borders of neighboring states and cities or from the citizens of his influence area. 'Chauth' was one-fourth (1/4) part of the annual income of that region or city. It was 25 percent, which was divided into 4 parts 1. Babati – 1/4 (25 percent) part of Chauth's income was for the King. 2. Sahotra – 6 percent part of income was for Pant Sachiv. 3. Nadgunda – 3 percent part, which depended on the king's will. 4. Mokasa – 66 percent (2/3) part of income was given to Maratha Sardars. Specific Facts: Mokasa- Land grant given in lieu of cash salary in Maratha administration was called Mokasa. It was revenue-free land received in lieu of military service.

questions.question_text: Which ruler of Vijayanagara built a dam to remove the shortage of water on the Tungabhadra river?
questions.explanation: After the death of Harihari II, a struggle for succession ensued among his three sons which lasted for two years. Deva Raya achieved success at the end of this struggle and sat on the throne in 1406 AD. Deva Raya I was a great warrior and his entire reign period was spent in military campaigns. First of all, in 1406 AD, he had to face the attack of Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah and Deva Raya had to make a forced compromise. Deva Raya reorganized the army and also recruited horsemen, Turkic archers, and gave them good salaries. He fought against Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah for a long time through this excellent army. Deva Raya was a great builder and patron of scholars. He built a dam on the Tungabhadra river, constructed many canals, and removed the trouble being faced by the public. Vijayanagara became a center of learning and knowledge during his reign

questions.question_text: Which city did Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya build?
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya's reign is considered the classical age of literature. Along with being a great ruler, Krishnadevaraya is also called a building builder. He is also given the title of Andhra Pitamaha. He founded a city Nagalapuram in memory of his mother Nagala Devi. He built the grand Hazara Rama temple and many temples in Vijayanagara. He also built temples named Hazara and Vitthala Swami. During his reign, along with temple construction, he built grand schools to encourage education, spreading a web throughout the Vijayanagara empire

questions.question_text: On the bank of which river was the capital of Vijayanagara state, Hampi, situated?
questions.explanation: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. It served as the capital of the Vijayanagara empire in the 14th century. Hampi was a city situated in northern Karnataka. Hampi is a famous pilgrimage site of Hindu and Jain religion. This place is situated on the bank of the Tungabhadra river. Hampi-Vijayanagara was considered the second largest medieval city of the world after Beijing after 1500 AD. The group of monuments in Hampi was included in the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1986. There are about 16000 monuments in this place

questions.question_text: Which of the following forts did Shivaji conquer first?
questions.explanation: When Shivaji was nineteen years old, he was made a military commander and the desire to establish his own state awakened in his heart. When Shivaji saw that Muslims were not focusing much on the forts, he started corresponding with the owner of the Torna fort. This fort was at a distance of 30 kilometers south-west from Pune city. Shivaji lured the chief guardian there with money and made him submissive and in one night took the Mavali army and captured the fort without much difficulty. This event of Torna conquest is of 1646 AD. Shivaji's name did not spread much from this conquest, but along with capturing this fort, the beginning of Shivaji's state establishment took place

questions.question_text: Name the volume on the history of Vijayanagara written by Robert Sewell, which was published in the year 1900?
questions.explanation: A Forgotten Empire Vijayanagara A Contribution to the History of India was written in 1900 AD. Its author Robert Sewell had worked in the Madras Presidency during the time of colonial rule in India. Famous historian Robert Sewell has described the political background of South India and the rise of the state, its expansion throughout South India, and all the events that led to the fall of this empire

questions.question_text: Between whom was the battle of Shakarkhedo fought?
questions.explanation: In 1722 AD, Nizam-ul-Mulk became Vazir and tried to establish law and order in Delhi but he was unsuccessful and being sad, he left for Deccan on the pretext of a hunting expedition. Muhammad Shah, being angry with Chin Qilich Khan, appointed Mubariz Khan as the Subahdar of Deccan. But in 1724 AD, in the battle of Shakarkhedo, Nizam-ul-Mulk defeated Mubariz Khan and in 1724 AD established the independent Hyderabad state. Muhammad Shah gave Nizam-ul-Mulk the title of 'Asaf Jah'

questions.question_text: In which year was the battle of Tunga fought between Maratha Sardar Mahadji Scindia and the Rajputs?
questions.explanation: The battle of Tunga between Maratha Sardar Mahadji Scindia and the Rajputs took place in 1787 AD in which the joint army of Vijay Singh and Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh of Jaipur defeated the army of Maratha Mahadji Scindia

questions.question_text: In the Bahmani kingdom, 'Sadr-i-Jahan' was the head of which department?
questions.explanation: The head of the important department that helped the Bahmani Sultan in running the administration was known by the following names S.No. Department Head (1) Religious and Judicial Sadr-i-Jahan (2) Military Amir-ul-Umara (3) Foreign-Minister Wazir-i-Ashraf (4) Finance Minister Amir-i-Jumla (5) Prime Minister Vakil-us-Saltanat

questions.question_text: Which fort of South India did the Mughals keep under siege for eight years?
questions.explanation: The fort of Gingee situated in South India is in Tamil Nadu. Shivaji called this fort the most impregnable fort of India. Aurangzeb took this fort under his control in 1691 AD and kept Rajaram imprisoned in this fort for 8 years. Hence, the Mughals also had dominance over this fort for eight years

questions.question_text: About which architectural style did Herman Goetz write that in temples usually there is a large lamp-post or pillar for lamps?
questions.explanation: About Maratha temple architectural style, Herman Goetz has written that in temples usually there is a large lamp-post or pillar for lamps on which a series of lamps is made to illuminate the temple; this pillar must have been the specialty

questions.question_text: In the context of Shivaji, which date is not matched?
questions.explanation: Correct chronology of events in the context of Shivaji– 1. Capture of the fort of Purandar - 1648 2. First loot of Surat – 1664 3. Treaty of Purandar – 1665 4. Capture of Javali – 1655 Note– Shivaji captured Javali not in 1647 but in 1655. This question in the above question is wrong.

questions.question_text: At the time of the Talikota battle (1565), in whose hands was the real power of the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: During the reign of Sadashiva, the real power remained in the hands of Ram Raya. He made fundamental changes in the administration of the empire. The battle of Talikota was fought in 1565 near Rakkasa-Tangadi village. In this battle, the Muslim confederacy which happened between the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagara, in which Vijayanagara was devastated and Ram Raya was killed. Tirumala took Sadashiva and started ruling from Penukonda and later he became the founder of the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagara, the Aravidu dynasty

questions.question_text: Keep the units of administration of the Vijayanagara Empire in descending order: 1. Valanadu 4. Nadu 2. Grama 5. Sthala
questions.explanation: For the administration of the Vijayanagara Empire, the descending order given in the source is: Mandalam → Valanadu or Kottam → Nadu → Kottam → Sthala and Seema → Grama.

questions.question_text: Mandalam 6. Kottam Select the correct answer group:
questions.explanation: For the administration of the Vijayanagara Empire, it was divided into many provinces, whose descending order is as follows Province (State)  Mandalam  Valanadu or Kottam  Nadu  Kottam  Sthala and Seema  Grama

questions.question_text: Which ruler of Vijayanagara recruited Turkic archers among the following?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Deva Raya First (1406–22 AD) remained the ruler of Vijayanagara during his period. According to Ferishta, he recruited Muslim soldiers, although the description of the recruitment of Turkic archers is obtained in the context of Deva Raya II. In this way, both Deva Raya I and II recruited Turks into their army.

questions.question_text: To which ruler did Isami dedicate his work Futuh-us-Salatin?
questions.explanation: Isami has dedicated his book "Futuh-us-Salatin" to Alauddin Hasan Gangu, who was the founder of the Bahmani kingdom. Hasan Gangu assumed the title of Bahman Shah. It contains descriptions from Ghaznavids up to the founders of the Bahmani kingdom

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the Marathas?

options.A: After the death of Aurangzeb, under the leadership of Shahu, the Marathas tried to establish an independent kingdom in Odisha.
options.C: In 1740, the Marathas tried to establish control over Rajasthan, parts of Doab and Punjab.
options.D: In the eighteenth century, the expansion of Maratha power took place under the leadership of Maratha Sardars.

questions.explanation: It is a false statement that the expansion of Maratha power took place under the leadership of Maratha Sardars True statement is– In the eighteenth century, the expansion of Maratha power took place under the leadership of Maratha Peshwas.

questions.question_text: In the Nayakara system of Vijayanagara, land was assigned to _______

options.B: For people committed to annual fee and military service
options.C: For Brahmins running charitable service institutions

questions.explanation: Under the Nayakara system of Vijayanagara, land was assigned to persons (Nayaka) committed to annual fee and military service

questions.question_text: Identify the false statement about the third battle of Panipat:

options.A: The defeat in the battle of Panipat proved disastrous for the Marathas.
options.B: Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao died shortly after this battle.
options.C: Although the Peshwa was away from the battlefield, he tried his best to maintain the arrangement of supplies, etc. for his armies.
options.D: The character of the Marathas was a major reason for defeat in this battle.

questions.explanation: The Peshwa did not make any effort to maintain the arrangement of supplies for his armies. Due to financial crunch, the Peshwa could not give any help, which led to a state of starvation in the Maratha camps

questions.question_text: Who was the chief commander of the Maratha army in the third battle of Panipat-
questions.explanation: The third battle of Panipat took place between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas, in which the Marathas were defeated. Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao sent the army under the leadership of his minor son Vishwasrao, but the actual commander-in-chief was his cousin Sadashiv Rao Bhau. In this battle, Bhil chief Ibrahim Khan Gardi helped the Marathas. Rohilla Sardar Najib-ud-Daulah and Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daulah helped Abdali

questions.question_text: During whose reign did the Marathas realize their glory?
questions.explanation: In reality, the rise of the Marathas started during the reign of Shah Jahan, while an expansionist policy was adopted by Shivaji and he also achieved success in it. After this, during the Peshwa period, the power of the Marathas put even the Mughals in doubt

questions.question_text: Which of the following sultanates of the South was not included in the alliance against the Vijayanagara Empire in the Rakshasa-Tangadi (also called Talikota) battle?
questions.explanation: Berar was not included in the confederacy of Muslim rulers of the South against the Vijayanagara Empire. In this anti-Vijayanagara Empire confederacy, Ahmednagar, Bijapur, Golconda and Bidar were included. At the time of this war, the ruler of Vijayanagara was Sadashivaraya

questions.question_text: Names of temples built by Krishnadevaraya in Hampi of Vijayanagara are~ 1. Varadaraja temple 2. Parvati temple 3. Krishnaswami temple 4. Vitthalaswami temple 5. Hazara Ramaswami temple 6. Ekabarnath temple Select the correctly matched answer group:
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya was the most powerful king of the Vijayanagara empire. Krishnadevaraya built the Krishnaswami temple around 1513 AD to mark the victory over Odisha. He also founded a new city named 'Nagalapuram'

questions.question_text: When was the Bahmani kingdom established?
questions.explanation: As a result of the rebellion of Amiran-i-Sada in the Deccan, in the last days of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, the Bahmani empire was established in 1347 AD by Hasan by assuming the title of Abul-Muzaffar Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah and laid the foundation of the Bahmani empire

questions.question_text: .........under the leadership of Peshwa the power of Marathas reached its zenith.
questions.explanation: Under Bajirao I (1720-40 AD), the Maratha power reached its zenith. His policy in the direction of empire expansion remained focused towards the north. Its aim was - "Marathas' flag from Krishna river to Attock". His policy towards the Mughal empire was clear. His belief was that "We should attack the stem of this decaying tree, the branches will fall on their own."

questions.question_text: Which of the following elements can be seen in the temples of the developed phase of the Vijayanagara empire? 1. Gopuram 2. Kalyana Mandapam 3. Decorated pillars and ceilings 4. Pillar-bottom carving decoration
questions.explanation: The establishment of the Vijayanagara empire was done by Harihar-I and Bukka-I during the reign of Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq in 1336 AD. Features of temples built in the Vijayanagara empire (1) Gopuram (2) Kalyana Mandapam (3) Decorated pillars and ceilings (4) Pillar-bottom carving decoration

questions.question_text: (2) To avoid treachery, each fort was under the charge of three people of equal level. Which of the statement(s) above is/are true? Consider the following statements about Shivaji's strategic policy : (1) Forts were important factors in Shivaji's strategic system.
questions.explanation: Under Shivaji's strategic policy, forts were important factors. Shivaji had about 250 forts. Each fort was kept under triple control. It included one Brahmin, one Maratha and one Kunbi. The Brahmin looked after civil and revenue administration and the remaining two looked after military management and supply management. Although some historians have also described this system as a means to prevent treachery

questions.question_text: Among the four southern provinces of Shivaji's state, the provincial governor of one province was:
questions.explanation: In Shivaji's administrative system, a provincial governor was appointed in each province. Each provincial governor had his own council of ministers. He had divided his state into three provinces Northern Province – Nasik to Pune – Trimbak Pingle (Governor) Southern Province – Northern Karnataka region – Annaji Datto (Governor) Southern-Eastern Province (Southern part of Shivaji's state) – Satara to Dharwad (up to Koppal) – Dattaji Pant (Governor)

questions.question_text: Shivaji's first clash with the Mughals happened in 1657. At that time who was the Governor of the southern Mughal empire?
questions.explanation: In 1657 AD, at the time of the first clash between Shivaji and the Mughals, Aurangzeb was the Subahdar of the South, but due to Shah Jahan becoming ill on 6 September 1657 AD, due to the war of succession, Aurangzeb could not take any action on this. Ultimately, in 1659 AD, he appointed his maternal uncle Shaista Khan as the Subahdar of the South and handed him the task of stopping Shivaji's expansion

questions.question_text: By whom was the title of 'Raja' given to Chhatrasal?
questions.explanation: Chhatrasal (1649-1731) was a great valiant warrior of the medieval period of India, who after defeating the Mughal ruler Aurangzeb in war, established his own state in Bundelkhand. In 1705 AD, Chhatrasal made a treaty with Aurangzeb. Ultimately, Chhatrasal was given a mansab of 4000 and the title of 'Raja'

questions.question_text: Who among the following was handed the work of supplying rations to the Maratha army during the third battle of Panipat?
questions.explanation: The third battle of Panipat took place on 14 January 1761 between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali. In this battle, the Marathas were completely defeated. In the third battle of Panipat, the work of Maratha army ration was in the hands of Govind Ballal Kher

questions.question_text: Which European traveler described the Bahmani kingdom?
questions.explanation: Nikitin was a famous Russian merchant and traveler who toured the Bahmani kingdom of the south between 1470-1474. According to him, the condition of ordinary humans in the south was very miserable. There was a very big gap between the nobles and the poor. While the ruling class and nobles were living a luxurious life. He also lived in Bidar state for some time. He came during the time of Muhammad III

questions.question_text: In 1568, after defeating which king did the Mughal army take control of Chittor?
questions.explanation: In 1568 AD, at the time of Akbar's attack on Chittor, Maharana Uday Singh ruled there. Akbar's army defeated the 8000 Rajputs led by Jaimal and Patta and 40 thousand farmers in the Chittorgarh fort. On this occasion, Akbar issued a 'Fatehnama'

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding Chauth?

options.A: Chauth was a source of income for Maratha rulers.
options.B: Shivaji used to collect Chauth from neighboring states.
options.C: It was 1/4 part of the state's income.
options.D: It was collected by Shivaji from his own people too.

questions.explanation: Chauth was a major source of income for Maratha rulers, which was collected from neighboring states in return for providing protection. It was 1/4 part of the state's income. Chauth was not collected from his own state's people. 'Sardeshmukhi' was also a source of Maratha income

questions.question_text: In which year did Shivaji defeat Shaista Khan?
questions.explanation: Shivaji defeated Shaista Khan in 1663 AD. Aurangzeb appointed Shaista Khan as the Subahdar of the South with the objective of keeping control over Shivaji. In this sequence, in 1663 AD, Shivaji attacked him at night and defeated him

questions.question_text: Harihar and Bukka belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara empire (1336-1652 AD) was an empire of the medieval period. Its establishment was done by two brothers named Harihar and Bukka, who belonged to the Sangama dynasty of Vijayanagara. Portuguese knew this empire by the name 'Bisnaga state' Dynasties of Vijayanagara- Sangama Dynasty - 1336-1485 - Harihar I and Bukka Saluva Dynasty - 1485-1505 - Narasimha Saluva Tuluva Dynasty - 1505-1570 - Vir Narasimha Aravidu Dynasty - 1570-1652 - Tirumala

questions.question_text: During which Maratha Peshwa's reign did the third battle of Panipat take place?
questions.explanation: Balaji Bajirao is also known by the name Nana Saheb. During his reign, the Maratha empire reached its zenith. In 1740, the Chhatrapati appointed him his Peshwa. In his time, in 1761 AD, the Marathas suffered a decisive defeat in the third battle of Panipat

questions.question_text: Which Bahmani ruler laid the foundation of the famous city Firozabad for plan and architecture?
questions.explanation: In South India, the foundation of the Bahmani kingdom was laid in 1347 AD by Hasan Gangu. At this time, the Sultan of Delhi was Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq, the most learned ruler of the Bahmani dynasty was Tajuddin Firoz Shah (1397–1422 AD), who laid the foundation of Firozabad city on the banks of the Bhima river. He built an observatory in Daulatabad. His reign became tainted due to conflict with Saint Gesu Daraz

questions.question_text: Shivaji's revenue policy was influenced by:
questions.explanation: Shivaji's revenue system was adopted by Malik Ambar in Ahmednagar state, which was based on the Ryotwari system. Malik Ambar was an Abyssinian slave, who after getting freedom from slavery became the Wazir of Ahmednagar

questions.question_text: The classical age of Telugu literature was during which king's reign?
questions.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya's (1509-1529) reign is called the classical age of Telugu literature. There were eight great Telugu scholars in his court, among whom Peddana was prominent, who was a scholar of both Sanskrit and Telugu languages. Krishnadeva Raya himself was a scholar. He authored 'Amuktamalyada' (book on politics) and also composed 'Jambavatikalyanam' and 'Ushaparinayam' in Sanskrit language

questions.question_text: Which states did the Tungabhadra river provide support (food) to?
questions.explanation: For Vijayanagara situated on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra river, this river was helpful in the commercial and agricultural activities there, whereas the Chola empire was situated on the bank of the Kaveri river

questions.question_text: Who among the following is called the pioneer of guerrilla warfare in the Deccan region?
questions.explanation: The pioneer of guerrilla warfare in the Deccan region was Malik Ambar. The successful use of this policy was first done by Chhatrapati Shivaji against the Mughals. After this, Bajirao I took it to the peak

questions.question_text: Ashtapradhan, who helped in the administration of Shivaji's Maratha empire, in the context of which were the in-charges of central administration?
questions.explanation: Peshwa was a Persian word, which Shivaji gave the name 'Chief Prime' or Prime Minister. At the time of state establishment, Ramchandra Pant Amatya or Ramchandra Neelkanth Bawdekar was the Prime Minister. Later Moropant Trimbak Pingle became the Prime Minister. In the context of Ashtapradhan who helped in the administration of Shivaji's Maratha empire, the in-charge of central administration was Moropant Trimbak Pingle. He was the first Peshwa of the Maratha empire. Shivaji's administrative system was mostly influenced by the administrative system of southern states and Mughals

questions.question_text: What was 'Jamindari system' under the Marathas called?
questions.explanation: Mirasidar (Jamindar) - Were those cultivators who had their own land and had rights over the means of production (plough, oxen etc.). Their land was probably tax-exempt. Although Shivaji placed strict control over them Mokasa - Land grant given to officers, later called Jagir. Deshmukhi or Sardeshmukhi - Area under Marathas which had to pay 10% tax. Ashtapradhan - Group of 8 ministers as advisors to Shivaji.

questions.question_text: Which Bahmani Sultan shifted his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
questions.explanation: The dynasty established by Bahman Shah in the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq was called the Bahmani dynasty. The limits of the Bahmani empire extended from Berar in the north to Krishna river in the south. The major ruler of this dynasty was Shihabuddin Ahmad Shah I (1422–1436 AD). He shifted his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar in 1425 AD. Which was named Muhammadabad

questions.question_text: Which Peshwa has been described as the "greatest exponent of guerrilla warfare" after Shivaji?
questions.explanation: The Peshwas have a distinct role in the rise of the Maratha empire. After the death of Balaji Vishwanath in 1720 AD, Bajirao I (1720-1740) AD became Peshwa. He is remembered as the fighting Peshwa. After Shivaji, Bajirao I was the greatest exponent of the guerrilla warfare system. Shahu called Bajirao I the worthy son of a worthy father. Bajirao I kept the ideal of Hindu Pad Padshahi

questions.question_text: Which ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire recruited Muslims into the army on a large scale?
questions.explanation: Deva Raya II ruled Vijayanagara from 1422-1446 AD. Deva Raya II was so influenced by the Muslim cavalry army that he decided to recruit Muslim horsemen into his army too. He was the one called Praudha Deva Raya

questions.question_text: Which foreign traveler visiting the Vijayanagara Empire wrote that "the king of this empire is more powerful than all other kings of India?"
questions.explanation: Nicolo Conti, a resident of Italy, visited the Vijayanagara empire during the reign of Deva Raya I. He described his travel in a book named 'Travels of Nicolo Conti'. He went beyond India to Southeast Asia and China

questions.question_text: Which Bahmani ruler, who was a great patron of art, built a magnificent madrasa or seat of learning in the capital Bidar?
questions.explanation: Mahmud Gawan was the Prime Minister during the reign of Bahmani ruler Muhammad III. He was given the title of Khwaja Jahan. He was a possessor of literary and cultural taste. In the capital Bidar, he established a seat of learning or college

questions.question_text: Assertion (A) : From the time of Firoz Shah Bahmani, Deccani Hindus came into prominent roles in the Bahmani administration. Reason (R) : Firoz Shah Bahmani included Hindus in his administration on a large scale. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following statement is true?

options.D: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.E: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Bahmani encouraged foreign immigrants or Afaqis to come and settle in the Bahmani empire. As a result of this, the Bahmani Amirs class got divided into two groups, Afaqi and Deccani. They included Hindus in his administration on a large scale. Due to which Deccani Hindus started playing an important role in the administration. He built an observatory in Daulatabad. His rule became tainted due to conflict with Saint Gesu Daraz

questions.question_text: Assertion (A) : For three separate and distinct areas Tungabhadra Doab, Krishna-Godavari Delta, Marathwada, Vijayanagara and Bahmani rulers' interests collided with each other. Reason (R) : Due to its wealth and economic resources, this had been a cause of dispute for a long time in the past. In the context of both the above statements, which of the following statement is true?

options.D: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.E: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: There was a dispute between Vijayanagara Empire and Bahmani rulers regarding Krishna-Godavari Delta, Tungabhadra Doab region because this region was special mainly due to wealth and economic resources. Both empires wanted to make themselves strong by winning this region, due to which continuous struggle remained between these two

questions.question_text: Ferishta writes- "There was good settlement in their country and the people were dedicated to his authority. The merchants of Malabar, Ceylon and other countries had kept ambassadors in his court and sent expensive gifts every year." Identify this ruler of Vijayanagara:
questions.explanation: "Ferishta" was the author of the famous work of medieval India "Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi. He had the patronage of the ruler of Bijapur state Ibrahim II. During his reign, Ferishta authored Tarikh-i-Ferishta. The above statement has been quoted by Ferishta in the context of Bukka First (1356-77)

questions.question_text: Which ruler of Vijayanagara Empire, Krishnadeva Raya, did give patronage?
questions.explanation: Vallabhacharya was born in 1479 AD in Kashi (Varanasi), his parents were coming on a trip from Telangana to Kashi when he was born on the travel route. During the time of Krishnadeva Raya, he established the Vaishnava sect. He believed in Shuddhadvaita. The Vijayanagara emperor adorned him with the title of Jagadguru Mahaprabhu Shrimadacharya

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called statement (A) and other is called reason (R) ~ Read the statements and select the correct answer using the code given below~ Statement (A) : The middle of the 14th century was witness to the independence of Ma'bar and Bengal and the establishment of the Vijayanagara empire and Bahmani sultanate. Reason (R) : Muhammad Tughlaq became soft towards the regional powers in the last years of his reign and he granted them more autonomy. Code :

options.A: (A) and (R) are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: In the beginning of the 14th century, the Sultanate saw maximum expansion but by the middle of the century, its disintegration started. Its beginning started from Madurai (Ma'bar). Where Jalaluddin Ahsan Khan established independent power in 1333-34 AD. Bengal became independent from it in 1338 AD. Whereas the establishment of Vijayanagara and Bahmani provincial dynasties happened in 1336 and 1347 AD respectively. Whereas Muhammad bin Tughlaq spent his last years of reign in suppressing continuous rebellions, therefore, he was clearly strict towards regional autonomy. Hence: (A) is true, but (R) is false

questions.question_text: Where and when did Shivaji's coronation take place?
questions.explanation: Shivaji was born on 20 April 1627 AD in the fort of Shivneri near Pune. His father's name was Shahji Bhonsle and mother's name was Jijabai. In June 1674 AD, Shivaji had his coronation done by the famous scholar of Kashi, Gangabhatt, in Raigad and assumed the title of Chhatrapati. Shivaji gave help to Bijapur against the Mughals in his last time. On 12 April 1680 AD, Shivaji died

questions.question_text: In which language did the ruler of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya, compose his famous work Amuktamalyada?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 M.P. Asst. Prof. 2017 UPPSC Indian History 2002, 2003, 2008 Explanation – The reign of the best ruler of the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya, was till 1509-1529 AD. A circle of eight poets lived in his court which was called Ashtadiggaja. Krishnadeva Raya himself was a scholar. He had composed `Amuktamalyada` in Telugu language and assumed the title of 'Yavana Sthapanacharya'. Babur in his autobiography called Krishnadeva Raya the most powerful ruler of India.

questions.question_text: Who was the Muslim military commander who died fighting from the side of the Marathas in the third battle of Panipat –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – On 14 January, 1761, the third battle of Panipat took place between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas. In this battle, the Marathas were defeated. In this battle, Ibrahim Khan Gardi's heavy artillery did not prove useful; on the other hand, Abdali's revolving guns kept on camels destroyed the Marathas. In this battle, great commanders of the Marathas like Dattaji, Tukoji Scindia, Ibrahim Gardi, Sadashiv Rao Bhau died. At this time, the Maratha ruler was Balaji Bajirao who died a few days after the war.

questions.question_text: 'Bakhar' is –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – In the Maratha empire, descriptive means of history composition were called 'Bakhar'. These are considered valuable resources for depicting the history of the Maratha region. Some common Bakhars are- Sabhasad, Mahikavatichi, Kalmi, Chitnis, etc.

questions.question_text: Which condition was responsible for the establishment of the Bahmani empire among the following–

options.A: Disintegration of the Chalukya empire of Kalyani
options.B: Chain of rebellions against Tughlaq rule in the Deccan
options.C: Military support and encouragement received from Delhi Sultans

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Due to the rebellion of 'Amiran-i-Sada' of the Deccan, the Bahmani empire was established in the last days of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign. A commander named Hasan (Zafar Khan 1347-1358 AD) assumed the title of Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah and sat on the throne in 1347 AD and laid the foundation of the Bahmani empire. Gulbarga was made the capital and its name was changed to Ahsanabad.

questions.question_text: Who were the Afaqi people in the Bahmani empire?

options.A: Immigrant Muslims from Iran, Iraq, Turkic and Arab countries
options.B: Foreign merchants living in the Bahmani empire
options.C: South Indians accepting the Islamic religion
options.D: Shia nobles of the Bahmani court

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- With the arrival of the Afaqis, foreign influence, especially Persian, increased on Bahmani rule and culture. In this way, mixed influence of foreigners, Deccanis, and Hindus fell on the Bahmani empire during this era. But there was growth in enmity between these two classes i.e. Deccanis and Afaqis (Iranians, Arabs, and Turks) to the extent that it became the main cause of the destruction of the Bahmani empire.

questions.question_text: In which language did Sayana write his commentary on the Vedas?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– Sayana wrote his commentary on the Vedas in Sanskrit language. Throughout South India, the language of the elite class was Sanskrit. Among the common people, there was propagation of local Telugu, Kannada and Tamil. During the time of Bukka I, special progress took place in the study and teaching of Vedic literature (Sanskrit). During his time, scholars like Madhavacharya Vidyaranya and his brother Sayana prepared interpretations (commentaries) independently on Vedic texts.

questions.question_text: Who established the Vijayanagara state?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– In 1336 AD, the credit for establishing the Vijayanagara state on the south-western coast of India goes to two brothers named Harihar and Bukka. The first ruler of Vijayanagara was Harihar First who ruled from 1336-1356 AD. His initial capital was Anegondi and later became Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: Which Muslim traveler came to the Vijayanagara court?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 PGT 2004, 2010 Explanation– Abdur Razzaq was a Persian traveler who came as an ambassador of Shahrukh to the Zamorin of Calicut. Abdur Razzaq also visited Vijayanagara in April 1443 during the reign of Deva Raya II. Amazed by the wonderful form and splendor of Vijayanagara city, he wrote in his travel account Matla-us-Sadain wa Majma-ul-Bahrain, I have not seen another city like Vijayanagara in the whole world, nor heard of one. It is built in such a way that there are seven fortresses inside one another.

questions.question_text: What was the group of twelve officials in the Vijayanagara empire, who used to look after the affairs of the villages, called–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– Like the Nayakara system, the Ayangar system was also a very important feature of the Vijayanagara period administration system. Under this system, twelve people were appointed for administration at the village administrative unit level. This group of twelve administrative officials was called 'Ayangar'.

questions.question_text: The main rivals of the Vijayanagara state of South India were.........Sultans–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Harihar and Bukka established Vijayanagara in 1336 AD. Whereas the Bahmani state was established in 1347 AD by Hasan Gangu. The dispute between these two states regarding the Krishna-Tungabhadra Doab continued for many years. The main rivals of Vijayanagara were the rulers of the Bahmani state.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Muslim states of the South first trained the Marathas for guerrilla warfare?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Malik Ambar was the Wazir of Ahmednagar state. To face the Mughal attack, he recruited Marathas into his army and trained them in guerrilla warfare (guerrilla warfare method). The benefit of this warfare method was later taken by Shivaji and he established the Maratha empire. Due to the extensive use of this method by Shivaji, he is considered the father of guerrilla method.

questions.question_text: Which of the following provinces was not included in the Bahmani kingdom –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – In the given options, Doab was not included in the Bahmani kingdom because Doab was an important fertile land region, regarding the control of which continuous struggle used to take place between the Bahmani and Vijayanagara empires and eventually the control of Doab went to Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: Shivaji's capital was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The founder of the Maratha empire was Shivaji. He was born in 1627 AD in Shivneri fort (near Junnar). His guru was Kondadev. Under his military campaign, in 1646 AD, Shivaji first captured the hill fort named Torna of Bijapur principality. In 1674 AD, Shivaji made Raigad (Rayari) his capital.

questions.question_text: A feature of Shivaji's council of ministers 'Ashtapradhan' was –

options.B: Seven of his ministers were Brahmins
options.C: Only one of his ministers was a Brahmin
options.D: There was no caste restriction in it

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – An important feature of the Ashtapradhan in Shivaji's council of ministers was that seven of his ministers were Brahmins. Each minister of this council was the head of his department. Which was appointed by Shivaji. Apart from Nyayadhish and Panditrao, all others had to lead the armies when needed.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select your answer from the code given below– List-I List-II
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The matched code is as follows – A. Sadashiva – Battle of Talikota B. Sangama Dynasty – Deva Raya I C. Ramaraya – Aravidu Dynasty D. Amuktamalyada – Krishnadeva Raya

questions.question_text: After the death of Rajaram, his widow Tarabai ruled in the name of whom?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – After the death of Rajaram, his widow Tarabai ruled in the name of her minor son Shivaji II and she won forts like Raigad, Satara, and Sinhagad from the Mughals.

questions.question_text: Why did Raja Jai Singh besiege the fort of Purandar?

options.C: It was surrounded by Mughal territory
options.D: It was situated in the middle of Shivaji's territories and his family and treasury were kept there

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Raja Jai Singh besieged the fort of Purandar in 1665 AD because that area was situated in the middle of Shivaji's borders and his family and treasury were kept there.

questions.question_text: What were the important reasons for the rise of the Marathas among the following?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Important reasons for the rise of the Marathas included the geographical situation of Maharashtra, contemporary religious movement and Shivaji's fighting personality.

questions.question_text: Who was the ruler of the Vijayanagara empire at the time of Babur's invasion?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– At the time of Babur's invasion (1526 AD), the ruler of Vijayanagara was Krishnadeva Raya. According to Tuzuk-i-Babari (Babur's autobiography), Krishnadeva Raya was the most powerful among the contemporary Hindu rulers. Krishnadeva Raya ruled from 1509-1529 AD.

questions.question_text: Who were the 'Ashtadiggaja' in the court of Krishnadeva Raya?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– The reign of the great ruler of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya, is also called the classical age of Telugu literature because there were 'Ashtadiggajas' in his court. These Ashtadiggajas were the eight best poets of Telugu literature. He himself was a high-class scholar.

questions.question_text: Based on available sources, Shivaji's rise can be tracked from–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Based on available sources, Shivaji's rise can be considered from the year 1644. Shivaji first captured the fort of Sinhagad in 1643 AD, followed by which in 1646 AD at the age of 19, he captured the Torna fort of Bijapur principality.

questions.question_text: In the third battle of Panipat, from whom did the Marathas successfully obtain temporary help?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– In the third battle of Panipat, no regional power provided help to the Marathas. The third battle of Panipat was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas in 1761 AD.

questions.question_text: The founder of the Bahmani kingdom in the south was–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 PGT 2010 Explanation– The beginning of the Bahmani state and dynasty in the south was done in 1347 by an officer of Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Hasan (alias Zafar Khan). Hasan considered himself a descendant of the Persian heroic warrior Bahman, hence his dynasty came to be called Bahmani. After sitting on the throne, Hasan assumed the title of Alauddin Bahman Shah and made his capital in Gulbarga or Gulbarga.

questions.question_text: Match the states of List-I with the founders of List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below~ List-I (State) List-II (Founder)
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Khandesh-Faruqi Dynasty, Berar-Imadshahi Dynasty, Bijapur-Adilshahi Dynasty; Golconda-Qutbshahi Dynasty; Bidar-Baridshahi Dynasty.

questions.question_text: The founder of Maratha power, Shivaji, was born in–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– The founder of Maratha power, Shivaji, was born on 20 April 1627 AD in Shivner fort. His father was Shahji Bhonsle and mother was Jijabai. His guardians were Dadaji Kondadev and Guru Samarth Ramdas.

questions.question_text: Maratha Chhatrapati Shivaji's first clash with the Mughal army happened–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– After the conquest of Junnar by Chhatrapati Shivaji, in 1657 AD, his first encounter with Aurangzeb's army took place when he attacked Ahmednagar, in which Shivaji's Maratha army had to retreat. In this, Shivaji fought from the side of the Mughals, Bijapur's Adil Shah.

questions.question_text: What was the main duty of Amatya or Majumdar in Maratha administration–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– In Maratha administration, Ashtapradhan system was done, in which Amatya or Majumdar was the state's Finance Minister. His main duty was to look after the state's income and expenditure and to keep an eye on revenue administration. Shivaji's finance minister was Ramchandra Pant.

questions.question_text: Krishnadeva Raya of Vijayanagara's court poet was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Krishnadeva Raya himself was a great scholar and poet. He wrote a poem named ‘Amuktamalyada’ in Telugu language. Many litterateurs got patronage in his court. In which Telugu poet Allasani Peddana (Allasani Peddanna) was the court poet.

questions.question_text: The founder of Bidar was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Barid Shahi dynasty of Bidar was established by Amir Ali Barid in 1527 AD. He is also known by the name 'Fox of the Deccan'.

questions.question_text: Nicolo Conti, a traveler who came to Vijayanagara, was a resident of where?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – During the reign of Sangama Dynasty ruler Deva Raya I (1406-22), Italian traveler Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara in 1420 AD. In the court of Deva Raya I, famous Telugu poet Srinatha, author of Harivilasa and other books, was present.

questions.question_text: Abdur Razzaq was a traveler –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Persian ambassador Abdur Razzaq came to Vijayanagara in 1443 AD during the reign of Sangama Dynasty ruler Deva Raya II (1422 to 1446). He considers Vijayanagara one of the most magnificent cities in the world.

questions.question_text: Vijayanagara was situated on the bank of which river?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001, 2011 Explanation – Vijayanagara is situated on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra river. The establishment of the Vijayanagara empire was done by Harihar and Bukka, among the five sons of Sangama.

questions.question_text: Which of the following goods were exported in large quantities in the Vijayanagara empire?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002, 2008 Explanation– Black pepper was exported in large quantities in Vijayanagara. Cloth, rice, iron, sugar, sugar were other major goods of export.

questions.question_text: The battle of Talikota took place –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– On 23 January 1565, the battle of Talikota took place between Vijayanagara and the Muslim confederacy, in which Vijayanagara was defeated. This war is also called the battle of Rakshasa-Tangadi. As far as the confederacy is concerned, it included Bijapur, Golconda, Bidar and Ahmednagar. These five Muslim states were formed from the fragments of the Bahmani state. Berar did not take part in this war.

questions.question_text: Match the states of List-I with the founders of List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below the lists – List-I List-II A. Bidar (i) Yusuf Adil Shah B. Ahmednagar (ii) Quli Qutb Shah C. Bijapur (iii) Amir Ali Barid D. Golconda (iv) Malik Ahmed A B C D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– Bidar state was established by Amir Ali Barid in 1527 AD, he was of the Barid Shahi dynasty. Ahmednagar state was established by Malik Ahmed in 1490 AD, he was of the Nizam Shahi dynasty. Bijapur state was established by Yusuf Adil Shah in 1489-90 AD, he was of the Adil Shahi dynasty. Golconda state was established by Quli Qutb Shah in 1512 AD or 1518 AD, he was the ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty.

questions.question_text: Which Vijayanagara ruler agreed to marry his daughter to the Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah after being defeated by him?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Historian Ferishta writes that after being defeated by Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah, the Vijayanagara ruler Devaraya I agreed to marry his daughter to the Bahmani Sultan to establish peace between Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis. As a dowry, he gave the Raichur Doab area and Bankapur. Additionally, he also paid a penalty of 10 lakhs in the form of pearls and elephants.

questions.question_text: What was land revenue called in the Vijayanagara Empire:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Sidda was the land tax which was the main source of income for the Vijayanagara state. Whereas Athvana was the central revenue department. Bhoga and Uparikar were a part of the gifts given by the people. The state used to collect 1/6th part of the produce as land tax.

questions.question_text: What did Krishnadevaraya do?

options.C: Sent an army to Sri Lanka

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Krishnadevaraya was a great ruler of the Tuluva dynasty. His reign was from 1509 to 1529 AD. In 1513 AD, he attacked the ruler of Odisha, Gajapati Pratap Rudra, and captured the Udayagiri fort. In 1520 AD, he defeated Bijapur and captured the entire Raichur Doab.

questions.question_text: That Maratha diplomat whose death also marked the end of the Maratha government's intellect and restraint was:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Nana Phadnavis was the most intelligent person who returned alive from the Third Battle of Panipat. Upon his death in 1800 AD, an English writer rightly wrote that "with the death of Phadnavis, all the capability, cleverness, and wisdom of the Marathas ended."

questions.question_text: In the time of Shivaji, the land revenue rate was likely, of the produce:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation – Accepting the revenue system of Malik Ambar prevalent in the South as a model, Shivaji fixed his land revenue with some changes. Initially, it was 1/3rd of the produce, but due to rising military expenses, it was increased to 2/5th, i.e., 40%, some time later.

questions.question_text: Which ruler of Vijayanagara started the policy of appointing Muslims in his army?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 PGT History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – Devaraya II (1422–1446 AD) was a great ruler of the Sangama dynasty of Vijayanagara. His reign is an indicator of the peak of the glory and prosperity of the Sangam-era Vijayanagara Empire. To make his army powerful and to be on par with the Bahmanis, he started the tradition of recruiting Muslims into the army and granted them jagirs.

questions.question_text: Whose claim is it that Shivaji's Swarajya was merely a replica of Watan?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation – English historian Andre Wink has claimed that Shivaji's Swarajya was merely a replica of Watan. In the end, Smith also added that Shivaji's state was a robber state.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) – Assertion (A): Aurangzeb's administration was not decorated in the context of military perspective. Reason (R): He could not bring the Marathas under control. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements? Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation – From a military perspective, Aurangzeb's administration was an organized administration which included many classes. However, despite many efforts, he remained unsuccessful in controlling the Marathas.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below – (List-I) (List-II) (Names of departments (Post of the head under Shivaji's rule) of the department)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation – (a) Department related to royal family and court affairs - Mantri, (b) Department related to foreign affairs - Sumant, (c) Department related to royal correspondence - Sachiv, (d) Finance department - Amatya.

questions.question_text: Which eight great poets of Telugu literature were in the court?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Krishnadevaraya's reign is considered the classical age of Telugu literature. His court was graced by eight great scholars and poets of Telugu. They were also called Ashtadiggaja.

questions.question_text: 'In the country, mostly there are good agricultural holdings and the land is very fertile, the military number is about eleven lakhs.' Whose statement is the above regarding the Vijayanagara state?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation – Abdur Razzaq, who was an ambassador from Iran. In 1443 AD, during the reign of Devaraya II, he visited the Vijayanagara Empire and while praising Vijayanagara, he said that "In the country, mostly there are good agricultural holdings and the land is very fertile, the military number is about 11 lakhs."

questions.question_text: The claim of revenue of the Marathas for protection is called–
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Chauth was mainly one-fourth of the income of the suzerain lands of the Mughal areas and neighboring states, which was taken by the Marathas in return for protection from looting. Whereas Shivaji collected Sardeshmukhi because he considered himself the hereditary Sardeshmukh of Maharashtra. This tax was 1/10th of the income of the states.

questions.question_text: What is the literal meaning of Amuktamalyada of Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya–
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – The literal meaning of the book Amuktamalyada, written in Telugu by Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya, is 'garland of pearls'. It is a discussion of political thoughts and administrative policies.

questions.question_text: Regarding the Marathas, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Shivaji had demanded the Deshmukhi of Junnar and Ahmednagar parganas, regarding which Prince Murad, who was the governor of the Deccan, promised to try and ensure it after appearing before the Emperor.
options.B: In a 1644 farman, it was said that Shahji had been removed from the court due to the rebellious activities of his representative (agent) Dadaji Kondadev in Kondana.
options.C: Maval infantry soldiers had become a powerful part of Prince Murad's army from the Deccan.
options.D: Shivaji had won Javli from Maratha chief Chandra Rao More in 1656.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – Maval infantry soldiers had become a powerful part of Prince Murad's army from the Deccan. Among the four options given, this is not correct.

questions.question_text: The Nayankara system of the Vijayanagara Empire was based on which of the following?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation – The 'Nayankara system' of the Vijayanagara Empire was based on the Sultanate-era Iqta system. In the Vijayanagara Empire, land areas were granted to military and civil officers in return for special services. Which were called 'Amaram'. The one receiving tax from Amaram was called 'Amar Nayaka'. Although there were many differences in these, such as the Iqta system was not hereditary, whereas the posts of Nayakas gradually became hereditary.

questions.question_text: Regarding the Marathas, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Within his own state (Swarajya), Shivaji attempted to prepare his administration on the model of the Deccani Sultanates. In this, the taxes were very light (less).
options.B: With the death of Shivaji, the politics established by him suffered a momentary collapse because Aurangzeb imprisoned and got his son Sambhaji executed.
options.C: The Marathas, by strictly collecting Chauth, expanded their economic resources.
options.D: From 1681, Aurangzeb stayed in the Deccan continuously.

questions.explanation: Explanation – Shivaji's Swarajya (which English writers had termed a petty state) was mainly divided into three areas – (a) Northern province – the part from Supe to Pune, (b) area from Southern Konkan to Northern Kanara, and (c) the area from Satara to Dharwad. In these areas, the tax burden was not less but was more. Shivaji's administration was influenced by Malik Ambar's administration.

questions.question_text: Which traveler mentioned the 'Sati practice prevalent in Vijayanagara' in his book –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – In the Vijayanagara Empire, Sati practice was called Sahagamana, i.e., great departure with the dead husband. Barbosa, Nuniz, Caesar Frederick, Pietro Della Valle, and other foreign travelers saw this practice as prevalent during their visit to Vijayanagara and mentioned it in their accounts. Additionally, in an inscription of Vijayanagara of 1354 AD, there is a mention of a woman named Mallagauda achieving heaven after performing Sati or Sahagamana after her husband's death.

questions.question_text: In whose reign did court poet Allasani Peddana compose 'Manu Charitra' which contains an interesting description of romance and passion, and in this, Arabic and Persian words have been used freely?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation – Krishnadevaraya freed Telugu from the influence of Sanskrit and paved the way for independent Telugu creations called Prabandhas. In his court, there were 'eight great poets of Telugu' which included Peddana. Peddana composed Manucharitram in which there is an interesting description of romance and passion. Peddana had received the title of Grandfather of Telugu Poetry and Grandfather of Andhra Poetry.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) : Assertion (A): The political history of the Vijayanagara Empire is a history of changes of different dynasties and internal wars. Reason (R): Bahmani Sultanate and its successor states remained a serious threat to the Vijayanagara Empire. Read the above statements and select the correct answer from the code given below~

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct Explanation (continued)

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation – The political history of the Vijayanagara Empire is a history of changes of different dynasties and internal wars. Bahmani Sultanate and its successor states remained a serious threat to the Vijayanagara Empire, both statement and reason are correct. The reason is not the correct explanation of the statement.

questions.question_text: The synonym of the Maratha vocabulary 'Deshmukh' in North India is:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation – In the administration of the Marathas, the head of the district used to be Deshmukh or Deshpande. They worked as controllers over the Mamlatdar. The synonym of Deshmukh in North India was Chaudhari. He was the main official of the village who was called Khut, Mukaddam, or Chaudhari.

questions.question_text: Who got the Atala Mosque built in Jaunpur:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation – The construction of Atala Mosque was started by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Ibrahim Shah Sharqi completed it in 1408 AD. This mosque presents a beautiful example of the Hindu-Muslim architectural style. Inside the mosque, there is a square courtyard whose diameter is 177 feet.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the help of the codes given below. In List-I, there are provincial states and in List-II, there is the period of their peak power. (List-I) (List-II)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – The correct matches are as follows– List-I List-II (Provincial states) (Peak period) Nizam Shahi state 1489-1636 AD Qutb Shahi state 1512-1687 AD Adil Shahi state 1489-1686 AD Maratha state From the middle of the seventeenth century

questions.question_text: "The Vijayanagara state was glorified as the protector of Hindu, Varnashrama Dharma against Islam, but its primary enemies were Hindu kings-maharajas themselves, and inside the city, a 'Turushka' dwelling, a mosque, and a Muslim tomb were built. In its grand architecture, military organization, and urban manner, it looked like a Muslim capital instead of a Hindu one in many ways." Whose excerpt is this?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – "The Vijayanagara state was glorified as the protector of Hindu, Varnashrama Dharma against Islam, but its primary enemies were Hindu kings-maharajas themselves, and inside the city, a 'Turushka' dwelling, a mosque, and a Muslim tomb were built. In its grand architecture, military-organization, and urban manner, it looked like a Muslim capital instead of a Hindu one in many ways." This statement is of Burton Stein.

questions.question_text: Under whose influence did Harihara and Bukka establish the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – The credit for establishing the Vijayanagara state on the southwestern coast of India goes to two brothers named Harihara and Bukka. They were ministers in the Kampili state. When Muhammad Tughlaq conquered Kampili, Harihara and Bukka were caught and taken to Delhi and they were made Muslims. On the occasion of a rebellion in Kampili, Muhammad Tughlaq sent them there to establish the power of Delhi. They were not successful in that task and in the end, under the influence of a saint, Vidyaranya, they became ready to become Hindus again from Muslims. Vidyaranya persuaded his guru and head of Sringeri, Vidyatirtha, to make them Hindus, and they became Hindus. In 1336, Harihara and Bukka established the new city of Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal commander forced Shivaji to sign the Treaty of Purandar (1665 AD)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 TGT 2003 Explanation – In 1665 AD, Aurangzeb sent Raja Jai Singh against Shivaji. Raja Jai Singh was a capable commander and diplomat of his time. He was a scholar of Turkish, Persian, Urdu, and Rajasthani languages. During the reign of Shah Jahan, he had participated in every war of the Mughal Empire. After winning Raigad, Jai Singh surrounded Shivaji in the Purandar fort. Seeing no possibility of defending Purandar fort, Shivaji surrendered and went to meet Jai Singh without any conditions. In June 1665 AD, the Treaty of Purandar was signed. Within three months, Jai Singh's diplomacy and power forced Shivaji to accept the suzerainty of the Mughals. Shivaji suffered greatly from this attack and treaty.

questions.question_text: Where did Shivaji keep his naval fleet?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – Shivaji formed a massive naval fleet at Colaba for the protection of his trade and tax collection. Shivaji's navy had 400 ships of different types. This naval fleet was divided into two parts - Dariya-Sarangi and Mai Nayak. Each of these parts had a head. Shivaji's navy became a matter of concern for foreign traders, the Siddis of Janjira, and Aurangzeb. On many occasions, he took on Portuguese, Dutch, and English ships and succeeded in saving the Khanderi island from the combined attack of the Siddis and the English.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below– List-I List-II A. Chhatrapati Shahu 1. 1680-1689 AD B. Sambhaji 2. 1700-1707 AD C. Shivaji II 3. 1689-1700 AD D. Rajaram 4. 1707-1749 AD Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – Chronologically- Sambhaji - 1680–1689 AD Rajaram - 1689–1700 AD Shivaji-II - 1700–1707 AD Chhatrapati Shahu - 1707–1749 AD

questions.question_text: ‘‘Maratha expansion in Hindustan will take our victory flag from Krishna to Attock.’’ Which Maratha Peshwa presented this proposal?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – After Balaji Vishwanath, his son Baji Rao I (1720-1740 AD) was appointed Peshwa. He was a born leader and a judge of quality. He challenged Shahu in these words ‘‘The time has come that we should drive the foreigners out of India and earn eternal fame for Hindus. Let us strike at the trunk of this old tree, the branches will fall on their own. Through our efforts, the Maratha flag will start fluttering from the Krishna River to Attock.’’

questions.question_text: Which Maratha leader helped the Sayyid brothers in deposing the Mughal Emperor in 1719 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – In the politics for power, in 1713 Farrukhsiyar sat on the throne with the help of the Sayyid brothers (Husain Ali and Abdullah Khan). Soon, opposition arose between the two and the court once again became a center of conspiracies. Maratha Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath made a treaty with the Sayyid brothers in 1719 AD and set out for Delhi with Husain Ali along with 15000 soldiers. With the help of these soldiers, the Sayyid brothers removed Emperor Farrukhsiyar from the throne and the next emperor Rafi-ud-Darajat accepted this treaty. Sir Richard Temple termed this treaty the Magna Carta of the Maratha Empire.

questions.question_text: How many times did Ahmad Shah Abdali attack India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Ahmad Shah Abdali attacked India about 7 times. He attacked a total of five times (between 1748 and 1759) during the time of North Mughal ruler Ahmad Shah. After that, he defeated the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 and his last attack on India was in 1767 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Maratha rulers did not sit on the throne despite being a king?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – After the death of Sambhaji, his step-brother Rajaram (1689-1700 AD) was declared king by the Maratha Council of Ministers. Rajaram's coronation took place at Raigad in February 1689 AD. Rajaram considered himself Shahu's representative and never sat on the throne.

questions.question_text: What type of grant was 'Mokasa'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – 'Mokasa' was a type of land-related grant. This grant became hereditary during the time of Rajaram and Shahu, which was given to the officials. They started being called 'Jagir'.

questions.question_text: On the ruins of which ancient Hindu empire was the Muslim empire Golconda built?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The Muslim empire Golconda was built on the ruins of the Warangal Hindu empire. Warangal was ruled by the Kakatiya dynasty.

questions.question_text: The dynasty established by Harihara and Bukka was known by the name of Sangama dynasty, because

options.A: It was inspired by the Sangam era
options.B: The capital of the new kingdom was on the confluence (Sangam) of Krishna and Tungabhadra
options.C: The new kingdom kept organizing a confluence (Sangam) of scholars
options.D: The name of the father of Harihara and Bukka was Sangama

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- In 1336 AD, Harihara and Bukka laid the foundation of Vijayanagara on the inspiration of Madhav Vidyaranya and commentator Sayana and declared their independence. Brothers Harihara and Bukka were sons of Sangama and they established their dynasty in the name of their father. Therefore, the first dynasty of Vijayanagara established in 1336 AD is called the Sangama dynasty.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Saluva dynasty?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The founder of the second dynasty of Vijayanagara was Saluva Narasimha. He first suppressed the revolts of the feudal rulers and rebel Nayakas of Vijayanagara. Narasimha Saluva captured the throne in 1485 AD. This has been termed 'First Usurpation' in the history of the state.

questions.question_text: What was the largest administrative division of the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The administrative division of the Vijayanagara state was as follows– Province - Rajya Mandalam - Commissionerate Kottama or Valanadu - District Nadu - Pargana or Tehsil Melagrama - Group of 50 villages Sthala and Seema - Group of some villages

questions.question_text: Which South Indian dance style emerged for the first time during the Vijayanagara rule?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The Indian dance style Yakshagana first came into existence in the Vijayanagara Empire. In the field of entertainment, drama and Yakshagana (in which acting was performed on stage through music and instruments) were very popular during this period. Acting was generally performed on special occasions. Both men and women took part in it. Vyomalata shadow plays were also very popular. Playing chess and dice was very popular. Krishnadevaraya himself was a big chess lover and he also gave sufficient encouragement to skilled chess players. Evidence of women and men of the aristocratic class gambling is also found.

questions.question_text: Under the Marathas, who had the responsibility of collecting land revenue?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Under the Maratha administration, the responsibility of collecting land revenue lay with the head of the village (Patel). The post of Patel was hereditary and transferable. Kulkarni prepared the details of land revenue. To determine the land revenue, careful classification was done keeping in mind the land's production and irrigation facilities, in which the village's Patil or Patel had a special role.

questions.question_text: After its downfall, the Bahmani Empire was divided into five parts, which of the following was not among them?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ After its downfall, the Bahmani Empire was divided into five parts─ 1. Adil Shahi state from Bijapur 2. Qutb Shahi state from Golconda 3. Nizam Shahi state from Ahmednagar 4. Barid Shahi state from Bidar 5. Imad Shahi state from Berar

questions.question_text: In the time of Shivaji's rule, what was the finance minister called?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 PGT History, 2013 Explanation- In Shivaji's administration, the King or Chhatrapati was the ultimate law-maker, administrative head, judge, and commander-in-chief. Although there were eight ministers named "Ashtapradhan" for consultation, who performed the work of administrative operations. 1. Peshwa or Chief Pradhan – Prime Minister. 2. Amatya or Majumdar – Finance and Revenue Minister. 3. Mantri or Waqianavis – Details of court activities (Home Minister). 4.
