Sachiv or Shurunavis – Royal correspondence and checking accounts of parganas. 5. Sumant or Dabir – Foreign Minister. 6. Senapati or Sar-i-Naubat – Recruitment, organization, rations, etc., of the army. 7. Panditrao – Responsibility for grants given for scholars and religious activities. 8. Nyayadhish – Chief Justice after the King. Military service was not mandatory for Panditrao and Nyayadhish. Seven of these ministers were Brahmins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kings of the Vijayanagara Empire was known as 'Andhra Bhoja'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation- Krishnadevaraya was a famous Tuluva dynasty ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire. Krishnadevaraya was not only a great warrior but in the history of Vijayanagara, he was the greatest military commander. Along with being a successful administrator, Krishnadevaraya was a great scholar, lover of learning, and patron of art. His reign is considered the 'classical age' of Telugu literature. His court was graced by eight great scholars of Telugu (who are called Ashtadiggaja). Therefore, he is also called 'Andhra Bhoja'. He has also written two Sanskrit poetic books in addition to 'Amuktamalyada'. He encouraged Sanskrit and other regional languages of South India in addition to Telugu.

questions.question_text: To which dynasty did Krishnadevaraya belong?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty. In 1509, after the death of Vira Narasimha Tuluva, Krishnadevaraya became the ruler of this dynasty.

questions.question_text: To which period did the famous commentator of Vedic literature, Sayana, belong?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The famous commentator of the Vedas, Sayana, belonged to the Vijayanagara state. He gave inspiration to Harihara and Bukka to establish the Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R)- Assertion (A): By 1750 AD, the Maratha state had become a confederacy under the leadership of the Peshwa. Reason (R): Shahu's successors did not have real power. Code:

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is correct but R is incorrect.
options.D: A is incorrect but R is correct.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The head of the Maratha Empire was the descendant of Shivaji, the Chhatrapati, who was the king of Satara. He used to make all appointments. However, the king's powers and prestige had decreased, especially since the Peshwa post became hereditary in Balaji Vishwanath's family. Under the leadership of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao (1740-1761 AD), the Maratha state had become a state confederacy and the real power was in the hands of the Peshwa. During the Peshwa's reign, Shahu's successors were only nominal Chhatrapatis. As long as Shahu lived, he ran both the state and the administration. Shahu's son remained only a nominal king. By the 1750 Sangola Treaty, the Peshwa himself became the real head of the state.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below under the list- List I List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The correct match is as follows– Pune - Peshwa Gwalior - Scindia Nagpur - Bhonsles Baroda - Gaekwad

questions.question_text: Who among the following has given a detailed description about the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Fernao Nuniz visited Vijayanagara in 1535–37 AD during the reign of Vijayanagara ruler Achyuta Devaraya. He has described the central secretariat, Nayankara system, etc., in Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: Who said, ‘‘We should attack the trunk of this rotten tree, the branches will fall on their own.’’

options.B: Baji Rao I (Peshwa) for the Mughal Empire
options.D: Clive for the Nawab of Bengal

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The aim of Peshwa Baji Rao I (1720-40) was to create a situation where different Maratha leaders would depend on each other and with that dependence, they would cooperate with each other. Baji Rao's other main objective was to establish a Maratha state in India on the ruins of the falling Mughal Empire. He said ‘‘We should attack the trunk of this rotten tree, the branches will fall on their own.’’ This policy was opposed by Shripati Rao, who was of the view that the Marathas should keep their power limited to South India only.

questions.question_text: The main objective of the establishment of the Vijayanagara state was-

options.A: To stop the expansion of the Tughlaq state in South India
options.B: To defeat and destroy the Bahmani state
options.C: To save Hindus from religious persecution
options.D: To establish a powerful Hindu state

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The establishment of the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 AD in South India is a great event in Indian history. The establishment of this powerful Hindu state was the result of a political and cultural movement against the Tughlaq power by two brothers named Harihara and Bukka. Hampi was the old capital of Vijayanagara. Its other capitals were - Anegundi, Vijayanagara, Penukonda, and Chandragiri.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Krishnadevaraya is not correct? Select your answer from the code given below- 1. He was the greatest among the kings of Vijayanagara. 2. Foreign travelers Ibn Battuta and Nicolo Conti came to his kingdom. 3. He was a scholar ruler and patron of art and literature. 4. He defeated the combined Muslim army in the Battle of Talikota. Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara in 1420-21 AD during the time of Devaraya I. The Battle of Talikota took place on 23 January 1565 AD between Rama Raya and the confederacy of Ahmednagar, Bijapur, Golconda, and Bidar states. Thus, code 2 and 4 are not correct regarding Krishnadevaraya. Code 1 and 3 are events related to Krishnadevaraya.

questions.question_text: Who was the foreign traveler who visited and described Vijayanagara after the defeat in the Talikota war?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – In 1565 AD, Bijapur, Ahmednagar, Golconda, and Bidar badly defeated Vijayanagara in the Battle of Talikota, which is also called the Battle of Rakshasa Tangadi or Bannihatti. After this war, a foreign traveler named Caesar Frederick visited Vijayanagara.

questions.question_text: On the construction of religious buildings in which of the following places did Ahilyabai spend a lot of money? 1. Rameshwar 2. Jagannath Puri 3. Dwarka 4. Kedarnath Select the correct answer from the code below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Holkar dynasty ruler Ahilyabai spent a lot of money on the construction of religious buildings in many places including Rameshwar, Jagannath Puri, Dwarka, and Kedarnath.

questions.question_text: The responsibility of the Maratha Navy under the Peshwas was handed over to a leader of extraordinary ability, whose name was -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Under the Peshwas, the responsibility of the Maratha Navy was handed over to a leader of extraordinary ability, Kanhoji Angre. In 1698 AD, Kanhoji took the responsibility of Naval Chief.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and use the codes given below the lists to select the correct answer List-I List-II A. Barbosa 1. Iranian B. Niccolo Conti 2. Italian C. Abdur Razzaq 3. Russian D. Nikitin 4. Portuguese Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Barbosa (1500-16) - He remained as a Portuguese official in India from 1500 to 1516. In 1502 he remained as a Portuguese agent in Cannanore and later worked as a translator for the Portuguese governor Albuquerque in India. He visited Vijayanagara during the time of Krishnadevaraya. Niccolo Conti : He was the first Italian traveler to come to Vijayanagara. He reached here in 1420-21 during the reign of Devaraya I. Abdur Razzaq : He was a Persian (Iranian) traveler who came as an ambassador of Shah Rukh to the Zamorin of Calicut. He also visited Vijayanagara in 1443 during the reign of Devaraya II. Nikitin (1470-74) : He was a Russian horse trader. He spent some years in South India and visited the Bahmani state in the reign of Muhammad III.

questions.question_text: Among the below mentioned Vijayanagara rulers, who was the first ruler to adopt the title of Maharajadhiraja?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- After the death of Bukka I, Harihara II became the next ruler of the Sangama dynasty in 1377 AD. He was the first ruler to adopt the title of 'Maharajadhiraja'. He was a great conqueror. He conquered Mysore, Kanara, Trichinopoly, Kanchipuram, etc. He was the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka. In his Vellore grant inscription, he has been called Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki, which is an indicator that along with being a scholar, he was also a patron of scholars.

questions.question_text: The first capital of the Vijayanagara Empire was Hampi. Where was its second capital?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- Harihara and Bukka established Vijayanagara in 1336 AD. Hampi was the first capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, later on, the Vijayanagara rulers made Penukonda their second capital.

questions.question_text: Regarding the 'Treaty of Purandar' (1665), which of the following is not true?

options.A: Shivaji had to give 23 out of 35 forts to the Mughals
options.B: Sambhaji had to appear in Mughal service
options.C: Sambhaji was granted a mansab of 5000
options.D: Shivaji did not have to cooperate with Mughal commanders in Southern campaigns.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb sent Jai Singh in 1665 against Maratha ruler Shivaji. Jai Singh forced the indomitable Shivaji to make the 'Purandar Treaty' on 22 June 1665. Under the terms of the treaty, Shivaji had to hand over 23 out of his 35 forts to the Mughals. Shivaji himself appearing in the Mughal court, helping the Mughals against Bijapur, and giving Sambhaji a five-thousand mansab in the Mughal court were the other conditions of the treaty. Thus, Shivaji cooperating with the Mughals in Southern campaigns (Bijapur, etc.) was included in the treaty. Therefore, option (d) will be the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List-I List-II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Abdur Razzaq (1443-44 AD) – Persian (Iran) traveler- In the reign of the Zamorin of Calicut and Devaraya-II of Vijayanagara. Niccolo Conti (1420–21 AD) – Italy – In the reign of Devaraya-I (Vijayanagara). Fernao Nuniz (1535-37 AD) – Portugal – Horse trader, in the reign of Achyuta Devaraya (Vijayanagara). Ibn Battuta (1333-47 AD) – Morocco (African) – In the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: What were districts called in the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Information about a total of six provinces is found in the Vijayanagara Empire. Provinces were called 'Mandalam'. Their heads were honored with titles like Amarnayaka, Dandanayaka, and Nayaka. Mandalam was divided into districts, which were called 'Kottama' or 'Valanadu'. Kottama was divided into 'Nadus' which are today called pargana or 'Taluka'. Nadus were divided into 'Melagramas'. The smallest unit of administration was 'Ur' or village. In this period, groups of some villages were also called Sthala and Seema.

questions.question_text: Under which Peshwa did Maratha power reach its peak?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- After the death of Baji Rao I, his son Balaji Baji Rao became Peshwa. Although during the time of Baji Rao I, the Marathas had started strengthening their position and defeated almost all contemporary regional powers. Among these powers, the Nizam was prominent. Apart from this, Baji Rao I also ended the internal rivalry existing within the Maratha confederacy. However, during the time of Balaji Baji Rao (1740–61), the maximum expansion of the Maratha Empire occurred.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following factors was not responsible for the rise of the Marathas?

options.B: Social consciousness prevalent among the people of Maharashtra
options.C: The distance of Delhi, the center of Mughal court and power, from Maharashtra
options.D: Patronage given to Maratha leaders by Qutb Shahi rulers

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- If the home land, caste, and characteristics of the Marathas that made them distinct from other castes of India are analyzed. Maharashtra is called that region which is situated between the mountain range that ran parallel to the Vindhyas in the south of the Narmada river and the Satpura mountain ranges. Due to the special natural characteristics of their nation, some physical characteristics developed in the Marathas which made them distinct from their other countrymen. In the 15th and 16th centuries, the religious movement of North India entered Maharashtra in the 16th and 17th centuries, which the Marathas welcomed accordingly. The Pandharpur movement was a major reason for unifying the Maratha-nation. Marathas had acquired sufficient expertise in military and public administration under the Shia Sultans of Bijapur and Golconda. Therefore, answer (c) will be correct.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R)~ Assertion (A) : The practice of Devadasi was prevalent in the Vijayanagara Empire. Reason (R) : Dancing girls associated with South Indian temples were viewed with respect. Which one of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements? Code:

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are correct and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is correct but R is incorrect.
options.D: A is incorrect but R is correct.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The practice of Devadasi was not prevalent in the Vijayanagara Empire, this practice existed since the Chola, Chalukya period. The condition of women was good in the Sangam period. Some women used to earn their living through prostitution and dance-singing. There is a mention of prostitutes and dancers in Sangam literature. Adultery was considered a crime in society. Dancers could not do any other work besides dance.

questions.question_text: The 'Treaty of Purandar' (1665 AD) was held between Shivaji and whom?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation ─ The Treaty of Purandar was held between Shivaji and Jai Singh in 1665. As a result of this treaty, Shivaji had to give three-fourths of his forts and land to the Mughals and had to accept the suzerainty of the Mughals.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Adil Shahi 1. Ahmednagar B. Nizam Shahi 2. Bijapur C. Imad Shahi 3. Golconda D. Qutb Shahi 4. Berar Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: RPSC College Lect. 2016 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation ─ After the murder of Mahmud Gawan in 1482 AD, anarchy spread in the Bahmani Empire and within two decades the Bahmani Empire became a victim of disintegration. Later, five new states were consolidated in this region─ 1. Adil Shahi state of Bijapur (1489 AD) 2. Nizam Shahi state of Ahmednagar (1490 AD) 3. Imad Shahi state of Berar (1490 AD) 4. Qutb Shahi state of Golconda (1518 AD) 5. Barid Shahi state of Bidar (1526 AD)

questions.question_text: In the Vijayanagara Empire, the word ‘Kudi’ was used:

options.A: As a unit of land measurement
options.B: For the army of feudal Nayakas
options.D: In lieu of low peasant labor

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Harihara and Bukka established Vijayanagara in 1336. The law and order and economy in this state were good, yet at the time of war, people were caught. They were taken prisoner and made to work in the fields. In addition to this, peasant laborers working in the fields were called 'Kudi'. Along with the sale and purchase of land, the aforementioned peasant laborers were also transferred.

questions.question_text: The 1782 Treaty of Salbai of the Marathas with the English was done at whose insistence?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation ─ Mahadji Scindia played the role of mediator between the English and the Marathas and in May 1782, a treaty was signed between the two parties at the place of Salbai. With this, both gave up the conquered areas. Only Salsette and Elephanta islands remained with the English. They stopped supporting Raghunathrao. The Peshwa gave a pension to Raghunathrao and the English accepted Madhavrao Narayan as Peshwa. With this treaty, the situation before the war was established. Although the company's prestige was saved, it had to bear heavy financial loss. With this, the company got complete independence in the matter of Mysore, on the other hand, the company also came to know the power of the Marathas and for the next 20 years, there was peace between the two.

questions.question_text: The main administrator of the Maratha artillery was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation ─ Ibrahim Khan Gardi was a skilled commander of the 18th century. French commander Bussy trained him. He remained at the Nizam's place for a year and the next year (1758 AD) he moved to the Peshwa's place and Peshwa Baji Rao II made him the head of the artillery. On the field of Panipat, Ibrahim Khan Gardi led the Maratha artillery.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Vijayanagara kings first recognized the importance of cavalry and bought horses in large numbers from Persia and Arabia?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Sangama dynasty's Devaraya I was not only a skilled conqueror but also a skilled administrator and military organizer. He made sufficient increase in the military power of Vijayanagara. Understanding the utility of cavalry, he bought horses on a large scale from Arabia and Persia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Englishmen was present at Shivaji's coronation and presented gifts on behalf of the East India Company?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Shivaji performed his coronation in Raigad on 15 June 1674 according to complete Vedic rituals, in which the main priest duty was performed by Gaga Bhatta. On this occasion, Shivaji adopted the title of 'Chhatrapati' and from the year of his coronation, he also started a new era like other Hindu kings. English Henry Oxenden was present on this occasion; he presented gifts to Shivaji on behalf of the East India Company.

questions.question_text: Which Maratha leader was granted the revenue of a part of Odisha by Alivardi Khan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - To appease the opposition of the Maratha leaders, the Peshwa gave them complete freedom in Odisha, Bengal, and Bihar, which were completely independent under the suzerainty of Alivardi Khan. Raghuji Bhonsle entered Alivardi Khan's territory, did heavy massacre, and forced him to hand over the Odisha province and imposed an annual Chauth of 12 lakh rupees on Bengal and Bihar (1751 AD).

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code below : Assertion (A) : The rise of Maratha power in the second half of the seventeenth century initiated a new element in Indian politics, just as Vijayanagara had done in the previous era? Reason (R) : In early medieval Indian history, due to standing for the national interest under the leadership of the Yadavas of Devagiri, a legacy of high-level political and cultural activities existed in the background of the Marathas. Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Although most of the credit for the rise and development of Maratha power in India goes to Shivaji, it is equally true that when Shivaji emerged on the stage of Indian history, its background was already prepared. In Bijapur and Golconda, Maratha soldiers and politicians had special importance in practice, who had gradually acquired sufficient power in the management of these states. In fact, a legacy of high-level political and cultural activities existed in the background of the Marathas.

questions.question_text: Historian Sewell has written a book named 'A Forgotten Empire'. What was the name of that empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation ─ After the defeat of the ruler of Vijayanagara in the Battle of Talikota on 23 January 1565 AD, Robert Sewell has written in his book 'A Forgotten Empire Vijayanagar: A Contribution to the History of India (1900)' about the scene of looting Vijayanagara that 'in the history of the world, never before had such a magnificent city been destroyed so suddenly as the destruction of Vijayanagara.'

questions.question_text: What was the real name of Afzal Khan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation ─ Shivaji had caused great damage to the Bijapur government by snatching away many of its forts and territories, so he appointed his first-class commander General Afzal Khan, title-holder Abdullah Bhatari, to suppress Shivaji, after showing strength. A meeting between the two took place in a village named Par, which is situated in Pratapgad, Maharashtra. Afzal Khan hugged Shivaji and tried to strangle him by bending him. Shivaji, being alert, pulled out his own intestines with his 'Wagh Nakh' (tiger claws), due to which he died. This incident happened on 2 November 1659 AD.

questions.question_text: What was Bargir in the Maratha army?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation ─ Shivaji's army had two classes of riders - Silahdar and Bargir. Silahdar were high-class soldiers who brought their own horses and weapons and received higher salaries, and Bargir were state-paid direct service-takers who received necessary equipment from the state. In addition to riders and infantry, elephants, camels, donkeys, etc., were also part of the army. Shivaji also had a small but powerful navy for coastal protection. There was also a small artillery in the army.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was at the lowest level of Maratha infantry?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation ─ Shivaji's land army had a systematic administrative form. There was one Nayaka for every nine soldiers and one Havaldar for every fifty. The head of 135 soldiers was called Jumladar and the head of 1350 soldiers was called Hazari. Under the Senapati, there were Panch-Hazari, Ek-Hazari, Havaldar, and Jumladar. The army was paid in cash. The soldiers' life was simple and laborious. The cavalry army had a Havaldar for the Nayaka of 25 soldiers, one Jumladar for every 5 Havaldars, and one Hazari for every 10 Jumladars. Other high posts included Panch-Hazari and the Sar-i-Naubat or Senapati of the cavalry.

questions.question_text: Who defeated the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation ─ The Third Battle of Panipat took place on 14 January 1761 AD between the Marathas and Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali. The leadership of the Marathas was given to Vishwasrao, although the actual commander was his cousin Sadashivrao Bhau. The Marathas were defeated in this war and suffered heavy losses.

questions.question_text: Where were the ruins of Vijayanagara found?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Ruins of Vijayanagara have been found at a place named Hampi on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra river.

questions.question_text: Whose revenue system was Shivaji inspired by?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- After the division of the Bahmani state, there were five states, among which Ahmednagar was also one. Malik Ambar was the ruler there. His revenue system was quite excellent and he used to interact directly with the ryots (peasants). Shivaji also adopted the same system and took 40 percent tax.

questions.question_text: In the Vijayanagara Empire, what did the word 'Amaram' mean –

options.C: Grant given to scholars and poets
options.D: Grant given to widows and the poor

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In the Vijayanagara Empire, 'Nayakas' were actually 'land-lords' who were given special land-plots 'Amaram' in return for salary or for the maintenance of subordinate army. Because these military Nayakas used the 'Amaram' land, they were also called "Amar Nayaka".

questions.question_text: Which subject is the book ‘Amuktamalyada’ related to?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The book ‘Amuktamalyada’ is related to civil and military administration as well as political thoughts and subjects. The reign of Krishnadevaraya starts in 1509 AD. He was a ruler of the Tuluva dynasty. During his reign, Portuguese traveler Domingo Paes visited Vijayanagara. Krishnadevaraya wrote ‘Amuktamalyada’ in Telugu.

questions.question_text: Under the 'Ashta Pradhan' system, what was the duty of 'Shurunavis' or 'Chitnis'?

options.A: He helped the ruler in correspondence.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Under the Shivaji Ashta Pradhan system, Shurunavis or Sachiv had to look after the work of royal correspondence and check the accounts of parganas. While Chitnis (correspondence clerk) was there, who did the work of letter editing.

questions.question_text: In the agricultural produce, how much was the state's share as land revenue in Shivaji's land tax system?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Initially, Shivaji took 33% land revenue. However, after land measurement, the division of land was done based on production. Based on these categories, the government's share in the produce was fixed. The government used to take 2/5th part, i.e., 40% as land tax which was given in cash or in the form of grain. The state provided seeds and animals to the farmers. Whose price was paid in installments. There was a provision for the state to provide help to farmers even during emergencies.

questions.question_text: Who signed the Treaty of Pune on 13 June, 1817?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The Governor-General ordered Mountstuart Elphinstone on 10 May 1817, ‘‘He should restrict the powers of the Peshwa in such a way that he stops the evils occurring during the policy followed by the Pune court for many years.’’ A treaty was signed with the Peshwa on 13 June 1817, according to which he had to leave the presidency of the Maratha confederacy. He had to hand over the land area with an annual income of thirty-five lakh rupees for the auxiliary force and the fort of Ahmednagar to the English. All the territories of the Peshwa outside Maharashtra merged into the British government. The Peshwa promised not to have any relationship or correspondence with any other ruler without the prior consent of the English. Baji Rao's Pune territory was merged into the English state.

questions.question_text: Marco Polo expresses grief over the destruction (wastage) of a large part of Indian wealth on the import of whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–Marco Polo expresses grief over the destruction of a large part of Indian wealth on the import of horses. Marco Polo mentions those traders of South India who had monopolized the import of horses along with Arab traders. According to him, the people of India did not know how to breed horses and they always imported them from abroad. According to him, the Pandya ruler imported 2000 horses every year. He expresses grief over this type of wastage.

questions.question_text: Which fort of the ones given to the Mughals in the 'Treaty of Purandar' (1665 AD) could not be reconquered by Shivaji?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In June 1665, the Treaty of Purandar was held between Raja Jai Singh and Shivaji, according to which Shivaji had to hand over 23 of his forts to the Mughals and keep only 12 forts of general income with him. However, after his coronation, Shivaji achieved victory over the Karnataka region in 1677. Victories of Jinji, Vellore, Purandar, Mahuli, Lohagad, and other forts increased Shivaji's prestige. Shivneri fort could not be reconquered by Shivaji. Shivaji died on 4 April 1680.

questions.question_text: Who was the 'Peshwa' in Shivaji's reign-time?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In Shivaji's reign-time, the Peshwa was Moropant Pingle. In Shivaji's time, the area from Pune to Supe, which also included Northern Konkan, was under the control of Peshwa Moropant Pingle and the area of Southern Konkan up to Northern Kanara was under the control of Annaji Datto.

questions.question_text: In Maratha administration, the accountant of the village was called:
questions.explanation: In Maratha administration, the village accountant was called the Kulkarni. The same source explicitly identifies Kulkarni as a rural accountant.

questions.question_text: In Vijayanagara state, Ayangars:
questions.explanation: In Vijayanagara state, Ayangars were local administrators. Who were hereditary village officials. Twelve administrative powers were appointed for village administration. These 12 administrative officials were called Ayangars. Ayangars could sell or mortgage their posts

questions.question_text: The rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire claimed to rule as representatives of which God?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–The establishment of the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 AD was a great event in the history of South India specifically and India generally. Among the five sons of Sangama, Harihara and Bukka established the Vijayanagara city in front of the Anegundi fort situated on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra. In this adventurous task, Harihara and Bukka got inspiration from their guru Vidyaranya and the famous commentator of the Vedas, Sayana. The rulers of this empire claimed to rule as representatives of Lord Virupaksha.

questions.question_text: 'Ashta Pradhan' were related to which king?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- 'Ashta Pradhan' were related to Shivaji. Shivaji's cabinet of ministers was called 'Ashta Pradhan'. In Ashta Pradhan, the post of Peshwa was of the highest importance and honor while 'Ashta Diggaja' was a group of eight Telugu poets in the court of Krishnadevaraya.

questions.question_text: In Shivaji's administration, the cavalry army was called
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Sar-i-Naubat was the head of the cavalry army. Bargir – Cavalry soldiers provided with horses and weapons by the state. Paga – Regular organization of the cavalry army. Silahdar – Independent soldiers, who kept their own arms and weapons.

questions.question_text: Who established the Peshwa dynasty?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Balaji Vishwanath established the Peshwa dynasty. In 1713 AD, Shahu made Balaji Vishwanath the Peshwa. He died in 1720 AD. Under the leadership of Shahu, the originators of the new Maratha Empire were the Peshwas, who were the hereditary Prime Ministers of Shahu. The Peshwa post became hereditary with the first Peshwa itself.

questions.question_text: The famous Hazara temple of Vijayanagara was built during whose reign?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Krishnadevaraya was a ruler of the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara. During his time, many temples were built in his kingdom. Among them was the Hazara temple which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. During his time, the Vithala Swami temple was also built.

questions.question_text: In which of the following years did Shivaji adopt the title of 'Chhatrapati'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- In June 1674 AD, Shivaji got his coronation done in Raigad by the famous scholar of Kashi, Gaga Bhatta, and adopted the title of 'Chhatrapati'.

questions.question_text: Deshmukh, Patil, and Nayaka were different names given to whom?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–Deshmukh, Patil, and Nayaka were Zamindars during the Maratha rule. They used to perform tax-related judicial and other administrative tasks. Shivaji took away their powers and gave them to government employees.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Chhatrapati Shivaji was a famous Maratha king who had the courage to stand alone against the vast ocean of Mughal rule, Shivaji is famous for challenging the powerful Mughal Empire during Aurangzeb's rule. Due to a long illness, Shivaji breathed his last in 1680 AD. Aurangzeb got his son Sambhaji imprisoned and executed. In the year 1681 AD, because of giving shelter to Aurangzeb's rebellious son Akbar, Aurangzeb got Sambhaji executed in 1689 AD. This dealt a deep blow to the state and policies established by Shivaji

questions.question_text: Barbosa writes, ‘The king provides such freedom that every person can come and go according to his wish without any trouble and can live according to his faith without any questioning whether he is a Christian, Jew, Muslim or Hindu. Equity and justice are followed not only by the ruler but also by the people towards each other.’ Mark the ruler during whose reign the state was tolerant:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Regarding Krishnadevaraya's reign, Barbosa writes, ‘The king provides such freedom that every person can come and go according to his wish without any trouble and can live according to his faith without any questioning whether he is a Christian, Jew, Muslim or Hindu. Equity and justice are followed not only by the ruler but also by the people towards each other.’ Barbosa remained in India as a Portuguese official from 1500 AD – 1516 AD.

questions.question_text: ‘On the way to Karnataka, he went on a pilgrimage to the Shiva temple of Shri Shaila on the bank of the Krishna river. While going, he also gave sufficient money to build bathing ghats, mathas, and rest houses for pilgrims on the river.’ This remark is about which Maratha ruler?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– ‘On the way to Karnataka, he went on a pilgrimage to the Shiva temple of Shri Shaila on the bank of the Krishna river. While going, he also gave sufficient money to build bathing ghats, mathas, and rest houses for pilgrims on the river.’ This remark has been made about Shivaji (Maratha ruler).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was not a South Indian commercial/maritime organization?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Mahajan was not a South Indian commercial/maritime organization whereas Anjuvannam, Manigramam, and Valanjiyar were commercial organizations. Their work was to encourage trade and business.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R)~ Assertion (A) : The Indian tradition of state system was not completely erased by the coming of the Turks, it continued in many frontier regions. Reason (R) : Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya's works, Rajasthani Vigat and Khyat literature and Ramchandra Amatya's Ajnapatra provide useful information on the Indian state system methods. Which of the following is the correct answer in the context of the above statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation–The Indian tradition of state system was not completely erased by the coming of the Turks and it continued in many frontier regions. Like ancient India, stress was laid on the 'saptanga thought-stream' of the state. In these seven organs of the state, the king was supreme. Krishnadevaraya's court was graced by eight great scholars and poets of Telugu (who were called Ashtadiggaja). Therefore, he was also called ‘Andhra Bhoja’. Krishnadevaraya's various works, Rajasthani Vigat and Khyat literature, and Ramchandra Amatya's Ajnapatra provide useful information on the Indian state system methods. Information regarding the contemporary Indian state system is obtained from these various texts.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R)~ Assertion (A) : When in 1714 Nizam-ul-Mulk reached the Deccan as Viceroy, he refused to accept the settlement related to the payment of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi of the Deccan with Shahu. Reason (R) : Nizam-ul-Mulk defeated them many times and demolished the small mud forts built in every district which they used to use as a center for conducting attacks and as a shelter for the Maratha soldier units. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation–After the death of Zulfiqar Khan, Nizam-ul-Mulk became the Viceroy of the Deccan through the efforts of the Sayyid brothers. He refused to accept the new settlement related to the payment of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi of the Deccan with Shahu. Therefore, the statement is true, whereas Reason (R) is not true. Because the Nizam could not defeat them.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below – List-I List-II (Foreign traveler) (Ruler)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The correct match is – List-I List-II (Foreign traveler) (Ruler) (A) Abdur Razzaq (I) Devaraya II (B) Ibn Battuta (II) Muhammad bin Tughlaq (C) Sidar Ali Rais (III) Akbar (D) William Finch (IV) Jahangir

questions.question_text: Who among the following has termed the royal economic policy of the sixteenth-century Vijayanagara rule as feudal?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation–Noboru Karashima's ‘Towards a New Formation: South Indian Society under Vijayanagar Rule’ contains a detailed description of social development in South India. According to him, in the 15th century, a new social formation took place under the Nayankara rule in Vijayanagara, due to which eventually in the 16th century the royal economic policy of the rule became feudal.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements : (i) Shivaji controlled the intrusion of Deccan powers in his Swarajya territory. (ii) He looted Surat in 1664. (iii) He successfully faced the attacks of Shaista Khan and Mirza Raja Jai Singh. (iv) The Mughals merged Bijapur and Golconda into the Mughal Empire with the aim of weakening Shivaji's power. Which of the following statements is not correct? Select the correct answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation–Shivaji made the Treaty of Purandar with Mirza Jai Singh in 1665 AD and Shivaji died in 1680 AD. Whereas Bijapur was won by the Mughals in 1686 AD and Golconda in 1687 AD. It is known that Shivaji controlled the intrusion of Deccan powers in his Swarajya territory and looted Surat in 1664.

questions.question_text: (i) Balaji Baji Rao (ii) Baji Rao II (iii) Madhavrao I (iv) Madhavrao Narayan Select the correct answer from the given code : Arrange the following Peshwas chronologically :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation–Chronologically arranged– (i) Balaji Baji Rao (1740-1761 AD) (ii) Madhavrao I (1761-1772 AD) (iii) Madhavrao Narayan (1774-1796 AD) (iv) Baji Rao II (1796-1818 AD)

questions.question_text: The real name of Alauddin Bahman was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The real name of Alauddin Bahman was Hasan Khan Gangu, who sat on the throne in 1347 AD after assuming the title of Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, he laid the foundation of the Bahmani Empire in the South. He made Gulbarga the capital of his newly established state and kept its name Ahsanabad.

questions.question_text: The founder of the Ahmednagar state was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation–The real founder of the Ahmednagar state was Malik Ahmed. He declared his independence from the Bahmani state in 1490 AD and founded the Nizam Shahi dynasty. Malik Ahmed founded the Ahmednagar state and made it his capital.

questions.question_text: Who was the greatest Sultan of Kashmir in the medieval period who is also called ‘Badshah’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Kashmir ruler Zain-ul-Abidin sat on the throne of Kashmir from 1420 to 1470 AD. He got the Hindu temples destroyed by his father Sikandar (1389-1413 AD) rebuilt. He encouraged the Brahmins who were forced to leave Kashmir to return to their homeland. He abolished the Jizya tax and banned cow slaughter. The Kashmiri people honored him with the title of Badshah (Great King). Due to his liberal policies, he is called ‘Akbar of Kashmir’ and due to his price control system, he is called ‘Alauddin Khilji of Kashmir’.

questions.question_text: Arrange the visit of the following foreign travelers to South India in chronological order and select the correct answer from the given code: (i) A. Nikitin (ii) Abdur Razzaq (iii) Caesar Frederick (iv) Domingo Paes Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation–The correct order is as follows– (i) Abdur Razzaq (1443-44) (ii) A. Nikitin (1470-74) (iii) Domingo Paes (1520-22) (iv) Caesar Frederick (1567-68)

questions.question_text: The title ‘Malik-ush-Shu’ara’ (King of Poets) was given to which poet?
questions.explanation: The title of Malik-ush-Shu’ara (King of Poets) was given to Sheikh Abul Faizi Special Facts 1. Sheikh Abul Faizi was the only Navratna of Akbar who turned from a poet to a philosopher and changed his name to Faizi. In 'Nal-o-Daman', he states the reason for this change as divine inspiration. Akbar gave Faizi the rank of Poet Laureate and made him the head of the Translation Department and the Agra Library. Sheikh Abul Faizi died in 1595 AD. 2. Dara Shikoh was given the titles of Sultan-e-Buland Iqbal and Shikoh-e-Buland Iqbal.

questions.question_text: Where is the Tughlaq Sultan’s palace?
questions.explanation: The Tughlaq Sultan's palace is a beautiful small-sized building. It has only one floor and a plan of a verandah based on pillars. The interior wall has been decorated with trees, plants, and animals/birds. Its construction was done by Akbar in Fatehpur Sikri. Its construction style is likely based on the construction of the Punjab. Percy Brown has called it the pearl of architectural art

questions.question_text: Bhaskaracharya’s work ‘Lilavati’ was translated into Persian by:
questions.explanation: The Persian translation of Bhaskaracharya's book Lilavati was done by Abul Faizi. Lilavati is a book written on mathematics in the Sanskrit language. Abul Fazl has translated the Sanskrit book Panchatantra into Persian language under the name Anwar-i-Suhaili. Dara Shikoh has translated Safinat-ul-Awliya and Majma-ul-Bahrain into Persian language. Al-Biruni's famous work is Kitab-ul-Hind

questions.question_text: Which of the following Gurus started ‘Langar’?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Sikh religion, Guru Nanak, started the Langar (community kitchen) system. He was born on 15 April 1469 AD in Talwandi (modern Nankana Sahib, Pakistan). His father's name was Kalu and mother's name was Tripta Devi. He gave the doctrine of Monotheism and emphasized the worship of Nirguna Brahma. He opposed idol worship, untouchability, Sati system, external show, and rituals. His teachings and poems were compiled by the fifth Sikh Guru Arjan Dev in the Adi Guru Granth. He died in 1537 AD in Kartarpur (Pakistan)

questions.question_text: Who composed ‘Nuh Sipihr’?
questions.explanation: The book named Nuh Sipihr/Nuh-i-Sipihr was composed by Amir Khusrau. This book describes the acts of Alauddin Khilji's son Mubarak Khilji. Along with the victories of Mubarak Khilji, details of India's climate, animals-birds, and religious life are also obtained in this book. questions.explanation: The Khanqah of Sufi saint Sayyid Gesu Daraz is situated in Gulbarga (modern Karnataka). Gesu Daraz was born in Delhi. He was the main disciple of Nasiruddin Chirag-e-Delhi. questions.explanation: Coins with figures of different signs of the zodiac were issued by Jahangir. One of his coins has the signs of the Indian zodiac wheel engraved. Signs expressing the zodiacs - Lion, Sheep, Scorpio, Libra, and Archer are engraved on it. questions.explanation: The correct match is as follows– List-I List-II (Author) (Book) A. Muhammad Al-Ghazali - Tanqid-al-Falsafa B. Ali Hajweri - Kashf-ul-Mahjub C. Dara Shikoh - Safinat-ul-Awliya D. Shah Waliullah - Tafhimat-e-Ilahiya Instruction– (14-18) Read the passage below and answer the questions given on its basis. Under Akbar, roughly from 1560 to 1575, official policy remained to accommodate the prejudices of those theologians who had a deep influence on the Muslim community. They often provoked him to remain strict and religiously inclined towards atheists and so-called heretics. According to Badauni, this period also saw considerable generosity of Akbar towards theologians, which appeared on an unprecedented scale in the form of land grants. Clearly, most of those who benefited from this generosity were those Indian Muslims who were managing mosques and shrines (Khanqahs) in various places. One can also estimate that one purpose of this policy of appeasing the Imams (officials of Islamic religious institutions) was to free themselves from the influence of Afghan chieftains, who were under the influence of those Afghan chieftains who had been their rulers until recent years. Evidently, these people present in the Muslim population as nobles and Ashraafs were considered by the Mughals as their most powerful opponents at that time.

questions.question_text: How were ‘Indian Muslims’ recognized?
questions.explanation: Indian Muslims were known by the name ‘Shaikh-zada’. Apart from the Sayyids of Barha and Kabul, some other important clans were also included in these, whom Akbar gave many important ranks, even making them his Amirs. During Aurangzeb's reign, the importance of Barha and Kabul ended because they were supporters of Dara Shikoh in the war of succession. Iranians (Khurasani / Irani) were followers of the Shia sect, in which there were chieftains like Asad Khan and his son Zulfiqar Khan. Turanis (Central Asians) were supporters of the Sunni sect, in which there were people like Chin Qilich Khan and Firoz Ghaziuddin Jung. Deccani Muslims included those Deccani nobles who worked in Bijapur or Golconda. Both those of Indian origin and foreigners were included in these

questions.question_text: Which of the following words is used in the context of a pilgrimage to the holy tomb of a Sufi saint?
questions.explanation: Dargah is used in the context of a pilgrimage to the holy tomb of a Sufi saint. The hermitages where Sufis lived were called ‘Khanqah’ or ‘Math’. questions.question_text: In the early days of his reign, Akbar gave land grants to theologians with considerable generosity. What was this land grant called?
questions.explanation: Akbar gave land grants to theologians with considerable generosity, which was known as Madad-i-Maash or Suyurghal land. This land grant was permanent and hereditary and was given by Sadr-us-Sudur for the livelihood of religious persons, the poor, scholars, the disabled, and widows Altamgha was a land revenue system started by Jahangir. It was given hereditarily to specially favored religious persons. It could be canceled only by a royal order in special circumstances. Jagir land was given to Mansabdars in exchange for their salary. It was transferable. The Icta system was started by Iltutmish. In this practice, specific pieces of land were given to soldiers in exchange for their salary.

questions.question_text: Identify the author who casts new light on the nobles present during Akbar's reign and the development of his religious policy:
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar’s religious policy is considered the best and impartial among all the Sultans and Emperors of the medieval period. Akbar's policy was completely of religious tolerance. His religious policy was based on the principle of ‘Peace with all’ (Sulh-i-kul). Historians have different opinions on his religious policy (1) According to Iqtidar Alam Khan, ‘‘The purpose of Akbar's religious policy was to establish stability in the aristocratic administrative class, which was formed by people of different castes, classes, and religions. His liberal nature was conducive to this.’’ (2) According to Dr. R.P. Tripathi, ‘‘Generosity and active sympathy and support towards all religions and spiritual movements were sometimes attempted by provincial kingdoms, but the Emperors of Delhi and Agra had never done this. Akbar was the first ruler who, from the beginning of his reign, gradually adopted the policy of progressive generosity and active sympathy towards all religions and spiritual movements.’’

questions.question_text: ‘Which theologians with prejudices were not harsh and sectarian towards people?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar is known for his religious tolerant policy. He was a patron of theologians and scholars. His religious policy was to accommodate the prejudices of the theologians who had a deep influence on the Muslim community. These theologians were not harsh and sectarian towards the Sunni sect because they maintained a harsh and religiously inclined behavior towards most atheists and heretics. They did not have any kind of ideological differences with the Sunni sect. The word Sunni has come from the Arabic Sunnah, which means the deeds of the Prophet or his ideals

questions.question_text: Which of the following did Akbar appoint as the superintendent of the construction of the Agra Fort, who was famous as a military engineer as well as a building builder?
questions.explanation: Jalaluddin Muhammad Akbar (1542-1605) appointed ‘Qasim Khan’ as the superintendent for the construction of the Agra Fort, who was famous as a military engineer as well as a building builder. Agra Fort is the first example of Akbar's style. This fort started in 1565 and was completed in about 15 years. About 3.5 million rupees were spent on its construction. It is situated on the right bank of the Yamuna River in a circumference of about one and a half miles. It has two entrance gates. The main entrance gate is called ‘Delhi Gate’. Inside the fort, Akbar got more than five hundred buildings built with red stones. Some of these buildings have been constructed in the architectural style of Bengal and Gujarat. It is situated 2.5 km north-west of the Taj Mahal. Agra Fort was the main residence of the Mughal dynasty emperors until 1638. In 1983 AD, Agra Fort was inscribed in UNESCO's World Heritage

questions.explanation: Sheikh Abdul Quddus Gangohi was related to the Sabiri branch of the Chishti order. He was born in Rudauli (presently Fatehpur). questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Dabistan-i-Mazahib?
questions.explanation: ‘Dabistan-i-Mazahib’ was written in the Persian language in the 17th century (1665). It gives important information regarding the organization of the early Sikh community. Dabistan is divided into 12 sections related to various sects of Islam, Christianity, Sufi, Nanakpanthi, and Hindu religion. After much controversy, the credit for the authorship of Dabistan-i-Mazahib is given to a Persian named Maubad Zulfiqar Ardistani. He was a person with a liberal religious ideology. He mentions the tradition of praying before the whole assembly for the fulfillment of a person's wish. ‘Dabistan’ describes Guru Nanak's compositions as full of praise for God and moral instructions There is no mention of Adi Granth anywhere in Dabistan-i-Mazahib. The Adi Granth was compiled by Guru Arjan.

questions.question_text: Siyahi Kalam or Nim Kalam technique was brought to India by the following artists? (1) Arabia (2) Iran (3) Transoxiana (4) Turkey
questions.explanation: The Siyahi Kalam or Nim Kalam technique in painting was brought to India from the region of Transoxiana by artists. Several paintings of Siyahi Kalam technique are obtained in Central Asia before the arrival of Islam. Siyahi Kalam is known for line drawings without filling colors. In the Mughal period, special attention has been paid to physical structure in such depictions, where even a single hair has been shown separately and light tint is visible on other parts. Sometimes on silk fabrics, materials, symbols, and calligraphy are obtained which stand at par with Chinese art and Buddhist art in technique and skill

questions.explanation: Sanskrit scholars Jagannath Panditraja and Kavindracharya Saraswati were court poets of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Shah Jahan gave the title of ‘Mahakavi’ to Panditraja Jagannath, the author of Ganga Lahiri and Rasagangadhara. Shah Jahan's reign was the time of the emergence of the Ritikaal in Hindi literature. questions.question_text: Which of the following Sikh Gurus established the first symbolic pilgrimage center for Sikhs, in which a well with 84 steps was built to reach the water for bathing, which became a holy place for Sikhs?
questions.explanation: Guru Amardas (1552 – 1574 AD) was the third Guru of the Sikhs. He was a follower of the Vaishnava religion and a contemporary of Akbar. He established his seat in Goindwal. He got a Baoli built here. He also got a well with 84 steps built here. It is believed that bathing in the Baoli cures all diseases. He started a new marriage method 'Lavan' among Sikhs. Guru Nanak was the founder of the Sikh religion; he was born in Talwandi (Pakistan) in 1469 AD and died in Kartarpur in 1539 AD. Guru Angad was the second Guru of the Sikhs; his title/other name was Lehna. He expanded the Langar system. Guru Ram Das was the fourth Guru of the Sikhs; 500 bighas of land was granted to him by Akbar, on which the city of Amritsar was built

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct about Chokhamela?
questions.explanation: Chokhamela was a famous saint of the Varkari sect of Maharashtra in the 14th century. He was born in the Mahar caste. He composed many Abhangs. He was a disciple of Saint Namdev. Chokhamela was a devotee of Vitthal since childhood. Devotion to Vitthal has been expressed in his poems. His works also shed light on the Dalit society. He lived with his wife Soyra Bai and son Karmamela at a place called Mangalvedha near Pandharpur. His death occurred in Pandharpur. After death, he was buried in front of the Vitthal temple, and his Samadhi was built in front of the temple, not inside the temple. Hence, option (c) is wrong

questions.question_text: What were the didactic poems in Marathi Bhakti poetry called?
questions.explanation: The Marathi dramatic song presented by the folk artists is a Marathi dramatic song presented in the form of a play. It is divided into two forms: (1) Didactic or physical form (2) Spiritual form. It provides entertainment as well as moral guidance to the audience, and the credit for writing 300 such songs on 125 subjects is given to Sant Eknath (1533-99 AD). The songs written in regional language to awaken the society during the 13th century by the saints of the Varkari sect are known as Abhang. The songs sung in memory of family deities after the birth of children are known as Palki or Palna. Vachana is a type of collection of Marathi poems

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of father-son Iranian painters was in Humayun's court?
questions.explanation: The foundation of Mughal painting was laid during Humayun's time. questions.question_text: During Jahangir's reign, some painters had achieved proficiency in special styles in the field of Mughal painting. In this regard, which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Jahangir himself was a skilled painter. His era was the pinnacle of Mughal painting. Among the famous painters of Jahangir's court were Abul Hasan, Bishandas, Mansur, Govardhan, Manohar, Madhav, Muhammad Murad, Daulat, Farrukh Beg, etc. Among them, some painters had achieved proficiency in special styles in the field of Mughal painting, such as- Ustad Mansur, Jahangir had conferred upon him the title of Nadir-ul-Asr Mansur was proficient in making paintings of animals and flowers. Among his important works, 'a rare crane of Siberia' and a unique flower of Bengal are notable. Abul Hasan, Emperor Shah Jahan had conferred upon him the title of Nadir-uz-Zaman. Abul Hasan had attained mastery in portraiture (portrait painting). Govardhan was proficient in making paintings of sadhus, saints, musicians, and fakirs.

questions.question_text: In which of the following monuments was the use of jeweled ceiling and mixed decoration of marble, gold, and precious stones used?

questions.explanation: Kufic/Calligraphy related to Quran – Calligraphy had an important place in the art of decoration in Islamic architecture. questions.explanation: The South Indian Meera, Andal/Aandal, was a famous poet and saint of Tamil Nadu. She is considered an incarnation of Bhumi Devi (Mother Earth). During the month of Margashirsha, on the Thiruppavai festival, sermons are given; the Srivilliputhur temple is dedicated to Andal. In most Vishnu temples, there is a separate temple for Andal. Andal is considered dedicated to Lord Vishnu

questions.question_text: Who was/were the propagator/s of the Lingayat movement?
questions.explanation: Allamaprabhu and his disciple Channabasava are considered the propagators of the Lingayat movement. This was a folk movement. This movement of South India played a powerful role in the process of Sanskritization of customs and religious rituals of many lower castes of Karnataka state. The Lingayat movement was a folk movement in the true sense of the 12th century, which attracted followers of all castes and especially lower castes. It was Brahmanism-opposing in its voice and soul as well. Lingayats of Mysore do not even eat food cooked by Brahmins

questions.question_text: Who were 'Urfi' and 'Naziri'?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Husain Naziri and Sayyid Jamaluddin Urfi were famous Persian poets of the Mughal era. Naziri was skilled in ghazal composition and Urfi was unique in writing Qasidas. They are considered to be of Akbar's reign. During his time, Persian literature can be divided into two parts. First- Original Persian literature which also includes historical texts. Second- Creation of Persian texts through translation

questions.question_text: Who built the 'Charminar' of Hyderabad?
questions.explanation: Charminar is one of the important historical and cultural buildings of India, which was built in 1591 AD by the fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, Sultan Muh. Quli Qutb Shah. It is located in Hyderabad. Hyderabad is settled on the banks of the Musi river. Known as the best example of Indian Islamic architecture, this Charminar is also considered a symbol of the immense love between Qutb Shah and Bhagmati

questions.question_text: Which Sufi order adopted yoga practice?
questions.explanation: Some practices of the Shattari branch are mainly taken from yoga practices. It influenced both Hindus and Muslims. Because of these yogic practices, Shah Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior was called the Qutb of his time. He translated the Hindus' yoga book Amritkund as Bahr-ul-Hayat. Sufis of the Chishtiya branch were influenced by Indian Advaita philosophy, their principle was Wahdat-ul-Wajud. Gangohi, who was a prominent saint of the Chishtiya branch, emphasized yogic practices. That is why the Shattari order used pure yoga practices

Tarikh-i-Firozshahi - Shams-i-Siraj Afif (1398) AD.

questions.question_text: By what pseudonym did Dara Shikoh translate the Upanishads into Persian?
questions.explanation: In history, Dara Shikoh is known as a liberal Muslim who tried to bring equality between Hindu and Islamic traditions. Dara is considered a great thinker and scholarly Sufi saint of that time. He translated 52 Upanishads into Persian under the name Sirr-i-Akbar and also composed in Sanskrit under the name Samudra Sangam Majma-ul-Bahrain. Majma-ul-Bahrain is Dara's immortal work in Persian, in which he stated fundamental similarities between the concepts of Islam and Vedanta

questions.question_text: With what is Tibb-i-Sikandari, which was compiled from Sanskrit sources, related?
questions.explanation: Tibb-i-Sikandari is a book on medical science, which is a text on the subject of medical science written by Miyan Bhua, the Vazir of Sultan Sikandar Lodi of the Sultanate period. This text is also known as Farhang-i-Sikandari in some places. Sultan Sikandar Lodi got many Sanskrit texts translated into Persian

questions.question_text: Which work among the following was given the title 'Razmnama' by its Arabic translators?
questions.explanation: 'Razmnama' is the Persian translation of 'Mahabharata', whose translator was Abdul Qadir Badauni, who was a famous scholar of Akbar's time and a knower of Sanskrit. The Persian translation of Mahabharata took place by him under the name Razmnama, which took him a full year to complete and it was completed in the year 1582 AD

questions.question_text: Which book among the following was not written by Amir Khusrau?
questions.explanation: Nuskha-i-Dilkusha was written by Bhimsen of Kayastha caste in Persian language; he used to work as a clerk in the army of Mughal ruler Aurangzeb Special Facts- Amir Khusrau was a famous writer of the Sultanate period. His talent was multifaceted. He has written many books related to literature, history, and art. Among Amir Khusrau's texts, the prominent ones are - Miftah-ul-Futuh, Khaza'in-ul-Futuh, Nuh-Sipihr, Deval Devi, Khizr Khan (this is also known as Ashiqa).

questions.question_text: 'Sirr-i-Akbar' is a Persian translation of
questions.explanation: The translation named Sirr-i-Akbar is an excellent work of Dara Shikoh. In this, by doing a comparative study of Hindu religion and Islam, their fundamental unity was propounded. Besides this text, Dara also translated Yoga Vashistha, Shat-Darsana, Prabodh Chandrodaya, and Upanishad. In this, apart from the introduction and Sanskrit-Persian glossary, there is a translation of three of the Rigveda, twelve of the Yajurveda, one of the Samaveda, and thirty-six of the Atharvaveda Upanishads. In this, Hindu ideas and definitions have been molded according to Muslim beliefs

questions.question_text: Who among the following is the architect of the Red Fort?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan started its construction work in 1638. He also brought his capital from Agra to Delhi. The main architect of this fort was Ustad Ahmad Lahori. The start of this construction happened on the day considered holy by the Muharram. It took a period of 10 years to complete its construction. The construction of the Red Fort was considered a unique example of the contemporary Mughal style

He is a singer of the Khayal style of Indian Hindustani classical music whose connection is considered to be with the Gwalior Gharana. He traveled to Gwalior when it was the center of the Khayal style of Indian music then and studied music under Vasudevrao Joshi and then returned to his province and settled there

questions.question_text: In which book is the theory of sovereignty of Abul Fazl contained?
questions.explanation: Abul Fazl was born on 14 January 1551. He was one of the nine gems of Akbar. He wrote books like Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari. In Akbarnama, a description of all geographical, social, administrative, and cultural aspects of the empire of Akbar's time has been presented. Abul Fazl has placed Mughal sovereignty at the highest place in the hierarchy of things that receive light emanating from God. Abul Fazl defines sovereignty as a social contract; he has written that the king should protect the four attributes of his subjects (life, property, honor, and belief); in return, he demands obedience and participation in resources. Only just sovereigns could honor this contract with power and divine guidance

questions.question_text: Which scholar among the following published "Marwari Grammar"?
questions.explanation: Marwari is the standard dialect of Rajasthan, which is the main dialect of Western Rajasthan. Abul Fazl in Ain-i-Akbari and Kavi Kushal Labh in Pingal Shiromani used the word Marwari. Ramkaran Asopa wrote the first grammar of Marwari. Soratha, Chhand and Raga are its technical specialties. questions.question_text: What was the original name of the famous painter Nagaridas?
questions.explanation: Sawant Singh, son of Raj Singh, became famous as a devotee of the Vallabha sect, a poet, and a painter himself. He fell in love with one of his attendants (Bani-Thani), who wore beautiful and novel-style clothes, hence her name was Bani-Thani. The king considered Bani-Thani to be the embodiment of Radha. Since Nagari is also another name for Radha, the king took the name Nagaridas for himself. The credit for the progress and development of the Kishangarh style goes to Nagaridas, whose literary taste and love of art have presented before us those rare examples of painting whose literary artistry serves as a guiding light for the world of painting

questions.explanation: Shankaracharya is considered the first propagator of the Bhakti era. The initial protagonist of the Bhakti movement is considered to be the great Vaishnava guru Ramanujacharya.
