questions.question_text: Where is Aurangzeb's tomb located?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb's tomb is located at a place named Aurangabad in Maharashtra state of India. Aurangzeb had built it himself during his lifetime. He was the last important ruler of the Mughal sultanate. After his death (1707 AD), the Mughal empire scattered

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered the oldest Mughal-era example of double dome in India?
questions.explanation: Humayun's tomb is the first example of Mughal architecture in India. This tomb was built by Humayun's widow Begum in 1565 AD. A double dome has been used in this tomb. Because of the Charbagh style of this tomb, it is considered the predecessor of the Taj Mahal

questions.question_text: The original name of the most famous musician of the Mughal period, Tansen, was
questions.explanation: Tansen or Ramtanu Pandey was a great knower of 'Hindustani classical music'. He was one of the nine gems of Emperor Akbar. His connection is with Gwalior city. Tansen received music education in Vrindavan from Haridas

questions.question_text: Who translated 'Panchatantra' into Persian during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: Abul Fazl translated Panchatantra into Persian under the name Anvar-i-Suhaili. Abul Fazl also wrote famous books like Akbarnama. He first came to Akbar's court in 1573. He was born on 14 January 1551

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'Siyar-ul-Mutakherin'?
questions.explanation: Siyar-ul-Mutakherin is a historical work written by Ghulam Hussain Khan Tabatabai. This book is in 3 volumes, the first volume relates to the geography, climate, etc., of Hindustan, the second volume relates to Bengal after the death of Aurangzeb, and the third volume relates to the Nawabs of Bengal

questions.question_text: Which of the following presented a Bengali version of the Ramayana?
questions.explanation: Krittivasa did the Bengali version of the Ramayana. This text is not a literal translation of the original Ramayana, but it also contains diverse depictions of medieval Bengali society and culture. This epic of Bengali language has 6 Kandas (Adi Kanda, Ayodhya Kanda, Aranya Kanda, Kishkindha Kanda, Sundara Kanda, and Lanka Kanda)

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Futuh-us-Salatin'?
questions.explanation: Abdul Malik Isami was a 14th-century Indian historian and court poet. He was under the patronage of Alauddin Bahman Shah, the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate. He composed the poetic history of Muslim conquest of India, Futuh-us-Salatin, in the Persian language

questions.question_text: Regarding which musician did Abul Fazl say that "a singer like him has not been in India in the last one thousand years"?
questions.explanation: Abul Fazl said regarding the musician Tansen that "a singer like him has not been in India in the last one thousand years". Tansen was the best musician of Akbar's time. He was a great musician of the Dhrupad singing style. Akbar conferred upon him the title of Kanthabharana Vani Vilas. He was one of Akbar's nine gems

questions.question_text: The Sufi saint known by the popular name Mujaddid was:
questions.explanation: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi was given the title of Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani and Sheikh Nasiruddin was given the title of Chirag-i-Dehlavi

questions.question_text: Which Bhakti-era saint used the Hindi language in his teachings for the first time?
questions.explanation: Ramananda was the first saint of the Bhakti era who gave the Bhakti movement a popular base by making the Hindi language the medium for the propagation of his views. He started the devotion of Rama and Sita instead of Krishna and Radha. Kabir did not write any of his compositions, his principles were compiled in Bijak by his disciple Dharmadas

questions.question_text: Which Sufi called India 'heaven on earth'?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau called India 'heaven on earth'. He was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, he only invented Khayal music and also invented musical instruments, Sitar and Tabla. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya and Baba Farid were saints of the 'Chishti order'

questions.question_text: Saint Namdev was a ............. by profession.
questions.explanation: Saint Namdev was a tailor by profession. He had an important role in popularizing the Bhakti movement in Maharashtra. He was associated with the Varkari sect, Saint Gyaneshwar was his guru

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Sufi saints in chronological order and select the correct option from the following options:
questions.explanation: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (up to 1143-1236 AD) Nizamuddin Auliya (up to 1236-1325 AD) Mir Sayyid Gesudaraz (up to 1321-1422 AD) Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi (up to 1563-1625 AD) The center of education for Khwaja Sayyid Muhammad Gesudaraz was Gulbarga of Karnataka. Due to his compassion for the poor and the afflicted, he received the title of Banda Nawaz.

questions.question_text: The guru of Bhakti saint Ramananda, Raghavananda, was related to?
questions.explanation: Ramananda's guru Raghavananda was related to the Shri Sampradaya; by staying in the Shrimath of Swami Raghavananda of Kashi, Ramananda studied Vedas, Puranas and other texts Shri Sampradaya was established in the 12th century by Ramanuja, which is related to Vaishnava religion. His view is Vishishtadvaitavada.

questions.question_text: Which Chishti Sufi saint is known by the popular name 'Chirag-i-Dehlavi'?
questions.explanation: Chishti Sufi saint Sheikh Nasiruddin Mahmud was also known by the name 'Chirag-i-Dehlavi'. He was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. He authored Tausid-i-Wajudi. Khair-ul-Majalis is a collection of his sayings. The Chishti order was established in India in Ajmer by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (1143–1236 AD)

questions.question_text: Who among the following authored "Bhaktamal", which contains the compilation of biographies of saints?
questions.explanation: Nabhadas, a disciple of Agradasji and a devotee, authored a book named 'Bhaktamal' in which there is a discussion on the compilations of the biographies of saints. In this book, all the sects and saints of all sects have been remembered with devotion and equal respect. Bhaktamal, i.e., just as there are four main things in a garland – beads, thread, Sumeru, tassels (bunch), similarly ...in Bhaktamal, devotees are beads, devotion is the thread, the Sumeru that is on the garland is Shri Gurudev, and the bunch in the form of the knot of Sumeru is our Shri Bhagavan. Bhaktamal is not an ordinary composition; rather, it is a benedictory text.

questions.question_text: The saint of the Bhakti period who had twelve (12) disciples of different castes–
questions.explanation: The credit for bringing the Bhakti movement from the South to the North goes to Ramananda. He was born in Allahabad (Prayagraj). Ramananda was a disciple of Raghavananda, a follower of Ramanuja. His perspective was liberal and he made all castes, religions, even Muslims his disciples. He was the first preacher who used Hindi. He had two female disciples– Padmavati and Surasari. Among Ramananda's 12 disciples, Jat Dhanna, barber Sen, cobbler Raidas, weaver Kabir and Rajput Pipa were prominent

questions.question_text: Who established 'Pushti Marg'?
questions.explanation: Vallabhacharya is considered the foundation pillar of the Krishna Bhakti branch of the Saguna stream of the Bhakti period and the proponent of 'Pushtimarg'. He has been called "Vaishvanaravatar, incarnation of fire". He was well-versed in Vedic scriptures. Ramanuja, Nimbarkacharya, Madhvacharya and Vallabhacharya tried to make Vedanta accessible to the general public by giving more priority to Bhakti instead of knowledge. Apart from Vaishnava religion, they were unique scholars of religions and sects like Jain, Buddhist, Shaiva, Shakta, etc

questions.question_text: In the period of which sultan did the Firdawsi Sufis have to face oppression and execution?
questions.explanation: Firoz's religious policy was narrow-minded and intolerant. He was also intolerant towards Muslim sections like Shia, Sufi, Mahdavis, etc., because they were not supporters of the Sunni sect. During his period, there was a rebellion of Firdawsis in which the Firdawsi leader named Rukn was also given the death penalty

questions.question_text: Where was the Sufi saint Moinuddin Chishti buried?
questions.explanation: After the death of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in 1236 AD, he was buried in Ajmer. He was born in Sistan in Iran in 1143 AD. Khwaja Sahab, Garib Nawaz, Khwaja Ajmeri and Sultan-ul-Hind were his titles. 'Munis-ul-Arwah' is the autobiography of Khwaja Sahab, which was compiled by Jahanara Begum

questions.question_text: After which event did Guru Gobind change his name to Guru Gobind Singh?

options.A: After the organization of a huge assembly of Sikhs in Anandpur in 1699 AD
options.B: After the organization of a magnificent court in Keshgarh
options.C: After the first war of Anandpur
options.D: After accepting the 'Khande ka Pahul' at the hands of the Panj Piare

questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last Guru of the Sikhs. He started the 'Pahul system'. In this, the initiated person was called 'Khalsa'. The person getting initiated had to accept the five K's—Kesh, Kangha, Kirpan, Kachha and Kada and the use of the word 'Singh' started at the end of the name. In 1699 AD, Guru Gobind Singh established the 'Khalsa Panth'. He compiled a supplementary text named 'Dasam Padshah ka Granth'

questions.question_text: How many climates (seasons) has Babur described in India in Tuzuk-i-Baburi?
questions.explanation: Babur's biography is famous by the name of Tuzuk-i-Baburi or Baburnama, which is originally in the Turkish language. In it, Babur has described the existence of three climates in India– rain, cold and heat; he has given a detailed description of all three seasons. Along with this, contemporary political, social, economic and cultural information is also available in it

questions.question_text: In medieval society, the word 'Khalk' was used for

options.A: For the upper class of society

questions.explanation: The word 'Khalk' was used for people or masses in medieval India. Its other meanings can be– world, universe or crowd

questions.question_text: Teachings are contained in 'Bijak'.
questions.explanation: 'Bijak' is called the authentic text of Kabir Vani. Kabir gave his principles and sermons only in oral form. Among Kabirpanthis and general readers, 'Bijak' is considered the original text of Kabir Sahab's principles. The total number of verses in Bijak is 619. With the commentary of Rewa Naresh 'Shri Vishwanath Singh', 'Bijak' was printed before 1872 AD. Ahmad Shah has done the English translation of 'Bijak of Kabir'

questions.question_text: Which of the following books was authored by Jain scholar Haribhadra Suri?
questions.explanation: The famous Jain scholar Haribhadra Suri was a great Prakrit author of the medieval period. His most important works composed in Prakrit were Samaradityakatha and Dhurtakhyana. Haribhadra was associated with the Shwetambar sect in Jain religion. He also wrote a book on yoga, Yoga-shatasamuchaya

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Gate) List-II (Location) A. Khooni Darwaza 1. Delhi B. Buland Darwaza 2. Fatehpur Sikri C. Lal Darwaza 3. Ahmedabad D. Rumi Darwaza 4. Lucknow A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Khooni Darwaza - Delhi Buland Darwaza - Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh) Lal Darwaza - Ahmedabad (Gujarat) Rumi Darwaza - Lucknow

questions.question_text: Match the list of authors of List-I with the list of books written on Delhi Sultanate in List-II. List-I List-II A. Minhaj-us-Siraj Juzjani 1. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri B. Kalyan Singh Ashiq 2. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi C. Zia-ud-din Barani 3. Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh D. Shams Siraj Afif 4. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Minhaj-us-Siraj Juzjani - Tabaqat-i-Nasiri Kalyan Singh Ashiq - Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh Zia-ud-din Barani - Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi Shams Siraj Afif - Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi 'Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh' is a work of Sujan Rai Bhandari, who was a contemporary of Aurangzeb. This is a general history of Hindustan which ends on the death of Shah Jahan.

questions.question_text: Match the mosques of List-I with the places given in List-II. List-I List-II A. Quwwat-ul-Islam 1. Gaur (Gaur) B. Adina 2. Lakhnauti C. Lotan 3. Pandua D. Tiley Wali Masjid 4. Delhi A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque - New Delhi Adina Mosque - Pandua (West Bengal) Lotan Mosque - Gaur (West Bengal) Tiley Wali Masjid - Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh)

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Gol Gumbaz 1. Muhammad Adil Shah B. Taj Mahal 2. Akbar C. Bibi Ka Maqbara 3. Rabia-ud-Daurani D. Sikandra 4. Mumtaz Mahal A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Gol Gumbaz - Muhammad Adil Shah II Taj Mahal - Mumtaz Mahal Bibi Ka Maqbara - Rabia-ud-Daurani Sikandra - Akbar The tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah II is known by the name Gol Gumbaz, who was the ruler of Bijapur.

questions.question_text: Match the authors of List-I with their books given in List-II. List-I List-II A. Chakrapani Mishra 1. Vrikshayurveda B. Surapala 2. Vishwavallabha C. Dara Shikoh 3. Dastur-ul-Amalguzari D. Khwaja Yasin 4. Nuskha dar Fanni-Falahat A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Chakrapani Mishra - Vishwavallabha Surapala - Vrikshayurveda Dara Shikoh - Nuskha dar Fanni-Falahat Khwaja Yasin - Dastur-ul-Amalguzari

questions.question_text: Which of the following remarks about the Sufi faith in India is not correct?

options.A: Ba-Shara (who followed Islamic law) and Be-Shara (who were not bound by it) are roughly two divided sects of Sufi lineages.
options.B: Chishti and Suhrawardy were the two most prominent Sufi silsilas in India.
options.C: Chishti were active in South India, while Delhi and surrounding areas were the regions of the Suhrawardis.
options.D: A prominent mystic living in the Khanqah led the lineage comprehensively.
options.E: Suhrawardis did not believe in fasting or self-renunciation. They supported a simple life.

questions.explanation: Sufi faith is an ideology representing liberal, mystical and integrative tendencies in the Islamic religion. Mainly two prominent silsilas, Chishti and Suhrawardy, were prevalent in India. Chishti spread in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh; they first made Ajmer of India their spiritual center. While the headquarters of the Suhrawardy silsila was in Multan

questions.question_text: ‘‘My caste is low, my deeds are low, And low is my profession, Because of this low condition, The Lord has raised me high.’’ Which Bhakti saint wrote the above verse?
questions.explanation: Sant Ravidas (Raidas) was born in Kashi. He was one of the prominent disciples of Sant Ramananda (Prayagraj). Raidas, due to being from the cobbler family, worked of making shoes. His famous statement was ‘‘Man changa to kathauti mein Ganga’’. Sant Ravidas worked throughout his life for the end of evils spread in society like caste-based discrimination

questions.question_text: Select the collection whose all cities have observatories built by Sawai Jai Singh-II:
questions.explanation: Amer ruler Sawai Jai Singh-II got 5 observatories built Delhi - 1724 AD (oldest) Jaipur - 1728 AD (biggest and best) Ujjain Banaras Mathura

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Sikh religion are correct? (i) From the 1750s, the Sikh groups and Misls (groups) became more powerful under the leadership of different chiefs (Sardars), who organized armed soldiers in a very professional manner. (ii) There was a tradition of organizing the annual 'Sarbat Khalsa' in Chak Guru (Amritsar), but due to mutual differences, every Sardar made a plan to build a separate region for himself. (iii) Ranjit Singh (1780-1839) put a stop to this process in the end; he established a state in Punjab in the name of Khalsa. (iv) All Gurus were Khatri, but in the seventeenth century, their army commanders, i.e., Masands, were mostly Jat. Select the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Misls were small political Sikh regions. There was harassment of Sikhs on a large scale due to the imperial order of Mughal Bahadur Shah in 1710. Further, Farrukhsiyar also continued this policy. Therefore, Sikhs organized themselves into Taruna Dal and Buddha Dal. Later on, many state unions were formed from these, which were called Misls

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Rishi silsila in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The Rishi movement inspired by the Sufi ideology was run in Kashmir by Sheikh Nuruddin Rishi. The Rishi sect of Sufism emerged in Kashmir in the 15th-16th centuries. Sheikh Nuruddin Rishi is also known by the name Nand Rishi, who had a deep influence on the life of the people of Kashmir

questions.question_text: Arrange the following monuments in chronological order:
questions.explanation: Salim Chishti was the grandson of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer. Only by the blessings of him did Akbar get a son. In honor of Baba Salim Chishti, Akbar established Fatehpur Sikri in 1572 AD. Akbar made Fatehpur Sikri his capital and built Jodha Bai Palace, Panch Mahal, Sheikh Salim Chishti's tomb, Birbal's palace, etc., there too. Charminar in Hyderabad was built by Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah (Qutb Shahi dynasty). In Sikandra (4 kilometers away from Agra), Akbar started the construction of his tomb himself and Jahangir completed it. Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Sultan Muhammad Adil Shah II of Bijapur The correct chronological order is- Sheikh Salim Chishti's Tomb (1580-81 Fatehpur Sikri) - Charminar (1591 Hyderabad) - Akbar's Tomb (1613, Sikandra) - Gol Gumbaz (1656, Bijapur).

questions.question_text: 'The Sultan reorganized the military forces, thereafter the commander was called Amir-ul-Umara and a group of officers named Barbardaran was formed, whose job was to collect the army at the time of need. Apart from this, there were two hundred bodyguards or Sila-daran whose job was to protect the Sultan's personal weapons. The Sultan had 400 bodyguards, who were called Khas Khel.' Identify this Bahmani Sultan of Gulbarga:
questions.explanation: Alauddin Bahman Shah I was the first sultan of the Bahmani dynasty of the South. He received the title of "Zafar Khan" in the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. After this, Muhammad Shah I became the second sultan of the Bahmani dynasty, he ran a new administration system which was conducted by his eight ministers. He reorganized the guard of the palace protectors. By reorganizing the military forces, his commander was called Amir-ul-Umara and the responsibility of the 400 bodyguards of the Sultan was given to Khas Khel. His death occurred due to excessive drinking

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Chishti Sufi Sheikhs in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The first saint of the Chishti tradition in India was Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, a disciple of Sheikh Usman. Moinuddin Chishti came to India with Muhammad Ghori in 1192 AD. He laid the foundation of the "Chishtiya tradition". After him, Baba Farid, Nizamuddin Auliya, Amir Khusrau, Gesudaraz and Sheikh Salim Chishti carried forward the Chishti tradition. Akbar, due to having respect for Salim Chishti, had the tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti built in 'Fatehpur Sikri'

questions.question_text: Which of the following were painters of Shah Jahan?
questions.explanation: The foundation of Mughal painting was laid in the reign of Humayun. During his exile, he obtained the services of two Persian painters named Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad. Shah Jahan-era famous painters were- Faqirullah, Mir Hashim, Muhammad Nadir Samarqandi, Anup and Murad, Bichitr, etc. Although Shah Jahan had more interest in architectural art than painting, yet one of his famous paintings is available in the Indian Museum, in which Shah Jahan is shown doing Sufi dance

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is not matched? Author - Book
questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows Author - Book Inayat Khan - Shahjahannama Bhimsen - Nuskha-i-Dilkusha Muhammad Kazim - Alamgirnama Abul Kazim Nabir - Bahar-i-Azam

questions.question_text: Which of the following are works composed by Amir Khusrau?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau's real name was Abul Hasan. He was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. He is called the first poet of Khari Boli. His major works- Hasht Bihisht, Matla-ul-Anwar, Khazain-ul-Futuh, Nuh Sipihr, Miftah-ul-Futuh, Qiran-us-Sadain, Ashiqa, Tughlaq-Nama, Aina-i-Sikandari are

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: 'Qasim Khan' became famous as the son of Mir Murad Juwani in Subzawar (present Afghanistan). Murad taught archery to Jahangir's son Shah Jahan. During the reign of Islam Khan Chishti, Qasim Khan worked as a Treasurer for the first time in Bengal. Later on, Mughal ruler Jahangir appointed him as the Subedar of Agra. Prior to this, due to his fame as a military engineer as well as a building builder, he was also chosen as the supervisor of the Agra Fort building. In 1628, Shah Jahan appointed him as the Subedar of Bengal. He was not included among the eight people appointed to look after the royal buildings built by Akbar in 1583

questions.question_text: Sheikh Salim Chishti's tomb is located in-
questions.explanation: Sheikh Salim Chishti's tomb is located inside the Jama Masjid in Fatehpur Sikri in Agra district. In 1572 AD, Akbar, along with the Gujarat conquest, conquered this region and named it Fatehpur Sikri. Akbar got this tomb built in 1580-81 AD

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in order of their construction date and select the correct answer using the code given below: 1. Agra Fort 2. Red Fort of Delhi 3. Qutub Minar 4. Taj Mahal Code:
questions.explanation: Qutub Minar - 1199 – (1231-32) AD Agra Fort - 1565 AD Red Fort of Delhi - 1638-48 AD Taj Mahal - 1631-53 AD

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The Bhakti movement attained its completeness in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. This movement was a reformist movement of Hindus. Vallabhacharya has an important place among the prominent saints of the Bhakti movement. He was the second great saint of the Krishna-lineage branch of Vaishnava religion. He was a Brahmin of Andhra Pradesh but he lived in Banaras. Vallabhacharya believed in Shuddhadvaita. He wrote many religious texts in which 'Subodhini' and 'Siddhant Rahasya' are extremely famous. Vallabhacharya's philosophy is centered on the concept of an individual and loving God. He believed in Pushtimarg and Bhakti-marga Choose from the codes given below: (a) Only (i) and (ii) (b) Only (ii) and (iii) (c) Only (ii), (iii) and (iv) (d) Only (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) UGC/NTA Dec 2018 IInd Paper Ans : (d) The Bhakti movement reached its fullness in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. This movement was a reformist movement of the Hindus. Vallabhacharya holds an important place among the prominent saints of the Bhakti movement. He was the second great saint of the Krishna-margi branch of Vaishnava religion. He was a Brahmin from Andhra Pradesh but lived in Banaras. Vallabhacharya believed in Shuddhadvaita. He wrote many religious books, among which 'Subodhini' and 'Siddhant Rahasya' are extremely famous. Vallabhacharya's philosophy is centered on the concept of an individual and loving God. He believed in Pushtimarga and Bhaktimarga.

questions.question_text: Which of the following books is not a work of Amir Khusrau?
questions.explanation: Ghunyat-ul-Munya is a work of Shahab Sarbadi. He was Persian (a) Tuhfat-us-Sighar (b) Nuh-Sipihr (c) Qiran-us-Sa'dain - These three are works of Amir Khusrau.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Sultans of Kashmir authorized Mulla Ahmad to translate the Mahabharata into Persian?
questions.explanation: Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir authorized Mulla Ahmad for the translation of the Mahabharata into Persian. Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin has authored the book 'Shikayat-nama'. He used to write poetry in Persian under the pen name 'Kulebi'. Because of his liberal policy, he is also called the Akbar of Kashmir. Abidin abolished the Jizya tax before Akbar and imposed a ban on the Sati practice

questions.question_text: The oldest paintings of the Jain Kalpasutra were related to which of the following regions?
questions.explanation: The Jain text 'Kalpasutra' is related to Malwa and Gujarat. The lives of Tirthankaras are described in the Jain text named Kalpasutra; Bhadrabahu is considered its author

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is termed as Assertion and the other as Reason. Assertion (A) : Balban appointed 'Khwaja' in important Iqtas, who were selected from among 'Mustaufis'. He was a Diwani officer and his work was related to accounts and records. Reason (R) : The appointment of such an officer by the Sultan on the recommendation of the Wazir indicates a sharp eye on revenue distribution and control over the activities of 'Muqtis'. With reference to the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Both Assertion and Reason are correct because Balban was a ruler of the Slave Dynasty of Delhi Sultanate who appointed Khwaja in his important Iqtas, whose work was related to accounts and records; this indicates such officers were those who kept a sharp eye on revenue distribution and control over the activities of Muqtis

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Kabir's works is correct?
questions.explanation: Kabir was an Indian mystic poet of the 15th century who authored the Bijak book. Poems composed in Panchvani by Dadu Panthis are relatively less authentic than the Punjabi tradition. Charlotte Vaudeville's argument is that the text collected in the Adi Granth is free from the sectarian traps of Kabir Panthis

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (Traveler) (Country of Origin)
questions.explanation: Niccolo de Conti came to the court of Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I in 1420 AD from Italy. He was a resident of Italy, whereas Afanasy Nikitin was a resident of Russia. He came during the reign of Bahmani ruler Muhammad III. Ibn Battuta was a resident of Morocco; he came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, whereas Abdur Razzaq was not from Syria but from Persia. He came to India during the reign of Deva Raya II

questions.question_text: His grandfather wrote about many animals, plants, and people, but "did not order his painters to make pictures of them." Identify this royal grandfather-grandson pair:
questions.explanation: The Mughals have made a distinct contribution in the field of painting. They started new subjects related to the royal court, nature, animals, and war scenes. The pair of grandfather and grandson Babur and Jahangir was such that he did write about all these subjects but did not order his painters to make pictures of them

questions.question_text: What are the features of the manuscript illustrated in the Akbar-nama?
questions.explanation: 'Akbar-nama' has been written by Abul Fazl; it has been written in the Persian language. In the Mughal painting of the Akbar-nama, often two painters were associated with one painting, and in Mughal-era painting, coloring and sketching were often done by one painter. Assistants only completed the portraits, but in some special paintings, sketching, coloring, and portraits were done by three different painters; this is what Abul Fazl has written in the manuscript illustrated in the Akbar-nama

questions.question_text: Which of the following painters were in the court of Jahangir?
questions.explanation: Ustad Mansur was known by the name Mansur, who was a famous painter of the Mughal court. Mughal Emperor Jahangir provided him patronage. Jahangir had given Mansur the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asr'. Abul Hasan was also the most famous painter of Jahangir's court, whom the Emperor adorned with the title of 'Nadir-uz-Zaman'. The painting of the squirrel made on a chinar tree by Abul Hasan was liked especially by Jahangir

questions.question_text: Arrange the following monuments in chronological order:
questions.explanation: 'Sher Shah Suri's Tomb' is located in Sasaram, which Sher Shah had built during his lifetime. Cunningham considered it superior to the Taj Mahal. This tomb is octagonal (b) 'Humayun's Tomb' is located in Delhi and was built in 1565 AD as per the orders of Humayun's widow Haji Begum. It has been called the predecessor of the Taj Mahal. (a) 'Charminar' is the most famous and important monument of the capital city, Hyderabad, of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built it in 1591 AD. (d) 'Gol Gumbaz' is the tomb of Bijapur's Sultan Muhammad Adil Shah II. Built by Persian architect Yaqut in 1656 AD.

questions.question_text: Consider the names of the following cities of Delhi– (i) Jahanpanah (ii) Siri (iii) Tughlaqabad (iv) Khizrabad Which of the following orders shows the correct chronological order of their establishment?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The chronological order of the establishment of the following cities of Delhi is as follows– Siri (1303 AD, Alauddin Khilji), Tughlaqabad (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, 1320 AD), Jahanpanah city (Muhammad bin Tughlaq-1325 AD-1351 AD) and the city of Khizrabad was established by Khizr Khan in 1414-1421 AD. In 1303 AD, Alauddin Khilji achieved victory over Chittor and named Chittor 'Khizrabad' after his son Khizr Khan.

questions.question_text: Regarding which of the following painters did Jahangir believe that no one had any competitor in their specific field? (i) Abul Hasan (ii) Bishandas (iii) Ustad Mansur (iv) Manohar Select the correct answer from the following short list – Code :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – During Jahangir's time, the two best painters were Ustad Mansur and Abul Hasan. Mansur (was an expert in animal-bird) to whom he granted the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asr' and Abul Hasan (was an expert in portrait painting) he granted the title of 'Nadir-uz-Zaman'.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is termed as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) – Assertion (A) : In the medieval period, many books written on music in Sanskrit were translated into Persian. Reason (R) : Early Chishti Sufi saints were fond of musical gatherings, which were called Sama. Consider the above statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below – Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct Explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct Explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Amir Khusrau is credited with the inclusion of many Persian and Arabic elements in Indian music. In which new forms of singing like Qawwali and Tarana are included. Sultan Hussain Shah, who was the ruler of Jaunpur, was a pioneer in the field of music. His important contribution to music is the singing of 'Khayal'. Sikandar Lodi authored 'Lahjat-e-Sikandar Shahi' (Lazzat-e-Sikandar Shahi), this is the first Indian work on music. Abul Fazl gives a list of thirty-six musicians. In this way, many Sanskrit texts were translated into Persian in the medieval period. Early Sufis had great love for music (Sama). They used to worship God through Sama.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is termed as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) – Assertion (A) : Music and dance arts reached their zenith during the reign of Shah Jahan. Reason (R) : He was a patron of arts and literature. Consider the above statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below – Code :

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct Explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct Explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Regarding Akbar's patronage of music, Abul Fazl writes that the Emperor paid great attention to music and provided patronage to all those who practiced the appealing art. There were many musicians in his court, including Hindu, Iranian, Turanian, Kashmiri, female and male artists. During the reign of Shah Jahan, music did not develop as much as it did during the reign of Akbar. According to Abul Fazl, Akbar had given royal patronage to 36 singers in his court. Tansen and Baiju Bawra were the most famous among them. Dhrupad singing was prevalent in Akbar's time. Shah Jahan himself was a very good singer. The musicians of Shah Jahan's time were Lal Khan, Khushal Khan and Bisham Khan. Shah Jahan gave Lal Khan the title of Gunasamudra. Akbar's period is called the zenith period of music.

questions.question_text: Whose tomb was Sultan-Ghari?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – 'Sultan-Ghari's tomb' is the tomb of Iltutmish's eldest son Nasiruddin. Which is famous by the name of Sultan-Ghari. Iltutmish had built it in 1231 AD. Its central room is octagonal (eight-cornered dome) and towers are built on all four corners. The style of its pillars is Hindu and arches are used which are a part of the Muslim style. Iltutmish is called the father of the Indian tomb style. This was the first tomb to be built in India.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below – List-I List-II (Sufi Terminology) (Meaning)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Correct matching is– List-I List-II (Sufi Terminology) (Meaning) (A) Futuh (I) Unasked for alms (B) Khanqah (II) Sufi Khanqah (C) Barkat (III) Spiritual holiness of a Sufi (D) Malfuzat (IV) Conversation of Sufi saint (E) Sama ⇒ Sufi music gathering

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: (i) Guru Nanak had interest in all prominent contemporary religious beliefs and practices, whether they were 'Hindu' or 'Muslim'. (ii) Guru Nanak was liberal towards Jain monks. (iii) In his view, the traditional reading of religious books is a waste of time. (iv) Guru Nanak spent the last fifteen years of his life in Kartarpur. Which of the following statements is not correct? Select your answer from the code given below. Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– Guru Nanak was born on 15 April, 1469 AD in Talwandi, Punjab. Nanak believed in all prominent contemporary religions, he had special interest in Hindu, Muslim religion. Guru Nanak did not have a liberal nature towards Jain monks. He spent the last 15 years of his life in Kartarpur and here on 22 September 1539 AD, he died. Guru Har Gobind Singh established the city of Kiratpur in Kashmir.

questions.question_text: Whose statement is this that for a woman, the best place is veil or grave?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– 'For a woman, the best place is veil or grave', this statement is of Badauni. Badauni was a scholar appointed in Akbar's court, he authored 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh'. Among the Sanskrit texts, he did Persian translation of Mahabharata, Ramayana, Rajatarangini, Sinhasan Battisi, etc.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : During the reign of Jahangir, painting reached its peak. Reason (R) : He did not have interest in other arts. Read the above statements and select the correct answer from the code given below: Code:

options.A: (A) and (R) are both correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– In the Mughal period, the seed of painting that Humayun planted, reached its peak during Jahangir's time, because Jahangir himself was well-versed in painting. He started the picture gallery in Agra under the chairmanship of Aqa Reza. And he also had interest in architecture and other arts.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A) : Guru Amardas adopted the old tradition in the appointment of his successor. Reason (R) : He decided to give the position of Guru to his son-in-law Ramdas and his descendants as his successor, thus making the position of Guru hereditary. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) are both correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Guru Amardas was the third Guru of the Sikhs, he adopted the old tradition in the appointment of his successor, this statement is incorrect. While the reason is absolutely correct because he made his son-in-law 'Ramdas' his successor and decided to give it to his descendants, thus making the Guru position hereditary. Guru Amardas is known for the expansion of his langar tradition

questions.question_text: After the Sirhind attack, Banda Bahadur assumed the title of Badshah, started a new calendar and issued coins in the name of which Gurus?

options.A: Guru Nanak and Guru Har Gobind
options.B: Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh
options.C: Guru Har Gobind and Guru Arjan Singh
options.D: Guru Gobind Singh and Guru Tegh Bahadur

questions.explanation: Banda Bahadur was a famous Sikh military and political leader. He was the first Sikh military chief to wage war against the Mughal rulers of India. And after the Sirhind attack, Banda Bahadur assumed the title of 'Badshah', started a new calendar and issued coins in the name of the first Guru of Sikhs, Guru Nanak and the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh

questions.question_text: 'Cities look attractive from a distance, but as soon as one enters inside, all the grandeur gets lost in the rush of narrow alleys and crowd.' About the cities of Mughal-era India, the above remark was made by whom?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Father Monserrate came in 1578 AD to participate in the religious discussions taking place in Ibadat Khana at the invitation of Akbar. Akbar appointed him as the teacher of Prince Murad. He described the character and personality of Akbar, the Mughal court, and cities like Mandu, Surat, Delhi, Lahore, Gwalior, etc., in his travelogue. Peter Mundy came during Shah Jahan's time. He described the contemporary famine. Tavernier also came during Shah Jahan's time. He traveled throughout India for 6 times and traveled throughout almost all of India. Sir Thomas Roe came during Jahangir's time in 1615 AD as an ambassador of the British Emperor James I.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements related to Amir Khusrau – (i) He was a disciple of Sufi saint Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. (ii) It is said that he wrote many books on music. (iii) His text 'Khazain-ul-Futuh' gives information about the reign of Sultan Kaikubad. (iv) The musical instrument 'Sitar' is considered his invention. Which of the following statements are correct? Select the correct answer from the codes given below – Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Amir Khusrau was a favorite disciple of Chishti sect's Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. He wrote many books on music. His text Khazain-ul-Futuh or Tarikh-i-Alai gives a description of 15 victories and economic reforms of Alauddin. Amir Khusrau invented the 'Sitar'.

questions.question_text: Which sultan of Delhi got Qutub Minar repaired, got the abandoned Hauz Khas cleaned and got an attractive madrasa built on its bank?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Qutub Minar was built by Qutubuddin Aibak. But from time to time Delhi sultans like - Iltutmish, Alauddin Khalji, Firoz Shah Tughlaq got it reconstructed. But in the time of Firoz Shah, repair work was done and madrasas were built.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair of authors and works is not matched correctly? (Author) (Work)
questions.explanation: Khafi Khan's book or work is named Muntakhab-ul-Lubab. Saqi Musta'id Khan (Mustaid Khan)'s work is 'Ma'asir-i-Alamgiri' in which there is a description of the reign of Aurangzeb

questions.question_text: During the reign of which Mughal emperor did the depiction of natural scenes reach its peak in Mughal painting?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Jahangir was a patron of art. He was influenced by European painting. He sent oil paintings as gifts to the British Queen. The depiction of natural scenes in Mughal painting reached its peak during Jahangir's reign. Abul Hasan was a famous painter of natural scenes.

questions.question_text: Regarding Baburnama, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: The memoirs of Babur are a historical source of high literary value.
options.B: Actual events are not given in chronological order in it.
options.C: Babur has described every good and bad event with utmost impartiality.
options.D: Historical events are mixed with Babur's personal thoughts, emotions and discretion in such a way that they cannot be separated from each other.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– The name of Babur's autobiography is `Baburnama' or `Tuzuk-i-Baburi'. This is written in Chagatai Turkish language. Babur was the founder of the Mughal Empire in India. Akbar had `Baburnama' translated into Persian language by his courtier Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana during his time. Babur has written `Baburnama' clearly and truthfully as much as possible. He did not make any attempt to hide his weaknesses, habits of taking intoxicants, parties, faults, etc. He started his account from the time of sitting on his throne and wrote until almost the end of 1529 AD, leaving some time in between.

questions.question_text: Sheikh Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri belonged to the Sufi silsila:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Sheikh Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri was a famous saint of the Firdawsi branch of Suhrawardy. The region of the Firdawsi branch in India remained limited only up to Bihar. Sheikh Yahya tried to bring the principle of 'Wahdat-ul-Wujud' closer to the law of Islam through his letters.

questions.question_text: Two sentences are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A) : The medieval Bhakti movement was successful in connecting the followers of Buddhist and Jain faiths with the Hindu religion. Reason (R) : In the process of cultural integration, many people of tribal origin were included in the Hindu caste system. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above statements? Select your answer from the code given below: Code:

options.A: (A) and (R) are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation─The medieval Bhakti movement attacked the delusions that spread in the social system. Opposed idol worship. The Islamic society benefited from the Hindu caste system. Therefore, the religion preachers tried to end the restrictions of the caste system. Apart from this, saints of the Bhakti movement tried to connect people from Buddhist, Jain religion to their religion. Apart from this, tribal people were also met by the preaching of influenced saints. Kabir, Nanak, Raidas, Tulsi, Surdas, etc., made efforts for social reform.

questions.question_text: Sheikh Nuruddin established –

options.A: The Rishi silsila of Sufis in Kashmir
options.B: The Chishti silsila of Sufis in Ajmer
options.C: The Firdawsi silsila of Sufis in Bihar
options.D: The Suhrawardy silsila of Sufis in Multan

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation─Medieval Sufi saint Sheikh Nuruddin established the Rishi silsila in Kashmir and he emphasized on Hindu-Muslim unity. Sheikh Nuruddin ran the Rishi silsila after coming under the influence of his spiritual guru Shaivite saint Lalleshwari (Lalla Yogeshwari).

questions.question_text: In the context of relations between the Ulema and the Sultan in the Sultanate period, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The Ulema received powers from Sharia.
options.B: The Ulema did not give the Sultan the authority to interpret divine words.
options.C: The Sultan could not leave the Ulema according to his will.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation─In the Sultanate period, there is a lot of disagreement in the description given about the relations between the Sultan and Ulema. In the beginning of the Sultanate, the control or influence of Ulema on the administration is visible. But the first opposition to the Ulema is done by Alauddin Khalji. He neither took advice from the Ulema nor took the support of the name of the Caliph. Similarly, Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq also did not allow the Ulema class to interfere in the administration. Therefore, even after this, the influence of the Ulema in the Delhi Sultanate was considerable.

questions.question_text: Two sentences are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : Turks did not follow the tradition of depicting human and animal forms according to the Hindu style on buildings. Reason (R) : They depicted geometric and floral shapes and verses of the Quran on panels. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two sentences? Select the code given below: Code :

options.A: (A) and (R) are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation─In the field of art and architecture, the synthesis (mixture of Indian Islamic art) between Hindu-Islamic cultures is more visible. Turks often used models of Hindu ornamentation like models of bells, models of vines, Swastika, Lotus, etc. But these did not follow the tradition of depicting human and animal forms. The most prominent feature of Islamic architectural art is the use of arches and domes. Because of the prohibition of depicting living beings in Islam, the depiction of calligraphy and geometric designs was prevalent.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below: (i) Propagation of Vaishnava Bhakti by Ramananda (ii) Compilation of Adi Granth (iii) Closing of Ibadat Khana (iv) Foundation of Chishti Sufi silsila in Deccan Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation─ The chronological order of events is as follows– • Ramananda (1299-1411) was born in Allahabad. He started Rama Bhakti instead of Vishnu. • Sheikh Burhanuddin Gharib made Daulatabad his center of education and propagated the Chishti silsila in the South (14th Century). Sheikh Burhanuddin Gharib was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. • Akbar built Ibadat Khana in 1575 AD. • Ibadat Khana was closed by Akbar in 1582 AD. • Compilation of Adi Granth was done by the fifth Guru of Sikh religion, Arjan Dev in 1604 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following painters was matchless in depicting animals?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation─Ustad Mansur (of 17th century) was a bird painter. He adorned Jahangir's court. He did matchless depiction of various animals. He was the first one to depict the Siberian crane. Jahangir gave him the title of Nadir-ul-Asr (rare in the era). Abul Hasan made a painting of Jahangir's coronation and received the title of Nadir-uz-Zaman. Mir Sayyid Ali was a painter and also a poet, Humayun gave him the title of Nadir-ul-Asr. In Akbar's time, Basawan was considered an expert in European style.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List–I List–II (Historical Text) (Author)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Correct answer is– (Historical Text) (Author) (A) Shahjahannama (i) Inayat Khan (B) Nuskha-i-Dilkusha (ii) Bhimsen (C) Padshahnama (iii) Abdul Hamid Lahori (D) Alamgirnama (iv) Muhammad Kazim

questions.question_text: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is written by whom?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2011) Explanation– Ziauddin Barani was a Muslim historian and political thinker. He was in the time of Delhi Sultanate rulers Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah. The text written by him, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, is a major document to know medieval India. Shams-i-Siraj Afif in his work ‘Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi’ has given a detailed description of all events of Firoz Shah Tughlaq's reign from beginning to end.

questions.question_text: Name the historians who questioned the centralized tendency of the medieval Indian state?
questions.explanation: Burton Stein and Frank Perlin were such historians who discussed the subject of medieval India and questioned the centralized tendency of the Indian state

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List–I List–II (Sufi Saint) (Work Area)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation: The correct matching is as follows: (Sufi Saint) (Place) (A) Sheikh Muinuddin Chishti (i) Ajmer (B) Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya (ii) Multan (C) Sheikh Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar (iii) Ajodhan (D) Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya (iv) Delhi

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The Sultans of Delhi made extensive use of high-quality lime mortar in their buildings. The Turkish rulers used the beam system in their buildings. Before the advent of Islam, the local style was called the trabeate architecture. Indians learned the art of domes and arches from the Arabs.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II i. A method under the Mughals for land revenue assessment and collection b. Hasil ii. Practice of giving land on contract c. Ghalla Bakhshi iii. The area where crops have been damaged d. Nabud iv. Actual collection of land revenue under the Mughals Codes: a. Ijaras
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The correct matching sequence is as follows: a. Ijara - Practice of giving land on contract b. Hasil - Actual collection of land revenue under the Mughals c. Ghalla Bakhshi - A method under the Mughals for land revenue assessment and collection d. Nabud - The area where crops have been damaged.

questions.question_text: Whose view is it that "A woman cannot perform her duties as a ruler well because she fundamentally lacks intellectual capacity"?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Isami was an important historian of the Sultanate period. It is his view that "A woman cannot perform her duties as a ruler well because she fundamentally lacks intellectual capacity." Isami's important book is 'Futuh-us-Salatin', which describes from the rise of the Yamini dynasty of Ghazni to the reign of Muhammad Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal rulers wore earrings as a gesture of thanks to the Sufi saint Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti after recovering from illness?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Jahangir had become very ill due to his addiction to alcohol. He had gone to seek blessings at the court of Chishti Khwaja Muinuddin of Ajmer. Subsequently, he wore earrings. Jahangir was very fond of jewelry.

questions.question_text: Who said about his father's rule, "Iran is only for the Shias and the Turks and Turan are only for the Sunnis, whereas in India, Sunni and Shia gather in one mosque and Christians and Jews gather in one church to worship"?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Mughal ruler Jahangir had said about his father's rule– Iran is only for the Shias and the Turks and Turan are only for the Sunnis, whereas in India, Sunni and Shia gather in one mosque and Christians and Jews gather in one church to worship.

questions.question_text: With what did the Altamgha Jagir, started by Jahangir, correspond in features?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The Altamgha Jagir was started during Jahangir's time. It was a feature of Watan Jagir. And it was given only as a government grant to those families upon whom the Emperor had special favor.

questions.question_text: Who built a mosque named Khairul Manzil in Delhi opposite the Old Fort?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Akbar's foster mother Maham Anga established a madrasa in Delhi which was famous by the name Khair-ul-Manzil. Maham Anga ran the petticoat-government from 1560-62 and remained all-powerful in the state.

questions.question_text: Identify the pair of architect and calligrapher (Khushnavis) associated with the tomb of Ataga Khan, which his son Mirza Aziz Koka had built in 1566-67:

options.A: Ustad Khuda Quli and Baqi Muhammad
options.B: Mirke Saiyid Ghiyas and Mirke Mirza Ghiyas
options.D: Ustad Bilal and Ustad Qayamat Husain

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Ustad Khuda Quli and Baqi Muhammad were the calligraphers who were associated with the Ataga Khan tomb. The Ataga Khan tomb was built by his son Mirza Aziz Koka in 1566-67 AD. It is known that the architect of the world-famous monument Taj Mahal was Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I (Vocabulary) List-II (Meaning)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The correct matching is as follows: (a) Bitikchi - (i) Military Clerk or Secretary (b) Mir Adl - (ii) Chief Justice (c) Ulus - (iii) Tribe (d) Waqia Navis - (iv) Court Historian

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal rulers claimed that he could distinguish which painter had made the sketch and who had filled in the colors or prepared the face in it?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The seeds of Mughal painting were sown during the Humayun era, which reached its zenith during Jahangir's time. Because Jahangir himself was a great painter. He had claimed that "he could distinguish which painter had made the sketch and who had filled in the colors or prepared the face in it."

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not matched?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– History writing was in its prime position in the medieval period. Various historians described the administrative systems related to the rule of rulers of various time periods in their history writing. Such as– Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, Abdul Qadir Badauni, Maasir-i-Alamgiri, Saqi Mustaid Khan and Akhbar-ul-Akhyar, Abdul Haq etc. The author of Maasir-ul-Umara is Shah Nawaz Khan. Written in three parts, this book contains a description of the Mughal nobles from Babur to Aurangzeb's period. This book is a useful source for the depiction of Rajput-Mughal nobles.

questions.question_text: In the last reign of which ruler was the decoration of walls (design) with precious stones (semi-precious stones) started, which was called 'Pietra Dura'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) RPSC 2018 Explanation– During Jahangir's period, the construction of Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb was done by Nur Jahan. Nur Jahan's father's name was Ghiyas Beg, Jahangir gave him the title of 'Itmad-ud-Daula'. 'Pietra Dura' has been used in his tomb. This tomb is situated in Agra. Both red stone and marble have been used in the construction of this tomb. It was built by Nur Jahan in 1626 AD based on the Persian style.

questions.question_text: The popular feature of the popular monotheistic movement of the fifteenth-sixteenth century was:

options.A: It was a movement of the subordinate class, its leaders came from the middle class and addressed the common people in their language.
options.B: It was a movement of the common people, exploited by the aristocratic class for their benefit.
options.C: It was a movement of the subordinate class, its leaders were also from the subordinate class, and they addressed the people in the public language.
options.D: It was such a movement in which teachings of monotheism were given by citing religious texts.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– The main feature of the popular monotheistic movement in the fifteenth-sixteenth century was that it was a movement of a subordinate class, its leaders also came from the subordinate class and the common people were addressed in their language. It was an anti-untouchability movement. Popular reformers like Kabir, Nanak, Dadu led it.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– List-I List-II A. Qila Rai Pithora I. Centre of Iltutmish's Delhi, which in the 14th century came to be known as Delhi-i-Kuhna (Old Delhi) B. Kilokhri II. Here Sultan Jalaluddin Khalji built a new city, Shahr-i-Nau C. Hauz-i-Khas and Tughlaqabad III. Alauddin Khalji and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq respectively D. Adilabad and Jahanpanah city IV. Muhammad Tughlaq

questions.question_text: Who wrote a poem of charming rising emotions for Hindostan: "The prosperity of Hindostan is magnificent, Heaven itself feels jealous of this garden. Its land is the main jewel of the earth in such a way; As there is a sign of beauty on the face of an attractive young woman."
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– The above statement "The prosperity of Hindostan is magnificent, Heaven itself feels jealous of this garden. Its land is the main jewel of the earth in such a way, as there is a sign of beauty on the face of an attractive young woman" is of Abdul Malik Isami. Isami was a 14th-century Indian historian and court poet. He composed the poetic work Futuh-us-Salatin in praise of Muslim victory under the patronage of Alauddin Bahman Shah, the founder of the Bahmani dynasty. He described about the natural beauty, equanimity, and prosperity of India, etc. UGC has considered its answer (a) as correct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following indicates that in the second half of the thirteenth century, young women were trained in Persian and Indian (Hindi) music by courtesans for the court?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– The above statement is of Ziauddin Barani that 'In the second half of the thirteenth century, young women were trained in Persian and Indian (Hindi) music by courtesans for the court.' Barani composed 'Tarikh-i-Firozshahi' and 'Fatawa-i-Jahandari'.

questions.question_text: Whose compositions are included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Guru Nanak and his successors have been mentioned in the Guru Granth Sahib (Adi Granth) compiled by Sikh Guru Arjan Dev. Apart from this, Namdev, Kabir, Ravidas, Sheikh Baba Farid, etc., have been mentioned in the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.question_text: Who was the one who for the first time gave a description of the languages of different regions of India and reminded us that Hindvi is the contact language of the country and Sanskrit is the classical language?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Amir Khusrau for the first time gave a description of the various regional languages of India and told that Hindvi is the contact language of the country and Sanskrit is the classical language. Amir Khusrau saw the tenure of 8 Sultans. First of all, Alauddin Khalji gave him the post of court poet. Zaban-e-Hindvi, which was later also called Urdu or Rekhta, and he developed a new style of Persian which is called Sabk-i-Hindi or the Indian style.

questions.question_text: Which of the following were Sufis of the Suhrawardi silsila?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) PGT History, 2003 Explanation– The Suhrawardi branch was first propagated in India by Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya Suhrawardi. He was born in Multan in 1181 AD. He had traveled to Medina and Baghdad to receive higher education. There he became a disciple of Sheikh Shahabuddin Suhrawardi and came to India and made Multan his center.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (Source) (Author)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Source Author 1. Abbas Khan Sarwani I. Tarikh-i-Sher Shahi 2. Jauhar Aftabchi II. Tazkirat-ul-Waqiat 3. Abdul Qadir Badauni III. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh 4. Ferishta IV. Tarikh-i-Ferishta

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and give the correct answer from the codes given below the lists: List-I (Author) List-II (Book)
questions.explanation: List-I (Author) List-II (Book) (a) Ibn Hasan - The Central Structure of the Mughal Empire (b) P. Saran - The Provincial Government of the Mughals (c) Moreland - India at the Death of Akbar (d) M. Athar Ali - The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb

questions.question_text: Regarding painting, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Compared to sculpture, the attitude of Muslims towards painting was relatively less strict.
options.B: Among Muslims outside Hindustan, especially on the walls of private buildings, the practice of painting already existed before this.
options.C: The art of miniature painting that the Mughal emperors patronized and promoted was, in fact, originally a branch of Persian painting, in which emphasis was placed on line work, considerable attention was paid to fineness of detail, and there was a deliberate detachment with respect to context.
options.D: The famous painters Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali came to India with Akbar from Kabul.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– Compared to sculpture, the attitude of Muslims towards painting was simple. Among Muslims outside of Hindostan, the practice of painting on the walls of private buildings was already existing. The art of miniatures that was patronized and encouraged by the Mughal Emperors was actually in the beginning a branch of Persian painting. All these statements are true. Whereas painters Abdus Samad and Mir Saiyid Ali came with Humayun. Humayun gave the title of Shirin Qalam to Abdus Samad. Abdus Samad taught painting to Humayun and Akbar. Humayun had given the title of Nadir-ul-Asr to Mir Saiyid Ali.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a collection of conversations of Sufis?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Sufism or Tasawwuf is a mystical sect of Islam. Its followers are called Sufis (Sufi saints). Sufis did not accept donations or gifts from kings and liked to live a simple life. It is believed that Sufism was born about a thousand years ago in the Basra city of Iraq. Personalities like Rabia, Al Adham, Mansur Hallaj are called their pioneers. The collections of conversations of Sufis are Fawaid-ul-Fuwad, Khair-ul-Majalis and Siyar-ul-Sudur. The compiler of Fawaid-ul-Fuwad is Amir Hasan Ala Sijzi Dehlavi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Fatehpur Sikri is a skillful combination of arch-bearing and pillar-bearing styles.
options.B: Red sandstone was the main material in the construction of Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri city.
options.C: The plan of Fatehpur Sikri was made after the final form of Akbar's religious policies.
options.D: Akbar's own tomb in Sikandra was built by his son Jahangir.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– In the given question, Fatehpur Sikri is a skillful combination of arch-bearing and pillar-bearing styles. Akbar's own tomb in Sikandra was built by his son Jahangir. Red sandstone was the main material in the construction of Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. These three statements are correct whereas "The plan of Fatehpur Sikri was made after the final form of Akbar's religious policies" is false.

questions.question_text: Which of the following buildings is Persian in inspiration and Indian in execution?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– Humayun's tomb is the only Mughal-era architecture whose inspiration is Persian architecture and its material form is Indian. The construction of Humayun's tomb was done in Delhi by Haji Begum (Humayun's wife). This tomb is called the precursor of the Taj Mahal. It is the first monument built with the Charbagh style.

questions.question_text: Gulbadan Begum led a delegation of Hajj pilgrims going to Mecca and stayed there for two and a half years before returning in 1582. Which of the following royal ladies was not a part of this delegation?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– Gulbadan Begum led a delegation of Hajj pilgrims going to Mecca and stayed there for two and a half years before returning in 1582. Gulnar Agha, Salima Sultan, Umme Kulsum Khanam were members of this delegation. Whereas Hamida Banu Begum was not a part of this delegation. During Akbar's time, Gulbadan Begum composed Humayun-nama in Persian.

questions.question_text: In which of the following book/books is the use of a capstan (charkhi) to lift heavy weights found for the first time?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The use of a capstan to lift heavy weights is found for the first time in Afif's Tarikh-i-Firozshahi and Sirat-i-Firozshahi. The book Tarikh-i-Firozshahi was authored by Shams-i-Siraj Afif. This book of Afif gives a detailed description of the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Sirat-i-Firozshahi was authored by some unknown scholar. Firoz Shah authored his autobiography Futuhat-i-Firozshahi.

questions.question_text: Which Sufi saint has mentioned 'Shri Gorakh', 'Alakh Niranjan' and 'Omkar' in his 'Rushdnama'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Sheikh Abdul Quddus Gangohi was of the 'Chishti-Sabiri' tradition, he had expressed a desire to implement Sharia in India by writing letters to Sikandar Lodi and Babur. On the other hand, Quddus Gangohi also believed in the monotheistic principles of Nath Yogis, he wrote a book named 'Rushdnama'. Gangohi also used to write poems with the pen name 'Alakh'. Gangohi has mentioned Shri Gorakh, Alakh Niranjan and Omkar in his 'Rushdnama'. Gangohi gave recognition to Wahdat-ul-Wujud. Chishti Sabiri was a branch of the Chishti order.

questions.question_text: When the Chief Qazi traveled with the royal camp, he was called –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– When the Chief Qazi traveled with the royal camp, he was called Qazi-i-Askar. Qisas, Ta'zir and Tashir were types of punishments. Qazi-ul-Quzat (Qazi) was the head of the judicial department and the chief justice of the empire. Sadr-us-Sudur is considered the medium connecting the Emperor and the people, the proponent of Sharia, and the representative of the Ulema. The assistant to the Qazi, the interpreter of laws, was the Mufti or Wakil-i-Shar.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: According to Chaitanya, love and devotion in worship, as well as song and dance are included, which provide a state of ecstasy, in which the presence of God (Hari) can be felt.
options.B: Abdul Wahid Bilgrami's Haqaiq-i-Hindi shows the influence of devotional songs of Vaishnava saints on the Sufis.
options.C: Mahadevi Akka of Karnataka, Lalleshwari of Kashmir and Mirabai of Rajasthan probably indicate that it was not possible for the inner desire to love God to fit with worldly marriage.
options.D: Sheikh Nuruddin Rishi of Kashmir rejected local traditions and started a puritanical movement.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– Sheikh Nuruddin Rishi of Kashmir rejected local traditions and started a puritanical movement. The above statement is wrong. Kashmir was the center of the activities of the Rishi Silsila. This silsila demonstrates Hindu-Muslim harmony. Nuruddin had started the Rishi Silsila under the influence of his spiritual teacher, Shaiva saint Lalleshwari (Lalla Yogeshwari). Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correct? Author Source
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– The author of Adab-ul-Harb wa Shujaat is Fath-i-Mujab. Muhammad Kabir wrote Afsana-i-Shahan. Ziauddin Barani is the author of 'Fatawa-i-Jahandari' whereas 'Khazain-ul-Futuh' is a work by Amir Khusrau, while Sad-uddin Muhammad Awfi composed 'Jawami-ul-Hikayat' and 'Lubab-ul-Albab'.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): In the medieval period, Greek books were understood through Arabic translations. Ptolemy and Galen remained the main experts of astronomy and medicine. Reason (R): Thomas Roe has written that 'The "Muslim Maulvis" of the Mughal court had knowledge of philosophy and mathematics and they are great astrologers and can talk about Aristotle, Euclid and Averroes'. Which of the following is correct regarding the context of the above two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–In the medieval period, Greek books were translated into the Arabic language. In the medieval period, Ptolemy and Galen continued to be the main experts in astronomy and medical science. Thomas Roe arrived in India in 1615 AD during the reign of Emperor Jahangir. Thomas Roe met Jahangir in the fort of Ajmer. Standing before the Emperor, he sought permission to trade in India as a petitioner. Thomas Roe wrote that 'the Muslim mullahs of the Mughal court had knowledge of philosophy and mathematics. The Muslim mullahs also had information about Aristotle, Euclid, and Averroes.'

questions.question_text: Where did such a school develop where, along with dictionaries like Miftah-ul-Fuzala, other manuscripts were profusely illustrated?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation–Such a school developed in Malwa where, along with dictionaries like Miftah-ul-Fuzala, other manuscripts were profusely illustrated. The founder of the Khalji dynasty in Malwa was Mahmud Shah, who had established a hospital and a residential college in Mandu.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the presentation of the Persian translation of the Upanishads prepared by Dara Shikoh with the help of Sanskrit scholars –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 PGT History, 2013 U.P. Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2018 Explanation – Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. He was very liberal from a religious point of view. The most important work of Dara was the 'compilation of the Vedas' which he considered to be a divine creation. Apart from this, he also got the Bhagavad Gita and Yoga Vashistha translated. Dara Shikoh, with the help of the scholars of Kashi, translated fifty-two Upanishads into Persian under the name 'Sirr-i-Akbar'.

questions.question_text: Who was the Hindu painter who was sent by Jahangir to make the portrait of Shah Abbas I of Iran?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Among the Mughal rulers, Jahangir took the most interest in painting. Painters like Abul Hasan and Mansur lived in his court. Apart from this, there were also Muhammad Murad, Bishandas, Manohar, and Govardhan, etc. Bishandas was an expert in making portrait paintings. Jahangir sent him to Iran to make the portrait of Shah Abbas I of Iran. This has been described by Jahangir in his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri'.

questions.question_text: Who composed the famous work Tabaqat-i-Akbari?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation–The work 'Tabaqat-i-Akbari' was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Nizamuddin divided Tabaqat-i-Akbari into three parts. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh – Badauni Akbarnama – Abul Fazl Qanun-i-Humayuni – Khwand Mir

questions.question_text: Which of the following was responsible for the pronouncement of Muslim law–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation-Apart from the Emperor, Qazis were appointed in the capital, Qazis of the provinces in the capital of the provinces, and Qazis were also appointed in big cities and towns. In some places, Muftis (those who interpret the law of the Quran) were also there to assist the Qazi. Mir Adl used to prepare and pronounce judicial verdicts and they were the ones responsible for the pronouncement of Muslim law.

questions.question_text: The architectural plan of which building/buildings of the Akbar period got inspiration from Buddhist architecture?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation-The architectural plan of Akbar period's Panch Mahal in Fatehpur Sikri and Akbar's tomb in Sikandra got inspiration from Buddhist architecture. Akbar's tomb in Sikandra is a five-storey tomb, whereas the Panch Mahal is also called the Wind Palace (Hawa Mahal), this is also a five-storey rectangular room.

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' is written in the Persian language by Jahangir. This is Jahangir's autobiography. In this, Jahangir wrote from the time of his ascension to the throne up to the seventeenth year of his reign. Later, due to poor health, he handed over the responsibility of writing to his Mir Bakshi Mutamid Khan. Who completed it up to the 19th year of Jahangir's reign, but this book was finally completed by Muhammad Hadi.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R)– Assertion (A) : In the medieval period, madrasas remained mainly related to Muslim theology and its vast literature. Reason (R) : Most of the higher education was given individually by teachers outside the madrasas, who often used to give their personal certificates. Which of the following is correct regarding the context of the above two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–Agra was the best center as a center of education in the Mughal period, Delhi was at the second place. Humayun's madrasa in Delhi and Khair-ul-Manazil built by Maham Anga were famous centers of education, this was also called Madrasa-i-Begum. Shah Jahan got the Madrasa-ul-Baqa built near Jama Masjid. In the medieval period, madrasas remained mainly related to Muslim theology and its vast literature. In the medieval period, most of the higher education was given individually by teachers outside the madrasas, who often used to give their personal certificates.

questions.question_text: Mirza Ghalib was in whose time of Emperor?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─Bahadur Shah II (Zafar) was the last Mughal Emperor. Mirza Ghalib was in his time. He was an Urdu poet. Mirza Ghalib was born on 27 December, 1797 AD in Agra (Uttar Pradesh), he died in Delhi in 1869 AD.

questions.question_text: Jodha Bai palace is situated–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─Jodha Bai's palace was built by Akbar in Fatehpur Sikri. This is a rectangular building, its length is 320 feet and width is 215 feet and its height is 32 feet. Akbar laid the foundation of Fatehpur Sikri in 1572 AD and its construction work was completed in 1585 AD. It was constructed by Bahuddin. Jodha Bai palace is the largest among the buildings of Fatehpur Sikri.

questions.question_text: Who is the composer of 'Padmavat'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─The composer of 'Padmavat' is Jayasi. The real name of Jayasi was Malik Muhammad and due to being born (1477 AD) in a village named Jais located in Awadh (present-day Amethi), he became famous by the name Jayasi. His death happened around 1542 AD. Jayasi composed works named Padmavat, Akhrawat, and Akhiri Kalaam. Padmavat is composed in the Awadhi language.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Akbarnama'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─The work Akbarnama was composed by Abul Fazl during the reign of Emperor Akbar. Akbarnama has been divided into three parts. In the first part, the history of the Mughal rulers from Amir Timur to Humayun has been described. In the second and third parts, the history of Akbar up to 1602 AD has been given. After the death of Abul Fazl, this work was completed by Inayat Khan.

questions.question_text: An eyewitness, inspired by which building in India, said that 'If it has been brought down to earth from heaven'?

options.A: Building of the Red Fort of Delhi

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─An eyewitness, inspired by the building of the Red Fort of Delhi in India, said that 'If it has been brought down to earth from heaven'. The famous Diwan-i-Khas is situated in the northern part of the Red Fort of Delhi. This building is more decorated than other buildings built during the reign of Shah Jahan. From the point of view of architectural art, its style is not perfect, but still, it is extremely impressive. It lacks the simplicity of the 'Taj Mahal', because it was not built according to that idea. This is an indicator of Shah Jahan's grandeur. These lines of the famous poet Amir Khusrau present a beautiful depiction of the grandeur of the building. ``Gar firdaus bar ruye zami ast, hami ast, hami ast, hami ast''

questions.question_text: Who was the connoisseur of painting among the Mughal emperors?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─Jahangir did not just have an interest in painting, but he was also a skilled painter. Jahangir writes in his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' that ``My interest in painting and proficiency in identification had reached such a limit that when any painting of dead or today's painters comes before me without telling its name, I immediately tell that this painting is of such and such person.'' Aqa Riza was the head of his art department.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'Ain-i-Akbari'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─Abul Fazl composed Akbarnama during Akbar's time. This work is divided into three parts. Its third part is known by the name of Ain-i-Akbari.
