In this work, the governance system of Akbar and the rules and laws related to it have been described in a detailed form. In this work, Abul Fazl has also written his genealogy and life story, this work was completed by Inayat Khan. Because Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 AD at the time of writing work.

questions.question_text: The name of the author of the book 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh' is-
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─Abdul Qadir Badauni was born on 21 August, 1540 AD in a place named Toda Bhim located in Jaipur. He received education under Shaikh Hatim Sambhali and Shaikh Mubarak Nagauri. He was a high-class writer and translator. He had composed 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh' and 'Kitab-ul-Ahadis' and presented it to Emperor Akbar. Abdul Qadir Badauni was under Akbar's protection. He was present there at the time of the Battle of Haldighati. His book is considered the general history of Hindustan. He was a critic of Akbar's religious policy. His death happened in Badaun (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.question_text: Who was a famous Hindi poet of Akbar's court?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─In the era of Akbar, Hindi was not just the heritage of Hindus but Muslims also had a right to it, their compositions are surprising. Among Persian, Arabic, Turk, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana was the most prominent who was a connoisseur of Hindi and Sanskrit alike. Any history of Hindi poetry is incomplete without the mention of the respect of Khan-i-Khana. Rahim's dohas (couplets) are prevalent even today.

questions.question_text: 'Waqiat-i-Babari' is –

options.D: Collection of verses composed by Babur

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─'Waqiat-i-Babari' or 'Baburnama' is the autobiography of Babur. He has written his autobiography in his mother tongue Chagatai Turkic to which various names like Tuzuk-i-Babari, Waqiat-i-Babari or generally Baburnama have been given. Babur has mentioned Hindu states like Vijayanagara and Mewar in his autobiography.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below– List-I List-II
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Amir Khusrau composed Tughlaqnama and Ibn Battuta composed Rehla in which Ibn Battuta has described his journey. Ziauddin Barani composed Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi to please Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was composed by Minhaj-i-Siraj.

questions.question_text: The name of the author of the book 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' is–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Dara Shikoh got the Sanskrit works 'Bhagavad Gita' and 'Yoga Vashistha' translated into Persian under his own supervision. His most important work was the 'compilation of the Vedas' which he considered to be a divine creation. Dara himself composed a book named 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' (The Meeting of Two Oceans) in the Persian language.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R)– Assertion (A) : Sikh Dharamshala was the place where Sikhs used to sit and engage themselves in the worship of God. Reason (R) : When Thag Sajjan surrendered before Guru Arjun, a Dharamshala was built. Which of the following is correct regarding the context of the above two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation–The foundation of the Sikh religion was laid by Guru Nanak in Punjab. Actually, the history of Sikhs starts from the history of Sikh Gurus. A total of 10 Sikh Gurus happened. Sikh Dharamshala is that place where Sikhs used to sit and engage themselves in the worship of God. Guru Arjan Dev is also called Sacha Badshah (True Emperor). He got pools named Amritsar and Santokhsar built in Ramdaspur. In 1604 AD, he composed the Adi Granth. Thag Sajjan had surrendered before Guru Nanak.

questions.question_text: Match the books given in List-I with the names of their authors given in List-II and select the correct option from the codes given : List-I List-II (Books names) (Authors)
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– In the Mughal and Sultanate periods, various books were written. Some of them are as follows: Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi-Muhammad Qasim Ferishta, Tarikh-i-Firozshahi was composed by Ziauddin Barani and Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh was composed by Abdul Qadir Badauni and Akbarnama is a famous work of Abul Fazl.

questions.question_text: Which Sufi saint established the 'Suhrawardi Order' of Sufis in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– The main credit for the propagation of the Suhrawardi silsila in India goes to Bahauddin Zakariya and Jalaluddin Tabrizi. Their headquarters was in Multan. Zakariya helped Iltutmish against Qubacha, as a result of which Sultan Iltutmish gave him the title of 'Sheikh-ul-Islam'. The branch of this sect was established by Sheikh Shahabuddin Suhrawardi, who was a contemporary of Muhammad Ghaznavi.

questions.question_text: Which saint started the tradition of singing devotional songs in the form of Sankirtan and Nagarkirtan?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– Chaitanya was born in Nadiya (West Bengal). He is considered the founder of modern Vaishnavism. He did not oppose idol worship and gave God the name Hari or Krishna. He worshiped Radha-Krishna and encouraged this by singing Kirtan and Nagarkirtan in devotion. In the love of God, he sometimes used to faint while dancing.

questions.question_text: The author of the book 'Storia do Mogor', Niccolao Manucci was a native of–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– Manucci was a traveler from Venice (Italy) who came to India at the age of 14. After coming to India, he worked as an artilleryman for Dara Shikoh and after Dara's defeat in the war of succession, he adopted the profession of a physician. He wrote memoirs named Storia do Mogor which is called the mirror of the 17th-century India. After Dara's death, Manucci went into the service of Jai Singh. He died in 1717.

questions.question_text: In which state is the largest tomb in the world, Gol Gumbaz, situated?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Ibrahim Adil Shah II's son Muhammad Adil Shah became his successor. Muhammad Adil Shah is buried in the world-famous tomb named Gol Gumbaz (Karnataka), which is considered one of the architectural wonders of the world. Ibrahim Adil Shah II (1580-1627 AD) was a great scholar and patron of knowledge. Due to his liberal attitude, his subjects addressed him with the title of Jagatguru. He is also called Abla Baba and friend of the poor. He composed the Hindi song collection 'Kitab-i-Nauras'. During his reign, the historian Ferishta completed his book 'Tarikh-i-Ferishta'.

questions.question_text: What is not correct about the Ramdasi sect of Maharashtra?

options.A: The traditional feature of Ramdasis was their non-political attitude.
options.B: The Ramdasi sect was entirely composed of Brahmins.
options.C: Ramdasis were more directly connected to the Marathas.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Ramdas (1608-1681) was a famous saint of Maharashtra. He was the Guru of Chhatrapati Shivaji. He composed a book named Dasbodh which is in Marathi. Samarth Ramdas Ji created a conscious organized society in society through his disciples. The sect established by Samarth Ji is called Samarth sect or Ramdasi sect. The Ramdasi sect was entirely composed of Brahmins. Ramdasis were more directly connected to the Marathas. Ramdasis openly supported Shivaji.

questions.question_text: Who took the initiative to have the Upanishads translated into Persian?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– Shah Jahan's son Dara Shikoh got the Atharvaveda and Upanishads translated into Persian. He got 52 Upanishads translated into Persian under the name 'Sirr-i-Akbar' (Great Mystery). Dara Shikoh composed an original book 'Majma ul Bahrain' (confluence of two oceans). In which it has been told that Hindu and Islam religions are two paths to reach the same God.

questions.question_text: The construction work of Qutub Minar situated near Mehrauli in Delhi was completed by–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– Iltutmish (1210 to 1236 AD) who is called the real founder of the Slave dynasty. He completed the incomplete work of Qutub Minar situated in Delhi, which was built by Qutubuddin Aibak. Which was considered a prime example of early Islamic art. He started the customs and behavior of the Persian royal court in his court.

questions.question_text: The 'Adina Mosque' of North Bengal was built by–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– In the regional styles, a different style of architecture developed in Bengal. In this, bricks, bamboo, Gaur stone, and wood have been used in large quantities. The main center of architecture in Bengal was 'Pandua' where the 'Adina Mosque' built by Sikandar Shah is the largest Muslim building in India.

questions.question_text: 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' and 'Masnavi' were literary works of–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– The Mughal emperor Babur himself wrote his autobiography Tuzuk-i-Baburi or Baburnama in the Turkish language. He also composed Masnavi. Elphinstone has written that Tuzuk-i-Baburi is the only book of real history found in Asia.

questions.question_text: Whose reign is called the 'Golden Age of Architecture'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– In Mughal-era history, from the perspective of architecture, Shah Jahan's era is considered the Golden Age. Built by him are Agra's Taj Mahal, Delhi's Jama Masjid, Moti Masjid in Agra fort, Diwan-i-Khas, Sheesh Mahal, Diwan-i-Aam, and Nagina Masjid, etc.

questions.question_text: "The rule is that the favored servant puts the back of his right hand on the ground and then lifts it up slowly, when the person stands straight he places the palm of his hand on the middle part of his head." Abul Fazl indicates which method of obeisance (dandavat pranam) in the above statement?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– 'Taslim' is a method of obeisance which Abul Fazl has mentioned. In 'Taslim', the rule is that the favored servant puts the back of his right hand on the ground and then lifts it up slowly, when the person stands straight he places the palm of his hand on the middle part of his head. Sijda and Paibos are also a method of obeisance. Sijda (sitting on knees and bowing head) and Paibos (kissing the sultan's foot) were started by Balban.

questions.question_text: North India's Bhakti movement developed around the devotion of –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– Among the saints giving momentum to the Bhakti movement in North India, Ram devotee Goswami Tulsidas and Krishna devotee Surdas have an important place. The beginning of the Bhakti movement is considered from the time of Shankaracharya. Ramanuja developed it. Swami Ramananda brought the Bhakti movement to North India in the 14th century.

questions.question_text: Ravidas was a disciple of–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation– Swami Ramananda was born in 1299 AD in a Kanyakubja Brahmin family of Prayag. He broke the bonds of the caste system and made people of all castes his disciples. Kabir, Ravidas, Dhanna, etc., were his disciples. He made women like Padmavati and Surasari his disciples.

questions.question_text: Who got the Red Fort of Delhi built?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation– The construction of the Red Fort of Delhi was got done by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. The construction of this fort was done after the establishment of the Shahjahanabad city in 1638. In this, Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas and Rang Mahal are especially famous buildings.

questions.question_text: Which is the first building in the Mughal period that is made entirely of marble?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb is the first Mughal-era building which is built entirely of marble. It is situated in Agra. Its construction was done by Nur Jahan in 1626 AD based on the Persian style. Pietra Dura was used for the first time in this.

questions.question_text: Who founded the Patna city?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – As a famous building constructor, Sher Shah's tomb in Sasaram is considered the pinnacle of the pre-era style and the indicator of the beginning of the new style. He destroyed the Kannauj city and founded a city named 'Sher Sur' and the modern Patna city in ancient Pataliputra.

questions.question_text: Who built a magnificent tomb in Sasaram?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – During his short tenure of rule, Sher Shah also did the work of building buildings. His best work is his own tomb in Sasaram (Bihar). Dr. Qanungo has written about it "Muslim from outside and Hindu from inside". Built on a platform in the middle of a lake, Sher Shah's tomb is undoubtedly one of the best buildings in India.

questions.question_text: Agra city was built by –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Agra city was built in 1504 AD by Sikandar Lodi. He founded this city with the aim of establishing control over trade routes. In Agra itself, he also got built the Badalgarh fort. He declared Agra as his capital in 1506 AD.

questions.question_text: Which period did art historian Percy Brown call the 'period of tombs'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation– Art historian Percy Brown called the Saiyid and Lodi period the 'period of tombs'. In the buildings built in this time, Mubarak Shah Saiyid, Muhammad Shah Saiyid and Sultan Lodi's tombs were built.

questions.question_text: Which Sanskrit work was not translated into Persian under Dara Shikoh's patronage?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation– Under Dara Shikoh's patronage, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita and Yoga Vashistha were translated into Persian. Apart from this, he got 52 Upanishads translated into Persian under the name 'Sirr-i-Akbar' with the help of scholars of Kashi. It should be known that Bhagavata Purana was translated into Persian in Akbar's time by Todarmal. Grant Duff has written that in the second half of the seventeenth century, the rise of the Marathas was like a 'sudden fire'.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and choose your answer from the codes written below~ List-I List-II A. Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh w. Bhimsen Burhanpuri B. Lubb-ut-Tawarikh x. Ishwardas Nagar C. Futuhat-i-Alamgiri y. Rai Vrindavan D. Nuskha-i-Dilkusha z. Sujan Rai Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– List-I List-II Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh - Sujan Rai Lubb-ut-Tawarikh - Rai Vrindavan Futuhat-i-Alamgiri - Ishwardas Nagar Nuskha-i-Dilkusha - Bhimsen Burhanpuri

questions.question_text: The Sultan who wrote poems by the name 'Gulrukhi' was-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517) was the second son of Bahlul Lodi. His name was Nizam Shah. He assumed the title of Sultan Sikandar Shah. His mother was a goldsmith Hindu. He used to write poems in Persian by his pen name 'Gulrukhi'.

questions.question_text: The prominent Acharyas of Sanak sect are considered to be–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– The prominent Acharya of Sanak (Sanakadi) sect is considered to be Nimbarkacharya. The founder of Shri sect is Ramanujacharya (considered an avatar of Sheshnag), the founder of Brahma sect is Madhvacharya, and the founder of Rudra sect is Vishnu Swami.

questions.question_text: The Vaishnava saint who gave his sermons in the Hindi language–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Vaishnava saint Ramananda gave his sermons in Hindi language. It is noteworthy that Ramananda was born in 1299 in a Kanyakubja Brahmin family of Prayag, his education took place in Prayag and Varanasi. He made Raghavananda his guru. Raghavananda was a great saint of 'Shri sect'.

questions.question_text: Among the following Mughal painters, who are known for making portraits of themselves?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The founder of Mughal painting is considered to be Humayun. During his exile in Persia, he met Mir Saiyid Ali and Khwaja Abdus Samad. With the cooperation of these disciples of Bihzad, Humayun laid the foundation of Mughal painting in India. The leading painter of Akbar's time was Daswanth. Jahangir's time was the golden age from the point of view of Mughal painting, the Emperor himself was a skilled painter. In the Mughal period, Manohar, Daulat, and Keshavdas are known for making portraits of themselves.

questions.question_text: Who started the practice of the Persian festival 'Nauroz'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The practice of the Persian festival Nauroz was started by Balban (1265-1287). It is noteworthy that Balban started the custom of Sijda and Paibos (bowing before the Emperor and kissing his feet) in his court and Mughal ruler Shah Jahan ended this custom. This was originally Persian and it was considered non-Islamic. Balban considered himself a descendant of the Persian ruler Afrasiyab.

questions.question_text: Match the following and select the correct answer from the codes given below – A. Jama Masjid (i) Sikandar Lodi B. Moth Mosque (ii) Ibrahim Shah Sharqi C. Panjeri Mosque (iii) Hussain Shah Sharqi D. Hazara Sutun Palace (iv) Qutubuddin Aibak E. Quwwat-ul-Islam (v) Alauddin Khalji Codes: A B C D E
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Jaunpur Mosques – This mosque is situated on the southern bank of the Gomti river in Jaunpur. Ibrahim Shah Sharqi got it built during the time of Atala and Khalis Mukhlis Mosque. This Sihana locality was established by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi himself. Moth Masjid – Moth Masjid, which literally means 'Lentil Mosque'. It was built in 1505 by Wazir Miyan Bhua, who was the Prime Minister during the reign of Sultan Sikandar Lodi. Jama Masjid – This largest mosque of Jaunpur was built by Hussain Shah Sharqi in 1470 A.D. A high and attractive dome is built in the inner part of the prayer hall. Hazar Situn Palace – Alauddin Khalji's original name was Ali Gurshasp. During his reign, the Siri Fort, Hazar-Situn Palace, Hauz-i-Alai, Hauz-i-Khas, and circular 'Alai Darwaza' or 'Kushk-i-Shikar' were constructed. Quwwat-ul-Islam – Qutb-ud-din Aibak was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate and the founder of the Slave Dynasty. He got mosques named 'Quwwat-ul-Islam' (in place of Vishnu temple) built in Delhi and 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' (in place of a Sanskrit school) built in Ajmer.

questions.question_text: Who are called the leaders of the Sikh movement –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Guru Nanak (1469-1539) was the founder of the Sikh religion. He was born in 1469 A.D. in a Khatri family in Nankana Sahib, Punjab. He believed in the worship of a formless God. He fiercely criticized religious hypocrisy and emphasized Hindu-Muslim unity. He led the Sikh movement.

questions.question_text: The book named 'Dasbodh' was written by –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The credit for propagating the Bhakti movement in Maharashtra goes to Samarth Guru Ramdas. He was born in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, in 1608 A.D. He was the spiritual guru of Shivaji. His spiritual creation is "Dasbodh", in which the methods of spiritual practice have been described.

questions.question_text: When did Akbar abolish 'Jizya'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Akbar imposed a ban on pilgrimage tax in 1563 A.D. He abolished the Jizya tax in 1564 A.D. He made Fatehpur Sikri the capital in 1571. It is noteworthy that Akbar built 'Ibadat Khana' in Fatehpur Sikri (in 1575 A.D.) to hold discussions on philosophical and theological questions. Collecting the essence of all religions, he started a religion named Din-i-Ilahi in 1582 A.D., of which he himself was the chief interpreter. The first Hindu king to join this religion was Birbal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following forts was not built by Akbar?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Agra Fort, Lahore Fort, and Allahabad Fort were built by Akbar. The Delhi Fort, Moti Masjid of Agra (it is also called Masjid-i-Jahanuma), etc., were built by Shah Jahan.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below – List-I | List-II A. Namdev | (i) West Bengal B. Chaitanya | (ii) Uttar Pradesh D. Nanak | (iv) Punjab Code: | A | B | C | D C. Surdas | (iii) Maharashtra
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Namdev - Maharashtra, Chaitanya - West Bengal, Surdas - Uttar Pradesh, Guru Nanak - Punjab.

questions.question_text: Who was the person who translated 'Srimad Bhagavata' into the Bengali language during the time of Hussain Shah –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – During the reign of Hussain Shah (ruler of Bengal), Maladhar Basu translated Srimad Bhagavata into the Bengali language. Barbak Shah had conferred the title of Gunaraj Khan upon Maladhar Basu.

questions.question_text: How many years older was Amir Khusrau than Barani?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Amir Khusrau was a great scholar of his time who had seen the rule of eight Sultans. He was born in 1253 A.D. in Patiyali village of Kasganj district of U.P. Ziauddin Barani was born in 1285 A.D. in Baran (modern Bulandshahr) of Uttar Pradesh. At that time, Balban was the Sultan of Delhi. He remained under the patronage of Muhammad bin Tughlaq for 17 years. After the death of Muhammad Tughlaq, he remained under the patronage of Firoz Shah Tughlaq for 6 years. Because of this, Firoz Tughlaq became displeased. Due to which, the last life of Barani was spent in financial crisis. In praise of Firoz Shah, he composed a book in the Persian language named 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi'. In his book, he described the events up to the initial reign (6 years) of Firoz Shah. Khusrau was 32 years older than Barani.

questions.question_text: The main deity of the 'Warkari sect' is –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – In the Warkari sect, Bal Krishna is worshipped in the form of "Vitthal". The tradition of Vitthal worship in South India was started by Namdev. The three great Gurus of the Vitthal Panth were - 1. Dnyaneshwar or Dnyandev, 2. Namdev, 3. Tukaram.

questions.question_text: Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya was born in –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya was born in Budaun in 1236 A.D. He was a disciple of Baba Farid. At the age of twenty, he went to Ajodhan where he accepted the discipleship of Baba Farid. In 1258 A.D., he came to Delhi and started the propagation of his teachings from here. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya is also called 'Mahbub-i-Ilahi' and 'Sultan-ul-Auliya'.

questions.question_text: The name of that medieval Indian saint-poet who advocated the path of 'Nipak' –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Saint Dadu Dayal advocated the path of 'Nipak'. He was a resident of Gujarat; he founded the Brahma sect. The sect started by Dadu was called Dadu Panth. Dadu's teaching was - "Be humble and free from ego." Dadu's teachings are compiled in the book named 'Dadu Ram Ki Vani'.

questions.question_text: The place where Ramanuja used to do teaching work –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Ramanuja used to do teaching work in Srirangam. He was born in Sriperumbudur near Kanchipuram. Living in the monastery of Srirangam, he propagated Vaishnava religion. As a result of his tireless propagation, this religion kept increasing progressively.

questions.question_text: The 'Bhedabheda' doctrine was propounded by –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Nimbarka was a contemporary of Ramanuja. He was a devotee of Radha-Krishna. He had propounded the philosophical doctrine named Dvaitadvaita or Bhedabheda, according to which the difference between the soul and the Supreme Soul appears, but there is no difference. Apart from this, Ramanujacharya (Vishishtadvaita), Vallabhacharya (Shuddhadvaita), Madhvacharya (Dvaitavada) were supporters of the sects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following painters of Jahangir's court was famous for painting natural subjects?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Ustad Mansur adorned Jahangir's court. He was very skilled in painting natural subjects. The paintings of rare animals, birds, and flowers, etc., by Ustad Mansur are especially worth seeing. Jahangir conferred upon him the title of Nadir-ul-Asr. Along with him, Bishandas, Abul Hasan, Agha Reza were other painters of Jahangir's time.

questions.question_text: Who among the following wrote 'Tabaqat-i-Akbari'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – The composition of Abdul Qadir Badauni is Tarikh-i-Badauni, whereas Tarikh-i-Sher Shahi is the work of Abbas Khan Sherwani. Nizamuddin Ahmad wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari, whereas Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama.

questions.question_text: Which of the following books is not a work of Dara Shikoh?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – 'Dara Nama' is not a work of Dara Shikoh. Dara Shikoh translated 52 Upanishads under the name 'Sirr-i-Akbar' and he also wrote a book named 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' (Meeting of two oceans). The Hindi version of Majma-ul-Bahrain is Samudra Sangam.

questions.question_text: The concept of 'Sulh-i-kul' was based on –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – Akbar felt that the objective of all religions is the same. Hence, he adopted the path of religious harmony, i.e., taking good things from all religions. This was called 'Sulh-i-kul'. It contained the monotheism of Islam (principle of Wahdat-al-Wujud), while according to Parsi religion, the Sun and Fire were to be worshipped as the light and radiance of that God. The non-violence of Hindu and Jain religions had a deep impact on this religion.

questions.question_text: Akbar opened the Ibadat-Khana of Fatehpur Sikri for non-Muslim scholars –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – The Ibadat Khana was built by Akbar in Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 A.D. In this, discussions on religious subjects used to take place under the chairmanship of the Emperor. In which initially only Saiyids, Sheikhs, and Ulema used to participate, but in 1578 A.D., Akbar opened its doors for followers of all religions.

questions.question_text: The author of 'Prem Vatika' was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – Bhakti-era Muslim Krishna-devotee poet Raskhan, whose real name was Saiyid Ibrahim, wrote Prem Vatika, 'Sujan Raskhan' titled compositions in Savaiya, Kavitta, and Doha meters. Raskhan, a disciple of Swami Vitthalnath, has his entire composition in Braj Bhasha.

questions.question_text: The names of Abul Fazl's compositions are –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2009 TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Abul Fazl, one of the nine gems (Navratnas) of Akbar, wrote 'Akbarnama'. 'Ain-i-Akbari' is also the third part of this 'Akbarnama' book. In the three parts of Akbarnama, the first part describes the history of Mughal rulers from Timur to Humayun. Whereas the second and third parts contain the recorded history of Emperor Akbar up to 1602 A.D.

questions.question_text: 'Kalila wa Dimna' is an Arabic adaptation of which of the following books –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation – 'Kalila' and 'Dimna' is an Arabic adaptation of Panchatantra. The Persian translation of Mahabharata was done under the name 'Razmnama'. The translation of Panchatantra into Persian language is done under the name 'Anwar-i-Suhaili'. The translation of Sinhasan Battisi into Persian language was done by Abdul Qadir Badauni under the name 'Nama-i-Khirad Afza'.

questions.question_text: Which is the best specimen of Lodi era architecture?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – The Moth Masjid built by Lodi rulers holds an important place, which is built on an octagonal dome. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan has written while praising it that this is a beautiful gift of Lodi architecture in shape. Sir John Marshall has also praised it. He has called it one of the best specimens of Lodi era architectural style. Sikandar Lodi's Prime Minister Miyan Bhua (Bhuya) got the Moth Masjid built in Delhi.

questions.question_text: The history of medieval India was written in –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – During the medieval period in India, Turkish rule was established, who were mainly residents of Arabia, but their original language was Persian. Therefore, the history that was written at that time was recorded in the official language, Persian. For which the word 'Tawarikh' was used.

questions.question_text: There were many effects of the Bhakti movement. Which of the following was not an effect of the Bhakti movement?

options.B: Loosening of the bonds of the caste system

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – The Bhakti movement was a great feature of the medieval period. The Bhakti movement was started by Ramanuja in South India and by Ramananda in North India. Due to the Bhakti movement, many positive reforms took place in Hindu and Muslim religions. The proponents of Bhakti movements emphasized Hindu-Muslim unity and synthesis, gave a message of peace and brotherhood to humanity, by which they were successful in bringing Hindus and Muslims closer. Religion was no longer the exclusive right of Brahmins but became a subject of the common people. In the 14th and 15th centuries, great saints like Kabir, Pipa, Dhana, Raidas were born in the lower class of Hindu society. Due to which the bond of the caste system loosened. Many saints gave sermons in regional languages, due to which regional languages developed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct according to the sale deed document slave letter method (1230 A.D.) described in Lekh Paddhati?

options.A: Wars were an important source of acquiring slaves.
options.B: Slaves were sold in the open market.
options.C: If a slave commits suicide, the owner should be held responsible and he should be punished.
options.D: Choosing the Rakshapal (guard) and residents of the city as witnesses for the implementation of the document.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – If a slave commits suicide, the owner should be held responsible and he should be punished. This statement is not correct according to the sale deed document slave letter method (1230 A.D.) described in Lekh Paddhati.

questions.question_text: The year of issuing 'Mahzar' was:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – In 1579 A.D., Akbar got it prepared by Sheikh Mubarak and he himself read the Khutbah in his name in the Jama Masjid of Fatehpur. And Akbar declared himself in the form of Imam-i-Adil or Sultan-i-Adil through the Mahzar. This Mahzar had the signatures of Sadr-us-Sudur Abdulnabi, Makhdum-ul-Mulk, Jalaluddin Multani, Sadr-i-Jahan Ghazi Khan Badakhshi, Sheikh Mubarak, and other Ulema. Sheikh Mubarak was the father of historian Abul Fazl and poet Faizi, all related to Agra in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question_text: "Alai Darwaza is the most beautiful gem of the treasury of Islamic architectural art." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – "Alai Darwaza is the most beautiful gem of the treasury of Islamic architectural art." This statement belongs to Marshall. Alai Darwaza was constructed by the Khalji Sultan Alauddin Khalji.

questions.question_text: With the arrival of the Turks, which language started in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – With the arrival of the Turks, the beginning of the Persian language is considered in India. Lahore was the first center for Persian development. During the Sultanate period, books were written in Persian, Sanskrit, Hindi, and Urdu.

questions.question_text: Amir Khusrau was a famous disciple of?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Amir Khusrau was a disciple of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. Amir Khusrau holds a superior place among Persian poets. He holds the credit for inventing the Sitar and Tabla. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya was born in Budaun in Uttar Pradesh. He had seen the reign of 7 Sultans of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given codes: List-I | List-II A. Kabir | 1. Farmer B. Raidas | 2. Barber C. Sena | 3. Cobbler D. Dhanna | 4. Weaver Code: | A | B | C | D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The correct matching will be as follows – List-I | List-II Kabir | - | Weaver Raidas | - | Cobbler Sena | - | Barber Dhanna | - | Farmer

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given codes: List-I | List-II A. Tomb in Sasaram | 1. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah B. Fatehpur Sikri | 2. Shah Jahan C. Jama Masjid | 3. Akbar D. Charminar | 4. Sher Shah Code: | A | B | C | D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The correct matching will be as follows – List-I | List-II Tomb in Sasaram | - | Sher Shah Fatehpur Sikri | - | Akbar Jama Masjid | - | Shah Jahan Charminar | - | Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah

questions.question_text: Mansur and Madhav were chief painters of whose court?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation – The chief painters of Jahangir's court were Abul Hasan, Ustad Mansur, Farrukh Beg, Bishandas, Aqa Riza, Madhav, and Govardhan. Among these, Ustad Mansur was a famous bird-specialist painter, whereas the leading painter was Bishandas.

questions.question_text: In which part of the Mughal monument are arches found?

options.B: Walls on all four sides of the fort

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Arches are found on the main gate of Mughal monuments. During the time of Mughal Emperor Akbar, the use of the arched style in buildings started in equal proportion with the beam style (trabeate style).

questions.question_text: Aurangzeb completely banned the Sati system in the year 1663 A.D. Before this, which Mughal ruler attempted to stop the Sati system?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Aurangzeb completely banned the Sati system in the year 1663 A.D. Before this, Akbar had attempted to put a ban on the Sati system. By the 19th century, Sati system was completely prohibited by Lord William Bentinck legally in 1829 under Regulation 17.

questions.question_text: Which building is not constructed in Fatehpur Sikri by Akbar?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The construction of Sheesh Mahal in Agra Fort was done by Shah Jahan. Apart from this, Akbar had the other three buildings mentioned in the question constructed in Fatehpur Sikri.

questions.question_text: Tansen invented which of the following musical styles/musical instruments?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Tansen was one of the Navratnas of Akbar. Akbar conferred upon him the title of 'Kanthabharana Vani Vilas'. Tansen invented Miyan Ki Todi, Darbari Kanada raga, and Rudra Veena (musical instrument).

questions.question_text: What view is most appropriate regarding Sher Shah's religious policy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Sher Shah believed in religious tolerance. He had assumed the title of 'Sultan-ul-Adl'. His justice-loving nature was very impartial and strict.

questions.question_text: 'Akbarnama' was written in which language?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Abul Fazl wrote 'Akbarnama' in the Persian language. This book is divided into three parts; its last part is Ain-i-Akbari.

questions.question_text: Who said about Mughal-era architecture that "The Mughal period is the summer of Indian architecture which is considered a symbol of light and fertility"?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Percy Brown has said that "The Mughal period is the summer of Indian architecture which is considered a symbol of light and fertility."

questions.question_text: Which of the following books is the autobiography of Firoz Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Firoz Tughlaq (1351-1388 A.D.) wrote his autobiography 'Futuhat-i-Firozshahi'. 'Futuhat-i-Firozshahi' has a total of eight chapters. It mentions the various orders of the administration and the buildings constructed by him. Tarikh-i-Firozshahi is a work of Ziauddin Barani.

questions.question_text: Tell the name of that Sufi saint who saw the rule of seven Sultans in Delhi?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya had seen the reigns of seven Sultans in Delhi, who kept ascending one after another, but he never went to anyone's court.

questions.question_text: Which of the following places was a major center of Hindu education during the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The major centers of Hindu education in the Mughal period were Banaras, Mathura, Allahabad, Ayodhya, Nadia, Mithila, Srinagar, etc., among which Banaras has been a center for education of Hindu religious texts, Sanskrit literature, and Sanskrit language since ancient times.

questions.question_text: In the languages prevalent during the Mughal period, one was Rekhta. What was the popular name of this language?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Among the languages prevalent during the Mughal period, there was also 'Urdu', which over time came to be called Rekhta. The birth of the Urdu language took place during the Sultanate period and in the beginning, it was called 'Zaban-e-Hindvi'.

questions.question_text: During whose reign did portrait painting develop the most?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – In the Mughal period, the maximum development of painting took place during the reign of Jahangir, but portrait painting, i.e., Shabah/individual painting, had received prominence during the reign of Akbar.

questions.question_text: Which of the following books is not of the Akbar era?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Padshahnama or Badshahnama is a work of Shah Jahan's time. It starts from the history of Timur-Lang. It was written sequentially by Muhammad Amin Qazvini (wrote history up to the initial ten years), Abdul Hamid Lahori (died during writing history), Muhammad Waris (completed the remaining history). The other three books mentioned in the option are of the Akbar era. In which Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl, Tabaqat-i-Akbari by its author Nizamuddin Ahmad, and Tarikh-i-Badauni was written by Abdul Qadir Badauni.

questions.question_text: Who was the only Sultan of Delhi who wrote his autobiography?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – The only Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate is Firoz Tughlaq who wrote his autobiography in the Persian language, the name of which is 'Futuhat-i-Firozshahi'.

questions.question_text: Nizamuddin Auliya was related to which of the following Silsilas?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Nizamuddin Auliya was related to the Chishti order. He saw the reign of seven sultans of the Delhi Sultanate but never went to anyone's court. Nizamuddin Auliya was given the titles of 'Mahbub-i-Ilahi' and 'Sultan-ul-Auliya'. Amir Khusro was his chief disciple. He was born in Badaun in Uttar Pradesh and died in Delhi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following officials was the protector of Islamic law?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Qazi-ul-Quzat was the protector of Islamic law. He was related to religious matters along with the judiciary department. The main duty of the Muhtasib was to keep the conduct of the public high. He was the head of the public conduct inspection department. Sadr-us-Sudur was related to the religious department. He was the chief officer of the religious department. Khan-i-Saman (Saman) used to be the chief officer of the royal kitchen.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered the earliest example of a 'double dome'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Humayun's tomb is considered the earliest example of a double dome. Its construction was commissioned by Humayun's wife Hamida Banu Begum (Haji Begum). The engraving of this tomb was prepared by the Persian sculptor Mirak Mirza Ghiyas. The Charbagh style was used for the first time in Humayun's tomb and it is situated in Delhi.

questions.question_text: Which Mughal emperor was an excellent connoisseur of painting?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 TGT History, 2005 Explanation ─ Mughal-era ruler Jahangir was an excellent connoisseur of painting. In Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, he writes, "My interest in painting and proficiency in identifying reached this extent that I could tell by looking at a painting which artist's work it is." The best painters of Jahangir's time were Ustad Mansur and Abul Hasan.

questions.question_text: The book 'Anwar-i-Suhaili' is a Persian translation of─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Anwar-i-Suhaili is a Persian translation of the Panchatantra. Kalila Dimna has been translated into the Persian language under the name Yar-i-Danish, and its translator is Abul Fazl.

questions.question_text: Who built Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Nur Jahan built the tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula in the Iranian style in 1626 AD. It is an important tomb among Jahangir-era buildings. Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb is dedicated to Nur Jahan's father Mirza Ghiyas Beg, situated in Agra city of Uttar Pradesh state. After emperor Jahangir sat on the throne, Mirza Ghiyas Beg was given the title of Itmad-ud-Daula. Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb is the first tomb built in India that was made entirely of marble.

questions.question_text: Among the following writers, who was a fierce critic of Akbar?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Abdul Qadir Badauni, who wrote the book named Tarikh-i-Badauni or Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh. Emperor Akbar appointed him to the post of Imam. He has criticized Akbar's religious thoughts. Badauni was an orthodox Sunni Muslim, so he weighed everything on the scale of Sharia. Naturally, he used to criticize Akbar's liberal religious policy. He has also made many accusations against Akbar of oppressing Muslims, but there is no truth in them.

questions.question_text: The important book of Aurangzeb's reign 'Futuhat-i-Alamgiri' was written by whom?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The author of the important book of Aurangzeb's reign, 'Futuhat-i-Alamgiri', was Ishwardas Nagar. Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was against history writing. This book has seven chapters, which contain a detailed history from Aurangzeb's rise to the 34th year of his reign.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book named 'Nuskha-i-Dilkusha' during Aurangzeb's reign?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The book named Nuskha-i-Dilkusha was written by Bhimsen. Ishwardas wrote Futuhat-i-Alamgiri. Bhimsen was among those Aurangzeb-era Hindu historians who wrote their books in the Persian language. Earlier, he worked as a Mushrif in the Bijapur artillery. Bhimsen has written an eyewitness account in his book Nuskha-i-Dilkusha and since it was not written under the patronage of any emperor, there is no flattery visible in the book. He has also shed light on economic and social aspects.

questions.question_text: Which monument is called 'Taj Mahal of the Deccan'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Bibi ka Maqbara is called the Taj Mahal of the Deccan. Mughal emperor Aurangzeb built this tomb in 1678 AD in Aurangabad in memory of his beloved wife Rabia-ud-Daurani (Rabia-ud-Durrani). Its architectural style is based on the Taj Mahal. Bibi ka Maqbara is called a poor copy of the Taj Mahal.

questions.question_text: In memory of which victory was the Buland Darwaza built by Akbar in Fatehpur Sikri?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The Buland Darwaza in Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar in memory of the Gujarat victory. It is a gate built on a 42-foot high platform, which is 134 feet high. That is, the height from the ground is 176 feet.

questions.question_text: Which style of painting did Nihal Chand enrich?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Nihal Chand enriched the Kishangarh style of painting. Kishangarh was a small principality situated between Ajmer and Jaipur. Nihal Chand was a high-quality painter of the Kishangarh style.

questions.question_text: Who of the following did not contribute to the construction of Qutub Minar?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Qutbuddin Aibak was the Sultan of Delhi from 1206 to 1210 AD. He laid the foundation of Qutub Minar in Delhi in the name of the famous Sufi saint "Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki". The construction of this minaret was completed during the time of Iltutmish. It was initially built with four storeys. During the time of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, the top storey was damaged due to a lightning strike, in place of which Firoz Shah Tughlaq built two storeys. At present, there are a total of five storeys in it. It was generally used for giving Azaan (call to prayer).

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below. One is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): The middle-Persian poet of the Tughlaq period, Badr Chach, who came some time after Amir Khusro, said about music, 'There are no more than twelve basic modes (parda)', and he links each of them with specific parts of day and night. Reason (R): Amir Khusro talks about only ten modes (tariqas). There is similarity in the information found in the lists given by these two poets and in old dictionaries and music books. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following options is correct?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – The middle-Persian poet of the Tughlaq period, Badr Chach, who came some time after Amir Khusro, said about music, 'There are no more than twelve basic modes (parda)', and he links each of them with specific parts of day and night. This statement is correct. Whereas, the reason that Amir Khusro talks about only ten modes (tariqas). There is similarity in the information found in the lists given by these two poets and in old dictionaries and music books, is incorrect.

questions.question_text: In whose reign was the Shahi Qila of Jaunpur built?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Jaunpur city was founded by Firoz Tughlaq. The founder of the Jaunpur kingdom was Malik Sarwar (Malik-us-Sharq). During the time of Ibrahim Shah, Jaunpur became an important cultural centre and the Shahi Qila of Jaunpur was built during the time of Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

questions.question_text: In which building are the features of Hindu architecture clearly visible? (Because material obtained by demolishing temples was used in it)
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Qutbuddin Aibak was the Sultan of India from 1206 to 1210 AD. In the initial years of his reign, he attacked Ajmer and built 'Adhai Din ka Jhopra'. It is said that Adhai Din ka Jhopra was previously a temple of Goddess Saraswati, which was demolished to build a mosque named Adhai Din ka Jhopra.

questions.question_text: Who was the officer of the judicial department in Babur's administration?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - During Babur's time, the head of the judicial department in his administration was Sadr. Sadr-us-Sudur was also called Sheikh-ul-Islam. Sadr-us-Sudur was sometimes given the post of Chief Qazi as well. That is, when he acted as the head of the judicial department, then he was called 'Qazi-ul-Quzat'.

questions.question_text: Who gave the name 'Grand Trunk Road' to Sarak-i-Azam/Sadak-i-Azam?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Sher Shah had many roads built and got old roads repaired in his time. The initial construction of Sarai-i-Azam/Sadak-i-Azam as Grand Trunk Road was done by Sher Shah. It was given the name Grand Trunk Road later by the British.

questions.question_text: In Mughal administration, who was known as 'Daroga-i-Topkhana'?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - In Mughal administration, Mir Atish was known as 'Daroga-i-Topkhana', meaning he was the head of the royal artillery. This was not a ministerial post. On his recommendation, Kotwals were appointed by the centre in important cities.

questions.question_text: Who translated Tuzuk-i-Baburi into the Persian language?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Babur took great interest in literature. He wrote his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' (Baburnama) in the Turkish language. It was translated into Persian three times. During Humayun's time by Zain Khan and Payanda Hasan Khan, during Akbar's time by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, and during Shah Jahan's time by Mir Abul Talib Turbati.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Hindu to attain literary proficiency in Persian during the medieval period?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - The first Hindu to attain literary proficiency in Persian during the medieval period was Chandrabhan.

questions.question_text: The Mughal princess who established a library (Bait-ul-Uloom) in Delhi was:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Mughal princess Zeb-un-Nissa established a library (Bait-ul-Uloom) in Delhi. Zeb-un-Nissa was Aurangzeb's daughter. Aurangzeb's eldest son was Akbar II, who revolted against Aurangzeb, for which Aurangzeb tried to arrest him. But Akbar II fled to Iran. Zeb-un-Nissa used to correspond with her brother, due to which Aurangzeb put Zeb-un-Nissa in jail.

questions.question_text: Who translated the Ramayana into the Persian language?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation - Akbar's poet laureate Faizi was the best poet of his time. Akbar formed a 'Translation Department' under his chairmanship. At this time, Akbar ordered Abdul Qadir Badauni to translate the Ramayana into Persian. Badauni did translate it. But he was very sad that he had to write the names of Hindu gods and goddesses with his own hand.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi was written by Shams-i-Siraj Afif. This book contains a detailed description of all events of the reign of Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq from beginning to end. He has presented Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq as an ideal sultan. Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq himself wrote Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi.

questions.question_text: The design of Sher Shah's tomb in Sasaram is:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - The construction of 'Octagonal' tombs is found in the graves of rulers in the Sayyid dynasty. The rulers of the Lodi dynasty also continued this tradition. Sher Shah's tomb is built in the middle of a pond in Sasaram, Bihar. This tomb is built in an octagonal shape.

questions.question_text: Which musician was given the title of 'Gun Samudra' by Shah Jahan?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - Shah Jahan was a great patron of musicians. In his court, there were singers like Khushal Khan and Bisram Khan and Lal Khan. Shah Jahan gave the title of 'Gun Samudra' to Lal Khan. Shah Jahan, pleased with the singing of his Sanskrit court poet Pandit Jagannath, gave him his own weight in gold as a reward. Pandit Jagannath was a court poet of Shah Jahan. He has written Rasgangadhar and Gangalahari.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Jharokha Darshan was a new custom started by Akbar and its purpose was to establish a personal relationship between the ruler and his subjects. Reason (R): As Akbar's prestige increased, some people made a rule that they would not eat or drink anything until they had Darshan of the Badshah. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – Jharokha Darshan was a new custom started by Akbar and its purpose was to establish a personal relationship between the ruler and his subjects. As Akbar's prestige increased, some people made a rule that they would not eat or drink anything until they had Darshan of the Badshah. The above two statements and reason are correct and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.question_text: Most of the Muslim writers and poets who contributed to Hindi literature through their works were?

options.B: Sufi saints or followers of Sufism

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Most of the Muslim writers and poets who contributed to Hindi literature/language through their works were Sufi saints or followers of Sufi faith. The famous poet Amir Khusro, who first made the Hindi language the medium of his writing, was a disciple of the famous Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya.

questions.question_text: Who first used 'Fana' in the Sufi order among the following?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation – The use of 'Fana' in the Sufi order was first done by Abu Yazid. Abu Yazid was the founder of the Taifur order. Fana is the state of destruction of the worldly inclinations within the Sufi. The death of the human soul has been called Fana.

questions.question_text: Who built Itmad-ud-Daula's tomb in Agra?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation – Itmad-ud-Daula was a prominent mansabdar during the time of Akbar and Jahangir. He died during Jahangir's time. After the death of Itmad-ud-Daula, his daughter Nur Jahan built a beautiful tomb in Agra which is made almost entirely of marble.

questions.question_text: Ain-i-Akbari is a

options.A: Mughal history from Timur to Akbar.

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in 7 years, its last volume is 'Ain-i-Akbari', which is the statistical document of Akbar-era administration and empire.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of Alamgirnama?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Aurangzeb's official historian was Mirza Muhammad Kazim. Aurangzeb had entrusted him with the task of writing Alamgirnama. Some other people were engaged in this work along with Kazim.

questions.question_text: Who among the following assumed the title of Amir Khusro?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Abul Hasan Yaminuddin assumed the title of Amir Khusro. He was a prominent poet, singer, and musician living near Delhi around the fourteenth century.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Correctly matched order is as follows– Atala Masjid – Jaunpur Charminar – Hyderabad, Telangana Muhammad Adil Shah II – Bijapur tomb Firoz Shah Bahmani – Gulbarga tomb

questions.question_text: Which of the following books is written in Persian?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Hasht Bihisht is written in Persian. Whereas Babur wrote Baburnama in Turkish language. Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic. Whereas Ibn Battuta also wrote Rehla in the Arabic language.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Aurangzeb was born on 3 November 1618. He was a religious Muslim ruler. He became the Mughal emperor after defeating his brothers in the war of succession. During his time, the maximum number of Mughal provinces became 21. He died on 4 March 1707 in Aurangabad in the south. Aurangzeb was buried near the grave of Sheikh Zain-ul-Haq four miles away from Daulatabad.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was a good scholar of Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Al-Biruni was born in 973 AD in Khiva. In 1017 AD, Mahmud of Ghazni achieved victory over Khiva and made Al-Biruni a captive, and impressed by his scholarship, gave him a place in the court. Al-Biruni wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind in the Arabic language.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II A. Amir Khusro 1. Qadiriyya B. Mian Mir 2. Naqshbandiyya C. Shah Daula Daryai 3. Suhrawardiyya D. Shah Waliullah 4. Chishtiyya Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Amir Khusro was a disciple of the famous Sufi Nizamuddin Auliya, whose relation was with the Chishtiyya order. Sheikh Mian Mir's relation was with the Qadiriyya order, Shah Daula Daryai with the Suhrawardiyya silsila, and Shah Waliullah's relation was with the Naqshbandiyya order. Shah Waliullah's relation was with the Naqshbandi order.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II A. Futuhat-i-Alamgiri 1. Muhammad Kazim B. Maasir-i-Alamgiri 2. Khafi Khan C. Alamgirnama 3. Ishwardas Nagar D. Muntakhab-ul-Lubab 4. Saqi Mustaid Khan Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Futuhat-i-Alamgiri was written by Ishwardas Nagar during Aurangzeb's time and Maasir-i-Alamgiri was written by Saqi Mustaid Khan during Aurangzeb's time. Alamgirnama was written by Aurangzeb's official historian Muhammad Kazim, and Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II A. Tabaqat-i-Akbari 1. Nizamuddin Ahmed B. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri 2. Ziauddin Barani C. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi 3. Mulla Ahmed D. Tarikh-i-Alfi 4. Minhaj-us-Siraj Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmed. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is an important Sultanate-era book, which was written by Barani to please Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Tarikh-i-Alfi is a work of Mulla Ahmed.

questions.question_text: Regarding the interest of Mughal rulers in music, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Regarding Akbar's interest in music, Abul Fazl writes that 'the Badshah had so much knowledge of the science of music that even a skilled musician did not have'.
options.B: Shah Jahan patronized music in his court and it is said that he himself possessed significant proficiency in this art.
options.C: Many books on music were written during Aurangzeb's reign. Among these, the most famous Tuhfat-ul-Hind was written for Aurangzeb's grandson Jahandar Shah.
options.D: During the reign of Muhammad Shah, the most famous singers were Niyamat Khan Sadarang and Firoz Khan Adarang. He was a master of Bhairavi.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – Among the options given, option (d) that during the reign of Muhammad Shah, the most famous singers were Niyamat Khan Sadarang and Firoz Khan Adarang. He was a master of Bhairavi. This statement regarding the interest of Mughal rulers in music is not correct. Famous singers Niyamat Khan Sadarang and Firoz Khan Adarang are considered masters of Khayal singing. Khayal consists of a mixture of Indian and Persian music.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is not linked to Sufism?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Ulema were called religious people who were special knowers of the Quran, whereas words like Khanqah, Peer, and Sheikh are linked to Sufism. Sufi people were secular to some extent and respected people of other religions as well.

questions.question_text: Humayun's tomb is
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Humayun was the eldest among Babur's four sons. After Babur's death, he sat on the throne of Hindustan in 1530 AD, but in 1540 AD, Sher Shah ousted him from the throne. Humayun became the Badshah of Hindustan again in 1556 and died in the same year due to falling from the stairs. After his death, his tomb was built in Delhi.

questions.question_text: Baba Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar's tomb is situated in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Baba Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar was born in Multan. He liked solitude very much, so he made his residence far from Delhi. His tomb is situated in Pakpattan (Punjab) of Pakistan. He was a prestigious Sufi of the Chishti faith.

questions.question_text: Tulsidas was contemporary of
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Tulsidas was a contemporary of Akbar but he had no relation with Akbar's court. Tulsidas was a poet of the Saguna Bhakti branch and he wrote Sri Ramcharitmanas in the Awadhi language. In which there is the story of the family of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya.

questions.question_text: Prince Khusro was buried in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - Jahangir's first wife was Manbai. Manbai was the daughter of Bhagwandas. Prince Khusro was the son of this Manbai. There were differences between Jahangir and Khusro. After the sudden death of Khusro, Jahangir sent him to Allahabad to be buried. Where Khusro's grave is still there today. Named after him, there is also Khusro Bagh in Allahabad.

questions.question_text: Which famous Sufi saint was born in Awadh?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Famous Sufi saint 'Nasiruddin Mahmud Chirag-i-Delhi' was born in Awadh. Baba Farid was a famous Sufi saint of the Chishti order. Nizamuddin Auliya had seen the working period of seven sultans of Delhi. Bakhtiyar Kaki was known by the name of 'Roti' wale Baba.

questions.question_text: The reasons for the fame of the Chishtiyya silsila in the Deccan were:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Saiyid Muhammad 'Gesudaraz' preached and spread the Chishtiyya silsila in the Deccan. Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti has an important contribution in establishing the Chishti order in India. The main centre of the Chishti silsila was Ajmer. The credit for spreading the Chishti silsila in South India goes to Saiyid Muhammad Gesudaraz. Gesudaraz settled permanently in Gulbarga of Karnataka after the establishment of the Bahmani empire.

questions.question_text: Shalimar Bagh was built by
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - Shalimar Bagh was built by Jahangir in Srinagar in 1619 AD. Its construction was commissioned by Mughal Badshah Jahangir for his Begum Nur Jahan. The design of this garden is based on the Charbagh of Persia. This garden is known for its Chinese-khannas or arch-niches. Shalimar Bagh is spread over about 31 acres of land which is surrounded by Chinar trees on all sides.

questions.question_text: The concept of 'Wahdat-ul-Wujud' which Akbar supported meant
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - The concept of 'Wahdat-ul-Wujud' which Akbar supported meant purity of Islam. Akbar was religiously liberal despite being a powerful ruler, although he was quite religious in the early years of his reign. With time, a change occurred in him and he established 'Din-i-Ilahi'.

questions.question_text: The work 'Tuhfat-ul-Hind' is related to which subject?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - The work 'Tuhfat-ul-Hind' is related to the subject of music. Its author was Mirza Muhammad. Although music was prohibited in Islam, even then the Muslim rulers encouraged it a lot. Aurangzeb was the only ruler who strongly opposed music. This work was written for Aurangzeb's grandson Jahandar Shah.

questions.question_text: Who got the Bengali translation of Mahabharata and Ramayana done?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation - The Bengali translation of Mahabharata and Ramayana was commissioned by Nusrat Shah. Krittivasa translated the Ramayana and Kashiram translated the Mahabharata. Some Muslim rulers of Bengal were quite liberal, during whose reign people of Vaishnava and Nirguna Bhakti branch also got full opportunity to move forward. Alauddin Hussain Shah gave shelter to prominent writers in his court.

questions.question_text: Which famous Chishti saint was there, whose tomb was built in Fatehpur Sikri?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - When Akbar had no children, he used to meet Sheikh Salim Chishti in Fatehpur Sikri while going to Ajmer to the shrine of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. When Akbar had a son due to the blessings of Sheikh Salim Chishti, he built the tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti in Fatehpur Sikri, which is made of marble.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Sufis is known as 'Mujaddid' (reformer)?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Among the Sufi saints of the Naqshbandiyya order and disciples of Khwaja Baqi Billah was Sheikh Ahmed Faruq Sirhindi. Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi was famous as 'Mujaddid', i.e., reformer of the Islamic religion. He was born in Sirhind in 1563 AD.

questions.question_text: To which silsila was Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki related?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Among the disciples of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was prominent. He was born in 1186 AD in Farghana. He came to India during the reign of Sultan Iltutmish. Iltutmish wanted to appoint Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki to the high post of 'Sheikh-ul-Islam', but 'Kaki' refused.

questions.question_text: To which Sufi order was Dara Shikoh related?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - The Qadiriyya order was founded in Baghdad by Sheikh Muinuddin Qadir Jilani. In India, it was preached in the 15th century by Shah Niamatullah. Sheikh Mir Muhammad was the prominent Sufi of this silsila. Dara Shikoh went to Lahore with his father Shah Jahan to meet Sheikh Mir Muhammad.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Sufis did Iltutmish address as 'Father'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - Iltutmish (1210-1236 AD) addressed Sheikh Najmuddin Sughra as 'Father'. Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya was born in Punjab in 1170. They were also known as 'Waj-ul-Haq'. They were related to the Suhrawardi silsila. Whereas Nizamuddin Auliya was born in 1238 in Badaun (U.P.), they were disciples of Baba Farid. They received the title of Mahbub-i-Ilahi.

questions.question_text: Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was contemporary of
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - Khwaja Bakhtiyar Kaki was a contemporary of Sultan Iltutmish. He was the one who initiated Baba Farid into the Chishti tradition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the first white marble building built in Agra Fort?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - The first marble building built in Agra Fort is Diwan-i-Aam. Diwan-i-Aam was a rectangular courtyard. The Badshah's throne used to be kept here. Its main feature was the roof of the veranda projecting on pillars.

questions.question_text: To which Sufi silsila was Khwaja Baqi Billah related?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - During Akbar's reign (1556-1605 AD), the last Naqshbandi silsila among the six prominent silsilas was established in India by Khwaja Baqi Billah. Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi was a prominent Sufi saint of this silsila who was famous as 'Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani'. This was the most orthodox silsila in Sufism. They resisted (opposed) Akbar's liberal policies.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Sufis was called 'Qutb of that time'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - During the Lodi period, Shah Abulala Shattari founded the Shattari silsila. Shah Muhammad Ghaus (Gwalior) was the most famous saint of this order. He was called 'Qutb of that time'. Mughal rulers Humayun and Tansen were more influenced by Ghaus. Shattari Sufis made an earnest effort to bring Hindus and Muslims closer by showing parity in their religious thoughts and practices.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the book named 'Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - The book named 'Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi' was written by Yahya-bin-Ahmad Sirhindi. Yahya Ahmad Sirhindi had the patronage of Mubarak Shah, the ruler of the Sayyid dynasty. Yahya-bin-Ahmad wrote the history from the invasion of Muhammad Ghori to the third ruler of the Sayyid dynasty, Muhammad Shah. This book is the only source to know the history of the Sayyid dynasty.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correct?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Kali Masjid in Delhi was built during Firoz Shah's time. Its construction was commissioned by Juna Shah. This building equipped with semi-circular arches is an excellent specimen of Sultanate-era architecture. Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque was built by Qutbuddin Aibak in Delhi over the ruins of 27 Jain temples.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and tell the correct answer: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Sheikh Moinuddin Chishti laid the foundation of the Sufi tradition in India by making Ajmer the centre. The headquarters of Suhrawardi silsila's Bahauddin Zakariya was in Multan. Sheikh Fariduddin Masud Ganj-i-Shakar of the Chishti order was born in Multan but he propagated the Sufi faith in Hansi (Haryana) and Ajodhan (Punjab). Nizamuddin Auliya's tomb is situated in Delhi.

questions.question_text: Who brought the Bhakti movement from the South to the North?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Ramananda (14th century) was the first great Bhakti saint of North India. He was a disciple of Ramanuja. Ramananda acted as a bridge between the Bhakti movement of South and North India, i.e., brought the Bhakti movement from South to North India. He was born in Allahabad. He started the devotion of Ram instead of Vishnu.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a Chishti saint?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Sheikh Sadruddin Arif was not a Sufi saint (of the Chishti order). Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti came to India in 1192 AD with the army of Shihabuddin Muhammad Ghori and laid the foundation of the Sufi order named Chishti in India. He made Ajmer his residence. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya was also a Sufi saint of the Chishti order. His tomb is in Delhi. Sheikh Hamiduddin Nagauri was also a Sufi saint of the Chishtiyya order (12th century). Later he propagated the Suhrawardi faith. Sheikh Sadruddin Arif was not of the Chishti faith.

questions.question_text: Which of the following works is not Amir Khusro's?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Qiran-us-Sa'dain, Miftah-ul-Futuh, and Tughlaqnama etc., are works of Amir Khusro. Tarikh-i-Yamini is a work of Utbi, the court historian of Mahmud Ghaznavi. In this work, Utbi has praised Mahmud Ghaznavi.

questions.question_text: Who was the most famous painter of Jahangir's time?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Jahangir has declared Abul Hasan the best painter of his court. Jahangir has written in 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' that there is no painter like Abul Hasan at this time. Jahangir, impressed by his art, honoured him with the title of 'Nadir-uz-Zaman'.

questions.question_text: Which monument is famous by the name of 'Second Taj Mahal'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Rabia-ud-Daurani's tomb is famous by the name of 'Second Taj Mahal'. Sher Shah's tomb is situated in Sasaram (Bihar). Jahangir and Nur Jahan's tomb is situated in Shahdara of Lahore.

questions.question_text: Who among the Sufis was given the title of 'Turk-ullah'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Amir Khusro was quite close to Sufis, especially Nizamuddin Auliya, and through his poetry and music, he made a great contribution to the creation of India's Sufi culture. Amir Khusro became a disciple of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya, who is also called Mahbub-i-Ilahi and Sultan-ul-Auliya. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya also honoured Khusro with the term 'Turk-ullah'. Sufi saints have given this message to the public that the wall of discrimination between humans is useless. All humans are equal and they should be hugged with love. The goal of all religions is to reach the same place through different means and that is the realization of God. The entire human race is one; fighting in the name of religion and country is mere foolishness.

questions.question_text: Who translated the story of 'Nal-Damayanti' into Persian?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Faizi, the elder brother of Abul Fazl and court poet of Akbar. According to Abul Fazl, Emperor Akbar was a great literary patron. There were books in his library written in Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, Greek, and Kashmiri languages. Abul Fazl says that "linguists are engaged in translating Sanskrit, Greek, Arabic, and Persian books into other languages." Other best works of Sanskrit were translated into Persian. These translated works include the Mahabharata named Razmnama, Ramayana, Atharvaveda, Panchatantra, and the mathematics-related work of Bhaskar, Lilavati. In this context, the Masnavi of Faizi named 'Nal-Daman' is noteworthy.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below– List-I List-II A. Tarikh-i-Hind 1. Motamid Khan B. Tarikh-i-Khan Jahani 2. Al-Biruni C. Iqbalnama-i-Jahangir 3. Niamatullah D. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh 4. Abdul Qadir Badauni Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– (A) Tarikh-i-Hind - Al-Biruni (C) Iqbalnama-i-Jahangiri - Motamid Khan, (B) Tarikh-i-Khan Jahani - Niamatullah, (D) Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh - Badauni. Al-Biruni came to India with Mahmud Ghaznavi. He wrote the work named Tarikh-i-Hind or Kitab-ul-Hind.

questions.question_text: Which Sheikh Allama Faizi Sirhindi wrote?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Sheikh Faizi Ahmed Sirhindi, Abul Fazl, etc., together wrote Akbarnama. Abul Fazl's intention was to highlight the heroic aspects of Akbar's life. Spreading Akbar's policy of Sulh-i-kul to the people and making the grandeur of the Badshah's personality accepted was also included in the objectives of this book. Abul Fazl thought that sovereignty is a gift from God. That's why he narrated the special story of Genghis Khan in a unique style. Akbar was much greater than a Badshah in Abul Fazl's view. He was considered Insan-i-Kamil from whom no mistake could be made and who had a mission before him. Abul Fazl rejected the style of writing of old historians. Also rejected the phrasing of language and the twisting-turning of words. He claimed that his style was untouched and unique. He used the language and style of philosophy to fulfil historical needs.

questions.question_text: The 'Moti Masjid' of 'Red Fort' was built by-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The Red Fort of Delhi was built by Shah Jahan, whereas the Moti Masjid situated in this fort was built by Aurangzeb. Moti Masjid in Agra was built by Shah Jahan. The Bibi ka Maqbara built in Aurangabad in 1678 AD is inspired by the great Taj Mahal, although it is half the size of it. The Lahore Badshahi Masjid (1674), which has a powerful and firm concept, is the one with an opposite effect to the graceful beauty of the Moti Masjid built in the Red Fort in 1662 AD. Possibly, this small mosque was built by Aurangzeb for his personal use. Its features are the circular Bengali roof and a full-blown dome, and another notable building is the Safdarjung's tomb in Delhi. (1753 AD) which is the tomb of the second Nawab of Awadh.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Ishwardas Nagar's Futuhat-i-Alamgiri is the history up to the 34th year of Aurangzeb. Aurangzeb's relations with Rajputs, especially with the Rathores, have been narrated in full detail. This is the best book on this subject. In it, an attempt has been made to say that by 1691-92, Aurangzeb's policies had become troubled and nobles started dreaming of establishing their independent governments. He writes that once the barber was cutting Shahabuddin's hair. Looking at the mirror, the Khan asked the barber, "How do we look?" The barber replied, "Your Excellency, such a prosperous developed face should be on the Peacock Throne." From this story, an estimate can be made that the barber's state can be understood, that the throne was not secure, any noble could capture it. This statement came true after Aurangzeb's death and Shahabuddin Khan and Zulfiqar Ali Khan established their independent governments.

questions.question_text: The court poet of Shah Jahan's court was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Shah Jahan appointed Kalim, the creator of Saqinama, Masnavis, and Qasidas, as his court poet. Shah Jahan was a ruler of a very romantic nature and was also a music connoisseur. Such evidence is found on the basis of which it can be said that he used to enjoy music for an hour and a half daily in the harem. Shah Jahan honoured Lal Khan, son-in-law of Vilas Khan, with the title of 'Gunsamudra'. Shah Jahan's fondness for music is proven by the fact that once his court singers Khushal Khan and Bisram Khan had so enchanted Shah Jahan by singing Raga Rodi that he signed the order to send Muqarrab Khan with Aurangzeb to the south without reading it.

questions.question_text: Which play's parts are inscribed in the stone pieces used in 'Adhai Din ka Jhopra' mosque?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- 'Adhai Din ka Jhopra' is situated in Ajmer. Previously it was a Sanskrit school which was built by Vigraharaja IV. On this, some parts of the Sanskrit play Harikeli are inscribed. Qutbuddin Aibak had demolished the upper part of this building and built 'Adhai Din ka Jhopra'.
