Apart from this, Aibak started the construction of the mosque named "Quwwat-ul-Islam" near Rai Pithora Fort in Delhi and Qutub Minar in Delhi. The mosques built by Aibak have a harmony of Hindu and Muslim art. Later various sultans made changes in it. Iltutmish expanded Adhai Din ka Jhopra and Quwwat-ul-Islam mosques.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statement and select the correct answer from the code given below- Statement (A) : Sufi saints of the Chishti order did not keep themselves related to kings, nobles, and the wealthy. Reason (R) : They hated wealth and power and considered the wealthy as trivial. Code :

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- In India, after Moinuddin, Chishti Sheikhs like Bakhtiyar Kaki, Baba Farid, and Nizamuddin maintained spiritual independence despite receiving royal patronage. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya remained contemporary to the rulers of the Sultanate for nearly sixty years. But he did not go to any court and it is famous about him that "there are two doors of my house. If the Sultan comes in from one, I go out from the other." Despite Muhammad Tughlaq's efforts, the Sufis did not consider it appropriate to keep relations with the government. The Chishti silsila was not only away from state relations, but they also did not accept financial help and jagirs, etc. Early Chishti Sufis kept themselves away from the government and royal pomp to a great extent. The followers of the Chishti silsila led a simple life. Their belief was that God can be attained through song, economic hardship, and mystical knowledge. They kept themselves away from kings, nobles, and the wealthy because they hated wealth and power.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List-I List-II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- "Ain-i-Akbari" mentions fourteen Sufi silsilas. Among these, the Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiriyya, and Naqshbandiyya have remained extremely famous. The preaching of the Suhrawardi silsila in India was done by Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya. Safiuddin Yahya Maneri founded the Firdousi silsila. The main centre of this silsila in Bihar was Rajgir. Khwaja Baqi Billah founded the Naqshbandiyya silsila in India and Abdul Qadir Jilani was the founder of the Qadiriyya silsila. The Suhrawardi silsila kept its relation with the state from the beginning. Their belief was that they could solve the sufferings of the poor people of society through the cooperation and financial help of the government. According to Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya, they could often bring changes in their ideologies and policies by establishing relations with the rulers.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Maasir-i-Alamgiri'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Saqi Mustaid Khan's Maasir-i-Alamgiri is an important source of Aurangzeb's time. It contains contemporary description of conditions from the 11th year to the 20th year of Aurangzeb. The condition of the first ten years is a summary of Kazim Shirazi's Alamgir-nama. Mustaid Khan has explained the Satnami revolt in a very interesting way. Changes of officers, appointments, and promotions after 1680 have also been discussed. For this reason, Sir Jadunath Sarkar has called it the gazetteer of the Mughal state, whereas Badauni's book is Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh. He has described the influence of Akbar's liberalism and religious neutrality on society. He had criticized Akbar along with praising him. Abul Fazl considered Akbar a hero. Badauni came to Agra in 1574 and entered Akbar's audience.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is considered the founder of the Mughal painting style?

options.B: Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The style of painting that the Mughals laid the foundation of in India developed as such a progressive and powerful art movement that it changed the course of the history of Indian art in the later medieval era. Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali are considered the founders of the Mughal painting style. Mughal ruler Humayun brought them from Persia. Humayun gave the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asr' to Mir Sayyid Ali and 'Shirin Qalam' to Abdus Samad. The works prepared by these two artists, some of which are collected in the Gulshan painting style prepared by Emperor Jahangir, which is now preserved in Tehran's Gulistan Palace. There is no detail of what works were prepared in Humayun's Kabul painting studio because nothing has been said about it in any contemporary history.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an octagonal tomb?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Along with square tombs of Delhi Sultans, a large number of octagonal tombs were built. Their beginning started in 1368-69 AD with the tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani (Vazir) situated in Nizamuddin, Delhi. It has an octagonal state which has a veranda on all four sides and each side of the octagon has three arches and the roof of the state is made of a dome. This design and plan were later adopted with appropriate changes in the tombs built later. Its other counterparts are Mubarak Sayyid's tomb (1454), Muhammad Sayyid's tomb (1444), Sikandar Lodi's tomb (1517), and Sasaram Hasan Khan Sur's tomb (1540-45), Sher Shah Suri's tomb (1545), and Islam Shah Sur's tomb (1550). For example, Sher Shah's tomb is situated on a high platform in the middle of a huge lake. On its corners, there are very attractive figures in the form of octagonal pavilions.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List-I List-II A. Taj-ul-Maasir 1. Afif B. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri 2. Isami C. Futuh-us-Salatin 3. Hasan Nizami D. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi 4. Minhaj Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' is the ambitious achievement of Minhaj-us-Siraj. Which is dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud. A chronological description of the first Delhi Sultanate has been presented. The author of 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi' is 'Shams-i-Siraj' Afif. There is another book by this name whose author is Barani. Afif's Firoz Shahi is complementary to the artistic merit of Barani and Minhaj. It is written in 90 chapters. 'Futuh-us-Salatin' is a book of Khwaja Abdullah Malik Isami. Harsh criticism of Muhammad Tughlaq has been made in this book. It is written in poetry and its creation happened in the court of Bahman Shah. The author of 'Taj-ul-Maasir' is Hasan Nizami. This work has a detailed account of Muhammad Ghori's invasion of India and the battle of Tarain with Prithviraj Chauhan.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List-I List-II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Correctly matched list is as follows List-I List-II A Baba Farid Chishtiyya branch B Sheikh Hamiduddin Nagauri Suhrawardiyya branch C Mian Mir Qadiriyya branch D Shah Waliullah Naqshbandiyya branch Note : Sheikh Hamiduddin Nagauri joined the Suhrawardiyya branch. He was a resident of Nagaur (Rajasthan). Like the Chishtis, he had a special attachment to 'Sama' music assemblies.

questions.question_text: Among the following Persian poets, who is called the 'Saadi of India'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Amir Hasan was a famous scholar of Balban's time. Fawaid-ul-Fawad is his famous work. Amir-Hasan-i-Dehlavi was a high-quality ghazal creator. He was called the 'Saadi of India'. He created two main features of Balban's theory of kingship- first, the position of the Sultan is given by God and second, the absolute nature of the Sultan is necessary. According to him "the position of the Sultan is a living symbol of absolutism on earth (Niyabat-i-Khudai) and his place is after the Prophet. The Sultan receives the motivation and power to work from God. In this way, the general public or nobles have no right to criticize his actions." He told his son Bughra Khan that "the position of the Sultan is a living symbol of absolutism. He believed that the special status and respect of the Sultan alone could force his citizens to obey his orders."

questions.question_text: The Moti Masjid of Agra Fort was built by-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Mughal Badshah Shah Jahan, due to his preference for marble over red stone, carried out construction work in Agra and Lahore forts with marble instead of red stone. The Diwan-i-Aam (1627) of Agra Fort was the first building made of marble. After that, Diwan-i-Khas (1637) and Moti Masjid (1664) were built of marble. Later, Khas Mahal, Sheesh Mahal, Nagina Masjid, and Musamman Burj were built in Agra Fort with this stone. Among all these, the most beautiful and attractive is Moti Masjid. Especially the beauty of the dome of this mosque is notable. Similarly, construction of buildings was done in Lahore Fort too. Akbar built the Lahore Fort in 1560 AD. It has been included in the UNESCO World Heritage site since 1981.

questions.question_text: Which of the following painters did Jahangir give the title of Nadir-uz-Zaman?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Countless painters worked under Mughal Badshah Jahangir, among them Farrukh Beg, Daulat, Manohar, Bishandas, Mansur, and Abul Hasan were those who etched their names in golden letters in the history of Mughal painting due to their artistic talent. Farrukh Beg entered the Akbari painting studio when Mughal painting was in its early golden age. He remained true to his personal style. Among the Jahangiri painters, the most important were Ustad Mansur and Abul Hasan. The Badshah himself praised them. Respecting their specialization, he gave them the titles of 'Nadir-ul-Asr' and 'Nadir-uz-Zaman' respectively. An amazing painting is available in the India Office Library, London, in which there is a Chinar tree and on it many squirrels are depicted in every possible pose. That painting is generally believed to have been made by Abul Hasan.

questions.question_text: Sanskrit work 'Prabodh Chandrodaya' was translated into Persian, whose title was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Krishna Mishra wrote the Sanskrit work 'Prabodh Chandrodaya'. Its Persian translation was done under the title 'Gulzar-i-Hal'. Other Sanskrit books which were translated into Persian- Mahabharata translation was done by Naqib Khan, Badauni, Abul Fazl, etc., various scholars' collective efforts. Badauni translated the Ramayana. He started the translation of 'Atharvaveda' and its completion was done by Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi. Lilavati's translation was done by Faizi. Rajatarangini's translation was done by Shah Muhammad Shahabadi, 'Kalila Dimna' by Abul Fazl, 'Nal Damayanti Katha' by Faizi, and Harivamsa Purana's translation was done by Maulana Sheri.

questions.question_text: Determine the correct chronological order of the following saints of Maharashtra from the code given below- 1. Eknath 2. Ramdas 3. Tukaram 4. Namdev Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Namdev (1270-1350)- These were Maharashtrian saints and were contemporaries of Dnyandev. He was a tailor by caste and opposed all types of caste discrimination. His presiding deity was Vitthal or Vithal (Vishnu) of Pandharpur. The worship of Vithal is known by the name of Varkari sect. In the establishment of which Namdev contributed. Eknath (1533-1599)- These were scholarly saints of Maharashtra. He wrote a commentary on Ramayana under the name 'Bhavartha Ramayana' and wrote a commentary on the eleventh chapter of Bhagavata Purana. Tukaram (1598-1650)- These were also great Bhakti poets of Maharashtra. He wrote devotional poems which are called 'Abhanga'. These Abhangas are the light-beams of devotion-based poetry. Ramdas (1608-1681)- These are the last great saint poet of Maharashtra. 'Dasbodh' is the collection of his works and teachings.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Sufis is called Alakh?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- People of the Chishti tradition give maximum importance to Sharia but also accept the Wajudi theory and Hindu thoughts. This contradiction of thoughts is seen in the character of Sheikh Abdul Quddus Gangohi (1538), who belonged to the Chishti-Sabiri tradition of the Chishti order. Accepting the Wajudi ideology, perhaps Sheikh Abdul Quddus also believes in the monistic philosophy of Nath Yogis. He wrote "Rushd Nama" in which monism was accepted and in which there are also poems written by him under the pseudonym 'Alakh'. According to Sheikh Abdul Quddus, 'Alakh Niranjan' cannot be seen. People who experience Him remain lost in themselves. In a poem, he considered God and Niranjan as one. According to him, praying while hanging upside down from a tree or roof is a symbol of the union of Shiva and Shakti.

questions.question_text: The author of the book named Yog Qalandar was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Saiyid Murtaza wrote the book named Yog Qalandar.

questions.question_text: Which two of the following Sufi branches provided revival to Indian Islam in the 17th century- 1. Chishtiyya 2. Naqshbandiyya 3. Suhrawardiyya 4. Qadiriyya Indicate the correct answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Sufi silsilas have an important place in the medieval religious movement. Among these silsilas, the Qadiriyya and Naqshbandiyya Sufi silsilas worked to revive Indian Islam in the 17th century. The Qadiriyya silsila established by Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani is a mystical sect of Islam. Mughal ruler Dara Shikoh was a follower of the saint Mian Mir of the Qadiriyya silsila. During Akbar's time (1556-1605 AD), Baqi Billah established the Naqshbandiyya silsila. Akbar and Jahangir's contemporary Naqshbandi saint Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi is famous as 'Mujaddid', i.e., revivalist or reformer of Islam.

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following saints? 1. Vallabhacharya 2. Shankaracharya 3. Ramanujacharya 4. Nimbarka 5. Madhvacharya Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The correct chronological order of the saints is as follows- Shankaracharya 788-820 AD., Ramanujacharya 1017-1137 AD., Madhvacharya- 12th century, Nimbarkacharya 1197-1278, Vallabhacharya 1479-1531.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the hourglass?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – The first reference to the hourglass is found in the Rihla of Ibn Khaldun in Afghanistan. Hourglasses began to be depicted in Mughal miniatures from Akbar's time. Yantra Prakash of Ramchandra and Sundar Siddhant of Ganesha Daivajna describe the hourglass. The above three things are correct regarding the hourglass.

questions.question_text: Who was the first poet to Indianize Persian poetry -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Amir Khusro was not a historian. He was primarily a poet, who started his life during the time of Sultan Balban. The 'Masnavis' and 'Diwans' written by him throw enough light on the contemporary history.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation─ In India, the first popular saint of the Suhrawardi-sect was Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya. Bahauddin Zakariya provided help to Iltutmish against Qubacha, for which Iltutmish gave him the title of Sheikh-ul-Islam. Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi was a prominent saint of the Naqshbandi sect. Baba Farid was an important saint of the Chishti sect.

questions.question_text: To which sect or silsila of Sufis was Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya related?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation : The founder of the Suhrawardi branch was Sheikh Ziauddin, who was a contemporary of Ghazali. In India, the first preaching of this branch was done by Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya Suhrawardi. He was born in Multan in 1181 AD. He also travelled to Medina and Baghdad with the aim of obtaining higher education. The first preaching of the Chishti branch in India was done by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. The first preaching of the Qadiriyya branch in India was done by Shah Niamatullah and Makhdum Jilani in the 15th century. The Naqshbandi branch was founded in the 14th century by Khwaja Bahauddin Naqshband.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below : List-I List-II A. Al-Biruni 1. Tarikh-i-Fakhruddin Mubarak Shahi B. Isami 2. Khazain-ul-Futuh C. Amir Khusro 3. Insha-i-Mahru D. Fakhr-i-Mudabbir 4. Tarikh-i-Hind Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – Al-Biruni travelled to India during the invasion of Mahmud Ghaznavi and compiled whatever he saw with his own eyes in his book 'Tarikh-i-Hind'. He gives a detailed account of the 11th-century Indian society, religion, science, etc., in this book of his. Ain-ul-Mulk Multani wrote the 'Insha-i-Mahru' book, which is an important means to obtain information of the contemporary time. Amir Khusro was a prominent Sufi saint, poet, and court poet of Alauddin Khalji. He wrote many Masnavis like Ashiqa, Khazain-ul-Futuh, Tughlaqnama, etc. Fakhr-i-Mudabbir was the court historian of Qutbuddin Aibak who wrote the book Tarikh-i-Fakhruddin. Al-Biruni - Tarikh-i-Hind Ain-ul-Mulk Multani - Insha-i-Mahru Amir Khusro - Khazain-ul-Futuh Fakhr-i-Mudabbir - Tarikh-i-Fakhruddin

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below : List-I List-II A. Ramanuja 1. Shuddhadvaita B. Madhvacharya 2. Dvaitadvaita C. Nimbarka 3. Dvaita D. Vallabhacharya 4. Vishishtadvaita Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- Ramanuja was born in 1017 AD. He propounded systematic philosophical principles which are known as 'Vishishtadvaitavada'. Madhvacharya was born in 1199 AD. He was a very great leader of the Bhakti movement of the South. His belief was in 'Dvaitavada' and he considered the soul and God both as separate. He was mainly a worshipper of 'Lakshmi Narayana'. Nimbarka was another important saint whose time was the 12th century. He was a worshipper of Radha-Krishna. His philosophy is known as 'Dvaitadvaitavada'. His sect is also known as the 'Sanaka sect'. Vallabhacharya was born in 1479 AD in Varanasi. He belonged to a Brahmin family of Telugu and believed in Krishna Bhakti. His philosophy is known by the name of 'Shuddhadvaitavada'. Based on the above facts, the answer to the question– Ramanuja-Vishishtadvaita; Madhvacharya-Dvaitavada; Nimbarka-Dvaitadvaita; Vallabhacharya-Shuddhadvaita.

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following saints? 1. Ramanuja 2. Shankaracharya 3. Shankaradeva 4. Dadu
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- Ramanuja was born in 1017 AD in a place named Sriperumbudur of Andhra Pradesh. He was a prominent saint of the Bhakti movement. His philosophy is known as 'Vishisht Dvaitavada'. Shankaracharya was born in 788 AD in a village named Kaladi of Kerala province. He gave the idea of 'Advaitavada'. According to him, Brahma is truth and the world is false. Shankaradeva was an important saint of Assam. He was born in 1449 AD. He was an opponent of idol worship and ritualism. He was the only such saint who despite being Krishna-margi (following the path of Krishna) was an opponent of idol worship. He is called the 'Chaitanya of Assam'. 'Dadu' was a resident of Gujarat. He was born in 1554 AD in Ahmedabad. He founded the 'Brahma sect'. Correct order is- Shankaracharya - 788 AD; Ramanuja – 1017 AD; Shankaradeva – 1449 AD; Dadu – 1554 AD.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below : List-I List-II A. Bahauddin Zakariya 1. Chishti B. Saiyid Muhammad Jilani 2. Suhrawardi C. Nizamuddin Auliya 3. Qadiriyya D. Muhammad Ghaus 4. Shattari Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- The founder of the Sufi branch named Suhrawardi in India was Bahauddin Zakariya. Its main centre was Multan. Unlike the Chishti silsila, the Suhrawardi silsila believed in accumulating wealth and living a life of luxury. Saiyid Muhammad Jilani was related to the Qadiriyya silsila. Nizamuddin Auliya was a famous Sufi saint of the Chishti silsila. He was called 'Mahbub-i-Ilahi'. Muhammad Ghaus was another Sufi saint, who was related to the Shattari silsila. Muhammad Ghaus and his brother 'Bahlol' had an important role in making the Shattari silsila popular. Bahauddin Zakariya – Suhrawardi; Saiyid Muhammad Jilani – Qadiriyya; Nizamuddin Auliya – Chishti; Muhammad Ghaus – Shattari.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below: List-I (A) Kabir (B) Raidas (C) Sena (D) Dhanna; List-II (1) Kisan (2) Nai (3) Mochi (4) Julaha
questions.explanation: Kabir was born around 1440 AD in a place named Lahartara of Varanasi district. It is said that he was born from the womb of a widow, but his upbringing happened in the house of a weaver. He was a Nirguna saint of the Bhakti movement. Ravidas was one of the 12 disciples of Ramananda and worked as a cobbler in Varanasi. His followers started the Ravidasi sect. Sen was also a prominent one among the 12 disciples of Ramananda and was a 'Nai' (barber), whereas 'Dhanna' was a Jat farmer. According to the above facts- Kabir-weaver; Ravidas-cobbler; Sen-barber; Dhanna-Jat (farmer).

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Tughlaqnama is the work of Amir Khusro. This is the last Masnavi of Khusro. In this, the victory of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq against Khusro Shah is mentioned. The whole story has been presented in a religious colour. Nuh Sipihr, Ashiqa, Khazain-ul-Futuh (Tarikh-i-Alai), etc., are other works of Amir Khusro. Translation of Mahabharata by the name Razmnama was done by Badauni. Tarikh-i-Hind is the work of Al-Biruni, whereas Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is the work of Minhaj-us-Siraj.

questions.question_text: The subject of 'Tibb-i-Sikandari', collected from Sanskrit sources, was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Collected from Sanskrit sources, `Tibb-i-Sikandari' is a book of medical science. Prime Minister of Sultan Sikandar Lodi, Mian Shua, wrote a huge book on the subject of medical science, which is called `Madan-ul-Shifa' or `Tibb-i-Sikandari'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.B: Akbar's 'dam' was 1/40th part of his silver rupee in proportion
options.C: Plenty of use of red stone is found in Akbar's buildings
options.D: Original Baburnama was written in Persian

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ Original Baburnama was written in the Turkish language. This is the work of Mughal Badshah Babur. Its translation into Persian was done by Payanda Khan, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, Abul Talib Turbati, etc. scholars. Use of red stone is found in Akbar's buildings. Akbar's 'dam' was 1/40th part of his silver rupee in proportion. Sher Shah introduced silver rupee.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of Humayunnama?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Gulbadan Begum was the daughter of Babur and the sister of Humayun. Her marriage took place with a powerful noble Khwaja Khan. On the request of Akbar, she wrote a book between 1580 and 1590 AD, which became famous as 'Humayun-Nama'. We get important information about Babur and Humayun in this book. She died during the time of Akbar.

questions.question_text: Among the following painters, who was appointed to the post of 'Diwan' in Multan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - When Mughal emperor Humayun went to Persia, he came into contact with Khwaja Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali, the disciples of the famous painter Behzad of Herat, and invited them to come to him. When Humayun was in Kabul, both of them reached him. Both Humayun and Akbar received training in painting from Khwaja Abdus Samad. Abdus Samad was a resident of Shiraz. Pleased with his talent, Akbar appointed him the Diwan of Multan. Akbar opened a separate department of painting under the leadership of Abdus Samad. He invited various artists from China and Persia to the court and provided training facilities in art to many Indians, gave them patronage, and gave them work according to each person's interest and ability. With these efforts of Akbar, hundreds of artists were encouraged.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below the lists: List-I (Monument) List-II (Builder) A. Badshahi Mosque, Lahore 1. Shahjahan B. Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula 2. Akbar C. Buland Darwaza 3. Nur Jahan D. Moti Masjid, Agra 4. Aurangzeb Codes: A B C D A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Badshahi Mosque - Aurangzeb got this mosque built in Lahore in 1675 AD. Its construction work took place under the supervision of Fidai Khan. Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula - The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula, the father-in-law of Jahangir and father of Nur Jahan, was built by Nur Jahan in 1626 AD on the basis of Iranian style. Buland Darwaza - Built during the time of Akbar, this gate is built in the southern wall of the Jama Masjid of Sikri. This is the tallest and most magnificent gateway in India. It is 176 feet high from the surface of the earth. Moti Masjid, Agra - Situated in the fort of Agra, this is the most beautiful building. It was built by Shahjahan (1645-1653 AD) at a cost of three lakh rupees.

questions.question_text: Which scholar among the following has been called 'Hujjat-ul-Islam'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The title of 'Hujjat-ul-Islam' was adopted by Abu Hamid Muhammad Al-Ghazali.

questions.question_text: 'Tutinama' is the Persian translation of which Sanskrit text?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Zia Nakhshabi's (died 1350) 'Tutinama' or 'Tales of a Parrot' is the best book of that era, which is based on a Sanskrit book 'Shuka Saptati'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following did not take Sannyasa?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Vallabhacharya and Guru Nanak did not take Sannyasa. Vallabhacharya was originally a Brahmin from Teligana. He was born in 1479 AD in Varanasi; he was a great saint of the Krishna Bhakti branch. Like Kabir and Nanak, he also did not consider marriage a hindrance to spiritual progress. He married a girl named Mahalakshmi of Banaras. They attained children and they continued to lead a householder's life, but did not leave their intellectual and spiritual duties.

questions.question_text: Who gave the title of 'Bakhtiyar' to Khwaja Qutubuddin?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti gave the title of 'Bakhtiyar' to Khwaja Qutubuddin. He was prominent among the disciples of Muinuddin Chishti. He was born in 1186 AD in Farghana (Isfahan). Regarding his birth, it is said that the night he was born, the entire room was illuminated with divine light. He came to India during the time of Sultan Iltutmish.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - 'Tabaqat-i-Akbari' is a book by Khwaja Nizamuddin Ahmad. Badauni composed 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh'. Nizamuddin Ahmad wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari during the reign of Akbar. This book is divided into 9 chapters; he has described the history of the Ghaznavids in the introduction of the book. His style is free from religious bigotry and partiality. He was the Mir Bakshi of Akbar.

questions.question_text: The Sanskrit work 'Hitopadesha' was translated into Persian by:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - The Sanskrit work 'Hitopadesha' was translated into Persian by Taj-ul-Mali. In the Sultanate period, the translation of Hitopadesha into Persian was done under the name 'Mufarrih-ul-Qulub'.

questions.question_text: In the Mughal period, who among the following had unlimited powers?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Wazir or Diwan was an important officer of the Mughal Empire. It was divided into two parts. First, Wazir-i-Tafweez, second Wazir-i-Tanfeez. Wazir-i-Tafweez was the Wazir with unlimited powers. He was considered the house manager and intimate friend of the ruler. Sometimes he used to appoint officers without the prior permission of the emperor and informed the emperor later. Whereas Wazir-i-Tanfeez was an officer with limited powers. In the Mughal period, Mir Bakshi was the head of the military department. Khan-i-Saman was the head of the royal kitchen (House Department).

questions.question_text: During the reign of Akbar, which of the following books was not illustrated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - During the reign of Akbar, Niyamatnama was not illustrated. Niyamatnama is a book on culinary science. Unfortunately, no date is given in this book, but it is certain that this manuscript was illustrated in Mandu. There is a mention of Sultan Nasiruddin Khalji, son of Ghiyasuddin Khalji in its colophon, whose personal portraits have been displayed through many miniatures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true?

options.A: The depiction of Babur in Mughal miniatures appears to represent the informal group of friends in his court.
options.B: In many Mughal paintings, such a depiction of Humayun's court is found in which luxury, order, and immutability are reflected prominently in his court.
options.C: Akbar had fixed separate places for princes and nobles in his court in a disciplined manner.
options.D: When Bairam Khan came before Akbar riding a horse and caught his hand, it was considered such a serious breach of etiquette that Akbar considered it a very serious crime of Bairam Khan.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - Among the given options, option (b) that in many Mughal paintings, such a depiction of Humayun's court is found in which luxury, order, and immutability are reflected prominently in his court, is not the correct option. Whereas the other three clarify correct facts.

questions.question_text: Who translated the Ramayana into Persian?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - During the reign of Mughal Emperor Shahjahan, Ibn Har Karan translated the Ramayana into Persian. Munshi Banvali Das translated Prabodh Chandrodaya into Persian and named it 'Gulzar-e-Hal'. Abdul Hamid Lahori was Shahjahan's court historian; he composed the Padshahnama.

questions.question_text: Which scholar was given the title of 'Amir-i-Akhbar' by Humayun?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - Humayun gave patronage and encouragement to Khwandamir, who composed Humayun-nama or Qanun-i-Humayuni. In this, the author presented a strange description of Humayun's administrative management. Humayun also gave the title of 'Amir-i-Akhbar' to Khwandamir.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not built by Qutubuddin Aibak?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - The reign of Qutubuddin was till 1206-1210 AD. He established the first Indian Muslim state. He did not get an opportunity to complete the arrangements of his state, but on the foundation laid by him, later rulers built a magnificent edifice of the Turkic state in India. During his time, two mosques were built in Delhi and Ajmer. The Qutub Minar of Delhi is also from his time, whereas 'Alai Darwaza' was built by Alauddin Khalji, which is the expanded form of Delhi's Qutubi mosque. Apart from this, Alauddin also built the fort of Siri and the Thousand Pillar Palace.

questions.question_text: What was a Khanqah?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - A place of Sufi activities, where the descriptions of God's leelas (pastimes) took place. There lived one or more Sheikhs who entertained the wandering Sufis and gave teachings to their disciples.

questions.question_text: Which of the following were saints of the Varkari sect? 1. Chakradhar 2. Dnyaneshwar 3. Namdev 4. Ramdas Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - The Bhakti movement of Maharashtra was mainly divided into two sects. The first sect of the mystics was Varkari, i.e., the mystic sect of the devotees of Lord Vithoba of Pandharpur, and the second sect was the Dharkari sect, devotees of Lord Rama. People of the Dharkari sect called themselves by the name Dasa. The three gurus of the Vitthoba sect, i.e., Varkari sect, were Dnyaneshwar or Dnyandev, Namdev, and Tukaram. Namdev was a supreme devotee of Vithoba of Pandharpur. He had a major role in establishing the glorious tradition of the famous ideology as the Varkari sect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a Jahangiri painter?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - Countless painters worked under Jahangir; among them are Farrukh Beg, Daulat, Manohar, Bishandas, Mansur, and Abul Hasan, such painters who, thanks to their artistic genius, have inscribed their name in golden letters in the history of Mughal painting. Emperor Jahangir himself praised Abul Hasan and Ustad Mansur. Respecting their specialization, he gave the title of 'Nadir-ul-Zaman' to Abul Hasan and 'Nadir-ul-Asr' to Mansur. Both Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali were Persian painters of Humayun. These two artists taught Akbar the knowledge of painting. After Humayun, when Akbar sat on the throne, these two painters started enhancing the beauty of his court. Due to the tireless efforts of these two painters, Hamzanama was illustrated. In Ain-i-Akbari, apart from Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad, fifteen painters have been named. These painters were - Daswanth, Basawan, Keshav, Lal, Mukund, Miskin, Farrukh, Kalamak, Madhu, Jagan, Mahesh, Khemkaran, Tara Chand, Sanwaldas, Haribans, and Ram. Daswanth was the son of a palanquin bearer, whose work impressed Akbar so much that he helped him become the "first leading artist of his time." The works of this artist were "in no way less than Behzad."

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sufi texts was composed in Lahore at the beginning of the eleventh century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation - In the early phase of the 11th century, after the invasion of India by Mahmud Ghaznavi, many saints and philosophers arrived in India, among whom the name of Ali bin Usman Al Hujwiri is especially noteworthy. Hujwiri composed the famous text 'Kashful Mahjub'. He was a resident of Ghazni and after Mahmud Ghaznavi's invasion, he came to India and started living in Lahore, and he passed away there too.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'Kitab-ul-Yamini'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - Al-Biruni composed the book named Tahqiq-i-Hind or Kitab-ul-Hind, whereas Kitab-ul-Yamini was composed by Utbi. Barani composed Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Firdausi composed the book named Shahnameh.

questions.question_text: Who introduced the Vaishnava religion in Kamarupa?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - Shankardeva introduced the Vaishnava religion in Kamarupa (Assam). Shankardeva (1449-1568 AD) was the greatest reformer of medieval Assam. His message was centered on complete devotion to Vishnu or his incarnation Krishna. The essence of his teachings is Monotheism. The sect established by him is famous as the Ekasarana sect.

questions.question_text: The teachings of which medieval saint are compiled in 'Abhang'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - Saint Tukaram (1598-1650 AD) was an important saint of Maharashtra. He composed the popular poetic text Abhang (Veda of Maharashtra). In terms of popularity, he was one of the greatest saints who refused the honor of Shivaji.

questions.question_text: Who started the Raushaniya movement in India in the sixteenth century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - In the sixteenth century, the Raushaniya movement in India was started by Miyan Bayazid Ansari. People of the Raushaniya sect were followers of Bayazid, who "were giving teachings of a specific form of Muslim religion, in which on one hand socialism and on the other hand destruction of enemies of Islam, these two major characteristics appear. In this, add his influence that the coming Mahdi (Messiah) was here, and then we would get all the elements of religious explosion."

questions.question_text: Which of the following believed in the 'Bhedabhed' principle?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - Nimbarkacharya believed in the Bhedabhed principle. The Acharyas fiercely opposed Advaitism when they got the opportunity and the following four sects were established by Vaishnava saints - Founder - Sect Ramanujacharya - Vishishtadvaitavada Madhvacharya - Dvaitavada Vallabhacharya - Shuddhadvaitavada Nimbarkacharya - Dvaitadvaitavada

questions.question_text: Fawaid-ul-Fuad is an account of the conversations of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. Who compiled this?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - In the book named Fawaid-ul-Fuad, there is a description of the assemblies of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. It contains many stories from which we get information regarding the arrival, transportation, and trade of contemporary people. At one place, there is a story of a dervish who used to trade in slaves. Fawaid-ul-Fuad was compiled by Amir Hasan Sijzi. Apart from this, Hasan Nizami compiled Taj-ul-Maasir, and Nizamuddin Barani compiled Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

questions.question_text: The book named Kashful Mahjub, composed in Persian in Lahore city, is about Sufis and was written by whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - Among the Sufis who came to India and settled, Sheikh Ali Hujwiri (around 1088) is the most prominent. He wrote a book named Kashful Mahjub. Written in Persian, this text is a standard document written on Sufi doctrine.

questions.question_text: Who started the Mahdavi movement in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - The Mahdavi movement in India was started by Sayyid Muhammad Jaunpuri. During the reign of Sultan Mahmud Shah, Sheikh Abdullah Niyazi and Sheikh Alai, who were leading the Mahdavi movement, were exiled from the state.

questions.question_text: By whom was the Guru Granth Sahib prepared in its present form?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation - Guru Granth Sahib was prepared in its present form by Guru Gobind Singh. Guru Gobind Singh also included the thoughts of his father and 9th Guru Tegh Bahadur in the Adi Granth. Although he compiled his own thoughts in a separate book, which was called the book of the Tenth King or Dasham Granth.

questions.question_text: Consider these two statements: Statement (A): Akbar built the Buland Darwaza in Fatehpur Sikri. Reason (R): Akbar wished to preserve the memory of his victory. In the context of these two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct, but (A)'s Explanation (R) is not correct

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation - Akbar made his second attack on Gujarat in 1572. Gujarat's second attack is considered a very 'fast attack' not only in Akbar's but in world history. Gujarat became part of the Mughal Empire. Akbar built the Buland Darwaza in Fatehpur Sikri in memory of his victory because he wished to preserve the memory of his victory. Buland Darwaza is 134 feet high. There are 42 feet long steps to reach the gate. In this way, the total height of the gate from the road is 176 feet. This gate is made of red and yellow sandstone.

questions.question_text: 'Agra and Fatehpur Sikri are both larger than London.' Who gave this statement?
questions.explanation: During the reign of Akbar, English traveler Ralph Fitch came on a trip to India. Ralph Fitch said that Agra and Fatehpur Sikri are both larger than London. Hawkins came to Jahangir's court. Hawkins brought a letter in the name of Akbar

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the founder of the Sufi Chishti branch?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Chishtiya branch was Khwaja Abu Abdal. Khwaja Bahuddin Zakariya was related to Suhrawardi. The founder of the Chishti sect was Ishaq Shami. The founder of the Chishti sect in India was Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti. He built his Khanqah in Ajmer. There are two opinions about the founder of the Chishtiya branch. According to the first opinion of scholars, its foundation was laid by Khwaja Abu Abdal Chishti. According to the second opinion of scholars, its founder was Khwaja Abu Ishaq Chishti

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Rihla'?
questions.explanation: The author of Rihla was Ibn-Battuta. Rihla means traveler! African traveler Ibn-Battuta came to India in 1333 AD during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. The Sultan appointed him the Qazi of Delhi. According to Ibn-Battuta, there were 23 provinces in Tughlaq's empire at that time. Rihla was written in the Arabic language

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Padshahnama'?
questions.explanation: The author of the book 'Padshahnama' was Muhammad Amin Qazwini. Muhammad Amin Qazwini was the official historian of the reign of Shahjahan. Qazwini mentioned up to 10 years of Shahjahan's reign in his book. Abdul Hamid Lahori has also composed Padshahnama

questions.question_text: Who adopted the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asr'?
questions.explanation: Ustad Mansur is considered the best painter of Jahangir's era. Jahangir gave the title of Nadir-ul-Asr to Ustad Mansur. Ustad Mansur is considered an expert in making paintings of animals and birds. Abul Hasan's title was Nadir-uz-Zaman. He was an expert in making portraits of people

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Hasan Nizami was a great scholar of Qutubuddin Aibak's reign. His work is Taj-ul-Maasir (Pearls of Conquests). Khazain-ul-Futuh (Tarikh-i-Alai) is a work of Alauddin's time. Its author was Amir Khusrau

questions.question_text: Who was the author of 'Amal-i-Saleh'?
questions.explanation: The author of Amal-i-Saleh was Muhammad Saleh. Muhammad Saleh lived in Shahjahan's court. Muhammad Saleh has described the governance and construction department of Shahjahan's reign

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: I. Prithviraj Chauhan was a contemporary of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti. II. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was a contemporary of Nizamuddin Auliya. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Prithviraj Chauhan (1166 – 1192 AD) was a valiant ruler of the Chauhan dynasty who was a contemporary of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (1143 – 1236 AD). He was the founder of the Chishti Silsila (order) in India. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (reign 1320 – 25 AD) was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty. Nizamuddin Auliya (1236-1325 AD) was his contemporary. He was also called Mahbub-i-Ilahi

questions.question_text: Who built the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque?
questions.explanation: Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque situated near Qutub Minar in Delhi was built by the first ruler of the Slave dynasty, Qutubuddin Aibak, in 1192 AD. Iltutmish added some more parts to it in 1230 AD and Alauddin Khalji in 1351 AD

questions.question_text: The tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti is situated in–
questions.explanation: The tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti is situated inside the Jama Masjid in Fatehpur Sikri, Agra district. In 1573 AD, along with the Gujarat victory, Akbar conquered this area and named it Fatehpur Sikri. Akbar got this tomb built in 1580–81 AD

questions.question_text: 'Sri Sampradaya' is related to which religion?
questions.explanation: Vaishnava saint Ramanujacharya gave immense emphasis on the worship of Lakshmi and Vishnu in his worship. It is believed that his doctrine was based on the teachings given by Lakshmi, hence this sect is also called 'Sri Sampradaya'. Ramanujacharya is considered an incarnation of Sheshnag

questions.question_text: Match the Persian/Arabic books given in List-I with their authors given in List-II and indicate the correct answer with the help of codes~ List-I (Book) List-II (Author) A. Taj-ul-Maasir (i) Al-Kashandi B. Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi (ii) Hasan Nizami C. Masalik-ul-Absar Fi (iii) Yahya bin Ahmad Mamalik-ul-Amsar Sirhindi D. Subh-ul-Asha (iv) Shihabuddin Al-Umari Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The correct matching of Arabic/Persian books with their authors is as follows– Taj-ul-Maasir – Hasan Nizami Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi – Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi Masalik-ul-Absar Fi- Mamalik-ul-Amsar – Shihabuddin Al-Umari Subh-ul-Asha – Al-Kashandi

questions.question_text: Vallabhacharya preached the devotion of whom?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– Vallabhacharya preached the devotion of Krishna. The personality of Vallabhacharya was greatly influenced by Vishnu Swami's Rudra sect. Vallabhacharya named his philosophy Pushti Marg Philosophy. He accepted the main objective of his Pushti as singing the glorious deeds of Lord Krishna.

questions.question_text: Which of the following saints is considered an incarnation of Vishnu by his followers?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation– Saint Chaitanya was born in a Brahmin family at a place called Nadiya in Bengal. At the age of 22, he received Krishna mantra from a monk named Ishwarpuri and became a monk at the age of 24. He did not oppose idol worship and religious books. He considered everyone fit for Krishna devotion. His followers consider him an incarnation of Vishnu.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers granted royal patronage to Urdu?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The development of Urdu literature took place in the Mughal period. Later Mughal ruler Muhammad Shah (1719-48 AD) granted royal patronage to Urdu. He called Shamsuddin Wali to his court and encouraged him for the development of Urdu. According to famous writer William Irvine, there were many factions in the Mughal court. There were four main ones: Turani, Irani, Afghani, and Hindustani. Among them, three were descendants of Central Asian, Persian, and Afghan soldiers who had won India and helped in establishing the state there. Their numbers increased a lot in the last 25 years of Aurangzeb, especially when he was busy in the wars of the South. Their descendants were appointed to military and non-military posts in different parts of India.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Baba Farid 1. Qadiri branch B. Sheikh Hamiduddin Nagauri 2. Chishti branch C. Miyan Mir 3. Suhrawardi branch D. Shah Waliullah 4. Naqshbandi branch Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– In 'Ain-i-Akbari', Abul Fazl has mentioned fourteen Sufi silsilas. Among these, Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi have been very famous. According to Sayyid Muhammad Hafiz, Chishti is the oldest Sufi silsila of India. Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti came to India with the army of Shihabuddin Ghori in 1192 AD and later he laid the foundation of 'Chishtiya tradition' here. After coming here and traveling to many places, he made Ajmer his permanent residence. His mausoleum is in Ajmer. Khwaja Bakhtiyar Kaki was a contemporary of Sultan Iltutmish and he was the one who initiated Baba Farid into the Chishtiya tradition. Due to Baba Farid, the Chishtiya silsila gained widespread popularity in India.

questions.question_text: By what name do we know the works of the 14th-century saint poetess Lalla Ded?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– We know the works of the 14th-century saint poetess Lalla Ded by the name 'Vakh'.

questions.question_text: Who presented the following argument to understand his work Madan-ush-Shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi? 'First point is that Greek medicines were not suitable for India's climate and the second point is that it was not possible to identify or obtain the medicinal plants mentioned in that system in India.'
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Miyan Bhuwa (Bhuvah) presented an argument to understand his work Madan-ush-Shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi that 'First point is that Greek medicines were not suitable for India's climate and the second point is that it was not possible to identify or obtain the medicinal plants mentioned in that system in India.' He was the Wazir of Sikandar Lodi.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the book for the guidance of Qazis, which Aurangzeb got compiled by extracting important citations from the authentic work Hanfi Fiqh?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– For the guidance of Qazis, the work Aurangzeb (1658-1707 AD) got done by extracting important citations from the authentic work Hanfi Fiqh and compiling them is named 'Fatawa-e-Alamgiri'. Aurangzeb ruled for a long time. He had all the qualities of being a great ruler of the Middle Ages. 'Fatawa-e-Alamgiri' is considered the "biggest digest" (summarized book) of Muslim law composed in India.

questions.question_text: Whom did Abul Fazl call 'Sada Lauh' ('a simple person') because he mourned the loss of the deity he used to worship, and Abul Fazl also called him 'blind follower of customs'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Abul Fazl has said the aforementioned statement regarding Raja Todar Mal. Emperor Akbar (1556-1605 AD) started the Dahsala system in 1580 AD and gave it a permanent form of revenue system. At that time, Raja Todar Mal was the Finance Minister and his main assistant was Khwaja Shah Mansur. Todar Mal provided his support in this work. For this reason, it is also called 'Todar Mal Bandobast'.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer in the codes given below: List-I (Author) List-II (Works) B. Jagannatha Pandita (ii) Rajavali Pataka C. Krishnadev (iii) Bhojaprabandha D. Shuka (iv) Parsiprakasha Codes : A B C D A. Ballalasena (i) Rasagangadhara
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The correct matching of List-I with List-II is~ Bhoja Prakash was not written by Ballalasena but by Ballaladeva Ballaladeva – Bhojaprabandha Jagannatha Pandita – Rasagangadhara Krishnadev – Parsiprakasha Shuka – Rajavali Pataka Question is wrong--

questions.question_text: Show the following historical buildings according to their time of construction: (i) Tomb of Humayun – Delhi (ii) Atala Mosque – Jaunpur (iii) Tomb of Rabia Daurani – Aurangabad (iv) Tomb of Sher Shah – Sasaram Answer with the help of codes: Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Famous Atala Mosque which is situated in Jaunpur. It was completed in 1408 AD during the time of Ibrahim Shah. The tomb of Sher Shah (1540-45 AD) situated in Sasaram is considered the zenith of pre-period architectural style and a sign of the beginning of the new style. The tomb of Humayun was built during the time of Emperor Akbar (1556-1605 AD) and the tomb of Rabia-ud-Daurani, which is situated in Aurangabad, was built by Aurangzeb in 1678.

questions.question_text: During his conversation with Mirza Mukarram Safawi, Aurangzeb was asked to express his views about music. In the context of Aurangzeb's views about music, which of the following statement/statements is/are correct? (i) Music is 'mubah', neither it is good nor bad. (ii) I dislike vocal and instrumental music. (iii) I cannot listen to music without a flute, especially pakhawaj. (iv) Flute is prohibited (haram) by consensus, hence I gave up music. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Aurangzeb told Mirza Mukarram Safawi about music that music is 'mubah', neither is it good, nor bad. I cannot listen to music without a flute, especially pakhawaj. Flute is prohibited (haram) by consensus, hence I gave up music. These statements were said. Aurangzeb (1658-1707 AD) removed singers and dancers from the court, stopped the production of Bhang, tried to stop drinking alcohol and playing gambling, banned Sati practice.

questions.question_text: Show the following buildings built by Shahjahan in their historical order of construction: (i) Diwan-i-Aam in Agra Fort (ii) Moti Masjid in Agra Fort (iii) Taj Mahal, Agra (iv) Jama Masjid, Shahjahanabad Indicate the correct answer with the help of codes: Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– 'Diwan-i-Aam' (1627 AD) situated in Agra fort was the first building of Shahjahan's time built with marble. After this is the 'Taj Mahal'. Which was built in 22 years. Moti Masjid (1654 AD) was built with marble. After this, Shahjahan got his new capital 'Shahjahanabad' built on the banks of Yamuna river in Delhi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Amir Khusrau and his music are correct? (i) Amir Khusrau studied Carnatic school's Dakhini music. (ii) The great founder of Dakhini/Carnatic music, Nayaka Gopala, was a contemporary of Amir Khusrau. (iii) Amir Khusrau praised his discovery of Sitar in his book Gurrat-ul-Kamal. (iv) In later texts, Amir Khusrau has been credited with the discovery of nearly nineteen sweet forms of singing, especially Khayal, Tarana, and Qawwali. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Amir Khusrau was born in 1253 AD in Patiyali town of Kasganj district of Uttar Pradesh. He had complete knowledge of both music and language. He studied the Dakhini music of the Carnatic school. After the victory of the South, Carnatic musician Nayaka Gopala was also presented to the court of Alauddin Khalji as a gift. There is a mention of the organization of music competition between Amir Khusrau and Nayaka Gopala. In later texts, Amir Khusrau is credited with the discovery of nearly nineteen sweet forms of singing, especially Khayal, Tarana, and Qawwali. Thus: statements (i), (ii), and (iv) are correct.

questions.question_text: Which Sufi saints made the Qadiri silsila popular in Punjab and Sindh among the following?

options.A: Sheikh Muhammad Al-Hussaini and Sheikh Abdul Qadir
options.B: Sheikh Wajihuddin Ahmad and Sheikh Muhammad Ghaus

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Sheikh Muhammad Al-Hussaini and Sheikh Abdul Qadir made the Qadiri silsila popular in Punjab and Sindh. The Qadiri sect was the first mystic sect in Islam. Its foundation was laid by 'Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani'.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is statement (A) and the other is Reason (R). Statement (A): Adab literature also provided form to Muslim political thought. Reason (R): Adab literature was influenced by Panchatantra to some extent, with which Arabic literature had already been introduced to the translation 'Kalila wa Dimna' by Ibn Al-Muqaffa. Choose the correct answer from the following in the context of the above statements:

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Adab literature also provided form to Muslim political thought because Adab literature was influenced by Panchatantra to some extent, with which Arabic literature had already been introduced to the translation 'Kalila wa Dimna' by Ibn-Al-Muqaffa. Panchatantra was likely written in Sanskrit in Kashmir. Ibn-Al-Muqaffa translated it into Arabic language. The translation of Panchatantra into Arabic language is done under the name Kalila wa Dimna. Abul Fazl has translated it into Persian under the name Ayar-i-Danish.

questions.question_text: Which pair of author and source is not among the following? Author Source
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The author of Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was Khafi Khan. He wrote the history of the Mughal period starting from the invasions made by Emperor Babur on India up to the first fifteen years of the reign of later Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah. Khafi Khan was at a high post during Aurangzeb's reign.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct? (i) Great litterateur Khan-i-Khanan Abdul Rahim and prominent theologian Sheikh Abdul Nabi were given the responsibility of the education of Prince Salim. (ii) Prince Salim had good knowledge of Persian, Hindi, and to some extent Turkish language, and along with this he had good knowledge of history, natural science, geography, war skills, and theology, which is considered appropriate for a prince. (iii) Prince Shahjahan was proficient in the art of war. He was an expert in military skills. (iv) Prince Shahjahan, born in Ahmedabad, showed his interest in the care of old monuments by ordering the repair of Mughal period and pre-Mughal period buildings. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– On 5 January 1592, Prince Khurram (Shahjahan) was born in Lahore. Thus: statement (iv) is wrong because Shahjahan was not born in Ahmedabad but in Lahore. The remaining statements are correct. During the time of Shahjahan (1627-1658 AD), the most progress happened in architecture. From this point of view, his period was undoubtedly the golden age of Mughal architecture.

questions.question_text: In the time of the Mughals, a newness that came in the technique of building construction was the use of pre-built wooden frames. Houses capable of being moved from one place to another were called Bengali in the 17th century, from which later the name 'Bungalow' came into vogue in Anglo-Indian languages. Which Mughal emperor is credited with this new technique?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– In the time of the Mughals, a newness that came in the technique of building construction was the use of pre-built wooden frames. Houses capable of being moved from one place to another were called Bengali in the 17th century. The credit for this new technique goes to Mughal Emperor Akbar (1556-1605). Abul Fazl presents a list of many types of wood, but only eight types were generally used. Sisua was used by specific classes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct? (i) The tradition of the annual gathering of 'Sarbat Khalsa' was in Chak Guru (Amritsar), but slowly mutual differences increased and every prominent person started trying to create a separate area for himself. (ii) There are compositions of Guru Gobind Singh in Dasham Granth. (iii) All Sikh Gurus were Khatri and their prominent assistants Masands were also Khatri. (iv) The army of Gurus became most powerful during the time of the tenth and last Guru, Gobind Singh. Select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below: Codes :
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– All Sikh Gurus and their prominent assistants Masands were not Khatri. Although Guru Nanak's (1469-1539 AD) birth took place in a Khatri family in 1469 AD at a place called Talwandi (modern Nankana), 36 meters south-west of Lahore. The tradition of the annual gathering of 'Sarbat Khalsa' was in Chak Guru (Amritsar). The last Guru Gobind Singh succeeded in transforming the Sikhs into a powerful military community (Khalsa) and he struggled against Aurangzeb till the end of his life. At this time, the army of Gurus became most powerful. There are compositions of Guru Gobind Singh in Dasham Granth.

questions.question_text: Which Sufi among the following accepted Lalla Ded as his spiritual guru?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2016 Explanation– Sufi saint Sheikh Nur-ud-din accepted the Kashmiri Shaiva tradition's Hindu poetess Lalla Ded as his spiritual guru.

questions.question_text: A poetess from Mysore, who opposed women being considered inferior to men in her book Hadibade Dharma (religion of holy and chaste women):
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2016 Explanation– In the 17th century, Kannada language poetess Sanchi Honnamma of Mysore opposed women being considered inferior to men in her book 'Hadibade Dharma'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not matched?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2016 Explanation– Miftah-ul-Futuh - Amir Khusrau Tarikh-i-Salatin-i-Afghana - Ahmad Yadgar Siyasatnama - Nizamul Mulk Tusi Zafarnama - Sharf-ud-din Ali Yazdi

questions.question_text: Arrange the following tombs according to their chronological order:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2016 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– The correct chronological order of the tombs is as follows– Tomb of Ataga Khan - Delhi Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti - Fatehpur Sikri Tomb of Akbar - Sikandra Tomb of Asaf Khan - Lahore

questions.question_text: In which historical site among the following are Ibadat Khana, Birbal Bhavan, Tansen's Baradari, and Khan-i-Khana's residence situated?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2016 Explanation– Fatehpur Sikri is situated 36 km away from Agra. The buildings of this place were built by Akbar. Among which Buland Darwaza, Ibadat Khana, Birbal Bhavan etc. are prominent buildings. It was founded in 1572 AD.

questions.question_text: Which city among the following was condemned by Jahangir by calling it Gardabad (dusty city) and Jahannumabad (hellish city)?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– Ahmadabad was condemned by Jahangir by calling it Gardabad (dusty city) and Jahannumabad (hellish city).

questions.question_text: Regarding music, which of the following statements are not correct? (i) Barani writes that in the latter half of the thirteenth century, young women were trained in Persian and Hindustani music by Indian dancers for the Delhi court. (ii) Amir Khusrau claimed in 1318 that Indian music has superiority over the music of other countries. (iii) In Ain-i-Akbari, Abul Fazl has not included the names of musicians. (iv) Nayaka Bakshu was a well-known master of Khayal singing. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
questions.explanation: Abul Fazl has mentioned 36 music artists in Ain-i-Akbari, in which Tansen, Haridas, Surdas, Baiju Bawra, Shah Khan etc. are included. Nayaka Bakshu invented ragas like Bahaduri Todi, Nayaki Kalyan, and Nayaki Kanhra

questions.question_text: What explanation did Miyan Bhuwa give about his book Madan-ush-Shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi written on the basis of the compilation of all major Sanskrit books of Ayurveda? (i) Greek medicines are not useful in Hindustani climate. (ii) The herbs mentioned in the Greek system, either they are not identifiable here or they are not available. (iii) Greek system medicines had dominance in Delhi court. (iv) Greek-Arabic traditions were identical in practice. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
questions.explanation: Miyan Bhuwa (Bhuwah) - In the 16th century AD, Miyan Bhuwa composed Madan-ush-Shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi (1512 AD) on the subject of medicine. He was the Wazir of Sikandar Lodi

questions.question_text: Regarding Sayyid and Lodi architecture, which of the following statement is not correct?

options.A: The tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani inspired the Sayyid and Lodi rulers to build octagonal tombs.
options.B: In Sikandar's tomb, the space left between the inner and outer shell is a sign of the beginning of the double tomb construction style.
options.C: Sayyid and Lodi rulers did not build any tomb with a square plan.
options.D: All the tombs of the Sur family situated in Sasaram are octagonal.

questions.explanation: Sayyid, Lodi, and Sur dynasty tombs have been built of two types - square, octagonal. During the Sayyid and Lodi period, seven square tombs were built around Delhi, not that any tomb with a square plan was not built. In the given options (i) The tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani inspired the Sayyid and Lodi rulers to build octagonal tombs. (ii) In Sikandar's tomb, the space left between the inner and outer shell is a sign of the beginning of the double tomb construction style. (iii) All the tombs of the Sur family situated in Sasaram are octagonal, is correct

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the organization of the Sikh community and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: The correct matching of the codes given is as follows– Masand - Representative of Guru Khalsa - Those to whom Guru gave initiation himself Meli - Assistant of Masand Sahlang - Person initiated by Masand

questions.question_text: In the construction of medieval monuments, marks, symbols, and even names of individuals are inscribed on a large scale on almost every stone used. There were some objectives behind these marks and symbols. Regarding the objectives of these inscribed inscriptions, which of the following objective is not correct?

options.B: Inscribed marks should be specific to the builder.
options.C: These marks were put by stone suppliers and workers.
options.D: These marks were put to identify a building and the building builder.

questions.explanation: Marks and symbols inscribed on the stones used in medieval monuments were put for the identification of that building and the building builder

questions.question_text: Which European traveler remarked that 'There is no system of education in India (except for madrasas for religious education), where the study of Western science could be taught in an organized manner. Therefore, here the interest in Western science and philosophy is born only with a specific person and ends with him'?
questions.explanation: Bernier - (1656-1668) French traveler, who came in the latter half of Shahjahan's reign, when the war of succession among Shahjahan's sons was going on. He wrote about the farmers, industries, education etc. of India in his travelogue 'Travels in the Mughal Empire'. He compared Banaras with Athens

questions.question_text: Regarding painting art, which of the following statement is not correct:

options.A: Mughal Emperor Humayun brought key painters-Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali from Iran in 1555.
options.B: Akbar established a huge painting gallery in which Hamzanama was illustrated in the 1560s.
options.C: During Jahangir's time, the influence of Europe on painting was rejected.
options.D: In the 18th century, especially regional paintings displaying Krishna leelas came into existence.

questions.explanation: During Akbar's reign, Portuguese missionaries started the practice of European painting in the court; due to Jahangir's special interest in painting, more work was done in this direction

questions.question_text: What is the subject matter of the book Tuhfat-ul-Hind written by Mirza Muhammad for Aurangzeb's grandson Shahzada Muizuddin Jahandar Shah?
questions.explanation: – Mirza Muhammad composed 'Tuhfat-ul-Hind' for Aurangzeb's grandson Shahzada Muizuddin Jahandar Shah, whose subject matter is music

questions.question_text: The work Fawaid-ul-Fuad compiled by Amir Hasan Ala Sijzi (Sijzi) is a record of whose deeds and sayings?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2011) Explanation– The work 'Fawaid-ul-Fuad' compiled by Amir Hasan Ala Sijzi (Sijzi) contains the assemblies of Nizamuddin Auliya. The main objective of this book was the publication of Auliya's sayings and actions. It is known that Nizamuddin Auliya was an important Sufi saint of the Chishti sect in India. Amir Hasan was a prominent poet of Balban's time, he is called 'Saadi of India'. He was a disciple of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya. Nizamuddin Auliya reviewed his book, which contains his and Nizamuddin Auliya's conversations.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of Wilayat in Sufi terminology?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2011) Explanation– In Sufi terminology, Wilayat means a private spiritual territory, where Sufi saints perform worship. Or where they perform spiritual practices. It is noteworthy that the residence of Sufis is called Khanqah.

questions.question_text: Who laid the foundation of Jama Masjid situated in Delhi?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2011) Explanation– The foundation of Jama Masjid situated in Delhi was laid by Shahjahan on 6 October 1650 AD, which was completed in 1656 AD. This mosque is made entirely of red sandstone. The mosque is situated on a high platform. It has 4-4 storied minarets on all four sides.

questions.question_text: Tulsidas was the author of which book?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Tulsidas composed books (texts) like Kavitavali, Ramcharitmanas, and Gitavali. It is noteworthy that Tulsidas was a contemporary of Mughal ruler Akbar and he composed Ramcharitmanas in the Awadhi language.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Mughal painters was a caricature painter?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Names of 17 painters are found in Abul Fazl's Ain-i-Akbari. Prominent painters of Akbar's time were Basawan, Daswanth, Miskin, Khwaja Abdus Samad, Mukund, Mir Sayyid Ali etc. Basawan was the best painter of Akbar's time. He was an expert in all fields of painting, use of colors, sketching, portrait painting, and landscape painting. His best work is a painting of Majnun wandering in a desolate area with an emaciated (thin) horse. Miskin was the best among painters with European influence, not among caricature painters.

questions.question_text: What new stylistic features are found in the tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani built in Delhi during the reign of the Sultans of Delhi?

options.A: Use of white marble on red sandstone

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012) Explanation– The first octagonal tomb of the Sultanate period is that of Firoz Tughlaq built by Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani. Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani was Firoz Tughlaq's Prime Minister. It is known that in Tughlaq architecture, there is a dominance of sloping walls, which is called 'Salami'.

questions.question_text: When were pointed arches used for the first time in Indian Muslim architecture?

options.A: In the buildings of Sikandar Lodi
options.B: In the buildings of Sher Shah
options.C: In the buildings of Nur Jahan

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Pointed arches were used for the first time in Indian Muslim architecture in the buildings of Shahjahan. It is noteworthy that Shahjahan's reign is called the 'Golden Age' of Mughal architecture. Shahjahan built the world-famous Taj Mahal (Agra).

questions.question_text: According to whose statement, the Mughal harem was a 'pavilion of chastity'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2012) Explanation– Mughal historian Nizamuddin Ahmad has described the Mughal harem as a 'pavilion of chastity'. Nizamuddin composed 'Tabaqat-i-Akbari'. It is noteworthy that Gulbadan Begum composed Humayun-nama which mentions information regarding Humayun and Akbar's reign.

questions.question_text: Regarding Abul Fazl's Akbarnama, which of the following statement is not correct?

options.A: He has generally not mentioned his sources.
options.B: He has made some immature comments.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Akbarnama has been divided into three parts– the history of Mughal rulers from Amir Timur to Humayun is described in the first part, whereas the history of Emperor Akbar up to 1602 AD is given in the second and third parts. Abul Fazl generally has not mentioned the sources in his book and has also made some immature comments.

questions.question_text: Why was the "double dome" used in Indian-Islamic architecture?

options.A: For the strength of the building.
options.B: To keep the building cool inside.
options.C: To maintain the height of the building.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation– "Double dome" was used in Indian-Islamic architecture to keep the building cool inside.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Mughal painting?

options.A: Combination of spiritual and mystical elements
options.B: Mainly for the spread of Islam

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Humayun laid the foundation of Mughal painting, which reached its zenith during Jahangir's time. Its features include the combination of spiritual and mystical elements, portraits and miniatures, and the inclusion of elements like courtly and aristocratic class.

questions.question_text: Among the following historical works of Amir Khusrau, which work is in prose?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Amir Khusrau composed Khazain-ul-Futuh. In which Amir Khusrau has thrown light on the military system of Alauddin Khalji. Along with this, he has decorated Alauddin with titles like Sultan of the world, conqueror of the era, and shepherd of the people in this book.

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following Sufi saints? (i) Khwaja Ali Hujwiri (ii) Sheikh Badruddin Samarqandi (iii) Shah Niamatullah Qadiri (iv) Khwaja Baqi Billah Select the correct answer from the following codes: Codes :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The correct chronological order of the Sufi saints is as follows– (i) Khwaja Ali Hujwiri (ii) Sheikh Badruddin Samarqandi (iii) Shah Niamatullah Qadiri (iv) Khwaja Baqi Billah

questions.question_text: Nizamuddin Junaidi was a famous Wazir of-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Iltutmish was the first Iltutmish ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who made Delhi his capital. 'Nizamuddin Junaidi' was his capable Wazir. Apart from this, Minhaj-us-Siraj and Malik Tajuddin also received patronage in the court of Iltutmish. Iltutmish also got the help of Wazir Nizamuddin Junaidi in establishing permanent rule in India and establishing Muslim power among the vast Hindu population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Bhakti saints was not a disciple of Chaitanya?
questions.explanation: Bhakti era saint Ishwarpuri was not a disciple of Chaitanya. Chaitanya was born in 1486 AD in Nadiya/Navadvipa of Bengal and died in 1533 AD in Puri (Odisha). Ishwarpuri gave Chaitanya the Krishna mantra, who was a follower of the Madhva sect of Vaishnava religion. Gopala Bhatta Goswami, Jiva Goswami, Sanatan Goswami were disciples of Chaitanya

questions.question_text: Regarding the Balutedars of the Deccan, which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Balutedars (Balutedar) were, in other words, the "service providers" of the village. Baluta is a symbol of a share of grain (or agricultural produce). In most cases, these people were paid annually. This makes it clear that Balutedars were village servants and artisans. Vatan-dar Balutedars had a permanent right to work in the village and receive remuneration. Because the Balutedari system was, in a way, a complete structure of the rural economy. Upari Balutedar and Bade Alutedar worked for the village to make it self-reliant and to meet all the requirements and needs of the village. They received remuneration from the farmers in the form of food grains for their services because the Upari Balutedar did not have permanent rights in the village and were migrant, this statement is correct

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below: List-I (Author) | List-II (Book) --- | --- A. Blochmann | 1. Rajput Painting B. P. Hardy | 2. History of Fine Arts in India and Ceylon C. V.A. Smith | 3. Historians of Medieval India Codes: A B C D D. A.K. Coomaraswamy | 4. Gram Akbar Aurangzeb
questions.explanation: The matched order is as follows List-I (Author) | List-II (Book) A. Blochmann | Gram Akbar Aurangzeb B. P. Hardy | Historians of Medieval India C. V.A. Smith | History of Fine Arts in India and Ceylon D. A.K. Coomaraswamy | Rajput Painting

questions.question_text: During the reign of Aurangzeb, the weight of the silver Rupee was: (1) 176 grains (2) 178 grains (3) 180 grains (4) 182 grains
questions.explanation: The 'Rupee' (silver coin) introduced by Sher Shah weighed 178 grains, which was in circulation during Akbar's reign. Babur introduced a silver coin named 'Shahrukhi' in Kabul and 'Baburi' in Kandahar. Akbar introduced a new silver coin called 'Jalali' of square shape, which weighed 175.5 grains. Jahangir introduced a silver coin named 'Nisar', while the weight of the 'Rupee' (silver coin) prevalent during Aurangzeb's reign was 180 grains. The smallest unit of the Rupee was 'Sukri' (20th part of a Rupee), while its 16th part was 'Kala' Special Facts: The Mughal era currency system was extremely well-organized. Gold, silver, and copper were used in the making of coins. In the Mughal era, the minting of coins took place in mints. These mints were established at various places across the entire empire, mainly in Lahore, Jaunpur, Ahmedabad, Delhi, Bengal, Patna, and Kabul. Aurangzeb's reign had the maximum number of mints. The officer of this mint was called Daroga-i-Mint. It was under the control of the central government. The maximum minting of silver coins (Rupee) occurred during Aurangzeb's reign. Aurangzeb, from a religious point of view, stopped the inscription of the Kalima and the names of the four Caliphs on the coins.

questions.question_text: Regarding Asian maritime trade, which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: In medieval India, maritime trade took place through both land and sea routes. Arabs living on the African coast made trade between Gujarat and East Africa progressive. Malacca was an important international port of South-East Asia, where trade ships came from the ports of Cambay, Rander, Calicut, Sri Lanka, Coromandel, Bengal, and Thailand. People from Gujarat, Java, and nearby islands had come and settled in Malacca, who played an important part in commercial activities.
