Albuquerque writes that "Gujaratis have a better knowledge of the navigation of that region than the people of other nations because they had commercial relations with the people there." Pegu (Myanmar) was another port of that region. Before the rise of Malacca as a commercial center, Chinese ships went through the Red Sea entrance and up to the Persian Gulf, but after the 14th century, they began reaching the Coromandel coast. Thus, Indian trade ships also stopped at Malacca, resulting in a rapid decline in Indian maritime enterprise

questions.question_text: In the Ain-i-Akbari, of which of the following crops is no mention found in any harvest cycle:

options.E: Tobacco Select the correct answer from the options given below:

questions.explanation: Detailed information about the Mughal era economic life is obtained from 'Ain-i-Akbari' and the memoirs of foreign travelers. In 'Ain-i-Akbari', there is a detailed mention of the revenue received from 16 crops of Rabi (spring) and 25 crops of Kharif (autumn). Therefore, according to Abul Fazl - "Wheat, gram, barley, bajra, maize, sugarcane, cotton, opium, indigo, poppy, etc., were cultivated in various parts of the country. Wheat produce was mainly in Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar; sugarcane in Bengal and Bihar; gram and barley in Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar; bajra and maize in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan; indigo mainly in Bayana district; opium mainly in Malwa and Bihar." There is no mention of tea, coffee, and tobacco in Ain-i-Akbari Note: Tobacco was brought to India by the Portuguese in the late 1604 or early 1605 (Akbar's period).

questions.question_text: Regarding Sher Shah Suri, which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri was an Afghan ruler. Sher Shah is known as an administrative reformer. To promote trade and commerce, he stopped mixed-metal currencies and introduced pure gold, silver, and copper coins, whose weight and size were fixed. Sher Shah issued gold coins named Ashrafi, silver Rupee, and copper Dam. He also made attempts at standardizing weights and measures. In his empire, goods were taxed only twice – once at the place of entry and second at the time of sale. Sher Shah had 1700 inns built along the roads at a distance of every 4 miles for travelers to stay, in which there were separate arrangements for Hindus and Muslims to stay, and each inn had arrangements for horses, through which messengers used to carry messages from one place to another. Apart from travelers, there were other people in Sher Shah's inns, not just travelers

questions.question_text: Arrange the various Firmans/notifications issued by the Mughal emperors/nobles in chronological order:
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar met the fourth Sikh Guru Ramdas in 1577 AD and granted 500 bighas of land as 'Madad-i-Maash', which had a natural pond; this pond later became the city of 'Amritsar', and the Golden Temple was built here In 1580, Akbar made Todar Mal Diwan-i-Ashraf (Finance Minister) and Khwaja Mansur his assistant. He divided the Mughal province into 12 parts in 1580. In 1580, Dastur-ul-Amal was created, and based on this, the 'Ain-i-Dahasala' system was implemented. This system of measurement and the assessment based on it is called 'Zabti'. The Zabti system is associated with Raja Todar Mal (and is sometimes called Todar Mal's system). The training center for Naib Tehsildar (NT) is in Hardoi (UP) district in his name. Raikandas Karori's Firman (1665-66 AD) was about the problem of declining Khalsa land and agricultural production, oppressive taxation, and the migration of farmers from the land. Firman issued to Muhammad Hashim (1668-69 AD); his full name was Muhammad Hashim Ali Khan Khafi Khan. He entered Mughal service during Aurangzeb's reign. 'Muntakhab-ul-Lubab' is his work, which contains a critical description of Aurangzeb. During the reign of Emperor Farrukhsiyar, Nizam-ul-Mulk appointed him to the post of 'Diwan'.

questions.question_text: In the context of the Mughal financial system, which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, a developed financial and credit system existed. Information about granting loans and receiving interest by Sarrafs, Mahajans, and Baniyas is obtained. Their main task was to issue Hundis, which was a very useful function in the banking system of that time. Transportation of goods was expensive in itself, which made it risky in the context of the demands of autonomous chieftains and rebels. Option (c) is incorrect because an insurance system was prevalent in commercial activities in the Mughal period. There is a description of this in the papers of the English factories and in the Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh written by Sujan Rai. This work was also done by Sarrafs, who took full care of the risk during the security and transport of goods

questions.question_text: Who was the first Wazir during Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: Muzaffar Khan was appointed as the first Wazir during Akbar's reign. This post was known as Diwan-i-Ala, which later had the Wazir's financial powers given to the Diwan. He also had the authority of land revenue administration. He used to assess land revenue and supervise its collection. The first Diwan-i-Ala was Muzaffar Khan. To assist his duties, he had many officers under him

questions.question_text: "Baraj Rekh" meant –

options.A: The estimated amount of revenue determined by the Raja which the chieftain had to deposit in the royal treasury.
options.B: The actual amount of revenue which the chieftain deposited in the royal treasury.
options.C: Amount to be given by the chieftain on the occasion of any marriage in the royal family.
options.D: The amount of tribute to be given to the Raja by a chieftain upon his death for the recognition of his Jagir.

questions.explanation: "Baraj Rekh" meant the actual annual revenue of the Jagir, which the ruler mentioned in the papers in the granted Jagir. Rekh also means military tax. Accounts of the state revenue were kept based on the standards of income determined by Rekh. Based on Rekh, succession duty, military service, and Newta (invitation) tax, etc., were determined from the chieftain. Rekh was neither collected regularly every year, nor was its rate fixed

questions.question_text: Who filled the trade gap left by the Chinese in the 15th century?
questions.explanation: The trade gap left by the Chinese in the 15th century was filled by Gujarati merchants. In the Ming rule, the decline of trade from India was observed, and due to Muslim control on land routes, this trade almost stopped completely, and a race for maritime trade started, due to which Muslim merchants in Gujarat filled this gap

questions.question_text: In the Mughal period, 'Pahi Kasht' meant –

options.A: A farmer who was the owner of the land himself and whose field and house were in the same village.
options.B: A farmer whose fields and house were in different villages.
options.C: Farmers who had more land than capability and gave land to others to cultivate.

questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, 'Pahi Kasht' were farmers who did not have any farming land; they had ploughs and oxen and went to other villages to cultivate, i.e., farmers who went to other villages temporarily to cultivate as sharecroppers. This was greatly encouraged in the Mughal period

questions.question_text: In which text is the first description of 'Charkha' and 'Rehat' (Persian wheel) found respectively?
questions.explanation: The first description of 'Charkha' and 'Rehat' (Persian wheel) is found in Futuh-us-Salatin and Baburnama. Khwaja Abu Bakr Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin in the time of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. The word Charkha came into use in this book. Isami says, "That woman is good who keeps spinning the Charkha." Rehat was first described by Babur. Later, Sujan Rai Bhandari also gave a description in 1645

questions.question_text: Who can be called the Todar Mal of South India?
questions.explanation: Malik Ambar is called the Todar Mal of South India. He organized the land system in his state by measuring it properly and strengthened the agricultural relief and the economic condition of the state. He adopted the land settlement of Akbar's time in his state Ahmednagar. Malik Ambar was an Abyssinian slave who achieved high office through his ability and made a place for himself in history

questions.question_text: What was the land given as a grant to pundits called?
questions.explanation: & d) : Land given as a grant to pundits was called Madad-i-Maash or Sayurghal. This land was given by the Sultan/Emperor to religious persons, scholars, and needy people (widows, poor, Brahmins) etc., for permanent livelihood

questions.question_text: Which word was used for measuring land during the time of the Sultans?
questions.explanation: The word Masahat was first started by Alauddin Khilji, under which the assessment of produce was done based on the measurement of land

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities was not an important commercial center in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, Agra, Lahore, and Burhanpur were important commercial centers. Lahore was connected to Kabul and Kandahar on one side and Delhi and Agra on the other side. Apart from this, Golconda, Malabar, and Red Sea were also developed as commercial centers of the Mughal period, but they were less important centers compared to Agra, Burhanpur, and Lahore

questions.question_text: According to Badauni, in which year did Akbar abolish Jizya?
questions.explanation: As a result of his Rajput policy, Akbar abolished the Jizya tax in 1564 AD and the pilgrimage tax in 1563 AD. Akbar built Ibadat Khana in 1575 AD and declared Mahzarnama in 1579 AD. However, Badauni stated the date of Akbar's abolition of the Jizya tax as 1579 AD

questions.question_text: Which new crops came to India in the seventeenth century?
questions.explanation: Tobacco and maize were brought to India by the Portuguese in the 17th century. All others have been available in India since ancient times

questions.question_text: What was the most fertile land called in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period, there were 4 types of land - Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, and Banjar. Among these, the most fertile land in the Mughal period was Polaj, in which 2 crops were grown throughout the year. Cultivation took place on Parauti land after one year and on Chachar land after 5 years. Banjar land was infertile land

questions.question_text: In the medieval period, to whom was the land grant named 'Milk or Madad-i-Maash' given for their services?
questions.explanation: Madad-i-Maash land was given to clerics or scholars. It was also known as Sayurghal and Milk land. This land grant was permanent and hereditary. This land was not transferable

questions.question_text: Which Mughal ruler opened the 'Muhtasib' department?
questions.explanation: The Muhtasib department was established by Aurangzeb. Its purpose was to stop those who worked against Shariat, to protect the common people from immorality, to stop the use of alcohol and cannabis, to stop gambling, and to break temples by the Emperor's order, etc., were its main tasks

questions.question_text: Which region between the 15th and 17th centuries became the world's largest mulberry silk producing region?
questions.explanation: Bengal was the region between the 16th and 17th centuries where the world's largest mulberry silk production was done

questions.question_text: With which department was 'Abdar Khana' related?
questions.explanation: Abdar Khana is situated in Fatehpur Sikri, north of the Anup pond. It was related to the water supply department. It was built by Akbar in his capital Fatehpur Sikri in 1585 AD

questions.question_text: Who was made the legal head of the royal mint after the currency reforms initiated by Akbar?
questions.explanation: Khwaja Abdus Samad was made the legal head of the royal mint after the currency reforms initiated by Akbar

questions.question_text: Into how many Sarkars (districts) did Sher Shah divide Bengal?
questions.explanation: The victory of Chausa made Sher Khan (Sher Shah) the real ruler of Bengal and Bihar. In 1539 AD, Sher Khan declared himself the king of Bengal and Bihar. Sher Shah established a new type of 'Provincial Administration' in Bengal, in which the province was divided into Sarkars. The description of the 'Sarkar' unit during Sher Shah's time was given by K.R. Qanungo. According to him, Bengal was divided into 19 sub-units (Sarkars). The Commission has considered option (c) as the answer to this question. Sher Shah divided his empire into 47 Sarkars

questions.question_text: 'Ain-i-Dahasala', which is also known as the Zabti system, was implemented in:
questions.explanation: Akbar implemented a new tax system called Ain-i-Dahasala in the 24th year of his reign, 1580 AD. The real initiator of this system was Todar Mal, hence it is also called Todar Mal Bandobast. Under this system, the average of the last ten years' production of different crops and their current prevalent prices were calculated, and 1/3 of that average was collected as revenue. 1/10 part of the total determined tax was collected every year, which was called 'Mal-i-Harsala'. Under this system, the payment of tax had to be made in cash Note- The Commission has considered option (a) as the answer to this question.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct statement:

options.A: Shah Jahan got the Western Yamuna Canal dug and named it Nahr-i-Bahisht.
options.B: Shah Jahan reduced the land revenue.
options.C: Shah Jahan renovated the Western Yamuna Canal and named it Nahr-i-Bahisht.
options.D: The condition of farmers improved during Shah Jahan's reign.

questions.explanation: In the medieval period, water came to the city from the canals emerging from the Yamuna river. In the 13th century, Firoz Shah Tughlaq had built this canal, which was improved during the times of Akbar and Jahangir. In the year 1643, Emperor Shah Jahan's Faujdar Ali Mardan arranged water for Delhi from an old canal. This Western Yamuna Canal was renovated and called Nahr-i-Bahisht

questions.question_text: Who built the longest 'Grand Trunk Road'?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah built many roads and got old roads repaired. He built four roads. The first road was from Sonargaon in Bengal to the Indus river (Punjab, Attock). It was called 'Sadak-i-Azam', which was 1500 kos long. It is called the modern Grand Trunk Road. The second road was from Agra to Burhanpur, the third from Agra to Chittor, and the fourth from Lahore to Multan

questions.question_text: Latha and Kuntala are related to:

options.A: Tax imposed on farmers by landlords of Marwar
options.B: Tax imposed on irrigation facilities in Marwar state
options.C: Method of assessing tax on produce

questions.explanation: Latha and Kuntala are related to the method of assessing tax on produce. Latha and Kuntala are methods of collecting land revenue in the Marwar state. Latha was like the 'Galla Bakhshi' of the Mughal era, while Kuntala was like the Danabandi of the Mughal era

questions.question_text: Which emperor implemented Do-aspa, Sih-aspa in the Mansabdari system?
questions.explanation: The Mansabdari system was started by Akbar in 1575. Along with Mansabdar, the post of Sawar was also added in 1594-95 AD. Jahangir, while making some changes in the Mansabdari system, implemented the system of Do-aspa and Sih-aspa in the Sawar post. In Do-aspa, Mansabdars had to keep as many additional horses as the fixed number of troopers, while in Sih-aspa, Mansabdars had to keep double the additional horses. Shah Jahan made rules for those Mansabdars who kept fewer troopers compared to their rank to stop corruption during his reign

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched? Administrative Unit | Official (1) Suba - Tarfdar (2) Pargana - Sardar (3) Sarkar - Faujdar (4) Vatan - Vatandar
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri divided his empire into many provinces; provinces were called 'Suba'. The highest official of each Suba was Tarfdar/Subedar, who was usually the king's son, friend, or trusted person. Iktas were divided into 'Sarkar' (district), whose head was called Faujdar. Each Sarkar was divided into many 'Parganas'. Each Pargana had a Shiqdar (Head), a Munsif, a Fotedar (Treasurer), and two Karkuns (clerks). The smallest unit of administration was the village. A Pargana consisted of many villages. The village administration's head was the "Mukhiya", who was a non-governmental official

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a tax-free land grant?
questions.explanation: Under the Mughal revenue system, land tax was mainly divided into three categories - Khalsa land, Jagir land, Sayurghal land. Income received through all this land was deposited in the royal treasury. After that, salaries for employees and religious work were managed from this very treasury. Sayurghal, Madad-i-Maash, Punya-Oka are considered main tax-free land, while Altamgha Jagir started during Jahangir's time. It was given only to those families as a government grant on whom the Emperor had special favor

questions.question_text: Match the initial contexts of various technologies given in List-I with their sources given in List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I (Technology) | List-II (Source)
questions.explanation: The first mention of Charkha in India was by Isami, while the talk of soap making is written in Sirat-i-Firozshahi. The mention of cylinder and piston syringe was done by Monserrate. The mention of screw thread on metal was done by Thevenot

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): In the medieval period, the price of copper was as much an indicator of knowing the value as the price of silver. The interesting thing is that in relation to copper metal, regional price variation held much more importance than gold and silver. Reason (R): The supply of copper was mainly from mines on the northern and eastern slopes of the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges. Along with this, its proximity could play a big role in determining the spread of price differences in various markets. Which of the following is correct regarding the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: In the medieval period, the price of copper was as much an indicator of knowing the value as the price of silver. The interesting thing is that in relation to copper metal, regional price variation held much more importance than gold and silver – this statement is correct. But the reason "The supply of copper was mainly from mines on the northern and eastern slopes of the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges" is incorrect. Copper is obtained from the eastern regions of Rajasthan and Jharkhand

questions.question_text: Through a royal Firman, which Raja of Amber was restrained from using white marble in his Vatan Jagir?
questions.explanation: From a Firman issued by Shah Jahan on 21 June 1637 for Jai Singh, it was known that the laborers and stonecutters engaged in the mining of marble for Jai Singh's people were stopped from going to the mines. Due to which the work of extracting stones almost stopped

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Akbar was desirous of expanding land measurement and cash collection of land revenue. He was not ready to make any kind of compromise in this area and implemented its implementation strictly. Reason (R): These reforms of Akbar were implemented under the leadership of Shah Mansur and Todar Mal, but rebellion broke out in Bihar and Bengal. Which of the following is correct regarding the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: In the Mughal administration, revenue sources were mainly divided into two parts - Central and Local. Land revenue was the most important source. The given Assertion (A) is incorrect because Akbar was not desirous of expanding land measurement and cash collection of land revenue and he was also ready to make compromises in this area. Reason (R) is true because Akbar implemented land reforms under the leadership of Shah Mansur and Todar Mal. Akbar provided a permanent form to the Mughal land revenue system by starting a new tax system named Ain-i-Dahasala in the 24th year of his reign, 1580 AD. The real initiator of this system was Todar Mal (Shah Mansur provided help). This is also called the Todar Mal Bandobast system

questions.question_text: The discount rate for cash payment for Hundi was known in the medieval period:
questions.explanation: Hundi was a system in which the letter or paper on which one merchant writes for another merchant with whom there is a transaction of giving/taking money, gives money to someone in exchange for money. Such Hundi system also operated in the medieval period, in which the discount rate was Eight (Ath)

questions.question_text: Match the artisans involved in building activities given in List-I with their modern designations given in List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I (Artisan) | List-II (Modern Designation)
questions.explanation: List-I (Artisan) | List-II (Modern Designation) Adha-pujane | Chunegar Khisht-malane | Rajgir Pachanakkar | Nakqash Sukhasab | Brick-breaker
