questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - Correct match is as follows- Sar Khel - Junior military officer Shab-navis - Night writer Shifa Khana - Hospital Silahdar - Armed soldier

questions.question_text: Match the various categories of documents given below with their nature. List-I | List-II
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - Correct match is as follows- Yaddasht - Memorandum Talika - Brief document Patta - Right (land property right related) document Qabuliyat - Document regarding acceptance by farmers about their revenue responsibilities

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.A: Karori: A revenue officer in Mughal administration
options.B: Khalisa: The land region whose revenue is deposited directly into the royal treasury.
options.C: Tarfdar: Provincial governor in Bahmani Sultanate
options.D: Paibaqi: Allotment of revenue to Jagir

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation- a. Karori - A revenue officer in Mughal administration b. Khalisa - The land region whose revenue is deposited directly into the royal treasury. c. Tarfdar - Provincial governor in Bahmani Sultanate d. Paibaqi - Land reserved for allotment to Mansabdars

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Nasqi was started as an alternative to Zabti-i-Harsala. Reason (R): Diwan-i-Khalisa Muzaffar Khan ended Zabti-i-Harsala and established Nasqi. Which of the following is correct regarding the above two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation- Akbar adopted the Zabti system followed by Sher Shah in the beginning of his reign, but on the recommendation of Shihabuddin Ahmed, the Nasq system was started in its place. In Zabti, revenue was determined based on land measurement and the type of grain, whereas, in Nasq or Kankut, the field was measured by rope or feet, estimating the yield per bigha, and by guessing the yield and revenue payment of previous years, the revenue was collected. Thus the assertion is correct and the reason is incorrect.

questions.question_text: "Prejudices and biases blur the critical view and hinder critical investigation." This statement is of which medieval historian?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation- Alberuni has explained the actual situation of India honestly in his book Tahqiq-i-Hind. Alberuni himself has said that "Prejudices and biases blur the critical view and hinder critical investigation."

questions.question_text: For the determination of which was the Dastur-ul-Amal prepared?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- In the Mughal period, every Jagirdar had to determine land revenue according to the 'Dastur', and even in cases of revenue collection, if the Emperor gave any kind of exemption to the farmers in case of crop failure, then in such a situation, he had to give up a part of his claim.

questions.question_text: From which metal was the coin 'Naha' prevalent in the medieval period made?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- The most famous gold coin in the Vijayanagara Empire of the medieval period was Varaha (50 grains), which was recognized as a national coin. It is called Naha, Pone, Pardao Pagoda. Pratap and Fanam were also small gold coins in the Vijayanagara Empire. Silver coin is called Tar and copper coin is called Jital.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation - A. Kasba - Small town B. Ijara - Land taken on contract C. Shraf - Currency exchanger D. Jimmi - Protected non-Muslim

questions.question_text: To whom was 'Nanakar' given as a reward or additional benefit?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- In the Mughal period, the Zamindar received tax-free land from the state in return for his service, which was 'Nanakar'. Jagirdars were those Mansabdars who were given some revenue area instead of cash salary, which was called Jagir. An Amin was appointed in the Pargana. His work was to keep accounts of agricultural land, determine revenue, and give Pattas to the farmers.

questions.question_text: What is meant by Qur Khana?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- Qur Khana was the department of the Royal Armoury. It was formed during the Sultanate period. During the reign of the early Sultans, the central army was called Hashm-i-Qalb. The central cavalry army was called Sawar-i-Qalb.

questions.question_text: Who among the following established a separate department named Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi for improvement in farming?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq established Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi for agricultural development. The work of this department was to run the revenue system properly and make the land fit for farming where no farming was taking place. The Sultan had direct control over this department.

questions.question_text: Mughal India was mainly –

options.A: A one-crop economy in a year
options.B: A two-crop economy in a year
options.C: A three-crop economy in a year
options.D: A four-crop economy in a year

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- Mughal India mainly had a two-crop economy (current Rabi and Kharif) in a year. In the Mughal period, land was divided into 4 parts - Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, and Banjar. At this time, the land revenue rate was 1/3 part of the total produce. Note that Akbar had done the system of Ain-i-Dahasala.

questions.question_text: 'Khilat', which was given to Amirs by Mughal rulers, was a –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- 'Khilat' was a garment that was given to Amirs by Mughal rulers in the Mughal period. This garment was made of silk. It was made loose-fitting. It is known that Khilat was beyond the reach of the common people.

questions.question_text: Who among the following expressed the opinion that women should live within the four walls of the house and should spin the Charkha?

options.C: Yahiya bin Ahmed and Ziauddin Barani

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- Medieval historians Amir Khusrau and Isami expressed the opinion regarding contemporary women that women should live within the four walls of the house and should spin the Charkha.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Ramchandra Pant Amatya has disliked hereditary grants (Vritti) of land revenue in his Ajnapatra on the ground that it leads to constant decrease in government income. Reason (R): Ramchandra Pant says that even the smallest hereditary grant (Vritti) is a sin. Neither should it be transferred to others, nor should it be re-allotted. Which of the following is correct regarding the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - Ramchandra Pant Amatya has disliked hereditary grants (Vritti) of land revenue in his Ajnapatra on the ground that it leads to constant decrease in government income. Ramchandra Pant says that even the smallest hereditary grant (Vritti) is a sin. Neither should it be transferred to others, nor should it be re-allotted. Both Assertion and Reason are correct but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): In the 11th year (1567) of Akbar's reign, Muzaffar Khan and Raja Todar Mal made an important change. The Qanungo was asked to give information about the total area of land being cultivated and not being cultivated. Reason (R): Based on the information given by the Qanungo, instead of a single price list for the entire empire, the crop rate started being converted into cash based on prices prevalent in different regions. Which of the following is correct regarding the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - In the 11th year (1567) of Akbar's reign, Muzaffar Khan and Raja Todar Mal made an important change. The Qanungo was asked to give information about the total area of land being cultivated and not being cultivated. For this work, he appointed 'Qanungo' and attempted to collect actual data. Based on the actual data, a new account named 'Jama-Hal-i-Hasil' was prepared. Based on the information given by the Qanungo, instead of a single price list for the entire empire, the crop rate started being converted into cash based on prices prevalent in different regions. The above Assertion and Reason are both correct and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cities was not a mint city in Mughal India?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation - Akbar made important changes in the mint and currency system of the Mughals. The circulation of Mughal currency was done through mints controlled by the state. These mints were in different parts of the empire. Among which Delhi, Agra, Ahmedabad, Ajmer are important cities. According to Abul Fazl, there were four mints for casting gold coins, fourteen for silver coins, and forty-two for copper coins in the empire in 1595.

questions.question_text: Sarkhej and Bayana were famous for the abundance of which crop in the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation - The best quality indigo was produced in a place named Sarkhej near Ahmedabad. This place was the most important center for the supply of dyeing materials. Good quality indigo was also produced in Bayana, Rajasthan. This was described by Pelsaert.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) – Assertion (A): There were many reasons for the neglect of technological development and mechanization by producers in medieval India. Reason (R): There was risk in any improvement and it also needed capital. The profit of Indian artisans was so meager that they did not want to put their hands into any such effort. In such a situation, the scope of technological improvement remained limited only to what was started by the state or some wealthy merchants. Codes:

options.A: (A) is correct, however (R) is only a partial explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – There were many reasons for the neglect of technological development and mechanization by producers in medieval India. This assertion is correct. There is more risk in any improvement, and there is a need for capital. Due to less profit, technological improvement is less because there is a lack of capital. Due to which the use of technology remains limited to wealthy merchants. Thus, the reason explains the assertion correctly.

questions.question_text: Irfan Habib rejected the estimate of Ekins devised that the population of Mughal India remained stable at 125 million from 1600 to 1750, giving the argument that –

options.A: Ekins probably got carried away in over-enthusiasm for the benefit of British rule.
options.B: He exaggerated the per-acre yield of Akbar's time.
options.C: He did not differentiate between Zabti provinces and other areas.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation - Irfan Habib rejected the estimate of Ekins devised that the population of Mughal India remained stable at 125 million from 1600 to 1750, giving the argument that Ekins probably got carried away in over-enthusiasm for the benefit of British rule.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below: one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) – Assertion (A): Jarokha Darshan, starting the day with the Emperor's view, is a symbol of transferring divine blessings. Reason (R): The Darshaniya sect is known by this name because they start their day with the Emperor's view. Which of the following answers is correct regarding the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation - Jarokha Darshan, starting the day with the Emperor's view, is a symbol of transferring divine blessings. This assertion is true, and as far as the reason is concerned, it is also correct. But there is no connection between the Assertion and the Reason.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not correct regarding the village community?

options.A: According to Bernier, Indian farmers were not stratified.
options.B: The rural community was full of internal contradictions and 'exploitation from within'.
options.C: High-class farmers were known as Khud-kasht in North India, Gharuhala in Rajasthan, and Mirasdar in Maharashtra.
options.D: The lower-class population was 'reserved' to work in the fields at the time of harvest. They were also forced to do forced labor (Begar).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation - The rural community was full of internal contradictions and 'exploitation from within'. High-class farmers were known as Khud-kasht in North India, Gharuhala in Rajasthan, and Mirasdar in Maharashtra, and the third statement, the lower-class population was reserved to work in the fields at the time of harvest. They were also forced to do forced labor. These three statements are correct. According to Bernier, Indian farmers were stratified.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not correct regarding technology developed during the time of the Mughals?

options.A: The clothes that were famous all over the world were not prepared with the help of multi-wheeled looms.
options.B: There was no modern maritime equipment other than the Astrolabe in boats going on sea voyages.
options.C: The construction of Mughal monuments was done with the help of primitive tools like single-wheeled carts.
options.D: Even screws with proper threads were not made for mechanical work.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation - The construction of monuments of the great Mughal era was done with the help of primitive tools like single-wheeled carts. This statement is not correct, while the other three options are correct. The clothes made during the Mughal period were famous in the world. In boats going on sea voyages, there was no other sea equipment besides the Astrolabe. Even screws with proper threads were not made for mechanical work.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the claims of Mansab and select the correct answer using the codes given below – List-I | List-II
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation- Correct code regarding Mansab is as follows- (A) Muhaasiba | (iii) Settlement of accounts (B) Mutaliba | (iv) Claim of royal treasury on money borrowed by deceased person from royal treasury (C) Muqarrara Talab | (i) Accepted claims (D) Tasih | (ii) Renewed certificate for Mansabdar's claim

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements about Iktas:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - Ikta-i-Tamlik were hereditary, in which the Ikta holder's almost personal property was considered. Ikta-i-Mustaghall were not hereditary and initially their nature was administrative and military both. The above statement regarding Ikta is correct.

questions.question_text: Silver coins named 'Tanka' were introduced by –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation - Iltutmish was the first Turkish Sultan who introduced pure Arabic coins. Two important coins of the Sultanate era, the silver 'Tanka' and the copper 'Jital', were started by him. He also started engraving the name of the city on the Tanka where it was minted. During Iltutmish's reign, the copper coin was called Jital.

questions.question_text: In the administrative system of which Indian ruler was a border tax named 'Mohtarfa and Zakate' imposed?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation - In the administrative system of the Marathas, a border tax named Mohtarfa and Zakate was imposed. Apart from this, the main means of Maratha income was land revenue, Chauth, and Sardeshmukhi mainly.

questions.question_text: From which Mughal Emperor did Sir Thomas Roe obtain permission to trade in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation - Sir Thomas Roe obtained permission to trade in India from Mughal Emperor Jahangir. In 1615 AD, James I sent Sir Thomas Roe to the Mughal court on behalf of the company. Due to special efforts, the English established their factories in Broach, Surat, Agra, Ahmedabad, and Machilipatnam.

questions.question_text: In the Mughal period, the determined land revenue (Jama) was always higher than the actual collection (Hasil), what was the primary reason for this?

options.A: Farmers used to run away at the time of revenue collection.
options.B: Land revenue officials used to embezzle revenue.
options.C: More land revenue was determined intentionally.

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation - In the Mughal period, the determined land revenue was always higher than the actual collection. The primary reason for this was - land revenue officials used to embezzle revenue because there was a lack of honesty.

questions.question_text: Who was the effective officer of Alauddin Khilji's market control system?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation - The effective officer of Alauddin Khilji's market control system was 'Shahna-i-Mandi'. 'Diwan-i-Arz' was the military department and 'Ariz-i-Mumalik' was its head. 'Shahna-i-Mandi' was the head of the grain market or grain Mandi.

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, 'Dar-ul-Shafa' used to be :
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation - In the Sultanate period, 'Dar-ul-Shafa' was called the Royal Hospital. Firoz Shah Tughlaq established 'Dar-ul-Shafa', where treatment was free.

questions.question_text: Who started Altamgha land grant?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation - Altamgha land grant was started by Jahangir. It was based on Timurid tradition. It was given hereditarily to special royal-favored religious persons. It could be canceled only in special circumstances by royal order.

questions.question_text: 'Nanakar' and 'Bandh' are
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation - Under the Mughal administration, revenue-free land was called 'Nanakar' and 'Bandh'. The Zamindars who sent the amount of land revenue to the government received a part of the revenue as remuneration, which was called Nanakar.

questions.question_text: Jarib was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation - Jarib was the land measuring tool of the Mughal era, which was introduced by Mughal ruler Akbar. It was a bamboo stick which had iron rings attached to it.

questions.question_text: Which famous woman of the Mughal dynasty is credited with discovering the method of extracting perfume from rose flowers?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation - Nur Jahan's father Ghiyas Beg (whom Jahangir gave the title of Itmad-ud-Daula) and mother Asmat Begum were residents of Persia, who came to the Mughal court during Akbar's reign. Asmat Begum discovered the method of making perfume from flowers in the Mughal period.

questions.question_text: From which mine was the world-famous Kohinoor diamond obtained?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation - The world-famous Kohinoor diamond was obtained from the Golconda mine. In 1636 AD, the Vizier of Golconda, Muhammad Sayyid (Mir Jumla), gifted the Kohinoor to Shah Jahan.

questions.question_text: Which land revenue system was developed by Raja Todar Mal?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation - During the time of Mughal Emperor Jalaluddin Muhammad Akbar, Raja Todar Mal developed the land revenue system called Zabti, in which the land was measured. He was also a good scholar and did the Persian translation of 'Bhagavad Purana'. Todar Mal died in 1589 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following taxes was imposed by the Sultans of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- During the time of the Delhi Sultans, apart from some special taxes, the following five taxes were main: Jizya, Zakat, Kharaj, Khams, and Ushr. Jizya was charged at 12, 24, and 48 dirhams. Zakat was taken from Muslims as a religious tax. Kharaj was a land tax on non-Muslims, Khams was wealth looted in war by the army, and Ushr was a land tax taken from Muslims.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan among the following got Goddess Lakshmi inscribed on one side of a gold coin and the Goddess's name on the other?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Muhammad Ghori first attacked India in 1175 AD and initially he was defeated, but after defeating Prithviraj Chauhan III in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 AD, he achieved many victories in India. Muhammad Ghori or Muhammad Ibn-Sam got Goddess Lakshmi inscribed on one side of a gold coin and the Goddess's name on the other.

questions.question_text: What was meant by 'Chachar land' in the medieval period:

options.A: Land with a risk of being infertile
options.B: Land in which farming happens every year
options.C: Land in which nothing has been sown for five years
options.D: Land that has not been ploughed/sown for a year or so

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- In the medieval period, agricultural land was of several types, where Chachar land meant land that had not been brought to work for three to four years. 'Polaj' was land where cultivation took place every year. Parauti or Parait was land left for some time to gain fertility. Banjar was land left for more than five years.

questions.question_text: The kingship theory of the Lodis was based on-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation - Afghan nobles considered the Sultan as one of the big nobles among themselves. They were not ready to consider any element of divinity in the Sultan. They considered their share in power, influence, and governance of the state. Thus, the Afghans' theory of kingship was based on the equality of nobles, and in such a situation, their administrative system was not monarchical but aristocratic, which was against the Hindu and Turkish administrative system valid in India at that time. Its main features were that each Afghan noble claimed to be the head of his army and did not consider his army an integral part of the Sultan's army. They were not ready to recognize any authority of the Sultan as a special right, but they themselves considered enjoying all such rights as their right. Regarding succession, they did not accept hereditary rights or the right to be nominated, but recognized the right of the nobles to choose the Sultan based on merit.

questions.question_text: What is not correct about Mughal Zamindars?

options.A: Except for the Emperor, no one could remove or appoint a Zamindar to his authority.
options.B: An official or Jagirdar could send his recommendation to the court for the appointment of only Zamindari rights.
options.C: Sometimes the Subedar of the province could remove a rebel Zamindar and appoint a member of the same old family.
options.D: The income of a Mughal Zamindar was 10 percent of his property-related claim (Malikana) (25 percent in Gujarat), to which 5-10 percent Nanakar was added, which he received from the land revenue officials in exchange for collecting revenue.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - Sometimes the Subedar of the province could remove a rebel Zamindar and appoint a member of the same old family. This statement regarding Mughal Zamindars is not correct.

questions.question_text: The Sultan who stopped the allotment of 'Iqta' in lieu of cash salary-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - Iltutmish started the Iqta system but under Alauddin Khilji, the circulation of such appointments ended. While incorporating a complex system in provincial administration, sufficient changes were made in the Iqta system. The coming of a new system was natural in the root of this change. Such changes were seen during the reign of Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316). Along with an unprecedented increase in the revenue of the ruling class, many such steps were taken which affected his system.

questions.question_text: In the Sultanate period, the head of the Royal Secretariat was called-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation - Ariz-i-Mumalik was the head of the military department. He used to arrange for the recruitment of soldiers, their supplies, their inspection, branding of horses, and writing descriptive rolls of soldiers. Barid-i-Mumalik was the head official of the intelligence department. Different spies, messengers, and post-stations were under him. Qazi-i-Mumalik was the head of the justice department, although there was a larger court than his, which was the Sultan's, but because of being the Chief Qazi of the state, lawsuits started in his court and he could also review the decisions of lower Qazis. Dabir-i-Mumalik was the head of the Royal Secretariat in the Sultanate period.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) – Assertion (A): Many Mughal Amirs were trading in their own name or in partnership with merchants. Reason (R): In the capacity of the governor of Bengal, Mir Jumla attempted to establish his monopoly over the trade of all important commodities. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the context of the above two statements? Select the correct answer from the code given below – Codes:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation - Mir Jumla's real name was Muhammad Sayyid. He was a famous Persian merchant. He gifted the Kohinoor diamond to Shah Jahan. Through his ability, he pleased Abdullah Qutb Shah and became the Vizier of the state (Golconda) and accumulated immense wealth through his diplomacy. A French traveler Tavernier wrote that he had diamonds weighing 20 maunds. Later, Mir Jumla was made the Governor of Bengal by the Mughal Emperor, which made his power even stronger and he established a monopoly over the trade of Eastern India.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the list- List I | List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Correct match: (A) Parauti land- This was land that was left for two-three years to become fertile, just left like that so that the crop is better. (B) Polaj- This was considered superior land and cultivation took place on it every year. (C) Chachar- This land was left for more than three years. (D) Banjar- This is land where agricultural work cannot be done.

questions.question_text: Who were the owners of 'Tushari' land?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation- In the Sultanate period, land was divided into two categories from the perspective of revenue assessment. Tushari land and Kharaji land. The land owners of Tushari land were Turk Muslims. Kharaji land was land whose land owners were Hindus. 1/5 part of the produce from Kharaji land was collected as Kharaj land revenue. 1/10 or 1/20 part of the produce was taken as land revenue from Tushari land.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct-

options.A: Persian equivalent of the Arabic word Khilat is Sar-o-pa.
options.B: Sarpa included Sarpech and turban in Khilat and Sar-o-pa.
options.C: There was a sense of completeness in Sar-o-pa which was inherent in the king's personality, which is now given to the recipient.
options.D: Since the king's personality was inherent in the entire empire, therefore the person receiving the Khilat is also symbolically included in royal presence and he becomes a part and extension of it.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation - The Persian equivalent of the Arabic word Khilat is Sar-o-pa. Mughal era rulers used to grant Khilat to honor their officials. Usually, Dastar (turban), Jama (coat), and Kamarband were given as Khilat. There was a sense of completeness in Sar-o-pa which was inherent in the king's personality, which is now given to the recipient. The person receiving the Khilat is also symbolically included in royal presence and he becomes a part and extension of it.

questions.question_text: Ziauddin Barani mentions that despite the ban on alcohol, "addicts, adulterers and debauched people used to make breweries inside their houses and prepare alcohol.... They used to drink it and also sold it secretly at high prices." In the above statement, which Sultan has Ziauddin Barani mentioned, who imposed a ban on drinking and selling alcohol in his state?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation - Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316 AD) imposed a ban on drinking and selling alcohol in his state. In the above statement, Ziauddin Barani has mentioned Sultan Alauddin Khilji. Understanding the causes of rebellions, Alauddin came to Delhi and issued four ordinances to eliminate them. Through the third ordinance, Alauddin stopped the use of intoxicating substances like alcohol and cannabis and gambling.

questions.question_text: Which post was given to Todar Mal in 1582?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation - Mughal ruler Akbar appointed Todar Mal to the post of Diwan-i-Ashraf in 1582. He was the head of the finance department. Todar Mal is credited with implementing the new tax system 'Dahasala method'. From the ninth year of Akbar's reign to the thirtieth year, the Diwan post kept going into the hands of Muzaffar Khan, Raja Todar Mal, and Khwaja Shah Mansur. Raja Todar Mal combined his abilities in the military and financial fields beautifully and provided valuable services in Gujarat. Todar Mal was sent to Gujarat in 1573 AD to organize the financial situation of that province. In 1582, Todar Mal was made Royal Diwan and was entrusted with the responsibility of preparing a special scheme for improvement in financial administration.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - In Sultanate era administration, Royal Workshops had an important place. Each workshop was kept under a high-ranking master. They were called Mutasarrif. The Mutasarrif had to keep accounts of his own department and had to give them to the Diwan-i-Wizarat for annual inspection. There was a Mutasarrif over the workshops, whose duty was to inspect all departments and follow royal orders. During the reign of Firoz, Khwaja Abu Hasan was the Chief Mutasarrif, he was appointed for the regular audit of workshops. He had a separate office. Afif has divided royal workshops into two parts. Ratibi and non-Ratibi. Ratibi workshops were those where people working in them received regular salary. Non-Ratibi where there were employees getting indefinite salary.

questions.question_text: Shashgani was a small silver coin, which was equal to-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - The Delhi Sultanate ruler Firoz Shah Tughlaq circulated Adha, Bikh, and Shashgani coins. Shashgani was a small silver coin which was equal to 6 Jitals. Firoz imposed only four taxes accepted by Islamic laws - Kharaj (Land revenue), Khams (1/5 part of looted wealth in war), Jizya (Religious tax on Hindus), and Zakat (2-1/2 of income, which was taken from Muslims and spent for their welfare). He took Khams only as much as his right. While many previous Sultans kept most of the looted wealth for themselves. He also took Jizya from Brahmins, which previous Sultans did not take due to indifference or practicality. Apart from this, he also imposed irrigation tax after the approval of the Ulema class.

questions.question_text: What was the difference between 'Gaz-i-Sikandari' and 'Gaz-i-Ilahi'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation - According to Ain-i-Akbari, the standard unit for measuring land until the 31st year of the reign was 'Gaz-i-Sikandari' (i.e., length equal to the sum of the diameter of 41 corn kernels and the radius of one corn kernel - length of a copper coin of Lodi era was Sikandari). Sikandari Gaz was equal to 39 fingers or 30 inches. Humayun ordered that this length be equal to 42 fingers (32 units). In the 31st year of his reign, when Akbar saw that having different measurements caused great inconvenience to the public and that it promoted dishonesty, he ended it. He introduced a 'Gaz' through 41 units. Akbar used Gaz-i-Ilahi which is of 41 fingers or 33-1/2 inches.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is/are not a type (form) of Hundi? (i) Peth Hundi (ii) Darshani Hundi (iii) Miyadi Hundi (iv) Hasalana Hundi Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation–Hundis are mainly of two types - Darshani Hundi and Miyadi Hundi. Whereas Peth Hundi and Hasalana Hundi are not types of Hundi.

questions.question_text: The land kept reserved for land revenue allotment was called:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation– Khalisa land was the land from which the income obtained went directly into the royal treasury. From this, the king's personal expenses, royal family, king's bodyguards, private soldiers, and war preparation expenses were met. In Jagir land, Jagirs were given to the state's main servants in lieu of their salary. Giving Jagirs was entirely in the hands of the Badshah, and he could change them at any time. In the Mughal period, the transfer of Jagirs became a common process. At the time of such transfers, that land remained under the care of the center, and this was called 'Paibaqi'. When some employees were given some other work in addition to their fixed duties, they were given some land as an honorarium, on which they used to collect revenue. Such land also came under 'Paibaqi'. Upon completion of the work, the person's right over it also ended.

questions.question_text: Under the Mughal rulers, where did the Mansabdari system originate?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– The main feature of the Mughal military system was the Mansabdari system. Among the Mughal emperors, Akbar started this. Other Mughal emperors kept it established with some minor changes. During the time of later Mughal emperors, it became ineffective. The Mansabdari system started by Akbar was not entirely new, although he gave it proper organization and made it according to his needs. Possibly, Akbar derived the inspiration for this from the military system started by Caliph Abbas Safid and adopted by Genghis Khan and Timur. The rulers of the Delhi Sultanate had also adopted this system in some form or other. There was a system of this type during the time of Balban as well. The Mansabdari system, whose main basis was the division of official ranks based on the decimal system, was not new for India. However, Akbar certainly made it superior in his own way.

questions.question_text: From what did the Mughal emperors grant Jagirs?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation– During the Mughal rule, during the Jagirdari crisis, the most important change that occurred was that Khalisa land started being distributed in the form of Jagirs. The reason for this was that by then the nobility class had become very powerful and started demanding Jagirs with great insistence. To compensate the Mansabdars, the Badshah adopted the path of giving Khalisa land in the form of a Mahal. The result was that within a short time, all the Khalisa land went into the hands of the Jagirdars. In this way, the class which was once created for the service and help of the state, now became a heavy and disadvantageous burden for the state and, moving forward, snatched the state's authority. In this way, the inherent anomalies of the Jagirdari system were now fully exposed.

questions.question_text: Under Muhammad Tughlaq, what kind of work did the Diwan-i-Koh department look after?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq had established this department for agricultural development, whose head was called 'Amir-i-Koh'. This department experimented with the production of various crops in a land area of 60 square miles, but due to poor quality land, the experiment could not be successful. In this experiment, seventy lakh tankas of the royal treasury were spent.

questions.question_text: Which Sultan of Delhi made the rule that land revenue should not be increased by more than 1/10 or 1/11 in any one year?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – From the farmers, like before, 1/5 to 1/3 part of the produce started being collected as revenue. In addition to this, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq ordered that in any one year, the increase in revenue of an Iqta should not be more than 1/11 or 1/10 percent.

questions.question_text: By what name was the land known from which the Sultan directly collected revenue?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – The land which was considered the central government's or Sultan's land and from which the Sultan's employees collected revenue was called 'Khalisa' land.

questions.question_text: Where did the Ijaradari system first become prevalent?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – The Ijaradari system first started in Jagir land. To avoid the problems faced in collecting land revenue, Jagirdars started the 'Ijara' (contract for collecting land revenue) system. Later on, the Ijaradari system started causing excessive harm to the farmers because the Ijaradars started exploiting the farmers to earn more profit. In the first half of the eighteenth century, especially after the death of Bahadur Shah, this practice became very prevalent on Khalisa land as well.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the exponent of the royal secretariat in the Sultanate period?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– In the Sultanate period, the exponent (head) of the royal secretariat was Diwan-i-Insha. His work was to prepare drafts of royal orders and letters, correspond with provincial governors and local officials, and keep a record of government matters. He had many secretaries, who were called 'Dabir'. Its head was Dabir-i-Mamalik. Diwan-i-Wizarat– Among all the ministers, Wazir was the chief. Although theoretically he was the finance minister, his administrative control was practically in all fields of public administration. Diwan-i-Arz– Was the military or defense ministry. Its head was Ariz-i-Mamalik. Diwan-i-Barid– Was the intelligence department.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: In the provincial divisions of the subas, many officials were appointed in the Sarkar.
options.B: The top official of the Sarkar was called Faujdar.
options.C: One of the officials was called the head of the Sarkar.
options.D: The duty of the Faujdar was to maintain law and order in his Sarkar.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– During the Mughal period, every suba was divided into several Sarkars (districts). Establishing peace in his Sarkar, protecting the public from thieves and robbers, and getting the state's orders obeyed by the public were the main duties of the Faujdar. His appointment was done by the Badshah. Although he had to work under the Subedar. Every Sarkar had main officials: Faujdar, Amalguzar, Qazi, Kotwal, Bitikchi, and Khazandar. None of the officials was called the head of the Sarkar. The remaining statements are correct.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding Fakhr-i-Mudabbir and his Adab-ul-Harb wal Shujaat: (i) It is a book written on the art of war in the early days of Iltutmish's reign. (ii) Fakhr-i-Mudabbir has praised the swords made in India a lot. (iii) Mudabbir has written that the work of melting iron ores was done in Khetri, Rajasthan. (iv) He describes the oldest known technique of making Damascus steel. Select the correct answer from the following codes:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Fakhr-i-Mudabbir and his Adab-ul-Harb wal Shujaat is a book written on the art of war in the early days of Iltutmish's (1210-1236 AD) reign. Fakhr-i-Mudabbir has praised the swords made in India a lot. He describes the oldest known technique of making Damascus steel. In Khetri, Rajasthan, the work of melting copper, not iron, was done. According to Abul Fazl, iron was manufactured in Bengal, Allahabad, Agra, Bihar, Gujarat, Delhi, and Kashmir.

questions.question_text: Regarding words and their meanings, match List-I with List-II: List-I (Word) List-II (Meaning) A. Bakkal (i) Lowest class of farmers B. Balahar (ii) An armed person C. Silahdar (iii) A group of ten thousand soldiers D. Tuman (iv) Grain trader Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The correct matching of List-I with List-II is as follows– A. Bakkal – Grain trader B. Balahar – Lowest class of farmers C. Silahdar – An armed person D. Tuman – A group of ten thousand soldiers

questions.question_text: How many total subas were there in Akbar's empire?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– For administrative convenience, Akbar divided the entire empire into 12 subas in 1580 AD (24th year) – Agra, Delhi, Allahabad, Awadh, Ajmer, Ahmedabad, Bihar, Bengal, Kabul, Lahore, Multan, and Malwa. But after the conquest of the South, three more subas were established: Khandesh, Berar, and Ahmednagar. In this way, the number of subas in Akbar's empire became (15).

questions.question_text: In whose reign did Dagh (branding) and Chehra (descriptive rolls) start in the Mughal military administration?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Under the Mughal army, there were cavalry, infantry, elephants, and artillery, etc. Mughal emperors paid special attention to the organization of the cavalry army. They revived the practice of keeping Chehra (Huliya/descriptive roll) of soldiers and branding horses. Modern historian William Irvine writes that the Mughal army was basically based on cavalry, which was started by Akbar and later Mughal rulers also adopted it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: In Mughal India, Zamindari rights were hereditary and saleable.
options.B: All villages were under the control of Zamindars.
options.C: The share of Zamindars in the agricultural surplus was uniform throughout the Mughal empire.
options.D: All Zamindars were Maliks-i-Zamin (owners of the land).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June 2014) Explanation– In the Mughal period, Zamindars were those landowners who had hereditary rights to collect land revenue from some villages. For the collection of land revenue, Zamindars received a portion of the revenue in the form of a commission, which could range from 10% to 25%. In the Mughal period, Zamindars were known by names such as Deshmukh, Patil, or Nayak, etc. Jahangir, despite being a hereditary holder of his Zamindari, was not the owner of the land. As long as a farmer kept paying the regular land revenue, he could not be evicted from the land.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Sultans was not associated with land measurement for revenue assessment?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was not associated with land measurement for revenue assessment. He abandoned the Masahat system (measurement) of Alauddin Khilji and re-introduced the Bataie and Nasq systems for revenue assessment. He worked in the interest of the farmers and ordered revenue officials that the increase in the revenue rate should not be more than 1/10 or 1/11 part in a year.

questions.question_text: Among the following officials, who was the superintendent of the port under the Mughals?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– Mutasaddi was the chief administrator of the port. Without his permission, no foreign trader had permission to land at the port. In fact, a port was a Sarkar which was divided into several Mahals; its administration was actually in the hands of one person who was called Mutasaddi. The position of this official was equivalent to a provincial governor. A superintendent of the customs office was appointed by the port's Mutasaddi. Customs officials collected customs duty with great vigilance. Mir-i-Bahr was the chief of the naval forces. His main work was to look after royal boats. Tahvildar looked after the royal workshops (karkhanas), who was an assistant to the Diwan-i-Buyutat. Mushrif used to audit the accounts of the state's income and expenditure.

questions.question_text: What was 'Narnal' or 'Haqqari' cannon during the Mughal period?

options.A: Cannon kept on the back of an elephant
options.B: Cannon kept on the back of a camel

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– In India, the first use of cannons in war was done by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat, but in this war, large cannons were used which were very difficult to move from one place to another. During Akbar's time, along with matchlock guns, the casting of light cannons also started. The work compiled in Sanskrit in the 16th century, "Shukraniti", sheds light on the issue of small-large cannons and gunpowder. Akbar named the cannons carried on a camel's back 'Shuturnal' and the cannons carried by a human 'Narnal'. The cannon kept on an elephant's back was called 'Gajnal'. In the Mughal period, besides light cannons, Aurangzeb's 'Fath-i-Rahbar' and 'Malika-i-Maidan' are prominent among heavy cannons. In the 17th century, the world's largest cannon 'Jaivana' was also made by Amer ruler Jai Singh, from which two-maund balls could be fired.

questions.question_text: In the 16th-century Mughal administrative terminology, what did the words 'Elchi' or 'Safir' mean?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– In Mughal-era Persian terminology, an ambassador or royal representative of any state was called 'Elchi' or 'Safir'. The word 'Elchi' was mainly used for European ambassadors, whereas the ambassador of neighboring Indian rulers was called 'Safir'.

questions.question_text: Who started the Month-scale (Mashrut system) in the Mansabdari system?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– Shahjahan, after studying the actual situation, found a solution to the problem and started a system of monthly (Month scale) Jagirs (Shashmaha, Sihmaha, etc.) based on the actual collection of Jagirs. According to this, if revenue collection from a Jagir was fifty percent, it was considered a Shashmaha (six-month) Jagir, and if the collection was one-fourth, the Jagir was considered Sihmaha (three-month). In this way, if a Mansabdar was granted a Shashmaha Jagir, his responsibilities were also reduced and deductions were made in the same proportion.

questions.question_text: What was 'Jihat' in Mughal land revenue administrative terminology?

options.A: A liability in addition to the fixed taxes

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– In Mughal land revenue administrative terminology, 'Jihat' was a liability in addition to the fixed taxes. A main objective of the administration was to obtain the maximum portion of the farmer's surplus. There were many rural taxes which were collectively called "Jihat" and "Sair Jihat Phiraut" and "Abwab". Under these various items, about 25 percent of the land revenue was collected.

questions.question_text: Apart from land revenue, what was the percentage of the additional tax (of the total land revenue due) taken by Sher Shah for public welfare?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– Hasan Khan says that Sher Shah had kept a system in such a way that every landlord and revenue payer deposited two and a half percent of their tax in the public treasury so that that money could be spent on accidents or heavy punishments. This tax was definitely collected in the form of grain, which was stored in local granaries and used for the resolution of crisis in days of famine. (Source - Medieval India - A. C. Verma)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct regarding the Mughal Mansabdari system?

options.A: That, under this, there were thirty-three (33) classes of Mansabdars.
options.B: That, they (Mansabdars) could also be given 'Mashrut' or conditional rank.
options.C: That, through this, the Mughal transport system was organized on a strong basis.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Mansabdars were not hereditary officials; they were given Mansabs based on their merit. Akbar divided his total Mansabdars into 66 (based on the sum of the digits of the word Allah: 1+30+30+5) classes. Although Abul Fazl has described only 33 classes. During Akbar's time, Mansabdars were compelled to keep cavalry equal to the number of their 'Sawar' rank. However, later in the time of Mughal emperors, this was not possible, but the Mughal transport system was strengthened by the Mansabdari system. In his final years, Akbar started the 'Zat' and 'Sawar' ranks in the Mansabdari system and each Mansabdar was granted 'Zat' and 'Sawar' ranks simultaneously.

questions.question_text: 'Diwan-i-Koh' was related to:
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq had created a new department Diwan-i-Koh to deal with the situation of crisis, which was related to the Agriculture Department. Under this department, loans were distributed to farmers, so that farmers could increase their produce

questions.question_text: What was meant by 'Tamgha' and 'Mir Bahri' during Jahangir's period:
questions.explanation: During Jahangir's period, Tamgha and Mir Bahri were taxes. Which were related to 'toll tax' on river routes. If any goods were transported through a boat, it was mandatory to pay tax in a fixed amount on it. Jahangir issued 12 edicts in which one was that the taxes Takal, Tamgha, and Mir Bahri should be removed or abolished

questions.question_text: Who established 'Diwan-i-Mustakhraj'?
questions.explanation: Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was related to the revenue system; it was established by Alauddin Khilji. Alauddin had established it to end corruption and loot in the revenue system. Muhammad bin Tughlaq had established Amir-i-Koh related to agriculture

questions.question_text: 'Iqta' was land whose income was controlled by:
questions.explanation: Iltutmish had started the practice of granting Iqta to soldiers as salary. In the Delhi Sultanate period itself, in 1210 AD, along with his accession, Iltutmish established the Iqta system as the foundation of the governance system. Whereas the Jagirdari system existed in the Mughal period

questions.question_text: 'Paibaqi' was:
questions.explanation: Paibaqi land was kept reserved for giving to Mansabdars as salary. There was a system of Paibaqi in the Mughal period. Mansab is generally considered to be a system of Akbar's reign. The Mansabdar was not given cash salary but land in the form of a Jagir. From which the Mansabdar collected tax

questions.question_text: Who was the only female minister of the Mughal period among the following?
questions.explanation: Akbar's wet-nurse was Maham Anga, who was the only female minister of the Mughal period. Maham Anga ran the curtain government or petticoat government from 1560-62 AD. Maham Anga established Madrassa-i-Begum in Delhi. It is also called Khair-ul-Manazil Madrassa

questions.question_text: 'Nankar' was:
questions.explanation: Nankar was a part of revenue or tax-free land. In exchange for the amount of land revenue that Zamindars sent to the government, Zamindars used to get a portion of the revenue, which was called Nankar. According to Abul Fazl- "1 percent of the revenue collected by the Qanungo, which he used to get as an allowance, was called Nankar."

questions.question_text: The word 'Karori' was used for which revenue official in whose administrative system?
questions.explanation: Akbar started the Dahsala management in 1580 AD and gave it a permanent form of revenue system. At that time Raja Todar Mal was the Finance Minister and his main assistant was Khwaja Shah Mansur. Akbar had appointed a district official 'Karori' to implement his Dahsala system. The Dahsala management was not implemented in the entire state. Instead, different systems were used in different places to fix the revenue

questions.question_text: In the decimal currency prevalent during Akbar's reign, a 'Dam' was equal to how many paisa?
questions.explanation: Akbar circulated a copper coin, which was called 'Dam'. There were 40 dams in one rupee. In this way, 'Dam' in decimal currency was equal to 1/40 rupee or 1/2.5 paisa. A coin named 'Anna' between Dam and Rupee was circulated by Shahjahan

questions.question_text: Among the following, who legalized corruption in the land revenue department?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Firoz Tughlaq did not promote corruption in the land revenue department, but he had promoted corruption in the military field when he gave a gold tanka to a soldier to give a bribe to the clerk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rulers divided his military units into units of fifty, two hundred, two hundred fifty, and five hundred?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June, 2013) Explanation – Sher Shah's successor Islam Shah improved his military units and divided them into many units. He classified the cavalry from a salary and rank perspective. His units of soldiers consisted of 50, 200, 250, 500 soldiers respectively. After this, he divided the army into 2000, 5000, and 10,000.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the different uses of Gaj in the Mughal period: (i) Abul Fazl writes that Humayun's Gaj-i-Sikandari was 32 digits long. (ii) Abul Fazl states that the length of Gaj-i-Ilahi was equal to 41 digits. (iii) Dira (Gaj)-i-Shahjahani was slightly less than 33.5 digits. (iv) Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri mentions that the length of Gaj-i-Shar'i is 26 digits. Select the correct answer with the help of the codes given below:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Akbar adopted 'Gaj-i-Ilahi' in place of 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' in the 31st year of his reign; the ratio between these two was 39:41. According to Abul Fazl, there were 32 signs in Gaj-i-Sikandari. Whereas Gaj-i-Ilahi was equal to 41 digits/fingers. Later, Shahjahan, after modifying Bigha-i-Ilahi, used Dira-i-Shahjahani, which was slightly less than 33.5 digits. In this way, options one, two, and three are correct, and option four is wrong because in Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, there is a mention of Gaj-i-Ilahi for measurement, which was equal to 41 digits.

questions.question_text: Match List-I related to books and authors with List-II: List-I (Author) List-II (Book) A. Catherine B. Asher (i) Mughal Architecture: An Outline of its History and Development B. R. Nath (ii) Architecture of Mughal India C. S.P. Kesar (iii) History of Mughal Architecture D. Ebba Koch (iv) Building Construction in Mughal India: The Evidence of Frame Pattra [Note: The matching above is based on the Hindi text provided; the actual titles are transliterated]. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes: A B C D
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The correct matching is as follows– A. Catherine B. Asher – Architecture of Mughal India B. R. Nath – History of Mughal Architecture C. S.P. Kesar – Building Construction in Mughal India: The Evidence of Frame Pattra D. Ebba Koch – Mughal Architecture: An Outline of its History and Development

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below. One is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): In the first half of the seventeenth century, European trade in indigo became very important, and after this, there was a sharp decline in it. Reason (R): There was an increase in the price of Agra's indigo and competition was established from plantations located in West Indies, where slaves worked. Which of the following is correct regarding both the above statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– In the first half of the seventeenth century, European trade in indigo became very important, but after this, there was a rapid decline in it. The reason for this was that there was an increase in the price of Agra's indigo and competition was established from plantations located in West Indies, where slaves worked. Consequently, there was a decline in it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Sarrafs (money changers) were experts in issuing Hundis for the payment of the remitted amount.
options.B: Hundi was a negotiable instrument which was generally transferred by giving a small discount.
options.C: For bills made for one place to another, only 'one' rate of exchange was fixed for the payment of the amount sent or for credit.
options.D: In Hundi, it was automatically clear whether it was payable immediately or payable after the expiry of a fixed period after presenting the Hundi to the customer.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– For the payment of the amount sent or for credit for bills made from one place to another, exchange rates were fixed according to convenience. All other options are correct. Many traders started making payments through Hundis only. Many documents are available in this regard. This was also convenient. This was a negotiable instrument which was generally transferred by giving a discount. In this way, a Sahukar's Hundi was like a modern cheque or bank-draft.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Persian was not the language of higher administration in the Mughal empire and Delhi Sultanate only, but it had spread even to the courts of Rajput states.
options.B: Sirajuddin Ali Arzoo established the view that there were some basic similarities between Persian and Hindi.
options.C: In his book 'Bahar-i-Ajam' written in 1539-40, Tekchand Bahar has given examples of such poets and prose compositions.
options.D: Due to the contact of Persian with the local dialects of Hindi, a new language, Urdu, came into existence.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Persian language spread to the courts of Rajput kings along with the Mughal court. Sirajuddin Ali's view was that there were some basic similarities between Persian and Hindi. Statement (c) is not correct. Due to the contact of Persian with local dialects of Hindi, Urdu came into existence. In 1752 AD, under the name 'Bahar-i-Ajam', Tekchand Bahar of Delhi used Urdu in an old Persian dictionary.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below. One is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): French traveler Jean-Baptiste Tavernier has written that people in Surat usually do not drink the water of the Tapti river. Reason (R): The river's water was salty. Which of the following is correct regarding both the above statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are correct. French traveler Jean-Baptiste Tavernier has written that the people of Surat usually do not drink the water of the Tapti river because the river's water was salty.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the customs duty prevalent in the Mughal empire: (i) Abul Fazl writes that in Akbar's time, the maximum customs duty was 4 1/2 percent. (ii) During Jahangir's time, there was 3 1/2 percent customs duty on all types of imports-exports. (iii) During Shahjahan's time, there was 2 percent customs duty on money, whether it was gold or silver. (iv) Aurangzeb kept the customs duty rate high for non-Muslims. Therefore, Muslim traders used to bring their goods hidden to save Hindus from high duty rates. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– During Shahjahan's time, the customs duty rate was high. Therefore, Aurangzeb, with the aim of attracting the interest of Muslims towards trade, ordered to reduce the customs duty from five percent to two percent. But he kept the customs duty rate high for non-Muslims. Therefore, Muslim traders used to bring their goods hidden to save Hindus from high duty rates. In Akbar's time, the customs duty was 4 1/2 percent and in Jahangir's time, the rate was 3 1/2 percent.

Among the given options, the statement that Dam was known as Paisa is wrong. Jital was known as Fulus or Paisa. This was the smallest copper coin which was equal to the 25th part of a Dam.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding Jizya tax in the Mughal period – (i) Akbar abolished the Jizya tax in 1564. (ii) Akbar re-imposed the Jizya tax in 1575. (iii) Akbar again abolished the Jizya tax in 1579-80. (iv) Aurangzeb re-imposed the Jizya tax in 1679. Which of the given statements are correct?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The first Mughal ruler to abolish the Jizya tax was Akbar. In March 1564 AD, Akbar exempted all non-Muslims from the Jizya tax, which was taken according to their income. In return, they were provided protection by the state. In 1575 AD, Akbar again imposed Jizya tax on Hindus but after some time in 1579-80, he again abolished Jizya. Aurangzeb also imposed Jizya tax on non-Muslims in 1679 AD.

questions.question_text: Which historian has considered the triangular relations between Zamindars, Jagirdars, and peasants as the reason for the crisis and fall of the Mughal empire?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– Historian Satish Chandra has considered the triangular relations between Zamindars, Jagirdars, and peasants as the reason for the crisis and fall of the Mughal empire.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: The monetary system of the Mughals was mainly based on silver Rupee.
options.B: All Mughal rulers from Babur to Shahjahan had an ambition to establish their empire in Central Asia.
options.C: There was no middle class in the Mughal period.
options.D: Important changes were made in the Mansab and Jagir system in the 1605-1658 period.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– The land revenue policy of all Mughal rulers from Babur to Shahjahan was better for the relationship between the kings and the public. The Mansabdari and Jagirdari system of the Mughals prepared a strong middle class. Note that the monetary system of the Mughals was mainly based on the silver Rupee. In the period from 1605 to 1658, changes were made in the Mansabdari and Jagirdari system by Jahangir and Shahjahan. Jahangir made important experiments in the Mansabdari system; he started the Do Aspa and Sih Aspa category. In the time of Shahjahan, the birth of the monthly ratio system occurred.

questions.question_text: Which crops were not cultivated in the Sultanate period India? 1. Potato 2. Barley 3. Sesame 4. Maize Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– In Sultanate period India, except for potato and maize, crops like wheat, barley, paddy, sugarcane, sesame, etc., were grown. There were mainly three methods prevalent for land revenue assessment in the Sultanate period– (a) Bataie (Kism-i-Galla) (b) Masahat (Assessment of produce based on measurement of land) (c) Muqtai (Division system), etc.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): Among all the industries of Mughal-era India, the textile industry was the most important. Reason (R): The export of cotton fabrics was the main source of foreign exchange earnings for India. Which one of the following is correct regarding the context of the above two statements? Codes:

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is correct, but R is wrong.
options.D: A is wrong, but R is correct.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The biggest export industry in Mughal-era India was cloth. All types of cotton, woolen, and silk cloth were prepared. India had made superior progress in preparing cotton cloth. Sonargaon in Bengal, Banaras and Agra in Uttar Pradesh, Lahore, Multan and Thatta in Sindh and Punjab, Ahmedabad, Patna, Baroda, Bharuch and Surat in Gujarat, Burhanpur in Khandesh, and Golconda were famous for preparing cotton cloth. The demand for Indian cotton cloth from countries like China, Japan, Persia, Arabia, Egypt, Africa, and Europe was the highest. India's cotton cloth industry continued successfully until the Industrial Revolution happened in England and an attempt was made to destroy this important industry of India under the rule of the East India Company.

questions.question_text: Which of the following facts about Abdul Qadir Badauni is not correct?

options.A: He was a strict Sunni historian.
options.B: The publication of his book ‘Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh’ happened after the death of Akbar.
options.D: He was liberal towards the concept of ‘Din-i-Ilahi’.

questions.explanation: Abdul Qadir Badauni was born in 1540 AD in Badaun (India), he was a strict Sunni historian. The publication of the second volume of Badauni's most notable book ‘Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh’ was done after the death of Akbar, in which he criticized Akbar's religious policy and conduct. He has translated many Arabic and Sanskrit texts into Persian. He did not hold a liberal attitude towards Akbar’s ‘Din-i-Ilahi’ policy. His major works include Bahar-ul-Asmar, Kitab-ul-Ahadis, Tarikh-i-Alfi, Najat-ur-Rashid etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Persian source ‘Tazkira-i-Pir Hassu Teli’ and its author? (1) The Persian Tazkira-i-Pir Hassu Teli was written during the reign of Jahangir in Punjab. (2) The family of the author Surjit Singh was a trader by profession. (3) He was taken to Sheikh Kamal, the chief disciple of the Teli saint Pir Hassu, to become his disciple. (4) This was a Sufi order, known as Malamatiya, in which both Hindus and Muslims were included. Select the most appropriate answer from the options given below–
questions.explanation: The Persian source ‘Tazkira-i-Pir Hassu Teli’ was written by Surjit Singh. This is a poetry-filled work, in which about 7000 verses are compiled. They were scholars of Persian language of Shah Jahan’s time, who were known for religious tolerance. Their family was related to trading activities. This book reveals the moral character of the middle class of the Mughal period. He was sent to become a disciple of Sheikh Kamal, the chief disciple of the Teli saint Pir Hassu, who belonged to the Malamatiya branch of the Sufi order. The Malamatiya branch was a religiously tolerant branch, in which people of both Hindu and Muslim classes were included

questions.question_text: Founder of Burhanpur city, Nasir Khan, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The founder of Burhanpur city ‘Nasir Khan’ belonged to the ‘Faruqi dynasty’ of Khandesh. The independent Muslim kingdom of Khandesh, situated in the Tapti river valley region, was established by ‘Malik Raja Faruqi’ in 1399 AD. This dynasty was named ‘Faruqi dynasty’ after Malik Raja Faruqi. The next ruler of this dynasty, Nasir Khan, conquered the Asirgarh fort and made it his capital. He established the new capital Burhanpur. The fort of Asirgarh was a powerful military stronghold. The famous ruler of this dynasty was Adil Khan II. He established his dominance over the Hindu rulers of Gondwana and Garh-Mandla. All the Sultans of this dynasty assumed the title of Khan. Therefore, the Faruqi empire came to be known as Khandesh (Land of Khans). In 1601 AD, the Mughal emperor Akbar included Khandesh in the Mughal empire

questions.question_text: In 1623-24, which traveller saw a ‘hospital for birds’ in Cambay, where some lame, sick, birds without pairs, and some small orphaned rats were seen? He wrote, ‘A respectable old man with a white beard was keeping them in between pieces of cotton. He had spectacles on his nose and was trying to feed those small rats with milk with the help of bird feathers because they were still so small that they could not eat anything else. And as he said, his intention was that when they grew up, he would release them, then they could go wherever they wanted’?
questions.explanation: Pietro Della Valle (1622-1626) was an Italian traveller who reached Surat in 1622 AD during the time of Jahangir. He travelled extensively to the coastal regions of India and compiled his travelogue into books. During his visit to Cambay in 1623-24, he saw a ‘hospital for birds’ where he saw orphaned and newborn rats along with sick birds, who were being looked after by a respectable, old man who would release them when they grew up so that they could wander freely. His major works include ‘‘The Travels of Pietro Della Valle in India’’, ‘‘The Pilgrim: The Journey of Pietro Della Valle’’ etc

questions.question_text: Among the foreign travellers who came to India, who was not Portuguese?
questions.explanation: Niccolo Conti was an Italian traveller who came to India in 1420 AD during the reign of Devaraya I. During his journey, describing the city of Vijayanagara, he wrote that ‘‘The circumference of the city is 70 miles. Its wall extends to the mountains. In this city, 90 thousand men were capable of wielding arms. Their king was the most powerful compared to other kings in India.’’ Niccolo Conti has given a detailed description of the slave and Sati practice

questions.question_text: Where is the mention of mercantile 'Chaukis' first found in medieval texts?
questions.explanation: The mention of mercantile Chaukis is first found in the text named Tabaqat-i-Nasiri by Minhaj-us-Siraj. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is a detailed text, in which not only the reign of the Sultans of the slave dynasty of Delhi Sultanate has been described, but also the rise of Islam, the reign of Caliphs, the rulers of Iran, the beginning of Turkish rule in India, the history of Ghazni and Ghor dynasty, the Mongol invasions of Muslim states etc. have also been described in detail. Minhaj dedicated his text Tabaqat-i-Nasiri to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud and described him as the ideal Sultan of Delhi

questions.question_text: The famous play titled ‘The Nawab’ has been written by whom?
questions.explanation: The famous play titled ‘The Nawab’ has been written by Pelsaert. Francisco Pelsaert was a Dutch factor (gumashta) who came to India during the time of Jahangir. He was the head of the Dutch mint in Agra. In his travelogue, he has given an interesting description of the social and economic conditions of many places in India French Bernier - French Bernier was a French traveller who was a doctor by profession. He came to India in the second half of Shah Jahan’s reign. At the time he came to India, a war of succession was going on among the sons of Shah Jahan. He was a witness to the war of succession between Dara Shikoh and Aurangzeb.

questions.question_text: Who was the last ruler of the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur?
questions.explanation: Jaunpur was established by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq of the Tughlaq dynasty. Later, Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Tughlaq dynasty conferred the title of ‘Malik-us-Sharq’ to his Wazir ‘Khwaja Jahan’ and appointed him the ruler of the Eastern Province. He founded the independent Sharqi dynasty. The most important ruler of this dynasty was Ibrahim Shah Sharqi. The last ruler of the Sharqi dynasty was Husain Shah Sharqi, who was defeated by Bahlol Lodi and he merged Jaunpur into the Delhi Sultanate

questions.question_text: Zamorin was—
questions.explanation: Zamorin was a Hindu king of Calicut, Zamorin was his paternal title. Calicut is situated on the Malabar coast. In the middle ages, due to being a center of production of calico, i.e., muslin, it is known as Calicut. The word Zamorin is a form of the Malayalam language word Samuthiri, which has been made by adding the Sanskrit word ‘Swami or Shri’

questions.question_text: Which ruler is known as ‘Akbar of Kashmir’?
questions.explanation: In 1420 AD, Shahi Khan sat on the throne of Kashmir under the name ‘Zain-ul-Abidin’. He was a great ruler of Kashmir. From a religious perspective, he was a tolerant ruler. Due to his religious liberalism, many historians call him the Akbar of Kashmir. During his time, remarkable progress was made in the physical and cultural fields of Kashmir. Like Alauddin Khilji, he also implemented price control in Kashmir, due to which he is also called the Alauddin of Kashmir. He was the first ruler who also abolished the ‘Jizya’ tax imposed on non-Muslims

questions.question_text: Among the following foreign travellers, who visited India during the reign of Jahangir?
questions.explanation: Francisco Pelsaert was a Dutch traveller who came to India during the reign of Jahangir. He presented the description of the travelogue of that time in his book 'Jahangir’s India: The Remonstrantie of Francisco Pelsaert'. He has described the industries and commercial activities of Indian cities, mainly spices and indigo trade. He was also the head of the Dutch mint of that time, which was situated in Agra

questions.question_text: The Battle of Diu between the Portuguese and Gujarat, supported by Muslim allied armies, was fought in the year ________.
questions.explanation: Sultan Malik Ayyaz of Gujarat had changed one of the main ports of Gujarat and one of the main entry points between India and the Persian Gulf. The Battle of Diu took place on 2 February, 1509 between the Portuguese and the Sultan of Gujarat Malik Ayyaz. The reason was that the Sultan's merchant ships were being stopped by the Portuguese from going out and destroying them

questions.question_text: In which language was Malfuzat-i-Timuri written?
questions.explanation: Malfuzat-i-Timuri is the autobiography of Timur Lang. Its language is Mongol Turkish. Abu Talib Hussaini translated it into Persian. In this context, Zafarnama, which is the biography of Timur and a copy of Malfuzat-i-Timuri. It was written by Surajuddin Ali Yazdi under the patronage of Timur's son

questions.question_text: What was the number of first-class nobles determined in Mewar by Maharana Amar Singh II?
questions.explanation: After the death of Maharana Jai Singh, his son Amar Singh II became the ruler of Mewar. He created many rules for following royal rules and managements of Mewar. Amar Singh II also made rules for the nobles in the state and created two types of categories of jagirs in which the determination of first and second class jagirs was done. During the reign of Amar Singh II, the number of first-class nobles was 16 and the number of second-class nobles was 32. He played the role of a good administrator and strengthened the administrative system of the state

questions.question_text: The Battle of Hirajeer was fought between whom among the following?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Hirajeer took place between Rathore king Maldeo of Marwar and Sher Shah Suri’s general Daulat Khan. In this, Daulat Khan was defeated and Maldeo was victorious. On account of this defeat, Sher Shah Suri fought the battle of Giri-Sumel and after heavy destruction, he was victorious. In this battle, he said ‘‘that I lost the empire of Hindustan for a handful of millet’’

questions.question_text: According to Atpur inscription, from which place did the Guhilas of Mewar come?
questions.explanation: According to the Atpur inscription, the description of the founder of the Guhila dynasty of Mewar is found in this way. Anandpur vinirgatviprakulanand mahideva :- whose meaning is that the lineage origin has been traced from the Brahmin family of Anandpur. The inscription contains a claim of Brahma-Kshatriya status. A claim of Solar dynasty, emergence from the Sun has been made. According to tradition, from the second half of the tenth century to the second half of the eleventh century, Gopinath Sharma believes that Guhilas were originally residents of Anandpur (Vadnagar), who were descendants of Brahmins and came from here and established a kingdom in Mewar
