questions.question_text: Among the following scholars, who has considered the origin of Guhilas from the Kshatriya dynasty?
questions.explanation: Gauri Shankar Hirachand Ojha is considered a renowned historian of Rajasthani history. His opinion regarding the origin of Rajputs is quite popular. He believed that the origin of Rajputs has happened from the descendants of ancient Kshatriyas, from which these are Chandravanshi and Suryavanshi Rajputs. He gave proof of this from many inscriptions and literary texts that Rajputs are descendants of ancient Kshatriyas. This very opinion related to the origin of Rajputs is his most favorite

questions.question_text: Which of the following inscriptions does not support the theory of the origin of Rajputs from the Brahmin dynasty?
questions.explanation: Scholars who proved the Brahmin dynasty origin of Rajputs have called Rajputs related to the Brahmin class by considering the Bijolia inscription as an example. In this inscription, the successor of Vasudeva, Samanta, has been called a Vatsagotriya Brahmin. This statement has been confirmed in Sundha Inscription and Sundha Mata Inscription and Achaleshwar Inscription. Rishi Shringi inscription is not related to the evidence of the Brahmin dynasty origin of Rajputs

questions.question_text: From which of the following inscriptions is information about the genealogy from Bappa Rawal to Maharana Kumbha found?
questions.explanation: Bappa Rawal or Kalbhoj were the sons of Mahendra II. His genealogy is obtained from the Ranakpur inscription or Prashasti. It has a description of the genealogy from Bappa to Kumbha. This inscription has a description of their victories and achievements

questions.question_text: Which Chauhan ruler constructed the Sambhar Lake?
questions.explanation: In the seventh century, Vasudeva established the Chauhan dynasty of Shakambhari in the Sambhar-Ajmer region. Chauhans were feudatories of the Pratiharas. He only got the Sambhar Lake constructed. In the Bijolia record, Vasudeva has been called the builder of Sambhar Lake. In the Puranas, as a story, this lake is considered as the blessing of the guardian goddess of the Chauhan dynasty, Shakambhari Devi

questions.question_text: What is included in Theocracy (Dharmatantra) history-
questions.explanation: Theocracy is a state in which religion and religious officials are given prominence in the operation of the state. In such a state, God reveals his laws to the people through some vision or prophet. During the Sultanate period, the Sultans operated their state on the faith in God on the theory of kingship. It is written in the belief of divine origin of kingship in Manusmriti that the creation of the king was done by God, hence he has irresistible power and supreme authority

questions.question_text: Who compiled the book named Mriga-Pakshi-Shastra in the field of biology in the thirteenth century?
questions.explanation: The Sanskrit book written by Jain writer Hamsa Deva is Mriga Pakshi Shastra. Hamsadeva is a saint of the 13th century. This book has been written in two parts. Its first part is on the description of animals and the second part is a brief description of their nature and other physical characteristics in groups related to various birds

questions.question_text: "Efforts to extend Mughal administration to Golconda, Bijapur and Karnataka brought it to the brink of collapse-------Perhaps it would have been better advice for Aurangzeb to accept this advice of his eldest son Shah Alam that some parts of Bijapur and Golconda should be merged with himself, an agreement should be made with them and they should be allowed to rule over Karnataka, which was very far and whose management was difficult." Whose thoughts are these?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) "The attempt to spread the Mughal administration to Golconda, Bijapur, and Karnataka brought it to the verge of ruin.... Perhaps Aurangzeb would have been given better advice if he had accepted the advice of his eldest son Shah Alam to reach an understanding with Golconda and Bijapur by taking some parts with him and allowing them to rule over Karnataka, which was very far and whose management was difficult." This thought is by 'Satish Chandra'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a jagirdar state of the Bengal Sultanate?
questions.explanation: The glorious era of Bengal began during the reign of Alauddin Hussain Shah (1493 - 1519 AD). During his reign, Bengal expanded into Assam in the north, and Odisha, Chittagong, and Arakan in the south-west. Alauddin Khalji won Malwa in 1305 AD and merged it into the Delhi Sultanate. Malwa remained an integral part of Delhi until 1398 AD

questions.question_text: Poet Chandidas contributed to the popularity of which language?
questions.explanation: Chandidas was a poet of the Bengali language in the 14th century. His 'love songs addressed to Rami Dhobi' were very popular in the medieval period. And they were also the inspiration for Vaishnava and Sahajiya religious movements. His songs sought equality between human and divine love

questions.question_text: What is not a feature of Abul Fazl's historical writing?

options.A: Use of a logic-based approach towards history
options.B: Giving space to the achievements of non-Muslims in historical writing
options.C: Writing on the basis of all available sources of that time
options.D: According to the tradition of historical writing of the Sultanate period (38)

questions.explanation: Features of Abul Fazl's historical writing– 1. He gave a detailed account of the political events of the medieval period and used an approach based on his own logic. 2. He also gave space to the achievements of non-Muslims in historical writing. 3. And he did the work of writing history based on all the sources available at that time, in which the writing work was not done according to the sources of the Sultanate period.

questions.question_text: Radha Vallabh sect is a branch of which?
questions.explanation: In the Radha Vallabh sect of Shri Hit Harivansh, there was a practice of collective worship of Radha-Krishna. This sect is considered based on Nimbarka's method of practice. Shri Hit Harivansh gave the sermon of the worship of Lord Radha Vallabh and his love-devotion. Radha Vallabh sect is a branch of the Sanakadi sect

questions.question_text: In medieval South India, what was 'Baji-giri'?
questions.explanation: In medieval India, Bajigiri was a guerrilla warfare method; this word is used in the sense of 'chhapamar' (guerrilla). This word originated from the Spanish language, which means short war

questions.question_text: Who composed 'Chandi di Var'?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh included 116 hymns of his father Guru Tegh Bahadur in the Adi Granth Sahib compiled by Guru Arjan Dev, but his own compositions mainly included Japji Sahib, Krishna Avtar, Pakhyan Charitra, Chandi di Var, etc. In this way, Guru Gobind Singh compiled 16 works

questions.question_text: Which saint of Maharashtra is known as 'India's first Dalit poet'?
questions.explanation: The famous saint of Maharashtra, Chokhamela, is considered India's first Dalit poet, who composed many Abhangs. Because of this, he has been called the first great poet of the Dalit Mahar caste of India

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Jean-Baptiste Tavernier is false?

options.A: He came to India six times during the reign of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb.
options.B: His work 'Six Voyages' was published in 1676 AD and received extraordinary success.

questions.explanation: The most famous traveler of the seventeenth century, Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, was born in 1605 AD in the city of Paris, France. He was a jeweler by profession and traveled to India 6 times during the era of Shah Jahan (1627-1658) and Aurangzeb (1658-1707). His work 'The Six Voyages' was published in 1676 AD and it received extraordinary success

questions.question_text: In the time of Sher Shah Suri, the main officers in the Pargana were–
questions.explanation: In the administration of Sher Shah Suri, the Sarkar was divided into Parganas. In which there used to be one Shiqdar, one Munsif, one Fotedar, and two Karkuns. The work of the Munsif was to decide civil cases and to arrange for the measurement of land and revenue

questions.question_text: Due to differences regarding concessions to the Portuguese, which ruler was called to the ship by the Portuguese and drowned after being dropped from the ship under the pretext of meeting, which ruler of the 16th century was that?
questions.explanation: Bahadur Shah was the last great ruler of Gujarat. He was very angry with the Portuguese about building a fort at Diu. In this context, when he was returning after reaching an agreement on a Portuguese warship, on 13 January 1537 AD, the Portuguese killed him. With the death of Bahadur Shah, the great era of Gujarat set

questions.question_text: Who was the head officer of the Intelligence Department under Sher Shah?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - For an arbitrary and despotic ruler, there is an absolute need for an organized intelligence department. Realizing the importance of the intelligence department, Sher Shah arranged for it and paid special attention to it. Barid-i-Mumalik was its head officer.

questions.question_text: Who granted the post of 'Wakil-e-Mutlaq' to Nizam-ul-Mulk?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation - The independent Asaf Jahi dynasty was established in Hyderabad by Chin Qilich Khan (Nizam-ul-Mulk), appointed Subedar in the Deccan by Muhammad Shah (Mughal Emperor), in 1724 AD. In 1722 AD, Muhammad Shah had entrusted the Subedari of the six Subas of the Deccan to Chin Qilich Khan and granted the post of 'Wakil-e-Mutlaq'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correct?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – Marco Polo - Maravarman Kulasekhara Sir Thomas Roe - Jahangir Father Anthony Monserrate - Akbar Tavernier - Shah Jahan

questions.question_text: What was the main basis of the Sultan's power in medieval India?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation - In medieval India, the army was the main basis of the Sultan's power. Only through the army could peace be maintained in the state. Sultan Balban established a military department for the first time in the Sultanate period and first of all Alauddin Khalji organized a standing army.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Sayyid Muhammad was the founder of the Nurbakhshiya sect.
options.B: The ideas of the Nurbakhshiya sect are contained in the book named Fiqh-i-Ahwal.
options.D: The Nurbakhshiyas had to face troubles during the time of Mirza Haidar Dughlat, who committed atrocities on them.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation – Nurbakhshiyas do not celebrate Muharram, this statement is not correct. Whereas Sayyid Muhammad Nurbakhsh Kahistani was the founder of the Nurbakhshiya sect. The ideas of the Nurbakhshiya sect are contained in the book named Fiqh-i-Ahwal. The Nurbakhshiyas had to face troubles during the time of Mirza Haidar Dughlat, who committed atrocities on them. These things are correct.

questions.question_text: To whom were Madad-e-Maash grants given?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– Based on the division of land tax, all the land of the Mughal Empire was divided into three parts. 1. Khalisa land 2. Jagir land 3. Sayurghal land Sayurghal land was also called Madad-e-Maash or Milk land. This land was given as a grant to saints and scholars (people of religious inclination).

questions.question_text: Match the following – List-I (Author) | List-II (Work)
questions.explanation: 1. Tenali Ram - Panduranga Mahatmyam 2. Allasani Peddana - Manu Charitra 3. Bhattumurthi - Narasabhupaliyam 4. Timmanna - Parijathapaharan Prabandham

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra - Nagaur Hindola Mahal - Mandu Adina Mosque - Malda-West Bengal Atala Mosque - Jaunpur Note – In the above question, the match of Adina Mosque was given as Ahmedabad, which is wrong. This mosque is situated in Malda district of West Bengal, which was built as a Royal Mosque by Sikandar Shah of the Bengal Sultanate.

questions.question_text: Match the museum and library of List-I with their given places in List-II. List-I | List-II A. Salar Jung Museum | 1. Kolkata B. National Museum | 2. New Delhi C. National Library | 3. Hyderabad D. National Archives | 4. New Delhi A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Salar Jung Museum - Hyderabad National Museum - New Delhi National Library - Kolkata National Archives - New Delhi

questions.question_text: Match Table I with Table II: I | II A. Silver Tanka | 1. Alauddin Khalji B. Diwan-i-Amir Kohi | 2. Firoz Tughlaq C. Dar-ul-Shafa | 3. Iltutmish D. Shahna-i-Mandi | 4. Muhammad bin Tughlaq Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched table is as follows I | II Silver Tanka - Iltutmish Diwan-i-Amir Kohi - Muhammad bin Tughlaq Dar-ul-Shafa - Firoz Tughlaq Shahna-i-Mandi - Alauddin Khalji

questions.question_text: Here, which traveller is not correctly matched with the king in whose reign he came?
questions.explanation: Niccolo Conti (1420-21) - Deva Raya I Ibn Battuta (1333-47) - Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq Abdur Razzak (1443-1444) - Deva Raya II Niccolao Manucci (1614-15) - Jahangir

questions.question_text: Match the medieval cities of List-I with the rivers given in List-II on whose banks these cities were established. List-I | List-II A. Hoshangabad | 1. Narmada B. Hampi | 2. Tungabhadra C. Srirangapatna | 3. Kaveri D. Hyderabad | 4. Musi A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Hoshangabad - Narmada river Hampi - Tungabhadra river Srirangapatna - Kaveri Hyderabad - Musi

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I | List-II A. Jodhpur region | 1. Marwari B. Jaipur | 2. Dhundhari C. Kota-Bundi | 3. Hadauti D. Mathura-Barsana | 4. Braj Bhasha A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Jodhpur region - Hadauti Jaipur - Dhundhari Kota-Bundi - Marwari Mathura-Barsana - Braj Bhasha

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II~ List-I List-II A. Padmavat 1. Braj Bhasha B. Sur Sagar 2. Awadhi C. Ramcharitmanas 3. Awadhi D. Vinaya Patrika 4. Braj Bhasha A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct matching is Padmavat Awadhi Sur Sagar Braj Bhasha Ramcharitmanas Awadhi Vinaya Patrika Braj Bhasha

questions.question_text: Which of the following painters was not associated with Bikaner painting style?
questions.explanation: Painters associated with Bikaner painting style are (1) Jayakishan Metherane, (2) Shah Muhammad, (3) Abu Hamid, (4) Ramlal, (5) Mastaram, (6) Shahdin Hamid, (7) Ruknuddin, Sahabdin.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following documentary writer travellers who came to travel to India in chronological order and choose the correct option from the given options:
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ibn Ahmed Abu Rihan Al-Biruni came to India with Mahmud Ghaznavi in 998 AD Ibn Battuta came from Morocco to the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in 1333 AD and Abdur Razzak Kamaluddin Ibn Ishaq Al Samarkandi came as an ambassador of the ruler of Persia to the Vijayanagara empire of Devaraya II in 1442-43 AD. Mahmud Wali Balkhi remained in India till 1626-31 AD.

questions.question_text: The founder of the Ranthambore branch of Chauhans was:
questions.explanation: The founder of the Ranthambore branch of Chauhans was Govind Raj. After the second battle of Tarain (1192 AD), Ghori made Govind Raj the ruler of Ajmer under his subordination. The Chauhans of Ajmer considered this as their insult. Therefore, under the leadership of Govind Raj’s uncle Hariraj, the Chauhans attacked Govind Raj. Govind Raj ran away to Ranthambore and developed his power here

questions.question_text: Which city was named ‘Khizrabad’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─ Alauddin Khilji attacked Chittor in January 1303 and defeated the ruler King Ratan Singh there and took possession of it. The Sultan named Chittor ‘Khizrabad’ and after handing it over to his son Khizr Khan, he himself returned to Delhi.

questions.question_text: Under feudalism, what was the fundamental difference between jagir (fief) and jagirdari (vassalage)?

options.A: Jagir was a personal element whereas jagirdari was a property element
options.B: Jagir was a property element whereas jagirdari was a personal element
options.C: Jagir was the person who surrendered property and jagirdari was the surrendered property
options.D: Jagirdar was more important than jagir

questions.explanation: During the Mughal reign, the jagirdari system was widely prevalent, which later became the cause of its downfall. Jagirs were changeable and did not remain with a mansabdar for more than three or four years, i.e., jagir was a property element. Whereas jagirdari was a personal element because they were transferred, which did not make any difference to them. The major part of land revenue went to the jagirdar

questions.question_text: In the historical sources of medieval India, in what sense has the word ‘Chakla’ been used?

options.D: Regional unit between Subah and Pargana, but not necessarily equivalent to Sarkar.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation─ ‘Chakla’ in the Mughal period was the unit between Sarkar and Pargana, whose existence was in Shah Jahan’s time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Tax was collected for the empire's treasury under Khalisa Sharifa.
options.B: Continuous transfers of jagirs kept happening. It was possible that an area which was under Khalisa, could later be transferred to Jagir.
options.C: Jama-dami has no role in the allotment of jagirs.
options.D: Jagirs were given to mansabdars in lieu of cash salary.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation─ Among the given options, the statement (c) ``Jama-dami has no role in the allotment of jagirs'' is wrong, the estimated income of jagir was called Jama or Jama-dami, based on this the allotment of jagirs was done. Whereas tax was collected for the empire's treasury under Khalisa Sharifa. Jagirs were given to mansabdars in lieu of cash salary, not only this, continuous transfers of jagirs also kept happening. This fact is correct.

questions.question_text: Regarding music, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: The work related to classical music, Lajjat-i-Sikandari was composed under the patronage of Sultan Sikandar.
options.B: Abul Fazl has mentioned thirty-six musicians who played vocal and instrumental music in Akbar’s court.
options.C: Shah Jahan neither encouraged music in his court nor gave rewards to musicians. His interest was in architecture.
options.D: Aurangzeb generally gave rewards to musicians during the first ten years of his reign and it seems that he was dedicated to music.

questions.explanation: Shah Jahan was a very fond and music connoisseur. He used to listen to music daily in Diwan-i-Khas. He himself was a good singer. In Shah Jahan’s court, Lal Khan, Khushal Khan and Vilas Khan were major musicians. New styles of music also developed in Shah Jahan’s time

questions.question_text: Which of the following tax-free trade facilities come under the category of providing and reducing taxes?
questions.explanation: Sairdami, Mapha and Rahadari come under the category of providing tax-free trade facilities and reducing taxes. The collection of revenue on contract is called ‘Mukata’ (Mukata)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct? (i) Sectarian religious groups developed in early medieval India. Among these, theistic sects emphasizing bhakti worship became popular. (ii) Temples became dynamic sites of political, social, cultural and economic activities. (iii) Urban centers of early medieval India can be divided into two classes - one can be called administrative city and the other can be called commercial city. (iv) Chankya temples attracted various social groups, in this way they opposed the supporters of exclusion. Select the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Sectarian religious groups developed in early medieval India. Among these, theistic sects emphasizing bhakti worship became popular. During this period, temples became dynamic sites of political, social, cultural and economic activities. Because temples attracted various social groups, in this way they opposed the supporters of exclusion. This is not true (iii) Early medieval India's urban centers can be divided into two classes - one can be called administrative city and the other can be called commercial city. (iv) Chankya temples attracted various social groups, in this way they opposed the supporters of exclusion. Select the correct answer from the options given below : (a) (i), (ii), (iv) (b) (ii), (iii), (iv) (c) (i), (ii), (iii) (d) (i), (ii) UGC/NTA June 2019 IInd Paper Ans. (a) : Sectarian religious groups developed in early medieval India. Among these, theistic sects emphasizing bhakti worship became popular. During this period, temples became dynamic sites of political, social, cultural and economic activities. Because temples attracted various social groups, in this way they opposed the supporters of exclusion. This is not true.

questions.question_text: Name two emperors of India and Uzbekistan who agreed to set the boundary of both empires on Hindu-Kush.
questions.explanation: In the year 1583, Abdullah Khan Uzbeg snatched Balkh from Timurid ruler Shahrukh Mirza and after that in 1585 he also won Badakhshan. After the death of Mirza Hakim (1585), Akbar included Kabul in his empire. In this way, now the Mughal and Uzbeg boundaries touched each other. Akbar sent one of his envoys Hakim Humam to Abdullah Khan with a letter and oral message, after which an agreement was reached between the two states to set the boundary on Hindu-Kush

questions.question_text: Where was the concept of free kitchen (Langar) adopted by the Sikhs from?
questions.explanation: Langar practice started around the 15th century. It is clear from the preaching and travels of Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji that he used to eat with companions, devotees while sitting on the ground. But Guru Angad Dev Ji started the regular practice of Langar. The concept of Langar or free kitchen was adopted by the Sikh Gurus from Sufi dargahs or Khanqahs

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta was a traveller from Morocco who came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. He has described the mango produced in India with exaggeration. According to him, people of India make pickle of raw mangoes and eat ripe fruits by sucking or cutting them. Ibn Battuta mentions the production of cotton by sowing its seeds

questions.question_text: Which of the following sources are related to the history of Sindh? (i) Fatawa-i-Jahandari (ii) Mirat-i-Sikandari (iii) Tarikh-i-Tahiri (iv) Majma-i-Shahjahani Select the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Tarikh-i-Tahiri was written by Mir Tahir Muhammad Nasyani whereas the author of Majma-i-Shahjahani was Yusuf Mirak. These books are important sources to know the history of Sindh

questions.question_text: In the 18th-century source ‘Tuhfat-ul-Hind’, a vast vocabulary of which dialect has been given?
questions.explanation: ‘Tuhfat-ul-Hind’ composed by Mirza Khan is a very famous dictionary of medieval times. This book mentions the region of Braj Bhasha. This book, composed in the 18th century, contains a collection of vast vocabularies of Braj Bhasha

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II : List-I List-II
questions.explanation: UGC/NTA June 2019 IInd Paper Explanation : List-I List-II (A) Malik Sarvar Jaunpur Sultanate (B) Zafar Khan Gujarat Sultanate (C) Dilawar Khan Ghauri Malwa Sultanate (D) Alauddin Hasan Bahmani Sultanate

questions.question_text: Who founded the city of Burhanpur on the banks of Tapti river around 1400 AD?
questions.explanation: UGC/NTA June 2019 IInd Paper Explanation : Burhanpur is a famous city of Khandesh situated on the banks of Tapti river in Madhya Pradesh. Its foundation was laid around 1400 AD by Sultan Nasir Khan Faruqi of the Faruqi dynasty. Akbar occupied Burhanpur in 1599 AD and merged Khandesh into the Mughal empire in 1601 AD. Burhanpur was the capital of Khandesh. Mumtaz Mahal died at this place in 1631 AD.

questions.question_text: Which city was called ‘Shiraz of the East’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In 1394 AD, a chieftain of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, Malik Sarvar (eunuch), established an independent Sharqi kingdom in Jaunpur. Whose title was ``Malik-ush-Sharq’’ (Lord of the East). Due to its literary and artistic progress, Jaunpur was called ``Shiraz of India’’.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below – List-I List-II A. Tughlaqabad (i) Alauddin B. Adilabad (ii) Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq C. Firozabad (iii) Muhammad Tughlaq D. Khizrabad (iv) Firoz Tughlaq Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– Tughlaqabad - Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, Adilabad - Muhammad Tughlaq, Firozabad - Firoz Tughlaq, Khizrabad - Alauddin Khilji.

questions.question_text: Which of the following revenue grants was not given to religious intellectuals?
questions.explanation: UGC/NTA June 2019 IInd Paper Explanation : Amalaka, Idrar and Inam revenue grants were given to religious intellectuals. Auqaf were ‘Waqf properties’. The word ‘Waqf’ is derived from the Arabic word ‘Waqafa’ which means to stop or to bind and keep.

questions.question_text: Below two statements are given, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) : Assertion (A): Some important characteristics of feudalism are found in early medieval period, but it was quite different from European feudalism. Reason (R) : South India was the period of early medieval urban development as is clear from the development of crafts, trade, trade unions and urban centers. What is correct among the following with reference to both the above statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Some important characteristics of feudalism are found in early medieval period, but it was different from European feudalism in the sense that there is a lack of agricultural slavery (serfdom) and manor system in Indian feudalism. Hence Indian feudalism has been called semi-feudal. South India was the period of early medieval urban development as is clear from the development of crafts, trade, unions and urban centers

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Thomas Roe was the ambassador of English Emperor James I who came to Jahangir’s court in 1615 AD, with the aim of obtaining his commercial facilities he won over Nurjahan, Asaf Khan and Khurram by giving expensive gifts and made them on his side. Jahangir issued a farman and provided commercial facilities to the English in Surat. He lived in the Mughal court for 3 years. Jahangir gave him the title of Khan. He wrote a book named ‘‘Travels in the East Indies’’

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I List-II (Source) (Region)
questions.explanation: List-I List-II (Source) (Region) (A) Chachnama Sindh (B) Riyaz-us-Salatin Bengal (C) Mirat-i-Ahmadi Gujarat (D) Nuskh-i-Dilkusha Deccan

questions.question_text: In which Persian book is the initial literary reference to the carding bow for cotton found?
questions.explanation: In the Persian book Qavaid-i-Leksikan, the initial literary reference to the carding bow for cotton is found

questions.question_text: Shah Jahan was the first Mughal emperor who started a new flag named Mahi-Maratib. It was considered the highest honour granted to any person. Before Shah Jahan, which Indian ruler used to grant this?
questions.explanation: The flag named Mahi-Maratib which was the highest honour granted to any person in the Mughal period and it was granted only to those whose rank was 7 thousand or above. This flag started being granted during Shah Jahan’s time. Before this, this flag was granted by the Sultans of Delhi

questions.question_text: In 1641, in which language did Banarsidas write a very interesting autobiography, Ardh-Kathanak?
questions.explanation: Banarsidas was originally a wealthy Jain merchant and poet. He is known for his poetic autobiography Ardh-Kathanak (1641). This autobiography is a verse-based autobiography in Braj Bhasha. This is the first autobiography written in any Indian language. At the time he composed this, his age was 35 years. (In Jain tradition, life is considered to be 110 years, hence the autobiography has been called Ardh-Kathanak)

questions.question_text: Match the places obtained by the Portuguese in India with their years and choose the correct answer using the code given below~ A. Calicut 1. 1522 B. Cannanore 2. 1525 C. Dabul 3. 1500 D. Pasvani 4. 1502 Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: A. Calicut – 1500 AD B. Cannanore – 1502 AD C. Dabul – 1522 AD D. Pasvani – 1525 AD

questions.question_text: Which product was not introduced in India by the Portuguese?
questions.explanation: The place of origin of betel leaf is the Malay archipelago of Southeast Asia. It has many names, such as Tambul, Nagavalli, Nagavallidal, Tambuli, Parna, Nagarbel etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched? Event Year

options.A: Murder of Sultan Jalaluddin Khilji 1296 AD
options.B: Khizr Khan captured the throne of Delhi 1414 AD
options.C: Sikandar Lodi founded a new city Agra 1504 AD

questions.explanation: The Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram was fought in 1540 AD between Sher Shah Suri and Mughal ruler Humayun. After defeating Humayun in this battle, Sher Shah occupied Agra, Delhi, Sambhal, Gwalior, Lahore etc., drove Humayun out of India and re-established the Afghan empire in North India

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and use the code given below to choose the correct answer~ 1. Timur’s invasion 2. Introduction of symbolic currency 3. Market control policy 4. Rebellion of Malik Chhajju Code–
questions.explanation: Rebellion of Malik Chhajju – 1290 AD Market control policy – 1296–1316 AD Introduction of symbolic currency - 1329–30 AD Timur’s invasion - 1398 AD

questions.question_text: The author of Second Rajatarangini was–
questions.explanation: Jonaraja was a 15th-century Kashmiri historian and Sanskrit poet. He wrote a history book named Second Rajatarangini in which he continued Kalhana’s Rajatarangini's account up to the year 1149 AD and wrote the description till his contemporary Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin. But Jonaraja could not write the entire account of his reign. Because Jonaraja died in the 35th year of his reign. His disciple Srivara wrote the further account and the name of his work was ‘Third Rajatarangini’ which is about the years 1459 – 1486 AD

questions.question_text: The main subjects of Kangra style of painting were:
questions.explanation: In the history of Indian painting, the Kangra style has a special place within the Pahari style developed in the middle ages. This style developed during the time of Rajput dynasties (mainly Katoch dynasty). In Kangra style, there is a dominance of mythological stories in which Radha-Krishna, Shiva-Parvati and hero-heroine of Ritikaal, women’s beauty, union-separation etc. are the main paintings. In Kangra style, female figures have been depicted effectively and in an ideal form. And in a secondary form, portrait paintings are also dominant

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer using the code given below : List-I (Artist) List-II (Title received)

His father Ramdev was a Bharadwaj Rajput, who was a simple farmer. Banda's objective was to establish a Sikh state in Punjab. For this, he made Lohgarh his capital. He minted coins in the name of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh and also had a seal or stamp of the Sikh state made. He removed Mughal officials in Sirhind and appointed Sikh officials and continued to fight continuously against the Mughals. New Mughal Emperor Jahandar Shah and after him Farrukhsiyar were also ready to suppress the Sikh rebellion. Finally, in 1716 A.D., the Mughal army surrounded Banda Bahadur at a place named Gurdaspur. After a siege of about eight months, Banda Bahadur surrendered. He and his companions were brought to Delhi, where, upon refusing to accept Islam, he and his companions were hanged.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– In the Vijayanagara Empire, courtesans were divided into two categories. One was those who were associated with temples and the other was those who lived an independent life. Courtesans, regardless of their caste or community, had a single caste. Women of this class were sufficiently educated. Most of the courtesans were wealthy and privileged. Poor parents either handed over their young daughters to courtesans or sold them. The special thing is that these courtesans were not looked down upon in society. All courtesans mandatorily participated in public festivals. Both the King and the feudatories unhesitatingly maintained contact with courtesans. However, they were not appointed to important posts in the administration. daughters to courtesans, or sold them. On public festivals, all courtesans mandatorily participated in the festival.

questions.question_text: Which ruler of Malabar in 1766 stopped the incursions from Mysore and imposed his conditions on the trade of black pepper to keep the Dutch and English trading companies under control?
questions.explanation: In the second half of the 18th century, the Hindu ruler Varma Palassi Raja ruled on the Malabar coast. During his reign, the English trading companies (East India Company) were expanding their trade and political influence towards South India. Those companies were increasing their authority over the states by creating discord among Indian kings. Due to this, the British would assign the task of collecting revenue from farmers to Indian kings and would not care at all about the farmers who did the farming. Gradually, the British kept increasing the amount of revenue on the farmers, due to which the patience of the farmers broke. At this same time in 1766 AD, Varma Palassi Raja helped the British against the ruler of Mysore, Tipu Sultan. In return for this help, a verbal condition was made with the British that 'Varma Palassi Raja' would collect the revenue of Kochi and would regulate (monitor) the farming and trade of black pepper, but after the Mysore war, the British backed out of their promises, due to which 'Varma Palassi Raja' rebelled against the British and stopped giving revenue of Kochi to the British and did not care at all about the farmers who were farming. Gradually, the British increased the revenue amount for the farmers, due to which the patience of the farmers broke. At this same time in 1766 AD, 'Varma Palassi Raja' helped the British against the ruler of Mysore, Tipu Sultan. In return for this help, a verbal condition was made with the British that 'Varma Palassi Raja' would have the right to collect the revenue of Kochi and the regulation (oversight) of the cultivation and trade of black pepper, but after the Mysore war, the British reneged on their promises, due to which 'Varma Palassi Raja' rebelled against the British and stopped paying revenue of Kochi to the British.

Under this policy, if a state did not have a legitimate heir, it was merged into the British Empire. The order of merging the states given in the question is Annexation of Satara - 1848 AD Annexation of Jaitpur - 1849 AD Annexation of Jhansi - 1853 AD Annexation of Nagpur - 1854 AD

questions.question_text: In British rule, to whom did the future buyers of Indian exports pay pound sterling to buy from the India Secretary located in London?
questions.explanation: During British rule, the future buyers of Indian exports used to pay pound sterling to the India Secretary located in London to buy Council Bills Special Facts Interest on the foreign loans of the East India Company, military expenditure, railways, irrigation, road transport and other various infrastructural facilities, guaranteed interest on foreign investments, the government's purchase policy, due to which it kept buying all its stationery from England and ultimately 'Home Charges', i.e., the expenditure of the entire establishment of the India Secretary at the India Office in London, and along with it, the payment of salaries, pensions, and training expenses of military and non-military personnel, i.e., the people governing India, etc. The actual transfer of wealth happened through the sale of "Council Bills".

questions.question_text: The Doctrine of Lapse was applied to which state in 1852?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie annexed the following states according to the Doctrine of Lapse – State Year (i) Satara 1848 (ii) Jaitpur and Sambalpur 1849 (iii) Baghat 1850 (iv) Udaipur 1852 (v) Jhansi 1853 (vi) Nagpur 1854 Note– In 1856 AD, Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh on the basis of misgovernance.

questions.question_text: Where did Job Charnock establish an English factory in 1690?
questions.explanation:  In February, 1690 AD, upon a Mughal settlement being reached, Job Charnock (under the leadership of Company officials) was appointed as the Company's agent in Bengal.  On 10 February, 1691 AD, Job Charnock established an English factory in Sutanuti.  In 1698-99 AD, after the permission of Bengal Subahdar Azim-us-Shan, the company received the zamindari of Sutanuti, Gobindapur, and Calcutta for paying Rs 1200. (Calcutta = Gobindapur + Sutanuti = Modern Kolkata) The foundation was laid by Job Charnock. Later, the foundation of Fort William was laid in Kolkata.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Dutch East India Company established?
questions.explanation: In 1602 AD, the Dutch East India Company 'Vereenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie' was established. The parliament of Holland gave it the right to trade with India and countries of the East for 21 years. It also had the right to wage war and make treaties, build forts, and conquer Indian territories. In India, the Dutch established the first Dutch factory in Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) of Andhra Pradesh in 1605 AD

questions.question_text: Who captured Goa from Bijapur in 1510?

options.A: Antonio de Albuquerque (Wait, the source says "Antonio de Ubray" but meant de Albuquerque, will translate based on "Albuquerque")

questions.explanation: In 1510 AD, Albuquerque captured Goa, which was the main port of the Sultan of Bijapur; this was the first Indian territory after Alexander that came under Europeans. By 1511 AD, Portuguese dominance had been established over Malacca and Hormuz. Established new forts at Socotra island located at the mouth of the Red Sea, Achin fort of Sumatra, etc

questions.question_text: Under which practice was it necessary for every Asian ship to take a passport from the Portuguese?
questions.explanation: The Portuguese tried to control the trade happening through the sea route and impose tax on it. Through their Cartaz-Amada-Capila system, they had a deep impact on Asian trade. Their main means was Cartaz or permit, which was backed by Amada force; no Indian or Arab ship could go into the Arabian Sea without taking a Cartaz from Portuguese officials. Cartaz meant a permit or entry paper Special Facts (1) Akbar's first introduction to the Portuguese was in Cambay (Gulf of Khambhat) of Gujarat. (2) Cartaz was a document issued by the Portuguese to provide permission to European traders for collective activities in Asian countries.

questions.question_text: Who discovered the direct sea route to Asia around the Cape of Good Hope?

options.D: Pedro (Wait, the Hindi text is garbled "PeWi ns". Based on standard history, Diaz found the Cape, Gama found India).

questions.explanation: Portuguese and Spaniards started the era of geographical discoveries. Portuguese navigator Bartolomeu Dias discovered the Cape of Good Hope in 1487 AD, which is called the Stormy Cape. In 1498 AD, Portuguese resident Vasco da Gama succeeded in reaching India by going around the Cape of Good Hope

questions.question_text: Under whose leadership did the British army defeat Haider Ali at Porto Novo?
questions.explanation: In July 1780 AD, Haider attacked Arcot in Carnatic. The Nawab ran to the British. As a result, two separate armies were sent under the leadership of Colonel Baillie and Hector Munro. Tipu did not let these two armies meet. Haider defeated Colonel Baillie in the Battle of Perambakkam (the Hindi text says "Ardoi" / Arni / Perambakkam, standard history is Perambakkam for Baillie). Hearing this news, Hector Munro threw war materials in the pond and fled. In this way, Haider Ali won Arcot in 1780 AD. Now the British separated the Nizam from Haider by giving him the Guntur region. They signed the Treaty of Salbai in 1782 AD with the Marathas, due to which the Marathas also got separated from Haider. Now Warren Hastings sent an army under the leadership of Eyre Coote. In the Battle of Porto Novo, Haider Ali was defeated and got injured. Haider Ali died on 7 December 1782 AD

questions.question_text: Which war ended with the Treaty of 'Aix-la-Chapelle'?
questions.explanation: The First Carnatic War (1746-48) is directly connected to European events. British and French were both fighting with the aim of establishing their sovereignty over Austria. On 21 September 1746 AD, under the leadership of La Bourdonnais, the French contingent captured Madras. Madras had been one of the main trading centers of the British since the middle of the 17th century. On the other hand, the British besieged Pondicherry from all sides from 6 September 1748 AD to 15 October 1748 AD. But Dupleix faced them with bravery and forced the British to sign a treaty, and the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle took place between the two armies in 1748. The war ended after this treaty, and Madras was returned to the British, and in return, France got Louisbourg in North America Special Facts- In the First Carnatic War, the French realized that even a small European army can face the biggest army of India with the help of Indian soldiers.

questions.question_text: When did the First Burma War happen?
questions.explanation: After capturing Bengal, the company's authorized territory reached the border of Burma. In 1818 AD, the King of Burma wrote a letter to Lord William Hastings and claimed Chittagong, Murshidabad, Dhaka, Kasimbazar. In 1821-22 AD, the King of Burma conquered the Ahom kingdom. In 1823 AD, the Burmese captured Shahpuri Island near Chittagong. On this, Amherst declared war and captured Burma from 1824 to 1826 AD and signed the Treaty of Yandabo

questions.question_text: Which of the following battles was not related to the First Anglo-Sikh War?
questions.explanation: The First Anglo-Sikh War was the result of Maharani Jindan's ambition. Major Broadfoot incited the Sikh army and Lal Singh and Tej Singh against the British. Khalsa gave the Sikhs permission to attack. In this way, four consecutive battles were fought between the British and Sikh armies, these are as follows (1) Mudki (1845) (2) Ferozeshah (iii) Aliwal (1846) (iv) Battle of Sobraon (10 February 1846) Note:- The Battle of Chillianwala was fought on 13 January 1849 AD, an indecisive battle during the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

questions.question_text: Between whom was the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon signed?
questions.explanation: This was an unwise decision of the Jodhpur Maharaja because fifteen days before this, Daulat Rao Sindhia, fed up with repeated defeats, signed a friendship treaty with the British. It happened on 30 December 1803 in Surji-Anjangaon. In this treaty, Sindhia promised not to attack the kings tied in the British treaty, besides not collecting tribute from them. In this situation, the Sambhar and Ajmer territories from Sindhia's possession went to the British

questions.question_text: Which fort was given to the British as a dowry by the Portuguese in 1661 AD?
questions.explanation: The Portuguese snatched Bombay from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1534 AD. In 1661 AD, on the occasion of the marriage of Portuguese princess Catherine of Braganza with Charles II, it was given to the British as a dowry

questions.explanation: To sign a treaty with the East India Company on 6 January, 1818 AD, Vishnaram Asopa represented the Jodhpur state

questions.question_text: Who ended the Dual Government system in Bengal?
questions.explanation: When Warren Hastings came as the Governor of Bengal, anarchy was spread in Bengal. He first ended the Dual Government system in which big mess was spread and started tax collection by employees. In this way, the work of Diwani was assigned to the Company. Appointed British collectors in every district and made Calcutta the capital and the center of the treasury. He freed the Nawab of Bengal from administration and made him a pensioner kept the work of the Company. Appointed British collectors in every district and made Calcutta the capital and the center of the royal treasury. Freed the Nawab of Bengal from administration and made him a pensioner.

questions.question_text: In 1665, who among the following took Bombay into their possession?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- Job Charnock settled Calcutta. Gerald Aungier took possession of Bombay; at that time this city was in a very ordinary condition. Later, the British developed it in a commercial form.

questions.question_text: The Treaty of Rajghat in 1806 was signed by the East India Company with whom?
questions.explanation: On 7 January 1806 AD, Jaswantrao Holkar signed the Treaty of Rajghat with General Lake

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below– List-I | List-II (State, annexed by Britain) | (Year)
questions.explanation: The correct match is as follows– List-I | List-II (State, annexed by Britain) | (Year) (A) Satara | (ii) 1848 (B) Nagpur | (iv) 1854 (C) Jhansi | (i) 1853 (D) Sambalpur | (iii) 1849 Lord Dalhousie annexed states based on the Doctrine of Lapse, they were Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854). UGC has considered option (c) as the answer to this question.

questions.question_text: Under the 'Doctrine of Lapse', which of the following princely states was not annexed?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie's 'Doctrine of Lapse' played a major role in increasing the rebellion of 1857. Through this, he expanded the British state to the natural borders of India. States included under the Doctrine of Lapse - Satara (1848), Jaitpur, Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854). At that time, the first Nawab of Awadh was Wajid Ali Shah. In 1848 AD, Colonel Sleeman's report about the Awadh region was presented. Under this, disorder was spread all over Awadh. Which he termed as anarchy. The entire blame for misgovernance was put on the head of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. Later, in 1856, Lord Dalhousie merged the Awadh state into British rule by accusing it of misgovernance based on the report of James Outram in 1854

questions.question_text: Which of these remained the initial capital of the Portuguese in India?
questions.explanation: The initial capital of the Portuguese in India was Cochin. In 1503 AD, the Portuguese established their first factory in Cochin and the second factory was established in Cannanore in 1505 AD. Portuguese Governor Albuquerque captured Goa from Bijapur, which was made the capital of the Portuguese in 1530 in place of Cochin

questions.explanation: Chinsurah, Balasore, and Nagapattinam were Dutch settlements in India, where they established their factories in 1653 AD in Chinsurah, 1658 AD in Balasore, and Nagapattinam. Mahe was a French settlement located on the Malabar coast

questions.question_text: Madras was returned to the British by the French-
questions.explanation: Madras was returned to the British under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle. The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle was about the succession of Austria. In the 17th-18th centuries, Anglo-French were eternal enemies; whenever their war started in Europe, war would erupt in whatever corner of the world those companies lived, and when there was a treaty, there was peace everywhere

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false about the British East India Company?

options.A: In 1609 AD, Captain Hawkins came to Jahangir's court with the intention of taking permission to open a factory in Surat.
options.B: Jahangir initially gave permission but later refused after coming under pressure from the Portuguese.
options.C: When the British defeated a Portuguese fleet at Swally, Jahangir issued a farman in favor of the British.
options.D: The Portuguese fleet was defeated under the leadership of Thomas Roe.

questions.explanation: Hawkins met Jahangir in 1609, Jahangir gave permission to open a factory, but refused ultimately after the Portuguese poisoned his ears. Later, after the defeat of the Portuguese, Jahangir issued a farman in favor of the British. The defeat of the Portuguese happened in 1612 AD at Swally (near Surat) by the British army under the command of Captain Thomas Best, not by Thomas Roe

questions.question_text: The Treaty of Bassein is related to which Anglo-Maratha war?
questions.explanation: Peshwa Bajirao II started putting discord among Maratha chieftains to maintain his dominance in Pune. Due to which there was a war among themselves. The result of this war was the Treaty of Bassein in 1802 AD with the British. Maratha chieftains considered the Treaty of Bassein a national insult and the Second Anglo-Maratha War started

questions.question_text: After the death of Tipu in 1799, whom did Wellesley seat on the throne of Mysore?
questions.explanation: Tipu died in 1799 AD while fighting against the British at Srirangapatnam fort. The British captured Srirangapatnam. The British took the Mysore state under their protection by making Krishnaraja, a two-year-old child of the Wodeyar dynasty, the Raja and also imposed a subsidiary alliance on him

questions.question_text: Who was the Governor General at the time of the Salbai Treaty?
questions.explanation: On 17 May 1782, the Treaty of Salbai was signed between the Marathas and the British. During this time, the Governor General of India was Warren Hastings. In the Treaty of Salbai, Sindhia played the role of mediator between the British and the Marathas, due to which peace remained between the two for the next 20 years

questions.question_text: The partition of Bengal done by Lord Curzon was cancelled by whom?
questions.explanation: The announcement of the partition of Bengal was made in Curzon's era on 19 July 1905, while the partition was effective from 16 October. Lord Hardinge Second cancelled the partition of Bengal on 12 December, 1911

questions.question_text: Where did the Danes establish their center for Indian trade in 1620 AD?
questions.explanation: The Danes came to India in 1616 AD after the British. In 1620 AD, they established their first factory in Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. After this, they established their second factory in Serampore, Bengal in 1676 AD. In 1745 AD, they sold all their factories to the British company and left India

questions.question_text: Who among the following successfully formed a tripartite treaty with the Nizam and Marathas against Tipu Sultan?
questions.explanation: Before the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92), Lord Cornwallis formed a tripartite organization against Tipu in 1790 AD, inspired by the anti-Tipu feelings of the Nizam and Marathas. In this war itself, Cornwallis said 'I have made my enemy cripple without making my allies strong'

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding Subsidiary Alliance is not true?

options.A: Subsidiary Alliance was an important clever step for the expansion of the British Empire.
options.B: The Subsidiary Alliance took place between the British and the native kings.
options.C: Native kings did not give permission for British envoys (Residents) to stay in their state.
options.D: Native kings agreed to bear the expenditure of the British army living in their state.

questions.explanation: Subsidiary Alliance was a policy propagated by Lord Wellesley from 1799-1805, through which Indian states received a guarantee of security from the British. In this treaty, foreign policy, war or peace was done after asking the British, and every state had to keep a British envoy in their capital

questions.question_text: From which sultanate of the Deccan did Albuquerque capture Goa?
questions.explanation: Albuquerque was appointed Viceroy in India in 1509 AD. He is considered the first actual founder of the Portuguese empire in India. Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510 AD from the Bijapur ruler Adil Shah Yusuf, which later became the capital of the Portuguese trading center in India

questions.question_text: Which of the following European wars was responsible for the beginning of the First Carnatic War?
questions.explanation: The reason for the First Carnatic War was the Austrian War of Succession, which lasted in Europe in 1746 AD. In this struggle for succession, the French won under the leadership of the Pondicherry Governor Dupleix. In return for sitting their claimant on the throne, they got the Northern Circars region

questions.question_text: Who laid the foundation of Calcutta in 1690 in the trade center Sutanuti?
questions.explanation: The history of Kolkata as a British settlement starts in 1690 AD with the establishment of a trading post here by an official of the British East India Company, Job Charnock. Later, Kolkata became the most important center of the Indian national movement. Till 1912 AD, Kolkata remained the capital of British India

questions.question_text: Which Governor of Madras among the following had signed the Treaty of Mangalore with Tipu Sultan?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Mangalore was signed between Tipu Sultan and the Governor of Madras, Lord Macartney, in March 1784. Under this, both returned each other's conquered territories and an agreement was made to release war prisoners from both sides. The British assured that they would maintain friendship with Mysore. Warren Hastings said on the Treaty of Mangalore, "What kind of man is Macartney, who despite the treaty loses the Carnatic."

questions.question_text: Who among the following was defeated in 'Porto Novo'?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Porto Novo was fought in 1782 between Haider Ali of Mysore and the Company under the leadership of Sir Eyre Coote. In this battle fought on the banks of the Kollidam river, Tipu Sultan, with the cooperation of 400 French soldiers, defeated 100 British and 1800 Indian soldiers, but the British navy captured Nagapattinam and convinced Haider Ali that he could not defeat the British. Consequently, Haider Ali had to pay a heavy penalty

questions.question_text: Where was Elphinstone a Governor?
questions.explanation: Mountstuart Elphinstone was a diplomat and historian from Scotland who was the Governor of Bombay (1819-1827 AD) on behalf of the British government, where he started many educational institutions. He wrote books about India and Afghanistan

questions.question_text: Where did the Dutch establish their first colony in India?
questions.explanation: The Dutch established their first factory in India in 1605 in Masulipatnam, in 1610 in Pulicat, in 1616 in Surat, in 1645 in Karikal, in 1653 in Chinsurah, in 1658 in Kasimbazar, and in 1663 in Cochin. It is noteworthy that the Dutch made Pulicat their headquarters

questions.question_text: Which European company among the following made Hooghly their base (base land) to carry out sea piracy in the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: In 1534, the Portuguese received permission from Bengal ruler Mahmud Shah to open their factory in Chittagong-Satgaon, through which the Portuguese captured the trade of the Bay of Bengal, which was later cleared by Aurangzeb from sea looters of Chittagong

questions.question_text: Which of the following options matches List I and List II: List I | List II I. Portuguese | A. Panaji, in 1510 II. Dutch | B. Masulipatnam, 1605 IV. French | D. Pondicherry, 1673 Options : I II III IV III. British | C. Madras, 1639
questions.explanation: Portuguese Governor Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510 AD and made it his headquarters Dutch naval leader Wader Haug in 1605 AD established the first Dutch factory in Masulipatnam. In 1639, the Frenchman Francis Day had a warehouse constructed in Madras (Note: Historically Francis Day was English, the text says Frenchman [Frenchman], I will translate the text's claim even if historically questionable, but usually text says 'Francis Day', I will write Francis Day). In 1673, the Director of the French Company, François Martin, established the Pondicherry settlement by taking a village from Sher Khan Lodi.

questions.question_text: In which year was the western coast regional headquarters shifted from Surat to Bombay?
questions.explanation: During British rule, a Governor used to be the main administrative and political official of Bombay. The executive government of the presidency was administered by the Governor. As Governor General of India, he had the same power and rights in the Presidency. Abraham Shipman was appointed the first Royal Governor of Bombay in 1662. When a raid was carried out by Maratha bands under Shivaji in Surat in 1664, the British factory was defended by George Oxenden. In 1668 AD, Bombay was transferred to the East India Company for an annual payment of 10 pounds. Ultimately, in 1687, the Company's headquarters was also shifted from Surat to Bombay and the British Crown formally took over this region after the company was dissolved

questions.question_text: Before the establishment of Calcutta, what was the biggest settlement of the British in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Among the European commercial companies, the British company was the most successful. The main reason for their success was their understanding of the nature of the entire Asian trade including India and taking the support of political military power in trade expansion. The initial objective of the company was 'not territory but trade'. By 1619 AD, company's commercial factories were established in Ahmedabad, Broach, Baroda, and Agra. All these trading houses were controlled from Surat. Shah Jahan, angry with the Portuguese, gave the British permission to trade in a limited area of Bengal. The British built their biggest settlement in Hooghly (Bengal). Hooghly was the biggest settlement of the British in Bengal before the establishment of Calcutta. After this, they also opened factories in Kasimbazar, Patna, Rajmahal. Ultimately, a farman was issued by Aurangzeb for the British for trade and in 1672, the commercial facility received by the British from the Mughal Subahdar Shaista Khan of Bengal was restored

questions.question_text: Which Carnatic war is remembered as the 'Battle of St. Thomé'?
questions.explanation: Carnatic war was a war fought between England and France in India in the middle of the 18th century to establish their dominance. The center of the war remained the territory of Carnatic, hence it is called Carnatic war. In the First Carnatic War (1746-48), the British took possession of some French ships under the leadership of British Admiral Boscawen; in return, with the help of French Governor La Bourdonnais, Dupleix forced the British Governor of Madras, Morse, to surrender. This war is known by the name of the 'Battle of St. Thomé'. This conflict ended between the two under a treaty named Aix-la-Chapelle. Madras was returned to the British

questions.question_text: Who among the following said, "It is better to live one day like a lion, than to live a whole life like a sheep"?
questions.explanation: The prominent rulers of the Mysore dynasty were Haider Ali and Tipu Sultan. After the death of his father Haider Ali, Tipu Sultan sat on the throne of Mysore. He had knowledge of Arabic, Persian, Urdu, and Kannada languages. He took the title of 'Sultan' and issued coins in his name in 1787. Influenced by the French Revolution, Tipu established the 'Jacobin Club' in Srirangapatnam and became its member and started calling himself 'Citizen Tipu'. He planted the 'Tree of Liberty', a symbol of the friendship between France and Mysore, in his capital Srirangapatnam. During the Fourth Anglo-Mysore (1799 AD) war, Tipu Sultan said "It is better to live one day like a lion than to live a whole life like a sheep". In this same war, on 4 May 1799, Tipu died while fighting the joint British army

questions.question_text: Who among the following started the four peripheral courts ('circuit courts'), of which three were for Bengal and one for Bihar?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793) remained the Governor General of Fort William Presidency. He started a new revenue system in the form of Permanent Settlement in Bengal in 1793 AD. He is credited with starting the civil service in India, hence he is called the 'Father of Civil Service'. Cornwallis gave his judicial reforms a final shape till 1793 and presented them as Cornwallis Code, which was based on 'separation of powers'. Under this, tasks were given in district civil courts. He ended the district criminal courts and started four peripheral courts (circuit courts), of which three courts were for Bengal and one for Bihar

questions.question_text: In the year 1739, the Marathas captured Salsette and Bassein from-
questions.explanation: Salsette is a group of islands located near Mumbai on the west coast of India. It has become the 7th most densely populated and 13th most populous island in the world, after the islands of Salsette, Hong Kong, and the Maldives. Salsette was captured by the Marathas in 1737, and the majority of the Northern Portuguese province was also taken by the Marathas in 1739. The British recaptured Salsette in 1774, which was formally given to the East India Company under the Treaty of Salbai (1782)

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first Nawab of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Murshid Quli Khan was the independent founder of Bengal. Aurangzeb appointed Murshid Quli Khan as the Subahdar of Bengal in 1701 AD. Farrukhsiyar handed over the Subahdari of Orissa to him in 1719 AD. Murshid Quli Khan shifted his capital from Dhaka to Murshidabad. Murshid Quli Khan was the first Nawab of Bengal

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy among the following was famous in the literary world by the name of 'Owen Meredith' because of being a litterateur?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton was the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880, who was a famous poet, novelist, and essayist. He was famous in the literary world by the name of 'Owen Meredith'. During his time, the Vernacular Press Act was implemented in 1878 AD

questions.question_text: Lord Wellesley sent whom as his envoy to the Shah's court of Iran?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) left the policy of peace in India and followed only the war policy. For empire expansion, he used the Subsidiary Alliance system. In 1799 AD, he sent an envoy named Mehdi Ali Khan to the court of the Shah of Iran. In November, 1800 AD, another envoy John Malcolm was sent to Iran with many valuable gifts. As a result, a treaty was made with the Shah in which the Shah promised not to give permission to the French to enter his country. Actually, Wellesley was a follower of Machiavelli

questions.question_text: Where did the Portuguese first construct their fort in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation— The rulers of Portugal were firmly determined to create a royal monopoly over eastern trade, in which there would be no interference not only from competing countries of Europe and Asia but also from private Portuguese traders. In this way, in establishing control over the Indian Ocean, the Portuguese adopted the method of using force from the beginning. Portuguese factories soon took the form of forts. In 1503 AD, the Portuguese constructed a small fort in Cochin, which was their first fort in India. Two years later, the second fort was constructed in Cannanore. In the same year 1505, the first Portuguese Viceroy Francisco de Almeida was sent to India, so that he could establish Portuguese rule in India. He was instructed by the Portuguese government to build Portuguese forts in India whose goal should not be security but establishing Portuguese control over Indian Ocean trade. The one who laid the foundation of the Portuguese empire in India was Afonso de Albuquerque. Other Portuguese forts were—Kilwa, Anjadiva, Goa. Goa was captured in 1510.

questions.question_text: When did the Battle of Buxar happen?
questions.explanation: On 22 October, 1764, the joint army of Mir Qasim, Nawab Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Badshah Shah Alam came face to face with the British army on the battlefield of Buxar. In this famous Battle of Buxar, the British army defeated the joint army on 23 October, 1764. Along with this, the path for the dominance of the East India Company over Bengal was paved

questions.question_text: Where was the first British factory in South India located?
questions.explanation: The European companies coming to India were successively: Portuguese, Dutch, British, Danes, French. In 1601 AD, the British company ship reached the spice islands of Indonesia. Under the leadership of Captain Hawkins, the Hector ship opened a permanent factory at the port of Surat in 1608 AD and established the first British factory in South India in Masulipatnam. Masulipatnam was the main port of the Golconda state

questions.explanation: The chronological order of the native princely states annexed during Dalhousie's era is Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), followed by Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854), and Awadh (1856).
