questions.question_text: Regarding the provisions of the Treaty of Salbai (1782), which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Salsette and Elephanta remained with the British.
options.B: Raghoba was given a 2500-member troop of the British army.
options.C: Broach was to be given to Sindhia.
options.D: Peshwa will expel all foreigners from his service.

questions.explanation: The following provisions (conditions) were there in the Treaty of Salbai (1782) 1. Salsette and Elephanta remained with the British. 2. The British abandoned the side of Raghunath Rao (Raghoba) and arrangements for his pension were made on behalf of the Peshwa. 3. Sindhia got back all his land west of the Yamuna river. 4. Conquered land territories in Bombay and the South were returned by one another. 5. As a result of this treaty, Haider Ali had to leave the land won from the Nawab of Arcot.

questions.question_text: What were Cartezes?

options.A: Permission letters issued by the Portuguese to ships in the Indian Ocean.
options.B: An ancient city destroyed by the Roman Republic.
options.C: A tax imposed by the Portuguese on Indian traders.
options.D: Large ships used by the Dutch for trade with India.

questions.explanation: Permission letters issued by the Portuguese to ships in the Indian Ocean are called Cartezes. Cartaz or Cartridge meant a permit, which every trader travelling through the Indian Ocean route had to take. To force the taking of Cartaz, the Portuguese used to show the fear of Amada power. This system itself was termed as the Cartaz-Amada-System. Under this system, Indian or other foreign ships were not allowed to carry black pepper and gunpowder. It is noteworthy that for trade from regions under Portuguese authority, even the Mughal Emperor Akbar had to take a Cartaz. The Portuguese called themselves "Masters of the Sea"

questions.question_text: Which Bengal Subahdar gave permission to the French to establish a factory in Chandernagore in 1673 AD?
questions.explanation: Mughal Subahdar of Bengal, Shaista Khan, gave a site to the French in 1673-74 AD where they established the famous French factory in Chandernagore in 1690-92 AD. It is noteworthy that in the year 1668, the first French factory (kothi) was established in Surat under the chairmanship of François Caron. Subsequently, in the year 1669, the second factory was established in Masulipatnam, located on the east coast of India

questions.question_text: Who was the first Governor of Portuguese settlements in India?
questions.explanation: The first Governor of Portuguese settlements in India was Francisco de Almeida (till 1505-09 AD). He adopted the 'Policy of Blue Water' to secure the trade of the Portuguese in the South-East Asia. It is noteworthy that in 1498 AD, Vasco da Gama was the first Portuguese traveller to come to India, Afonso de Albuquerque (1509-15) became the Governor of Portuguese settlements after Francisco de Almeida and Nuno da Cunha remained the Governor of Portuguese settlements in India from the year 1529-38

questions.question_text: It was a unique event in the history of British India that Mysore was returned to its old ruling family. Who accomplished this?
questions.explanation: William Bentinck annexed Mysore into British rule in 1831 on the basis of misgovernance, which Lord Ripon returned to its old ruling dynasty after fifty years, which was an unprecedented event in the history of British India. Florence Nightingale termed Lord Ripon as the savior of India

questions.question_text: Under which system or settlement did Indian states lose their rights to foreign and defense affairs?
questions.explanation: The Subsidiary Alliance in India was first started by Dupleix by making Indian kings rent his soldiers for money. Later, Clive and Cornwallis also adopted this policy. Wellesley gave it a certain and comprehensive form. The Subsidiary Alliance promised to give military support to the company and native states and in return, it took fixed financial support from them. States accepting this alliance lost their rights to foreign and defense affairs

questions.question_text: This debate still hasn't ended whether the Indian economy under British rule was a recorded development or stagnation, or if poverty was increasing continuously. What is the main reason for the inconclusive nature of this debate?

options.A: Qualitative evidence is interpreted in various ways.
options.D: Colonial nature of the Indian economy.

questions.explanation: Relevant qualitative data to determine the recorded development or stagnation of the Indian economy under British rule is insufficient, which makes it difficult to decide whether the Indian economy saw recorded development or stagnation or if poverty was increasing continuously

questions.question_text: When did François Caron establish the first French factory in India?
questions.explanation: In 1667, a batch of sailors left from France under the leadership of François Caron. In 1668 AD, François Caron established the first French factory in Surat. In 1669 AD, Marcara established the second factory in Masulipatnam after taking permission from the Sultan of Golconda

questions.question_text: In which year was the 'Dramatic Performances Act' that imposed strict state control over programs exhibited on public platforms passed?
questions.explanation: The 'Dramatic Performances Act' that imposed strict state control over programs exhibited on public platforms was implemented by the British government in 1876 AD. The Dramatic Performances Act, which we often know by the name 'D.P.A.', was brought in 1876 under the administration of Viceroy Northbrook. The act had a provision to empower the British administration to better control theatre in India

questions.question_text: Which treaty was signed after the First Anglo-Burma War (1824-26)?
questions.explanation: The First Anglo-Burma War happened in 1824-26. The main reason for the war was the expansion of the borders of the Burma state near the British Empire, due to which a danger of trouble arose before the British. After this war, the Treaty of Yandabo was signed

questions.question_text: As a result of the Seven Years' War (1756-1763) in Europe, open hostility also arose between the French and British settlements in India. In the south, the gains of Dupleix and Bussy were destroyed in 1760-61. Which treaty provided for the restoration of French assets in India?
questions.explanation: The Third Carnatic War between the British and the French lasted from 1756 AD to 1763 AD. During this time, the 'Seven Years' War' started in Europe. The Third Carnatic War is considered an important part of the Seven Years' War. Through the Treaty of Paris, which was completed in 1763 AD, the British returned other territories that were in French possession till 1749 AD, except Chandernagore, and these regions remained with them until India became independent

questions.question_text: Regarding official records, what were 'Consultations'?

options.A: All kinds of business of the British East India Company in Bengal.
options.B: Military records of all kinds of the British East India Company.
options.C: Reports of the advisors to the Governors of the Presidencies.
options.D: Records related to education and judiciary.

questions.explanation: British East India Company's rule in India started in 1773 AD. In the context of official records, all kinds of business of the East India Company in Bengal are called Consultations

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one of which is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R): Assertion (A): From nearly 1715, Bengali traders gave preference to the use of British shipping and the use of British ships for their cargo transport as an alternative to British navigation services. Reason (R): In reality, by entrusting their cargo to private ships, they were handing over the cargo to that company which had special rights with the British. Regarding both these statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar was the Mughal emperor from 1713 AD to 1719 AD. The British sent a representative to the Mughal emperor. In 1715 AD, Bengal traders gave preference to the use of British ships and navigation services for transport. These traders used the special rights received by the British to further their trade. Later on, on the request of British doctor Hamilton, in 1715, Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar made the annual duty of British goods in Bengal completely exempt for a mere token value of 3000 rupees. This achievement is called the company's Magna Carta

questions.question_text: Consider the following events and arrange them chronologically and select the correct answer using the code given below- 1. Treaty of Srirangapatnam 2. Treaty of Surat 3. Treaty of Salbai 4. Treaty of Bassein Code-
questions.explanation: Treaty of Surat - 1775 AD Treaty of Salbai - 1782 AD Treaty of Srirangapatnam - 1792 AD Treaty of Bassein - 1802 AD

questions.question_text: Who among the following considered the activities of Baptist missionaries in India as 'destructive'?
questions.explanation: Wellesley was the Governor General of India from 1798-1805 AD. He considered the activities of Baptist missionaries in India as destructive. He had merged many Indian states into the British Empire through the Subsidiary Alliance system

questions.question_text: Which Mysore war ended with the 'Treaty of Mangalore'?
questions.explanation: The Second Anglo-Mysore War lasted till 1780-84 AD. It ended with the Treaty of Mangalore in 1784. This treaty was an excellent diplomatic success of Tipu. However, Governor General Warren Hastings was unhappy with this treaty. Warren Hastings said "What kind of man is Macartney, who despite the treaty will lose the Carnatic." Through the Treaty of Mangalore, conquered territories of one another were also returned

questions.question_text: Before Dalhousie, the 'Doctrine of Lapse' had already been applied to which state?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse was first used by the Court of Directors of the East India Company in 1831. Although its most extensive use was done by Lord Dalhousie. First, the Mandvi state was taken into possession by the company through this doctrine in 1839 AD. Subsequently, Colaba and Jalore in 1840 AD and Surat in 1842 AD were taken into possession by the company

questions.question_text: Who became the first Governor of East Bengal after the partition of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The partition of Bengal happened during the time of Lord Curzon in 1905 AD. In 1905, one became East Bengal and the other became West Bengal. Bampfylde Fuller was the first Governor of East Bengal. The Governor of West Bengal was under the control of the state government

questions.question_text: Who ended the 'Vernacular Press Act'?
questions.explanation: Among the acts made to restrict newspapers, the Vernacular Press Act 1878 made by Lord Lytton was the most dangerous. The Vernacular Press Act was the biggest blow to the freedom of newspapers in Indian languages. Lord Ripon ended it in 1882 AD. Now any newspaper could be printed in any language. For this, taking permission from the government was not necessary

questions.question_text: Among the following Indian rulers, who was the first to join the Subsidiary Alliance?
questions.explanation: In India, Dupleix had first used the Subsidiary Alliance to make Indian Nawabs provide his soldiers on rent for money. Later, Clive and Cornwallis also adopted this policy. Lord Wellesley carried out the work of merging Indian territories into the British Empire through the Subsidiary Alliance. The first state to accept the Subsidiary Alliance was the Nizam of Hyderabad. The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798 AD. Other states to accept the Subsidiary Alliance were - Mysore-1799, Tanjore-1799, Peshwa-1801, Bhonsle-1803, Sindhia-1804. The Secondary Education Commission has considered its answer (a) Nawab of Awadh

questions.question_text: Behind the British East India Company returning Madras by ignoring Dupleix, which of the following was not a factor?

options.A: Not surrendering before Dupleix's power and showing his independence.
options.B: Probably he received some gift for himself from the British East India Company.
options.C: La Bourdonnais had already promised the British to return Madras in exchange for a ransom.
options.D: The home government of France ordered La Bourdonnais to return leaving the port and return to Mauritius.

questions.explanation: In the First Carnatic War, French Governor Dupleix called the French Governor of Mauritius, La Bourdonnais, for his help. La Bourdonnais captured Madras under the control of the British East India Company. Ignoring Dupleix's order, he received a good amount in exchange for the ransom of the city and returned it to the British. Although Dupleix was not happy with this, he re-captured Madras

questions.question_text: Arrange the following treaties made by the British with native princely states in chronological order and select the correct answer code:

questions.question_text: Arrange the following treaties made by the British with native princely states in correct chronological order and select the correct answer with the help of the code: (i) Treaty of Assaye (ii) Treaty of Lahore (iii) Treaty of Rajghat (iv) Subsidiary Alliance with Nizam of Hyderabad Code:
questions.explanation: – The correct chronological order of treaties made by the British with native princely states is– (i) Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam of Hyderabad-1798 AD (ii) Treaty of Assaye 1803 AD (iii) Treaty of Rajghat – 1804 AD (iv) Treaty of Lahore – 1846 AD

questions.question_text: When was the British East India Company established?

options.A: In the early period of the fifteenth century
options.B: In the early period of the sixteenth century
options.C: In the late period of the sixteenth century
options.D: In the early period of the seventeenth century

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2011) Explanation– The British East India Company was established in the late period of the sixteenth century. It was established under the name 'Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'.

questions.question_text: Who made the black hole ('Black Hole') event sensational?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The 'Black Hole' event happened on 20 June, 1756, in Fort William of Calcutta. This event was made sensational by Holwell. Whereas, the Treaty of Allahabad after the Battle of Buxar happened during the time of Robert Clive in the year 1765.

questions.question_text: Who was the first President of Fort William, Calcutta?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – Fort William was established in Calcutta in honor of the King of England. Sir Charles Eyre was its first President. In the year 1700 AD, it was declared the first Presidency city, which remained the capital of British India from 1774 AD to 1911 AD.

questions.question_text: Two statements are being given below, one of which is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R): Assertion (A): After accepting Diwani rights in Bengal, the company directly planned 'Drain of Wealth' itself. questions.question_text: In the year 1661, who among the following was the Governor of Madras?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– In the year 1661 AD, the company appointed British official Foxcroft as the Governor of Madras.

questions.question_text: Who was the Governor of Bengal between the years 1767 and 1769?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Between the years 1767 and 1769 AD, the Governor of Bengal was 'Verelst'. During this time, the Dual Government was implemented in Bengal. The tenure of others is as follows – Robert Clive - 1757-1760, Cartier - 1769-1772, Count de Lally was a French Governor.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– List-I List-II (A) Treaty of Allahabad (i) 1765 (B) Treaty of Madras (ii) 1769 (C) Treaty of Purandar (iii) 1776 (D) Treaty of Mangalore (iv)

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given code: List-I List-II (Place) (Year of annexation into British Empire)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Correct answer is– (Place) (Year of annexation into British Empire) (A) Jhansi (i) 1853 (B) Sambalpur (ii) 1849 (C) Awadh (iii) 1856 (D) Nagpur (iv)

questions.question_text: Arrange the states in chronological order which were annexed by Lord Dalhousie under the Doctrine of Lapse – (i) Jhansi (ii) Udaipur (iii) Satara (iv) Sambalpur Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Lord Dalhousie was an imperialist Governor-General who initiated the 'Doctrine of Lapse' for the expansion of the British Empire. Under this, the states merged into the British Empire are as follows– Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852) and Jhansi (1853).

questions.question_text: Paramount power is the situation which the British government uses as a supreme power –

options.D: In relation to the states of Kings and Princes

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Paramount power is the situation which the British government uses as a supreme power in relation to the states of Kings and Princes and British provinces. Upon the partition of British India in 1947, all these states, except Sikkim, decided to merge into either India or Pakistan.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements~ Assertion (A) : Early British administrators in India viewed the 18th century as a period of instability and insecurity. Reason (R) : During this period, the rise of British power in India happened due to the decline of Mughal power and as a result, political, military and economic disorder had spread. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– After the death of Aurangzeb, his successors were not capable, as a result, the central power declined after Aurangzeb. Later, the vast territory split into small autonomous states which kept fighting among themselves for various reasons. The British observed this period of instability and insecurity of the 18th century and started the attempt to occupy India. With the decline of Mughal power, the British defeated the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, in the Battle of Plassey of 1757 AD and started their rule. At that time, political, military and economic disorder had spread in India. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct clarification of Assertion (A).

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Indian regions captured by the English East India Company chronologically :
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Sindh was won by the English East India Company in 1843 AD. After this, Satara, Nagpur, and Punjab states were won. Dalhousie annexed Satara in 1848 AD. Punjab was annexed in 1849 AD and Nagpur was annexed in 1854 AD.

questions.question_text: In the changes made by Tipu in the desire for freedom, which one of the following was not included?

options.A: He included his name in Khutba
options.B: Requested a Sanad from the Khalifa for the legitimacy of his rule
options.C: He issued his own independent currency
options.D: He threatened to expel all European companies from South India

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Tipu Sultan assumed the title of Badshah in 1787. He kept French soldiers in his service. Tipu made efforts to get help from foreign powers in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799). After the French Revolution, when the French soldiers formed the Jacobin Club, he took its membership and called himself Citizen Tipu. He planted the Tree of Liberty in Srirangapatnam. He adopted a new system of minting coins and issued coins in his name. In this way, option 4 is not correct; all remaining options are correct.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the military campaigns of Count de Lally in Karnataka : (i) The local government instructed Lally to gradually establish control over internal territories. (ii) To provide the greatest benefit to the French in India, to get involved in the mutual disputes of Indian states. (iii) To pay attention to the efforts of capturing the fortified places of the British on the Indian coasts. (iv) Presented reforms considered necessary for the administration of the company. Select the correct answer with the help of the code given below
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– Count de Lally in Karnataka emphasized capturing the fortified places of the British on the Indian coasts and implementing the reforms considered necessary for the company's administration in his military campaigns.

questions.question_text: Between whom was the Treaty of Bassein signed in 1802?

options.A: Gaekwad of Baroda and Marquess of Wellesley
options.C: Peshwa Baji Rao II (Second) and Marquess of Wellesley
options.D: Raja Pratap Singh of Satara and Mountstuart Elphinstone

questions.explanation: UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015 UGC Net II Paper June-2012 TGT History, 2013 Explanation– In December 1802 AD, the Treaty of Bassein was signed by Peshwa Baji Rao II and Lord Wellesley. Under this subsidiary alliance, Peshwa Baji Rao II accepted the protection/hegemony of the British. According to the terms of the treaty, the British promised to reinstate Peshwa Baji Rao II in Pune and keep about 60 thousand soldiers in the state for the protection of the Peshwa, while in return, the Peshwa agreed to provide the British with regions having an annual income of 26 lakh Rs.

questions.question_text: Name the English officer who took Madras on a lease from the ruler of Chandragiri in the year 1639?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation– In 1599 AD, a British traveler named John Mildenhall came to India by land route. In 1599 AD, some traders established the English East India Company. In 1639, an Englishman named Francis Day obtained Madras on lease from the King of Chandragiri. Here, the British established a fort named 'Fort St. George', and in 1641, St. George became the headquarters of the company on the Coromandel coast.

questions.question_text: Two statements are being given below, out of which the first is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : The British won the Battle of Plassey without any real fight. Reason (R) : The Battle of Plassey gave the British the opportunity to get a foothold in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. Read the above statements and select the correct answer on the basis of the given code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The British won the Battle of Plassey of 23 June 1757 without any real fight. After this, it provided the British the opportunity to get a foothold in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. As a result of the Battle of Plassey, historian Jadunath Sarkar said that "On 23 June, 1757, the medieval age ended in India and the modern age began."

questions.question_text: Which of the following centers was not a Dutch commercial center in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation– In 1602 AD, a joint Dutch East India Company was established by a proposal passed by the Dutch (Netherlands) Parliament. In 1605 AD, the Dutch established their first factory in Masulipatnam. Apart from this, they expanded it according to time and in 1616 at Surat, in 1645 at Karikal, in 1650 AD at Balasore, and in Nagapattinam established factories. At this time, the Portuguese were engaged in Hugli, due to which the Dutch established their factory in Chinsurah near Hugli in 1653 AD.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one of which is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : By the end of the seventeenth century, the East India Company had removed its Portuguese and Dutch commercial rivals from the path. Reason (R) : English traders sold high-quality goods at cheap prices. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct? Select the correct answer from the code written below Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– In the race in the field of trade and commerce in India, the East India Company had almost removed its Portuguese and Dutch commercial rivals from the path by the end of the seventeenth century. English traders established commercial monopoly in India and prepared a market in Europe for Indian goods and used to buy high-quality goods at low prices and sell them at higher prices.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with the policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation– The second chapter in Anglo-Afghan relations starts from the time of Lord Ellenborough and goes up to the Viceroyalty of Lord Northbrook. This period is called the policy of masterly inactivity or clever passivity. This was the direct result of the destruction that happened in the Afghan war. This policy is generally associated with the name of John Lawrence, because he got a clear opportunity to follow this policy during his Viceroyalty.

questions.question_text: By what popular name was the East India Company called?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The East India Company was called the Company of Merchants of London. There were 28 directors of this company in London who were elected annually by its shareholders. The daily work of the company was done by Directors, who were called the Court of Directors.

questions.question_text: Who were the first Europeans to come to India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– The Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India. Vasco da Gama, a resident of Portugal, was the first European who arrived at the sea coast of Calicut, India, on 17 May, 1498 AD via the Cape of Good Hope. He came to India as a representative of the ruler of Portugal. The King of Calicut, Zamorin, welcomed him.

questions.question_text: Who had the prior right over Bombay possessed by the English?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– In 1661 AD, the marriage of King Charles II of England took place with the Portuguese princess Catherine. On this occasion, the Portuguese gave Bombay to Charles II as dowry. In 1668, Charles II gave Bombay to the East India Company on an annual rent of 10 pounds. In 1687 AD, instead of Surat, Bombay became the main commercial settlement of the British.

questions.question_text: When did the 'Black Hole' tragedy occur?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– Without the order of the Nawab of Bengal, the British did the fortification of Fort William in Calcutta. The Nawab surrounded Fort William on 15 June 1756 and a total of 146 British were made prisoners. On 20 June 1756, they were locked in a room. The next day, only 23 people remained alive. This is called the Black Hole tragedy. The eyewitness of this incident was 'Holwell'.

questions.question_text: In what order did the Europeans come to India for trade?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009, 2001 R.P.S.C. 2018 U.G.C. Net II Paper Dec-2014, 2015 Explanation– Vasco-da-Gama reached Calicut on 17 May, 1498, the king there, Zamorin, welcomed him, in this way the arrival of Europeans began. In 1602 AD, the Dutch Company arrived in India. In 1608, the British attempted to establish their first factory in India and in 1664, the French Company arrived in India.

questions.question_text: During whose time was the first railway line laid in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 DSSSB PGT, 2019 Explanation– To increase Indian security and internal communication system, the first railway line in India was laid from Bombay to Thane in 1853 AD during the reign of Dalhousie and soon, the entire Indian Empire was tied together in the thread of railway lines and made one.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements – Assertion (A) : Siraj-ud-Daulah was defeated by a very small army unit of the English East India Company. Reason (R) : He could not get the help of the Hindus. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The Battle of Plassey between Siraj-ud-Daulah and East India Company took place on 23 June 1757. In the battle, Siraj-ud-Daulah was defeated by a small army unit of the East India Company because Siraj-ud-Daulah's chief commander Mir Jafar had betrayed him.

questions.question_text: Where did Vasco-da-Gama reach in India in 1498?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– On 17 May, 1498 AD, Vasco-da-Gama reached the port of Calicut with the help of a Gujarati guide Abdul Majid. The Hindu ruler of Calicut, Zamorin, welcomed him and provided spices, herbs, etc., for taking them to Portugal. Vasco da Gama took those goods to Portugal and after deducting his travel expenses, sold them at 60 times the profit.

questions.question_text: In the Battle of Plassey, the British defeated -
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– Due to the betrayal of Mir Jafar and Rai Durlabh, the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, was defeated in the Battle of Plassey on 23 June 1757. In this battle, the British army of Lord Clive was victorious. The Nawab's trusted Mir Madan and Mohanlal were killed.

questions.question_text: Which ruler of India became a member of the Jacobin Club?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Influenced by the French Revolution, Tipu Sultan established the Jacobin Club in Srirangapatnam in 1794 AD and became its member and started calling himself 'Citizen Tipu'. In the capital Srirangapatnam itself, he planted the "Tree of Liberty", the symbol of friendship between France and Mysore.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct option from the codes given below– List-I List-II
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Primarily, foreigners could enter India via two routes. First, by crossing the North-West frontier via a famous and traditional land route and second, via the sea route. With the arrival of Vasco da Gama at the port of Calicut on 17 May, 1498 AD, the arrival of European traders happened. Portuguese trade started in India in 1503, British East India Company in 1600 AD, Dutch East India Company in 1602, and French East India Company in 1664 AD.

questions.question_text: In Bengal, 'Dual Government' ended during whose Governor's reign?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Ashram Paddhati Lecturer Exam-2009 R.P.S.C. 2018 Explanation – Clive tried to resolve the problem of Bengal through the infamous Dual Government system. In this, the actual power was with the Company, but the burden of administration was on the Nawab's shoulders. During Warren Hastings' time in 1772, the Court of Directors decided to end the Dual Government system.

questions.question_text: When the Battle of Plassey 1757 was at its peak, who left Siraj-ud-Daulah's side and joined the British under Lord Clive?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – On 23 June, 1757 AD, in the Battle of Plassey, Mir Jafar left Siraj-ud-Daulah's side and joined the British under Lord Clive. In this battle, Lord Clive succeeded in his diplomacy and defeated the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, and on 28 June, 1757 AD, Lord Clive declared Mir Jafar as the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.question_text: When did the Portuguese sailor Vasco-da-Gama reach the port of Calicut and discover the sea route for India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation– First Portuguese traveler Vasco da Gama reached the port of Calicut on 17 May, 1498, where the Hindu king Zamorin welcomed him. According to the question, 17 May, 1498, option (c) is correct.

questions.question_text: By whom was the additional allowance 'Double Batta' given to the English army?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – The Battle of Plassey took place on 23 June, 1757. In this battle, Clive was victorious due to Mir Jafar's betrayal. Mir Jafar became Nawab. He provided many facilities to the British. Under this, he doubled the allowance of the English army.

questions.question_text: Pondicherry was established by this person –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – The establishment of Pondicherry was done by Francois Martin and Bellanger de Lespinay in 1673. Its establishment was done by these two by obtaining a small village Puducherry from the Muslim governor Sher Khan Lodi and laying its foundation (Pondicherry). Moving forward, in 1674, Martin was appointed the head of this settlement.

questions.question_text: Who is considered the founder of Indian Civil Service?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) PGT History-2011 TGT History-2009 Explanation– Lord Cornwallis is considered the father of Civil Service in India. He brought the police and judicial service directly under the administration; previously, this work was looked after by the Zamindars. His indelible mark was on the administrative system. Later, it became famous by the name 'Cornwallis System'. Civil Service was called the steel frame. Wellesley established Fort William College in Calcutta in 1800 AD for the training of civil service.

questions.question_text: That European country which first started trade with India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – The first Portuguese and European traveler Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (India) in 1498 AD after a 90-day sea voyage with the help of a Gujarati guide named 'Abdul Majid'. The ruler of Calicut, Zamorin, welcomed him.

questions.question_text: Where was the first presidency of the British East India Company in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) DSSSB PGT-2019 Explanation– The British established a commercial factory in Masulipatnam in 1611 AD on the south-east sea coast. This was the port of the Golconda state. The British built a fort named Fort St. George in Madras in 1641 AD. This was the first fort and first presidency of the British in India. Francis Day is considered the founder of Madras.

questions.question_text: Which Governor General suppressed the Pindaris and Pathans?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Lord Hastings had suppressed the Pindaris and Pathans. It is noteworthy that the Pindari was basically a group of robbers in which both Hindus and Muslims were included. Their increased terror could be ended by 1824.

questions.question_text: Clive used the fake signature of a person. That was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Seth Amir Chand of Calcutta made secret talks between the British and the opponents of the Nawab to depose Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah and make Mir Jafar the Nawab of Bengal, and in return, demanded a long commission in the loot of the Nawab's treasury in Murshidabad and said that if this is not done, he would inform the Nawab about the conspiracy. Consequently, Clive had two drafts of the treaty prepared with Mir Jafar - one was a fake draft in which the talk of giving commission was mentioned. On this, Clive also forged Admiral Watson's signature. While there was no talk of commission in the original agreement draft. Amir Chand came to know about this fraud after the Battle of Plassey and it is said that ultimately Amir Chand died, being disappointed and mad.

questions.question_text: A Nawab of Awadh was also defeated in the Battle of Buxar. He was :
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– The Battle of Buxar took place in 1764 between the British and Mir Qasim. In this battle, Mir Qasim was supported by the Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daulah and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. On 22 October, 1764, under the leadership of Hector Munro, the British army defeated the combined army of these three.

questions.question_text: Who did the East India Company make the first Governor General?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 TGT History, 2009 Explanation– According to the provisions of the Regulating Act, 1773 AD, the Governor of Bengal started being called the Governor General of British territories. Therefore, Warren Hastings was made the first Governor General of Bengal by the East India Company.

questions.question_text: Peace remained between the British and the Marathas for twenty years through a treaty. That was :
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Peace remained between the British and the Marathas for about 20 years through the Treaty of Salbai (17 May, 1782 AD). This treaty was the result of the First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-82 AD). The First Anglo-Maratha War took place during the time of Madhavrao Narayan-Second.

questions.question_text: Who is called the founder of modern Indian judicial system?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– The founder of modern Indian judicial system was Cornwallis. In the judicial field, he codified the laws and established the Revenue Board. Cornwallis was also the creator of Indian Civil Service.

questions.question_text: On which date did the British re-occupy Calcutta?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– When the news of the occupation of Calcutta reached Madras, the British sent a powerful navy and infantry from Madras under the leadership of Admiral Watson and Colonel Clive respectively to Calcutta. Clive re-occupied Calcutta on 2 January 1757. Siraj-ud-Daulah was forced to sign the Treaty of Alinagar with Clive on 9 February, 1757 AD.

questions.question_text: When did the East India Company get the 'Golden Farman'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– In 1632 AD, the Sultan of Golconda gave the British a 'Golden' Farman, whose purpose was to grant them permission to trade freely in the Golconda state on paying a tax of five hundred pagodas annually.

questions.question_text: "Now the empire of the East is in our feet" - to which Anglo-Mysore war is this statement of Lord Wellesley related–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Happy with the success of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, Lord Wellesley said in boastful words that "Now the empire of the East is in our feet." It is noteworthy that in the Fourth War, Tipu Sultan was killed while defending his capital Srirangapatnam, and most of his empire was usurped by the British, and the remaining part was handed over to the old dynasty.

questions.question_text: The Farman for free trade in Bengal was obtained by the British –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The East India Company sent a delegation to the Mughal court in 1715 under the chairmanship of Sir John Surman, in which a doctor named William Hamilton was also included, who relieved Farrukhsiyar from a chronic disease, pleased with which Emperor Farrukhsiyar issued a Royal Farman in 1717 AD, according to which the company was granted permission to do free trade in Bengal in exchange for 3000 Rs. annual tax.

questions.question_text: Which commercial company was established in March, 1602 AD?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In 1596 AD, Cornelius Houtman was the first Dutch traveler to reach Sumatra and Bantam via Cape of Good Hope. He encouraged other Dutch people and after this, in a few years, other Dutch companies were formed for Indian trade. On 20 March, 1602 AD, the first Dutch company for trade in India, 'United East India', emerged, which was formed by combining many companies.

questions.question_text: The trade between Portugal and India started –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The trade between Portugal and India started in 1498 AD. Portuguese traveler Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (India) in 1498 AD with the help of a Gujarati guide Abdul Majid and from then on trade started between India and Portugal.

questions.question_text: When did the Dual Government in Bengal end?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Dual Government started in Bengal in 1765 and Warren Hastings ended it in 1772. In Dual Government, the Diwani right was with the Company and the responsibility of administration was on the Nawab's shoulders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following options according to the incident is true in ascending order?

options.A: Battle of Buxar, Battle of Plassey, Battle of Wandiwash
options.B: Battle of Wandiwash, Battle of Buxar, Battle of Plassey
options.C: Battle of Plassey, Battle of Wandiwash, Battle of Buxar
options.D: Battle of Buxar, Battle of Wandiwash, Battle of Plassey

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Battle of Plassey 23 June 1757, Battle of Wandiwash - 1760 (between British and French) and Battle of Buxar - 22 October, 1764 happened.

questions.question_text: In 1757, Siraj-ud-Daulah was defeated by –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – On 23 June, 1757, the British army led by Lord Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah (the battle was symbolic only because people had betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah).

questions.question_text: Where did the Black Hole incident happen?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, captured the British factory in Kasimbazar and then after coming to Calcutta, captured Fort William on 20 June, 1756. The British took shelter at a place called Fulta near the sea, which their superior naval system had made safe. Even then, the Nawab made many British prisoners. He locked 146 British in one room, out of which only 23 people could remain alive. This massacre is known as the 'Black Hole' incident. The author of this incident was Holwell.

questions.question_text: By the treaty of September 1760, Mir Qasim handed over which three districts to the East India Company?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– The British removed the Nawab of Bengal, Mir Jafar, and made Mir Qasim the Nawab there under an agreement. Under this agreement, by a treaty in September 1760, Mir Qasim handed over the Diwani of three districts named Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong to the British.

questions.question_text: Who got Bombay as dowry?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005, 2010 Explanation– Bombay was received as dowry by British Emperor Charles-II. In 1661 AD, the marriage of Portuguese princess Catherine took place with Charles-II. In this marriage, the Portuguese gave Bombay as dowry. Charles gave Bombay to the East India Company in 1668 AD by taking 10 pounds annual rent.

questions.question_text: Carnatic wars happened –

options.A: Between the British and the Dutch
options.B: Between the British and the Portuguese
options.C: Between the British and the French
options.D: Between the British and the Marathas

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– Carnatic wars happened between the British and the French. Starting from trade, the French and British companies got entangled in the politics of India. The aim of both these companies was to do maximum trade. For this, monopoly was needed. Consequently, a war happened between the two. This war happened three times. First, 1746-48, second 1749-54, and third 1756-63 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a correct reason for the decline of Portuguese power in India?

options.A: Spain's control over Portugal in 1580 AD
options.B: Establishment of Mughal power in India
options.C: Rise of British and Dutch naval power

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation– The reasons for the decline of Portuguese power include Spain's control over Portugal, the rise of British and Dutch naval power, Aurangzeb's anti-trade policy, etc. Whereas, it had no relation to the establishment of Mughal power.

questions.question_text: At the time of the annexation of Awadh into the British Empire, the Nawab there was-
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – The last Nawab of Awadh was Wajid Ali Shah. On 13 February, 1856, Dalhousie annexed the state of Awadh into the British Empire on the report of Outram by accusing it of maladministration and ended the independent Awadh state. Dalhousie said, "If the British government continues to help in running such maladministration in which crores of people are suffering, it will be guilty in the eyes of both humanity and God."

questions.question_text: The immediate cause of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was-

options.A: The removal of the British Resident from the court by Tipu
options.C: The keen desire of the British to grab Mysore
options.D: Tipu's refusal to accept the subjugation of the British

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The immediate cause of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was Tipu's refusal to accept the subjugation of the British. Tipu Sultan was defeated in this war and was killed on 4 May, 1799, while fighting against the British.

questions.question_text: Which facility did the English Company not get through the Farman of 1717 AD?

options.A: Facility of trade in exchange for a three thousand Rs. annual tax
options.B: No need to pay any additional duty
options.C: Permission to take additional land around Calcutta
options.D: Assurance was given to give this right elsewhere after three years

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Through the Farman of 1717 AD of the Mughal Emperor, the East India Company was exempted from customs duty on all its trade in Bengal by paying 3000 Rs. annual tax. Through this Farman, the company got the right to buy 38 villages around Calcutta and the company got permission to run the coins minted in Bombay in the entire Mughal Empire. Through the Farman in Surat, by paying 10,000 Rs. annual tax, the entire trade of the company was exempted from import-export tax.

questions.question_text: Ranjit Singh did the Treaty of Amritsar –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – The Treaty of Amritsar took place on 25 April, 1809 AD between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and Lord Minto's envoy Sir Charles Metcalfe. As a result of the immediate effect of the treaty, Ranjit Singh's dream of establishing hegemony over the Sikh states across the Sutlej broke, but on the other hand, as Kaye has said, Ranjit Singh got a free hand to expand in the western direction.

questions.question_text: Which Frenchman laid the foundation of Pondicherry in 1673?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – In 1673 AD, Francois Martin, the director of the French East India Company, obtained a village named Puducherry from the subedar of Valikondapuram, Sher Khan Lodi, which was known as Pondicherry later.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first Governor General of India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – By the Charter Act 1833, the Governor of Bengal was now made the Governor General of India. Under this Act, William Bentinck had the good fortune of being the first Governor General of India.

questions.question_text: The 'Black Hole' tragedy is related to whom being made prisoner?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- On 15 June 1756, Siraj-ud-Daulah's soldiers surrounded Fort William of Bengal and the British surrendered. On the order of Siraj-ud-Daulah, all 146 prisoners were locked in a room 18 feet long and 14 feet 10 inches wide on 20 June 1756. In the morning, only 23 people survived. This incident is termed the 'Black Hole' tragedy.

questions.question_text: Who had established the Dual Government in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- When Clive came to India again as the Governor of the British Company. At that time, Mir Qasim had been removed from the throne. Mir Jafar had already died. A small child Najm-ud-Daulah was the Nawab of Bengal. Clive took the Diwani for the Company in 1765 and let the Nizam (administration) remain with the Nawab, that is, it was called the Dual Government system which ran from 1765 to 1772 AD.

questions.question_text: The judicial reforms taken by Cornwallis for improvement in Indian methods were criticized by :
questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- The judicial reforms taken by Cornwallis for improvement in Indian methods were criticized by James Mill. Cornwallis's work in the judicial system was even more important. He not only separated the executive and judicial officers but also made efforts to take justice to the common people.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Indian rulers first joined the subsidiary alliance?
questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- The Subsidiary Alliance was an important tool of Wellesley's policy of imperial expansion. Through it, Wellesley expanded the empire of the British Company. The creator of the subsidiary alliance was Dupleix. In 1798 AD, Wellesley first did a subsidiary alliance with Nizam Ali, the Nawab of Hyderabad. Under this treaty, Nizam Ali became completely dependent on the Company.

questions.question_text: The Treaty of Seringapatam (Srirangapatnam) took place between the British and which other power?
questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– In 1787, Tipu Sultan planted the Tree of Liberty in his capital Srirangapatnam as a symbol of friendship between France and Mysore and, influenced by the French Revolution, became a member of the Jacobin Club. In 1796 AD, he tried to set up a modern navy. Tipu Sultan made the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 AD with Cornwallis, as a result of which the Third Anglo-Mysore War ended.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?

options.D: Sir John Shore – Third Anglo-Maratha War

questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012, 2009 Explanation– Lord Wellesley – Fourth Anglo-Mysore War Lord Dalhousie – Annexation of Awadh Lord Ellenborough – Annexation of Sindh Lord Hastings – Third Anglo-Maratha War

questions.question_text: Who was sent via sea route to re-occupy Calcutta in 1756?
questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– To re-occupy Calcutta in 1756, Watson was sent via the sea route as an assistant to Lord Clive.

questions.question_text: The first commercial center of the East India Company was established–
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012, PGT History-2009, 2016 Explanation- The first commercial center of the East India Company was established temporarily in Surat. This commercial center of the company was established in 1608 AD, whereas in South India, it was established permanently in Masulipatnam in 1611 AD. Although this remains a subject of dispute, where the British established their first commercial center.

questions.question_text: Who was the Governor there at the time of Siraj-ud-Daulah's attack on Calcutta (16 June, 1756)?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Ashram Paddhati Lecturer Exam-2012 Explanation- On 16 June 1756, Siraj-ud-Daulah attacked Calcutta and liberated it from the British. Drake was the Governor of Calcutta at that time. He had to flee and take shelter in Fulta Island; Mr. Holwell surrendered before the Nawab with some of his companions.

questions.question_text: Who among the following has accepted Farrukhsiyar's Farman (1717) as the Magna Carta of the British East India Company?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- An important event in the history of the East India Company happened in 1717 AD. A British diplomatic delegation under the leadership of John Surman reached the court of Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar with the objective of obtaining some more commercial concessions. Edward Stephenson, William Hamilton (surgeon), and Khwaja Serhad (Armenian interpreter) were included in the British diplomatic delegation. Surgeon Hamilton cured the Emperor of a serious disease; as a result, pleased Farrukhsiyar issued three Farmans in the names of the governors of Bengal, Hyderabad, and Gujarat. The Company was exempted from customs duty on all its trade in Bengal by paying 3000 rupees annual tax. Through this Farman, the company got the right to buy 38 villages around Calcutta. By the Farman of Farrukhsiyar, permission was received to run the coins minted in Bombay in the entire Mughal Empire. By the Farman in Surat, the entire trade of the company was exempted from import-export tax by paying 10,000 rupees annual tax. The concessions given to the company by Farrukhsiyar through the Farman proved to be of far-reaching consequences in the later period. Mr. Orme gave this Farman the title of 'Magna Carta' (great charter) of the company.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the last Nawab of Awadh?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The last Nawab of Awadh was Wajid Ali Shah. Wajid Ali Shah remained the Nawab of Lucknow and Awadh. His reign was from 1847 to 1856. In the world of music, the name of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah is unforgettable. He is known as the creator of the 'Thumri' music style. His son Birjis Qadr was the last (minor) Nawab of Awadh, but the real power was in the hands of Wajid Ali Shah's wife Begum Hazrat Mahal. Hence, Wajid Ali Shah is considered the last Nawab of Awadh.

questions.question_text: The Treaty of Seringapatam was made between:
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– The Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92) ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam (March, 1792). In this treaty, Cornwallis on behalf of the British and Tipu Sultan from Mysore were involved. According to this treaty, Tipu had to give about half of his state to the British and their allies. Along with this, as war compensation, Tipu Sultan had to pay three crore rupees to the British. It was included in this treaty that until Tipu Sultan pays three crore rupees, his two sons will remain in the captivity of the British. Cornwallis made this comment after this treaty– "We have effectively crippled our enemy, and have not made our allies powerful."

questions.question_text: In which year did Robert Clive accept the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Odisha from the Mughal ruler?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 UGC Net II Paper June 2012 TGT History-2013 Explanation– According to the first treaty of Allahabad (August–1765), the British took the exiled emperor Shah Alam under their protection and he was kept in Allahabad. On 12 August, 1765, through his Farman, the Mughal Emperor Second gave the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the East India Company permanently, in exchange for which the Company had to pay 26 lakh rupees to the Emperor and 53 lakh rupees for Nizamat expenses. At that time, Robert Clive was the Governor of Bengal of the East India Company.

questions.question_text: Dalhousie's biggest blunder was -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– On 13 February, 1856 AD, Lord Dalhousie, making an excuse of maladministration, asked the Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah, to leave the throne and merged Awadh into the British state. This annexation was Dalhousie's biggest political blunder. The main reason for the annexation of Awadh was just the maladministration there. Attention was not paid to the fact that the British themselves were the main reason for this maladministration. Many contemporary writers said again and again that the British intervened in that country and made the governance there such that it is a very big blot on the name of the British. Maladministration was an easy reason for annexation. According to Professor K.K. Dutta, the existence of a state with such maladministration like Awadh in the middle of the rapidly expanding British empire in India was a very big and highly undesirable fact for the builders of the British empire, and the sooner it was ended, the better it was.

questions.question_text: Who helped Shah Alam to rule from Delhi, his ancestral capital, after leaving Allahabad in 1771 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– After being defeated in the Battle of Buxar, Mughal ruler Shah Alam Second was living in Allahabad as a pensioner of the British. Maratha chieftain Mahadji Scindia, after winning Delhi in February 1771, brought Mughal emperor Shah Alam Second from Allahabad and seated him on the Delhi throne. Buxar put a solid stamp on the decisions of Plassey. Now there was no one else left in India to challenge the British. Now the new Nawab was their puppet. The Nawab of Awadh was their pensioner. The region up to Allahabad came under the feet of the British and the path to Delhi was open. After this, Bengal and Awadh did not try to come out of the control of the British and their grip kept becoming stronger and stronger.

questions.question_text: Which Nawab of Awadh agreed to keep a British Resident in his court?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– After the death of Safdarjung, his son Shuja-ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Awadh. During his time, serious changes took place in the politics of Awadh. He gave shelter to Mughal prince Ali Gauhar in his state. He supported Ahmad Shah Abdali against the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat. He gave shelter to the Nawab of Bengal and Mir Qasim in his state and fought the Battle of Buxar against the British. He was defeated in that battle. The British did not capture his state at that time. They took 50 lakh rupees from him and he agreed to keep a British Resident in his court and keep the British army at his own expense for the protection of the border and gave the districts of Allahabad and Kara to Mughal emperor Shah Alam. On 26 January, 1775 AD, Shuja-ud-Daulah died.

questions.question_text: In the First Anglo-Sikh War, the Sikhs were defeated. Who helped the British?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46 AD) happened during the time of Lord Hardinge. In this, the root cause of the defeat of the Sikhs was the selfishness and treachery of their chieftains. Their big commanders were joined with the British, sent them information, and did not fight at the right time. On 31 December, 1845 AD, the Sikh army had crossed the Sutlej river and possibly its intention was to suddenly attack Ferozepur, but this intention could not be fulfilled due to the treachery of Lal Singh. Lal Singh had written to the British representative Nicholson in Ferozepur- "I have crossed the Sutlej with the Sikh army. You know my friendship with the British, tell me what I should do now." Nicholson replied "Do not attack Ferozepur as long as it is possible and then move towards the Governor General." Lal Singh did exactly that and Ferozepur was saved.

questions.question_text: Which Indian rulers participated against the British in the Battle of Buxar?

options.A: Shah Alam, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Mir Qasim
options.B: Mir Qasim, Muhammad Shah and Shuja-ud-Daulah

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- In the battle fought on 22 October, 1764 AD, the combined army of Mughal emperor Shah Alam, Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Mir Qasim faced the East India Company's army led by Hector Munro. Broome wrote "The famous Battle of Buxar was fought bravely, and in terms of results, it was equally important. 'The Battle of Plassey had given the British the ownership of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha, but the Battle of Buxar left the Nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor's Vizier Shuja-ud-Daulah and the Mughal emperor himself at the mercy of the British. The Mughal emperor was not powerful but he was definitely the Mughal emperor by name. With this battle, the prestige of the British spread in the whole of India. Now Awadh became a puppet in their hands and the Mughal emperor became their pensioner.

questions.question_text: In what form is Sir John Shore's policy known in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The origin of the policy of non-intervention is obtained from the Pitt's India Act. Under one of its sections, it was declared- "To implement plans for victory and imperial expansion in India is against the will and honor of this nation (England)." After the formation of this Act, Lord Cornwallis was the first Governor General. According to this section, he tried to follow the policy of non-intervention. After him, Sir John Shore was the first Governor-General who actually followed this policy of non-intervention completely. He refused to give help to the Nizam of Hyderabad, the old friend of the British, against the Marathas, removed the British protection from Rajput states, and tried so that the British did not have to get entangled in the mutual quarrels of any Indian ruler. He followed the policy of non-intervention towards Mysore. After him, Sir John Shore was the first Governor-General who actually fully followed this policy of non-intervention. He refused to provide assistance to the Nizam of Hyderabad, the old ally of the British, against the Marathas, removed British protection from the Rajput states and attempted to ensure that the British did not have to get involved in the mutual conflicts of any Indian ruler. He followed a policy of non-intervention towards Mysore.

questions.question_text: Who had executed the Treaty of Allahabad?

options.B: Robert Clive, Mir Qasim, Balwant Singh

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 PGT History-2013, 2000 Explanation- After the end of the Buxar war, British Robert Clive made the Treaty of Allahabad with the Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daulah and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam. Through this treaty, the British took Kara and Allahabad from Awadh and gave them to the Mughal emperor. The Mughal emperor gave the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the British. The British agreed to pay twenty-six lakh rupees annually to the Mughal emperor and the British received 'Northern Circars', north of Hyderabad, as a jagir from the Mughal government for the Nizamat expenses. Under the second treaty with Shuja-ud-Daulah- Awadh was returned to the Nawab. The Nawab gave 50 lakh rupees to the British. The Nawab gave Kara and Allahabad to Mughal emperor Shah Alam. The Nawab gave Chunar to the British and the jagir of Benares and Ghazipur was given to Raja Balwant Singh and his family under British protection as an ancestral jagir.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true regarding the Battle of Plassey?

options.A: This battle started on the morning of 23 June, 1757 AD and ended on the evening of the same day
options.B: Siraj-ud-Daulah called Mir Jafar to his camp during the battle
options.C: The Nawab's artillery chief Mir Madan was killed at the beginning of the battle
options.D: In the middle of the day on 23 June, the Nawab fled the battlefield

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June, 1757 between the Nawab of Bengal Siraj-ud-Daulah and the British under the leadership of Robert Clive. In this battle, the Nawab's artillery chief Mir Madan was not killed at the beginning of the battle but some hours later. All other options are correct.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was his advisor in Lord Cornwallis's judicial reforms?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Sir William Jones was his advisor in Lord Cornwallis's judicial reforms. Cornwallis presented the "Cornwallis Code" in 1793 AD for improvement in the judicial system. These reforms were based on the principle of separation of powers. Cornwallis's justice system was based on Western judicial concepts and impartiality. A neutral law replaced the personal law or religious law of the King or his officials. Supremacy of law was established. However, the immediate results of this Cornwallis Code were not very good.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sons of Tipu Sultan was not given to the British as a hostage in the Seringapatam agreement?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Considering defeat inevitable in the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Tipu signed the Treaty of Seringapatam with the British in March 1792 AD. According to this, he had to give about half of the country to the British and their allies. Under this, the British got Dindigul, Baramahal, and Malabar, and the Marathas got the part north of Tungabhadra river and the Nizam got the part between the Pennar and Krishna rivers. Tipu had to pay 3 crore rupees as compensation. In this phase of the war, Tipu suffered a lot and could only save his state from complete destruction with great difficulty. Until Tipu pays the money, his two sons had to remain in the custody of the British. Fateh Haider was not given to the British as a hostage. Cornwallis described this situation in the following words: "We have effectively crippled our enemy, and have not made our allies powerful."

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The Second Anglo-Mysore War took place in 1780-84 AD between Haider Ali and the British. At that time, the British Governor was Warren Hastings. He decided to bring all French settlements in India under his control. He also won the Mahe port located on the Malabar coast, which Haider Ali considered under his control. Warren Hastings argued that French help could reach Haider Ali via Mahe port. Apart from this, the British sent their army into Haider Ali's territory without his permission for the victory of Guntur situated in the Northern Circars. Haider Ali brought the Marathas and the Nizam together and took a promise of French help and then attacked the Carnatic in July 1780. In this way, the Company had to face defeat from both the Marathas and Mysore. As Alfred Lyall wrote, in the summer of 1780, the Company's reputation was at its lowest level, but Warren Hastings managed the situation. In December 1782, Haider Ali died but his son Tipu continued the war.

questions.question_text: Between which years did the First Anglo-Maratha War take place?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The First Anglo-Maratha War took place between 1775-1782 AD. The reason for this war was the internal conflict of the Marathas and Clive's desire to implement Dual Government in Maharashtra. The Anglo-Maratha war happened due to the 'Treaty of Surat' made between Raghunath Rao and the British in 1775. The second war between the British and Marathas was fought in 1803-1805 AD and the third war was fought between 1817-1818 AD.

questions.question_text: Who among the following were involved in the conspiracy hatched by Clive against the Nawab of Bengal Siraj-ud-Daulah?

options.C: Mir Jafar, Mir Qasim and Amir Chand

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- In the conspiracy against the Nawab of Bengal Siraj-ud-Daulah (1756-57), his commander Mir Jafar and the trader of Bengal Amir Chand were involved with Clive. Due to these traitors, Siraj-ud-Daulah had to face defeat in the Battle of Plassey (1757).

questions.question_text: Consider the following treaties related to the Anglo-Maratha War - 1. Treaty of Argaon 2. Treaty of Deogaon 3. Treaty of Bassein Obtain the correct chronological order of these treaties from the following code -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005, 2003 UP PCS Special Exam-2004 Explanation – The Treaty of Bassein (31 December, 1802) took place between the British and Peshwa Baji Rao II. The following are the provisions of this treaty- 1. Peshwa accepted British protection and agreed to keep the Indian and British army in Pune. 2. Peshwa gave regions between Gujarat, Tapti and Narmada rivers and all nearby regions of Tungabhadra river, whose income was 26 lakh rupees, to the Company. 3. Peshwa gave Surat city to the Company. 4. Peshwa relinquished the right to obtain Chauth from the Nizam and promised not to fight against the Gaekwad. 5. Peshwa accepted the Company's mediation in mutual disputes with the Nizam and Gaekwad. 6. Peshwa retired all anti-British Europeans. 7. Put his foreign affairs under the Company. Deogaon Treaty (17 December, 1803) - By this, Bhonsle gave Cuttack and the western part of Wardha river to the British. Scindia gave the region between Ganga and Yamuna to the Company by the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (30 December, 1803) and gave up his hegemony over Rajput states of Jaipur, Jodhpur, and Gohad. He also gave the fort of Ahmednagar, Broach, and parts of Godavari and Ajanta Ghat to the Company. Both kings also agreed to keep a Resident.

questions.question_text: Determine the correct chronological order of the following events from the code given below - 1. End of Dual Government in Bengal 2. Treaty of Allahabad 3. Battle of Plassey 4. Battle of Wandiwash Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005, 2003 Explanation– Battle of Plassey 1757- The Battle of Plassey was fought between the Nawab of Bengal Siraj-ud-Daulah and the British army on 23 June, 1757 at a place named Plassey (on the banks of the Bhagirathi river) located 22 miles south of Murshidabad, in which the British army was victorious. Battle of Wandiwash- 22 January, 1760 AD. The French army led by Count de Lally and the British army led by Eyre Coote fought, in which the French were defeated and a chapter of their decline in India began. Treaty of Allahabad- The first Treaty of Allahabad was held on 12 August, 1765 AD between Clive and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam, in which the emperor handed over the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the Company and the Company snatched Kara and Manikpur from the Nawab of Awadh and gave them to the Mughal Emperor. The second Treaty of Allahabad was held on 16 August, 1765 between the Nawab of Awadh and the Company (Clive); the Nawab promised to pay 50 lakh rupees to the Company as compensation. The end of Dual Government in Bengal was done by Warren Hastings in 1772 AD.

questions.question_text: Who were the two people who betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah in the Battle of Plassey?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : In the Battle of Plassey, both the Nawab's commanders Mir Jafar and Rai Durlabh, and the rich banker Jagat Seth were involved in the conspiracy. Amir Chand was acting as a mediator between the conspirators and the British. On the night of 22 June, 1757, Clive reached the mango orchard of Plassey located on the banks of the Bhagirathi, where the Nawab was already present with his soldiers. Fighting started on the morning of 23 June. Mir Jafar and Rai Durlabh kept standing silently with their huge armies on behalf of the Nawab. Only a small army under the command of Mohanlal and Mir Madan, which a French officer was supporting, took part in the fight. Hence, Answer (b) is correct.

questions.question_text: Who was the Governor General of India at the time of the annexation of Sindh?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : In 1842 AD, Lord Ellenborough came to India as Governor-General in place of Auckland. In September 1842 AD, he appointed Charles Napier as the Resident of the Company in Sindh in place of Major Outram. By August 1843 AD, the entire Sindh was merged into the British state. All Amirs were made prisoners and expelled from the country. Lord Ellenborough praised Napier a lot for having "merged such a big and fertile region into the British empire." Lord Mayo's tenure in India was from 1869 to 1872 and Lord Dalhousie's tenure was from 1848 to 1856.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the initial motto of the East India Company?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 UP PCS Pre History, 2007 TGT History-2010 UPPCS Pre. History 2010 NVS PGT-2019 Explanation - By the Charter Act of December, 1600 AD, Queen Elizabeth I of Britain established a commercial company 'The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies' and granted a monopoly to trade in the eastern regions for the first 15 years. With the intention of starting commercial activities in India, Captain William Hawkins was sent to the court of then Mughal Emperor Jahangir so that the British could get permission to open a factory in Surat and trade in India. Although Hawkins did not get success in his objectives. However, in 1615 AD, British envoy Thomas Roe got success and commercial houses were established in various places including Surat. But in this phase, the company's only objective was trade. Their objectives started changing after 1740 AD and the Battle of Plassey of 1757 AD made their objectives completely political.

questions.question_text: Which of the following historians has said that the government of Bengal was a 'dacoit-state' in the period 1765 AD to 1772 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – In 1765 AD, Clive came to India for the second time and became the Governor of Bengal. During his second India visit, he obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha in 1765, in exchange for which 53 lakh rupees were to be paid to the Nawab by the Company. After these provisions, the Company had control over all land revenue. Clive, under the Dual Government system, kept administration, revenue collection, and Diwani justice to himself and left internal peace system, Faujdari justice, and all other administrative responsibilities to the Nawab. That is, Clive took the right of administration but did not accept the responsibility. This is what was called the 'Dual Government system', which had many bad consequences. Where law and order stopped completely, agriculture and trade were also devastated. The 'Society for Trade' established by Clive was also a means of loot. K.M. Panikkar has targeted this and said that "In the period 1765 AD to 1772 AD, the government of Bengal was a 'dacoit-state'."

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding the Treaty of Allahabad executed in August 1765 is false?

options.A: There were eleven clauses in it
options.B: Through this treaty, the British East India Company obtained the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha provinces from Mughal Emperor Shah Alam
options.C: By this treaty, except Kara and Allahabad, the whole of Awadh was given to Shuja-ud-Daulah
options.D: As war compensation, Shuja-ud-Daulah agreed to pay 50 lakh rupees in a single installment immediately after the execution of the treaty

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - After the Buxar war, the Treaty of Allahabad was concluded between the Company and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam Second in 1765 AD. There were a total of eleven clauses in this treaty - 1. Took Kara and Allahabad from Awadh and gave them to the Mughal emperor. 2. Mughal emperor gave the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the British. 3. The British agreed to pay 26 lakh rupees annually to the Mughal emperor. 4. The British obtained Northern Circar, the district north of Hyderabad, as a jagir from the Mughal emperor. Apart from these 4 clauses, the remaining 7 clauses were made with the Nawab. However, the fourth reason of the question is not true because Shuja-ud-Daulah did not pay 50 lakh rupees in a single installment immediately after the execution of the treaty but agreed to pay in nine installments. Therefore, the fourth reason of the question is not true.

questions.question_text: The policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' was related to–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' is related to the Afghan policy adopted by the British government. This policy was followed from the time of John Lawrence up to the time of Lord Northbrook. In fact, the loss that the British suffered in the Afghan war and the independent feeling of the Afghans that they encountered, as a reaction to that, the policy of masterly inactivity started. Although the basis of the origin of this policy is found in Lord Canning's letters, its name is mainly associated with 'Lord Lawrence'.

questions.question_text: By Jahangir, which company was authorized to set up a factory in Surat?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– In 1613 AD, through a Farman, Jahangir granted permission to the English East India Company to open a factory in Surat. Encouraged by this, the British sent Sir Thomas Roe to Jahangir's court in 1615 AD, so that they could get permission to open factories in other places and trade. He came as an envoy of King James I of England.

questions.question_text: Which Governor General among the following knew Arabic, Persian, and Bengali languages besides English?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– Warren Hastings protected ancient traditions and literature. He knew Arabic and Persian and could speak Bengali. He wrote the preface to the first translation of Gita by Charles Wilkins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following European wars sparked the First Carnatic War in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008, 2010 Explanation– The First Carnatic War (1746-48 AD) was merely an extension of the Austrian War of Succession which started in 1740. The First Carnatic War is memorable for the Battle of St. Thome, which was fought between the French army and the Nawab of Carnatic Anwaruddin. With the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), the Austrian War of Succession ended, the First Carnatic War also ended, in which both the British and French teams remained equal.

questions.question_text: What was the purpose of the fortified factory at the beginning of British rule in India?

options.A: Commercial site where company officers worked
options.C: Warehouse for goods collected to be sent to Europe

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– In 1608, the East India Company decided to open a factory in Surat on the western coast of India, then commercial centers were known as factories only.
