There were three types of people involved in the factory- clerks, writers, merchants. The factory was actually for the warehouse of goods collected to be sent to Europe.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Fort William Presidency come into existence?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - In 1698 AD, the Subedar of Bengal, Azim-us-Shan, granted the zamindari of three villages named Sutanuti, Calcutta, and Govindpur to the British, in exchange for which the British had to pay 1200 Rs. to the owners of these villages. Here, the British established a fortified commercial establishment named Fort William in 1700 AD in honor of the Emperor of England William III. Charles Eyre was its first President.

questions.question_text: Which British officer defeated Mir Qasim in several battles of 1763?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The war between the East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal Mir Qasim started in 1763 AD itself. Several skirmishes happened and Mir Qasim was defeated. He escaped and reached Awadh and along with the Nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor, planned to expel the British from Bengal. The combined army of these three, which had 40 to 50 thousand soldiers, faced the Company's army. The Company's army had 7072 soldiers, and its command was in the hands of Major Hector Munro. The decisive battle happened on 22 October, 1764 at a place named Buxar. The British were victorious.

questions.question_text: Who was Ranjit Singh's Finance Minister?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Ranjit Singh's finance minister was Deena Nath. Fakir Aziz-ud-Din was his foreign minister. Ranjit Singh's special ideal army which was called 'Fauj-i-Khas', was formed in 1822 by General Ventura and Allard. Ilahi Bakhsh was the operator of his artillery.

questions.question_text: During which Viceroy's tenure did the 'White Mutiny' occur?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - White Mutiny occurred during the tenure of Lord Ripon (1880-84). The cause of the White Mutiny was the 'Ilbert Bill' which was presented during Ripon's time. In the Ilbert Bill, Indian judges were given the right to hear European cases.

questions.question_text: During whose time did the 'Black Hole' incident happen?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 TGT History-2004 PGT History-2003 Explanation– This heart-wrenching incident happened during the time of Siraj-ud-Daulah on 20 June, 1756 AD. According to the usual method of war, British prisoners including women and children were locked in a room. It is said that 146 prisoners were locked in a room 18 feet long and 14 feet 10 inches wide. On the night of 20 June, they were locked and the next morning only 23 people survived. The rest died due to the heat of June or being crushed against each other. J.Z. Holwell, who was one of those who survived, is considered the creator of this narrative, but the names of those who died in this incident were not given.

questions.question_text: Who among the following gave the title of 'Jagat Seth' to Fateh Chand?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– Due to local and foreign trade, commercial capitalists developed and banking system also developed. In North India, the rise of Jagat Seths and in South India, the rise of Chettis happened. In the later Mughal period, Fateh Chand was the main trader who used to lend money to the Mughal rulers as well, Muhammad Shah gave him the title of 'Jagat Seth'. They used to give loans to the people of royal families from their capital but they did not have the desire to progress. Amir Chand was a descendant of Fateh Chand himself.

questions.question_text: Among the following, who first admitted that the British victory in Plassey was a victory of treachery?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– The answer to the above question will be 'd'. In the context of the results of the Battle of Plassey, Mill wrote: "No war has had such immediate, permanent, and influential results. The victory of this war laid the foundation of the British empire in Bengal." According to Indian historian K.M. Panikkar, "Plassey was a deal in which the rich people of Bengal and Mir Jafar sold the Nawab to the British."

questions.question_text: When was the Treaty of Alinagar signed?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– The Treaty of Alinagar was done on 9 February 1757. According to this treaty, the rights given by Farrukhsiyar to the British were returned. Siraj-ud-Daulah gave three lakh Rs. as compensation. Permission for fortification of Calcutta was also granted and the British also got the right to keep an army in Bengal. It was also decided that on the attack of a third power, the British would support the Nawab with money and army. Clive was apprehensive that he might be called back to Madras or that there might be a compromise between the French and the Nawab, so he had made this treaty considering it only a convenient diplomatic measure.

questions.question_text: Raja Ranjit Singh obtained the world-famous Kohinoor diamond:
questions.explanation: In 1809 AD, Shah Shuja sought help from Ranjit Singh to obtain the throne of Kabul and in 1831 AD gifted him the Kohinoor diamond. Later, Shah Shuja came under the control of the Company and lived in Ludhiana

questions.question_text: 1831 AD Battle of Balakot was fought between the following armies:

options.D: Raja Ranjit Singh and Syed Ahmad Rai Barelvi

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In 1831 A.D., the Battle of Balakot was fought between Sikh Raja Ranjit Singh and Syed Ahmad Rai Barelvi. Syed Ahmad gave a call for Jihad regarding the issue of ill-treatment of Muslim population in Sikh states of Punjab. Thousands of Mujahids were prepared and a war was declared against the Sikh states. This movement started in 1826 and continued for five years and in 1831, Syed Ahmad was killed while fighting at Balakot in Abbottabad district of North-West Frontier Province.

questions.question_text: 'Battle of Wandiwash (1760)' was fought–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was fought between British and French companies. The third war of Carnatic (1756-63) was also a part of the European struggle. British fleet defeated the French fleet three times under the leadership of Pocock and forced it to return from the Indian Ocean. This made the British victory clear and in 1760, Sir Eyre Coote defeated the French badly at the place of Wandiwash. Bussy was made a war prisoner. After the complete French defeat in January 1761, they returned to Pondicherry.

questions.question_text: Through which treaty did the English East India Company obtain the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – According to the second Treaty of Allahabad (August 1765), the exiled emperor Shah Alam was taken under British protection and kept in Allahabad. The districts of Allahabad and Kara which the Nawab had left, were received by Shah Alam. Shah Alam gave the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha to the Company through his Farman of 12 August.

questions.question_text: During the 'Third Anglo-Mysore War', who was the Governor General of India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Third Anglo-Mysore War took place between 1790-92 between the British and Sultan Tipu. At this time, the Governor of India was Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793). At the end of this war, Tipu signed the Treaty of Seringapatam (March 1792) with the British. According to this, he had to give about half of his country to the British and their allies. Under this, the British got Baramahal, Dindigul and Malabar and the Marathas got the part north of Tungabhadra river and the Nizam got the part between the Pennar and Krishna rivers. ...part received. Tipu also had to pay 3 crore rupees as war damages. During this period of war, Tipu suffered great loss and could only save his kingdom from being completely finished with great difficulty. Cornwallis described this situation in the following words, "We have effectively crippled our enemy and have not allowed our allies to become powerful either."

questions.question_text: Who among the following signed the Treaty of Bassein with the British East India Company in 1802?
questions.explanation: After the death of Madhav Narayan, Raghunath Rao's son Baji Rao II became Peshwa. Due to accepting the subsidiary alliance under the Treaty of Bassein in 1802, differences began among the Maratha officials. Scindia and Bhonsle strongly opposed this treaty. Baji Rao II was an incompetent ruler

questions.question_text: At whose instance was the Treaty of Salbai signed by the Marathas with the British in 1782 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Mahadji Scindia played the role of mediator between the British and the Marathas and in May 1782, a treaty was signed between the two parties at the place called Salbai. With this, both gave up conquered territories. Only Salsette and Elephanta Island remained with the British. They stopped supporting Ragoba. The Peshwa gave a pension to Ragoba and the British accepted Madhav Rao Narayan as Peshwa. With this treaty, the situation prevailing before the war was established. Although the prestige of the company was saved, it had to suffer heavy financial loss. With this, the company got complete freedom only in the case of Mysore. On the other hand, the company also came to know about the power of the Marathas and peace remained between the two for the next 20 years.

questions.question_text: Which Maratha state accepted the subsidiary alliance of the British at the very end?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation - Among the Maratha states, Holkar chief Yashwant Rao Holkar accepted the subsidiary alliance with the British through the Treaty of Rajpur Ghat (25 December, 1805) at the very end, whereas among the Marathas, the Peshwa was the first to accept the subsidiary alliance through the Treaty of Bassein (1802).

questions.question_text: Which Mughal Subahdar gave the Zamindari of Sutanuti, Kalighat (Kalikata), and Govindpur to the British in 1698 AD?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Mughal Subahdar Azim-us-Shan gave the Zamindari of Sutanuti, Govindpur and Kalikata (Kalighat) to the British in 1698 AD. Company official Job Charnock established an English factory in Sutanuti.

questions.question_text: On which date was the Treaty of Salbai completed?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 UK GIC 2018 Explanation : The Treaty of Salbai was concluded between the East India Company and Mahadji Scindia (Maratha) on 17 May 1782. With this treaty, the First Anglo-Maratha War ended and the British and Marathas returned each other's conquered territories. The main and long-term objective of this treaty was to establish long peace between the Marathas and the British.

questions.question_text: The East India Company was given the special right to trade duty-free in Bengal-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation – An important event occurred in the history of the East India Company in 1717 AD. Under the leadership of John Surman, the British delegation reached the court of Farrukhsiyar, which included William Hamilton (surgeon), Khwaja Sehrod (Armenian interpreter), and Edward Stephenson. The Mughal Emperor issued three firmans in the name of the Subahdars of Bengal, Hyderabad, and Gujarat – according to this, in exchange for 3000 rupees annual tax, the company's trade was exempted from border customs in Bengal and the company got the right to buy 38 villages. Orme has termed this firman as the 'Magna Carta of the Company'.

questions.question_text: The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended with:
questions.explanation: The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended after the Treaty of Mangalore. This treaty took place in 1784 AD between British Governor Lord Macartney and Tipu. Through this treaty, both sides returned the territories won by each other. This treaty was a diplomatic success for Tipu. Warren Hastings, the Governor of Bengal, did not like this treaty

questions.question_text: Which of the following started the Mahalwari system of land revenue in the North-Western Provinces?
questions.explanation: The credit for starting the Mahalwari system in the North-Western Provinces and Central Provinces goes to Holt Mackenzie. Under this system, 30% of the land was brought. In this system, the settlement of land revenue was done with the landlords or village headmen of a whole village or Mahal. Farmers used to deposit the tax amount with the headmen/landlords, after which the landlords paid the tax to the British government. The main defect of this system was that it gradually made the landlords powerful

questions.question_text: According to Morris D. Morris, deindustrialization in the nineteenth century in India is a myth, because (1) It is difficult to obtain data indicating the decline of handicrafts (2) He obtained his research material from the early 19th century, at a time when handicrafts were flourishing (3) There is sufficient evidence that rich landlords patronized handicrafts (4) 20th-century sources shed light on the past of handicrafts
questions.explanation: Morris D. Morris has rejected the process of deindustrialization during the British rule period in his research paper ‘Indian Economy in the Nineteenth Century: A Symposium’ and while calling it a myth, he says that it is difficult to obtain data on deindustrialization. He believes that economic activities increased during this period. Although Indian scholars do not accept his opinion. Actually: Deindustrialization was a truth of the British period

questions.question_text: Which tax was permanently imposed on Indians in 1886? (1) Salt tax (2) Income tax (3) Education cess (4) Pilgrimage tax
questions.explanation: Tax was first implemented in India by Sir James Wilson. The first "Central Budget" of India was presented by the pre-independence Finance Minister, James Wilson, on 7 April 1860. The Indian Income Tax Act of 1860 was implemented to make up for the losses suffered by the government due to the military rebellion of 1857 A separate Income Tax Act was passed in 1886. This Act remained in force with various amendments from time to time. Under the Indian Income Tax Act of 1886, income was divided into four schedules, on which separate taxes were imposed. In this way, income tax was permanently imposed on Indians in 1886. Salt tax in India started in 1835 since the British East India Company started establishing its rule over the provinces in India. Salt March, which is also called Dandi March or Salt Satyagraha, was started by Gandhiji and he broke the salt law by making salt illegally in Dandi on 6 April 1930. The British East India Company did not make efforts for the spread of education in India in the early days of its rule. However, information about education cess is not available. Pilgrimage tax was probably started in the 17th century, but no information about any pilgrimage tax is available around 1886 AD.

questions.question_text: "At no time and place will there be roads, docks, ports, irrigation systems, hospitals, schools, colleges, and printing presses, until the government builds them." Taken from John Stuart Mill's Political Economy, this excerpt points towards which policy adopted by the Company government?
questions.explanation: The above statement "At no time and place will there be roads, docks, ports, irrigation systems, hospitals, schools, colleges, and printing presses, until the government builds them" has been taken from John Stuart Mill's famous book 'Political Economy'. This excerpt is an indicator of the interventionist policy adopted by the Company government, because until the Company government actively participates in the tasks of social development, i.e., until it does not intervene directly, such developmental works will not be possible. For the growth in economic activities, the free trade (Laissez-faire) policy was adopted by the government, which led to an increase in Mercantilism, i.e., trade and commerce. Indifferentism shows the passive interest of the Company government towards any tasks

questions.question_text: In the context of colonial cities, which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: In the context of colonial cities, the following statements are correct - with political and commercial reorganization, old cities like - Agra, Lahore, Delhi, Dhaka, Murshidabad, and Patna became decadent, while new cities like - Madras, Mumbai, Calcutta emerged, which became important centers of education, trade, administration, commerce, etc According to C.A. Bayly, after the 1720s, there was considerable expansion of small towns in the mid-Ganga region. Mumbai's Victoria Terminus was built based on Indo-Saracenic style (Neo-Gothic style). It was designed by F.W. Stevens.

questions.question_text: Who said that the Permanent Settlement was a painful and dreadful error?
questions.explanation: The Permanent Settlement was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Varanasi and Ghazipur regions of Uttar Pradesh, and the regions of Northern Karnataka. This settlement was implemented by Lord Cornwallis through his decree. In this system, 10/11 parts of the tax were fixed for the government and 1/11 parts for the landlords. Landlords benefited the most from this because their actual right over the land was accepted. Seeing this anarchy, T.R. Metcalfe said that "The Permanent Settlement was a painful and dreadful error."

questions.question_text: In which year was the Workmen's Compensation Act passed?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, provides for payment of compensation to workmen and their dependents for injury and accident (including some occupational diseases) sustained during and because of employment, which results in disability or death. This Act applies to railway employees and those engaged in such works as specified in the schedule of the Act.

questions.question_text: (i) MacDonnell (ii) Strachey (iii) Lyall (iv) Campbell Select the correct answer from the code given below: Arrange the following famine commissions in chronological order:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– In the given code, the Campbell Commission (1866-67) was constituted first. A famine commission was constituted in 1878 AD under the chairmanship of Richard Strachey. A famine commission was constituted under the name of 'Lyall Commission' during the time of Lord Elgin II (1894-1899 AD). In 1900 AD, a famine commission was constituted under the chairmanship of Sir Anthony MacDonnell.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the economic critique of colonialism?
questions.explanation: In the context of the economic critique of colonialism, British rulers viewed the construction of railways and foreign trade as a sign of India's prosperity. According to them, the construction of railways facilitated the movement of goods, consequently boosting trade and commerce, which led to the country's progress, whereas nationalists logically refuted this ideology of the British government. According to nationalists, foreign trade and negative impact on railways indicate the underdevelopment of the Indian economy because this trade made the Indian market an exporter and importer of raw materials and finished goods. Option (c) is wrong that expenditure was fulfilling the requirements of the British government and consequently was also bringing prosperity to Indian people. Option (d) is also wrong, because the theory of wealth drain (Drain Theory) was presented at the 1896 AD Calcutta session of Congress (President – M. Rahimtulla Sayani)

questions.question_text: In which year was the ‘Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act’ implemented?
questions.explanation: The Deccan farmers' rebellion was mainly against the Marwari and Gujarati moneylenders. Under the Ryotwari system, the ryots had to face heavy taxation. In the year 1874, the ryots organized a social boycott movement against the moneylenders. This social boycott spread rapidly in the villages of Pune, Ahmednagar, Sholapur, and Satara. The government was successful in suppressing this movement. As a conciliation measure, the Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act was passed in 1879

questions.question_text: Permanent Settlement was made:
questions.explanation: The Permanent Settlement system is the modified form of the Dousala system implemented during Lord Cornwallis's time, which took the form of Permanent Settlement in 1793. This system was implemented on about 19% of India's part, which included Bengal, Bihar, and Varanasi of U.P. and Northern Karnataka. It was related to landlords The Ryotwari system was founded by Thomas Munro and Captain Reed, which was first implemented in the Baramahal district of Tamil Nadu. In this, tax was taken directly from the farmer. 51% of India's part was included under this. In the Mahalwari system, a group of villages used to pay the tax. 30% of India's total part was included under this.

questions.question_text: Who said, ‘The economic interests of India and Britain clash in every field’?
questions.explanation: The economic interests of India and England clash in every field. This statement was given by Jawaharlal Nehru. When there was a time of wealth drain in India and the destruction of Indian handicrafts and a new economic progress in India. In the 18th century, the continuous flow of wealth of the Indian colony was towards England, in return for which India did not get adequate economic, commercial or material benefits, such wealth has been termed by Indian national leaders and economists as the drain of wealth. England has considered this drain of wealth as an indirect gift or contribution from India. Thus, when the British left in 1947, the economic condition of the country was such that the country was reeling under centuries of economic exploitation and determined underdevelopment, a country that had many natural resources but people were poor

questions.question_text: In October 1921, under whose chairmanship did the British government appoint a Revenue Commission?
questions.explanation: In October 1921 AD, the government constituted a Revenue Commission, whose chairman was made Sir Ibrahim Rahimtullah. It recommended that industries should be given protection in special circumstances. Although in the eyes of Indians, the recommendations of this commission were inadequate, still the government provided the facility of protection

questions.question_text: Who said, ‘This misery is perhaps never in the history of commerce. The bones of the weavers are bleaching the plains of India’?
questions.explanation: The destruction of Indian handicrafts came to light as the destruction of those cities which were famous for their manufactured goods, cities which survived after the destruction of war and looting, could not remain alive due to British victory. Dhaka, Surat, Murshidabad, and many other densely populated rich industrial centers became deserted and turned into ruins. By the end of the nineteenth century, the city's population was hardly 1/3rd of the total population. Governor-General William Bentinck wrote in 1834-35 - The misery like this misery is perhaps never in the history of commerce. The bones of the weavers are bleaching the plains of India

questions.question_text: Who established the "Society of Trades"?
questions.explanation: After success in the battles of Plassey and Buxar, Company employees amassed a lot of wealth through gifts and private trade. Clive stopped this and made internal duty mandatory. To compensate for the loss caused by these restrictions, a trade committee of Company workers was formed in 1765 AD. It was given a monopoly on the trade of salt, betel nut, and tobacco. This plan was terminated in 1768 AD

questions.question_text: Who was the proponent of the Ryotwari land settlement?
questions.explanation: Individual tax agreements made with farmers were called Ryotwari. This system was implemented in Madras, Bombay, Eastern Bengal, Assam, and Coorg. Under this system, 51% of India's land came. Two officers named Colonel Reed and Thomas Munro are credited with implementing this system. This Ryotwari system was first implemented in the Baramahal district in 1792 AD. In 1820 AD, Madras Governor Thomas Munro implemented it in the remaining parts of Madras

questions.question_text: Where did the first cotton mill start in India?
questions.explanation: The first cotton mill in India was established in Kolkata. It was established in 1818 AD near Kolkata at Fort Gloster but it was unsuccessful. Again, in 1851 AD, a mill was established in Mumbai which was the most modern mill. But this too was unsuccessful. Later in 1854 AD, a mill was opened in Mumbai by Cowasji Nanabhoy Davar which was successful. The success of this mill paved the way for the manufacturing of cotton clothes in India

questions.question_text: What was Nij-Abad?
questions.explanation: Indigo cultivation in Bengal had been going on since the 18th century. It was prevalent in two main forms: Nij-Abad and Ryoti. In Nij-Abad or self-system, planters used to produce Indigo on the lands which they controlled themselves. In Ryoti, farmers used to cultivate Indigo on their own land under a contract with planters

questions.question_text: 'Bombay Mill Hands Association' was a type of first trade union in India. Its founder was:
questions.explanation: In 1890, N.M. Lokhande established the Bombay Mill Hands Association. It was considered the first labor organization of India. Lokhande published a weekly newspaper named Deenbandhu in English and Marathi in 1880 AD

questions.question_text: Which was the most exported item from India in the 17th century?
questions.explanation: In the 17th century, the export of cotton cloth from India started in the largest quantity. In the 17th century, the monopoly of the Portuguese on India's trade ended and the commercial power of the Dutch reached its peak. The Dutch mainly gave more importance to cotton cloth export. Although they also exported opium, silk, spices, etc. In this period, Gujarat and Coromandel established themselves as the two most prominent commercial centers. From where the Dutch exported cotton cloth in large quantities

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’?
questions.explanation: India's veteran Parsi educationist and cotton businessman Dadabhai Naoroji wrote the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’. Through his book, he highlighted the money sent to England from India under the theory of wealth drain. He said that "The drain of wealth is the root of all evils and is the root cause of Indian poverty."

questions.question_text: Who said, ‘The railway system will become the forerunner of the modern era of India’?
questions.explanation: In the first phase of industrialization in India, the railway system was started in India by Lord Dalhousie in 1853 AD, whose first trial started between Mumbai and Thane. Its purpose was to export India's cotton and easily reach coastal ports and military capability in case of rebellion. In this development, on 23 July 1853 AD, Marx wrote in the Daily Tribune: 'In a big country where it is impossible to create an opportunity for the growth of its industry without creating a network of railways for iron and coal, therefore the railway system itself will become the forerunner of the modern era of India.'

questions.question_text: What was the main element of the 'Economic Drain' theory?

options.A: Interest paid on foreign capital investment

questions.explanation: The theory of drain of wealth from India was first presented by Dadabhai Naoroji on 2 May 1867, in a meeting of the East India Association in London. He said that Britain is taking away India's wealth at the cost of its own rule. A quarter of the revenue collected in India goes out of India. India's blood is being continuously sucked. In his theory, he gave the following points regarding India's home revenue expenditure - As a result of the drain of wealth, capital accumulation could not happen in India. - The living standard of people kept falling continuously, poverty kept increasing. - Due to the drain of wealth, the burden of taxes on the people increased a lot. - Along with this, the destruction of cottage industries happened. - Pressure on land increased and the number of landless agricultural laborers kept increasing. It is noteworthy that home expenditure included India Secretary of State and expenditure related to it.

questions.question_text: In which year was the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ published?
questions.explanation: There could be no more powerful denunciation of British rule in India than this. Naoroji tried to resolve this internal contradiction by calling British rule in India ‘Un-British Rule’ and named his excellent creation Poverty and Un-British Rule in India, which was published in London in 1901 AD. In this book, he discussed the drain of capital from India by Britain that Britain is taking away this country's wealth as the cost of its rule in India

questions.question_text: Who said, "Drain of wealth is the evil of all evils"?
questions.explanation: The drain of wealth refers to all those payments made by India to Britain without any reward and responsibility. The description of the theory of wealth drain was first done by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book ‘The Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the world's oldest publicly listed company?
questions.explanation: In 1602 AD, by merging various Dutch companies, a massive commercial establishment was established in the name of United East India Company of Netherlands. A board of 17 people was formed to oversee it. This board managed the company according to the ideals of the Dutch government. At the time of the establishment of the company, its total initial capital was 6.5 million guilders

questions.question_text: Under which Governor-General was the ‘Bengal Permanent Settlement’ Act passed?
questions.explanation: Bengal's Governor Lord Cornwallis implemented the Permanent Settlement or Zamindari settlement in Bengal on 22 March 1793 AD. This system was a permanent system related to tax collection between the Company and the landlords of Bengal, which was a form of agreement. The Zamindari system of tax collection in Bengal and Bihar was chosen as the official method. Due to the contract farming system established in Bengal by Warren Hastings, the condition of the farmers had become poor. To improve this situation, the Company appointed Lord Cornwallis

questions.question_text: When did the Congress Working Committee accept the proposal recommending Zamindari abolition?
questions.explanation: The Congress Working Committee accepted the proposal recommending Zamindari abolition in 1950 AD

questions.question_text: Which European power started trading with India via the sea route for the first time?
questions.explanation: In 1498, when Portuguese traveler Vasco da Gama came via the sea route and sold spices of India in Europe for a huge sum, after that the Portuguese first started sea trade from India

questions.question_text: In which of the following regions did the British East India Company implement the Ryotwari system in the 18th century?
questions.explanation: This was the second system for British land revenue; its founders are considered Thomas Munro and Captain Reed. In 1792 AD, it was first implemented in the Baramahal district of Tamil Nadu/Madras. Apart from this, it was implemented in some parts of Bombay, Eastern Bengal, and some parts of Assam

questions.question_text: Which philosophy influenced the Permanent Settlement of Bengal (1793)?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis attempted to replace the policy adopted by Warren Hastings with further Anglicization of his administration and to implement the Whig theories of the British government in India. Its purpose was to abandon the so-called despotic aspects of Indian political tradition and for this, to ensure the separation of powers between the judiciary and the executive, to limit the government's intervention. That is why Cornwallis started the Permanent Settlement and through this, the rule of law and private property rights would free individual enterprise from the shackles of customs and would modernize society and the economy

questions.question_text: Cowasji Nanabhoy set up the first textile industry (taxile mill) in 1853 –
questions.explanation: In the third phase of British colonial rule, capital was invested by Indians in some Indian industries. Cotton textile was the first industry in Indian industries in which capital was invested by Indians. The first mill of cotton textiles was established in 1853 in Bombay through the efforts of Parsi Cowasji Nanabhoy. By 1904-05, about 266 cloth mills were established in India. The first jute mill in India was established in 1855 at a place named Srirampur in Bengal

questions.question_text: Who said, "Ryotwari is a system that has always been prevalent in India"?
questions.explanation: The British implemented Permanent Land Settlement, Ryotwari system, and Mahalwari system for land revenue. The founders of the Ryotwari system are considered Thomas Munro and Captain Reed. This system was implemented in Madras, some parts of Bombay, Eastern Bengal, and Assam. Under this system, the collection of revenue was done harshly and the rate of revenue was also very high, the result of which was that the farmer got trapped in the clutches of moneylenders, which later became the cause of conflict between moneylenders and farmers. That is why Munro said "Ryotwari is a system that has always been prevalent in India."

questions.question_text: What was the meaning of the Sunset Law?

options.A: Land revenue collected by the revenue officer had to be deposited by sunset on a certain day.
options.B: According to the Permanent Settlement, if the tax was not deposited by sunset on a fixed day, the Zamindari could be auctioned.
options.C: Military officers had to inform the headquarters by sunset on the return of their military campaigns.
options.D: During the Dual Government, government workers were given wages at the time of sunset.

questions.explanation: Sunset law means the Permanent Settlement law established by Cornwallis in 1793; according to this, if the tax was not paid to the government by sunset of the pre-determined date, then the Zamindari would be auctioned. 19% area of British India came under this

questions.question_text: Canning-Lawrence school, Mill school, and Mayo-Northbrook school were related to which administrative dispute?

options.B: Implementation, continuation, and expansion of Permanent Settlement.
options.C: Start of Mahalwari settlement in new areas.
options.D: Adoption of a liberal outlook towards India after the 1857 rebellion.

questions.explanation: Canning-Lawrence school, Mill school, and Mayo-Northbrook school were related to the dispute of implementation, continuation, and expansion of Permanent Settlement. The Permanent Settlement was started in 1790 as a 10-year agreement with landlords, which was made permanent in 1793. This system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, the Banaras division of Uttar Pradesh, and Northern Karnataka. Approximately 19 percent of the total area of British India was included under this system

questions.question_text: Who started the Permanent Settlement agreement?
questions.explanation: For land revenue management, Lord Cornwallis implemented the Permanent Settlement in Bengal on 22 March 1793 AD. This law is known by various other names like Istemrari system, Malguzari system, Jagirdari or Zamindari system, etc. This system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Assam, Banaras and Ghazipur of Uttar Pradesh, and Northern Karnataka

questions.question_text: Which of the following systems was opposed by Sir John Shore?
questions.explanation: Permanent Settlement was adopted in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, U.P.'s Banaras division, and Northern Karnataka. It was implemented on 19% of all British Indian land. Initially, Sir John Shore opposed the Permanent Settlement. He was a supporter of the 10-year settlement

questions.question_text: In which of the following areas did the British invest their maximum capital?
questions.explanation: The British invested the most capital in India in railways, banking, insurance, and shipping. To provide raw materials to Britain's industries, the British first worked on connecting cotton-producing areas with railway lines

questions.question_text: British governance is sucking the blood of India - who said this?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji called the British governance system an organization that sucks the blood of India. Dadabhai Naoroji first presented the theory of wealth drain in his book ‘The Poverty and Un-British Rule in India-1901’

questions.question_text: Who were the proponents of the drain theory?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the drain theory in his book "The Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" published in 1901

questions.question_text: In 1834, who said that "Cotton weavers' bones are bleaching the plains of India"?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck (1828-35) was the main Governor-General of India. Major reforms done by him in India - ban on Sati system (1829), end of Thuggee system and infanticide (1830), prohibition of human sacrifice, end of slavery. He was a supporter of free trade and free competition. He, along with correcting the Company's economic mess and administrative defects, also did public welfare works. By the Charter Act of 1833, the Governor-General of Bengal started being called the 'Governor-General of India'. In this way, he became the first Governor-General of India. In opposition to cotton textiles, he said that "Cotton weavers' bones are bleaching the plains of India."

questions.question_text: Who established the ‘East India Association’ in London?
questions.explanation: In 1866 AD, the East India Association was established in London by Dadabhai Naoroji. Dadabhai Naoroji was called the ‘Grand Old Man of India’. He also established the Rahnumae Mazdayasnan Sabha. He published 'Rast Goftar' (truth-telling newspaper). Wrote the book named ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’

questions.question_text: In what did the core element of the wealth-drain theory propagated by Dadabhai Naoroji lie?

options.A: Misuse of commercial activities by traders of the ruling class.
options.B: Obtaining money unfairly from princely states and sending it to England.
options.D: Filling Indian markets with British-produced goods.

questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji, in his important book Indian Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901), logically proved the drain of wealth. He confirmed the drain of wealth theory and the core element of this theory lay in the one-sided export from India to Britain.

questions.question_text: Before the arrival of the British, India's economy was
questions.explanation: Before the arrival of the British, the Indian economy was a village-based economy. There was self-reliance and self-governing community in the village. Except for salt and iron, they had nothing to do with the outside world. The village economy was self-contained (self-sufficient)

questions.question_text: The meaning of laissez-faire policy or liberalism is
questions.explanation: In the laissez-faire policy, no intervention of any kind is done by the state in trade, which makes trade free

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true regarding ‘economic drain’?

options.A: Economic drain means the transfer of Indian wealth to England.
options.B: Drain of capital happened in the form of salary and pension of civil and military officers working in India.
options.C: Dadabhai Naoroji presented the theory of economic drain in the British Parliament.
options.D: Economic drain theory exposed the colonial exploitation of India.

questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji first raised the issue of capital drain from India. He first propounded capital drain in his article ‘England Debt to India’ in 1867 AD and said ‘Britain is sucking the blood of India’

questions.question_text: After independence, which of the following industries was not kept in the private sector?
questions.explanation: After independence, petroleum and its products were not kept under the private sector. After independence, the first industrial policy in India came in 1948 AD. The entire focus of the Second Five Year Plan was centered on industrial development

questions.question_text: "Neel Darpan" was related to
questions.explanation: The play ‘Neel Darpan’ was related to farmers cultivating indigo, which was written by Dinabandhu Mitra. This was the first commercial play performed in 1872 AD at the National Theater in Kolkata, Bengal

questions.question_text: The first cloth mill was established in 1853 AD by Cowasji Nanabhoy
questions.explanation: Cotton textile mills were established in Kolkata in 1818 AD and in Mumbai in 1851 AD, which were unsuccessful. The first successful modern factory was opened in 1854 AD in Mumbai (then Bombay) by Cowasji Nanabhoy Davar. Production started in this in 1856 AD

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, A is a statement and R is a reason:

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, and R is false.
options.D: R is true and A is false.

questions.explanation: Under the guarantee system of railway construction, companies were guaranteed a minimum 5% profit on their capital investment. This system is called the ‘guarantee system of profit’. This guarantee system (system) made a huge contribution to the drain of wealth from India. It is noteworthy that this system was a well-thought-out strategy of the British, which R.P. Dutt called ‘State of Financial Capitalism’ (1858-1947 AD) in his book ‘India Today’

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: Land Reform Year Punjab Land Transfer Act 1900 AD Deccan Agricultural Relief Act 1879 AD North-Western Provinces Land Transfer Act 1873 AD Central Provinces Land Transfer Act 1916 AD

questions.question_text: Select the reason/reasons for the commercialization of agriculture during the British rule: 1. India was limited as a supplier of raw materials. 2. Better means of transport made the trade of agricultural produce easy. 4. Industrial revolution in England. Select the correct option: 3. Monetization of payment of land revenue.
questions.explanation: The reasons for the commercialization of agriculture during British rule are 1. India was limited as a supplier of raw materials. 2. Better means of transport made the trade of agricultural produce easy. 3. Monetization of payment of land revenue. 4. Industrial revolution in England. 5. Investment of foreign capital in cash crops.

questions.question_text: Which British officer wrote about the uncertain land property conditions prevalent in North India that "The land-holding property of this region is suffering from an overly comprehensive and painful revolution."
questions.explanation: Holt Mackenzie was a British officer who started the Mahalwari system in 1822 AD in Punjab, Agra, Central Provinces, and the Deccan and he wrote about the land property conditions prevalent in North India, "The land-holding property of this region is suffering from an overly comprehensive and painful revolution."

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one is called assertion (A) and the other is called reason (R): Assertion (A): Some farmer rebellions before 1857 saw the participation of tribals entirely, because the policies of British rule had put their political autonomy and their control over local resources in danger. Which of the following is correct regarding the above statements? Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Some small rebellions occurred even before the first freedom struggle of 1857 AD, in which tribals participated because the British started controlling their autonomy and local resources because the improvements made till the first half of the 19th century changed the basic nature of Indian rural society

questions.question_text: Whose statement was this in the House of Commons that "Our Indian empire is shrouded in deep darkness. questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– "Our Indian empire is shrouded in deep darkness. questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one is called assertion (A) and the other is called reason (R): Assertion (A): Chiefs colleges were established in India to provide education to the aristocratic class and royal families of India. Whereas the natives were not interested in receiving education in English. It was Curzon's policy that spreading English education in the upper class would eventually reach the lower class slowly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following did not support the opinion that protected monarchs in India were merely 'vassals' of the British Crown?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Sir William Lee-Warner did not support the opinion that protected monarchs in India were merely 'vassals' of the British Crown. Sir William Lee-Warner (1846-1914 AD) was an administrator.

questions.question_text: When was the first Factory Act passed by the British colonial government?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The first Factory Act was passed by the British colonial government in 1881 AD. At this time, the Viceroy of India was Lord Ripon (1880-1884 AD). The purpose of this Act was to provide protection to child workers.

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one is called statement (A) and the other is reason (R): Statement (A): The decline of traditional artisan cottage industries was a result of British commercial policy. Reason (R): Imperial conquests had made limitless resources available to the British. Which of the following is correct regarding both the above statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The decline of traditional artisan cottage industries was a result of British commercial policy. By 1800 AD, Indian industries were the most developed in the world. After this, industrial decline happened in India. Imperial conquests had made limitless resources available to the British. But reason (R) is not the correct explanation of statement (A).

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book named 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2012) PGT (History) 2005 Explanation– The book named ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ was written by Dadabhai Naoroji. He mentioned in this book that the root cause of Indian poverty and starvation was British regulations. It is known that the book named ‘The Wants and Means of India’ and ‘On the Commerce of India’ were also written by Dadabhai Naoroji.

questions.question_text: Under the Ryotwari system in Madras, in which year was the land revenue rate finally fixed at fifty percent of net produce and the settlement fixed for thirty years?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – In the year 1802, the then Governor of Madras Thomas Munro started the Ryotwari system. This system was implemented in some parts of Madras, Bombay, and Assam. Under the Ryotwari system in Madras, the year in which land revenue was finally fixed at 50% of net produce and settlement was fixed for 30 years was 1864 AD.

questions.question_text: During which period was the policy of import duty relief adopted by the British government?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The policy of import duty relief was adopted by the British government during 1882 to 1894. It is noteworthy that the British government increased the export duty and reduced the import duty to discourage Indian trade and encourage British trade.

questions.question_text: Below are two statements, one is called statement (A) and the other is reason (R) – Statement (A): The basic premise of the Permanent Settlement implemented in Bengal in 1793 was to fix the tax forever. Reason (R): Cornwallis believed that the landlords would develop their land. Which of the following is correct regarding the above statements? Code:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation– Cornwallis implemented Permanent Settlement in West Bengal on 22 March, 1793 AD. In this system, land revenue was fixed forever, which landlords had to deposit every year. In this system, 10/11 parts of the tax were fixed for the government and 1/11 parts for the landlords. Landlords benefited the most from this because their actual right over the land was accepted and ownership of land became hereditary. Cornwallis believed that due to Permanent Settlement, landlords would develop agriculture and encourage new techniques and fertilizers. Thus, statement (A) and reason (R) both are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of statement (A).

questions.question_text: Which of the following reasons was not a cause for the rise of moneylenders in British India?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– Some policies adopted by the British in British India, such as new revenue policy, new legal system, and commercialization of agriculture, etc., became the main reason for the rise of moneylenders. Whereas the new education system provided an opportunity for Indian nationalist ideology to flourish.

questions.question_text: In which was the largest British capital investment made in India?

options.B: In railways, banking, insurance, and shipping

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– After 1860, British capitalists invested capital in India on a large scale. This capital investment was mainly made in the construction of railways, banking systems, insurance, and shipping. Later, investment was made in implementing irrigation schemes, developing plantation industries (tea, rubber, and coffee), and in the coal mining sector.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a major outcome of the East India Company's Permanent Revenue Settlement?

options.A: It created a loyal class of landlords.
options.B: Farmers were left at the mercy of landlords.
options.C: There was a halt in the company's revenue growth process.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Lord Cornwallis implemented Permanent Settlement in 1786 AD. This system was implemented in Bengal and Bihar. John Shore recognized landlords as owners of the land. In this way, the British got a loyal class in the form of landlords. Farmers were left at the mercy of landlords. This did not give special impetus to agricultural production; instead, the exploitation of farmers increased.

questions.question_text: Out of many individuals in India, three Indians made a brilliant economic analysis of British rule on India during 1870-1905. Who were they?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Dadabhai Naoroji first presented this belief in his article ‘England Debt to India’ read at the East India Association meeting held in London on 2 May 1867 AD, that Britain is taking away this country's wealth at the cost of its rule in India. Mahadev Govind Ranade was the first announcer of the industrialization of India who called upon people to establish industries in the country. R.C. Dutt supported Dadabhai Naoroji in propounding the ‘Drain Theory’ as an economic analysis in the context of wealth drain by the British.

questions.question_text: 'Mercantilist, Free Trade Mercantilist, Capitalism and Financial Imperialism - are the three stages of British imperialism.' Who first propounded this theory?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Imperialist historian Karl Marx first propounded British imperialism in three stages or three phases as Mercantilist, Free Trade Mercantilist, Capitalism, and Financial Imperialism, which includes the Commercial phase (1757-1813), Industrial Free Trade (1813-1858), Financial Capitalism after 1860. Later, R.P. Dutt also, in his book 'India Today', ignored British economic policies by dividing British imperialist history into three phases, taking the phases divided by Karl Marx as the basis.

questions.question_text: What was the main reason for deindustrialization during the Company period?

options.A: Indian handicrafts could not face the pressure.
options.B: Indian markets were filled with machine-made low-priced goods of England.
options.C: Indian rulers could not provide protection to indigenous handicrafts.
options.D: Local jagirdars and landlords had disappeared.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The period between 1800 AD to 1850 AD in India is known by the name of Deindustrialization. During this period, while Britain was going through the phase of industrial revolution, the phase of decline of industrialization was going on in India. The decline of Indian handicrafts happened.

questions.question_text: In the second half of the 19th century, which main industry was in the hands of Indian capitalists?
questions.explanation: Explanation– India has been the leading country in the world in the production and trade of cotton textiles since ancient times, but after the British power occupied it, the trade of cotton textile industry gradually started to decline. In the second half of the 19th century, the cotton-made cloth industry was the only main industry in the hands of Indian capitalists.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a factor of economic (wealth wealth) drain going from India to Britain?

options.B: Dividend paid to the shareholders of the East India Company

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Dadabhai Naoroji first gave the theory of wealth drain. On 2 May, 1867 AD, he mentioned this in ‘England Debt to India’. Naoroji declared wealth drain the real and root cause of all diseases, sorrow, and poverty of the country.

questions.question_text: What was the promised profit that British companies investing in railways under the ‘old guarantee system’ had?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Higher Education Exam (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– After 1850 AD, Britain's capitalists invested capital on a large scale in India to earn profit on their wealth in railway construction, loans to the government, tea, rubber, coffee, etc. industries. Under the guarantee of profit, the government guaranteed 5% profit on capital investment in railway construction.

questions.question_text: Consider the following regarding the Ryotwari system:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– According to the Ryotwari practice, every registered landowner was accepted as the owner of the land. He was responsible for giving land tax to the Company government. He had permission to mortgage and sell his land. He could not be deprived of his land as long as he paid the land tax on time. The re-examination of the payment of tax would be done every 30 years.

questions.question_text: What was that permit called, under which the East India Company (from 1757) had the freedom to use it in every type of transaction, supervision, and exemption from payment of customs duty?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – That permit was known as Dastak, under which the East India Company had exemption from supervision and payment of customs duty for use in every type of transaction in trade. In the farman given to the Company by Farrukhsiyar in 1717 AD, an exemption was given not to pay 2 percent duty. Keeping in mind the misuse of this Dastak system, it was completely ended during Lord Cornwallis's time.

questions.question_text: When did the British East India Company lose its monopoly on trade in India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – By the Charter Act of 1813, the British East India Company's monopoly on Indian trade was ended. Although its monopoly on trade with China and the tea trade continued. Now all British traders were given permission to trade from India. Under the Charter Act of 1833, trade with China and tea trade was also ended.

questions.question_text: In which year did Bihar separate from Bengal Presidency and become a separate province?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – In 1905, the British government tried to end the growing influence of Bengali and Indian nationalism by ending the Bengal partition. Which was cancelled in 1911 and along with this, by separating Odisha and Bihar from Bengal Presidency, these two provinces were made separate states in 1936 AD.

questions.question_text: Which nationalists gave the name 'Drain Theory' to the economic exploitation of the British?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation – Dadabhai Naoroji gave the name 'Drain Theory' to the economic exploitation of the British. Wealth drain means all those payments made by India to Britain without any reward and responsibility. The description of the theory of wealth drain was first done by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book ‘The Poverty & Un-British Rule in India’.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the main item exported from Bengal in the eighteenth century?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Saltpetre and cotton textiles were the main items exported from Bengal in the eighteenth century.

questions.question_text: When and where did the first industrial strike occur in India?

options.B: 1877 AD in Empress cotton mill Kanpur
options.C: 1905 AD in Empress cotton mill Kanpur

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Modern industrial development in India started with the establishment of the first cotton cloth mill in Mumbai. Indian capital and Indian management were the main factors in the establishment of this factory. The first industrial strike in India occurred in 1885 AD in the textile mill located in Mumbai. From 1882 to 1890, the number of strikes in Mumbai and Madras reached 25. The leadership of this movement was done by N.M. Lokhande.

questions.question_text: Where did the Congress announce its agricultural policy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– In the session of the Indian National Congress held in Faizpur (Bengal) in 1937 AD, a 13-point temporary agricultural policy was announced by the Congress. This was the first occasion when a Congress session took place in a village. This session of Faizpur (Bengal) was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question_text: The British committed atrocities on some artisans in Bengal:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– The period from 1800 AD to 1850 AD in India is known by the name of ‘Deindustrialization’. During this period, the most damage was done to India's traditional handicraft industries, especially weavers. The Company and British capitalists together completely destroyed the Indian handicraft industry. ‘Loom’ and ‘Charkha’, which were famous as the axis of ancient Indian society, were broken and Indian markets were filled with cloth manufactured in Lancashire and Manchester.

questions.question_text: Taluqdari system was related to–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Taluqdari system was related to Awadh province, which was in the form of a synonym for the Mahalwari system. The Mahalwari system was implemented in 30% of the total area of British India.

questions.question_text: Who established the ‘All India Spinners Association’ in the field of handloom development?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– To reduce the excessive poverty of Indians and to encourage Indians to boycott European goods, as a way to encourage the production of handmade and woven cloth of India and Khadi, Gandhi started a movement. For which Mahatma Gandhi established the ‘All India Spinners Association’ on 6 November 1904 in the field of handloom development.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'The Economic History of India' –
questions.explanation: Explanation – 'The Economic History of India' is the book of Ramesh Chandra Dutt. In this, he described the drain of wealth.

questions.question_text: What happened with the Permanent Settlement in Bengal?

options.A: Encouragement of the interests of the ryot
options.C: Creation of an elite system that supported the British

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – The Permanent Settlement in Bengal was implemented by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 AD, in which 10/11 parts of land tax had to be given to the Company government and 1/11 parts had to be kept by the landlord for his services. With this Permanent Settlement, an elite system (landlord class) that supported the British was created, which remained their supporter until India's independence.

questions.question_text: Whitley Commission was related to –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – To get information about the existing conditions of workers in industrial enterprises in India, the Royal Commission on Labor was established in 1929. This commission was presided over by John Henry. It is also known as the Whitley Commission. This commission presented its report in 1931. Under this report, the main reason for poverty in India was the backward social and industrial structure of India.

questions.question_text: Due to corruption and bribery of Company officers, private trade and taking gifts were stopped. Who forced them to sign a special contract?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Due to corruption and bribery of Company officers, private trade and taking gifts were stopped. Lord Cornwallis forced them to sign a special contract.

questions.question_text: 'Sunset Law' was related to which land revenue system of the British government?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- 'Sunset Law' was related to the Permanent Settlement land revenue system of the British government. A lot of landlords were also affected by the laws made by the British. Many people lost their entire land due to this rule. A few landlords benefited the most from the Permanent Settlement system.

questions.question_text: Where was the Ryotwari practice started?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 PGT History 2005 PCS (Pre) Indian History 2002 Explanation- The founders of the Ryotwari system implemented by the British for land revenue collection in India are considered Thomas Munro and Captain Reed. In 1792 AD, through the efforts of Captain Reed, the Ryotwari system was first implemented in the ‘Baramahal’ district of Tamil Nadu. In this system, the government gave land, i.e., ryot to the farmers, this system was implemented in Bombay, Madras, and Assam.

questions.question_text: Which settlement destroyed the rights of the farmers over the land they cultivated?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Cornwallis implemented the Permanent Settlement system in 1793 AD. This system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha, and the regions of Varanasi and Northern Karnataka of Uttar Pradesh. Under this, landlords, who were recognized as owners of land, had to collect land revenue in their areas and keep 1/11th part for themselves and deposit the remaining part with the Company. The landlord used to collect revenue from the tenants as they pleased and land was snatched away from those tenants who did not pay revenue on time. Overall, the tenant was entirely dependent on the mercy of the landlords. There was no government control over the landlords.

questions.question_text: Who has been called the 'father of British land system'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Martins Bird is called the 'father of British land system'. After the failure of Permanent and Ryotwari systems, the proposal for the Mahalwari system was brought by Holt Mackenzie. Macaulay had the most contribution in making English the official language of India and the medium of education and making European racial philosophy and science the goal of Indian education.

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions was the drain theory formally accepted by the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The Indian National Congress formally accepted the theory of wealth drain in the 1896 AD Calcutta session. Probably, the greatest service of the moderate party happened at that time when these people evaluated the economic impact of the British Empire on India. They drew attention to Indian poverty and explained that this poverty is due to British colonial exploitation. The drain theory propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji, R.C. Dutt, and Wacha was an accusation of the economic role of the British in India. Later on, the extremist party users used this theory to defame the British. In the words of Edward Bevan, "There was a kind of iron structure in British Raj, which bound the damaged body of India until the displaced bones and the broken threads due to internal changes joined slowly and the patient regained his internal unity and connection."

questions.question_text: Which newspaper said that "The development of railways in India is a handcuff"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- During Dalhousie's tenure, the first rail line was laid in India in 1853 from Bombay to Thane and soon the entire Indian empire was tied in the thread of railway lines and became one. For Indian security and to increase internal communication system, strategically important lines were laid. The detailed blueprint of this project was given by Lord Dalhousie in his famous railway letter and this remained the basis of future expansion in India. In 1865, Sir Arnold wrote 'Railways will be able to do in India what the great dynasties could not do, nor could Tipu succeed in doing by his atrocities, it will make India a nation'. But in 1885 AD, the newspaper named 'Sanjivani' wrote in one of its issues that the development of railways in India is a handcuff.

questions.question_text: In whose reign was the first railway line laid in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- In the time of Lord Dalhousie, the Governor-General who implemented the 'Doctrine of Lapse' which merged Indian princely states into the British Empire, the work of laying the first railway lines started. In 1853 AD, during Dalhousie's tenure, the operation of the first railway train started between Bombay and Thane. Other reforms of Dalhousie include the establishment of the postal department, establishment of the Public Works Department (P.W.D.), and the passing of the Widow Remarriage Act (1856). William Bentinck declared the Sati system prohibited by making a law in 1829 AD. Lord Canning was the first Viceroy and the last Governor-General of India.

questions.question_text: Who benefited from Lord Lytton's decision to reduce import duty on cotton cloth production?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Lord Lytton was a supporter of the policy of free trade. Due to the industrial revolution, Britain was leading trade and industry at that time and the policy of free trade was in its interest. Britain needed raw materials in India and its finished goods received a good market. Due to this, adopting the policy of free trade in India was in the interest of Britain's industry and trade. British traders were opposing the various import-export taxes imposed by the Indian government. Eventually, on the orders of the India Secretary and his own consent, Lord Lytton adopted the policy of free trade and probably abolished the import-export tax on items and in this way, India's interest was sacrificed for the fulfillment of Britain's interest.

questions.question_text: Who divided the economic history of colonial India into the following four phases?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Karl Marx divided the economic history of colonial India into four phases - Commercial Capitalism, Free Trade Capitalism, Industrial Capitalism, Financial Capitalism. Whereas R.P. Dutt divided this into three phases in his book 'India Today' - Commercial Capitalism, Free Trade, Financial Capitalism. Dadabhai Naoroji is related to the drain of wealth in India. He has termed the drain of wealth as ‘evil of evils’ and called it the main reason for India's poverty. According to him, England is sucking the blood of India and destroying it. In a letter written to Hyndman in 1905, he said "India's condition is very bad. It is not in the condition of master and slave but even worse than that. This is the condition of a looted nation where the looter is constantly looting and then escapes clean." R.C. Dutt, in ‘Economics History of India’, mentioning the drain of wealth, stated that about half of India's total revenue goes out of the country every year. Explanation– Among European companies, except for Holland, everyone prohibited the import of Indian cloth or imposed heavy import duties on them. India's goods were so excellent and were in demand in almost all countries of Europe that some countries were very unhappy. In the first half of the 18th century, the Whig government eliminated those who bought Indian goods from their competitors (French, Dutch, Dane) and the weavers making goods for the Indian traders who gave so little price, stopped making goods. With the English industrial revolution that came in the last phases of the 18th century, English goods started being made and after the war with Napoleon, a lot of goods started coming here, so this goods were allowed to come into India with little or no import duty. In this way, Indian industry was almost finished.

questions.question_text: In the permanent land system, what was the landlord's share?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004, 2008 Explanation- With the desire for tax reform, Cornwallis divided the obtained tax into revenue areas in 1787 AD. On which one collector was appointed. Their number was reduced from 36 to 23. The name of the revenue board was kept Revenue Board. Its work was to supervise the work of collectors. In 1790 AD, Cornwallis, with the permission of the Board of Directors, made landlords the owner of the land. The condition was that they accept to pay the annual tax to the Company. In the contract amount, 1/11th part was reduced. Landlords were considered owners of the land and in 1790, he made a 10-year system. This system was made permanent in 1793 and landlords and their successors had to pay land tax at this rate forever. 10/11th part of land tax had to be given to the Company and 1/11th part had to be kept by the landlord for his services.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below - Statement (A): European traders introduced the Hundi system in India. Reason (R): Hundi was in practice in Mughal India. Code:

options.A: A and R are both true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History 2003, 2005 Explanation – Hundi was in practice in Mughal India. Large and small trades were done through this medium. In this method, traders did not have any difficulty in taking and bringing money. In the Mughal period, the use of Hundi was also done to send money from one place to another. In this way, in the Mughal period, Hundis also performed the work of modern money order system. Hundi system is prevalent at present.

questions.question_text: Identify those districts of Bengal whose revenue administration was transferred to the East India Company in 1760 and Mir Qasim obtained the Nawabship of Bengal -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – In 1760 AD, a treaty took place between Mir Qasim and the British, in which the British removed Mir Jafar from the throne and made Mir Qasim the ruler, in return for which Mir Qasim handed over the districts of Burdwan, Midnapore, and Chittagong to the British.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below - List-I List-II A. Jonathan Duncan 1. Mahalwari Settlement B. Thomas Munro 2. Permanent Settlement of Bengal C. Cornwallis 3. Ryotwari Settlement D. Holt Mackenzie Code: A B C D 4. Permanent Settlement of Banaras
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History 2003, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl. 2004 Explanation – (A) Jonathan Duncan - Permanent settlement of Banaras (B) Thomas Munro - Ryotwari Settlement (C) Cornwallis - Permanent settlement of Bengal (D) Holt Mackenzie - Mahalwari Settlement

questions.question_text: Which of the following advisors of Lord Cornwallis opposed the proposal of Permanent Settlement?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Bengal's tax system was a problem for the British since 1765 AD and at the time Cornwallis came to India, this problem still existed. At this time, there were many problems regarding the tax system, i.e., from whom should tax be collected, who should be considered the owner of the land, for how many days should the tax be fixed. Regarding the existing problems, John Shore's views were different. John Shore was in favor of accepting only landlords as landowners, but James Grant's views were different from John Shore and Cornwallis. According to him, all land belongs to the government. Regarding the amount of revenue also, James Grant's views were different from John Shore and Cornwallis. Based on the above facts, the proposal for Permanent Settlement was opposed by ‘James Grant’.

questions.question_text: Which of the following countries did not impose a ban or impose heavy duty on the import of Indian cloth?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Among European companies, except for Holland, everyone imposed a ban on the import of Indian cloth or imposed heavy import duty on them. Indian goods were excellent and their demand was in almost all countries of Europe, which made some countries very unhappy. In the first half of the 18th century, the Whig government eliminated those who bought Indian goods from their competitors (French, Dutch, Dane) and the weavers making goods for the Indian traders who gave so little price, stopped making goods. With the English industrial revolution that came in the last phases of the 18th century, English goods started being made and after the war with Napoleon, a lot of goods started coming here, so these goods were allowed to come into India with little or no import duty. In this way, Indian industry was almost finished.

questions.question_text: In which of the following settlements was the landlord as a middleman in collecting land revenue?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Under the Company, three types of agricultural policies were adopted in India - Mahalwari which was in Punjab, Central Province, Western part of United Province, Rajasthan, etc., which was 19% of total British land. Here a different policy was adopted for revenue collection. Since land in this system was collective of the entire village council, all villagers were collectively responsible for payment of tax. There was no role for middlemen here. The second type of agricultural policy was Ryotwari, which was implemented in Madras, Maharashtra, Assam, Burma, etc., and which was 51% of total British land. Since in this system an agreement was made directly with the farmers, the farmers were directly responsible for paying the tax. Permanent settlement was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Banaras division, and Northern Sarkar. Here the work of revenue collection was done by landlords who were middlemen between the ryot and the government.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Ryotwari land settlement in Madras-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– Thomas Munro was the Governor of Madras from 1820 AD to 1827 AD and he implemented the Ryotwari practice by taking one-third of the total produce as the basis of land tax. Munro implemented this system in all other provinces except the areas of permanent land system. Munro's land tax system continued for about 30 years as 30 percent of the total produce, which caused extensive oppression and difficulties for farmers. Ryotwari land system was also implemented in Bombay.

questions.question_text: The drain of wealth for England started after which event?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– The flow of wealth from India was towards England, for which India did not receive sufficient economic, commercial or material results; such wealth was termed 'Drain of Wealth' by Indian national leaders and economists. The flow of wealth from India to England started immediately after the victory at Plassey. In 1765 AD, after the grant of Diwani to the British by Shah Alam II, the drain of wealth increased.

questions.question_text: Who was the first to present a statistical estimate of the average per capita income of India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History 2008, 2010 Explanation– Dadabhai Naoroji presented the statistical estimate of the average per capita income of India for the first time in 1868 AD, while the first scientific estimate was made by V.K.R. Rao. Notable estimates of national income during the British period are– Dadabhai Naoroji (1868), William Digby (1899), Findlay Shirras (1911, 1922, 1931), Shah and Khambata (1921), V.K.R. Rao (1925-29) and (1930-31) and R.C. Desai (1931-40)

questions.question_text: What was the Kammiya system in Bihar and Odisha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008, 2010 Explanation– Kammiya system means the involvement of a lower income group in some work, where only people from one group would remain.
