In states like Bihar and Odisha, it is considered a form of bonded labor. The laborers falling under this work under some high officer or trade.

questions.question_text: Which was the first commercial bank established in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– The first bank in India based on the European method was established in Calcutta in 1770 under the name Bank of Hindustan with the support of foreign capital by Alexander and Company, but this bank soon failed. In 1806, the Bank of Bengal, in 1840, the Bank of Bombay and in 1843 AD, the Bank of Madras were established.

questions.question_text: Who first started the system of giving the right to collect land revenue to the highest bidder?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– Clive first started the system of giving the right to collect land revenue to the highest bidder. In 1772 AD, Warren Hastings auctioned off the right of tax collection to the highest bidder for five years. In 1776, upon the completion of the five-year contract, the one-year system was adopted again and the rights of tax collection were auctioned.

questions.question_text: Who classified British colonialism into three successive phases: Free Trade, Commercial Capitalism, and Financial Imperialism?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation– R.P. Dutt (Rajani Palme Dutt) divided the economic history of colonial India into three phases - Free Trade, Commercial Capitalism, and Financial Imperialism (Capitalism). Karl Marx divided it into four phases - Mercantile Capitalism, Free Trade Capitalism, Industrial Capitalism, and Financial Capitalism.

questions.question_text: Where was the first railway line in India opened from and to?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– Railway lines were being laid in England after 1825 AD. During Dalhousie's time, in 1853 AD, the first railway line was laid in India from Mumbai to Thane (V.T.) and soon, by tying the entire Indian empire in the thread of railway lines, it was united. Strategic lines were built for Indian security and to increase economic exploitation and internal communication systems. The next year, a line was laid from Calcutta to the Raniganj coal region. In this way, some lines were also laid in the Madras Presidency. By 1856 AD, a survey of many lines had been completed throughout the country.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Permanent Settlement?

options.A: It ensured fixed annual land revenue for the government.
options.B: The government became free from settlements made from time to time by proposing Permanent Settlement.
options.C: It created a loyal Zamindar class for the company.
options.D: It protected the interests of the farmers.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The interests of the farmers were not protected in the Permanent Settlement. The interests of the farmers or raiyats were shelved. Due to the Permanent Settlement system, the farmer class became deprived of land ownership.

questions.question_text: During the time of which Governor-General were the telegraph and rail services started in India for the first time?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – For the first time, telegraph and rail services were started in India during the time of Lord Dalhousie (1848-56 AD). On 16 April 1853 AD, the first railway line was started between Bombay and Thane. Lord Dalhousie established the Postal Department. Under this, the telegraph system started in India. The first telegraph line was laid between Calcutta and Agra.

questions.question_text: Who received land ownership through the 1793 AD Permanent Land System?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– In 1793 AD, Lord Cornwallis implemented the Permanent Land Tax System in Bengal and Bihar. Under this, 10/11 parts had to be kept by the company and 1/11 part by the Zamindars. With this settlement, the British made the Zamindars the owners of the land. Before this settlement, the position of the Zamindar was like that of an employee or representative of the government, who helped the government in collecting revenue from the farmers and had the right to receive some share in return, but now after this, the owners of the land were not the government, but the Zamindars who gave fixed annual revenue to the government. This gave two benefits: first, from a political point of view, the British got a class in India that was ready to support the British in every situation. Second, it benefited from an economic point of view.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT a characteristic of the Permanent (Land) Settlement?

options.A: This system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
options.B: There were three parties in this, i.e., government, Zamindar and raiyat.
options.C: Through this system, land revenue was permanently fixed.
options.D: The total amount collected as land revenue was fixed at four crore rupees.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Zamindari system was adopted in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Banaras region of UP, Northern Karnataka and about 19 percent of the total British India land came under this. The Zamindari system was a gift of the British and several economic objectives were inherent in it. This system is also remembered by various other names like Jagirdari, Malguzari, Biswedari, etc. Under this, the demand of the states was fixed forever. In other systems, the land tax was changed after 10 to 40 years. According to the Zamindari system, the Zamindar (who was usually the land tax collector) was accepted as the owner of the land. He could sell, mortgage, or give the land in charity. In this way, there were three parties in it, i.e., government, Zamindar and raiyat. The total amount fixed as land revenue was not 4 crores, but this amount was 2,68,00,000 rupees.

questions.question_text: When did the Indian National Congress accept the 'Drain of Wealth' theory?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The 'Drain of Wealth theory' was accepted in the twelfth session of the Indian National Congress, i.e., the 1896 Calcutta session. This session was presided over by M.A. Sayani.

questions.question_text: Who first talked about the 'Theory of Economic Drain'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Dadabhai Naoroji exposed the exploitative policies of the British Raj and said that this Raj is engaged in looting India day by day, due to which India is becoming a poor country. In his important book 'Indian Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901), he proved his thesis with facts and arguments. In a letter in 1905, he wrote to J.T. Sunderland that "The condition of India is certainly very pathetic. It is being continuously looted. Even in ancient times, looters used to come, but after looting, they used to go back and India would compensate for its loss in a few years, but now it is becoming continuously poorer and poorer. It does not even get a chance to catch its breath from this loot."

questions.question_text: Whose disciples converted the Moplahs of the South Coast to Islam?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The Moplahs of the South Coast were tenants in the Malabar district of Kerala. In the 19th century, Moplah farmers struggled against the Zamindars. In the first phase of the rebellion, the rebels targeted notorious Zamindars and institutions of foreign government like courts, police stations, treasuries, other government offices, and foreign plantation owners. The liberal Zamindars and poor Hindus were hardly ever harassed. Rebel leaders kept traveling from village to village and setting fire to the houses of Zamindars and looting. Some rebel leaders like Muhammad Haji took full care that Hindus should not be harassed. If any rebel leader raised a hand on Hindus, he was punished. Disciples of Abdullah Kharaji had converted the Moplahs of the South Coast to Islam.

questions.question_text: In which of his articles did Dadabhai Naoroji present the 'drain of Indian wealth to England' for the first time?

options.A: The Wants and Means of India

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History 2000, 2002, 2007 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl 2004 Explanation- Dadabhai Naoroji drew people's attention to the drain of wealth from India or economic drain through his articles and books. For the first time, he explained the theory of "drain of Indian wealth to England" in 'England's Debt to India'. Dadabhai Naoroji exposed the exploitative policies of the British Raj and said that this Raj is engaged in looting India day by day, due to which India is becoming a poor country. In his important book (Indian Poverty and Un British Rule in India (1901), On the Commerce of India, The Wants and Means of India, he proved his thesis with facts and arguments. In 1905, in a question, he wrote to J.P. Sunderland that "The condition of India is certainly very pathetic, it is being continuously looted, looters used to come in ancient times also but after looting they used to return and India used to recover its loss in a few years, but now it is becoming poorer and poorer continuously, it does not even get a chance to catch its breath from this loot."

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Permanent Settlement?

options.A: It ensured regular annual land revenue for the government
options.B: The government became free from settlements made from time to time by initiating Permanent Settlement.
options.C: It created a loyal Zamindar class for the company
options.D: It protected the interests of the farmers

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- At the time of the appointment of Lord Cornwallis, he received orders that he should find such a solution for the land tax system in India so that the interests of both the company and the farmers could be protected. His first task was that he completely settled the rent of land and pattas prevalent in Bengal. After a lot of debate, in which Revenue Board Chief John Shore, Archivist James Grant, and Governor-General Cornwallis took part mainly. From this, the following conclusions were drawn - Zamindars were accepted as owners of the land and a 10-year system was made from 1790 AD. This system was made permanent in 1793 AD and Zamindars and their successors had to pay land tax at this rate eternally. 10/11th part of the land revenue had to be given to the company and 1/11th part had to be kept with themselves for their services.

questions.question_text: British industrial policy in India is, in the true sense, _______ policy.
questions.explanation: British industrial policy in India is colonialization of the economy, in which market process is made according to the concept of demand and supply

questions.question_text: Who commented on the utility of railways in British India, "There is no utility of railways in British India, it is like decorating someone else's wife"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Nationalist leaders exposed the truth of this claim of the British government that the railways were not kept in accordance with the industrial needs of India. In this way, there was not an industrial but a commercial revolution from the railways, because through this, the sale of domestic products got a severe blow, not only this, in matters of encouraging steel and machine industry and capital investment (which we call connection between backward and developed areas today), the full benefit went to Britain and not to India. G.V. Joshi has clearly said that 'railways is actually financial aid given by India for British industries'. Tilak commented on this that "This is like spending money on the makeup of someone else's wife."

questions.question_text: By which Act was the civil service recruitment examination ensured to be conducted in India along with England?
questions.explanation: Through the Government of India Act, 1919, it was ensured that the recruitment examination for civil service would be conducted in India along with England. The Indian National Congress, along with its establishment year 1885 AD, emphasized increasing the age for entry into civil services and conducting the civil service entrance examination in India along with England. Subsequently, in 1886 AD, the 'Aitchison Commission' was constituted. This commission recommended increasing the maximum age for appearing in the examination to 23 years, but opposed conducting the examination in India along with England. Again, in 1918 AD, the Montagu-Chelmsford report was presented to improve Indian administration. It was suggested in this report that civil service examinations should be conducted simultaneously in India and England. Finally, under the 'Government of India Act, 1919', it was ensured that civil services would be conducted in India along with England, and for the first time in 1922 AD, the examination was conducted in Allahabad (India) along with England. Later in 1923 AD, the Lee Commission was formed for administrative reforms under the chairmanship of 'Lord Lee' Note - The Secondary Education Selection Board considered (b) as the answer to this question.

questions.question_text: 'Saharanpur Law of 1855' was related to what?
questions.explanation: The Saharanpur Law of 1855 AD was related to revenue. In 1819 AD, Holt Mackenzie initiated the Mahalwari system; this system was effectively implemented in the regions of Central Provinces, United Provinces, and Punjab. 33% of British India's land was included under this. After 1833 AD, the work of collecting up to 66% tax under the Mahalwari system began in North India under the leadership of James Thomason. Later, in the Saharanpur Rules of 1855, this was amended to 50% of revenue and Constitutional Development

questions.question_text: The first Factory Act of 1881 was mainly related to whom? related to?

options.D: Regarding compensation to laborers in case of an accident

questions.explanation: The Factory Act of 1881 was related to Governor General Lord Ripon, whose objective was to protect underage workers and provide arrangements for the security of their health. This Act was implemented in those factories where the number of workers was less than 100. Under the provisions of this Act, prohibiting children under 7 years of age from working, limiting the working hours of children aged 7 to 12 years to 9 hours, and keeping 4 days of leave in a month mandatorily was required 4. Consider the following events and arrange them in correct order: I. Bengal Tenancy Act II. Vernacular Press Act III. Dramatic Performances Act IV. North-Western Provinces and Oudh Act Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes: (a) I, II, IV and III (b) III, II, I and IV (c) II, III, I and IV (d) III, I, II and IV UPPSC GDC 2021 Ans. (b) : The correct chronology is as follows: List-I List-II (i) Dramatic Performances Act - 1876 AD. (ii) Vernacular Press Act - 1878 AD. (iii) Bengal Tenancy Act - 1885 AD. (iv) North-Western Provinces and Oudh Act - 1890 AD.

questions.question_text: Who prepared and presented the first primary education bill in modern India?
questions.explanation: In modern India, the task of preparing and presenting the first primary education bill was done by Indian freedom fighter, thinker, and social worker Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866-1915). These were the disciples of Mahadev Govind Ranade. In 1905 AD, he founded the 'Servants of India Society' so that the youth could be trained for public life. He believed that scientific and technical education is an important requirement for India, through which self-government and the formation and spread of moral ideas could get strength. Mahatma Gandhi considered him his political guru. He was a member of the Indian National Congress; he also presided over the 1905 Banaras session of the Congress. He died in 1915 AD.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below: Assertion (A) : The establishment of Fort William College in 1800 was for the purpose of training clerks and cadets for the East India Company. Reason (R) : The primary objective behind the study of Sanskrit by Sir William Jones was to create a common Hindu law code for the judiciary. In the light of the above statements, select the correct answer from the options given below:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: Wellesley established Fort William College in Calcutta in 1800 AD for the training of civil servants (clerks and cadets). Through this institution, many books were translated into Arabic, Persian, Bengali, Sanskrit, Hindi, Urdu, etc. For the education of the company's employees, Wellesley established an 'Oriental Seminary' under the chairmanship of Gilchrist, which later turned into Fort William College. In India, the main objective behind William Jones' study of Sanskrit was to create a common Hindu legal code for the judiciary. He showed serious interest in the study of other subjects so that he could know about India. With this objective, in 1784, he established the Asiatic Society in Bengal. The first book translated by this society is the Bhagavad Gita. Thus, both statement and reason are true, but are not the correct explanation of each other

questions.question_text: Who founded the 'Bharat Stree Mahamandal' in India to promote women's education?
questions.explanation: Sarala Devi Chaudhurani established 'Bharat Stree Mahamandal' (in Allahabad) in 1910 AD to promote women's education. This was the first women's organization in India, and Sarala Devi is known as a famous feminist woman. Through her, a school 'Bharat Stree Shiksha Sadan' was established for girls in Calcutta. Sarala Devi also worked for the education of women in the villages around Lahore. Margaret Cousins founded the 'All India Women's Conference (in Pune)' in 1927. Cousins talked about improvements in educational activities for women and children and their rights. Through the efforts of Margaret Cousins, Annie Besant, Dorothy Jinarajadasa, and Srimati Ammu Swaminathan, etc., the 'Women's Indian Association (in Madras)' was established in 1917 AD and its first president became Annie Besant. Dorothy Jinarajadasa worked to eliminate child marriage and female illiteracy in India. Srimati Ammu Swaminathan was elected as a member of the Indian Constituent Assembly. On the occasion of International Women's Year in 1975, Srimati Ammu Swaminathan was selected as 'Mother of the Year'

questions.question_text: By which of the following Acts was the "India Council" (India Council) abolished?
questions.explanation: By the Government of India Act-1935, the 15-member India Council established by the Government of India Act, 1858, was abolished. The head of the India Council was the Secretary of State for India, who was a member of the British Parliament. Indian leaders had been demanding to end this for a long time

questions.question_text: The free and compulsory primary education related bill presented by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in the Imperial Legislative Assembly was rejected due to whose influence?
questions.explanation: A bill for free and compulsory education was presented by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in the Imperial Legislative Assembly on 18 March 1910 AD; after this, he presented a similar bill in 1911 also. But due to the influence of George Clarke and other British and landlords, this bill was rejected. Madan Mohan Malaviya and Jinnah had seconded this bill It is noteworthy that in 1906 AD, the princely state of Baroda had started compulsory primary education there.

questions.question_text: Who was of the Orientalist group in the Anglo-Oriental controversy regarding education policy in the General Committee of Public Instruction in 1835?
questions.explanation: Lord Macaulay gave the theory of 'Downward Infiltration theory' to provide education to Indians, which was announced by Lord Auckland, but due to controversy, a committee was formed which had two groups 1. Supporters of Oriental learning – Secretary of the General Committee of Public Instruction H.T. Prinsep and H.H. Wilson were there, according to whom study of Sanskrit and Arabic should be encouraged in India. These people gave importance to the study of science, but the language of science should also be indigenous, which would be easy for the common people. Warren Hastings and Lord Minto also supported Oriental learning. Special Fact 2. Supporters of Western learning – English language should be the medium of education. Leadership of its support was being done by Lord Munro and Elphinstone. Lord Macaulay, who was the legal member of the executive council who was later appointed as the chairman of the Education Committee, rejecting Indian culture and literature, said, "A single shelf of a good European library is worth more than the whole literature of India and Arabia." 2 February 1835, wrote his important memorandum and placed it before the council, which the then Governor General William Bentinck accepted on 7 March, 1835 and made English the medium of education in India.

questions.question_text: According to the Regulating Act, how many judges were there in the Supreme Court (besides the Chief Justice)?
questions.explanation: Under the Regulating Act 1773 AD, a rule for the establishment of a Supreme Court was passed and it was constituted in 1774 AD, in which one Chief Justice and three junior judges were appointed, and at the same time an administrative board was also formed in which four councilors were appointed. Decisions were taken by majority here. The jurisdiction and member count of the court were expanded by the Amendment Act of 1781 AD. The Rajasthan Public Service Commission has considered (d) as the answer to this question in the first answer key

questions.question_text: By which Act was the provision for having a law member for the first time in the Governor General's Council made?
questions.explanation: Under the Charter Act of 1833 AD, Lord Macaulay was appointed as a fourth member in the Governor General's Council, who was appointed as a law member. Under this Act, the Governor General's executive council was given the power to make laws, and at the same time, the councils of Madras and Bombay were given the power to make laws, and the law-making power of Madras and Bombay councils was terminated. Under the chairmanship of Lord Macaulay, the first Law Commission was constituted in India

questions.question_text: Under which Act would India be governed by and in the name of the Crown, acting directly through the Secretary of State?

options.D: Act for the Better Government of India

questions.explanation: By the Government of India Act, 1858, the Company's rule in India ended. The British Parliament and the King's authority were established in India. The name of the Governor General was changed to Viceroy. The Secretary of State for India and his council were established. By ending the Board of Directors, Board of Control, and secret committees, the right to exercise the powers and rights received from them was handed over to the Secretary of State for India. A council was formed with the help of the Secretary of State for India. In which there were 15 members. 8 members were appointed by the British Crown and 7 members by the board of directors

questions.question_text: In which Act did the British Parliament allow the free flow of European missionaries?
questions.explanation: By the Charter Act of 1813, important educational issues were discussed, and strong permission was given for Christian missionaries to come to India for the propagation of the Christian religion. It was said in this Act that all people living in India and those going there were given the right to propagate useful knowledge, religion, and moral upliftment among Indians. In this way, this Act was the first step for the propagation of the Christian religion and Western education in India. But to hide this objective, it was said in the Act that the company's policy was to give Indians the freedom to fully follow their religion

questions.question_text: The abolition of the slavery system happened by which of the following Indian Acts?
questions.explanation: Many reforms happened in the Charter Act of 1833. This Act opened the doors of liberal policies, because before the passing of the 1833 Act, the legal system was in a state of chaos—corruption, fraud, lying, slavery, forced labor were many such inconsistent things. The result of this was that there was complete disorder and mess in criminal law. By this Act, the government was also ordered to improve the condition of slaves and ultimately to end slavery, but it took years for this rule to be formed and finally in 1843 AD, Lord Ellenborough declared this practice illegal under Rule Five and abolished it

questions.question_text: Where was the first Christian mission established in India?
questions.explanation: Christian missionaries active in India in the 19th century strongly opposed the arguments being given in favor of practical education. The missionaries believed that the purpose of education should be to bring improvement in the moral character of people, and moral upliftment is possible only through Christian education. In this perspective, with the help of Scottish Christian missionary William Carey, a Christian mission was established in Serampore, Bengal, India, which came under the control of the Danish East India Company. Until 1813, the East India Company was against missionary activities in India. The company feared that due to the activities of missionaries, discontent would arise among the local people and they would start looking at the presence of the British in India with suspicion. Due to these reasons, because the regions under British control could not open their institutions, the missionaries finally established their mission in Serampore

questions.question_text: Who established the Asiatic Society of Bengal (1783) in Calcutta for the development of education?
questions.explanation: After the establishment of the Asiatic Society, William Jones himself became its president. Through the Asiatic Researches magazine published by this institution, the first real effort was made to bring India's past into the light. Wilkins' Bhagavad Gita is the first translated manuscript, the translation of which was done under the Asiatic Society of Bengal from original Sanskrit to English in November 1784 AD in Pune. To encourage the revival of Indian knowledge, Sir William Jones established the Asiatic Society in Calcutta during the time of Warren Hastings, the objective of which was to promote Indian knowledge along with Western education

questions.question_text: 'A single shelf of a good European library is worth more than the whole literature of India and Arabia.' Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: Macaulay wanted to create such a group among Indians for the propagation of Western education which would be Indian in color and blood but English in thought, interest, and intellect. Macaulay believed that 'A book from a shelf of a good European library is more valuable than the entire literature of India and Arabia.' The 'Downward Infiltration theory' was also made by Macaulay, through which education should be given to the higher class of society, and the effect of education should reach the common people only by filtering down from this class. This theory was first implemented by Auckland as a government policy. Until the 'Wood's Despatch', Indians were educated under this theory

questions.question_text: By which of the following Charter Acts were Christian missionaries allowed to come to India?
questions.explanation: Before 1813 AD, there was a restriction on the arrival of Christian missionaries in India and they were not given permission for religious propagation in India. By the Charter Act of 1813 AD, Christian missionaries were given permission for religious propagation in India, even then they were not given direct government patronage. For this reason, missionaries and priests started propagating their religion through education. After 1854 AD, when the decision was made to provide grants to non-Christian private schools, then Christian missionary schools also started receiving government grants. As the British empire expanded, the activities of these Christian missionaries also increased. The government provided full support and facilities to the missionaries. English education was also declared a means of propagating the Christian religion. The suspicion of conservative Indians increased at that time when girls were also started being given Western education. Christian missionaries used to criticize Hindu-Muslim religions. They appealed to people to adopt the Christian religion. In missionary schools and government schools also, the Bible was studied

questions.question_text: Which document is called the Magna Carta of Indian Education?
questions.explanation: The head of the Board of Control, Charles Wood, presented a comprehensive plan on Indian education on 19 July 1854 AD, which was called Wood's Despatch. In this proposal of 100 paragraphs, thoughts were expressed on the objective, medium, reforms, etc., of education. This declaration is also called the 'Magna Carta of Indian Education'. Its recommendations were as follows 1- The government should make the expansion of Western education its objective. 2- Emphasis was given on providing higher education through the English medium, but along with it, importance was given to the development of indigenous languages. 3- Primary schools should be established for studies through the medium of indigenous languages at the village level. 4- Public education departments were established under a director in each of the five provinces of the company. 5- To encourage private efforts, a system of grant-in-aid was started. 6- Women's education was also supported in this proposal letter. The methods and ideals approved by Wood remained prevalent for almost 50 years. During this period, Indian education was westernized at a fast pace and many institutions were established. Wood's Despatch was mainly related to university-level education.

questions.question_text: Who among the following established a Sanskrit college in Banaras?
questions.explanation: Jonathan Duncan was made the Governor of Banaras Presidency by Lord Cornwallis because he was successful in effectively ending the corruption spread among British officers there. Like Colebrooke, Duncan was also of a studious nature and proficient in Indian languages. The respect he had for Sanskrit is proved by the fact that in 1791 AD, he established a Hindu College in Banaras, which today is known as the Sanskrit University. Jonathan Duncan's tenure in Banaras ended in 1794 AD. Duncan also played an important role in ending the practice of female infanticide

questions.question_text: Who presided over the Indian Education Commission in 1882 AD?
questions.explanation: To review the progress made in the field of education through Wood's declaration letter, the government appointed a commission in 1882 AD under the chairmanship of W.W. Hunter. There were 8 Indian members in this commission. This commission was limited only to reviewing primary and secondary education  Important recommendations of the commission were as follows- 1- The government should pay special attention to the improvement and development of primary education. Education should be made available in the mother tongue at the primary level. 2- There should be a system of two types of education at the high school level, in which emphasis should be given to providing vocational and commercial education, and the other should be literary education so that it helps in admission to the university. 3- Private efforts in the field of education should be encouraged, but primary education should be provided even without it. 4- Adequate arrangements for women's education should be made.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Calcutta?
questions.explanation: By the Regulating Act of 1773 AD, a Supreme Court was established in Bengal in 1774. All the employees of the company were brought under its jurisdiction. The Chief Justice of this court was Sir Elijah Impey. He was born on 13 June 1732 AD in Hammersmith, London. By this Act, besides Impey, three other judges Chambers, Lemaistre, and Hyde were appointed, who are known as judicial officers in India. After leaving India, an impeachment was filed against them, in which after presenting his arguments, he was acquitted and honored with the title of Knight

questions.question_text: Under which of the following Acts was one seat reserved for an Indian in the Governor-General's Executive Council?
questions.explanation: The Indian Council Act, 1909 is also known as the Morley-Minto Reform Act. Under this Act, a provision was made to appoint an Indian member to the Governor General's Executive Council. Satyendra Sinha was appointed as the first Indian member

questions.question_text: Under which government act was Santhal Pargana declared a "Partially Excluded Area", where no legislation of the legislature would be applicable until the Governor notified it through a prior public notification?
questions.explanation: In the Government of India Act of 1935, these areas were kept outside either completely or partially. After Indian independence, the sub-committee of the Constituent Assembly marked them as notified areas. Under this, the areas kept completely outside were recorded in the sixth schedule, and the areas kept partially outside were kept in the fifth schedule. In this way, the tribals of the regions including Odisha, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Jharkhand got the status of special area constitutionally only after their long struggle

questions.question_text: In which year was the Factory Act, in which a demand was made to limit the working hours of children and women, passed?
questions.explanation: The second Factory Act was passed in 1891 AD. At this time, the Governor General of India was Lord Lansdowne. This Act was implemented in places with at least 50 workers. In this Act, children under 9 years of age were forbidden from working. In this, the time limit for children aged 9 to 19 years to work was set at 7 hours, and for women, working from 8 pm to 5 am was forbidden, and a ban was placed on working more than 11 hours by increasing the duration of work

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct option with the help of the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Correct chronology of the following events Sir Charles Wood's Despatch – 1854 AD Sadler Commission – 1917-19 AD Hartog Committee – 1929 AD Sargent Plan – 1944 AD

questions.question_text: Who established the Supreme Court in Calcutta?
questions.explanation: Under the Regulating Act in 1773 AD, the authority to establish a Supreme Court in Calcutta was obtained by the King of England. King George II issued a charter on 26 July 1774 AD and established the Supreme Court in Calcutta. This was a court of record. In this, one Chief Justice and three other judges were appointed. Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey and Chambers, Lemaistre, and Hyde were junior judges. At this time, Warren Hastings was the Governor General of India

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first law member in the Governor General's Council?
questions.explanation: Under the Charter Act of 1833 AD, Lord Macaulay was appointed as a fourth member in the Governor General's Council, who was appointed as a law member. Under this Act, the Governor General's executive council was given the power to make laws, and at the same time, the councils of Madras and Bombay were given the power to make laws, and the law-making power of Madras and Bombay councils was terminated. Under the chairmanship of Lord Macaulay, the first Law Commission was constituted in India

questions.question_text: In British India, by which Act was the provision for recruitment through Indian Civil Service examination made?
questions.explanation: The Act of 1853 implemented the provision for recruitment through Indian Civil Service examination. Before this, all public servants were recruited by the Company's Board of Directors, but the Charter Act of 1853 changed this tradition and made the examination the medium. By this same Act, a functional legislative council was created for the first time

questions.question_text: Who was the chairman of the Indian University Commission constituted in 1902 AD?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon wanted to establish full control of the government over the education system. He believed in the centralization of education; he called a conference of education experts in Shimla in 1901. No Indian was invited to this conference. In this conference, in January 1902 AD, the University Commission was appointed under the chairmanship of the Viceroy's Executive Council's legal member Thomas Raleigh. In this commission, Syed Hussain Bilgrami and Gurudas Banerjee were made members. Based on the recommendations of the Raleigh Commission, the University Act was passed in 1904

questions.question_text: By which Act was the provision for bicameral legislature made in the central legislature of British India?
questions.explanation: The provision for bicameral legislature in the central legislature of British India was made under the Montagu-Chelmsford reform or Government of India Act 1919. According to this Act, a Central Legislative Assembly and another State Council were formed at the center. The number of members in these houses was 145 and 60 respectively. The tenure of the lower house was 3 years and the upper house was kept 5 years. And through this Act, the control of the India Minister over central and provincial administration was reduced

questions.question_text: Who started the Central Hindu College in Varanasi?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant came to India in 1883 AD; she was an Irish woman. The entry of Srimati Annie Besant into Indian politics happened in 1914. She came to India as a member of the Theosophical Society, which later became its president as well. She had established the Central Hindu College in Varanasi in 1898 AD, which later became known as Banaras Hindu University in 1916 AD

questions.question_text: In which year was the first Famine Commission established?
questions.explanation: Due to the famine that occurred between 1876-78, Viceroy Lytton constituted a Famine Commission in 1880 AD under the chairmanship of Sir Richard Strachey. The impact of the 1876-78 famine was mainly in the regions of Madras, Bombay, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab, in which, according to R.C. Dutt, 50 lakh people died. It is noteworthy that in 1866, a famine occurred in Odisha, Madras, Northern Bengal, and Bihar, in which Odisha was most affected. Following this famine, a Famine Committee was constituted under the chairmanship of Sir George Campbell

questions.question_text: In which year was the 'Vernacular Press Act' repealed?
questions.explanation: Through this Act of 1878, the Vernacular Press Act, newspapers in Indian languages were restricted. Surendranath Banerjee called the Vernacular Press Act a 'thunderbolt from the sky'. Lord Lytton, whose tenure was 1876-80, had closed all newspapers and magazines so that the public anger and revolution being run through newspapers in India would not get encouragement. This means the freedom of the press was restricted. Later, Lord Ripon repealed this Act in 1882 AD. The Delhi Subordinate Services Commission has considered (d) as the answer to this question

questions.question_text: 'Minutes on Indian Education' due to which English Education Act, 1835 was formed, was prepared by which of these English scholars?
questions.explanation: The Oriental and Occidental controversy that arose in India during the time of Lord William Bentinck had assumed its acute form. To solve this, on 10 June 1834, Lord Macaulay was inducted into the Governor General's Council as a legal member, and Bentinck believed that Macaulay would settle this controversy. With this thought, Macaulay was appointed as the chairman of the Bengal General Committee of Public Instruction. After that, Macaulay was requested to give legal advice on the controversy going on over one lakh rupees earmarked in the 43rd section of the Company's Act of 1813 which was to be spent on the development of Indian education and science. On this, Macaulay studied deeply and after proving the futility of Indian languages, Macaulay, giving a much higher place to English in comparison to Arabic, Persian, and Sanskrit, wrote a secret note and sent it to the Governor General on 2 February 1835. Bentinck accepted it on 7 March 1835 AD. According to the proposal, the Company government had to develop literature and science education in India through the English language. Along with this, money was to be spent on this in the future. Macaulay, neglecting Indian culture, called it a 'storehouse of superstitions'

questions.question_text: Which Act passed by the British Parliament promoted the revival and development of literature and science in India?
questions.explanation: Charter Act 1813 - Under this Act, the monopoly of the East India Company in all major sectors was abolished. Although the monopoly of tea trade in India and trade with China country remained. The British were allowed to settle in India, missionaries were also allowed to start useful knowledge and religious and moral reforms under a system of licenses, and traders were also allowed to propagate for their legitimate objectives. Provision was also made to provide a sum of one lakh rupees annually for the development of literature and science education in India

questions.question_text: Tell on the basis of the codes given in proper chronological order: i. Hartog Committee ii. Hunter Education Commission iii. Wood's Despatch iv. Sadler University Commission Codes:
questions.explanation: The order is correct Order No. Committee / Commission Year 1. Wood's Despatch/Charles Wood's Despatch 1854 2. Hunter Education Commission 1882 3. Sadler University Commission 1917 4. Hartog Committee 1929

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Act of 1833 is not correct?

options.A: The commercial rights of the company were abolished
options.B: The Governor of Bengal was made the Governor General of India
options.C: Order given to improve the condition of slaves and eventually to end it
options.D: The Governor General in council and the legislative councils of Bombay and Madras were given the power to make laws

questions.explanation: The influence of Macaulay and James Mill is clearly visible in the Act of 1833. The main features of this Act are as follows –  Company's administrative right was extended again for 20 years.  The commercial right of the company was completely abolished, including tea and China.  The Governor of Bengal was made the Governor General of India.  An additional legal member was included in the Governor General's executive council as the fourth member.  Order given to improve the condition of slaves and eventually to end it.  A Law Commission was constituted with the objective of consolidating, codifying, and improving the laws.  The most important section of this Act was 87, by which discrimination in government selection on the basis of caste, color was abolished.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act passed?
questions.explanation: The objective of the Vernacular Newspaper Act of 1878 (Vernacular Press Act) was to establish government control over newspapers in Indian languages and to suppress seditious writings and to punish newspapers for such attempts. This Act was given the title of "Gagging Act". The most despicable aspect of this Act was that 1- Discrimination was made between English and vernacular language newspapers through it. 2- There was no right to appeal in this. Main provisions of this Act were as follows– 1- District magistrates were given the right that with the permission of the local government, they could call the publisher or printer of any Indian language newspaper and ask them to sign a bond. In this bond, it was a provision that these publishers or printers would not publish any such material that would incite discontent against the government or increase mutual animosity among people of different castes, religions, and colors of the empire's subjects. 2- The magistrate's decision would be final and no appeal of any kind would be allowed against it.

questions.question_text: When did the East India Company lose its monopoly on Indian trade completely?
questions.explanation: Through the Act of 1833 AD, the commercial monopoly of the company ended and the company was handed over administrative and political responsibilities Through 1833 - The Governor General of Bengal was made the Governor General of entire India. • In 1834, the first Law Commission with four members was constituted by Lord Macaulay. • The slavery system was declared illegal in India. It was abolished in 1843. Through the 1853 Act - Legislative functions were separated from administrative functions. • Recruitment started to be based on competitive examination instead of nomination. Through the Regulating Act of 1773 - The Governor of Bengal was made the Governor General of all three presidencies (Bengal, Bombay, Madras). • In 1774, establishment of a Supreme Court in Calcutta.

questions.question_text: The establishment of the Supreme Court of Calcutta took place from________.
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of Calcutta was established in 1774 AD through the Regulating Act of 1773 AD, for which Sir Elijah Impey was appointed as Chief Justice. Besides this, other judges were Chambers, Lemaistre, and Hyde

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding 18th-century Kerala: (1) There was a decline in Malayalam literature here. (2) The kings and chieftains of Kerala paid excessive attention to the knowledge of the English language. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: In the 18th century, there was extraordinary progress in Malayalam literature. This happened partly due to the kings and chieftains of Kerala, who were great patrons of Malayalam literature. In this, Martanda Varma and Rama Varma were prominent

questions.question_text: Who was the British Prime Minister at the time of the enactment of the Regulating Act in 1773?
questions.explanation: The British government passed the Regulating Act in 1773 AD to remove corruption and mismanagement prevalent in the company. At this time, the British Prime Minister was Lord North. Under this Act, a Supreme Court was established in Calcutta (1774), in whose jurisdiction Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha were included

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the highest court of India during the British period?
questions.explanation: In 1774 AD, a Supreme Court was established in Calcutta. Sir Elijah Impey was made Chief Justice and three others, Chambers, Lemaistre, and Hyde were made judges. This was a court of record; appeals against it were made in the Privy Council. In this way, the highest court of India during the British rule was the Privy Council

questions.question_text: Who among the following influenced Jahangir to issue a farman for the establishment of a factory by the British in Surat in 1613?

options.A: Coordination between the British and the Portuguese
options.B: A secret naval aid to oust the Portuguese by the Mughal emperors
options.D: Victory of the British naval squadron over the Portuguese

questions.explanation: Through a royal farman issued on 6 February 1613 AD (by Jahangir), the British received permission to establish a commercial house in Surat and keep an ambassador in the Mughal court. Jahangir did this because he was influenced by the victory of the British naval squadron over the Portuguese. The British commercial house was established in Surat under Thomas Aldworth

questions.question_text: In which year was the Asiatic Society established in Calcutta?
questions.explanation: The Asiatic Society was established in Calcutta by Sir William Jones on 15 January 1784. Its objective was to translate India's Vedas, Puranas, and religious texts into English. Through this institution, in 1784 AD, Wilkins translated the Bhagavad Gita and in 1789 AD, William Jones translated Abhigyan Shakuntalam into the English language

questions.question_text: By which Act was the Law Commission constituted to codify Indian law?
questions.explanation: The Indian Law Commission is neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body. It is an executive body constituted by the order of the Government of India. Under the Charter Act of 1833, the first Law Commission was constituted in 1834 under the chairmanship of Lord Macaulay, which recommended codifying the Penal Code and Criminal Procedure Code. After independence, the first Law Commission was constituted in 1955 AD and its chairman was M.C. Setalvad

questions.question_text: Under which Act was the appointment of Indian members made for the first time in the Governor General's Executive Council?
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Council Act, 1909, Indian members were included in the India Council (England) and the Viceroy's Executive Council (India) for the first time. Two Indians, K.G. Gupta and Syed Hussain Bilgrami, were appointed to the India Council located in England. While S.P. Sinha was included in the Viceroy's Executive Council as a legal member, who was later adorned with the title of Lord

questions.question_text: Match the following: Officer Land Revenue System A. Thomas Law 1. Permanent Settlement B. Alexander Read 2. Ryotwari Settlement C. H.E. Goldsmid 3. Mahalwari Settlement D. Holt Mackenzie 4. Bombay Plan A B C D
questions.explanation: Officer Land Revenue System A. Thomas Law (1756-1834) 1. Played an important role in the Permanent Settlement implemented by Cornwallis. Permanent Settlement was implemented on 19% of the land area of British India. B. Alexander Read 2. Thomas Munro and Alexander Read were the proponents of the Ryotwari settlement. This system was implemented on 51% of the land area of British India. C. H.E. Goldsmid 4. Bombay Plan D. Holt Mackenzie 3. Holt Mackenzie first presented the proposal for the Mahalwari settlement in the year 1819. This system was implemented on 30% of the land area of British India.

questions.question_text: When was the phrase declaring the Governor-General 'the servant of the servants' removed from the official seal?

questions.question_text: Under which Act was the first examination for I.C.S. organized in Allahabad?
questions.explanation: A legislation passed by the Parliament of the United Kingdom, which is known as 'Montagu-Chelmsford reform' because at the time of the passing of this Act, Montagu was the Secretary of State for India and Chelmsford was the Viceroy. It is also called the Government of India Act 1919. The main feature of this Act is 'progress of responsible government'. Other features of the Government of India Act 1919 are as follows- (I) The first examination for I.C.S. was organized in Allahabad. (II) Beginning of the dyarchy governance system in provinces. (III) A public service commission was constituted. (IV) Establishment of bicameral legislature at the center

questions.question_text: Who among the following passed the 'Calcutta Corporation Act' in 1899?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon was the architect of the Bengal partition. After becoming Viceroy, Lord Curzon passed the Calcutta Corporation Act in 1899 AD. The Bengal partition of 1905 became effective. Bengal partition was repealed in 1911 AD. Bengal partition was repealed on the arrival of British Emperor George V and Queen Mary

questions.question_text: Under which Act was it provided that the Governor General of Bengal would be the Governor General of entire India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Through the Charter Act 1833, the administration of India was centralized. The Governor General of Bengal was now made the Governor General of India. The Governor General in Council was entrusted with the control, inspection, and direction of the company's military and civil activities in India.

questions.question_text: When did the Governor General receive the additional title of Viceroy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – In the year 1858 AD, the Governor General was granted the additional title of Viceroy. Due to the activities of the company not being right, to make the administration stronger, the Act 1858 was implemented in India. Lord Canning was the last Governor General appointed under the Company's rule and the first Viceroy appointed under the British Crown.

questions.question_text: When was parliamentary control established over the East India Company?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Parliamentary control over the East India Company was established in 1773 AD. In 1772 AD, British Prime Minister Lord North, on one hand, provided economic assistance by giving a loan to the company, and on the other hand, established a committee of inquiry to establish parliamentary control over its governance. Based on the report of this committee of inquiry, that Act was passed, which we call the Regulating Act and which can be called the first important milestone of constitutional history, the 1773 Regulating Act established a supreme governance in India for the first time. The Governor of Bengal was appointed as the Governor General of the entire state of the company in India, and a four-member executive was appointed to assist him.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the Governor General's Council given in the Regulating Act?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The Regulating Act was passed in 1773 AD. According to this, the burden of governance in India was placed on the Governor General and his 4-member council. Although the chairman of this council was the Governor General, decisions had to be taken by majority. The Governor General could use his casting vote only in the event of a tie, which could be very less in a 5-member council. There were 5 members in this council - Hastings, Barwell, Clavering, Francis, and Monson. Among these above-mentioned members, Francis was the most ambitious and capable. Among the options given in the question, Lemaistre was not included.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the Governor General's Council mentioned in the Regulating Act, 1773?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The Regulating Act was passed in 1773 AD. According to this, the burden of governance in India was placed on the Governor General and his 4-member council. Although the chairman of this council was the Governor General, decisions were taken by majority. The names of these five members were given in the Act. Among these, Hastings and Barwell were already in India. The remaining Clavering, Francis, and Monson reached India from England in October 1774.

questions.question_text: When did Lord Curzon pass the Indian University Act?
questions.explanation: Based on the recommendation of the Raleigh Commission constituted in 1902, Lord Curzon passed the Indian University Act in 1904. He also paid attention to the search and conservation of archaeological sites. He had also restored many ancient sites

questions.question_text: By which Act was Provincial Autonomy established?
questions.explanation: By the Government of India Act 1935, the dyarchy governance in provinces was abolished and dyarchy governance was implemented at the center

questions.question_text: According to which Act did the power pass from the hands of the East India Company and convert into the British royal territory?
questions.explanation: Under the Government of India Act of 1858, the power went from the hands of the company to the British throne, after which the Governor General of India started being called Viceroy

questions.question_text: Which descending Act closed the East India Company's trade with China?
questions.explanation: Under the Charter Act 1833, the East India Company's trade with China closed. Under the 1833 Act, the commercial rights of the company were abolished and the company only had to perform administrative and political tasks in the future

questions.question_text: By which Act was an All India Federation and provincial autonomy system established?
questions.explanation: By the Government of India Act 1935, the Federation was created by combining British Indian provinces and some Indian princely states that wanted to join the federation. Provinces were granted autonomy and the right to make laws was given to the provinces

questions.question_text: To correct the defects of which, was Pitt's India Act accepted?

options.B: Madras treaty made with Hyder Ali
options.D: Subsidiary alliance of Bassein made with Peshwa

questions.explanation: To remove the shortcomings of the Regulating Act 1773, the British government brought Pitt's India Act in 1784. It was named after British Prime Minister William Pitt

questions.question_text: Who started the Sanskrit University in Varanasi in the 18th century?
questions.explanation: In 1791, Jonathan Duncan established the Sanskrit College in Banaras. In 1958, this college became a university and then in 1974, its name was changed to Sampurnanand Sanskrit University

questions.question_text: Who was the chairman of the Indian Education Commission 1882?
questions.explanation: In 1882 AD, an Education Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of Hunter in which there were 8 members. This commission was asked to review primary and secondary education. It recommended giving education in mother tongue at primary level, making adequate arrangements for women's education, and giving vocational and literary education

questions.question_text: Fort William College was established by_______.
questions.explanation: Fort William College was established in Calcutta by Lord Wellesley on 10 July 1800 AD. Its objective was to train civil service officers in language and culture, but due to opposition from the home government of Britain, it was closed. Originally, this institution was established as a research and publication unit

questions.question_text: Who was the first Indian to enter the field of civil service in 1863?
questions.explanation: The first Indian to be selected in civil service in 1863 AD was Satyendranath Tagore. He was the elder brother of Rabindranath Tagore

questions.question_text: When was the Royal Indian Navy established________?
questions.explanation: The Royal Indian Navy was established on 8 September 1934. Its headquarters is in Mumbai. Its former name was 'Bombay Marine'

questions.question_text: In which year was the maximum age for the civil service examination made 19 years?
questions.explanation: In 1878 AD, the civil service age was reduced from 21 years to 19 years. In 1860 AD, their age was reduced from 23 years to 22 years. In 1866 AD, the age of civil servants was reduced from 22 years to 21 years. In 1878-79, Lord Lytton presented a scheme for Statutory Civil Service. Under the statutory civil service scheme, the age of the examinee was reduced from 21 years to 19 years

questions.question_text: Who called Lord Ripon the 'Savior of India'?
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale, seeing Ripon's liberal actions, gave Ripon the title of Savior of India. She considered Ripon's period as the beginning of a golden age in India. She remembers him by the name of Gentleman Ripon

questions.question_text: When did Indian universities start teaching work?
questions.explanation: The Indian University Act 1904 was passed by Lord Curzon, through which teaching work started in universities. Through this Act, the number of fellows of the university should not be less than 50 or more than 100, and these fellows should not be life-long but only for 6 years

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book named "The Praise of Folly"?
questions.explanation: "The Praise of Folly", whose Hindi translation is "Praise of Folly", is an essay written in Latin by Erasmus in Rotterdam in 1509 AD, which was first printed in June 1511

questions.question_text: During the anti-partition movement, the 'Carlyle Circular' was related to
questions.explanation: In the 1905 Swadeshi movement, Indian students opposed Western education. The then Chief Secretary of Bengal, Carlyle, sent the 'Carlyle Circular' on 22 October 1905. Under this, people involved in any opposition could not get admission to government educational institutions

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'The Economic History of India'?
questions.explanation: The first book on the economic history of India was written by R. C. Dutt

questions.question_text: By which charter Act did the East India Company's trade with China and tea-trade monopoly remain?
questions.explanation: By the Charter Act of 1813, the monopoly of the company over Indian trade was abolished, although its monopoly over China trade and tea trade remained. Under this Act, one lakh rupees per year was kept for the encouragement of learned Indians and for the improvement and revival of literature. Christian missionaries received permission for religious propagation in India. By this Act, the right of the company's control over Indian territories and revenue was extended for 20 years

questions.question_text: In which year was the Indian University Act passed?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905. He established a University Commission in 1902 AD under the chairmanship of Sir Thomas Raleigh, in which Syed Hussain Bilgrami and Justice Gurudas Banerjee were included as Indian members. Based on the recommendation of this commission, the Indian University Act, 1904 was passed for higher education. In this, an arrangement of 5 lakh rupees per year was made for 5 years for university reforms

questions.question_text: Which of the following commissions was not related to the development of education in India?
questions.explanation: According to the question, the Simon Commission was not related to the development of education in India. This commission was made to determine the limits of the principle of responsible government in India. Among the remaining options, Hunter Commission in 1882-83 AD under the chairmanship of W.W. Hunter, Sadler Commission in 1917-19 AD under the leadership of Dr. Sadler, and Kothari Commission in 1964-66 AD were constituted under the chairmanship of Dr. Daulat Singh Kothari

questions.question_text: From which of the following Acts was the Imperial Legislative Council constituted in colonial India?
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Council Act 1861, the Viceroy's executive council was expanded. A fifth member was included in this, who was a jurist. Under this Act, the Imperial Legislative Council was constituted in colonial India. The establishment of Bombay, Madras, and Calcutta High Courts was done in 1862 under the "Indian High Court Act 1861" passed by the British Parliament

questions.question_text: Match the authors of List-I with their books given in List-II. List-I List-II A. R.P. Dutt 1. Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India B. Jadunath Sarkar 2. History of the Freedom Movement in India C. Tara Chand 3. The Fall of the Mughal Empire D. Bipan Chandra 4. India Today A B C D

questions.question_text: Which of the following Acts were passed by the Company government in 1856? 1. Hindu Widow Remarriage Act 2. Religious Disabilities Act 3. General Service Enlistment Act 4. Consent Age Act
questions.explanation: In 1856 AD, the company government passed the following Acts 1. Hindu Widow Remarriage Act - 1856 AD. 2. Religious Disabilities Act - 1856 AD. 3. General Service Enlistment Act - 1856 AD. The Age of Consent Act was passed in 1891 AD. In this Act, a ban was placed on the marriage of girls under 12 years of age. This Act was passed during the rule of Lord Lansdowne.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below: A is a statement and R is a reason: (A) On 20 August 1917, Montagu announced, "The British objective is the gradual development of responsible government in India." (R) Montagu announcement was the cumulative result of the Home Rule Movement and the First World War. In the context of the above statement, select the correct answer:

options.A: A and R both are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: A and R both are true and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true and R is false.
options.D: R is true and A is false.

questions.explanation: Due to the discontent arising from the policy of the voting system based on communal grounds of the Indian Council Act, 1909, the settlement between Congress and Muslim League in 1916 AD, awakening among Indians due to the Home Rule Movement, national consciousness, and the expectation of Indian support in the First World War, the then Secretary of State for India Lord Montagu announced the proposed reforms of the British government on 20 August 1917, in which for the first time the matter of providing the status of free dominion (self-government) to India was talked about. Montagu while announcing said that "The British government's objective is the gradual development of responsible government in India." As a result of this, the Government of India Act 1919 was passed

questions.question_text: In which year was the "Reform Enquiry Committee" appointed?
questions.explanation: To fulfill the demands of Indian leaders and keeping in mind the proposals accepted by the Swaraj Party, the British government constituted a committee in the year 1924 under the chairmanship of Sir Alexander Muddiman, which is known as the Muddiman Committee or Reform Enquiry Committee. Apart from British representatives, four Indian members were also there in this committee - Sir Sivaswami Iyer, Dr. R.P. Paranjape, Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, and Mohammad Ali Jinnah. The main task of this committee was to review the functioning of the constitution and dyarchy governance system established in 1921 under the Indian Council Act 1919. This committee presented its report in the year 1925

questions.question_text: Sindh was separated from Bombay province:
questions.explanation: By the Government of India Act, 1935, Sindh was separated from Bombay province. Apart from this, Burma was separated from India and Odisha from Bihar. By this same Act, the formation of legislative assemblies was done in 11 provinces. Bicameral legislative councils were established in 6 provinces, namely Bihar, Bengal, Assam, United Provinces, Bombay, and Madras

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Council Act, 1861: 1. The maximum number of additional members in the Governor General's council was proposed to be twelve. 2. The tenure of additional members was proposed for one year. 3. Additional members were allowed to participate in the council meeting only when a bill was to be passed.
questions.explanation: The Indian Council Act, 1861 provided for 6 to 12 nominated additional members of the Governor General's council, with a two-year tenure. Additional members could participate in council meetings only when a bill was to be passed. Lord Canning nominated the Raja of Banaras and the Maharaja of Patiala to the council.

questions.question_text: Lord Canning nominated the Raja of Banaras and the Maharaja of Patiala to the council.
questions.explanation: The Indian Council Act, 1861 had the following provisions 1. The maximum number of additional members in the Governor General's council was proposed to be 6 to 12, all of whom were to be nominated. Their tenure used to be 2 years. 2. Additional members were allowed to participate in the council meeting only when a bill was to be passed, that is, they had no right to keep control over the executive, and the Governor General had full power to veto their opinion. 3. Lord Canning nominated the Raja of Banaras and the Maharaja of Patiala to the council. 4. Through the Act, the number of members of the central executive was increased from 4 to 5. It was mandatory for the fifth member to be a jurist.

questions.question_text: The main feature of the Indian Council Act, 1892 was:

options.A: Increase in the number of additional members to sixty.
options.B: Additional members were given the right to ask questions on matters of public interest.
options.D: Beginning of direct election for the selection of additional members.

questions.explanation: The main features of the Indian Council Act, 1892 are as follows 1. The number of additional members in the Central Legislature was increased to 16, in which it was necessary for 10 members to be non-official. 2. Indian members of the council were given the right to discuss the budget and ask questions, but no right to vote or ask supplementary questions was given. 3. Indirect election system was implemented in provincial councils.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct about Statutory Civil Service?

options.A: Only Indians were nominated for this service
options.B: The criterion for selection in this service was high social prestige.
options.C: The selected person was posted only in his province.
options.D: Statutory civil service was abolished in 1913.

questions.explanation: In 1878-79, Lord Lytton presented a scheme for Statutory Civil Service. The following things are true regarding this scheme • People with high social prestige were to be nominated for 1/6 of the total posts of administration. • For these posts, the provincial governments would recommend, and after the permission of the Viceroy and the Secretary of State, the candidates would be appointed in the provinces. • This statutory civil service failed and after 8 years, it was closed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Acts is known as the Gagging Act?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton (1876-80 AD) issued the 1878 Vernacular Press Act to restrict Indian newspapers. In this Act, a provision was made that the magistrate would either take a bond from the editors of Indian newspapers that they would not publish objectionable material, or present a certificate for scrutiny before printing. The magistrate's decision would be final and there would be no right to appeal after that. This Act was called the Gagging Act. Surendranath Banerjee called it a 'thunderbolt from the sky'

questions.question_text: "I want different and competitive feelings in different regiments so that if needed, Sikhs can shoot Hindus and Gurkhas can shoot both of them without hesitation." Whose statement is this among the following?
questions.explanation: The statement given in the question is of Charles Wood. Charles Wood issued 'Wood's Declaration Letter' in 1854 for the future education policy of India, which is called the 'Magna Carta of Indian Education', in which a regulatory system of education was formed at the all-India level. Through this declaration letter, primary schools were established at the village level for studies through the medium of indigenous languages and Anglo-Vernacular colleges were opened at the high school level. He wanted to create such a mentality by changing the education policy, so that if needed, there would be no hesitation in standing against each other

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
