The start of this revolution happened on 10 May 1857 AD in Meerut, which gradually spread to places like Kanpur, Bareilly, Jhansi, Delhi, Awadh, etc. After the arrest of Tantia Tope in April 1859 AD, the end of the 1857 rebellion is almost considered to be. The original name of Tantia Tope was Ramchandra Pandurang Rao

questions.question_text: When did Jhansi's 'Jhokan Bagh' massacre take place?
questions.explanation: Jhansi's Jhokan Bagh massacre took place on 8 June 1857 AD. The rebellion of 1857 AD in Jhansi was led by Rani Lakshmibai. The rebellion started in Jhansi on 5 June 1857. Rani Lakshmibai was defeated by Sir Hugh Rose

questions.question_text: During the rebellion of 1857 AD, Veer Kunwar Singh was associated with –
questions.explanation: In the rebellion of 1857 AD, Veer Kunwar Singh was leading the Indians from Jagdishpur (Bihar). Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope from Kanpur, Begum Hazrat Mahal from Lucknow, and Maulvi Ahmadullah from Faizabad led the rebellion

questions.question_text: What was the original name of Nana Saheb?
questions.explanation: The original name of Nana Saheb was Dhondu Pant. He was the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II. Nana Saheb led Kanpur during the rebellion of 1857

questions.question_text: Among the following, which ruler was refused pension by the British before the rebel movement of 1857?
questions.explanation: Nana Saheb, the adopted son of the last Peshwa of Kanpur Baji Rao II, was deprived of both the title and the palace (pension) by the Company. He was forced to leave Pune and live in Kanpur. Upon Lakshmibai's death, Hugh Rose said that "She was the only man in the whole war."

questions.question_text: Arranging the events related to the 1857 rebel movement in chronological order, select the correct option from the given options:
questions.explanation: The chronological order of the above events of the 1857 rebellion is– (b) Soldiers rebel in Aligarh- 11 May 1857 (d) Azamgarh Proclamation- 3 June, 1857 (c) James Outram and Henry Havelock come to Lucknow- 4-5 June 1857 (a) Henry Lawrence is defeated by Maulvi Ahmadullah in the Battle of Chinhat- 30 June, 1857

questions.question_text: 1. Rebellion in Lucknow 2. Promise of namesake leadership of the rebellion by Bahadur Shah 3. Rebellion of soldiers in Mainpuri, Etah 4. Death of the 'Rani' of Jhansi Code: Arrange the following events related to the 1857 revolt in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The chronological order of the above events of the 1857 rebellion is as follows 2. Leadership of rebellion by Bahadur Shah - 11 May 1857 3. Rebellion of soldiers in Mainpuri, Etah - 23 May 1857 1. Rebellion in Lucknow - 4 June 1857 4. Death of the 'Rani' of Jhansi - 18 June 1858

questions.question_text: Who led the sepoy mutiny in Bareilly in 1857?
questions.explanation: Khan Bahadur Khan, the successor of the former ruler of Rohilkhand, declared himself the Emperor of Bareilly. Dissatisfied with the pension fixed by the Company, Khan Bahadur kept the flag of rebellion high for a long time with the help of his 40 thousand soldiers. Tantia Tope in Kanpur and Bakht Khan participated as the commander of the Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah's army

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): Peasant discontent was one of the main reasons for the rebellion of 1857. Reason (R): Almost every peasant family of Awadh was a member of the British army. In the context of the two above statements, which of the following statements is correct?

options.D: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.E: (A) and (R) both are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Political, social, economic, and religious reasons were all responsible for giving birth to the rebellion of 1857. Among them, the discontent of farmers is considered a major reason because the company's land-revenue system made the majority of the aristocratic class poor. At the time of this rebellion, the highest number of soldiers in the British army were from peasant families of Awadh

questions.question_text: Match List-I of leaders of 1857 with their related regions given in List-II. List-I List-II A. Kunwar Singh 1. Faizabad B. Hazrat Mahal 2. Bareilly C. Khan Bahadur 3. Jagdishpur D. Maulvi Ahmadullah 4. Lucknow A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is Kunwar Singh Jagdishpur Hazrat Mahal Lucknow Khan Bahadur Bareilly Maulvi Ahmadullah Faizabad

questions.question_text: Match List-I authors with books written on 1857 given in List-II. List-I List-II A. V.D. Savarkar 1. The First War of Independence B. S.N. Sen 2. The Peasant and the Raj C. Eric Stokes 3. Civil Rebellion and In the Indian Mutinies D. S.B. Chaudhuri 4. Eighteen Fifty-Seven A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is V.D. Savarkar The First War of Independence S.N. Sen Eighteen Fifty-Seven Eric Stokes The Peasant and the Raj S.B. Chaudhuri Civil Rebellion and In the Indian Mutinies

questions.question_text: During the rebellion of 1857, which of the following estate owners helped Tantia Tope?
questions.explanation: During the rebellion of 1857, the estate owner of Salumbar, Kesar Singh, also helped Tantia Tope. Apart from them, Rajasthan's Bhil soldiers, the army of the Nawab of Tonk under the leadership of Mir Alam, and Prince Firoz Shah also helped Tantia Tope

questions.question_text: The regiment that rebelled in Nasirabad was:
questions.explanation: The start of the 1857 rebellion in Rajasthan happened from Nasirabad. On 28 May 1857 AD, the soldiers of the 15th Native Infantry of Nasirabad rebelled. At the time of the 1857 AD rebellion, 6 military cantonments in Rajasthan were situated in Nasirabad, Neemuch, Deoli (Tonk), Beawar (Ajmer), Erinpura (Pali), and Kherwara (Udaipur)

questions.question_text: During the rebellion of 1857, where were Major Burton and his two sons killed?
questions.explanation: On 15 October, 1857 AD in Kota, under the leadership of Mehrab Khan and Jai Dayal, the British army was badly defeated and on the indication of the Kota ruler, killed the British Resident Major Burton posted in Kota, his two sons, and one doctor soldier. On 30 March 1858 AD, General Roberts suppressed their rebellion

questions.question_text: Among the following, who considers the rebellion of 1857 as only 'Sepoy's Mutiny'?
questions.explanation: John William Kaye was a British military historian, civil servant, and army officer. On the major works done by him on military history, the book 'The History of Sepoy War in India 1857-58' was written in India. In 1844, he started the Calcutta Review and in 1856 he entered the civil service of the East India Company. He considered the rebellion of 1857 as only 'Sepoy's Mutiny'. He also edited many works related to Indian affairs, wrote essays of an optimist (London 1870), and contributed continuously for the Awadhis

questions.question_text: Which tribe of Palamu (Ranchi) did not participate in the rebellion of 1857 among the following?
questions.explanation: Many armed struggles broke out against the British in Palamu at the time of the 1857 revolution. In the rebellion of Palamu, not only common people but also kings, landlords, and zamindars participated. This struggle continued till 1858. The major tribes of Jharkhand, Munda and Oraon, did not participate in this rebellion (1857), whereas people of Chero, Bhogta, and Kharwar tribes participated openly

questions.question_text: Who was the Mughal ruler at the time of the 1857 rebellion?
questions.explanation: At the time of the 1857 rebellion, the Mughal Emperor was Bahadur Shah Zafar, who was only a namesake leader in this rebellion in Delhi. But the real leadership was done by his commander Bakht Khan. At this time, the Governor General of India was Lord Canning

questions.question_text: Who considers the 1857 rebellion as 'spark of national movement'?
questions.explanation: Puran Chandra Joshi has interpreted this rebellion from a Marxist perspective. In his book "Rebellion 1857 A Symposium", he has analyzed it in detail and said that 'This rebellion was the spark of national movement or a revolution spread to the national and common people.'

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below: List-I (Author) List-II (Book)
questions.explanation: List-I (Author) | List-II (Book) (a) John William Kaye | A History of the Sepoy War in India (b) G.B. Malleson | Indian Mutiny in 1857 (c) Edward J. Thompson | The Other Side of the Medal (d) Sir George MacMunn | The Indian Mutiny in Perspective

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II. Show the correct answer with the help of the code. List-I List-II
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Correct match is as follows– A. Bakht Khan – Bareilly B. Maulvi Ahmadullah – Faizabad C. Kunwar Singh – Jagdishpur D. Hazrat Mahal – Lucknow

questions.question_text: The main reason for the participation of farmers in the rebellion of 1857 was–

options.B: Revenue policy not only ruined farmers but also the nobility of the country
options.C: Beneficiaries of the new revenue policy were also not satisfied

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– The main reason for the participation of farmers in the rebellion of 1857 was the policy of economic exploitation by the British. This exploitation was done by new inventions of land-revenue systems, increase in taxes, and destroying small-scale industries. Due to drought, flood, etc., if crops were not produced, one had to pay revenue by borrowing from moneylenders. On failure to repay the loan, moneylenders used to capture land. Apart from this, there were many reasons that encouraged farmers to participate in the rebellion of 1857.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT a reason for the Indian rebellion of 1857 AD?

options.A: Indian soldiers had to work in India and abroad.
options.C: Great inequality between Indian and British soldiers.
options.D: The desire of all Indians to get rid of the colonial era.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The main reason for the rebellion of 1857 was the use of cow fat greased cartridges in Enfield rifles. Which Indian soldiers considered against their religion. Indian soldiers also linked serving military duty in other countries after crossing the sea with religion.

questions.question_text: Who preached Jihad against the British in 1857?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 PGT History, 2013 UPPCS Indian History 2006 Explanation– Maulvi Ahmadullah was originally a resident of Arcot district of Tamil Nadu and had settled in Faizabad. Calling upon all religious followers of India, he said, "Stand against the infidel British and drive them out of India." Fearing his activities, the British announced a reward of 50,000 rupees to catch him. On 5 June, 1858, he was killed on the Awadh-Rohilkhand border.

questions.question_text: The place where the rebellion of 1857 was equally promoted by Maulvis and Pandits –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – Due to the social, political, economic, and religious policies of the British, rebellions happened against them in India in 1857. During this rebellion, it was equally promoted by Maulvis and Pandits in Bihar.

questions.question_text: Who led the rebellion of 1857 in Kanpur–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – Kanpur went out of the hands of the British on 5 June, 1857. Nana Saheb was declared Peshwa. General Sir Hugh Wheeler, who was the commander of the Kanpur cantonment, surrendered on 27 June. During this time, Nana Saheb received the help of Tantia Tope.

questions.question_text: Who led the rebellion of 1857 in Allahabad (Prayag)?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – The rebellion of 1857 in Allahabad was led by Liaquat Ali. This rebellion started in the month of June in 1857. In this rebellion, the district subedar was declared as Liaquat Ali. Colonel Neil finally suppressed the rebellion of Allahabad and ended it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements sheds light on the nature and character of the revolution of 1857 AD in a more logical manner –

options.A: It was just a conspiracy of Muslims to exploit the anger of Hindus
options.B: It was a war fought for national independence
options.C: It was just discipline and anger against British officers, which was expressed by Indian soldiers
options.D: It was a final attempt by the rising middle class, so that they could regain old glory

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Different opinions have been expressed regarding the nature of the rebellion of 1857. British historians, who were biased towards the empire, have given it the name of just a military rebellion, while the main nationalist historian V.D. Savarkar has given it the name of a war fought for independence.

questions.question_text: During the rebellion of 1857, what was the main reason for the discontent of religious leaders–

options.B: Attempt to reform the Indian social system
options.C: Collecting tax by the company government even from land attached to temples-mosques (Muafi / Khalsa)
options.D: Not getting entry for Maulvis-Pandits like Christian missionaries in the army

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The main reason for the discontent of religious leaders during the rebellion of 1857 was - the increasing activities of Christian missionaries. Through the Charter Act of 1813, Christian missionaries were allowed to propagate religion in India.

questions.question_text: When did Babu Kunwar Singh fight his last battle against the British?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation– Babu Kunwar Singh fought his last battle against the British on 23 April, 1858. He was a resident of Jagdishpur of Shahabad district. He defeated the British army in this war.

questions.question_text: About the thought of Dr. R.C. Majumdar regarding the rebellion of 1857, there was severe criticism of his views:

options.B: It was a rebellion of the people
options.C: The attitude of the common people towards the British was sympathetic
options.D: It was against the Christian religion

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Regarding the rebellion of 1857, Dr. R.C. Majumdar expressed this thought that "The attitude of the common people towards the British was sympathetic", which was severely criticized.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of books and authors is NOT true–

options.A: V.D. Savarkar – The First War of Indian Independence
options.C: Ashok Mehta-Civil Rebellion in Indian Mutiny

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Regarding the rebellion of 1857 AD, Ashok Mehta wrote the book named The Great Rebellion. The author of Civil Rebellion in Indian Mutiny 1857-59 is Shashi Bhushan Chaudhuri.

questions.question_text: Consider the centers of the rebellion of 1857 and their leaders and match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer in the code– List-I List-II
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– At the time of the rebellion of 1857 leadership, Nana Saheb-Kanpur, Nawab Hamid Ali Khan-Delhi, Maulvi Ahmadullah-Awadh, Maniram Dewan-Assam.

questions.question_text: Who led the rebellion of 1857 in Lucknow?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– In 1857, the rebellion in Lucknow was led by Birjis Qadir. Wajid Ali Shah was the last Nawab of Awadh. Birjis Qadir was the son of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. His mother Begum Hazrat Mahal seated him on the throne under her guardianship and led the rebellion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following provinces was called the 'nursery of soldiers' in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– Awadh province is called the nursery of soldiers because most soldiers in the Anglo-Indian army were recruited from this province.

questions.question_text: Where did the first military rebellion of Indian soldiers serving in the British army take place?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– The 1806 AD Vellore rebellion took place in the city of Vellore in Madras state. Some Indian soldiers rebelled due to the British interference in their social-religious customs. It was the first military rebellion on a large scale by Indian soldiers against the East India Company.

questions.question_text: At the time of the rebellion of 1857, the leadership of the rebels in Jagdishpur was provided by–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 L.T. Grade Exam. 2018 Explanation– At the time of the rebellion of 1857, the leadership of the rebels in Jagdishpur was provided by Kunwar Singh. Angry with this attitude of his, the British captured all his property. Even after repeated appeals from his side, the British were not affected. Although he had not prepared any kind of plan for the rebellion. Finally, due to this kind of behavior of the British, as soon as the squad of rebel soldiers reached Arrah from Dinapore, Kunwar Singh joined them.

questions.question_text: After the rebellion of 1857, the British?

options.A: Stopped the recruitment of Marathas in the army

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – After the rebellion of 1857, the 'British Crown' took back all rights to rule India from the East India Company and made many declarations directly under its own, which are as follows – restriction on the expansion of the British empire in India, not to interfere in the religious matters of the people, equal legal protection for all, expressing respect for the ancient rights and customs of the people, etc.

questions.question_text: In which place did Begum Hazrat Mahal lead the rebellion in the revolution of 1857?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – In the revolution of 1857, on 30 May, 1857, the soldiers had rebelled in Lucknow also. On 4 June, 1857, declaring her minor son Birjis Qadir as the Nawab, Begum Hazrat Mahal handled the leadership of Lucknow's rebellion.

questions.question_text: Who was the Prime Minister of Britain at the time of the 1857 rebellion?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation- At the time of the rebellion of 1857, the Prime Minister of Britain was Viscount Palmerston. His tenure was till 1855-1858 AD.

questions.question_text: The reason for the failure of the rebellion of 1857 was

options.A: The rebellion being in a limited area
options.B: People not participating in the rebellion

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – There were many reasons for the failure of the rebellion of 1857, in which prominent were – unity, lack of skilled leadership, organization, and resources. Regarding this rebellion, John Lawrence said – "If there had been even one capable leader among them (rebels), we would have lost forever."

questions.question_text: Which contemporary British Member of Parliament called the 1857 rebellion a 'National Revolt'?
questions.explanation: Ashram Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– At the time of the 1857 rebellion, Lord Canning was the Governor General of India and Britain's Prime Minister was Palmerston and Disraeli was the leader of the opposition. He gave it the name of 'National Revolt'.

questions.question_text: Who was the British commanding officer in Barrackpore at the time of the 1857 mutiny?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- On 29 March, 1857, Mangal Pandey killed his British Adjutant Lieutenant Baugh and killed Major Sergeant Hewsey by shooting him and stabbed Baugh with a sword. Mangal Pandey was a soldier of the 34th Regiment in Barrackpore at that time and was upset due to the grease case due to which he committed these murders. Later, the British broke the 34th Regiment and hanged Mangal Pandey.

questions.question_text: The author of the book "The First Indian War of Independence (1857-1859)" was...............
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- V.D. Savarkar was a great freedom fighter, who called the 1857 revolution a national rebellion. He was also associated with some revolutionary organizations, in which Abhinav Bharat is important. He reached England by sea in 1906 AD and there joined the revolutionary group led by Shyamji Krishna Varma. On the 50th anniversary of the 1857 AD rebellion, Savarkar wrote a book titled "The First Indian War of Independence, 1857". In his book, he considered this rebellion as the first war of independence. In London, he, along with Madan Lal Dhingra, helped in the assassination of Curzon Wyllie. From 1937 to 1942 AD, he remained the President of the Hindu Mahasabha for five consecutive years.

questions.question_text: Who was the Governor General, when the 1857 rebellion happened?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- At the time of the 1857 rebellion, the Governor General of India was Lord Canning. His tenure in India was from 1856 AD to 1858 AD. On 10 May, 1857, the rebellion started formally from Meerut. Soldiers rebelled in Delhi and forced Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah to lead the rebellion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following army commanders was NOT involved in the suppression of the 1857 rebellion?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Neil, Hugh Rose, and Havelock were involved in the suppression of the 1857 rebellion in Kanpur, Jhansi, and Delhi respectively, whereas Nott was not involved in the 1857 rebellion.

questions.question_text: Who was the Commander-in-Chief at the time of the military rebellion (1857) in India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation- At the time of the 1857 rebellion in India, the Commander-in-Chief was George Anson, whereas after the rebellion started, Colin Campbell was made the Commander-in-Chief.

questions.question_text: Who led the rebels of Bareilly in the 1857 revolution?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation- Khan Bahadur Khan led the 1857 rebellion of Rohilkhand (Bareilly). He was appointed to the post of Subedar by Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah II. Later he was captured by the British and hanged.

questions.question_text: Which British among the following did NOT consider the 1857 event a 'Sepoy Mutiny'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- James Outram, W. Taylor did not consider the 1857 rebellion as a military or sepoy rebellion, but a 'Hindu-Muslim conspiracy', whereas Holmes, Charles Ball, and J.W. Kaye considered the 1857 rebellion as a sepoy mutiny.

questions.question_text: What was the new role of Talukdars of Awadh after the rebellion of 1857 AD?

options.B: They organized and fought against the British
options.C: They became supporters of the Congress
options.D: They became deep friends of the British

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– At the time of the 1857 rebellion, the sentiments of most Indians were not against the British. A judge of another Agra court, Raikes, has supported this. After the rebellion of 1857, the Talukdars of Awadh were promised to have their estates returned and their privileges protected by the British. After this, they became supporters of the British and started living their lives as pensioners of the British.

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List I List II
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Correct match- (a) Lakshmibai- Died in battle, (b) Tantia Tope- Arrested and hanged (c) Nana Saheb- Exiled to Nepal (d) Bahadur Shah - Exiled to Rangoon In the rebellion of 1857, Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died at the hands of General Hugh Rose in battle. Tantia Tope was arrested and hanged. Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal and Bahadur Shah, who had led the rebellion of 1857, was exiled to Rangoon.

questions.question_text: In which of the following places was the construction of grease-filled cartridges done?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- In 1856 AD, the Indian government wanted to use the new 'Enfield Rifle' in the army instead of the old guns. Arrangements for their training were made in Dum Dum, Ambala, and Sialkot. The cartridges made for it had to be opened by mouth before being loaded into the rifle. In 1857 AD, news spread in the Bengal army that cow and pig fat has been used in these cartridges. British officers denied this, but the soldiers did not believe. They became convinced that the British were determined to corrupt the religion of both Hindus and Muslims. There was no doubt that the grease cartridges were the main cause of the rebellion.

questions.question_text: Specify the correct order of the start of the 1857 AD rebellion in the following places-
questions.explanation: The rebellion started in Lucknow on 4 June 1857, in Kanpur on 5 June 1857, and then in Allahabad. Therefore, the order is Lucknow, Kanpur, Allahabad.

questions.question_text: Kanpur 2. Lucknow 3. Allahabad Select the correct answer from the code below- Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Within a month of capture in Delhi, the rebellion spread to almost all major centers Kanpur, Lucknow, Banaras, Allahabad, Bareilly, Jagdishpur, and Jhansi. In all these places, there was deep hatred among people against the British. The rebels uprooted the feet of British administration everywhere. Since the rebel soldiers had no leader of their own, they took local landlords, Nawabs, and kings with them and handed over the responsibility of leadership to them. These people had also been quite harassed at the hands of British rule, hence there was dissatisfaction among them and they came with the rebels. This rebellion started in Lucknow on 4 June, 1857 AD and in Kanpur on 5 June 1857 AD. After this, it started in Allahabad.

questions.question_text: Who is the official historian of the First War of Independence of 1857 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Dr. Surendranath Sen is the official historian of the First War of Independence of 1857 AD. The Government of India asked him to write an authorized history on the freedom struggle of 1857 AD. Sen wrote the history related to this movement in his book 1857 that in every revolution, only a minority of citizens participate. This situation was also there at the time of America's freedom struggle and the great revolution of France. Many Americans were supporting the British at that time and in France also, during the revolution, there were many people who were against the revolution or were indifferent to them. The same situation was in India. Most Indians did not participate in this rebellion, rather many helped the British in suppressing that rebellion.

questions.question_text: Among the following freedom fighters of the 1857 AD rebellion, who was given the title of 'Mahak Pari'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- In the rebellion of 1857, Begum Hazrat Mahal took leadership in Lucknow, where there was deep sympathy among the people for the deposed Nawab. Hazrat Mahal's son Birjis Qadir declared himself the Nawab there and established his administration. He appointed Muslims and Hindus to all important posts. Begum Hazrat Mahal was given the title of 'Mahak Pari', whereas Lakshmibai took command of the soldiers in Jhansi. Lord Dalhousie had refused to recognize her adopted son as her successor and under the policy of annexation, took away her state. The Rani knocked on the door of every big officer to get this decision changed, repeated appeals were made but her talk was not heard, so after she took the field in March 1858, Jhansi gave a very big challenge to the British. Capturing it proved to be really very difficult for the British.

questions.question_text: Read the start of the 1857 AD rebellion in the following places- 1. Kanpur 2. Lucknow 3. Allahabad 4. Meerut Find the correct chronological order of the events from the code given below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- It was decided to start the 1857 rebellion on 31 May, 1857 AD, but it started from Meerut on 10 May, 1857 AD. Meerut's rebellion and capture of Delhi was just a beginning. After this, a fast wave of rebellion was moving among soldiers and civilians in the entire North India and some parts of West and Central India. Begum Hazrat Mahal took leadership in Lucknow and started the rebellion on 4 June, 1857. Where the deposed Nawab was declared Nawab and established his own administration. After this, on 5 June, the rebels handed over their command to Nana Saheb, son of the last Maratha Peshwa Baji Rao II in Kanpur. The British had not recognized Nana Saheb as the successor and exiled him from Pune. Hence he was living in Kanpur at that time.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first Indian historian who did NOT consider the 1857 AD mutiny as the first national war of independence?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- According to R.C. Majumdar, we can call the 1857 non-military rebellion a war of independence only if we consider its meaning as a small struggle against the British. But in that situation, the struggle of Pindaris against the British or the struggle of Wahabis against the Sikhs will also have to be accepted as such, while those who consider it in this form will have to see to what extent the rebels of 1857 were motivated by economic or religious goals. With what motivations were the Pindaris or Wahabis motivated and to what extent they were motivated by independent sentiments and patriotism. Apart from isolated examples, no such facts have come to light so far which prove that the main goal of people's rebellion was to get freedom from bondage. In the end, it is proved that this so-called first national war of independence was neither first, nor national, and nor a war of independence.

questions.question_text: Where was the highest number of soldiers who participated in the 1857 struggle?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The 1857 rebellion started from the Bengal army. There was excessive sentiment of unity and brotherhood in the Bengal army. 60 percent of soldiers in the Bengal army came from Awadh and Uttar Pradesh provinces. Thus, the highest number of soldiers in the rebellion were from Awadh. Soldiers of Awadh are called the nursery of soldiers.

questions.question_text: Thakur Kushal Singh, who joined the rebels in 1857 and defeated the British army, was the chief of where?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – In the rebellion of 1857, the rebellion in a place named Auwa in Rajasthan was led by Thakur Kushal Singh.

questions.question_text: Match the following leaders of the First War of Independence and their places and select the correct answer from the code given below : Leader Place A. Begum Hazrat Mahal 1. Lucknow B. Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah 2. Faizabad C. Begum Zeenat Mahal 3. Delhi D. Kunwar Singh 4. Arrah Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Begum Hazrat Mahal- Was the wife of deposed Awadh Nawab Wajid Ali Shah by the British in 1856. She played an unforgettable role by leading the 1857 mutiny in Awadh. She very intelligently ruled in the name of her 11-year-old son Birjis Qadir and reorganized the administrative system. She attacked the Residency in Lucknow. After the fall of Lucknow, she joined Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah in Shahjahanpur but was defeated and escaped to Nepal. Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah : He was originally a resident of Tamil Nadu and had settled in Faizabad. Calling upon all religious followers of India, he said 'Stand against the infidel British and drive them out of India.' Begum Zeenat Mahal : Was the wife of the last Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah. Along with Bahadur Shah, she was also exiled to Rangoon. Kunwar Singh : Was the prominent landlord of Arrah district in Bihar. When he raised the flag of rebellion against the British, he was 80 years old. He died on 26 April, 1858.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book "Indian War of Independence, 1857"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - 'Vir Damodar Savarkar' was a great revolutionary who later became a leader of the 'Hindu Mahasabha'. In 1899 AD, he formed the first revolutionary society 'Mitra Mela', whose name fell to 'Abhinav Bharat Society' (New India Society) in 1904 AD. In 1906 AD, Savarkar reached England by sea and there joined the revolutionary group led by Shyamji Krishna Varma. On the 50th anniversary of the 1857 AD rebellion, Savarkar wrote a book whose title was "Indian War of Independence, 1857". In his book, he considered this rebellion as the First War of Independence. In London, he, along with Madan Lal Dhingra, helped in the assassination of Curzon Wyllie. He remained the President of the Hindu Mahasabha for five consecutive years from 1937 to 1942 AD.

questions.question_text: Read the following events related to the First Indian War of Independence, 1857 and tell their correct chronological order with the help of the code given below : 1. Rebellion in Meerut 2. Rebellion in Lucknow 3. Rebellion in Jhansi 4. Rebellion in Allahabad Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Due to the exploitative policy of the British, dissatisfaction had been prevailing in people's hearts for many years. By 1857 AD, this dissatisfaction reached its peak, to suppress which the British had to use all their political skills. Although the initial spark of this rebellion was seen in Barrackpore on 29 March, 1857. But its real genesis happened on 10 May, 1857 AD when the soldiers rebelled in Meerut. This rebellion started in Lucknow on 4 June, 1857 when Begum Hazrat Mahal took command of the rebellion. This rebellion started in Jhansi on 5 June, 1857 AD, which was led by Rani Lakshmibai. Subsequently, the spark of rebellion spread in Allahabad, which was led by Liaquat Ali. According to the above options, the answer to the question will be Meerut, Lucknow, Jhansi and Allahabad. A-1-2-3-4 will be.

questions.question_text: Which leader of 1857 had a reward of 50,000 on his head?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation– Maulvi Ahmadullah prepared the ground for the famous rebellion against the British. He was originally a resident of Arcot in Tamil Nadu, but had settled in Faizabad. The British were so scared of his activities that the Governor General announced a reward of 50,000 rupees to anyone who caught him. On 5 June, 1858, he was shot dead on the Awadh-Rohilkhand border in Powayan.

questions.question_text: Which of the following books is the official history of the 1857 rebellion?

options.C: The Sepoy Mutiny And The Revolt of 1857

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation– On the occasion of the centenary of this rebellion in 1957 AD, many books were published, in which Surendranath Sen's book "1857" (Eighteen Fifty Seven) was published in 1957 AD from New Delhi. Sen's book was written on the request of the Government of India, it contains a fairly balanced account of events. In this book, Sen argues that although it cannot be called a 'national struggle', calling it a military rebellion would also be wrong because it was not limited to soldiers only. In Awadh, it became a mass movement where patriots fought for their king and state. Despite this, Sen does not consider the rebels of Awadh as the pioneers of freedom because they were completely ignorant of national and individual freedom sentiments. The Government of India appointed famous historian Ramesh Chandra Majumdar to write the history of the 1857-58 AD rebellion but due to differences with the government committee, he refused to do this work and published his book independently whose name was "The Sepoy Mutiny And The Revolt of 1857". Majumdar did not write a chronological history of this rebellion but kept some facts before the public for the purpose of removing misconceptions. The author of 'Theories of Indian Mutiny' was S.B. Chaudhuri. motive of freeing from bondage. In the end, it is proved that this so-called first national war of independence was neither first, nor national, and nor a war of independence.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Enfield rifle introduced in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– In 1856 AD, the government decided to use the new Enfield Rifle, which was better, instead of the old iron-made Brown Bess gun. Training for the use of this new rifle was to be given in Dum-Dum, Ambala, and Sialkot. The upper part of the cartridge had to be bitten by mouth in this rifle. In January 1857, a rumor spread in the Bengal army that there is cow and pig fat in the grease cartridge. Military officers immediately denied this rumor without investigation. Later inquiries proved that "cow and bull fat was actually used in the Woolwich Arsenal." The use of these grease cartridges became the reason for the rebellion.

questions.question_text: From where did Mangal Pandey first learn from a lascar that the cartridges used in Enfield rifles were greased with cow and pig fat?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– Soldiers of Dum-Dum and Berhampore refused to use the cartridges. They were punished by charging them with indiscipline. On 29 March, 1857, soldiers in Barrackpore refused to use these cartridges and one soldier Mangal Pandey, who had come to know about the grease in the cartridge in Barrackpore itself, attacked his Adjutant Baugh and killed him. On 10 May, soldiers openly rebelled and marched towards Delhi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following policies was adopted by the British towards the native states after the rebellion of 1857?

options.A: To merge Indian states into the British Empire.
options.B: To give more powers to Indian states.
options.C: To allow Indian states to make relations with foreign powers.
options.D: To maintain the status quo of Indian states.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– After the rebellion of 1857, the British followed the policy of maintaining the status quo towards the native states. The policy of merging native states into the empire was abandoned. The British clearly understood that the policy of indiscriminate expansion could prove fatal. But at the same time, they also realized that by establishing friendly relations with native states, they could save their empire from the danger arising from the rebellion of the people, but through Residents, their work began to be controlled even more and in the name of bringing modernity, as the means of transport spread. Interference in the activities of these states kept increasing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT a consequence of the 1857 rebellion?

options.A: Rebellion proved to be the final nail in the coffin of the Mughal Empire.
options.B: It wiped out all hopes of the rise of Maratha power.
options.C: It ended the rule of the Company.
options.D: Due to it, the spread of Christian religion happened.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– After this rebellion, the British adopted an attitude of caution in social policy. Many of them thought that the policy of implementing social reforms and the liberal attitude towards Christian missionaries had contributed significantly to creating the sentiment of rebellion. They thought that it was advisable to keep in mind the traditions and prejudices of the people here and their goal should be to maintain peace. Help to schools related to Christian religion was also stopped.

questions.question_text: 'Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind' on the causes of the 1857 rebellion was the first book written by an Indian in the Hindi language. Its creator was–
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was written by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan with the aim of increasing sympathetic behavior among the British rulers towards Muslims.

questions.question_text: At the time of the annexation of Jhansi to the British Empire, which of the following was the British Agent of Jhansi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– At the time of the annexation of Jhansi to the British Empire, the British Agent of Jhansi was Major Ellis. The rebellion started in Jhansi on 4 June, 1857, where the British Agent was Major Ellis. John Lawrence was the Chief Commissioner of Punjab. The end of the Jhansi rebellion took place on 17 June, 1858 with the death of Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi. General Hugh Rose, who defeated her, has said about his formidable enemy, "Here lies that woman, who was the only man among the rebels."

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events related to the 1857 Indian revolution in their correct chronological order with the help of the code given below: 1. Mangal Pandey incident in Barrackpore 2. Soldier-incident in Meerut 3. Rebellion in Jhansi 4. Rebellion in Kanpur Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– On 29 March, 1857, soldier Mangal Pandey sounded the bugle of rebellion against the emotional and anti-people policies of the British in Barrackpore (Calcutta). The soldiers' rebellion in Meerut took place on 10 May, 1857. The rebellion in Jhansi took place on 4 June, 1857, and in Kanpur on 5 June, 1857, in which Nana Saheb was declared Peshwa.

questions.question_text: Which first Indian wrote a book about the causes of 1857 in an Indian language:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The first Indian to write a book about the causes of the 1857 rebellion was Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, who became the bearer of the reaction of Muslim administrative officials in the 1857 rebellion. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote 'An Essay on the causes of Indian of Revolt' immediately after the rebellion, and Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, who wrote at the beginning of the twentieth century, were the first two Indians who expressed their views on this subject. Apart from this, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan composed 'Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind' with the aim of improving the image of his community from the ruler's perspective.

questions.question_text: Leaders of the 1857 rebellion who were caught and hanged:
questions.explanation: In the 1857 rebellion, Tantia Tope was caught and hanged. The main responsibility of fighting on behalf of Nana Saheb in Kanpur was that of Tantia Tope. His original name was Ramchandra Pandurang. Scindia's landlord Man Singh had him captured by the British by treachery in April 1859 AD. He was hanged in Gwalior in 1859 AD

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not associated with 'Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha'?
questions.explanation: The religious and social movement among Parsis started when Dadabhai Naoroji, Naoroji Furdoonji, S.S. Bengalee, R.K. Cama and other leaders formed the 'Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha' in Bombay in 1851 AD. It is noteworthy that Justice Ranade was not associated with this. The objective of the Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha was the revival of the social condition of the Parsis and the attainment of the ancient purity of the Parsi religion. Through this Sabha, emphasis was placed on improving the condition of women, ending the purdah system, and increasing the age of marriage

questions.question_text: By whom was the magazine named 'Satya Prakash' published in support of widow remarriage?
questions.explanation: Karsandas Mulji, a contemporary of Dadabhai Naoroji, was one of the leading Indian social reformers working for women's liberation. In Indian history, Karsandas's place as a reformer is due to the 1862 Maharaj Libel Case, which earned him the title of "a reformer, the Martin Luther of the Bania caste". He worked as the editor of a newspaper. In 1855, he edited 'Satya Prakash' in which he strongly supported widow remarriage

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book 'A Gift to Monotheists' in Persian?
questions.explanation: The reform movement that started in Bengal was led by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. He is called the pioneer of the renaissance, the progenitor of reform movements, the father of modern India, and the morning star of the new era. His first book in the Persian language, 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' (A Gift to Monotheists), was published in 1809 AD, in which he opposed idol worship and described monotheism as the essence of all religions Social-Religious Movement

questions.question_text: Who said "India is for Indians"?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand's childhood name was Mool Shankar. Swami Purnanand gave him the name Dayanand Saraswati in 1848 AD. In 1861 AD, he met the blind Swami Virjanand in Mathura. Dayanand became his disciple. To propagate his religion, he hoisted the 'Pakhand-Khandini Pataka' in Agra and established the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875 AD. In 1877 AD, he made Lahore his headquarters. He gave the slogans "Back to the Vedas" and "India is for Indians"

questions.question_text: In which of the following years was the 'Asiatic Society of Bombay' established?
questions.explanation: The Asiatic Society of Bombay was established by Sir James Mackintosh, who was a prestigious lawyer, jurist, and famous social figure in England, who became the Chief Justice of Bombay. The Asiatic Society of Bombay was initially known as the Literary Society. Its establishment took place on 26 November 1804. Its objective was to promote useful knowledge related to India during that time

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding social-religious movements are correct?
questions.explanation: The religious and social renaissance of the nineteenth century is an important event in modern Indian history. It forced Indians to self-reflect. At this time, the Hindu religion and society were in an inactive and weak state. The lower class of Hindu society started accepting the Christian religion for social respect and economic facilities. Therefore, there was a need for reform to protect society in the Hindu religion. The social-cultural renaissance of India in the nineteenth century occurred during the presence of colonial powers because British writers believe that the beginning of the Indian renaissance was started by them. 'Percival Spear' writes that "Whatever the British did in India, good or bad," their claim is true that they sparked the renaissance in India, not that they completely did the renaissance. It would be completely inappropriate to say that the inspiration for the reformist movement was entirely non-humanitarian, as one aspect of the reform movements was also that they wanted religious and social reforms. Whereas otherworldliness and salvation are considered the roots of Indian culture. Dr. Syed Ahmed's statement, "If religion does not walk according to the demands of time, then it becomes conservative." To prove this point, he wrote a 'commentary' on the Quran and edited a magazine 'Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq' to propagate his ideas

questions.question_text: Who wrote the original work 'Stree-Purush Tulana' in 1882?
questions.explanation: In 1882 AD, 'Tarabai Shinde' wrote 'Stree-Purush Tulana' (A Comparison between Women and Men) in the Marathi language Others – Ramabai Ranade – Ramabai Ranade (1863-1924 AD) was one of the first Indian social workers to fight for the rights of women in the 19th century. She was married to Mahadev Govind Ranade. She founded the Seva Sadan in Pune and the Arya Mahila Samaj for the welfare of women. Ramabai Ranade founded the 'Hindu Ladies Social Club' in Bombay and established the first high school for women in Pune in 1886 AD. Anandibai Joshi – She was a Marathi social-educational worker. She was the wife of Marathi education reformer 'Dhondo Keshav Karve'. Kashibai Kanitkar – She was the first prominent female writer of Marathi in Maharashtra, India, after the 'Saint' poet Kanhopatra of the 15th century. She was married to Govind Vasudev Kanitkar at the age of nine.

questions.question_text: Who started the Rajahmundry Social Reform Association in 1878? (1) Ram Aiyangar (2) Shesha Aiyangar (3) K. Veeresalingam Pantulu (4) Rumbugunadai Raghunath Rao
questions.explanation: In 1878 AD, 'Rajahmundry Social Reform Association' was founded by 'Kandukuri Veeresalingam'. Through his efforts, the first high-caste 'widow remarriage' was organized in Rajahmundry on 11 December 1881. This was the first widow remarriage in Andhra Pradesh

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the book "Gulamgiri"?
questions.explanation: Among the entire literature of social reformer Jyotiba Phule, 'Gulamgiri' is a very important work. This work was published in 1873. Phule has clearly described this in his book

questions.question_text: 'Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha' is associated with whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha was associated with the Parsi reform movement. This organization was founded in 1851 by Naoroji Furdoonji, Dadabhai Naoroji, and S.S. Bengalee. The main objective of this organization was to end the conservatism present in the religious field, encourage women's education, and oppose the purdah system and child marriage. Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha published a magazine named Rast Goftar (Truth-teller).

questions.question_text: Who was the inspiration behind the "Young Bengal" movement?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Young Bengal movement was the Anglo-Indian teacher Henry Vivian Derozio of Hindu College. The main objective of the Young Bengal movement, established in 1828 AD, was to raise a voice for the freedom of the press, protection of ryots from the oppression of landlords, and the appointment of Indians to higher posts in government jobs. Vivian Derozio was greatly influenced by the French Revolution

questions.question_text: Who started the social and religious organization Tattvabodhini Sabha and the magazine Tattvabodhini associated with it?
questions.explanation: UP PGT, 2021 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The main objective of Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Brahmo Samaj was to reform society. There was no such evil in Hindu society that he did not attack. In modern times, the Brahmo Samaj was the first to attack those evils which all social and political leaders have opposed and which the entire educated class looks upon with disdain today. The struggle against the evils which the Indian Constitution has now declared illegal was started by the Brahmo Samaj. To spread his religious and social ideas, the Brahmo Samaj used all the means of modern times. Establishment of various societies, speeches, writings, newspapers, magazines, schools and colleges, etc., all types of religious debates, etc., "Tattvabodhini Sabha", which was formed in 1839, worked like auxiliary societies for the propagation of the ideas of the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.question_text: What was the name of that Act which granted acceptance to Hindu converts to Christianity to obtain their ancestral property as inheritance?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Through the Caste Disabilities Removal Act XXI of 1850 AD, those expelled from the caste (Hindus converted to Christianity) were granted their ancestral property inheritance. The main work of Christian missionaries in India was to convert people. By the end of the 18th century, the state of Hindu religion and society had become very distorted. Religious evils like idol worship, polytheism, false rituals, magic, human sacrifice, animal sacrifice, superstition, casteism, untouchability, misery of women, and Sati practice were present among us. The state of Islam was also not good, especially the high-low discrimination, illiteracy, polygamy, and easy divorce methods were aspects that pricked any sensible person.

questions.question_text: By whom was 'Mirat-ul-Akbar' established?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011, 2010, 2009, 2004 Explanation – The credit for the establishment of the national press in India goes to Raja Ram Mohan Roy. He started the journalism of progressive national tendency newspapers in India by publishing Sambad Kaumudi (1821 AD) and Mirat-ul-Akbar (1822 AD, in Persian language).

questions.question_text: Who established the Academic Association?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– The originator of the Young Bengal movement in Bengal, Henry Vivian Derozio, established the 'Academic Association' for spiritual advancement and social reform.

questions.question_text: Who is called the father of Indian Nationalism?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the father of Indian nationalism, 'bridge between past and future', 'progenitor of Indian nationalism', etc.

questions.question_text: What was the name of the newspaper published by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– Raja Ram Mohan Roy is considered the 'pioneer of journalism'. He published the newspaper 'Sambad Kaumudi' in Bengali language in 1821 AD. It was in Sambad-Kaumudi that he strongly opposed the Sati practice tradition and launched a movement. Because of this society-wide movement, due to the efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Lord William Bentinck made a rule for the abolition of Sati practice in 1829 AD.

questions.question_text: The Age of Consent Act, 1860 AD determined the age of marriage for girls at how much?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Due to the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the Age of Consent Act was passed in 1860 AD. questions.question_text: Who passed the Minor Marriage Protection Act in 1901, which set the marriageable age in the state at 12 for girls and 16 for boys?

questions.question_text: Keep the following institutions in chronological order by their year of establishment.

questions.question_text: On 27 December 1891, the first public meeting of which social-religious reformist movement took place in Qadian, Punjab?
questions.explanation: The Ahmadiyya movement started in 1889 AD from a place named Qadian in Gurdaspur district (Punjab) by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. Arya Samaj and Dev Samaj were Hindu reformist movements, which were started respectively by Swami Dayanand Saraswati (1875) and Shivnarayan Agnihotri (1887). questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Annie Besant of the Madras Theosophical Society said that in ancient times, Hindu women were educated and moved in society with freedom.
options.B: Active Arya Samajists in North India strongly supported women's education.
options.C: The 1882 Hunter Commission report recommended providing more and liberal financial grants for girls' schools than for boys' schools and providing special scholarships and awards for female students.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Deccan Sabha?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Deccan Sabha was Gopal Krishna Gokhale. He was a great social reformer and educationist who provided exemplary leadership to India's freedom movement. For the expansion of Indian education, he founded the Servants of India Society in the year 1905. (Source - P.I.B.)

questions.question_text: In 1883 AD, where was the 'Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha' established?
questions.explanation: In 1883 AD, 'Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha' was established in Calcutta, Bengal. The main objective of the establishment of Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha was to remove the evils that had entered the Hindu religion

questions.question_text: Who was the one who awakened self-respect among the lower castes of South India?
questions.explanation: Kerala's great religious reformer Narayana Guru was the one who awakened self-respect among the lower castes of South India. He gave the famous slogan "One caste, one religion, one God". He consecrated the Shiva idol in Aruvippuram, which was against the caste-based restrictions at that time. Sree Narayana Guru was a multi-faceted talent, great sage, strong proponent of Advaita philosophy, poet, and a great spiritual personality. questions.question_text: In which year was the Atmiya Sabha established?
questions.explanation: The reform movement that started in Bengal was led by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. That is why he is called the pioneer of the renaissance, the progenitor of reform movements, the father of modern India, and the morning star of the new era. Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a polyglot. questions.question_text: Who brought out the newspaper named 'Sambad Kaumudi' in 1821?

questions.question_text: In 1887 AD, where was the 'Deva Samaj' established?
questions.explanation: Deva Samaj was established in Lahore in 1887 AD. Its founder was Shiv Narayan Agnihotri. He was a follower of Brahmo Samaj. He sharply condemned alcohol and meat consumption. questions.question_text: Sati practice was ended in India-

questions.question_text: "Neither should one depend blindly on India's past, nor should the West be blindly imitated. Taking the help of reason, the new India should obtain and preserve the best of both Eastern and Western ideas." Who expressed these views?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the leader of the 19th-century religious movement. He is considered the synthesizer of the ideas of East and West. It is his view that 'Neither should one depend blindly on India's past, nor should the West be blindly imitated. Taking the help of rational wisdom, the new India should obtain and preserve the best of both Eastern and Western ideas.'
