questions.question_text: 'Hicky's Bengal Gazette or The Original Calcutta General Advertiser', the first newspaper printed in Asia, was published in which year?
questions.explanation: 'James Augustus Hicky's Bengal Gazette or The Original Calcutta General Advertiser', printed in India, was the first newspaper printed in Asia which was a weekly paper whose editing started in 1780. The publication of Hicky's Gazette was to make market information available. His second newspaper, India Gazette, came out in 1780 AD. This newspaper mainly printed news of the company's business activities. In 1784 AD, the Calcutta Gazette and in 1785, Bengal Journal were brought out. Madras's first weekly newspaper, Madras Courier, was brought out in 1785, and Bombay Herald used to come out from Bombay in 1789 AD

questions.question_text: Who was the founding president of Prarthana Samaj?
questions.explanation: Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay in 1867 AD due to the inspiration of Keshav Chandra Sen. Its founder was Atmaram Pandurang. In 1869 AD, Mahadev Govind Ranade became a member of Prarthana Samaj. The credit for making this society famous goes to Ranade. He had deep faith in monotheism. He raised his voice against the corruption prevalent in the Hindu religion. He did important work in the direction of social reform in Prarthana Samaj. He opposed child marriage, purdah system, polygamy, and caste system and encouraged women's education and widow remarriage

questions.question_text: Annie Besant – 1. Was responsible for starting the Home Rule Movement. 2. Was the founder of the Theosophical Society. 3. Remained the president of the Indian National Congress once. Select the correct statement/statements using the code given below:
questions.explanation: In 1893 AD, Theosophist woman Annie Besant came to India. After the First World War, she also decided to start a movement in India on the lines of the Irish Home Rule League to provide support to the Indian freedom movement. Annie Besant announced the establishment of the All India Home Rule League in Madras in September 1916. The real meaning of the Home Rule League movement was to make the Indian public aware of the real meaning of home rule, i.e., self-governance, and this was also its objective. Annie Besant was nominated as the president at the thirty-second session of the Congress, which was organized in Calcutta in 1917 AD

questions.question_text: Match the following and select the correct answer from the code given below:
questions.explanation: Correct matching A- Raja Ram Mohan Roy - Atmiya Sabha (1814) B- Debendranath Tagore - Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) C- Swami Vivekananda - Ramakrishna Mission (1897) D- Atmaram Pandurang - Prarthana Samaj (1867)

questions.question_text: Sambad Kaumudi, Bengali, supportive reformist, weekly newspaper, under whose ownership was this among these reformers?
questions.explanation: The publication of Sambad Kaumudi was started in 1821 AD. Its editors were Bhabani Charan Bandyopadhyay and Tarachand Sanchalak. It was a weekly paper which was published in the Bengali language. Its ownership was in the hands of Raja Ram Mohan Roy. In this very newspaper, articles against Sati practice were continuously published

questions.question_text: Who was the editor of 'The Adyar Bulletin' magazine?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant was born on 1 October, 1847. She was a social and spiritual woman. Her arrival in India was in 1893 AD and she remained the president of the Theosophical Society and participated actively in works like campaigning for Indian freedom, women's awareness, etc She edited many newspapers and magazines in India, the main ones are New India, Commonweal, and Adyar Bulletin. And also popularized her own movement, the Home Rule movement, in Indian movements.

questions.question_text: When was the Ramakrishna Mission established?
questions.explanation: In memory of Ramakrishna Paramahansa, his disciple Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 AD in Baranagar (Bengal). In 1899 AD, a monastery was established in Belur which became the central operational place for many monasteries established in India

questions.question_text: By what other name was the social-religious reform movement known?
questions.explanation: The renaissance of the 19th century has a special place in the history of modern India. This renaissance was multi-faceted and comprehensive. This awakening ended India's inertia and provided an intellectual, social mobility. It generated a sense of self-confidence in Indians by awakening the sense of pride in the past and ultimately this gave inspiration to the national movement. Indian youth were deeply influenced by Western education. Raja Ram Mohan Roy is considered the progenitor of the Indian renaissance

questions.question_text: Who established the Theosophical Society?
questions.explanation: The Theosophical Society was established in 1875 by a Russian woman Helena Petrovna Blavatsky and an English military officer Col. H.S. Olcott in America. In 1882 AD, the international headquarters of this society was established near Madras at a place named Adyar. Annie Besant also remained associated with this organization. In the field of social work, this organization opposed child marriage

questions.question_text: Who established the Arya Samaj?
questions.explanation: Arya Samaj was established in 1875 AD. The credit for its establishment goes to Swami Dayanand Saraswati. Its headquarters was shifted from Bombay to Lahore. In this, untouchability and caste discrimination were opposed and women and Shudras were also given the right to wear Yajnopavita and study Vedas. His famous slogan was "Back to the Vedas"

questions.question_text: Who established the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: DSSSB PGT 10/07/2021 TGT History 2010 Ans. (d) : Raja Ram Mohan Roy was born in 1772 AD in Hooghly, Bengal. He is called the father of modern India. Ideologically, where he was modern, he also tried to connect modernity with tradition. He had established Brahmo Samaj in 1828 AD.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of Renaissance?
questions.explanation: The literal meaning of Renaissance is rebirth. In a limited sense, this word is used for the interest again generated in the knowledge-science of the ancient civilization of Greece and Rome. The meaning of Renaissance is 're-awakening'. It is basically a French word whose other names are rebirth, intellectual consciousness, cultural revival, etc

questions.question_text: Who were the founders of "Atmiya Sabha" among the following?
questions.explanation: The reform movement that started in Bengal was led by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. That is why he is called the pioneer of the renaissance, the progenitor of reform movements, the father of modern India, and the morning star of the new era. After resigning from the service of the East India Company, he formed the Atmiya Sabha in 1814-15 AD and established the Vedanta Society in 1816 AD

questions.question_text: Among the following freedom fighters, who established the "Servants of India Society"?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the "Servants of India Society" in 1905 in Pune. The main objective of its establishment was to prepare missionaries for the service of India and to promote the true interests of the Indian people in a constitutional way

questions.question_text: Among the following social reformers, who gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas"?
questions.explanation: The slogan "Back to the Vedas" was given by Swami Dayanand Saraswati. The source also states that he established the Arya Samaj in 1875 and used the slogan to propagate his religious reform movement.

questions.question_text: 'Satyashodhak Samaj' was established by whom:
questions.explanation: Satyashodhak Samaj was established on 24 September 1873 AD in Maharashtra. It was founded by Jyotiba Rao Phule, whose objective remained connected from corner to corner of India regarding the need for social change against the economic, social, and cultural corruption prevalent in society along with the caste system, priestcraft, man-woman inequality, and superstition. The continuity of their activities was carried forward by Jyotiba Phule's wife, Savitribai Phule

questions.question_text: In which year was the Bengal Sati Regulation Act (Regulation XVII) passed?
questions.explanation: The founder of Brahmo Samaj, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, made people aware to end the Sati practice and called it a stain on Indian culture and started the movement and tried to stop Sati practice with the help of the then British government's Governor-General Lord William Bentinck. Raja Ram Mohan Roy got books written on the wrong tradition like Sati practice and its bad effects along with its remedies in Hindi, English, and Bengali languages and distributed them for free. On 4 December 1829 AD, Lord William Bentinck declared it illegal under Rule 17 and imposed a complete ban in India

questions.question_text: Parsi social reformer Behramji M. Malabari ran his campaign:
questions.explanation: Parsi social reformer Behramji M. Malabari was a companion of India's veteran leader Dadabhai Naoroji. Malabari was an Indian poet, writer, and social reformer. He is known for his strong activities against child marriage. He was born in 1853 in Baroda (Gujarat). Due to the efforts of Behramji Malabari, the British government passed the Age of Consent Act, 1891, in which the minimum age of girl marriage was set at 12 years

questions.question_text: Who was not associated with the Aligarh Movement?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In 1875 AD, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan started a Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental School in Aligarh where both Western subjects and science and Muslim religion were taught. Soon Aligarh became the center of the religious and cultural movement of the Muslim community. Its leaders were Altaf Hussain Hali, Nazir Ahmed, and Chiragh Ali, etc.

questions.question_text: In 1889 AD, who started the Ahmadiyya movement?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Ahmadiyya movement was a famous Muslim movement of the 19th century. Its originator was Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (1835-1908). This movement started from a place named Qadian in Gurdaspur district of Punjab. Mirza Sahib explained his principles in his book Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya (which was published in 1880).

questions.question_text: Who wrote the work named "Gift to Monotheists"?
questions.explanation: In 1809 AD, Raja Ram Mohan Roy wrote Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, i.e., 'A Gift to Monotheists' in Persian, which was introduced in the Arabic language

questions.question_text: Before Lord William Bentinck, who among the following did not make efforts to limit Sati practice?
questions.explanation: Efforts to end Sati practice before Lord William Bentinck were not made by Lord Amherst. Lord Cornwallis, Lord Minto I, and Lord Hastings had tried to limit Sati practice. Success in ending Sati practice was received by Bentinck, who ended it under Rule 17 in 1829 AD. In 1830 AD, this ban was implemented in the whole of India. This work of Bentinck fulfilled the demand of Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Brahmo Samaj

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was the inspiration behind the Young Bengal movement that emerged in the first half of the nineteenth century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– In the third and fourth decades of the nineteenth century, a 'Radical' or extremist trend was born among the intellectuals of Bengal. This trend was more modern and revolutionary than the ideas of Ram Mohan Roy. This movement is known as the 'Young Bengal' movement. The inspiration source and leader of this movement was the young Henry Vivian Derozio (1809-31). Derozio was an Anglo-Indian who had immense love for India. He was a professor at Hindu College from 1826 to 31. His talent was amazing. He was an influential teacher, who in a short time made many brilliant and devout students his admirers and followers.

questions.question_text: Who founded the 'United Indian Patriotic Association' with both Hindu and Muslim members in 1888?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The 'United Indian Patriotic Association' with both Hindu and Muslim members was founded by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan in 1888. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan was a Hindustani teacher and leader who started modern education for the Muslims of India. He founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College which later developed into the Aligarh Muslim University.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Darul Uloom Deoband school established?
questions.explanation: Darul Uloom Deoband school was established in May, 1866 in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Its founders were Qasim Nanautawi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi. Deoband's religious ideas are influenced excessively by Shah Waliullah and Indian Wahhabism, which give it a puritanical and conservative perspective. Deoband emphasizes the study of Quran, Hadith, Fiqh, Kalam, and Philosophy

questions.question_text: Where was the headquarters of the Theosophical Society in India?
questions.explanation: The Theosophical Society was established in 1875 by Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott in America. In 1879, its headquarters in India was in Bombay and in 1882, the headquarters was made in Adyar (Chennai). Annie Besant popularized its propagation in India

questions.question_text: In the year 1916, how many Home Rule Leagues were made in India?
questions.explanation: In April 1916, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and in September 1916, Annie Besant established Home Rule Leagues and opened many branches of it in various places so that more and more people could be connected with this ideology

questions.question_text: Who started the 'Bahishkrit Bharat' magazine?
questions.explanation: 'Bahishkrit Bharat' magazine was started by B.R. Ambedkar on the visit to the Koregaon Bhima war memorial. It was published in Marathi on 3 April 1927

questions.question_text: Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in ________.
questions.explanation: Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828. Due to his efforts, a ban was imposed on Sati practice in 1829 AD in India. In 1831, Mughal ruler Akbar II gave him the title of Raja and sent him to the court of the then British Emperor William IV for conversation regarding his pension amount

questions.question_text: The Widow Remarriage Act was passed in ________.
questions.explanation: Under the leadership of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, many reform acts were made for women in the 19th century. In 1856, this law was made, by which women could remarry after becoming widows. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar himself gave a message to reject the evils prevalent in society by marrying his son to a widow

questions.question_text: Adyar is the headquarters of which organization?
questions.explanation: Adyar is the headquarters of the Theosophical Society in India. Its establishment was done by Madame Blavatsky and Henry Olcott in 1875 AD in New York city, America. It was shifted to Adyar in 1882

questions.question_text: When did Vivekananda participate in the World Religion Parliament in Chicago?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda gave a very famous speech at the World Religion Conference held in Chicago (America) on 11 September 1893. My heart is filled with immense joy from your affectionate and forceful welcome of sisters and brothers of America. I thank you on behalf of the world's most ancient order of monks

questions.question_text: Which samaj was formed by Keshav Chandra Sen and his supporters in 1866?
questions.explanation: Keshav Chandra Sen became a member of Brahmo Samaj in 1856. To propagate the ideas of the samaj, he founded the Sangat Sabha. Later, he had a difference of opinion with Debendranath Tagore and he founded the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866

questions.question_text: What is the name of the famous work of Swami Dayanand Saraswati in which his thoughts are published?
questions.explanation: Satyarth Prakash was written in Hindi in 1874 AD by the founder of Arya Samaj, Swami Dayanand Saraswati. Its main objective was the promotion and expansion of the principles of Arya Samaj

questions.question_text: In which year was the Tattvabodhini Sabha established to spread the thoughts of Rammohan Roy?
questions.explanation: On 6 October 1839, Debendranath Tagore established the Tattvabodhini Sabha. In 1859, the Tattvabodhini Sabha was merged back into the Brahmo Samaj by Debendranath Tagore

questions.question_text: With whom did Raja Ram Mohan Roy work to carry out his educational activities?
questions.explanation: Rammohan Roy is called the pioneer of Indian Renaissance and the father of modern India. He established the Brahmo Samaj and, with the help of an Englishman, David Hare, established the Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817 AD

questions.question_text: What was the name of the English newspaper edited by Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
questions.explanation: The publication of Mahratta by Bal Gangadhar Tilak was done in the English language and the publication of Kesari in the Marathi language. Tilak was the first popular leader of the Indian freedom struggle whom the British government called the 'father of Indian unrest'. He also received the honorable title of 'Lokmanya'

questions.question_text: Who started the ‘Som Prakash’ newspaper?
questions.explanation: Renowned social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar started the editing of Som Prakash in the Bengali language in the year 1859. This was the first such newspaper against which Lytton's Vernacular Press Act was applied. At the inspiration of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Gangadhar Bhattacharya started the Bengal Gazette in Calcutta in 1816. On 20 April 1822, in Calcutta itself, Raja Ram Mohan Roy brought out the Persian language Mirat-ul-Akhbar

questions.question_text: Arrange the following organizations chronologically according to their year of establishment and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: (i) Prarthana Samaj (ii) Ramakrishna Mission (iii) Brahmo Samaj (iv) Arya Samaj Code:
questions.explanation: Institutions Establishment Year Brahmo Samaj 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy Prarthana Samaj 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang and M.G. Ranade Arya Samaj 1875 by Dayanand Saraswati Ramakrishna Mission 1897 by Swami Vivekananda.

questions.question_text: The English newspaper named ‘Prabuddha Bharata’ was published by
questions.explanation: Prabuddha Bharata is an English monthly magazine published by the Ramakrishna Mission. It has been published since 1896. It contains articles on various cultural and religious subjects by monks, sadhus, and sannyasis. Its editing is done by Advaita Ashrama in Uttarakhand and publication and printing are done from Kolkata

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Dharma Sabha established in opposition to the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: The main objective of the ‘Brahmo Samaj’ established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 AD was regarding the ban on the ‘Sati practice’. Contemporary social reformer ‘Radhakanta Deb’ established the ‘Dharma Sabha’ in 1830 AD in opposition to the Brahmo Samaj, which supported the Sati practice

questions.question_text: In the Bombay Prarthana Samaj, whom were M.G. Ranade influenced by?
questions.explanation: In 1867, in Bombay, with the cooperation of Keshav Chandra Sen, Atmaram Pandurang established the Prarthana Samaj. There was participation of many important powers in this, in which M.G. Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar and N.G. Chandavarkar were prominent

questions.question_text: Below, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given. Considering them, choose the correct option from the options given below: Assertion (A) : As a result of the continuous efforts of Jyotiba Phule, non-Brahmins received special representation under the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms. Reason (R) : Jyotiba Phule openly said in his book ‘Gulamgiri’ that a person born in any caste has their own individual personality and identity. Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Jyotiba Phule wrote his book Gulamgiri, which he composed in 1872-73. In it, he openly stated that a person born in any caste establishes their own individuality

questions.question_text: Which of the following social reformers supported widow remarriage in India in the 19th century?
questions.explanation: The contribution of four people is important for the remarriage of widows: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, D.K. Karve, Veeresalingam Pantulu and Vishnu Shastri Pandit. The Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 AD was passed due to the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar

questions.question_text: Who among the following went to England as the emperor's envoy to plead on behalf of the Mughal emperor Akbar II?
questions.explanation: After the death of Shah Alam II, his son Akbar II was the first Mughal ruler to become emperor under British protection. He sent Raja Ram Mohan Roy to Britain as an envoy with the title of ‘Raja’ to get his pension. During his time, the empire was reduced to just the Red Fort. Akbar II died in 1837 AD

questions.question_text: Who among the following advocated strongly for religious education in Indian universities?
questions.explanation: Madan Mohan Malviya strongly advocated for religious education in Indian universities. He established the Banaras Hindu University in Varanasi

questions.question_text: Match the social laws with the years they were passed. List-I List-II
questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Event Year (AD) Abolition of Sati 1829–30 Widow Remarriage Act Female infanticide prohibition Abolition of slavery

questions.question_text: ‘‘Patriotism is religion and religion is love for India.’’ Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was a learned scholar, great poet, and novelist of 19th-century Bengal. He composed the ‘Vande Mataram’ song in his famous work Anandmath. The Vande Mataram song was first sung at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Congress. He was adept at writing historical novels; he is considered the Alexander Dumas of India. In 1865, he wrote his first novel ‘Durgeshnandini’ in the Bengali language. He said that new national religiosity can only be brought through the development and expansion of education. Understanding the utility of education, he emphasized the establishment of cultural institutions across the country. Regarding religion, he said that ‘‘Patriotism is religion and religion is love for India.’’

questions.question_text: Who became famous by the nickname ‘Lokhitwadi’?
questions.explanation: Gopal Hari Deshmukh was a renowned social reformer of Maharashtra. He is also known by the nickname ‘Lokhitwadi’. He attacked the followers of the Hindu religion based on religious neutrality, rationality, and modernity and supported social and religious equality. He edited a monthly Marathi magazine ‘Lokhitwadi’. He established the Remarriage Mandal in Ahmedabad to encourage widow remarriage

questions.question_text: Who had the main role in getting ‘Sati practice’ ended in India?
questions.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy was the first Indian who ran a movement against the medieval evils prevalent in Indian society. Due to his new thoughts, the Renaissance in 19th-century India was born. He holds the honor of being the father of modern India, the father of Indian nationalism. He helped the government in implementing the laws brought by the Governor-General of India Lord William Bentinck in 1829 to ban the Sati practice. He also opposed practices like idol worship, child marriage, prostitution, casteism, etc

questions.question_text: In 1791 AD, who started the ‘Sanskrit College’ in Varanasi?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis appointed Jonathan Duncan as superintendent in Banaras in 1788, where he helped in putting a seal on the practice of infanticide and he remained the Governor of Bombay from 1795-1881. In 1791, he started a ‘Sanskrit College’ in Banaras for the study of Hindu law and philosophy. Later, this Sanskrit College became a university and in 1974 its name was changed to Sampurnanand Sanskrit University

questions.question_text: Who founded the ‘United Patriotic Association’?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the ‘United Indian Patriotic Association’ in 1888 AD in opposition to the establishment of the Congress. Ahmed Khan propagated his thoughts through a magazine, Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq

questions.question_text: Who was the leader of the Dola Palki movement?
questions.explanation: The Dola Palki movement was by the artisans (silpkar) of Uttarakhand. Its main objective was to achieve a position equal to the upper-caste grooms in the social system. The artisans did not have the right to sit in a Dola Palki for weddings. Around 1930, under the leadership of Jayanand Bharti, the artisans received this right

questions.question_text: Who is the author of the famous book Gulamgiri?
questions.explanation: Jyotiba Phule was a great thinker, social worker, writer, and philosopher of India. He opened the country's first girls' school for the upliftment of women in society. He launched a campaign of awareness among the people through his book ‘Gulamgiri’ for the abolition of the caste system prevalent in Maharashtra. He also established the ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’ (1873) to get justice for the poor and weak sections

questions.question_text: Match the social reformers of List-I with their societies given in List-II. List-I List-II A. Brahmo Samaj 1. Vishnu Shastri Pandit B. Ramakrishna Mission 2. Swami Vivekananda C. Servants of India Society 3. Raja Rammohan Roy D. Widow Remarriage Society 4. Gopal Krishna Gokhale A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is– Brahmo Samaj Raja Rammohan Roy Ramakrishna Mission Swami Vivekananda Servants of India Society Gopal Krishna Gokhale Widow Remarriage Society Vishnu Shastri Pandit

questions.question_text: Read the following statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy and choose the wrong statement:

options.C: In 'Precepts of Jesus', he rejected the principle of Jesus being divine.
options.D: His newspaper Sambad Kaumudi was the first Bengali language newspaper.

questions.explanation: The following statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy are correct 1. Raja Ram Mohan Roy published ‘Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin’, i.e., Gift of Monotheists, in the year 1809 AD. 2. He, with the help of David Hare, established Calcutta Hindu College (1817 AD) and Vedanta College (1825 AD). 3. In 1820 AD, he wrote a book named ‘Precepts of Jesus’ based on the Bible, in which he rejected the theory of Jesus being divine. 4. He started the publication of Sambad Kaumudi (Moon of Intelligence) in the Bengali language in the year 1821, Mirat-ul-Akhbar in the Persian language in 1822 AD, and Brahmanical Magazine in English. It is noteworthy that J.C. Marshman started the publication of ‘Digdarshan’ in the Bengali language in the year 1818 and Samachar Darpan (1818 AD) was the first weekly magazine published in the Bengali language. So, it is clear that statement (A) and statement (D) are both untrue.

questions.question_text: Who published ‘Shat Patre’ (Hundred Letters) in a newspaper in a serialized form for the spread of social consciousness?
questions.explanation: For the spread of social consciousness, Gopal Hari Deshmukh (1823) published 108 articles in a newspaper in a serialized form, which is known in Marathi literature as ‘Lokhitwadichi Shat Patre’. Apart from this, he wrote a book named Jati Bhed for the abolition of the caste system. Deshmukh is also known by the nickname Lokhitwadi. He edited a weekly newspaper named Prabhakar and authored books like Gita Tattva, Subhashit

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Central Hindu School in Banaras?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Annie Besant laid the foundation of Central Hindu College in Banaras in 1898 AD, where Hindu religion and Western scientific subjects were taught. Later, in the year 1916, through the efforts of Madan Mohan Malviya, this college became Banaras Hindu University (BHU). Annie Besant ran the Home Rule League (1916 AD) movement in India. In the year 1917, she became the first woman president of the Indian National Congress. She also edited newspapers named Commonweal and New India

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Deoband movement are true? 1. It started in Deoband in 1866. 2. One of its founders was Badruddin Tyabji. 3. Its main objective was to bring improvement in the spiritual and moral condition of Muslims. 4. The Deoband movement emphasized composite nationalism. Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: The Deoband movement was a revivalist movement. The following statements about it are true 1. This movement was started in 1866 AD with the establishment of Darul Uloom at a place named Deoband in Saharanpur, under the leadership of Ulama Muhammad Qasim Nanotvi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi. 2. The main objective of this movement was to bring improvement in the spiritual and moral condition of Muslims and to promote the teaching of the Quran and Hadith. 3. The Deoband movement emphasized composite nationalism, opposing the ‘United Indian Patriotic Association’ and ‘Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental Defence Association’ created by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. 4. It welcomed the establishment of the Indian National Congress (1885 AD).

questions.question_text: Which of the following (Institution and Founder) is not matched correctly?

options.A: Poona Seva Sadan - Mrs. Ramabai Ranade
options.C: Seva Samiti Boy Scout Union - Shri Ram Bajpai

questions.explanation: Poona Seva Sadan (1909 AD) Poona - Mrs. Ramabai Ranade Seva Samiti (1914 AD) Allahabad - H.N. Kunzru Seva Samiti Boy Scout Union (1914 AD) Bombay - Shri Ram Bajpai Paramhansa Sabha (Mandali) (1849 AD) Bombay - Dadoba Pandurang Social Service League (1911 AD) Bombay - Narayan Malhar Joshi

questions.question_text: Who established the Rajahmundry Social Reform Association?
questions.explanation: Veeresalingam Pantulu established the Rajahmundry Social Reform Association in the year 1878. D.K. Karve established the Widow Remarriage Association (Widow Home) and Women's University in Poona. E.V. Ramaswamy Periyar led the Self-Respect Movement, was the proponent of the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924 AD), and managed the Justice Party (Dravidian Kadam). C. Rajagopalachari became the first and last Indian Governor-General of independent India and was elected for the post of Chief Minister of Madras in 1952

questions.question_text: Who gave the slogan ‘One religion, one caste and one God for humanity’?
questions.explanation: Sree Narayana Guru (1855-1928 AD) was born in an Ezhava family of Kerala. He said that ‘There is one religion, one caste and one God for humanity.’ It was on the advice of Narayana Guru that Mahatma Gandhi changed the name of his newspaper from ‘Navajivan’ to ‘Harijan’. He established the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam in the year 1903

questions.question_text: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
questions.explanation: In the year 1932, Mahatma Gandhi named the lower castes ‘Harijan’ with the objective of improving them and established the Harijan Sevak Sangh, whose founding president was Ghanshyam Das Birla. In 1932 itself, Mahatma Gandhi established the All India Depressed Classes Association in Bombay. In the year 1933, Gandhiji brought out a weekly magazine named Harijan

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not matched correctly? A (Sangh) B (Associated)

options.A: Bharat Stree Mahamandal (i) Sarala Devi Chaudhurani
options.C: The National Council (iii) Lady Meherbai Tata
options.D: All India Women's Conference (iv) Margaret Cousins

questions.question_text: Who said, "India's only hope is the masses. The upper classes are physically and morally dead"?

Narendranath participated in the first World Parliament of Religions held in Chicago, USA in 1893. Before going to America, on the suggestion of the Raja of Khetri, Narendranath adopted the name 'Swami Vivekananda'. In February 1896, he formed the Vedanta Society in New York for the propagation of Indian religion and philosophy. He also participated in the Second World Parliament of Religions held in Paris in 1900. His belief was that "service to man is service to God". He said to the educated community that "I consider those educated people guilty who, after being educated with the money of poor and hungry people, do not pay attention to them." Indian Reform Association was established by Keshav Chandra Sen for women's reform, whereas Deva Samaj was established in Lahore in 1887 AD by Shivnarine Agnihotri. Its perspective was religious and this organization emphasized on its followers to adopt a social code of conduct and ethics. No talk of women's upliftment was done by this organization.

questions.question_text: Which Baptist missionary expressed faith in Raja Ram Mohan Roy's monotheistic principles and established the 'Unitarian Mission' with him?
questions.explanation: William Adam was a Baptist missionary who, along with Raja Ram Mohan, established the Unitarian Mission in Calcutta. Calcutta Unitarian Mission was done in 1821 AD.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not associated with the Baptist missionary community?
questions.explanation: William Carey, Joshua Marshman, and William Ward were associated with the Baptist missionary community. The Baptist missionary community was established in 1800 AD in Serampore (W. Bengal) where William Ward and Joshua Marshman are prominent. Through the press established by them, about 212,000 books were published between 1800 AD and 1832 AD.

questions.question_text: Dayanand Saraswati was not an opponent of which religious thought?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati (Mool Shankar) founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay on 10 April 1875, whose main objective was to re-establish the ancient Vedic religion in its pure form. In the religious field, Swami Dayanand Saraswati was an opponent of idol worship, polytheism, incarnation, animal sacrifice, tantra-mantra, and false rituals. In the religious thoughts of Swami Dayanand Saraswati, emphasis was given to respect for the cow, and he formed the 'Gorakshini Sabha'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not an Orientalist?
questions.explanation: H.T. Colebrooke, William Carey, and James Prinsep were all Orientalists, whereas Charles Grant was included among the supporters of Western education.

questions.question_text: Match the social movements mentioned in List-I with the regions mentioned in List-II, in which regions they occurred. Select the correct code and give the answer: List-I | List-II
questions.explanation: The correct matching given in the source is: Paramhansa Mandali — Maharashtra; Kayastha Sabha — Uttar Pradesh; Sarin Sabha — Punjab; Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Sabha — Kerala.

questions.question_text: Through whose efforts was the Devadasi system abolished in Madras Presidency?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Muthulakshmi Reddy was a social activist. Through her efforts, the Devadasi system was abolished in Madras Presidency. She also received the support of local people in this movement.

questions.question_text: Who established the Radhasoami Satsang in Agra in 1861?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ In 1861, Tulsi Ram, who is also known as Shiv Dayal Singh, established Radhasoami Satsang in Agra. His objective was to emphasize belief in one God, religious unity, simplicity in social life, and social service.

questions.question_text: Where was the Arya Samaj established?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 PGT History, 2003, 2013 Explanation – Dayanand's childhood name was Mool Shankar. He did not have faith in idol worship at a young age. In 1861 AD, he made Swami Virjanand of Mathura his guru and studied Vedas there. Separating from his guru, he started the work of propagating Hindu religion, culture, and language, and first established Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875.

questions.question_text: Who presided over the first National Social Conference held in 1888 AD in Madras?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation– T. Madhava Rao presided over the first National Social Conference held in 1888 AD in Madras.

questions.question_text: Who propagated the principle 'Jiva Shiva Hai' (The living being is Shiva)?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation─ Swami Ramakrishna Paramhansa (1834-1886), priest of the Kali temple situated in Dakshineswar, tried to attain religious liberation through the traditional ways of devotion, renunciation, and worship. Ramakrishna, who had complete faith in Indian culture and civilization, considered all religions as true. He believed in idol worship and also considered it a means to attain the eternal, almighty God. He propagated the principle that 'Jiva is Shiva'.

questions.question_text: 'Jati Mimamsa' is authored by –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – Sree Narayana Guru was associated with the Ezhava (an untouchable) caste of Kerala. Sree Narayana Guru tried to end the practice of untouchability against the lower castes below him. He simplified the rituals of marriage, religious worship, and funeral. Sree Narayana Guru had special success in transforming untouchable castes into backward castes. He is considered the author of 'Jati Mimamsa'.

questions.question_text: In India, the Theosophical Society received success and popularity mainly due to whom?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The Theosophical Society received success and popularity in India mainly due to Smt. Annie Besant. She laid the foundation of Central Hindu College in Banaras in 1898, where Hindu religion and Western scientific subjects were taught. Later, in 1916, this became the Banaras Hindu University. The Home Rule Movement was also run in 1916 by Smt. Annie Besant.

questions.question_text: Which courageous act of the Theosophical Society received public acceptance and full support?

options.B: Support for the revival and strengthening of ancient religions like Hindu, Zoroastrian, and Buddhist, etc.
options.C: Promoting the universal brotherhood of man.

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- The Theosophical Society was established in 1875 in America. It was established by a Russian woman, Helena Petrovna Blavatsky (1831-91) and an American army officer, Colonel Steve Olcott (1831-97). Followers of this society advocated for reviving ancient religions like Hindu religion, which was a national religion, and Buddhist religion, and strengthening them. They accepted the principle of rebirth and karma and considered the philosophy of Samkhya and Upanishads as their source of inspiration. They supported the spirit of universal brotherhood. The work of education of India's youth received public acceptance and full support.

questions.question_text: Who said to the Indian people, "Be brave, be courageous, have hope, be proud of the fact that you are an Indian, every Indian is my brother."
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Swami Vivekananda said to the Indian people, "Be brave, be courageous, have hope, be proud of the fact that you are an Indian, every Indian is my brother." He also founded the Ramakrishna Mission.

questions.question_text: A social reformer of Maharashtra who was famous by the nickname 'Lokhitwadi' –
questions.explanation: UKPSC Lect. Mains 2020 TGT History, 2011 Explanation- A social reformer of Maharashtra who was famous by the nickname 'Lokhitwadi' was Gopal Hari Deshmukh. Dadabhai Naoroji is called the 'Grand Old Man of India'. Mahadev Govind Ranade is called the Socrates of Maharashtra. Jyotiba Phule founded Satyashodhak Samaj and wrote a book named 'Gulamgiri'.

questions.question_text: Match List-I and List-II and select the correct answer from the given codes: List-I | List-II B. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan | (ii) Tattvabodhini Sabha C. Rammohan Roy | (iii) Arya Samaj D. Debendranath Tagore | (iv) Brahmo Samaj Codes : A B C D A. Dayanand Saraswati | (i) Khudai Khidmatgar
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─ Correct match is of this type─ List-I | List-II A. Dayanand Saraswati | (iii) Arya Samaj B. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan | (i) Khudai Khidmatgar C. Rammohan Roy | (iv) Brahmo Samaj D. Debendranath Tagore | (ii) Tattvabodhini Sabha

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─ Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta on 20 August 1828. Raja Ram Mohan Roy was born in 1774 AD in a village named Radhanagar. He studied languages like Arabic, Persian, English, Greek, Hebrew, etc. in his life. At the age of 17, he became an opponent of idol worship. He established Vedanta College. His death occurred in Britain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct match?

options.B: Arya Samaj – Raja Ram Mohan Roy

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─ In 1875, Madam H.P. Blavatsky, a Russian lady, laid the foundation of Theosophical Society in America. Subsequently, Colonel Olcott also joined her. In 1882, they established the headquarters of their society in Adyar near Madras city. After the death of Colonel Olcott in 1907, Annie Besant became its president.

questions.question_text: Who is called the father of modern India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─ Raja Ram Mohan Roy has been given various titles such as father of modern India, innovator of the new age, father of Indian Renaissance, deity of Indian nationalism, etc. Raja Ram Mohan Roy is undoubtedly the creator of modern India. There was no social, religious, and political movement of the 19th century in which he did not have direct or indirect cooperation in its beginning. He died in the city of Bristol in England.

questions.question_text: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar supported -
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─ Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was basically an educationist and teacher and was serving as the principal of Calcutta Sanskrit College. He supported widow remarriage, women's education, and opposition to child marriage. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820-91) was a famous scholar and another social reformer of Bengal.

questions.question_text: 'Ramakrishna Mission' was established by–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2003, 2005, 2010 Explanation – After returning from his American tour in 1897 AD, Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission, and in 1909, got it registered under the Societies Registration Act. The main headquarters of Ramakrishna Mission were opened at Baranagar-Belur near Calcutta and Mayavati named places of Almora.

questions.question_text: In which field did Arya Samaj achieve the greatest achievement?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – Arya Samaj achieved the greatest achievement in the field of educational reform. Social reformer Swami Dayanand Saraswati established Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875 AD, whose main objective was to re-establish the ancient Vedic religion in its pure form, deciding to uproot the false religious pretenses and social evils that had come into Hindu society.

questions.question_text: Deoband, U.P. Dar-ul-Uloom is associated with whom?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (cancelled) Explanation – Deoband Saharanpur in Uttar Pradesh Dar-ul-Uloom is associated with the Muslim reform movement. Ulama Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi started the Dar-ul-Uloom or Deoband movement in 1867 AD with the aim of giving a call for 'Jihad' against foreign rulers, along with the teachings of Quran and Hadith, and also established a school in Deoband to provide religious training to new leaders.

questions.question_text: Among the following, who was associated with Arya Samaj?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Pandit Guru Datta Vidyarthi was associated with the Arya Samaj established by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay in 1875 and later became a prominent leader of the Arya Samaj and died at the young age of 46. Annie Besant had said that Swami Dayanand Saraswati was the first person who said "India is for Indians".

questions.question_text: Who was associated with Tattvabodhini Patrika?
questions.explanation: DSSSB PGT 2021, MP Asst. Prof. 2017, UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004, 2005 PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Tattvabodhini Patrika is associated with Debendranath Tagore. Not only this, he founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839. The main work of Tattvabodhini Sabha included reading the 'Brahmo Dharma' text and propagating/disseminating the knowledge of Upanishads.

questions.question_text: Who was responsible for getting the famous Hindu Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 passed?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013, 2000 Explanation – The famous Hindu Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 was passed on 26 July 1856 during the time of Lord Canning. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar has a significant contribution in this.

questions.question_text: Under the Age of Consent Act of 1891, what minimum age was fixed for the marriage of girls?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Under the Age of Consent Act of 1891 AD, the minimum age for the marriage of girls was fixed at 12 years. Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed this act and considered it foreign interference in Indian social affairs.

questions.question_text: Who gave the inspiration for the establishment of Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The credit for the inspiration for the establishment of Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra goes to Keshav Chandra Sen. As a result, Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay in 1867. Its founders were Atmaram Pandurang.

questions.question_text: There is sufficient similarity in the reform-related thoughts of Vivekananda and Theosophical Society. Which of the following thoughts matches the thoughts of the Theosophical Society?

options.A: They believed in tantra and superstitions
options.B: They tried to normalize the feeling of inferiority existing in Hindus
options.C: They believed that just as God is free, every person is also free
options.D: They awakened self-confidence and self-respect in people

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – There is sufficient similarity in the reform-related thoughts of Vivekananda and Theosophical Society. Among the four options given, option (d), i.e., they awakened self-confidence and self-respect in people. This thought is associated with both Vivekananda and Theosophical Society.

questions.question_text: Who was the national leader who raised his voice against untouchability for the first time?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The national leader who raised his voice against untouchability for the first time was Jyotiba Phule. It is noteworthy that the start of the lower caste movement first happened in Maharashtra. Phule established the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873. He wrote a book named Gulamgiri in 1872, through which he made the lower castes aware.

questions.question_text: The call for "One religion, one caste, and one God for man" was made by─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005, Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013, UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation─ The call for "One religion, one caste, and one God for man" was made by Sree Narayana Guru. Later, one of his disciples improved this sentence like this 'There is no religion, no caste, and no God for mankind'.

questions.question_text: Which reformer made the main contribution towards widow remarriage?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was not only a scholar but also a famous social reformer of Bengal. Who sent a petition signed by 994 people to the British Governor General in 1855, in which it was urged that the government should make a Widow Remarriage Act. Due to this effort of his, the 'Widow Remarriage Act 1856' was passed by Lord Canning on 26 July 1856. In which legal recognition was given to widow remarriage.

questions.question_text: The principle of adoption prohibition was applied to which?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Dalhousie's doctrine of lapse (policy of annexation) made all native kings restless. The right to adopt a son was snatched from Hindu kings. The right of succession "was not theirs in whose veins the blood of the founder of the dynasty was not flowing". The difference between dependent states and protected allies was very subtle. It was only a matter of skinning a cat. In disputed cases, the company's decision was binding and the decision of the Court of Directors was final.

questions.question_text: Whose influence was most on the English-educated youth of the first generation of Bengal?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Father of the Young Bengal movement, Henry Vivian Derozio, had the most influence on the English-educated youth of the first generation of Bengal.

questions.question_text: Who said that "Hindu and Muslim are two eyes of India"?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Sir Syed Ahmad Khan said that "Hindu and Muslim are two eyes of India".

questions.question_text: Who revived the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015, Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014, PGT History, 2013, 2010 Explanation – After the death of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Debendranath Tagore revived the Brahmo Samaj. Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy on 20 August 1828.

questions.question_text: Whose real name was Mool Shankar?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Swami Dayanand Saraswati's childhood name was Mool Shankar. He was born in 1824 at a place named Maurvi in Gujarat. He established Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875.

questions.question_text: Among the following, who was more influenced by Western philosophy than Indian philosophy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Raja Ram Mohan Roy was essentially a democrat and humanist. He has also been called 'Messiah of Indian Renaissance', bridge between past and future, father of Indian nationalism, and modern India's father and Yugavtar.

questions.question_text: Through which Act of 1843 was slavery declared illegal?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ India's Governor-General Lord Ellenborough declared slavery or the slavery system illegal through rule V of the India Act of 1843 AD.

questions.question_text: Which institution first spread English education in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ English religious preachers and Christian missionaries established their center at Baptist Mission College, Serampore, Calcutta for the spread of education in India, and they were the first to spread English education in India. The college established in 1818 by the Serampore Trio (William Carey, Marshman, and William Ward) is still functioning as Serampore College.

questions.question_text: By whom was the Prarthana Samaj started?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Brahmo ideology also spread in Maharashtra and a Paramhansa Sabha started here in 1849. In 1867, due to the inspiration of Keshav Chandra Sen, Atmaram Pandurang established Prarthana Samaj in Bombay. Other prominent leaders of Prarthana Samaj were Mahadev Govind Ranade, N.G. Chandavarkar, etc. Prarthana Samaj had four main objectives of social reform, which are as follows- 1- Opposition to caste-system 2- Increasing the marriage age of men and women 3- Widow remarriage 4- Women's education

questions.question_text: By whom was the title 'Raja' given to Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Raja Ram Mohan Roy was given the title of 'Raja' by Akbar Shah II. He was sent to the court of British King William IV as his representative to present the Mughal Emperor's case regarding the insufficient pension given to the Mughal Emperor.

questions.question_text: In which year did Swami Vivekananda establish the Ramakrishna Mission?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009, G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In 1897 AD, Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission near Calcutta in Baranagar and in 1899 AD, he established his ancient monastery in Belur. In 1899, he went to America and he traveled throughout Europe and established Vedanta societies at various places. He came to India in 1902 AD.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given code: List-I | List-II A. Adi Brahmo Samaj | 1. Jyotiba Phule B. Indian Brahmo Samaj | 2. Debendranath Tagore C. Theosophical Society | 3. Colonel Olcott D. Satyashodhak Samaj | 4. Keshav Chandra Sen Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012, G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– A. Adi Brahmo Samaj – Debendranath Tagore B. Indian Brahmo Samaj – Keshav Chandra Sen C. Theosophical Society – Colonel Olcott D. Satyashodhak Samaj – Jyotiba Phule

questions.question_text: Where did the Wahabi sect originate?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– The Wahabi sect born in Arabia is a strict branch of Islam. This movement run by Maulvi Abdul Wahhab believes in the Quran and emphasizes the decision through inner consciousness in the situation of contradictory interpretations of Quran and Hadith. Along with this, it emphasized reconciling the four legal scriptures of Islam. In India, Syed Ahmad Barelvi made the Wahabi movement popular and gave it a political form.

questions.question_text: Where was the first Asiatic Society established in India?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The first Asiatic Society in India was established in Bengal Calcutta in 1784 AD. Sir William Jones established this institution. Later, various books were translated in this institution.

questions.question_text: By whose serious efforts was the first Women's University established in Bombay?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013, UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000, 2004 Explanation─ Through D.K. Karve's efforts, the first Women's University was established in 1906 AD in Bombay. He established a Widow Ashram in Pune in 1896 AD.

questions.question_text: Prarthana Samaj was started by
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- Brahmo ideology also spread in Maharashtra and a Paramhansa Sabha started here in 1849. In 1867, due to the inspiration of Keshav Chandra Sen, a Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay. Its main founders included Atmaram Pandurang. There were four objectives of social reform in it, which are as follows- 1- Opposition to caste-system 2- Increasing the marriage age of men and women 3- Widow remarriage 4- Women's education

questions.question_text: Who called the Wahabi movement a holy war?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Syed Ahmad Barelvi called the Wahabi movement a holy war. The Wahabi movement kept making efforts for purity in the Muslim religion, eventually, this movement moved towards religious devotion and was suppressed by the British. After the 1857 AD rebellion, the British looked at Muslims with suspicion. They believed that they had active participation in the 1857 AD rebellion.

questions.question_text: Who were the 'Derozians'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The start of the Young Bengal movement was done by Henry Vivian Derozio. Born in 1809 AD, Derozio taught at the Hindu College in Calcutta from 1826 to 1831. The Anglo-Indian Derozio is called the first nationalist poet. For extreme progress and social reform, Derozio established organizations like Society for Acquisition of General Knowledge.

questions.question_text: Through which act did Lord Dalhousie declare widow remarriage legal?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In 1855 AD, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar raised his voice in favour of widow remarriage. He demanded the government to make a law for this. Widow-remarriage was declared legal by the government. On 7 December 1856 AD, the first legal widow-marriage was completed in Calcutta.

questions.question_text: Who started the Widow Ashram in Pune in 1896 AD?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Maharashtra social reformer D.K. Karve established a Widow Ashram in Pune in 1896 AD. He established the first Women's University in Bombay in 1906 AD.

questions.question_text: Shivli Numani (alive till 1914 AD) was among the supporters of Deoband Madrasa. Which of the following statements about him is not true?

options.A: He was a democrat as well as an opponent of imperialism.
options.B: He was an admirer of the high ideals of the Congress.
options.C: He considered Syed Ahmad Khan's loyalty to the English as appropriate.
options.D: He was a supporter of Islamic unity.

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Among the supporters of Deoband Madrasa, Shivli Numani did not consider Syed Ahmad Khan's loyalty to the English as appropriate. In 1884-85, he established Nadwat-ul-Ulama and Dar-ul-Uloom in Lucknow. He was a supporter of including English and European science in the Muslim education system for reform.

questions.question_text: Who had the most contribution to the 19th-century Indian Renaissance?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Western education can be said to have the highest contribution to the 19th-century Indian Renaissance. Due to the English education, Western knowledge-science and thought propagated by the English and Christian missionaries in India, the influence began to increase. Attacks on Indian religion, society, and heritage were started to establish the supremacy of the English themselves, in retaliation to which the Indian Renaissance started.

questions.question_text: Which class of India adopted Western culture in the beginning?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Educated Hindu elite (middle) class adopted Western culture first.

questions.question_text: Raja Ram Mohan Roy published a weekly journal. That was:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– The weekly journal published by Raja Ram Mohan Roy was Sambad Kaumudi. This Bengali journal was published in 1821. Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a social reformer as well as a pioneer of Indian journalism. Raja Ram Mohan Roy also published Mirat-ul-Akhbar in Persian.

questions.question_text: What age for girls' marriage was fixed by the Sharda Act of 1929?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003 Explanation– Due to the efforts of Dr. Harbilas Sarda, the Sharda Act was passed in 1929 AD. Through this act, the age of boys was fixed at 18 years and the age of girls at 14 years.

questions.question_text: The Muslim scholar known as the father of Muslim Renaissance in Bengal is–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2003, UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Abdul Latif Khan is considered the father of Muslim Renaissance in Bengal. The Literary Society established by him in Calcutta in 1863 was the first effort at reform among Muslims.

questions.question_text: Who gets the credit for ending the "Thuggee system"?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The credit for ending the Thuggee system goes to Colonel Sleeman (the then Governor General was Lord William Bentinck).

questions.question_text: Which British administrator translated the 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita' into English?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– Sir William Jones established the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784 AD. Whose objective was to uncover ancient Indian literature and bring India's past to light. Through this Asiatic Society of Bengal, Wilkins translated Shrimad Bhagavad Gita and Hitopadesha into English in 1785 AD.

questions.question_text: Who were the founders of 'Royal Asiatic Society' of Bengal?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000, 2001 Explanation– William Jones established "Asiatic Society of Bengal" in Calcutta in 1784 for the study of Asia's social and natural history, archaeology, science, and literature. Later it came to be known as Royal Asiatic Society of Bengal. William Jones wrote Abhijñānaśākuntalam in English in 1789. English translation of Bhagavad Gita was done by Charles Wilkins in 1785.

questions.question_text: Where did Swami Vivekananda establish the Ramakrishna Math in 1897 AD?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 AD. The first monastery was established in Baranagar near Calcutta. After that, in 1899 AD, transferring it from Baranagar, he established the Ramakrishna Mission/Ramakrishna Math in Vellore near Calcutta. The second monastery of the mission was established in a place named Mayavati in Almora. The objective of Ramakrishna Mission was religious and social reform.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not correct regarding the Brahmo Marriage Act?

options.B: It gave approval to inter-caste marriages
options.C: It gave approval to widow marriages
options.D: It did not impose restrictions on polygamy

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– When the condition of women did not improve by stopping Sati system and infanticide, it was necessary to perform positive acts like giving permission for widow remarriage for them and increasing the age of marriage. The Brahmo Samajists debated on the issue of widow remarriage. Subsequently, the Brahmo Samajists tried to make it popular. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar proved from ancient Sanskrit and Vedic references that the Vedas allow widow remarriage. He sent a petition approved by nearly one thousand signatures to the Indian government and finally, the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (1856) recognized widow-remarriage as legal and made the child born from that marriage legitimate, and later the Child Marriage Act was passed, through which child marriage was approved and restrictions were imposed on polygamy.

questions.question_text: Who is called the 'father of Renaissance of Western India' -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000, 2001 Explanation– Due to the efforts of social reformer of Western India, Mahadev Govind Ranade, the Public Social Reform Association society was established. Influenced by Brahmo Samaj, he did this work, but he did not consider himself a follower of any new religion or outside of Hindu religion or simultaneously a follower of any new sect, but only as a movement within this religion. He did not want to collide with Hindu dogmatists but emphasized on education and explaining. His four main prominent objectives in social reform were. (1) Opposition to caste-system, (2) Increasing the marriage age of men and women (3) Widow remarriage, (4) Women's education. Mahadev Govind Ranade was a prominent leader of this. That is why he was called the father of Renaissance of Western India and the Socrates of Maharashtra.

questions.question_text: Who was the Hindu Luther of Northern India in the 19th century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Dayanand Saraswati is called the Hindu Luther of Northern India. He wrote a book named Satyarth Prakash. He was born in 1824 in a Brahmin family living in the princely state of Maurvi, Gujarat. In 1863, he hoisted the 'Pakhand Khandini Pataka' to refute false religions. In 1875, he established Arya Samaj in Bombay, whose main objective was to re-establish the ancient Vedic religion in its pure form, deciding to uproot the false religious beliefs and social evils that had come into Hindu society over time. In 1877, Arya Samaj was established in Lahore, after which Arya Samaj became more popular. Swami Dayanand's objective was that India should be united religiously, socially, and nationally. His desire was that Arya Dharma should be the common religion of the country. He saw many defects in the contemporary Hindu religion and society. He worked tirelessly in both these fields throughout his life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Mahatma Jyotiba Phule is not correct?

options.A: He synthesized the revolutionary ideas of Buddha and Kabir in his own.
options.B: He took untouchability as a blot on Hindu religion.
options.D: He founded the Pune Sarvajanik Sabha.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Pune Sarvajanik Sabha was established in 1870 by M.G. Ranade. Jyotiba Phule struggled for the lower castes. Jyotiba criticized the leaders of the Indian National Congress for ignoring the interests of the weaker sections. His statement was that Congress is not entitled to be called national in the true sense until it pays attention to the interests of the lower and backward castes. In 1873, Jyotiba formed the Satyashodhak Sabha whose objective was to provide social justice to the weaker sections of society. He opened many schools and orphanages for orphans and women of all varnas. He was elected as a member of Pune Municipality in 1876. Among Phule's publications are Dharma Tritiya Ratna (exposure of Puranas), Ishara (a warning), life of Shivaji, etc. In 1888, people started calling him 'Mahatma'.

questions.question_text: What was the main provision of the 1929 Sharda Act?

options.A: It gave recognition to widow remarriage.
options.B: It banned the employment of children in factories.
options.C: It fixed the minimum age for marriage of boys and girls.
options.D: It made rules for women's employment in factories.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The Sharda Act made in 1929, which is called the Civil Marriage Act. Through this act, marriages of girls under the age of 14 and boys under the age of 18 were prohibited and polygamy was also ended.

questions.question_text: Where is the international headquarters of Theosophical Society?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 by Madam Helena Petrovna Blavatsky and M.S. Olcott in New York. In 1892, its branch was established at a place named Adyar near Madras. Its main objectives are - (a) to form a society of all human beings in the spirit of brotherhood, (b) to help in the study of ancient religious philosophy and science which can be found anywhere in the world, (c) discovery of nature's laws and the development of human divine powers.

questions.question_text: Which facts are correct about Keshav Chandra Sen? (i) He became a member of Brahmo Samaj in 1857. (ii) Leaving Brahmo Samaj, he established a new organization. (iii) He was the first social reformer who traveled extensively. Codes : (iv) His death occurred in 1905 AD.
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – About Keshav Chandra Sen, options (a), (b), (c) are correct and (d) is wrong. Keshav Chandra Sen's death occurred in 1884.

questions.question_text: Who established the 'Satyashodhak Mandal'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004, 2010 Explanation – For the first time in Maharashtra in 1870, Jyotiba Phule started an anti-Brahmin movement. He wrote a book named Gulamgiri (1872) and also made an organization named 'Satyashodhak Mandal (Samaj)'.

questions.question_text: Which social-religious movement gave the slogan 'India is for Indians'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Arya Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1875. Its founder Dayanand Saraswati propagated Indianness and Swadeshi. He gave the slogan 'India is for Indians'. The principles of Arya Samaj are as follows- Vedas are the source of true knowledge. Basing on Vedas, chanting mantras and performing havan, rejection of idol worship, opposition to pilgrimage and incarnation, belief in karma and reincarnation or the theory of transmigration of life, belief in one God who is formless. Belief in women's education, opposition to child marriage and polygamy, support for widow remarriage in some special circumstances, support for the propagation of Hindi and Sanskrit language, etc. In the religious field, Arya Samaj claimed the supremacy of Vedas and based on that it emphasized mantra chanting, havan, yajna, karma, etc. Arya Samaj contributed to the creation of many such staunch individuals who became supporters of Indian nationalism with the spirit of staunch Hindu religion. This helped a lot in the creation of Indian nationalism.

questions.question_text: Among the following, who became famous by the nickname 'Lokhitwadi'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005, 2013 Explanation─ Gopal Hari Deshmukh is known by the nickname 'Lokhitwadi'. He started the social reform movement in Maharashtra. He also wrote a book named 'Jati Bhed' in opposition to caste-system discrimination. He wrote many articles on social, economic, and political issues in a weekly newspaper named 'Prabhakar'. His writings were called 'Shatpatre'.

questions.question_text: Who published the Persian pamphlet named Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Raja Ram Mohan Roy published the Persian pamphlet named Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin in 1809 AD, in which Raja Ram Mohan Roy refuted idol worship and polytheism. Apart from this, he published 'The Precepts of Jesus', 'Sambad Kaumudi', and 'Mirat-ul-Akhbar'. Although Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a multifaceted personality, he had special love for religious reform. At a time when young Bengalis influenced by Western education were being attracted towards Christianity, at that time Raja Ram Mohan Roy appeared as a protector of Hindu religion. On one hand, he defended Hindu religion against the Christian preachers; on the other hand, he also tried to remove the falsehood and superstitions that had entered the Hindu religion.

questions.question_text: What was the inspiration behind the 'Young Bengal Movement' that emerged in the first half of the 19th century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002, 2008 Explanation- During the last years of the third decade and the fourth decade of the 19th century, a 'Young Bengal movement' happened in Bengal. Its leadership was taken by an Anglo-Indian Henry Vivian Derozio. He was influenced by the French Great Revolution. He asked the students to think and take decisions in their own rational and completely free manner. He exhorted them to love freedom, equality, and truth. Derozio and his followers were symbols of the latest thought-current in Bengal. In terms of thought, they were completely revolutionary and true patriots. Because of his revolutionary ideas, Derozio had to lose his job in 1831. Very soon, at the age of 22, he also died. A prominent leader of the national movement, Surendra Nath Banerjee, honored Derozio's followers by calling them 'pioneers of Bengal civilization', 'fathers of our race', etc.

questions.question_text: In which of the following regulations was the Sati practice declared illegal in the British India era?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- There was an inhuman practice prevalent in India which was called Sati practice, in which a woman used to burn alive with the corpse of her husband after his death. Whatever may have been the reason for the origin of this practice, but this act was inhuman and barbaric. Possibly some women used to burn willingly, but many were forced to burn due to social inequality, fear of relatives, and jealousy, etc. At that time, liberal Indians like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Devendranath Tagore, etc., expressed their views in protest against it and demanded to declare this practice illegal. Bentinck collected facts on this subject and consulted with government employees of all classes, and when he was satisfied that there was no risk of rebellion by ending this evil, he declared Sati practice illegal under Regulation XVII in 1829 AD. Initially, this law was only for Bengal, but in 1850 AD it was implemented in the provinces of Madras and Bombay as well.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is untrue regarding Ram Mohan Roy?

options.A: He translated the Upanishads from Sanskrit to Bengali
options.C: He supported constitutional movement as a method for the attainment of India's freedom
options.D: His funeral took place in Calcutta

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004, 2008 Explanation- The funeral of Raja Ram Mohan Roy did not take place in Calcutta but on 27 December 1833 in Bristol (England). Raja Ram Mohan Roy translated the Upanishads from Sanskrit to Bengali and also wrote 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' in Persian. He supported constitutional movement as a method for the attainment of India's freedom. In the political field, his view was that British empire is a reality and he believed that it would act as a rejuvenating force in the development of India. In fact, he was the pioneer of the liberal thinkers of the nineteenth century. According to him, India would need British rule for many years so that the country would not suffer much when it strives for its political independence, i.e., according to him, only under the British can India achieve civil and political freedom and can obtain its place in the civilized world.

questions.question_text: In which year was legal permission for widow-remarriage obtained through the Widow Remarriage Act?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar made every possible effort for women's upliftment. His main work in this direction was to encourage widow-remarriage. In 1855 AD, he raised his voice in favor of widow-remarriage and demanded the government to make a law for this. His effort was successful, and the Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856 AD during the time of Lord Canning. The first legal widow-remarriage in India took place in Calcutta on 7 December 1856 under the inspiration and supervision of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. He also strongly opposed the practice of child marriage and polygamy. For women's education, he established 35 girls' schools through his own efforts. From the perspective of the secretary of Bethune School, he also contributed to the progress of higher education for women. For this reason, after Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the prominent name among the primary and contemporary social reformers of Bengal is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

questions.question_text: Indicate the correct chronological order of the following movements using the code given below- 1. Prarthana Samaj 2. Arya Samaj 3. Brahmo Samaj 4. Ramakrishna Mission Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Brahmo Samaj was established in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta. Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867 AD in Maharashtra by Mahadev Govind Ranade, Atmaram Pandurang, etc. Arya Samaj was established in 1875 AD in Bombay by Swami Dayanand Saraswati. 'Satyarth Prakash' is his famous book. Ramakrishna Mission was established in 1897 AD in Baranagar (Kolkata) by Swami Vivekananda, the disciple of Swami Ramakrishna Paramahansa.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and find the correct answer from the code given below- List-I List-II A. Ahmadiyya Movement (1) Waliullah B. Deoband Movement (2) Shibli Nomani C. Nadwat-ul-Ulama (3) Muhammad Qasim Nanotvi D. Ahl-i-Hadith Movement (4) Mirza Ghulam Ahmad Qadiyani Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Ahmadiyya Movement - Mirza Ghulam Ahmad Qadiyani, Deoband Movement - Mo. Qasim Nanotvi, Nadwat-ul-Ulama - Shibli Nomani, Ahl-i-Hadith Movement - Waliullah.

questions.question_text: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the author of whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004, 2008 Explanation- Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Persian language newspaper 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' (Gift to Monotheists) was published. Brahmo Samaj brought out various journals and newspapers from time to time, such as Raja Ram Mohan Roy's 'Sambad Kaumudi' and 'Mirat-ul-Akhbar', etc. Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Brahmo Samaj gave new life to Indian society in all spheres of life. From the religious point of view, Brahmo Samaj based its thoughts on the Upanishads and the Vedas, stating that God is one, idol worship and rituals are useless, and social evils have no relation to religion. He was the first to give India the idea of interpreting religion on the basis of logic. For this reason, in attaining its original form, the general Brahmo Samaj even refused to accept the Vedas as the final divine message.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book 'Bhrantivilas'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- 'Bhrantivilas' (1863 AD) is a work of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. This work is a translation of Shakespeare's 'Comedy of Errors' in Bengali language. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar gave birth to a new method for learning Sanskrit. He wrote Bengali, which is used even in modern times, and contributed to the development of modern prose style through his works. In 1855, he raised his voice in favor of widow-remarriage and demanded the government to make a law for this. In 1856, the Widow Remarriage Act was made. The first legal widow-remarriage in India took place in Calcutta on 7 December 1856 under his inspiration and supervision. He also strongly opposed the practice of child marriage and polygamy. For women's education, he established 25 girls' schools through his own efforts. From the perspective of the secretary of Bethune School, he also contributed to the progress of higher education for women. For this reason, after Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the prominent name among the primary and contemporary social reformers of Bengal is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

questions.question_text: Raja Ram Mohan Roy's organization 'Brahmo Samaj' was opposed to child marriage. Despite this, one of his followers married his own daughter in minority, paving the way for the disintegration of the organization. Who was that follower?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Devendranath Tagore, as the sole trustee, expelled Keshab Chandra Sen from the position of Acharya in 1865. Keshab Chandra Sen formed a new Brahmo Samaj, which began to be called Adi Brahmo Samaj. This emphasized on, in addition to reforms, women's liberation, spread of education, distribution of cheap literature, prohibition of alcohol, and donating. In 1878, another split occurred in this. Keshab Chandra Sen and other Brahmo Samajists used to propagate for minimum age. Acharya Keshab Chandra Sen, violating the Brahmo Marriage Act 1872, married his minor daughter (13-year-old daughter) to the minor King of Cooch Behar with full Vedic rituals. It was said that this is all "God's command." Most of Keshab Chandra Sen's followers were saddened and formed a new Brahmo Samaj, 'Sadharan Brahmo Samaj'. Soon, Keshab Chandra's Brahmo Samaj got lost in the obscurity of history's darkness.

questions.question_text: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin is-

options.B: A writing in which Sati practice is condemned
options.C: A writing in which women's education is supported
