questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- In Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Persian language book Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, propaganda against idol worship has been done and support for monotheism has been expressed. At the time when young Bengalis were getting attracted towards Christianity, at that time Raja Ram Mohan Roy appeared as the protector of Hindu religion. On one hand, he protected the Hindu religion against missionary propagandists. On the other hand, he also attempted to remove the lies and superstitions that had entered Hindu religion. At the age of 15, he criticized idol worship and attempted to prove his side through Vedic texts. He reinterpreted the principles of Hindu religion and searched for enough base from the Upanishads for his service to humanity. He rejected Christianity and did not even accept the divinity of Jesus Christ. However, he definitely accepted European humanism.

questions.question_text: What was the main objective of the Aligarh Movement among Indian Muslims?

options.C: Keeping friendship between Muslims and the British strong
options.D: Giving strength to nascent nationalism in India

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Sir Syed Ahmed Khan attempted to remove social evils in Islam. He attempted to make the outlook of Muslims modern. His effort was that Muslim people should accept the facts of the British government and start serving under it. He was very successful in his effort. He also called the slavery system against Islam. However, his most important work was the 'commentary on the Quran' in which he criticized traditional commentators and expressed his thoughts in the light of contemporary scientific knowledge. He emphasized on the study of the Quran and said that the interpretation of divine knowledge should be through divine work, which is in front of everyone.

questions.question_text: Dnyan Prakash newspaper relates to-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Dnyan-Prakash newspaper is the newspaper of the Paramhansa Mandali group. Bengal Gazette, James Augustus Hicky started, but he exposed the faults of the Governor General and judges of the Supreme Court. Later, Calcutta Gazette in 1785 AD, Oriental Magazine of Calcutta in 1788, Madras Courier in 1789 AD, Bombay Herald started publication. The weekly newspaper Samachar Darpan, started by Marshman in 1818, continued to be published for a sufficient time. In 1821 AD, through the encouragement of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, a weekly newspaper Sambad Kaumudi started. Raja Ram Mohan Roy himself started the publication of Mirat-ul-Akhbar in Persian language and Brahmanical Magazine in English. The first and major newspaper printed in English by Indians was Hindu-Patriot. In Bengali language newspapers, Amrita Bazar Patrika, Som Prakash, Bangabasi, and Sanjivani were prominent.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book titled 'The Precepts of Jesus, The Guide to Peace and Happiness'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – In 1820, Ram Mohan Roy created the book titled 'The Precepts of Jesus' and in 1821 'The Guide to Peace and Happiness'.

questions.question_text: Who was the first president of the Depressed Classes Mission Society formed in 1906?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation- The Depressed Classes Mission Society formed in 1906 was established by B.R. Shinde, but its first president was Chandavarkar.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists - List-I (Reform Organization) List-II (Place where they were established) A. Arya Samaj 1. Mumbai B. Arya Mahila Samaj 2. Pune C. Mohammedan Literary Society 3. Kolkata D. Veda Samaj 4. Chennai Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation – (A) Arya Samaj - Mumbai (B) Arya Mahila Samaj - Pune (C) Mohammedan Literary Society - Kolkata (D) Veda Samaj - Chennai

questions.question_text: What did the India Act V of 1843 make illegal?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation– Governor General Ellenborough ended slavery through the 5th rule of the India Act of 1843 AD.

questions.question_text: Match the following and select the correct answer from the code given below: A. Raja Ram Mohan Roy 1. Tattvabodhini Sabha B. Devendranath Tagore 2. Atmiya Sabha C. Vivekananda 3. Ramakrishna Mission D. Atmaram Pandurang 4. Prarthana Samaj Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : To propagate the monotheistic doctrine of Hindu religion, Raja Ram Mohan Roy established 'Atmiya Sabha' (1815-19). In 1828, he established 'Brahmo Sabha', which later became prevalent as Brahmo Samaj. After the death of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Dwarkanath Tagore and Pandit Ramchandra Vidya Vagish, who were disciples of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, managed it for about 10 years. Subsequently, as the eldest son of Dwarkanath Tagore, Devendranath Tagore, they got a true leader. Before coming into Brahmo Samaj, the 'Tattvaranjini Sabha' which Devendranath Tagore had formed in Jorasanko (Kolkata), this later came to be called 'Tattvabodhini Sabha'. Swami Vivekananda established 'Ramakrishna Mission' in 1896. 'Prarthana Samaj' was established in 1867 AD by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang and Mahadev Govind Ranade.

questions.question_text: J. E. D. Bethune was deeply associated with:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : J. E. D. Bethune (J.E.D. Bethune) was deeply associated with women's education. He was the one who did the real work in the context of women's education. He was the chairman of the Education Council. He established a girls' school in Kolkata in 1849.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not related to Prarthana Samaj?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867 in Maharashtra with the inspiration of Keshab Chandra Sen. Its prominent founders were Dr. Atmaram Pandurang and Mahadev Govind Ranade. Ranade is mentioned as a 'pioneer of cultural resurgence in Western India'. R.G. Bhandarkar was another prominent leader of it. Worship (Prarthana) and social reform were the two main parts of this samaj. Ranade also started a purity movement in which movements were run against dance and alcohol consumption by prostitutes, and against the extravagant spending in marriages. Devendranath Tagore had established 'Tattvabodhini Sabha' and he was an important leader of Brahmo Samaj.

questions.question_text: Who was the founding president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Mahatma Gandhi established the Harijan Sevak Sangh. Its main office was in Delhi and it had branches in all provinces. Shri Ghanshyamdas Birla was its president and Shri A.V. Thakkar was the general secretary. Mahadev Desai: Remained secretary of Mahatma Gandhi for 25 years and he participated in all movements from Champaran Satyagraha (1917) to Quit India Movement (1942). On the occasion of the Quit India Movement, he was arrested along with Gandhi ji and kept imprisoned in Aga Khan Palace, where he died on 15 August 1942. B.R. Ambedkar established 'Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha' in 1924 and established Samaj Samata Sangh in 1927. He was also elected as the Law Minister in the interim government and chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question_text: 'Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha' was established in 1851 to initiate social-religious reforms among Parsis. Whose name is not in the list of its founders?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The effect of Indian resurgence fell on the Parsi society, and as a result of its influence, in 1851 AD, some English-educated Parsis formed 'Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha', whose purpose was to reform the social condition of Parsis and to regain the ancient purity of the Parsi religion. The leaders of this movement were - Naoroji Furdoonji, Dadabhai Naoroji, S.S. Bengalee, and R.K. Cama. To convey the message of this Sabha to the Parsis, a journal 'Rast Goftar' (Truth Teller) was run. Among the options given above, Shibli Nomani was not among the founders of 'Mazdayasan Sabha'.

questions.question_text: The Act that enabled converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property was -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - By the end of the 18th century, Western culture had started spreading rapidly in India. In this context, the Charter of 1813 AD was passed. Under this act, Christian missionaries got permission to propagate religion in India. The next link to this was Section 21 of 1850, in which there was a provision that converts to Christianity should not be deprived of inheritance from their ancestral property. This act was a deep blow to the Indian social system. This also proved to be an important reason for the Great Rebellion of 1857.

questions.question_text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale established which of the following?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a renowned educationist, humanist, social reformer, and a great patriot. He was associated with the moderate politics of the Congress. In 1905 AD, Gokhale established the "Servants of India Society" (India Servants Society). The main objective of this organization was to help people during famine, epidemic, or any such disaster and to protect their life and property. Gokhale presided over the annual session of the Congress held in Varanasi in 1905 AD and supported the Swadeshi proposal. He died in 1915 AD. Tilak called him 'Diamond of India'.

questions.question_text: 'Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha' was related to?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– In 1851 AD, some English-educated Parsis formed the Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha, whose objective was to reform the social condition of Parsis and to regain the ancient purity of the Parsi religion. Its leaders were- Naoroji Furdoonji, Dadabhai Naoroji, and R.K. Cama, S.S. Bengalee.

questions.question_text: In India, the women's movement was primarily started with the inspiration of whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation– Ramabai Ranade was a great female social worker and social reformer of Maharashtra. She started the women's movement in India. In 1909, she established the Pune Seva Sadan for the education of widows and other women. She also established Mukti Sadan to provide shelter to helpless women and a rescue home, Kripa Sadan, for fallen women.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the 'Calcutta Unitarian Society'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation – Raja Ram Mohan Roy is considered the pioneer of the reformist movement in India. After working for the East India Company from 1805 AD to 1814 AD, he jumped into public life and engaged in social reform. He led a powerful movement against the Sati practice and kept it continuing until it was declared illegal in 1829 AD. He established the Atmiya Sabha in 1815 AD, Vedanta College in 1816 AD, and 'Unitarian Society' in 1821 AD. On 20 August 1828, he laid the foundation of Brahmo Samaj.

questions.question_text: Excluding which of the following were all great journalists of the nineteenth century?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Durgadas was a famous Rathore chieftain of Marwar, not a journalist of the nineteenth century, whereas Shishir Kumar Ghosh, James Augustus Hicky, and Kasturi Ranga Ayyangar were great journalists of the 19th century.

questions.question_text: The early orientalist William Jones in India was:

options.D: Officer in the British East India Company

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - William Jones was born in 1746 AD in England. In 1770 AD, he translated the biography of Nadir Shah (which was written in Persian) into English. In 1774 AD, he started his life as a barrister. Jones came to India in 1783 as a judge of the Federal Court of India and was given the title of 'Sir'. In 1784 AD, he established the Asiatic Society of Bengal and remained its president for life (until 1794 AD).

questions.question_text: In the twentieth century, many organizations were made by women and for women. What is the correct chronological order of the establishment of the following organizations? (i) All India Women's Conference (iv) National Council of Women Select your answer from the code below: (ii) Madras Women's Indian Association (iii) Mahila Rashtriya Sangha
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation – (i) All India Women's Conference – Established by Margaret Cousins in 1927. (ii) Madras Women's Indian Association – In 1917, established in Adyar, Madras by Margaret Cousins' cousin, Jeena Raja Dasa. (iii) Mahila Rashtriya Sangha – Mahila Rashtriya Sangha was the first organization established with the objective of involving women in political activity in India. It was formed in 1928 in Bengal Presidency, British India, by Latika Ghosh on the responsibility of leader Subhash Chandra Bose. (iv) National Council of Women – A statutory body formed on 10 January 1992 under an act passed by the Indian Parliament.

questions.question_text: Who established the Central Mohammedan National Association?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, under the influence of Theodore Beck, became distant from the national movement and, while non-cooperating with the Congress, he also established a reactionary organization in opposition to the Congress. Under his influence, the 'Central National Mohammedan Association' also non-cooperated with the Congress. In 1887, he established the Mohammedan Educational Congress, whose objective was to stop educated Muslims from joining the Indian National Congress.

questions.question_text: Who is known as the 'Father of Muslim Renaissance in Bengal'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– The father of Muslim renaissance in Bengal was Abdul Latif. In 1863 AD, he established the 'Mohammedan Literary and Scientific Society' in Kolkata. Along with this, the National Mohammedan Association was also established in Kolkata in 1878 AD by Sir Ameer Ali. The objective of these organizations was to create awareness among Muslims regarding Western education and loyalty towards the British rule.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first Indian who wrote English poetry?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– First of all, Kashiprasad Ghosh composed the first Indian work in English. Kashiprasad Ghosh wrote the first Indian English poetry. His famous poem titled 'The Shair' (The Boatman's Song) was published in 1835.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Bengali plays was directed against the polygamy practice?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– Like widow remarriage, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's contribution regarding polygamy was significant. Giving an account of the historical development of the Kulins, he attempted to prove that the practice of polygamy among the Kulins is not according to scriptures. In Bengal, the family of a daughter used to be exploited due to the practice of Kulin marriage, and innocent girls often did not get the opportunity to see their husbands. Bengali playwrights played a great role in shattering this belief of society. For public awareness, the play titled 'Kulin Kulasarvasva' was written against the polygamy practice.

questions.question_text: Which Bengali writer first suggested that Hindi should be adopted as the national language of India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– Bhudev Mukhopadhyay suggested the use of Hindi in place of Persian in the courts. He wrote in Social Essays, most people in India are capable of conversation in Hindi, therefore, in the meetings of pure Indians, Hindi should be used instead of English. He first gave a speech in Hindi in the Congress committee in 1919.

questions.question_text: Who among the following prepared the draft of the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– In 1856 AD, the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was made, in which many reforms were brought, i.e., compared to the past, the current marriage is easy and comfortable. At this time, the Governor General was Lord Canning (1856-62). This act was drafted by Lord Dalhousie.

questions.question_text: Who authored the book titled 'Gulamgiri'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009, 2011 Explanation– Mahatma Jyotiba Phule established the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 AD, through which he worked for the upliftment of Dalits and lower castes. Jyotiba Phule emphasized the need to protect the lower castes from hypocritical Brahmins and their opportunist religious texts through his books like 'Gulamgiri' (1872) and 'Sarvajanik Satya Dharma', and organizations like Satyashodhak Samaj. Deenbandhu Sarvajanik Sabha was another one of his social organizations.

questions.question_text: 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin', a writing by Ram Mohan Roy is –
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The reform movement that started from Bengal was led by Raja Ram Mohan. For this reason, Ram Mohan Roy is called the pioneer of India's renaissance, initiator of reform movements, and the leader of modern India. Raja Ram Mohan Roy's first treatise 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' was published in 1809, in which he opposed idol worship and declared monotheism as the root of all religions. Regarding this treatise, Tara Chand writes – In the campaign for truth-seeking, he created 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin'.

questions.question_text: Who has called whom the spiritual father of Indian nationalism?

options.C: Bipin Chandra Pal – Swami Dayanand Saraswati

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Swami Vivekananda (1863-1902) was a Vedantic scholar and Hindu religious preacher of Bengal. He established Ramakrishna Mission in 1897. He emphasized on the ideals of Karma Yoga, Raja Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, writings of East and West, and social service and self-sacrifice. Subhash Chandra Bose has called Swami Vivekananda the spiritual father of nationalism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following published translations of Vedic texts in Bengali language?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Raja Ram Mohan Roy criticized idol worship and, with proof, expressed this view that all the ancient original religious texts of Hindus have preached for one God. In support of this claim, he published translations of the Vedas and five main Upanishads in Bengali.

questions.question_text: Who among the following said, "India must be one again and must conquer the whole world with its power"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– Swami Vivekananda was born in 1863 in a Kayastha family in Bengal. He established Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 and remained engaged in social service works and was a great Hindu preacher. Swami Vivekananda said, "India must be one again and must conquer the whole world with its power."

questions.question_text: The main feature of Indian cultural renaissance was:

options.C: Research-based study of past history and archaeology
options.D: Development of novels instead of other forms of writing

questions.explanation: The main feature of Indian cultural renaissance is considered to be the birth of new regional language. Because due to the renaissance, various journals started from every corner of India and people chose newspapers and journals as a medium to reach their voices against the British

questions.question_text: In which of the following places was the headquarters of 'Theosophical Society' established?
questions.explanation: The headquarters of 'Theosophical Society' was in Adyar. The Theosophical Society was established in 1875 AD in New York by Madam H.P. Blavatsky, who was a Russian woman. In 1879 AD, its head office was shifted from New York to Bombay. In 1882 AD, she again established the international headquarters of her society in Adyar near Madras

questions.question_text: Who among the following ended the Sati practice?
questions.explanation: During the time of Governor General Lord William Bentinck, the Sati practice was closed through regulation 17 (XVII) of 1829 AD. Raja Ram Mohan Roy had a significant contribution in getting this regulation passed. Radhakant Deb established the Dharma Sabha in 1830 AD and supported the Sati practice

questions.question_text: Who first suggested that Sanskrit, Latin, and Greek are related to the same language family?
questions.explanation: Sir William Jones first suggested that Sanskrit, Latin, and Greek are related to the same language family. To verify his suggestion, he made the clear closeness in words of languages like ancient Persian, Sanskrit, Greek, Latin, and German the basis. Some examples of this are as follows Ancient Persian Sanskrit Greek Latin German English Pitar Pitar Pater Pater Vater Father Matar Matar Meter Mater Mutter Mother Name Nama Onoma Nomen Namen Name GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018

questions.question_text: Which practice was declared illegal (unlawful) in India by the India Act V of 1843?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– In 1843, 'Slavery' practice was declared illegal (unlawful) by India Act V. At this time, the Governor General of India was Lord Ellenborough (1842-1844 AD). The tenure of Lord Ellenborough is called the period of 'policy of masterly inactivity'. GIC Lecturer Exam, 2018

questions.question_text: 1860 AD Kuka movement was started by–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– The Kuka movement started in 1860 AD by Ram Singh. The Kuka movement was a religious movement initially, whose objective was to remove evils prevalent in Sikh religion.

questions.question_text: 'Hindu Widow Remarriage Act' was passed?
questions.explanation: Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was passed on 26 July 1856 AD. Through this act, Hindu widows got legal recognition for remarriage. This act was drafted by Lord Dalhousie

questions.question_text: During the Quit India Movement, parallel governments were established in which of the following periods for the longest duration?
questions.explanation: During the Quit India Movement of 1942, parallel governments were formed in several parts of the country. Parallel governments were formed under the leadership of Chittu Pandey in Ballia, as a national government in Tamluk (Midnapore, W. Bengal) and Satara (Maharashtra) from mid-1943 to 1945 AD. In Satara, the government was formed under the name of 'Prati Sarkar' (Parallel Government) for the longest time, in which leaders like Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil had a major role. Its main activities included the organization of Gandhi marriages, anti-liquor campaigns, establishment of rural libraries, and the declaration of freedom against colonial rule, etc

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was passed in the special session of Congress in Calcutta (1920), the proposal for the Non-Cooperation Movement was confirmed in the annual session of Congress held in Nagpur in December, 1920. The Non-Cooperation Movement was started by Gandhi ji on 1st August, 1920. In this movement, Gandhi ji appealed to the people to ♦ Non-cooperate with the unjust system, i.e., the evil system. ♦ Calling the Indian administrative system of the British (British) evil, Gandhi removed the fear of 'terror of law' from the hearts of the people. ♦ Gandhi ji asked to go to jail fearlessly, which he used to call the Maharaja's hotel (His Majesty's hotel). Therefore, the Non-Cooperation Movement was indeed the first mass movement of India. Its initiation was a revolutionary step, which brought fundamental changes in the form and nature of the Congress. Now the Congress became a popular democratic all-India organization and a medium of non-violent rebellion against foreign rule in India.

questions.question_text: Which Sikh patriot was tried and hanged by the British government in 1940 for killing Sir Michael O'Dwyer, who was involved in the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.explanation: On 13th April 1919, in the Jallianwala Bagh of Amritsar, the English General Sir Michael O'Dwyer opened fire without any prior notice or warning on the crowd present at the meeting place, in which about 1000 people were killed. According to the government report, about 379 people were killed and 1200 injured in the firing which lasted for 10 minutes. On the basis of the Hunter Committee report, Michael O'Dwyer was proven innocent. The government removed him from the army and the British newspapers honored Michael O'Dwyer by calling him the 'Lion of the Empire'. When Michael O'Dwyer went to his home country (London), Udham Singh changed his name to 'Ram Mohammad Singh Azad' and killed Michael O'Dwyer in London in March 1940. Udham Singh was hanged for this crime. In the year 1974 AD, the ashes of Udham Singh were brought to India Manjit Singh Kashid was a friend and associate of revolutionary Sardar Udham Singh. Instructions– The Indian National Congress was not just a party, but a movement. It included people and groups with wide-ranging political and ideological perspectives. It was the organization of the mainstream, but not the only stream. It is clear that non-Congress movements were never seen as parallel streams, as some people have said. Although they were outside the Congress, most of them were not really separate from it and at no stage did they become an alternative to the Congress. The only ones about which it can be said that they created an alternative stream of politics were the streams of communal and casteist movements, which were neither national nor anti-imperialist. Between 1919 and 1942, apart from countless mass movements, many Satyagraha campaigns were launched. This movement brought a new type of politics before the people in many forms and phases. It did not shake their religion, caste, and place-based pre-modern consciousness or loyalty to the traditional ruler. Although in some cases caste structures were used to bring discipline in some movements in villages, yet the goals and demands of the movement had nothing to do with caste. The social and religious reform movements that arose in the 19th century to prevent the colonialization of Indian culture also merged into the national movement. As a mass movement, the Indian national movement was able to use diverse talents, energies, and the capabilities of people on a large scale to fight against British rule, and at the same time, emphasis was also placed on constructive programs. 4. Which of the following was not an alternative stream of the movement, but was definitely parallel to it? (A) Ghadar Movement (B) Civil Disobedience Movement (C) Indian National Army (D) Royal Indian Navy Revolt Select the most appropriate answer from the options given below: (a) Only (A) and (B) (b) Only (A), (C) and (D) (c) Only (B) and (D) (d) Only (B), (C) and (D) NTA UGC NET/JRF Dec 2020/June 2021 Shift-I Ans. (b) : The Indian National Congress played an important role in the Indian freedom movement. The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 AD at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay (Mumbai). It was not just a political organization but also a mass movement. In which people and groups with different political and ideological perspectives were included. Congress was the organization of the mainstream. But not the only stream. The Civil Disobedience Movement was also an organization of the mainstream, some scholars believed that non-Congress movements were never included in the parallel stream, although they were outside the Congress and could not become an alternative to the Congress even at the ideological level. Only communal and casteist movements created an alternative stream of politics, which were neither national nor anti-imperialist, but were movements done against the violation of their rights, but some later movements like Ghadar Movement, National Army Movement, Royal Indian Navy Movement etc. were not alternative streams but were definitely parallel because their opposition was also against colonial rule.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a non-Congress movement?

options.C: All India Depressed Classes Mission Society of India

questions.explanation: All India Depressed Classes Mission Society of India was a non-Congress movement. Whose main objective was to create awareness among the Dalit castes about their rights. This society was established by V.R. Shinde (Vitthal Ramji Shinde) in 1906 AD in Maharashtra. The first president of this society was made N.G. Chandavarkar. Due to his efforts, the first All India Dalit Class Conference was organized in 1918, in which the first All India Anti-Untouchability Declaration letter was issued. The Extremists (Charampanthi) were related to the Congress. In 1907, in the Surat session of the Congress, the Congress was divided into two parts - Moderates (Narampanthi) and Extremists (Charampanthi) The most prominent leaders of the Extremists were Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh. The All India Trade Union Congress was founded in 1920 AD in Bombay by N.M. Joshi. Its first president was Lala Lajpat Rai. In 1936, the first All India Kisan Sabha was formed in Lucknow. On 11 April 1936, the conference of the All India Kisan Sabha was held, whose president was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati. Before this, Kisan Sabhas were formed in Bengal, Punjab, U.P., and A.P.

questions.question_text: What kind of people were not associated with the Indian National Movement?
questions.explanation: The beginning of the Indian National Movement is considered to be from the formation of the Congress in 1885 AD. People and groups with wide-ranging diverse political and ideological perspectives were included in the Indian National Movement, but imperialist people were not associated with this movement. Moderates played an important role in the Indian National Movement. They criticized the British government in their speeches and sent their representatives to different parts of the country for public opinion gathering. In 1920, M.N. Roy and some other Indian immigrants living in Tashkent formed the Indian Communist Party formation. They remained continuously active in the national movement. The Swarajists also had a prominent role in the Indian National Movement. On 1 January 1923, Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party. They did many works for self-governance and political independence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Satyagraha movements was not a part of the Indian National Congress's program?
questions.explanation: Mahad Sweets Tank (Mahad Water Reservoir) Satyagraha was an effective Satyagraha done in 1927 under the leadership of Bhimrao Ambedkar at a place called Mahad in Raigad district of Maharashtra state to give Dalits the right to drink and use water from the public Chavdar lake. This Satyagraha was not a part of the Indian National Congress's program In March 1919, the Rowlatt Act was passed, Indians called it 'Black Act' and opposed it. In this Act, a provision was made that the magistrate could arrest any suspicious person and put them in jail. In August 1920, the Non-Cooperation Movement was started by Gandhi ji. In August 1942 AD, the Quit India Movement happened, this is also called the 'August Revolution'.

questions.question_text: In which year did women participate in the activities of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Women participated in the activities of the Indian National Congress for the first time in the fifth session in 1889. The chairmanship of this session was done by Sir William Wedderburn in Bombay. In this session, a resolution for 21-year-old voting rights was passed. After this, in 1890, in the sixth session, the first female graduate of Calcutta University, ''Kadambini Ganguly'' also addressed. Mrs. Annie Besant, Sarojini Naidu, and Nalini Sen Gupta presided over the Indian National Congress respectively in 1917 (Calcutta), 1925 (Kanpur), and 1933 (Calcutta)

questions.question_text: On whose suggestion were Indians kept out of the Simon Commission?
questions.explanation: The 1919 Act had a provision for its review after 10 years, but due to the general elections in Britain in 1929 AD, the government announced it on 8 November 1927 AD itself. 7 members of the British Parliament were included in this commission. Among these, Simon of the Liberal Party was made the president, Conservative party's Batham and Strachey, in the House of Commons, Lane Fox and Cadogan, and Labour party's Attlee and Vernon Hartshorn were other members. All members of the commission were European. It is noteworthy that on the suggestion of Lord Irwin, Indians were kept out of the Simon Commission

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in 1885 AD?
questions.explanation: The first session of the Congress was held on 28-31 December 1885 AD at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay. Initially, its name was ''Indian National Union'' but on the suggestion of Dadabhai Naoroji, it was changed to ''Indian National Congress''. Initially, this session was to be held in Pune, but due to the plague, its location was changed to Bombay. Its chairmanship was done by W.C. Bonnerjee (Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee)

questions.question_text: Which of the following was closely associated with the 'Indian Civil Liberties Union'?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru formed the first human rights organization in India, Indian Civil Liberties Union (ICLU) in Bombay in 1936. While inaugurating the Indian Civil Liberties Union, he said that the idea behind its formation was the right to oppose the government

questions.question_text: In the second Round Table Conference, by whom was Smt. Sarojini Naidu appointed as a member and participated?
questions.explanation: The second Round Table Conference ran in St. James Palace (London) from 7 September 1931 AD to 1 December 1931 AD. Gandhi ji was the only representative of Congress in the second Round Table Conference. Sarojini Naidu also went to participate in it as a member of the Government of India, along with her Annie Besant was also there. She represented Indian women. Madan Mohan Malviya went as a representative of the Nationalist party

questions.question_text: Which of the following called the Indian National Congress a 'Safety Valve Theory'?
questions.explanation: Various scholars have expressed their opinion on the establishment of the Indian National Congress. Lala Lajpat Rai gave the safety valve theory in his book ''Young India: An Interpretation and a History of the Nationalist Movement from Within'' and he has written that the main reason for the establishment of the ''Indian National Congress'' was that the desire of the founders was to save the British Empire from crumbling. Hume's biographer Wedderburn wrote, "There is a need for a Safety Valve to save from the growing forces of discontent in India and there can be no other thing better than the Congress movement to be a safety valve."

questions.question_text: The Harcourt Butler Committee appointed in 1927 recommended:

options.A: To grant complete autonomy to the princely states.
options.B: High level and more extensive recruitment of Indians in public services.
options.C: Protection of princely states through British paramountcy.
options.D: Official assistance to the sufferers in case of famine.

questions.explanation: In 1927, the British government Harcourt Butler Committee recommended the protection of princely states through British paramountcy. This commission clarified the relations between Indian princely states and the British government and emphasized the protection of princely states

questions.question_text: Which statement/statements is/are correct in the context of the Non-Cooperation Movement? (1) Initially, Lala Lajpat Rai was against Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement. (2) With the cooperation of Jamnalal and Motilal Nehru, Lala Lajpat Rai founded the 'Swaraj Party'. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: The opposition to the Non-Cooperation Movement was initially done by Surendranath Banerjee, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai, C.R. Das, Mohammad Ali Jinnah, etc. But with the support of Motilal Nehru and Ali Brothers, the proposal of the Non-Cooperation Movement was accepted. After the start of this movement, the Gandhian phase of the national movement started. In the December 1920 Nagpur session, Lala Lajpat Rai and C.R. Das withdrew their opposition The 'Swaraj Party' was founded by Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das. Whereas Lala Lajpat Rai had supported the formation of the Swaraj Party. Therefore, statement (2) is incorrect.

questions.question_text: (1) This was a special session of the Congress to endorse the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. (2) It was presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Which of the above statement/statements is/are correct? Consider the following statements in the context of Karachi Session 1931:
questions.explanation: In 1931 AD, the 45th session of the Congress was held in Karachi. This conference was presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. This was a special session of the Congress to endorse the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. In this session itself, Gandhi ji said that 'Gandhi can die but Gandhism cannot'. In this session, socialist elements were adopted for the development of India

questions.question_text: Who founded the 'Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company' during the Swadeshi Movement?
questions.explanation: During the Swadeshi Movement, Chidambaram Pillai founded the 'Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company' and 'Bengal Chemicals Swadeshi Stores' was founded by P.C. Ray Special Facts ♦ 'Vande Mataram' became the title song of the Indian National Movement during the Swadeshi Movement. ♦ British journalist H.W. Nevinson was associated with the Swadeshi Movement. ♦ 'Swadeshi Vastu Pracharini Sabha' for the promotion and propagation of Swadeshi was founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Maharashtra.

questions.question_text: In which year and at which place was the first session of the All India Kisan Sabha held?
questions.explanation: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in 1936 AD in Lucknow by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati Special Facts ♦ Due to the efforts of Gauri Shankar Mishra, Indra Narayan Dwivedi, and Madan Mohan Malviya, the U.P. Kisan Sabha was established in Awadh in February 1918. Baba Ramchandra, Chhinguri Pal Singh, and Durga Pal Singh had an important role in making the U.P. Kisan Sabha powerful. ♦ In 1920 AD, Baba Ramchandra met Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra asked Jawaharlal and Gauri Shankar to observe the misery of the farmers. In 1920, the U.P. Kisan Movement joined with the Non-Cooperation Movement. ♦ On 17 October 1920, due to the efforts of Baba Ramchandra, 'Awadh Kisan Sabha' was formed. Jawaharlal Nehru, Gauri Shankar, Mata Badal Pandey, Devnarayan Pandey, Kedarnath worked to make this organization strong.

questions.question_text: Who led an intense movement against Begar and Forest Laws in the hills of Kumaon and Garhwal during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: During the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1921 AD, Hargovind Pant and Badridutt Pandey led an intense movement against Begar and Forest Laws in the hills of Kumaon and Garhwal

questions.question_text: Which British Prime Minister started the "Communal Award"?
questions.explanation: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award on 16 August 1932. This announcement was made during the second Round Table Conference due to communal deadlock. Under this, separate election arrangements were made for Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans, and women, and at the same time, Harijans were considered separate from the Hindu community and they were given the right to separate elections. In reality, the Communal Award was a trick of the British, whose sole purpose was to divide various sections with the aim of weakening the national movement in India and to maintain British rule

questions.question_text: Which movement was suspended after the mob violence in Chauri Chaura, Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji started the Non-Cooperation Movement on 1 August 1920, but on 5 February 1922 AD, due to firing on farmers at a place named Chauri-Chaura in Gorakhpur district of United Province, some mob set the police station on fire, due to which 21 policemen including a station in-charge died. Gandhi ji was very hurt by this incident and suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events of the National Movement in chronological order and select the correct option with the help of the code given below:
questions.explanation: The correct chronology of the following events Formation of Swaraj Party – 1923 AD. Resignation by Congress Ministers – 1939 AD. Wavell Plan – 1945 AD. Muslim League's Direct Action – 1946 AD.

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the first session of ''All India Trade Union Congress''?
questions.explanation: On the initiative of Diwan Chaman Lall and B.M. Pawar, a conference was called in Bombay on 31 October 1920 under the chairmanship of Lala Lajpat Rai. In this conference, the All India Trade Union Congress (A.I.T.U.C.) was founded. Lala Lajpat Rai was elected the first president of this organization and Diwan Chaman Lall was made the general secretary

questions.question_text: Which of the following freedom fighters did not participate in the Kakori conspiracy?
questions.explanation: The revolutionaries of the Hindustan Republican Association successfully looted the 8 Down train going to Kakori on the Saharanpur-Lucknow line. In this connection, 29 revolutionaries were arrested and tried in the Kakori conspiracy case. Among these revolutionaries were Ram Prasad Bismil, Rajendra Lahiri, Ashfaqullah Khan, and Roshan Lal, etc. This incident was executed on 9 August 1925. The name of Rajguru comes in the Lahore Conspiracy and Saunders Murder Case

questions.question_text: Which of the following women did not actively participate in the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: The role of women in the Quit India Movement is a story of their dedication, sacrifice, and patriotism, which has an important place in the history of the fight for achieving Swaraj. Women actively participated in Satyagraha and various activities. They organized meetings and opposed the British Empire through their speeches and took Gandhi ji's 'Do or Die' slogan to every village and spread the message of Quit India to the masses. Although countless women freedom fighters contributed to the Quit India Movement, some important faces like Usha Mehta, Sucheta Kriplani, Aruna Asaf Ali, Sumati Mukherjee, etc., participated enthusiastically. In the above question, Begum Rokeya's character was that of a writer and social worker

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events of the National Movement in chronological order and select the correct option with the help of the code given below:
questions.explanation: Correct chronology of the events of the National Movement (A) Communal Award – 1932 (B) Deliverance Day – 1939 (C) August Offer – 1940 (D) Gandhi-Jinnah Talks – 1944

questions.question_text: Which organization did Indira Gandhi establish at the age of 12?
questions.explanation: At the age of 12, Indira Gandhi (Priyadarshini) formed a Charkha Sangh and Vanar Sena with children, whose purpose was to provide active help in the Civil Disobedience Movement and to take it forward with a solid foundation

questions.question_text: Who took the group to break the salt law to the Marina Beach in Madras?
questions.explanation: Durgabai Deshmukh was born on 15 July 1909 AD in Kakinada of Rajahmundry district of Andhra Pradesh. She used to roam with her mother during the British rule selling Khadi and also used to give speeches in the freedom movement. During Gandhi ji's Salt Satyagraha, she participated with the famous leader T. Prakasham and took the group to break the salt law from Madras to Marina beach and she was also arrested and sent to jail from Akat

questions.question_text: Which of the following was sponsored by the Congress to promote planning as a means of integrated and comprehensive development?

options.B: Resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Program

questions.explanation: In the Haripura session of Congress, Subhash Chandra Bose had said in his presidential speech that the development of India will now be under national planning. In the 1938 session, a rift arose between Gandhi and Netaji regarding the method of achieving independence. This rift widened when Netaji formed the National Planning Committee. Its purpose was to formulate a plan for the economic development of India based on industrialization. This was against Gandhi ji's Charkha policy

questions.question_text: Which of the following movements was a movement based outside India with the goal of achieving independence for India?
questions.explanation: At the end of the 19th century, many Indians had gone to settle in America and Canada. On 1 November 1913 AD, the Ghadar Party was formed in San Francisco city of America. Its founder was Lala Hardayal while the president of this party was Sohan Singh. The purpose of the formation of this party was to create a feeling of rebellion in the Indian army, especially among Sikhs, and to prepare them for the future revolution. This movement was taking the initiative to oppose the English rule from outside India and to liberate India

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress, the party was divided into extremists and moderates?
questions.explanation: In the 1907 Surat session of the Indian National Congress, the differences leading to the separation of Extremists and Moderates had started forming from the Partition of Bengal movement itself, but its immediate cause was that the session should be held in Nagpur and Bal Gangadhar Tilak or Lala Lajpat Rai should become its president and a resolution in full support of Swadeshi boycott movement and national education should be passed. Whereas the Liberals wanted to hold the session in Surat and wanted to make Rash Bihari Ghosh the president, due to which they wanted to forcefully demand the withdrawal of the Swadeshi boycott and national education resolution. Due to this argument, both groups had become aggressive, but this session was calmed down by making Dadabhai Naoroji the president. There was a lot of heated argument regarding the demand for Swaraj in this and fighting started, due to which both wings scattered separately

questions.question_text: Which of the following organization was in strong support of the concept of Akhand Bharat (Undivided India)?
questions.explanation: Azad Muslim Conference was established in 1929 AD. It was established by Allah Bakhsh. This conference was an organization of nationalist Muslims in India. Its purpose was to advocate for complete nationalism and a united India

questions.question_text: The Swaraj Party decided in favor of Council entry because:

options.A: It wanted to gain political experience.
options.B: It wanted to expose the weaknesses of the 1919 Act.
options.C: It wanted to cooperate with the government.
options.D: It wanted facilities from the government.

questions.explanation: On 5 February 1922, the Chauri Chaura incident happened due to which Gandhi ji withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement, from which some leaders were unhappy with Gandhi ji. In December 1922, the Congress session was held in Gaya under the chairmanship of Chittaranjan Das, in which the proposal to enter the Legislative Council was passed. Chittaranjan Das wanted to expose the weaknesses of the government in the Legislative Council, therefore Chittaranjan Das resigned and in January 1923, together with Motilal Nehru, founded the Swaraj Party. In the November 1923 elections, the Swarajists participated and performed well. After the election, the Swarajists did important work in the Central and Provincial Legislative Councils, in which the struggle for the appointment of 'Muddiman Committee' for the investigation of the 1919 Act, getting oppressive laws abolished, etc., are included

questions.question_text: Who presided over the special session of Calcutta (1920) in which the proposal of the Non-Cooperation Movement was passed?
questions.explanation: The special session of Calcutta (1920) was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai. From this platform, the proposal for the Non-Cooperation Movement was accepted. Before starting the movement, Gandhi ji returned the title of Kaiser-e-Hind. Jamnalal Bajaj returned his title of Rai Bahadur. The Non-Cooperation Movement was started by Gandhi ji on 1 August 1920. Unfortunately, the movement was withdrawn due to the Chauri-Chaura incident (Gorakhpur) on 5 February 1922. questions.question_text: Which of the following was not associated with the Leftist movement in India?
questions.explanation: Ram Manohar Lohia was a socialist. People associated with the Leftist movement included P.C. Joshi, Manavendra Nath Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, S.A. Dange, Ghulam Hussain and Singaravelu Chettiar, etc. The use of Left and Right words happened for the first time during the French Revolution. In the French parliament, people sitting on the left side (Leftists), who wanted to remove the emperor and wanted a republic and secularism, were called Leftists and those sitting on the right side (Rightists) who were supporters of the king were called Rightists. The development of the Leftist movement in India started in the second decade of the 20th century Special Facts Leftist politics is called that ideology which wants to change society and bring maximum economic equality into it. In this ideology, sympathy is expressed for those people who for any reason have fallen behind or become powerless compared to other people.

questions.question_text: Who was the hero of the Peshawar incident?
questions.explanation: The hero of the Peshawar incident was Chandra Singh Garhwali. He was born on 25 December 1891 in Pauri Garhwal of Uttarakhand. At the age of 15, he joined the army. In the year 1930, the Garhwal Rifles were sent to Peshawar, where the Salt Satyagraha was going on. On 23 April 1930, Chandra Singh refused to open fire on the countrymen against his captain's orders. After this, weapons were taken back from the entire Garhwal regiment and they were given 11 years of punishment. After independence, he kept doing social service, he died on 1 October 1979. The Uttarakhand government issued a postage stamp on him in 1994

questions.question_text: "After 1857, the 'Quit India Movement' was a very serious rebellion." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The Quit India Movement started on 8 August 1942. questions.question_text: Who was the first proponent of the idea of creating Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The word Pakistan was first used by Cambridge University student Choudhry Rahmat Ali. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan had conceived the creation of Pakistan, Mohammad Ali Jinnah was elected as the Governor of independent Pakistan

questions.question_text: Who led the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: The movement started at the call of Gandhi ji, but the British caught Gandhi ji and the main Congress leaders and put them in jail, due to which the leadership of the movement was with the public itself, all the leaders were being caught and put in jail, people kept expressing their opposition everywhere

questions.question_text: When was the Non-Cooperation Movement stopped?
questions.explanation: The beginning of the Non-Cooperation Movement was done on 1 August 1920. During this movement, educational institutions were boycotted by the students. questions.question_text: Which parties participated in the 1916 Lucknow Pact?

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the Congress session held in Madras that boycotted the Simon Commission?
questions.explanation: 1927 Madras Session, its chairmanship was done by Dr. Ansari, in this, the proposal to oppose the Simon Commission was passed. Badruddin Tyabji presided over the Congress in Madras in 1887. Mohammad Ali Jinnah never presided over the Indian National Congress

questions.explanation: In 1939 AD, the Ambari Satyagraha in Bihar was led by Rahul Sankrityayan. questions.question_text: When did the Simon Commission come to India?
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission had a group of 7 British MPs, which was formed in 1927 AD to study constitutional reforms in India. The chairman of this Simon Commission was Sir John Simon. This commission reached Bombay on 3 February, 1928 AD in India and on this day, slogans of 'Simon Commission Go Back' were raised in opposition to the Simon Commission

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not kept in Ahmednagar Fort after being arrested during the Quit India Movement?

questions.explanation: 'Quit India Movement was no less than the revolutions of Russia and France' is the statement of Jayaprakash Narayan. The Quit India Movement started on 8 August 1942 during the Second World War. Its goal was to end the British empire from India

questions.explanation: Bardoli Satyagraha was a major peasant movement in Gujarat in the year 1928 during the Indian freedom struggle, which was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The provincial government increased the tax of the farmers up to 22%, due to which farmers of the whole Gujarat opposed it, as a result, the tax increase rate was reduced from 22% to 6.03%, after this success, Vallabhbhai got the title of 'Sardar'

questions.question_text: The names of the two other revolutionaries who were hanged along with Bhagat Singh on 23 March 1931 AD were

questions.explanation: On 1 November 1913, the Ghadar Party was founded in San Francisco due to the efforts of Lala Hardayal. questions.question_text: After considering the following statements, select the correct option from the given options and answer: Statement 1: The Indian National Congress and the Muslim League won an equal number of seats in the United Provinces in 1937. Statement 2: The Muslim League wanted to form a coalition government in the United Provinces by joining the Congress in 1937. Statement 3: When the proposal was rejected by the Congress, the League felt that if India remained undivided, it would be difficult for Muslims to get political power.

options.A: Statement 1, 2 and 3 are correct and statement 3 explains statement 1 and statement 2.
options.B: Statement 1 is not correct and statement 2 and 3 are correct.
options.D: Statement 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is not correct.

questions.explanation: Among the given statements, statement (1) is incorrect, whereas statement (2) and statement (3) are true The Indian National Congress won a majority in the 1937 elections, whereas the Muslim League received very few seats. Therefore: Statement (1) is false. Although the Muslim League wanted to form the government by joining the Congress, due to the conditions of the League, the Congress rejected its proposal. After this, the League started turning rapidly towards communalism. The top leaders of the League clearly felt that if India remained undivided, it would be difficult for Muslims to get political power. Therefore, clearly: Statement (2) and Statement (3) are true.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Acts was it that inflamed people's sentiments due to which the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred?

options.B: Obstructing legislative work by working as dissatisfied people

questions.question_text: Who among the following attacked Lieutenant Colonel Sir William Curzon Wyllie in 1909 as the first act of revolution in the Indian independence movement?

Savarkar, Hardayal, Madan Lal Dhingra

questions.question_text: In which session of the following, did Congress give concessions to the Muslim League by accepting separate electorate areas in 1916?
questions.explanation: Through the Lucknow Pact (1916), Congress officially accepted the demand for a separate electoral constituency for Muslims for the first time, which proved to be a big mistake in later times. questions.explanation: The bill passed in the Central Legislative Council on 17 March 1919 AD was known as the Rowlatt Act or Rowlatt Act. questions.question_text: Urdu poet who was the representative of both the Second and Third Round Table Conferences?
questions.explanation: The second Round Table Conference ran in London from 7 September 1931 to 1 December, 1931. The Third Round Table Conference ran from 17 November 1932 to 24 December 1932. questions.question_text: Indra Narayan Dwivedi, who had formed the Kisan Sabha in the United Province, was basically a follower of~

questions.question_text: The most fearless and brave woman of the peasant movement who sacrificed her life to protect the rights of farmers~
questions.explanation: Veera Gunamma was born in a poor family in Rajahemdry village of Mandsa district of Andhra Pradesh. In the year 1988, Governor Kumudben Joshi inaugurated the memorial of Veera Gunamma and the name of her village was changed to Veera Gunamma Rajahemdry.

questions.question_text: The women's movement in India was mainly started under whose leadership~
questions.explanation: Ramabai Ranade (1862-1924) started the women's movement. She started speaking against child marriage and the conditions of widows. questions.question_text: Which of the following was not associated with the establishment of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in 1928?
questions.explanation: 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)' is the modified form of 'Hindustan Republican Association' established in 1924 AD. questions.question_text: Which of the following was not associated with the Congress Socialist Party?
questions.explanation: The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934 AD in Bombay due to the efforts of Acharya Narendra Dev, Jayaprakash Narayan, Minoo Masani, and Ashok Mehta. The purpose of the formation of this party was - the process of economic development of the country should be planned and controlled by the state. questions.question_text: Who founded the All India Women's Conference in 1927?
questions.explanation: Margaret Cousins was a theosophist and nationalist activist, she became the first female magistrate in India. She was elected the first non-Indian member of the Indian Women's University, Pune (1916). She founded the All India Women's Conference (Pune) in 1927. Its establishment did important work in the field of women's education, women's development in the social field, improvement in the status of women at a professional level, and other women-related rights so that improvement in the status of women could happen. In the All India Conference, not only were efforts made to remove various restrictions on women like child marriage, purdah system, etc., but the 1927 child marriage act was the result of her efforts. This was later called the Sharda Act (1929)

questions.question_text: The first All India Peasant Organization, 'All India Kisan Sabha' was formed in 1936 under whose leadership, was~

questions.question_text: While leading a group studying in England, who proposed a separate Muslim state 'Pakistan' in 1933?
questions.explanation: Choudhry Rahmat Ali was born in the town of Balachaur in Hoshiarpur district of Punjab. Choudhry Rahmat Ali first presented the word Pakistan before the world. questions.question_text: During the Anti-Partition movement, the Carlyle Circular was related to
questions.explanation: In the boycott movement as a protest against the Bengal partition, the idea of Swadeshi was also included, as a result of which students of Bengal participated in it enthusiastically. In this context, the Chief Secretary of Bengal, Carlyle, wrote a letter to institutions in October 1905, warning that if students and colleges violate government orders, then no aid will be provided to the institution by the government. This is called the Carlyle Circular

questions.question_text: Who participated in the Dandi March from Uttarakhand?

options.B: Keshav Singh Rawat, Mohan Singh Mehta

questions.explanation: On 12 March 1930, Mahatma Gandhi started the Dandi March. Three Satyagrahis from Uttarakhand participated in it. Jyotiram Kandpal (Almora), Khadag Bahadur Singh (Dehradun), and Bhairav Datt Joshi (Pithoragarh). Bhairav Datt Joshi returned due to illness. A total of 78 Satyagrahis participated with Gandhi ji in this Dandi March

questions.question_text: During the Quit India Movement, the emergence of parallel governments was a major feature. Who was the leader of such a parallel government in Ballia (Eastern Uttar Pradesh) in August 1942?
questions.explanation: During the Quit India Movement, a parallel government was established in Ballia under the leadership of Chittu Pandey. Chittu Pandey's government took all administrative powers from the local district collector and released all the Congress leaders imprisoned in jail. A parallel government was formed in Satara under the leadership of Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil. These governments ran respectively until 1944 and 1945. In Midnapore district of Bengal, at a place called Tamluk, the Tamluk National (National) Government was established. The parallel government of Satara remained in existence for the longest time

questions.question_text: During the Quit India Movement, the 'Gentlemen's Agreement' was reached between whom?
questions.explanation: During the Quit India Movement, the Gentlemen's Agreement (1942 AD) was reached between Mirza Ismail and Hiralal Shastri. According to this agreement, the members of Jaipur Prajamandal did not participate in the Quit India Movement, but members who wanted to participate, formed 'Azad Morcha' under the leadership of Baba Harishchandra and participated

questions.question_text: Select the pair of places where parallel governments were formed during the Quit India Movement:
questions.explanation: During the Quit India Movement, parallel governments were formed in the following areas 1. Ballia - (For only one week in August 1942 under the leadership of Chittu Pandey) 2. Tamluk - (Midnapore, from December 1942 to September 1944) 3. Satara - (From mid-1943 to 1945)

questions.question_text: In which year did Gandhi ji leave Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) and vowed to return only after achieving Swaraj?
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji founded Sabarmati Ashram in 1917 on the banks of Sabarmati river. On 12 March 1930, while starting the Dandi march from here, Gandhi ji took an oath that he would not keep his feet in the ashram until India gets independence

questions.question_text: During which of the following movements were many effective means, methods of Satyagraha, boycott, and mass-opposition developed and used?
questions.explanation: The English decided to partition Bengal to create a split among Indians and announced 16 October 1905 as the date of partition. Indians opposed it on a large scale. Leaders appealed to people for the boycott of foreign clothes and goods. The date of the implementation of the plan was celebrated as a day of mourning. Rabindranath Tagore gave a call for it to be celebrated as a Raksha Bandhan festival

questions.question_text: Which representative (delegate) did not oppose the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in the Karachi (1931) session of Congress?
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel chaired the Karachi session of Congress (1931). This session had a long-term impact on the direction of the national movement and the political and social development of Indian society. In this session, a resolution related to fundamental rights was adopted. In this session itself, Purushottam Das Tandon supported the Gandhi-Irwin Pact as a representative, which provided the Congress an opportunity to talk to the government at an equal level. K.M. Munshi called this pact a 'trend-setting event' in India's constitutional history

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not related to the Kakori conspiracy case?
questions.explanation: Shaukat Usmani was related to the Communist Party, he was not related to the Kakori incident. He was a founding member of the Communist Party established in Tashkent in 1920 and the Communist Party of India formed in Kanpur in 1925. He was sentenced to 16 years of jail in the Meerut conspiracy case

questions.question_text: Which Rani of Nagaland protested against foreign rule at the call of Gandhi ji and she was sentenced to life imprisonment?
questions.explanation: Rani Gaidinliu ran a revolutionary movement for India's independence in Nagaland. For acting bravely like Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, she is called 'Rani Lakshmibai of Nagaland'. She was a Naga spiritual and political leader of India who led a protest against British rule in India. She was expert in guerrilla warfare and arms movement. She had decided to build a large fort during the protest in which four thousand Naga companions could stay, work was going on this when on 17 April 1932, the English army suddenly attacked. Gaidinliu was arrested and a case was tried against her and she was sentenced to life imprisonment. After the country became independent in 1947, she came out of jail. Jawaharlal Nehru called her "Rani of the Nagas"

questions.question_text: Who recommended the 'Quit India Resolution'?
questions.explanation: On 8 August 1942, the annual meeting of the All India Congress Committee was held in Bombay at the historic Gowalia Tank ground. (Presided over by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad) the Wardha proposal (Quit India) was confirmed in the meeting. Whose recommendation was done by Jawaharlal Nehru. The Quit India movement is also known as the 'August Revolution'. It is considered the last fight of the Indian freedom struggle. It is also called a spontaneous movement

questions.question_text: Famous revolutionary Ashutosh Kuila was a member of which revolutionary organization?
questions.explanation: Famous revolutionary Ashutosh Kuila was a member of the revolutionary organization named Vidyut Vahini. In Tamluk of Midnapore district of Bengal, on 17 December 1942, after the establishment of the Tamluk National Government, the government formed an armed Vidyut Vahini. The national government remained operational until 1 September 1944 AD

questions.question_text: On which day was the Quit India resolution passed?
questions.explanation: On 8 August 1942 AD, the annual meeting of the All India Congress Committee was held in Bombay at the historic Gowalia Tank ground. (Presided over by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad) the Wardha proposal (Quit India) was confirmed in the meeting. The Quit India movement is also known as the 'August Revolution'. It is considered the last great fight of India's freedom struggle

questions.question_text: In which session of Congress was 'Purna Swaraj' adopted as the goal by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation: After the expiry of the one-year time limit (in the context of Dominion Status) given to the British government at the Calcutta session of the Congress, the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) was made at the Lahore session of the Congress on 31 December 1929, which was presided over by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. It was decided in this meeting that 26 January 1930 should be celebrated as 'Purna Swaraj' day

questions.question_text: Which of the following gave up his knighthood (honor) as a protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore returned his 'Knighthood' title in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 in Amritsar. Viceroy's Executive Council member Shankaran Nair resigned. On increasing pressure from all sides, the government formed a committee to investigate this massacre. It included Sir Thomas Smith, Sir Chimanlal Setalvad, Sahabzada Sultan Ahmed, and Jagat Narayan

questions.question_text: In whose presided Congress session was the proposal of 'Non-Cooperation Movement' passed?
questions.explanation: The proposal for non-cooperation was placed by Gandhiji in the 1920 Calcutta session of the Congress. This session was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai. The proposal regarding the Non-Cooperation Movement passed in the special session of Congress in Calcutta (1920) was confirmed in the annual session of Congress held in Nagpur in December 1920

questions.question_text: Who was the Viceroy in India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919 AD, a peaceful meeting was organized in Jallianwala Bagh of Amritsar against the shooting incident and the arrest of leaders. The British General Dyer present at the meeting site opened fire without any notice. 1000 people were killed in this. Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy of India at the time of this incident

questions.question_text: Which of the following Governor Generals was addressed with the epithet 'Merciful' (Clemency)?
questions.explanation: Lord Canning was the first Viceroy of India and his tenure as Governor General was from 1856-1862 AD. The revolt of 1857 AD took place during his reign, in which lakhs of revolutionaries including women and children were killed. He suppressed this revolt and because he did not take any cruel action against these revolutionaries, he got the recognition of 'Merciful Canning'

questions.question_text: Due to the 'Open Letters' written on the Indian economy by whom to Lord Curzon, the British Indian government had to publish an official rebuttal and also had to take reformative economic steps?
questions.explanation: Ramesh Chandra Dutt was an administrative officer as well as a politician, writer, and economic thinker. He was an expert in the economic field, due to which the open letters written by him on the Indian economy to Lord Curzon forced the British Indian government to publish an official rebuttal and also had to take reformative economic steps. R.C. Dutt's major work is 'The Economic History of India'

questions.question_text: Whose famous painting of Mother India or 'Mother India' (1904-05) appeared as a symbol of the new image of India in nationalist talent science?
questions.explanation: Abanindranath Tagore was a major artist and creator of the “Indian Society of Oriental Art”. He was the first promoter of this institution in India. The famous painting of Mother India or Mother India by Abanindranath Tagore appeared as a symbol of the new image of India in nationalist consciousness

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List- I (Nationalist woman) List- II (Their activities)
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu participated in many satyagrahas in which she participated in the salt satyagraha in Dharasana and led it. Usha Mehta played an active role in India's freedom struggle. She conducted a secret radio during the Quit India Movement while Aruna Asaf Ali was a leader of the underground movement. Dr. Lakshmi Swaminathan joined the Azad Hind Fauj

questions.question_text: Which country imposed strict restrictions on the disembarkation of Indian immigrants who were taken by the Komagata Maru ship in March 1914?
questions.explanation: Komagata Maru was a Japanese merchant ship which was bought by Baba Gurudutt Singh, who lived in Hong Kong. Baba Gurudutt Singh left for Vancouver on 4 March 1914 with about 376 people from South and East Asia on the ship. But the Canadian government imposed strict restrictions on the disembarkation of Indian immigrants

questions.question_text: In which session of the Indian National Congress, Congress President Motilal Nehru and Muslim League President Hakim Ajmal Khan jointly led the procession?
questions.explanation: In the Amritsar Session, 1919, under the leadership of Pt. Motilal Nehru. In this session, Congress President Motilal Nehru and Muslim League President and Hakim Ajmal Khan jointly led the procession. The Lucknow Session, 1916 was presided over by Ambika Charan Majumdar. Lala Lajpat Rai was elected President of the special Calcutta session, 1920. The executive president of the Ahmedabad session, 1921 was Hakim Ajmal Khan

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events chronologically and select the correct code given below:
questions.explanation: The correct order chronologically is The Deccan Association – 1884 (Pune), Mahadev Govind Ranade East India Association – 1866 (London), Dadabhai Naoroji Indian National Congress – 28 December, 1885, A.O. Hume Indian League – September, 1875, by Sisir Kumar Ghosh

questions.question_text: In whose Viceroyalty was the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act passed?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Lord Curzon was a scholar of history and archaeology. He passed an Act in 1904 AD for the protection of ancient monuments and fixed 50 thousand pounds for the repair of ancient monuments in India. Curzon was the most unpopular Viceroy of India. He forced the Indian princely states for such important work. He also inspired provincial governments to build museums for rare items and in this way, he paid his tribute to the artists of the ancient era.

questions.question_text: Who were the signatories of the 'Bombay Manifesto' of 1936 among the following industrialists?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The signatories of the 1936 Bombay Manifesto were Purushottam Thakurdas and Walchand Hirachand. In 1944, 8 industrialists of Bombay also presented a 15-year capitalist plan named Bombay Plan under the leadership of Ardeshir Dalal. A few days after the publication of the Bombay Plan, Sir Ardeshir Dalal received an invitation from the government to join the Viceroy's executive council and start the planning department, which he accepted.

questions.question_text: Which armed tribal movement started in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– During the Non-Cooperation Movement, the armed Chenchu tribal movement started in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh. The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) was passed in the special session of Congress in Calcutta (1920). The proposal regarding the Non-Cooperation Movement was confirmed in the annual session of the Congress held in Nagpur in December 1920. In the Calcutta Congress session of September 1920, Mahatma Gandhi himself presented the Non-Cooperation proposal.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of the Bengali book 'Kuli Kahini' similar to 'Uncle Tom's Cabin'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The author of the Bengali book 'Kuli Kahini' similar to 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' is Pandit Ramkumar Vidyaratna. The Congress session was held in Madras in 1887, and at that time, some delegates who came from Bengal raised the issue of atrocities being committed on tea plantation workers in Assam. Pandit Ramkumar Vidyaratna of Sadharan Brahmo Samaj visited Assam's tea plantations and found during this visit that the owners of tea plantations were behaving inhumanly towards the workers.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code given below: List-I (Political Organization) List-II (Year of Establishment)
questions.explanation: Explanation– The correct match is as follows– Indian Association – 1876 Mahajan Sabha – 1884 The Bombay Association – 1852 Poona Sarvajanik Sabha – 1867

questions.question_text: What was not correct about the 'Statutory Civil Service' started in 1880?

options.A: Appointments were generally limited to youth from families of good and social status.
options.B: The ratio of this service should not be more than 1/6 of the total number of covenanted civil servants appointed in a year.
options.C: Appointments for this service were made by nomination.
options.D: This service provided a component of completeness and did justice to the claims of Indians for appointment to high posts.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The father of Civil Service in India was Cornwallis. The gates of Civil Service were opened for Indians in 1853 AD when a competitive examination began to be held in it. The maximum age for appearing in this examination was 22 years. Appointments in the Statutory Civil Service started in 1880 were generally limited to youth from families of good and social status. The ratio of this service should not be more than 1/6 of the total number of covenanted civil servants appointed in a year, and appointments for this service were made by nomination.

questions.question_text: Who among the following princely rulers was called the most loyal to the British by Lord Canning because he openly declared, 'Keep India safe for the British'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Scindia was called the most loyal to the British by Lord Canning because he openly declared, 'Keep India safe for the British'.

questions.question_text: Regarding whom did Captain Sleeman write, '...they come for looting, not for fighting...'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– 'Pindari' is a word of Marathi language. This was a group of looters in which both Hindus and Muslims were included. They also had the support of the Marathas. Maratha leader Malhar Rao Holkar had given them the 'Golden Flag'. Malcolm gave them the title of 'hunting dog with Maratha hunters'. Malcolm himself took the command of the northern army for the suppression of Pindaris, while the command of the southern army was given to Thomas Hislop. Captain Sleeman wrote – 'Pindaris come to loot, not to fight'.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following books in chronological order in which they were published. Answer with the help of the code given below– (Author) (Title of the book)
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The correct chronological order is– R.C. Dutt – Economic History of India Mahatma Gandhi – My Experiments With Truth Jawaharlal Nehru – An Autobiography R. Palme Dutt – India Today

questions.question_text: Which famous woman revolutionary was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Chittagong Armoury raid case? After her release in 1939, she joined the Communist Party of India?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Kalpana Datta was associated with the 'Indian Republican Army' of the great revolutionary Surya Sen. They did the daring work of looting the Chittagong Armoury in 1930 AD and were later arrested. In 1934 AD, at the age of 21, Kalpana Datta was sentenced to life imprisonment. Due to the special efforts of Gandhiji and Rabindranath Tagore, she came out of jail in 1939 AD.
