She later joined the Communist Party and married the party's General Secretary Puran Chand Joshi in 1943 AD. In September 1979 AD, Kalpana Datta was honored with the title of 'Veer Mahila' in Pune.

questions.question_text: Which of the following revolutionary organizations is not correctly matched with its founder? (Organization) (Founder)

options.D: Hindustan Socialist Republican Association: Sachindranath Sanyal

questions.explanation: /c) UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– In the given options, Roshan Lal was not the founder of Shree Sangha. Its founder was Anil Roy. Whereas the organization named 'Shree Sangha' was founded in Bengal in 1921 AD by Anil Baran Roy. The founder of the organization named 'Anand Math' was Mahatma Satya. The members of this organization were considered a group opposing British company rule. UGC NET has considered the answer to this question as option (b & c).

questions.question_text: Who received the title of 'Fakhr-e-Afghan'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a great politician of the frontier province and Balochistan who participated in India's independence and due to his work and determination, he began to be called 'Sarhadi Gandhi' (Frontier Gandhi), 'Bachha Khan', 'Badshah Khan'. They are known for the use of non-violence against British rule in the Indian subcontinent. In 1929, he founded an organization named Khudai Khidmatgar. The Khudai Khidmatgar organization is also called the Red Shirt organization. This organization was inspired by Gandhiji's principles like non-violence and satyagraha; they are also known by the name of Frontier Gandhi. Keeping his achievements in mind, he has been awarded the Bharat Ratna by the Government of India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following newspapers supported the interests of the farmers and strongly criticized the Indigo planters during the 'Indigo Revolt'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Indigo revolt was a movement carried out by farmers which was done by the farmers of Bengal in 1859. This movement was completely non-violent and both Hindus and Muslims of India participated equally in it. By 1860, Indigo cultivation in Bengal almost came to a standstill. A commission was constituted for this in 1860. During the Indigo revolt, the Hindu Patriot newspaper supported the interests of the farmers and strongly criticized the Indigo planters.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– Under the Meerut Conspiracy Case, the British government arrested 31 labor leaders in March 1929 and brought them to Meerut and filed a case against them. In which three British communists Philip Spratt, Ben Bradley, and Lester Hutchinson were also included. These three British communists were expelled from India. Jawaharlal Nehru, M.A. Ansari, Kailash Nath Katju, and M.C. Chagla pleaded for the prisoners involved in this case.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was a great innovator in politics? Being completely and consciously secular, he clearly understood the danger of communalism before the nation. Who often used to say that communalism is as big an enemy as imperialism?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Bhagat Singh often used to say that communalism is as big an enemy as imperialism. On 23 March 1931, Bhagat Singh was hanged along with Rajguru and Sukhdev.

questions.question_text: There are two statements below, one is statement (A) and the other is reason (R): Statement (A): The moderates actually believed that there was a constitutional path to self-rule for India. Reason (R): They had firm faith in British love for justice. Which of the following is correct in the context of these two statements?

options.A: (A) and (R) are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) are both true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Moderates believed that there is a constitutional path to self-rule in India because they had firm faith in British love for justice. In 1887, Bipin Chandra Pal said, “I am loyal to the British because for me loyalty to the British empire is actually loyalty to my country and its residents, both are distinct. I am loyal to the British because I love 'self-rule'.”

questions.question_text: Who were the revolutionary leaders among the following? (i) Barkatullah (ii) Khizr Hayat Khan (iii) Ubaidullah Sindhi (iv) Mahmud Hasan Show the correct answer from the code given below: Code:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Barkatullah, Ubaidullah Sindhi and Mahmud Hasan were revolutionary leaders. Khizr Hayat Khan was a moderate leader. Barkatullah and Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi together with Raja Mahendra Pratap in 1915 formed the first government in exile in Afghanistan. Raja Mahendra Pratap was the President and Barkatullah was the Prime Minister in this.

questions.question_text: In which session of the Indian National Congress, for the first time, some policy regarding princely states was articulated?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– In the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in 1920 AD, for the first time, some policy regarding princely states was articulated. C.R. Das placed a proposal related to the Non-Cooperation Movement in this conference, under which the return of titles and honorary letters, boycott of government schools, colleges, courts, and foreign clothes, etc., were included.

questions.question_text: Which organization was founded by the leftist women leaders of Bengal in 1942?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The leftist women leaders of Bengal founded the 'Mahila Atmaraksha Samiti' organization in 1942. Rani Mitra Das Gupta, Manikuntala Sen, and Renu Chakravarty were the main leaders of the Mahila Atmaraksha Samiti.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first Indian woman President of the Indian Congress?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress was Sarojini Naidu. She presided over the Kanpur session in 1925. The first woman President of the Indian National Congress was Srimati Annie Besant. She presided over the Calcutta session of the Congress in 1917 AD.

questions.question_text: By what name did the common people know the Khudai Khidmatgars?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The common people knew the Khudai Khidmatgars by the name of 'Red Shirts'. Their movement started under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan. This movement was carried out in the North-West Frontier Province.

questions.question_text: The communists of which region started their heavy campaign with this slogan, 'Throw the American model into the Arabian Sea'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The communists of the Western Travancore State region started their campaign with this slogan, 'Throw the American model into the Arabian Sea'. In December 1947, the Communist Party of India (CPI) abandoned Indian independence. They gave a slogan that 'This freedom is false' and called the Congress and Nehru government puppets of Anglo-American imperialism and feudal forces within the country.

questions.question_text: The Tebhaga struggle of Bengal's sharecroppers (share-cropper) was the most forceful, in which the farmers had declared that they would not pay ______ part of the crop to the landlords.
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The Tebhaga struggle of Bengal's sharecroppers was the most forceful, in which the farmers had declared that they would not pay 1/2 part of the crop to the landlords. In the second half of 1946, the sharecroppers of Bengal started the announcement that they would not give half the share of the produce to the Jotedars or landowners, but would give a one-third share.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Indian National Congress pass the proposal to 'stop using Japanese goods', in which an appeal was made to Indians for this?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– The proposal to 'stop using Japanese goods' was passed by the Indian National Congress in the year 1937, in which an appeal was made to Indians for this. In 1937, Japan attacked China. The proposal that Congress passed on this condemned Japan. The Indian people were requested to boycott Japanese goods to express sympathy towards the Chinese people.

questions.question_text: When was the All India Trade Union Congress founded?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Answer (b) The All India Trade Union Congress was founded on 31 October, 1920. Lala Lajpat Rai became its first President. The joint efforts of N.M. Joshi and Joseph Baptista contributed to its establishment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Viceroys presented the 'August Offer' to ensure India's cooperation in the World War?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– In the 'August Offer' proposed by the then Viceroy Lord Linlithgow in August 1940, talk of forming a Constituent Assembly in India in exchange for cooperation in the World War was made, simultaneously minorities were assured that they would not support such a state system, which a major caste of that country rejects.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Indian National Social Conference and the Indian National Congress hold their sessions separately?
questions.explanation: Tilak stopped the Social Conference started by M.G. Ranade from the 11th Pune session (1895) of the Congress. Surendranath Banerjee was the President of this Congress session. After this, the Social Conference and the Indian National Congress started being organized separately

questions.question_text: Match the facts of List-I with List-II and select the correct pairs of the following Presidents of the Indian National Congress and the years they remained in office with the help of the code: List-I List-II
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji - 1886, 1893 Surendranath Banerjee - 1895, 1902 William Wedderburn - 1889, 1910 Dr. Annie Besant - 1917 Note– Dr. Annie Besant became the President of the Congress session only once in 1917. While the Calcutta session (1911) was presided over by Pandit Bishan Narayan Dar.

questions.question_text: At which of the following places did Swami Vivekananda establish Vedanta centers during his visit to America in 1899?
questions.explanation: – Swami Vivekananda participated in the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago, America in 1893 and Swami ji established two Vedanta centers in America 1. Vedanta Society, New York 1896 AD. 2. Vedanta Society, San Francisco 1896 AD. Shanti Ashram

questions.question_text: Who among the following accepted the 'Safety Valve Theory' regarding the emergence of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: In his article published in Young India in 1916, Lala Lajpat Rai used the safety valve theory and said – Congress is a product of Lord Dufferin's brain. C.F. Andrews and Girija Mukherjee accepted this theory in 1938. In addition to this, communist leader R. Palme Dutt and RSS leader M.S. Golwalkar also used this theory

questions.question_text: In which year were Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh deported?
questions.explanation: – After the riots in the urban areas of Punjab in 1907, Lala Lajpat Rai and Sardar Ajit Singh were expelled from the country. They were interned in Mandalay jail

questions.question_text: Who among the following started the first regular propaganda paper 'The Free Hindusthan' in America in 1908?
questions.explanation: – Taraknath Das (1884 - 1958) was a revolutionary originally from Bengal, who started the editing of the regular propaganda paper 'The Free Hindusthan' in English in America from 1908

questions.question_text: Who led the Mulshi Dam Satyagraha in 1922?
questions.explanation: – Pandurang Mahadev Bapat (1880-1967) – Bapat started the Mulshi Dam Satyagraha due to the danger of drowning of 54 villages and their farming due to the proposed dam at the confluence of the rivers Mula and Nila near Mulshi. He was sent to Yerwada jail. Because of this satyagraha, he was called Senapati Bapat. This is considered the world's first dam-opposition satyagraha

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer with the help of the code: List- I List- II
questions.explanation: – Golmuri Tinplate Strike - 1929 Great Indian Peninsular Railway Strike - 1930 Assam-Bengal Railway Strike - 1921 Ahmedabad Textile Strike - 1918

questions.question_text: Which nationalist leader said in 1929 that the Congress is 'no labor organization' but 'a large group of people of all kinds'?
questions.explanation: – In the Lahore session of 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru in his presidential address said that 'Congress is no labor organization, but a large group of people of all kinds.' The demand for complete independence was made in this session

questions.question_text: In which of the following places did the first Swadeshi theft or loot take place in the year 1906?
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2012 Explanation– The first Swadeshi theft or loot took place in the year 1906 at a place named Rangpur. Whereas the Kakori loot was done on 9 August 1925, the government treasury was looted at a station named Kakori near Lucknow. It is known that the Chittagong Armoury raid (Chittagong Armoury loot) incident took place on 18 April 1930.

questions.question_text: What was the objective of the Home Rule movement started by Annie Besant?

options.D: To launch a movement against British monopoly in administration

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2012) Explanation– The objective of the Home Rule movement started by Annie Besant was to achieve self-rule for India. She started the Home Rule movement in September 1916 AD. Whereas the Home Rule movement started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak began in April 1916.

questions.question_text: Why is the day of August 8, 1942, important in Indian history?

options.A: Formation of the Indian National Congress in Singapore by Subhash Chandra Bose
options.B: Cripps proposal for a colonial state
options.C: Non-cooperation movement started by Mahatma Gandhi
options.D: Quit India Movement started by Mahatma Gandhi

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2012) Explanation– The day of August 8, 1942, is important in Indian history because it was on this day that Mahatma Gandhi started the Quit India Movement. During the Quit India Movement, Mahatma Gandhi said “Nothing less than freedom” and gave the slogan of ‘Do or Die’.

questions.question_text: Who was the first President of the All India Depressed Classes Association?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The first President of the All India Depressed Classes Association was Dewan Bahadur Mylai Chinnathambi Pillai Rajah, who was a Tamil social and political activist. Whereas, Mahatma Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932 for the upliftment of Dalits.

questions.question_text: How did the Muslim League celebrate the resignation of the Congress-led cabinet on 1 November, 1939?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The Muslim League celebrated the resignation of the Congress-led cabinet on 1 November, 1939, as Deliverance Day (Mukti Diwas). It is noteworthy that in the 1937 elections, Congress had formed governments in about 6 provinces along with the central legislative.

questions.question_text: Under which Act were the provinces re-granted legislative powers?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The Act of 1861, which is called the Indian Council Act of 1861 AD. Under this Act, the provinces were re-granted legislative powers, and at the same time, the Governor General was also given the power to issue ordinances.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the following code – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The correct match is – List-I List-II (a) Mahatma Gandhi (I) President of Belgaum session (b) Rash Behari Ghosh (II) President of Surat session (c) Dadabhai Naoroji (III) President of Calcutta session (d) Jawaharlal Nehru (IV) President of Lahore session

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the following code – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation– The correct match is – List-I List-II (a) V.D. Savarkar (I) Abhinav Bharat (b) Lala Har Dayal (II) Gadar Party (c) Taraknath Das (III) Free Hindusthan (d) Madanlal Dhingra (IV) Curzon Wyllie

questions.question_text: Who named 'Indian National Congress'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– The Indian National Congress was founded in British rule on 28 December, 1885. Its founder was A.O. Hume. This name was suggested by Dadabhai Naoroji, which later became a major organization. Its role has been prominent in the Indian freedom struggle.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given code : List-I List-II (Name) (Newspaper/Magazine)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– During the Indian nationalist movement, many newspapers were published from time to time by major Indian leaders for public awareness. Such as – Al-Hilal by Abul Kalam Azad, Bombay Chronicle by Pherozeshah Mehta, New India and Commonweal by Annie Besant, and Young India by Mahatma Gandhi, etc.

questions.question_text: Who was the first woman nominated for the Madras Legislative Assembly in 1927:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– The first woman nominated for the Madras Legislative Assembly in 1927 was Muthulakshmi Reddy. In 1954, she laid the foundation of 'Adyar Cancer Institute' and in 1956, she was honored with the Padma Bhushan award.

questions.question_text: Two statements are being given below, first is Assertion (A) and second is reason (R) : Assertion (A): Soon after the resignation of the Congress-led cabinet in 1939, the Muslim League celebrated 'Deliverance Day'. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements? Code: Reason (R): Ambedkar supported it.

options.A: A and R are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: (A) and (R) are both true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– The Indian Viceroy Lord Linlithgow had declared without the permission of Indians that India is also involved in the war with Britain against Germany in the Second World War. Against this, the ministers of Congress-governed provinces resigned from the cabinet on 15 November 1939 after the permission of the Congress Working Committee. Ambedkar supported this.

questions.question_text: What is the common characteristic in Wahabi and Kuka movements?

options.A: Both started as religious movements but both slowly became political movements
options.B: Both were political and economic movements.
options.D: Both were not plagued by some weaknesses, such as communal sentiments, rigidity, and factionalism in the organization.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June, 2013) Explanation– A similarity in Wahabi and Kuka movements was that both started as religious movements but both slowly became political movements. It is known that the pioneer of the Kuka movement was Bhagat Jawahar Mal. Whereas the pioneer of the Wahabi movement was Syed Ahmed, who was a resident of Rae Bareli.

questions.question_text: In which year was the 'Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science' established?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– 'Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science' (IACS) is an autonomous research institute under India's Department of Science and Technology. It was established on 29 July 1876 AD by Dr. Mahendra Lal Sarkar in Kolkata (West Bengal). This is the oldest scientific institute in Asia. Note- In 1876 AD, 'Indian Association' was established under the leadership of young nationalists of Bengal, Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose.

questions.question_text: In which army were General Shah Nawaz, Gurdial Singh Dhillon, and Prem Sehgal officers in the East?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – The British government conducted a trial against the arrested officers of the Azad Hind Fauj in the Red Fort in November 1945. The main accused Major Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sehgal, and Gurdial Singh Dhillon were charged with treason. These three were included in the British Indian Army before joining the INA.

questions.question_text: Rani Gaidinliu, who fought against the British, was from–
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Civil Disobedience Movement also gained momentum in the northeastern states, which is known as the Zeliangrong movement. Nagas also participated. Jadonang was hanged and his cousin Gaidinliu took over the command of the Naga movement, she was sentenced to life imprisonment. Jawaharlal Nehru gave her the title of Rani of Nagaland like Lakshmibai.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not related to the I.N.A. (Indian National Army)?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Indian National Army or Azad Hind Fauj was founded by Rash Behari Bose in 1942. On 5 July, 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose took over its command in Singapore and gave the slogan of 'Delhi Chalo'. Lakshmi Sehgal and General Mohan Singh were related to INA, whereas Rash Behari Ghosh was mainly a moderate and in 1907 he presided over the Congress session held in Surat.

questions.question_text: As a result of the Poona Pact, the number of seats reserved for Dalit classes out of the seats of general voters–
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – The Poona Pact took place between Dr. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi on 24 September, 1932. Under this, separate electorates for Dalit classes were abolished, but the number of seats reserved for Dalit classes in provincial legislative councils was increased from 71 to 147. An 18 percent increase was made in the number of seats reserved for Harijans in the Central Legislative Council.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Governor-Generals started Indian Civil Services?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation– Cornwallis is considered the father of Civil Service in India. Competitive examinations started in this service from 1853 AD. Initially, this used to happen in England, but in 1922 AD it started happening in India. The first Indian I.C.S. in 1863 AD was Satyendranath Tagore.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is not correctly matched? (Organization) (Founder)

options.A: All India Kisan Sabha: Mahatma Gandhi

questions.explanation: Organization Founder All India Kisan Sabha – Swami Sahajanand Saraswati Atmiya Sabha – Raja Rammohan Roy Forward Block – Subhash Chandra Bose Ramakrishna Mission – Vivekananda

questions.question_text: In which year did Srimati Annie Besant become the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– Annie Besant was a British socialist, a writer working for the rights of women. She was also associated with Indian politics. In 1917, she became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in the Calcutta session.

questions.question_text: In 1904, who said that “United Bengal is a power, divided Bengal will move on several different paths”?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– On 6 December 1904, H.H. Risley, Secretary of State for India in the British government, said on the occasion of the Bengal partition that a united Bengal is a power, divided Bengal will move on several different paths.

questions.question_text: In which year did Shyamji Krishna Varma establish 'India House' in London to work for India's freedom?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– The Indian Home Rule Society was founded in 1905 in London by Shyamji Krishna Varma. He founded the Indian Home Rule Society with the aim of achieving self-rule for India, he got inspiration for this from Hind Swaraj. He established 'India House' for the residence of Indian visitors.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below – List-I List-II
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation─ List-I List-II (a) Death of Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (i) 1898 (b) Madan Lal Dhingra killed (ii) 1909 Curzon Wyllie in London (c) Chapekar brothers killed plague (iii) 1897 commissioner Rand and Lt. Ayerst (d) Delhi coronation durbar organized (iv)

questions.question_text: Choose the name of the historian about whom Aurobindo Ghosh had said that he created the mind of the people for the boycott movement.
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Aurobindo Ghosh had said about Ramesh Chandra Dutt that he created the mind of the people for the boycott movement. Ramesh Chandra Dutt is known as a historian, economist, linguist, civil servant, and politician. His major work is 'The Economic History of India'.

questions.question_text: On which issue was the resolution passed after the debate in the Congress session held in Haripura in 1938?

options.A: Working for the fundamental rights of the people.
options.B: Supporting the mass movements in the princely states.
options.C: Supporting the British government against Germany.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The Indian National Congress was organized in Haripura (Gujarat) in 1938. Its President was Subhash Chandra Bose. A National Planning Committee was formed in this session and the Indian princely states were also included.

questions.question_text: The woman who shot the Governor of Bengal while receiving the degree:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– After the Chittagong Armoury raid, there was a sudden surge in revolutionary terrorist activities in Bengal. In February 1932 AD, Bina Das shot at the Governor of Bengal while receiving the degree at the convocation of Calcutta University, but he survived.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was India's first modern trade union?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The first organized trade union with regular membership and fees was the Madras Labour Union. Which was established by B.P. Wadia in 1918 AD in Madras. It was related to the textile industry. It is considered India's first real trade union.

questions.question_text: Two statements are being given below, one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R): Assertion (A): Lord Ripon passed the Ilbert Bill. Reason (R): It brought the native press on par with the English press. Read the above statements and select the correct answer based on the given code:

options.A: A and R are both true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: A and R are both true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– During the tenure of Lord Ripon (1880-84 AD), the Ilbert Bill controversy occurred in 1884 AD. Due to this controversy, Ripon resigned. He was the most popular Governor of India. The Ilbert Bill was not related to the press but was a law suggested by Ripon under which district-level Indian judges were to be given the power to issue judicial orders on British subjects.

questions.question_text: With what objective did the All India Women's Congress start in 1927?

options.B: To increase the participation of women in legislative assemblies.
options.D: To run a campaign for women's suffrage

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– In 1927, the All India Women's Congress started with the objective of increasing women's education. Another goal was to free women from oppression. In the prevailing situation, this organization was prominent among the organizations formed for the political, social, and educational upliftment of women.

questions.question_text: Who led the delegation that went to London to demand women's suffrage?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The delegation that went to London to demand women's suffrage was led by Sarojini Naidu. It is noteworthy that in 1916, Annie Besant herself founded the Home Rule League in India. Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session (1917), who was the first woman President of the Congress.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given code – List-I (Commission) List-II (Chairman)
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– (a) Famine Commission 1899 - Antony MacDonnell, (b) Railway Commission 1901 - Thomas Robertson, (c) Irrigation Commission 1901 - Sir Colin Scott Moncrieff, (d) University Commission 1902 - Thomas Raleigh.

questions.question_text: Who among the following poets wrote poetry in honor of the Russian Revolution 1917?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Subramania Bharati wrote poetry in honor of the Russian revolution of 1917. It is known that Lenin did the Bolshevik revolution in 1917 to end Russia's Tsarist system. Its immediate cause was Russia's defeat in the First World War.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Dhaka Anushilan Samiti founded?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The Dhaka Anushilan Samiti was founded in 1905 by P. Mitra and Pulin Das in Dhaka, whereas the Anushilan Samiti was founded in Calcutta in 1907 by Barindra Ghosh and Bhupendra Datta. UGC has released the answer (*) for this. That is, it has been cancelled.

questions.question_text: A youth from Maharashtra who participated in the revolutionary movement of Punjab?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Rajguru, a youth from Maharashtra, participated in the revolutionary movement of Punjab. At this time, the youngest revolutionary of Punjab was Bhagat Singh, who bombed the Central Assembly. It is noteworthy that Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in Lahore jail along with Bhagat Singh in March 1931. The full name of martyr Rajguru was Shivaram Hari Rajguru. He was born on 24 August 1908 in Pune, Maharashtra.

questions.question_text: Who among the following said that "the aim of political dacoities is to obtain government money"?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Young revolutionary of the Indian National Movement Ram Prasad Bismil said that "the aim of political dacoities is to obtain government money". It is noteworthy that Ram Prasad Bismil, along with other companions, especially Chandrashekhar Azad, looted the government treasury at a station named Kakori from the 8 Down train.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following chronologically and select the correct answer with the help of the given code: (i) Minto (ii) John Shore (iii) Cornwallis (iv) Warren Hastings Code:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The correct chronological order of the Governor Generals of British India is as follows– Warren Hastings (1773-85 AD), Cornwallis (1786-93 AD), John Shore (1793-98 AD), and Lord Minto (1807-1813 AD).

questions.question_text: Who were called 'Neo-Nationalists'?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The extremist faction was called Neo-Nationalists. Upset by the failure of the Non-Cooperation Movement, Pt. Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 AD for a new stir among the Indians. In the 1923 election, the Swaraj Party achieved a complete majority in Central Province.

questions.question_text: In which Viceroy's case did an accused stab and kill him in the Andaman Islands?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Lord Mayo was made the Viceroy of India between 1869-72 AD. He was killed by stabbing in Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar. In 1872 AD, the first census of India was started during the time of Mayo.

(UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– In the 1937 AD election, Congress formed its governments in a total of eight states. To run the administration smoothly here, a central control council was formed. This council was named the Parliamentary Sub-Committee. C. Rajagopalachari was made the Prime Minister of Madras.
examinations: During 1937-39, the Congress cabinet in Madras was led by:

questions.question_text: Who worked on the principle that "the annexation of Sindh is a very profitable villainy...... a probable robbery will be executed"?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– In 1842 AD, Lord Ellenborough came to India as Governor General. He appointed Charles Napier as the company's resident in Sindh in place of Major Outram. In August 1843 AD, the entire territory of Sindh was included in the British Empire. Charles Napier wrote in his diary that we have no right to bring Sindh under our control, yet we will do so.

questions.question_text: Who has compared the Indian National Congress to the war situation of Gramsci?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Bipan Chandra has written about the Congress in his famous book 'India's Struggle for Independence' that for running the national movement, the first requirement was a strong nationalist political leadership. Italy's famous Marxist thinker Antonio Gramsci has called this the headquarters of the movement. In this way, any political movement in any country can succeed only when the people there are organized, meaning the whole country is one. Therefore, Bipan Chandra compared the Indian National Congress to Gramsci's war situation. Dadabhai Naoroji had said that 'kings are made for the people, people are not for the kings.'

questions.question_text: 'The Emergence of Indian Nationalism' is the name of a book, whose author is –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Anil Seal is known as a Cambridge historian. His major book is 'The Emergence of Indian Nationalism', in which he analyzed the social roots of political stirrings of the 1870 and 1880 decades. Which laid the foundation of the Indian National Congress. This book mentions politicians, Viceroys, and civil servants as well as the social and political movements of those parts of India that were prominently associated with people. 'Locality, Province and Nation' is a major work of Anil Seal.

questions.question_text: Who was not included in the Swaraj group in the Congress in 1922-23?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Upset by the failure of the 1920 Non-Cooperation Movement, Pt. Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 AD for a new stir among the people. Another prominent member of which was Hakim Ajmal Khan. Whereas Dr. Rajendra Prasad was not a member of this organization.

questions.question_text: The Silk Letter conspiracy was organized by –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The Silk Letter conspiracy was organized by Ubaidullah Sindhi and Barkatullah in Afghanistan. This was an anti-British movement which was run by the Deobandi leadership between 1913 and 1920. Whose aim was to liberate India from British power.

questions.question_text: Where did the Congress adopt the proposal of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– In the 46th session 1931 Karachi of the Indian National Congress, under the presidency of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the proposal for Fundamental Rights and National Economic Policy was passed. Whereas the proposal for Purna Swaraj was passed in the Lahore session 1929 under the presidency of Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question_text: Who among the following has said that in India, the British "have to deal with such people of the human race who take a long time to change, who are bound by religious prejudices and old traditions"?
questions.explanation: Sir Charles Wood's statement was that in India, the British have to deal with such people of the human race who take a long time to change, who are bound by religious prejudices and old traditions. Macaulay was a supporter of the English group. He expressed his disdain for Indian customs in his own words.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is not correct Name of the author Title of the book

options.A: R.C. Dutt – Economic History of India
options.B: Dadabhai Naoroji – The Drain of Wealth and Indian Nationalism at the Turn of the Century
options.D: V. Anstey – Economic Development of India

questions.explanation: (Name of the author) (Title of the book) 1. R.C. Dutt - Economic History of India 2. Dadabhai Naoroji – Discussed the theory of drain of wealth in ‘The Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ 3. W. Digby – Prosperous British India 4. Vera Anstey - Economic Development of India

questions.question_text: Which of the following books has not been written by Vijayalakshmi Pandit?

options.A: Role of Women in the Modern World

questions.explanation: The author of Ways of the City is 'O. Henry', the rest are written by Vijayalakshmi Pandit. Vijayalakshmi Pandit's famous book was ‘The Scope of Happiness: A Personal Memoir’.

questions.question_text: Consider the following: State the correct chronological order from the code given below:
questions.explanation: British government made this law to end the influence of revolutionaries in India through the Rowlatt Act 1919. Entry of Swaraj Party in Legislative Councils happened in November 1923. Lala Lajpat Rai died in December 1928 AD during lathi charge in protest against the Simon Commission. Gurudwara Reform Act was passed in 1925 AD.

questions.question_text: Tripuri, where the famous Congress session of 1939 was held, is located where?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Tripuri where the famous Congress session of 1939 was held is located in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. Here Subhash Chandra Bose adorned the post of Congress President. Subhash Chandra Bose resigned from the President's post due to differences with Gandhiji. After this, Rajendra Prasad was made the President.

questions.question_text: Which leader left his very rich legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – During the Non-Cooperation Movement, Motilal Nehru left his very rich legal practice. He did this under the proposal related to the boycott of courts related to the Non-Cooperation Movement. Along with him, many distinguished lawyers like Chittaranjan Das, Pt. Nehru, Patel, Rajendra Prasad, C. Rajagopalachari also left their legal practice.

questions.question_text: Who was the President of the interim government formed in Kabul in 1915?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The President of the interim government formed in Kabul in 1915 was Mahendra Pratap. It is noteworthy that Mahendra Pratap was the President and Barkatullah was the Prime Minister. This government was also recognized by Germany and Russia.

questions.question_text: Who among the following Indian leaders never became the President of the All India Congress?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Among the Indian leaders, Bal Gangadhar Tilak never became the President of the All India National Congress. They were often called Lokmanya and the uncrowned king of India. Tilak was the first person to say that “Swaraj is my birthright and I will have it.”

questions.question_text: Who hoisted the flag of independent India at the Stuttgart Congress in the Second International in 1907 AD?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Madam Bhikaiji Cama belonged to a Parsi family of Maharashtra and was an associate of Shyamji Varma. She left India in 1902 AD and started revolutionary propaganda against British rule in various countries of Europe and America. She lived in Paris, she participated as an Indian representative in the conference of the Second International Socialist Congress in Stuttgart in August 1907 AD and hoisted the national tricolor there. She is called the Mother of Indian Revolution.

questions.question_text: In which Congress session was the national song 'Vande Mataram' opposed by the Congress President?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – In the December 1923 AD Kakinada (Kakinada Congress) session of the Indian National Congress, the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ was opposed by the Congress President, which was presided over by Maulana Muhammad Ali.

questions.question_text: Nationalists used the secret transmitter for the first time near Bombay –

options.B: In the first phase of Civil Disobedience Movement
options.C: In the second phase of Civil Disobedience Movement

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Nationalists used the secret transmitter for the first time near Bombay in the Quit India Movement (1942). The work of radio broadcasting from various centers was first done by Usha Mehta. Which was later shut down after being discovered by the police in November 1942.

questions.question_text: 'Congress is born as a safety valve', whose statement was this among the following:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – "Congress is born as a safety valve" – this statement belongs to Wedderburn. He has written that "a lightning conductor is needed to avoid the increasing powers of dissatisfaction in India and no other thing is a better lightning conductor than the Congress movement."

questions.question_text: Who prepared the Nehru Report?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation– Due to no Indian being in the Simon Commission, the Simon Commission was boycotted by the Congress. Consequently, the then Secretary of State for India Lord Birkenhead challenged the Indians to prepare a consensus constitution and present it to the British Parliament. Accepting this challenge, a 9-member committee was formed in 1928 under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru. On 28 August, 1928, Nehru Report was presented by Motilal Nehru. The inspiration for the Nehru Report was taken from the Bill of Rights of the USA. Special– Jawaharlal Nehru was not a member, he was its secretary.

questions.question_text: In which case was a case filed against Aurobindo:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– A case was filed against Aurobindo (Aurobindo Ghosh) in the Alipore bomb case. In this case, a person named Naren Gosain became a government witness.

questions.question_text: When did Annie Besant stop the Home Rule movement?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– In September 1916, Home Rule League was founded by Annie Besant and Tilak. The Home Rule movement became very popular; consequently, the Secretary of State for India had to speak in the British Parliament and talk about providing responsible government to India. Due to this reason, Annie Besant stopped the Home Rule League in August 1917.

questions.question_text: Where was the Indian National Congress session originally to be held in 1885?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Founder of Congress A.O. Hume had originally announced the organization of the 1885 session of the Indian National Congress in 'Pune', but due to the outbreak of plague in Pune, its location was changed to Bombay.

questions.question_text: Between whom was the Lucknow Pact of 1916 made?

options.C: Between Congress and Home Rule supporters

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002, 2009, 2011 Explanation– The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was made between the Congress and the Muslim League. Under this, for the first time, Congress accepted the demand for separate electorate for Muslims. The 1916 AD Congress session was presided over by Ambika Charan Majumdar and the Muslim League was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

questions.question_text: Who started the 'Khilafat Movement'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Khilafat Movement lasted from 1919 to 1924. This movement was started by Ali Brothers (Shaukat Ali, Muhammad Ali). Later on, Gandhiji joined this movement. The reason for Gandhiji joining this was to increase Muslim cooperation in the freedom movement.

questions.question_text: Who founded 'Punjab Hindu Sabha'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation- Punjab Hindu Sabha was founded in 1909 AD by U.N. Mukherjee and Lal Chand. Lal Chand emphasized Hindu interests and encouraged separatist tendencies among Hindus. After the establishment of Hindu Mahasabha in 1915 AD, he remained actively associated with it. He was also a close associate of Lala Lajpat Rai.

questions.question_text: The Kapila Raj conference is related to which movement?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Hali system is related to 'bonded labor'. Under this system, people of Kapila Raj caste in Bardoli region had to work as hereditary servants for the upper castes. Gandhiji gave Kapila Raj the title of Raniparaj (forest dwellers).

questions.question_text: The second session of Congress was held at –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The first session of the Indian National Congress was held on 28 December 1885 in Bombay. It was presided over by W.C. Banerjee. The second session of Congress was held in 1886 in Calcutta and was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.

questions.question_text: Who was the Congress President in the year 1906 AD?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1886, the Lahore session in 1893, and the Calcutta session in 1906. It is noteworthy that the word 'Swaraj' was used for the first time in the 1906 Calcutta session.

questions.question_text: Which of the following options is true in ascending order?

options.A: Lucknow Pact, Champaran Satyagraha, Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement
options.B: Non-Cooperation Movement, Champaran Satyagraha, Lucknow Pact, Civil Disobedience Movement
options.C: Civil Disobedience Movement, Non-Cooperation Movement, Lucknow Pact, Champaran Satyagraha

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation– Lucknow Pact (1916), Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), and Civil Disobedience Movement (took place in 1930).

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called statement (A) and the other is called reason (R)~ Reason (R): Its objective was to establish a democratic state in India, where there is a representative government of all communities. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: A is true but R is false
options.B: R is true, but A is false
options.C: A and R are both true but R is the correct explanation of A
options.D: A and R are both true but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Gadar Party was born in 1913 in San Francisco's Stockton, America, with the aim of uprooting the British Empire. The founder president of Gadar Party was Sohan Singh Bhakna. Other founding members included Kesar Singh (Vice President), Lala Har Dayal (General Secretary), Lala Thakur Das, etc. The proposal passed on 21 April 1913 said that “Gadar party will liberate India from British rule with the help of armed revolution and establish a national republic (republic).” Thus statement and reason both are true.
examinations: Statement (A): Gadar Party was founded by Lala Har Dayal in the year 1913 AD.

questions.question_text: Who among the following two other leaders besides Dadabhai Naoroji pointed to the evil of economic drain?
questions.explanation: The Theory of drain of wealth was first described by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book (The Poverty and Un British Rule in India). R.C. Dutt has a special place among those who discussed the drain of Indian capital. Mahadev Govind Ranade has also discussed the drain of wealth.

questions.question_text: Match the list of peasant movements given in List-I with their leaders given in List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II (Peasant Movement) (Leader) (i) Swami Sahajanand Saraswati

options.D: Bihar Kisan Sabha (iv) Chittur Singh A B C D A B C D

questions.explanation: Explanation–(Peasant Movement) (Leader) A. Fakir I. Manju Shah B. Ramosi II. Chittur Singh C. Pagal Panthi III. Karam Shah D. Bihar Kisan Sabha IV. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not hanged along with Bhagat Singh?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – On 23 March, 1931 (under the Saunders murder case and Lahore conspiracy case), Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru (Shivram) were hanged. Jatin Das died in Lahore Central Jail due to a hunger strike.

questions.question_text: When was the Dandi March started by Gandhi ji?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─The historic Dandi March was started by Mahatma Gandhi on 12 March 1930. This journey started from Sabarmati Ashram. After his long journey, he reached Dandi on 6 April 1930, broke the salt law by making salt illegally and started the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true?

options.A: The partition of Bengal in 1905 was done with the intention of creating a rift between Hindus and Muslims
options.B: The Muslim League was established in 1906 by Agha Khan
options.C: The Lucknow Pact was an important step towards establishing Hindu-Muslim unity
options.D: The Swadeshi movement was started by Gandhi ji in 1905.

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─The origin of the Swadeshi movement started in opposition to the partition of Bengal. The announcement of the partition of Bengal was made by Lord Curzon on 20 July 1905. In opposition to the partition of Bengal, 7 August 1905 was celebrated as Black Day and the formal declaration of the Swadeshi movement was made. The partition of Bengal was implemented on 16 October 1905. Gopal Krishna Gokhale said that the partition of Bengal is a great cruel mistake. In 1911, on the occasion of the Delhi Durbar, the announcement of the end of the partition of Bengal was made through a document jointly signed by King George V, Queen Mary and Secretary of State for India George Mall.

questions.question_text: Match the revolutionary organizations mentioned in List-I with their founders mentioned in List-II and select the correct answer from the given code: List-I List-II A. Anushilan Samiti (i) Vinayak Damodar Savarkar B. Abhinav Bharat (ii) Barindra Kumar Ghosh C. Gadar Party (iii) Lala Hardayal D. Hindustan Socialist (iv) Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Republican Army Bhagat Singh (H.S.R.A.)
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─The Gadar Party was formed by Lala Hardayal in America in 1913. Anushilan Samiti was established in Kolkata in 1907 by Barindra Kumar and Bhupendra Dutt. Abhinav Bharat was established in Nashik by V.D. Savarkar in 1904. Similarly, the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army was established by Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Bhagat Singh in 1928.

questions.question_text: Baba Ramchandra organized the farmers :
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005, 2009, UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation─Baba Ramchandra emerged as a peasant leader in the mid-1920s. He started organizing the farmers of Awadh. He provided inspiration to the farmers of Awadh through the chaupais of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not included in the first interim national government announced in August, 1946?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was not included in the first interim national government announced in August 1946. Pt. Nehru formed a 12-member interim government on 2 September 1946. The Congress members who were included in this were─ Pt. Nehru, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajagopalachari, Aruna Asaf Ali, Sardar Baldev Singh, Dr. John Matthai, Sarat Chandra Bose, Syed Ali Zaheer, C.H. Bhabha, Jagjivan Ram and Sir Shafaat Ahmed.

questions.question_text: Who among the following did not participate in the All Party Conference called under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru?
questions.explanation: In the conference called under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru in 1928, M. R. Jayakar, Sardar Mangal Singh and Sir Ali Imam were involved.

questions.question_text: Which national movement was supported by Indian capitalists?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─The Civil Disobedience movement was one of the mass movements launched by the Indian National Congress against British imperialism. Under this movement, withholding tax, violating salt laws and making salt by themselves, boycotting foreign goods were included. The Civil Disobedience movement (1930) was supported by Indian capitalists.

questions.question_text: Who presided over the first session of the All India Trade Union Congress held in Bombay in 1920?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 DSSSB PGT 2019 Explanation─Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the All India Trade Union Congress established in Bombay in 1920. Its founder was Narayan Malhar Joshi. Dewan Chaman Lal was appointed the first General Secretary of the All India Trade Union Congress.

questions.question_text: Swaraj Party was established in─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation─The Swaraj Party was established in 1923. C. R. Das was its president and Motilal Nehru was the general secretary. Its purpose was to get Swaraj for India and to oppose those proposals of the government by which attempts were made to make the bureaucracy powerful.

questions.question_text: Who was the first individual satyagrahi after 1940?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – Mahatma Gandhi proposed individual satyagraha on 17 October 1940, for which Acharya Vinoba Bhave was chosen as the first satyagrahi and the second satyagrahi was Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question_text: By whom was the Swaraj Dal formed?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2009 Explanation – After the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn, political consciousness remained among Indians and British policies should be opposed in the house of the British themselves. Working on this policy, in 1923, Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Dal. Its president was C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru was the General Secretary.

questions.question_text: Which European did not become the president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – A.O. Hume was the founder and first general secretary of the Indian National Congress. He never presided over the Congress, whereas George Yule presided over the Allahabad (1888) session, William Wedderburn presided over the Bombay (1889) Congress session, and Henry Cotton presided over the Bombay session (1904).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The national anthem was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee
options.B: The top strip in the Indian flag is green
options.C: Vande Mataram is the national anthem of India
options.D: The flag of independent India was adopted on 22 July, 1947.

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The flag of independent India 'Tiranga' was adopted on 22 July, 1947. The ratio of width to length of the national flag was 2:3. It has a wheel of blue color in it, which has 24 spokes.

questions.question_text: How many Indian women participated in the 1889 Bombay session of the All India Congress?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – A total of ten women participated in the 1889 Bombay session of the All India National Congress, out of which five were Indian women.

questions.question_text: What was the operation run by the British ruler to arrest the leaders of the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – During the Quit India Movement, Operation Zero Hour was run by the British government on 9 August 1942 to arrest the leaders. In this movement, Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of Do or Die.

questions.question_text: Which Indian woman became a minister in the United Provinces in the 1936 elections?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation– In the 1936 provincial elections, Vijayalakshmi Pandit became a woman minister in the United Provinces. Govind Ballabh Pant was elected the Prime Minister (Chief Minister) in the United Provinces.

questions.question_text: How many members of the Muslim League were included in the interim government?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – On 2 September, 1946 AD, the interim government was formed under the leadership of Pandit Nehru. In the beginning, the Muslim League was not included in it, but on 26 October, 1946 AD, five representatives of the League were included in the interim government in place of three original members, not with the spirit of cooperation but to strengthen the fight for a separate Muslim nation (Pakistan).

questions.question_text: Who is the president of the 1925 Kanpur Congress?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─The Congress was established in 1885. The first president of the Congress was Womesh Chandra Banerjee. Sarojini Naidu presided over the Congress session held in Kanpur in 1925. This was the forty-first session of the Congress.

questions.question_text: From which place was Dadabhai Naoroji elected a member of the British Parliament?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Dadabhai Naoroji was elected a member of the British Parliament from the Finsbury constituency. He is also called the Grand Old Man of India. Known as the patriarch of Indian politics, Dadabhai Naoroji used to say, 'I am an Indian beyond religion and caste.'

questions.question_text: At the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress, the Viceroy of India was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – At the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress in 1885, the Viceroy of India was Lord Dufferin (1884-1888). During the time of Lord Lytton (1876-80 AD), the Indian Newspaper Act, i.e., the Vernacular Press Act, was passed in 1878 AD. Lord Ripon (1880-84 AD) repealed Lytton's Vernacular Press Act in 1882 AD and restored the freedom of the press. During the time of Lord Lansdowne (1888-94 AD), under the Age of Consent Act (1891), the minimum age of marriage for girls in India was increased from 10 years to 12 years.

questions.question_text: When was the partition of Bengal annulled?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– During the tenure of Viceroy Lord Hardinge II (1910-1916), the announcement (1911 AD) was made to annul the partition of Bengal in Delhi and shift India's capital from Kolkata to Delhi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the freedom struggle is false?

options.A: The partition of Bengal happened in 1905
options.B: The formation of the Muslim League in 1907
options.C: Independent election rights to Muslims through Minto-Morley reforms

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation– The Muslim League was established in 1906 AD in Dhaka. The first annual session of the Muslim League was held in Karachi in 1907 AD.

questions.question_text: The first European president of the Indian National Congress was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – In the Allahabad session of the Indian National Congress in December 1888, a European person named George Yule was elected president. A.O. Hume is considered the founder of the Indian National Congress. William Wedderburn presided over the Bombay session of Congress (1889 AD). It was in this session that women participated for the first time. William Wedderburn is also known as Hume's biographer. Alfred Webb was elected president of the Congress session in Madras in 1894 AD and the textile industry received protection in this very session.

questions.question_text: Which of the following women was the first female president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation – In 1917 AD, the first female president of the Indian National Congress was Annie Besant and the first Indian female president was Sarojini Naidu. It was in the 1917 Kolkata session that the Congress adopted the tricolor flag for the first time. Programs related to social reforms were also run under the chairmanship of Annie Besant.

questions.question_text: Who founded the 'Depressed Class Mission Society' in Bombay in 1906?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ In 1906, V. R. Shinde founded the Depressed Class Mission Society in Mumbai. Its purpose was to uplift the level of the lower castes and give them a proper place in the field of society-religion and education.

questions.question_text: In which movement did Vallabhbhai Patel emerge as an important leader and was honored with the title of 'Sardar'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ During the Bardoli Satyagraha, Vallabhbhai Patel was honored with the title of Sardar. As a result of the success received from Mahatma Gandhi's movement, the farmers of Bardoli in Surat started a campaign against the increase in land revenue. The peasant leaders there asked Patel to lead the movement. On 4 February, 1928, he took the reins of leadership in his hands. As a result of efficient leadership, this title was conferred upon him.

questions.question_text: Who started the 'Indian Home Rule Society' in London─
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The Indian Home Rule Society was started in London by Shyamji Krishna Varma in 1905. With the cooperation of V.D. Savarkar, Lala Hardayal and Madan Lal Dhingra, he founded this organization with the aim of attaining self-rule for India.

questions.question_text: Which freedom fighter died while fasting in jail?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Jatin Das was a freedom fighter who attained martyrdom on 13 September 1929 after 64 days of 'fasting' in jail. He had gone on a hunger strike to get political prisoner status instead of the ordinary criminals locked in jail.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is known as 'Frontier Gandhi'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Abdul Ghaffar Khan is known as Frontier Gandhi. He played an extremely active role in the Civil Disobedience movement with his organization Khudai Khidmatgar. He was honored with the Bharat Ratna award in 1987.

questions.question_text: Who was directly affected by the 1932 'Poona Pact'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The Dalit class was directly affected by the Poona Pact held on 24 September, 1932. Under this, 147 seats were reserved for the Dalit class in the provincial legislative councils.

questions.question_text: When was the 'All India Untouchability League', which later came to be known as 'Harijan Sevak Sangh', formed?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi founded the 'All India Untouchability League' on 30 September, 1932 for the upliftment of Harijans, which later transformed into the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

questions.question_text: In 1943, where did Subhash Chandra Bose form the Government of Independent India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ In 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose formed the government of independent India in Singapore. It was here that he gave the slogan, "Delhi Chalo and give me blood, I will give you freedom."

questions.question_text: Who is remembered for annulling the partition of Bengal?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Lord Hardinge had an important role in annulling the partition of Bengal. It was during his tenure that the third Delhi Durbar was organized. In this event, King George V annulled the partition of Bengal.

questions.question_text: Who among the following participated in the International Congress organized at Stuttgart and hoisted the Indian tricolor flag there?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ In 1907, Madame Bhikaiji Cama participated in the International Socialist Congress conference in the German city of Stuttgart. It was there that on 22 August, 1907, India's first national tricolor flag was hoisted.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first president of the Indian Home Rule League established in 1916?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation─ The first president of the Indian Home Rule League was Joseph Baptista. On 28 April, 1916, Tilak established the Home Rule League. Five months after Tilak, Annie Besant established her League in September 1916 AD. Annie Besant publicized the programs of the League through her papers Commonweal and New India, and Tilak through Maratha and Kesari.

questions.question_text: Where was the Theosophical Society established?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The Theosophical Society was first established in New York. It was founded by Madame H.P. Blavatsky in 1875. Later, in 1882, the headquarters of this society was opened in Adyar, Madras. The purpose of this organization was to develop national pride and brotherhood among the people of India.

questions.question_text: From where did Mahatma Gandhi start his first Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Mahatma Gandhi started his first Satyagraha from Champaran in 1917 AD. The Champaran movement was related to the farmers. During this Satyagraha, Rabindranath Tagore gave the title of 'Mahatma' to Gandhi ji.

questions.question_text: In the 1923 Legislative Council elections, where did the Swaraj Party gain a majority?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ In the 1923 legislative council election, the Swaraj Party gained a majority in the Central Provinces, winning 42 out of 101 elected seats.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the president of the All India Trade Union Congress organized in Nagpur in 1929?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The All India Trade Union Congress organized in Nagpur in the year 1929 was presided over by N. M. Joshi. It was at this time that the first split occurred in it, the main reason for which was the disagreement between the communists and reformers.

questions.question_text: Who among the following hoisted the tricolor flag with the 'Vande Mataram' slogan in the Chittagong Armoury?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ Surya Sen hoisted the tricolor flag with the Vande Mataram slogan in the Chittagong Armoury. Surya Sen was a teacher at the National School of Chittagong. The 'Indian Republican Army' (I.R.A.) was established in Chittagong by him.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of 'Abhinav Bharat'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ 'Abhinav Bharat' was founded by V.D. Savarkar in 1904 AD in Nashik (Maharashtra). It was a secret organization. Its annual conference used to be organized by the revolutionaries.

questions.question_text: In which session of Congress did the split between moderates and extremists become inevitable?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The 23rd session of Congress was held in Surat in 1907. Its president was Rashbehari Ghosh. In this session, the Congress split into two parts, the moderate group and the extremist group.

questions.question_text: In the moderate era of the Indian National Congress, the title of 'Grand Old Man of India' was given to:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Dadabhai Naoroji was born in a Parsi family in Maharashtra in 1825. In 1892, he was the first Indian who was elected a member of the British Parliament on behalf of the moderate group. He was also the president of the Indian National Congress in 1886, 1893 and 1906. People used to call Dadabhai Naoroji with reverence by the name of ''Old Leader of India''. In this way, Dadabhai Naoroji was definitely an unprecedented person, he was the 'Grand Old Man' of India.

questions.question_text: In which of its sessions did the Congress declare its policy towards the native states for the first time?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- In 1920 only, the Congress session was held in Nagpur, in which the Congress declared its policy towards the native states for the first time and Chakravarti Vijay Raghavachari presided. In this session, changes were made in the constitution of Congress and the Non-Cooperation Movement proposal was also presented.

questions.question_text: What was the subject of discussion in the first part of the 1930 Simon Commission's report, which was distributed publicly in England:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- In the Government of India Act of 1919, it was said that a constitutional commission should be appointed after every ten years. Under this, the Simon Commission was formed in 1927 AD. Indian political parties opposed it. The Simon Commission report was made public in England in 1930, whose main subject was constitutional development.

questions.question_text: Which revolutionary is known by the name of "Master da"?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- In Bengal, Surya Sen, the main leader of Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement, founded the Indian Republican Army. Surya Sen, as part of revolutionary activities, declared war against the British on 18 April 1930, attacking Chittagong, Barisal, etc. Revolutionaries used to call him 'Master da'. On 16 February 1933, the British arrested him.

questions.question_text: Who was the first recipient of the scholarship given by the Indian Society of Oriental Art established in 1907 AD?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- In the first half of the 20th century, where there was political upheaval in India, progress was also happening in the cultural field. Art was developing rapidly in Bengal. In this sequence, in 1907 AD, Abanindranath Tagore established the Indian Society of Oriental Art; the first recipient of the 'Drawing of Youth and Indian Nationalism at the Turn of the Century' scholarship given by it was Nandalal Bose.

questions.question_text: Who was the principal of the National College, Calcutta during the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- On 1 August, 1920, the Non-Cooperation Movement started and continued till 12 February 1922. After this, Gandhi ji postponed it due to the Chauri-Chaura incident. The maximum boycott of educational institutions during the Non-Cooperation Movement happened in Bengal. During this time, Subhash Chandra Bose became the Principal of 'National College Calcutta'. In Punjab, Lala Lajpat Rai boycotted education.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the president of the 1929 Lahore session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- After the expiration of the one-year time limit given to the British government in the Kolkata session of Congress, the Lahore session of Congress was organized on 31 December 1929. This session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question_text: Who was responsible for the appointment of the Simon Commission
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- Secretary of State for India, Lord Birkenhead, who appointed the Simon Commission, was constantly saying that Indian people are incapable of making concrete proposals for constitutional reforms, which would be acceptable to all Indian political parties. Keeping in mind the general elections to be held in Britain in 1929 AD, the government appointed the Simon Commission on 9 November 1927 AD. There were a total of 7 members in this commission, including the chairman- (1) John Simon (2) Mr. Attlee (3) Strathcona (4) Lane Fox (5) Cadogan (6) Attlee (7) Vernon Hartshorn

questions.question_text: Which of the following titles was renounced by Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009, Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- On 13 April 1919 (the day of Baisakhi), a peaceful meeting was organized in Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar in opposition to the firing and arrest of leaders. General O'Dwyer ordered firing without notice at the meeting venue. Many people were killed in this. Hurt by this incident, Rabindranath Tagore returned his 'Knighthood' title to the British.

questions.question_text: When and who formed the Azad Hind Fauj?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- In June 1942, an Indian revolutionary Rash Bihari Bose and Mohan Singh formed the Indian Independence League in Bangkok. On 2 July 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose reached Singapore, to whom the command of the Indian Independence League or Azad Hind Fauj was handed over.

questions.question_text: During whose reign did the Ilbert Bill controversy happen?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009, Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- George Frederick Samuel Robinson, 1st Marquess of Ripon, was the Governor General and Viceroy in India from 1880 to 1884 AD. He did a lot for Indians, in which passing the first Factory Act, economic decentralization, etc., were prominent, but he resigned due to the Ilbert Bill controversy.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in their correct chronological order and select the correct answer from the code given below: A. Deccan Riots case B. Pavana rebellion C. Indigo rebellion D. Rebellion of Poligars of Tamil Nadu Code:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– A. Deccan Riots – 1874-75 B. Pavana rebellion – 1873-76 C. Indigo rebellion – 1859-60 D. Rebellion of Poligars of Tamil Nadu – 1799

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the All India Muslim League?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka, the announcement of the establishment of the All India Muslim League was made in a meeting organized in Dhaka on 30 December, 1906 AD.

questions.question_text: Who were the trio of Indian nationalism

options.A: Mahatma Gandhi, Subhash Chandra Bose, Jawaharlal Nehru
options.B: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal
options.C: Subhash Chandra Bose, Jayaprakash Narayan, Rash Bihari Bose
options.D: V.D. Savarkar, Lala Hardayal, Chandra Shekhar Azad

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal were the trio of Indian nationalism. Due to opposing the Non-Cooperation Movement, the importance of Bipin Chandra Pal decreased. Lala Lajpat Rai and Bal Gangadhar Tilak remained dominant in Indian politics until their death.

questions.question_text: By what name was the Gadar Party known initially?

options.D: Hindustan Association of the Pacific Coast

questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– The Gadar Party was established in America with the cooperation of Lala Hardayal. It was initially known as the Hindustan Association of the Pacific Coast. Prior to the First World War, there was an increase in revolutionary activities in India.

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy said with emphasis that 'benevolent bureaucracy' cannot run forever?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Lord Ripon's tenure is 1880 to 1884 AD. During his time, the Factory Bill Act (1881 AD) and the famous Ilbert Bill controversy happened.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in their correct chronological order and select the correct answer from the following code: A. Nasik Conspiracy Case B. Ahmedabad Bomb Case C. Peshawar Conspiracy Case D. Alipore Conspiracy Case Code:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– The chronological order of the various conspiracy cases that occurred during the freedom movement is as follows– Alipore Conspiracy Case - 1908 Ahmedabad Bomb Case - 1909 Nasik Conspiracy Case – 1910 Peshawar Conspiracy Case - 1923

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the book 'Bandi Jeevan'?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– 'Bandi Jeevan' was written by the great revolutionary Sachindranath Sanyal. The book Bandi Jeevan is called the Bible of revolutionaries.

questions.question_text: Who appointed the National Planning Committee in the year 1938?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– In the Haripura session of Gujarat in 1938 AD, Subhash Chandra Bose formed the National Planning Committee and made Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru its president.

questions.question_text: Who was the first General Secretary of the All India Trade Union Congress?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation– The All India Trade Union Congress was established in 1920 and its first president was Lala Lajpat Rai and its first general secretary was Dewan Chamanlal.

questions.question_text: 'Indian Sociologist' was started by
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– 'Indian Sociologist' was started by S. Krishna Varma.

questions.question_text: Khudiram Bose was connected to–
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation- Khudiram Bose was born in Bengal on 3 December 1880 AD. He was connected to Muzaffarpur.

questions.question_text: Which Nawab of Bengal compared the Europeans to bees?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- In 1740, the Naib Subedar of Bihar, Alivardi Khan, became the Nawab of Bengal through a rebellion. He obtained the acceptance of this from Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah. Alivardi Khan was capable; he drove the British out of Bengal. His thought was that Europeans are like bees. If they are not bothered, they will give honey, and if they are bothered, they will sting and kill. Alivardi Khan's words proved true in the future.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the founder of the independent Awadh state?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The subah of Awadh, spread from Kanpur in the west to the Karmanasa river in the east, was a vast and prosperous region.
