The founder of the Awadh state was Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk. He had declared independence from the Mughal state during the time of Muhammad Shah.

questions.question_text: Where did the Santhal rebellion take place?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The Santhal people of Rajmahal district expressed their resentment against the ill-treatment at the hands of land revenue officials, police oppression, and the collections of zamindars and moneylenders, and under the leadership of Sidhu and Kanhu, they declared the end of the Company's rule and declared themselves independent, and only after extensive military action in 1856 AD did the situation come under control. Special– Among all tribal rebellions, the Santhal rebellion was the most armed rebellion. The government quieted their rebellion by creating the 'Santhal Parganas' due to the rebellion of the Santhals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following women was not related to the revolutionary movement?
questions.explanation: In the revolutionary organization of Bengal, women revolutionaries Kalpana Datta and Bina Das were involved in the Chittagong armoury raid. Bina Das shot Bengal Governor Stanley Jackson while receiving her degree at the Kolkata University convocation. In 1907, Madame Bhikaiji Cama hoisted the national tricolor flag in Stuttgart (Germany). She is called the `Mother of Indian Revolution'. Toru Dutt, born in Bengal on 4 March 1856, was a famous English language poetess.

questions.question_text: In which session of the Indian National Congress was Sarojini Naidu elected as its president?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu was elected president of the Congress in the 1925 Kanpur session. She was elected as the first Indian woman president of the Congress. In this session, Hindi was used as the national language. A prominent Congress leader, Hasrat Mohani, presented the proposal for "Purna Swaraj" for the first time, but it could not be passed.

questions.question_text: Who was the author of the book 'Unhappy India'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- Lala Lajpat Rai was a leader of the extremist group and protested against the Simon Commission that came to India in 1928 in Lahore, and he died due to injuries received in a lathi charge by the police during this protest. He wrote 'Unhappy India'. He started 'Punjabi' and 'Vandemataram' newspapers and started an English paper 'The People'.

questions.question_text: Who among the following threw a bomb on the legislative assembly on 8 April, 1929?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw two bombs and some leaflets in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April, 1929 AD, when the Public Safety Bill and Trade Dispute Bill were being discussed in the assembly. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt were arrested and a case was filed against them in the Central Assembly Bomb case.

questions.question_text: As a result of the Poona Pact, the number of seats reserved for the Dalit class out of the total constituency seats:
questions.explanation: Against the Communal Award, Gandhi ji went on a fast in jail on 20 September, 1932. His health started deteriorating rapidly. Due to the efforts of Madan Mohan Malviya, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, etc., the Poona Pact took place between Gandhi ji and Ambedkar on 24 September, 1932. Under this, the separate electorate for Dalit classes was abolished. But the number of reserved seats for Dalit classes in provincial legislative councils was increased from 71 to 147.

questions.question_text: In which year was the 'Indian Press Emergency Powers Act' passed?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- The 'Indian Press Emergency Powers Act' was passed in 1931 AD. Due to the momentum in the political movement in the fourth decade of the 20th century and the Civil Disobedience movement started by Mahatma Gandhi ji, the government passed the Indian Newspaper (Emergency Powers) Act in 1931 AD. Through this, provincial governments were given excessive powers to suppress the propaganda of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question_text: Dandi is situated in-
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009, UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Dandi is situated in the Navsari district (Gujarat) on the sea coast. During the Civil Disobedience movement, Gandhi ji reached Dandi with his 78 followers, picked up a handful of salt, and broke the salt law.

questions.question_text: Jallianwala Bagh incident happened
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened in Amritsar on 13 April, 1919. General Dyer ordered indiscriminate firing on a meeting being held in opposition to the arrest of Dr. Satyapal and Saifuddin Kitchlew. According to the government report, 379 people and according to the Congress committee, approximately 1000 people were killed.

questions.question_text: Which Governor General declared that after the death of Bahadur Shah, the Mughals would be deprived of the title of King?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- In 1856, Governor-General Canning decided that Bahadur Shah Zafar would be the last Mughal Emperor. After his death, no descendant of his would be considered Emperor. They would be recognized only as princes. Special Fact - In 1849, Governor General Lord Dalhousie announced that after the death of Bahadur Zafar, the emperor's family would be removed from the Red Fort and would be settled somewhere else in Delhi.

questions.question_text: 'Secular-e-Azadi' named circular is related to
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Ramanath Puri is related to the Secular-e-Azadi named circular, whereas Taraknath Das started Free Hindustan in Vancouver and G.D. Kumar brought out a newspaper named Swadesh Sevak in Gurmukhi script in Vancouver.

questions.question_text: Kalpana Datta's connection was with
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Kalpana Datta's connection was with the Indian Republican Army. Among the revolutionaries of Bengal, the name of Surya Sen is prominent, whom people often used to call 'Master da'. Angry with the policies of the British, he established the Indian Republican Army. Women like Kalpana Datta and Bina Das were associated with this. Members of the Indian Republican Army– (1) Ganesh Ghosh (2) Ananda Gupta (3) Tegraval (4) Lokenath (5) Kalpana Datta (6) Pritilata Waddedar (7) Tulemian and Mir Ahmed etc. were involved.

questions.question_text: Who was the editor of 'Struggle for Freedom'
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The editor of 'Struggle for Freedom' was R.C. Majumdar. Bipin Chandra, Satish Chandra, and Jadunath Sarkar are authors of various histories. Jadunath Sarkar wrote more about Shivaji (Maratha history), whereas Bipin Chandra provided important information about the freedom struggle.

questions.question_text: The first conference of the Congress Socialist Party was held in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The Congress Socialist Party was established inside the Congress in October, 1934. Its first conference was held in October, 1934 AD. Jawaharlal Nehru's inclination was towards socialism. In a conference, he said I believe in socialism, that is why after becoming Prime Minister, he toured various socialist countries.

questions.question_text: Who is known by the name of 'Grand Old Man of India'
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Dadabhai Naoroji is known by the name of 'Grand Old Man of India'. He termed the drain of wealth as 'the evil of all evils'. Dadabhai Naoroji was the first person in India to calculate the per capita income of Indians. He was born in a Parsi family.

G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- After the victory in the July 1937 elections, the Congress formed governments in a total of 6 provinces. These provinces were Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar, Bombay and Orissa. At that time, there were a total of 11 provinces in India, in which the Congress formed its government in two places (North-West Province, Assam) by joining with like-minded parties.
examinations: Congress ministries were formed in July 1937 in:

questions.question_text: Who was the honorary editor of 'Indian Opinion'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Mansukhlal Nazar is known as the honorary editor of 'Indian Opinion'. Gandhi ji had started the publication of this magazine during his South African tour, which was quite popular among Indians.

questions.question_text: Underground movements were associated with which Gandhian movement?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Underground movements were associated with Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi's Quit India Movement. On 9 August, 1942 AD, all other important leaders including Gandhi ji were arrested. Some important leaders were leading the movement by going underground. Prominent among them are Usha Mehta, Ram Manohar Lohia, Achyut Patwardhan, Sucheta Kripalani, etc. Usha Mehta operated the radio.

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the 'Uttar Pradesh Kisan Conference' held in Allahabad in 1935?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- In the year 1935 AD, the president of the Uttar Pradesh Kisan Conference held in Allahabad was Jawaharlal Nehru. In this conference, the problems of farmers as well as the atrocities being committed on farmers by the British were also thought about.

questions.question_text: In the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League, the Pakistan proposal was passed
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- In this session, the 'Pakistan proposal' was passed. On 23 March, 1940, the Muslim League session was held in Lahore. This session was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah and this proposal was passed that a new separate state 'Pakistan' should be made from India. The originator of the word Pakistan was Chaudhary Rahmat Ali. The Public Service Commission accepted option (d) as correct in the first answer key.

questions.question_text: Who among the following were associated with the labor union movement in India? 1. B.P. Wadia 2. N.M. Joshi 3. K. Kamaraj 4. Vithalbhai Patel
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- B.P. Wadia and N.M. Joshi were associated with the labor union movement in India. The 'Madras Labour Union' formed by B.P. Wadia in 1918 AD was India's first modern labor organization. Vithalbhai Patel was a prominent leader of the Swaraj Party. The Swaraj Party was founded by Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das.

questions.question_text: Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association was founded by:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Gandhi ji had founded the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association in 1918 AD. Mahatma Gandhi wanted to improve the condition of workers through the Textile Labour Association and wanted to bring a new consciousness into their lives, which was the biggest trade union of that time, and during the establishment of this organization, Gandhi ji had expounded his famous trusteeship theory.

questions.question_text: The founder of Krishak Praja Party in Bengal was
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The founder of the Krishak Praja Party in Bengal was Fazlul Huq. Fazlul Huq joined the Congress in 1904 but later became a member of the Muslim League. He represented the Muslim League in the first and second Round Table Conference. He was also the Chief Minister of Bengal from 1937 to 1943 AD.

questions.question_text: What proposal was given in the 1940 'August Offer'?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Viceroy Lord Linlithgow presented the August Offer on 8 August 1940. In the 1940 'August Offer', the proposal of Dominion Status was given. All the political parties of India rejected the British proposal, ultimately the August Offer was not very successful.

questions.question_text: In colonial Indian history, the Telangana movement was related to
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- In colonial Indian history, the Telangana movement was related to the peasant movement. The purpose of this peasant movement, which took place in the Telangana estate of Andhra Pradesh between 1946 and 1951, was to oppose the exploitation policy of moneylenders and the atrocities of corrupt officials. Collecting grain at a low price was the main reason for this movement.

questions.question_text: In 1936, the Independent Labour Party was founded by one of the following:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar formed the Independent Labour Party in 1936 regarding his demands. During the freedom movement, Dr. Ambedkar, along with Muhammad Ali Jinnah, demanded a separate country for the untouchables. He was given the law ministry in the Nehru cabinet against his wishes.

questions.question_text: The Trade Disputes Act passed in 1938 was mainly related to
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- The Trade Disputes Act passed in 1938 AD was mainly related to a ban on strikes. In 1926, a right was given to workers under which strike was accepted as legal; this improved the condition of workers significantly.

questions.question_text: Who synthesized the famous slogan 'Vande Mataram' with Vande-O-Vande Mataram?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Swami Sahajanand synthesized the famous slogan 'Vande Mataram' with Vande-O-Vande Mataram. Swami Sahajanand was a nationalist leader.

questions.question_text: The first Indian Civil Service examination in 1922 was held in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- In 1922, for the first time in India, the Indian Civil Service examination was held in Allahabad. Lord Cornwallis is considered the founder of Civil Service in India. Cornwallis implemented the Permanent Settlement (Land Revenue) system in India in 1793 AD.

questions.question_text: Who founded the East India Association in London?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Dadabhai Naoroji remained active socially and politically during his lifetime. He spent his time in London from 1855 to 1869 and for this, he established the "London Indian Society" and the "East India Association".

questions.question_text: Before obtaining Hastings, where was the Company's treasury?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In 1772, Warren Hastings was appointed as the Governor of Bengal by the East India Company. Immediately upon coming to India, Warren Hastings ended the Dual system in 1772 and gave orders to the Kolkata Council and its head that they themselves should become Diwans and take the management of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa into their hands, and he ordered the treasury to be brought from Murshidabad to Kolkata.

questions.question_text: Which Indian leader clearly believed that the Indian National Congress was formed so that it could act as a 'safety valve' to protect British rule?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The failure of the 'petition-request policy' of the Congress leadership created dissatisfaction inside the country and inside the Congress. Lala Lajpat Rai believed that the Indian National Congress was formed so that it could act as a 'safety valve' to protect British rule.

questions.question_text: For promoting nationalism, Bal Gangadhar Tilak used to bring out a newspaper
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Tilak was the first nationalist leader who tried to establish close relations with the public. He started Shivaji and Ganpati festivals so that the feeling of nation service could awaken in the public. He started two newspapers for the propagation of his ideas, 'Maratha' in English and 'Kesari' in Marathi. He founded the Lathi Club.

questions.question_text: Who described the policies of the moderate leaders as "political mendicancy"?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation- Bal Gangadhar Tilak described the policies of the moderate leaders as "political mendicancy". Tilak was a leader of the extremist group, that is why he used to criticize the policies of the British, due to which he also had to go to jail. People used to call him the 'Uncrowned King' of India. He founded gyms, lathi clubs, and anti-cow slaughter societies.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct answer from the code given below: 1. Dandi March 2. Jallianwala Bagh massacre 3. Quit India Movement 4. Swadeshi movement Code:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The Swadeshi movement was started on 7 August, 1905, in opposition to the partition of Bengal. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar. Dandi March happened on 12 March 1930 under the leadership of Gandhi ji. The Quit India Movement started on 9 August 1942 from the Gowalia Tank Maidan of Mumbai. It was in this movement that Gandhi ji gave the slogan of 'Do or Die'.

questions.question_text: Who shot Sir Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation- On 1 July, 1909 AD, in London, Madan Lal Dhingra shot and killed the political advisor to the India Office, Curzon Wyllie. Dhingra was arrested and hanged. After this, Veer Savarkar was arrested and sent to India so that he could be tried in the Nasik conspiracy case.

questions.question_text: When did the Muslim League demand a separate Muslim state?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The Muslim League session was held in Lahore on 23 March 1940 AD. It was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah. In this session, the demand for a separate Muslim state (nation) 'Pakistan' from India was made. While addressing the session, Jinnah said that they would not accept anything other than a separate Muslim nation.

questions.question_text: Why did Mahatma Gandhi withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922?

options.A: Most leaders were arrested and were in jail.
options.B: The British were somewhat ready to accept the demands.
options.C: He did not see any possibility of the success of the movement.
options.D: Due to the violence that happened in Chauri-Chaura.

questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- On 4 February 1922 AD, in Chauri-Chaura, a place in Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces, where an angry mob set fire to the police station due to police firing on a farmers' procession, in which 21 policemen including a station officer died. Hurt by this incident, Gandhi ji postponed the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February in Bardoli. Note Š Currently, the date of the Chauri-Chaura incident is considered 4 February 1922, before this, this date was considered 5 February 1922.

questions.question_text: "We will either take independent India or die in the attempt." This slogan was given by
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- The Congress session was held in Mumbai on 7 August, 1942, presided over by Abul Kalam Azad. Nehru presented the "Quit India Proposal" and it was accepted on 8 August, 1942. Gandhi ji gave a 70-minute speech in this historic Congress conference and said that "We will either take independent India or die in the attempt."

questions.question_text: In which year did Jawaharlal Nehru hoist the tricolor flag on the banks of the Ravi river in Lahore and declare 'Purna Swaraj' as the goal of the freedom struggle?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In December, 1929 AD, the annual session of the Congress was held. Gandhi ji was elected president of this session, but he made Jawaharlal Nehru president in his place. Jawaharlal Nehru said that "Today we have only one goal - the goal of independence. For us, independence means complete independence from the British empire."

questions.question_text: At which place was the proposal for complete independence of India passed?:
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- In December 1929 AD, the annual session of Congress was held in Lahore. In this session, the proposal for Purna Swaraj (independence) was passed. In this very meeting of the Congress, it was decided to celebrate Independence Day on 26 January, 1930 AD in all of India.

questions.question_text: Who formed the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885?

options.A: S. N. Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose
options.B: P. Ananda Charlu and M. V. Raghava Chariar
options.C: Ferozeshah Mehta and P. Ananda Charlu
options.D: K. T. Telang and Ferozeshah Mehta

questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Ferozeshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji, K. T. Telang and Kashinath Trimbak formed the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885 AD in Mumbai. On 31 January, 1885 AD, a meeting of citizens was called in Mumbai under the chairmanship of Jamsetjee Jeejeebhoy, and this association was formed in this meeting. Its purpose was to propagate political ideas among the people.

questions.question_text: Subhash Chandra Bose formed the 'Government of Independent India' in Singapore
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Subhash Chandra Bose reached Singapore on 2 July, 1943 AD. On 5 July, 1943 AD, Rash Bihari Bose handed over the presidency of the Indian Independence League to Subhash Chandra Bose. On 21 October 1943 AD, Subhash Chandra Bose, in the capacity of Supreme Commander of the Azad Hind Fauj, established the temporary government of independent India in Singapore.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Indian Governor General of independent India?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- At the time of independence, the Governor General of India was Lord Mountbatten; in 1948, he resigned and went back to England. After this, Chakravarti Rajagopalachari was appointed as the first Indian Governor General. He also remained the last Governor General of independent India. On 26 November, 1949 AD, the Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly and the post of Governor General was abolished.

questions.question_text: Which of the following started suspecting Bengali and Maratha leaders of running a revolutionary plan like Ireland after 1885?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Lord Curzon was the Governor General of India from 1899 to 1905 AD. During his time, revolutionary activities increased in India. Observing the incident in Pune in Maharashtra and the movement going on in Bengal, Curzon started suspecting. Are Bengali and Maratha leaders running revolutionary activities like Ireland?

questions.question_text: Which Act is called 'Black Law' in India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- To suppress the increasing revolutionary activities in India, the government formed a committee in 1917 under the chairmanship of Sydney Rowlatt, whose purpose was to form an effective plan to suppress revolutionary activities. The bill passed in March, 1919, based on the suggestions of this committee, was known as the 'Rowlatt Act'. Through the Rowlatt Act, the British government could keep anyone in jail for as long as they wanted without trial, hence this law was called no lawyer, no appeal, no argument, and Black Law.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a member of the 'Board of Three' (Board of Three) to whom the administration of Punjab was handed over after the victory of Punjab?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- After the Punjab victory, Governor General Lord Dalhousie formed a three-member council to look after the administration of Punjab. The members of this council were John Lawrence, Robert Montgomery, and Sir Henry Lawrence.

questions.question_text: Who used the American slogan 'No taxation without representation' for the first time in Indian politics?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Dadabhai Naoroji used the American slogan "No taxation without representation" for the first time in Indian politics. Dadabhai Naoroji was the first such nationalist leader of modern India who, based on deep research and analysis, proved that Britain was economically exploiting India and a fixed amount was being taken to England every year. In this context, he expounded his 'Drain Theory'.

questions.question_text: Which international event influenced the Indian National Movement the most?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The Russo-Japanese war happened for the first time between 1904-1905. Japan won this war. After this war, the Russian revolution started and the second Russo-Japanese war happened in 1945. Both these wars influenced the Indian National Movement excessively.

questions.question_text: Who among the following presided over two sessions of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- William Wedderburn presided over the following sessions of the Indian National Congress:- (a) 5th December, 1889 Mumbai (b) 25th December, 1910 Allahabad

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started his historic Dandi march from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) with his 78 chosen followers on 12 March, 1930 AD. On 5 April, 1930, after traveling 243 miles, he reached Dandi, and on 6 April, 1930, he broke the salt law by illegally making salt in Dandi. In this movement, leaders like Sarojini Naidu, C. Rajagopalachari, Abbas Tyabji, etc., participated along with Gandhi ji.

questions.question_text: Who among the following started his political life as a moderate, but later became its critic?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- After 1906 AD, along with the rise of the extremist group inside the Congress in Indian politics, a revolutionary group also appeared in the country. There were four main leaders of the extremist ideology- Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Arvind Ghosh. Bipin Chandra Pal started his political life as a moderate, but later became its critic.

questions.question_text: Who presented the Gandhi-Irwin Pact proposal at the Karachi session (1931) of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - The Congress authorised Gandhiji for talks with the Viceroy. After long talks between Gandhi and Irwin, on 5 March, 1931, an agreement was signed between both, which is known as the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. The proposal for this agreement was presented by Jawaharlal Nehru at the Indian National Congress session (1931) of Karachi, where this proposal was passed.

questions.question_text: Who gave the presidential address at the 1930 Muslim League session?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - Poet Mohammad Iqbal is considered the initiator of the idea of a separate nation for Muslims. Inspired by the sentiment of 'Pan-Islam', in his presidential address at the 1930 Allahabad session of the All India Muslim League, Iqbal said, "If this principle is accepted that Indian Muslims have the right to full and independent development of their culture and traditions in their own country, then my desire would be that, by combining Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan, a separate state be created. Within or outside the British Empire, the formation of a North-West Indian Muslim state appears to me to be the ultimate goal of the North-West Indian Muslims at the very least."

questions.question_text: Who called Lala Lajpat Rai "Prince of Peace Makers"?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - Motilal Nehru called Lala Lajpat Rai "Prince of Peace Makers". Lala Lajpat Rai was born on 28 January 1865. He is also called Punjab Kesari. He established the Punjab National Bank. He was a prominent leader of the extremist faction in the Indian National Congress. He took part in a demonstration against the Simon Commission in 1928, during which he was injured in a lathi charge and eventually died.

questions.question_text: What was the name of the revolutionary who threw a bomb at Lord Hardinge?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - At the time of the capital transfer from Calcutta to Delhi (22 December, 1912), the great revolutionary of Bengal, Rash Behari Bose, had planned to throw a bomb at Lord Hardinge.

questions.question_text: The first graduate woman who addressed the Congress session in 1890?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - Kadambini Ganguly was the first graduate woman who addressed the sixth session (Calcutta-December, 1890) of the Indian National Congress.

questions.question_text: Who was the second Governor General of India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - The first Governor General of India was William Bentinck (1828-1835) and the second Governor General was Charles Metcalfe (1835-1836). During the tenure of Charles Metcalfe, the restrictions on newspapers were removed; he was called the 'Liberator of newspapers'.

questions.question_text: Who called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation - The Anglo-Indian bureaucracy considered Bal Gangadhar Tilak a rebel. Valentine Chirol had called him the 'Father of Indian Unrest'. Tilak went to England with the purpose of filing a defamation suit against Chirol. Although he lost the suit, it had a widespread impact.

questions.question_text: Who became the Premier (Prime Minister) of the United Provinces in 1937?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–In the provincial legislative elections held in January–February, 1937, wiping out their rival parties, Congress obtained a full majority in five provinces: Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar, and Orissa. Govind Ballabh Pant was made the Premier, i.e., Prime Minister, of the United Provinces in 1937 AD.

questions.question_text: Due to the intervention of Gandhi ji in the Ahmedabad mill strike in the year 1918, the income of the workers increased by:
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–After the success of Champaran, the next experiment of Gandhi ji's satyagraha was to intervene in the dispute going on between mill owners and workers regarding increasing wages in a cotton mill in Ahmedabad in 1918. This dispute was regarding the plague bonus. After deeply studying the production, cost, profit, and the living expenses of the workers, Gandhi ji declared that the workers should receive a 35 percent bonus. The tribunal formed after Gandhi ji's fast accepted this fact.

questions.question_text: In which session of the Indian National Congress did it pass a resolution on Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–To give approval to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Delhi Pact), the Karachi session of Congress was held on 29 March, 1931, under the presidency of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. In this very session, resolutions related to Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programmes were passed by the Congress for the first time. Jawaharlal Nehru had pioneered the resolution on fundamental rights and economic programmes passed in this session, and M.N. Roy played a supporting role in it.

questions.question_text: Who was the initiator of Indian Communism?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–The initiator of Indian Communism was M.N. Roy. The Communist Party of India was established in Kanpur in December, 1925 AD. This is the oldest Communist party of India, whose existence continues in India's current politics even today. The Communist Party of India was first established in Tashkent on 17 October, 1920, by Manabendra Nath Roy.

questions.question_text: When did the first session of the Indian National Congress take place?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–The first session of the Indian National Union was organised on 28 December, 1885, at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit School located in Bombay. In this conference, on the suggestion of Dadabhai Naoroji, the name of the Indian National Union was changed to 'Indian National Congress'. This first session was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee.

questions.question_text: On which day did the Muslim League celebrate 'Deliverance Day'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation–The then Viceroy Lord Linlithgow declared without the consent of Indians that India is also involved in the war along with Britain against Germany in the Second World War. In protest against this, ministers of Congress-governed provinces resigned from the ministries on 1 November, 1939, after the approval of the Congress Working Committee. After the resignation of the Congress ministers, the Muslim League, along with the Dalit leader Bhimrao Ambedkar, celebrated 'Deliverance Day or Deliverance Day' (Day of Deliverance) on 22 December 1939.

questions.question_text: Who were the Presidents of the Constituent Assembly of India:
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–On 9 December, 1946, in the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly, Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the temporary President. On 11 December, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was appointed as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the Irwin-Gandhi Pact?

options.A: Release all political prisoners including those convicted for violence.
options.B: Agreed to waive all fines not yet collected by the government.
options.C: Liberal treatment should be meted out to government employees who had resigned.
options.D: The government accepted the right to make salt for the use of villagers living on the sea coast.

questions.explanation: The following points related to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact are correct – (i) Liberal treatment should be meted out to government employees who have resigned. (ii) Agreement was reached on waiving all fines not yet collected by the government. (iii) The government accepted the right to make salt for the use of villagers living on the sea coast. Whereas the statement given in option (a) to release all political prisoners including those convicted for violence is not correct.

questions.question_text: Who was the leader of the Indian revolutionaries in Paris during the First World War?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–In 1905, the associate of the founder of the India House society in London, Shyamji Krishna Varma, Madam Bhikaiji Rustom K.R. Cama, who is also called the 'Mother of Indian Revolution', led the Indian revolutionaries in Paris during the First World War.

questions.question_text: Who coined the name 'Pakistan' first?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 TGT History, 2009, 2003, 2001 PGT History 2004 Explanation–Between 1933 and 1935 AD, a Muslim student named Choudhury Rahmat Ali, who was studying at Britain's Cambridge University, issued a pamphlet and gave birth to the concept of a separate state 'Pakistan'. This concept of Pakistan by Rahmat Ali included Punjab, Afghan province, Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events of the Indian national movement in chronological order according to the codes given below- 1. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 2. Poona Pact 3. Karachi session of the Indian National Congress 4. Individual Satyagraha Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– The Gandhi-Irwin Pact took place in March 1931, in which the government promised that except for those guilty of violence, all political prisoners would be released. The seized property would be returned. Permission would be given to prepare salt within a specific limit of the sea coast. And Congress would participate in the Second Round Table Conference, etc. A Congress meeting was held in Karachi on 29 March, 1931, to give approval to the Gandhi Irwin Pact (Delhi Pact). The Karachi session became a memorable session. It was in this session that for the first time Congress passed resolutions related to Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programmes. In 1932, the Poona Pact took place between Gandhi and Ambedkar. Under this agreement, the separate electorate for the Dalit classes was ended. Individual Satyagraha was started in 1940 AD.

questions.question_text: Who declared Queen Victoria as the Empress of India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- During the reign of Lord Lytton, in the time from 1876 to 1878 AD, a terrible famine occurred in India. Madras, Bombay, Mysore, Hyderabad, Punjab and most parts of Central India were affected by this famine. Lakhs of people died in this famine and the arrangements made by the government to help the famine victims did not prove sufficient. At that very time, in 1876 AD, under the Imperial Title Act, Queen Victoria was granted the title of Empress of India. For its announcement, Lord Lytton organised a big Durbar in Delhi in January 1877 AD. Excessive money was spent on the splendour of the Durbar and that too at a time when a severe famine was occurring in most parts of India. This caused intense discontent in India. From that very time, Lala Lajpat Rai and Surendra Nath Banerjee started their public movement.

questions.question_text: Who said on the death of Tilak, "My strongest bulwark is gone"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Tilak, along with Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal, formed the Nationalist or Extremist faction. This faction was an opponent of the moderate policy of the 'old generation' of the Moderate faction. If the birth of extremism in Indian politics happened due to the plague outbreak and the strict policy of the officials in 1897 as per Mrs. Annie Besant's view, then the credit for that change goes to Tilak only. Tilak was the first person who clearly demanded Swaraj. His words, "Swaraj is my birthright and I will have it", generated a new wave of enthusiasm in every corner of the country. Sir Valentine Chirol considered him the "Father of Unrest in India". Tilak died in 1920. On his demise, Gandhi ji said that "My strongest bulwark is gone". to generate a new wave of enthusiasm in every corner of the country. Sir Valentine Chirol considered him the "Father of Unrest in India". Tilak died in 1920. On his demise, Gandhi ji said that "My strongest bulwark is gone".

questions.question_text: Who instigated the 'Bengal Partition'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Lord Curzon's policy, mainly the Bengal-Partition and its bitter language, generated intense discontent among Indians. An intense movement arose in India against the Bengal partition. On the occasion of the Bengal partition, the movement of 'boycott of foreign goods' and 'use of Swadeshi goods' was started, which the Congress used in the future as the main means to struggle against the British rule. At different places in Bengal, foreign goods were burnt, washermen refused to wash foreign clothes, public meetings were held. Indeed: Indians started their struggle on the occasion of the Bengal partition. Undoubtedly, it gave a boost to extremist nationalism.

questions.question_text: From the point of view of chronology, which of the following events was the last?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- From the point of view of chronology, the event that happened last was the Moplah rebellion which took place in 1921 AD. The Home Rule League movement was run in 1916. The Khilafat movement took place in 1919 and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April, 1919 AD. In August, 1921, on the other end of the country in the Malabar district (Kerala), the rebellion of the tenants was far more widespread and aggressive than many other peasant struggles. Their problems were like those of the peasants of the Awadh province. The landlords used to evict them whenever they wanted, collect arbitrary rent, and commit various types of atrocities. Even in the 19th century, Moplah peasants had struggled against the landlords, but the rebellion that erupted in 1921 was on an entirely different scale than before.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below- Assertion (A) : Mrs. Annie Besant organised the Home Rule Movement against British rule. Reason (R) : She wanted to organise people of all classes on the basis of a slogan. Code :

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Annie Besant formed the Home Rule League in September 1916 and wanted to organize people of all classes through it. She organized public meetings and conferences. Her demand was that just as the people in white colonies have been given the right to form their own government, the Indian people should also get the right to self-rule. The Home Rule demand was based entirely on religious neutrality. In the words of Tilak, "Whether it is English or Muslim, if he works for the welfare of the people of this country, then he is not an outsider to us. This foreignness has nothing to do with religion or profession. This is a question directly related to interests." The biggest achievement of the Home Rule movement was that it prepared combative soldiers for future national movements. The Home Rule movement included many new regions in the national movement, such as Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Sindh, Madras, Central Province, and Berar.

questions.question_text: Who was the first president of the Muslim League?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in Dhaka under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah. Its first president was Viqar-ul-Mulk Mushtaq Hussain. Nawab Salimullah was its founding president.

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Statement (A) and the other is called Reason (R)- Statement (A): The leading leaders of the Indian National Congress did not like the idea of giving independent status to the princely states. Reason (R): It was believed that the existence of their independent states would not have any impact on India becoming a progressive nation. Which of the following is correct regarding both the above statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (A) is the correct explanation of (R).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (A) is not the correct explanation of (R).

questions.explanation: "The leading leaders of the Indian National Congress did not like the idea of giving independent status to the princely states." This statement is true, while the given reason is false.

questions.question_text: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, where did Sarojini Naidu lead the satyagrahis to raid the salt depot?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation– Sarojini Naidu led the satyagrahis to raid the Dharasana salt depot. She was also the first Indian woman president of the Congress (Kanpur, 1925). Describing the terrifying form of Dharasana, journalist Miller has written that "As a correspondent, I have witnessed countless civil rebellions in the last 18 years, but I have never seen such a terrifying scene as Dharasana in my life."

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions did the Muslim League pass a resolution in which cow slaughter was prohibited on the occasion of Bakrid?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- After the First World War, during the protest against Rowlatt Acts and during the Khilafat and Non-cooperation movements, the nationalist current became stronger and slogans of Hindu-Muslim unity were raised. The Muslim League passed a resolution in the 1919 Amritsar session and banned cow slaughter on the occasion of Bakrid. The Muslim League passed this resolution keeping in mind Hindu-Muslim unity. As if to show the whole world that Hindus and Muslims are one. Famous Arya Samaj leader Swami Shraddhanand was invited to speak from the stage of Delhi's Jama Masjid, and the keys of Amritsar's Golden Temple were handed over to Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew. The storm of 'Jai of Hindu-Muslim unity' started blowing across the country. Landlords, communalists, and former bureaucrats started breaking their ties with the Muslim League. The importance of the League started decreasing day by day due to the Khilafat Committee. The Khilafat movement was religious, but it was helpful in awakening national and anti-imperialist sentiments among the Muslim public and middle class.

questions.question_text: Who was the first person to advocate for the ideology of the Swadeshi movement?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- First of all, Bholanath Chandra of Bengal advocated for the ideology of the Swadeshi movement. He advised not to use foreign goods. Arya Samaj founder Swami Dayanand Saraswati also supported Swadeshi. In the 1905 Benares session and in Bengal, the Swadeshi and boycott movements were supported. Extremist leaders like Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Aurobindo Ghosh wanted to spread this movement across the country. They were not satisfied with mere Swadeshi and boycott but wanted to give it the form of a political mass struggle. "The demand to end the partition of Bengal had now become a very small issue." But the moderate leaders were not ready for this yet.

questions.question_text: In the context of Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi march, which of the following is not true?

options.B: It started with 78 satyagrahis, in which Hindus, Muslims and Christians were included.
options.C: Its goal was the violation of salt law.
options.D: Reaching the seashore, Mahatma Gandhi made salt.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- On 12 March 1930 AD, Gandhi ji started a foot march for Dandi with his 78 supporters and after traveling 241 miles in 24 days, he reached Dandi in April and violated the salt law by picking up a handful of salt. Gandhi ji, Sardar Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru, and other leaders were all arrested. Indians broke the salt law at various places, boycotted foreign goods, and got liquor shops closed. The government's repression cycle also started, and on that occasion, nearly one lakh people were imprisoned. In this movement, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and his supporters 'Khudai Khidmatgar' were at the forefront. On this occasion, Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru and Dr. Jayakar tried to mediate, but it could not be possible because the government wanted the movement to end without any conditions, for which the Congress was not ready.

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions did the Indian National Congress adopt the Swadeshi resolution?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- In the 1905 Benares session of the Indian National Congress, which was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, a suggestion to adopt Satyagraha was made for the first time. In the 1906 Calcutta session, resolutions regarding Swadeshi, boycott, and national education were passed. Extremist leaders like Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Aurobindo Ghosh wanted to spread this movement across the country. They were not satisfied with mere Swadeshi and boycott but wanted to give it the form of a political mass struggle. Now the goal was 'Swaraj'. The demand to end the partition had now become a very small issue, but the moderate leaders were not ready for this yet. Meanwhile, differences continued between the moderate and extremist factions of the Congress regarding the speed of the movement and methods of struggle, and in the 1907 Surat session of the Congress, the party split. This split had a serious impact on the Swadeshi movement.

questions.question_text: Why was the Swaraj Party founded?

options.B: To create obstruction in legislative assemblies
options.C: To form a parallel organization to Congress
options.D: Due to a split in Congress leadership

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- The Swaraj Party was founded by C.R. Das with the help of Motilal Nehru. In its manifesto, declaring its policy, it pledged that they would follow the policy of continuous, consistent, and uninterrupted obstruction to stop the government's work through the central legislative assembly and provincial councils. Leaders like Vithalbhai Patel, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and M.R. Jayakar had the support of the Swaraj Party. To stop the government's work through the central legislative assembly and provincial councils. Leaders like Vithalbhai Patel, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and M.R. Jayakar had the support of the Swaraj Party.

questions.question_text: Who founded the All India Harijan Sangh in 1932 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Mahatma Gandhi honored the backward and Dalit people of society by calling them Harijan and founded the "All India Harijan Sangh" in 1932 AD. Whereas B.R. Ambedkar had formed an organization called 'Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha' in Bombay in July 1924, whose purpose was to uplift the untouchable people morally and physically. He adopted the policy of movement and tried to achieve civil rights like entry into temples and drawing water from public wells for the untouchables. Ambedkar opposed the Indian National Congress's demand for independence and said that British empire should remain in India so that the interests of the Dalit class could be protected. In April 1942, he formed the Scheduled Castes Federation as an all-India party. Behind this, he declared that the scheduled castes would completely renounce the Hindu religion, and he himself, along with many of his followers, became Buddhist.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the secret revolutionary organization named 'Abhinav Bharat'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003, 2005

questions.question_text: Who among the following did not face trial in the Kakori case?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- In October 1924, a conference of revolutionary youths was held in Kanpur, and the Hindustan Republican Association (or Army) was formed. Its goal was to overthrow colonial power through armed revolution and establish a 'federal republic' 'United States of India'. Before starting the struggle, the youth had to be brought into their party, trained, and weapons gathered. For this, money was needed. The Hindustan Republican Army's first big operation for collecting money took place in Kakori. This incident of looting the government treasury is known as the 'Kakori' case, which occurred on 9 August 1925 near Lucknow. The government was very furious over this incident. A large number of youths were arrested, and they were tried in court, and Ashfaqulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri were hanged, and four were sentenced to life imprisonment and sent to Andamans, and 17 others were given long sentences, in which Chandrashekhar Azad remained absconding.

questions.question_text: Which session was the Surat session where the first split occurred in the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Under the Indian National Congress, an extremist group was established which was in favor of the demand for complete Swaraj. Differences between the extremist group and the moderate leaders kept increasing. In 1906 AD, due to the skill of President Dadabhai Naoroji, the struggle between the two groups was stopped that year, but on the occasion of the Congress's twenty-third (1907) Surat session, there was a fight between the two groups. That same year, Rash Behari Bose was chosen for the post of president, whereas the extremists wanted to make Lala Lajpat Rai, who had withdrawn his name, the president. However, the main fight was on the issue of boycott, Swadeshi, and national education, which the Congress had already accepted in its Calcutta session. The extremist group was in their favor, whereas the moderate group did not want to give them re-acceptance. For this reason, there was an open fight between the two, and Tilak and his associates were separated from the Congress.

questions.question_text: Where is Haripura, where Congress held a session in 1938 AD, located?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003, 2005 Explanation- Subhash Chandra Bose was a staunch opponent of the 'moderate group' of the National Congress. During the 1928 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, he strongly opposed the resolution of provincial governance autonomy approved by the Nehru Report in the 'Special Committee'. He wanted complete independence. In February 1938, in the Haripura (Gujarat) session, Subhash Babu was elected president of the Congress. Again, in the 1939 Tripuri Congress session, despite Mahatma Gandhi's opposition, he was elected Congress president. Possibly this was Mahatma Gandhi's biggest defeat. However, in the Congress Working Committee, Gandhi's supporters had a majority. Therefore, he resigned from the post of Congress president in April 1939.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a leader of the Hindu Mahasabha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- In 1915, Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya founded the Hindu Mahasabha in Haridwar. In 1933 AD, Bhai Parmanand presided over the Hindu Mahasabha conference held in Ajmer. In 1938 AD, V.D. Savarkar became its president. Syama Prasad Mookerjee remained the president of the Hindu Mahasabha from 1940-44 AD. M.R. Jayakar never became the president of the Hindu Mahasabha, but he was associated with this Sabha. The leaders of the Hindu Mahasabha were not behind in spreading communalism. Two main moderate Hindu communal leaders of the 1920s, Lala Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya, were no longer present on the political stage. Lala Lajpat Rai had already died, and Malaviya ji had retired from active politics. Since Hindu communalism was not going to end due to historical reasons, the reins of it were taken over by the Hindu Mahasabha under the leadership of V.D. Savarkar. Savarkar was warning Hindus that Muslims wanted to dominate Hindus and wanted to make them slaves in their own country.

questions.question_text: Who was the first secretary of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003, 2005 Explanation- In 1884 AD, an organization named "Indian National Union Congress" was founded through the efforts of a retired English civil officer named A.O. Hume. This Union decided to hold a conference of representatives of the nation in Pune in 1885 AD and handed over the responsibility of this task to A.O. Hume. Due to the spread of plague in Pune, that year this conference was held in Bombay. This conference was held in December 1885 AD, and there, an organization named "All India Congress" was established. Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee was elected its first president, and Hume became the first secretary. In this way, in 1885 AD, during the time of Lord Dufferin, this national organization was born.

questions.question_text: On which of the following dates was the decision of Bengal partition implemented?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – The decision of the Bengal partition was announced by Viceroy Curzon on 19 July 1905. This partition became effective from 16 October 1905.

questions.question_text: The title of the Cambridge pamphlet was-

options.A: Now or Never Are We to Live or Perish Forever

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- The title of the Cambridge pamphlet of 1933 AD was "Now or Never Are We to Live or Perish Forever". In this pamphlet, the word 'Pakistan' was introduced for the first time. Political thinker Muhammad Iqbal is considered the pioneer of the idea of a separate state 'Pakistan' for Muslims. Inspired by the idea of Pan-Islamism, Iqbal said in the 1930 All India Muslim League's Allahabad session, "If this principle is accepted that the permanent solution to India's communal problem is that Indian Muslims have the right to full and independent development of their culture and traditions in their own country, then it would be my desire that Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, Sindh, and Baluchistan should be joined to form a state. It seems that the ultimate goal of Muslims in a North-West India within or outside the British Empire is this."

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Swadeshi movement is not true?

options.A: Women refused to wear foreign bangles in the movement.
options.B: Washermen favored washing foreign clothes, so that their income would increase.
options.C: Ganapati and Shivaji festivals became the medium for the promotion of Swadeshi in Bengal.
options.D: The song 'Amar Sonar Bangla' was written by Rabindranath Tagore during this movement.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The movement that arose in protest against the Bengal partition started taking a new path, a path of new struggle for new goals. Its base also started getting stronger very quickly. The president of the Barisal conference (1906), S. Abdul Rasul, said, "What we could not achieve in the last 50 to 100 years, we have achieved in six months, and the Bengal partition has brought us here." The shameful event of partition gave birth to the great national movement - the Swadeshi movement. Through the Swadeshi and boycott movement, women participated in the movement. They refused to wear foreign bangles. Ganapati and Shivaji festivals became the medium for the promotion of Swadeshi in Bengal. Rabindranath Tagore composed the song "Amar Sonar Bangla" during this movement. Washermen also refused to wash foreign clothes. Women participated enthusiastically in the Swadeshi movement. They boycotted foreign clothes and goods and picketed liquor shops.

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Philosophy of the Bomb'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003, 2005 Explanation- Revolutionaries Sukhdev, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Shiv Verma, Vijay Sinha, Yashpal were all educated and intellectuals. Chandrashekhar Azad, who had very little knowledge of English, did not accept any idea or ideology until he understood it completely. The statement or document that the revolutionaries issued to make the public aware of their ideology titled 'The Philosophy of the Bomb' (Philosophy of the Bomb) was prepared by Bhagwati Charan Vohra at Azad's request. Before writing, every issue was discussed with Azad. Bhagat Singh's belief in the actions of individual heroism and terrorism had faded even before his arrest. He had become a Marxist and had started believing that revolution can be brought only through a massive mass movement. In other words, "the people can make a revolution for the people."

questions.question_text: What was the goal of which movement to achieve Swaraj within a year?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- In December, the annual session of the Congress was held in Nagpur. C.R. Das presented the program of the Non-Cooperation movement. Its president was Vijay Raghavachariar. Everything came under this. Like returning titles and honors, boycott of government schools, colleges, courts, foreign clothes. In this proposal, it was also said that later, the public could also be told to resign from government jobs and disobey laws, in which non-payment of taxes was also included. There was a strict instruction to encourage hand spinning and weaving and to follow non-violence in every condition. Gandhi ji gave assurance that if these programs were implemented completely, independence would be achieved within a year.

questions.question_text: On which date did Edwin Montagu announce the British policy of increasing cooperation with Indians in every part of the administration?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Edwin Montagu announced the British policy of increasing cooperation with Indians in every part of the administration on 20 August, 1917. This is also called the August Declaration.

questions.question_text: Who among the following were appointed as members of the India Council in England in 1909?

options.B: K.G. Gupta and Syed Hussain Bilgrami
options.C: Sir Ganga Singh and Aga Khan
options.D: C.P. Ramaswami Aiyer and Ali Imam

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Through the Morley-Minto Reform Act of 1909, two Indians – K.G. Gupta and Syed Hussain Bilgrami were appointed to the India Council located in England.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and indicate your correct answer from the codes given below the lists- List I (Organization) List II (Year) Code: A B C D A. Gadar Party 1. 1925 B. Communist Party of India 2. 1928 C. Congress Socialist Party 3. 1913 D. Hindustan Socialist Republican Association 4. 1934
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The chronology of organizations formed before independence is as follows- Gadar Party- 1913 AD, Communist Party of India 1925 AD, Congress Socialist Party 1934, Hindustan Socialist Republican Association 1928 AD.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Muslim League openly demand a separate country for Indian Muslims for the first time in its annual session?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- In March 1940, the session of the Muslim League was held in Lahore. In this session, it passed a resolution for the partition of the country. The Indian national press gave this Lahore resolution the name 'Pakistan Resolution'.

questions.question_text: In the announcement of the 'Communal Award' in 1932 by Ramsay MacDonald, who was given the right of separate electorate?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Ramsay MacDonald announced the 'Communal Award' in 1932, under which a separate electoral college was announced for minorities. Muslims and Sikhs were already considered minorities; now, under this law, the Dalit class, i.e., Harijans, were also considered minorities and arrangements were made for their separate electorate.

questions.question_text: Who among the following did not face the trial in the Kakori case?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation- On 9 August 1925 AD, the 8 Down train was stopped and looted in Kakori, in which ten revolutionaries were sent by H.R.A, but the trial was conducted on 40 people, among whom Chandrashekhar Azad could not be arrested.

questions.question_text: Indicate the correct chronology of the following events with the help of the group given below- 1. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 3. Jallianwala Bagh massacre 4. Quit India Movement Code: 2. Cabinet Mission
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The correct chronology of the given events is- Jallianwala Bagh massacre - 13 April 1919 AD. Gandhi-Irwin Pact - 5 March 1931 AD. Quit India Movement - 8 August 1942 AD. Cabinet Mission - 16 May 1946 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not present at the founding session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013, TGT History 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation- The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 AD at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay. There were a total of 72 members in it, one-third of whom were journalists. Surendranath Banerjee was not present at this session; rather, he merged his National Conference into the Indian National Congress in 1886.

questions.question_text: What was the goal of the Swaraj governance movement started by Annie Besant?

options.C: To agitate against British monopoly in administration

questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – In early 1915, Annie Besant started a movement through two newspapers, 'New India' and 'Commonweal'. Her demand was that just as the people in white colonies have been given the right to form their own government, the Indian people should also get the right to self-rule.

questions.question_text: Congress accepted the separate electorate for Muslims -
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – In the 1916 Lucknow Congress session, Tilak was re-included in the Congress. In this session, the important Congress-League Pact took place, which is known as the 'Lucknow Pact'. Tilak and Annie Besant played an important role in this pact. In this session, Congress accepted the separate electorate for Muslims. Madan Mohan Malaviya believed that too much importance was being given to the Muslim League.

questions.question_text: After the resignation of Subhas Chandra Bose, who became the President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2013 Explanation – The annual session of Congress was held at Tripuri in March 1939. In the election for the post of President, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the representative of Gandhi ji. Due to differences over the formation of the Congress Working Committee, Subhas Chandra Bose resigned. Again, Rajendra Prasad was elected President in his place. In the same year, Subhas Chandra Bose established the Forward Bloc.

questions.question_text: Who was the biographer of A.O. Hume?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation- Wedderburn wrote the biography of A.O. Hume, which was published in 1913. This biography discussed a secret report of seven volumes for the first time. Among the documents related to the establishment of the Congress that Hume possessed, Wedderburn found one such document on which no date was written. Wedderburn referred to this document in detail in Hume's biography. According to Lala Lajpat Rai, despite this fact, "even though Hume was a lover of freedom, he was first and foremost an 'English patriot'." When he saw that "a serious crisis was about to befall the British rule," he decided to create a safety valve for the safe development of discontent.

questions.question_text: Who among the following read Dadabhai Naoroji's presidential address at the 1906 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation- In the 1906 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, a right step was taken in the direction of the national movement. In his presidential address, Dadabhai Naoroji said that the objective of the Indian National Congress is to form its own government in India like Britain or its colonies, that is, the establishment of Swaraj. Meanwhile, differences between the Moderate and Extremist factions of the Congress regarding the pace of the movement and methods of struggle continued, and in the 1907 Surat session, the party split over the Swadeshi movement. This split had a serious impact on the Swadeshi movement. The president of the 1906 Indian National Congress was Dadabhai Naoroji; his presidential address was read by Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

questions.question_text: Which Englishman participated in the 1907 Surat session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The 1907 Surat session of the Indian National Congress was held on 26 December on the banks of the Tapti river, in which the Congress was split. At that time, the new Secretary of State for India was John Morley. He prepared an alternative policy to weaken the national movement. Instead of appeasing the moderates, he adopted the policy of taking them along. This policy had three objectives - repression, conciliation, and suppression. An Englishman named H.W. Nevinson, who was a journalist by profession, participated in the 1907 Indian National Congress session at Surat. He has also given a description of the incident that happened in the Congress pandal on 27 December. In this session, the leader of the moderates was Ferozeshah Mehta and the leader of the extremists was Aurobindo Ghosh. The president of the Surat session was Rash Behari Ghosh. There was only this one Englishman in this session.

questions.question_text: Who supported Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation resolution at the 1920 Calcutta special session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- In 1920, Gandhi ji advised the Khilafat Committee to launch a non-violent non-cooperation movement against the British government. On 9 June 1920, the Khilafat Committee in Allahabad accepted this advice unanimously and entrusted the task of leading this movement to Gandhi ji. In May 1920, a meeting of the All India Congress Committee took place and it was decided to organize a special session of the Congress in September. The Congress session was held in Calcutta in September. Despite opposition from many senior leaders, the Congress gave approval to the Non-Cooperation movement and accepted it as its own movement. Prominent among the opponents were C.R. Das, while supporters included Motilal Nehru, Saifuddin Kitchlew, Shaukat Ali, Yakub Hasan, Dr. Ansari, Jitendra Nath Banerjee, whereas among the opponents were C.R. Das, Madan Mohan Malviya and Annie Besant.

questions.question_text: Who was the Governor of Bombay Presidency during the Bardoli Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The Bardoli Satyagraha took place in the Bardoli taluka of Gujarat in the year 1928. During the Bardoli Satyagraha, the Governor of Bombay Presidency was Leslie Wilson. Born in 1874, Vallabhbhai Patel was already known as an organizer, speaker, and person with a struggling personality. In the Bardoli Satyagraha, he was given the title of 'Sardar'. This title was conferred upon him by the women of Bardoli. The people of Bardoli still remember the speeches of Vallabhbhai Patel, those speeches which used to touch the hearts of the farmers. The farmers of Bardoli even today say that 'Vallabhbhai Patel's speeches were such that they could even bring the dead to life.' Sardar Patel was the second most important leader after Mahatma Gandhi. Due to the participation of Vallabhbhai Patel, the revenue officer Maxwell reduced the tax limit to 6 percent and on this achievement, the women here gave Vallabhbhai Patel the title of Sardar.

questions.question_text: In which session did the Muslim League give the 'Divide and Quit' slogan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The Muslim League passed a resolution in the Karachi session (1943) and gave the 'Divide and Quit' slogan. In the League's presidential address in April 1943, Jinnah himself used words like "in-charge of making the war-propaganda and spreading anti-Hindu influence in them" for Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan. A Muslim leader from Sindh, M.H. Gazdar, said in the League meeting in Karachi in March 1943 that "if Hindus do not come to the path, they will have to be finished in the same way as Jews were in Germany". Since Jinnah's tone in his speeches was also like this, how could he stop these leaders from using such language?

questions.question_text: Who presided over the first session of the All India Trade Union Congress (A.I.T.U.C.) in Bombay?
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004, 2005 TGT History, 2004 Explanation- In 1920, the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was established. Lokmanya Tilak had become very close to the workers of Bombay. He holds an important place among those who inspired the establishment of AITUC. Famous leader of the extremist faction of Punjab, Lala Lajpat Rai became its first president and Dewan Chaman Lal became the General Secretary. In the first session of AITUC, Lala Lajpat Rai emphasized that "Indian laborers should not lose even a moment in organizing at the national level. There is the greatest need to organize, agitate, and educate in the country. We must organize our workers at all costs and make them class-conscious."

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists- List I List II (a) Rajendra Lahiri 1. Gonda jail (b) Sukhdev 2. Lahore Central jail (c) Roshan Singh 3. Gorakhpur jail (d) Ram Prasad Bismil 4. Allahabad jail
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- A. Rajendra Lahiri - Gonda jail B. Sukhdev - Lahore Central jail C. Roshan Singh - Allahabad jail D. Ram Prasad Bismil - Gorakhpur jail Sukhdev, Bhagat Singh and Rajguru were hanged in Lahore Central jail and Rajendra Lahiri in Gonda jail, Ram Prasad Bismil in Gorakhpur jail and Roshan Singh in Allahabad jail.

questions.question_text: The jail where Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, Bhai Parmanand and Ashutosh Lahiri spent their imprisonment life was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Savarkar was a prominent revolutionary of Maharashtra and a true son of Mother India. In the year 1904 AD, he established a revolutionary organization named 'Abhinav Bharat'. Under his leadership, revolutionaries like Chapekar brothers, Shyamji Krishna Varma, Ganesh Savarkar etc. did many terrorist acts to overthrow the British government. Savarkar conducted revolutionary activities while living in England for some days. Finally, the British government arrested him and sent him to the Andaman Islands. Along with Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, Bhai Parmanand and Ashutosh Lahiri also spent their prison life in Cellular Jail.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correctly matched?

options.B: The Indian Unrest : Subhas Chandra Bose

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- 'The Indian Opinion' is a newspaper brought out by Gandhi ji from South Africa. 'Commonweal' is Annie Besant's newspaper. 'The Indian Unrest' is Valentine Chirol's newspaper and Allan Octavian Hume's biographer is William Wedderburn. He wrote the biography of A.O. Hume which was published in 1913. In this biography, a secret report of seven volumes was discussed for the first time. Among the documents related to the establishment of the Congress that Hume possessed, Wedderburn found one such document on which no date was written. Wedderburn has referenced this document in Hume's biography.

questions.question_text: Why was there a split in the All India Trade Union Congress in 1929, due to which N.M. Joshi had to form the Indian Trade Union Federation?

options.B: To obtain government grants for the organization
options.C: Differences over joining the organization with the international communist movement
options.D: Personality clash between Nehru and Jayaprakash Narayan

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- In 1929, the All India Trade Union Congress split into two parts. Under the leadership of N.M. Joshi, the moderate people separated from the Trade Union and established the Indian Trade Union Federation (I.T.U.F). An important reason for the split of the All India Trade Union Congress was the growing influence of communists on it. By the time of the 1928 Jharia session, the position of leftists, including communists, in "AITUC" had become quite influential. After this, when Jawaharlal Nehru was presiding over the session, during that time, some people separated from it under the leadership of N.M. Joshi, and from here the trend of economism (economism) in the labor movement started. At the end of 1928, the government became worried and started giving reports that "hardly any public service or industry remains in which communism, which has influenced the whole country, is not fully or partially present."

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below- List I List II (a) Mahatma Gandhi in Champaran 1. D.P. Mishra (b) The Springing Tiger 2. Rajendra Prasad (c) Living in Era 3. Hugh Toye (d) India from Curzon to Nehru and After 4. Durgadas
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- (a) Mahatma Gandhi in Champaran - Rajendra Prasad (b) The Springing Tiger - Hugh Toye (c) Living in Era - D.P. Mishra (d) India from Curzon to Nehru and After - Durgadas

questions.question_text: Indicate the name of that I.C.S. officer who worked secretly for the communist movement and who carried out subversion of the British empire in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- H.V. Kamath used to work secretly for the communist movement. The influence of the Russian Revolution was the main motivating force behind the Indian communist movement. People were suddenly attracted towards socialist theories, especially towards Marxism, which was the important theory of the Bolshevik party (Communist Party). People of Asia were especially attracted to this. Together with M.N. Roy, Indians established the 'Indian Communist Party' in Tashkent in October 1920. The main form of political work of the early communists was to organize the groups of workers and farmers and work through them. In 1924, in Kanpur, the government tried to crush the communists by embroiling Sripad Amrit Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Nalini Gupta, and Shaukat Usmani in a conspiracy case. All four were sentenced to four years of imprisonment.

questions.question_text: Who among the following defended Aurobindo Ghosh with great skill in the Alipore conspiracy case?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Chittaranjan Das defended Aurobindo Ghosh with great skill in the Alipore conspiracy case of 1908 AD. In the Alipore conspiracy case, 34 people, including Aurobindo Ghosh and his brother Barindra Ghosh, were arrested. In which 15 people were convicted and some of them (in which Barindra Ghosh was also included) were sentenced to life imprisonment and sent to Kala Pani. Aurobindo Ghosh was released.

questions.question_text: Who wore hand-spun Khadi cloth and participated in the Imperial Durbar (1877)?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Ganesh Vasudev Joshi wore hand-made Khadi clothes and participated in the Imperial Durbar (1877 AD). On 12 January 1872, he had taken a pledge to use Khadi and followed it throughout his life. G.V. Joshi was the first patriot to promote and propagate the use of Khadi. He was the one who first gave the idea of Swadeshi in India. Due to the public works done by him, he was also known as "Sarvajanik Kaka".
