questions.question_text: When was India's capital shifted from Old Delhi to New Delhi?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation─On 12 December 1911 AD, a grand durbar was organized in Delhi. Here, the announcement of the annulment of the partition of Bengal was made and the announcement to shift India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi was made. In 1912 AD, Delhi became the capital of India. Again, on 6 February 1931, India's capital was shifted from Old Delhi to New Delhi.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the Gadar Party?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– In the first phase of the revolutionary terrorist movement, many Indians settled in the United States of America and Canada. Among these immigrants was the revolutionary from Punjab, Lala Hardayal. Through his efforts, on 1 November 1913, the Gadar Party was founded in San Francisco, USA. Among its prominent leaders were Bhai Parmanand, Ram Chandra, and Barkatullah, etc. Sohan Singh Bhakna was its first president, and Lala Hardayal was the general secretary.

The British decided to partition Bengal with the intention of attacking this combative consciousness. On 20 July 1905, Curzon announced the Bengal partition. The Bengal partition became effective from 16 October 1905.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005, 2003 Explanation– Mahatma Gandhi was the writer of the Quit India resolution; later, due to his ill health, this responsibility was handed over to Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question_text: Consider the following - 1. Rajagopalachari Formula 2. Wavell Plan 4. Mountbatten Plan Decide their correct chronology from the code given below - Code : 3. Cabinet Mission
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation– Raja ji Formula On 6 May 1944, the government released Mahatma Gandhi from jail. At this time, the future strategy of the Congress's national movement was in confusion because Indian leaders and the public had no information about the government's next step. Taking advantage of these circumstances, the government started encouraging anti-Congress groups, mainly the Muslim League, the benefit of which the Muslim League took and, in response to the Congress's Quit India movement, gave a new slogan (Divide and Quit), due to which Jinnah's demand for Pakistan became even more powerful. To remove these political deadlocks, Mahatma Gandhi wrote a letter to Muhammad Ali Jinnah, through which he once again emphasized the establishment of communal unity. Jinnah did not agree with Mahatma Gandhi's ideas. On this, Chakravarti Rajagopalachari, who had resigned in 1942 over a policy difference with the Congress on the issue of Pakistan, prepared a formula, which became famous in Indian history by the name of 'Raja ji Formula'. Jinnah rejected this formula as well. In September 1944, Mahatma Gandhi tried several times to get Muhammad Ali Jinnah to accept this formula. But Jinnah said that in this formula, he was being given only a slice of bread, whereas he wanted a full loaf; he presented his demands. Wavell Plan In place of Lord Linlithgow, Lord Archibald Wavell became the Viceroy of India in October 1943. After the failure of the talks with Gandhi and Jinnah, Lord Wavell went to England in March 1945 to resolve the Indian constitutional deadlocks. He discussed the Indian issues with the British government there. Lord Wavell and the Secretary of State for India, Amery, were of one opinion regarding removing political deadlocks and moving India towards the goal of complete self-rule and conducting constitutional agreements. They presented the following plan which was presented in London and then in New Delhi on 14 June 1945 - 1. The British government wants to end the political deadlocks and move India towards the goal of self-rule. 2. In the new executive council of the Viceroy, all members except the Viceroy and the Commander-in-Chief should be Indians. 3. The foreign department should be with an Indian member. 4. The number of high-caste Hindus and Muslims in the council should be equal. 5. A temporary interim government should be formed at the center in which the Governor-General does not use special powers. 6. High Commissioners should be appointed for the protection of British commercial and trade interests in India like in other colonies. 7. The Indians themselves should formulate the future constitution. Simla Conference Following the announcement of the Wavell Plan, all members of the Congress Working Committee were released. The order of house arrest that was on Gandhi had already been lifted before that. The announcement to hold a meeting of political leaders on 25 June 1945 in Simla was made on 14 June. Cabinet Mission On 18 February 1946, the Royal Navy mutiny started, and on 19 February 1946, British Prime Minister Attlee announced sending the Cabinet Mission to India to solve the problems, whose members were three cabinet ministers - 1. Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India) 2. Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade) 3. Lord A.V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty) Mountbatten Plan Lord Mountbatten was sworn in as Viceroy on 24 March 1947. Upon arriving in India, Mountbatten started talks with Congress, League, and Akali leaders. Keeping the goal of the Mountbatten Plan in view, his advisors reached the decision that the transfer of power could not be stopped until June 1948 because communal riots were increasing day by day. Therefore, on 18 May, he went to London and informed the British government of his thoughts and, after discussing with the British government, presented a plan on 3 June 1947, which is known in Indian history as the Mountbatten Plan, which contained the following facts - 1. In this plan, the establishment of Pakistan was accepted, but the whole of Assam, Punjab, and Bengal were not included in it. 2. The British government expressed its desire to announce independence in 1947 itself. 3. Assam and Bengal (Sylhet, which was a Muslim-majority region) should be given the opportunity to decide their fate through a referendum. This same opportunity was also provided to the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan. 4. A proposal to constitute a commission to determine the border of partition. 5. An agreement to divide the liabilities and assets of the dominions of India and Pakistan. 6. Native princely states to have the freedom to join India or Pakistan. 7. India and Pakistan would have the right to withdraw from Commonwealth membership.

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the Indian National Congress at the time of India's independence?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation– At the time of India's independence, the president of the Indian National Congress was J.B. Kripalani.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in correct order with the help of the code below :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The Hunter Committee was formed on 14 October 1919 to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919, whose president was William Hunter. There were three other English members in it and there were also three Indian members - Chimanlal Setalvad and Pandit Jagat Narayan and Sahibzada Sultan Ahmed Khan. The Hunter Committee submitted its investigation report in March 1920. Home Rule Movement: After the outbreak of the First World War and the release of Tilak in 1914 after completing his imprisonment sentence, Tilak and Annie Besant decided to start the Home Rule Movement with each other's mutual cooperation. In April 1916, Tilak founded the Indian Home Rule League and 5 months later, in September 1916, Annie Besant established the Home Rule League. Jallianwala Bagh massacre: Occurred on 13 April 1919. Rowlatt Act: A sedition investigation committee was formed on 10 December 1917 under the chairmanship of Justice Rowlatt. Based on this, the law that was passed on 15 April 1919 is called the Rowlatt Act. Thus Answer (a) is correct.

questions.question_text: Who was not associated with the Gadar Party?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The Gadar Party was founded in America through the inspiration and efforts of Lala Hardayal, and he had gone to America according to the plan of the India House Society. India House Society was organized by Sardar Kishan Singh; Lala Hardayal was also among its prominent members. The main members of the Gadar Party were Lala Hardayal, Bhai Parmanand, Pandit Kanshiram, Kartar Singh Sarabha, Ram Chandra, and Ganesh Vishnu Abhyankar. Shyamji Krishna Varma promoted the Indian revolutionary movement abroad. He had gone to London on Tilak's recommendation. With the help of some English friends, he started a newspaper named 'Indian Sociologist' and founded the Home Rule Society and India House in 1905. Thus Shyamji Krishna Varma was not associated with the Gadar Party.

questions.question_text: During which Viceroy's tenure did the 'White Mutiny' occur?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The White Mutiny occurred during the tenure of Lord Ripon (1880-84). This rebellion was done by Europeans against the Ilbert Bill. Sir C.P. Ilbert was a law member of the Viceroy's council; he had placed a bill in the legislative council, which is generally called the Ilbert Bill. The purpose of this bill was that all judicial disqualifications based on caste should be abolished immediately and the powers of Indian and European judges should be made equal. As soon as this bill was introduced, a storm arose. Europeans considered this an attack on their special privileges. To protect their special privileges, the European community formed a defense association. Finally, Ripon had to bow down. According to a compromise, such a decision was made that the purpose could not be fulfilled.

questions.question_text: Who was not a member of the Motilal Nehru Committee?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Following the boycott of the Simon Commission, Indian political parties, forgetting their ideological differences, established a joint platform, which is called the All-Party Conference. In the Bombay meeting of the conference on 19 May 1928, a committee was formed under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru, whose other members were - Tej Bahadur Sapru, Sir Ali Imam, Shoaib Qureshi, M.R. Jayakar, Subhash Chandra Bose, M.S. Aney, N.M. Joshi, Mangal Singh, G.R. Pradhan. Jayakar later withdrew his name from this committee. The report presented by this committee is called the Nehru-Sapru report or generally the Nehru report. Aurobindo Ghosh was not a member of this committee. He had gone to Pondicherry in 1910, where he spent his life in meditation and spiritual activities. Jawaharlal Nehru did not serve as a member in the Nehru committee, but as a secretary.

questions.question_text: During which Viceroy's tenure was India's capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : During the tenure of Viceroy Lord Hardinge II (1910-1916), in 1912, the British capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi. In 1912 only, the announcement to make Delhi a province was made. The appointment of the Sadler Commission in 1916 and the establishment of Banaras Hindu University in Varanasi were also done during his tenure. Lord Chelmsford's tenure is 1916-21. Lord Reading's tenure is 1921-26. Lord Curzon's tenure is 1899-1905.

questions.question_text: Who called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Author of 'Indian Unrest', Valentine Chirol (Valentine Chirol), called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of unrest in India'. For this, Tilak filed a defamation case against Chirol and even went to England for that purpose. Although Tilak lost the case, it had a fair impact. Valentine Chirol has also called Arya Samaj the 'Father of Indian Unrest'.

questions.question_text: Match the following individuals with places and select the correct answer from the code given below : A. Baba Ramchandra 1. Bihar (Hajipur) B. Swami Sahajanand 2. Faizabad (Oudh) C. Vallabhbhai Patel 3. Bardoli (Gujarat) D. N.G. Ranga 4. Guntur (Andhra Pradesh) Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Baba Ramchandra: He was from a Brahmin family of Maharashtra and had left home at the age of 13. He was of a wandering nature, went to Fiji. He did hard labor there and returned in 1909, went to Faizabad (Uttar Pradesh). He organized the peasants of Oudh. Swami Sahajanand: He was a lifelong ascetic, freedom fighter, and prominent peasant leader of Bihar. He formed the Bihar Kisan Sabha in 1929. He also presided over various conferences of the All India Kisan Sabha. Due to his selfless service towards the peasants, he came to be known as 'Kisan-Pran'. Vallabhbhai Patel: He entered politics after participating in the Kheda Satyagraha in 1918. In 1922, he conducted another peasant movement in Bardoli taluka of Gujarat, which is generally known as the Bardoli Satyagraha. In this Satyagraha, the women of Bardoli gave him the title of 'Sardar'. N.G. Ranga: Associated with Guntur (Andhra Pradesh).

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy has been called the 'Promoter of Indian Nationalism'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905. He has been called the 'Promoter of Indian Nationalism'. Curzon's administration was known for intense activities and realism, efficiency and also infamous. In the 1904 budget, Curzon declared that 'In my view, the other name for the efficiency of administration is the contentment of the subjects.' Its overall result was: The start of a new phase in the history of Indian nationalism along with the anti-Bengal partition struggle.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Muslim League's first session take place?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in the Muslim Educational Conference session in Dhaka. Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk was the president of this conference. The annual session of the League was successfully completed in 1907 in Karachi, in which the constitution of the League was accepted.

questions.question_text: Who hoisted the Indian national flag at the international socialist conference held in Stuttgart?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Madam Bhikaiji Cama was a well-known Indian woman revolutionary. From 1909, Paris became her headquarters, and it became a meeting place for young revolutionaries like Lala Hardayal and Shyamji Krishna Varma. She was also the inspiring force of the Abhinav Bharat and India Society of Indians living in Europe. In 1907, she participated in the international socialist congress held in Stuttgart, where she hoisted the first Indian national flag, whose design she had prepared herself. This was, in fact, the original form of independent India's flag, only there was a difference in color. In this, instead of saffron, there was red color. In this same conference, she announced her resolution to struggle for independence with all her might.

questions.question_text: Who gave the four-fold program - boycott, Swadeshi, Swaraj, and national education - to the nation?
questions.explanation: GIC Lecturer exam, 2018 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Bal Gangadhar Tilak first suggested the use of means like boycott of foreign goods, love for Swadeshi goods, national-style education, etc. Tilak was the first Indian who gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'. His firm belief was that foreign rule, no matter how good it may be, can never be better than self-rule. He considered the use of Swadeshi goods a religious duty. Dr. Sher has written in the book 'The Life of Lokmanya' "Tilak only first explored the methods of the movement: boycott, love for Swadeshi goods, national-style education, popular joint political marches, etc., through which significant help would be received in achieving the goal of Swaraj."

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a member of the 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : In October 1924, a conference of revolutionary youths was held in Kanpur, and the Hindustan Republican Association or Army (HRA) was formed. HRA did its first big operation to collect money in Kakori. On 9 August 1925, ten people stopped the 8 Down train near a village Kakori and looted the railway department's treasury, due to which a large number of youths were arrested and Ashfaqulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged. Later, in Uttar Pradesh, Vijay Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, and Jaydev Kapur, and in Punjab, Bhagat Singh, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, and Sukhdev tried to reorganize the HRA under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad. On 9 and 10 September 1928, in the meeting of north India's young revolutionaries at Ferozeshah Kotla ground (Delhi), the name of the organization was changed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (H.S.R.A.).

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the Indian Legislative Assembly between 1925-1930?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Between 1925-1930, V.J. Patel served as the president of the Indian Legislative Assembly. Swarajists got a prominent nationalist leader Vithalbhai Patel elected as the president of the Central Legislative Assembly in March 1925. It is noteworthy that Vithalbhai Patel was elected to the Bombay Legislative Assembly in 1917. He represented the Indian National Congress in the London conference (1919) regarding the Government of India Act. He went to jail several times and died during his Switzerland trip in 1933.

questions.question_text: Match the authors with their works and select the correct answer from the code given below : Authors Book A. S.N. Banerjee 1. A Nation in the Making B. Dadabhai Naoroji 2. Gita Rahasya C. Bal Gangadhar Tilak 3. Poverty and Un-British Rule in India D. Bankim Chandra 4. Anand Math Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : 'A Nation in the Making' book was written by S.N. Banerjee. 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' was written by Dadabhai Naoroji. 'Gita Rahasya' is Bal Gangadhar Tilak's work, and Anand Math is Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's work. In Anand Math itself, there is the 'Vande Mataram' song, which is now also our national song.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was not a member of the Indian Constitution's drafting committee?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The Drafting Committee was formed on 29 August 1947, and Dr. Ambedkar was elected its president. Other members in it were: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, Mohammad Saadulla, K.M. Munshi, B.L. Mitter, and D.P. Khaitan. After some time, B.L. Mitter was replaced by N. Madhava Rao. And in 1948, on the death of D.P. Khaitan, his place was taken by T.T. Krishnamachari. S.N. Mukherjee was not its member.

questions.question_text: Which was India's first national news agency?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - By 1935 AD, a total of four news agencies were founded. Among these, the first news agency was 'Reuters', founded in 1860 AD. After this, Associated Press of India was founded in 1905 AD. The third news agency was 'Free Press of India', founded in 1927 AD. This was India's first national news agency. In 1934 AD, 'United Press of India' was founded. According to the U.P. Public Service Commission, option (c) is correct.

questions.question_text: Who among the following wrote the Non-cooperation movement resolution?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007, 2002 Explanation - The first massive mass movement against British policies was the Non-cooperation movement, whose originator was Mahatma Gandhi. The first resolution related to this rebellion was passed in the Calcutta special session of the Congress, 1920 AD. A four-stage program was presented in the resolution, which included the boycott of titles, courts, educational institutions, etc., establishment of national educational institutions, non-payment of taxes, and the boycott of the Prince of Wales's visit to India. Gandhi ji himself prepared the draft of this resolution, although Chittaranjan Das opposed this resolution. However, with the support of other leaders, including Motilal Nehru, the resolution was passed. Finally, in the Nagpur session, this resolution was passed in its final form.

questions.question_text: Who was the president of the Indian National Congress's Lucknow session (1916)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The Indian National Congress's Lucknow session was organized in 1916, whose president was Ambika Charan Majumdar. In the history of the Indian National Congress, this Lucknow session has an important place because, in this session, the split of the Congress that occurred in the 1907 Surat session ended and the Congress was reunified. Along with this, in this session, the provision of separate electorates given by the British government to Muslims on a communal basis being granted acceptance by the Congress was a very big mistake, because this mistake of the Congress made the basis of communalism even stronger, the result of which appeared in the form of the two-nation theory.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events chronologically and choose the appropriate answer based on the code given -
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation– The Indian National Congress was formed in Bombay in 1885. On 13 April 1919, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in Amritsar and under the leadership of Gandhi ji, the Non-cooperation movement was started in 1920 and in 1942, the Quit India movement started from Bombay.

questions.question_text: In whose presidency was the session of the Communist Party of India, founded in Kanpur in 1925, successfully completed?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - The rise of the leftist movement in India happened due to the development of modern industries, severe economic depression between the two world wars, and the Bolshevik revolution in Russia. Some Indian intellectuals working inside and outside India decided to found the Communist Party of India. Manabendra Nath Roy visited Russia and established contact with the Russian Communist Party. He also participated in the second Communist International held in Moscow in July-August 1920, and soon after, he founded the Indian Communist Party in Tashkent in October 1920. Between 1921 and 1925, various communist groups were founded in various parts of the country, and finally, in December 1925, 'Satya Bhakt' organized the All India Communist Conference in Kanpur, whose president was Singaravelu Chettiar.

questions.question_text: How much was the increase in land revenue determination in Bardoli taluka, which was the issue of the Bardoli Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - In 1928 AD, a movement to not pay tax was conducted in the Bardoli taluka of Surat district, which was in many aspects a gift of the Non-cooperation movement. In fact, the main reason for this peasant movement was an unexpected increase in land revenue. Under the leadership of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Congress interfered in this. Gandhi ji also had their direct support. Seeing the intensity of the movement, finally, a committee was appointed by the government. After sufficient investigation, the committee considered the 30 percent revenue increase unfair and reduced the revenue increase to 22% (21.97%).

questions.question_text: In the 1937 provincial elections, the Congress won a majority in five out of eleven provinces and in one of the following, its majority was less by only a few seats:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Provincial elections were held in 1937 based on the 1935 Government of India Act. The Congress got big success in this election. It got victory in 711 seats out of 1585 assembly seats. In these eleven provincial elections, Congress got an absolute majority in five provinces - Madras, Bihar, Odisha, Central Province, and United Province (modern Uttar Pradesh), and here the Congress formed governments on its own. In Bombay, out of 175 total seats, 86 seats were received, and here the Congress did not get an absolute majority, but despite this, the Congress formed its governments in eight provinces including Bombay. Only in Bengal, Punjab, and Sindh were non-Congress governments formed.

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the All India Muslim League?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation – The Bengal partition gave birth to communal division. So, immediately after the announcement of the Bengal partition, on 1 October 1906, a delegation of Muslims under the leadership of Aga Khan III met Lord Minto in Simla. In the memorandum presented by this delegation, a special demand was made for Muslims keeping in mind political importance, military service, and the historical memory of the past political prestige of Muslims. Minto also gave assurance to protect the political rights and interests of Muslims. Against this background, on the inspiration of Lord Curzon, Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka organized a meeting in Dhaka on 30 December 1906, in which the decision to establish the 'All India Muslim League' was taken. Aga Khan was made its first honorary president.

questions.question_text: "The only key to the solution of the problems of India and the world lies in socialism." This famous statement is -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation– The great leader of the Gandhi era, Jawaharlal Nehru, was born in the house of Motilal Nehru on 14 November 1889 AD. In the 1912 Bankipore annual session of the Congress, Jawaharlal Nehru participated as a common worker. During the Non-cooperation movement, he came into close contact with Gandhi ji. Along with Subhash Chandra Bose, Jawaharlal Nehru was also a true socialist and his loyalty lay in socialism. J.L. Nehru, along with Subhash, opposed the 1928 Nehru Report because their goal was to achieve complete independence instead of dominion status. In 1929, Nehru presided over the Lahore session of the Congress and made the declaration of complete Swaraj on the banks of the Ravi. Nehru had a deep understanding of international-national politics. During his Europe tour, he visited many countries and participated in the International Socialist Congress held in Brussels. He believed that "The only key to the solution of the problems of India and the world lies in socialism."

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was the Swadeshi resolution adopted?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007, 2010 Explanation - The father of the word Swadeshi was Dayanand Saraswati, who used words like Swadeshi to awaken the spirit of self-reliance and national love among Indians. Lord Curzon's reactionary policies had an important contribution to its propagation. Curzon adopted the policy of Bengal partition to weaken the national movement. As a result, a massive movement started in other parts of the country including Bengal. In this movement, the spirit of Swadeshi and boycott also got widespread support. In 1905 AD, the Congress session was held in Benares, which was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale. In the 1906 Calcutta session, Naoroji demanded Swaraj from the Congress stage. In this session, the Swadeshi resolution was adopted for the first time.

questions.question_text: Who prepared the draft of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- At the time when the Civil Disobedience Movement in India was at its peak, preparations for the Round Table Conference were going on in England. Against this background, on 12 November 1930, the first Round Table Conference was organized. The Congress did not participate in this conference. So, with the intention of involving the Congress in the movement, efforts for an agreement between the Congress and the British government started. In this, Dr. Jayakar, Tej Bahadur Sapru, and the Nawab of Bhopal played an important role and in 1931 AD, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was successfully completed. The draft of this pact was prepared by 'Herbert Emerson'. According to the pact– 1. Except for violent criminals, all political prisoners should be released. 2. The confiscated property should be returned. 3. People living in coastal areas will have the right to make salt. 4. Right to peaceful picketing/demonstration against foreign goods, etc.

questions.question_text: Because the 1932 Communal Award had clearly classified India into political communities. Name that community for which Mahatma Gandhi did 'fast unto death' to remove this unacceptable classification?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — On 16 August 1932, British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced his Communal Award, according to which Muslims, Europeans, and Sikhs were to elect their representatives by voting in separate communal electorates. There was also a provision for a separate electorate for the depressed classes. Mahatma Gandhi went on a hunger strike in Yerwada jail opposing the provision of a separate electorate for the depressed classes as well.

questions.question_text: In which Act of the Government of India was the system of separate electorates for Muslims accepted?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — The biggest flaw of the 1909 Act was providing separate electorates for Muslims. The election of Muslim members in the councils was not done by the general electorate but by a separate electorate formed only for Muslims. In fact, its intention was to accept the Muslim community as a class completely separate from the Indian nation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following names was not included in the Swaraj organization in Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — Leaders like Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, and Hakim Ajmal Khan were included in the Swaraj organization in Congress. Whereas Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Ansari, Rajagopalachari, and Kasturi Ranga Iyengar were in favor of doing Gandhian constructive work in the villages. The proposal for council entry was rejected by 1740 votes against 890 in the Gaya session, but Das and Motilal Nehru established the Swaraj Party on January 1, 1923, to fight the upcoming elections in November 1923.

questions.question_text: Who was the person who first demanded a separate state for the Muslims of India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — Muhammad Iqbal was the person who first demanded a separate state for the Muslims of India. He is considered the pioneer of the separate state Pakistan idea. Inspired by the sentiment of 'Pan-Islamism', Iqbal demanded a separate state at the Allahabad session of the All India Muslim League in 1930. A separate homeland for Muslims, which should be called Pakistan, was a clear idea that arose in the mind of Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student.

questions.question_text: The objective of the conspiracy of the Partition of Bengal was —

options.A: To weaken the national freedom movement
options.C: To bring Hindus into the minority in the new state

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — On 20 July 1905, Lord Curzon issued an order and divided Bengal into two parts. The real objective of the British government behind the partition of Bengal was to weaken the national freedom movement, because Bengal was considered the center of nationalism. Another objective of the partition was also to create a rift between Hindus and Muslims. The new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam was created especially so that the population of Muslims would be less than that of Hindus in it.

questions.question_text: Which movement gave Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel the inspiration to become a follower of Gandhi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — In the year 1918, despite the crop failure of farmers in the Kheda district of Gujarat, the government refused to waive the tax and was bent on collecting the full tax. Mahatma Gandhi supported the farmers and advised them that until they got a tax waiver, they should stop paying taxes. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel became a disciple of Gandhi during the Kheda farmers' movement.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Lala Har Dayal 1. Ghadar B. Surendranath Banerjee 2. Bengali C. Bipin Chandra Pal 3. Vande Mataram D. Shyamji Krishna Varma 4. Indian Sociologist Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — List-I List-II Lala Har Dayal — Ghadar Surendranath Banerjee — Bengali Bipin Chandra Pal — Vande Mataram Shyamji Krishna Varma — Indian Sociologist Satish Chandra Mukherjee — Dawn Krishna Chandra Mishra — Sanjivani B.R. Ambedkar — Mooknayak Sachchidananda Sinha — Searchlight

questions.question_text: In what way did Bal Gangadhar Tilak work to instill national sentiment in people?

options.A: By publishing the atrocities committed by the British government against Indians in his newspaper 'Kesari'
options.B: By organizing festivals in honor of Lord Ganesha and by reviving the tradition of Shivaji

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the first nationalist leader who tried to establish close relations with the public and in this sense, he was the precursor to Gandhi. With this objective, he established gymnasiums, lathi clubs, and anti-cow slaughter societies. He started the Shivaji and Ganapati festivals so that the sentiment of service to the nation would awaken in the public. For the propagation of his ideas, he started two newspapers, 'Maratha' in English and 'Kesari' in Marathi. Tilak saw the Khilafat movement as a golden opportunity to establish Hindu-Muslim unity and to bring the Muslim population into the national movement.

questions.question_text: Where did the Congress pass the program of Non-Cooperation and boycott in its special session?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — In September 1920, a special session of the Congress was held in Calcutta. Despite the opposition of many senior leaders, the Congress approved the Non-Cooperation movement and adopted it as its own movement. Among the opponents, the main one was C.R. Das. His opposition was regarding the boycott of the Legislative Council. Elections for these were to be held in a few days. However, even those who disagreed with the idea of boycott followed the Congress discipline and did not participate in the elections. In December, the annual session of the Congress was held in Nagpur. By this time, the internal opposition within the Congress had almost ended.

questions.question_text: Name the foreign journalist who reported on the Satyagraha at Dharasana Salt Works:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — During the Civil Disobedience Movement, the Satyagraha at the Dharasana salt factory took place under the leadership of Sarojini Naidu; Gandhi's son Manilal was also with them. A detailed account of the police atrocities committed against the Satyagrahis here was provided by the present American journalist Webb Miller.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation — Congress Session Place President 1. 1885 Bombay W.C. Bonnerjee 2. 1886 Calcutta Dadabhai Naoroji 3. 1887 Madras Badruddin Tyabji 4. 1888 Allahabad George Yule 5. 1889 Bombay William Wedderburn 6. 1890 Calcutta Pherozeshah Mehta 7. 1891 Nagpur P. Ananda Charlu 8. 1892 Allahabad W.C. Bonnerjee 9. 1893 Lahore Dadabhai Naoroji 10. 1894 Madras Alfred Webb

questions.question_text: Which organization was founded by N.M. Joshi among the following?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The All India Trade Union Congress was founded in 1920 by Narayan Malhar Joshi; Lala Lajpat Rai was made its President.

questions.question_text: Who made the taunt that Indians are unable to reach a consensus on any constitution?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Upon the boycott of the Simon Commission by the Indian National Congress, the Secretary of State for India, Lord Birkenhead, taunted that Indians are unable to reach a consensus on any constitution. He challenged Indian leaders to draft a constitution that would have the support and consent of all parties. Consequently, in 1928, Indian leaders called an all-party conference, in which a committee was formed under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru to draft a constitution. The Nehru Committee submitted its report on 28 August 1928.

questions.question_text: Who among the following called the early sessions of Congress a 'three-day tamasha' (show)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Ashwini Kumar Datta was actively associated with the Congress from the beginning. The partition of Bengal had a revolutionary impact on him, so he went from being a moderate to an extremist. He had called the Congress sessions a 'three-day tamasha'. Because of his nationalist activities, he was deported from Bengal in December 1908 AD. He had founded the Braj Samaj School, Hitaisini Sabha, and People's Association.

questions.question_text: Which member was not part of the Nehru Committee formed under the chairmanship of Pandit Motilal Nehru?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Accepting the challenge of Secretary of State for India Birkenhead, Indian leaders formed a committee under the chairmanship of Pandit Motilal Nehru to draft a constitution (1928). The members of this committee were - Tej Bahadur Sapru, Ali Imam, Shoaib Qureshi, Subhas Chandra Bose, M.S. Aney, Jayakar, N.M. Joshi, and Mangal Singh. Jayakar had later withdrawn his name from this committee. Aurobindo Ghosh was not a member of the Nehru Committee.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following movements in chronological order and select the correct answer based on the code given below: (i) Ghadar Movement (ii) Swadeshi Movement (iii) Khilafat Movement (iv) Neel (Indigo) Movement Code :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Ghadar Movement - Lala Har Dayal founded the Ghadar Party in the USA on 1 November 1913. Swadeshi Movement - Launched in 1905 in protest against the partition of Bengal. Khilafat Movement (1920-22) - In 1919, Mahatma Gandhi was elected the President of the All India Khilafat Conference. The Khilafat movement received more support at the Amritsar session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1919. Neel (Indigo) Movement - (1860) - This movement was carried out against British landlords.

questions.question_text: A revolutionary spent 24 years in different jails, during which he remained on hunger strike for a total of two and a half years on various occasions. His name was -
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation- Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee was a revolutionary. In Bengal, he was associated with the activities of the Anushilan Samiti, but later he made Kanpur the center of his organization. He was among the founders of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association. He was arrested in the Kakori conspiracy case and sentenced to life imprisonment. Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee spent 24 years in various jails, remaining on hunger strike for a total of two and a half years on various occasions.

questions.question_text: When was the first independence day celebrated in India with the pledge of 'Purna Swaraj'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - In the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress (1929), the Nehru report was declared null and void, and the goal of the national movement was set as Purna Swaraj or complete independence. On 31 December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the flag of Indian independence on the banks of the Ravi in Lahore. In its meeting on 2 January 1930, the Congress Working Committee decided that 26 January 1930 should be celebrated as Purna Swaraj Day.

UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - In the Congress Working Committee meeting held in Wardha on 14 July 1942, a long resolution was passed, which is generally called the 'Quit India' resolution. On 7 August 1942, the Wardha resolution was confirmed by a huge majority in the All India Congress Committee meeting held in Bombay. The place in Bombay where the Quit India resolution was confirmed in the Congress Committee meeting is now famous as the August Kranti Maidan. The Quit India movement is also called the August Kranti.
examinations: Congress passed the famous 'Quit India' resolution in August 1942:

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not involved in the Kakori conspiracy?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - On 9 August 1925, revolutionaries of Uttar Pradesh successfully looted the train going to Kakori on the Saharanpur-Lucknow line. The public showed great sympathy for the trial of this Kakori case. In the Kakori case, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Lal, Ashfaq Ullah Khan, and Rajendra Lahiri were punished. Surya Sen was not associated with the Kakori case. He raided the Chittagong armory in Bengal in April 1930 and declared himself the head of the provincial independent Indian government. He was hanged in 1933.

questions.question_text: Who named the 'Indian National Congress'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation- Retired British officer of the Indian Civil Service, A.O. Hume founded the Indian National Union in 1884, which was the predecessor of the Indian National Congress. Its first session was held on 28 December 1885 in Bombay. On the suggestion of Dadabhai Naoroji, the name of this organization was changed to Indian National Congress.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has not been the President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation- A.O. Hume was the founder and first General Secretary of the Indian National Congress. He founded the Indian National Congress in 1885. He was never the President of the Indian National Congress. Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session in 1923, Ambica Charan Majumdar over the Lucknow session in 1916, and Sardar Patel presided over the Karachi session in 1931.

questions.question_text: In 1928, where was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association founded?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - Under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad, the only absconding person left of the Kakori conspiracy case, revolutionaries held a meeting of a new party on 9-10 September 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi, and the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (H.S.R.A.) was founded here. Its objective was to establish a socialist republican state in India. This was a democratic organization; everyone was bound to accept the decision of the majority in it. The manifesto of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was 'Philosophy of the Bomb', which Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote.

questions.question_text: Who among the following supported Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation proposal at the special session of Congress in Calcutta in 1920?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation─The special session of the Congress held in 1920 was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai. In this special session of the Congress, it was decided to boycott the elections to be held in 1920 according to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms. The program of Gandhi's gradual non-cooperation movement was accepted. The demands of this proposal presented by Gandhi himself were only three—(a) The mistake made with Khilafat should be corrected, (b) The mistake made with Punjab should be corrected, and (c) Swaraj should be established. This proposal, especially the boycott of the new legislative councils, was strongly opposed by Chittaranjan Das, Lala Lajpat Rai, Annie Besant, Madan Mohan Malaviya, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, etc. However, Motilal Nehru, Maulana Muhammad Ali, and Shaukat Ali, etc., supported it, and after much debate, Gandhi was able to get it passed, in which the main support was from Pandit Motilal Nehru.

questions.question_text: Who among the following drafted the resolution on Fundamental Rights at the 1931 Karachi session?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─To give approval to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, the Congress session was called in Karachi at the end of March, whose president was Vallabhbhai Patel. Here the pact was accepted unanimously, but outside the Congress, movements by youth and labor groups criticized the pact sharply. Perhaps to satisfy this side, a resolution on famous fundamental rights was accepted in this session, the draft of which was prepared by Jawaharlal Nehru. It was said that fundamental rights must be included in the constitution of India after independence. But in this session, the Lahore declaration of Purna Swaraj and the talk of not making any compromise with imperialism in this connection were forgotten, and the Congress was forced to participate in the same Round Table Conference which it had decided to boycott. Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose were quite unhappy with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact because the goal of Purna Swaraj was practically abandoned.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is known as the mother of Indian revolutionaries?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─Madam Bhikaiji Cama was born in 1861 in a Parsi family in Bombay. The family sent her to England for higher education, but she did not enjoy her studies there and started working for India's freedom with people like Shyamji Krishna Varma and Savarkar. On 18 August 1907, at the conference of world socialist nations held in Stuttgart, Germany, she hoisted India's first flag. She was put in jail during the First World War. Even four years of extreme suffering could not divert her from her path. She returned to India in 1934 and kept working for independence. Because of this revolutionary spirit, she is called "the mother of Indian revolutionaries".

questions.question_text: 'I asked for bread on bended knees and received a stone in return.' With what is this statement related?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─Before starting the Satyagraha movement, Gandhi had written a letter to the Viceroy on 2 March 1930, in which the adverse effects of British rule on India were discussed. He said that if the English government made no attempt to fulfill those demands, he would violate the salt law on 12 March. The decision was that he and his few chosen companions would first break the salt law. Collective Civil Disobedience would only begin when they were arrested or if they gave a call to the public for this. The response sent by the Viceroy to the letter was quite unsatisfactory, but what else could be expected from the English? In his reply to it, Gandhi wrote, "I asked for bread and received a stone." According to the plan, Gandhi started the Dandi Yatra along the seaside with his 78 chosen disciples. Walking nearly 200 miles in 24 days, they reached Dandi on 5 April. On 6 April, Gandhi collected salt from the seashore and thus violated the salt law. After 6 April 1930, the nationwide Satyagraha and Disobedience movement began. Finally, with the declaration of control over the Dharasana salt factory, the government arrested Gandhi on 5 May.

questions.question_text: The campaign launched by the British government to arrest the leaders of the Quit India movement was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─Gandhi said in the All India Congress Committee conference on 8 August 1942 that a small struggle does not mean the beginning of a movement. You have given your power only into my hands. I will now meet the Viceroy and wait for the acceptance of the Congress demand by him. But even before Gandhi could meet the Viceroy, the government arrested Gandhi and all other Congress leaders at midnight on 9 August 1942 under 'Operation Zero Hour'. Gandhi was kept under house arrest at the Aga Khan Palace in Pune and Congress Working Committee members Jawaharlal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Asaf Ali, Govind Ballabh Pant, Dr. Prafulla Chandra Ghosh, Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Dr. Syed Mahmud, and Acharya Kripalani were kept in Ahmednagar Fort. Congress Working Committee member Dr. Rajendra Prasad was kept under house arrest in Patna. These Congress leaders remained in custody until 15 June 1945. Along with this, the British government also declared the All India Congress Committee, Congress Working Committee, and provincial Congress committees as illegal.

questions.question_text: Who among the following read the English translation of the presidential address at the 1939 Tripuri session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─At the 1939 Tripuri (Jabalpur) session of the Indian National Congress, Subhas Chandra Bose could not participate in the opening session due to bad health (high fever), due to which the session was presided over by Maulana Azad. Subhas Chandra Bose's presidential address was read in Hindi by Acharya Narendra Deva and in English by Sarat Chandra Bose.

questions.question_text: The first President of the Muslim League was-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─On 30 December 1906, when the "Mohammedan Educational Conference" meeting was going on in Dhaka, at that very moment, under the chairmanship of Dhaka's Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk Mushtaq Hussain, the All India Muslim League was established. In 1908 AD, Aga Khan was made the permanent president of the Muslim League. The initial leadership of the League remained in the hands of Nawabs and landlords. In 1908 AD, at the Amritsar session, a forty-member central committee was established. After that, its provincial branches were established. The president of the London branch of the Muslim League was Sir Ameer Ali.

questions.question_text: Who among the following prepared the draft of the 'Quit India Resolution'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─In such an agitated atmosphere, the All India Congress Committee session was held in Bombay on 7-8 August 1942, in which a long resolution was passed asking the British to leave India. The draft of this resolution was prepared by Mahatma Gandhi himself. In the Congress meeting, Jawaharlal Nehru presented this resolution, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad supported the resolution. The committee gave leadership to Gandhi but at the same time warned people that such a time could also come when the Congress might not be able to give leadership to the people. Gandhi, while issuing orders to the people, said for 'Do or Die', 'Either get India liberated or die in this attempt.'

questions.question_text: At which of the following places was the Hindu Mahasabha formed for the first time in 1915?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─The history of the origin and early period of the Hindu Mahasabha is unclear. In 1910, prominent Hindus of Allahabad decided to form an All India Hindu Mahasabha. In 1911 AD, the Punjab Hindu Mahasabha organized a Hindu conference in Amritsar. The Hindu Mahasabha established its main office in Haridwar and organized conferences on the occasions of important Hindu fairs. Therefore, the Hindu Mahasabha was established in Haridwar in 1915 AD, whose founder was Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.

questions.question_text: In which session of the Muslim League was the two-nation theory advocated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─In the Lahore session of 22 March 1940 AD, Jinnah said that provincial autonomy has proven that in the future, Muslims will have to be ruled under a Hindu majority. Therefore, Jinnah also declared that from any perspective, Muslims are not a minority but a nation and for a nation, a 'single geographical territory, state and homeland' is necessary. In this same session, the famous 'Pakistan Resolution' was passed, whose main basis was that no constitution for India would be acceptable to Muslims until the Muslim majority areas of the East and West of India were accepted as a free and sovereign state. For a nation, a 'single geographical territory, state and homeland' is necessary. In this same session, the famous 'Pakistan Resolution' was passed, the main basis of which was that no constitution for India would be acceptable to the Muslims until the Muslim-majority areas in the East and West of India were accepted as an independent and sovereign state.

questions.question_text: When did the Simon Commission come to India?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation─The Simon Commission was formed in December 1927 under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon. There were a total of seven members in this, and all were British. Congress termed it a 'White Commission'. On 13 February 1928, this commission reached Bombay. On that day, a strike was organized in all of Bombay, and slogans of "Simon Go Back" were raised with black flags.

questions.question_text: Which of the following leaders was not a part of the Non-Cooperation movement?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─S.N. Banerjee, Madan Mohan Malaviya, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, C.R. Das, V.C. Pal, etc., opposed the Non-Cooperation movement, but with the support of the Ali Brothers and Motilal Nehru, the Non-Cooperation movement proposal was passed. Later, Jinnah left the Congress party and did not take part in the Non-Cooperation movement.

questions.question_text: Who was the young woman leader symbolizing disobedience and resistance during the Quit India movement?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─Aruna was born into a Bengali family. In 1928, she left her studies and married Asaf Ali. Aruna participated in the 1941 individual Satyagraha, for which she even had to go to jail. She also hoisted the national flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan in Bombay in 1942 AD. If it is said that she was the heroine of 1942, it would not be inappropriate. Her significant work was to conduct the revolution while remaining underground during the 1942 movement. The government was wary of her work. Therefore, she had to work while remaining underground until 1946. The Daily Tribune called her the Rani of Jhansi of the 1942 revolution. She appeared only after the expiry of the warrant period in 1946. Gandhi said, "I admire your courage and bravery." Even after independence, her constructive work continued. In 1947 AD, she became the President of the Delhi Congress Committee and in 1958 AD, the first woman Chairperson of the Delhi Municipal Council.

questions.question_text: Who called Gandhi's 'Quit India' movement a 'unique movement'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─The Quit India movement started on 8 August 1942, and that very night all the leaders of the Congress were arrested. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel has called the Quit India movement a 'unique movement'.

questions.question_text: Bijolia movement was related to whom?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─The Bijolia peasant movement was started by Ashok Parmar against the imposition of Chauri and Talwarbandi taxes by the jagirdar of Maharaj, Rawat Krishna Singh. In 1916 AD, Vijay Singh Pathik led it and established the Kisan Panch Board under the chairmanship of Sitaram Das and got the farmers to refuse to take war loans. Seeing this situation deteriorating, the Government of India sent A.G.G. Holland to Bijolia; an agreement was reached between the farmers and Holland. 33 taxes out of 84 were waived, and an assurance of land settlement was given in three years. However, the jagirdars did not follow the agreement. Finally, Jamnalal Bajaj and Mewar Prime Minister Vijay Raghavacharya talked to the leaders of the Praja Mandal and got the movement ended. This peasant movement played an extraordinary role in generating political consciousness.

questions.question_text: Which book has been related to the development of the national movement in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─The plot of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's famous novel 'Anand Math' is based on the Sanyasi rebellion. The Sanyasis were very angry with the restrictions imposed on visiting pilgrimage sites. The Sanyasis had a tradition of fighting against injustice, and they, together with the public, attacked the company's factories and treasuries. They fought very bravely against the company's soldiers, and Warren Hastings could suppress this rebellion only after great effort. The plot compiled in Anand Math continued to inspire people to fight against British rule until the later period. This rebellion lasted from 1770 to 1820 AD.

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was the 'Drain Theory' officially accepted?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The Indian National Congress officially accepted the 'Drain Theory' in its 1896 Calcutta session. This session was presided over by M.A. Sayani. Therefore, it is not related to the 1906 Calcutta session.

questions.question_text: Match List-I and List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I List-II (Person) (Movement) A. Baba Ram Singh 1. Satya Mahima Dharma B. Mirza Ghulam Ahmad 2. Rahnumai C. Mukunda Das 3. Namdhari Movement D. Naoroji Fardunji 4. Ahmadiyya Movement Code : A B C D A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Baba Ram Singh is related to the Kuka movement that spread in Western Punjab in 1860-70 AD, which had ended British power in Punjab. Later, this movement was suppressed by the Company government, and Ram Singh Kuka was arrested and exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1885 AD. Mirza Ghulam Ahmad laid the foundation of the Ahmadiyya movement in 1889 AD; after being the messiah and mahdi himself, he claimed to be the avatar of the Hindu deity Krishna and Jesus Christ on earth. Mukunda Das was related to the Satya Mahima Dharma movement. Naoroji Fardunji is associated with the Parsi reform movement Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, which was established in 1851 AD.

questions.question_text: Who among the following presided over the 1907 Surat session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The 1907 Surat session was presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh. In this same Surat session, the first split of the Congress into Moderates and Extremists occurred. This remained for 10 years. In the 1916 Lucknow session, the split groups of the Congress united, whose president was Ambica Charan Majumdar. Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the 1905 Banaras Congress session. Pherozeshah Mehta presided over the 1890 Calcutta session. Dadabhai Naoroji had been the president of Congress three times. The order of which is like this – 1886 AD – Calcutta, 1893 AD – Lahore, 1906 AD – Calcutta Congress.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correctly matched?

options.A: Shyamji Krishna Varma: Indian Home Rule Society
options.B: Ram Prasad Bismil: Hindustan Socialist Republican Association

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The famous revolutionary Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the Indian Home Rule Society and India House in 1905 AD in London. Ram Prasad Bismil, Yogesh Chatterjee, and Sachindra Nath Sanyal founded the 'Hindustan Republican Association' in 1924 in Kanpur. Whereas the 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association' was founded in 1928 by Bhagat Singh in Delhi. Bhupendranath Datta and Barindra Ghosh founded the organization named "Yugantar" in 1906 in Calcutta, whereas 'Abhinav Bharat' was V.D. Savarkar's organization, which was established in 1906 in London and India. 'Bandi Jeevan' is the autobiography of Sachindranath Sanyal, not any organization.

questions.question_text: During the Quit India movement, before he was arrested, which of the following orders did Mahatma Gandhi not set for people?

options.B: Paralyze the government administration through a complete strike
options.C: Keep the nation alive even at the risk of death
options.D: See yourself as subjects of the British Emperor

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Gandhi never said in the 1942 mass movement that 'See yourself as subjects of the British Emperor', rather, some part of the speeches given by Gandhi before he was arrested is as follows – "I will not be satisfied with anything less than complete independence, the administration may offer a proposal to end salt tax, alcoholism, etc. But my words will be nothing less than independence; I give you a mantra 'Do or Die'. The meaning of this mantra is that either we will get India independent, or we will give our lives in the attempt."

questions.question_text: In 1946, the naval mutiny was started on which ship?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – In February 1946, some sailors of the navy were being given training in the barracks of Bombay. The sailors of the training ship 'Talwar' presented their complaint about the mess to the British officer. The British officer replied with great sarcasm - "Beggar selectors cannot be choosers," he also said that those who do not eat the rice found with stones and gravel, should clean the rice themselves with their own hands. The sailors protested against this statement of the officer. Soon, slogans appeared on the walls of the barracks. 'British Quit India', 'Hindustan Zindabad'. The commander considered radio operator Datta responsible for this. Officers suspected that Datta was a man from the Communist Party. He was arrested. The sailors gave an answer to this through a strike on 18 February 1946. This strike started with the sailors of the barracks, and by the afternoon, all the sailors of 'Talwar' had joined the strike.

questions.question_text: In which of the following acts was separate electorate for Muslims started?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Through the 1909 Act, in the name of reforms, communalism was promoted in the election system so that the unity of Indian nationalists could be broken and they could be divided into different parts. This policy of separatism was not limited only to Muslims, but it was adopted with the intention of dividing the countrymen by dividing landlords, traders, and capitalists, etc., into separate classes. This policy proved to be extremely fatal for India's future political history. The Secretary of State for India himself, Morley, wrote in a letter to Viceroy Minto quite rightly, "Remember that by creating separate electorate areas, we are sowing the seeds of such a fatal poison that its harvest will be very bitter."

questions.question_text: Who among the following supported the Quit India resolution in 1942?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Quit India resolution in 1942 was supported by Abul Kalam Azad. The Quit India movement is also known as the 'August Kranti'. On 14 July 1942, the Congress Working Committee passed the resolution for the British to leave, and clearly said, "If this appeal is not accepted, then we will be forced to launch a civil disobedience movement in the country under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi." The support for this resolution happened in the All India Congress Committee meeting held in Bombay on 8 August 1942. The Quit India resolution of Mahatma Gandhi was supported by A.K. Azad.

questions.question_text: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress did Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi participate for the first time?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Mahatma Gandhi participated for the first time in the Congress session held in Calcutta in 1901. This session was presided over by Dinshaw Wacha. Mahatma Gandhi was elected President of the Belgaum session of the Congress in 1924.

questions.question_text: When was the Quit India movement suspended?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation – On 7 August 1942 AD, the Congress session was held in Gowalia Tank, Bombay, which was presided over by Abul Kalam Azad. Nehru presented the Quit India resolution, which was accepted after some minor amendments on 8 August 1942 AD. As soon as the Quit India movement started on 9 August 1942, all the main leaders including Gandhi were arrested by the government. This movement lasted for quite a few days and gradually slowed down. The Congress had not officially suspended it.

questions.question_text: Consider the formation of the following associations before the establishment of the Indian National Congress: 3. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha 4. Indian League Find the correct chronological order of the formation (establishment) of the associations from the code given below: 1. The Indian Association 2. Madras Native Association
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Madras Native Association was established in 1852 AD as a branch of the British Indian Association of Calcutta. It also sent a petition to the British Parliament before the 1853 charter, which was based on the model of the Bombay and Calcutta Association. In 1867, the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was created in Poona, whose objective was to work as a bridge between the government and the people. In September 1875, Babu Shishir Kumar Ghosh created an Indian League whose objective was to awaken the feeling of nationalism in people and to promote political education. On 26 July 1876, the Indian Association replaced the Indian League. This was established by Anand Mohan Bose and Surendranath.

questions.question_text: When was the 'Communist Party of India' established?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 Explanation – On 1 September 1924, in India, as soon as the Kanpur conspiracy case ended, Satyabhakta announced that he had established the Communist Party of India and he himself had become its Secretary. It was presided over by Singaravelu and its office was shifted to Bombay in 1925. Its prominent members were Maulana Hasrat Mohani, B.M. Joshi, Pandit Ram Gopal, and Ramashankar Avasthi.

questions.question_text: Who among the following proposed the name of W.C. Bonnerjee for the President's post for the first session of the Indian National Congress, Bombay (1885)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The Indian National Congress was established in 1885 AD. Its first session was organized on 28 September 1885 in Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College located in Bombay. Its first President was W.C. Bonnerjee. The name of W.C. Bonnerjee was proposed for the post of President for the first session of the Indian National Congress, Bombay (1885) by A.O. Hume.

questions.question_text: Who was the President of the National Planning Committee (National Planning Committee) established by the Indian National Congress in 1938?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 (c) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (d) J.B. Kripalani Answer – (a) UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In this regard, it is memorable that in 1938, the Congress formed a National Planning Committee, whose President was Jawaharlal Nehru. The committee studied all aspects of planning in detail.

questions.question_text: Who was the father of 'Communal Award'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Ramsay MacDonald was the 'father of the Communal Award'. Both Round Table Conferences did not find any solution to the question of communal representation. To resolve this problem, in August 1932, British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald presented his communal award regarding the representation of minorities in the provincial legislative assemblies. Under this, some seats were reserved in provincial legislative councils for every minority community, whose members were to be elected by separate electorates. Muslims and Sikhs were already considered minorities, now under this law, Dalits were also considered minorities and separated from Hindus.

questions.question_text: Vinoba Bhave was selected as the first Satyagrahi for 'Individual Satyagraha', who was the second Satyagrahi?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Vinoba Bhave was the first Satyagrahi for Individual Satyagraha (17 October 1940) and Jawaharlal Nehru was the second. The selection of Satyagrahis used to be done very carefully, and when they came to the stage, people would surround them in such a way that the war-protest speech would have already happened by the time of their arrest.

questions.question_text: Who founded the 'All India Muslim League'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – On 30 December 1906, when the Mohammedan Educational Conference meeting was going on in Dhaka, at that very moment, that session was declared in the name of the All India Muslim League under the chairmanship of the Nawab (Nawab Salimullah Khan) of Dhaka. In this way, the All India Muslim League was established.

questions.question_text: On the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore, the day of the partition of Bengal (October 16, 1905) was celebrated as–

options.B: As a day of Raksha Bandhan

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–The day of 16 October 1905 (the day the partition became effective) was celebrated in all of Bengal as a day of mourning. In houses, the stove was not lit, people kept a fast, and a strike was declared in Calcutta. The public took out a procession; in the morning, groups of people took a dip in the Ganga and then started demonstrating on the roads while singing Vande Mataram. This Vande Mataram was the war cry from the side of the entire movement. People tied rakhis on each other's wrists to show that by dividing Bengal, the English could not create a rift in their unity.

questions.question_text: What was the President of the 1927 Madras Congress session, where the Indian National Congress accepted the proposal for the boycott of the 'Simon Commission'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – In its annual meeting of December 1927 in Madras, the Congress put forward a proposal that the goal of the Congress would be 'Purna Swarajya', and that proposal was passed in one go. The president of this session was Dr. M.A. Ansari.

questions.question_text: Use the code given below the events to arrange the following events related to the Indian freedom movement in their correct chronological order: 1. The incident of throwing a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly of Delhi. 2. Martyrdom of Jatin Das. 3. Martyrdom of Bhagat Singh.
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929. Jatin Das died after 64 days on 13 September 1929. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931. The Congress met in Karachi on 29 March 1931 to approve the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Thus the chronological order is 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.question_text: Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–Two members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929, at the time when the debate on the Trade Dispute Bill and Safety Bill was going on. Jatin Das, who sat on a hunger strike, died after 64 days on 13 September 1929. On 23 March 1931, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were hanged. A meeting of the Congress was held in Karachi on 29 March 1931 to approve the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Delhi pact).
examinations: Karachi session of the Indian National Congress. (1931)

questions.question_text: Which of the following gave the convocation address at Banaras Hindu University on the subject 'Constituent Assembly for India'; and also vehemently opposed the future drafting of India's constitution by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation–Sir Maurice Gwyer gave the convocation address at Banaras Hindu University on the subject 'Constituent Assembly for India'. In this, he vehemently opposed the future drafting of India's constitution by the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order and select the correct answer from the code given below: 1. Throwing of bomb in the Central Assembly 2. Killing of Saunders 3. Hanging of Sardar Bhagat Singh Code: 4. Death of Chandrashekhar Azad
questions.explanation: he Saunders murder case happened in 1928 AD. Bhagat Singh shot Saunders. On 8 April 1929 AD, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly against the Trade Dispute Bill and Public Safety Bill. On 27 February 1931 AD, Chandrashekhar Azad shot himself after being surrounded by the British in Alfred Park, Allahabad. On 23 March 1931 AD, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were hanged.

questions.question_text: The first Factory Act of 1881 was mainly related to:

options.D: Compensation to laborers in case of accident

questions.explanation: The first Factory Act 1881 was related to child labor. This act was brought during the tenure of Lord Ripon. Under this, an attempt was made to prohibit child labor. A ban was imposed on keeping children under seven years of age in factories. Along with this, children under 12 years of age were prohibited from working for more than 9 hours. At least four holidays in a month were made mandatory for children

questions.question_text: Frontier Gandhi (Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan) formed a party of Pathans. The name of that party was:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – The Civil Disobedience Movement spread across India under the leadership of Gandhi. The Muslims of the North-West Frontier Province ran the Civil Disobedience Movement under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi), and the organization 'Khudai Khidmatgar' or 'Lal Kurta' formed under his leadership in 1929 AD played an active role in the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following chronologically and select the correct answer from the code given below: 1. Second Round Table Conference 2. Dandi March 3. Poona Pact 4. Gandhi Irwin Pact Code:
questions.explanation: Dandi March (12 March to 6 April 1930) AD was started by Gandhi. Gandhi broke the salt law after walking 385 km in 24 days with 78 followers. Gandhi-Irwin Pact took place on 5 March 1931 AD. This pact was made to have Gandhi participate in the Second Round Table Conference. The Second Round Table Conference started on 7 September 1931 AD. The Poona Pact took place in 1932 AD. It is also called the Communal Award

questions.question_text: Where is Dandi located?
questions.explanation: Dandi is in the Navsari district of Gujarat. Dandi was the name of a village, where Gandhi reached on 6 April 1930 AD and violated the salt law by picking up a fistful of salt. Gandhi had announced the program of this movement from Dandi on 9 April 1930 AD

questions.question_text: The Carlyle Circular is related to:
questions.explanation: The Carlyle Circular is related to the Anti-Partition of Bengal movement. To strengthen the boycott and Swadeshi movement, volunteers were organized, and public committees were formed; as a result, the British government issued the Carlyle Circular on 22 October 1905 to suppress this movement

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of 'Dharma Sabha' in Bengal?
questions.explanation: The founder of 'Dharma Sabha' in Bengal was Radhakanta Deb. Radhakanta Deb founded the Dharma Sabha in 1830 AD. Its headquarters was in Calcutta. Radhakanta Deb had supported the Sati system. He had opposed the Brahmo Samaj advocated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Radhakanta Deb had established the Widow Ashram Sangh in Pune in 1899 AD. To promote female education, the Indian Women's University was established in Bombay in 1916 AD. He had compiled the Sanskrit dictionary named 'Shabda Kalpadrum'

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the publication of the 'Bombay Chronicle'?
questions.explanation: Leader of the Indian National Congress Ferozeshah Mehta started the publication of the 'Bombay Chronicle' from Bombay in 1913 AD, whose editor was B.G. Horniman. It is notable that it was established to convey moderate ideas to the public after the Surat split. Ferozeshah Mehta belonged to the Parsi religion

questions.question_text: When did the All India Workers and Peasants Party come into existence?
questions.explanation: The All India Workers and Peasants Party was established in 1928 AD. All provincial parties were included in it. Its first session was held in Calcutta, which was presided over by Sohan Lal Joshi. When its existence became active again in 1945 AD, the Congress separated from it in 1947 AD and established the 'Indian National Trade Union Congress'

questions.question_text: The 'Ancient Monuments Preservation Act' was passed during the tenure of which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: The Ancient Monuments Preservation Act was passed during the tenure of Lord Curzon. It was established in 1904 AD. Based on this, an Archaeological Department was established, and a provision of £50,000 in funds was made for it. General Cunningham was made its head. General Cunningham is called the father of Indian Archaeology

questions.question_text: Who was the first female President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: The first female President of the Indian National Congress was Annie Besant. The 32nd session of Congress was organized in 1917 AD in Calcutta, which was presided over by Annie Besant. For the first time, the Congress adopted the tricolor flag in this same conference. Sarojini Naidu presided over the Congress organized in Kanpur in 1925 AD

questions.question_text: After which event did Rabindranath Tagore renounce the title of Knighthood?

options.A: Start of the First World War
options.C: Arrival of the Simon Commission in India

questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore returned the title of Knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre is an event of 13 April 1919 AD.
