The government had arrested Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew without any reason. To protest against this, on 13 April 1919 AD, on Baisakhi, a meeting was organized in the afternoon in Jallianwala Bagh. Colonel Dyer ordered blind firing on the meeting, in which 1000 people were killed.

questions.question_text: In 1905 AD, the Servants of India Society was established:
questions.explanation: In 1905 AD, the Servants of India Society was established in Poona, Bombay. Its founder was Gopal Krishna Gokhale. This was a society in which people of different religions were included and were devoted to serving the motherland in some form or another

questions.question_text: Where did the 'idea of non-cooperation' originate in the Indian National Movement?

options.A: In the 1920 Khilafat Conference in Bombay

questions.explanation: The idea of Non-Cooperation in the Indian National Movement originated in the 1920 Khilafat Conference in Bombay. The Non-Cooperation movement was the first mass movement run by Gandhi in 1920. Non-Cooperation means not cooperating with the government. The draft of the Non-Cooperation movement was prepared by Gandhi

questions.question_text: Who were the founders of the 'Madras Hindu Association'?
questions.explanation: Its founder was Annie Besant in 1904 AD. Annie Besant was also the first female President of the Indian National Congress. Annie Besant had started the Home Rule League movement in India with the help of Tilak. Her biggest contribution was in bringing the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League together

questions.question_text: Who gave the call to celebrate the day of Bengal partition as Rakhi Day?
questions.explanation: The partition of Bengal happened on 16 October 1905 AD. Rabindranath Tagore had given a call to people to celebrate this day as Rakhi Day. Rabindranath Tagore wrote his famous song 'Amar Sonar Bangla'. This song is now the national anthem of Bangladesh. The Swadeshi and Boycott movement was born in protest against this partition

questions.question_text: The author of the book 'Unhappy India' is:
questions.explanation: The author of the book 'Unhappy India' was Lala Lajpat Rai. Lala Lajpat Rai had presided over the Calcutta special session of Congress in 1920 AD. The name of Subhas Chandra Bose's book was Indian Struggle. The name of Bal Gangadhar's book is Gita Rahasya

questions.question_text: In the context of the Kuka movement, who among the following was sentenced to life imprisonment (Kala Pani)?
questions.explanation: The main leader of the Kuka movement was Baba Guru Ram Singh. The British had sentenced him to life imprisonment. Ram Singh is considered the avatar of the 10th Sikh Guru Govind Singh. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1872 AD and he died in 1885 AD

questions.question_text: The editor of the newspaper 'Indian Mirror' was:
questions.explanation: The newspaper Indian Mirror started being published from Calcutta in 1861. Its editors were N.N. Sen and Devendranath Tagore

questions.question_text: Who established the 'East India Association' in London?
questions.explanation: The East India Association was established by Dadabhai Naoroji in London in 1866 AD. Dadabhai Naoroji is called the ‘Grand Old Man of India’. He also established the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha. He also edited the newspaper 'Rast Goftar'. He wrote the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'

questions.question_text: Who was the Census Commissioner of India's census in 1891?
questions.explanation: The Census Commissioner for India's census in 1891 AD was Jervoise Athelstane Baines

questions.question_text: Which of these were not associated with the 'Deoband School'?
questions.explanation: The Deoband school was established by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi. The start of this school was made in 1866-1867 AD in Deoband, Saharanpur. Its main objective was to prepare religious leaders for the Muslim community, to prohibit English education and Western culture in the school curriculum, to revive the moral and religious aspects of the Muslim community, and to do non-cooperation with the British government. Leaders of this institution, Mahmood-ul-Hasan, tried to give a political, intellectual color to the religious ideas of the institution. Famous scholars and writers of Persian and Arabic like Shibli Nomani were also supporters of the Deoband school. Shah Abdul Aziz was not associated with the Deoband school

questions.question_text: Who formed the Veer Bharat Sabha in 1910 as a branch of the Abhinav Bharat Sangh?
questions.explanation: In the year 1910 AD, Kesari Singh Barhath formed the Veer Bharat Sabha as a branch of the Abhinav Bharat Sangh with the cooperation of Rao Gopal Singh 'Kharwa'. This was a secret revolutionary organization in which soldiers of princely states, jagirdars, and some chiefs were included. Other members of Veer Bharat Sabha were - Dr. Gurudatt, Lakshman Narayan, Hiralal Lahoti, Ramkaran, etc

questions.question_text: In which session did the Congress first declare its policy towards princely states?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation–The Indian National Congress was established in 1885 AD. After this, the annual session of Congress was held every year. The session was held in Nagpur in 1920. In this session, the Congress declared its policy towards princely states.

questions.question_text: When was the All India Trade Union Congress formed in India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation–The International Labor Conference established in 1919 AD and the Non-Cooperation movement of nationalists prepared the foundation for the establishment of the All India Trade Union Congress in India. The All India Trade Union Congress was formed on 31 October 1920 by the efforts of Lala Lajpat Rai, Joseph Baptista, and N.M. Joshi.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and indicate which of the following are not correctly matched. List- I List- II (Author) (Work)

options.B: Aurobindo Ghosh The Ideal of Human Unity
options.C: J.L. Nehru The Unity of India

questions.question_text: In which public meeting did Mahatma Gandhi give the slogan of 'Do or Die'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – On 7 August 1942, the annual meeting of the All India Congress Committee was held at the historic Gowalia Tank ground in Bombay. In this, the Wardha resolution was confirmed. On 8 August 1942, Gandhi gave a slogan in his historic speech 'Do or Die', whose meaning was that either we will get India liberated or we will give our lives in the attempt.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct answer based on the code given below:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – The description of various events during the freedom movement is as follows – The Swadeshi movement started in Bengal in 1905. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened on 13 April 1919, the Dandi March under the Civil Disobedience movement happened in 1930, and the Quit India movement started in 1942.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Civil Disobedience movement started by Gandhi?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Gandhi started the Civil Disobedience movement to connect the public with the national movement, taking issues like reduction in land revenue, prohibition of liquor, abolition of salt tax, reduction in military expenditure, release of political prisoners, and license for weapons for self-defense, etc., and by doing a march named Dandi March (March 1930), he made salt by breaking the salt law at a place called Dandi located near the seashore. Viceroy Lord Irwin tried to suppress the movement with harshness. By 1932, most leaders were put in jail. As a result, the movement was withdrawn in 1934.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Indian National Congress born?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – The Indian National Congress was established on 28 December 1885 in a meeting organized at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College located in Bombay. A total of 72 people were present in it, in which one-third were journalists. Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee was its first President.

questions.question_text: After the failure of the Non-Cooperation movement, under whose leadership did the Congressmen form a new party named 'Swaraj Party'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Angered by Gandhi's withdrawal of this movement after seeing the violent incident of the Chauri-Chaura incident during the Non-Cooperation movement, Shri Chittaranjan Das and Motilal formed the Swaraj Party on 1 January 1923 AD. Their main objective was to make the English aware of their deeds.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Indian elected to the British Parliament?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – The first Indian elected to the British Parliament was Dadabhai Naoroji. He was the first such Indian leader to be elected to the British Parliament from Finsbury on behalf of the Liberal Party. During his London stay (1855-69 AD), he established the 'London Indian Society' and 'East India Association' to make the British aware of Indian problems.

questions.question_text: Who played a special role in the Swadeshi movement?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – During the time of Lord Curzon, the partition of Bengal was announced on 20 July 1905. The movement against this partition started on 7 August 1905. Youth, students, and women came into active politics for the first time. Students played a key role in this movement.

questions.question_text: Who is known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Chittaranjan Das is known as 'Deshbandhu'. Chittaranjan Das, a leading leader of the Non-Cooperation movement, became the President of the Indian National Congress in 1922. He founded the Swaraj Party. Charles Freer Andrews (C.F. Andrews) is known as Deenbandhu.

questions.question_text: When were Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru hanged?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Caught on charges of throwing a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931 AD by linking them to the Saunders murder case and the Lahore conspiracy case.

questions.question_text: When did the Muslim League first demand Pakistan?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – In November 1939 AD, when Congress ministries resigned from their posts, the 'Muslim League' celebrated Independence Day all over India on 22 December 1939 AD. On the start of the Second World War, the British started giving assurance to India that the ultimate goal of Britain is to grant independence to India. In such a situation, in 1940, the Muslim League presented the demand for Pakistan in its Lahore session.

questions.question_text: Which of the following events happened first?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – During the Indian freedom movement, various events happened. The Champaran Satyagraha happened in 1917 AD under the leadership of Gandhi, the Non-Cooperation movement started in 1920 AD, the Dandi March happened from 12 March to 6 April 1930, and the Quit India movement started on 8 August 1942.

questions.question_text: Sardar Patel was associated with this –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – Sardar Patel was associated with Bardoli. Farmers of Bardoli taluka in Surat district of Gujarat did a movement in 1928 AD not to pay taxes. Mehta brothers had a significant contribution to this movement. Mehta invited Vallabhbhai Patel for this movement in January 1928 AD. The women of Bardoli gave the title of 'Sardar' to Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.question_text: Who among the following did not face trial in the 'Kakori Case'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation–Revolutionaries of U.P. successfully looted the train going to Kakori on the Saharanpur-Lucknow railway line on 9 August 1925. Its leaders Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, and Ashfaqullah were hanged. Chandrashekhar Azad escaped the police's grip.

questions.question_text: Who was the drafter of the 'Quit India' resolution?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – On 7 August 1942, the annual meeting of the All India Congress Committee was held at the historic Gowalia Tank ground in Bombay. It was presided over by Abul Kalam Azad. Nehru presented the Quit India resolution, which was accepted after some minor amendments on 8 August 1942 AD.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events chronologically:
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Chauri-Chaura case happened on 5 February 1922. Due to this, Gandhi withdrew his Non-Cooperation movement on 12 February 1922 AD. The Moplah rebellion happened in 1921 in Kerala, whereas the Chittagong armory raid case happened in 1930 AD.

questions.question_text: For which contribution are Lal, Bal, Pal famous, it was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – Lal-Bal-Pal are famous for their extremist path. Extremist ideology emerged under their leadership. This movement was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh. The moderate leaders' belief was the establishment of colonial rule under British rule, whereas the extremist leaders' core idea was to end it and establish self-rule.

questions.question_text: With what was V.D. Savarkar associated?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation– V.D. Savarkar was associated with Abhinav Bharat. In 1904, in Nashik, he established this secret organization whose main objective was to uproot British power in a very secret manner.

questions.question_text: (1) Anushilan Samiti (2) Yugantar Party (3) Ghadar Party (4) Abhinav Bharat Arrange the following events chronologically –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation – In the early phase of the freedom movement, the following organizations originated in revolutionary activities. In 1903, M.N. Roy suggested the name Anushilan Samiti, in this way Anushilan Samiti was born in 1903 AD. Its initial name was 'Bharat Anushilan Samiti'. In 1906 AD, its first conference was held at Subodh Mullick's house in Calcutta. In 1907, in Calcutta, its establishment was done by Barindra Ghosh and Bhupendranath Datta. Yugantar Party was formed in April 1906, while Abhinav Bharat originated in 1904. With the help of Lala Har Dayal, the Ghadar Party was established in 1913.

questions.question_text: At the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress, who was the then Viceroy of India –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation– Lord Dufferin was the Viceroy at the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress. It is notable that the idea of establishing the Congress was the brainchild of Lord Dufferin. His associate A.O. Hume gave it a concrete form.

questions.question_text: The Muslim League was established –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – On 30 December 1906 AD, a conference was held at the invitation of Dhaka's Nawab Salimullah Khan. Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk was its president. The All India Muslim League emerged in this very conference. The constitution of the League was made in Karachi in 1907 AD, and according to this constitution, the first session was held in Amritsar in 1908, where Aga Khan was made its president.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the author of the song 'Vande Mataram' –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The author of the song Vande Mataram is Bankim Chandra Chatterjee. This song has been taken from his book named Anand Math. It was accepted in the 1896 Congress session.

questions.question_text: Indigo rebellion started –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Indigo rebellion started in 1859-60 AD. This movement started from Govindpur village of Nadia district in Bengal. It was led by Digambar Biswas and Vishnu Biswas. The objective of this movement was the open struggle of farmers against the exploitation by indigo producers.

questions.question_text: The founding President of 'Indian Association' was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The founding President of Indian Association was Surendranath Banerjee. It was formed on 26 July 1876 in the Albert Hall of Calcutta. The first objective of this organization was to form a powerful organization for public opinion in the country.

questions.question_text: The real name of the freedom fighter famous by the name of 'Master Da' was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – India's famous freedom fighter Master Da was called Surya Sen of Bengal. He founded the Indian Republican Army in Bengal. He had an active role in the Non-Cooperation movement. Later, after becoming a teacher in a school, he became famous by the name of Master Da.

questions.question_text: What was the name of the committee formed to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Hunter Commission was constituted to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. It was presided over by Lord Hunter. This commission was constituted in 1919, whose members were Lord Hunter, Mr. Justice Rankin, W.F. Rice, Sir George Barrow, Sir Thomas Smith, Jagat Narayan, Shahabji Sultan Ahmed.

questions.question_text: In which month of 1942 AD did the Quit India movement start?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – The Quit India movement started in the month of August 1942 AD. This movement, which started on 9 August 1942, is also known as the August Kranti. This was India's last great fight against British rule, which shook the foundation of British rule. In this very movement, Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die'.

questions.question_text: Gandhi-Irwin Pact was made –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 Explanation – Gandhi-Irwin Pact was made on 5 March 1931. This pact is also called the Delhi Pact. Under this pact, Congress accepted to participate in the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was related to the Commonweal newspaper?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – The Commonweal newspaper was related to Annie Besant. Through this newspaper, she voiced the demand for Home Rule. Annie Besant founded the Home Rule League in September 1916. Her second newspaper was New India.

questions.question_text: Feroz Shah Mehta started the publication of 'Bombay Chronicle' in 1913. Who was the editor of this publication?
questions.explanation: The English language newspaper named 'Bombay Chronicle' was published by Feroz Shah Mehta in 1913. B.G. Horniman provided his support as the editor of this newspaper from 1913 to 1919 AD. Horniman provided support to Indian nationalism in the fight against the British government for press freedom and for the people of deprived and exploited sections. Bombay Chronicle was a significant nationalist newspaper of its time

questions.question_text: Who among the following compared Tilak to the 'ocean' and Gokhale to the 'Ganga' river?
questions.explanation: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi had compared Tilak to the 'ocean' and Gokhale to the 'Ganga' river. In this context, he had compared Pherozeshah Mehta to the 'Himalayas'. Dadabhai Naoroji (Grand Old Man of India) was a member of the 'House of Commons' of the United Kingdom; his famous work is 'Poverty and UnBritish Rule in India'. Annie Besant was a supporter of women's rights and an author. She established the Home Rule League in 1916 and also presided over the Indian National Congress in 1917. She was a supporter of the Indian freedom movement

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below: One as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A) : Gandhi was more concerned about religious beliefs than religious values. Reason (R) : Gandhi was not the creator of any system, he had such a systematic perspective towards human life that ensures peace and joy for the world. (1) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A) (2) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A) (3) (A) is true but (R) is not true (4) (A) is not true but (R) is true
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji himself gave clarification regarding the meaning of 'Dharma' (religion) in his book 'Young India', which is described as follows (1) By religion, I do not mean Hindu religion, although I give more respect to it than all other religions. Religion is that which is beyond Hinduism, which strengthens the very nature of man, which establishes our identity with the truth within us and keeps on purifying us constantly. This is a permanent element of human nature which remains ready to make any sacrifice to achieve complete expression. (2) There are no geographical boundaries to my religion. If there is living faith in it, it will go beyond my love for India. My religion is not the religion of a prison, it has a place for God's destitute creatures, but it tolerates this arrogance and the pride of caste, religion, and color. I firmly believe that if a person does any work in the name of God and with full faith in Him, then even if it is done in the last days of his life, that work is never in vain. Gandhi ji had immense faith in humanity. Indian humanity is not inferior to anyone, perhaps it is superior. The assertion (A) of the above question is not true, but the reason (R) is true.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'At the Feet of Mahatma Gandhi'?
questions.explanation: The author of 'At the Feet of Mahatma Gandhi' is Louis Fischer. Famous American journalist Mr. Louis Fischer came to India in May 1942. He was in India for two months. In the scorching heat of June, he spent a week with Gandhi ji in Gandhi ji's ashram. Gandhi ji gave him one hour every day. He kept talking to Gandhi ji during other activities as well, such as eating, walking, etc. Fischer wrote the book 'Seven Days with the Mahatma'. In this book, Fischer has described the life, likes, and dislikes of Gandhi ji's ashram in a very touching way

questions.question_text: Regarding Gandhi's concept of Satyagraha, which of the following statements is true?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi (1869 - 1948) dominated the Indian political stage from 1919 AD to 1948 AD in such a way that this era is called the Gandhian era of Indian history. Gandhi ji named his entire non-violent method of work as Satyagraha. For him, Satyagraha meant the use of pure soul power against all kinds of injustice, atrocities, and exploitation. Fearlessness was an essential part of his Satyagraha, according to him, "Satyagraha and non-cooperation are not weapons of those who roar and boast, this is the touchstone of your honesty." Satyagraha is not just a resistance method, but also a specific lifestyle, at the root of which are eleven vows like non-violence, truth, non-possession, non-stealing, fearlessness, celibacy, equality of all religions, etc. However, critically, Gandhi's political realism weighed heavily on his moral ideals and contrary to his claims, his Satyagrahas were not always of a purely spiritual nature. He did not get any good results from disobedience in constitutional authority, which is opposed by anti-social elements who oppose the government in the name of Satyagraha. Arthur Moore criticized this by calling it "mental torture". Critics termed fasting as a form of Satyagraha as terrorism and political pressure. Gandhi ji himself said that "Satyagraha is a very dangerous weapon, it should be used with great care." Despite these criticisms, it can be said that the success of this theory depends on the user. Today, this theory can be made successful by sacrificing personal interests Therefore: The theory of Satyagraha is an important and eternal contribution of Gandhi ji.

questions.question_text: Which newspaper wrote at the time of Mahatma Gandhi's assassination that – "He was a Mahatma among politicians and a politician among Mahatmas"?
questions.explanation: The Manchester Guardian newspaper was founded in 1821 as 'The Guardian' previously (1821-1959), a powerful daily newspaper published in London, which is generally considered one of the leading newspapers of the United Kingdom. It was the Manchester Guardian that wrote at the time of Mahatma Gandhi's assassination that – "He was a Mahatma among politicians and a politician among Mahatmas."

questions.question_text: What was the important step of Subhash Chandra Bose during the Haripura Congress session in 1938?

options.A: Because all Indian leaders in this session declared war against the British
options.B: Because Jawaharlal Nehru was chosen as the Prime Minister of future India
options.C: Because Congress started the idea of the Planning Commission
options.D: Because people boycotted foreign goods and liquor

questions.explanation: The 1938 Congress session was held on 19-21 February 1938 at a place called Haripura in Gujarat. The president of this session was Subhash Chandra Bose. This session took place in a village. In this session, the National Planning Committee was formed and Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru was made its president. In this session itself, the princely states were also included in India's independence

questions.question_text: Which event occurred after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
questions.explanation: Gandhi-Irwin Pact, which is also known as the Delhi Pact. It happened in Delhi on 5 March 1931. This pact is also called the Delhi Pact. Congress leaders welcomed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact with a majority. Shri K.M. Munshi called this pact "an era-defining event in the constitutional history of India." After this pact, the Second Round Table Conference was organized from 7 September 1931 AD to 1 December 1931 AD at St. James Palace (London)

questions.question_text: At which place did the first Round Table Conference take place in London?
questions.explanation: The first Round Table Conference was organized from 12 November 1930 to 19 January 1931 AD at St. James Palace (London). It was inaugurated by George V and was presided over by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. The number of delegates in this conference was 89. Congress did not participate in this. According to Bradsford, delegates of Indian princes, depressed classes, Hindus, Sikhs, Christians, Zamindars, Muslim classes, labor unions, and commerce unions participated in St. James Palace

questions.question_text: "Whoever works for the welfare of the people of this country, whether he is a Muslim or a British, is not a foreigner." Who made this declaration in 1916?
questions.explanation: In the year 1916 AD, during the Home Rule League movement, while describing the demand for Home Rule as being based on secularism, 'Bal Gangadhar Tilak' said that - "Whoever works for the welfare of the people of this country, whether he is a Muslim or a British, is not a foreigner. This alienation has nothing to do with religion or profession. This is a matter directly related to interests."

questions.question_text: Who wrote a letter from jail in 1940 saying that "the individual will have to die so that the nation can live. Today I must die so that India can achieve freedom and glory"?
questions.explanation: Subhash Chandra Bose wrote a letter from jail in 1940 saying that "the individual will have to die so that the nation can live. Today I must die so that India can achieve freedom and glory." Special Facts 1. "I, Subhash Chandra Bose, swear by God that I will fight for the freedom of India and its 38 crore inhabitants till my last breath." 2. Jatin Das – In the Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929), along with all the revolutionaries, Jatin Das was also arrested. Very inhumane treatment was being meted out to these revolutionaries in jail, troubled by which Jatin Das went on a hunger strike demanding that all arrested persons be declared political prisoners, where after a hunger strike of 64 days, Jatin Das died. 3. Jatindra Nath Mukherjee – (Howrah Conspiracy Case – 1910 AD) – This conspiracy is related to Jatindra Nath Mukherjee, who is famous by the title of 'Bagha Jatin'. The Howrah Conspiracy Case was filed against Bagha Jatin on charges of murdering Deputy Police Superintendent Samsul Alam, in which he was sentenced to one year of imprisonment. On 9 September 1915 AD, Jatindra Nath Mukherjee (Bagha Jatin) was martyred in a police encounter in Balasore (Odisha).

questions.question_text: When did Gandhi ji step into Durban, South Africa as a young lawyer?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from London after finishing his law studies in 1891 AD and started practicing in Rajkot, but he did not like it there. Then he went to Mumbai and from there, a call letter came from Africa for the hearing of a case of businessman Seth Abdullah. After much family struggle, Gandhi ji got permission to go to Africa. Then in 1893 AD, Gandhi ji left for South Africa. He reached Durban, South Africa by ship and after the incident at Pietermaritzburg station, Gandhi ji stayed in Africa for 21 years and carried out movements there, ended the policy of apartheid, and then returned to India on 9 January 1915 AD

questions.question_text: After how many years of imprisonment was Bal Gangadhar Tilak released (freed)?
questions.explanation: Due to his extremist ideology, Tilak was arrested again in the year 1908. This time he was sentenced to 6 years of imprisonment and was sent to Mandalay Jail. In this jail, he composed many books like Gita Rahasya, etc., and kept moving his revolutionary activities forward through letters. He kept sending letters and kept checking on his colleagues. After completing the 6-year sentence, he was released in the year 1914 (16 June) and returned to India Special Fact - Tilak was the first Congress leader who went to jail many times for the country. On 27 July 1897, he was sentenced to 18 months of rigorous imprisonment for writing an objectionable article in his newspaper 'Kesari'.

questions.question_text: For the resolution of the problems of farmers through the 1917-18 Champaran Satyagraha, which very new and original method did Mahatma Gandhi adopt?

options.B: He emphasized non-payment of taxes along with the Civil Disobedience Movement.
options.C: He conducted a gradual and official inquiry to get information about the sufferings of the farmers.
options.D: He encouraged the farmers to self-surrender (arrest) for not following the instructions of indigo production.

questions.explanation: Gandhi ji made his first major experiment of Satyagraha in Champaran district of Bihar in 1917. Here, the European indigo planters used to commit many atrocities on the farmers working in indigo fields. After hearing the story of Gandhi ji's struggles in South Africa, many farmers of Champaran came there and invited him for help. Gandhi ji reached there in 1917 with Rajendra Prasad, Mazharul Haque, J.B. Kripalani, Narhari Parikh, and Mahadev Desai and started a detailed investigation of the condition of the farmers. The district officials were furious and ordered him to leave Champaran. But he disobeyed the order and was ready for the jail case. The government was forced to revoke the previous order and set up an inquiry committee, one of whose members was Gandhi ji himself. Ultimately, the problems the farmers were suffering from were resolved and Gandhi ji's first effort was successful

questions.question_text: Who organized the 'Satyagraha Sabha' whose members took an oath to disobey the Rowlatt Act?
questions.explanation: In April 1919, Gandhi ji formed a Satyagraha Sabha whose members took an oath not to follow the Rowlatt Act and to face arrest and going to jail. This was a new form of struggle. The nationalist movement, whether under the leadership of moderates or extremists, was limited to movements till now Big meetings and demonstrations, refusal to cooperate with the government, boycotting foreign goods and schools, or individual terrorist actions, these were the only forms of political work known to nationalists till now. Satyagraha immediately raised the movement to a new and higher level. Now there was also talk of just doing the movement and keeping one's dissatisfaction and anger in verbal form and doing active work.

questions.question_text: On whose recommendation did Veer Savarkar receive the "Chhatrapati Shivaji Scholarship" in London?
questions.explanation: After college expulsion, Veer Savarkar was chosen for studies in London. In 1906 AD, on the recommendation of Lokmanya Tilak, Savarkar was chosen to study in London through Pandit Shyamji Krishna Varma. Regarding this scholarship, Balraj Madhok, who was a senior leader of the Bharatiya Sangh, said that for the scholarship Savarkar was chosen for, he had to write something or other about the goals of his life in his application. Savarkar ji wrote and received the scholarship

questions.question_text: Name the freedom fighter who wrote the following lines to the Governor General- "I begged for bread on my knees but instead I got stones. I am not surprised at such a response. The British nation bows only before power."
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji placed 11 demands before Lord Irwin through his newspaper Young India, on which the government did not adopt any positive attitude. Consequently, on 14 February 1930, in a meeting of Congress in Sabarmati, it was decided to launch the Civil Disobedience Movement under the leadership of Gandhi ji. But even this was not considered. Then Gandhi ji said, "I begged for bread on my knees but instead I got stones. I am not surprised at such a response. The British nation bows only before power." Gandhi ji started the Dandi March with his 78 followers and broke the salt law

questions.question_text: Which island did Subhash Chandra Bose name "Swaraj Island" in 1943 AD?
questions.explanation: Subhash Chandra Bose declared war against the Allied Powers in October 1943 and Japan handed over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to Netaji i.e., Subhash Chandra Bose, to this provisional government in November 1943. Netaji himself came to these islands and named Andaman as "Shaheed Island" and Nicobar as "Swaraj Island". On 30 December 1945, the flag of independent India was hoisted on these islands

questions.question_text: Who included women's upliftment as an important part of Congress's constructive work program?
questions.explanation: During the non-cooperation program of Congress, after Gandhi ji's arrest, an appeal was made to the countrymen to try to fulfill Gandhi ji's constructive program. During the Civil Disobedience Movement, there were four to five thousand women in Mahatma Gandhi's meeting. In this meeting, on the advice of Gandhi ji, Stree Swaraj was established. During his struggles in South Africa, Gandhi ji had already experienced the power of women. Gandhi ji knew that widespread participation of women during the national movement was very necessary. Gandhi ji presented the concept of ideal Indian women and called upon women to engage in the service of the nation and to be sacrificed for the country

questions.question_text: Who presided over the Karachi Congress session, 1931?
questions.explanation: To give approval to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact or Delhi Pact, the Congress session was organized in Karachi on 29 March 1931, which was presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. In this session itself, Gandhi ji was shown intense anger, demonstrations, and black flags during his journey. Punjab's Naujawan Sabha also criticized Gandhi ji

questions.question_text: In which year was the Marathi newspaper 'Kesari', started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and still in circulation today, established?
questions.explanation: Kesari: It is a newspaper of Marathi language which was established by Bal Gangadhar Tilak on 4 January 1881 AD. Its use was started to give voice to the Indian freedom struggle. This newspaper is still being published by Kesari Mahratta Trust by the descendants of Tilak Mahratta: The Mahratta newspaper was published in the English language by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, which he started in 1881 AD with the help of his associate Agarkar brothers. Tilak had criticized the cruelty of British rule and the inferiority complex towards Indian culture through these newspapers and this was the reason why he was also sentenced to jail.

questions.question_text: Who among these extremists started Ganesh and Shivaji festivals to oppose Westernization in India?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak started the Ganesh festival in Maharashtra in 1893. Tilak was considered a young revolutionary and leader of the extremist faction at this time. Tilak was struggling for Swaraj and his message was not reaching the masses, to convey which he had chosen the Ganesh festival. Celebrating this festival gave Tilak two advantages: firstly, he could convey his ideas to the masses, and secondly, he could prepare the common people for Swaraj. In this way, Ganpati festival played an important role in the fight for freedom. In 1895 AD, to further the spirit of nationalism, he started the Shivaji festival from Raigad and reached Japan by 1905 AD. Later, when the British government banned political ceremonies, Tilak used the festivals to develop nationalism among the common people and make them aware of their freedom

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the first 'Satyagraha' movement under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: In the national session of Congress in December 1916, Rajkumar Shukla, acting as a representative of the farmers of Bihar, participated in Lucknow and placed the plight of Champaran farmers before the top leaders. On the request of the indigo-growing tenant Rajkumar Shukla, Gandhi ji agreed to go to Champaran. Gandhi ji reached Motihari via Kolkata and Muzaffarpur on 10 April 1917. In the Tin-Kathia system imposed for indigo crops, i.e., 3/20th part of the land, it was mandatory to grow indigo. Gandhi ji opposed this and made the first successful experiment of Satyagraha in Champaran

questions.question_text: Who among the following formed the 'Indian National Army'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—The Azad Hind Fauj was formed by Mohan Singh in September 1942. But in December 1942, he was arrested. Consequently, the INA was dissolved. In 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose formed it in Singapore.

questions.question_text: 'My Experiments with Truth' is authored by
questions.explanation: 'My Experiments with Truth' is an autobiography written by Gandhi ji in the Gujarati language

questions.question_text: Which institution was established by Gopal Krishna Gokhale?
questions.explanation: Servants of India Society was established by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in 1905 in Pune, Maharashtra. Its purpose was to train youth for public life. The members of this society took a vow to serve the country for their entire life

questions.question_text: The newspaper 'Indian Opinion' is related to
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation—During his South Africa trip, Gandhi ji kept continuously trying to organize different Indian communities and publicize their demands well. For this, he formed the 'Natal Indian Congress' and started a newspaper named 'Indian Opinion'.

questions.question_text: Jawaharlal Nehru has been called
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru has been called a socialist. He was a person with modern and progressive ideology from the beginning. In 1936, Nehru wrote that I am confident that the ultimate solution to the problems of the world and India lies in socialism

questions.question_text: As soon as a separate election proposal was announced for _________, Gandhi ji started a hunger strike?
questions.explanation: Regarding a separate electorate for the Depressed Classes, Gandhi ji sat on a hunger strike. After which B.R. Ambedkar reached Yerwada Jail to meet him, where Gandhi was opposing this, while Ambedkar was supporting it. In the end, after dividing the seats between the two, it is called the Poona Pact, earlier the seats of the Dalits were 71, which increased to 148 after the pact. Although this number is found to be 147 in some books

questions.question_text: Who gave Gandhi the title of 'Father of the Nation'?
questions.explanation: Subhash Chandra Bose called Gandhi 'Father of the Nation'. Mahatma Gandhi was addressed as 'Father of the Nation' for the first time by Subhash Chandra Bose. While broadcasting a message from Singapore radio on 4 June 1944, he called 'Father of the Nation' Mahatma Gandhi

questions.question_text: Who founded the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army?
questions.explanation: Under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad, the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was established at Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi in September 1928. The main objective of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was to establish a socialist, republican state in India. It was a democratic organization where majority was given importance

questions.question_text: Match the following: A. Subhash Chandra Bose 1. President of Constituent Assembly B. Vallabhbhai Patel 2. Establishment of State Ministry C. C. Rajagopalachari 3. President of Indian Freedom League Code- A B C D D. Dr. Rajendra Prasad 4. Prepared a plan to solve India's communal problem
questions.explanation: Correct matching is as follows Subhash Chandra Bose - President of Indian Freedom League Vallabhbhai Patel - Establishment of State Ministry C. Rajagopalachari - Prepared a plan to solve India's communal problem Dr. Rajendra Prasad - President of Constituent Assembly

questions.question_text: Gandhi ji's famous Dandi March was organized at the same time as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji's famous Dandi March was organized at the same time as the Civil Disobedience Movement. During the Civil Disobedience Movement, Gandhi ji started the historical salt Satyagraha on 12 March 1930. Gandhi ji did the "Dandi March" with his 78 followers from Sabarmati Ashram. After a long journey of 24 days, Gandhi ji broke the salt law symbolically on 6 April 1930, after which the Civil Disobedience Movement started from here

questions.question_text: In light of the Chauri-Chaura incident, where did the Congress Working Committee meeting take place to stop the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: After the Chauri-Chaura incident, in the Congress meeting held at Bardoli on 22 February 1922, a decision was taken to end the Non-Cooperation Movement and the movement ended

questions.question_text: What is the name of Subhash Chandra Bose's autobiography?
questions.explanation: 'The Indian Struggle' is Subhash Chandra Bose's book and Subhash Chandra Bose's autobiography is 'An Indian Pilgrim' (An Indian Pilgrim)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements related to Young India published by Gandhi ji is true?

options.C: It was published in Hindi and Gujarati together

questions.explanation: 'Young India' was an English language weekly newspaper which was published by Mahatma Gandhi ji. It was first published in 1919 and it was stopped in the year 1931. Therefore: among the above options, only option (b) will be the correct answer Special – The author of Young India book was Lala Lajpat Rai. In this book, he presented the 'Safety Valve' theory in the context of the establishment of Congress that "the main reason for the establishment of the Indian National Congress was that the founders wanted to save the British Empire from being torn apart."

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: Correctly matched pairs are as follows Mahatma Gandhi - Young India Maulana Azad - Al-Hilal Bharatendu Harishchandra - Kavi Vachan Sudha Chandan Mitra - The Pioneer

questions.question_text: "Nehru was as dominant over India as De Gaulle over France." Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: Percival Spear was a British historian who spent a lot of his time in India in the field of teaching. It was Percival Spear who said 'Nehru was as dominant over India as De Gaulle over France'

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Gandhi ji is not true?

options.A: Gandhi ji studied Gita at the insistence of his theosophist friends in London
options.B: He created a book named Gita-Darshan
options.D: He sought solutions to all his problems in Gita

questions.explanation: Gandhi ji's contribution to the Indian National Movement is unforgettable. The period from 1919-1948 during the national movement is known as the Gandhian era. During this period, Gandhi ji led the Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, and Quit India movements. Gandhi ji did not create a book named Gita-Darshan

questions.question_text: Who among the following is called the Bismarck of India?
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel is called the Bismarck of India. Just as Bismarck established a powerful German empire by unifying various German-speaking states for the establishment of Germany, in the same way, Sardar Patel unified 562 princely states at the time of independence, whose area was about 40% of India's area. Sardar Patel, along with V.P. Menon, did the work of merging these princely states into India before independence (during the transition period), for which he was called the Bismarck of India

questions.question_text: When did the Dandi March start at the call of Gandhi ji?
questions.explanation: On 12 March 1930, Gandhi ji started the Dandi Yatra. This foot journey, which lasted for 24 days, started from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad and ended at Dandi located in Navsari. This movement was against the monopoly of the British rule on salt, due to which the taxes imposed on natural resources like salt were abolished

questions.question_text: Who among the following presided over the Indian National Congress session twice?
questions.explanation: William Wedderburn presided over the meetings of the Indian National Congress held in 1889 and 1910. George Yule presided in 1888, being the first Englishman. Alfred Webb presided over the Congress sessions in 1894 and Sir Henry Cotton in 1904

questions.question_text: Gandhi ji went on a hunger strike in 1932 mainly because:

options.A: No conclusion of discussion was reached in the Round Table Conference.
options.B: Congress and Muslim League could not agree on important issues.
options.D: He was arrested against the government's promise.

questions.explanation: Gandhi ji undertook a fast unto death in 1932 in opposition to Ramsay MacDonald's communal policies, particularly the Communal Award.

source_metadata.raw_text_segment: Q43 confirmed from the source page image; answer and explanation shown on the page.

questions.question_text: At which place did Gandhi ji first record his presence publicly in India?
questions.explanation: Champaran Satyagraha in 1917 was the first time Gandhi ji recorded his presence publicly in India. In this revolt against indigo cultivation in Champaran, Gandhi ji opposed it along with the farmers

questions.question_text: After leaving Congress, name the party (party) established by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose in 1939.
questions.explanation: After resigning from the Tripuri Congress session in March 1939, Subhash Chandra Bose established the Forward Bloc in 1939. Later, in 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose joined the Azad Hind Fauj in Singapore, which was established by Captain Mohan Singh

questions.question_text: In the several allegations of British salt monopoly, which of the following did Mahatma Gandhi not mention?

options.A: It deprives people of a simple valuable rural industry
options.B: Unregulated destruction of the wealth that nature has given in abundance
options.C: Forcing people to use more salt
options.D: Charging more than 1000 percent from starving people, never heard of such a thing.

questions.explanation: Forcing people to use more salt, Gandhi ji did not mention this phrase/concept for breaking the salt law

questions.question_text: When did Gandhi ji go to Wardha Sevagram?
questions.explanation: In 1934, Gandhi ji received a proposal to come to Wardha by a big businessman of the country Jamnalal Bajaj. After coming to Wardha, he lived in Maganwadi for one and a half years and after that, he established Sevagram Ashram in 1936

questions.question_text: What name was given by Subhash Chandra Bose to Andaman Island?
questions.explanation: Subhash Chandra Bose established the provisional government of independent India in Singapore on 21 October 1943 in the capacity of supreme commander of Azad Hind Fauj. Japan handed over the Andaman Nicobar Island to Netaji's provisional government on 8 November 1943. Netaji named Andaman as 'Shaheed Island' and Nicobar as 'Swaraj Island'. Subhash Chandra Bose celebrated 'Shaheed Diwas' on 22 September 1944

questions.question_text: What is the chronological order of the following movements led by Gandhi? 1. Ahmedabad 2. Kheda 3. Champaran 4. Rajkot
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915. The British government awarded him the title of 'Kaiser-e-Hind'. He first established the Satyagraha Ashram/Sabarmati Ashram on the banks of the Sabarmati river in Ahmedabad (Gujarat) in India. Under his leadership, India achieved success in many Satyagrahas/movements which are sequentially: Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Ahmedabad Mill Labor Movement (1918), Kheda Satyagraha (1918), and Rajkot Fast-Satyagraha (1939)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Poona Pact between Gandhi and Ambedkar is not true?

options.A: Gandhi went on a hunger strike in opposition to separate electorates.
options.B: Later, a treaty was signed between him and Dr. Ambedkar, which is known as the Poona Pact.
options.C: According to the Poona Pact, the colonial structure of separate electorate for the Dalit class was removed.
options.D: The number of reserved seats for the Dalit class in provincial legislative assemblies was increased from 71 to 147. A provision was made to reserve 18% of the total seats in the central legislature for the Dalit class.
options.E: The pact also included a provision that there would be a basis for limited numbers in government service seats.

questions.explanation: The Poona Pact (September 1932) took place between Mahatma Gandhi and Dalit leader Ambedkar. According to this, the separate electorate system for Dalits was abolished and the number of reserved seats for the Dalit class in various provincial legislative assemblies was increased from 71 to 148 (although this number is 147 in some books) and the number of reserved seats in the central legislature was increased by 18 percent. There was no provision made for this in the government service seats

questions.question_text: In which Congress session was the goal of 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) declared instead of Dominion Status?
questions.explanation: In the Lahore session (1929) of the Indian National Congress, the goal of 'Purna Swaraj' was declared instead of Dominion Status. This session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. In this session itself, the tricolor flag as a symbol of India's independence, Purna Swaraj, Vande Mataram, and Inquilab Zindabad slogans were hoisted

questions.question_text: From which place did Subhash Chandra Bose make his famous call of 'Delhi Chalo'?
questions.explanation: Subhash Chandra Bose gave the slogan of 'Delhi Chalo' while addressing the army as the supreme commander of Azad Hind Fauj on 2 July 1943. On 21 October 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose formed the provisional government of independent India in the capacity of supreme commander of Azad Hind Fauj

questions.question_text: Which of the following Satyagraha was not led by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi joined active Indian politics after returning from S. Africa in 1915 AD and established the "Sabarmati Ashram" near Ahmedabad in 1915 AD. After this, he conducted Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act along with Champaran Satyagraha (1917 AD), Ahmedabad Mill Worker Movement (1918 AD), Kheda Satyagraha (1918 AD), Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement. He also supported the demand for temple entry of untouchables in the Vaikom Satyagraha movement in Travancore state of Kerala. Mahad Chavdar Tank Satyagraha was an effective Satyagraha led by Bhimrao Ambedkar on 20 March 1927 at Mahad, a place in Raigad district of Maharashtra, to give Dalits the right to drink and use water from the public Chavdar tank

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A) : Apart from Dr. Ambedkar, no other person was successful in making the Dalit classes conscious and united for their own development because he gave them an identity-consciousness. Reason (R) : Dr. Ambedkar's entire personality was dedicated to the vocal opposition of such a social system that pushed him and his people towards social boycott, physical deprivation, and social hurt and insult. Regarding both the above statements, which of the following is true?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a scholar, social reformer, and a leader. He dedicated his life to removing social inequality in India. He accepted three great men as gurus in his life- Mahatma Buddha, Kabir, Jyotiba Phule. All these made every effort to unite the Dalit classes, but Ambedkar ji gave it momentum and by taking Dalit people out of social boycott, physical deprivation, and social hurt and insult, he made new laws for them. He decided on active movement against untouchability regarding public drinking water resources in 1927 and the right to enter Hindu temples. On 15 August 1947, when India became an independent nation, he was appointed as the Central Law Minister and Chairman of the Constitution Drafting Committee, who was given the responsibility of writing India's new constitution

questions.question_text: Subhash Chandra Bose declared the formation of the provisional government of independent India on:
questions.explanation: On 21 October 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose formed the provisional government of independent India in Singapore, whose ministers included S.C. Chatterjee (Finance), M.A. Aiyar (Propaganda), and Lakshmi Swaminathan (Women's Department), etc. Subhash Chandra Bose made the headquarters of the provisional government Rangoon, which was supported by Germany and Japan

questions.question_text: Regarding Mahatma Gandhi, which of the following statements is true? ii. He started the Village Industries Association. Select the correct answer with the help of the code given below- Code : i. He started the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 AD.
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was started by Gandhi ji on 1 August 1920. His idea was that if non-cooperation is followed in the right way, then India will achieve Swaraj within a year. He urged the people not to go to schools, colleges, and courts and not to pay taxes. Being saddened by the Chauri-Chaura incident in Gorakhpur on 5 February 1922 AD, Gandhi ji withdrew the movement on 12 February 1922. In his newspaper Young India, he wrote that 'to save the movement from being violent, I can choose every insult, torture, even death.' Gandhi ji established the All India Village Industries Association in Wardha on 14 December 1934. To lead this movement, Congress selected the famous Dr. Joseph Cornelius Kumarappa for the principle of the economy of stability. The first president of this organization was Shri Krishnadas Jaju

questions.question_text: In the liberal era of the Indian National Congress, the title of 'Grand Old Man of India' was given to-
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji, in Poverty and UnBritish Rule in India, described the economic ills of British rule; he is called the 'Grand Old Man of India'. Gokhale said about him, "If there is divinity in humans anywhere, then it is in Dadabhai Naoroji."

questions.question_text: In which of the following did Nehru not believe?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was a person with progressive and modern thoughts from the beginning. Therefore, he was a supporter of freedom of the press, freedom of speech, secular state, etc. He was an advocate of economic equality, not economic inequality

questions.question_text: During the initial years of Gandhi's work, which of the following person did not influence him?
questions.explanation: Gandhi ji went to South Africa in 1893 AD. As soon as he reached there, he experienced the harsh behavior meted out to Indians in South Africa. Gandhi ji established the "Natal Indian Congress" in 1894 AD in South Africa and during the long movement in S. Africa, he visited jail many times. He did in-depth study of Srimad Bhagavad Gita, Ruskin, David Thoreau, Leo Tolstoy's books and got inspiration from them. He also commented on Srimad Bhagavad Gita. He started the newspaper "Indian Opinion" in S. Africa and established "Phoenix Ashram" in 1904 AD. He explained Swaraj in his book "Hind Swaraj" written in 1909 AD

questions.question_text: Who spoke the following words? "The university is a symbol of humanism, tolerance, reason, courage of ideas, and the search for truth. It is always a symbol of humanity's march towards higher goals. If the university performs its duties adequately, then it is good for the nation and the people."
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India. Under the patronage of Mahatma Gandhi, he emerged as the supreme leader of the Indian freedom movement and he ruled from the establishment of India as an independent nation in 1947 till his death in 1964. He is considered the architect of the modern Indian nation, state, sovereign socialist, secular and democratic republic. Jawaharlal Nehru wrote the book 'Discovery of India' and he considered the university as a symbol of the search for truth and said that if they perform their duties adequately, then it is considered good for the nation and the people

questions.question_text: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I will have it.' Who among the following said this?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, famous by the name of Father of Indian Nationalism, was born in Maharashtra. It was he who first made a clear demand for 'Swaraj' and said, "Swaraj is my birthright and I will have it." He started the Home Rule League movement in Pune in 1916 AD. Valentine Chirol called him 'the father of Indian unrest.'

questions.question_text: Who established the 'Free India Society' in England?
questions.explanation: 'Free India Society' was formed in London in 1907 by V.D. Savarkar. Madam Bhikaiji Cama was one of the founding members of the Free India Society

questions.question_text: What was 'Tin-Kathia' in British India?

options.A: Where the farmer was forced to grow indigo on 3/20th part of the land

questions.explanation: During the 1917 Champaran Satyagraha, for the first time, Gandhi ji threatened to conduct Satyagraha in India. In Champaran, farmers were forced to grow indigo on 3/20th part of the land, which was called the 'Tin-Kathia' system. Gandhi ji started his movement from Champaran itself, which was completely successful

questions.question_text: Who among the following is called the 'Frontier Gandhi'?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, famous by titles like Frontier Gandhi, Badshah Khan. During the Civil Disobedience Movement, he started the 'Red Shirt' movement in the North-West Frontier Province with the help of an organization named 'Khudai Khidmatgar' (Servants of God). He brought out a newspaper named Pakhthun (in Pashto language) which was later published by the name of 'Dost'

questions.question_text: With which movement of Gandhi did Vallabhbhai Patel first join?
questions.explanation: Farmers of Kheda district of Gujarat moved under the leadership of Gandhi ji against the collection of increased revenue by the government. In this movement, Vallabhbhai Patel first joined Gandhi ji's movement. Gandhi ji helped the farmers of Kheda with Indulal Yajnik and Vallabhbhai Patel. He suggested the farmers not to pay the tax

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R): Assertion (A): Mahatma Gandhi wrote: "Swadeshi can also be an embrace of death for some other good thing if it is adopted like blind faith." Reason (R): Mahatma Gandhi's view was: Swadeshi is such a principle whose roots are hidden in pure non-violence, i.e., love. Regarding the above statements, which of the following is true?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation: The meaning of Swadeshi is - of one's own country. Mahatma Gandhi's desire was that all goods in India should be manufactured in India and he was associated with the Swadeshi movement. He also wrote, "Swadeshi can also be an embrace of death for some other good thing. Therefore, the statement (A) is true and the reason (R) is also true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of the statement."

questions.question_text: To communicate his thoughts, Mahatma Gandhi was not associated with which of the following newspapers?
questions.explanation: The Leader - newspaper of Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya, not of Mahatma Gandhi. Harijan, Indian Opinion, and Young India, these three are Mahatma Gandhi's newspapers

questions.question_text: "Any government is a tool of service only as long as it is based on the will and consent of the people. When it tries to force the public, it becomes an instrument of oppression. Therefore, the moment the fear of that terror ends in the public- whether it is of law or of weapons, that oppression also ends." - Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: "Any government is a tool of service only as long as it is based on the will and consent of the people. When it tries to force the public, it becomes an instrument of oppression. Therefore, the moment the fear of that terror ends in the public- whether it is of law or of weapons, that oppression also ends." This famous statement is of Gandhi ji in opposition to the oppressive policy of the British government

questions.question_text: Who among the following did not have any influence on Gandhi during his initial period?
questions.explanation: Utilitarian and individualist philosopher John Stuart Mill's philosophical anarchist thought had no influence on Mahatma Gandhi during his initial period. Although in 1920, Gandhi ji was not influenced by philosophical anarchism in his initial period, later in the period, his inclination towards Mill's thoughts started

questions.question_text: Which Indian revolutionary handed over the command of I.N.A. to Subhash Chandra Bose in 1943?
questions.explanation: In July 1943, in Singapore, Rash Behari Bose handed over the command of Azad Hind Fauj to Subhash Chandra Bose and kept himself only in the role of advisor to the I.N.A. Rash Behari Bose founded the Indian Independence League

questions.question_text: 'Hind Swaraj' book was written in which year?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – Mahatma Gandhi explained 'Swaraj' in his book Hind Swaraj written in 1909 AD. This book was originally written in the Gujarati language, which Gandhi ji wrote on a water ship during his journey from England to South Africa.

questions.question_text: For what did Gandhi ji start Vaikom Satyagraha in Kerala?

options.A: For the eradication of Devadasi system in temples.
options.D: To get the doors of temples opened for the entry of lower castes or untouchables.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation– The movement related to untouchability, Vaikom Satyagraha, took place in Kerala in 1924 AD. In 1925 AD, Gandhi ji went to Travancore and talked to the queen there. After this, roads there were opened for Harijans, but entry inside the temple remained prohibited.

questions.question_text: Who was the other editor of 'Kesari' and 'Mahratta' with Tilak?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2014) Explanation– The editor of Bal Gangadhar Tilak's own newspapers Kesari and Mahratta was his colleague G.G. Agarkar. With his help, both newspapers were edited.

questions.question_text: "Every minimum action of mine is directed by that which I consider religion." Whose statement is this among the following?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– Mahatma Gandhi said that 'Every minimum action of mine is directed by that which I consider religion.' While Subhash Chandra Bose said, "You give me blood, I will give you freedom." It is noteworthy that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Subhash Chandra Bose said that "Gandhi ji failed as a politician."

questions.question_text: Who proposed the theory of using 'sub-contractors' in Gandhi's political organization?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation- Judith Brown proposed the theory of using 'sub-contractors' in Gandhi ji's political organization.

questions.question_text: Due to the intervention of Mahatma Gandhi, the wages of workers increased in the 1917 Ahmedabad mill strike:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Gandhi ji launched a movement against mill owners along with workers in 1918. Workers launched a movement regarding bonus. Gandhi ji asked the workers to go on strike and declared that they should get a 35% bonus because inflation increased significantly due to the First World War. The tribunal asked to give a 35% bonus. In 1918 AD, Gandhi ji did his first hunger strike in the Ahmedabad mill worker movement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following newspaper changed to 'Harijan Bandhu' in 1932?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Mahatma Gandhi gave the name Harijan to untouchables in 1932. Along with this, he established the Harijan Sevak Sangh. He also brought out a magazine 'Harijan'. Navjivan newspaper changed to Harijan Bandhu newspaper in 1932 AD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not with Mahatma Gandhi during Champaran Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Gandhi ji made his first major experiment of Satyagraha in 1917 AD in the Champaran district of Bihar. In 1917 AD, a Champaran farmer Rajkumar Shukla met Gandhi ji in Lucknow and requested him to come to Champaran. Gandhi ji's other associates in Champaran included Rajendra Prasad, J.B. Kripalani, Mahadev Desai, Mazhar-ul-Haque, Narhari Parikh, and Braj Kishore.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the author of the book The Indian Struggle 1935-1942?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation—Lala Lajpat Rai wrote 'Unhappy India' and Subhash Chandra Bose wrote the book 'The Indian Struggle 1935-1942'.

questions.question_text: Who was the founding president of the Harijan Sangh established by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- The founding president of the Harijan Sangh established by Mahatma Gandhi was Ghanshyam Das Birla. After the Poona Pact (September 1932), Mahatma Gandhi started taking interest in the anti-untouchability movement and in this way, the 'All India Anti-Untouchability League' was established, whose name was changed to 'Harijan Sevak Sangh'.

questions.question_text: Mahatma Gandhi presided over which annual session of the Congress only once–
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 TGT History, 2011 UP Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History), 2018 Explanation- Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session of Congress only once in 1924. The Kanpur (1925 AD) session was presided over by Sarojini Naidu and the Kakinada session (1923 AD) was presided over by Maulana Muhammad Ali. The Guwahati session (1926) was presided over by S. Srinivasa Iyengar. In this session, for the first time, it was made mandatory for Congress workers to wear Khadi.

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy has been called the stimulator of Indian nationalism?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2011 Explanation- Lord Curzon (1899-1905 AD) has been called the stimulator of Indian nationalism. Supporters of Curzon's policies like Fraser believe that nationalism in India was started by Curzon. Gokhale compared Curzon to the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

questions.question_text: Which author gave Mahatma Gandhi the title of 'Prophetic Leaders'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2010 Explanation– Influenced by the strategy of various movements started by Gandhi ji according to the circumstances during the freedom movement, Gandhi ji was given the title of 'Prophetic Leaders' by Romain Rolland.

questions.question_text: "You give me blood, I will give you freedom" - This declaration was made by–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation– On 21 October 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose established the provisional government of independent India in Singapore. Here he gave the slogan of 'Delhi Chalo' and 'You give me blood, I will give you freedom'. Azad Hind Fauj was dissolved on 21 October 1945 AD. Bhagat Singh gave the slogan of 'Inquilab Zindabad'.

questions.question_text: The founder of Forward Bloc party was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Subhash Chandra Bose was elected President of the Congress unanimously in 1938. After Gandhi ji's opposition on this post, he was elected again in 1939 but due to lack of support from the working committee formed under his leadership, he resigned from the committee and Congress and established the Forward Bloc party in 1939 itself.

questions.question_text: Towards whom did Gandhi ji turn the face of nationalism day-by-day?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Annulled) Explanation – Gandhi ji's message of peace and non-violence was exemplary not only for India but for the entire world. Gandhi ji awakened the minds of all Indians through Satyagraha, Non-Cooperation movement, and Quit India movement and turned towards the common people for the actual use of nationalism.

questions.question_text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi come actively into politics?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Annulled) Explanation – Mahatma Gandhi came actively into politics in 1917 when he started Satyagraha against the atrocities committed on indigo farmers in Champaran district of Bihar province. The Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act in March 1919 was Gandhi's first attempt to launch a nationwide struggle in India. By this time, he had reached the age of fifty.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was generally known as 'Lokmanya'?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Annulled) Explanation – Bal Gangadhar Tilak is known by the name 'Lokmanya'. He awakened the spirit of patriotism and expanded the Congress movement.

questions.question_text: Who gave the title of 'Mahatma' to Gandhi ji?
questions.explanation: PGT 2016 Higher Edu. Exam.(Med. History), 2013 TGT History, 2004 UPPCS (Pre.) Indian History, 2001 Explanation– At the invitation of Bihar farmer leader Rajkumar Shukla, Gandhi ji started Satyagraha in 1917 AD regarding the problems of indigo farmers. Impressed by Gandhi ji's skilled leadership during the Champaran Satyagraha, Rabindranath Tagore gave him the title of 'Mahatma'. Gandhi ji gave him the title of 'Gurudev'.

questions.question_text: During which movement did the new leader named Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi take over the reins of the national movement?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2003 Explanation– When Gandhi launched the 'Rowlatt Act' Satyagraha in March 1919, his effort was the first step in launching a nationwide struggle in India. By this time he had reached the age of fifty.

questions.question_text: The author of the book 'Young India' was –
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2001 PGT History 2005 Explanation – Young India (magazine), Harijan, Navjivan were published by Mahatma Gandhi. Lala Lajpat Rai's book 'Unhappy India', Aurobindo Ghosh's books 'Yugantar', 'Vande Mataram', 'Life Divine' and 'Savitri'. Young India book was written by Lala Lajpat Rai.

questions.question_text: Who among the following asked the British to quit Asia:
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– During the Second World War, to save India from a possible Japanese attack, Gandhi ji appealed to the British to quit Asia.

questions.question_text: Who signed the Poona Pact?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– The Poona Pact was signed by Madan Mohan Malviya and Dr. Ambedkar. Gandhi ji started a hunger strike on 20 September 1932 against Ramsay MacDonald's Communal Award but on 26 September 1932, due to the efforts of Madan Mohan Malviya, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Purushottam Das, and C. Rajagopalachari, the Poona Pact took place between Gandhi ji and Dr. Ambedkar. Under the pact, Ambedkar took back the demand for separate representation of Harijans.

questions.question_text: When did Subhash Chandra Bose take over the command of Azad Hind Fauj?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Subhash Chandra Bose reached Singapore on 2 July 1943 at the invitation of Rash Behari Bose where the presidency of the Indian Independence League was handed over to him. On 21 October 1943, the command of the Azad Hind Fauj was taken over by Subhash Chandra Bose.

questions.question_text: Who edited the newspaper named 'Young India'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Young India newspaper was edited by Mahatma Gandhi. It is noteworthy that Mahatma Gandhi's autobiography is 'My Experiments with Truth'.

questions.question_text: In which Round Table Conference did Gandhi ji participate for the first time?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – Gandhi-Irwin Pact took place in March 1931, as a result of which Gandhi ji participated in the Second Round Table Conference of 1931. But no agreement could be reached in this conference.

questions.question_text: The center for the organization of the Second Round Table Conference in London was –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The Second Round Table Conference (1931 AD) in London was organized at St. James Palace. In which Mahatma Gandhi represented the Congress. The conference was adjourned on the issue of communal electorate.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book 'Gita Rahasya'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – 'Gita Rahasya' book was written by Bal Gangadhar Tilak (in Mandalay Jail). It is noteworthy that Tilak only started 'Ganpati festival' in 1893 and 'Shivaji festival' in 1895 for the propaganda of national ideas.

questions.question_text: Which institution was established by Subhash Chandra Bose in 1939?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 PGT History, 2013 Explanation– Subhash Chandra Bose established Forward Bloc in 1939 AD. Subhash Chandra Bose did this work after resigning from the post of Congress President at the Tripuri conference. The purpose of this conference was to gather anti-imperialist and progressive elements in opposition to the government to achieve independence for India.

questions.question_text: Find the correct sequence of the movements started by Gandhi ji: (i) Rowlatt Act Movement (ii) Kheda Movement (iii) Champaran Movement (iv) Ahmedabad Mill Strike A B C D
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation– Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in the year 1915. The first Satyagraha by Gandhi ji in India took place in 1917 regarding the problems of indigo farmers in Champaran district of Bihar. After this, the Kheda movement in 1918, followed by the Ahmedabad Mill Workers' Satyagraha, and in 1919, Gandhi ji conducted Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act.

questions.question_text: Who led the Kheda Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – In 1917-18, the British were collecting revenue in Kheda district of Gujarat despite the crop being damaged. In opposition to this, Gandhi ji took over the reins of the Kheda movement on 22 March 1918, after which the British government retreated and issued a secret document to this effect that revenue should be collected only from those who are capable of paying. It was in Kheda that Gandhi ji started his first real farmer Satyagraha. Shankar Lal Banker, Indulal Yagnik, Mahadev Desai, and Anasuya Ben also actively participated in the movement. In the end, the government bowed down and made the tax payment optional.

questions.question_text: In which session of the Indian National Congress was Subhash Chandra Bose elected president?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Subhash Chandra Bose was elected president of the 52nd session of the Indian National Congress, which took place in Tripuri (Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh) in 1939.

questions.question_text: Who was Mahatma Gandhi's eldest son?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Mahatma Gandhi had four sons– Harilal, Ramdas, Manilal, and Devdas. Among these, Harilal was the eldest. Some historians consider Jamnalal Bajaj as the fifth son.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is called the 'father of Indian political unrest'?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Bal Gangadhar Tilak believed in the spirit of sacrifice and selfless service. It was through his efforts that the Congress changed from an organization praising the government to an organization critical of the government. Valentine Chirol called him the 'father of Indian unrest'.

questions.question_text: Where was 'Azad Hind Fauj' founded?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – The idea of forming Azad Hind Fauj first came to the mind of British Indian Army officer Captain Mohan Singh. After this, Mohan Singh formed the first division of Azad Hind Fauj in Malaya on 15 December 1941. The formal establishment of 'Azad Hind Fauj' was done in Singapore on 21 October 1943 and its command was handed over to Subhash Chandra Bose in Singapore only.

questions.question_text: The political guru of Mahatma Gandhi was –
questions.explanation: PGT History 2011, 2013 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Gokhale was a leader who believed in non-violence, liberal, and impartial and justice-loving in his thoughts. Impressed by these thoughts of Gokhale, Gandhi ji made him his political guru.

questions.question_text: After returning from South Africa, which organization did Mahatma Gandhi join?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Gandhi ji returned to India from South Africa in 1915 and during the period from 1915 to 1918, Gandhi kept hovering on the periphery of Indian politics with uncertainty. During this period, he refused to join any political movement.

questions.question_text: Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded the Home Rule League in –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Home Rule League was founded in Pune by Bal Gangadhar Tilak on 28 April 1916. Its prominent members were V.S. Munje, R.P. Karandikar, and G.S.
