Khaparde. The work area of this league was Karnataka, Central Province, Maharashtra, and Berar, but Mumbai of Maharashtra was not included in this. Mumbai was included in Annie Besant's Home Rule League.

questions.question_text: In which year was the 'Harijan Weekly' magazine first published?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- After returning to India from South Africa, Gandhi ji established Satyagraha Ashram on the banks of Sabarmati in 1915. During the Civil Disobedience Movement that lasted from 1932 to 1934, Gandhi ji edited the "Harijan weekly" magazine in 1933 AD.

questions.question_text: On whose death did Mahatma Gandhi say: "His death has made me a widower"?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915 and after some time, he became active in Indian politics and along with this, Gandhi kept getting new assistants in India. Maganlal Gandhi was also one of those assistants whose thoughts matched Gandhi ji's thoughts a lot. For this reason, on the death of Maganlal Gandhi, Gandhi ji said, "His death has made me a widower."

questions.question_text: Indian Opinion was published from–
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation– Mahatma Gandhi went to South Africa in 1893 regarding a case. He stayed there for 22 years. During this period, he kept informing the government there about the problems of Indians. In the meantime, during his South Africa trip, Gandhi ji started the publication of Indian Opinion.

questions.question_text: Two I.N.A. headquarters, which Subhash Chandra Bose established, were situated in
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- In June 1942, an Indian revolutionary Rash Behari Bose formally formed the Indian Independence League in Bangkok. Later this became Azad Hind Fauj. Eventually, its reins were handed over to Subhash Chandra Bose. He reached Singapore on 2 July 1943 and Subhash Chandra Bose was declared the supreme commander of the INA on (21 October 1943). Azad Hind Fauj had two headquarters, the first in Singapore and the second in Tokyo.

questions.question_text: Who appointed the National Planning Committee in 1938 AD?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- During the national movement, the leaders of the Indian National Congress thought of preparing a framework for the development of the nation. In which Jawaharlal Nehru formed a National Planning Committee in 1938 under the presidency of Subhash Chandra Bose. The purpose of forming this committee was to plan for the development of the country.

questions.question_text: Mahatma Gandhi was not associated with
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The reason for the Swadeshi movement was the Bengal partition done by the British (effective from 16 October 1905). The proponents of the concept of this movement were Aurobindo Ghosh, Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai. These people wanted to implement the Swadeshi movement in the whole country but the moderate group was against this.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following has called Mahatma Gandhi 'the land of wheat' and Tagore 'the garden of roses'?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Louis Fischer (29 February, 1896 - 15 January, 1970) was an American journalist. He called Gandhi 'Land of Gandhi' and Tagore 'Garden of Roses'. 'The Life of Mahatma Gandhi', 'Gandhi and Stalin' are excellent books by Louis Fischer.

questions.question_text: 'Mahatma Gandhi raises dust like a temporary ghost, he does not raise the level', with whom is this statement associated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Gandhi ji used to always focus on fundamental things during his visits to Harijan places. One of these was the issue of atrocities on Harijans. Gandhi ji's voice against atrocities on Harijans was becoming more intense day by day. He used to say that the social status of Harijans is like that of lepers, they are poor economically. On the religious level, their condition is such that their own Hindu brothers whom we consider to be the house of God, do not allow Harijans to enter temples, and they cannot even use public schools, roads, hospitals, wells, etc. Gandhi ji used to say repeatedly in his writings and speeches that 'We Hindu people have been committing atrocities on Harijans and Dalits for centuries, now we should do penance for them.' Perhaps this was the reason that Gandhi ji never felt bad about the criticism by Ambedkar and other Harijans. Dr. Ambedkar was a critic of Gandhi ji. He did not have faith in Gandhi ji. Ambedkar said that Mahatma Gandhi raises dust like a temporary ghost, he does not raise the level.

questions.question_text: According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, what was most necessary for the upliftment of Dalits?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar was a fighter for religion for the upliftment of lower castes. In July 1924, he formed an organization in Bombay called 'Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha'. Its objective was to bring about the moral and physical improvement of untouchables. In 1930, Ambedkar entered politics. He demanded separate electorates for the untouchables. Ambedkar said that political power is most necessary for the upliftment of Dalits. He believed that until political power comes into the hands of Dalits, improvement in the situation is not possible. Ambedkar, feeling hopeless, opposed the Indian National Congress's demand for freedom and said that the British government should remain in India so that the Dalits could be protected.

questions.question_text: In the context of the meeting between Mahatma Gandhi and George V in Buckingham Palace in 1931 AD, which of the following statements is false?

options.A: Sir Samuel Hoare introduced Gandhi to the Emperor at Buckingham Palace [BLOCK CONTINUATION] Emperor made him meet the Emperor.
options.B: On 15 November, 1931 AD, Gandhi met the Emperor.
options.C: The Emperor asked him "Mr. Gandhi, why did you boycott my son's [BLOCK CONTINUATION] India tour?" [BLOCK CONTINUATION]
options.D: Gandhi replied, "I did not boycott him as your son but as a representative of the British Crown."

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Sir Samuel Hoare introduced Gandhi to the Emperor at Buckingham Palace. The meeting between Mahatma Gandhi and George V took place on 19 November, 1931 AD. The Emperor asked him, Mr. Gandhi, why did you boycott my son's India tour? Gandhi replied that "I did not boycott him as your son but as a representative of the British Crown." Gandhi ji went to London on the ship Rajputana on 29 August, 1931, and returned to India in December 1931.

questions.question_text: Where did Subhash Chandra Bose establish the 'Azad Hind Fauj'?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- The idea of forming the Azad Hind Fauj first came to the mind of Mohan Singh, an officer of the British Indian Army. Taking the British Indian Army soldiers who had already surrendered to Japan during the Second World War, Mohan Singh formed the Azad Hind Fauj on 15 December, 1941. On 7 July, 1943, Rash Behari Bose called a conference in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, a country in South-East Asia, and declared Subhash Chandra Bose as the supreme commander of the I.N.A. On 21 October, 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose formed the provisional government of free India in Singapore.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has addressed Subhash Chandra Bose as "a blazing sword of Indian patriotism"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Subhash Chandra Bose was a staunch opponent of the moderate faction of the National Congress. During the 1928 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, he vehemently opposed the proposal for provincial administrative autonomy approved by the Nehru Report in the 'Subject Committee'. Because he wanted complete independence. On 21 October, 1943, Mr. Bose established the provisional government of India in Singapore and became its commander-in-chief. Subhash Babu gave the war cry of 'Dilli Chalo' to the Indian National Army. By May 1944, he had hoisted the tricolor flag at a place in Kohima, Assam, on free Indian soil. When Gandhi ji withdrew his Non-Cooperation movement in 1922, he considered it the greatest misfortune of the country.

questions.question_text: Where did Subhash Chandra Bose inaugurate the government of free India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- With the help of prisoners of war, Mohan Singh formed the Azad Hind Fauj in Singapore, which was supported by the 'Indian Independence League' organized by Rash Behari Bose. In this way, with the help and cooperation of soldiers and Indian citizens living in South-East Asia, the Azad Hind Fauj was formed in 1942. Subhash Chandra Bose was made the supreme commander of the Azad Hind Fauj. Under the leadership of Subhash Chandra Bose, the Azad Hind Fauj had reached Kohima. On that same occasion, Chakravarti Rajagopalachari had advised to reach an agreement with the Muslim League on the basis of certain conditions.

questions.question_text: "Future generations will scarcely believe that such a one as this ever in flesh and blood walked upon this earth." Which person expressed this thought about Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2009 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Albert Einstein said- Future generations will scarcely believe that such a one as this ever in flesh and blood walked upon this earth, whereas Arnold Toynbee had said that "The generation I was born into was not just the generation of Hitler or Stalin in the West, but also the generation of Gandhi in India. We can say with some certainty that Gandhi's influence on human history will be more lasting than the influence of Hitler and Stalin." Rabindranath Tagore had said that "Gandhi is great as a political organizer, leader of people, and moral reformer, but he is even greater as a human being because all these aspects do not limit his humanity. In fact, everyone gets strength from this. Although he is impossibly idealistic and measures every action by his definite standards, yet he is a lover of mankind, not a lover of hollow ideas."

questions.question_text: "Mahatma Gandhi was a gentle messenger of non-violent revolution" who said this?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- The above statement was by Larry Collins and Dominique Lapierre. Whereas, when Louis Fischer asked Gandhi ji in June 1942, "What is your program to bring about improvement in the condition of farmers?", his reply was "Farmers will capture the land", we don't have to say anything to them, they will take the land themselves, and when Fischer asked "Will the landowners be compensated?", then he replied that it would be impossible from an economic point of view. Then Fischer asked, tell me well, how do you see your upcoming civil disobedience movements? Gandhi ji's answer was "Farmers in the villages will stop paying taxes. They will make salt despite government restrictions. Their next job will be to capture the land."

questions.question_text: Who took the place of the leader of the movement when Gandhi ji was arrested during the Salt Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2005 Explanation─ Abbas Tyabji was given the place of the leader of the movement when Gandhi ji was arrested during the Salt Satyagraha.

questions.question_text: Who was the first commander of Subhash Chandra Bose's I.N.A.?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 GIC Lecturer, 2018 Explanation : After the fall of Singapore on 15 February, 1942, 40 thousand Indian soldiers were made prisoners of war. Japanese officer Major Fujiwara handed them over to Captain Mohan Singh. Taking these prisoners of war, Mohan Singh set up the Azad Hind Fauj under the name Indian National Army (I.N.A.). The following proposal to form the Azad Hind Fauj was passed at the Bangkok conference: "Indian National Army should be formed comprising Indian soldiers and Indian citizens of East Asia. Captain Mohan Singh will be the supreme commander of this liberation army of India."

questions.question_text: Under what name did Subhash Chandra Bose obtain a passport in Kabul to reach Berlin?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation - The hero of the Indian national movement, Subhash Chandra Bose, was born on 23 January, 1897 AD in Cuttack, Odisha. In 1919 AD, he obtained a graduation degree from Calcutta University, after which he went to England. In 1921 AD, he joined the Indian National Congress inspired by C.R. Das and Gandhi ji. In 1923, he was elected the Mayor of Calcutta. But in 1924 AD, he was arrested and sent to Mandalay jail. After being released from jail, he formed the 'Independence League' in 1927. He was elected Congress President in 1938 and 1939. But due to differences with Gandhi ji, he resigned from the post of President. During the Second World War, in 1940, he was put under house arrest in his own home. But in 1941 AD, he came out of his house wearing the guise of a Pathan named Ziauddin and from there he reached Peshawar. His companion Bhagat Ram helped him reach Kabul from Peshawar. From Kabul, he obtained a passport under the name 'Orlando Mazzotta' and reached Germany. There he formed a liberation army. Here, people called him by the name 'Netaji'.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book "Gandhi versus Lenin"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation - The book 'Gandhi versus Lenin' was written by S.A. Dange (Shripad Amrit Dange). Shri Dange has a very important place among the early communist leaders of India. He was a resident of Bombay and his inclination towards socialism was from the very beginning. To spread socialist ideas in India, he started publishing a newspaper named 'The Socialist'.

questions.question_text: In which of the following languages was the book named 'Hind Swaraj' written?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ This book written by Mahatma Gandhi was originally written in Gujarati. When it was published, it was banned by the Mumbai government due to anti-government contents in it. Later, Gandhi ji got it published in English. A copy was also sent to the veteran writer Tolstoy. Seeing the thoughts of his mind, the Russian writer was very happy and sent a message of thanks to Gandhi ji in this context. Gandhi ji's autobiography "My Experiments with Truth" was written in English. Later it was translated under the name 'Satya Ke Mere Prayog'.

questions.question_text: Who said on the utility of railways in British India, "There is no utility of railways in British India, it is like decorating another's wife"?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a leader of the extremist faction of the Indian National Congress. He had said on the subject of the utility of railways in India that "There is no utility of railways in British India, it is like decorating another's wife."

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Subhash Chandra Bose?

options.A: He participated in the I.C.S. examination in 1920 and secured the fourth position. [BLOCK CONTINUATION] and secured the fourth position.
options.B: He was the President of the Indian National Congress in the years 1938 and 1939.
options.C: He had spent prison life in Mandalay jail.
options.D: He had participated in the Quit India movement.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – All three statements are true regarding Subhash Chandra Bose. Only the statement (d) is false, because Subhash Chandra Bose had fled from Calcutta on 17 January, 1941 AD and reached Berlin via Peshawar, Kabul, Moscow, where he started working against the British Empire. On the invitation of Rash Behari Bose, on 4 July, 1943, Subhash Chandra took over the leadership of I.N.A. and Independence League. On 21 October, 1943, Netaji established the provisional government of India in Singapore. Thus it is clear that Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose did not participate in the Quit India movement because at that time he was on a foreign tour.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is not true regarding the book 'The Indian Struggle (1920-1942)' written by Subhash Chandra Bose?

options.A: It discusses the Indian independence movement between 1920 and 1942.
options.B: It discusses the Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939) sessions.
options.C: It has a chapter 'The Gandhi-Irwin Pact and After'.
options.D: It contains a detailed distribution of the peasant movement.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Subhash Chandra Bose (1897-1945 AD) resigned from the Indian Civil Service (I.C.S.) and participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement, and became the President of the National Congress in 1938-39. In his book 'The Indian Struggle (1920-1942)', the national movement has been described, but it does not contain a detailed account of the peasant movement.

questions.question_text: The author of the book 'At the Feet of Mahatma Gandhi' was:
questions.explanation: The author of the book named 'At the Feet of Mahatma Gandhi' was Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of independent India. He wrote this book being influenced by Gandhi ji. It contains a description of the efforts made by Gandhi ji in getting India its independence

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct answer using the code given below: (1) Simon Commission (2) First Round Table Conference (3) Cripps Mission (4) C.R. Formula Code-
questions.explanation: The chronological order of the following events is as follows • 3 February 1928 - Simon Commission reached Bombay. • 12 November 1930 - 19 January 1931 - First Round Table Conference. • 23 March 1942 - Cripps Mission reached India. • 10 July 1944 - C.R. Formula.

questions.question_text: Who among the following opposed the Mountbatten Plan in the Congress Working Committee on 14-06-1947?
questions.explanation: The Congress Working Committee meeting was held in Delhi on 14-15 June 1947, which was presided over by J.B. Kripalani. In the Congress Working Committee meeting, Govind Ballabh Pant presented the proposal to accept the Mountbatten Plan for the partition of the country. Along with Nehru, Gandhi also accepted this proposal, whereas Purushottam Das Tandon opposed the partition

questions.question_text: Why did Congress criticize the 1946 Cabinet Mission Plan?

options.A: There was pressure from princely states on Congress.
options.B: Congress did not want the integration of princely states.
options.C: Cabinet Mission ignored the need for elected representatives of princely states to be in the Constituent Assembly.
options.D: Cabinet Mission wanted to make princely states a part of the Constituent Assembly. to Mountbatten Plan

questions.explanation: In February 1946, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee sent a three-member team, the Cabinet Mission, to India in search of possibilities for transfer of power and formation of a Constituent Assembly, etc. It included Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade), and A.V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty). Along with other parties, Congress also criticized the Cabinet Mission, in which the main points were that representatives of princely states were not included in the Constituent Assembly, and the compulsory nature of grouping was against the principle of provincial autonomy

questions.question_text: The objective of the Cripps Mission led by Sir Stafford Cripps was –

options.A: To persuade Indian leaders to support British war efforts.
options.B: To stop the commencement of the Quit India Movement.
options.C: To persuade Congress ministers to withdraw their resignations.

questions.explanation: The international community was troubled by Japan's continuously rising power. America, Australia, and China pressured Britain to make India independent. As a result, Churchill announced the Cripps Mission on 11 March 1942. The Cripps Mission reached India on 23 March 1942. The objective of the Cripps Mission was to persuade Indian leaders to support British war efforts. In other words, we can say that its real objective was to coax Indians into cooperating in the war

questions.question_text: Who was the Chairman of the Partition Council for civil administration between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: After independence and partition, a Partition Council was constituted to resolve issues related to civil administration and the division of employees, which was chaired by the Governor-General of India, Lord Mountbatten. Two representatives each from India and Pakistan were included in this council. At the executive level, a two-member steering committee was appointed, in which Shri H.M. Patel and Shri Mohammad Ali were members

questions.question_text: When did the 'Indian Independence Bill' receive royal assent in Britain?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Bill received royal assent in Britain on 18 July, 1947. The Indian Independence Act was passed in the British Parliament in a short period of just 12 days (4 July, 1947 - 16 July 1947), and on 18 July, 1947, the British Emperor also signed his approval on it

questions.question_text: There is an opinion that top officials of the East India Company were responsible for looting the Indian economy and society; among these historians, who can be held responsible for this?
questions.explanation: Rajat Kanta Ray was born on 6 May, 1946 in Calcutta. He has shown the drainage of wealth and economic looting by the British East India Company in modern Indian history. He has held the British company responsible for looting the Indian economy and society

questions.question_text: In which year did the Royal Indian Navy mutiny take place?
questions.explanation: On 18 February, 1946, non-commissioned officers and soldiers of the Royal Indian Navy went on strike in protest against racial discrimination and low-standard food. This mutiny took place on the naval training ship N.M. Talwar in Bombay, led by M.S. Khan. Mutinous soldiers were demanding the release of soldiers of the Azad Hind Fauj and soldier B.C. Dutt. B.C. Dutt was arrested for writing 'Quit India' and 'Jai Hind' on the ship

questions.question_text: With reference to the Indian Constitution, pay attention to the following pairs and select the correct option with the help of the code given below:
questions.explanation: Correct match Parliamentary System – England Federal System – Canada Fundamental Rights – United States of America Directive Principles of State Policy – Ireland Note:- In the question, only B and D were correct, and A and C were wrong answers, which have been corrected to provide the right answer.

questions.question_text: Who was the acting President of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December, 1946?
questions.explanation: The first meeting of the Indian Constitution-making Assembly took place on 9 December 1946. At that time, Sachchidananda Sinha was made its acting President. Initially, it was decided to frame the constitution according to the Cabinet Mission's plan. Under this, the central government was to have only subjects of defense, foreign affairs, and transport; the provinces were to have authority over the remaining subjects

questions.question_text: Who prepared the draft of the Objectives Resolution?
questions.explanation: The draft of the Objectives Resolution (Objective Proposal) was presented in the Constitution-making Assembly by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946, which was granted approval on 22 January 1947

questions.question_text: When did the Indian Constituent Assembly start its first session?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly was constituted on 9 December 1946 based on the nature of the constitution provided by the Cabinet Mission. Its first meeting or session included 389 members, in which 93 members were from princely states and 296 members were from India. On 11 December 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President and H.C. Mukherjee was elected Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly

questions.question_text: In which year did the British government send the Cabinet Mission to India?
questions.explanation: In February 1946, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced the sending of a three-member high-level delegation to India. The three members of this mission were Lord Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade), and A.V. Alexander (Admiral or Naval Minister). This mission reached Delhi in India on 24 March 1946. This mission was given specific powers and its task was to search for means and possibilities for the peaceful transfer of power to India. Lord Pethick Lawrence was the Chairman of the Cabinet Mission

questions.question_text: In which year was the demand for Pakistan officially made?
questions.explanation: The session of the Muslim League was held in Lahore on 23 March, 1940. It was presided over by M. Ali Jinnah. In this session, the demand for a separate Muslim nation, Pakistan, was made from India. While giving a speech in the session, Jinnah said that they would accept nothing other than a separate Muslim nation, and they would remain steadfast on their decision till the end until the demand for the creation of Pakistan is completely accepted. The draft of the famous resolution of 23 March 1940 was made by Sikandar Hayat Khan and it was presented by Fazlul Huq and Khaliquzzaman had supported it Special fact- The name Pakistan was first coined by Cambridge University student Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933 AD, which included- Punjab (P), Afghanistan (A), Kashmir (K), Sindh (S), and Balochistan (TAN).

questions.question_text: The 'Mountbatten Plan' related to the partition of India was officially announced on
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 PGT History, 2005 Explanation- Lord Mountbatten came to India as Governor-General in March 1947. Upon arrival, he discussed the political situation here with various leaders of the country to get a grip on it and submitted his suggestions to the British government. Finally, the British government presented the India Partition Plan on 3 June 1947, which is also called the 'Mountbatten Plan'.

questions.question_text: Regarding the Rajagopalachari Plan, the correct statement is

options.A: It gave no facilities to the Muslim League

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2010 Explanation – Many Congress people opposed the Rajagopalachari Plan. Rajagopalachari presented a formula on 10 July 1944 AD to increase cooperation between the Congress and the Muslim League, which is known as the Rajagopalachari Formula after him. This formula was indirectly a proposal for the concept of a separate Pakistan. Gandhi supported this formula. Among Hindu leaders, Veer Savarkar had severely criticized the Rajagopalachari formula. Therefore, the given option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Who opposed the C.R. Formula (Rajagopalachari Plan)?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation – Chakravarti Rajagopalachari had brought out a formula in 1944 in which an agreement was suggested based on the right of self-determination for those areas that were Muslim-majority. This is what is called the C.R. Formula or Raja Ji Formula. Gandhi ji and Mohammad Ali Jinnah had discussions and correspondence regarding this formula, but Jinnah opposed it and it remained unsuccessful.

questions.question_text: Who among these is not a member of the Cabinet Mission?
questions.explanation: Antony Eden was not a member of the Cabinet Mission. In the year 1946, British Prime Minister Attlee announced the sending of a three-member high-level delegation to India. This delegation included three members of the British Cabinet - Lord Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade), and A.V. Alexander (Naval Minister). This mission was given specific powers and its task was to search for means and possibilities for the peaceful transfer of power to India

questions.question_text: When India got independence, who was the Prime Minister of England?
questions.explanation: When India got independence, the Prime Minister of England was Clement Attlee. In February 1947, Clement Attlee announced India's freedom that he would hand over power to Indians before June 1948

questions.question_text: Mountbatten's plan was about_________

options.A: Providing direction to the Constituent Assembly for framing the constitution for India
options.C: Making a plan to stop communal riots occurring across India simultaneously
options.D: Making provisions for handing over power from the hands of the British to the hands of the Indians

questions.explanation: On 3 June, 1947, Lord Mountbatten presented his plan in which an outline of various stages to solve India's political problem was presented. Initially, this transfer of power was to be given to the Indian governments of partitioned India in the form of a Dominion status

questions.question_text: On 16 August, 1946, how did the Muslim League observe the day?
questions.explanation: The Muslim League observed 16 August, 1946 as Direct Action Day in support of the demand for Pakistan. Its objective was to prove by spreading communal riots that Hindus and Muslims could not live together. It was led by Mohammad Ali Jinnah

questions.question_text: On which day did the sailors of the Royal Indian Navy mutiny?
questions.explanation: The naval mutiny of 18 February, 1946 spread from Karachi to Calcutta. In this, the naval soldiers of the Royal Indian Navy mutinied against the then British rule. Later, this mutiny ended at the urging of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below: (i) Announcement of Wavell Plan (ii) Muslim League's Direct Action Day (iv) Arrival of Cripps Mission Code: (iii) Announcement of Cabinet Mission Plan
questions.explanation: Plans - Time A. Arrival of Cripps Mission - (i) 23 March 1942 B. Announcement of Cabinet Mission - (ii) 19 February 1946 C. Muslim League's Direct Action Day - (iii) 16 August 1946 D. Wavell Plan - (iv) 14 June 1945

questions.question_text: Regarding the 1942 Quit India Movement, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.B: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
options.C: Workers did not participate in the movement.

questions.explanation: & c) : Before the Quit India Movement started in 1942, Gandhi ji was already arrested, so the leadership of it was not handled by Gandhi ji. After the arrest of senior leaders, the youth handled the movement; the movement could not remain non-violent. There was violence everywhere in this, which the then Viceroy Linlithgow had told Gandhi to condemn, which he refused to do

questions.question_text: Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option from the given options to answer: Assertion (A) : In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its consent given for the Cabinet Mission Plan. (117.0,701.4,306.4,726.7) Code : Reason (R) : The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946. Reason (R) : The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946.

options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) does not correctly explain (A).

questions.explanation: In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its consent for the Cabinet Mission Plan but joined the interim government formed in 1946 after Wavell persuaded them

The Simla Conference was held in Simla on 25 June, 1945 to discuss the Wavell Proposal. This was an all-party conference held in Simla. The Congress delegation to this conference was led by 'Abul Kalam Azad'. During this conference, a condition was kept by the 'Muslim League' that all Muslim members appointed to the Viceroy's executive council must not be from outside the Muslim League. This very rigid stance of the Muslim League became the main reason for the failure of the 'Simla Conference' held from 25 June to 14 July. Abul Kalam Azad termed the failure of the Simla Conference as a 'Water Shed' in India's political history. Mahatma Gandhi did not participate in this conference even though he was present in Simla
examinations: The Congress delegation to the 1945 Simla Conference was led by –

questions.question_text: Where was the seventh session of the All India States Peoples Conference held under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation: The seventh session (1945 AD) of the All India States Peoples Conference (AISPC) under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru was held in Udaipur. It is noteworthy that the sixth session of the AISPC (February 1939 AD, Ludhiana) was also chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru

questions.question_text: Who was the interim President of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly for the making of the Indian Constitution took place on 9 December, 1946 AD in the Parliament House. The senior-most member of the assembly, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, was elected as the temporary President of the assembly and H.C. Mukherjee as the Vice-President. On 11 December, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was unanimously appointed as the permanent President of the assembly and B.N. Rau as the Constitutional Advisor

questions.question_text: The Diwan of Junagadh, Bhutto, being compelled, invited the Indian government to handle the administration of Junagadh:
questions.explanation: In September 1947 AD, the Junagadh state announced its accession to Pakistan. However, the majority of the state's population was Hindu, who wanted to stay in India. The citizens of the state established a 'Free Temporary Government' (Azad Aarzi Hukumat) in protest against the Nawab's decision. Then, forced, the Nawab fled to Pakistan, and the Diwan there, Shah Nawaz Bhutto, wrote a letter on 8 November 1947, inviting the Indian government to handle the administration of Junagadh, and on 9 November 1947, the Indian government took the administration of Junagadh into its own hands. Later, on 20 January 1948, after conducting a plebiscite, the Junagadh state was included in the Indian Union

questions.question_text: Who led the Congress in the discussions regarding the Cripps Mission and Simla Conference?
questions.explanation: Congress was led by Abul Kalam Azad in the discussions regarding the Cripps Mission and Simla Conference. It is noteworthy that the Cripps Mission was announced on 11 March, 1942. This mission reached India on 23 March and Sir Stafford Cripps presented his plan on 30 March, 1942, and under the Wavell Plan, the conference was held in Simla from 25 June-14 July, 1945

questions.question_text: Who was the Nizam of Hyderabad during 1946-47?
questions.explanation: In 1946-47, the Nizam of Hyderabad was Mir Osman Ali Khan (Asaf Jah). He ruled over Hyderabad until 17 September 1948

questions.question_text: Who was made the Supreme Commander of the joint defense council, which was entrusted with the responsibility of dividing military personnel, weapons, and war materials after the partition of India in 1947?
questions.explanation: On 3 June, 1947, the British government announced the plan for the transfer of power on 15 August, 1947 to two states named India and Pakistan in the Indian subcontinent. On 3 June, 1947 AD, the leaders of the Muslim League and Congress, under the chairmanship of the then Viceroy Lord Mountbatten, expressed their agreement on the distribution of armed forces through the Partition Council. Field Marshal Auchinleck was appointed as the Joint Defense Supreme Commander under Mountbatten. He was entrusted with the responsibility of dividing soldiers, weapons, and war materials

questions.question_text: By whom was the idea of Pakistan pioneered?
questions.explanation: In 1930 AD, while presiding over the Allahabad session of the Muslim League, the great Urdu poet Iqbal said that the creation of a consolidated Muslim state in Northwest India alone seems to be the ultimate destiny of Muslims to me. In this way, the idea of Pakistan was pioneered by Mohammad Iqbal. The originator of the name Pakistan is Choudhry Rahmat Ali

questions.question_text: On which day was the declaration of independence of India and Pakistan made?
questions.explanation: On 3 June 1947, Prime Minister Attlee announced the partition plan (3 June Plan) in the House of Commons. The plan of 3 June 1947 was the India partition plan. It mentioned that process under which power was to be transferred to Indians by the British and Muslim-majority provinces had to choose whether they would stay in India or join Pakistan

questions.question_text: Arrange the following high-level agreement-talks in chronological order with the objective of bringing a moderate stance in the path adopted by the Muslim League:
questions.explanation: (a) Raja Ji (Rajagopalachari) Formula (1944 AD) - Brought with the objective of resolving the differences arising due to the two-nation theory and separate ideas of the Muslim League and the Indian National Congress regarding India's independence from the British (b) Gandhi-Jinnah talks- This talk was held regarding the Muslim League. (c) Bhulabhai Desai Liaquat Ali agreement took place in April 1945. The objective of the agreement was to ensure equal distribution of seats between Congress and the Muslim League. (d) Simla Conference 1945, 25 June - This conference was called to discuss the Wavell Plan. In which the distribution of seats for Muslims was talked about.

questions.question_text: After achieving independence from British rule, reminding Jawaharlal Nehru that 'independence has been received by India not by the Congress', who urged that the most qualified individuals should be included in cabinet formation without considering party relations?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi, after independence, reminding Jawaharlal Nehru, said "independence has been received by India, not by the Congress." He also urged Nehru that the most qualified individuals should be included in cabinet formation without considering party relations

questions.question_text: Who among the following has described the Cripps proposals as a 'post-dated cheque' of a bank going bankrupt?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006, 2001 Explanation– Churchill announced the Cripps Mission on 11 March, 1942. The Cripps Mission reached India on 23 March, 1942. After contacting various leaders here, Cripps presented his plan on 30 March, 1942. Both Congress and the Muslim League rejected the Cripps proposals. Mahatma Gandhi described these proposals as a 'post-dated cheque of a bankrupt bank'. The Muslim League rejected the Cripps proposals on two grounds: first, election, and second, partition.

questions.question_text: (i) Meeting of Subhash Chandra Bose with Shri Tojo. (ii) Arrival of Subhash Chandra Bose in Taiping. (iii) INA hoisted the national flag on the soil of free India. (iv) Establishment of the Indian National Army. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Arrange the following events in chronological order:
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– On 1 September 1942, the first division of the Azad Hind Fauj was constituted with 16,300 soldiers. In 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose reached Singapore, where he constituted the famous Indian National Army. Subsequently, he was brought to Singapore on 2 July 1943 by German submarines. From there, he went to Tokyo and had a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Tojo. The Indian National Army hoisted the tricolor flag in May 1944 at a place called Kohima in Assam on free Indian land. Subsequently, Subhash Chandra Bose arrived in Taiping. Finally, he died in an air crash on 18 August 1945.

questions.question_text: 'Whether they describe themselves as Muslims, Hindus, or anything else, when they act barbarically and commit cruel murders, instead of watching it with helplessness, I will pray to the Almighty to take me away from this sorrow-filled world.' These lines belong to which of the following?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– 'Whether they describe themselves as Muslims, Hindus, or anything else, when they act barbarically and commit cruel murders, instead of watching it with helplessness, I will pray to the Almighty to take me away from this sorrow-filled world.' These lines were said by Mahatma Gandhi when communal violence did not stop.

questions.question_text: Below there is an Assertion (A) and a Reason (R), one of each: Assertion (A): British Prime Minister Winston Churchill announced the departure of the Cripps Mission. Reason (R): Immediately after the fall of Rangoon, the courage of the British army in Southeast Asia was broken. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper July. 2017 Explanation– In March 1942, Japan captured Rangoon. In this way, to strengthen its position in Southeast Asia, British Prime Minister Churchill sent the Cripps Mission to India in 1942 with the desire to get cooperation from Indians. Its chairman was Sir Stafford Cripps.

questions.question_text: The concrete result of the Wavell Plan was–
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2012 Explanation– After the failure of Gandhi-Jinnah talks based on the C.R. Formula, the then Governor-General Lord Wavell presented the Wavell Plan in June 1945 to resolve the constitutional deadlock. The concrete result of which was calling the Simla Conference.

questions.question_text: In February 1947, Prime Minister Attlee announced that the British would leave India –
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013 Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2012 Explanation – British Prime Minister Attlee announced in the House of Commons on 20 February, 1947 AD that the British would hand over power to Indians before June 1948 AD.

questions.question_text: After Mountbatten left, who among the following served as Governor-General?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation — After Mountbatten left, Chakravarti Raja Gopalachari served as the Governor-General, who is also called the first Indian Governor-General of India. He remained on this post until 26 January, 1950. He remained the Chief Minister of Madras from 1952 to 1954. In 1959 AD, due to differences with Congress leaders on various issues, he left Congress and constituted the 'Swatantra Party'. He was a supporter of social equality and Dalit upliftment.

questions.question_text: Who was that first Congress leader who advised that Hindi written in the Devanagari script should be the national language of India?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi was the first Congress leader who advised that Hindi written in Devanagari script should be the national language of India. Gandhi ji believed that since more and more people in India understand Hindi, Hindi should be the national language of India. Gopal Krishna Gokhale was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question_text: On whose death did Mahatma Gandhi say: "Their death has made me a widower."
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- On the death of Maganlal Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi said: "Their death has made me a widower."

questions.question_text: Who was the chairman of the Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The Cabinet Mission reached India on 24 March, 1946. The members of this mission were Stafford Cripps (President, Board of Trade), Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), and A.V. Alexander (Naval Minister). Pethick Lawrence was the chairman of this mission. This mission suggested a three-tier governance system. It confirmed the right of the provinces to form small or large groups and divided the provinces into three categories named A, B, and C.

questions.question_text: Who announced that the British would leave India in June, 1948?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2013 Explanation- The then Prime Minister of Britain, Clement Attlee, announced in the House of Commons on 20 February, 1947 that the British would leave India after transferring power to the responsible people before June 1948.

questions.question_text: "I will create a movement from the sand of India that will be even bigger than the Congress-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Quit India Movement, which is also called the August Revolution, Gandhi ji asked the Congress to pass a resolution to launch it. Although Gandhi ji kept discussing the coming struggle, but now delaying it started seeming wrong to him. He threw this challenge to the Congress that if it did not accept his proposal for the struggle, then "I will raise a movement bigger than the Congress from the sand of the country itself." Consequently, the Congress Working Committee gave its approval for the decision of the struggle in its Wardha meeting (14 July, 1942). The All India Congress Committee meeting was to be held on 8 August 1942, in which this proposal was to be ratified. For this, a historic meeting was held at Gwalih Tank in Bombay. The enthusiasm of the public was worth seeing. Inside, leaders were discussing various issues and outside, a sea of people was swelling.

questions.question_text: As Viceroy, Lord Mountbatten held talks with the following Indians regarding the transfer of power- 1. Jawaharlal Nehru 2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel 3. Mohammad Ali Jinnah 4. Mahatma Gandhi Specify the correct sequence of talks from the code given below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– Lord Mountbatten was appointed Viceroy in March 1947 in place of Lord Wavell, in the 3 June, 1947 announcement, talked about the partition of India. According to this plan, it had to be decided through a plebiscite in the frontier province whether it would be included in India or Pakistan, but Mountbatten held talks with Nehru and Patel many times regarding the transfer. He held talks with Gandhi ji for the first time in this regard on 31 March, 1947 AD and with Jinnah in April, 1947 AD. Congress was ready for partition, although Gandhi ji was not in agreement with this. Based on this, the British Parliament passed the "Indian Independence Act 1947" based on which two independent states of India and Pakistan were created.

questions.question_text: The parallel government that was established during the Quit India Movement in Tamluk of Midnapore district was named-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2000 Explanation– During the Quit India Movement, a 'Jatiya Sarkar' (National Government) was constituted on 17 December, 1942 at a place called Tamluk in Midnapore district of Bengal. Its existence lasted until September 1944. Gandhian constructive work and mass movements had happened enough in Tamluk. The Jatiya Sarkar carried out relief work on a large scale rapidly, gave grants to schools, and also constituted an armed Vidyut Vahini. Courts were made to resolve disputes among themselves and the excess wealth of the rich was distributed among the poor. Since the geographical location of Tamluk was isolated, hence this independent government could run here for some more time. While the parallel government of Satara (Maharashtra) proved to be the most long-lived.

questions.question_text: Under Gandhi ji's leadership, the Gujarat Sabha played a major role–

options.A: In the strike of Ahmedabad mill-workers

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2013) Explanation – In 1918 AD, Gandhi ji fought a revolt with the farmers against the government because the government did not give relief in tax despite the destruction of crops of farmers in Kheda of Gujarat district. In this, Vallabhbhai Patel of Gujarat Sabha, Indulal Yagnik, and other youth revolted along with Gandhi.

questions.question_text: Who among the following presided over the group of lawyers for the defense in the famous trial of soldiers of the Azad Hind Fauj in Red Fort in 1946?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- The issue that agitated the people the most in 1946 was, what will happen to the soldiers of the Azad Hind Fauj? They were imprisoned as war prisoners and the government was going to run a trial against them for cruelty. Nehru appealed to show generosity towards these 'lost patriots'. Congress constituted the Azad Hind Fauj Defence Committee and also made 'Azad Hind Fauj Relief and Enquiry Committee' to provide financial aid to released prisoners and make arrangements for their employment. When this historic trial started in the Red Fort, Bhulabhai Desai was leading the team of defense lawyers. Tej Bahadur Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju, and Asaf Ali were among his assistants. On the first day of the proceedings, Nehru was also present in court wearing a lawyer's dress.

questions.question_text: During the Quit India Movement, in which of the following places was a parallel government of the people established?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- During the Quit India Movement in 1942 AD, parallel governments were formed in Ballia, Satara, and Tamluk. The parallel government of Satara (Maharashtra) proved to be the longest-lived. Since the beginning of the Quit India Movement, this area remained quite active. From the beginning of the movement, processions of thousands of people were taken out from the local headquarters of the government. After this, a series of sabotage, attacks on post offices, looting of banks, cutting of telephone wires, etc., started. Y.B. Chavan was a significant leader here. He also had contacts with Achyut Patwardhan and other underground leaders. From the beginning of 1943, the underground workers started reorganizing themselves and their organization was ready in about six months. A Prati Sarkar (parallel government) was established. Nana Patil was among its significant leaders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following reports was not prepared at the behest of the Muslim League regarding the offenses of the Congress government on the Muslim community?

options.C: Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule Report

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 Explanation- Pirpur report, Sharif report, and Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule report were prepared at the behest of the Muslim League regarding the offenses of the Congress government on the Muslim community, whereas Sir Mohammad Saadullah report was not prepared at the behest of the Muslim League. The League adopted the policy of supporting the British and opposing the Congress from the beginning. The League was against the national movement and in support of British rule from the beginning. One main basis of the League's organization was the Muslim religion. The League adopted the policy of giving impetus to the communal sentiments of Muslims from the beginning. There is no doubt that many Muslims and their leaders like Nawab Syed Ahmed, Maulana Muhammad Ul Hasan, and Mohammad Ali Jinnah (initially) were not in agreement with this policy of communalism of the League. But this policy of the League remained permanent.

questions.question_text: Read the following- 1. Rajagopalachari Formula 2. Wavell Plan 4. Mountbatten Plan Code: 3. Cabinet Mission Find the correct chronological order of the events from the code given below-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- Rajagopalachari Formula- Rajagopalachari presented a formula on 10 July, 1944 to increase cooperation between Congress and the Muslim League, which is called the Rajagopalachari formula. In this formula, it was accepted that after the end of the Second World War, a commission should be appointed in North-Eastern and North-Western India where Muslims are in majority and it should be decided whether they want to separate from India or not. Wavell Plan- Viceroy Lord Wavell called a conference in Simla in June 1945, whose objective was that until a new constitution is made, a proposal for the reorganization of the Viceroy's executive council should be presented on behalf of the government. In February 1946, three members of the British Cabinet, Lord Pethick Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander, were sent to search for means and possibilities for peaceful transfer of power in India. 3 June, 1947, Lord Mountbatten Plan is related to the partition of India and Pakistan.

questions.question_text: Among the following nationalists, write the name of one who was in favor of nation-building based on planned economic development. He was also an engineer-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya was also one of those who first called for planned development in the twenties. Renowned engineer, educationist, Bharat Ratna Visvesvaraya's first book written on the need for planning for the country's economic development "Planned Economy for India" which was published in 1934. In this, he presented a 10-year plan for India's planned economic development, whose main objective was to double national income, develop small and large industries, and increase production in the factory sector.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given code – List-I List-II (iii) Cabinet Mission
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation— List-I List-II (a) Clement Attlee (i) Cabinet Mission (b) Mountbatten (ii) Plan Balkan (c) Lord Linlithgow (iii) August Offer (d) Wavell (iv) Breakdown Plan

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct regarding the Cabinet Mission Plan?

options.A: It rejected the demand for the creation of a separate Pakistan.
options.B: It gave recognition to the right to break ties with the Commonwealth.
options.C: All members of the Indian cabinet would be Indians.
options.D: It indicated the possibility of communal representation.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2014) Explanation– 24 March, 1946, Cabinet Mission came to Delhi. Its objectives were the following– (a) Establishment of a federation in India. (b) Formation of a constitution-making assembly. (c) Giving recognition to the right to break ties with the Commonwealth. Note- It indicated the possibility of communal representation. This statement is not correct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the Cabinet Mission Plan?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : On 19 February, 1946, Lord Pethick Lawrence announced in the House of Lords that a cabinet delegation, which would include himself, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander, would all go to India so that they could talk to Indian leaders on political issues with the help of the Viceroy. This mission (Cabinet Mission) reached Delhi on 24 March, 1946 and long talks were held with various political parties of India. Lord Amery was not a member of this mission.

questions.question_text: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of the Cabinet Mission's arrival in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- In Britain, the British cabinet under the leadership of Clement Attlee took power on 26 July, 1945 AD. On 19 February, 1946 AD, Secretary of State for India Pethick Lawrence announced in the House of Lords that the British government had decided to send a cabinet mission for constitutional reforms in India. This delegation included a total of three members- Secretary of State for India Pethick Lawrence, (President of Board of Trade) Stafford Cripps, and Chief of Navy A.V. Alexander. The delegation reached Delhi on 24 March, 1946 and presented its report. At the time the delegation team came to India, the President of Congress was 'Maulana Abul Kalam Azad', who had been continuously working as the President of Congress since after 1940.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the drafting committee of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The drafting committee of the Indian Constitution (Drafting Committee) had 7 members apart from Chairman Dr. Ambedkar- 1. Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, 2. D.P. Khaitan, 3. N. Madhavrao, 4. K.M. Munshi, 5. N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, 6. T.T. Krishnamachari, (7) Saiyid Mohammad Saadulla. S.N. Mukherjee was not a member of this committee.

questions.question_text: In the interim government formed under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru, what was his designation:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - In the interim government formed under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru, he was the Vice President or Deputy President. The interim government was constituted on 2 September, 1946. It included 12 members (including 3 Muslims) nominated by the Congress, whose Vice President was Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question_text: How many days did the transfer of power and partition of India take in total?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - The transfer of power and partition of India took a total of 72 days. The 3 June plan was mainly the India partition plan. Power transfer was done by the British to India on 15 August, 1947. Therefore, the total period from 3 June to 15 August was 72.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): Ultimately, the Congress leaders accepted the proposal for the partition of India. Reason (R): They were convinced that this was the only suitable solution left. Which of the following is correct in the context of the above two statements?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– Mountbatten Plan 3 June, 1947, this plan presented the India partition plan. It is also called the Mountbatten Plan. This plan was opposed by leaders like Gandhi ji, Abul Kalam, etc. Ultimately, Indian leaders had to accept the India partition plan according to the Indian situation.

questions.question_text: Which party celebrated 'Black Day' against the partition of India on 3 July 1947?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation– Hindu Mahasabha celebrated Black Day against the partition of India on 3 July 1947. After the establishment of the Muslim League in 1906, Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya, and Lala Lajpat Rai established the Hindu Mahasabha in 1915.

questions.question_text: What was not part of the Mountbatten Plan?

options.A: It gave the Indian states the right to choose their future.
options.B: It suggested the partition of India.
options.C: It was not clear about the date of partition of India.
options.D: Congress and the Muslim League accepted it.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The date of 15 August, 1947, was fixed in the Mountbatten Plan to hand over power to Indians. Therefore, statement (c) is false.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was the Railway Minister in the Interim Government (1946)?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – Asaf Ali was the Railway Minister in the Interim Government (1946), whereas Baldev Singh received the Defense Department, I.I. Chundrigar received the Commerce Department, and Abdur-Rab-Nishtar received the Communications Department.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of the book 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States'?
questions.explanation: The author of the book named 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States' is V.P. Menon. This book was published in 1953 AD by Longman publishers in London

questions.question_text: Consider the following events: 1. Cripps Mission 2. Quit India Movement 3. Nehru Report 4. Wavell Plan The correct sequence of these events is:
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation Nehru Report– 1928, Cripps Mission–March/April 1942, Quit India Movement– 8 August, 1942, Wavell Plan– 1945.

questions.question_text: Consider the following events – 2. Bombay Plan 3. Simon Commission 4. Mountbatten Plan 1. Cabinet Mission The correct chronological order of these events is –
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2014) Explanation– The correct chronological order of the given events is as follows– Simon Commission – 1927-28 Bombay Plan – 1944 Cabinet Mission – 1946 Mountbatten Plan – 1947

questions.question_text: On which date was "Direct Action Day" (Direct Action Day) observed by the Muslim League?
questions.explanation: UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 MP Asst. Prof. 2017 Explanation– The Muslim League started the Direct Action Day on 16 August, 1946. The objective of this action of the League was to spread communal riots and create an atmosphere of terror and prove that Hindus and Muslims cannot live together. It was led by Mohammad Ali Jinnah.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the appropriate option from the codes given: List-I List-II (i) 1944 (ii) 1946 (iii) 1942 (iv) 1945
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – During the independence movement in India, various political activities happened, under which the Cripps Mission came to India in 1942 AD. Talks between Gandhi and Mohammad Ali Jinnah were held in Delhi in 1944 and the Simla Conference was held in 1945 AD, which failed due to Jinnah, and the Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946.

questions.question_text: The name of the Finance Minister of Nehru's Interim Government was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation- On 2 September, 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru took the oath for the post of Vice-President of the Executive Council. This was equivalent to the Prime Minister. There were a total of thirteen members in the cabinet formed under Nehru's leadership. Liaquat Ali Khan was given the Finance Department who misused his post very much.

questions.question_text: India's first Governor-General was–
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2005 Explanation – Independent India's first Governor-General was Lord Louis Mountbatten, whose tenure was 1947-48. After he resigned, Rajagopalachari became India's first Indian Governor-General whose tenure was from 1948 to 1950.

questions.question_text: Greed for power was also a reason for accepting the partition of India. Who has said this?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2002 Explanation– Born on 14 March 1925, Michael Brecher was a member of the 'Royal Society' of Canada who in 1959 published the book "Nehru: A Political Biography" and alleged that greed for power was also a reason for accepting the partition of India. This biography of Nehru describes Nehru's participation in the independence movement and the politics of the first forty years of Indian nationalism.

questions.question_text: When was Pakistan made?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005 Explanation—Pakistan was created on 14 August, 1947. Mohammad Ali Jinnah became the first Governor-General and Liaquat Ali became the Prime Minister of Pakistan. The name 'Pakistan' was created by Choudhry Rahmat Ali.

questions.question_text: When did the Cabinet Mission come to India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation — Attlee, the leader of Britain's Labour Party, decided on 19 February 1946 AD to send a parliamentary delegation to India to talk to Indian leaders, which included Sir Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander, and Pethick Lawrence, who reached India on 24 March 1946, which is known as the Cabinet Mission.

questions.question_text: In which year was the Oil and Natural Gas Commission established?
questions.explanation: The Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act was passed on 18 September 1959, by which the Oil and Natural Gas Commission was established. It is noteworthy that the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation was established on 14 August 1956. Its headquarters is in Dehradun. Its area of work is oil and natural gas. This is a Maharatna company Special Facts 1. Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) was established in 1964 AD, whose headquarters is in New Delhi and the area of work is electronics power industry. 2. National Thermal Power Corporation Limited (NTPC) was established in 1975 AD, whose headquarters is in New Delhi and the area of work is electrical energy. 3. Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) was established in 1959, whose headquarters is in New Delhi and the area of work is diesel, gas, and petrochemicals.

questions.question_text: Why was the Indian National Committee for Space Research established by the Department of Atomic Energy of the Government of India?

options.A: For assistance and advice to start a space program for
options.B: To establish Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launch Station
options.D: To develop a satellite communication network

questions.explanation: The Indian National Committee for Space Research was established in 1962 AD by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai under the Department of Atomic Energy of the Government of India, which was created for assistance and advice to start a space program

questions.question_text: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, which laid the foundation of the ‘License Raj’ in the industrial sector, when was it passed by the Parliament?
questions.explanation: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, which laid the foundation of the ‘License Raj’ in the industrial sector, was passed by the Parliament in 1951 AD. Under the Industries Act, 1951, industrial license was required for establishing a new industrial undertaking, manufacturing a new item by an existing undertaking, changing the location of the industry, expansion of existing capacity sufficiently, and for all other purposes

questions.question_text: In 1949, who said in the Constituent Assembly that the members of the Indian Civil Service have acted with "complete loyalty and faithfulness to the Union" (India)?
questions.explanation: In 1949 AD, remembering his past experiences of the Interim Government, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel said in the Indian Constituent Assembly debate on 10 October 1949, I want to say for the record of this assembly that if the civil service officers had not worked with a sense of patriotism and loyalty in the last two or three years, this Union would have ended. Ask the Premiers of all the provinces. Is any Premier ready to work without civil service officers? He will resign immediately. There is no alternative to them. We had only a few remaining officers of the civil service. We have worked with those few people with great difficulty

questions.question_text: Who played a leading role in bringing back abducted women at the time of the partition of India?
questions.explanation: Mridula Sarabhai kept making effective recommendations to the state on issues like fundamental rights of women, abortion, divorce, and illegitimate children. Mridula Sarabhai's contribution to the issue of protecting women during the freedom struggle is important. To ensure that women would not remain indifferent in the freedom movement, she laid the foundation of homes like "Jyoti Sangh" and "Vikas-Grih" and remained vocal on all social evils. The experience of working with Mahatma Gandhi in maintaining communal harmony was useful in working with the refugees who came after partition. From both sides of the border, she brought out thousands of women and got them rehabilitated

questions.question_text: Which of the statements are correct regarding the linguistic reorganization of Indian states? later in 1968.

options.E: Article 347 of the Constitution protects the rights of linguistic minorities. Select the correct answer from the options given below:

questions.explanation: Along with independence, keeping in view the demand for reorganization of states on a linguistic basis, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the President of the Constituent Assembly, constituted a 4-member 'Linguistic Provinces Commission' under the chairmanship of Justice S.K. Dhar on 27 November 1947. In its report submitted on 10 December 1948, the Commission suggested the reorganization of states on the basis of ‘administrative, geographical, financial and developmental convenience’ instead of language Supporting the demand for the formation of a separate state for Telugu speakers of Madras state on the basis of language, ‘Potti Sriramulu’ started a hunger strike, who died after 56 days on 15 December 1952, as a result of which Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru formed the separate state ‘Andhra State’ for Telugu speakers on 1 October 1953. This was the first state to be formed on a linguistic basis. - A three-member commission (K.M. Panikkar and Hriday Nath Kunzru) was constituted under the chairmanship of Justice Fazl Ali for the State Reorganization Commission, and they submitted their report to the Centre on 30 December 1955. On the basis of this report, the ‘States Reorganization Act’ 1956 was passed. According to this Act, the 7th amendment was made in the Constitution and 14 states and 5 union territories were formed. Thus, option C is incorrect. - Leaders of the Akali Dal agitated for the merger of Punjab and PEPSU and for the creation of a Punjabi Suba, in 1966 Indira Gandhi's government divided it into three parts according to the Punjab Reorganization Act - Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab. And Chandigarh was made a Union Territory. Article-347, special provisions regarding a language spoken by a section of the population of any state, protects the rights of minorities.

questions.question_text: Nehru-Liaquat Pact (1950) was to deal with what?

options.A: Dispute over Indus river water distribution

questions.explanation: Under the Liaquat Ali – Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru Pact (1950) or Delhi Pact, an agreement was reached between both countries on issues of refugees, property, and rights of minorities

questions.question_text: Supreme Commander of the Joint Defence Council, who was given the responsibility of the partition of military personnel, weapons, and war materials? After the partition of India in 1947, who was made the
questions.explanation: After getting independence, the process of partition of India and Pakistan was in full swing. Everything was being distributed, from population to border, money, weapons, etc., were also exchanged with mutual consent. In that context, the issue of distribution of India-Pakistan military weapons, ammunition, and soldiers was also complex. A joint defence council was constituted for its resolution, for which Claude Auchinleck was appointed as the Supreme Commander. It was decided that army units which have a large number of Muslims should be given to Pakistan and non-Muslim majority units should be given to India. On 17 August, the British started leaving India and this process of theirs was completed by 28 February 1948 AD. After this, the post of Supreme Commander from India was abolished

questions.question_text: Who were the architects of the Second Five-Year Plan who laid special emphasis on industrialization?
questions.explanation: Due to the success of the first five-year plan, the second five-year plan began with an atmosphere of hope and enthusiasm. In this plan, the goal was set to bring the economy to a state of rapid economic development through rapid industrialization. The work period of this plan lasted from 1956 to 1961. This plan is known by the name of Mahalanobis model

questions.question_text: In India, the Green Revolution started under whose Prime Ministerial leadership?
questions.explanation: During Lal Bahadur Shastri's tenure in 1966 AD, a new agricultural revolution policy was adopted in the Kharif season in India, which was called the High Yielding Variety Programme. Prof. Norman Ernest Borlaug is considered the father of the Green Revolution in the world. Who studied high-yield wheat crops in Mexico. M.S. Swaminathan is considered the father of the Green Revolution in India. As a result of the Indian Green Revolution, there was a significant increase in per-hectare production and total productivity of crops like wheat, sugarcane, maize, and millet, etc

questions.question_text: ‘Apsara’, India’s oldest research reactor, was built with the help of which country?
questions.explanation: In India, along with the establishment of the Atomic Energy Commission in the year 1948 under the chairmanship of Bhabha, the nuclear energy program started. This commission established the Department of Atomic Energy in the year 1954 for the implementation of its atomic energy policies. The first nuclear research reactor was built near Mumbai in 1956 named Apsara. Its work was completed with the support of Great Britain. It was a fuel and light water reactor

questions.question_text: The Indian National Committee for Space Research, which was dissolved with the formation of ISRO, was established in the following year:
questions.explanation: The Indian Space Research Organisation was established in India on 15 August 1969. When it was established, its name was Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR). The Indian space program is the vision of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. In 1962, the Indian National Committee for Space Research was constituted

questions.question_text: The theory that, ‘‘the greatest happiness of the greatest number is the measure of right or wrong action’’, is related to which of these English philosophers?
questions.explanation: Jeremy Bentham is a utilitarian political thinker. Utilitarianism emphasizes the concept of greatest happiness for the greatest number. In this way, utilitarians say that the goal of every action is to increase the measure of human happiness and to reduce the quantity of the measure of suffering

questions.question_text: In which year was the nationalization of the Reserve Bank of India done?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank Act, following the recommendations given by the Hilton Young Commission. This bank is the central bank of India which recognizes all banks. Its nationalization was done in 1949. Before nationalization, this bank was a privately owned bank; then after nationalization, complete ownership of the Government of India was established over it

questions.question_text: The term ‘‘License Raj’’ was coined by whom among the following:
questions.explanation: After independence, socialist groups, most importantly, influenced the concept of License Raj policies. All these ideas were opposed by Chakravarti Rajagopalachari who established the first favourable political party, the Swatantra Party. In the 1950s, Chakravarti coined the term ‘‘quota, permit-license raj’’ to describe the Indian regulatory system. ‘‘I want the corruption of permit-license raj to end.... I want real, equal opportunity for all and not the private monopoly suggested by permit/license raj.’’

questions.question_text: When did Matsya Sangha merge into Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The Government of India also fulfilled the formality of merging Matsya Sangha into Greater Rajasthan on 15 May 1949 in Rajasthan. When the Government of India made Matsya Sangha on 18 March 1948, it was written in the merger deed that later this union should be merged into Rajasthan. For this reason, this phase was also considered a mere formality

questions.question_text: Under which plan was the Damodar Valley Project related to high power and irrigation started?
questions.explanation: To deal with waterlogging and recurring floods, for hydroelectric production, developing irrigation, and for agricultural and industrial development of the related region, the Government of India started the Damodar Valley Project after consultation with the then Bihar and West Bengal governments. This plan was prepared by a leading engineer of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the United States of America, Mr. W.L. Voorduin. Later, under the First Five-Year Plan, it was named Damodar Valley Corporation

questions.question_text: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.explanation: India, that is Bharat, is a Union of States. It is an independent sovereign, socialist, democratic republic with a parliamentary system of government. This republic is governed according to the Constitution of India which was accepted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 which came into force on 26 January 1950

questions.question_text: When was the Hindu Code Bill passed?
questions.explanation: The Hindu Code Bill was presented in the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly in 1948, the outline of which had been started even before independence. It was reviewed in 1948 AD and it was presented by Ambedkar on 5 February 1950. This bill was already facing opposition, then after contemplating on this, while giving equal rights to all citizens in the Constitution, it also advocates for women's rights, which was presented in 1951 AD but could not be passed due to continuous opposition. For this reason, Ambedkar resigned. Later, after the first Lok Sabha elections, this Act was divided into several parts and presented and passed, which reduced its effectiveness to a great extent

questions.question_text: ‘‘Hindu Marriage Act’’ which grants women equal rights for divorce, remarriage and also prohibits polygamy, polyandry and child marriage, was passed in which year:
questions.explanation: In the Indian democratic process, all citizens of India have their personal matters according to their religious and caste customs and traditions, marriage, divorce, maintenance, inheritance, adoption, and child marriage related cases have been regularized. The Parliament of India has made four laws in Hindu law, in which (1) Hindu Marriage Act 1955 (2) Hindu Succession Act 1956 (3) Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956 (4) Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956. At present, the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 does not consider polygamy as valid for Hindus. But under scriptural law, in Hindu law, men were allowed to keep more than one wife. Under this Act, widows are granted recognition for remarriage. But in this same Act, by adding Section 13, the sacramental form of marriage has also been done. Section 13 of the Act is related to divorce, but there is no such concept as divorce in Hindu marriage. Section 5, Section 11, Section 12 of 1955, that is, necessary conditions for a valid marriage, void marriage and voidable marriage, only establish that marriage is a contract, not a sacrament
