questions.question_text: Which of these commissions was established for the purpose of seat reservation or quota to identify ‘‘socially or educationally’’ backward classes?
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission was established on 1 January 1979 AD by the then Janata Party government. The scope of work of this commission was to identify socially and economically backward classes and to provide for reservation in education and government jobs. The chairman of this Mandal Commission was Mr. Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal. The Mandal Commission report, while declaring 3743 castes of religions and sects on the basis of social, educational, and economic criteria, presented a report of 27% reservation

questions.question_text: On which of the following cases is the decision given by the Supreme Court related to equal rights of inheritance of property regardless of gender?

options.A: Mary Roy vs State of Kerala
options.B: Shreya Singhal vs Union of India
options.D: Lily Thomas vs Union of India

questions.explanation: Mary Roy is a teacher from the Indian state of Kerala and an activist of the women's rights movement who is known for winning the case against the inheritance law of her Syrian Christian community in the Supreme Court in 1986 AD. Through this verdict, equal rights for Syrian Christian women in their paternal property along with their male siblings were ensured Due to the 1916 Travancore Succession Act, Mary Roy was deprived of her share in the family property. After the death of her father, she filed a case against her brothers, which through the Indian court system, she paved her way and achieved victory.

questions.question_text: Who was the Chairman of the States Reorganization Commission (1953) among the following individuals?
questions.explanation: On 22 December 1953, on the basis of a resolution passed by the Central Cabinet, the Central Government constituted the States Reorganization Commission. The States Reorganization Commission was three-member, in which Justice Fazl Ali as Chairman, K.M. Panikkar, and Hriday Nath Kunzru as members were included. On 30 December 1955, the States Reorganization Commission submitted its report to the government. The States Reorganization Commission, in its report, said that while reorganizing states on the basis of language and culture alone, apart from language, national security, financial and administrative requirements, and the capacity to make five-year plans successful should also be kept in mind

questions.question_text: Who is considered the architect of India's Five-Year Plans among the following?
questions.explanation: P.C. Mahalanobis is considered the architect of the Five-Year Plans in India. He is known for drafting the second Five-Year Plan. He was a famous scientist and statistician. He was born in June 1893 in Kolkata, Bengal. Every year on 29 June, in his honour, it is celebrated as Statistics Day Five-Year Plan (1951-2017) was started for the economic and social development of India for every five years. Its mention is not in the Constitution. At present, NITI Aayog has taken its place.

questions.question_text: How much time was given to Sir Cyril Radcliffe to submit the demarcated report of the borders of Punjab and Bengal?
questions.explanation: For demarcating the borders of Punjab and Bengal, the British government appointed a Boundary Commission under the chairmanship of Justice Radcliffe. Whose job was to map and determine the contiguous regions or villages with Hindu and Muslim majority. Although Radcliffe got very little time (only 6 weeks)

questions.question_text: Which of the following states had to be forcibly merged into independent India?
questions.explanation: The military operation carried out to include Hyderabad in India is called ‘Operation Polo’. The Nizam of Hyderabad, Osman Ali, was defeated in this and the entire Hyderabad was included in the Indian Union

questions.question_text: The credit for merging the princely states of India goes to .............
questions.explanation: The credit for merging the princely states of India goes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. At that time, the number of Indian princely states was 562. It included an area of 712,508 square miles

questions.question_text: What was the inspiration behind the Five-Year Plan
questions.explanation: The inspiration behind the Five-Year Plan was Russia. Joseph Stalin implemented the first Five-Year Plan in the Soviet Union in 1928. This is a centralized and integrated national economic programme

questions.question_text: When was the Constituent Assembly established for making the Constitution for India?
questions.explanation: Based on the elections of the Constituent Assembly, the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held in Delhi on 9 December 1946 AD. Its temporary President was Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha. On 11 December, 1946 AD, the second meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held in Delhi, then Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President

questions.question_text: Which flag was raised after their qualification order determination for the Royal Indian Navy after their revolt?
questions.explanation: On 18 February 1946, the sailors at the Signal Training Establishment Talwar went on a hunger strike against bad food and racial insults. The next day, the strike spread to Castle and Fort barracks and 22 ships of the Bombay harbour. On the masts of the rebel fleet, the tricolor, the crescent, and the hammer and sickle signs waved together

questions.question_text: Who started the ‘Bhoodan Movement’?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation ─ The initiator of the Bhoodan movement was Vinoba Bhave. He started the Bhoodan movement on 18 April, 1951. He started this movement from Andhra Pradesh. It is noteworthy that on 18 April, 1951, at Pochampally in Telangana region, Vinoba Bhave received his first land in donation.

questions.question_text: Till the attainment of independence in 1947, at which place were the maximum number of Congress sessions organized?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of Indian National Congress sessions were held in Kolkata. Order of Congress sessions held in Kolkata Year | President | Location | Special Achievements --- | --- | --- | --- Second | 1886 | Dadabhai Naoroji | Kolkata | Separation of judiciary and executive. 6th | 1890 | Ferozeshah Mehta | Kolkata | Ban on participation of government officials in Congress. 12th | 1896 | Rahimtulla Sayani | Kolkata | 'Vande Mataram' national song sung for the first time. 17th | 1901 | Dinshaw Edulji | Kolkata | Ban on exploitation of tea garden workers. 22nd | 1906 | Dadabhai Naoroji | Kolkata | Aim of 'Swaraj' national movement declared. 26th | 1911 | Bishan Narayan Dar | Kolkata | 'National Anthem' (Jana-Gana-Mana) sung for the first time. 32nd | 1917 | Annie Besant | Kolkata | First female President. 43rd | 1928 | Motilal Nehru | Kolkata | First youth Congress meeting (President Nehru). 47th | 1933 | Srimati Nellie Sengupta | Kolkata | First English female President. Note- In September 1920 AD, a special session of the Indian National Congress was held in Kolkata, which was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai. In this session, the proposal for a non-cooperation and boycott programme was presented.

questions.question_text: When did the Cambridge historiography school come into existence in relation to Indian history?
questions.explanation: In relation to Indian history, the Cambridge historiography school came into existence in the 1970s

questions.question_text: In which region did the Tebhaga movement arise?
questions.explanation: Among the peasant movements, the 1946 AD Tebhaga movement of Bengal was the most militant movement in which the farmers started a struggle to reduce the rent to one-third according to the recommendation of the Floud Commission. The main centers of the Tebhaga movement were Dinajpur, Rangpur, Jalpaiguri, Khulna, Sunderbans, and Midnapore of Bengal

questions.question_text: On which date did the British Emperor sign the ‘Indian Independence Act’?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act 1947 is the legislation passed by the Parliament of England according to which British-ruled India was divided into 2 parts, India and Pakistan. This Act was accepted in the British Parliament on 18 July 1947 and the partition of India happened on 15 August 1947

questions.question_text: At the time of India's independence, the President of the Indian National Congress was:
questions.explanation: J.B. Kripalani was a veteran of India's freedom struggle and a Gandhian politician. He is affectionately called Acharya Kripalani. When India got independence in 1947, he was the President of the Congress. Kripalani played a key role in the formation of the Janata government in 1977

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Vinoba Bhave?

options.A: He was a leader of the Sarvodaya movement
options.C: He received the Ramon Magsaysay award
options.D: He was the founder of the Satyagraha magazine

questions.explanation: Satyagraha magazine was edited by Gandhiji, whereas Vinoba Bhave joined the Sarvodaya (all-round development) movement in Telangana in 1950 and became famous in 1951 from the Bhoodan movement. Due to his public reform movement, he was also honoured with the Ramon Magsaysay award in 1958

questions.question_text: Who was made the Rajpramukh of Matsya Sangha in 1948?
questions.explanation: On 17 March 1948 AD, Matsya Sangha was formed by merging four princely states - Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, and Karauli, whose Rajpramukh was made Maharaja Udaybhan Singh of Dholpur. The capital of this union was Alwar. Shobha Ram Kumawat was appointed the Prime Minister of Matsya Sangha. The naming of Matsya Sangha was done on the advice of K.M. Munshi

questions.question_text: Who gave one hundred acres of land in donation to Vinoba Bhave in 1951, which inspired Bhave to start the ‘‘Bhoodan Movement’’?
questions.explanation: On 18 April 1951, from Pochampally village located in the Telangana region, Vedire Ramachandra Reddy donated one hundred acres of land to Vinoba Bhave. Inspired by this, he started the ‘Bhoodan Movement’, which was a voluntary land reform movement. Vinoba's attempt was that land redistribution should not happen just through government laws, but through a movement, it should be successfully attempted. In the fifth decade of the 20th century, to make the Bhoodan movement successful, Vinoba put into practice the creative works and ideas like trusteeship while following Gandhian thoughts. He founded the Sarvodaya Samaj. This was an all-India association of creative workers. Its objective was to bring social change in the country through non-violent means

questions.question_text: Below are two statements given, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : Despite its name, the Hindu Code Bill was also to be applied to Sikhs, Buddhists, and Jains, along with Hindu castes and sects. Reason (R) : After independence, among the supporters of the uniform civil code were Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Which of the following is correct in the context of these statements? Codes: law minister Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The Hindu Code Bill was created to provide rights to women. Under this, the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 was passed. It was applicable to Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, and Jains, all. Assertion and Reason both are correct but Assertion and Reason are not explaining each other

questions.question_text: In the early years of the sixties decade of the nineteenth century, which province took the step to build irrigation canals on the basis of providing fixed profit on investment to private companies?
questions.explanation: In the early years of the sixties decade of the nineteenth century, the Madras province took the step to build irrigation canals on the basis of providing fixed profit on investment to private companies

questions.question_text: Who among the following is not a member of the Subaltern Studies project in India?
questions.explanation: Ramachandra Guha was not a member of the Subaltern Studies project in India, rather he was a writer, whereas Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, Dipesh Chakrabarty, Shahid Amin were associated with this

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not the objective of Non-alignment established by Jawaharlal Nehru?

options.A: It was related to the Cold War and the military alliances connected with it.
options.B: It was against the evil forces of colonialism, racism and oppression.
options.C: It was in the direction of promoting world peace and disarmament.
options.D: Its objective was the creation of a third force to face the U.S.A. and the U.S.S.R.

questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– The policy of Non-alignment is India's contribution to international relations. After taking over the charge of interim Prime Minister, the foreign policy that Jawaharlal Nehru announced developed later as the concept of Non-alignment. This concept is considered directly related to the ‘Cold War’. The objective of Non-alignment established by Jawaharlal Nehru was related to the Cold War and the military alliance connected with it, against the evil forces of colonialism, racism, and oppression, and it was in the direction of promoting world peace and disarmament.

questions.question_text: In the context of the reorganization of the United Rajasthan state, which princely ruler among the following was made the Maharajpramukh for his entire life?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Nov. 2017 Explanation– On 3 March 1948, a proposal was placed for the formation of a union of United Rajasthan by merging the princely states of Kota, Bundi, Alwar, Tonk, Dungarpur, Banswara, Pratapgarh, Kishangarh, and Shahpura. Under the policy of the princely department, Udaipur (Mewar) had the right to maintain its independent identity. Therefore, a decision was taken on the United Rajasthan state without Udaipur. Later, due to political changes and public opposition, the Maharana of Udaipur expressed his desire to join the Union. In return for this, he was made Maharajpramukh for life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the States Reorganization Commission?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-II Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– On 22 December, 1953, a `States Reorganization Commission' was established. Justice Saiyid Fazl Ali was made the Chairman of this Commission and Pt. Hriday Nath Kunzru and Sardar K.M. Panikkar were chosen as its members. Thus, it is clear that Shashipada Banerjee was not its member.

questions.question_text: Who among the following described the re-distribution of provinces on a linguistic basis as akin to the 'suicide of nationalism'?
questions.explanation: UGC NET-III Paper Jan. 2017 Explanation– Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel described the re-distribution of provinces on a linguistic basis as akin to the 'suicide of nationalism'. The first state to be formed on the basis of language was Andhra State.

questions.question_text: When was the States Reorganization Commission established by Prime Minister Nehru?
questions.explanation: – States Reorganization Commission - Pt. Nehru established this commission in August, 1953, whose members were made Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar and Hriday Nath Kunzru. This commission gave its report in 1955, in which it was said that while giving due importance to administrative and economic aspects, more emphasis should be given on a linguistic basis

questions.question_text: The responsibility to identify the line dividing India and Pakistan in 1947 was given to which commission?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2012) Explanation – The responsibility to identify the line dividing India and Pakistan in 1947 was given to the Radcliffe Commission.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the pressing problem that India had to face immediately after the attainment of independence?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2013) Explanation─ After 15 August, 1947 AD, violence erupted on both sides of the border. It is difficult to say how this started. Probably, it started from Kolkata which was the result of Direct Action on August 1946 AD. Sikhs blamed Muslims and Muslims blamed Sikhs and Hindus. On 8 April, 1950 AD, a treaty took place between the Prime Ministers of India and Pakistan to solve the question of the protection of minorities, which is known as the Nehru-Liaquat Pact. For the problem of rehabilitation of 60 lakh refugees who came from Pakistan, a department of rehabilitation was constituted.

questions.question_text: Which princely state was the one to sign the ‘Instrument of Accession’ for merger into the Indian Union?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Mountbatten had prepared two types of documents for the merger or accession of princely states– (a) Instrument of Accession – This was a type of accession document after signing which the princely state would become included in the Indian Union. First of all, Maharaja Sadul Singh of Bikaner signed the accession document on 7 August 1947. (b) Standstill Agreement – This was in a way an agreement for the status quo.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not kept by the preparatory committee for the NAM (Non-Aligned Movement) for the member countries?

options.B: Not to be a member of multilateral alliances
options.D: If they accept military bases, it does not mean they are for superpower conflict.

questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper June. 2015) Explanation– Five features were determined for the NON-ALIGN MOVEMENT (NAM) – (i) Independent foreign policy (ii) Opposition to colonialism (iii) Not to be a member of a military alliance (iv) Not having military alliance with a superpower (v) Not giving permission to any superpower to make military bases in their territory.

questions.question_text: Which of the big states expressed their desire to remain independent in June 1947?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- II Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation─ Among the given options, in June 1947, states named Travancore and Bhopal expressed their desire to remain independent. At the time of attaining independence, there were about 562 princely states in India. Among the important princely states, four states – Hyderabad, Jammu and Kashmir, Bhopal, and Travancore showed reluctance towards merger into India. Out of these, the merger of Bhopal happened in the end.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of princely states first established universities in their state?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper Dec. 2015) Explanation – Mysore University was established on 27 July, 1916 by the Mysore King Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV. This was the sixth university of the then India and the first university of Karnataka, whereas Osmania University in Andhra Pradesh was established in 1918-19 by the Nizam of Hyderabad Mir Osman Ali Khan.

questions.question_text: In which period was the fight between India and China fought?
questions.explanation: TGT History, 2004 (Cancelled) Explanation – India developed the forward policy-1960. Under which instructions were given to occupy the border regions and build outposts. India built more outposts near the McMahon line and in its Aksai Chin area. Which China publicized wrongly all over the world as India occupying Tibet and attacked India on 20 October, 1962 AD.

questions.question_text: When did the first general election take place in India?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2005, 2002 Explanation– The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January, 1950 and with this, the democratic process started. The first general election in India took place in 1951 AD. The process of the first election ran from 25 October, 1951 to 21 February, 1952. For the first time in the country, the Lok Sabha was formed in 1952.

questions.question_text: On which date did the Nizam of Hyderabad sign the standstill agreement with the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- On 29 November, 1947, Hyderabad signed a temporary agreement named ‘Standstill Treaty’ with the Indian Union for one year so that the situation before 15 August 1947 remained maintained, but the Nizam did not follow the agreement. On 13 September 1948, the Indian army entered Hyderabad state and captured it and this action is known as Operation Polo.

questions.question_text: General Niazi surrendered before the Mukti Bahini:
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- On 16 December, 1971, in a military ceremony in Dhaka, the Pakistani General Niazi surrendered before India's Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora. In 1970-71, the autonomy movement of Bangladesh started under the leadership of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. The people of Bangladesh were with Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. On 16 December 1971, the rise of independent Bangladesh took place.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the commission appointed by the Government of India in 1954 to investigate the question of reorganization of the states of the Indian Union?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- After independence, the voice for reorganization of states on the basis of language started rising, after which the Government of India constituted a commission whose Chairman was Fazl Ali and Pt. Hriday Nath Kunzru and Sardar K. M. Panikkar were chosen as its members. Andhra Pradesh became the first state on a linguistic basis. On the basis of state reorganization, 14 states and 5 union territories were formed in India.

questions.question_text: Who declared East Pakistan by the new name of an independent republic ‘Bangladesh’?
questions.explanation: Asharam Paddhati Lect. Exam. 2009 Explanation- In 1970-71, the autonomy movement of Bangladesh started under the leadership of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. The people of East Pakistan, i.e., Bangladesh, were completely with Mujibur Rahman. On 16 December 1971, independent Bangladesh emerged.

questions.question_text: Who led the struggle of the Dogras of Jammu between 1950-52?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2012 Explanation- Karan Singh led the struggle of the Dogras of Jammu between the years 1950-52 AD. He was the son of Maharaja Hari Singh.

questions.question_text: When did Junagadh join India?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– In September, 1947 AD, the Junagadh state announced its merger with Pakistan, whereas the majority of the state's population was Hindu, who wanted to remain in India. The citizens of the state opposed it and established a ‘Swatantra Asthayi Hukumat’. Forced, the Nawab fled to Pakistan, subsequently, the Diwan of Junagadh Shah Nawaz Bhutto (father of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto) wrote a letter related to the merger of Junagadh into India to the Government of India on 8 November, 1947. Mr. Bhutto's request was accepted and on 9 November, 1947 AD, India took the administration of Junagadh into its own hands.

questions.question_text: Who among the following took the responsibility of military governor in Hyderabad in the year 1948?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– Under the plan of merger of Hyderabad into India, the commander of the Hyderabad state force Major General El Edroos surrendered before the Indian Army commander Major General J.N. Chaudhuri. After keeping Hyderabad under the control of Major General J.N. Chaudhuri, he was appointed the military governor there.

questions.question_text: The first conference of Non-Aligned countries was held in the year 1961 AD at which place?
questions.explanation: UPPSC GDC 2021 UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008, 2002 Explanation- The Non-aligned movement was established with the support of Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, Egypt's Colonel Nasser, and Yugoslavia's Marshal Tito. In September 1961 AD, the first conference of Non-Aligned countries was held in the then capital of Yugoslavia, Belgrade.

questions.question_text: In which year did India and China announce the principles of Panchsheel?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2002 DSSSB PGT 2019 Explanation- India and China announced the principles of Panchsheel in 1954 AD. At that time, India's Prime Minister was Jawaharlal Nehru and China's Prime Minister was Zhou Enlai. Under this, some basic principles were established to make the mutual relations of various states friendly, which are as follows: (i) Respect for each other's border and sovereignty, (ii) Non-aggression (iii) Non-interference in each other's internal affairs, (iv) Equality and mutual benefit, (v) Peaceful coexistence.

questions.question_text: With what was the Bandung conference related?
questions.explanation: Higher Edu. Exam. (Med. History) 2014 Explanation– The Bandung conference was organized in Indonesia in 1955. From 18–24 April 1955, a meeting of Asian and African countries was organized in Bandung (Indonesia) by Indonesia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, India, and Pakistan, this itself was called the Bandung conference. From this conference, the Non-aligned movement was born.

questions.question_text: Where was the declaration of Panchsheel made by India and China?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2003 Explanation- India and China made the declaration of the principle of Panchsheel in 1954 AD in New Delhi. The Panchsheel principle agreed upon between Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Chinese Prime Minister Zhou Enlai was a principle of friendship and it was made for the establishment of international peace. On the occasion of the Panchsheel principle, some basic principles were established to make the mutual relations of various states friendly, which are as follows- (i) Respect for each other's border and sovereignty, (ii) Non-aggression, (iii) Non-interference in each other's internal affairs, (iv) Equality and mutual benefit and, (v) Peaceful coexistence. The above principles were made a part of India's foreign policy by India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not included in the principles of Panchsheel propagated by Jawaharlal Nehru?

options.D: Interference in each other's internal affairs

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- India's first Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, along with Chinese Prime Minister Zhou Enlai, had an agreement between the two countries regarding Tibet in 1954 AD, which is known as the Panchsheel Agreement. There were five principles of Panchsheel. (i) Mutual respect for the territorial integrity and sovereignty of each other (ii) Non-aggression, (iii) Peaceful coexistence, (iv) Establishment of friendly relations on the basis of equality and mutual benefit, (v) Non-interference in each other's internal affairs. It is clear that interference in each other's internal affairs was not a principle of Panchsheel.

questions.question_text: In which date did the India-China war start in 1962 AD?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : The act of aggression by China against India started in September, 1962. On 8 September, 1962, the Chinese army crossed the McMahon line in Arunachal Pradesh (called NEFA at that time) and entered India and took some of our areas under its control. The Chinese army made a fierce attack on 20 October, 1962, in both NEFA and Ladakh regions. Within 24 hours, China captured two of our important posts in NEFA. At that time, India's Defence Minister was Krishna Menon.

questions.question_text: Where was the principle of ‘Panchsheel’ propagated?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : India's peace-loving nature is reflected by the Panchsheel principles, it seems appropriate to call these the foundation of India's foreign policy. These are five principles: (a) Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty (b) Non-aggression (c) Non-interference in each other's internal affairs (d) Mutual benefit and equality (5) Peaceful existence The propagation of the above five principles was first done on 28 June, 1954, in a joint statement by the Prime Minister of the Chinese Republic Zhou Enlai and India's Prime Minister Pandit Nehru after detailed discussion of three days. In April, 1955, at the Bandung conference held in Indonesia, these principles were again accepted by 29 African-Asian countries. On 14 December, 1959, the United Nations General Assembly of 82 nations accepted the proposal presented by India.

questions.question_text: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of the Communist Party?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : As the first elected Chief Minister of the Communist Party, E.M.S. Namboodiripad took oath in Kerala state in 1957. Jyoti Basu became the Chief Minister of West Bengal in 1977.

questions.question_text: Which of the following called the Indian Independence Bill as 'a peace settlement without war' in the British parliamentary debate?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation- On the basis of the Mountbatten Plan, the Indian Independence Bill was presented in the British Parliament on 4 July, 1947 AD. It received approval on 18 July, 1947 AD. At the time when the Indian Independence Bill was being debated in the British Parliament, ‘Herbert Samuel’ who was a member of the Liberal Party, called this bill as ‘a peace settlement without war’. According to this settlement, it was decided to divide the country into two dominions India and Pakistan on 15 August, 1947 AD.

questions.question_text: Who among the following accused was hanged in the conspiracy of Mahatma Gandhi's assassination?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 Explanation - Mahatma Gandhi's assassination was done by Nathuram Godse on 30 January, 1948. In the crime of assassination, along with Nathuram Godse, Narayan Apte was also given the death penalty and six people including Madanlal Pahwa, Digambar Badge, and Vishnu Karkare were given life imprisonment.

questions.question_text: was related to
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2008 Explanation─ In 1954, Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru visited China and signed on the Panchsheel principles of coexistence, which were as follows─ 1. Respect each other's areas and sovereignty 2. Adopt a policy of non-aggression 3. Will not interfere in each other's internal affairs 4. Equality and mutual benefit 5. Follow the policy of peaceful coexistence.
examinations: According to the 1954 treaty, the principle of Panchsheel

questions.question_text: In 1957, when Nehru was Prime Minister, in the general elections held, except one, all states received a solid majority for the Congress. That exception was :
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation - In 1957, in Kerala state, the Congress did not get a solid majority. Here, under the leadership of Namboodiripad, the CPI (M) government was formed for the first time in the world in a democratic way.

questions.question_text: The Indian National Congress adopted the goal of socialist pattern in which of the following sessions?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2008 Explanation- In the 1955 Avadi session (President - U.N. Dhebar), the Indian National Congress gave approval to the proposal related to accepting the ideal of a socialist society. In the Avadi proposal, it declared- `Planning should be done in such a way that society can be established according to the socialist pattern’, where basic means of production are under social ownership and control, production can be gradually increased and national wealth can be distributed on the basis of equality.

questions.question_text: On the basis of language, which state was formed first?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ The first state formed on a linguistic basis was Andhra Pradesh. In 1952, freedom fighter Potti Sriramulu started a hunger strike on the demand for a separate Andhra state on a linguistic basis and after 58 days, he died, as a result of which riots, demonstrations, violence, and strikes continued. Ultimately the government yielded. In October 1953 AD, ultimately Andhra Pradesh came into existence. Along with this, Tamil Nadu was formed as a Tamil-speaking state.

questions.question_text: The name of the India-Pakistan border is-
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ With the acceptance of Congress and Muslim League, the British government published the plan for India's partition on 3 June, 1947 AD. Both Congress and Muslim League accepted the Mountbatten Plan for the country's partition and preparation for country partition started. In Bengal and Punjab, the work of district partition and border determination was entrusted under a commission which was presided over by Radcliffe. The border line between India and Pakistan was named after Radcliffe, which was determined on 15 August, 1947.

questions.question_text: Who was the chairman of the ‘Flag Committee’?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ After the acceptance of the Objectives Resolution on 22 January, 1947 AD, the Constituent Assembly appointed several committees. In this, the major committees and their chairmen are as follows─ Committee | Chairman (a) Steering Committee – Dr. Rajendra Prasad (b) Union Constitution Committee – Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru (c) Provincial Constitution Committee – Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (d) Drafting Committee – Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar (e) Flag Committee – J.B. Kripalani/Dr. Rajendra Prasad (f) Union Powers Committee – Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru In this way, the Indian National Flag was made of three colors, hence it is called Tricolor. The ratio of length to width of the flag is 3:2. In its middle, there is a wheel with twenty-four spokes. The Constituent Assembly of India adopted the draft of the National Flag on 22 July, 1947. The proper use and display of the flag is regulated by a code. Special– The Constitution Drafting Council constituted the Ad-hoc Flag Committee on 23 June, 1947 AD whose chairman was Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The Flag Committee formed in the Karachi session of Congress on 2 April, 1931 whose chairman was Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Note– At the time of the question, the commission had considered (b) as the answer to this question.

questions.question_text: Father of the Nation is no more’’?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ On 30 January, 1948 AD, in the evening when Mahatma Gandhi was going to offer prayers at Birla Temple, at that same time, Nathuram Godse, a member of an extremist Hindu organization, killed Gandhi Ji by shooting him with a pistol. Chanting Ram-Ram, Gandhiji fell on the ground and became a martyr. Announcing this assassination, Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru said ‘‘The Father of the Nation is no more’’. Grief spread across the whole country due to this brutal assassination. His samadhi was built at Rajghat on the Yamuna river in Delhi. The assassin Nathuram was given the death penalty.
examinations: On 30 January 1948, who said on the radio, ‘‘The

questions.question_text: In which year was the National Development Council formed?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2009 Explanation─ The National Development Council was formed on 6 August, 1952 AD. Like the Planning Commission, this is also a non-statutory body, which was formed to create an atmosphere of cooperation between the states and the Planning Commission for economic planning. The Prime Minister is its Chairman and the Secretary of the Planning Commission is its Secretary. Chief Ministers of states and members of the Union Council of Ministers, administrators of union territories, and all members of the Planning Commission are members of this body. Its main task is to study the plan prepared by the Planning Commission and give it final form after discussion. The National Development Council is considered the best example of cooperative federalism. K. Santhanam has called the National Development Council the highest council of ministers.

questions.question_text: ‘‘We should follow him...... Subhas was a great patriot. He sacrificed his life for the country. There was no utility for him of narrow-mindedness and caste-discrimination. He treated everyone equally.’’
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation- On the occasion of Subhas Chandra Bose's birthday on 23 January, 1948 AD, the Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi gave the above statement.
examinations: On 23 January, 1948, who said for Subhas Chandra Bose,

questions.question_text: How many countries participated in the first summit conference of Non-Aligned countries held in Belgrade?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – The first summit conference of Non-Aligned countries was organized in Belgrade in September 1961. On the suggestion of President Tito, 20 countries were invited to this conference in which 25 countries participated by sending their representatives and three countries participated by sending their observers.

questions.question_text: Under which Five-Year Plan was the community development program started?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation – On 1 April, 1951, the First Five-Year Plan was started, in which priority was given to the development of agriculture. Along with this, the community development program and national development plan were started in 1952 AD. In this Five-Year Plan, multi-purpose river valley projects like Bhakra Nangal, Damodar Valley, and Hirakud were launched.

questions.question_text: From which date was the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act implemented:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act was implemented on 1 July, 1952. Through this, progress has come in land reforms and zamindari abolition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.B: D.R. Mankekar : Witness to an Era
options.D: B.M. Kaul : The Guilty Men of 1962

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation – The book named India's China War was written by Neville Maxwell. The remaining options are not correctly matched. The Guilty Men of 1962 book was written by D.R. Mankekar. The Unsettled Story is a novel written by Monica Ali.

questions.question_text: Which political party first broke the monopoly of the non-Congress government in a state in India?
questions.explanation: The Communist Party of India emerged as the largest opposition party after the 1957 Lok Sabha elections. After the partition of the party in 1964, the CPI (M) was formed. The Communist Party of India formed a government in Kerala with the Congress between 1970-77. In this way, CPI broke the monopoly of the Congress first. Whereas, CPI (M) party formed the government in West Bengal in 1977 after winning a majority in the assembly elections there

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not correct regarding the first summit conference of the Non-Aligned movement?

options.A: This conference was held in Cairo
options.B: Jawaharlal Nehru and Sukarno participated in it.
options.C: At the time of the summit, the Cold War was at its peak.
options.D: Discussion on the consolidation of world peace and security took place in it.

questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 Explanation– The first non-aligned summit conference was organized in the capital of Yugoslavia, Belgrade, in 1961. In this summit conference, internal contradictions of the non-aligned fraternity came to the surface. A heated discussion took place between Nehru and Sukarno regarding the political proposal which was to be passed in the conference. At the time of this summit conference, the Cold War was at its peak. On India's initiative, the `United for Peace' proposal was passed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT among the principles accepted in the Bandung Conference (first major Non-Aligned Movement) summit?

options.D: Non-interference in each other's internal affairs

questions.explanation: In 1955, Indonesian President Ahmed Sukarno organized a conference of Asian and African countries in Bandung from 17 to 24 April. 29 countries participated in the conference. The prominent leaders included in this were Jawaharlal Nehru, Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai, and Egyptian Premier (later President) Gamal Abdel Nasser. Many countries were also included in this conference, such as Pakistan, Iran, Iraq, Philippines, Turkey, and Thailand, who were members of military alliances formed under the aegis of the United States, yet the declaration accepted by consensus in this clearly advocated those ideas which contained certain basic principles of non-alignment. The Bandung Conference was an important milestone in the history of the Non-Aligned Movement. Along with this, it was the largest conference of Asian and African countries, which was home to half the world's population Special Facts Panchsheel Agreement Pt. Nehru incorporated the Panchsheel principles into Indian foreign policy from Buddhist philosophy. Panchsheel includes a combination of five principles- 1. Respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty. 2. Mutual non-aggression. 3. Equality and mutual benefit. 4. Non-interference in each other's internal affairs. 5. Peaceful co-existence.

questions.question_text: By the Second Amendment Act of 1952, which article of the Constitution was amended?
questions.explanation: By the Second Amendment Act of 1952, the representation of states in Parliament was determined in Article 81(1) (b) of the Constitution so that the number of members of Parliament should not exceed 500. One Lok Sabha member can represent 7,50,000 individuals

questions.question_text: Who formulated the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.explanation: The meaning of the Doctrine of Lapse is that in relation to any state, if there is no natural heir, then the Company will decide regarding the heir there and he will be recognized by the Company. Lord Dalhousie, as the Governor-General of India from 1848-56, used the annexation policy as the Doctrine of Lapse to annex most Indian states for the expansion of the Company's empire

questions.question_text: Who was the founder of the French East India Company among the following?
questions.explanation: During the time of French Emperor Louis XIV, as a result of the efforts of his famous minister Colbert, a French trading company 'Compagnie des Indes Orientales' was established in 1664 AD. The French company was formed by the government and all its expenses were borne by the government itself

questions.question_text: Who was the first Portuguese Governor in India?
questions.explanation: Francisco de Almeida was made the first Portuguese Governor of India (1505-1509). He was instructed by the government to build such Portuguese forts in India whose goal was not security but to establish Portuguese control over trade in the Indian Ocean. Thus, the main objective of Almeida was to trade peacefully. This policy of his was called "Blue Water Policy" or "Policy of Peaceful Waters"

questions.question_text: The Governor-General who started regional languages in the courts –
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2011 Explanation – Governor-General Lord William Bentinck (1828-1835) started regional languages in the courts. Other important works of his reign are as follows – abolition of Sati system (1829), abolition of Thuggee system (1830), Charter Act of 1833, first Governor-General of India, creation of the post of Divisional Commissioner, etc.

questions.question_text: What is the correct chronological order of the following Governor-Generals who ruled over India? 1. Lord Mayo 2. Lord Lytton 3. Sir John Lawrence 4. Lord Northbrook Select the correct answer from the following code: Code:
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History Spl., 2004 Explanation- Sir John Lawrence 1864-69 AD, Lord Mayo- 1869-72 AD, Lord Northbrook - 1872-76 AD, Lord Lytton - 1876-80 AD.

questions.question_text: In whose time among the following Viceroys of India were the Indian Penal Code, Civil Procedure Code, and Criminal Procedure Code passed?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2004 Explanation- In 1861, the Indian Council Act, Penal and Civil Procedure Codes, and the Indian High Courts Act were passed. The number of members of the Central Legislative Council was fixed at a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 10. It was necessary for 10 of these to be non-official. In the provinces, the number of non-official and total members of the Legislative Council was also increased. This number was fixed at 15 in Uttar Pradesh and 20 in Bombay and Madras. Till that time, all members of the Legislative Councils were appointed by the Governor-General and Governors because the election system had not started in India, but through this act, provisions were made for the appointment of these members on the advice of some influential institutions like Calcutta Chamber of Commerce, or non-official members of the Provincial Legislative Council at the center. Lord Canning's time was from 1856-62.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2006 Explanation : Under the Act of 1858, although no major changes were made in the administration of India, but now the Governor-General, who was the representative of the Crown, began to be called 'Viceroy'. Although there was no constitutional provision for this title, and the English Parliament never used this title, but the common people used it often, and after a long time, when their residence was built, it was named 'Viceregal Lodge'. The Viceroy's salary was fixed at 2.5 lakh rupees per year. According to this Act, Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Viceroys decided to play the game of ‘divide and rule’?
questions.explanation: Lord Minto was the Viceroy of India. He also served as the 8th Governor-General of Canada before becoming Viceroy. He was held responsible for starting the ‘divide and rule’ policy in India through the Morley-Minto reforms. He attempted to divide Indians on a communal basis to weaken the national movement

questions.question_text: Which of the following Viceroys revoked the partition of Bengal to satisfy Indian public opinion?
questions.explanation: Lord Hardinge II remained the Viceroy of India from 1910 AD to 1916 AD. After Lord Minto II, he was sent as the Viceroy of India. The most important work of his time was the arrival of British King George V in India (12 December 1911), the organization of a grand durbar in Delhi, and the announcement of the revocation of the partition of Bengal in 1911. During Hardinge's tenure, the First World War started on 28 July 1914. During his time in 1912, the British capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi and an attempt on Lord Hardinge's life took place

questions.question_text: Who among the following were supporters of the freedom of the Indian press?
questions.explanation: Among the supporters of the freedom of the Indian press, the names of Lord Hastings, Charles Metcalfe, and Lord Ripon are notable, whereas the Governor-Generals who discouraged or imposed restrictions on the freedom of the Indian press are as follows – Lord Wellesley, Lord Lytton, Lord Adam. In 1823, John Adam imposed complete restrictions on the Indian press. Wellesley imposed censorship on all newspapers in 1799, and Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act in 1878

questions.question_text: Which British ruler got Fort William built in Calcutta?
questions.explanation: In 1698, the Mughal Subahdar of Bengal granted permission to the British to take the villages of Sutanuti and Gobindapur in addition to Calcutta by paying land revenue, and for the security of their trade, a factory was built, which was named Fort William after the British ruler William III. After its establishment, the security system started. Its first President was Charles Eyre

questions.question_text: Which Governor-General first adopted the policy of ‘‘Masterly Inactivity’’?
questions.explanation: Governor-General Lawrence first adopted the policy of Masterly Inactivity. In the First Afghan War, the British suffered a severe defeat and had to endure deep humiliation. This had an immediate effect on British policy makers and they abandoned the forward policy and adopted the policy of inactivity. Lawrence adopted his policy firmly and remained neutral without taking anyone's side in the succession war. However, as soon as Sher Ali crushed all his rivals and became the ruler of Afghanistan, Lord Lawrence granted him recognition

questions.question_text: Who started the policy of financial decentralization?
questions.explanation: Lord Mayo came to India as Governor-General or Viceroy in 1868 AD. His tenure lasted from 1868 to 1872 AD, during which he did many reform works. He started the policy of financial decentralization in the existing financial reform policy in India and increased the income tax rate from 1% to 2.5%. He established a separate Department of Agriculture and Indian Statistical Survey Department. For the first time, a census was conducted in India (1872). Mayo established Mayo College in Ajmer for the proper education of the sons of Indian kings

questions.question_text: Lord Mayo adopted the policy of
questions.explanation: Lord Mayo came to India as Governor-General/Viceroy in 1868 AD. His tenure lasted from 1868 to 1872 AD, during which he did many reform works 1- For the first time, a census was conducted in India (1872). 2- Mayo established Mayo College in Ajmer for the proper education of the sons of Indian kings. In 1870 AD, through the Mayo Resolution, the beginning of local self-government and financial decentralization in India was made.

questions.question_text: Under whose Viceroyalty was the Ilbert Bill introduced?
questions.explanation: The Ilbert Bill was introduced on 9 February 1883 AD to implement a single criminal law in the whole country and High Courts were established in every province. Before this, two laws were running in the country – English law was prevalent in English presidency cities, and Mughal-era laws were prevalent at the rural level. In this, there was a rule that in presidency cities, Indian criminal judges or magistrates and sessions judges could hear cases of both Indians and Europeans, but at the rural level, only British judges could hear cases of European defendants. In 1872 AD, three Indians were appointed to the Civil Service, one was Shri Bihari Lal Gupta. Thus, the objective of the Ilbert Bill was to give Indian judges the right to hear European criminal cases. This angered the Europeans, due to which Lord Ripon amended it on 26 January 1884. Now, after the amendment, if they came before an Indian magistrate or sessions judge, those people could hear the cases with the demand of a jury of 12 people, of which 7 should be European or American. Due to the pressure, Lord Ripon had to resign before his tenure

questions.question_text: Who started the work of census?
questions.explanation: The first census happened in 1872 during the time of Lord Mayo. After 1881, the decennial census started, which was started by Lord Ripon.

questions.question_text: Who proposed the Communal Award?
questions.explanation: The first census happened in 1872 during the time of Lord Mayo, but after 1881, decennial census started, which was started by Lord Ripon. The 2021 census was the 16th census of the country and the 8th census of independent India. The subject (theme) of Census 2021 is "Public welfare through public participation". Whereas the subject (theme) of the 15th Census-2011 is "Our Census, Our Future" DSSSB PGT 2019 Ans. (c) : On 16 August 1932, British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald gave a decision for separate election regions for the upper class, lower class, Muslim, Buddhist, Sikh, Indian Christian, Anglo-Indian, Parsi, and Dalits in India, which is called Communal Award.

questions.question_text: Who started the changes in civil services?
questions.explanation: Governor-General Lord Cornwallis is considered the father of civil service or bureaucratic service in India. Civil service was called the steel frame. Wellesley established the Fort William College in Calcutta in 1800 AD for the training of civil services

questions.question_text: During whose reign was the capital of India shifted from Calcutta to Delhi?
questions.explanation: During the time of Lord Hardinge II, at the third Delhi Durbar organized in 1911, British King George V announced the shifting of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi on 12 December 1911, and in 1912, the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi

questions.question_text: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal in India?
questions.explanation: The first Governor-General of Bengal was Warren Hastings. Through the Regulating Act of 1773, the Governor of Bengal began to be called the Governor-General of the British territory (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras). In this way, the Governors of Madras and Bombay came under him. Warren Hastings, who was appointed to the post of Governor of Bengal, later became the Governor-General of Bengal

questions.question_text: Keep them in the correct order according to their rule in India: 1. Warren Hastings 2. Dalhousie 3. Wellesley 4. Cornwallis
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings (1772-85), Cornwallis (1786-93), Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) and Lord Dalhousie (1848-56)

questions.question_text: Match these: A. Lord Ripon 1. Subsidiary Alliance System B. Lord Canning 2. Doctrine of Lapse C. Lord Dalhousie 3. End of Company Rule D. Lord Wellesley 4. Local Self Government Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: A. Lord Ripon Local Self Government B. Lord Canning End of Company Rule C. Lord Dalhousie Doctrine of Lapse D. Lord Wellesley Subsidiary Alliance System

questions.question_text: Match List I with List II: I II Portuguese-Governor Achievements A. Francisco-de-Almeida 1. Encouraged his fellow countrymen to marry Indian women. B. Alfonso-de-Albuquerque 2. Created Blue-Water policy. C. Nino-de-Cunha D. Martin Alfonso de Souza 4. Brought famous Jesuit saint Francis Xavier with him to India. Code: A B C D 3. Shifted the Portuguese capital from Cochin to Goa.
questions.explanation: A. Francisco-de-Almeida Created Blue-Water policy. B. Alfonso-de-Albuquerque Encouraged his fellow countrymen to marry Indian women. C. Nino-de-Cunha Shifted the Portuguese capital from Cochin to Goa. D. Martin Alfonso de Souza Brought famous Jesuit saint Francis Xavier with him to India.

questions.question_text: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.B: Northbrook – Prince of Edinburgh's visit to India

questions.explanation: During the time of Viceroy Lord Lytton (1876-1880), the Delhi Durbar was organized on 1 January 1877, in which Queen Victoria was honored with the title of Kaiser-e-Hind. Unfortunately, this event was organized when India was suffering from a severe famine

questions.question_text: About which Governor-General has it been said that he is a motor driver who spends all his time polishing the various parts of the machine, but he does not drive the motor because he does not know where he has to go?
questions.explanation: About Governor-General Curzon, it has been said that he is a motor driver who spends all his time polishing the various parts of the machine, but he does not drive the motor because he does not know where he has to go

questions.question_text: Which of the following is related to the suppression of Thuggee?
questions.explanation: During the 19th century, there was terror of Thugs in Bundelkhand to Vidarbha and some parts of Northern India. Governor-General Lord William Bentinck of India, together with Colonel Sleeman, ended the Thuggee system in 1830 AD. Sher Khan, Chhote, etc., were leaders of the Thugs

questions.question_text: In which year was Lord Mayo killed?
questions.explanation: Lord Mayo was killed by a person named Sher Afghan in the Andaman on 8 February 1872 AD. Lord Mayo conducted an experimental census in India in 1872 AD. The Agriculture Department and Mayo College in Ajmer were established by Mayo in 1872

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy started giving the title of 'Rai Bahadur' to Indians among the following?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton started honoring Hindus and Christians with the title of Rai Bahadur. Rai means king and Bahadur means more respectable. Just as Muslims were given the title of Khan Bahadur and Sikhs were given the title of Sardar Bahadur. Similarly, Hindus and Christians were given the title of Rai Bahadur

questions.question_text: Which of the following Governor-General/Viceroy was a scholar of history and archaeology?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon was a scholar of history and archaeology. He fixed 56 thousand pounds for the repair of ancient monuments in India. In 1902, he formed the University Commission under the chairmanship of Sir Thomas Raleigh. The establishment of CID in the Police Department in 1903 and the partition of Bengal in 1905 were his major works

questions.question_text: In which year was the Post Office Act passed?
questions.explanation: During the tenure of Lord Dalhousie, the Post Office Act was passed in 1854 AD, as a result of which the Post Department was established on 1 October 1854. At that time, 701 post offices which came under the East India Company were merged to establish the Post Department

questions.question_text: Which of the following Governor-Generals is known for police reforms?
questions.explanation: After Lord Elgin II, Lord Curzon came to India as Viceroy in 1899 AD. Lord Curzon formed a ‘Police Commission’ in 1902 AD under the chairmanship of Andrew Fraser for reforms in police administration. This commission considered the police administration to be completely inefficient, corrupt, and repressive. However, the Police Commission made arrangements for salary increases at all levels, training systems, establishment of provincial police, and establishment of a central intelligence department. During his tenure, the establishment of the University Commission under the chairmanship of Sir Thomas Raleigh (1902), and the formation of a Famine Commission under the chairmanship of Sir Anthony MacDonald (1899-90) were done

questions.question_text: Who established the Statutory Civil Service in India and when?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton (1876-1880) was called 'Owen Meredith' in the literary world due to his scholarship. The reform works done by him are as follows– A severe famine occurred in 1876-78. Therefore, he formed a Famine Commission in 1878 under the chairmanship of Richard Strachey. He imposed restrictions on newspapers published in Indian languages under the ‘Vernacular Press Act (1878)’. He made arrangements for a public examination for Indians and reduced the age for examination in civil service from 21 years to 19 years. Along with this, he passed the Cultivator Relief Act 1879 for the convenience of farmers. Lord Lytton presented the scheme of Statutory Civil Service in 1879, under which it was decided to appoint some high-born Indians to it

questions.question_text: Among the following, who is considered the main reformer of ‘‘Local Self-Government’’ in British times?
questions.explanation: Lord Ripon (1880-1884) was the most popular Viceroy of India. He took many reformist steps during his time, hence Florence Nightingale termed him ‘The Savior of India’. Major reforms done by him - abolition of Vernacular Press Act (1882), first Factory Act passed for improvement in the condition of laborers (1881), the start of the first real census (1881), government resolution regarding local self-government was passed. Under this, local boards were made in rural areas, districts, and sub-divisions, and a plan to make tehsil boards was formed. Municipalities were formed in cities and they were provided with freedom to work and means to obtain income

questions.question_text: Indian press was freed from restrictions in 1835 by–
questions.explanation: Due to the ‘Press Censorship Act’ in 1799 by Lord Wellesley and restrictions imposed on newspapers in 1823 by John Adam, Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Mirat-ul-Akhbar was closed. In 1830 AD, through the efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore, the publication of ‘Bangaduta’ began in the Bengali language. Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General who adopted a liberal attitude towards the freedom of the press. Ultimately, upon Charles Metcalfe (1835-36) becoming the Governor-General of India, the ‘Press Act’ was passed in 1835, by which the restrictions imposed on newspapers were removed. Hence, Charles Metcalfe is also known as the ‘Liberator of Newspapers’

questions.question_text: In which year was the first ‘Telegraph Line’ started between Calcutta and Agra?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie came to India as Governor-General in 1848 AD. His tenure was quite controversial because he accomplished many important tasks while expanding the British empire on the basis of war and Doctrine of Lapse. Based on the report of British Resident James Outram, Oudh was annexed (1856) by him, operation of the first railway between Bombay and Thane in 1853, the first ‘Telegraph Line’ between Calcutta and Agra was started in 1853 itself. During his time, the Public Works Department and the Department of Public Instruction (1854) were established for the first time

questions.question_text: Who among the following called Gandhi Ji's activities ‘Political Blackmail’?
questions.explanation: Lord Linlithgow remained the Viceroy of India from 1936-1943 AD. In the context of activities related to Gandhi Ji's Second World War and Quit India Movement, he called these activities ‘Political Blackmail’. It was during his time that the first elections were held in 1937

questions.question_text: Who among the following Governor-Generals/Viceroys showed deep interest in the upkeep of archaeological remains?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon was a scholar of history and archaeology. He passed the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904, in 1904 AD for the protection of ancient monuments and fixed 50 thousand pounds for the repair of ancient monuments in India. His other major works are – Irrigation Commission (1901), Police Commission (1902), University Commission (1902), etc

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy decentralized the colonial economic structure in India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mayo was the fourth Viceroy of India. He started the policy of decentralization of colonial economic structure in India and adopted the policy of non-interference in foreign policy. The first census of India (regular census was in Lord Ripon's time) happened during his time. In 1872 AD, he established the Agriculture Department. His assassination was done by an Afghan named Sher Khan

questions.question_text: Governor-General during whose tenure the income tax was started for the first time in India:
questions.explanation: Income tax was started for the first time in India during the tenure of Governor-General Lord Canning. For economic reforms in India, Lord Canning called British economist Lord Wilson to India. Wilson imposed income tax on annual income of more than 500 rupees in India and fixed 4% tax on exports and 10% on imports. The post of Comptroller General (1857 AD) was also created during the time of Lord Canning

questions.question_text: Which of the following steps was NOT taken by Lord Curzon?
questions.explanation: Vernacular Press Act was passed by Viceroy Lytton in 1878 AD. This Act imposed control over all newspapers published in Indian languages. However, this Act was not applied to newspapers published in English. This hated Act was revoked by Lord Ripon in 1882 AD

questions.question_text: By which Viceroy was the Congress banned?
questions.explanation: Returning from the Second Round Table Conference, Gandhi Ji wanted to meet Viceroy Willingdon. But Willingdon refused to meet, due to which Gandhi Ji started the Second Civil Disobedience Movement in January 1932 AD. At this time, Willingdon had banned the Congress. In the Second Civil Disobedience Movement, top leaders were arrested. Before becoming Viceroy, Lord Willingdon had participated in the Bombay session of the Indian National Congress in 1915 AD

questions.question_text: Lord Curzon passed the Ancient Indian Monuments Protection Act. The objective of this act was–

options.A: To preserve the symbols of pride in ancient India
options.C: To awaken national consciousness among people for the protection of national monuments
options.D: Contributed to the development of historical literature

questions.explanation: PGT History, 2000 Explanation – Lord Curzon passed the Ancient Indian Monuments Protection Act, the objective of which was - to awaken national consciousness among people for the protection of national monuments. This Ancient Indian Monuments Protection Act was passed in 1904 AD.

questions.question_text: Where is the tomb of Lord Cornwallis situated?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – The tomb of Lord Cornwallis is situated in Ghazipur. Cornwallis came to India as Governor-General of Bengal in 1786. He was the only Governor-General of British rule who died in India and was buried here.

questions.question_text: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of shifting the capital from Kolkata to Delhi?
questions.explanation: PGT History, 2013 Explanation – Lord Hardinge-II was the Viceroy during whose reign the capital of India was shifted from Kolkata to Delhi. Delhi became the capital in 1912 AD. Although the announcement of shifting the capital to Delhi was made in 1911 itself.

questions.question_text: In whose time were the executive and judicial powers of the servants of the British East India Company separated for the first time?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Lord Cornwallis, while giving final form to judicial reforms in 1793 AD, got a code prepared, which is called the Cornwallis Code. In this code, emphasizing the ‘principle of separation of power’, judicial and criminal powers were taken away from the District Collector and a class of District Judges was formed for district civil works and they were also given criminal work. In this way, through the Cornwallis Code, the judicial and executive works of the Company's officers were separated.

questions.question_text: Who among the following was responsible for the first telegraph service in India?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2001 Explanation- Lord Dalhousie gets the credit for starting the first telegraph service in India. He established the first Indian Telegraph Department in 1852. Arrangements for telegraph were made in about 4000 miles to connect Peshawar and Kolkata, Bombay and Madras, and other important parts of India. Telegraph arrangements were made from Rangoon to Mandalay in Burma. Based on the report of a commission, a Post Office Act was made in 1854 AD. For the postal system, a Director-General was appointed, post offices were established at various places, and a system was arranged in India to send letters through stamps from one place to another. All these works were done for the convenience of the administration and mainly for the strengthening of the British empire. However, in the end, all these benefited the public.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists- List-I List-II A. Lord Bentinck 1. Partition of Bengal B. Lord Dalhousie 2. Local Self Government C. Lord Ripon 3. Abolition of Sati system D. Lord Curzon 4. Doctrine of Lapse Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2007 TGT History 2005, 2009 Explanation - A. Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India. During his time, Rammohan Roy prepared a wide public base against the Sati system prevalent in India. As a result, Sati system was declared illegal under Section-17 in 1829. B. Lord Dalhousie remained the Governor-General of India from 1848-56 AD. Among his major works, the Doctrine of Lapse was prominent, under which he merged many independent states into the British empire. He also did many major reforms in which military reforms, communications, reforms in education, commercial reforms, etc., were important. C. Lord Ripon is called the father of local self-government. During his time, many major reforms took place, in which the first Factory Act, appointment of Hunter Commission in the context of education, Ilbert Bill, etc., remained prominent. D. Lord Curzon remained a highly controversial Governor-General due to his reactionary policy in India. The partition of Bengal in 1905 was a major event of his time. Among other works, police reform, establishment of CID, Irrigation Commission, Famine Commission, establishment of University Commission, etc., remained prominent.

questions.question_text: The ‘Ancient Monuments Preservation Act’ was passed during the tenure of which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2011 PGT History-2011 Explanation – The ‘Ancient Monuments Preservation Act’ was passed during the tenure of Governor-General Lord Curzon. He was a scholar of history and archaeology. He passed an Act in 1904 for the repair, restoration, and protection of ancient monuments of India and fixed 50,000 Rs for the repair of ancient monuments in India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is NOT matched?
questions.explanation: At the time of the Simon Commission, the Viceroy of India was Lord Irwin, not Sir Stafford Cripps The Simon Commission was formed under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon. The objective of this commission was to study the reforms of 1919.

questions.question_text: When did the ‘Partition of Bengal’ end?
questions.explanation: In 1905, India's Viceroy Lord Curzon had announced the partition of Bengal, which had started protests throughout India. This announcement of partition was revoked by Lord Hardinge II in 1911

questions.question_text: “Educating native people is our moral duty.” Whose statement is this?
questions.explanation: (UGC Net.- III Paper June. 2013) Explanation– Influenced by progressive ideas, Lord Mayo did the work of educating Indians. He considered educating people his moral duty and established Mayo College in Ajmer. It is notable that during his time the establishment of the Indian Statistical Survey took place and the first census happened in 1872 AD during his time.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the given code: List-I List-II A. Social Reforms 1. Curzon B. Partition of Bengal 2. Clive C. Dual Government in Bengal 3. Dalhousie D. Doctrine of Lapse 4. Bentinck Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2015 Explanation- Social reform works like abolition of Sati system, reforms in education were done by Lord William Bentinck. Partition of Bengal was during Curzon's time in 1905 and Clive implemented Dual Government in Bengal in 1765 and Lord Dalhousie is known for the Doctrine of Lapse in India.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Viceroys said emphatically that ‘loose-knit bureaucracy’ cannot run forever?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- After the reactionary Viceroy Lord Lytton, the gentle Viceroy Lord Ripon came to India in 1880. He was a good ruler. He provided facilities to Indians in various fields. He said emphatically that ‘loose-knit bureaucracy’ cannot run forever. In 1884, he resigned due to the Ilbert controversy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Governor-General, apart from English, was a scholar of Arabic, Persian, and Bengali language?
questions.explanation: UPPCS (Pre) Indian History, 2010 Explanation– Warren Hastings was born in 1732. He started his life as a clerk of the East India Company. He was a person of controversial personality. He had a lot of interest in literature. He gave protection to ancient learning and literature. He knew Arabic, Persian and could speak Bengali language. He wrote the introduction to the first translation of Gita by Charles Wilkins. Halhed published Sanskrit grammar in 1778. At his encouragement, Sir William Jones laid the foundation of the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784 so that the social and natural history, archaeology, art, science, and literature in Asia could be studied.

questions.question_text: In which year did Bengal Police first use the ‘Fingerprint’ system for detecting crime and for evidence?
questions.explanation: The idea of using fingerprints as a means of individual identification was first proposed in 1858 by District Magistrate of Hooghly district of Bengal province, Sir William Herschel. Subsequently, Dr. Henry Faulds concluded from the marks found at the crime scene that no two fingerprints are the same. The basic principles of specialty and permanence in fingerprints based on Herschel-Faulds's idea were scientifically established by scientific Francis Galton. In this way, the world's first fingerprint bureau was established in Writers' Building (Kolkata) in the year 1897. It was used for the first time by Bengal Police in 1898 for detecting crime

questions.question_text: Whom did Lord Curzon appoint as the Director-General of the Archaeological Department in 1901?
questions.explanation: G.I.C. Lect. Exam 2009 Explanation- Curzon became the Viceroy of India in 1899. He did reforms in India. Curzon appointed Sir John Marshall to the post of Director of the Archaeological Department in 1901. Marshall made efforts to bring the Indus civilization to light.

questions.question_text: Keep the following revolts in chronological order:
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order according to the year of the following revolts is: Revolt Year Place 1 Sannyasi Revolt 1763-1800 AD Bengal and Bihar 2 Odisha Zamindar Revolt 1817 AD Odisha 3 Bhil Revolt 1812-19 AD Rajasthan and Maharashtra 4 Satara Revolt 1840 AD Maharashtra

questions.question_text: Which movement was led by Digambar Biswas and Vishnu Biswas in 1859-60?
questions.explanation: The Indigo Revolt lasted until 1859-60 AD in Govindpur village located in the Nadia district of Bengal. This movement was led by Digambar Biswas and Vishnu Biswas. This practice was also called the 'Dadni Pratha' in the local language. This movement was also supported by Harishchandra Mukherjee, editor of the 'Hindu Patriot'. In 1859 AD, Dinabandhu Mitra supported the Indigo revolt in the play 'Neel Darpan'. This was the first successful movement of Indian peasants. Other movements mentioned in the options, Kuka revolt and Faraizi revolt, were political-religious movements, whereas the Munda revolt was a tribal revolt. The Kuka revolt was led by Bhagat Jawahar Mal, the Faraizi revolt was led by Haji Shariatullah and his son Dadu Miyan, and the Munda revolt was led by Birsa Munda

questions.question_text: Zeliangrong movement started-
questions.explanation: The Zeliangrong movement started in Manipur against the British rule. Its initial leader was Jadonang. During the Civil Disobedience Movement, the Naga woman Rani Gaidinliu strongly opposed British rule. The government put Rani Gaidinliu in jail. She was released from jail only after independence. Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru gave her the title of 'Rani'

questions.question_text: When was the Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Riots of 1875 were mainly the result of tension between peasants and moneylenders. This dispute started in Supa taluka in December 1874. From May to September 1875, these riots in the south left an impact on 33 places in 6 talukas of Pune and Ahmednagar districts. Subsequently, the government appointed a Deccan Riots Commission which investigated the causes of the riots. In 1879 AD, based on the report of this commission, a 'Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act' was passed

questions.question_text: Which of the following peasant movements was the last chronologically?
questions.explanation: The Tebhaga movement was mainly a movement of sharecropper peasants. They raised their voice that they would take two-thirds of the total produce and give only one-third to the Zamindars. That is why this movement was named the Tebhaga movement. This movement lasted from November 1946 to February-March 1947, i.e., for the entire period of the wheat harvest. It was a symbol of the unity of Hindu, Muslim, and tribal peasants. This was the last peasant movement in India in which the bravery of women was seen Special Facts- 1- Champaran Satyagraha - 1917 - Peasant movement 2- Kheda Satyagraha - 1918 - Peasant movement 3- Bardoli Satyagraha - 1928 - Peasant movement

questions.question_text: Sidhu and Kanhu led which movement?
questions.explanation: Among the tribal revolts, the Santhal revolt was the most intense. This revolt is known as Damin-i-Koh. The land area from Bhagalpur to Rajmahal was a Santhal-dominated area. On 30 June, 1855 AD, more than 6 thousand tribals gathered in Bhagnadih and decided to revolt to end the rule of foreigners. The two main leaders of this revolt were Sidhu and Kanhu

questions.question_text: Where did the first serious revolt take place in 1806?
questions.explanation: The Vellore revolt of 1806 AD was a military revolt. The main reason for this revolt was hurting their religious sentiments. New rules were implemented on Indian soldiers in the Madras Army, whereby soldiers were ordered not to wear tilak, not to wear traditional turbans, not to keep beards, and not to wear earrings in their ears. They were given leather caps to wear which had a turret on it. It was heard that it was made of cow or pig skin. Due to this order, there was so much increase in discontent among the soldiers that they revolted

questions.question_text: After the death of Rao Prithvi Singh during the peasant movement, who was appointed as the administrator of Bijolia by the government?
questions.explanation: After the death of Rao Prithvi Singh during the peasant movement, the government appointed Amar Singh Ranawat as the administrator of Bijolia. In this, when Prithvi Singh's son was a minor, the state government, through the court, appointed Amar Singh Ranawat as the administrator

questions.question_text: Where was 'Motilal Tejawat' born?
questions.explanation: Motilal Tejawat was born in 1886 AD in an Oswal family in Koliyari village of the tribal area Phalasia of Mewar. Motilal Tejawat was the Kamdar of Jhadol thikana

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a leader of the Santhal revolt?
questions.explanation: The Santhal revolt spread to Chota Nagpur near Singhbhum of Jharkhand. Its leaders were four brothers, Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, and Bhairav. Keeping in mind the looting of natural resources by the British and the exploitation of tribals by the local Zamindars, these four brothers carried out this revolt. The name of Jagannath is not recorded among the leaders of this revolt
