questions.question_text: Between which countries did the Opium War take place?
questions.explanation: The Opium War was fought between Britain and China. These wars were fought over the opium trade. The first Opium War lasted from 1840-1842 AD. China had to sign the 'Treaty of Nanking' with Britain and China became a semi-colonial country. Meanwhile, the second Opium War lasted from 1856-1860 AD and ended with the Treaty of Peking. In both these wars, European power fulfilled its imperialistic ambitions by defeating China

questions.question_text: On which date did Mao Zedong's famous 'Long March' begin?
questions.explanation: Mao Zedong was a Chinese revolutionary, political thinker, and leader of the Communist Party. He led the People's Republic of China from 1949-1976 AD. Mao Zedong's Long March began on 16 October 1934, which lasted until 20 October 1935. This was actually a military march when the communist army traveled approximately 6000 miles in 310 days. This Long March ended in the Shaanxi province after passing through the difficult regions of western China and turning first towards the west and then towards the north

questions.question_text: Who were the masterminds of the 'First International Workingmen's Association'?
questions.explanation: An important event in the history of the socialist movement was the establishment of the International Workingmen's Association or 'First International' committee in 1864 AD. Its masterminds were Karl Marx and Engels. Its founding meeting took place in London and representatives from Britain, France, Italy, Germany, Poland, Switzerland participated in it

questions.question_text: Who said, 'We cannot create great historical events'?
questions.explanation: Otto von Bismarck was born into a prestigious noble family of Prussia. He had no faith in democracy. Repudiating the principles of liberals in 1862 AD, while clarifying his policy, he said, "The great problems of our time cannot be solved by speeches and majority proposals but only by the policy of 'blood and iron'. We cannot create great historical events."

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not related to America's War of Independence?
questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President of the United States. He was not related to the American War of Independence. Lincoln started his political journey in 1834 and was elected for the Illinois State Legislature as a member of the Whig Party. Lincoln joined the Republican Party in 1856 AD. The civil war in America happened during his time. He was assassinated in 1865. The credit for the end of the slave system in America goes to him

questions.question_text: Which dynasty was ousted from Russia by the 1917 revolution?
questions.explanation: The Russian Revolution was the biggest event of the 20th century's history. At the time of the Russian Revolution in 1917, the power of the Romanov dynasty was there. On 24-25 October, 1917, under the leadership of the Bolshevik party, this revolution started. The Tsar's tyranny was its main reason. During this revolution, Tsar Nicholas II and his family were assassinated

questions.question_text: Who was the organizer of the 'Kuomintang Party'?
questions.explanation: Kuomintang (K.M.T.), which is known as China's Nationalist Party, played an important role in overthrowing China's last dynasty and creating the 'Republic of China'. Its organizer was Sun Yat-sen. Its three principles are – Nationalism, Democracy, and Socialism. Chiang Kai-shek was made the Director General of the Kuomintang party

questions.question_text: Which of the following is related to the 'Positivist' view of history?
questions.explanation: The scientific explanation of Positivism has been done by Auguste Comte. Comte has explained this concept in his books 'Course of Positive Philosophy' and 'The System of Positive Polity'. Comte is considered the founder of Positivism. By determining the place of industrial and scientific progress in human history, he expressed clear faith that by giving proper functional form to these laws, human progress can be developed in a scientific way and achieve its perfection

questions.question_text: Nelson Mandela led which of the following movements?
questions.explanation: Nelson Mandela was born on 18 July, 1918 in Mvezo village in Eastern Cape (South Africa) in the Madiba tribe. Mandela, starting his political journey from 1942, joined the African National Congress in 1944. He fought against Apartheid all his life. He also became the first black head of South Africa. He remained in jail for 27 years in the struggle against Apartheid. Nelson Mandela is also called the Gandhi of Africa

questions.question_text: The unification of Italy was a process in which different leaders and their movements played their important role. Who was the leader of the Young Italy movement?
questions.explanation: Mazzini, a prominent leader of Italy's unification, established an organization named 'Young Italy (1831)' in Marseilles, France. He is considered the main leader of the Young Italy movement. Mazzini said, "If you want to bring revolution in society, then put the leadership in the hands of the youth, unlimited power is hidden in the hearts of the youth of society." Through this, Mazzini laid the foundation of Italy's unification

questions.question_text: Out of the following parts of divided Italy, which one did not have direct control of any foreign power or the Pope?
questions.explanation: In the unification of Italy, the development of railways contributed the most. Mazzini is called the herald of Italy's national movement. Later on, Italy kept getting divided and the regions - Lombardy, Venetia, Naples, Sicily came under the direct control of some foreign power or the Pope, however, Piedmont-Sardinia continued to work independently. Sardinia's conflict with other countries continued. Finally, in 1861 AD, the inauguration of the new parliament took place in the capital of Sardinia

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): The German states, which were thirty-nine in number, were organized into a weak confederation. The administration of this confederation was controlled by the federal Diet, which was controlled by the hands of the Austrian President. Reason (R): The feeling of separatism among the states was very strong and for the sake of the great goal of German unification, no one was ready to leave their individual identity. In the context of the two statements above, which of the following statements is correct?

options.D: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.E: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Germany was the most fragmented country among European countries politically. In which there were about 300 states, Napoleon paved the way for national unity by creating a confederation of 39 states in Germany. Opposing the unification of German states, the Vienna Congress kept it under the influence of Austria as a powerless confederation state. Austria was made the president of this confederation. Germany's federal 'Diet' proved to be a mere organization for making agreements. The feeling of separatism among the states was very strong because every state had its own separate individual identity, which they were not ready to leave

questions.question_text: The architect of German unification, Bismarck, fought three important wars against various European powers. Which of the following wars ended with the Peace of Frankfurt, in which Germany merged Alsace-Lorraine into the German Empire?
questions.explanation: Bismarck, the architect of German unification, fought wars against three different European powers (1) War with Denmark (End with Gastein agreement) (2) Austria-Prussia war (Treaty of Prague) (3) Franco-Prussian War (Treaty of Frankfurt) - This war took place between Prussia and France. Finally, on 10 May 1871 AD, the Treaty of Frankfurt was signed between the two countries, representatives of both countries accepted it. France had to give the regions of Alsace and Lorraine including Metz and Strasbourg to Germany.

questions.question_text: Who are the authors of the famous books 'Treatise on Government' and 'A Letter Concerning Toleration', which established the fundamental ideas of economic freedom, the right to hold property, and freedom of thought?
questions.explanation: John Locke was one of the most influential political philosophers of the modern era. Through his famous books 'A Treatise on Government' (1690) and 'A Letter Concerning Toleration', he established the fundamental rights of economic freedom, the right to hold property, and freedom of thought. Besides this, his thoughts on education are expressed in the book 'Thoughts on Education' (1691)

questions.question_text: What was the most important achievement of the victory of the North in the American Civil War?

options.A: Establishment of Northern banking and trade corporations in Southern America.
options.C: Abolition of slave system and liberation of four million slaves.
options.D: The emergence of Abraham Lincoln as the President of the United States of America.
options.E: Defeat of Union-soldiers by central forces.

questions.explanation: The American Civil War happened between 1861-65 AD between the United States of America and eleven states of the South. The reason for the North's victory in this war was President Abraham Lincoln's national government and the 20 independent states and four border and slave states coming together, whereas the abolition of the slave system and the liberation of four million slaves are known as the main reasons for his victory

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Balkan wars is not correct?

options.A: With the Balkan wars, the European Ottoman Empire ended. The Ottoman Empire lost about 90% of its old European territory and was confined to the South-Eastern corner of the Balkan Peninsula.
options.B: The Balkan wars did not resolve the conflict but rather instigated it further.
options.C: With the Balkan wars, the rivalry between Austria and Serbia increased further.
options.D: France emerged in the role of protector in the Balkan states.
options.E: The Balkan wars and their consequences prepared the ground for the First World War.

questions.explanation: The Balkan Peninsula is a region of South-Eastern Europe. It is the easternmost peninsula of Southern Europe. The Balkan War (1912-13) is considered one of the important reasons for the First World War to occur. With this war, the feeling of rivalry between Austria and Serbia increased excessively. The Ottoman Empire lost about 90 percent of its old European territory and remained confined to the South-Eastern corner of the Balkan Peninsula. The Balkan Alliance of 4 countries (Greece, Serbia, Bulgaria, Montenegro) had to face trouble in the Italo-Turkish war from 1912 to 1913. Russia and France both together fought the war against the Balkan Alliance

questions.question_text: The alliance between which of the following three European countries is known as the Triple Entente (1882)?
questions.explanation: The alliance agreement between Germany, Austria and Italy (European countries) is known as the Triple Entente (Actually, Triple Alliance). The main provisions of this treaty (1) If France attacks Italy, then Austria and Germany will help their friend Italy. (2) If France attacks Germany, then Italy will provide full help to Germany. This treaty was done for 5 years. As a result of the triple alliance treaty, a powerful group of Austria, Germany, and Italy states was formed in Central Europe.

questions.question_text: Match the names of the treaties in List-I with those countries in List-II with whom these treaties were made. List-I | List-II A. Treaty of Versailles | 1. Bulgaria B. Treaty of Saint-Germain | 2. Hungary C. Treaty of Neuilly | 3. Germany D. Treaty of Trianon | 4. Austria Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct matching is Treaty of Versailles (28 June, 1919) - Germany and Allied powers. Treaty of Saint-Germain (10 September, 1919) - Austria and Allied powers. Treaty of Neuilly (27 November, 1919) - Bulgaria and Allied powers. Treaty of Trianon (4 June, 1920) - Hungary and Allied powers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following leaders was behind the formation of the League of Nations after the First World War?
questions.explanation: Woodrow Wilson is known as an academic scholar, administrator, historian, jurist, and politician who interpreted the lights of public administration. He was one of the famous presidents of America. After the First World War, he established the 'League of Nations' (1920) and presented his ideas in the form of the Fourteen Points principle

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): The 1917 Bolshevik Revolution is considered a milestone in human civilization. Reason (R): It had a global impact on human society which encouraged the world and the deprived population to raise their voice against and fight all kinds of inequalities in the world system. In the context of the two statements above, which of the following statements is correct?

options.D: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation.
options.E: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation.

questions.explanation: In Russia, two revolutions took place in 1917, in February and October. The first overthrew the monarchy and the second occurred for the protection of the first revolution. It was against capitalism and in favor of socialism. The Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 in Russia is considered a milestone in human civilization because this revolution encouraged the world and the deprived population to raise their voice against and fight all kinds of inequalities in the world system

questions.question_text: Regarding Lenin's New Economic Policy implemented after the October Revolution in Russia, which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: As a class, farmers were the beneficiaries of the new policy, and farmers had to pay a fixed amount of tax.
options.B: Farmers had full freedom to sell their surplus produce in the open market.
options.C: For investment in private enterprises, even on a small scale, no allowance was given.
options.D: Facilities were given to foreign capitalists to secure liquid capital.
options.E: Private retail trade on a small scale was also allowed.

questions.explanation: After the October Revolution in Russia, Lenin announced the 'New Economic Policy' with the aim of bringing changes in the socialist system and returning towards the capitalist system. The aim of this New Economic Policy was to strengthen the economic cooperation of the working class and farmers, and to encourage all the working classes of cities and villages to develop the country's economy. With the permission to sell surplus produce in the market, the practice of private trade began; this improved the economic condition of the farmers

questions.question_text: The 1935 Laval-Mussolini Agreement is considered a big event of the Fascist regime. Which of the following statements is not true regarding this treaty?

options.A: The 1935 Laval-Mussolini treaty resolved the colonial dispute for the time being and improved relations between the two countries.
options.B: The joint relations of Italy and France was the most dangerous equation of the early period of post-war Europe.
options.C: France strongly opposed the decision of Italy to reject the Versailles Treaty.
options.D: Italy wanted to expand its influence in Northern Africa, Mediterranean region, Danube region, and the Balkans, and that is why it avoided conflict with France.
options.E: The Chinese structural integration with Austria, Germany, and Italy was clear to France and Italy.

questions.explanation: In the early days after the First World War, the objectives of the Fascist movement were not determined by the unity of the nation and basic principles. The 1935 Laval-Mussolini treaty resolved the colonial dispute of that time and relations between other countries improved, and France also gave its support to the Versailles treaty made by Italy

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Hitler's Nazi policies?

options.A: Hitler believed in the Herrenvolk principle, which was based on the idea of racial hatred.
options.B: Hitler supported the idea that the German race has the full right to remove minorities living in the country and suppress them.
options.C: He targeted slaves and Jews, especially Jews because their status was prosperous in Germany.
options.D: To implement Hitler's ideas in reality, he started a campaign named Final Solution.
options.E: His idea on the nation was based on the collective nationality of the original inhabitants of the German nation.

questions.explanation: In the 1930s, Nazism rose in Germany, whose leader was Hitler. Hitler believed in racial superiority and wanted to achieve the whole of Germany. He wanted to remove Jews from Germany

questions.question_text: Who wrote the book 'Rights of the Colonies Examined', which inspired the American Revolution?
questions.explanation: The book 'Rights of the Colonies Examined' which inspired the American Revolution was written by Stephen Hopkins. It was mainly an essay which was published in 1764 AD. Besides this, Thomas Paine's book 'Common Sense' (1775 AD) also played an important role in inspiring the American Revolution

questions.question_text: By the 1765 Quartering Act:

options.A: American colonists were compelled to pay for a part of the expenditure incurred on the British army.
options.B: American colonists' paper currencies were banned.
options.C: Import of rum from other countries was banned.
options.D: American colonists were forced to trade only through British ships.

questions.explanation: The British government passed four main acts for the American colonies 1. Sugar Act (Molasses Act, 1764 A.D.) 2. Stamp Act (1765 A.D.) 3. Currency Act (1765 A.D.) - To ban the use of prevalent 'hundi' and paper currency with other countries in American colonies, so that only English currency is used in trade. 4. Quartering Act (1765 A.D.) - It was necessary for the colonies to bear a part of the expenditure of the maintenance of England's armies in America.

questions.question_text: Colony which did not participate in the First Continental Congress.
questions.explanation: On September 5, 1774 A.D., the first Continental Congress meeting began, in which all colonies (New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York etc.) sent delegates except Georgia. Among the delegates, John Adams and Samuel Adams of Massachusetts, George Washington and Patrick Henry of Virginia, John Rutledge and Christopher Gadsden of South Carolina, Stephen Hopkins of Rhode Island, John Dickinson of Pennsylvania etc. were prominent

questions.question_text: Which Finance Minister suggested the policy of free trade to pre-revolutionary France:
questions.explanation: Louis XVI appointed several Finance Ministers to improve the country's economy, among whom Turgot, Necker and Calonne were prominent. Turgot was a capable economist who tried to follow a policy of fearless reforms by using land efficiently, adopting a policy of free trade, standardizing administration and ending social discrimination. He ended the powerful organization 'Guild' of various professions. Turgot kept a four-point program - no debt, no new taxes, no bankruptcy, and reduction in state expenditure

questions.question_text: Reform that was not implemented by the National Constituent Assembly (1789-1791):

options.B: Division of French administration into department and commune.

questions.explanation: As a result of the French Revolution, the National Constituent Assembly (1789-1791) was called in which the following declarations were made 1. Declaration of Human Rights 2. Division of French administration into department and commune 3. Nationalization of church land 4. Centralization of power should be in the interest of the state and the people 5. End of the tradition of buying-selling of judges' posts 6. End of feudalism and privileges 7. Religious freedom to the people of the state 8. State officials should be responsible to the people.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was not a member of the Jacobin party?
questions.explanation: After the French Revolution, many people wanted to establish a republic in the state. There were two main groups/people - (1) Jacobin party, (2) Girondin party. Among these, the ideas of the Jacobin party were more extremist and revolutionary; their leaders included Marat, Danton, and Robespierre etc. Key leaders of the Girondin party included Madame Roland, Buzot, Condorcet, Brissot etc

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, A is called assertion and R is called reason-

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true and R is false.
options.D: R is true and A is false.

questions.explanation: The first session of the Convention took place on 20 September, 1792 A.D. The Convention did the following work 1. Established a republic by ending monarchy 2. Abolition of slavery 3. Ban on the practice of being imprisoned for debt recovery 4. New metric system of measurement was adopted 5. Setting the prices of food grains and other essential goods. 6. Louis XVI was given the death penalty on 16 January, 1793 A.D. This constitution was accepted in the year 1795. In this way, compared to the National Constituent Assembly 1789-1791, the National Convention 1792-1795 structure was more revolutionary and democratic.

questions.question_text: In which year did Napoleon become the hereditary ruler of France?
questions.explanation: In 1802 A.D., Napoleon took another step in the path of progress. Through a referendum, this proposal of Napoleon was accepted that "He should remain the consul of France for life." Now Napoleon was made the hereditary ruler of France and Napoleon also got the right to appoint his successor. Napoleon's ambition was to become the Emperor of France; in 1804 A.D., he twisted the circumstances in such a way that the Senate had to declare him the Emperor of the French

questions.question_text: The main objective of Napoleon's Continental System was:

options.A: Destruction of Britain's commerce and trade.
options.C: To stop the rise of Russia in the Balkan region.

questions.explanation: Napoleon wanted to establish his dominance over the whole of Europe, in which Britain was the biggest obstacle. Since Britain was surrounded by sea on all four sides, it could not be attacked by land route and no one could defeat it by sea route. That is why, to defeat Britain, Napoleon implemented the Continental System. In this system, according to Napoleon's orders, European countries had to boycott Britain economically. That is, the plan adopted with the objective of stopping England's economic system is also called the Continental System or the policy of trade boycott

questions.question_text: The supporting forces of the Metternich system in Europe were: 1. Church, 2. Royalty, 3. Landlord, 4. Middle class
questions.explanation: After the French Revolution and the fall of Napoleon, the feeling of democracy started developing rapidly in Europe, seeing which the reactionaries started the Metternich system. The Metternich system was first started in Austria. Its main objective was to oppose democracy in the state in every condition. People of the Church, Royalty and Landlord classes were mainly involved in this system. Metternich was a reactionary person and his whole policy was contained in one sentence - "Govern and do not let any change happen." Metternich himself used to say "I have either come to the world too early or too late."

questions.question_text: Metternich's objective behind the Carlsbad Decrees was:

options.B: To control the nationalist student organizations of the Germans.
options.C: To stop the states from forming a political union.
options.D: To stop Prussia from leading the German states.

questions.explanation: In the universities of Germany, organizations named Burschenschaften used to promote liberal principles, which irritated Metternich. Taking advantage of the murder of a reactionary journalist named Kotzebue, Metternich made repressive declarations named Carlsbad Decrees. According to which, he banned the propagation of liberalism, closed all nationalist organizations, and appointed inspectors to keep strict surveillance on teachers and students in universities. Strict controls were established on newspapers etc. Metternich established peace there by following strict policies in all of Germany

questions.question_text: The repeal of the Corn Law (1846) in England indicated:

options.A: The landlord class was becoming weak.
options.B: Food grain production was decreasing in the middle of the 19th century.
options.C: England was following a policy of protectionism.
options.D: England was facing a terrible famine.

questions.explanation: In England in the year 1846, the import duty on food grains was removed through the Corn Law. Due to which the price of bread fell. This is considered a sign of the weakening of the landlord class. It is noteworthy that the period between 1832-1867 A.D. in Britain was the period of the development of liberalism and democracy, in which many important liberal changes took place, in which rules like abolition of slavery in 1833 A.D., ensuring people's participation in local administration, banning women and children from working in mines were made

questions.question_text: Which of the following leaders of Italy wrote the book titled "On the Moral and Civil Primacy of the Italians"?
questions.explanation: In 1843 A.D., Gioberti (a philosopher and patriot) advocated for a federation of Italian states in his book "On the Moral and Civil Primacy of the Italians". He wanted a federation of Italian states to be formed under the chairmanship of the Pope after driving Austria out of Italy. It is noteworthy that Austria had authority over Italy. In 1832 A.D., Silvio Pellico wrote an account of ten years of Austrian prisons titled "Le mie prigioni" (My Prisons)

questions.question_text: Which of the following (Italy's state - ruler description) is not correctly matched?

options.B: Modena - Governed by a prince of Austria
options.C: Bologna - Governed by Italy's royal family
options.D: Sicily - Governed by a Bourbon prince

questions.explanation: 1. Sardinia or Savoy-Piedmont - Governed by Italy's royal family 2. Lombardy and Venetia - Under direct control of Austria. 3. Parma, Modena and Tuscany - Governed by a prince of Austria. 4. In the central part - Pope's state. 5. Naples and Sicily - Governed by Bourbon prince. It is noteworthy that as a result of Napoleon's authority, all these states had been converted into one state, but after the Vienna Congress, they were separated again.

questions.question_text: After which event did Bismarck say - 'We have covered the crack with a piece of paper'?
questions.explanation: After becoming the Chancellor of Prussia in 1862 A.D., Bismarck accelerated the work of unification of Germany. On the problem of Schleswig and Holstein, Bismarck, along with Austria, defeated Denmark. After this, Bismarck made a treaty with Austria at a place named Gastein on 14 August, 1865 A.D., which is also called the Gastein Convention. According to this treaty, Schleswig went to Prussia and Holstein to Austria. The Gastein Convention was a great diplomatic victory for Bismarck. He had said that 'By this convention, we have covered the crack with a piece of paper.'

questions.question_text: The immediate cause of the France-Prussia war (1870-71) was:

options.B: Dispute over the administration of Schleswig-Holstein.
options.C: Attempt to assassinate Napoleon III by Orsini.

questions.explanation: The immediate cause of the France-Prussia war (1870-71) was the dispute over the Spanish succession. However, there were many other reasons for this war 1. Unification of Germany under the leadership of Bismarck. 2. France's unsuccessful attempt to buy Luxembourg (the region under Dutch control).

questions.question_text: Budi Utomo was:
questions.explanation: Indonesia was a colony of the Netherlands (Dutch). At the beginning of the twentieth century, like other countries of the world, a nationalist freedom movement took place in Indonesia. Western-educated youths established the first national organization 'Budi Utomo' in 1908 AD in Gada, whose main objective was to establish schools at the national level in Indonesia. In 1911 AD, with the objectives of promoting Indonesian commercial interests, increasing mutual economic cooperation, intellectual and physical welfare, and spreading Islam, an organization named 'Sarekat Islam' was formed

questions.question_text: The Tydings-McDuffie Act was related to which country?
questions.explanation: The Tydings-McDuffie Act (1934 AD) was the independence act of the Philippines. Philippines was an American colony, which became independent after a 10-year transition period

questions.question_text: What was the Roosevelt Corollary?

options.A: A farmer aid program created in the New Deal.
options.B: A declaration of the United States' right to intervene in matters related to Latin American countries.
options.C: Part of the Atlantic Charter added by Roosevelt.
options.D: A specific package declared by the United States for the Philippines.

questions.explanation: Roosevelt's corollary policy declares the United States' right to intervene in matters related to Latin American countries. In the year 1904, President Roosevelt clearly said that America will play the role of international police force against nations that ignore the Monroe Doctrine (1823 AD). On this basis, Roosevelt intervened in Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, and Nicaragua. Actually, Roosevelt's corollary policy was an additional or complementary policy of the Monroe Doctrine, in which the good neighbor policy and dollar diplomacy were also included

questions.question_text: The founder of Russia's Social Democratic Party was:
questions.explanation: Georgy Valentinovich Plekhanov was a Russian revolutionary, philosopher, and Marxist theorist. He was the founder of the Social Democratic movement in Russia. In 1898 AD, Russian Marxists established the Social Democratic Party. In the 1903 AD London conference, due to theoretical differences, this group split into two parts - Bolshevik and Menshevik. The leader of the Bolshevik was Lenin and the leader of the Menshevik was Martov

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs (Commander of White Army - Commanding region) is not matched correctly?
questions.explanation: After the Russian Revolution of November 1917 AD, the establishment of the Bolshevik government had taken place easily, but there was no lack of opponents in Russia. From November 1917-1919 AD, the Bolsheviks had to fight their opponents hard. The Bolshevik opponents staged rebellions in many regions against the Bolshevik government Siberia region - Admiral Kolchak Southern Russia - General Denikin North-Western Russia - Yudenich And South-West - Wrangel

questions.question_text: By the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, which group of countries given below was declared independent?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was made on 3 March 1918 AD between Russia's Bolshevik government and the Central or Axis powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria and the Ottoman Empire). According to this treaty, Russia separated from the First World War, Ukraine, Belarus, and Finland were made independent, Russia promised to pay 1.5 billion dollars as war indemnity, and Russia promised that it would not propagate communism in Central Europe

questions.question_text: Which of the following provisions was a part of 'War Communism' in Russia?

options.B: Forced seizure of surplus food grains from farmers

questions.explanation: The policy adopted by the Soviet government during the civil war is known as 'War Communism'. This policy remained implemented from July 1918 AD to March 1921 AD, which is also called economic revolution. According to this policy, forced seizure of surplus food grains from farmers was to be done. That is, no farmer could black-market his surplus grain. To stop this kind of black marketing, the government used to send armed squads to seize the farmers' grain and severe punishment was given to those who hoarded the grain grain. That is, no farmer could black-market his surplus grain. To stop this kind of black marketing, the government used to send armed squads to seize the farmers' grain and severe punishment was given to those who hoarded the grain.

questions.explanation: First World War pre-organization | Year A. Triple Alliance | 1. 1882 AD B. England-France agreement | 3. 1904 AD C. Russia-France treaty | 2. 1892 AD D. Triple Entente | 4. 1907 AD

questions.question_text: In the Agadir incident, which of the following two European powers were face to face?
questions.explanation: In the year 1911, France sent its army to suppress the rebellion of Fez and to protect the lives of European people, then Germany opposed it and sent its warship named 'Panther' to Agadir port. Seeing the danger of an international war, England issued a warning against Germany, seeing which Germany had to bow down

questions.question_text: Select the royal dynasties that ended during or immediately after the First World War: 1. Hohenzollern 2. Ottoman 3. Habsburg 4. Romanov Select the correct code-
questions.explanation: During or immediately after the First World War, many empires and royal dynasties ended. The empire of Austria-Hungary disintegrated and the Habsburg dynasty ended. In 1917 AD, the Romanov dynasty of Russia's revolution was ended and a republic was established there and the occupied territories were made independent. The First World War also ended royal dynasties like Turkey's Ottoman Empire and Germany's Hohenzollern

questions.question_text: Two statements are given below, A is assertion and R is reason-

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true and R is false.
options.D: R is true and A is false.

questions.explanation: Following the First World War, generally the European middle class became reactionary because the European middle class was badly affected by the economic consequences of the war

questions.question_text: Which event is considered the formal start of the Cold War?

options.A: The decision of American intervention in the Greek civil war.
options.D: Soviet Union emerging as a nuclear power.
